Areas with Vitamin A deficiency are also endemic with soil-transmitted intestinal worms which contribute to child under nutrition. Vitamin A supplementation and Albendazole is a simple and cost efficient way to alleviate Vitamin A deficiency

title: Help a Torture Survivor this Valentines Day
description: The majority of survivors of torture and trauma living in the US fled for their lives - leaving their loved ones behind. ASTT works with survivors of torture and trauma to help them get back on their feet and eventually become reunited with those they love. Your contribution to ASTT will help approximately 300 clients this year, enabling them to reach their goal of being united with loved ones and help them heal from the emotional wounds inflicted on them by their respective governments.

title: Install 30 Laptops Vietnam Reading Rooms
description: Computers are important learning tools that open doors to many opportunities for school children and gives teachers important resources to improve teaching.

title: Renovate homes for poor, HIV/AIDS infected persons
description:
The aim is to renovate homes of HIV/AIDS infected men, women and children in the biggest slum areas in Bangkok, Thailand. These are people who desperately need access to proper hygiene yet they struggle to  remain clean and dignified in their own homes or shacks.
This project will support full house renovation for two HIV/AIDS affected families in the poorest areas of Bangkok.

title: Safe Shelter & Education for 15 Girls in Thailand
description: This shelter home and education support program protects and prevents at-risk girls from being exploited and trafficked through a highly traversed border area in Northern Thailand. 15 girls receive shelter protection, government school education, life skills development training, nutritious homemade meals, and family outreach services.

title: Hoofin'it for Horse and Human Healing
description: On April 1, 2014, Lauren Davis and Nate Kramer are setting out on their 5+month journey of a lifetime hiking the Appalachian Trail to make a positive impact on their lives and contribute to their passion - the welfare of horses and their powerful bond with people. After completing the hike covering 2,200 miles from Springer Mountain, Georgia to the top of Mount Katahdin in Maine, they plan to continue on into the International Appalachian Trail by hiking up to another 690 to 1,900 miles.

title: Built the center for700 people with mental illness
description: This project will build a therapy , rehabilitaion , Destigmatize  and advocacy for people with mental illness in Thungsaliam, Sukhothai, Thailand, providing therapy, caregivers, and rehabilitation support services to 700 people with mental illnesses.

title: Art Workshops for 100 girls w/ bleeding disorders
description: The National Hemophilia Foundation (NHF) will train female members of its National Youth Leadership Institute to deliver free art workshops to empower 100 young women across the country affected by bleeding disorders.

title: Support Western Maryland Pullman Business Car 204
description: Returning the Western Maryland Railway Business Car #204 to operation on the Western Maryland Scenic Railroad will be a great accomplishment and a tool to educate the public on what life was like during the industrial age while serving to preserve railroad history for our customers and the community as a whole. The Western Maryland Scenic Railroad works hard not only for preservation of railroad history, but also the economic revitalization of Allegany County.

title: Providing Health Books in Bunyore to Western Kenya
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print 600 copies of Hesperian's "Where There Is No Doctor" in Bunyore. Kabala Women Centre (KWC) translated this book because it covers health topics affecting the Bunyore area-nutrition, vaccinations, childbirth & family planning. KWC is a local NGO with a mission of bringing health education and materials to Bunyore communities. Translation work is done & we need your help to get this book into the hands of villagers.

title: Environmental Health  Book in Dari for Afghanistan
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print 1000 copies & 500 CDs of Hesperian's "A Community Guide to Environmental Health" in Dari. Since 80% of the Afghan population is dependent on herding & farming, the welfare of the environment is critical to the economic welfare of the people. Coordination of Humanitarian Assistance (CHA)  has translated this book to give Afghanis tools/methods to improve their environment. CHA founded in 1997 delivers health and educational services.

title: Environmental Health Book in Tamil
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print & distribute 1000 copies of Hesperian's  "A Community Guide to Environmental Health" in Tamil. Adaiyaalam's translation of this book will be the first book in Tamil on environmental issues. It gives villagers methods/techniques for improving their environmental and thus their health. Adaiyaalam is a non-profit publishing group established in 1998 which focuses on women, the down-trodden, the environment and rural health issues.

title: Health Book in Bahasa to Remote Indonesian Islands
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print 500 copies ($6,000) of Hesperian's "Where Women Have No Doctor " in Bahasa to be distributed to Village Health Workers (VHWs) on remote islands ($2,400). 40-60 of these VHWs will receive training on information in the book. The translating NGO is PERDHAKI, a Catholic health organization working in the outlying islands of Indonesia to make medicine more available and to increase medical care to poor and rural communities.

title: Health Book for Disabled Mongolian Women
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to finish the translation of Hesperian's "A Handbook for Women with Disabilities" in Mongolian and print 1,000 copies. The translating NGO is Mongolian National Association of Wheelchair Users (MNAWU) which services all 13,000 people in wheelchairs across Mongolia with social services, empowerment of members & legal advocacy. The books will be accessible in public places and  thus help all women with disabilities.

title: Environmental Health Book in Urdu Ready to Print
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print & distribute 500 copies of Hesperian's  "A Community Guide to Environmental Health" in Urdu. This book will give villagers methods/techniques to improve their environment & general health.   The translating NGO is Swat Youth Front (SYF),  an independent youth organization working for poverty reduction, illiteracy, unemployment, women empowerment, disaster relief and peace in Malakand Region, KPK, Pakistan (Swat District) since 1997.

title: Women's Health Book in Cebuano for Rural Villages
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print and distribute 5,000 copies of Hesperian's "Where Women Have No Doctor" in Cebuano to health workers in remote areas of Negros Oriental.  Using this book, health workers can provide treatment/prevention methods as well as general health information to women in their communities. The translation was done by Silliman University Marina Mission Clinic (SUMMC), a community health clinic serving the rural population of Negros Oriental.

title: A Truck to Deliver a Million Meals on Wheels
description: Our project will buy a new truck to deliver over a million meals to older Americans. We have been feeding hungry homebound seniors and the disabled since 1974. Every day our truck is filled with hundreds (350-500) of hot meals from the kitchen and brought to the caring volunteers who will deliver them. The truck has served us well for 20 years - until now. It breaks down - a lot - and there are too many vulnerable citizens relying on us to put meal delivery at risk.

title: Typhoon Haiyan Coconut Replanting Project
description: The project will initiate the replanting of coconut trees in super-typhoon ravaged areas in the provinces of Leyte and Biliran. Vast tracts of coconut lands were destroyed leaving thousands of small coconut farmers destitute and without any source of income.

title: Hesperian Book to Help Blind Children in Georgia
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to finish the translation of Hesperian's "Helping Children who are Blind" in Georgian and print 1,000 copies. Services for blind children are mostly non-existent in Georgia.  There is no book in Georgian to help parents/teachers/counselors to deal with their blind children. The translating NGO is Mariani,  a group of professionals working towards the rehabilitation, education and social inclusion of blind and partially sighted people.

title: SoulMovement Yoga Young Women's Champions of Peace
description: An Empowerment program designed for young woman ranging from 16 -young adult. Aligned with Art Studio's Standards, artistic expression, a teen approach to Yoga and meditation, (cultivation of mindfulness in daily life), empowerment and leadership skills, fun approaches to wellness and SoulMovement, community,trust building and play embody this program. *serves as a precursor to participate in a Yoga teaching certification for those showing interest and commitment and follow through.

title: Empower Afghan girls with computer skills
description: By the time many Afghan girls reach puberty, they are pulled out of school and forced into early marriage for the short-term economic gain of their families. Help the Afghan Children's computer education program is making a difference for thousands of deserving Afghan girls every year, empowering them with computer literacy skills so they can secure jobs, help their families break the cycle of poverty, and become proud, productive citizens.

title: Saving Mothers' Lives in Sierra Leone and Liberia
description: Sierra Leone is one of the toughest places in the world to be a mother, with one in 23 women dying in childbirth. This project will improve access to maternal and child healthcare for women, adolescent girls and children under five in Sierra Leone and Liberia. Thanks to BRAC's partnerships with other donors, contributions to this project have extraordinary leverage: Funding of $22,000 raised through GlobalGiving will be matched and multiplied, unlocking $76,500 to reach 3,975 women.

title: Shoes and School Supplies for Dominican Children
description: The Mencia Foundation is a 501c3 nonprofit organization that helps underprivileged children in the Dominican Republic and other Latin American countries. We support children by providing the basic resources needed to attend school (i.e. notebooks, backpacks, pens/pencils). We also provide additional needed items such as shoes, socks, and undergarments. The purpose of this project is to provide walking shoes and school supplies to school children of rural andcommunities of the Dominican Republic

title: Need an adequate food for cow preservation
description: To lead a normal and peaceful life, there is drastically needed forest preservation, water preservation, animal preservation etc.that make the earth healthy, hygienic and pollution free.Our heartiest effort is to preserve cow for mankind in society.We, the organisation have been working with this unique concept for long time because of giving high flavor in every spare of life.We think, to materialise our innovative idea in every corner of life, donor should come forward to make it grand success

title: Initiation of Cervical Cancer Prevention program
description: Cervical cancer is big health problem in DRCongo and is the first cause of death by cancer in the country. This disease is fully preventable by simple means but continue killing women because of missing colposcopy service in the country.This project will help women getting access to screening and treatment of precancer and then we can save lives of women.We will perform colposcopy for 1000women and we'll treat all positive cases by cryotherapy or excision. Awareness for 360 women will be done.

title: Help Feed Hungry Children in Zimbabwe
description: Despite a change of leadership, nothing has changed for the ordinary citizen of Zimbabwe. Prices keep escalating and unemployment is around 99%. This project aims to assist the 250-day scholars at the local Primary School with daily nutritious lunch, essential stationery, exercise and textbooks, by assisting with these essential resources we hope to alleviate external struggles so that the children can focus on their education and continue further.

title: Catalyzing agricultural innovation in Tanzania
description: This project will raise the skills and productivity of small scale farmers, 84% of whom will be women. By establishing community support and providing high quality inputs and training, this project will increase agricultural productivity and incomes. Thanks to BRAC's partnerships with other donors, contributions to this project have extraordinary leverage: Funding of $21,382 raised through Global Giving will be matched and multiplied by others, unlocking $73,055 to reach 2,333 women farmers.

title: Education for Slums and Rural Kenyan Students
description:
Our mission at CSRD Education and Vocational Training Program is to create and promote an environment that empowers our young and precious generations of Slums and Rural Kenya to take up education as a way to enrich their own life, the life of others, thus the prosperity of the country. 
CSRD will provide encouragement, opportunity, and access to higher education to 200 poor but deserving students who have demonstrated academic excellence, moral character, integrity, and career objectives.

title: Water School - Environmental Education in Morocco
description: Living sustainably is a global challenge that requires active participation from people of all ages all around the world. February-June 2017, Dar Si Hmad's Mobile Water School will provide experiential learning opportunities for children ages 7-13 in southwest Morocco's Ait Baamrane region. The Water School uses environmental concerns to engage rural children in learning about the realities of the natural world, locally and globally.

title: Help Fix My Face Please
description: Jespa Ngong is a teenager who, as a toddler, was badly burned in a fire accident at his parents home in Babanki Tungo, North West Region of Cameroon. He has never received proper medical treatment, and as a result his face remains disfigured and he only has one functioning arm. His eyes have continued to become worse, sometimes bleeding if he touches them.

title: Help cancer patients in a care center in Slovakia
description: For the past 9 years, the Vrba volunteers have been actively involved at the Oncological Institution of St. Elizabeth. They regularly visit the patients, talk with them, play games, organize free-time activity groups, and operate a mobile library. We would like to expand the volunteer activities and engage those who are not able to commit to long-term support of terminally ill people, but are willing to be help with short-term activities such as delivering coffee, tea and magazines.

title: Support Small Business to Fight Hunger in Rwanda
description: The community of potters, formerly known as the "Batwa" pre-genocide, is a historically marginalized population that faces poverty and severe food shortages. To address the high prevalence of malnutrition in the community, HDI will help a community of 200 people to start a pig cooperative. The cooperative will give community members an income-generating activity to alleviate the effects of extreme poverty and provide the community with a rich protein source that will reduce malnutrition rates.

title: Navrat: Lets find every child in Slovakia a family
description: In Slovakia there are currently 4500 children without a mother or a father who would read them a bedtime story in the evening. They live in orphanages. 10 years ago, this number was one third more. These children often suffer from hurts and insecurities more than others. The Navrat organization has been helping them to find adoptive mothers and fathers, foster families and it also works on helping families in crisis.  Help us: We want every child in Slovakia to have a family.

title: Nthunguni Spring Project
description: KWENCH will work with the Nthunguni Water Project self-help group to develop water from a perennial spring and distribute it to 17 water points. At present, the village of Mumani has no developed water system at all. The project will also contain sanitation, hygiene and livelihood components.

title: Social center for mentally ill people in Slovakia
description: Dss-Most Center helps people with mental health disorders on their way to attaining self-sufficiency.  Your support can help them develop their ability to participate in daily life.  Give them the courage to do so.

title: Support grieving children and families in Slovakia
description: Plamienok is an organisation which takes care of a center for grieving and suffering children and families in Slovakia. We organize a summer camp for children who have lost a loved one (a parent, sibling, grandparent, ). The purpose of the camp is to provide children with a safe space to express and share the emotions experienced after losing a family member.

title: Vocational Skills 40 Indian Orphan school drop-out
description: This project plans to establish a open school to provide vocational skills for orphan children and victimized girls who hail from the poorest sections of rural villages in Salem and Namakkal districts. The project will empower 40 such children imparting Basic Computer skills, Photography, Communicative English and Small business management skills using practical hands on learning with free transportation.

title: Trigger the girl effect with education
description: Around the world, millions of primary-aged children are out of school - and girls are  are far more likely than boys to never set foot in a classroom. To address this, BRAC is training local women as teachers and opening pre-primary and primary schools for children from poor families, especially girls. Building on over 40 years of experience in Bangladesh, BRAC has now expanded its education work to Liberia, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, the Philippines, and Afghanistan.

title: Support a hatchery and feed mill in Liberia
description: There is big demand for hatchery operations and a variety of poultry feed in Liberia. This project will meet this demand by expanding profitable social enterprises in line with our broader goals of reducing poverty and hunger by creating livelihoods. Thanks to BRAC's partnerships with other donors, contributions to this project have extraordinary leverage: Funding of $20,514 raised through Global Giving will be matched and multiplied, unlocking $42,838 to reach hundreds poultry farmers.

title: Support Family Farming in Liberia and Sierra Leone
description: This project will reduce poverty and food insecurity among smallholder, women farmers in Liberia and Sierra Leone by supporting kitchen farms and promoting livestock production, health, and other good practices for rural households. Thanks to BRAC's partnerships with other donors, contributions to this project have extraordinary leverage: Funding of $18,975 raised through Global Giving will be matched and multiplied by others, unlocking $60,882 to reach 600 women farmers.

title: Women's Health Book in Tamil for Village Women
description: This project is to raise the final funding needed to print and distribute 1,000 copies of Hesperian's "Where Women Have No Doctor" in Tamil. This book will empower health workers and other educated women in Tamilnadu with current health information to treat and prevent common health problems experienced by women, especially in remote areas. Adaiyaalam, a non-profit publishing group established in 1998, focuses on women, the down-trodden, the environment and rural health issues.

title: Nevada Slaughter Auction Rescue
description: Rescue 10 - 15 horses from the brutal horrors of the slaughter pipeline at a Nevada Slaughter Auction.  The horses that we will be rescuing have only two choices: be rescued, or ship to slaughter.  The funds raised will be used for the purchase, transporting to our shelter in California, health certificates, coggins test, vet check and veterinarian care, rehabilitation, feed, training and care of the horses.

title: One Billion Rising for Mamafrica Congo
description: At Mamafrica, we work to change the commonly known narrative of the women living in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) from victim to SURVIVOR. We are calling on all men and women this Valentine's Day, February 14th, to RISE UP for JUSTICE and support the women of DRC. At Mamafrica we help women to become leaders in the community, educate their children, and break the norm of a male dominated work force. With your help we can RISE UP and change the narrative of women in DRC.

title: Cycle for Survival
description: Cycle for Survival is the movement to beat rare cancers. Our high-energy indoor team cycling events provide a tangible way for you to fight back. 100% of every dollar raised directly funds lifesaving rare cancer research at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK).

title: Afterschool Education for 50 Tuskegee 6-18 yr olds
description: Your donation helps provide 50 at-risk 6-18 year olds with an enhanced after school education program of mentoring, tutoring and nutritional meals, to help them successfully complete their school year.

title: Education for Children with Disabilities in Kabul
description: This project benefits the community-driven Rahyab School for Children with Disabilities located in Kabul, Afghanistan, where children aged 6 to 18 years receive basic education and vocational training from trained teachers, often with a disability themselves. This school helps filling the lack of assistance to children with disabilities in the public school system, providing this marginalized community the necessary skills to integrate into Afghan's society as active members.

title: Vietnam Technology for Education
description: Your gift will support the donation of technology and supporting services to improve the quality of education in Vietnam

title: Kapadia Education Foundation (KEF)
description: KEF is a philanthropic organization founded to help students achieve their educational goals through direct involvement with each student. We firmly believe that education is the key to personal growth and a thriving local community. By helping students advance their education, we empower them to solve their community's social problems, end poverty and remove barriers that lead to ignorance and despair. Help KEF sponsor 5 or more students for up to four years of college education today

title: Generating Organic Compost for Farming in Haiti
description: Haiti is one of the most climate-vulnerable and food-insecure countries in the world. By producing organic, agriculture-grade compost from safely-treated human waste, SOIL is transforming a public health crisis into a climate-positive environmental solution. Our lifesaving sanitation service provides a safe in-home toilet to over 6,000 people in urban Haiti and produces 80+ tons of compost annually to support agriculture and reforestation.

title: Help stop cholera and save lives in Haiti
description: This project will empower the 15,000 members of Crochu to achieve their goals of reducing Cholera and other diarrheal diseases in children and improving safe motherhood practices.  We will do this by training community health workers, improving sanitation, and educating locals on prevention sources of cholera and diarrhea.

title: $18/month for educating underprivileged poor child
description: This project aims in providing  free education to underprivileged children, both boys and girls, who are first generation learners, coming from broken or shattered homes. Providing education to them helps in eradicating child labor in the region. Sevalaya's Mahakavi Bharathiyar Higher Secondary School is a Government recognized free school, started in the year 1988 and for the past 26 years has been producing excellent results in terms of Pass percentage, top scorers and drop out ratio

title: Get 5,000 Poor Filipino Children To Eat Apples
description: For many Filipino children an apple is just a representation of the letter A in the English alphabet they learned in school.They never tasted apples in their life.The Appledrive Project by Aral Pinoy Affiliate RJ "Appleboy" Garcia Jr will provide Apples and Appleboy Comic Books to 5,000 Filipino children in Metro Manila, Pangasinan and Tacloban for them to eat apples more often and to educate them and their parents about the importance of living healthy and why they should eat apples.

title: Train Workers Caring for Orphans in Togo
description: This project will provide 30 workers at 10 orphanages in Togo with training in holistic care, child development, abuse, common mental illnesses, basic hygienic care and first aid, and it will connect them to the existing mental health network and assist them in formalizing their centers. Together, these workers care for about 1,500 children who will benefit from improved care and services.

title: A HOME FOR 158 ANIMALS RESCUED
description: This project seeks to acquire a permanent home to 158 animals that have been rescued from abuse and neglect their owners on the streets, with the possibility of giving them better conditions and emotional balance, stability and enough space to allow rehabilitation and future adoption.

title: Helping Gabonese children access their rights
description: Child helplines are at the forefront of child protection, giving children and young people a voice and providing them with care, support and protection. In order to ensure all children have access to such a vital resource, Child Helpline International supports child helplines across the globe by providing capacity building opportunities. In Gabon there is no such child helpline at present and children are denied access to basic help and protection.

title: Repair drainage problems and septic failure
description: The Sawaquat Center works toward preventing community deterioration by working with At-Risk Youth, Homeless Teens, Veterans with PTSD and Individuals or Families In Need, learning valuable life skills such as sustainable living and teamwork, promoting tolerance and understanding and increasing self-worth and self-reliance. The Center's septic system is failing, and it is imperative that it be be completed by the end of May, before the anticipated influx of Volunteers and Individuals In Need.

title: Support children from tribal families in India
description: The project will improve the quality of life of underprivileged children,their families and communities in Mulshi Taluka,District Pune,India by ensuring education and improving the health of tribal children.Community Aid and Sponsorship Programme works with school going children in unconnected areas where the children have few opportunities for education and are in poor health.The project will provide educational support, health services and opportunities to cultivate hobbies in children.

title: Bring Safe Water to School Kids in Vietnam
description: Many children in Vietnam lack access to safe water for both drinking and hand-washing. Safe water is defined as water free of disease-causing organisms and chemicals that harm human health. Hygiene education is severely lacking and diseases like diarrhea run rampant. MEDRIX addresses these issues by providing water filtration systems, hand-washing stations, and hygiene education to create a sustainable future for the next generation.

title: Sustainable Agriculture in Guatemala
description: This project will be the first to support our new grassroots partner AMMID (Association Maya-Mam for Research and Development) in Comitancillo, San Marcos, Guatemala. AMMID is an inclusive organization, which sustainably strengthens the social, cultural, political, economic and environmental development of families and communities in the municipality of Comitancillo, based on principles of harmony, fairness and respect for nature.

title: Meals for 1850 Young Students in Pakistan
description: In 1985, the NUR Community Outreach Program (NCOP) was launched with the mission "to work towards poverty alleviation by creating access to better education, health and economic development". As part of the NUR Community Outreach Program, the NUR Food Bank was started to provide meals on a weekly basis to every child at the NUR Foundation Schools. In the future, we aim to provide such meals on a daily basis in order to alleviate the hunger crisis among the school going children.

title: HELPING CARAMA  SURVIVORS OF FLOODING DISASTER
description: This project is about building 100 houses for 100 families in Carama, to provide shelters to the survivors of  the Sunday, February 9th, 2014 torrential  rains and landslides that have left at list 77 people dead, about 12,000 displaced in Bujumbura and around 1000 houses destroyed in the northern  areas of Bujumbura, Capital City. The Carama location is where JRMD  helped 786 families to build 786 houses  whom their homes were destroyed during the ethnic ware in 1993.

title: Food and basic needs for the poor.
description: We are collecting resources that are available by the truck loads in San Diego and delivering them to where there is great need just over the international border into Tijuana. We will provide food and basic needs to homes for children, the elderly, infirmaries, shelters, and rehabs. We also lead 2 outreaches a week where 400+ people go through our food lines.

title: Empower 40 Orphans with Computer Skills Training
description: This program providing computer skills training through skilled trainer to 40 abandoned orphan children in Joy Home Orphanage. Training in basic computer skills provides essential job-related skills and empowers orphans, Street Children through this innovative program. Data entry typing & Desktop Publishing to give job security & self employment opportunity to destitute children and a secured life to them. Computer competency or proficiency is a vital skill in today's computer connected society.

title: Access To Quality Education For Youth In Korogocho
description: This project will provide financial support to Korogocho slum youth towards achieving high school education as well as offer mentorship. Poverty denies many youth a chance to get an education and therefore, the project will allow the youth a fair chance not only to get their right to education but also improve their chances of employability.

title: A CORONARY CARE UNIT FOR  LOW-INCOME PEOPLE
description:
Project of the Help for the Andes Foundation in a joint venture with Hospital Clinico U Chile:

This Coronary Unit, in addition to its indisputable role in caring for patients, plays an important teaching role, participating in the training of a large number of specialists, as the principal post-graduate training center in Chile. For this important task, it is necessary to have better technology for the benefit of our patients, as well as to better prepare our doctors-in-training.

title: Education for 300 Indigenous Children in India
description: Children in South India live in abject poverty, especially in discriminated Dalit and Tribal social groups. Parents lack education, are illiterate, and work menial jobs for little pay. Their unsupported children fall behind and drop out of school. Our after school Education Centers operate 3 hours a day 6 days a week and are free for students. The tutoring is associated with a 20 point increase in math and language performance. Please visit our website link below for more information.

title: Running the World, For the World
description: We are embarking on a journey to run the 7 continents and promote the importance of sustainability. Our focus is on the vital role that forests play in development, and we protect them by planting trees & curbing deforestation through sustainable agriculture. With your support, we are providing holistic solutions to the environmental and social challenges facing rural forest-edge communities. For each step we take, we will plant a tree, protect a tree, or change a life. Join us in the challenge!

title: Youth March 2 A Different Beat in Southern Alberta
description: Help youth gain access to supports they need to March 2 A Different Beat.  This project will provide funding for youth programs that support youth at risk, immigrants, victims of sexual violence, bullying, and suicide.  By giving them access to a variety of services including counselling, mentoring, community involvement, and much more we help them live a better life either independently or with their family, we reduce crime rates, and we help them build a feeling of hope.

title: Girls Leading Our World (GLOW) Leadership Academy
description: GLOW Leadership Academy 2014 will empower 75 teenage Bulgarian girls by giving them the social skills needed to think beyond the traditional limitations which our man dominated society still has.

title: 195 Emergency Health Kits for Refugee Women
description: This project will provide Emergency Health Kits of 195 South Sudanese women and their families currently taking refuge at Nyumanzi refugee camp in Adjumani, Uganda. These kits will include essential items such as soap, salt, rope, a dish towel, a washing basin, sanitary pads, underwear, and educational pamphlets designed for the refugee population on topics such as peace-building, emergency health, and refugee rights.

title: Sponsor a Child Education - Save the Future
description: Education is the key to sustainable development especially female education. SSD believes if we want to change the destiny of Pakistan, it has to be through educating its masses especially females. SSD recently launched its "Sponsor a Child Education" Program, wherein SSD through its supporters and sponsors finance education of deserving out of schools girls as "Pakistan is the second largest country after Nigeria - having a large number of out of school children" (UNESCO).

title: Education/Arts Orphan, Disabled Children Cambodia
description: This project will help up to 25 orphans some with HIV and epilepsy, as well as blind children. By living at our school, this allows them to receive full time care, scholastic education with Braille, traditional Cambodian performing arts training, as therapy and vocational training. The children (except for the blind) have no parents, no extended families and have no alternative care except for our school; We work with the Ministries of Culture, Education & Social Affairs and local authorities.

title: Give Mobility Devices for People in Haiti
description: The project is operating on the grounds of the Hopital Adventiste d'Haiti in Port-au-Prince and have provided free mobility devices to over 860 people since 2010, after the disastrous earthquake. About half of people who benefit from the project are children under 12 years of age. The project is also training 4 Haitians to become prosthetic and orthotic expert technicians to make sure that people with disabilities in Haiti receive service in the future, after WRF's project is over .

title: Protect 15 families from earthquakes in Indonesia
description: This project will provide 15 families in Cekal Village, in the Aceh Province of Indonesia, with engineering guidance so they can rebuild safe, earthquake-resistant homes. We will also train local builders, engineers and government officials to promote wide acceptance of safe building techniques.

title: Stock a Reuse Medical Library For Seattle
description: This project will stock Go Anywhere Medical Library in Seattle with reusable medical equipment and supplies, supporting seniors who can't afford these items on their monthly budgets.

title: Lab technician training for 15girls in South India
description: The training is supposed to educate 15 girls from rural areas in Tamil Nadu as medical lab technicians. After the training, they will have many possibilities to work in the medical field and therefore support their own families with food and money. Not only their education will increase but also their self esteem and -determination. The girls come from particularly disadvantaged families such as HIV patients or one parented families.

title: Rescue Displaced Families in South Sudan
description: In South Sudan, families are being forced from their homes due to the ongoing violence and food crisis. The situation right now is dire as women and children are arriving in displacement camps without food, clothing, shelter materials, or support. World Concern is responding to help families who have fled violence by providing emergency supplies, food, water, trauma counseling, and more.

title: Stomp out tuberculosis in South Sudan
description: South Sudan became an independent state on July 9, 2011. The young country is grappling with a myriad of problems including several health challenges that, if left uncontrolled, have serious negative implications not only for the general health of people, but also for economic growth. Controlling tuberculosis (TB) is one of these health challenges. This project seeks to strengthen South Sudan's National Strategic Plan for TB Control.

title: SUPPORT 1,500 MOST VULNERABLE CHILDREN IN TANGA
description: PASADIT Organization plans to reach 1,500 Most Vulnerable Children affected by HIV/AIDS pandemic by supporting them to access education and health care, by providing them with school uniforms and school materials and Health Fee Exemption Cards for free health services, send  out of school to vocational training. Likewise the project will build the capacity of Care Givers  on economic aspects so that households can manage their daily lives without depending on donor support

title: Fight against Cancer - Need of the hour
description: 10 lakh new cases of cancer occur and 7 lakh die of various forms of cancer every year in India. In Tamilnadu, burden of cancer is predicted to increase by 32 per cent in 2016, translating to 55,000 new cancer cases per year as per a study by cancer institute. 80% of the cancer patients go to a doctor at an advanced stage and this hampers the treatment. SWESTIC plans to do awareness&screening camps and referral linkages so as to facilitate early detection, timely treatment in Dindigul district.

title: Education for 100 Tribal children in India
description: The aim of this project - Literacy & Civic Education is to build capacities of Marginalized Poor Yanadi Tribe to be a better citizen through our Student Learning Centre program for un-enrolled working class poor children and illiterate adults to inculcate the Ethics & Civic Sense along with literacy to this community, eventually to reduce the incidence of behavioral problems, increase recreational and social opportunities to promote positive attitude for a better and responsible future citizen.

title: Saving the lives of poor Heart Patients in Narowal
description: Narowal is one of the remotest and underdeveloped districts of Pakistan. Sughra Shafi Medical Complex-Narowal a project of SAHARA for Life Trust, a 250 bedded Hospital is providing state of art cardiac health facilities to more than 4 million population of catchment area. All types of treatment to heart patients including injection Streptokinase are being offered 24/7 and free of cost. Through this project 540 lives of  poor & marginalized patients of Acute Myocardial Infarction can be saved.

title: Volunteer With Us to Support 12 informal Schools
description: Nairobi's informal schools face formidable challenges with lack of teaching staff and learning materials. In our work in local schools over the last 6 years it has become clear to us that they need support to improve the quality of education, access to reading materials and help the community gain skills and experience. Our team of 5 volunteers together with yourself will help support targeted mentoring in the 12 informal schools in Ruaraka schools and donate reading materials.

title: Scholarships to Live Dreams and Move Forward
description: This project helps students and their families affected by the disaster pursue their education at Sendai YMCA College.  Without these scholarships the student's families would not have the resources for them to pursue their chosen hotelier career.     Tohoku youth will lead the recovery of Tohoku and this initiative helps train future leaders of the area's tourism industry.   The program also provides English conversation lessons, volunteer, leadership and exchange opportunities.

title: BICYCLES FOR 200 UNDERPRIVILEGED SCHOOL GIRLS
description:
This project seeks to provide bicycles to 200 underprivileged school girls in the deprived and hard to reach communities in the East Mamprusi District in the Northern region of Ghana, who walk long distance between 5 to 10 kilometers to attend Junior High School daily.
The distance these underprivileged school girls walk to school every day is impacting negatively on their academic lives some of which are; truancy, lateness to school, high dropout rate and poor academic performance.

title: FISTULA SURGERY SAVE WOMEN'S LIVES IN SIERRA LEONE
description: WHH serves women in under served areas worldwide. WHH is traveling this year to Sierra Leone, partnering with Dr. Maggi - founder of the West Africa Fistula Foundation. Sierra Leone, is one of the most dangerous places on earth to give birth, infant mortality and maternal deaths among the highest in the world. Sierra Leone, a country of about 6 million has only 1 OB/GYN. Women spend from 2 -15 days in labor - no midwife - no Cesarean childbirth; causing obstetric fistula to become inevitable.

title: Help Kenyan and Ugandan Women Provide Clean Water
description: Over 3.4 million people die per year from poor water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) conditions. Global Women's Water Initiative (GWWI) trains African women to build and sell water filters, promote good hygiene practices and become social entrepreneurs launching WASH businesses. Help GWWI support female technicians to build 200 biosand filters providing clean water and promoting good hygiene to 1000s of students and families in Kenya and Uganda, keeping girls in schools and women earning income!

title: Rebuilding community from tsunami with education
description: Rebuilding community of Ogatsu, northern Japan, lost 80% of town from the tsunami of March 11, 2011.  In a still damaged town, creating a sustainable learning center for children in Japan and all over the world.  Providing Fishery, Agriculture, Forestry, Cooking, and Arts/Crafts experiences with locals in rich natural environment, to become active for the our planet's future.  Restoring old wooden school into accommodation, restaurant, and classrooms to receive children and a place for community

title: FEED A HUNGRY CHILD (UKRAINE)
description: Standard of living in Ukraine is low. Average wage in most Ukrainian towns is not more than 150 US dollars per month. At that, normal nutrition for 1 person costs 465 US dollars per month. In this situation we created a project, directed mainly on support of children from broken, large or crisis families. We give children more chances to grow up and become healthy and well-educated persons.

title: Orphaned Abandoned Children Pack for 100 Children!
description: The Baby Steps programme welcomes orphaned and abandoned children to 14 orphanages under our care. Children arrive generally with no more than the clothes they stand up in and are traumatised. A staff member meets each child arriving, to be their mentor. They greet the child and introduce them to their new 'Home'.  We provide each child with a welcome pack: often the very first things they ever owned. It includes a Teddy Bear because everybody needs a Teddy to hold in times of crisis!

title: Help Students, Families and Schools Recover
description: This project will continue the work of TAMF in three areas:  - Taylor Anderson Reading Corners (Bunkos) - donate books shelves with English books to Ishinomaki schools to encourage students to enjoy English and to become future bridges between the U.S. and Japan.  Support book clubs which use the bunko's.  -  High School Exchange programs between Ishinomaki and Richmond, VA. to promote relations. -  Donate "Taylor Award"  trophy to English speech competition champions in Ishinomaki JH schools.

title: Smile Together Ishinomaki
description: One of the long term effects of the disaster is the mental stress that comes with losing loved ones, homes, jobs and community.  This Ishinomaki based project provides support to help rebuild neighborhood comunities in Ishinomaki.  .Big Up Ishinomaki in the Okaido neighborhood of Ishinomaki and Kodopany Community Space in the Watanoha neighborhood of Ishinomaki and Project Yui are partners in this project.

title: Economic Self-sufficiency for 280 Senegalese Women
description: This project would help nearly 280 women in CREATE!'s six partner villages enhance their garden cooperatives' entrepreneurial endeavors through a poultry raising initiative.  Poultry raising will allow cooperative members to increase their incomes and provide a well rounded diet for their families. CREATE! works with villages in rural Senegal to improve access to water and provide comprehensive training in year-round sustainable crop cultivation and income generation.

title: Dr. Morris Cerullo Teaching Hospital in Kamashi
description: The project aims to equip a new hospital building with medical supplies and equipment in the remote and rural Kamashi Zone in Ethiopia. Kamashi is located in west Ethiopia and has a population of 88,028. There is  no hospital within 100 km (62 mile) radius. Therefore,KHI began constructing a hospital here to serve the population's health needs. KHI needs your help to ship containers with needed medical equipment, and transport them over land and sea to the community's first hospital.

title: Camp for children with Type 1 Diabetes in Haiti
description: For a Haitian child with Type 1 Diabetes,  a lack of education is just as dangerous as a lack of insulin. With local partner FHADIMAC, AYUDA volunteers will staff an overnight camp for 50 children living with Type 1 Diabetes in Haiti.  Using a peer to peer diabetes education program, campers will learning from other youth living with the same condition.  The campers will gain life-saving resources to better manage their own diabetes and live happier, healthier lives.

title: Build Health Center for 5,000 Pakistani Villagers
description: This project will build a Clinical Health Center in Samundari - a remote area of Faisalabad, Pakistan, comprising of more than 500,000 population. In Pakistan, more than 1,800 active viral diseases are present which include dengue, hepatitis, tuberculosis, HIV, hey fever, dysentery, etc. Due to unemployment and poverty people could not take proper medication and health care. This Project will provide a Clinical Health Center to give FREE medical check-ups, medicines, lab-tests and food advice.

title: Help a deserving student in NYC earn a degree
description: St. George's Society of New York's Scholarship Program provides critical financial aid to final-year college students who have achieved excellent academic standing, but due to financial hardship are unable to complete their final year of undergraduate studies.

title: Empowering the deaf through technical Skills
description:
The deaf and or hard -to-  hearing people  are more useful to society. But, they are  discriminated against  politically, socially and economically in the least developed country of Nepal. Their misery is multiplied  as they do not have technical skills that a job requires.

To address this  grave issue of human dimension, Synergy Nepal (SN) has a plan to empower about 50 thousand  deaf/hard to hearing in a span of  5 years. The project has a strategy  for their empowerment at the local level.

title: Art Programs For 5,000 In-Need New York Children
description: ARTS FOR ALL serves approximately 5,000 children per year through both our in-person and virtual programming. Through our programming, our workshops are offered in many artistic disciplines, and are free of charge to the children and youth organizations we serve.

title: Rehabilitate Mammals and Raptors in Georgia
description: AWARE Wildlife Center is the only facility in the Atlanta area that rehabilitates all species of injured and orphaned native Georgia wildlife. In 2013, AWARE rescued over 1,300 wild animals, many harmed by human carelessness. Most of these animals were successfully returned to the wild. Because wildlife is a precious natural resource, providing invaluable services such as seed dispersal, pollination, pest control, and sanitation, to name just a few, we believe that it is worth protecting.

title: Give a Future to 100 Kids in Vietnam
description: Make a difference to very poor, incredibly hard working, smiling, grateful children of Cam Ranh (Vietnam). The timing has never been better - or more critical. Many of the children in the nearby villages are not equipped to share in economic success of this rapidly developing area. They need English and computer skills. We are providing that education. With this training, these young children can have a very bright future. Without it, they will continue to struggle to eke out a meager existence

title: Help 16 women launch clean energy enterprises
description: What do women in Namibia and the Navajo Nation have in common? They are part of the 1.4 billion people worldwide (70% of whom are women) who live off the electric grid. Without electricity, businesses must close when the sun goes down, children do not have the light they need to study after dark, and people are cut off from global news and the marketplace. Elephant Energy brings energy to off-grid areas and generates income in rural communities by engaging women as Energy Entrepreneurs.

title: Making sure vulnerable teens will never be alone
description: Teen Legal Helpline is growing quickly and we need your help. Our service connects the most vulnerable teens in Ontario with experienced lawyers who give guide them through their most difficult problems. It is free and anonymous, powered by lawyers who care. Your support will let us reach every young person who needs us.

title: Egg Laying Hens for Haitian Families
description: GreaterGood.org is working to fight hunger and malnutrition in Haiti. With your help, we can provide egg laying hens, and the materials and instruction to build coops for the people of La Gonave, an island of Haiti.     This program is part of a larger initiative called The Other Side Campaign, a partnership between  GreaterGood.org, The Mad Girls, Dreamweaver Foundation, The Literacy Site, & Affinity.is, dedicated to improving the lives of the people of La Gonave.

title: Change life for 40 destitute families in Ethiopia
description: The main objective is to affect change in the lives of hardworking yet impoverished families with children, for the long term and in a sustainable way. We want to uplift them and support their ability to help themselves. With the support of Wegene Ethiopian Foundation (WEF) deserving families will be able to meet their basic daily needs, recieve health care treatment, educate their children, maintain their family structure, and gain the means to earn income with either training or small business

title: Sponsor 4 Students in Aflao, Ghana
description: Students of Success Foundation will provide scholarships for low-income students in southeast Ghana through partnerships with high quality private schools in Aflao.

title: Myanmar 9-1-1: Train & Equip Emergency Medic Teams
description: This project will provide training, support and essential supplies to 40 mobile, community-based medics who hike through difficult terrain to deliver lifesaving emergency care to 65,000 people in remote communities of Eastern Myanmar. This region remains in the grip of a protracted health crisis after decades of civil war and chronic under-investment in health. In many cases, these mobile emergency medics provide the only access to health services for the poorest and most vulnerable communities.

title: Home care  for sick elderly people in Romania
description: Many of the Romanian older people live in poor, isolated rural areas having to struggle with very low incomes that are hardly enough for the daily food. There are no medical or social services and the sick, lonely people survive on the help assured by the neighbors. As a respond to this situation our organisation (Community Support Foundation) has set up a network of home care service to assist 500 sick elderly in 10 rural communities located in the east side of Bacau County.

title: Rescue Children from Forced Sex Work in India
description:
In CMM's orphanage, children of sex workers find a safe place away from abuse, prostitution and criminality. 
The project enables a better future to about 30 girls who would otherwise be the victims of human traffickers and forced sex work.

title: Educate 160 out of school slum children in India
description: This  project will provide enjoyable and meaningful learning experience to 160  out of school slum children in Delhi .These children are forced to miss regular school as they work as rag pickers, street vendors or help at roadside eateries to meet their family's economic needs .Many of them  stay at home to take care of their younger siblings and do household chores so that their parents can work to support the family. The project will also provide periodic health check ups of children.

title: Help Populate our Library! We need books!
description: Committed to bridging the weakest link in Pakistan's education system we require funds to provide faculty/students with quality e-resources and seminal texts for teaching rapidly developing disciplines. The very basic component to providing quality education is an updated and current text book covering the course material in depth as well as whetting a student's appetite for research and discovering new knowledge. Invest in Pakistan's future entrepreneurs!

title: Housing & education for street children in Ghana
description: Mama Laadi supports children at risk of being trafficked or fending for themselves living on the streets in northern Ghana with a safe nurturing home.  They can recover from trauma, attend school, receive medical care and, when they are older, get skills training to help them build a stable future. Mama Laadi is a trained community nurse -once a street child herself -her mission is to ensure very vulnerable children who cannot be resettled with their families are safe and have a future.

title: SA Hospice Plett - Home and 24HR nursing 70,000
description: HIV, TB, Cancer, Strokes and other conditions are hitting the previously disadvantaged of South Africa hard and in out town, they have no access to Hospice Palliative Care other than us. We partner Department of Health and add value to primary health care by offering service to the chronically ill, terminally ill and those most neglected in shacks and sub economic townships. Including delivering food to the starving.

title: 200 Pakistani youth Interfaith Dialogue for Peace
description: The aim of this project is to facilitate and provide avenues to promote peace and interfaith understanding among the 200 youth in Pakistan, particularly in Sargodha, Faisalabad, Jhang and Okara as the pilot project areas.

title: Computers for the Club
description: Your support will supply computers to our kids as well as seed our Computer Program.  We received a donation of 150 towers with motherboards and processors intact. This money will enable us to buy the needed PC components and will allow our staff and volunteers to teach our Kids how to assemble and operate a PC.  Our Kids will benefit with not only the computer but the much needed tech knowledge they will gain through building it from the ground up!

title: Epilepsy Early Education & Awareness
description: Epilepsy Early Education and Awareness Program is designed to educate and increase basic knowledge about epilepsy and seizure management among students, school personnel, and families. This program is to implement the knowledge about types of seizures, how to recognize a seizure, and what to do when a seizure occurs. This program is to eliminate perceived stigma and dispel myths that is associated with epilepsy and provide a safe and supportive environment for youths living with epilepsy.

title: Communication tools for young adults with autism
description: For young adults with autism, technology can often make the difference between a life of isolation and a chance for a vibrant, related social learning experience.  This challenge is to raise $5,000 to buy interactive white boards for young adults in 3LPlace's new Life College. The white boards provide different ways of presenting information: through sight, touch and real time, active engagement with the material. If we have 40 donors in 30 days, we also win a spot here on Global Giving!

title: COMPUTER TRAINING FOR POOR RURAL PRIMARY SCHOOLS
description: KIRUCODO in partnership with Maendeleo Foundation will be extending Mobile Solar Computer classes to Kikandwa C/U Primary School and Kibiribiri C/U Primary school. Both schools are based in rural communities of Mukono District in Uganda and they lack electricity and a great number of things for proper learning of their pupils. The innovative solar technologies that Maendeleo Foundation utilizes, will enable the pupils of the two schools to be trained in computer skills right at their location.

title: Help 60 residents of Quepos, Costa Rica!
description: We are helping 60 disadvantaged residents have access to free English classes in order to keep jobs for local residents in Quepos, Costa Rica.

title: Saving 100 youths in Bhutan
description:
Youth Media Center plans to provide a free, need based Multimedia skills Training, to 100 Economically Disadvantaged Youths in Bhutan, to enable them to find a decent job and livelihood.  
This project aims to rescue and build the career for 100 worst effected youths in Bhutan, who have been hit hard by the unemployment crisis and literally brought them on the streets. Providing free multimedia skills to these 100 youths means100 guaranteed employed youths.

title: Buy Solar lamps for 100 rural children in Uganda
description: This project will introduce creative program to make solar lights available at an affordable cost, especially to the poorest in selected families. Selected families will benefit from the availability of lighting derived from clean solar energy for the provision of more reading hours for their school age children, and creating more opportunity for improved health and savings from frequent purchase of kerosene.

title: Help a girl in domestic labour have a skill
description:
The project seeks to help young girls 12-20 years who are in child domestic labour without any skill or career but rather exploited by the employers and abused in katwe slums. 

The training will help them attain a career, resettled and start small scale businesses to sustain their living.

The problem is solved by rescuing, community sensitization, continuous follow-up and engaging the victims in vocational skills to attain skills as well as empowering them to help others who fall prey.

title: Social Health Care for Healing Syrian Refugees
description: In any war or conflict, it is the children who are the most vulnerable and devastated. Children are the largest and fastest growing number of victims in the Syrian conflict, and women are the 2nd. We are working to heal a whole generation of Syrian children from the deep and life draining trauma of violence and rebuild devastated families. Our Social Health Care Program conducts disaster health care field clinics and trains a growing pool of local therapists in emergency trauma recovery skills.

title: Hope for Street Children in Malawi
description: The Chisomo Children's Club in Malawi promotes long-term change by providing direct services to hundreds of street children and their families, enabling them to lift themselves out of poverty and to have hope for the future.

title: OFFER WATER IN 5 RURAL HEALTH CENTERS
description: Health centers are built to treat poor villagers in Ivory Coast. We observed after missions that some centers do not have water for care. face this situation which threatens staff and patients, we propose to install manual kits on existing wells in these villages and send water in small castles built in the centers. This little system will reduce the risk of contamination of users.

title: Supporting Education for Girls in Rural India
description: Education for Equality International plans to support 15 girls' school related costs for their entire secondary education. This will include admission and exam fees, uniforms, books, stationary supplies, and transportation. Our goal for this program is to help female students continue their education and to reduce the drop-out rate.

title: Provide facilities  for 100 orphans in Bako
description:
This project will provide story books, required text books and  school lunch for  abandoned children and  the orphans at Christ Treasured Royal Orphanage based in a village, Bako, outside Gwagwalada.
These children are crammed into small tight rooms with dilapidated facilities. We seek to renovate the kitchen and provide modern cooking facilities for preparation of nutritious meals,  supply a new power generating set and sink a borehole in the premises.

title: Vaccination for kids and adults
description: Disease prevention is key to public health. It is always better to prevent a disease than to treat it. Vaccines can protect both the people who receive them and those with whom they contact.

title: Help Global Sorority to Expand our Reach
description: Girls around the world are marginalized and subject to abuse and violence, but are given the smallest collective voice to stand up against their situation. Global Sorority delivers essential self development and leadership education to a global community of young women. We focus on the internal strengths and tools needed for girls to live to their full potential. We provide them with education, resources, community support and a platform from where they feel heard and valued.

title: "For Those Who Remain" Stipend Program
description: The inverse relationship between education and emigration rates makes it clear that when children stay in school, entire communities are benefited. BBVA Bancomer Foundation grants scholarships to the children of emigrated parents so they can finish their middle school studies.

title: Medical Fund for Needy Chinese Children
description: A Life A Time Foundation (the "Foundation"), formerly known as OSCCF (Overseas Save Chinese Children Foundation), has been helping orphaned and impoverished children in China suffering from congenital illnesses and traumatic injuries such as burns since 2008 by covering their medical expenses in part or in full.  We also provide a network of available medical providers through our ongoing collaboration with both local and specialized hospitals.

title: Safe  water supply for 500 villagers in Bangladesh
description: The purpose of this project is to reduce the treatment cost of the target people by supplying safe water and prevent water-borne diseases through which poverty reduction initiatives are achieved

title: Send 8 HIV-affected Ugandan youth to AIDS 2014
description: Baylor-Uganda has selected 8 HIV-affected youth out of over 3,000 to attend the AIDS 2014 conference in Melbourne, Australia in July 2014. These youth have overcome stigma and discrimination to be open about their HIV status in order to share their stories and inspire others. The AIDS 2014 conference is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for them to meet with and influence global leaders in the HIV/AIDS community and to develop their advocacy, mobilization, and public speaking skills.

title: Blind Students Rock Chaalo Gujarat-2014
description: Chaalo Gujarat is cultural event organized every 2 years in New Jersey to show case achievements & cultural heritage of Gujarat. About 40000 people from across the world participate in the event. During 2012, a team of 11 blind students of Blind People's Association, participated in this event. They performed 6 dance items before an audience of more than 10000 people and received a standing ovation. Our team has been invited to participate in Chaalo Gujarat to be held during 29-31 August 2014

title: Restore hope to 183 HIV+ women in Uganda-Pallisa
description: The project plan is to purchase and supply local goats to 183 HIV+ women families. This project will help 183 HIV+ women in Pallisa District improve their family incomes and meet competitive resource demands such as fortified foods, clothings and health services like ARVs costs. It is a one year project. Project main activities will include; women training, procure and supply of local 183 goats, monitoring and evaluation.

title: Sponsor School Kits to Underprivileged Children
description: While trying to address the issues regarding enrollment of underprivileged children in Govt. schools in rural parts of India, we realised that despite Govt. education being almost free of cost, many children did not take the first step towards the school, simply because they did not have the very basic school supplies. As a humble attempt to change this situation we started a School Kit Sponsorship program. This project is now being executed yearly before the beginning of the new academic year.

title: E-Learning: An innovative solution
description: We are seeking assistance to refurbish an E-Learning Centre in the community of Kanjarga in Builsa South District in Upper East Region through provision of computer sets and laptops, servers, software, ICT data and broadband connections. We also need multi-media computers for children office equipment, audio visual equipment, furniture and fixtures and books. Capacity building is also necessary for the personnel to manage and operate the centre for sustainability.

title: counseling line for children victims of violence
description: Blue phone is a free and anonymous counseling line for children. Blue phone is primarily aimed to support children who are victims and witnesses of violence, but it is also the line opened to the problems that children have which are not related to violence. So far, there has been calls referring to sexual exploitation, domestic abuse, bullying, physical and psychological violence. All of these calls reaffirm us that violence against children is greatly present all around us.

title: Help Ethiopia Feed Itself and Benefit Millions
description: Partners in Food Solutions (PFS) improves food security and nutrition across Africa by expanding and increasing the competitiveness of the food processing sector which creates markets for smallholder farmers and increased availability of nutritious foods.  This positive transformation occur by delivering customized food technology and business wisdom and solutions from volunteer experts of world-class companies, providing industry-wide training and catalyzing financial investment.

title: Provide SAFE Delivery for Rural Mothers
description: Obstructed labor is a direct cause of Bangladesh's high maternal and neonatal mortality rates. In rural areas, over 90% of women give birth at home, at the hands of untrained birth attendants. HOPE aims to give women with high risk pregnancies, safe delivery to save their and their children's lives.

title: Toilets & Water for school children in Srilanka
description: Toilets and water is a basic necessity in schools, however it is not available in many rural schools in North Central in Srilanka ! Due to this, children are irregular to school and eventually drop out. This project will help to build in toilets and maintain them, provide running and clean drinking water for school children in rural schools in Srilanka! The expected impact of the project is better health and improved school attendance and reduction is school drop outs among the project villages

title: Healthcare and food for 70 Cameroonian orphans
description: This project will save the life of 70 Cameroonian motherless orphans and vulnerable children by providing them healthcare and balanced food. Those orphans and vulnerable children aged from 0 to 2,5 years, are from villages where no attention is given to them after the dead of their mother at childbirth or shortly after childbirth because  left parents can not support them due to poverty. This lack of care exposes the new born babies to many sickness with sudden death as consequences.

title: Help the Mentally Sick People in Somaliland.
description: Horizon is a Non profit Organization based in Hargeisa -Somaliland. It has been established in early 2007 by a group of youth volunteers of both genders. This Organization was set up to promote and work as a voluntary to the social basic needs and the development activities in Somaliland. It works in a different social basic activities. Particularly, it provide humanitarian care for the mentally sick people and the mentally Disabled people in Hargeisa - Somaliland

title: GIVE CLEAN WATER TO 663 VILLAGERS IN RURAL GHANA .
description:
This project will seek to provide clean water to ordinary typical rural village dwellers to improve their living standard,we have plan to drill a bore hole in Kwaanan village Ghana.
Giving  good drinking water to 663 village people will change their water from dirty water to good drinkable water,we have put some measures in place to make this project sustainable,also, we have arranged with district water coordinator to train two people on how to repair bore hole when it spoil after the project.

title: From disability to ability with Therapy & Training
description: Project will help re-build and restore to near-normalcy the lives of around fifty cerebral palsy (CP) affected children who are brought to Balajothi Centre where we provide physiotherapy, speech-therapy, vocational training and counselling sessions to help the CP affected children become self-reliant, confident and useful individuals. Parents of CP affected children are also involved so that they are cared for in their home environment as well.

title: Self-Sufficient Haiti through Vocational Training
description: Haiti is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. LFBS rescues youth from corrupt orphanages and from the streets and gives them a chance to break the cycle of poverty. With love, food, shelter, medical, education, then Vocational Training so they can become the self-sufficient, self-empowered new generation, with skills, training, opportunity and hope! Sewing, Office Technology, English language, Window Repair, Carpentry and other training is available. Change a life. Change the future.

title: Provide Food And Education For A Child In India
description: Hundreds of thousands of children are at risk of malnutrition due to shortage of rain and electricity in India. This project aims to provide food and scholarships to 100 children living in poverty in rural India, so that they can get the education they need to build a brighter future and escape poverty.

title: Bring Clean Water to 15 Villages in Rural Gambia
description: This campaign began as way to raise funds for the Gambia Lifewater Project and the work of its leader Jeremy Mak. He wound up doing a TON of well & handpump repair in The Gambia, as well as other water projects wherever he found himself. (Colombia, Uganda etc.)  Jeremy has shifted his focus now, and this campaign is continuing w/ focus on Water Charity's many projects in The Gambia & nearby regions. We continue to repair broken handpumps & help with water issues in other ways there. Thank you!

title: Skill Training For 100 Poor Girl Youth In India
description: 100 poor girl youth beneficiaries in Punjab india under this project will train in computer skill courses namely Tally, desk top publishing, IT skill and web designing. This project will train them in computer skill which have more and more demand in marketing. And make them self reliance, self dependent

title: Unlocking potentials of children in abject Poverty
description: To educate girl children in the rural areas through informal school-E-caravan-     the project will bridge the gap between Rural girls and Modern Educational facilities, to provide the latest Information and Communication Technology ( ICT) as well as to extend Innovative sustainable project at their door step and to reduce the cost, Time and energy for overall empowerment & development of girl children is the idea of the project.

title: Promoting Humane Education in Schools
description: Crime rate   ranging from  robbery, murder,  rape, animal cruelty etc, has become common and hence a serious concern in Sierra Leone. Most of such crimes, violence and lawlessness are perpetrated by young men.  Though the law had always dealt with them according, they do not seem to stop. 60% of  youths released from detention always revert to the same habit. Awareness raising and education provided by this project will meaningfully contribute to positively transforming their lives

title: The Ishinomaki Social Farm for Elderly Care
description: Elderly people in the disaster area make friends and have fun by participating in agriculture activities. After having lost their houses and family it is difficult to reestablish their lives. Many of them live in temporary housing and live solitary lives. We set up social farms that enable them to interact with others and find a purpose to get excited about another day. Together with trained psychologists and volunteers we provide them with daily activities that get them out of the house.

title: Outreach Centre for Child-Headed Households Uganda
description: Wings of Courage Orphan Outreach builds a centre for Child headed households outside Gulu in Uganda, to provide community outreach programs, 24 hour emergency adult assistance, and a home for orphans without extended family.

title: COVID education/"Safe Park" for Children
description: COVID education is provided to orphans and vulnerable children living in impoverished communities in Lusaka, Zambia. About 20-30 children participate each week. Health care personnel conduct workshops on COVID prevention. A small snack and masks are provided. These workshops were started in July 2020 to keep children and families safe from COVID.  Once COVID is over, we will revert back to our old format of engaging children in educational games,  activities, and workshops on HIV prevention.

title: Help people with handicap openning  bakery in Togo
description:
This project will help improve the lives of people with handicap and aims to provide their power purchase therefore people with handicap who employ more than 15 people also with handicap in this bakery. 
The realization of this project will allow short term 
- Strengthen the capacity of production and sale of a unit of production of biscuits, bread, hamburger, croissants, cake, etc.. 
- Train other people with disabilities 
- Increase sales volume

title: Mobile Library for Rural Kenyan Youths
description: This project will operate a mobile library that will ply two secondary schools in the Tana River Delta region in Kenya. It will provide books to 300 secondary school students whose schools were vandalized during the ethnic conflicts during 2012-2013. This would be the first library they will experience in their lives.

title: Educate and Empower the blind through Technology
description: Snehadeep Trust for the disabled is a non profit organisation whose goals are to empower India's disabled community, by training them in using Computers, English speaking and communication skills, soft skills,Career guidance, and then finding them suitable jobs in both Government and private sectors. Ebenezer a 3rdstd student of Bishop cotton's School, I losing his vision gradually, We are giving him training in computers (with the help of JAWS) &Braille,Our Student Ms.Farahan got job at Cisco.

title: Invest in 45 vulnerable girls change kiandutu slum
description: This project focuses on vulnerable adolescents girls, young women and teenage mothers and helps them gain access to female driven development activities addressing life skills, HIV and AIDS, culture, leadership, peer education, sexual reproductive health, teenage pregnancy, rape, gender based violence and prostitution and crime. It aims at impacting the whole community through empowering girls and young women to be change makers within Kiandutu slums and beyond.

title: ENGLISH AS A TOOL OF POVERTY ALLEVIATION
description:
This Project will launch 5 Wi-Fi  Language Class on Wheel for under privileged students in 5 most poor states of India to develop their English Speaking and employ them in major companies & encourage entrepreneurship through LEDER.
Lead India Foundation will train 500 under privileged students in the slums and very remote areas of India to uplift their living standard through training them and developing their skill in English Language and promote their enterprise skill through LEDER program

title: Supporting Gender Equality in Rural Cameroon
description: This project will allow 10,000 women to have greater access and management of their own land. Women are severely disadvantaged under customary law in Cameroon but we aim to sensitize and educate women and the entire community on their rights and how to advocate for them. We will hold multiple training's, workshops and community meetings, we will provide legal advising for women to facilitate civil status certificates and advocate to bring about policy and practice changes with regard to land.

title: Save Cleft Lip & Palate Patients of Pakistan
description: The journey of supporting these children and changing their lives started in 2002. Since then more than 18000 free cleft and plate surgeries has successfully performed and that's why CLAPP Hospital has been recognized as No. 1 hospital in the world to perform the highest number of free Cleft Surgeries. CLAPP Trust is dedicated to the noble cause, to provide equal opportunities in life for the children born with deformities as the children born without. Thousands of Cleft lip and palate patients.

title: Create college opportunities for Latino students
description: Scholars Latino Initiative (SLI) supports Latino/a/x high school students with college access through rigorous academic challenge, leadership development, scholarships, and supportive mentorships.

title: Send family to conference for rare disorder!
description: Dup15q Alliance provides family support and promotes awareness, research and targeted treatments for dup15q syndrome. Symptoms of this rare genetic disorder include autism, seizures and developmental delays. Every two years we hold a conference for affected families to provide education on the latest treatments for dup15q and to create a sense of hope and community that is often difficult for our 1,000 registered families to find locally due to the rarity of the disorder.

title: Help Cerebral Palsy (CP) affected children
