description: Project will help re-build and restore to near-normalcy the lives of around fifty cerebral palsy (CP) affected children who are brought to Balajothi Centre where we provide physiotherapy, speech-therapy, vocational training and counselling sessions to help the CP affected children become self-reliant, confident and useful individuals. Parents of CP affected children are also involved so that they are cared for in their home environment as well.

title: Help 30 children overcome domestic violence
description: 15.5 million children in the U.S. live in families in which domestic violence has occurred in the past year. When Lisa was just six years old, she awoke to the sounds of her dad's angry voice, smashing objects and her mom's pleas to "stop!" This project will help 30 children like Lisa and her mom escape from the violence and provide the children with counseling, tools to keep them safe, play therapy and access to a support group for children to help them heal from the trauma they experienced.

title: A fuller life: help 160 disabled familyless youth
description: This project will help more than 160 young multiple disabled people in Russia, who live in a large residential home, to get regular special need physical exesices,hydrarehabilitation,for the weakest once - to get also everyday assistance and training in things like dressing up and having a meal, and for all take part at a broad range of activities (from wood and ceramic workshops to concerts and even birthday parties - wihich they never would have but which are also celebrated by our volunteers)

title: Family Assistance Fund
description: The Family Assistance Fund helps patients and their families pay for food, lodging, and transportation. We provide this fund for any of our patient families who may need assistance while their child receives care at our hospital. The Twin Cities hospital strives to treat the entire child and that includes the family as well. We are dedicated to our mission, in providing world-class care regardless of the family's ability to pay.

title: Beekeeping for 100 widows in Tanzania
description: The poorest and impoverished people in the rural areas in Tanzania are the HIV/AIDS widows.They are weak but still have  the burden to care their families. This project aims to empower 100 widows in Imalinyi Njombe to break poverty circle.

title: Hands On with Nicaraguan Sign Language
description:
Program Summary
'Hands On' is a multifaceted approach to sign language education in a real life setting, educating deaf youth, hearing parents, and the hearing community in general about deaf issues and capacities. This program is also aimed to create a very important deaf community for these otherwise isolated individuals.
Our priorities are: Sign Language Access, Customized Deaf Education Materials, and the Deaf community

title: Improve 2000 Kom girls education with solar lamps
description: Girl children in the local Kom community of Muteff hardly have an opportunity to go to school, talk less of completing elementary education. Even when they have the opportunity to complete school they encounter lots of difficulty copping as they lack what people elsewhere take for granted-electricity.  Productivity is low as they hardly concentrate on their studies.

title: One Dollar One Meal
description: Each dollar will purchase a meal ($3.00/day, less than one Starbuck's specialty drink) for a visually impaired child in remote area in Vietnam.  $100 will provide food, clothing, and minor health care for a child for two months.  Blind Vietnamese Children Foundation has been supporting 310 children with visual impairment and blind children with additional disability throughout Vietnam since 2000.

title: e-Learning for 125 Underprivileged Filipino Youth
description: This project aims to provide e-Learning opportunities for 125 underprivileged Filipino students, including out-of-school youth (OSY) in the slums of Barangay Commonwealth, Quezon City, Philippines.  Access to interactive e-Learning computer center for children right in their neighborhood will help them finish their elementary or high school studies and acquire lifelong learning skills, an effective way in helping them become productive adults, and break away from the vicious cycle of poverty.

title: Africa Super 7s - continental 7-a-side football
description:
Let's make history together.
Be a founding supporter of the world's biggest 7-a-side Club football tournament and watch the Super 7s Foundation generate millions of dollars to fund long term, sustainable, life-style improvements to millions of the less fortunate citizens around Africa.
While almost 40% of the continent's 1 billion people live in poverty, the Super 7s Foundation will provide health, education, sports, micro-finance, employment, shelter and more.
$10 will make the difference

title: Student Nurses Hostel for Kitovu Hospital
description: Kitovu Hospital currently receives 100 student nurses from Kalungi, Villa maria and Rakai Nursing Schools who are accommodated outside the hospital premisses; which is a challenge for the hospital to control them for purposes  of discipline and education. Kitovu Hospital wants to raise $88,302 to construct a hostel so that all these students reside with in the hospital during their clinical placement.

title: Promoting Quality Education for Girls in Uganda
description: This project will increase access, retention and quality education for girls in primary schools in Dokolo district through providing scholastic materials, provision of sanitary pads, changing rooms and Establishing child-friendly school for effective schools linked to community empowerment by providing sport kits to help make school attractive place for children to increase enrollment, retention and quality of lives of children while in school.

title: Feed and educate  99  Children in Narok Kenya
description: Fountain of life center is is non profit administering to the most needy in the community.we have been able to rescue street children,orphans and supported them to go to school.  also ministering  to the needs of brothel workers,bar maids,drug addicts,child labour , female genital mutilation and early marriage victims  The center provide care for the orphans especially girls who have been married at early age,provide education ,heath care ,reproductive ,  food clothing provision and counseling

title: Aashrya- Shelter for HIV infected children at high
description: Ajit Foundation has identified 4 blocks in periphery 45 Km of Solpur district place, where 2000 children are HIV infected and required support. We have closely monitored and analyzed that these children required emotional, social and economic supports to survive healthy life. Shelter for 500 HIV infected children, will provide all required services under one roof. This project will ensure all services which are include medical treatment,  counselling, education and socialization support

title: Supporting the Victims of Protests in Ukraine
description: We need your support to help children and families of those who lost their lives, had been permanently injured or require immediate treatment and rehabilitation due to the tragic events that took place in Ukraine over the last three months. Through comprehensive financial and medical assistance, your donations will provide victims and families of those who paid the ultimate sacrifice for democracy in Ukraine with an opportunity to rebuild their lives and face the future with confidence and hope.

title: Free Medical Care for Poor Lepers
description:
We are giving every month free chemotherapy treatment (MDT) to all detected  leprosy  cases. Every new found patient gets MDT treatment for curing the infection. This activity aims to prevent deformity through early detection and treatment.

    Physiotherapy treatment is also given to our deformed patients as well as active and passive exercises, wax baths and oil massages. Ulcer patients are getting ulcer dressing treatment and we advise these patients how to keep the limbs (hands &feet)

title: Business for 20 Village Teachers in Sierra Leone
description: Small business has been identified as a way of improving family income of low paid primary school teachers/volunteers in rural Sierra Leone. Quality Primary education depends mainly on the ability of the teachers and volunteers to perform under reasonable conditions in terms of family income and sustenance.  The grant will provide start up for 20 teachers in 3 village schools in MILE 91 to operate home businesses for economic empowerment to improve performance and quality of children education.

title: Cosmetology for 50 Adolescent Mothers in Grenada
description: The Programme for Adolescent Mothers, serves teenage mothers and pregnant adolescents of Grenada W. I. offering an opportunity for them to complete their educational career through an integrated program of academics, skills training & personal development. From 1994 to 2013, 598 young women have benefited from the program. This Cosmetology training would develop self-sufficiency & employability skills which would enhance their lives and reduce the possibility of an unwanted second pregnancy.

title: Help 50 Women in Liberia Receive Training
description: Jola House is a Liberian social enterprise committed to addressing some of the social and economic needs of the community following the country's civil war. This project will fund a training program for 50 women in machine-based sewing techniques, pattern making and merchandising. Our vocational and business development training will increase the number of women who will have their own source of income, thus contributing to their family, community and larger society.

title: TAKE CARE OF CHILDREN WITH AUTISM
description: Children from autistic spectrum will receive professional treatment according to their individual abilities, enabling them to better integration in the social environment and improve their quality of life.

title: Raise the Voices of Haitian Women!
description: This project will train rural women in Haiti to make community radio programs aimed at bringing their concerns to the attention of local decision and policy makers. Three training workshops on digital production techniques will empower 15 women from 5 community radio stations to speak publicly about the problems and challenges they face in their daily lives, especially those of poverty, lack of resources, and violence. The project is run by REFRAKA, a non-governmental organisation run by women.

title: EMPOWER 100 BENIN POOR WOMEN OF MANGROVE AREA
description:
The most vulnerable and the poorest are the first victims of climate change, women belong to these two categories. Being faced with more barriers than men before to access and control resources, women protect themselves against problems with droughts, floods, and hurricanes.
This activity will help strengthen the capacity of women's groups through training in literacy, health, development of business plan. The construction of a room used as for training and meeting will reap a great harvest.

title: Feed Orphan Children in Juarez, Chihuahua Mexico
description: Due to extreme crimes in the city of Juarez, Chihuahua Mexico, many children have been left orphans, without parents to take care of them. Orphanages are overflowing with children and do not have enough food to provide to the children. Sometimes all they have to eat is a bowl noodle soup. We are seeking funds to provide them with nutritious food. They rely on our society to help provide this basic need.

title: Therapeutic Horsemanship for Special Needs Kids
description: Zia Ranch provides therapeutic horsemanship programs for special needs students. Therapeutic horsemanship provides significant benefits to people with physical, developmental and emotional disabilities. Therapeutic horseback riding improves motor skills, improves core strength, improves balance and coordination, provides sensory integration and improves self-confidence and a sense of belonging. In 2014, Zia Ranch will provide 50 individual lessons per week and week-long camps for 50 students.

title: Teaching Children to Be Caring World Citizens
description: This project will give children worldwide the various tools, support, motivation and rewards necessary to become responsible, knowledgeable and caring world citizens. It will provide resources for children and families of every country of the world to better understand and serve their counterparts internationally, fostering world-class citizenship through five central programs:  Community-Building, Cultural Exchange, Service to Others, Personal Excellence and Environmental Stewardship.

title: Help Filipino Kids Learn Better &Survive Disasters
description: This project will train over 100 principals and teachers from the 38 public schools in Coron, a vulnerable island in Palawan, Philippines on Learning Effectively through Enhanced Pedagogies (LEEP) with special emphasis on disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. Each school will also receive a hard disk drive with educational videos. This will give them an opportunity to improve educational outcomes and increase the chance of survival of their students when disaster strikes.

title: Ensure 100 Pakistani women have a better life
description: Women in ultra poor households struggle to provide for their families in Pakistan. Assistance in kind is provided to women to become entrepreneurs enabling them to fulfill basic needs for a healthier life.

title: Help to100 most disadvantaged orphans (disability)
description: We help the most disadvantaged orphans with disabilities in Russia to develop mentally and physically and improve their quality of life. It's hard to see that the social system in Russia still does not believe in the ability of these children to learn nor believe they should support the development of these children! By our project, these children are learning to walk, acquiring social skills and showing great results! It is a human right for every child to learn and reach their fullest potental

title: Support 300 poor women to earn income in Tanzania
description: This project intends to empower 250 widows and 50 physically disabled women living in Vingunguti and Buguruni wards of Ilala Municipality, in Dar Es Salaam region, Tanzania to combat poverty-stricken through carrying out income generating activities (IGAs). Thus, the targeted 300 women will be equipped with skills on entrepreneurship and financial management and thereafter they will be given seed capital for fostering their respective income generating activities for their well being.

title: Van for Custom footwear for Leprosy Patients
description: This project will support a Mobile Medical Van Unit (MMV Unit)  enabled with the capacity to fabricate custom protective footwear for persons suffering from leprosy related disability and deformity of the feet, living in remote, rural and vulnerable parts of the country.

title: Temporary Home for 35 children in ARG
description: Since 2005, Mensajeros de la Paz has had a temporary home - located in Buenos Aires - for children from ages 6 to 12 who have been legally removed from their homes and families by social services to protect their rights. Colibries is a temporary home that provides assistance, care and support to these children facing this challenging moment.

title: Women's Income Generating Group
description: Shanti Uganda's Women's Income Generating Group (WIGG) is made up of 12 HIV positive grandmothers in Luweero District. Historically, members successfully worked in textile and beading groups to create artisanal products that were sold at fair-trade prices in international markets. Beginning in 2017 the women will partake in business formation training courses to help them focus on creating their own businesses which will allow them to forge sustainable paths to future stability and success.

title: Restoring Human Rights for Girls in Guatemala
description: El Refugio de la Ninez will provide housing, psychological and social atention services to girls and adolescents survivors of sexual violence, and will support their families in creating safe enviroments for their reintegration.  El Refugio will also provide legal advise and support for their access to justice.  El Refugio will support the implementation of girls Life Projects, so they can advance in their development.

title: Emergency Flood Response to 150 Families, Somalia
description: Devastating floods stirred by the outburst of the Shabele River has displaced approximately 11 thousand families in Jowhar, Middle Shabelle region, Somalia, causing one of the worst humanitarian crises in the region. The flooding steadily started early April 2013 but during September spread to dozens of villages in Jowhar mainly inhabited by a predominantly peasant Somali Bantu regarded politically as one of the minor clans in the country. The disaster affected mainly women, children and elderly

title: Change Her Story - Get 75 Girls in School!
description: THANK YOU! You have nearly covered the cost of 75 new girls in school! We are currently doing our summer school program and recruiting for new kindergarten classes for September. We will be adding 100 more kindergarteners to our school this year, bringing our total number up to 225! more girls who need their school fees covered for the 2014-2015 school year. Let's start with the next 25. If we reach our goal, we'll cover the cost of 75 girls in school next year. Will you change her story with us

title: uplift and empower the victims of patriarchy
description: to empower and mainstreamise the most stigmatised and discreminated women. They are sweepers, dumping ground workers, sex workers, trafficked women and HIV+ women, through micro-entrepreneurship and financial inclusion program and community leadership program. the project will  provide micro-entrepreneurship training to 20 women peers to lead 20+ groups from the above discriminated communities, advocate their cause for financial inclusion and link them with banks, and give micro skill support.

title: Creating economic opportunities for 9 mine victims
description: The purpose of this project is to provide small grants for economic integration of landmine victims who live in poor rural region of Azerbaijan in order to support socio-economic development, entrepreneurship and self-sufficiency. Through financing small entrepreneurship activities that will be designed and implemented by landmine survivors themselves, this project will enhance the economic and social life of these people and their families and becoming self-sufficient members of the community.

title: Transform lives of 5000 dairy farmers in Kenya
description: Fair trade Organization of Kenya (FTOK) empowers farmers to reap substantial returns from farming by offering training to farmers through our capacity building program. FTOK would like to set up a dairy farming demonstration farm in Gakundu FCS from where farmers can learn through demonstration. We are changing the farming communities through dairy farming by providing technical assistance. The Technical assistance equips farmers with knowledge on how to run their dairy farming as a business.

title: Support children Affected and infected with HIV
description: HLFPPT has worked extensively in Andhra Pradesh on prevention and care in HIV / AIDS among Most At Risk Population, including Vulnerable women and children. Facilitating emergence and development of Community Bases Organizations' (CBOs) is one such initiative we have undertaken in AP. HLFPPT is planning to provide vulnerable infected and affected children with counseling, nutrition support & back to school facilitation and linkages to government programs and vocational institutes.

title: FEED & EDUCATE 230 DISABLED CHILDREN IN ZAMBIA
description: Provide revolving fund for disabled children, special education, child care and physiotherapy services to 230 disabled children from poor and disadvantaged families, and training caregivers and families in Zambia

title: Help Animals in 10 Countries Get Needed Care
description: Animal-Kind International supports existing animal welfare orgs run by local people in Ghana, Malawi, Namibia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Honduras, Jamaica, Armenia & Bosnia. There are few opportunities to raise funds & supplies for animal welfare in these countries so they need to look to outside support for assistance. AKI does the due diligence on the orgs, ensures they track use of AKI funds & always sends 100% of donations to our partner orgs to be used only for animal welfare.

title: Sponsor a women related program of WAAF
description: The West African AIDS Foundation, (WAAF), continues to offer services to a range of vulnerable populations, one of which are HIV pregnant women. With the upcoming 2014 International Women's Day, we are not only working with many of our female beneficiaries to celebrate this day but we want to use the opportunity to raise funds for the onsite clinic to purchase a (portable) ultra sound machine which will not only go a long way in servicing these women but also lead to sustainability of the PMTCT

title: Post-Earthquake Child Education Program in Nepal
description: GlobeMed at Tufts is a student-run organization comprised of over 45 members dedicated to promoting and supporting global health and education equity. We are a part of a larger national organization that pairs each of its 50+ participating collegiate chapters with a grassroots international health-based organization. Through these cooperative and sustainable relationships students and communities are able to work together to pursue the mutual goal of improving health globally.

title: Letsema - Mobilising caregivers in South Africa
description: The Letsema Programme is a collaboration of 11 Early Childhood Development (ECD) organisations in South Africa working to connect and strengthen grassroots caregivers of young children by unlocking resourcefulness and developing community leadership.

title: vocational education to 70 poorest women in india
description: Economic Empowerment of the dropout women's through vocational training livelihood project intends to give skill training in Bag making & tailoring for sustainable livelihoods to 70 women's with this vocational skills training women live with dignity by earning themselves. During this training, beneficiaries will learn and develop skills in bag making and tailoring work. They can earn 6000 - 8000 Rs. Every month. We provide sewing machine, tool kit to survive on their own and live with dignity.

title: Sponsoring Kolhewadi, new project village of 750
description: Since 1970, CRHP has worked with over 300 villages in rural Maharashtra, bringing health to the poorest of the poor. CRHP's unique approach focuses on enabling the community members to bring about desired community development, putting health in their own hands. Utilizing principles of empowerment, equity and integration, CRHP's staff of social workers, health professionals and community development coordinators works closely with villagers, compelling sustainable, impacting change.

title: Digital Empowerment Of Poor and Challenged Girls.
description: SUGAM JAGRITI is continuously working with unemployed youth particularly with dalit girls & Needy Youths who are literate with skill of reading and writing Hindi and English. For employment they need skill training best suit them i.e. computer training.Further they will be supported in getting employed  . It improve their income generation opportunity.The organization has made employed 500 youth after training in computer education  . It has strengthened the economic status of the families.

title: Literacy for Dominican-Haitian Youth in the Batey
description: Yspaniola's Learning Centers serves 65 children aged 4-17 in Batey Libertad, a marginalized community in the agricultural heart of the Dominican Republic. The Learning Center provides critical access to small-group instruction and Spanish literacy support for children in the community, including those who speak Haitian Creole as their first language. This project will support materials to sustain our educational programs for at-risk youth in the community and help maintain our teachers salary's.

title: Support Teachers to Educate 200 Children Monthly
description: Since 2005, Acres of Mercy through its Education Support Program has provided access to education for over 200 children from poverty annually. This project supports teachers and their work . It  provides technology support to improve teaching delivery and planning, mental well-being of teachers, provides for staff welfare as well as tools the teachers utilize to improve children's learning outcomes. It also facilitates teacher training, coaching and mentoring for success in their teaching work.

title: Safe Drinking Water for 15000 Villagers in Fundong
description: Most villages within Fundong subdivision presently have limited access to clean drinking water, especially during the dry season. Community members must trek to a stream in order to collect their drinking water-- thus leaving many to drinking dirty water. Your donation will bring this community water by creating an additional spring catchment, expanding the currently existing infrastructure and by providing training to the community to help ensure sustainable management.

title: Food & Self-Reliance for 300 orphans & handicapped
description: THIS PROJECT WILL HELP 300 NEEDY AND ORPHANS IN INDIA, TO MAKE AVAILABLE THE RESIDENTIAL FACILITIES, BOARDING ARRANGEMENTS, CLOTHING,LIVABLE SALARIES FOR TEACHERS & MEDICAL AID TO THE PHYSICALLY HANDICAPPED, POOR NEED & HELPLESS ORPHANS 300 STUDENTS.

title: Improving Basic Education for Children
description: This  project  is  to renovate 6 classrooms for a primary and  nursery  school   at Afienya, a farming  community in  Ghana  to enhance teaching  and  learning.  We  intend  to renovate  the  dilapidated classrooms    and  repair  the  roofing  of  the  classrooms   so  that  these  children,  the  future  leaders,     can  have  a safe environment   for  their learning toward    development

title: Guarantee education to 120 kids in Huaycan, Peru
description: IBO Italia is cooperating with Amici di Huaycan to create a daycare structure where children living in Huaycan, a shantytown close to Lima, are helped in their studies, to prevent school drop-off. Local educators will support children in their homework and favour the relationship between school and families. A daily canteen service will provide them an healthy and nutritious meal and not formal learning activities will be organized.

title: Girls Glory - Improve Menstrual Health in India
description: In India, many young girls lack the adequate solutions to manage menstruation. 88% of women and girls use extremely unhygienic practices such as; old rags, ashes and husk sand and at least 636 million Indians lack toilets, according to the latest census data, a crisis that contributes to school dropouts disease and childhood malnutrition. Hence "Girls Glory" Project. We want to provide toilets and WASH education to all the little girls in the Government Schools to put an end to this issue.

title: Training Center for 12 Remote Nicaraguan Villages
description: This project will equip teachers, small business owners, and pastors to better educate, lead and help families in 12 remote villages in Nicaragua, the second-poorest country in the western hemisphere. The poorest, most disadvantaged Nicaraguans live in these rural areas and have few resources. The Center will serve as a hub for training and resource distribution for the more than 3,000 people living in these communities. By equipping leaders we hope to help families rise out of poverty.

title: Give The Gift of Sight To 312 Poor Blind Woman
description: Pakistan is a male dominated society where women have last call on family resources. Their healthcare needs have lesser priority and as 2/3rds of the population lives around the poverty line there is never any money to get them treated. Conscious of this LRBT has in its 28 years of operations focused especially on female blindness treating 13 million women which has significantly reduced the extent of female blindness. Still there are approx. 9.6 million poor blind/visually impaired women.

title: Education as a Bridge Between Communities
description: Bringing together all communities - Jews, Muslims, Christians, Druze and others - in Jerusalem, through environmental education to inspire members of divided communities to conserve the environment and local wildlife. Finding common ground facilitates mutual respect, understanding and dialogue as well as a sense of the wider community between diverse ethnic and religious groups so that together we can strive toward a shared future.

title: Help German students create a production company
description: Empower 11th grade students at Schloss Neubeuern secondary school to work together to transform learning school-wide and create a more engaging curriculum catering to student preference and learning styles. The students will achieve this by creating a company, together with their teachers, to produce learning videos for their own school and curriculum, with long-term goal of making them available to other schools and teachers.

title: Support Appleby Create A OneNote Notebook system
description:
Finalist of the Microsoft in Education School Pitch Competition!

At Appleby College secondary school we have a special designed OneNote Notebook for every class. Our IT staff has discovered some amazing things working with OneNote and our SharePoint system, especially about how we can use them to improve the learning environment.

title: Help students worldwide create intl companies
description: Broadclyst Primary School would like to establish a global enterprise challenge, where children from schools around the world connect to run an international company. Overall, there will be 10 international companies, each with a different product, competing to become the most successful company globally. In each country, the participating schools will organise their children into 10 'subsidiary companies' or 'regional office' of the international company.

title: Help 200 Survivors of Torture from 84 Countries
description: No one likes to talk about torture, and we understand that our mission might make some people uneasy. That being said, there are individuals who have experienced torture who need your help today. ASTT alleviates the suffering of individuals applying for asylum who have experienced torture or war trauma at the hands of their governments. We have helped over 5,300 people from 80 countries get back on their feet and live fulfilled lives using our unique combination of holistic services.

title: Support students in Uganda create an e-library
description:
Finalist of the Microsoft in Education School Pitch Competition!

In Gayaza High School in Uganda students want to create an online library page with links to videos showing the processes of production within the small scale local enterprises in Uganda and where they are located.

title: RAKSHA (Protection and Restoration 50 Survivors)
description: Thousands of girls affected by poverty, disaster and lack of opportunities got trafficked from West Bengal. More than 800 sex trafficked victims who were rescued by GGBK from dehumanizing slavery like conditions will be restored dignity through psycho-social support and economic empowerment for a safe and dignified life in the society.

title: 1000 Days of Motherhood
description: Your donation will provide mothers in a rural listening group the ability to access life saving nutrition and related health radio content. Groups can listen to the programs as often as they like on our solar and wind-up MP3 player. Using the Lifeplayer MP3, mothers will listen to persuasive behavior change messages in their language created by Zambia's Food and Nutrition Commission about nutrition and diet, taking iron tablets and folic acid during pregnancy.

title: Help save food and keep young people out of prison
description: FoodCycle is working with young offenders to deliver a community payback scheme. The young people will deliver a free three course meal to a sheltered housing scheme, elders groups and families in need, by cooking up surplus food. These young people are at the fringes of society and without structured activity 1 in 3 will return to crime. Over three months this project will save the taxpayer 171,000 by keeping at least 9 young people out of prison and supporting them into positive activities.

title: Malaria treatment for 10,000 children in Malawi
description: For the children who live in the remote villages of Malawi prompt access to essential medicines is often the difference between life and death. Our mobile health clinic takes medical care to where it is most needed: to the children in the hard to reach areas. We also deliver public health education to the communities served by the mobile clinic as we believe prevention is better than cure. Our appeal to you is to help us raise $33,500 to treat 10,000 cases of malaria.

title: Irish Cancer's vital services to families in Eire
description: In Ireland an average of 30,000 new cases of cancer are diagnosed each year and this number is expected to rise to over 40,000 per year by 2020. Most recent data from the National Cancer Registry shows that approximately every 15 minutes someone somewhere in Ireland hears the words 'you have cancer'. Funds raised go directly to facilitate the work of the Irish Cancer Society across support services, prevention, research and advocacy.

title: The Ambitious Girls Fund
description: Only 4% of Dalits in Nepal pass the final exam at the end of 10th grade that is required to continue their education. They must then complete the newly added 11th and 12th grades before they can go on to college. Imagine you're a Dalit girl graduating from the 10th grade, and you're faced with the overwhelming task of paying tuition fees as well as room and board in a distant city just to complete high school. This is where we come in - to provide a modest stipend to make this possible.

title: Steer to Change
description: This program will empower resource poor women of the community to become professional drivers and earn their livelihoods with dignity by taking up employment . Unemployed women are trained in driving for a period of three months and are placed as cab drivers or chauffeurs in corporate once the driving license is acquired.  Training curriculum includes communications skills, life skills and spoken English along with driving lessons. We empower them to become confident citizens in the community.

title: Unity Care's Summer of Learning for Foster Youth
description: While many of us have positive childhood memories, there are many foster youth who have faced poverty, physical and emotional abuse and neglect. For thirteen years, the Summer of Learning program has been one of the important tools by which our children develop their social, intellectual and personal skills. The program reaches up to 400 foster children and families through academic readiness, environmental awareness and social activities.

title: To build a charity hospital in Palestine
description: This Project is aimed at constructing a comprehensive health center the following :#An advanced medical center and hospital equipped with the latest in health technology # Offer the most advanced emergency and trauma services  # Provide all diagnostic and treatment services # Provide a comprehensive building which will enhance the surrounding area . This will be a four-floor hospital .

title: 'ART PRIVE' CHARITY EVENTS by Artist Stacie Krupa
description: Master Artist Stacie Krupa, brings her "ART PRIVE" Charity Events global to support the LIFE ARTS programs for youth in need at Art Studio World locations nationally. All of the proceeds support the sustainability of Art Studio's programs so schools/students currently on wait-lists can receive LIFE ARTS in their community. Funding of these programs allows consistent personal & professional development workshops for youth ages 8-18yrs to discover their full potential on a "cradle to career" path.

title: Basic Education for the children of slum-dwellers
description: The rural poor and unskilled workers migrate to the city in search of livelihood, as the employment in the unskilled sector is high.  But due to the costly city life and higher rentals, these poor people form into groups and build make shift houses in the suburbs or open places which finally become slum areas due to the unorganised, unplanned occupation and living. These poor migrants who live a hand to mouth life by earning very little on daily labour and miserable living conditions make them.

title: Upland Forest Rehabilitation Project
description: The project of rehabilitating the 150 hectares forest located in Badiangan, Ajuy Iloilo which was damaged by typhoon Haiyan will help revitalize the livelihood of the 295 affected families who have been depending on the forest resources. The scheme of sub-contracting the disaster victims in planting the seedlings and forestry management will help them in their immediate recovery hence improve their quality of life.

title: Gloves for All
description: When thinking about baseball, people often think immediately of a glove and ball.  Gloves are core to the sport.  Whether you're having a catch with a family member or friend, or playing a game, gloves are essential, so it comes as no surprise that it is our highest demand item.  Our Gloves for All program enables Pitch In For Baseball to fulfill requests for equipment in their entirety and is key to our achieving our mission to make baseball/softball accessible to every child.

title: without you, no education, no future!
description: This project is supporting over 80 orphans who came up as result of HIV/AIDS,civil wars and others!these children are supported with free education,scholastic materials,free food and clothes!we stay with them during day hours and they go back to their guardians,because of extreme poverty in this area,long distances from nearby schools,we resolved to start this orphanage school to create a bright future for these children.Currently they have no enough classrooms and school supplies are not enough

title: Education for 36,000 sickle cell in Kinshasa Step1
description: It is a management school sickle cell victims of discrimination, stigma and school late due to absenteeism or for repeated or prolonged hospitalization or incapacity of parents to provide school fees for impoverished by disease their children .

title: Providing Life Skills to 300 Girls living in Slums
description: The project is for training minimum 300 poor girls from slums in important life skills in Mumbai and in other districts through a resource center. They learn computer use, spoken English, photography, speech making, social networking and more. The project provides training in leadership and encourages girls' participation in community life through learning opportunities and assuring they complete school education for a productive and useful life. Our permanent center commits to do it every year.

title: Improve Education For 2000 Deaf Children in Kenya
description: Deaf children and youth can't access information when oral method is used as medium of instruction at school.The project seeks to apply visual method of teaching and learning that will lead to active participation in education process.

title: Restore a Truck for an Orphanage in Haiti
description: In January 2010, a massive earthquake destroyed our orphanage and 10 of our children.  The 12 survivors moved into the childhood home of the orphanage's founder, Jacque Senat.  Jacque's business, the sole financial supporter of the orphanage was also destroyed.  Jacques moved to Kansas City, MO. and took on a job as a cab driver to fund the expenses of the orphanage.  To this day, Jacques works 20 hours a day as a cab driver to provide over 75% of the annual funding for Orphanage Life Savers.

title: "A Book for Midwives" in French for West Africa
description: This project is to raise the final funding to print in Senegal and distribute in West Africa 2,000 copies of Hesperian's "A Book for Midwives," already translated into French and beautifully designed and illustrated. Developed for women with little formal education, the book will be used as a text to train new midwives, and give practicing midwives and traditional birth attendants a trusted reference for up to date medical information and technique.

title: Grant Wishes for Kids in the Greater Bay Area
description: We grant the wishes of children with life-threatening medical conditions to enrich the human experience with hope, strength and joy.

title: EDUCATE BOYS & GIRLS AND TRANSFORM THE COMMUNITY
description: Alpha Glory community Center advocates for Educational needs of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged children in the society.The Center is creating awareness and changing lives of hundreds of children in Kabiria who go through a lot of challenges,abuses and negligence.

title: Support children at poverty risk in Spain
description: One in three children lives under risk of poverty in Spain. What is their only opportunity to build a better future? Education. This is a social-educational project that takes place outside school hours. We give educational and nutritional support to children between 3 and 12 years old, who have scarce material resources and/or emotional support and are risking school failure.

title: Young Ambassador Programme
description: A Young Ambassador works as part of a network of young people who are speaking out against bullying. They increase awareness of the detrimental affects of bullying whilst promoting the benefits of youth volunteering and how it can help empower and inspire young people to realise their true potential and how, by developing their confidence and skills, they become role models and leaders.

title: Goats for children affected by HIV/AIDS
description: Buy some goats and seeds for orphaned families in Congo and Zimbabwe - and improve a child's potential in life. Malnutrition is a serious and widespread problem both these countries, exacerbated by COVID19, and you can help fight it through the gift of goats and gardens and the training we provide beneficiaries.  So simple, yet SO powerful!

title: China Foundation for Poverty Alleviation (CFPA)
description: Help resource-deficient poor communities enhance their capacity for self- sustainability;  Upgrade basic production conditions and primary social service levels;  Mitigate social suffering while promoting social harmony.

title: Take a stand with LGBT Voice Tanzania
description: Tanzania is yet another country facing even more severe LGBT persecution, as a tougher anti-LGBT bill is being introduced into the Parliament and may be up for vote.As you're well aware, these laws are making it ever more dangerous for people living with HIV/AIDS to get access to health care, not to mention all of the other effects of the rising homophobia. Kindly make a donation to support our efforts towards preventing this anti- LGBT  bill before it becomes a law.

title: Send Tom to the 2016 Rio Paralympics
description: This project is to send Pipat 'Tom' Thongjapo to the 2016 Rio Paralympics. Tom is currently #1 Wheelchair Fencer in Thailand, Category B, and ranked at #33 worldwide.  For a chance to get the Gold Tom must increase his ranking by competing in 11 international competitions  over the next 2 years. Funds are needed to cover travel, tax and registration.  By supporting Tom you're helping to inspire change in attitudes towards disabled people in Thailand, who are often marginalised by society.

title: Piggery Business Project for Children in Uganda
description: Mountains of Hope is currently building an orphanage and school for 50 vulnerable children in rural Uganda. In order to make the school self-sustaining, we are creating businesses, such as a piggery. The piggery will primarily serve to funding scholarships. Furthermore, the piggery will teach children book-keeping and business skills, provide food for the school, and give piglets to the surrounding community.

title: Legal Advice for Women Prisoners
description: This project will provide free legal advice and support/intervention to women prisoners in England & Wales. In doing so we will advocate for the protection of their human rights, which are compromised by the general imbalance of power in prisons between staff and prisoners. Our interventions and legal advice (given by telephone, mail, and face-to-face outreach clinics in prisons) will ensure that the human rights of women prisoners are defended and upheld.

title: Access to Water for 500 Rural Indian Families
description: 650 Million people on the planet lack reliable access to safe water. Many rural Indian women and girls travel at least half a mile to reach a safe water source, taking up 25% of a women's day. Water is HEAVY. A woman or girl would carry 20KG each trip several times a day. The Wello WaterWheel cuts down on the trips, eases the burden and saves time, which can be used more productively and means instead of carrying water a girl can go to school. More water means better health and hygiene.

title: Books by the pallet-load for African children
description: BookRelief UK in North Devon have worked in partnership for a number of years with Book-Cycle of Exeter to collect, store and send appropriate used educational and reading books to grassroots projects in sub-Saharan African countries where a selected local project partner ensures, and helps to monitor, their distribution to appropriate beneficiaries.

title: Save a School with Ashwini Charitable Trust (ACT)
description: ACT's mission is to send underprivileged children of unskilled and impoverished laborers to school. ACT facilitates and empowers the children of government schools to bring them on par with those in private schools. ACT adopted two government schools, in July 2013 and September 2016, and has undertaken the 'renewal' and 'repair' of the existing school buildings and premises and improve the existing utilities such as toilets and water tanks which are in ruins.

title: Buy a Pad, Keep a Girl in School
description: The lack of sanitary pads and panties in a young girl's life can lead to significant absences in school and work.Unable to afford these necessities, girls will often use dirty rags or mattress pieces instead. GlobeMed, along with nonprofit Set Her Free, is collaborating on a reusable sanitary pad project to target this issue. The reusable sanitary pad project will teach girls how to sew and distribute reusable pads to rural schools. Buying a pad helps keep a girl in school!

title: Ensure food security for 500 households in India
description: The project is scaling up traditional sustainable livelihoods to ensure food security for 500 underprivileged households who live in the fringes of the remotest Protected Forest Areas in northeastern India. Recurring flood and inaction of Wildlife Protection Act had made their livelihood earning extremely difficult. The project is strengthening the women of the poor households by providing trainings, free initial materials & equipments and facilitates access to micro-finances & markets.

title: Micro-business & Entrepreneur Activation - Phetoho
description: In collaboration with local charities and social enterprises, Future Families sources and sells high quality clothing at affordable below-market prices to trained groups of vulnerable women, in South Africa. This Phetoho project trains and activates budding community entrepreneurs to start micro-businesses for social and financial independence in communities where unemployment is high. "Phetoho" means change in the Sesotho language; representing positive economic impact and community uplifting.

title: Therapeutic recreation for patients in Boston
description: At Spaulding, we help people of all ages to find the strength to live life to the fullest after a devastating injury or illness.  Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital is a national and regional leader in patient care and research, serving people from greater Boston, eastern Massachusetts, across the country, and around the world.  The Spaulding Young Professionals Group is raising funds to support the therapeutic recreation space in our new Charlestown facility.

title: Good Bye Slums. Help 40 Uganda Women Build Homes.
description: Since 2007, our Jinja women's group has diligently learned business skills and used internally generated microloans to build and expand their businesses. They want to escape the Jinja slums and own their homes. Help them achieve their dream.  We have purchased land for these homes. Ten ladies each need $1300 to match the $1300 they are saving for a home down payment (2/3 to raise on globalgiving) Ladies who once lived on under $1 per day will escape poverty forever. Good bye slums!

title: Provide Computer Training at Freetown Computer Lab
description: A computer lab and the on-going training will complement our on-going educational and business development activities at the Door of Hope community in Freetown.  The community has over 1000 children, youths and adults that have LIMITED or NO exposure to computer training. Access to computers and training will enable them to become computer proficient.  This vital skill will facilitate their success in today's technology-driven society - helping them to obtain jobs or improve their businesses.

title: FEED & EDUCATE 230 DISABLED CHILDREN IN ZAMBIA
description: Provide revolving fund for disabled children, special education, child care and physiotherapy services to 230 disabled children from poor and disadvantaged families, and training caregivers and families in Zambia

title: Baby Incubators Needed in India
description: We are building a specialist centre dedicated to women and children in an area of India where this type of specialist service is not available. The centre will not only provide medical care but also work to instil a concept of disease prevention within this group. We are trying to achieve this through education and support within the local communities. We urgently need 2 incubators costing a total of 2,000 GBP.

title: Summer Camp for Refugee Girls
description: Madonna Mission's summer camp for refugee girls addresses the educational, social, and emotional needs of refugee girls by providing a safe, learning environment for them to grow and learn.  Campers participate in academic-based projects, arts and crafts, outdoor play, field trips, technology based activities and on-site educational presentations during a six week program.

title: Cultural Exchange Project
description: We help children aged 3-17 become engaged, knowledgeable, caring world citizens. Low income families travel abroad in cultural exchange programs so that children from income-strapped homes can broaden their horizons, gaining valuable exposure to the world and its diverse cultures. We fan into flame our youth's zeal for lifelong learning that will enable them to escape the lure of drugs, crime and gangs, and gain them active involvement in the solutions to the world's most pressing challenges.

title: Empowerment of 200000 Adolescent Girls in India
description: Almost half of girls in India will be married before the age of 18, and many will have their first child before they are 17. The Covid 19 pandemic has had a negative effect on adolescent girls. Child marriage perpetuates the poverty cycle and significantly increases the incidence of maternal and neonatal health issues and mortality. Our integrated interventions empower adolescent girls, prevent child marriage, help to delay conception and support young mothers.

title: Food Security and Agriculture
description: Darfur refugees were farmers before they fled Sudan in 2003. They are dependent on the World Food Program for food, but rations are low so the provisions do not cover their need. Refugees requested urgent assistance from the DWN in establishing small-scale farming and home gardening projects to produce their own food. The project will provide 1000 refugee families with rented land, seed and equipment they need to produce flourishing communities, agricultural security and personal empowerment.

title: Life-Saving Medical Equipment for Spay/Neuter
description: The Humane Society of South Mississippi has performed over 80,000 spay/neuter surgeries since opening in 2006. Much of the equipment still being used in the clinic is original and is showing its age. HSSM is devoted to saving more lives through spay/neuter but is in desperate need of 2 new Pulse Oximeters to monitor the 40-80 animals who undergo this lifesaving surgery each day. HSSM is in dire need of this vital equipment to keep each of our 4-legged patients safe during surgery.

title: 300 solar lamps for rural students in Zimbabwe
description:
The Big Idea:
This project aims to replace kerosene lamps with solar-based household lighting through an integrated approach of community mobilization and technological intervention. This will benefit the residents of Robert Sinyoka, Zimbabwe, a peri-urban settlement which is neglected, almost forgotten and without electricity

title: Help stop drowning in Sudan by training 60 people
description:
Nile Swimmers will train 30 male and 30 female young adults from Khartoum as swimming teachers.  These swimming teachers will then be supported by Nile Swimmers to provide life saving swim training in their local communities.  With each teacher providing further training through their community network, it is estimated that 9000 children will be directly impacted and their risk of drowning reduced within the first year.

This project has been part funded by a generous pledge from a Foundation.

title: Empowerment of 300 Street Children in India
description: This project will provide 300 street children in Vellore, Tamilnadu State, South India, with alternative education, vocational skill training, health and nutritional care and social and entrepreneurship  skill development thereby reducing negative impact of vulnerable environment on them by 2018.

title: Support Liberian Adult Education
description: Imani House, Inc. has provided Adult Education services to the Liberian people since 1993.  Between then and now the project has served thousands of people with literacy and math classes and operates sites at Duala Markets and VOA . All present and past students in the program were/are of low educational standing, the majority living in abject poverty.

title: Vanuatu Cyclone Relief Fund
description: Cyclone Pam has caused significant damage in Vanuatu, an island nation in the South Pacific. At least 8 people have been killed by the storm, and thousands of people have been displaced. The full extent of the damage is still being assessed, but aid groups are mobilizing to provide support and emergency supplies to the people impacted by the storm. All donations to this fund will exclusively support relief and recovery efforts  in Vanuatu.

title: Funding the Expansion of a School in Cambodia
description: This project will fund the expansion of our small English centre into a school with proper facilities. Our aim is to be able to increase enrollment gradually every year to accommodate more underprivileged children aged 4 to 16 years old. We provide a platform for young Cambodian children to learn the English language and widen their knowledge beyond the conventional curriculum, enabling them to be more equipped to pursue higher education or gain employment in.

title: sports for success of special children
description: Sports and physical education can improve special children's lives in many ways. Their experiences will stay with them throughout their lives and may be passed on to future generations. Sports & games give special children chance to become Independent, Self-reliant, Confident and a contributing part of the society. It will bring them to a bright future where they will not be burden for anyone and will become able support their family in all aspects.

title: Protect Girls from FGM in Tanzania
description: This program with FGM survivor and activist Rhobi Samwelly protects and empowers girls at risk of gender-based violence, including child marriage and female genital mutilation (FGM). Her organization Hope for Girls and Women runs safe houses to protect girls at risk, maps uncharted regions of Tanzania for rescue teams, initiates girls into womanhood without FGM, and educates cutters and community leaders around the impacts of gender-based violence.

title: Sierra Leonean Youth as Family Planning Educators
description: Marie Stopes Sierra Leone (MSSL) will train and support 60 youth peer educators to inform their peers about reproductive health and where to access services. MSSL seeks to support young people to speak with other youth about family planning and sexually transmitted infections to break down myths, provide accurate information in a confidential way, and show youth where they can access youth-friendly, non-judgmental services should they want them.

title: IMMEDIATE ASSISTANCE TO FIRE VICTIMS IN DAVAO CITY
description: Approximately 3, 700 families were displaced after a fire engulfed three coastal barangays in Davao City, Philippines last April 4, 2014. The Children's Joy Foundation Inc. aims to provide disaster assistance to these displaced families by giving their immediate basic needs such as the constant distribution of meals and food packs and help the community recover from the said disaster.

title: Hot lunches for 500 Cambodian children and youth
description: M'Lop Tapang works with disadvantaged children and families. We believe that education is a way to break a family cycle of poverty and to do this we provide a variety of education and training programs.  We know it's hard to study if you are hungry and so we make free hot meals available to more than 500 Cambodian children and youth as part of their regular school day.  These meals are not fancy, but they are healthy and filling and often the only nutritious meal a child gets on a regular basis

title: James, Nick & Paddy Climb Kili for Xavier Project
description: Xavier Project exists to provide opportunities to urban refugees in Kenya and Uganda who otherwise might not have the means to live fulfilled and dignified lives. In a holistic approach to development, Xavier Project arms urban refugees with the tools needed to to take back control of their lives and make a positive change to their communities through a comprehensive education program.

title: Build a Home for AIDS Orphans in Tanzania
description: Vine Trust builds houses for orphans in Tanzania, providing them with a comfortable home to help keep them safe, healthy and connected to their local community. The devastating effects of AIDS leave many Tanzanian children without parents from a very young age. Local communities are overwhelmed by the number of children, and cannot take care of them. By working with other agencies providing homes, education and foster care, Vine Trust helps save children from a life on the streets.

title: Provide Tutoring and Mentoring for 800 Students
description: City Year recruits and trains young AmeriCorps members to serve as tutors, mentors and role models full-time for an entire year in America's most underresourced public schools.   This project will enable these corps members to serve over 800 students with targeted interventions for an entire week. The majority of these students are facing the challenges of intergenerational poverty and the schools they attend struggle to meet their needs. City Year aims to help these students reach graduation!

title: Emergency Veterinary Care for Pets of the Homeless
description: Your donation will help a pet that belongs to a homeless person in the U.S., and Canada.  We provide emergency veterinary care and pet food to the hundreds of thousands of pets that are companions to the homeless.

title: Construct of Greenhouse in 10 schools in Uganda
description:
This project will construct low cost greenhouse within the ground of 10 schools so that local communities can generate a reliable source of nutrition as well as income to fund the education of children.

The secondary aim of the project is to use the greenhouses to cultivate the growth of banana tissue plantlets. The plantlets will provide a premium source of revenue for the community and help stable supply of bananas in the region- which fluctuates significantly- reducing food insecurity.

title: Provide shelter for 20 Ugandan Rural Grandmothers
description: The project will build 20 houses for Rural Ugandan Grandmothers looking after Aids orphans in Jinja District.This will provide decent shelter for them and orphans under their care.Grandmothers currently live in mud and wattle houses with very weak walls , a big threat to their lives and that of the orphans under their care.During the rains they are forced to seek refugee under the trees because its safer outside and yet it greatly affects their health  and that of the orphans under their care.

title: Bring Back Israel's Diving Ducks
description: The Diving Duck (Aythya nyroca) inhabits wetlands from Europe to Asia but is threatened by the destruction of wetland habitats and has markedly declined in Europe. Chiefly migratory, the species is listed as Near Threatened on IUCN Red List and has all but disappeared from Israeli wildlife as a nester. The Jerusalem Biblical Zoo has begun a captive breeding and reintroduction program coupled with raising public awareness of wetlands habitat preservation to stimulate a local population recovery.

title: 1 Month of Tutoring for 463 South Bronx Students
description: Corps members tutor one-on-one and in small groups during school hours and lead out-of-class extension activities that complement school instruction. Through focused literacy tutoring, working directly with each student to address their individual literacy needs, our corps members help students get back on track to reading at grade level.

title: City Year Chicago & John Hope HS - Finish Strong!
description: All children can learn, but some students face challenges in and out of the classroom that can hinder their success. City Year works with John Hope High School to meet the individual needs of students and get them on track to graduate. Your donation supports the school's Finishing Strong Plan, providing an extra push of targeted academic support, social emotional mentoring, attendance coaching, and a positive school environment between now and the end of the school year.

title: Increase Graduation Rates In Little Rock
description: Every 26 seconds a student gives up on school, resulting in more than one million American high school students who drop out every year. In urban public schools that serve primarily low-income and Latino or African American youth, between 40% and 60% of entering freshman do not graduate from high school. In Southwest Little Rock, City Year corps members serve in schools which contribute to one of the highest annual dropout rates in Arkansas.

title: Support DC students through Camp City Year!
description: City Year Washington, DC works with over 4,300 students in 13 public schools throughout the year. During the week of Spring Break for DC Public Schools, City Year welcomes students to join in a full-day camp experience to continue to positively impact students and keep them focused on education.   This year City Year Corps Members will lead campers through the week around the theme of Timeless Heroes--focusing students around learning about positive role models and heroes across time.

title: Uphold sexual minority rights in the great lakes
description: In the backdrop of tough anti gay laws regionally,and a discriminatory media stance,the project aims to shed light and demystify myths, hate speech and stereotypes targeting the LGBTI community in Rwanda and the great lakes region through advocacy, human rights education, legal aid and provision of psychosocial support with the intent to curb violation of basic human rights of this community and need for provision of equal opportunities and protection of rights like any other law abiding citizen

title: Help 50 Afghan Farmers Plant Fruit Trees
description: Providing fruit trees for 50 Afghan farmers will support sustainable livelihoods and help renew the environment. Tree planting will take place in 5 villages outside of Kabul where GPFA currently has ongoing community projects. Each farmer will receive 50-100 trees in an effort to develop new commercially viable orchards on individual jeribs of land (equivalent to about half an acre). The fruit harvested from these trees is anticipated to increase the income of each farm household by 25%.

title: Glover's Reef Research Station, Belize
description: Take action with the Wildlife Conservation Society by supporting Glover's Reef Research Station - a platform for cutting-edge marine science on the Belize Barrier Reef. The research conducted here by scientists and students from around the world helps protect threatened sharks and rays, sea turtles, reef fish, and much more at one of the Caribbean's most important coral reef systems, and advances the training and education of the next generation of marine scientists and ocean advocates.

title: Rehabilitate 200 Child SexWorkers in Soroti Uganda
description: This project will rehabilitate 200 child sex workers to enroll and stay in school through providing basic educational support like books, pens, uniforms and tuition, behavioral, psycho-social and legal interventions. The interventions will address household poverty and child abuse vulnerability conditions fueling child sex trade, through life skills development, counselling and rehabilitation. Strengthening and formation of community child protection mechanisms, to reduce vulnerability.

title: Camp for 400 Kids with Autism & Medical Needs
description: Every youngster deserves a normal childhood-a chance to dig in the dirt, to sing off key, to explore the world, and to discover new things along the way. The lives of certain children, by virtue of illness or disorder, are anything but normal. Sadly, these youngsters are suffering physically and emotionally not only from coping with the treatments necessary to sustain life, but also from coping with the loss of their childhood.  Dragonfly Forest provides a summer camp experience for these kids.

title: Stop TB Outreach Fellowship, Ghana
description: Sixty youth from Ghana's Awutu Senya Municipal will receive the opportunity to participate in a summer youth fellowship program. The fellowship program will create a platform for youth to gain experience in public health education, and reduce transmission of TB through community based health education. Youth will also act as bridges to care, referring individuals with symptoms of the disease for diagnostic testing at a local clinic's disease control unit.

title: Help Build a Trade School for Youth in Rural Kenya
description: Most children in rural Kenya do not have the possibility to further their education beyond elementary school due to learning disabilities and extreme poverty. Help us build a trade school for these youth so they may learn valuable skills such as carpentry, agriculture, cooking and hairdressing that will enable them to get jobs and become self-sustaining members of society. You can help by giving these youth the opportunity to learn a trade and help break the cycle of poverty.

title: ICT as a Tool for Young Voices
description: This project supports 110 young journalists in Armenia in helping them identify community problems and solve them through mass media and modern technology.

title: Help Women in India Become Professional Drivers
description: Our Women with Wheels project empowers poor women to become professional drivers to enable them get well-paying and respectful jobs and reclaim freedom. It helps these women get employed as cab drivers and chauffeurs for women, making transportation in Indian cities safer for women. Once earning, women drivers are able to double even triple their family income. The project does not only help lift many people out of poverty, it also empowers women to transform their lives in numerous ways.

title: Supporting victims of the fire in Valparaiso-Chile
description: This project will support schools and school communities affected by the big fire that happened on April 12th 2014 in Valparaiso, Chile. With your support we will be providing different kind of items depending on the different needs each school presents (school clothes, books, school supplies, repair of buildings, etc.). We need a lot of help! //  Con esta campana queremos apoyar a los colegios y comunidades escolares afectadas por el catastrofico incendio en Valparaiso de Chile (12 Abril).

title: QuietTime: Teaching TM in Low-Income Urban Schools
description: The Quiet Time program is a practical, evidence-based approach to reduce stress and dramatically improve academic performance, student wellness and the school environment.

title: Sewing Machines for Job Creation!
description: Mamafrica Designs is raising money to purchase an industrial sewing machine that will allow us to make leather goods in our workshop, in Democratic Republic of Congo. We work in a region where 85% of the women are unemployment. We create employment by making fair trade, handmade clothing and accessories. With the industrial sewing machine we can start to make leather gifts for the community and abroad.

title: Empowering India's Rural Poor through Poultry
description: Shivia empowers the poorest to create livelihoods, boost income and inspire permanent change. We aim to help families living in poverty in rural West Bengal earn money through poultry farming.  Our poultry toolkit has everything needed to start a small enterprise from home including 10 chicks and expert training from our team of Livelihood Service Providers. Please help us to help more families lift themselves out of poverty by rearing chickens - it's simple, it's cost effective and it works.

title: Support Nagina Sewing Center
description: Through education we can improve women's role in society. We provide career level sewing training to needy women and girls while advocating education as a means for prosperity. These women can earn money for their families after our 6 month training program. Our Center is very successful and we are planning for more 6 month programs. We bring our program to the communities in need therefore our location changes after every program. Our teacher and sewing machines will come along to our new site.

title: Save our Trees to the Sea
description: Between 2005 and 2008, more than 2000 volunteers planted 500 trees as a pollution barrier along the Los Angeles airport, with the initial understanding that the City of Los Angeles would care for the trees. Shortly before the first planting the City reneged, and Tree Musketeers managed to raise enough funds to ensure care for the trees until 2011. The lives of these 500 trees on the front lines in war against pollution are now in jeopardy!

title: School for 25 at-risk children in South Africa
description: Early education is the key to success and you can help provide a safe, nurturing environment to vulnerable children who are so hungry for this chance. This project will enable 25 children to attend school for an entire year.

title: Empowering Women in Nepal to Be a Voice for Change
description: Many women and girls in Nepal remain voiceless, which plays a role in the high rate of domestic violence, sex trafficking and other issues they face. Equal Access is empowering marginalized women by training them to be reporters so that they will capture the experiences of women in marginalized communities on a range of issues that affect their lives. Equipped with reporting skills and the recorders, these women are now employable and empowered to make a difference in their community.

title: Caring malnourished Korku tribe children in India
description: The project intends to provide non-institutional community care to 1000 severely malnourished Korku tribal children through early tracking, follow-up, health checks, doorstep counselling, revamping existing Child care centres (Anganwadis), managing community creches, and behaviour change communication.

title: Help street-active youth in Ghana start businesses
description: This project will provide business and financial skills training to marginalised youth in Sekondi-Takoradi, Ghana. In recent years, the number of street-active youth in this area has dramatically increased with many forced to survive through dangerous and illegal means. The project will provide youth with the skills and support they require to start or expand small businesses, find gainful employment or return to education, so that they are better able to support themselves and their families.

title: SEA:  Sisterhood Empowerment Academy
description: The Sisterhood Empowerment Academy (SEA) is Sisterhood Agenda's eco-friendly headquarters based on the island of St. John, U.S. Virgin Islands.  It is a global empowerment space featuring sustainable eco-design and nature-inspired architecture.  Women, girls, and community leaders come here for healing, training, enlightenment and sister support.

title: The Maya Musical: Find your Light
description: The Maya Musical is a story of our journey to find our light. Maya, a partnership between Teach For India and Artists Striving to End Poverty, is an original script, with Broadway composed music that tells the story of Princess Maya's journey. Tasked to bring light back into her Kingdom, Maya and her friends use the values of courage, compassion and wisdom to lift 3 great curses that have been cast on the world. The show will open in November 2014.

title: Empower Women's Dreams to Improve Children's Lives
description: Women around the globe want to make a difference in the lives of orphans and at-risk children. Many dream of supporting an under-served community by creating a project of education, nutrition, joy, health and/or peace. They have passion, commitment and skills, but need resources and support to ensure their project's success. This Mothering Across Continents initiative makes it possible for women catalysts to birth, guide and grow projects to improve vulnerable children's lives.

title: Give Backpack Of Hope To A Child In Nigeria
description: This project will provide school kits to impoverished and underprivileged school children in Ehime Mbano, Nigeria, so they may access the education needed to battle poverty and enable them go to school without a disadvantage, their very own school supplies and essentials, means they will be ready to achieve their educational goals. With your support, we can give children a chance at success by providing them with the tools necessary for a complete education.

title: Nepal Street Children's First Cricket Tournament
description: To celebrate International Day for Street Children on the 12th April we are holding a national cricket tournament where teams from 16 children's homes in the Hetauda and Chitwan regions will compete. This is a great opportunity for these boys to be part of a team and to compete with their peers. With the support of the National Cricket Association we want to make this day to remember for these boys and we need your help to make this dream a reality.

title: Sharing the Future - Young Papua New Guineans
description: This project will educate young people about the rich history of Papua New Guinea, building pride in the nation and hope for the future. It will promote the 5 National Goals and Directive Principles of the Papua New Guinea Constitution: for EVERY PERSON to have the opportunity to develop as a WHOLE PERSON; EQUAL OPPORTUNITY to benefit from the development of OUR COUNTRY; to be INDEPEDENT and SELF RELIANT; the ENVIRONMENT to be CONSERVED; and to use PAPUA NEW GUINEAN WAYS to shape our future.

title: 96 Permanent Homes for Haiyan Survivors
description: Typhoon Haiyan was one of the strongest storms ever to make landfall. The Philippines is used to storms, but even their concrete shelters were destroyed by Haiyan's vicious winds and massive storm surge. Today, hundreds of thousands are homeless. We're committed to rebuilding permanent homes for Haiyan survivors in partnership with Filipino group Gawad Kalinga.

title: Support Education in Tacloban
description: Typhoon Haiyan tore through the Philippines in November 2013.  It damaged or destroyed over 2,500 schools leaving the education of hundreds of thousands of kids in tatters.  We've already helped more than 5,000 children get back to school by rebuilding damaged classrooms, providing school supplies and school meals, and by making schools safe and fun places to learn.

title: Support New York City High School Students
description: We are concerned about the number of underfunded public schools in New York City. Less than 35% of the city's education budget goes toward purchasing new supplies. We seek to enrich the classroom experience by  providing workshops, field trips and academic mentors to the city's most in-need children. Our strategy is to expose students who normally would not have the opportunity to learn and research global issues with the long-term goal of improving students' academic outcomes.

title: Prevent Child Trafficking with 10000 Comics
description: Children are the main target of human trafficking for sexual exploitation, being sold by their own families to pay for debts. Raising awareness within the community is crucial for future prevention. The use of comic books to illiterate parent produces the best results when combined with community workshops. A picture is worth a thousand words!

title: Sema Magazine, Tanzania
description: Provides a unique opportunity for marginalized children's stories to be heard and call on local corporations to support them through inputting their ads on the magazine.

title: Vocational Training in Mnukwa, Zambia
description: The project started in 2011 with the building of 3 classrooms followed by a bore hole in 2012 and then the addition of solar panels in 2013. We are now supplying the centre with sewing machines and carpentry tools. The community is isolated and this project is opening up new opportunities for them and engaging the young people in exciting new projects. The solar panels and lights will allow access to the rooms in the evenings.

title: Keep 800 Girls in School in Kibuku, Uganda
description:
This project will train 40 women to make Eco-Sanitary pads for 800 girls who would not have been able to stay in school otherwise due to lack of appropriate menstruation sanitary products.
40 women will be provided with the skills, absorbent materials and machines to produce re-usable sanitary pads. Enabling young girls to stay in school, feel comfortable and less ashamed about an important stage in their development.

title: One Picture Saves a Life
description: With over 75% of pet adoptions starting online, a positive picture of a well groomed animal may be that animal's best chance of finding a forever home.
