One Picture Saves a Life has teamed up with Seth Casteel of Underwater Dogs fame and Jorge Bendersky from Animal Planet's Groomer Has It to train shelters, rescue groups, and volunteers all over the country to save animals' lives through improved grooming techniques and positive adoption photography.

title: Grass Roots Sea Turtle Conservation, Costa Rica
description: This projects aims to protect and rescue 100% of the sea turtle nests of Playa Buenavista in Costa Rica, by building a hatchery in order to relocate and monitor nests. When the eggs hatch, babies can be released in a controlled environment and scientific data can be taken to study turtle nesting behaviour in this area. This will enable us to ensure a high survival rate of the endangered sea turtle.

title: Healthcare Equipment to Destitute Elderly in India
description: Healthcare is a major concern for destitute elderly in India. Agewell Foundation has identified over 2800 destitute elderly who urgently need healthcare equipment/medical help. Agewell will provide a range of healthcare equipment to destitute and bedridden elderly including: wheelchairs to disabled elderly, walkers to help them walk around, adult diapers to bedridden elderly, eye tests and spectacles, hearing aids, regular medicines to elderly patients and support to meet medical expenses.

title: Return vulnerable children from Kibera to School
description: 1 in 4 children in Kibera, Kenya do not complete primary school. We provide a smooth transition back to school for children who have dropped out.

title: Improve the future for children with nystagmus
description: Infantile Nystagmus is a little known eye condition that can severely affect visual acuity and deeply impact upon quality of life. It occurs within the first few months of life and is a lifelong condition. It affects around 1 in 1,000 people and for so many infants it is not properly diagnosed making it impossible to help them. It is essential that these children are helped early on and the purchase of the right equipment, in the right hands, will make this happen while working towards a cure.

title: Life skills through sport for 2000 Nepali children
description: This project aims to develop the leadership, teamwork and awareness of social issues of 2,339 children at six schools in central Nepal through football workshops. These sessions address topics such as child rights; HIV/AIDS; conflict resolution; gender equality; child trafficking; and abuse, engaging children and encouraging participation through the innovative use of sport and games.

title: Reform the Philippine Judiciary with a Jury System
description: In the 50s, the Philippines were second only to Japan in terms of per-capita wealth in Asia. However, the current Single-Judge System allows corruption to go unpunished, leading to exploitation of Filipinos and the country's economic underdevelopment. We are working towards making our judicial system fairer and empowering every Filipino to act peacefully and positively for change. We aim to modernise our judicial system through the introduction of National Jury Law, as supported by the people.

title: Needs-based training for homeless women in Tbilisi
description: Urgent action is needed to equip 15 vulnerable women living in extreme poverty with needs-based training for potential employment opportunities. Living below poverty threshold, these women suffer from malnutrition, psychological and physical violence; they raise children with mental/physical disabilities and face multiple discrimination on governmental, social and domestic levels. Providing needs based training will equip them with skills of their choice to support themselves and family members.

title: Help child with rare disorder visit a clinic!
description: We have facilitated the establishment of 9 dup15q clinics around the United States. Our goal is for each of our 900 families be able to visit a clinic to receive the best medical care available for their children with this rare disorder.   Dup15q Alliance provides family support and promotes awareness, research and targeted treatments for chromosome 15q11.2-13.1 duplication syndrome. Symptoms of this rare genetic disorder include autism, seizures and developmental delays.

title: Changing lives in 20 child-headed homes in Rwanda
description: This project will improve the lives of 20 children head of households and their siblings in Rwanda. These children are orphaned or have been abandoned by their surviving parent and the oldest are forced to work to put food on the table, protect and support the younger ones going to school and get medical care when they fall sick. You can change a life by donating for their school material, pay health insurance or give the older one a means to make a living from hairdressing, sewing or farming

title: Education For Slums And Rural Kenyan Students
description:
Our mission at CSRD Education and Vocational Training Program is to create and promote an environment that empowers our young and precious generations of Slums and Rural Kenya to take up education as a way to enrich their own life, the life of others, thus the prosperity of the country. 
CSRD will provide encouragement, opportunity, and access to higher education to 200 poor but deserving students who have demonstrated academic excellence, moral character, integrity, and career objectives.

title: Refuge & Rehab for Street Children in Bangladesh
description: There are over 300,000 children living in the streets of Dhaka and many are being exposed to sexual trafficking, violence, organised crime, substance abuse, homelessness and malnutrition.  The Restless Beings Rehab Centre in Mohammadpur, Dhaka provides hundreds of children with safe accommodation, medical care, counselling, education, warm clothes and independence.  Help us continue to impact the lives of the most devastated and vulnerable street children in Dhaka by donating today!

title: Hope Abides
description: Imagine you live in a country where 40% of the population  lives on less than $1.25/day; now imagine you are an orphan with no one to provide even this meager level of sustenance. This is the reality of more than 25 million orphans in India.  An education is the best tool a child can have to escape poverty. Hope Abides provides hope and help to these orphans and other destitute children and is seeking funding to assist these children with education and other basic needs.

title: Help Survivors of Torture on Mother's Day
description: The vast majority of the women we help at ASTT are separated from their children on this Mother's Day. Though we cannot reunite them, ASTT can offer comfort and hope as they grapple with the emotional trauma and anxiety caused by this separation. Our clients needed to flee for their lives, leaving their children behind to come to our country. Your donation can make a difference in a mother's life today.

title: Sherpa Family Fund
description: A deadly avalanche on Mt. Everest recently claimed the lives of 16 Sherpas in the worst climbing accident in the mountain's history. In response, the American Himalayan Foundation has created the Sherpa Family Fund to support the families and educate the children left behind.

title: Provide Clean Water for Rural Family Home School
description: The Rural Family Home (CFR) is a three-year vocational school for rural young men and women that improves their quality of life and opportunities for sustainable livelihoods. To realize its potential and to become fully sustainable, the CFR needs improved facilities, particularly access to clean drinking water. The addition of an artesian well, which students will help to design and to construct, will enable the CFR to thrive for years to come. This amount will allow us to start the project.

title: Artisans Associations of Cambodia
description: Cambodia is among the poorest 1/3 of the world's nations.  The likelihood of poverty is increased by  factors such as disability and the pressures of maintaining a single parent household.  For such people, the possibility of work as an artisan provides a window of hope - they can produce items of value and be able to market them.

title: NO to child marriage in Kenya
description: To Mobilize and build the capacities and competencies of 2000 men, 1500boys and 200 community leaders toward the eradication of child marriage in Kenya. Girls as young as twelve are being forced to lose their childhoods for a life that is defined by isolation, violence and illness.

title: Mid day Meals for Disabled Children
description: Balajothi's objectives are to meet all the needs of the disabled children including Transportation, Rehabilitation, Therapy & Training, Special Education, Learning Aids, Learning Material and especially Nutrition. The importance of a nutritious and well balanced meal cannot be over stressed. We provide mid-day meals to every disabled child at Balajothi which ensures a healthy body leading to a healthy mind.

title: Childhood Psoriasis Trust Fund
description: There are no enough dermatologists and skin clinics in Nairobi.  Africa Psoriasis Organization organizes free medical camps to facilitate access to correct diagnosis and treatment of psoriasis to children from poor families in Nairobi slums. The free health camp projects are followed by psoriasis education to affected children to boost their confidence, schoolmates to increase understanding, parents to improve care and teachers to increase knowledge.

title: Care for Orphans and other Vulnerable Children
description: Children in Malawi experience many challenges requiring psychosocial support.Factors like HIV/ AIDS, poverty, social conflicts and family breakdown have psychosocial consequences for children. Promoting psychosocial support helps to instill hope in children. The project is committed to creating a safe environment to protect children from abuse, neglect and exploitation while mitigating the effect of the death of loved ones to ensure that children  grow and develop to their full potential.

title: Set Up A New Rural Healthcare Centre, India
description: Rural health Care Foundation intends to open basic health care centres in all those rural areas where basic medical facility is hindered due to problems in accessibility, affordability and quality of treatment. Through this project we would open a health care unit centre with a permanent set up comprising of four departments namely General Medicine, homeopathy, Dentistry and optometry-all facilities coming at a cost of Rs 60 ($0.90) for each patient.

title: Homeless Animals Hospital
description: The Homeless Animals Hospital is a new project launched by Romania Animal Rescue to provide veterinary help for homeless animals as well as for pets of the impoverished people in Romania.  Homeless Animals Hospital project was awarded "Project of the Month" by GlobalGiving following a visit by their representative in February 2015.

title: Kick out FGM in Kenya
description:
The project is to save 500 Samburu girls from FGM by mobilizing and building the capacities and competencies of 2000 Samburu men and boys towards the eradication of the vice. The FGM ritual has devastating consequences to the girl's health and well-being to an extent that it destroys their quality of live and subjects them to live long human rights violations. Project activities are:
5 community forums
7 focus group discussions
3 sporting day events,  
1000 posters
3 banners
3 radio show

title: Sprouting Seeds Learning Centre
description: Sprouting Seeds Learning Centre will provide a diverse range of practical life-skills training for Myanmar youth (focused primarily for girls from remote areas and ethnic backgrounds), which are rooted in principles of sustainability, preservation of traditional wisdom, and positive social engagement with a focus on youth and woman's empowerment as well as self-awareness through the Sprouting Seeds Learning Centre cafe, bakery, eco-shop and training centre.

title: Relief Fund for Arkansas and the Midwest States
description: While most of us were watching TV, eating dinner, or even sleeping the Central States were hit by a storm system culminating in tornadoes that left in its path destruction and unconfirmed deaths. At the time this project was written the hardest hit were Mayflower and Vilonia, Arkansas, by a tornado that left a path 30 miles long and half-mile wide. Three years ago from this past Sunday the 27th of April. 122 tornadoes touchdown and 316 people were lost, now, as then, survivors need your help.

title: Library and laboratory for 2500 uganda children
description: Your donations will help 2500 students and adult learners of Kawaala village in Uganda to access library services and science laboratory with up to date rich books with training in computer and internet.  The project was designed for talented but vulnerable (poor, orphans) children to allow them to have quality education which will enable them to get out of poverty cycle.

title: support 100 children in education in kenya
description:
Vision child believes in empowering, taking care of the needy and the most vulnerable children in the society. We believe in eradicating poverty and illiteracy by improving the lives of the extremely needy children through eduction. We shall provide various packages in education on the following:
1. life skills training
2.Talent nurturing 
3.Providing writing materials
4.Providing school uniforms and shoes
5.Providing nutritional support
6.Sustainable business opportunities to the youth

title: COMMUNITY BASED POWER FENCE TO SAVE ELEPHANTS
description: Man animal conflict is a humanly challenge in wildlife management and biodiversity conservation in India, this project secures farmers yearly livelihood & saves Elephant (Elephas maximus). 15,000 houses 10,00,000 ha of crops damage stay evidence of conflict every year. Due to anger and hardship farmers connect 440 volts electric line to farm fence, 200 Elephants die of electrocution and 200 humans die of conflict. Solar power fence will save wildlife, reduce man elephant conflict.

title: Brightening Girls Future through Education
description: Children from post conflict communities continue to experience challenging situations in accessing quality education, they perform poorly in Schools due to lack of basic Scholastic requirements. Girls miss class lessons during menstrual period in fear of the boys, early marriages & dropping out of Schools. Many children are also forced to seek employment to cater for their household needs at the expense of studies leading to high rate of Child labour and neglect however girls will be supported.

title: Support little champions with Cerebral Palsy!
description: Through the generosity of donors, we are able to pay for surgeries, treatments and rehabilitations for children with cerebral palsy. It is a great joy to help and see the results that the children can now walk alone, can better speak and are developing their abilities and potential. There are more than 80 children waiting for treatment! They are ready to work hard and endure all the procedures for the sake of their dream - to WALK! Help us make their dream come true!

title: Rescue sex workers & at-risk children in India
description: We provide support, empowerment, emergency rescue & healthcare to sex workers, including trafficked minors, transgenders, MSM and those affected by HIV. We enable them to become their own agents for social change, breaking the crippling cycles of exploitation. By sheltering & educating their children we prevent 2nd-generation prostitution & empower the same children to support their mothers to leave the sex trade & many also help other exploited women through social work.

title: New stage for the young circus artists in Russia
description: This project will help Upsala-Circus to construct a professional theatre stage in the circus tent. Upsala-Circus tent is the only children circus tent in all Russia. In this tent children from groups of social risk can train and perform, dream and work, be happy and fulfill themselves.

title: Improve Drop in Center for Mentally Ill in Nepal
description:
We aim to provide a weekly drop in center for 20-30 mentally ill clients, their carers & family members by offering activities that allow expression, engagement & build self esteem through counseling sessions, creative therapy classes like art, music, yoga & field visits along with vocational classes.
Also, to include family members & carers in our work plan to raise awareness in the community and to be a support system via interaction programs and home visits involving young volunteers.

title: Rehabilitation in the Philippines
description: Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) struck the Philippines in November of 2013. It was the deadliest and most massive typhoon in the nation's history. Some 7000 people were killed; over 30,000 injured and some 11 million persons lost their home, land, or were otherwise affected. Included in the destruction were severe damages to rehabilitation medical services in Tacloban area, and WRF is supporting 3 hospitals in the area with equipment to reestablish rehabilitation services for people with disabilities.

title: Equipping a New Kakata Primary Health Center
description: In December 2014 at the height of the ebola crisis HWHL made the critical decision to accelerate the construction of a new health center, filling a major gap in health infrastructure in Margibi County.  This large, purpose built facility, once operational will provide comprehensive basic medical and dental services, including a secure pharmacy, labs, and imaging.  We are working with the Ministry of Health for certification of the facility by the end of August.

title: Fountain of life women selp help group
description: This project was established to take care of the  people who were jobless, recovering from drug abuse and needy family members. The project has supported more than 200 members who are  running business to  support their families. The donations from well wishers has brought us this far. Young men and women have formed a music band and learned artskills to support them to cater for some of their dairy needs. Since we joined Global Giving, we have been hosting trainings for the new members thanks.

title: Empowering 50 HIV+ kids in India through education
description: Manavya aims at offering a helping hand to socially neglected 57 HIV+ children deprived of their right to become independent contributors in society by teaching English and Computer skills. Support this project that can transform 57 HIV+ children from being viewed as a liability to being celebrated as an asset. Manavya empowers these children to break free from the clutches of poverty and stigma by providing a place to live until adulthood and by supporting their education and healthcare.

title: Support Remote Area Medical Missions in Ghana
description: Rural dwellers in Central Region of Ghana suffer from adverse health conditions owing to mainly two reasons -first the lack of education and thus lack of awareness; and second poverty in area of standard of living, poor road network to the health facilities and rural settlement. The situation calls for timely care and diagnosis which can reduce the incidence of morbidity and mortality especially among children and women.

title: Provision of 2000 Fuel Efficient Stoves
description: Project will form and enhance the role of 50 Village Development Committees (VDCs) in safeguarding the global environment and contribute their part in village advancement (2) To increase community awareness of the consequences of deforestation and the need to conserve forests with the help of 50 trainings (3) To improve health by reducing the volume of harmful smoke produced by tradition stoves in the targeted villages with the provision of 2000 fuel efficient stoves.

title: Yak Sva: The Living Arts Mission
description: 192 underprivileged rural orphans will be able to attend Self-Sufficiency Program (SSP)-computer skills and English language skills-a gift for Lives with a brighter future. Your gift will be used for hiring 4 former OCTO Orphanage's residents with first hands experiences; 4 professional instructors; school supplies (computers, white boards, projectors, utility bills, books, copy machines, job site visits, job searches & job trainings, etc.) and health insurance for all 192 in OCTO Orphanage.

title: Emergency Appeal Landslide Badakhshan Afghanistan
description: On May 2014 landslides struck Argo district of Badakhshan causing significant loss of life and widespread damage to about 350 households, letting families homeless. The emergency appeal initially  focused on providing safe drinking water to the victims. Thanks to the generous donations 110 families have been provided with water filters. At the moment homeless families who live in empty school buildings, uncompleted house buildings or just tents need support to survive the freezing cold season.

title: 750 East Jerusalem Palestinian Women Demand Rights
description: Using a novel approach for activism called "MiniActive", the project will create an effective network of 750 Palestinian activist women who successfully demand their rights, and improve everyday life and their environment. One of the largest fully-volunteer networks in East Jerusalem, it currently works in 100 action groups of 5 people to solve hundreds of physical infrastructure problems each month. The activists also enhance their capacity by training in first aid, environment and leadership.

title: Save 880 poor Vietnamese from TB & Drug-Resistance
description: We are piloting an innovative active outreach and public-private collaboration model, in which community members are hired and professionally trained to visit urban slums and boarding houses to find, educate and link undeserved TB patients with free treatment from both the public TB care system and our network of participating private doctors. During treatment, we aim to ensure that all 880 patients in the district finish their antibiotic treatment to prevent the development of drug resistance.

title: Bringing Biblical Deer to the Holy Land
description: The Persian Fallow Deer (Dama dama mesopotamica) is one of the kosher animals mentioned in Deuteronomy 14:4-5. Thought to be extinct by the 1940's, a small population of this species was rediscovered in Iran in 1956. They are nearly extinct in the wild today, inhabiting only three small habitats in Iran and two areas in Israel where they have been successfully reintroduced since 1996. This conservation program focuses on their reintroduction into the wild at Nahal Soreq near Jerusalem, Israel.

title: Empower 600 Rural Women and Children in Rwanda
description: The Empower 600 Rural Women and Children in Rwanda project seeks to reduce the burden of maternal, neonatal and under-five mortality rates by targeting rural women and children in the Rulindo district with proven interventions such as health education, access to health services, and health systems strengthening.It seeks improve participants' standard of living through income generating activities and empower community health workers to better support the health of their communities.

title: Provide Housing Colony to 96 homeless Families
description: WWA will provide the living housing colony to Christians Community who is homeless in rural areas. WWA will make the housing colony for Christian's Community on 3 acres land (410sqft * 322sqft).  WWA will build 96 House in this colony, (each house is 25sqft * 32sqft). There would be 1 hospital, 1 school along with play ground & park, 1 Church and 1 Guest house for donor agencies/foreigners in this colony. This colony will be built on Mananwala Sheikhupura Punjab Pakistan.

title: Transform The Lives of 5 Entrepreneurs in Colombia
description: Being a successful entrepreneur is one of the most difficult, daunting and risky paths to follow, especially if you suffer from a physical disability. Despite the challenges, a handful of entrepreneurs with disabilities in Medellin are more determined than ever to run their own business and build a brighter future. This project assists 5 entrepreneurs with physical disabilities, providing them with top quality training and support in order guide their businesses in the appropriate direction.

title: Training Early Education Teachers in South Africa
description: Many Township Early Childhood teachers are under-educated themselves. They are hungry for opportunities to increase their skills and provide a better learning experience for the children in their care. A generous donor sponsored Love to Langa's first Reporting Workshop for teachers on January 30, 2014 and it was a tremendous success. The 20 women who attended raved about the experience and are clamoring for more. With a waiting list for future workshops, we need funding to make them happen.

title: The Teacher Fund: making a difference, together
description: May is "Teacher Appreciation Month" and 12+ would like to recognize all of the incredible teachers we have the privilege of working with. During this campaign, we will be asking supporters to make donations in honor of their favorite teachers by using the "Gift in Honor of" function on GlobalGiving. A portion of the funds that we collect will be used to create a "Teacher Fund," through which teachers at our partner schools will have the chance to sponsor events for their students!

title: Provide an ambulance in Wakiso, Uganda
description: Loyal Foundation Clinic in Entebbe provides free essential health care for some of the poorest people in Uganda. Last year we helped over 7,000 people who wouldn't have been able to afford healthcare and we saved lives. But sadly many adults and children die because they cannot reach the clinic in time. We can do something about this - we can buy an ambulance - but we need your help.

title: Book to School Project in the rural areas of Laos
description: The textbook situation in Lao PDR is of great concern for the country's educators at all levels. "Book to School" (BTOS) is designed to dually address both today's pressing needs of textbook and tomorrow's needs for quality learning in the Lao educational setting. "Book to School" aims to supply textbooks to meet the needs of the students; each student each textbooks is our goal.

title: Empowering the hearing-impaired through t-skills
description: The hearing-impaired youths under 25 are more useful to society. But, they are discriminated against  socially and economically in Nepal. Their misery is multiplied as they do not have computer skills that a job requires.To address this grave issue of human dimension, Synergy Nepal(SN) has a plan to empower about 10 thousand youths within 5 years. The project has a strategy for their empowerment by providing MS digital education, and Windows OS based technical skills enhancing entrepreneurship.

title: Support Youth Living with Disabilities in Armenia!
description: This project will build a day center for young people living with disabilities in the Kotayk region of Armenia, offering support services, recreational activities, and income generation opportunities for over 50 youth. Our goal is to help these youth to feel fully integrated and a part of society. This project aims to do this by creating a comfortable space where people with disabilities can gather with their peers to develop new skills, explore creativity, and feel fulfilled!

title: Infrastructure to Holy Trinity Monastery
description: This project aims to create conditions to serve adequately about a thousand people who come monthly to the Holy Trinity Monastery, in Brazil, searching for spiritual guidance and comfort.

title: Grant A Wish Food Program
description: Grant A Wish Food Program feeds hundreds of people every month. So many families are food insecure, by  giving away food every Saturday, we are helping to eliminate hunger in the community we serve through our food program.Children suffer the most, when there is a lack of nutritious food on the the table at home. We want to continue to do our part to make a difference.

title: Give Income Generation to Youth with Disabilities
description: All children, including disabled children, have the right to play, learn, and be included. But most children with disabilities in rural areas of Africa do not have the opportunity to explore the world around them. Give older youth with disabilities throughout rural parts of Africa a chance to gain social and livelihood skills through Uhambo's award-winning Ndinogona "I Can" Program that provides training to generate income by making handicrafts, in addition to learning valuable social skills.

title: Keep Snowsport Equipment Out of the Landfill
description: Recycle Utah's SnowSport Recycle Collection is the first program of its kind in Utah.  It is a social responsibility to divert equipment from the landfill so toxic materials don't leach into our water stream. We will now be charged a cost per pound of equipment from the recycling facility.  The costs are attributed to expensive material separation process. For Recycle Utah to keep the SnowSports Recycling Program running, we need individuals, businesses, suppliers and manufactures support.

title: Livelihood support for Muong survivors of violence
description: Domestic violence causes serious damage to physical and mental health of woman victims. Economic dependence is among the top reasons why many accept to live with such danger everyday. CSAGA wants to help 30 Muong women affected by domestic violence in Viet Nam through a livelihood support program, where they will be taught the practical skills to make traditional conical hats and knowledge of domestic violence. As a result, these ethnic minority women will be empowered economically.

title: Support Families of South Korea Ferry Disaster
description: This project will provide psycho-social training for hundreds of South Korean psychologists, social workers, school counselors, and teachers working with the families of the more than 300 people, mostly high school students, that tragically lost their lives (or are still missing) in the Sewol Ferry incident of April 2014. The training will focus on practical tools needed to aid the process of coping, and provide assistance towards preventing Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) in the community

title: WRITE FOR GOLD
description: WRITE FOR GOLD is educational project that seeks to assist school children in the deprived and hard to reach communities in the East Mamprusi district to develop a legible, fluent handwriting and reading skills. The project is targeted at school children between the ages of 6 years to 10 years who are at the lower primary. We will send our project volunteers to these deprived and hard to reach communities where there are no teachers to assist the school children to learn how to read and write.

title: Safe Center for Vulnerable Children in Douala
description: We provide a secure day and night center for underprivileged kids in Douala, offering a safe place to relax, play, and study after school. We cover school fees, meals, counseling, tutoring, basic medical care, and more. Without us, they'd face family-less hardship, resorting to begging and street-selling to survive, risking education gaps, vulnerability, extreme poverty, criminality, substance abuse, and exploitation.

title: Protect Elephants in Yankari Game Reserve, Nigeria
description: Yankari Game Reserve is Nigeria's richest wildlife oasis, home to important populations of lions, hippos, and many other species - as well as the last viable elephant population left in the country, and one of the largest remaining in all of West Africa. Like many of Africa's elephants, they are under severe threat from poaching and the illegal ivory trade. Help the Wildlife Conservation Society protect these elephants by supporting regular and effective ranger patrols.

title: Change a Ugandan Life with Sewing Lessons
description: In May 2013, with the help of donated peddle sewing machines and two volunteers from New Jersey, Change A Life Uganda taught women in Migyera and Nabbingo how to sew school uniforms. CALU hired a tailor to continue the program, holding a graduation ceremony after 8 month of training.  Top students received a microfinance loan to purchase their own machines. CALU wants to renew this program to meet the growing demand and empower women to become financially independent through skills development.

title: A Heroes Helping Hand
description: Center Point is committed to serving our Veterans in their reintegration to society with respect and honor.  Over 2 million American men  and women have served in Iraq and Afghanistan since 2001. As they return home, many with the invisible wounds of PTSD and MST, they also face the tremendous challenges and barriers presented by unemployment, poverty and homelessness. Our project will help ameliorate the stress and stigma our heroes face by providing financial assistance to Veterans in need.

title: Quality Education to 40 at Risk Youth in Korogocho
description: This project will provide financial support to Korogocho slum youth towards achieving high school education as well as offer mentorship. Poverty denies many youth a chance to get an education and therefore, the project will allow the youth a fair chance not only to get their right to education but also improve their chances of employability.

title: Educate a visually challenged child for one year
description: Indian Association for the Blind (IAB) is a non-profit organisation started in 1985 by visually challenged activist, Late.Mr.S.M.A.Jinnah.We provide education,food and accommodation facilities to the visually challenged from rural areas. Every year, around 130 children will be benefited.Four lakh blind children out of the fourteen lakh are from India, out of which only 5 percentage of them receive the right to education.IAB aims to make visually challenged lead lives of dignity and self-reliance

title: Using Animal Care to Promote Empathy in Children
description: With your support, an education campaign and free, veterinary clinic will be conducted annually at one community in Northern Swaziland. The clinic will provide much needed veterinary services to 200 dogs and cats, while the education campaign will teach positive animal care practices. Daily examples of good animal care will help promote the development of responsibility and empathy in rural Swazi children. Over time, this will help reverse Swaziland's high rate of domestic violence.

title: HOME & TEACH 7 INDIGENT DEAF CHILDREN IN S/AFRICA
description: This project will afford disadvantaged and compromised Deaf children the opportunity to access specialised education as well as accommodation at Fulton School for the Deaf in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

title: Planting Trees and Seeds of Hope in Nigeria
description: We do not only help the environment by planting trees, we also bring hope to an entire community, providing jobs, foods, growth and independence to rural areas that are left behind. We employ people from the local villages to plant the trees and maintain them. We also educate and encourage them to grow and harvest their own food in the plantation. We have already planted more than 150.000 trees in a plantation of 400 hectares (the land has been donated by the local government).

title: Help 50 Young Leaders from US & Korea Join KASC!
description: The Korea-America Student Conference (KASC) is student-led, academic and cultural exchange program that builds closer ties between young leaders in both countries. With rising tensions across the Pacific, the importance of a strong US-Korea relationship cannot be overstated. KASC addresses the need for cooperation and understanding between the two nations by bringing together 25 American and 25 Korean students every year for the month of July, building trust among the youth on a grassroots level

title: Educate Young People about the Environment
description: The project will raise awareness about the importance of the environment and the role individuals and communities have to play in preserving it.

title: Big Cat Conservation: A Global Alliance
description: Alone, neither science nor indigenous knowledge can stop the extinction of snow leopards, white lions, tigers, and jaguars. In 2013, for the first time ever, indigenous elders/shamans and scientists partnered to forge radical new conservation methods. Within months, the team helped forge the UN Global Snow Leopard policy, and now aim to carry the work into South Africa, home of the most endangered cat-the white lions.

title: Water Treatment Systems For Schools In Haiti
description: Fountains of Hope is helping to eliminate the cholera outbreak by providing safe water to schools and orphanages in Haiti.  We have identified 10+ school/orphanage locations near Archaie, Haiti that need FoH water purifier systems. Our goal is to raise funding for two or more water treatment facilities at $6,000 each.

title: Supporting People with Autism Spectrum Disorders
description: The Family Autism Center at The Arc of South Norfolk provides supports and services to people diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders and their families.  We provide respite care, specialized recreational programming, training for family members and provide information and referral sources to families looking for assistance.  Autism impacts 1 in every 68 children- we have seen an increase of 100 additional people requesting our services in the last 12 months alone- we serve 652 people currently

title: Provide Quality Care for Rescued Horses in Texas
description: This project will provide basic veterinary, dental, and farrier services to 10 horses at Easy R Equine Rescue for one year. Semi-annual vaccinations, regular dental work (floating teeth), and regular farrier work on their hooves are all very essential to the overall health and well-being of the horses.  Second to feed costs, these services are the largest expenses in providing quality care to all the Easy R herd.

title: Beat Ebola By Building Accountability in Liberia
description: Liberia is recovering from the worst Ebola outbreak of all time. We are working with thousands of Liberians in some of the poorest communities in the country and need your help to make sure a health crisis like this never happens again. For many years we've worked on the ground through our Community Justice Teams (CJTs) to build the trust and accountability that is critical to improve lives-- now help us to scale up the CJTs and build a better future for Liberia.

title: Urgent need to support the needy street children
description: We support street and orphan children from Jinja-Uganda to their full potential of life through involving them in education through trainings, medical counseling and guidance, ensuring food security and child sponsorship program.

title: Protect 2000 Nigeria Girls with school fence
description: 2000 Christ's School, Ado-Ekiti girls, daily live on campus without fence. Ado became a state capital and much bigger. Hostels are bugled, risk of rape, risk of girl abduction, inability to sleep at night from fear. Dilapidated teachers' houses, few convinced to stay on campus do not feel safe because their houses are broken in to. Risk of having girls in dormitories without adult supervision after school hours if they leave. Squatters encroach on land; lost access to brook. Goats invasion.

title: Provide School Sponsorships for 10 Kenyan Children
description: Action Two Africa's desire is very straight forward: we want to get kids off the streets and back into the classroom. Many children in Kenya are born into a cycle of poverty that perpetuates the broken system that they have become victims of. Action Two Africa wants to help break this pattern and get Kiambiu slum's youth back into school. We plan to meet this need by providing school fees for children who would otherwise not be able to continue their education.

title: Street to School - Mainstreaming Street Children
description: 'Street to School' is the first step of bringing children into education. This is where the magic happens. The program transforms the begging, rag picking and working 'Out of School' street & slum children into confident, happy children who can read and write. The aim of this program is to mainstream children into formal education. Our after school remedial classes reinforce their concepts and provide them support to thrive academically. WE ARE A VEHICLE FOR EMPOWERMENT THROUGH EDUCATION.

title: Enable 250 Liberian Children To Go To School
description: The  Cornerstone Academy was badly damaged during Liberia's civil war. The school  serves  war affected children, many of whom are ex-child soldiers. It  exists in temporary overcrowded quarters with little infrastructure and materials. Your donation will help the school build classrooms and desks and provide students with learning materials. It will enable  students to learn basic reading, writing, and mathematics skills, and support school efforts to teach tolerance and respect for all people

title: Train 10-30 women in Arusha to sew menswear
description: This project will increase the skills and incomes of 10-30 low-income young women (most of whom are under age 25) connected with the Rural Community Network (RUCONET) in Arusha, Tanzania, by training them to sew and manage their own businesses. Funds will pay for a skilled teacher and assistant to provide an advanced two-month course on menswear and embroidery and groom them to pass on their skills and knowledge. A digital camera will be used to photograph garments and teaching techniques.

title: Famine Preparedness -3000 Kenyan Girls/Families
description: Drought and the following famine has become devasting in Kenya over the past decade. 85% of our sponsored girls are Maasai who are traditionally pastorialists who do not farm. Their families have lost more than 70% of their livestock which is their primary source of food. Each sponsored girl will teach her family and community food preservation in preparation for famine.  We will teach food security through growing crops and food preservation - canning and drying fruits and vegtables

title: Safe Childbirth in Rural Tibet
description: Most women in Tibet give birth at home without access to emergency care or materials and training needed to prevent infection and hemorrhage. We have been working for 10 years in Eastern Tibet to provide a clinic, trained doctors and midwives, and community health educators who teach safe home birth messages, give out clean birthing kits and document birth outcomes. Our project will pay health workers' salaries for 1 year and help install solar electricity and heat in this rural clinic.

title: ONE BRICK AT A TIME - BUILD4DAKTARI
description: DAKTARI is a bush school and a wildlife orphanage. Our mission is to educate local underprivileged children to care for their environment. Because DAKTARI is developing, we need:  -To extend the office. We require more space to accommodate the volunteers who are working to develop our bush school and community projects.  -To build 2 ablution blocks, 1 for the children and another for our 8 dedicated local staff.  -To build 3 cement platforms on which to install tents that will house volunteers.

title: Hepatitis B Vaccination for Ghanaian Children
description: Chronic hepatitis B is a debilitating disease that affects >8% of Ghanaians. If left untreated it can lead to liver cancer, the country's highest source of cancer morbidity. While hepatitis B is easily transmissible - 50-100x more contagious than HIV - it can be prevented through a cheap and effective vaccine. Unfortunately, this solution is sorely underutilized in Ghana. This project aims to screen and vaccinate roughly 400 students at Nyanyano D. A. Government School.

title: Mushroom Farming for Rwandan Families
description: The Nyanya grandmothers, located in the Jabana Hills of Rwanda, currently have three agricultural projects: two pepper growing projects and one mushroom growing project. The Nyanya Project is interested in starting another mushroom project for multiple reasons. To date, selling mushrooms yields the highest income for the grandmothers. Furthermore, it will provide sustainable income and independence for our grandmothers while offering economical, nutritional, and practical benefits.

title: Komera Global Run
description:
The Komera Global Run is a global movement to run for girls' education and empowerment. It first started with a small fun run in rural Rwanda where we encouraged young women to find their confidence and voice through a girls only fun run.
Since then, it has grown into a global movement of people around the world taking action and running together to support the empowerment of young women.

title: Support 30 1st Generation Female Students of Color
description: The goal of the Art of Honoring Leadership Development College Mentoring Program is to empower women by providing students with the skills needed to successfully enter the workforce in Minnesota. The program works by connecting organizational female leaders with first generation female college students of color. The program runs for 8 months, consisting of monthly educational group sessions and one-on-one mentoring support. As a result, about 75% of participants find a job or paid internship.

title: Help Save Kittens, Puppies & Pregnant Moms
description: During kitten and puppy season, PetConnect Rescue responds to desperate shelter pleas to save kittens, puppies and pregnant moms who are at high-risk for euthanasia. Some may require special care, such as bottle-feeding. We see that they are properly vetted, including prenatal care, exams, vaccinations and deworming. All will eventually be adopted into loving homes. We help decrease pet-overpopulation by ensuring that every adopted animal is spayed or neutered to prevent future unwanted litters.

title: Expanding Climate-Positive Sanitation in Haiti
description: Since 2006, SOIL has been expanding access to safe, affordable, and restorative sanitation services in some of Haiti's most vulnerable communities. By producing organic, agriculture-grade compost from safely-treated human waste, SOIL is transforming a devastating public health crisis into a climate-positive solution for a more resilient future.

title: Uplift Jamaican Schoolchildren Through Science
description: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) drives economic success, yet the poorest and most socially disadvantaged Jamaican children avoid or perform poorly in the sciences. Their communities show little appreciation for STEM and under-resourced schools are ill equipped for constructive, engaging science teaching. Help us to correct this stifling inequity by exciting children with science and igniting them to apply reasoning and analytical skills to resolve everyday challenges.

title: Educate slum child in Kenya
description: Non formal schools in the slums of Nairobi face formidable challenges with lack of teaching staff and learning materials. We are working with 8 non-formal schools in Ruaraka, Nairobi which suffer from a severe shortage of teachers (with a teacher to student ratio of 1:40) and also a shortage of reading materials. With your donation, our team of 15 volunteers are teaching and carrying out targeted mentorship for the children in these schools.

title: Help Lithuanian Kids in their Battle with Cancer
description: This project will provide care to children with cancer in the two major hospitals in Lithuania. Medical, psychological, financial, and palliative support will be provided to the children and thier families.

title: One time food for 10 children in Mugular hostel
description:
Vidyanikethan Mugulur hostel for orphans consist of 10 children, who are being rehabilitated at the school through non-formal education and raising awareness of the child rights issues. The school also accommodates for life skills and encourages their participation in sports and extra curricular activities. They are provided with healthy and nutritious meals three times daily. 

The funding which is sanctioned by the department is insufficient for the proposed running of the hostel.

title: Send our girls to school in Tanzania
description: An African proverb says, "If we educate a boy, we educate one person. If we educate a girl, we educate a family - and a whole nation." Thanks to education of girls, the community as a whole can benefit from a strengthened socio-economic position of its female population and from local development. The project intention is to give a chance to girls who are living far away from the school.

title: HIV care to 5000 unattended children in Cameroon
description: This project will search and test 5000 children of HIV infected parents registered in three HIV clinics located in two regions of Cameroon and enrol positive cases in HIV care and treatment.

title: Free Summer Academy for 600 Bulgarian Children
description: The Academy aims to provide free summer education to children from low income communities in Sofia. The goal is to help children with less opportunities compensate their academic deficiencies during the summer. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we will also pay special attention to consolidating the knowledge acquired during distance learning. Your support will cover all costs related to the organization and execution of the Academy - food, training materials, transportation for the kids etc.

title: Help Victims of Turkey Mine Disaster
description: We are deeply saddened by the tragedy in Soma, Manisa that happened on May 13. Our thoughts are with the families, friends of the miners and everyone impacted by the disaster.   We created the "Soma Disaster Relief Fund". 100% of donations TPF receives will go to the victims of the accident through our local NGO partners.

title: Tackling "breast ironing" in Loum, Cameroon
description: Estelle (12) is happy, cared for by a mother who has fought against the mutilation of her daughter's breasts. She is one of the lucky ones. 1 in 4 girls in Cameroon are affected by breast ironing, a form of female mutilation inflicted on young girls, often by older female relatives. They apply hot stones to the girls' breasts to reduce their sexual activity. This project will campaign to raise awareness, educate girls and their families and offer psychological support to those already affected.

title: Help Revolutionize Education For Peruvian Children
description: We believe in the power of education and trust the potential of all Peruvians. We want a country where every student has the opportunity to realize their purpose and achieve their dreams. To do this, we work daily inspired by our dream,  that is to achieve that by 2032, at least 8 out of 10 children and young people receive an education of excellence.

title: Support Sustainable Agriculture in Haiti
description: Haiti is one of the most food-insecure countries in the world, in large part due to soil infertility and erosion that impede farming. SOIL is researching the use of compost that is generated through its ecological sanitation projects. This knowledge will enable farmers to improve the soil and raise crops that are healthier, can better sustain drought, and yield larger harvests.

title: Regenerating Fish Harvests in Cambodian Villages
description: Working with Santey Village in Northern Cambodia, Trailblazers Cambodia Organization (TCO) will assist in the construction and management of Community Fish Refuges (CFR)--a revolutionary new method of boosting fish populations against severe drought, desertification, and climate change. In Santey Village, 1,000 Villagers rely on fish harvests for nutrition, employment, and income. They will be trained  to manage CFRs, ensuring their rightful return to both self-sufficiency and sustainability.

title: Education for Underprivileged Indian Girls
description: In Indian society girls are often denied chances for personal growth and education, creating a variety of lifelong struggles.  The Janani Home offsets this gender discrimination by creating a safe and structured environment for underprivileged girls to pursue their studies and particular interests.  We want to remove limitations, and provide opportunities for these girls to reach their highest potential.  The Home currently serves 11 girls, but we hope to expand as support increases.

title: Help save 3,000 lives in Pakistan
description: Several ambulance services operate in Karachi, Pakistan, however, the missing link is the presence of trained medical personnel, equipment and life-saving medicines. Aman Ambulance, the only life-saving ambulances on the streets of Karachi have to-date, made more than 955,000 emergency interventions. We are committed to transforming lives of the underprivileged in our country, who are often denied their basic right to healthcare. Your support can help us enlarge this impact and save more lives!

title: Creating self employment for Poor Women in Kom
description: BERUDA will supply training in the raising, care, and business of chicken production for impoverished women of the Kom community, located in the Boyo division of Cameroon. This project aims to help widows and uneducated women with few options to generate income. We will provide chickens and the necessary equipment as start-up capital for their self-employed chicken business. This is a sustainable way of generating income for themselves and the family's they are trying desperately to support.

title: Autistic children's aid
description: Children from autistic spectrum will receive professional treatment according to their individual abilities, enabling them to better integration in the social environment and improve their quality of life.

title: Educate 648 pupils affected by Floods in Zimbabwe
description: PENYA plans to help 648 children, whose lives were devastated by floods in Zimbabwe, to attend school by providing them with educational materials such as books and stationery, uniforms as well as help to build 7 classroom blocks for a primary school.

title: Turning the Tide on Academic Achievment 4 all kids
description: Our Turning the Tide cutting edge program of early childhood education based on scientific evidence of early brain development.is exciting. We use the research on how poverty affects the brain/body of children and are addressing that issue with parents and educators. A critical element of our program  is parental empowerment and involvement. Our digital divide program with our learning software is a precedent for a new possibility, for childrren. We trained over 500 youth in non protfit work!

title: BE THE LIGHT FOR SOMA CHILDREN
description: Help Soma Children rise from the ashes of tragedy to a hopeful tomorrow!  Join us under "Bridge to Turkiye Fund" to support the children impacted by the recent mining tragedy in Soma, Turkey. As an organization dedicated to the empowerment of underserved children through education, we feel at this time that it is our responsibility to support the sons and daughters of the perished Soma miners. With your support, we will create an education fund for the children who lost parents in the mines.

title: Build a School in Senegal!
description: This project will build a junior high school to educate 250 students in the town of Mbouma, Senegal where there is currently no local option beyond primary school leaving those in this poor, rural area of Senegal with very limited prospects of a better life.

title: Provide a new school building for mountain village
description: We plan to build a new school building for Sichuan Xinyang Daji Elementary School. Students there are in desperate need for new school building, restroom and play ground. CTEF has investigated and approved the project after through investigation.

title: Send a Child to School in 2022
description: Your support will give 300 children the opportunity to learn, empower, gain self-esteem, and have a future they wouldn't otherwise have. Our goal is to ensure these children have uniforms, shoes, backpacks, books, pencils, paper, tuition, transportation, and tutors to help them succeed.

title: Provide shelter to abused women and kids in Kenya
description: Domestic violence in Muranga, Kenya is rampant.  We often take for granted the simple feeling of knowing that we are safe and secure.  This is not the case for many in Muranga.  To provide a safe haven for women and children who escape violence is our goal.  OFTENCH intends to provide a shelter that will provide all their basic needs.  This shelter will also provide life skills training, counselling, scholarships, micro financing, sports facilities, public education on DV and child abuse.

title: Funding needed to feed 300 children and 200 elders
description: We can end extreme poverty in our life time, if we promote economic growth that includes everyone, invest in people, and protect opportunities for future generations. By working together, we can build a prosperous world. Social protection not only pays off for individuals whose lives are improved, we now know that it contributes directly to economic growth and greater stability. So donations would help us greatly toward the implementation of our programs.

title: Set kids free from trauma of sexual/physical abuse
description: Children don't have words to say what horrible abuses have happened to them, and are told NOT to tell by abusers! We use play therapy to give them a voice, so they can SHOW counselors what happened and heal! Each dollar ensures another $16 continue to flow, so we can provide up to 6.5 months of FREE counseling to each victim to help them heal from heinous crimes! We must raise $155,000 every year & still need $37,000 for 2015-16! Anything raised over this amount will go toward next year's match.

title: Support for Children in Flooded Areas of Serbia
description: The heaviest rains and  floods recorded in 120 years have struck the people in Serbia, leaving thousands of children homeless, without food, water, warm and dry clothes. This project will provide immediate relief and development assistance to the children and their families. The assistance will help about 1000 children and youth get the essentials to continue education and  rebuild their lives. It will also support their parents to concentrate on repairing the houses and businesses.

title: Help 20 kids in rural Angola receive an education
description: Every child should have the chance to go to school, to learn to read and write. 4 million children in Angola do not have access to primary education. RISE builds primary schools in rural Angola to educate children, empower communities and contribute to the rebuilding of the country.

title: Resettle 150 widows and single mothers of Katsiru
description: After 20 years of devastating civil war, the project will help 150 widows and single mothers returning in their origin villages of Katsiru, North-Kivu province, Eastern of Congo to launch corn agricultural activities for sovereignty food and income-generating allowing their families get again access to basic needs like food, education and medical care. This marginalized group, most of them victims of raping, will regain confidence by piloting the vulgarization of corn seeds in their community.

title: Train 120 Health & Human Rights promoters in Kenya
description: HFAW will work with the 30 new graduates in health and human rights to train 120 new promoters in 4 locations, in Nyamira. The new tots will use transformative strategies based on popular education which has been highly effective in Chile (via EPES Foundation) changing the lives of poor women and will focuses on reproductive health and human rights as critical step to break the epidemic discrimination against women. HFAW has produced highly motivated women (&men) ready to scale up the methods.

title: Tailoring Training for 50 Muslim Women in India
description: This project will directly benefit 50 Muslim women in Lucknow, India by teaching them basic tailoring and embroidery skills. Women will also learn design skills, and how to promote and market their manufactured garments. These new professional skills will enhance their employability and capacity to earn more income. Bottom line: the success of the women results in their daughters being educated and wives being respected by their in-laws.

title: Technical Education to needy & deprived community
description: To educate the ignored and deprived community by giving them technical education, To reduce the unemployment in the area, The unemployment and poverty leading targeted community towards illegal activities like (Terrorism, Prostitutes, Drug using and suicides). The aim of the proposed activity is to reduce the illegal activities and let them the values of their lives

title: classes construction for 100 children of the MARA.
description:
MWEGO aims at constructing two classrooms for the children. These two classrooms will host
fifty children each hence a total of 100 children. Construction materials will include ballast,
MWEGO classrooms construction project in Kijirjir primary school.
5 cement, stones, and timber and iron sheets for roofing. Construction will begin immediately all
materials and funds are acquired. The beneficiary community will provide unskilled labour while
MWEGO organization will provide skilled labour.

title: Make 1,000 Poor Filipino Kids Eat Healthy Meals
description: 5 out of 10 Filipino kids are suffering from malnutrition. Nationwide, more than 3 million of them are suffering from this health problem. To 1,000 malnourished Filipino kids aged 5 to 10 years old from Imus, Rosario, Noveleta, Trece Martires in Cavite, Aral Pinoy and The Appledrive Project will provide FREE apples, healthy and nutritionally balanced meals and vitamins, and their parents will be given hands-on training on urban container gardening (UCG) to grow their own healthy vegetables.

title: Typhoon Haiyan Communal Hand-wash for Schools
description: When Super-typhoon Haiyan struck, it destroyed most water systems in more than 3,000 schools in its path. Water for hygiene and hand-washing is badly needed. Our project will install low-cost, robust, steel pipe communal hand-wash stations in Leyte and Samar Provinces with the goal of providing safe hygiene for school-children. We aim to produce and install a total of 500 hand-wash by the first month of classes in June 2014.

title: Increase access to safe water for the vulnerable
description:
This  project is aimed at increasing access to safe water, improve hygiene, reduce disease burden, and improve economic well-being among vulnerable communities of central Uganda. These communities include orphanage homes, homes of the elderly, single mother households and homes of people living with HIV & AIDS.

The project will include the installation of water tanks to harvest rain water in these different vulnerable communities and  training them in rain water harvest .

title: HIV Care for 5000 children/caregivers in Swaziland
description: Access to HIV health care in Swaziland is primarily a function of proximity to facilities and ability to pay for transport to reach them. With the highest HIV infection rate in the world, Swaziland struggles just to provide basic care. This project pushes HIV health services down to the local community level and reduces the financial burden on an already impoverished population to access these services.  Children and caregivers are the direct beneficiary to quality and compassionate HIV care.

title: Save Elephant Calves from Drowning in Unused Wells
description: The villagers of Chota Changru, Bara Changru, and Bantha Reladih in Jharkhand in Eastern India are farmers and use wells to irrigate their fields. Once their use is over, the wells are abandoned. With no fencing around them and the mouth almost hidden by tall weeds, these wells quickly turn into deathtraps for elephant herds crossing the area. In the past two years, five elephant calves have fallen into these wells. Of these, three were rescued in time, but two were not so lucky and drowned.

title: Save Hewar Alternative Arab School in Israel!
description: Hewar (Arabic for 'dialogue') is a community initiative, run by a group of parents in Haifa who decided to create an educational alternative for Arab children in Israel. After a long struggle, the officially registered school and kindergarten today serve 173 children from age 3 to 8th grade. However, Hewar is the only school in Israel forced to operate without any government funds and is thus under immense financial strain, as it relies solely on parents and community support to cover its costs.

title: Philippine Agricultural Economic Restoration
description: Typhoon Yolanda has stripped away the economic source of countless hill farmers in the Philippines. IsraAID's Agricultural and economic Long term restoration project will provide on going training, and physical support to rehabilitate this long term economic source that has been destroyed. IsraAID will establish a program whereby farmers will receive training, technology, equipment, and on going support through expert agronomists so that agriculture can once more sustain local population.

title: Education for 50 poor children in Kyrgyzstan
description: This project will restore 50 children from poorest families in Issyk-Kul region to school with our support. We will buy stationery, appropriate clothing such as uniform and shoes for these children. Also we provide these children with hygienic supplies such as toothpaste, toothbrush and hygiene kits for girls

title: Improve 100 Girls Education with Tutoring Program
description: This project enables 7th and 8th grade girls in Bankondji and a nearby village to develop the ability to understand texts in reading comprehension, math and other subjects, so they can successfully pass the exam needed to enroll in any high school in Cameroon. The 100 girls in the peer-to-peer tutoring projects are very engaged in the program and committed to their personal success. The project also provides scholarships to its graduates, so they can attend day high schools.

title: Sports to Empower 500+ Refugee Girls in Jordan
description: We use sports as a vehicle of empowerment for refugee girls & local women in Jordan. In a region where gender inequality is still the norm, sport is another privilege reserved for boys. RC hosts after-school leagues for young girls to gain the life-skills, confidence, hope and ambition that comes from team games. We also train and hire local young women as coaches, providing valuable income for their families and showing communities that female empowerment leads to positive changes for everyone.

title: Donate a Health-Center to the Philippines
description: Typhoons strike the Philippines every year. Supertyphoon Haiyan, locally known as Yolanda, destroyed the village of San Francisco in the Camotes Islands (Cebu). Healthcare is expensive and the closest hospital is 3-5hs away from the village. Kito delivered 1 Mobile Unit for emergencies (Kito-Health) to San Fernando and now aims to ship another one to San Francisco for long-lasting medical assistance to the population during the recovery. We only need $13.6k (1/5 of $68k) to complete the project!

title: FLOOD RELIEF APPEAL FOR SERBIA
description: Serbia has just been struck (May 2014) with a huge natural disaster, caused by heavy rain and overflowing rivers. The worst floods in the Balkans for decades left more than 35 dead and forced over 30,000 people to evacuate from the affected areas. Many towns and villages are completely cut off and emergency services are working around the clock to rescue people.

title: Save children life and the community
description: Disease prevention is key to public health. It is always better to prevent a disease than to treat it. Vaccines can protect both the people who receive them and those with whom they contact.

title: Bring the Arts to 240 Youth in Rural Ecuador
description: For seven consecutive years "Corporacion Humor y Vida" has brought the project "Tour around the Equator for a Culture of Peace" to the Colombian- Ecuadorian border.  Over 13,000 children, youth, adults and community leaders have learned dance, theater and other forms of expression in zones affected displacement and armed conflict from Colombia.

title: Stress reduction in 2 high-need classrooms in RI
description: ResilientKids teaches mindfulness and yoga strategies to students and their teachers to reduce stress, and increase focus, self-confidence and empathy. In high-need, high-poverty districts where toxic stress is prevalent, integrating this type of learning is essential to keeping kids in school, reducing teacher burn-out, bullying, other violence, and discipline referrals. Please help us to expand the program to 2 additional classrooms which will reach 56 additional schoolchildren and 2 teachers.

title: Humanitarian Assistance Through Prosthetics
description: IMAHelps has discovered many young people in the region of Zacatecoluca, El Salvador whom are missing limbs due to accidents which have occurred through accidental machete strikes while farming. Many others have lost their limbs during vehicle accidents and/or being struck by vehicles. IMAhelps is bringing a team of prosthetic specialists to create limbs for those who truly need them. Please consider partnering with us through our effort of making these people whole again.

title: Ounce of Prevention
description: Please consider partnering with ICEC (The Intervention Center for Early Childhood) to provide infants & toddlers with special needs the opportunity to achieve their optimum developmental potential and provide their parent's with the skills and resources to ensure their child a successful transition into preschool. Your donation will help us provide crucial early intervention services to more than 300 children per week and over 1,000 children each year in Southern California.

title: Protect a village of 155 households from erosion
description: 155 households live in Gatebe 2  village  in Rwanda, situated at the bottom of a hill . Due to heavy rain and unsustainable practices the community is hit by erosion and land degradation, threatening their subsistence farming livelihoods. Rwanda Development Organisation (RDO) plans to combat this situation by restoring the landscape by planting trees and improving drainage, and by sensitising the community about sustainable practices, including the distribution of 50 goats for organic manure.

title: Encouraging HR defenders in monitoring ESC rights
description: Donors should care about this project as it develops a grass root level mechanism in the community from the marginalized who will be developed as the monitors to monitor the rights situation of their community.At the National level it will impact on the development of a new strategy for safeguarding the fundamental rights of the people. Capacity of the community (marginalized) increased with intervention of this project and people will raise voices for their rights and violation of Human rights.

title: Supporting Higher Education for students in Ghana!
description: NAPE Foundation provides scholarships to students attending Palm Institute of Strategic Leadership. PISL is an organization committed to providing students in Ghana with the Leadership skills necessary to be successful in the business world, as well as provide them with the ethics and morals needed to be the next generation of leaders for Ghana and all of Africa.

title: Support 100 at-risk youth to and through college
description: This project will provide one year of academic and enrichment support for 100 low-income youth in Boulder County. Students will receive literacy and math assistance, cultural enrichment opportunities, college and career preparation activities, and a college scholarship. Our organization works with cohorts of 50 to 80 youth for 10+ years, from second grade to and through college. Your support empowers these youth and provides educational support needed to become successful adults.

title: Reach-3068-Nigerians-with-HIV-prevention-services
description: This project will contribute to the reduction of new HIV infections amongst 2520 youths, provide care and support for 400 Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVCs) and 100 People Living with HIV/AIDS, training of 48 community health workers and traditional births attendants in Rivers State of Nigeria. Presently the State has the highest HIV prevalence rate of 15.2% in Nigeria as announced by the Minister of Health during 2013 World AIDS day celebration.

title: Empower 50 Computer Illiterates in Val de Marne
description: This project equips a computer training center in priority zone of Val de Marne, providing FREE computer training in hardware and software applications to 50 disadvantaged computer illiterate youth and adults. Computer proficiency being indispensable for most job seekers, this would enable them acquire relevant knowledge and skills that would help them get a job, become productive and self-reliant, this would as a result enable them to contribute towards national development.

title: Train 25 At-risk Youth in Digital Business in DC
description: At-risk youth and young adults in the District of Columbia need 21st Century technology skills, along with community engagement strategies.  Our tax-exempt organization, Multi-Media Training Institute (MMTI) trains at-risk young people in Digital Media and Business with the goal of developing a team of Digital Entrepreneurs.  They will target small community-based businesses and create their digital footprint in the market place as a way to engage customers, patients, or clients.

title: Nutrition Support to 500 Children in Thar Desert
description: This project will provide energy biscuits, food ration and livelihood support for 500 acute malnourished children from Thar Desert where 93% of the households have zero buying power to buy anything to cook as per baseline assessments.

title: Help save 3000 underprivileged Mothers & Children
description: Provide basic health amenities, nutrition and psychological services for 3000 disadvantaged mothers and children in Dhanyala Pakistan, who can not afford these services otherwise. Help in training and empowering local women to provide professional healthcare services to mothers and children.

title: RESTORE HOPE TO 500 UGANDAN ORPHANS  (6-24 YEARS)
description: Eco-Agric Uganda plans to provide education, scholastic materials, improve nutrition and income to 500 orphans and their care givers in remote western Uganda.  The project will provide scholastic materials, pay school fees, give out beans and maize seeds for planting plus chicken to 500 orphans and vulnerable children aged 6-24 years. 300 f the orphans and vulnerable children will be females while 200 will be males

title: Feed and educate 3,500 children in rural Vietnam
description: Support the futures of the youngest and most vulnerable in Vietnam by funding healthy meals and educational scholarships for kids. PeaceTrees Vietnam has removed more than 110,000 bombs from the land to provide safety to children in Quang Tri and has built schools and libraries on the safely cleared land. The 11 libraries, 15 kindergartens, and mine risk education center we've helped construct bring education and literacy to more than 3,500 children each year and need your help to stay open.

title: Empower Students for success in STEAM careers
description: We provide free attendance to our experiential learning conference for students ages 13-18 that are eligible for free lunch through their schools.  These students will be able to participate for free as a result of your donations.  Each student will receive a tablet device with admission to the conference where they learn about career opportunities in STEAM and 21st century workforce skills.  These students remain within our online community to continue learning past the conference.

title: Empower 25 women waste collectors in Bolivia
description: The project will empower 25 women waste collectors and their families to improve their quality of life and their work conditions in Cochabamba, Bolivia. It will provide them with waste collector carts, a motorcycle cart, personal protection equipment, important work contacts and 180 educational workshops in: organization, health, hygiene, recycling and fabrication of crafts. These tools will allow them to optimize their work and consolidate a Recycling Waste Collectors and Artisans Association

title: Empower Girls to Prevent Gender Based Violence.
description: This project will empower 1500 Tanzanian girls to combat gender based violence (GBV) as the severe problem they face in their daily life. The girls will be equipped with brilliant skills and techniques on fighting against GBV includes economic skills. Also they will be enabled to understand their rights hence build self esteem and makes their own decisions towards living in GBV free zone whereas they will thrive and participate effectively to foster development in their respective families.

title: Give A New Smile to 20 Children in Uraba, Colombia
description: A child born with cleft palate misses out on more than a brilliant smile. They miss out on a life free of financial, emotional, and physical burdens related to this disability. Our goal for "Give A New Smile to 20 Children in Uraba" is to sponsor the entire treatment process for the 20 children ages 1 to 5 in Uraba suffering from cleft palate. Your donation helps to provide free reconstructive surgeries, speech therapy, and emotional counseling to support these children and their families.

title: Pathari Village Project for Indian farmers
description: A farmer in India commits suicide every 41 minutes. You can make a difference. We plan to repair canal in Pathari village of Vidarbha, Maharashtra, India, that connects to reservoir in coming months which will allow village of 1300 people harvest second crop,create small business opportunities for youth of the village and help  about 400+ livestock in the village.

title: HELP AFAR - HELP MORE - ANIMALS SMILE!
description:
There are no companion animal sanctuaries anywhere in Mid Michigan. Further, thousands of companion animals are euthanized daily, especially elderly and special needs animals.

Opening the AFAR No-Kill Companion Animal Sanctuary will solve this dilemma. Additionally, specializing in special needs and elderly animals, there will be a place for these otherwise unwanted animals to live out their natural lives here rather then being euthanized, thus lowering the overall euthanasia rate in Michigan

title: Brincando de Bola - Protect 750 Brazilian children
description: Help to protect 750 children of Sao Paulo, Brazil. The Fundacao Cafu institute ensures that children from 3 to 17 years old are protected from the social hazards of a region with no support from the public policies. Keep the children away from drugs and criminal activities through the practice of sports like soccer, basketball and volleyball and cultural activities like music, painting, singing and dancing.

title: Primary and Secondary Education in rural Pakistan
description: Your donations will help to cover the construction of Al-Sohail Model School (primary and secondary level school).  The building will consist of 5 well-furnished class rooms along with a veranda.
