description: Only 56% of the children in India get full immunization. For 1 in every 20 children in India, the 1st birthday might never happen.   To address the problem, CRY is focusing on ensuring complete immunizations for 42,430 children between the ages of 0 - 12 months in 3500 villages across India, during the month of July and August, by 1. Providing access to life saving immunization to the children in 3500 villages  2. Ensuring well equipped health centers and early childhood care centers

title: Help Syrian Refugees Heal in Gaza
description: Syrian refugees in Gaza, worried about family left behind, asked not to show their faces. 154 families sought refuge in Gaza when their homes in Syria were destroyed. They walked across to Lebanon, flew to Egypt, crossed to the Gaza Strip seeking specialized medical care, food, and jobs but now Gaza's economy is collapsing due to 12 years of blockade and the US cut of all aid. Please help these families get back on their feet with a 3-month job placement program and restorative medical care.

title: Donate a Health-Center to the Philippines
description: Typhoons strike the Philippines every year. Supertyphoon Haiyan, locally known as Yolanda, destroyed the village of San Francisco in the Camotes Islands (Cebu). Healthcare is expensive and the closest hospital is 3-5hs away from the village. Kito delivered 1 Mobile Unit for emergencies (Kito-Health) to San Fernando and now aims to ship another one to San Francisco for long-lasting medical assistance to the population during the recovery. We only need $13.6k (1/5 of $68k) to complete the project!

title: Empower 4,000 Adolescents in Violence Prevention
description: This nation-wide public awareness campaign "A Deal for Ideal Interactions" brings together over 4,000 Uruguayan adolescents and empowers them through violence prevention training to advocate for their rights.  Adolescent promoters learn how to identify abuse in their homes, schools and communities, and receive tools to actively promote the rights of children and adolescents through leadership.

title: Empower Women and Children in Pakistan
description: We are planning for the reopening of the Nagina Sewing Center to teach sewing skills to underprivileged women and to provide more School Supplies to impoverished kids through our EDUCATION FOR ALL Campaign. Through these projects many women and kids will be empowered to improve their situation and rise above poverty and fear of their future.

title: School Scholarships for Vulnerable Youth
description: Children's Voice (CV) provides high school and elementary school scholarships for youth and vocational training for uneducated teenagers in eastern DRC. During this period of economic hardship secondary to covid-19, this project will allow CV to keep providing scholarships.

title: Support 1 Year Children Education With $11
description: Indigenous people in North East India live under $1 a day! With no access to information, formal education, children roam the forest or are exposed to various manipulations and exploitation. Out of school children are trafficked and sold like commodities. More than 200 children were rescued in 2013 alone from individual and organizations in the pretext of giving them education or job! This project "Hold a Child" will sent indigenous children to school.

title: Improve children and teen life quality in Colombia
description: COLOMBIANITOS seeks to strengthen the program "Goals for a Better Life" in Bucaramanga, which have been developing sports activities like soccer, cheerleading, rugby, basketball, volleyball, music, singing, and school support activities including recreational activities, all with the objective of improve the children and teen quality life by providing opportunities for personal growth and showing that they have another opportunity to be happy and successful.

title: HELP AFAR - HELP MORE - ANIMALS SMILE!
description: There are no companion animal sanctuaries anywhere in Mid Michigan. Further, thousands of companion animals are euthanized daily, especially elderly and special needs animals.  Opening the AFAR No-Kill Companion Animal Sanctuary will solve this dilemma. Additionally, specializing in special needs and elderly animals, there will be a place for these otherwise unwanted animals to live out their natural lives here rather then being euthanized, thus lowering the overall euthanasia rate in Michigan

title: JOB SKILLS FOR 30 DISABLED YOUNG BULGARIAN PEOPLE
description: JOB SKILLS FOR 30 INTELLECTUALLY DISABLED YOUNG PEOPLE in Bulgaria is a program supporting people with intellectual disabilities to achieve their full potential by providing access to high-quality services, developmental training and possibilities for gainful employment that are suited to their needs. The project aims to help people with disabilities to enter the real world of work by focusing on individual abilities and by providing varying levels of training and individualized support.

title: Education for Afghans through Radio/TV
description: We have combined projects Radio Meraj and TV Meraj! The Afghan Institute of Learning provides education to Afghans but some people live too far from an AIL Learning Center or do not feel safe to travel. Reaching these people with education through broadcast media is an effective means and a popular solution. Radio Meraj has been going since 2015 providing educational programs and TV Meraj will soon start broadcasting. Both stations are housed in AIL's Herat office building.

title: America's Unofficial Ambassadors
description: America's Unofficial Ambassadors is a citizen diplomacy initiative, which builds mutual understanding and enhances people-to-people partnerships between America and the Muslim World. Through our Summer Service Internships, young people have the opportunity to serve as unofficial ambassadors and to teach in schools or volunteer in NGOs in Morocco, Indonesia, Tajikistan, and Tanzania. When they return home, they give presentations in their communities about their service.

title: Accessibility for All!
description: We offer a decent and cheap solution to the lack of accessible transportation which is a motorcycle drove by hands for wheelchair users. We also offer to remodel the wheelchair users' homes or schools with a steel ramp or making adjustments to their bathrooms to be accessible.

title: Fund 10 Cambodian graduates to educate rural youth
description: Each year Youth Star recruits, trains and places Cambodian graduate volunteers into under-served rural provinces to assist in community development. In 2015 volunteers will promote the benefits of education, organise and conduct lessons, run youth clubs, provide health instruction and foster gender equality. The Youth Star model helps graduates develop their skills, encourages a culture of community self-reliance and raises awareness of the critical importance of education to future prospects.

title: Assisting the Most Vulnerable in Gaza
description: The escalating conflict in Gaza is causing a drastic deterioration of humanitarian conditions in the Gaza Strip. Your gift helps to provide food assistance, personal and home hygiene kits, shelter kits for homeless families, and psycho-social support for some of the 25,000 traumatized children in Gaza. Global Communities has worked continuously in Gaza for 20 years and works directly with beneficiaries to ensure that the most vulnerable receive the assistance they so greatly need.

title: Provide Theater to 2,500 In-Need New York Children
description: As part of our "Audience Project," Arts For All will tour a professional live children's show, "The Emperor's New Clothes," FREE OF CHARGE to 2,500 in-need children grades K-5 in the New York area.

title: Estudio Damgo III: A Filipino Design+Build Studio
description: The Senior Architecture students of Foundation University is now on its third course of shaping the lives of people through sustainable and eco-friendly architecture that is to be built on the water at Brgy. Bantayan, Dumaguete City. A sophisticated structure that floats, that is not just any other traditional structure made out of stilts or rigid structural elements fixed to the ground but a structure that floats and will rise on top of the water by only using native bamboo and recycled plastic

title: Save Abandoned Orphan Destitute Children in India
description: Bal Asha Trust saves children from one day to 12 years who are destitute and found abandoned children in life threatening conditions.  We provide these vulnerable children a safe home, give love, care, Nutrition,  Medical & Educational and Developmental support through our project.   Many of them are special needs that with HIV, Hep. B. Deaf, CP, Leprosy and other Physical and Medical disabilities.  Bal Asha Trust has become home for more than 1400 children.  We rehabilitate children in society.

title: Empowering 100 Returnees Women of Kibabi
description: Due to financial constraint, the improved potato seeds have not been generalized to the entire returnees women of Kibabi. This project aims to empower and secure women households in Kibabi on food security and economically by making women leaders in the context of vulgarization of improved potato seeds. While implementing also the program to preserve environment by fighting against erosion, 100 returnees women regrouped in 4 ILDs (Development Local Initiatives) will operate on 10 hectares.

title: Better Futures for Cambodian Children and Youth
description: M'Lop Tapang has been working with disadvantaged children, youth and families of Sihanoukville since 2003. We currently work with over 5000 children and 3000 families providing shelter, medical care, sports and arts, education and training, counseling, family support and protection from all types of abuse.

title: Help Ukrainian Premature Babies to live
description: The team of Ukrainian Charity Fund "Social Partnership" has a mission to help the National Children's Hospital "OKHMATDYT" (Kyiv/Ukraine), which is now sorely in need of equipment for nursing premature babies (born before time children):  - Breathing apparatus;  - Apparatus for infusion of fluids;  - Apparatus for nursing  Right now, in the hospital "OKHMATDYT" there are 9 premature babies weighting up to 1 kg, who need high-quality rehabilitation.

title: "Feed The Dream" (of a job offer for job seekers)
description: Feeding the dream means informing & preparing low-income youth & employment candidates to be infinitely more compelling to prospective employers who will more likely invite them for an interview & then make a job offer.  Economic development = good employment statistics.  Our project offers free employability workshops: Effective resumes, realistic career choices, social media & the job search, business communication, English grammar, candidates' rights and interviewing tips & techniques.

title: Emergency Aid for Children in Gaza
description: Children in Gaza are living under a devastating blockade. They lack basic essentials such as water, housing, hospitals and safe places to play and learn. MECA and The Big Ride are teaming up to raise funds for Gaza to help meet children's basic needs.

title: Making a Healthplan for Life for Haitian Children
description: We can affect long-term health outcomes in under-served communities by addressing the relationship between individuals and healthcare. We enable children to see education and healthcare as a right, regardless of finances and family status, by fostering ownership of well-being, and creating a welcoming place of comfort, safety and opportunity where children go to find a healthy future. Our focus on individual education & health allows us to address the often overlooked girls health needs as well.

title: Educate Deaf Children in Mexico
description: This school for special education will provide free quality education to deaf children from poor families in San Miguel de Allende and surrounding rural areas. Deaf children are marginalized and isolated in the public school system where no one is able to communicate with them through sign language and they have no chance of learning to read and write.

title: Disability & Inclusion:Training Colombian Teachers
description: Help us to train inclusive teachers who give children with Down syndrome and intellectual disabilities the opportunity to learn what they need to succeed in our community.

title: Cazuca Dreams On
description: The issue that "Cazuca Dreams On" aims to tackle is the culture of violence and marginalization that is internalized by Cazuca's residents and, more specifically, by Cazuca's children and youth. This project employs theater, dance and music as powerful tools of social cohesion, incentivizing changes in behavior, turning kids into dreamers and encouraging them to be main agents of social transformation

title: Increase Food Security in Western Lane County, OR
description: The goal of this project is to increase the open hours of Florence Food Share, an emergency food box pantry in Florence, Oregon.  In order to better fulfill our mission of alleviating hunger in Western Lane County, we need to expand our open pantry hours.

title: WeOwnTV: Idriss Kpange Filmmaker Fellowship
description: The WeOwnTV Filmmaker Fellowship is a regional film fund and professional development program supporting the production of independent documentaries directed by West African filmmakers living in the region. The program was founded in the wake of the West African Ebola outbreak. In 2022 we began raising funds for the inaugural Idriss Kpange Filmmaker Fellowship Award which will provide filmmakers with funding for their projects, creative labs, one-on-one mentoring, and professional development.

title: Hands on kisima children's center narok kenya
description: Kisima children center is established to care for children from need families like orphans, street children, and those who are at risk of sexual abuse, early marriages, FGM, and those affected by broken marriages. We are able to support more than 500 children in East Africa by providing shelter, food, clothing, school fees, and many other humanitarian assistances. Since we started supporting children, some have completed university studies and are now employed.

title: Basketball Clinic for 500 school kids in Nigeria
description: TIMEOUT 4 AFRICA will help the Minna community build partnerships with families, schools, and volunteers to help underprivileged children reach academic and athletic success. By providing school supplies and hosting basketball clinics and tournaments, children will be encouraged to become model citizens and stay in school.  Promoting a positive recreational outlet provides a platform which encourages youth to take charge of their future and become positive contributing members of society

title: KIDS Support Groups in Brazil
description: Children are vulnerable when their parents drink. KIDS Support Groups are a place where children, affected by their parents' substance abuse are welcomed and get otientiation as a strategy of prevention and assistance to people in circumstances of social vulnerability and hazard. Through targeted training of KIDS Group leaders/facilitators, the Blue Cross Brazil is expanding its successful program of Self Help to reach beyond the substance abusers and provide much needed care for family members.

title: Build A Women's Center for 150 Kenyan Grandmothers
description: *Building a Women's Center and Hostel in rural Kipsitet, Kenya, will provide a safe environment for 150 Kenyan Grandmothers to have a space for business trade training, enclosed kiosks to sell their handicrafts, meeting space for women's conferences, and overnight lodging. To have this Women's Center/Hostel built will be a dream come true for these women ages 54 to 88 years old who are raising orphan children.

title: Stop Ebola: What you can do
description: *See reports for most recent updates* In response to the ongoing Ebola epidemic, this project will train BRAC's all-female frontline force of 400 community health promoters to stop the spread of the virus in remote communities in Sierra Leone. These women, trained by BRAC, are known in their own communities and are going door to door, educating people on how to prevent Ebola and recognize symptoms. But they need funding to pay for flyers and leaflets, food and travel costs, and disinfectant.

title: Help Us Stop the Ebola Crisis in Sierra Leone
description: Health officials say the Ebola outbreak, centered in West Africa, is the deadliest ever with over 1,093 infected and almost 500 of those from Sierra Leone.  Greatest Goal Ministries operates a free outpatient hospital in Lakka.  The military has set up Ebola isolation tents directly outside the doors of our hospital.  This project will provide the desperately needed supplies and protective clothing for health care workers as well as support information materials needed for the community.

title: Support Liberian Family Health Care and Education
description: Many rural areas in Liberia lack healthcare, health ed., or literacy services. Without this Liberians don't know how to use preventative methods that decrease infant and maternal mortality and improve the quality of life. Each year IHI's Clinic serves over 15,000 people, and our literacy programs work with 200 women and our new "Liberian Women's Health Manual" will be used by local women to teach women and girls improved health, sanitation, nutrition and human rights practices. Please contribute

title: Help MSF Battle the Ebola Outbreak in West Africa
description: As the Ebola outbreak continues to spread, with 1,093 cases and 660 deaths now reported across west Africa, Doctors Without Borders/Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) is stepping up its response in the most affected areas.

title: Malaria Prevention Saves Lives
description: Malaria is the biggest killer of man. Every 2 minutes a child dies from malaria. Until there is a cure prevention is the only way to save lives.  The Butterfly Tree runs a successful malaria prevention program in remote communities in Zambia, providing mosquito nets, a safe insecticide coating for the inside of houses, and larvicide granules to prevent the larva from developing into mosquitos when placed in the breeding grounds. These interventions can save the lives of vulnerable children.

title: GlobalGiving Ebola Epidemic Relief Fund
description: From December 2013 to January 2016, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea experienced the most lethal Ebola outbreak on record. It was the first large-scale outbreak of the virus in the region and communities are still recovering from the epidemic.

title: Mental Health Outreach for Canadian Youth 14-24
description: Reach Out is an interactive Jeopardy-style game, which gets students into teams and challenges them to think about what they know and don't know about mental health issues and illnesses. The multi player game is delivered using a computer, data projector and speakers, and is embedded with music, videos and information about emotional health and mental well being. When we play Reach Out with young people, our aim is to initiate conversations about mental health, well being and help seeking.

title: Sponsor a Kenyan Child's Education
description: Action Two Africa's desire is very straight forward: we want to get kids off the streets and back into the classroom. Many children in Kenya are born into a cycle of poverty that perpetuates the broken system that they are a part of. Action Two Africa wants to help break this pattern and get  Bungoma's youth back into school. We plan to meet this need by providing school fees for children who would otherwise not be able to continue their education.

title: Healthy food for 300 visually challenged children
description: This project helps provide nutritious food to the visually challenged children from rural areas who are underweight and malnourished. Your timely support will help in providing healthy meals to 300 visually challenged children and aid in their healthy growth. Indian Association for the Blind (IAB) was established in 1985 by visually challenged activist Late Mr. S.M.A.Jinnah to provide education, employment and rehabilitation for the visually challenged, especially from rural backgrounds.

title: Shelter And Education For needy Kids In Bangalore
description: Our project (NELE) aims to provide education and shelter to 250 children in the age group of 8 to 15 years in Bangalore. Most of these kids are from poorest of the poor background where they are deprived of basic necessities of life not to mention about Education & health. Because of lack of amenities, they either run away or become rag pickers on the street doing all kind of odd jobs. If these kids are not taken care properly at right age they become vulnerable to all kinds of social evils.

title: Build a Library for Refugee Students in Uganda
description: CIYOTA students aim to acquire knowledge that will enable them to become change makers in the refugee camp and beyond its boundaries. They are determined to build their desired communities and live quality life. They own their journey towards prosperous communities in Africa. This is a fundraising page for the library at the hostel. Your contribution in supporting these students will change lives of thousands of other people that the students projects and initiatives will impact.

title: Give Children After-School Education in Knoxville
description: Provide a free after school program to 15 Hispanic low income children from Knoxville and surrounding areas to strengthen their skills in math and reading to successfully achieve academic goals.

title: Vehicle for healthcare in 100  villages in Uganda
description: This project will conduct community based Medical outreaches, to offer the following services to rural communities in Kabarole district western Uganda: HIV Counseling and testing, Cervical Cancer screening, Screening and treatment of other Sexually transmitted Diseases, Health education and ant HIV stigma campaigns using testimonies of people living with HIV both the children, youth and adults.

title: Provide Dental Care for 60,000 Bolivian Children!
description: The Smiles Forever Dental Hygiene clinic in Cochabamba, Bolivia provides free or at-cost dental care to thousands of children a year.  Over the past 22 years, an astounding 60,000 indigenous children have a better future beginning with dental health.  A key research project for Smiles Forever is in the nearby highlands zone where the latest in cavity prevention and dental treatment is given.  Bolivia still has Covid 19  restrictions for health professionals, so our teaching program is paused.

title: Empower Girls in India Through Sports
description: CREA's "It's My Body!" campaign will inform 200 adolescent girls in India about their sexual and reproductive health and rights through the medium of sports. Trainings in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh (UP), and Jharkhand will build the leadership capacities of these girls, enhancing their physical well-being, independence, and self-esteem. This project will ultimately embolden these young girls to affirm their sexual rights so as to address the issues of child marriage and son preference.

title: Girls' Anti-FGM Education Camps in Kenya, Africa
description: Pastoralist Child Foundation's annual holiday camps (April, August, December) will educate and empower 180 girls ages 11-15 with vital information needed to resist FGM and forced early marriages, and to adopt safe and peaceful Alternative Rites of Passage to womanhood. The curriculum also includes the importance of knowing about the female sexual reproductive system, HIV/AIDS, teen pregnancy, rape, resisting gender-based violence, as well as the importance of getting a formal education.

title: Sponsor A Girl Child
description: The project gives educational sponsorship to poor girls, providing educational opportunity to girls from socially and economically disadvantaged communities, to orphans, children of child labour, and  HIV/AIDS affected, aged between 1 to 18 years. Nutrition supplementary, school uniforms, text and note books, life skill training from 16 year onward. Along with curricular input provided to them and taking them on study tour.

title: Save Lives of 37500 Children in Tanzania
description: This project aims at reaching 37500 children underfive with Vitamin A supplementation and Albendazole for deworming in Tanzania. The country Demographic Indicator Survey of 2010 shows that 33% of Children and 37% of pregnant women have Vitamin A deficiency. Areas with Vitamin A deficiency are also endemic with soil-transmitted intestinal worms which contribute to child under nutrition. Vitamin A supplementation and Albendazole is a simple and cost efficient way to alleviate Vitamin A deficiency.

title: Disaster Relief in Okanogan County, Washington
description: This project will start the rehabilitation process for hundreds of devastated homeowners whose homes were destroyed in the Carlton Complex Fire that swept through Washington State in July 2014 - the largest in its history. IsraAID and its US partner Team Rubicon will engage in debris removal and the retrieval of personal belongings. This action, and its timing, are crucial to breaking the cycle of overwhelming devastating suffered by the homeowner, and minimizing the chances of long-term trauma.

title: Conservation Without Borders
description: Conservation Without Borders will use practical action to turn vulnerable Australian landscapes into places where wildlife and people can thrive.

title: Transform  lives of 300 Ugandan young mothers
description: This project will provide help 300 orphaned and vulnerable girls including young mothers aged 6-24 years in western Uganda improve their lives through improved agriculture, education and enhancing their care givers income. The 300 girls will get school uniforms and scholastic materials to attend school, get tuition to attend vocational studies, start up kits for entrepreneurship skills and agricultural inputs to do agriculture.

title: Help Expand Academic Levels (HEAL)- Kisumu.
description: In Kenya the adoption of Free Primary Education by the government in 2003, education related problems still persist approximately one million school going age children are out of school. This is due to numerous hidden costs such as school uniforms expenses, enrolment fees, examination fees, stationery and library expenses, development levies, tuition levies and auxiliary staff wages and salaries. This has not made it easier especially for children who have lost one of both parents due to HIV.

title: Protect Unique Ecosystems in the Gulf of Honduras
description: Marine and coastal ecosystems in Belize and Guatemala support some of the greatest biodiversity on Earth. They also ensure livelihoods to local communities that rely on fishing, forestry, and tourism. However, these ecosystems are threatened by climate change and human behaviors. We train conservation leaders and educators to use arts-based tools to more effectively lead initiatives, encourage sustainable behaviors and engage communities in overcoming these challenges.

title: Equip Liberians to End Ebola
description: Liberia suffered the worst outbreak of Ebola in recorded history. Accurate information is one of the primary ways to slow and ultimately stop the spread of this horrible disease.  Donate now and help us continue to support grassroots organizations to mobilize, educate and bring accurate information into their communities to prevent the further spread of the Ebola Virus. Local communities have been the first responders so let's continue to help them keep their communities safe by supporting them!

title: Info Saves Lives: Ebola Outbreak in West Africa
description: The deadly Ebola outbreak in West Africa - the worst in recorded history - has so far claimed more than 7,800 lives. At Internews, we believe that during a public health emergency like this one, people need quick, free and reliable information about the disease and how to prevent it. Please help us to ensure that communities at risk, and especially those living in remote rural areas, get the right information now: how to identify early symptoms, prevent transmission, what to do and where to go.

title: Help Children Access Skin Treatment!
description: Children suffering from skin diseases and psoriasis fail to achieve their dreams due to Discrimination, Stigmatization, Hopelessness and Pain. Africa Psoriasis Organization facilitates free health camps to help these children access proper diagnosis and treatment and disseminate skin diseases and psoriasis education in schools.

title: Crisis Relief Fund for South Sudan
description: South Sudan is currently declared a "LEVEL 3" humanitarian emergency by the United Nations, only second to Syria in the world most terrible humanitarian catastrophe. Seven out of ten states are badly affected by conflict, famine and mass displacements. This is the first large-scale manmade & natural humanitarian crisis ever experience since independence of South Sudan from Sudan in 2011. With this funding, communities' resilience will be facilitated, enabling women and girls to have better life

title: FoodSecurity for 523 malnourished children,Eritrea
description: In the past five years the Sisters of the Daughters of St.Anne Institute (DSA) saved 1900 children from severe malnutrition. DSA decided to concentrate their efforts in Abo,Zagher,Akrur,Tokonda. 523 children are affected and for up to nine months they will be given milk, oil and DMK, a food supplement. The Sisters will give to their families some sheep, on completion of the treatment, when they will be released after having reached 86.5% of the standard index of malnutrition, to get daily milk.

title: ACTS 2 Comunity outreach hiv testing and treatment
description: The HIV and AIDS pandemic has ravaged Swaziland over the past two decades. The impact has been felt by all sectors of the society regardless of literacy levels, religious beliefs, and economic status. Acts 11 Clinic provides outreach into the communities of infected individuals by providing medications,HIV testing, education and training for local resources and provides for local centers for on-going care.

title: Responding to the Ebola Outbreak in West Africa
description: International Medical Corps is currently in Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali and Sierra Leone, and is one of a handful of international NGOs that is treating Ebola patients in West Africa. The WHO has reported over 27,500 cases and 11,200 deaths across West Africa. We are committed to getting to zero cases, and to rebuilding and strengthening the local and regional health systems; engaging community members in recovery through outreach and education programs; and bolstering preparedness.

title: Help to Educate the Disadvantaged Children
description: The destitute individuals which include Orphans, Victims of HIV/AIDS, Children affected with Albinism, Victims of Abuse, Domesticated Women and Girls, and the Disabled living with extreme poverty in rural areas will be send to school, provided with living grants, given school materials, and provided with education funds from primary level to tertiary level until they achieve professional qualifications.

title: SCHOOL FILTER PROJECT - 2706 children in INDIA
description: We are working for the downtrodden community. The women and children are more vulnerable. The targeted area have no water access or sanitaries facilities. The children are facing a lot of health problems. For them, providing safe drinking water is a must. The provision of filter units to the school children will improve the health, which in turn have a positive impact in the school attendance record. For sustainability, Child Watsan Committees will be formed to maintain these filters.

title: Help 250 Uganda Women Farmers attain Food Security
description: The project will train 250 rural women farmers in best farming practices, financial management skills and offer farming advisory services in Mubende district, Uganda. All trained women will have access to agricultural farming micro loans through our partnership with Kiva. (Kiva is a California based micro lending organization that has been a YICE partner since February 2013)

title: Build a future for children in a conflict zone
description: This project supports Child Protection in South-West Cameroon.This is done by helping outstanding orphanages and spaces for children operating in conflict areas. Since 2015, bore holes, livestock-rearing facilities, and schools have been built with the donations received. Currently most donations are used to pay teachers of two community schools and orphanages: Mah Di's and Hope Alive, with 250 children in total.The project also covers emergency response costs for vulnerable children at risk.

title: PROVIDE ENERGY AND WATER FOR 1315 VILLAGERS -BENIN
description: This project will gradually improve the access of poor villagers in Benin, including lake communities to basic social services to eliminate their vulnerability and ensure their welfare. The aim is to promote social and economic prosperity of vulnerable communities in lake villages of Benin to reduce poverty through access to affordable and sustainable renewable energy that can stimulate economic activities and improve education and care health and access to drinking water and to the Internet.

title: Help Save Kittens, Puppies & Pregnant Moms
description: During kitten and puppy season, PetConnect Rescue responds to desperate shelter pleas to save kittens, puppies and pregnant moms who are at high-risk for euthanasia. Some may require special care, such as bottle-feeding. We see that they are properly vetted, including prenatal care, exams, vaccinations and deworming. All will eventually be adopted into loving homes. We help decrease pet-overpopulation by ensuring that every adopted animal is spayed or neutered to prevent future unwanted litters.

title: Improve the Future of Construction Worker Families
description: CSSD will work with poverty stricken female construction workers and their families in the Mean Chey district of Phnom Penh. We aim to provide free health education, referrals, information for accessing appropriate services, vocational training and aid to construction worker families to break the cycle of poverty for women in this industry.

title: Shelter Home for sexually abused teenage girls
description: Fully recovery of children and teenage girls from 8 to 18yo, who suffered from family violence / sexual abuse, most of whom have broken family ties and scholar dropouts. Shelter works as a family home program, with 3 phases:  I. Uptake street or pass through public and community institutions II. Adaptation, integration and monitoring: development of values, life skills and school rehabilitation III. Family and/or social reintegration: workshops and family therapy; job training and placement

title: Meals on Wheels Wake County delivers 2500 lunches
description: What is for lunch?  Some people in Raleigh and surrounding Wake County would have nothing to eat except for the hot lunch delivered by a Meals on Wheels volunteer.  This is also often their only social interaction for the day.  People who eat a Meals on Wheels report eating better, maintaining or improving health, and feeling safer living at home independently.  Eliminating senior hunger is achievable.

title: A Night Out for 75 Victims of Domestic Violence
description: This project empowers 75 adult victims of domestic violence in the Chicagoland area by hosting special 'A Night Out' events that give them a brief escape from their daily struggles. Events encourage optimism and confidence through safe, healthy social interactions in different venue settings.

title: Send Children to School in Nigeria for a Year
description: This project will send at least 50 vulnerable children to school in Nigeria. These children are being exploited for hard labor in remote communities. And the only way to help them is to enroll them in school, provide school materials for them and empower their families economically.

title: It's For The Monkeys and 60 School Children
description: The project increases the recently planted 'For The Monkeys' biological corridor by 1.5 hectares (1600 trees) making a grand total of 8600 trees or 8.5 hectares of restored forest. The local students will also be participating in the project by collecting the baby trees, caring for them in the nursery, helping with the planting and watching them grow right across the street from their school.

title: From Child Labour to School
description: Poverty and hunger prevent children from going to school and work as child labour. The situation is worse in rural areas. In view of this situation, we run a school for the underprivileged children at Belabahol village in Purulia district of India where all children are from underprivileged sections, most of whome work as child labours in agricultural firms. Object is not only to provide quality education but also to provide nutritional food, books etc thus creating a conducive learning environm

title: Secondary Education for 144 Girls In Tanzania
description: Secondary school graduation rates for girls in East Africa are dismally low but ASAP has created a model of holistic support to increase' graduation rates to 80% or higher! The Kupanda Project includes safe housing, academic & health support and leadership development and can be easily replicated. It is being implemented for 144 girls at a secondary school in rural Tanzania but the girls must have a science lab to pass their national exams.  This lab will change the future for 144 girls!

title: Send 250 Bangolan girls to school
description: The United Nations Millennium Development Goal 2 targets the completion of primary education by all boys and girls. Unfortunately, compared to boys, girls are more likely to drop out of school and have less performance. This project will provide financial support to 250  girls from Bangolan village in the North West Region of Cameroon (West Africa) and this to permit them complete primary and secondary education.

title: Nutrition and food security support
description: We aim to improve quality of life for people living with HIV and to help those living positively to resist infection and reduce their frequency of contracting opportunistic infections, delay progression of AIDS, help medicine work effectively and reduce side effects. We hope to increase food security and supplement our current income generating projects (kitchen gardens, poultry rearing, and goat rearing) with additional access to foods such as maize, potatoes, beans, groundnuts and sorghum.

title: Colony1: Sustainability Hub
description: We are South Florida's first sustainability center, leading the way by demonstrating easily adoptable sustainable solutions for all. In the face of climate change Colony1 aims to provide the tools and resources to create a resilient community, with a zero packaging bulk food store, a learning CSA, a teaching event kitchen, and art and science residency program and a living youth classroom, our programming will be unique and accessible to all regardless of economics.

title: QualityEducation Matters to the  Most Vulnerable
description: School based Bridge Centers operated by our organization  will ensure quality and need based  academic support to most vulnerable children enrolled in school having unique and under defined disabilities.  Need based support will help children catch up with the syllabus ensuring their long term retention in schools.

title: Education and nutrition for 530 Indian children
description: Manav Sadhna runs an after school education program for more than 500 children living in Ahmedabad's largest slum, providing free education focusing on values, as well as providing milk and one nutritious snack each day.

title: Support shelter for survivor girls in Nicaragua
description: The Movement against Sexual Abuse MCAS is in process to support the EntreNosotras Shelter, located in Ocotal, 255km away from Managua, Nicaragua. This Shelter is part of MCAS and is one of the few homes designed to protect girls and teenagers who were forced to leave their hometown because of the risk that the abuser may have been released, or because their mother decides to support the abuser, or simply because it is the only place that provides integral protection and legal aid.

title: Keeping Kakata Liberia Safe From Ebola
description: When the local hospital closed and the government shutdown in July, our clinic was overwhelmed.  Other health workers in Kakata ran away, but our staff stayed and continued the work.  Since that time, as the hospital has reopened and closed a number of times, we have continued to build for the future.  We have laid the foundation for a new Medical Center.  With the help of a grant from Global Giving, we just recruited 10 new Community Health Workers bringing our total to 20.  Looking ahead.

title: we-care-global-youth-education-for-every-one
description: We are aiding women and children living in disadvantaged communities around the world to make sure they receive education and resources needed to lead better lives. *FUKUSHIMA KIDS California projects./ Fukushima Kid Hawaii Projects; Fukushima Children from Nuclear Disaster.*Russian orphans at Belskoye Ustye Orphanage to Medical & education.  * Uganda, at Wakisa Ministry for young girls education. *Philippines * Nepal,*Vietnam School supplies,Computers and Orphanage children's needs .

title: SUPPORT A GOOD LEARNING ENVIRONMENT IN TANGA
description: PASADIT is working in hand with the Tanga City Authority to improve learning environment in Tanga Cityl. Education being fundamental in bringing change and development amongst the community, Tanzania has been experiencing down fall in education sector. Teaching environment which is not conducive and friendly has continued to contribute to this downfall.  Currently the City Council is operating 79 Primary Schools with 47,652 pupils.The project will support Mapambano primary school in Tanga City.

title: Food Security for 3,000 Women & Children in Rwanda
description: YaLa Africa works to improve food security and nutrition in Kigali, Rwanda, by planting community gardens and training 3,000 youth, mothers with severely malnourished children, and those affected by HIV/AIDS, in micro-agriculture, health/hygiene and nutrition.

title: Support to Educate 25 Christian Girls
description: The purpose of this Support Educate 25 Christian Girls Initiative is to raise $8,000 to improve the lives of Christian girls in Tehsil Mandi Yazman, District of Bahawalpur, Pakistan. Since 2009, Kehkashan Development Organization (KDO) has provided educational opportunities for young women and girls. This campaign will provide education to over 25 girls belonging to christian community.

title: Education, Nutrition, Health and Safety to 60 Kids
description: Mammadu is a non-profit organization which provides education, nutritional services, healthcare, and a safe environment to 60 children who are vulnerable and/or orphaned due to extreme poverty or having lost a parent to HIV/AIDS or another health condition. These children live in informal housing settlements in Namibia, Africa, and without the help of Mammadu they would not have access to healthy regular meals, a proper education, or a safe place to learn and play.

title: Give Medical Care to 800 Indigent Adults in Rural
description: Hope Clinic provides free medical care, including medications, lab and diagnostic testing, mental health counseling, dental care, and case management to uninsured, indigent adults who suffer with chronic and life-threatening illnesses.

title: Training to augment organ donation in India
description: This project will support the invaluable task of training 100 Transplant Coordinators who do the unenviable job of counseling bereaved families to encourage them to donate the organs of their deceased loved one and save other lives.  Speaking to families who have just lost a dear one is no easy task and needs to be done with sensitivity which the coordinators are trained for in addition to coordinating the entire process of donation and transplant in a timely  and effective manner.

title: Rural agricultural to 10 youth group in Kenya.
description: Summary The project will establish a gricultural development, soil erosion control and training to improve the economic welfare of youth in rural village of Rongo Kenya through engagement in agricultural business, help youths without basic education or no education at all acquire practical skills to engage in agricultural productive income generating activities to make them selfreliant and employment (Job) in the rural area and break free from the cycle of poverty.

title: Mobile Clinics for Villages in Marakwet, Kenya
description: HealthRight's PMNH+ project seeks to improve access to quality health services in the remote communities of Marakwet, Kenya. To achieve this goal, this Global Giving project will provide medicines and health supplies for the health workers who travel across the county offering services through mobile clinics.

title: Mentoring & Trainings for 40 Armenian Girls
description: Nor Luyce Mentoring Center empowers 30 teenage girls from orphanages & low-income families through mentoring,skill building trainings,& financial assistance for college in Gyumri, Armenia.Our participants stay with our program for 3 to 4 years & gain skills that will help them leave their orphanages with the know how to live on their own emotionally & financially.Researches proved that teens with a mentor have a high "sense of self",feel more positive about their own identity,communicate easily.

title: Support 200 Women SHG Micro Entrepreneurs
description: The proposed  project aims to provide seed capital to poor Women entrepreneurs to fulfil their credit requirements and thereby free them from the clutches of local money lenders, who charges exorbitant rate of interest. This project aims to achieve economic development of the beneficiary thereby attempting to reverse the age-old vicious cycle of "low income, low savings, and low investment".We will work through women's SHG groups as women are the most vulnerable section of the society.

title: Care for 20 Children 0-10 Years Old in Philippines
description: Angel House cares for up to twenty children from newborn to ten years in the Philippines. Our dedicated team of staff can transform a neglected or abused child into a happy, well adjusted individual that is ready to be re-united with their family or adopted by loving parents.

title: Give Hope to 50 Children at Mbeere Children's Home
description: Mbeere Children's Home recently lost its Administrator, Henry, in a tragic road accident, leaving his wife and small child along with 50 children under the care of the home. Henry was very much a father figure to the children who have now lost hope. The home faces a difficult period without the man who has been in charge since it was opened ten years ago. Henry's wife has taken on his role but needs help to provide for the children in the short term as plans are developed for the future.

title: Keep 65 children from Kampala's slums in school
description: Every child has the right to Education. The project consist in offering a basic education to 65 disadvantaged children from the urban slum of Kibuye (suburbs of Kampala -Uganda) and aged 6-14. Your donation will contribute to providing them with school fees, scholastic materials, uniforms and sanitary pads for girls.

title: Help Children Cancer Patients in Colombia
description: This project will allow to buy the house that we are currently renting. The house is 718 m2 and fosters 13 children and their guardian. Besides the bedrooms, it is made of a play room, an interior patio, 2 living rooms, an administrative office, a psychology office, a kitchen, an infirmary and a dining room. It is a warm and welcoming temporary place for the kids where they feel like home and where they can escape the difficult time they spend at the hospital for their treatment.

title: After Ebola, Gardens Help Rebuild Lives
description: In a country where so many already lived on less than $2 a day, Ebola's truly crippling longer-term impact is on the whole population's ability to earn a livelihood and feed their families. The epidemic has caused missed planting and harvesting seasons, price spikes, and food shortages. Working with three in-country partners to reach those most isolated by poverty and disease, we are providing more than 25,000 packets of tested, appropriate vegetable seeds, along with support and training.

title: Medical Emergency Cancer Fund for Kenya
description: The Livestrong Foundation recently endorsed this project as 'promising' in cancer innovation by short-listing it as a semi-finalist from a field of 750 entries across the globe. A special pot of money will be open to adults and children living with cancer in Kenya who can't afford life-saving treatments such as chemotherapy and radiation.  Cancer is mostly a death sentence in Kenya but this project gives hope and a real chance of recovery to people fighting cancer, every year, forever.

title: Expanding Humane Education in Liberian Schools
description: Animal abuse is very  rampant in Liberia. Animal welfare is seen as a new phenomenon. As a result, animals are treated as commodities with no regard to their sentiments.  Children are the future leaders who will also own and be in charged of animals, equipping them with knowledge about animal sentiment will inspire them to start to make a change for animals resulting in a brighter future for animals and humans. Humane education is also vital in childhood development. It promotes empowerment.

title: Support Traumatized Child Soldiers in Liberia!
description: The world watched as Liberian children as young as ten years old were exploited as armed combatants. Under threat of death, they committed terrible acts of violence against the Liberian society. Many turned to substance abuse to cope with their experiences. We have built a residential facility in Little Bassa, Liberia where we want to provide groups of 20 former child soldiers a three-month program to help them recover from their trauma and obtain the skills necessary for social reintegration.

title: Educate 50 Kids with Disabilities in Honduras
description: Help children ages 4-21 born with disabilities receive needed Education and Health Care in Honduras. These children are living with disabilities such as Down's Syndrome or cerebral palsy and are not receiving services. They are bright children who have special needs and just need a chance to learn to read, do math, receive appropriate health care and therapy, and gain confidence. Un Mundo works with parents, children, teachers and the community to make these vital services a reality.

title: Educate a Girl in Pakistan & Give Her a Future
description: Provide education to a girl and give her the ability to transform her life, enter the workforce, and have a voice. $100 (+ GlobalGiving fees) covers the entire education of one girl at a partner institute). Join us in not only educating 1 girl, but 1000! We have just completed 1000 girls in Karachi successfully and 250 in Lahore. Your donation will go toward educating girls in Lahore, Pakistan. We are also working toward girls in Hyderabad, Pakistan as well as Balochistan, Pakistan.

title: Lifesaving Information: Halting Ebola in Liberia
description: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in history has already claimed almost 7,000 lives in West Africa - 70% have been women.  Accurate and timely information for public health campaigns is a key to halting the spread of the virus. Through the distribution of our solar and wind-up emergency radios, people living in isolated areas will be able to access information 24/7 to combat rumor and misinformation and learn facts on how to protect themselves and what to do if they suspect someone is infected.

title: Pinagpala Children Center Feeding Program
description: The Pinagpala Feeding Program is an ongoing project in the Philippines developed by Children Incorporated to keep children enrolled in the CI program fed so they are alert at school and ready to learn. The children are given a nutritional meal before and after school each day so they can have a full stomach for learning. CI provides funds for the program to buy grains, meets, vegetables, as well as cooking supplies to feed the children.

title: Life Saving Medical Equipment in Marakwet, Kenya
description: The objective of this project is to improve the health of mothers and children by expanding the availability of high quality health care services in Elgeyo-Marakwet County in Kenya. To achieve this goal, this Global Giving project will supply essential medicines and health supplies to nine maternal health centers in the region.

title: feed me at a school
description: This project is supporting over 80 orphans who came up as result of HIV/AIDS,civil wars and others!these children are supported with free education,scholastic materials,free food and clothes!we stay with them during day hours and they go back to their guardians,because of extreme poverty in this area,long distances from nearby schools,we resolved to start this orphanage school to create a bright future for these children.Currently they have no enough classrooms and school supplies are not enough

title: RESCUE DOGS in FLOOD AREAS - SAVE CHILDREN'S LIVES
description: Non-stop storms have physically devastated Philippine cities and rural villages.  A lack of nutrition and medicines/vaccinations has posed dangerous survival conditions for both children and homeless pet animals. Diseases like rabies, leptospirosis, and related forms of the medieval "plague" rival Ebola in Africa. Asia America Initiative has provided emergency food and medical care to more than 100,000 people in the flood zones. We are expanding our life saving missions to include 500 dogs.

title: The TOCO Permaculture School Garden
description: TOCO plans to establish a permaculture garden at a school in St Lucia to develop a School Feeding Program benefiting 100 children. The garden will also be a 'living classroom' to educate students in ecological and sustainable agriculture and nutrition and will generate income for the school.

title: HELP RECUE ABANDONED CHILDREN IN NAIROBI SLUMS.
description: By partnering with Home Of Hope International, you will not only be helping in our Abandoned Child Rescue Mission, but you will also be helping in giving then a home, food, medicare, education and love. You will also be helping educate the young mother on the life skills that will eventually turn around their economic status. We rescue Children,give them a home and hope, empower the community by educating them on basic life skills and  help young mother establish small businesses.

title: Build 3 Classrooms for 300 Refugee Kids in Uganda
description: This project will build 3 classrooms in Kyaka 2 Refugee camp Uganda, where Children have been studying under trees. It will Providing books and training to support 300 vulnerable refugees affected by the civil war and conflict in Africa.

title: productive 500 skilled youth for young india
description: Continuation of higher education became challenge for orphan and vulnerable youth. Hence  sponsorship for 500 youth for continuation of education by providing support services like tuition fee and study, education supplies will place them better in life. VMM regularly monitors their education performances through recording annual and semester marks and update their performances to the donors. Contribute for Sponsorship @ INR 10000 for higher education give an educated youth for better India.

title: Deformed Leper & poor disable youth therapy Centre
description: CHHASE aims to transform the lives of 32 deformed, cured leprosy patients and 52 disabled youth suffering from physical deformities caused by birth defects, accidents, abuse, or disease. Each child follows an individually designed program which is a combination of physiotherapy, massage, occupational and speech therapies. Deformed leprosy cured patients are neglected by their own family, struggle for bread and they will be provided with provisions and income generating program for a secure life

title: PREVENTING MALARIA AND HEALTH INSURANCE PROJECT
description: This project will raise awareness on Malaria and rescue children from contracting Malaria in the Gomoa-East District of Ghana by providing the children an opportunity to receive a mosquito net, insecticides  and be insured under the Ghana Health Insurance Scheme to receive free medical health care. For these vulnerable children, their continuous battle with malaria not only has wider implications for their long term development, it is a matter of life or death.

title: Stone By Stone
description: Stone by Stone is the project for raising funds to support the development of Monte Sahaja. Monte Sahaja is a retreat center and the spiritual home of Mooji Sangha. This center is being created so many people can come and be in this special place that is fully supportive to the realization of the Truth.  Any way you choose to participate is highly appreciated and is bringing work to completion more quickly.

title: Protecting Elephants and Rhinos in Malawi
description: Poaching and habitat destruction pushed the majority of wildlife in Malawi to the brink of extinction. A government-led, intensive conservation program has reintroduced more than 2,500 animals to the Majete Wildlife Reserve, including elephants, rhinos, leopards, lions, antelopes, water buffaloes and hyenas. Earthwatch is leading one of the first research initiatives to analyze how these reintroduced species are faring and what management decisions are needed to keep the ecosystem thriving.

title: Prevent the spread of Ebola in West Point, Liberia
description: The most densely populated slum in the Republic of Liberia, West Point is home to an estimated 60,000 women, men and children. A single confirmed case of Ebola could be completely devastating to the entire community. Preventing the spread of the disease from the remaining population would be extremely difficult.

title: Libraries in Rural Uganda
description: Grassroots Uganda is building 5 Libraries in rural areas of Uganda. The Libraries focus is on children to help the children grow with a sustainable reading culture. The Libraries are a an outlet where children and adults  can go to learn, create, explore and venture outside of the confines of poverty. Our librarians read children's stories aloud to the kids at least once per day, and we offer children's arts and crafts classes on Wednesdays to help the kids build their creative talents.

title: Saving Mothers' Lives in Rural Guatemala
description: The project supports part of the Casa Materna program in rural Guatemala, an area known as "The Triangle of Death" where women face a 1 in 20 lifetime chance of dying in childbirth.  We use low-cost, evidence-based interventions to train and equip Mayan community healthcare workers to provide life-saving care and education to women. Be part of sustainable community health and development in a high-need area where women and children die unnecessarily from readily preventable and treatable causes.

title: SEND 80 BATWA CHILDREN  TO SCHOOL IN RWANDA
description: This  project will Enable 80  children aged between 3- 6 year old from historically marginalized people formerly known as Batwa (pygmies) to access education by purchasing 0.5 hectares of land, building a three roomed classroom block, an office, a kitchen, pit latrine, purchasing desks and provide school uniforms to enable the children get quality education and thus a strong foundation.

title: Empower 50 Computer Illiterates in Val de Marne
description: This project equips a computer training center in priority zone of Val de Marne, providing FREE computer training in hardware and software applications to 50 disadvantaged computer illiterate youth and adults. Computer proficiency being indispensable for most job seekers, this would enable them acquire relevant knowledge and skills that would help them get a job, become productive and self-reliant, this would as a result enable them to contribute towards national development.

title: Education for tribal children in rural Rajasthan
description: This project aims to ensure that rural tribal children in Udaipur District, Rajasthan are able to receive a solid education, providing them with the skills they need to succeed in life. It will work through a 3-pronged approach, enrolling children in school and reducing instances of child labor, ensuring that children can easily get to school through providing escorts in remote areas, and ensuring children remain in school through holding school fairs and constructing sanitation facilities.

title: The Greater Boston Food Bank
description: The Greater Boston Food Bank (GBFB) is the largest hunger-relief organization in New England, and our mission is to end hunger here across Eastern Massachusetts. With your support, we can provide nutritious meals to over 400,000 children, adults and families - increasing access to fresh fruits and vegetables, and helping to ensure the continued health of our community.

title: Help us to send 50 orphans to Schools in Goma-DRC
description: This project  aims to support children orphaned and abandoned because of civil wars, with learning difficulties in North Kivu Province- Goma/DR.Congo to have access to education . Through this project, from your support, we expect to send 50 children in various schools of Goma  These children have no other chance to study without everyone implication, supporting one child will make his/her life change. Together we can save the future generation and contribute to an educated future World.

title: RespAct! Children stand up for their communities.
description: RespAct is a project of CamP Group gGmbH that encourages school children with different cultural and educational backgrounds to become active members and leaders in their communities. RespAct utilizes boxing exercises alongside participative videography and role plays to foster community engagement among children. We are building out our project online so that more students and teachers can benefit.

title: Adopt a Child out of 500 Children in Pakistan
description: ONAAR Development Organization, Mansehra KPK of Pakistan is going to provide Educational, Health and Nutritional support and Livelihood Assistance to the 500 deserving (poorest, orphans, CWDs) children and 50 Families especially women headed of District Mansehra KPK of Pakistan for the better future of the children, families and as well as for the betterment of the society.

title: Educate 25 Rural Children in Uganda
description: To assist 25 children in our rural community who because of poverty have dropped out of school and who need to get back to school, so we launched the Ugandan Children Scholarship Fund to provide formal education to disadvantaged rural children.

title: Fighting the Poverty
description: This project will support the reduction of poverty, family violence, the causes of alcoholism and drug addiction and also prevention of civil disobedience.

title: Send 60 Girls in Pakistan to School
description: Girls Education International supports access to education for 60 girls in various rural Pakistani villages, including secondary school, participation in self-growth and other extra-curricular (out-of-the-classroom) learning experiences, vocational training, exposure trips, and annual alumni celebrations. We partner with Bedari, a nonprofit based in Pakistan, to cover the costs associated with these important and holistic educational activities.

title: Save 3000 children from malnutrition in Danane
description: The crisis in Cote d'Ivoire, has impoverishes families and affecting especially the children. According statistics 70 % of children who die have suffered from anemia and of malnutrition. Many families in rural areas saw their stock of seed plundered and their farms destroyed. Today the women gather to reconstitute new stocks of rice and cassava to feed the households in there area. This project will give them nourishing seeds with high yield and learn them modern cultural methods to succeed.

title: Small business to 300 rural women in DRCongo
description: The project will support businesses run by women through increased access to rotary microloans  and help tthem to  access management training programs so that they can get the high-quality skills in the labor market. The project  provide not only resources, but also opportunities to use ways that lead to economic success  of better jobs, more opportunities for create and manage viable businesses, increased access to land, education and skills.

title: Rehabilitation of Partial Disabled Cows
description: In india Cows are treated as God by Hindu Community.In Rural areas,People,Partially illiterate,Use to shelter the cows mainly for milk production.They are Practising the anncient method for providing food and health hygyne to those innocent animals.They trated them as a productive tools not as a creature.So when the cows get herted use to realease them quickly from shelter or sell them to slaughter house.Our organisation with the view to serve the animal has taken up a project to provide shelter

title: 400 Baloch girls get entrepreneurship training
description: Smart Tajir by Youth Impact will enable 400 rural school girls from Balochistan to learn the science and art of entrepreneurship. Through an integrated program model, they will be able to connect local opportunities with their newly learnt skills. Young girls from some of the most neglected districts of Pakistan, i.e. Turbat, Gwadar, Panjgur and Lasbela will benefit from this program.

title: Support for flooded Mizia, Bulgaria
description: For the last months a lot of bulgarian areas were flooded. The most affected were the poorest people whose homes and possessions are fully submerged in water. The water left them homeless, desperate and dealing with the horror they experienced, watching their homes and livelihoods sank. Our volunteers will provide help, organizing charity campaigns, buy live saving supplies and offering assistance for the recovery of around  100 of most needed families in Mizia.

title: HELP victims of armed conflict of Medellin-Colombi
description: The AMBER project aims to help 1,500 people victims of the armed conflict, children, youth, teenage mothers and the elderly in the city of medellin-Colombia, with training, psychosocial care and self-management, promoting the internal value of each individual.

title: Safe home for bride kidnapping victims, Kyrgyzstan
description: Bride kidnapping, locally known as Ala Kachuu, is common in Kyrgyzstan. Victims of Ala Kachuu typically experience violent kidnapping followed by rape and forced marriage, which often involves physical and psychological abuse. Restless Beings' project in Kyrgyzstan provides victims with a counselling helpline and a safe transit home with a range of services to help women and their children to break out of their misery and start a new life. Help sustain and scale up our work by donating today!

title: Prevent mexican children from living in the street
description: The Family Care Program seeks to prevent at-risk boys and young men from leaving home to live in the streets. They may be at-risk because they have dropped out of school, are using drugs and come from homes with significant levels of violence and poverty. Our focus is on families living in Mexico City. Our specialized interventions allow the creation of safe and healthy environments that are conducive to children returning to school and having healthy social interactions.

title: Operate community mental health center in Pakistan
description: This project will help in operating mental health care center for one year in north-western Pakistan, providing a quality community-based mental health treatment & community-based rehab services to poor & needy men, women & children with mental disorders in a decentralized and non-discriminative way. The project will relies on a close collaboration between patients, their families & primary care providers within community settings for a better mental health, self-help and quality of life.

title: To Save Severe Malnourished Children in Bihar.
description: Nidan is running a Nutritional Rehabilitation Centre in Bihar. The project helps severe and acute malnourished (SAM) children in the age group of 6 months to 60 months. It's a facility-based care which provides nutritious food & medication to children & mothers. They are discharged only after complete recovery. Mothers are trained on feed preparation, basic healthcare, hygiene and nutrition. So far Nidan has saved 1189 SAM children and wants to save more with your generous support.

title: Help Support Scotland's Sick Children
description: Children from all over Scotland are treated at the Royal Hospital for Children in Glasgow. Some have minor ailments, others are fighting for their lives. Glasgow Children's Hospital Charity sits at the heart of the hospital and invests in initiatives that help to make their care and experience the best it can be.  Your support will help to ensure that we can invest in world class medical equipment, play programmes, family support services and pioneering research to make young lives better.

title: Give 3000 services for Lithuanian cancer patients
description: St. Francis oncology centre  provide professional cancer support services to people affected by cancer, their relatives and those who have already lost family members. We serve the all Lithuanian republic territory and also Lithuanian emigrants abroad. We provide all of our services free of charge. We organize many events for collecting  finances and  accept any possible donations to cover the costs of our services and building (communal)  maintenance.

title: Handicap Van and Wheelchairs
description: The Sports and Recreational Group (GDR), "A Joanita", founded in 1979, based in the Council of Oeiras, is a pioneer in the introduction of sports for the disabled in Portugal. It is a Public Utility Association, which has, since its inception, backed sport, most especially Wheelchair Basketball, believing it to be a way of promoting the social inclusion of disabled people. We need a van and wheelchairs.

title: Youngsters' traditional real life restaurant
description: The real life restaurant is a place in which young socially vulnerable cooking apprentices from Escuela Taller assume a restaurateurs' role in real life, so they can enhance their skills, access to worthy wages and profit-sharing as a result of the restaurant's operation. We want to be seen as food innovators, rescuers of real Colombian traditional cuisine, balanced meal makers and appealing dishes at affordable prices while including social responsibility.

title: Aquaponics Solution to Climate Change
description: The controlled environment provided by an aquaponics greenhouse solves obstacles to food production caused by climate change in El Salvador, including a proliferation of pests and irregular rainfall. Amun Shea students will benefit from nutritious meals at school, as well as from learning to manage scalable aguaponics production for home and small business application. Their current experience in fish farming and vegetable growing will be combined in this proactive solution to food production.

title: Give hope to children's education in Tehey (Ghana)
description: Give Hope to Children's Education in Tehey is an educational project aimed at providing access to education for children in Tehey community, a remote area in the Dangbe East District of Ghana, West- Africa. This project will build a six unit classroom block to provide free access to education for over 200 children in the community. The project will also include a library, computer room and provision of educational material to support their studies.

title: Dalit-girls Rights for Education and Advancement
description: Dalit are treated as extreme vulnerable segment and have been experiencing various forms of injustices in the social and economic context. However, these groups of people are victim of various forms of social injustices. The project will create a favourable atmosphere for Dalit girls to access education and opportunity to improve their livelihoods. Through successful implementation of the project, human rights violation will be reduced and human dignity will be increased.

title: Build a Classroom, Save the Amazon
description: Yachana Foundation is dedicated to providing community-based solutions to poverty and environmental degradation in the Ecuadorian Amazon. Currently Yachana, "place for learning" in Kichwa, educates, inspires, and empowers 200 youth of the Amazon to have a positive impact on the eco-sustainability of their region. Help us build a 1,787 square foot, thatched roof classroom and an aquaponic demonstration farm for co-cultivation of plants and fish in a recirculating environment.

title: Supporting Our Caregivers for TB Patients in Haiti
description: Funding will support our patient caregiving program in Haiti who provide care for over 50 tuberculosis (TB) patients each month. These caregivers will help us maintain our commitment to providing a full range of integrated care for patients while our inpatient ward is closed. Caregivers act as liaisons with patients' medical teams, help with oxygen, make home visits with food and medications, send live video for consults, and arrange visits with counselors.

title: Help 71 Young Colombians who fight against Cancer!
description: This project supports 71 young people between 14 and 24 years old, who have lived with a cancer that has passed. The initiative "Young People in Contact" of the Colombian Leukemia and Lymphoma Foundation, aims to provide emotional support and psycho-education to young people in the treatment, through the activities and testimonies of other young cancer survivors, allowing them to share their experiences, resolve doubts, promote emotional expression, coping strategies and other important skills.

title: CEE Yourself Today Campaign Experience
description: Are you sick and tired of you or your loved ones being chronically sick enough to do something about it? If you are, then this message is for you. The "CEE Yourself Today" campaign experience is a Celebration of You! It invites 6.7 million residents to (C)elebrate, (E)xplore and (E)ducation themselves around options available for leading a healthy, sustainable thriving lifestyle in the Central Florida region. The spotlight is on Alternative Health and Lifestyle.    Imagine Real Wellness Today!

title: Playgrounds for disabled children in Kyrgyzstan
description: This project aims to change the lives of 60 children with disabilities by building two accessible playgrounds thus giving them the chance to play with their peers and be included in their communities.

title: Ending Child Sexual Violence In120 Indian Villages
description: In India, just 3% of child rape and sexual abuse cases reach the police. Utthan is going to work with ex-victims and local leaders to create an environment that can tackle the problem of sexual violence head-on. We will begin by training 60 community leaders to provide gender sensitive and informed support to victims of child rape and sexual abuse in 120 villages.They will play a key role in overcoming the extreme social stigma and victim-blaming culture that prevents victims from speaking out.

title: Young Girls Fight Against Early & Forced Marriage
description: This project will help adolescent girls from socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society to use technology both as a tool and as a medium in helping them raise their voices and generate awareness on the issue of early and forced marriage (EFM). Girls associated with the Technical Center at Feminist Approach to Technology (FAT), a not-for-profit organization, would shoot and produce a film on EFM that would highlight their daily struggles in countering this social menace.

title: Housing for Homeless, Pregnant D.C. Teenagers
description: Half to two-thirds pregnant teenagers we serve in DC are homeless; 100% are hungry; DC's infant mortality rate is among the highest in the nation. This project provides for one month's rent for 12 pregnant women (or 6 mothers and 6 infants) at our Perennial Transitional House where they have a safe, clean place to live, healthy food , and medical care during pregnancy and early stages of parenting, so they can have healthy babies and prepare for independent living.

title: Send Sheetal from Red-Light Area to US Drum School
description: Hi, I'm Sheetal! I'm 19, in 10th grade and I love to dance and play drums. A normal teenage life? Yes, but I grew up in Mumbai's red-light area. I am the daughter of a sex worker and I've never met my dad. I'm still in 10th because I've only been to school 3 years of my life. I faced a lot of violence, rape and discrimination....But I have big dreams! I want to go to a music school in the US for drumming diploma so I can start music classes in the red-light area. Will you help me get to the USA?

title: School bus needed for Haitian orphans
description: After several years of feeding and clothing children in 5 orphanages in Haiti, Life Is Hope would like to have these children in school on a daily basis. We believe that the first step is locating a bus that can be used to get the children to the school safely. After that we will focus on land and a building. The bus can be used for transportation needs until all components are together.

title: Vulnerable young people: Job and life skills
description: FOP is a non-profit organization focused on increasing opportunities for economic and social development of young people in situation of social vulnerability in Argentina. In line with the MDGs, we advocate equal opportunities, gender equality and the promotion of valued work. We build a bridge between them and companies/universities through job training, mentoring and labour intermediation. So far, up to 85,000 young people have participated in our projects.

title: save an abandoned baby's life with formula milk
description: Mogra receives babies that are abandoned in hospitals immediately after birth and those whose mothers have died with no next of kin. We also receive those who are abandoned on streets and those rescued in different circumstances by authorities.  Every abandoned child below 6 months must be fed exclusively with infant formula.  We are commitment to ensure that every baby thrives and later placed for adoption. We continue providing basic needs and education to those not lucky to get a home.

title: Women Empowerment
description: FOP is a non-profit organization whose main task is increasing opportunities for economic and social integration of young Argentine women in a situation of social vulnerability. In line with the MDGs, we promote gender equality and the promotion of valued work. Since 2001, we work to build bridges between them and companies/universities through job mentoring and labor intermediation.  One opportunity can have a positive, long-lasting impact on a young woman's life.

title: Toilets & Water For School Children in Srilanka
