Through private land management, education, and on site scientific studies, ASANA and Rafiki hope to shift the paradigm of how local people view tapirs. We believe that if they appreciate the benefit of having tapirs in the environment, they will be more likely to support conservation efforts and help save the species from extinction.

title: #ISurvivedEbola Campaign
description: The ISurvivedEbola Campaign is a transmedia project that mobilizes Ebola survivors from Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone to share stories of recovery to inform the West African general public about the virus and how they can protect themselves and their communities from it, reduce stigmatization, and promote reintegration of Ebola survivors.

title: Help the VFS to buy a New Fire Truck
description: Since 1910 members of the VFSe in Kadlub Turawski risking their health and life taking care of the safety of the residents of the commune Turawa. Operatig in events of natural disasters, traffic accidents and other we rescue people, animals and natural environment as well asw human properties. Because the nearest State Fire Service is located 25 km from Kadlub Turawski the Voluntary Fire Service takes actions as an independent unit or arrives at place and starting rescue actions

title: Feed children's bodies, minds and souls Pasajquim
description: This project will create a rich learning environment for 150 children during the 2 months of school vacation while providing a healthy meal daily in this community rife with malnutrition.

title: Fin.& Entrepren.Educat.for 800 low-inc.Venez.women
description: While 38% of Latin American women are in charge of providing their homes' main income for their families, in Venezuela is approximately 40%.Jovenes Emprend. plans to provide financial education, business knowledge and entrepreneurship abilities to 800 women located in low income surroundings, as well as an initial seed capital will be provided by an allied bank for them to initiate their businesses improving their communities and their families'quality of life. Dir.popul.:800 women.Indirect:3200

title: By 2 Every Child Learning Reading,Math, Music+++
description: We have to empower and equip low-income parents to teach their babies reading, math, music, science and encyclopedic knowledge by two.  Most low-income children start school with a 75% vocabulary deficit, and cannot count. We will work with 10 or more parents that have received computers from us to transform this. We will send them to the course at the Institutes for the Achievement of Human Development and work with them to effectively use our Brillkids early learning software.

title: Partners In Health Ebola Response
description: The Ebola outbreak in West Africa is the worst in history and continues to sicken and kill thousands of people in Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea. As the outbreak advances and devastates already weak health systems, Partners In Health is leading a response effort along with partners on the ground that will deliver care, help contain the current outbreak, and strengthen health systems for the long term.

title: Donate to support  Usalama House- LGBTQ safe space
description: Usalama House (LGBT homeless shelter)  provides a safe and comfortable home for LGBT youth 6-24 years who are kicked out of  their parents' home because of their sex orientation and gender identity. The home also provide nutritious food, decent clothing, healthcare and valuable education which will help them obtain requisite skills as either entrepreneurs or entrepreneurs to be self employed, employ others and be marketable wherever they find themselves in this world.

title: Homestead nutrition for Korku tribe in India
description: This project will help 500 Korku tribe families of Madhya Pradesh to access more nutrition and added livelihood options through growing backyard organic vegetable gardens in most cost effective and simple manner.

title: Provide fistula repair surgery for women in Uganda
description: Fistula is the result of obstructed labour and occurs when women and girls do not receive the medical attention they need whilst giving birth. It leads to a lifetime of incontinence, nerve damage, infection and infertility and the baby will also be born dead. Yet fistula is both preventable and treatable.  Volunteers from the RCOG currently travel to Kitovu Hospital in Uganda to perform fistula surgery and to train local health care staff in fistula treatment and prevention.

title: Complete Center for 500  Farmers in Cameroon
description: Green Care is a small NGO that provides valuable agricultural training to farmers in the Northwest region of Cameroon. Their current office is two rooms in size, and too small. Located in Shisong, Green Care has been working on constructing a new seven room building since winter of 2013. Now, they need additional funding to complete construction. Green Care will provide farmers and general public with the uses of a lecture hall, mushroom training farm, and public library.

title: Support and give hope to Village Women in Bihar
description: Bihar is a state in the North of India. If it were a country it would be the sixth poorest in the world. Women in village communities have a low social status and often suffer social isolation.

title: Join Our Global Mentoring Movement
description: This project will support 100 orphaned youth from South Africa's most disinvested neighborhoods Infinite Family matches pre-teens and teens with adult video mentors. Our mentors act as role models who teach, discuss, challenge, encourage, befriend, and love; they act as agents of self-reliance.

title: Help sponsor a foster family in China
description: This project will sponsor four loving foster families in China for one year. Each family is composed of a foster father, a foster mother, and up to four children whose special needs are likely to preclude adoption.

title: Uplift Tribal Artists, Upgrade Rancho Tioracas
description: This project aims to renovate Rancho Maleku Tioracas in order to provide a secure place for community cultural activities and artisans to display and sell their work: arts and crafts, theater presentations, meetings and workshops  The rancho gives Maleku artisans and the residents of Palenque Margarita and nearby Tonjibe a venue that will  improve social collaboration and economic security.

title: Education and Protection Center for 200 Children
description: 2007, after the mass murder,disappearance of children of migrant labor from Nithari village, Noida, UP, India, parents from poor, backward communities were frightened about the safety of their children. MERA SAHARA Centre for non formal Education; Skill formation, Protection was started by us with local community support. It functions as a preparatory school, a bridge between non-formal and formal education. It sucessfully prevents child trafficking, labor & marriage, and needs financial support

title: Send Typhoon Haiyan Affected Students to College
description: The main problem with Typhoon Haiyan affected students especially girls is that they have difficulty going back to school as most lost their homes and livelihoods and some have parents and siblings who did not survive. They are indeed in very dire strait and they are prey to criminal syndicates offering them job in the cities but only to end up as prostitutes. This modest project will try to send 10 hardly affected girls to college or vocational school, so that they will have a good future ahead

title: Help Fund a Project Development Officer
description: A challenge that FORUDEF continually encounters is how to use their limited resources to affect the greatest possible change. Identifying needs is not difficult, nor is identifying innovative responses to those needs. The daily challenge is how to creatively use resources to make a lasting impact, and how to do that with a limited staff.   You can help increase FORUDEF's  capacity to empower communities in Cameroon by contributing resources to hiring a permanent Project Development Officer.

title: Save a Horse: Rescue and Rehabilitate Mustangs
description: In the early 1900's, the wild mustang population in the US was estimated to be over 2 million. Today, there are only 15,000 left in the wild and about 40,000 in captivity in need of rescue. The Wild Horse Rescue Center rescues and rehabilitates mustangs who have been abused and neglected. The center subsequently adopts the horses into loving homes. The funds for this project will go towards the care of the center's 40 horses, located in Mims, Florida, USA.

title: computer education to 100 students in kishanganj
description: AIF  is running computer lab with 5 computers in  district Kishanganj. This block is selected with in close vicinity of high and middle schools. AIF is imparting 3 months basic computer course keeping in mind the learning ability of the students who belong to marginalized and poor sections of the society.  The center is running 2 hours class for  students. 3 batches are running every day thrice a week. The  centre will  impart computer education to 100 students in the second year

title: Training 200 conflict affected girls in Uganda
description: RIC-NET provides psycho social, educational and livelihood support  to 200 abused and traumatized girls(12-22 years old) who are struggling to recover from ADF civil war and conflict in Rwenzori region. specifically focuses on supporting young women  with babies by enrolling their children in nursery schools, while helping the mothers to either go back to school or attain vocational skills ( ICT, tailoring, hair dressing, cloth design) and reproductive health. provides  girls with start up fund.

title: Plant it Forward 2015
description: Magulilwa Area Secondary School (MASS) is raising money to plant a total of 600 trees on the campus of Magulilwa Area Secondary School in rural Tanzania in order to lessen or impact on deforestation around the area, as the school needs to use firewood to cook meals for its students.  The community of residents and students on and off school grounds will benefit by receiving deforestation education with the hopes of creating new environmental leaders, as well as new jobs for the local villagers.

title: Help Children Survive the Ebola Outbreak
description: Save the Children is on the ground working with health ministries in Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea to address the outbreak in many ways. We are currently training teachers, health workers, nurses and local organizations on prevention measures against Ebola and are distributing protective kits and essential medical equipment. We are dedicated to ensuring that we reach people in hard-to-access locations, particularly children. Donate now to support our efforts.

title: Sustainable Income Plans in Latin America
description: The most important part of philanthropic work is to make sure the projects can sustainably run themselves for years and years to come. We aim to implement small businesses run by the families in the rural communities where we work so teachers' salaries are covered and local families receive extra income. These plans, once trialled, can be replicated in literally hundreds of communities over the next few years.

title: Meals on Wheels, Wichita Falls, TX
description: The Kitchen's Meals on Wheels program seeks to ensure no senior goes hungry in Wichita Falls, TX. Malnourished seniors may be overlooked until they show up in the ER for other reasons or injuries. In a recent study of Emergency Medicine at UNC, it was found that seniors "fly under the radar," and the rate of malnutrition in seniors in emergency treatment situations was 60 percent. Meals on Wheels helps seniors maintain a nutritionally balanced diet through our home-delivered meal program.

title: Seeds for Syria
description: Violent armed conflict in Syria has caused millions of Syrians to flee to other parts of Syria and to neighboring countries, creating a humanitarian crisis in which food is a top priority. With our Partner Organization Karam Foundation, SPI is establishing vegetable gardening projects for internally displaced refugee to produce their own food. The project will ship a pallet, which is about 30 cartons, or in total 42,000 packets. This grows 150 tons of food or more = 1.5 million vegetable serving

title: Brighten the holidays for children and teens!
description: BTAC provides holiday gifts for children and teens whose families cannot afford them.  Teens are often overlooked during the holidays.  While BTAC receives an abundance of gifts for younger children, gifts for teens are very rare, indeed.  Donations can help BTAC provide age-appropriate gifts (skateboards, cosmetics, gift cards for shoe stores, electronics, etc.) for teens.

title: Disabled Empowerment through Vocational Training
description: The proposed project to upgrade existing facilities of the Vocational Training center located in Matara district, Sri Lanka is an attempt to rehabilitate disabled by Saviya Development Foundation (SDF) It will create a comfortable, tidy and clean environment for disabled, marginalized youth who get the residential training annually (about 20 residential student per year) and socialize them by giving practical education to make their future career pathways.

title: Reducing stigma among people living with HIV/AIDS
description: Despite the progress made in the treatment of AIDS, and global attention moving on from AIDS to other diseases, people who are living with the virus often remain marginalised or forgotten in their own families and communities. This project will build on a previous successful workshop to explore the issue of stigmatisation with a further 60 people living with AIDS in the Coastal Region of Kenya, thus changing their relationships with their families and communities

title: Support for Children of Alcoholics in Denmark
description: One in ten Danish children is negatively affected by parental alcohol consumption, and at least 122,000 Danish children grow up in families with outright abuse. The Blue Cross has two houses for children that offer care, counseling and treatment in an alcohol-free environment. They can spend time with their peers and seek support for the harm caused by their parents' addiction.

title: Build Samdiar School for 120 Children in Timbuktu
description: Political circumstances have left literacy rates close to zero in many of the villages around historic Timbuktu, Mali, which once boasted of the world's largest universities in the 12th to 16th centuries. Caravan to Class (CTC) seeks to provide the dream of an education for the children of Samdiar, in the Timbuktu region, by building a school in this carefully-selected village. CTC plans to help reignite the region's rich history of literacy by providing education to 120 deserving children.

title: Christmas Operation You Project
description: Christmas Operation You Project bring great excitement, bright eyes, and happy faces on Christmas morning. This program provide new and unwrapped toys for children in need. Please join us in providing a memorable Christmas for a boy or girl.

title: PEDIATRIC CENTER FOR 15,600 CHILDREN IN NEED
description: This project created a Pediatric Health Center in Veron, an underserved community in Punta Cana, eastern region of the Dominican Republic, for the benefit of more than 15,600 children in need.  The child population has been greatly impacted given that there are not affordable options in the entire area in terms of primary health cares. The center offers outpatient consultations; besides dental, vaccination, emergency, laboratory, ambulance, x ray, ultrasound and pharmacy services, among others

title: Rehabilitate School in Timbuktu for 80 students
description: The Teshaq school in a village outside of Timbuktu, Mali was closed in 2012 as residents fled their homes due to conflict in Northern Mali. Teshaq villagers have since returned to their village to find the school partially destroyed. Caravan to Class (CTC) would like to rehabilitate the Teshaq school to allow 80 deserving children to resume their quest for literacy. CTC continues the legacy of the amazing work done by Irma Turtle and Turtlewill.org.

title: Schooling for  120 Students of Tourari in Timbuktu
description: Help 120 students of the Tourari school near Timbuktu, Mali continue their quest for literacy in the 2014-15 school year. The Big Birthday Wish Donors were incredibly generous in funding the rehabilitation of the Tourari School in 2013-14. To continue with their education, Caravan to Class needs help to fund the operation of the Tourari school paying teachers' salaries and providing basic nutrition and school supplies.

title: Soapmaking Program - Health & Income for Refugees
description: This project focuses on providing 10 groups of refugee women with training, ingredients, and tools to produce body and laundry soap to sell to over 29,000 refugees from Darfur for an affordable price. This project will help reduce illness and improve the health and well being of the refugees in the camp. It will also help build an income generating opportunity as well as empower women and  build teamwork skills.

title: Kenya's Urban Promise Begins with 300 Girls
description: Shining Hope for Communities (SHOFCO) combats gender inequality and extreme poverty in urban slums outside Nairobi, Kenya by linking tuition free schools for girls to holistic social services for all, making a girls' school a portal of social change. Today, we transform urban communities. Tomorrow, we create the next generation of female leaders.

title: Angel's Fruit Forest for the Maleku, Costa Rica
description: The project increases the 35,000 trees "Rio Sol Bio Corridor", planted 2011, by 3.4 hectares or 3,500 trees making a grand total of 44,000 trees (44 hectares) of restored forest @ the Maleku Indigenous reserve along the Rio Sol. Angel will focus on planting as many varieties of native fruit trees as possible, like Cacao, Pataste, Breadfruit, Mangos, etc. He has 1000 Cacao trees ready for planting now and will add another 2500 trees of more that 100 different species to his existing nursery.

title: Brighten the Future of Gaza's Children
description: In this time of darkness and need, send wearable solar-powered lights through the blockade to Gaza children. These lights will help children study and play safely in the long hours when the power is out. We are partnering with Little Sun to purchase solar lights with a rechargeable, replaceable battery, and with SunBox, to install whole home solar systems designed by a Gaza engineer to charge phones, laptops, run a refrigerator or TV, & turn lights on. Please hold Gaza's children in the light.

title: Increase SOS Fund to Save Expiring Microloans
description: Borrowers on our platform have a 30 day time limit to complete the funding of their loan. We have already created a fund that attempts to save worthy loans from expiring (The SOS Loan Fund) so that borrowers can lift themselves out of poverty through their own hard work. We are trying to increase this fund to the $10,000 mark so that we may save more loans - and it all gets paid back to lend again!

title: Use soccer as a tool to educate 3000 Kibera youths
description: KIMTA are an extraordinary business, supporting some of the most needy children in Kenya. Their passion for improvement is inspirational and they work day in day out to better the life for the families in the slums. Obviously hard work alone just isnt enough and they are constantly looking for financial support to buy the tools and equipment to carry out their work. Certain things in this part of Africa are cheap and easily accessible.

title: Rebuild a Community Destroyed by Hurricane Odile
description: The people of Las Pacas near La Paz, Mexico lost their homes in the recent hurricane. Olazul is helping Las Pacas to secure emergency assistance, rebuild their homes and guarantee a better future.

title: Support 250 children imprisoned in Mombasa, Kenya
description: Glad's House will be supporting street children who are arrested and/or detained in Mombasa and other children and young people who are imprisoned in Mombasa. We are working to improve living conditions for them. We will be delivering care packages, sport sessions as well as supporting children back home on release. We are also working with police and institutions to improve conditions in the long term ensure that each individual childs rights are realised

title: Less Privileged Elders Need Care & Meal Support
description: The less privileged elders need our love and care. This project will provide meal, medical care and recreation to 57 homeless old age persons. Every day we provide nutritious food to destitute elder, who are neglected by their families. Due to poverty some families not able to feed these older persons. Among 57 poor old age persons, some of them use to beg at neighbor houses, nearby locations to feed themselves. Our little contribution to the elderly make their world healthy and happy

title: Help an orphan go to University
description: Rahim is an orphan from Father House Orphanage in Muyuka, South-West Region, Cameroon. He is now in his second year of Geography in University of Buea. University fees and associated costs are too much for the orphanage to take care of alone. If we get the funding we will make sure he can pay for his University Fees and we will secure his most crucial expenses for the year, we will allocate some money for an economic activity that he can do at the same time than studying.

title: Provide 10 Dorset Cancer Support Retreat Places
description: Our first trial was for 9 women who had all experienced cancer and was set at the beautiful California Barn, Swanage. The barn is set in 11 acres of beautiful, tranquil countryside that offers the opportunity to calm your mind and allow yourself to be nurtured, improving your well being. The retreat was led by Andrea Johnstone (HND B.A.C.P.) Transpersonal transformation  Practitioner and all of the women reported having an amazing and very emotional experience.

title: Ebola Emergency: Help WFPUSA prevent a food crisis
description: The Ebola epidemic can quickly become food crisis. Hundreds of families in West Africa have already lost someone to the virus.To contain Ebola, families are quarantined, many unable to leave their homes for weeks. As a result, farmers cannot tend to their crops and livestock. This means that a year's harvest can literally be left to rot in the field.  That's why WFP has been on the ground since last March providing emergency humanitarian relief to families caught up in the epidemic.

title: Global Aid Needed to Stop Ebola Outbreak in Africa
description: WHO has declared this epidemic an international emergency. It's not too late to help meet the critical needs of our partners and their communities that have been impacted by the Ebola virus in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea.   World Harvest develops a proposal "Emergency Disaster Relief and Community Awareness and Sensitization on the Prevention & Precautions of the Ebola Epidemic Disease" to significantly enhance, educate and capacitate the local communities. We will be doing mission outrea

title: Help Baby Bats Take Flight!
description: More than 1000 flying foxes are killed or injured each year in Sydney, many on power lines or caught in garden netting. Tiny babies, still clinging to their mum, may survive even if she doesn't. Sadly, older pups, who are too big to carry, usually die of starvation if their mum is killed.  This project will help care for orphan baby bats so that they are ready to go to bat creche to learn to fly and learn the social skills they need to survive in the wild.

title: Early Intervention ( Infant to 6 years )
description: Vidya Sagar's Early Intervention Program, since 1986, caters to infants with cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, autism, learning disabilities and multiple disabilities. It includes special education, physiotherapy, occupation therapy, communication and vision training learning through play and field trips. The focus is to assess and identify abilities and needs of the child , provide intervention  and support and equip families to work with their children during the critical early year

title: Help Keep Battered Mothers And Children Together
description: Battered American mothers flee home for their safety to the USA with their children. Their abusers file petitions trying to force the return of their children to the foreign country even when the children are just American. There is no defense for battered American mothers. We need to hire good attorneys for these victims so the children won't be returned to the abuser in the foreign country and be subjected to more abuse and be separated from their primary caretaker, their mother.

title: Keep children safe from traffickers in India
description: Every 8 minutes a child goes missing in India. 40% of them are never found. They are sold as labour, as sex objects or worse. iPartner India needs your help to stop this modern day slavery. In just 5 years, we have supported NGOs working on the frontline in India and helped 20,250 child trafficking victims in 11 states in India. We do this by bringing together the Indian government, our partner NGOs and caring individuals in the global community - like you - to work towards ending child slavery.

title: Hospital classroom for sick children in Medellin
description: In the Hospital Classroom we have teachers and a space to accompany hospitalized children in their educational process, maintaining schooling and avoiding losses in the learning process through pedagogical strategies that reduce the negative impact of the disease; The Classroom is a space that articulates Education and Health promoting humanized care that impacts more than 10,000 hospitalized children each year.

title: Hudhud relief fund for 500 very poor families
description: The severe Cyclonic storm Hudhud was the strongest tropical cyclone of 2014 that resulted into unending damages in Vizag and the nearby areas. The misery of the people hardly has an end. The cyclone took thousands of life, as it hit the coastal district of Andhra Pradesh. . The city of Vizag has undergone a loss of almost Rs. 70,000 crore, while the rest of the losses are yet to be estimated. Almost 84 deaths are being confirmed.

title: Rescue & Protect Sea Turtles in Thailand and Asia
description: The turtle population is in a critical state worldwide, however, in areas with high tourist numbers the species is even more threatened.  Our goal is to create awareness around the sensitive nesting and breeding areas of these creatures,  create safe and effective breeding grounds for them as well as provide emergency care to those in need. By doing this we hope to allow for sustainable tourism that doesn't inhibit the population growth of the turtles

title: Helping Liberia's urban poor youths out of poverty
description: The project aims to develop sustainable livelihood skills and competitive income generating capabilities for 200 vulnerable urban youths in 5 slum communities of Gardnersville, a suburban district located northeast of Monrovia. The youths targeted by the project are those who are functionally illiterate, unemployed  and subsistent on the informal or illegal economy. Vocational training, literacy & numeracy, micro grants and self help cooperation are key activities to be promoted in the project.

title: Village Soccer Dream Teams
description: Our soccer program is complementary to our school  English  & Nutritional program. A sound mind and  healthy body go hand in hand to develop full potential and confidence for young students. This year we have four teams entered into a weekend Soccer League with our two Khmer coaches. This gives them the opportunity to develop skills and takes them out of their rural environment. Confidence building and sportsmanship are a great tool for success and encouragement to dream big.

title: LOCAL HANDICRAFTS FOR WOMEN EMPOWERMENT
description: Homeland Development Initiative Foundation ("HDIF") aims to initiate, facilitate, and nurture sustainable development initiatives in Armenian communities. One of its main projects is a grass root, non-profit organization dedicated to the creation of jobs for women in the regions of Armenia, using traditional techniques and materials.

title: Psycho Social support for Ebola victims
description: IsraAID in partnership with the first lady in Sierra Leone will conduct a 2 year training program that will focus on MHPSS- (Mental Health Psycho-Social Support) with the aim of building a national network of service providers.

title: Raise awareness of Child Marriages in Pakistan
description: This project will create momentum for preventing child marriages in Sindh province of Pakistan. Faith leaders and journalists will be trained. Awareness will be raised through interesting theatre stories about the harmful effects of child marriages and new laws passed against child marriages would be imparted to adolescent boys and girls students and their teachers, parents. Social, electronic and print media campaign and utilization of IEC material would also complement the campaign.

title: Empower Women and Save Lives through Cookstoves
description: Adoption of high efficiency cookstoves can save lives, empower women, and improve the environment.  WEEMA International will train 4 local cookstove associations on methods to make the Gonzye stove, an insulated fire stove made from clay, as well as purchase over 300 stoves for local distribution to our women's groups.  This large stove order will bring much needed money to the associations, help with marketing, and have a direct positive impact on the female stove recipients and their families.

title: Cycling for Bikes and Running for Shoes
description: On December 6th some M'Lop Tapang staff and friends participated in the annual Angkor Wat marathon and bike ride. Some cycled 100 kilometers and others joined in the running races.  They all sweated in out in the heat in an effort is raise funds to purchase 50 bicycles and 100 sports shoes/uniforms to give to the Cambodian children here.  But the challenge doesn't  stop there!  In true holiday spirit, a generous friend will be matching all funds donated on this page until December 31, 2014.

title: Educate Girls and Orphans in rural Uganda
description: There are millions of children living in extreme poverty in rural Uganda. They are mainly from poor farming communities that cannot afford basic needs. Girls, orphans and disabled children are most at risk. They lack access to education, basic healthcare, food and other basic needs. This exposes them to abject poverty, violence, abuse and forced marriages. We can stop this from happening by providing their school fees, basic healthcare, food, clean water, uniform and basic needs.

title: Campaign for Kids with Learning Disability inGhana
description: The campaign will enhance the quality of education and life for children with learning disabilities in Kasoa, Ghana by providing training for 100 teachers and 100 learning partners (peer teaching volunteers), organizing 10 radio talk shows, holding remedial clinics, and providing psychological counseling for 100 children with learning disabilities and parenting clinics for their  parents.

title: Microloans for Education/Tuition Fees
description: We're looking to help fund the most overlooked microloans on the lending platform we use - that is loans for educational purposes such as to pay for tuition for the borrower or the borrower's children (6-24 years old). It is a well proven fact that education provides future stability for both the individual and the family. This is one fantastic way to help lift a person or group of people out of poverty with just a help-out, not a hand-out. We enjoy a 99%+ repayment rate in our funds

title: Heal the Wound for our Innocent Children in DRC
description: We are raising money to support disadvantaged, vulnerable, orphaned, poor, disabled, children living on the street, children born following a rape incident, children living with a single mother who is a prostitute, children accused of witchcraft and were affected by war in Africa (Democratic Republic of Congo) in South Kivu, Bukavu. The money we are looking for is to help those children by paying they are education fees in yearly basis and to set up Computer training Centre.

title: Ambulance for our Thalassemia Care Centre
description: Due to daily incidents of terrorism in the biggest city of Pakistan, the requirement of Ambulances and Coffin Carrier Buses in Karachi has increased. If you are interested in supporting us for an Ambulance or Coffin Carrier Bus.

title: Gift Preschool Education to Children in India
description: This project seeks to raise funds for over 700 children who can be enrolled in our kindergarten programs in 400 villages in  Karnataka in 2016. These children are either orphans or belong to very poor families some of them with family incomes as low as $15 per month. These scholarships will ensure that their children are not denied access to education during the critical early formative years which are so crucial to their development and success in the later years.

title: Abundance School in Slums of Nairobi Kenya
description: Abundance School is currently fundraising for new text books to meet the requirements of  the new school curriculum.  Each of our six age-classes needs  new English, Mathematics, Environment, Hygiene and Creativity textbooks.  Thank you for your support at this time of transition and change.

title: Community Health Care Worker Project
description: The Community Health Care Worker Project has two phases. The First Phase involves medical treatment and medication for the elderly, expecting mothers and infants, in remote, difficult-to-reach rural communities and   the careful training of committed, dedicated and devoted medical students at our School of Health as the Community Health Care Workers. The Second Phase involves the construction of small Health Care Facilities in these rural areas to be operated by our trained medical students.

title: Give Me Another Chance
description: Give Me Another Chance (GAC) operates in slums of Nairobi, with people from all communities and ages living with, or struggling with, their HIV/AIDS diagnosis. Since the sudden death of Tiba's Chief Executive Daniel Marungu in September, 2018 the Tiba Board has been reviewing this important work. It has  notably been   supporting preventative work in Machokos with school children and has sponsored a 'Tiba marathon' and is planning breathwork sessions to increase vitality and wellbeing.

title: Cervical Cancer Project in Rural Bangladesh
description: In rural Bangladesh there are no cervical cancer screening programs despite the fact that over 50 million women are at risk and 17,686 cases are diagnosed and 10,362 deaths occur per year. This number will increase to over 31,000 new cases and 18,000 deaths per year by 2025. Help HOPE provide cervical cancer screening to rural communities in southeast Bangladesh.

title: Provide Gift & food to 700 Street Children
description: Under this project, 700 street & poor slum children will be given Nutrition food, Gift, New Dress, Lunch/Dinner, Toys & Happiness. The Program will be quite unique. For poor street & slum children all this is a dream. But will it be possible. A meal & gifts for 700 poor children life will become a golden memory.

title: Empower 200 Girls in Cameroon as Entrpreneurs
description: Quantitative analysis of the household survey of 2013 shows that; 40% of Cameroonians live in poverty. Women make up 52% of that population.If we do not focus on economically empower future female entrepreneurs, we may squander a historical opportunity to deliver fairness and equity to women. This project will build an entrepreneurship center in Mamfe, providing a rich training, start-up assistance and literacy support services to 200 marginalized female school drop-outs traumatized by poverty

title: Medical Care for Rural Guatemalan Families
description: Indigenous Guatemalan villagers face huge barriers to medical care. Desperately poor and remotely located, they cannot access the services provided by volunteer medical and surgical teams. Partner for Surgery removes those barriers by bringing the medical care to the villagers and accompanying them to the surgical sites.

title: Send 15 Orphaned Girls in Kenya to 1st grade!
description: This project will send 15 girls from Obunga slum in Kenya to their first year of school! Educating these young girls is the most effective way to combat the cycle of poverty.

title: Delay Marriage Promote Schooling for Ugandan Girls
description: Eradicate the harmful practice of child marriage through raising awareness, changing behaviour and empowering communities with the knowledge and tools needed to resist child marriage. Promote the effective implementation of strong laws and policies with a bearing on children especially the girl child and promote the fulfilment of their human rights. Develop and implement human developmental activities such as capacity building and entrepreneurial programs that would mitigate the effects

title: Preserving Himalayan Mountain Drops- India
description: "Preserve Mountain Drops" is our initiative to save and recharge 10 fresh water springs in district Solan of Himachal Pradesh, North India. These springs were perennial source of fresh water for residing population and local wild life. In recent times they have turned seasonal where few have even dried out. Their importance towards natural biodiversity cannot be measured. Under this project we will install counter measures to recharge and protect identified springs using holistic approach.

title: Help Me Get The Surgery I Need
description: Your support will allow this young boy to receive the surgery his family cannot afford and help him to  lead  a more normal life.

title: Helping local Somali children with Autism.
description: Columbus Ohio is home to over 35,000 Somali refugees. It is noted that Somali families are facing a higher rate of Autism diagnoses than the general population. The Columbus International Program wants to work to ensure that local service providers are able to provide care in a culturally sensitive manner. Also, through community outreach, the goal is to help Somali families better understand what Autism is, how to recognize its symptoms, and how to reach out for help.

title: Education for 10 mexican children with disability
description: We support 10 students with disabilities for a school year, which are deficient in the emotional, intellectual, language, motor skills, vision and hearing areas. . In the Special Child Care Centre, they offer group and individual therapies that allow them to develop their potential in school, social and family areas. Attend school Monday through Friday, from 8:00 until 13:00. Your parents and / or guardians are committed to rehabilitation, however, find it difficult to pay tuition.

title: Support 100  vulnerable girls  become self reliant
description: This project aims at breaking the vicious circle of household poverty, youth unemployment and enhancing access to sexual reproductive health services and information to 100 orphans and vulnerable girls  aged 10-18 years in Mityana district of Uganda,   by empowering them with vocational and life skills intended to  reduce their vulnerability to poor health, preventable diseases,early deaths and poor standards of living due to poverty.

title: Provide library books for orphans in India
description: This project has created libraries stocked with recreational reading books and encyclopedias for 28 orphanages and one school serving over 4,000 orphans and vulnerable children in India. We will continue to fund more libraries with your help. Reading can be the key to inspiring a love of learning and a hunger for education in children. Encyclopedias provide information and reading for pleasure kindles the imagination. Thank you for helping to ignite the love of learning through reading.

title: Support 50 rural schools to network with scholarly
description: This project is aiming to network 50 rural marginalized schools (10,000 students) in Vidarbha with nationally and Internationally scholar schools and to motivate and update them with various competitions, opportunities, exams, recent educational developments and education related stuff by publishing weekly newspaper dedicated to school education and activities.

title: Preventing life threatening infection in UK babies
description: Group B Strep is the most common cause of life-threatening infection in newborn babies. Our attendance at conferences for health professionals involved in maternity care is key to raising their knowledge and awareness about preventing group B strep infection. In 2015, Group B Strep Support aims to exhibit at 8 national maternity and healthcare conferences, attended by over 6000 delegates. We will have available free high-quality information packs to inform them and the families in their care.

title: Pathways to Education Mentoring Program
description: Your donation will be used to provide our 17 program sites with the support they need to deliver mentoring anto approximately 5,000 students across Canada who are at-risk of dropping out of high school. Pathways' mentoring program focuses on healthy social development of confidence building in a positive and safe environment that encourages youth to dream and plan for a successful future.

title: Teach 250 children basic reading and arithmetic
description: Despite 97% enrollment in schools, less than 50% of children can't read or do arithmetic at their grade level.  The absence of basic numeracy and literacy skills in the early grades creates an extremely weak foundation for future learning.  Pratham has innovated a model of 'learning camps' where children are tested and grouped by proficiency rather than grade or age and then taught basic reading and arithmetic.

title: Lakota Lands Recovery Project
description: The Lakota Lands Recovery Project began in 2003 to support Tribes and Individual American Indians in South Dakota to utilize their land base. Currently, of all the farms and ranches on South Dakota Reservations, less than 35% are operated by American Indians. The LLRP is working to reverse this statistic by providing grants to support Native land-based enterprises, providing technical support and outreach to Tribes and their members, educating the public and advocating for policy change.

title: Saving Retired Thoroughbred Racehorses
description: Second Chance Thoroughbreds saves thoroughbred racehorses from going to auction.  Once a racehorse enters into our program, we give them first lots of turn out to be able to be free and run around.  After a vet evaluation, we restart the thoroughbreds under saddle and retrain them for a suitable and desirable skill, i.e., jumping, dressage, western pleasure, trail riding.

title: Saving Lives, Human-Snake Conflict Mitigation
description: Even with under-reporting of snake bites, 126 people die each day due to snake-bites in India, while the total number of annual snake-bites are estimated to be around 1.4 million (bite to death ratio is 64:1). Victims are mainly farmers and farm laborers working or living in agricultural environments. Majority of these bites can be avoided with some basic precaution and proactive thinking. Awareness about right first aid and clinical treatment options can also bring down deaths or loss of limbs.

title: Support the self-determination for women in Gulu
description: Volunteer Action Network (Vac-Net) provides microfinance and educational opportunities to women recovering from brutal violence and poverty in northern Uganda. Our goal is poverty alleviation, increased human and food security and women's empowerment. Our intervention focuses on three areas in addition to economic development: literacy, leadership and health, as a way of addressing the systemic inequities that women face in post-conflict environment.

title: Tailoring workshop for young people in risk
description: Establishing a social enterprise for young people in risk /Roma, youngsters leaving social institutions, etc.,/. There they will have the chance for professional education and practice so they have new opportunities and chances for successful integration on the labor market and society.

title: Fresh Drinking water for Arsenic Affected Familes
description: Last year, nearly 100 people died due to Arsenic. At least one person of each family of this village is affected by the ARSENIC poison! In  Bishnupur village, Bangladesh there are only 2 hand tube-wells, which are contaminated by arsenic poison. There are 1000 families are living in this village with extreme poverty and they depends on these tube wells for drinking water. Through this project we will provide fresh water for families & schools, establish water plant & treatment for the patient

title: Sanitary Pads to Keep 600 Young Girls in School
description: For every year a girl stays in school, her future income increases with 10% to 20%. A woman invests 70% of her income in her family. We invest in girls, because investing in girls' means investing in a better future for everyone. We are offering social enterprise opportunities, creating  viable business for young girls training them to produce the Lucky Girl  Sanitary Pads. Distributed in rural schools to support girls to concentrate with their education and create an income stream for them.

title: Help prevent Ebola in Ghana-West Africa
description: The Anidaso Nsae Foundation (TANF) believes that we can help raise awareness of Ebola in West Africa to hopefully reduce the high risk of outbreak reaching neighbouring countries, like Ghana. TANF works closely alongside the youth community. We are going to train and educate our young people on Ebola, so that they can spread the word and their knowledge of the virus in local communities. To make this possible we need funding to pay for flyers and leaflets,T.shirts food and travel costs etc.

title: Sustainable Fuel Production for Poor Rural Women
description: Wood is a scarce resource worldwide and at the same time the rural poor, especially women, need income to support their families. Our goal is to promote sustainable human development and preserve our environment by training rural poor, wood-dependent communities to produce biomass briquettes which replaces wood as a fuel. By focusing the training particularly on rural women, they become empowered and are given the opportunity to contribute to the family income while conserving their environment.

title: TANF-Women/Girls Empowerment Programe
description: The Anidaso Nsae Foundation (TANF) gathers our women/girls together as one, to educate not just their children but themselves. We aim to develop them in understanding the significance of education and healthcare. As well as stimulating business like ideas, and cultivating how to start a successful business on their own, which will lead to a positive spark in their lives.

title: Winter wear for 55 worthy orphans
description: This project wil help to provide  some winter wear for our kids with your support. The Winter wear is sold by the migrants of Nepal. The cost of a blanket and a sweater is $ 25. All of this money will go directly towards a Winter wear, clothes and foot wear for the children to share, and any other important needs the children home deem pertinent. These are the ways we're seeking to fill in the hopes of injecting more creativity, fun, and happiness into the children's daily lives.

title: Quality education for Muslim Children in Madarsa
description: Integrated Approach to Technology in Education (ITE) in 20 Madarsa as a Model in Varanasi and Jaunpur  Madarsa students specially to girls.Improve Learning Processes and Pedagogy: The technology as an information processing tool takes away the traditional information giving role of the teacher. This basic functionality of technology by default requires the teachers to take a facilitative than an informative role. The ITE approach requires the teachers to play a central role.

title: Emergency Aid for Displaced People in Kurdish Iraq
description: This project will help the nearly 2 million Internally Displaced Peoples (IDPs) and refugees that are currently in the Kurdish Region of Iraq (KRI) after having fled from IS. The most pressing need today is 'winterization' - blankets, mattresses, coats, socks, warm clothes, and shoes. This project will also evaluate the long-term needs of these populations.

title: Support autistic children with drama in Glasgow
description: We are supporting families with children on the Autistic spectrum in Glasgow, by running free drama workshops. The project is based in an area of multi-levelled deprivation, and so we provide a free meal at the start of each session. We focus on social interaction and communication skills, and at the end of term would like to take the families to an autistic-friendly theatre performance.

title: Saving Kenya's Environment Through Family Planning
description: Kenya has one of the highest population growths in the world and has a poverty rate of 45%. As a result, Kenya's natural resources are dwindling! The Community Health Africa Trust (CHAT) is one of the few aid organizations providing innovative and FREE family planning services combined with ecological awareness education to underserved, often nomadic communities in central and northern Kenya. In turn, we conserve natural resources and reduce suffering - especially among women and children.

title: Help Ukrainian badly wounded soldiers to survive
description: Currently, at Mechnikov Dnipropetrovsk Hospital (Ukraine, Eastern Europe) there are about 100 seriously wounded Ukrainian military on the treatment who have suffered from the Russian aggression in the East of Ukraine.  The Hospital urgently needs in medical preparations "Octaplex" and "Tachocomb" that are used for blood clotting.

title: Donate a Blanket & Save a life this winter appeal
description: There is hard winter season every year in Bihar, where a lot single women and poorest old age person die due to lack of winter warm clothing. But government, local governance and society don't take care for facilities to these vulnerable old age persons. If they fall ill, also there are no one who take care and provide medical facilities. They urgently require warm clothing i.e. blanket to prevent from death due to hard cold. They live a very hard and miserable life in winter season.

title: Increasing access to Early Childhood Development
description: Nhaka Foundation channels support to preschools utilizing early learning centers or preschools as an entry point. We focus particularly on the needs of orphans and vulnerable children.  Nhaka Foundation partners with communities to renovate dilapidated classrooms that are turned into ECD classes. The classes are painted, floors relaid, broken windows replaced, new doors put in place,leaking roofs fixed and a new coat of paint is applied plus artistic drawings of whatever the children want to see

title: Medical care for escapers from Ukrainian crisis
description: Your donation will help get medical assistance and save lives of kids from the area of crisis in Ukraine.  Thousands of children from the crisis area are no longer able to get medical care in hometowns. As little Diego from Donetsk who is sick with severe genetic disease - thalassemia and needs regular blood transfusions while waiting for expensive non-relative bone marrow transplantation.  Transplantations are not covered by government and families no longer can fundraise in vulnerable country.

title: Help a young student to be trained in Word
description: Given the problems that Mexico faces of youth unemployment and the alarming threat of organized crime in young people whom dont study or work and live in poverty conditions. We will train 1000 young students in Word finishing in June 2015. With the aim of raise their level of skills. With this we looked for to give them the tools to get a better job and improve their quality of life. All of them will receive a certificate with official recognition that validates their knowledge

title: Build houses for 20 grandmothers in rural Kenya.
description: Women Fighting Aids in Kenya (WOFAK) aims at improving the quality of life for grandmothers severely affected or infected by HIV/AIDS in Kochia village, Homabay County in rural Kenya. The project will construct and/or renovate houses for 20 grandmothers to give them permanent decent housing and train local villagers to provide psycho-social support. This will enable the grandmothers to provide a homely environment for their AIDS- orphaned grandchildren.

title: The DC STEM Fair
description: The DC STEM Fair is an incredibly engaging science program in Washington, D.C. for all students in the District to compete in competitions and experience hands-on science activities.

title: Sponsor a membership, change a life
description: It's easy to backslide - We connect builders in Port-au-Prince to incentives to keep building safe houses, despite pressure from untrained bosses still using unsafe methods. Membership in a professional network called REZO ("network" in Haitian Creole) will connect these builders to job placement, apprenticeships, continuing education, and lower prices for building materials. This project will fund 25 builders' memberships, combined with support from local businesses and the Haitian government.

title: ECONOMIC EMPOWERMENT TO 100 WIDOWS OF IMALINYI
description: This project aims to empower economically 100 widows in Imalinyi Division through beekeeping project.    Each widow will be provided  with  5  beehives to start Beekeeping business. Honey  and its  products harvested   will  improve  their  economy, physical,  social  and their livelihood. Help us break poverty circle, diseases, and malnutrition by empowering economically these widows.

title: Support and Care for 40 Orphans in Africa
description: Orphans supported by Centre for HIV/AIDS and STD Research (CHISTRE) face severe physical, psychosocial, and legal challenges, rendering them disadvantaged and undereducated, and in turn more vulnerable to HIV infection. CHISTRE began to offer services to them currently in 11 communities. Working in partnership with the community and other philanthropist, CHISTRE takes a comprehensive, integrated, community-based program to support the Orphans.

title: Ebola Outbreak: West Africa
description: To date, officials are reporting nearly 10,000 deaths in West Africa due to this horrific virus.  With the death toll rising, MAP International continues to respond to the largest and most deadly Ebola outbreak in history by providing infectious disease protection suits and supplies to protect those treating the infected.

title: Step Up for 200 Students in Guatemala
description: Mayan Families provides opportunities for education to thousands of students through a variety of programs. This project will provide the basic yet critical necessity of shoes for rural, indigenous Guatemalan students who do not have have sponsorships through our Student Sponsorship Program. This will allow students to step forward on their path of education, which can equip them with the skills and knowledge to escape the crushing poverty that so many of their families face.

title: Bring smile to 300villagers Benin with beekeeping!
description: This project aims to use the modern beekeeping as a tool of environmental awareness, for wealth creation therefore the fight against poverty. In effect, this project aims at the creation of a value chain beekeeping by the development of the products of the hive (honey, pollen, propolis and wax) for the benefit of 300 villagers in the rural commune of Dassa-Zoume in Center of BENIN in West Africa.

title: Healthcare for 2500 Syrian refugees, south Lebanon
description: We deliver vital primary health care services to a widely dispersed group of refugees. They have escaped the fighting in Syria and survive in appalling conditions, in makeshift tents and abandoned buildings. Women and children are particularly vulnerable, with high levels of disease and disability, and struggle to access the local health system. Our mobile clinic, staffed by a doctor, nurse and health educator, visits each settlement weekly, providing free healthcare, vaccinations and education.

title: Free Education for 150 poor girls in Pakistan
description: Bola having population 6000, is remote village of Punjab, Pakistan. Due to poverty, the illiteracy rate particularly of women is very high. A well equipped school has been established with support of donors. Operational cost was supposed to be met with tuition fees. Unfortunately the poor peasant families cannot bear the nominal fees which resulted in very low enrolment in the school. A monthly support of $10 by adopting a child can change the fate of this village.

title: Training Peacebuilders in Yemen
description: The International Center for Religion & Diplomacy will conduct a 1 year training and capacity building program in Abyan, Yemen for a select team of 44 indigenous peacebuilders to help them lead a self-sustaining network of 250 Peace Committees that will provide non-violent conflict resolution and mediation services in their communities.  This project will empower a civilian network of peacebuilders in Abyan where judicial and legal systems are weak, and the risk of violent conflict is high.

title: Support for Children in Poverty in South Africa
description: Our Early Childhood Development Programme is our doorway of influence into the destitute township communities in Port Elizabeth, SA. We partner with disadvantaged Early Learning Centres to ensure that hungry children are fed, that they receive an education, that unqualified facilitators are mentored/trained, that sick (HIV/AIDS) children receive medication and that any maintenance or building revamping is sorted. Our teams create stability and accountability for these poverty-stricken places.

title: Educate One Empower Thousands
description: The We women foundation enables the women of Burma to make and influence policy decisions within their communities that would otherwise be made by others.  Through our campaign - Educate One, Empower Thousands - We women is committed to raising awareness and funds for supporting women from marginalized ethnic communities of Burma in their pursuit of meaningful educational and career objectives thereby promoting women's leadership in a critical moment in Burma's history.

title: Long Term Initiatives to Typhoon Haiyan Victims
description: The estimated damage of typhoon Haiyan is 34 billion pesos.  With this tremendous devastation, every recovery effort must be sustained to achieve greater impact to victims' lives. That is why CJFI will continue its long term recovery program to reach out more number of victims and gain wider scope of communities assisted.  This initiative will cover the municipalities including Tacloban City with coastal barangays facing Leyte Gulf with thousands of fishing families who were badly affected.

title: Diagnosing Dementia Faster
description: Dementia is the leading cause of death in women in the UK. Help Alzheimer's Research UK to support pioneering female scientists battling to cure dementia.

title: Virtual Classroom: Multi-literacy tools for all!
description: We are very excited to launch a brand new website that offers curated arts-integrated lessons and activities for educators, parents and concerned adults. Arts-based multiple literacy techniques can reach learners in every classroom, household and community. This new tool will put valuable lessons at the fingertips of users, organized for easy search by subject area and age group.  Expert Story Tapestries artists will give direct feedback, answer questions, and offer online courses.

title: Literacy for better employment
description: Cobb Literacy Council in conjunction with its parent company, Cobbworks, realizes the necessity of a literate workforce to support Cobb's economic development. We continue to serve the community by: Establishing Adult Basic Education and GED preparation throughout Cobb County; increasing the availability of a literate, prepared workforce; providing dictionaries and thesauruses to underserved students in Title I schools; training volunteers to help support the vast needs of our adult learners.

title: Reduce violence & stress for 60 students in RI
description: Our nation is at a critical point in recognizing the value of non-cognitive skills to support the rigor of academics & life. Author Paul Tough says optimism, social agility, and resilience are the core skills possessed by at-risk children who overcame adversity. ResilientKids' innovative social and emotional learning program works with students during the school day, promoting the development of life-long skills that will serve them now and into adulthood as they become our future leaders.

title: Help Feed and Send to School Poor Kids in the Phil
description: The Children's Joy Foundation, Inc. (CJFI) has been helping thousands of destitute children in the Philippines since 1998 by feeding, clothing, providing them with decent shelter, and sending them to school.  The primary intention of this noble work is to help these children reach their potentials to become strong pillar in nation building. CJFI established and maintain 7 Child Care Residential Homes run by professional Social Workers, Psychologists, and educators to carry out this mission.

title: Nirim Youth Village Individual Treatment Program
description: The village absorbs boys and girls aged 15-16 who have been referred under court order or who are at high risk. The youth village has a school for survival, preparation for army service, personal development and leadership. The aim is to offer rehabilitation in order that the youth may return to the education system and a normative track, equipping them with coping and life skills.

title: Ruach Nashit - Economic Independence for Women
description: Ruach Nashit - economic independence for women, victims of violence - assists abused women to get out of the cycle of violence by developing economic skills and personal growth. The organization comprises of women victims of violence, men and women from the academic world, business women and many volunteers from all circles of life.

title: Galgal Day Care Centers & Someone to Run With
description: The Galgal Day Care Centers in Jerusalem and Someone to Run With in Tel Aviv give support and assistance for homeless and at-risk youth aged 18-26 with the aim of providing a basic humanitarian solution  - food, hot shower, clothing and medical services.

title: Children at Risk - Rehabilitative Education
description: The organization helps children in boarding schools in areas not funded by the State in two specific subjects: a lobby campaigning for the rights of children and educational projects, treatment and rehabilitation e.g. individual tuition for basic skills of reading, writing and arithmetic.

title: Beit Hagalgalim - Provision of Weekend Breaks
description: Beit Hagalgalim - Provision of weekend Breaks provides respite for special needs children in one of five centers manned by volunteers, encouraging the development of social skills, personal empowerment and creating a leadership among adolescents with physical disabilities.

title: Help 1,600 Nicaraguan Farmers Rise Out Of Poverty
description: This project will allow 1,600 Nicaraguan farmers to get the financial assistance they need to expand their farms and work their way out of poverty. Farmers living in remote, rural areas of Nicaragua do not have access to basic financial services such small loans, financial education and technical assistance. WCCN is cooperating with a local microfinance institution to provide these services. These services and the community's work ethic will help this community bring itself out of poverty.

title: Ending Abuse, Saving Lives, Stop Violence Now!
description: Every year hundreds of women and children who are victims of domestic violence and human trafficking come to our shelter seeking refuge. Over 3,500 people call our crisis line for counseling and safety. We provide victims of violence a SAFE way out, intensive therapy, counseling, education support, job and housing placement, and long term follow-up care. We raise awareness and educate communities by providing workshops and presentations on domestic violence and human trafficking.

title: Smart phones for 100 Ebola health workers
description: Aid organizations fighting Ebola desperately need faster access to data from the field. Journey has built an app for health workers and volunteers, which saves time and provides decision makers with instant access to data. Already, 20 phones have been purchased for two NGOs in West Africa, which are already running the app. The project aims to give another 100 health workers low-end Android phones, with the app installed.

title: Educate street children in rural India
description: We believe in equal education, especially important in slums where the uneducated are targets for opportunists. 10 years after India's Right to Education Act guaranteed education for all up to 10 std, 75,000 children are still missing from our state classrooms. Our schools are vital in encouraging & supporting children to complete12 std & enroll in higher education. Counselling, personal development & extracurricular activities  provide extra knowledge, self-belief & hope.

title: Give Farm training to Indian HIV Families
description: It is harsh existing below the poverty line in rural India with drought and famine affecting your livelihood.  HIV spreads fast and goes undiagnosed, especially in areas where education rates are low.  In these circumstances people with HIV don't have access to life saving medication needed.  Our 25 acre farm allows 'untouchable' families to live together learning how to grow produce, raise cattle and live self sufficiently.  Our produce also supports our ADOPT, EDUCATE & RESCUE projects nearby

title: Education of Tamil War Affected Students
description: Tamil community in North and East of Sri Lanka was left with empty hands at the end of civil war. Needs of the community is much higher than the resources available. Most of the affected students found to be from women-headed families struggling to survive and educate their children. We have identified eligible university and grade school students to receive supplemental education funds so that they are not forced into labor and giving up education because of poverty.

title: Better health for 100 HIV+ adolescents in India
description: Despite progress made in the AIDS response, evidence suggests that adolescents living with HIV are falling behind because they don't receive the attention and services they require. According to UNAIDS, AIDS-related mortality among adolescents has increased by 50% globally in the past seven years, even while it fell in all other age groups. Our project will reach HIV+ adolescents in India with support services, education, and care they need to manage HIV and lead healthy and stigma-free lives.

title: STEM Education in Africa: Changing the Equation
description: We believe that the entire world will benefit when young people in all countries have the opportunity to pursue and realize their dreams. Today, opportunity is linked to competence in science and technologies and the culture of innovation. iNERDE teaches STEM and innovation skills to African youth. We aim to create leaders with the knowledge and confidence to bring their nations to the world table as equal partners.

title: Support Minority Hindu BAJANI Communities
description: Association for Humanitarian Development decided to support 100 Bajani families residing near Tando Muahmmed Khan, the families are poor & by professionally migration from one place to another place. their children and women illiterate and economic situation of BAJANI communities are very poor. AHD wants to empower one hundred communities towards sustainable development

title: Simple Surgery to restore Sight to Ethiopians
description: Orbis plans to conduct simple eye surgeries in remote regions of Ethiopia, in the hope to cure thousands of people suffering from the painful, blinding, and life-destroying eye disease - trachoma.

title: Distributing Antibiotics to Prevent Blindness
description: Trachoma, a bacterial infection of the eye which can cause blindness affects many people in impoverished regions. It is most common in children. However, there is an antibiotic available costing just 15 cents, that is effective in preventing the disease.

title: Empower 100 Child Brides in Pakistan
description: More than one-third of maternal deaths in Pakistan occurred among child brides ages of 14 and 17 years. Child marriage endangers girls' lives and limits their potential to get empowerment. Jaag Welfare Movement will provide education, skill, healthcare and gathered them in vibrant groups in rural areas of South Punjab for empowerment. This initiative will also be the collaborative & integrated approach to end child marriage by awareness raising and advocacy for change in laws and policy.

title: Let's Get 100 Turkish Youth Off the Street
description: In Turkey, 3.7 Million youth are out of school or jobless. That's one third of the population between 15-29 years old. We want to reduce that number by 100.

title: Sports & Education Center for James-Town (Ghana)
description: The construction of this center will give 250 at-risk youth an opportunity to a better life. Through sports, academic support (Education) and personal development, these children will be encouraged to become agents of change in their community. This project is seeking to replicate DUNK's Nima Project where 89% of members have improved in Math and English; 88% of parents have noted positive change in their children's behavior. Members were crowned 2013 league champs (U13), 2014 LCS Champs.

title: Orphaned Starfish Youth Computer Training Center
description: Over 400 children and adolescents encounter obstacles such as prostitution drugs gangs and other negative lives on the streets. By giving children access to a computer and the Internet, we are giving them a window to the outside world, access to vast amounts of information, a way to connect with each other, and a springboard into their future.

title: Eco-Soap Bank: Lifesaving Soap for Cambodia
description: In the modern era, 1 in 8 children in Cambodia die from a preventable illness, before they reach their 5th birthday.  In rural areas, 75% of Cambodians lack access to soap for hand washing. In the fight against preventable illness, the single-most powerful action one can take is hand-washing with soap. This practice can reduce the risk of death, or infection, by up to 60 percent. For an item which can have such a great effect on village communities, soap simply cannot go to waste.

title: Help 10,000 Pregnant Moms survive childbirt in NIG
description: This project will provide free clean birth and newborn kits to 10,000 Nigerian pregnant mothers living in rural communities thus saving them from giving birth in a dirty and unclean environment at homes and dirty traditional homes by quacks who may put the at risk of infection, other complications and death due to poverty and inability to purchase delivery items or pay for cost of delivery. This project will save more than 20,000 lives of both mothers and newborn in Nigerian rural communities

title: Jugaad (Innovation) Lab for Disadvantaged Girls
description: We seek to provide a much-needed space for young girls who come from socially and economically disadvantaged backgrounds to ignite their interest in STEM (Science Technology Engineering Mathematics). A lab for girls to continue to spark their imagination and aid their intellectual growth and development; a place where they can tinker, build, break and rebuild stuff to learn through hands-on work and experimentation to enable them to develop a keen eye towards problems in their communities.

title: Education for poor children on Tonle Sap Siem Riep
description: More than 2,400 children are estimated to be missing out on schooling because they live with their parents on small boats or homes on the Tonle Sap Lake for months at a time, where the parents try to earn a living by fishing. These families can't afford to send their children to school because of the cost of transport, books and uniforms. By providing the means of education, you can help break this cycle of poverty and give these children opportunities for a brighter future.

title: Paamonim - Economic Guidance for Families
description: Pa'amonim - Personal long-term guidance for families experiencing economic difficulties with the aim of getting to a point where finances are balanced according to sound decision making based on criteria, help in finding debt solutions. In this way the families may extricate themselves from the cycle of poverty.

title: "Lehoshit Yad" Support & Assistance for Children
description: This project establishes a holistic support system for sick children and their families including home visits between treatments, accompanies them to treatment while giving activities and play, helps with school studies, provides a social solution for isolated children, and organizes fun days making their wishes come true.

title: The Witness Theater by Holocaust Survivors
description: The Witness Theater - Holocaust Survivors meet with 2nd and 3rd generations via therapeutic drama and self -expression.

title: Kesher, the Home for Special Families
description: Kesher, the Home for Special Families - there are more than 330,000 children in Israel with special needs who require a range of different services. Kesher operates an information center and counselling for these families throughout the country including information regarding rights, counselling and mediation.

title: Green Course - Developing the Next Generation
description: Green Course is a program for developing the next generation of leadership for environmental organizations and activism in Israel.

title: Support a Small Charity? Why Not Support 8,175?
description: Every charity has to start somewhere. Skills and knowledge required to start and run a charity are diverse and often inaccessible. So in 2007 Patrick Cox, our Founder, had a simple but exceptional idea- a Small Charities Coalition to share skills and resources between charities through collaboration and partnerships. We have now facilitated 352 supporter-small charity matches, free training, a helpline and online resources. But we've only just begun. Support 8,175 small charities today.

title: Send 80 HIV-infected Children to Sanyuka Camp
description: In 2015, 80 HIV-positive Ugandan children aged 9 to 11 will attend the 5-day residential Sanyuka Camp, which focuses on healthy living and building self-esteem. Sanyuka Camp is a collaborative effort between Baylor-Uganda and Paul Newman's Serious Fun Global Partnership Initiative. Your generous support will ensure the successful continuation of Sanyuka Camp and will directly impact the lives of some of Uganda's most vulnerable-but also some of its most promising-young people.

title: Build More Literate Communities in Rural Honduras
description: Un Mundo's Literacy Connections program empowers people in rural communities of northern Honduras to transform their own educational opportunities - by training local citizens to teach literacy workshops, lead book clubs, invent dynamic story-time activities, and even perform literacy-themed community theater. By providing training, resources, dynamic activities, and a regional library, you can help put the power of learning into local people's hands!

title: Supply 500 Books to Courageous Students
description: Since our founding in 1991, the Courage Curriculum has positively impacted the academic performance of more than 150,000 sixth and ninth grade students in the Boston Public Schools and surrounding public, parochial, charter, pilot and private schools and religious academies.   This project puts 500 books into the hands of the courageous children that take part in the curriculum. It will allow for more classrooms to become involved and supply teachers with the tools they need.

title: Global Autism Project for Teacher Training
description: This project will launch an initiative to provide training in evidence-based services to professionals working in the field of autism in under-served communities. The program will provide clinical and administrative support and training to these professionals in order for them to increase the quality and quantity of services for those who need it most. Our aim to is empower communities to rally around their members on the autism spectrum.

title: Stop Ebola: UNICEF Responds to a Region in Crisis
description: The Ebola outbreak in West Africa is the deadliest in history. More than 10,000 cases have been reported since March, and nearly 5,000 people have died, with children being Ebola's most vulnerable victims.   We can stop Ebola. UNICEF is at work on the ground across West Africa - airlifting supplies, training health workers and caring for children and their families.   With early treatment, children and their families can survive this disease. Help UNICEF stop Ebola.

title: Christmas for 250 at-risk youth Wichita Falls, TX
description: This project will allow 250 at-risk young people in Wichita Falls, TX to have and experience a Christmas that is simply not possible without your help.  They live below the poverty level, many times on the streets, and in several cases are illegally sold for a parent's drug habit.  We can help give back HOPE where there is great despair, food, clothing and adults who will stand in the gap for them on many levels.  WE NEED YOUR HELP PLEASE.

title: Assistance to Pediatric Departments in Moldova
description: This project serves an extension to Support Moldovan Children With Cancer, our first project on GlobalGiving. Support Moldovan Children With Cancer worked with the Institute of Oncology in Chisinau, Moldovan capital. When project was fully funded, we decided to open a wider program to include other pediatric departments of Moldovan hospitals to serve needs of young patients, their families, as well as medical community, in a more comprehensive and encompassing way.

title: Give GIRLS in India a CHANCE at life
description: Not all parents in the north Indian state of Haryana think the way SANJAY THINKS, hence, there are 834 girls for every 1000 boys. This imbalance has been created by an AVERSION to having DAUGHTERS, assisted in recent times by advances in medical technology. It is the starkest possible representation of the LOW VALUE & STATUS OF GIRLS, denying them a place in the world.  We are working on the ground with families, community members & health workers to tackle the underlying causes of this problem.

title: Educate 400 Deprived Children for a Year in India
description: The vision of Chaitanya Charitable Trust is providing quality education and nutritional food to 400 marginalized children in 10 slum area for a year.
