Every day two hours education after school time with innovative model and "Learn with Fun" concept to rag picker, beggar, child labor, HIV/AIDS, out of school and govt. school students.We want to make difference in our slum students' lives by providing them vital academic information, skills, strategies, and by enhancing positive social growth.

title: Services for Women Survivors of Violence in Aizwal
description: Through this project, Foundation for Social Transformation (FST) will work with Lalthanzami, a domestic violence survivor turned women's rights activist from Aizwal, Mizoram, India, to establish a resource center on women's rights within the safe home that she runs, train 10 women as leaders working to prevent and eradicate violence against women in her community, and expand the community outreach to provide services to survivors of violence against women and build awareness on women's rights.

title: Bright Christmas 2014
description: On Bonaire there are many less fortunate children who don't get a toy to play with this Christmas. With your help, you can put a smile on the faces of these children.

title: Making shoes for barefoot children in Mozambique
description: 300 million children around the world can't afford shoes and are going barefoot. This puts them at risk of infection, and even death, from soil-transmitted diseases that enter their bodies through cuts in unprotected feet. Our project 1) teaches Mozambicans to make shoes for their children 2) provides medical care to those with foot disease 3) teaches preventive hygiene and 4) establishes a sustainable industry for economic empowerment  These steps will have a positive impact on health outcomes.

title: Help Protect Free-Roaming Black Rhino in Namibia
description: Namibia has the world's largest free-roaming population of the endangered black rhino in its remote and rugged north-west. That means these rhino are in the wild, not restricted to a specific park or reserve. Amazing! The Namibia Nature Foundation is working with local community-based conservancy organisations and Save the Rhino Trust to extend the Rhino Ranger program into an area not covered by regular rhino patrols. The goal is to fund a Rhino Ranger patrol in the field for a full year.

title: Education Project for 50 marginalized Liberian
description: This project will admit 50 Liberian youth who carry significant psychological burdens, compounded by social exclusion arising from their loss of family members and previous affiliations with conflict-participant groups, through the provision of vocational education, transforming them from excluded and burdened dependents into included and empowered citizens and productive workers and entrepreneur and they will in turn demonstrate to their peers and their communities that change is possible.

title: Help 60 UK children reach eye cancer treatment
description: Skylah is one of 60 children diagnosed in the UK each year with the aggressive eye cancer retinoblastoma. Every three weeks her family, like others supported by the Childhood Eye Cancer Trust (CHECT), travel 100s of miles to only two UK specialist treatment centres to save Skylah's sight, eyes and life. Fearful for her child's life, Skylah's mother also doesn't know how she will afford this journey for the next four years. Help us give her GBP 200 to make her life with cancer a little bit easier

title: Fund Future Leaders from the US, Japan, and Korea!
description: International Student Conferences (ISC) facilitates two academic and cultural exchange programs organized by university students in the U.S.,Japan, Korea:and the Japan-America Student Conference (JASC) and the Korea-America Student Conference (KASC) . With rising tensions across the Pacific, the importance of a strong relationship cannot be overstated. ISC programs provide an intensive, month-long experience to promote peace by furthering mutual understanding, friendship and trust.

title: Help Support the Fight against Blood Cancers #5639
description: Cure leukemia, lymphoma, Hodgkin's disease and myeloma, and improve the quality of life of patients and their families.

title: 75 Scholarships for At-Risk Youth in Guayaquil
description: This project will fund in-kind scholarships for 75 at-risk high school students in Guayaquil, Ecuador. We believe that education is the path to a better future and that all youth have the right to a good education. In Ecuador only 60% of students reach secondary school as many are forced to drop out for economic or other reasons. Our scholarships provide the materials necessary for success in school, as well as alleviate the economic burden of families putting their children through school.

title: Happy Chickens for Food Security and Environment
description: Rural communities in Fiji rely on subsistence farming and fishing for most of their needs. Chicken breeds available are imported and are expensive, bred for factory farming and poorly adapted to village conditions. This project will bring in productive heritage breeds of chickens that are well adapted to local free-range conditions, establishing breeding flocks and focusing on providing chicks at cost to communities. Local feeds will also be a major focus: coconut, cassava, moringa, etc

title: Promoting SRHR of among 5000 youth in TN, India
description: Protect 5000 youth from STI through enhancement of their understanding of Sex and Sexuality related issues and an orientation on SRHR.   Create a sustainable peer based first contact referral process for those youth with vulnerable sexual behavioral patterns. Equip 200 youth (each year 100) to serve as peers and ensure that the vulnerable youth are identified counselled, treated, and offered legal help where and integrated into mainstream institutional programmes sustained support over 2 years

title: Expand Our Vital Programs for Refugees in Uganda
description: HOCW provides education, counseling and business opportunities for over 340 refugees living in Ndejje, Uganda. We are committed to serving any local refugee in need and have outgrown our current space. $15,000 will enable us to move to a larger space down the road and to double the number of refugees we are able to serve. Counselors will be able to conduct therapy in private rooms, English teachers will be able to take on more students and we can include more children in our kids' programs.

title: WORI Uganda Domestic Violence Shelter
description: Due to the overwhelming amount of abuse women face in Eastern Uganda and the lack of facilities available to them, WORI Uganda wishes to construct a shelter to provide temporary refuge and basic necessities for  victims of domestic violence. In addition, it will provide psychological counseling and emergency medical care to the victims of domestic violence, as well as providing legal aid for the victims of gender domestic violence, whilst raising awareness on domestic violence

title: Provide clean water to 5000 villagers in Ghana
description: The town of Dawukwa, in the Central Region of Ghana, with approximately 5000 residents, has no access to clean water. The only water supply consists of a small stream of polluted water which is now being used for drinking, bathing and washing. The number of Cholera cases has risen alarmingly and there is an absolute need to establish a bore hole and a filtering system to make drinkable water available.

title: Early learning integration Centre for 400 Children
description: The EARLY LEARNING INTEGRATION & TELECONFERENCING CENTER (ELI&TC ) is for children (ages 6-15).  The Center will provide non-residential curriculum and Information Communication Technology (ICT) lesson integration and early intervention services for rural school children to use the Internet for collaborative education and sharing of modern resources in education development in the Central and South western region of Uganda.

title: Ambulance for Liberian Villages Impacted By Ebola
description: Liberians are dying every single day because of its failing health infrastructure. Ambulances are needed as the country had just 10 when the outbreak first started. Some people call more than 30 times before getting an ambulance to them to get medical treatment for Ebola. We want to get Liberians in rural villages an ambulance now so that we can save as many lives as possible. No one should have to die waiting for an ambulance.

title: Change the Lives of orphans,Poor children in India
description: Theressa Home for children aims to changing the lives of Orphans and providing shelter, food, Clothing, Medical care, Education, love for orphans and needy children. Now Theressa home have 23 children.These children belong to really poor segment of the society. We want to give them hope,opportunity and bright future.

title: Sustainable Water Filtration in Guatemala
description: GlobeMed at Cornell partners with AMMID, Asociacion Maya-Mam de Investigacion y Desarollo, to collaboratively create and implement sustainable projects to improve the health of the Maya-Mam of San Marcos, Guatemala.

title: Educate and Nourish 50 Students in Rural Malawi
description: This project provides critical small group and private tutoring through EKARI's Tutoring Program to students in southern Malawi, allowing them to receive 1:1 attention that they do not receive in their classrooms of typically 75 students or more per teacher. Without nutrition, students cannot focus on their studies. This project also provides nutritional meals during small group tutoring as well as additional food to supplement students' poor school diet through EKARI's 3 Meals a Day Program.

title: After School Programme for Underserved Children
description: Of the world's poorest 1.2 billion people, India is home to 33%. It largely affects the already vulnerable populations of children and comprises of a lack of resources especially education and extracurricular activities.This project is a two stage - poverty alleviation programme that aims to provide 200 underserved children of all ages from the slums of New Delhi, India with with a range of after school services.

title: Education for Deaf or Blind Children in Cambodia
description: Krousar Thmey is the only organization providing formal education to deaf, blind, visually and hearing-impaired children in Cambodia. The NGO has 5 schools that provide free education. For more than 25 years Krousar Thmey has contributed to ending social exclusion of disabled people.

title: Music tuition for 70 disadvantaged London children
description: Without free access to learning music, there is little opportunity for disadvantaged children to engage and benefit from learning a musical instrument. To address this issue, this project provides free music tuition and instruments to 70 disadvantaged and socially isolated young people, aged 5 to 19 years.

title: Rescuing and Empowering Child Brides
description: In southern Africa one in seven girls is married before age 15. Child marriage is a human rights violation with serious consequences for negative health and social impacts which include higher rates of maternal and infant mortality, sexually transmitted infection, social separation and gender based violence, higher risk of HIV infection, poverty, early termination of education. This project will help prevent and prohibit child marriage and empower girls.

title: Train 24 global artists for Edinburgh Festivals
description: This Visiting Arts project helps artists and creative businesses in Southern Africa, Trinidad and Tobago and the Pacific Islands grow their income, networks and markets through international working that helps them support both their artistic practice and their families. Our aim is to train and prepare 24 artists to be able to showcase their work at the Visiting Arts Producers' event at the Edinburgh International Festival 2016 where they will gain exposure, connections and expand their reach.

title: Educating designers to cut waste out of fashion
description: The Redress Design Award is a sustainable fashion design competition challenging emerging fashion designers to create clothing with minimal textile waste. The programme raises awareness of environmental issues and sustainable fashion amongst industry stakeholders, and provides designers with the information and practical skills to be part of the solution. In addition it supports emerging sustainable designers with career development and business opportunities.

title: Improve Education & Health of Cambodian Families
description: This project will provide daily nutrition to stop the cycle of malnutrition, maternal health classes to reduce rates of mortality, and community education training and support for 253 families in the villages of Sre Robong and Arak Svay, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia.

title: Build a Medical Clinic for 5 villages in Uganda
description: This project will build a Primary Care Clinic in central Uganda, providing much needed medical care and health education to Ugandans living in rural villages.

title: Waggin' Wheels Rescue From High Kill Shelters
description: This project will save countless lovable pets who have been misplaced due to life circumstances, abandoned, neglected, and last chancers whose time are up and at risk being euthanized.   We have commitments from no kill rescues to accept hundreds of dogs a year in other states. These rescues have plentiful fosters and prequalifed adoptive families ready and waiting for their new family member to arrive. We just need to get them out of the shelter and to these safe havens.

title: Harm Reduction for 3500 people in Moscow
description: ARF needs your support to continue providing daily lifesaving health and human rights services, health materials, legal advise and support to  disadvantaged people who use drugs in Moscow, Russia.

title: Send Teenagers with Cancer on an Activity Holiday
description: The Activity Holiday will give teenagers with cancer the chance to spend a week in a positive environment doing challenging activities surrounded by people who understand.

title: Give the Gift of Education to Children in Poverty
description: Children from poverty-stricken families require school supplies, uniforms, and shoes in order to attend public school in Costa Rica.  This volunteer-run scholarship project started in 2013, and now provides help for up to 30 students in San Ramon. Some of these students are in their eighth year in the program, and with your help we can continue to raise over $14,000 per year to keep these students on track to graduate high school. As of 2019, nine of our students have graduated.

title: Potable water for 400 in rural Mexico
description: The Independence Aquifer in central Mexico is in a permanent state of decline and contaminated with toxic levels of arsenic and fluoride, which has led to irreversible health complications like dental & crippling skeletal fluorosis in local communities.  This project will provide the training, materials and construction of 29 rainwater-harvesting cisterns and 44 water filter systems for 4 schools, 20 families, and 1 training institute - providing sustainable, safe drinking water for 400+ people.

title: HELP EMPLOY  VULNERABLE GIRLS
description: Kayayei are unskilled, 16-24 year-old girls who run away from the northern parts of Ghana to Accra. They sleep rough in open places and get raped, beaten up, robbed; have unwanted pregnancies and unsafe abortions; and many become single parents or prostitutes. We will train 120 girls, age 18-24, annually as housekeepers, cooks, cleaners and babysitters and place them in the hospitality industry, organizations and homes or help them start their own businesses to keep them safe and out of poverty.

title: Seeds and Skills for Women to Grow Vegetables
description: We enable access to quality seeds, training, and resources to empower women in agriculture! Women farmers produce more than half the food in developing nations yet own less than 2% of land and have limited access to quality seeds, improved technologies, agricultural resources, and training. We partner and work collaboratively with women's groups to improve food security, income, and nutrition worldwide, including Guatemala, Madagascar, South Sudan, Senegal, Ethiopia, Uganda, Liberia, and Kenya.

title: Finding Historic Fairfield Utah home of Camp Floyd
description: Many youth travel past Camp Floyd with their parents not realizing the rich educational resource that the State park offers. Proposed signage along the highway and throughout the town will enable parents to share the history of Utah and the US Army before the War Between the States.  Property along the highway has been donated, but signage is needed to a direct traffic into the town. A small state sign is all that exists. This project will provide a series of signs telling what is available.

title: School Equipment/Facility  400 Kids in Nigeria
description: Time Out 4Africa plans to adopt a primary school in Minna, Niger State. Nigeria.  This project will equip the school with classroom furniture such as chairs, desks, blackboards, and science learning supplies and help with updating a play ground .

title: Fill the Cross - United Against Addiction
description: Most of us know someone who abuses alcohol or drugs. Each year, 3.3 million people die due to alcohol-related harm and millions of children around the world suffer because of their parent's abuse. They face social exclusion, shame and are 10 times more likely to become addicts themselves.  Help the International Blue Cross this holiday season reduce harm to others and give these children a Christmas of joy and hope to remember. Join us for "Fill the Cross - United Against Addiction!"

title: Serve Africa; Essential Reconstructive Surgery
description: Support full time volunteer plastic surgeon Tertius Venter to serve with Mercy Ships (www.mercyships.org) for two months delivering free reconstructive surgeries to the poorest of the poor; correcting burn contractures, congenital hand and feet abnormalities that keep children from school and adults from work opportunities, treating facial tumors, cleft lip and palates, facial injuries to restore function and the right to look normal allowing people back into society. Training of surgeons.

title: Sponsor tribal girl student's college education
description: This project will support 100 tribal girl student's of JR College Phalasia to get college education in tribal populated area of Udaipur district of Rajasthan State. It is deprived and remote area.Their parents are not in condition to pay college fees. Your help can change girls life to become self dependent.

title: Make Rural Education Centre Functional
description: This centre was built to train teachers and support students of rural Southwestern Costa Rica. Less than 5 percent of High School graduates from this area pass the entry exam to a public university. The Foundation has recently won a 2-year grant to improve the training of all science teachers from this region, but we cannot start the project until the facilities are ready.  This grant does not allow for facility upgrades, so your support is needed to make the centre functional.

title: Bikes and Rights for 200 Schoolgirls in Nepal
description: This project will provide 200 disadvantaged girls in Mid-Western Nepal who have long and risky commutes to school with safe bicycles for quick and secure transportation, while providing them with powerful mentorship that will break the cycle of violence and enhance their freedom and dignity. Communities will also be provided with awareness of the dangers of child marriage and the importance of girls' education. Shoes and school supplies will also be provided.

title: Long-Term Food Security for 4000 Samburus in Kenya
description: SFK aims to sustainably bring back water, forest and life to degraded lands in Samburu County, Kenya, supporting local populations towards food self-sufficiency. The goal is to create forests of indigenous, food-producing trees that will provide long-term food security to the Samburu tribe while simultaneously curbing climate change. This is achieved through innovative training at our centre, as well as the distribution, cooperative planting and follow-up care of tree seedlings in the community.

title: Saving Babies in Southeast Asia
description: Every year, 1 million babies die from asphyxia right after birth. We want to help end infant mortality by training midwives and birth attendants how to take action within 1 minute of birth. "The Golden Minute" taught by our "Helping Babies Breathe" program will identify how to save babies lives, stimulate breathing and help lower infant mortality across South East Asia. Help us save babies lives by providing this life saving supplies and invaluable training!

title: Help feed 50 children this Christmas
description: We are young people living in London, UK and we want to help young people, who find themselves in difficult situations have the resources and confidence to cook nutritious meals on a budget, especially coming up this Christmas period.

title: Empower 200 Students to Own their Economic Success
description: Miami Dade County Public School students comprise one of the most ethnically and racially diverse populations in the U.S. This student population is also one of the poorest nationally, with one out of three students living at or below poverty level. Our volunteer-delivered, K-12 programs foster work-readiness, entrepreneurship and financial literacy skills, and use experiential learning to inspire kids to dream big and reach their potential.

title: Support Neighborhood Clinics in Liberia
description: The Ebola epidemic is a crisis of unprecedented scale in West Africa. The majority of aid funds go to large agencies focused on Ebola treatment. There is an urgent need for grassroots efforts to strengthen neighborhood healthcare, especially in Monrovia's slums and rural villages. Our Liberian team of ex-combatants provides desperately needed sanitation and medical supplies to neighborhood and village clinics that treat non-Ebola illnesses, building local resilience and protecting thousands.

title: Plant 1,000 Trees
description: Deforestation, soil erosion, and poverty are ongoing compounding problems in Haiti that degrade the quality of Haitian life, particularly for women who also endure the hardship of gender discrimination. By buying a few trees, many of them fruit trees, you can help provide the women and children of Fanm Kap Plante with resources to restore their local landscape, grow food and income, and connect with their personal power! Plant a tree, lower your impact, and help women and children in Haiti.

title: Training & Equipment for Nutrition Workers: Haiti
description: Since 1998 the Children's Nutrition Program of Haiti has carried out activities aimed at improving the health and development of Haitian children, particularly those suffering from malnutrition, who can in turn raise Haiti from poverty. Our nutrition workers, called monitrices, are the backbone of our programs. These women work tirelessly to ensure their communities are educated and making wise health decisions.  Our program works. Acute malnutrition dropped in our service areas from 24% to 3%.

title: Rescue 10 Million Meals with RLC
description: As of March 2022, global food prices have reached an all-time high. Over the course of the pandemic, the number of food insecure households in the U.S. has increased from 10 million households in 2020 to 14 million households in 2022. Help RLC prevent wasted food by rescuing and redistributing surplus meals to the people who need them most. Now is the time to spread our mission further across the United States!

title: Enable 50 South London boys to learn programming
description: This project is an after school programming club to teach software development skills to inner city boys who otherwise would not have access to the equipment, the experts and the shared space to learn with friends. We aim to train up to 50 boys over the next two terms, building an evidence base to access additional funding to continue the project. Donating will enable the boys to build new skills and confidence, raising their aspiration and career ambitions. It costs $15 a day for each child.

title: Help Us Purchase a School Building
description: When we did a street census in 2006, we found hundreds of Haitian immigrant children working on the streets with no opportunity for schooling, facing many challenges and dangers. We have since worked endlessly to empower and improve education initiatives begun by the Haitian immigration population in Puerto Plata, Dominican Republic. After renting 5 different facilities to house our school, it is time to buy! An old carpentry shop for sale is what we have our eye on.

title: Empower 5000 drop out Adolescent Girls in Lucknow
description: Condition of adolescent girls in slums of Lucknow is dire.51% girls are married before 19 years and 30% before 18 years. It shows extent of risks associated with  their life pattern and aspirations. Gender disparity on education is by 20%. The project will directly impact on 5000 adolescent girls  through integrated slum planning,  behaviour change communication, life skills, non traditional vocational skills, mainstreaming with government services and feed back system for quality services.

title: Rescue victims of child trafficking in India
description: Indigenous Women and Children Foundation helps victims of child trafficking in Manipur India rebuild their lives through free education and support. Safe accommodation is provided (schools are far from children's homes), along with counselling and meals. IWCF also seeks to prevent child trafficking, by creating public awareness. Each year 100s of indigenous children from poor families end up trafficked and enslaved, after false offers of education.

title: Care Home for HIV Impacted Children Kolkata,India
description: 25 children, infected by HIV and affected by the disease, directly benefit from this project. We offer them a loving, safe and secure environment in which they can receive healthcare and nutrition and engage in education, building the foundations for a productive and happy life. Approximately, a further 100 people will indirectly benefit as we work with family members, neighbours, the wider community and service sector officials to create awareness and decrease stigma.

title: Empower Environmental Leaders in Costa Rica
description: We need more environmental leaders! Let's empower local people in Costa Rica and motivate them to protect nature. Let's help them discover new opportunities to develop their communities in a sustainable way. This is posible with the help of Neotropica's Center for Studies and Community Empowerment, through it we are able to accompany locals as well as outsiders in the development of a sustainable living.

title: Furnish New English Classrooms
description: We had a generous donation of funds to build 2 new English Classrooms as well as a Computer Lab and a cultural center for movement and plays.  However, we need funds for desks, teachers tables, storage cabinets, whiteboards and tiles for the floor and a stage. We have 416 English and Computer students who will benefit from the new learning center.

title: Empower Students to Own Their Economic Success
description: Our children are our future.  Junior Achievement helps to prepare them by teaching skills in financial literacy, work readiness and entrepreneurship.  By elementary school age, attitudes and habits about money are already being formed.  Reaching students early in life with lessons about earning, spending, saving and sharing money, they can learn how to establish strong financial habits that will last a lifetime.

title: Empower Students to Succeed in a Global Economy
description: The mission of Junior Achievement of Northern New England is to inspire and prepare young people to succeed in a global economy.   Students participating in Junior Achievement practice the principles of financial management, along with developing the 21st century skills necessary to succeed in a global workforce. In addition to learning how to make and manage money, and how to become career and work ready, students are empowered to explore their potential to become successful entrepreneurs.

title: Today's Students, Tomorrow's Entrepreneurs
description: Junior Achievement of Northern New England entrepreneurship programs teach personal economic concepts to students in grades k-12.   These volunteer-delivered programs foster  use experiential learning to inspire students to dream big and reach their potential. JA's K-5 programs reinforce social studies Common Core standards.

title: Stopping Crime and Gun Violence Through Boxing
description: This project will provide Anti-Crime information to youth in slum areas of Nairobi through a series of  boxing based activities,drama plays and videos.

title: Enabling 400 Deaf children & youths in Addis Ababa
description: This project will support to enable Deaf children and youths to improve living condition in Addis Ababa at 10 sub cities and selected schools for the Deaf through creating accesses to inclusive education, healthy psycho social family environment & awareness creation.

title: Jusur Expanding Arab Women's Spheres of Influence
description: The program mobilizes Palestinian women citizens of Israel as social change agents and community leaders through long-term investment in the development of women's leadership. Members of the national Jusur (Bridges) Forum come together from 20 villages to exchange experiences, network, engage in mutual learning, and implement activities on the national level, with the aim of promoting the active participation of Palestinian women in public life and putting women's issues on the national agenda.

title: Kindergarten Nido d'Ape, Rome
description: A project addressing the lack of nurseries in Italy with a new parish nursery in Rome, supporting 15 children between 6-36 months old and their mothers, all of whom are in difficult social situations, through parenting support and caregiving to the children. This will respond to the urgent social need of day care whilst incorporating the need for the integration of mothers and their babies from marginalisation to inclusion into society allowing mothers in economic need to return to work.

title: Zanzibar Animal Welfare Improvement Project
description: This project will train and raise animal welfare awareness by providing humane education to 2500 school children in 20 secondary schools and 30 primary schools in Zanzibar Tanzania and through using different mass media tools.  The project will help in eliminating cruelty to animals in Zanzibar through raising animal welfare awareness by training how they can keep their animals in humane way and increase the productivity and raising income through animal keeping as income generation activity

title: SHAD: empowering youth for global impact
description: SHAD is Canada's network for transforming exceptional youth for global impact. SHAD empowers youth to make the world a better place.

title: Empowerment for 150 Young Women in Sierra Leone
description: AdvocAid will provide young-adult education classes and business & vocational skills training to 150 vulnerable girls & young women aged 14 to 24 who are currently or previously detained in prisons and police cells across Sierra Leone thereby enabling them to positively rebuild their lives.

title: Beginning the Capital Campaign: Caretaker Cottage
description: Our Sanctuary is in need of a cottage for our caretaker--the bees and the land are calling for the human presence, an element that can help to deter bears and deer, as well as providing the constant impulse of care and protection within the Sanctuary itself.  At Spikenard, we don't just KEEP bees, we CARE. Please help us complete this project--we have already raised 3/4 of the 38K needed, and we would be most grateful for your support in finishing this important work.

title: Give Colours to Mexican Children with Cancer
description: Since 1990, we have helped more than 12,600 low-income girls, boys and young people who suffer from cancer in Mexico. With your help, we can continue to do so for the 1,200 children we have in active treatment and the 4,800 children we have in present remission.

title: Fund City Year's community service in DC schools!
description: City Year Washington, DC serves over 6,500 students through daily service in public schools. AmeriCorps members are tutors, mentors and role models to students. City Year supports positive school climate by providing human capital as well as beautification and resources to provide an improved student experience.

title: Help Afghan Thalassemia Children
description: Child Foundation is a non-profit organization bases in Portland, OR, with office in Afghanistan. We help children in need to go to school. We also provide support and encouragement to families whose children are fighting Thalassemia. Our local staff and volunteers in Mazar-e-Sharif organize blood drive, conferences, raise funds to educate the community, ensure patients and parents are well aware of the latest in care, and can get to hospital for bloodwork.

title: Bring Community Gardens to 10,000+ in Cambodia
description: Steung Meanchey, a district of Phnom Penh, is a former garbage dump and home to thousands of the worlds most impoverished children and families. Cambodian Children's Fund (CCF) has supported the area for ten years by providing education, healthcare, food and nutrition, housing and valuable community services. We are now focused on raising funds to restore the community with productive green spaces/gardens providing food, education, empowerment and beauty amidst otherwise harsh living conditions.

title: Girls Leading Our World (GLOW) Leadership Academy
description: GLOW Leadership Academy 2015 will empower 75 teenage Bulgarian girls by giving them the social skills needed to think beyond the traditional limitations which our man dominated society still has.

title: Mobile health to 50,000 tribes in Denkanikota
description: aim: Curative and referral support to below poverty line people in remote and tribal villages-120 nos,    Objectives: identify, treat and or refer clinical, medical and surgical cases to complete cure and render follow up at household level and ensure continuation of their daily and development goals.  activities: diagnostic support, treatment, referral and follow up of patients esp women, children and the elderly.   methodology: daily visit, medical camps, transport & follow up.

title: 100 STREET CHILDREN REHABILITATION IN INDIA
description: The children at risk are a major social problem in the society which needs to be given due to consideration to address their problems of the children. The children in menace are not able to enjoy their legitimate right to play associate and educate. In this connection, Mother Society realized the need in rescuing the abandoned and runaway children and observed the growing intensity of the problem of massive migration of the rural children into city as an worrying phenomenon.

title: Nurture and Inspire Youth Leaders in Malawi
description: Students with Dreams inspires college students to develop creative and innovative projects that address pressing social issues through supporting them with training, mentorship and seed funding. Since 2011, more than 130 students from 3 colleges have created more than 50 projects in southern Malawi, which have impacted thousands of people.

title: To promote organized youth soccer in Haiti
description: The Haiti Soccer Project is a non profit organization dedicated to the promotion of organized youth soccer in Haiti.  Soccer is a passion in Haiti, but despite having the desire to play the game, most children are not able to participate in organized leagues with the proper equipment. Basic equipment such as soccer balls, cleats, and uniforms are not accessible for most children who wish to play. Our goal is to alleviate these problems and give those children an opportunity to play and have fun!

title: Support to 100 disabled for self-employed in Nepal
description: This project will uplift the livelihood opportunities of 100 persons with disabilities (PWDs) and their guardians from underprivileged groups residing in Kathmandu valley. The project will provides business management trainings, input supports, awareness programs, etc. to start their income generating activities (IGAs). These supports will lead to a better economic & social status of targeted PWDs that reduce dependency and contribute to their children's health and education or for better life.

title: Empower slum youths through ICT Training
description: This project will empower 540 out-of-school youths from Nairobi slums by training them (in class) in ICT skills,entrepreneurship,soft skills and also offer them (on-the-job) training through job shadowing and placements. This will help upgrade their living standards by offering them job opportunities which currently go to youths from main stream tertiary institutions.

title: Bereavement Program for children affected by HIV
description: South Africa has one of the highest recorded incidences of HIV/Aids in Africa and as a result, many children have lost one or both of their parents. These children are often left to deal with the death of a loved one and receive no counselling to help them through the confusion, pain and grief. Home-Start has successfully run Bereavement programs for HIV orphans since 2011 and 150 orphans have benefited. Home-Start would like to offer this program to other orphans that have been affected by HIV

title: HOSTEL FOR BLIND OLD AGE , CHILDREN AND GIRL
description: INDIAN MULTI PURPOSE TRUST FOR THE BLIND IS THE FIRST NGO IN INDIA. WHO WORKS FOR THE BLIND FAMILIES SINCE LAST 14 YEARS .We give special attention and care to the blind persons after their marriage and when they are in the process of settling down as a family. The real problem starts when they marry a similar partner, have kids and try to settle in some remote rural area because of financial constraint as no organization of hostel houses such families.

title: Creation of protected area for titi monkey in Peru
description: With the proposed project, the NGO Proyecto Mono Tocon wants to help local indigenous communities (more than 3000 persons), in Peru, to create and manage a Conservation Concessions (around 10 000 hectares). So this project plans to protect the last forests of the San Martin region which shelter the titi monkey (Callicebus oenanthe) who is critically endangered and forests which hold the source of drinking water for many villages.

title: give underpreviledged families small bussinesses
description: PROJECT SUMMARY; This project will help 200 households attain small businesses that will empower them depend on their own. Chinseu Community Based Organization Management staffs will  train all 200 household beneficiaries on how to run these businesses, the project shall be  monitored and evaluated on regular basis.

title: Empower 75 Youth in Nicaragua Through Education
description: Due to social and economic conditions, less than ten percent of adolescents in Nicaragua are able to earn a high school degree. Rayo de Sol focuses on creating educational opportunities for youth in Nicaragua, so that they may develop practical skills for the future. This project will provide scholarships for 75 adolescents in Matagalpa, Nicaragua. Students will receive school supplies, stipend, as well as participating in developmental activities, such as sports, art and personal development.

title: Feeding Beans and Rice to 200 Kenyan Orphans
description: Children's Garden Home is an orphanage and school which cares for 200 children. The entire home eats from a single kitchen which holds three fire burning stoves. Unfortunately, the old stoves need to be replaced or the home will be unable to cook food for the children. With three new 100 lt jiko stoves, the children can continue to eat hot meals everyday. The children only have two tables to eat from. They have need of 15 new tables and 30 benches. With our support, the children can sit down.

title: Orphans and Vulnerable people Accountanbility
description: In Ghana , more children were orphaned and continue to be, because of sickness, hunger, conflict and in ten region in Ghana becoming an orphan leaves countless children without a secure home and supportive environment. The project seeks to invest in the lives of vulnerable children, old age people by initiating educational programmes and assisting in the establishment of sustainable care and safe houses for those  are left to live with extended family, in foster care, or sometimes on the streets

title: Prevention & support for orphans of ebola victims
description: Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea are experiencing the most lethal Ebola outbreak on record. This is the first large scale outbreak of the virus in the region and communities are struggling to contain the epidemic. Hundreds of parents are been killed and their children are orphans without cares.

title: Education of vulnerable and orphaned girls.
description: This project will sustain and educate 1000 vulnerable girls and teenage mothers.we shall buy Doe for each and teach them how take care of the rabbit breed it so that after three months the Doe will have litter which will be ready for sale.The girl is expected to donate one mature doe to another needy girl for the chain to continue.During the three months the girl will be selling urine and manure to the farmers in  the community to pay school fees and upkeep .This project will sustain itself .

title: 2022 Vocational Training for Families
description: With your help, Little Footprints Big Steps will provide up to 20 youth with Vocational Training so they can become the self-sufficient, self-empowered new generation breaking the cycle of poverty - with skills, training, opportunity and hope! Sewing, Office Technology, English language, Masonry, Window Repair, Carpentry, Food preparation, Mechanics, Plumbing, Welding, Solar Panel building and other training is available. Change a life. Change the future.

title: Empowering innovative teachers in Latin America
description: FIDAL seeks to promote innovative teaching practices to improve quality of education in Latin America.  We seek to empower primary and secondary teachers from formal and non-formal education sector through an annual Education Excellence Contest that will recognize 20 innovative educational actions leaded by teachers in and out of class.  FIDAL will achieve this goal by granting these teachers: scholarships, exchange programs, educational materials, books, and visibility in the region.

title: SHELTER FOR 30 ORPHANED GIRLS IN BANGALORE, INDIA
description: We want to attract donors who will help in securing shelter for 30 very poor and orphaned children at our Ashanilaya Orphanage in Bangalore, India. Remember: Your contribution can change the life of these children! Our impact on these unfortunate children - who did not choose to be orphaned themselves - will be immense as their future will be secured. Proper shelter, food and clothing are important parts of growing up for any child. Your contribution will help a child be able to help itself.

title: chandana is a school  for farmers and rural poor
description: Chandana is a play-way model school situated in Narebail village, about 7 K.M.s from Sirsi town.   Here pre-school, primary and secondary education is rendered in a meaningful, child-centred and activity based manner.   Our motto is to provide quality education to farmers and rural poor children to enable them to develop physically and emotionally as healthy, thinking and creative individuals, who can intelligently and sensitively face the challenges of the future.

title: Help people with a disability
description: Jordan is a peaceful country in an area full of conflicts. Every day there is a rise in the number of people with conflict-related impairments, especially among the refugee community (Palestinian, Yemeni, Libyan, Kurdi, Iraqi, Syrian). Project aim: free healthcare for the most disadvantaged people with a physical disability, starting from amputees: the most part children, women and people under 30 years. We are able to provide full assistance. We need more support.

title: BazaBaza fights to improve Education in Africa
description: Baza Education, charitable organization initiative was launched in 2012 to help improve Education in Africa through adequate tutoring and financial support to poor and neglected children throughout Africa.  We take poor children in Africa off the street and enroll them into local schools while at the same time providing these kids with the moral, spiritual, financial and tutoring support needed to help them succeed. The current phase of the initiative is focused in Togo (West Africa).

title: Camp Love Without Limits
description: Shriners Hospitals for Children-Houston would like to provide the ultimate annual camp experience for up to 48 patients for Valentine's Day in 2016! Our staff and medical team are volunteering their Valentine's Day weekend to spend two days with our children at Houston's Camp For All. Camp For All is a unique, barrier-free camp that offers children, regardless of disability, the opportunity to participate in a true camp experience! Please help us provide an unforgettable weekend for our kids!

title: A rural community center for peace in Colombia
description: Rural quality of life for peace construction is a pilot model of intervention to improve living conditions of vulnerable rural communities towards social transformation and building a post-conflict peace in Colombia, through an integral and participatory intervention in the 180 inhabitants village of Vallecito in San Pablo, Bolivar. The next step of the innovative and replicable methodology consists in building the community center to strengthen social capital and active citizenship. Join us!

title: Help Families with Nodding Syndrome in N Uganda
description: To help provide a better life for children and families. To help children suffer less from the symptoms of Nodding Syndrome. We will provide psychosocial support and access to medical care which will restore dignity and hope to these children and their families. We will provide nutrition and play which will reduce stigma through education and support for the families affected. The region has experienced trauma and cultural disintegration over decades of war and neglect.

title: Transform Children's Lives Through Hip Hop Therapy
description: We believe that music is the glue that connects us all--we are all healed and transformed by music. Since 2004, Beats Rhymes and Life, BRL, has been using Hip Hop Therapy to address trauma among urban youth. Youth living in urban environments experience traumatic stress at rates higher than soldiers returning from combat. But unlike soldiers, children in the inner city never leave the combat zone. We need your help to offer Hip Hop Therapy to 150 youth.

title: Reintergrate 50 Female Ebola Survivors in Liberia
description: This project will help 50 female Ebola survivors and women affected by the disease in two of the hardest hit communities near Monrovia overcome post Ebola trauma, stigmatization, discrimination and social economic gaps. This will includes psychosocial counseling support, public education against stigmatization, survivors' reintegration community dialogues and provision of start-up reintegration and recovery assistance to survivors,

title: Help Autistic Youth find successful independence
description: Autism affects the whole family for a lifetime. InventSuccess will create educational, career and living opportunities that allow supported opportunities for independence in all of those areas for targeted youth and young adults on the autistic spectrum. This project will jump start our programs by building a virtual, interactive educational and career information community to explore educational and career options they are interested in and to set goals for achievement.

title: Take 50 poor kids from streets to school in India
description: The project is working towards rescuing poor kids and orphans from streets and child labour in Pandesara - industrial area of Surat, India. We admit these kids to our primary school - Pearl's Nursery Academy - running under UBNMET NGO. So far we have 150 students studying completely free of charge and we want to help more children.

title: Sensory Room for 52 Children with Disabilities
description: The Portable Sensory Room (PSR) will provide access to sensory integration activities to 52 children with special needs, coming from low income families and living in rural areas of Georgia. Over time, the children will develop their sensory integration making them feel more comfortable and capable in their environment. A commitment for the training of day care center teachers on the most effective use of the PSR has already been secured from the McLain Association for Children.

title: Rehabilitate of women victims of violence
description: The proposed project target 200 women who carry a social stigma and women victims of violence , this sector is one of the most marginalized and disadvantages groups in the Palestinian community   , and suffering from isolation , poverty ,  and exploitation , . The project aims to reintegrate these women  into their communities through using holistic rehabilitation program that based on ( Psycho social rehabilitation , vocational assessment and training , employment , and community integration)

title: Education support of children affected by AIDS
description: Our main focus is on educating those children who are either affected or infected by HIV/AIDS. In the age of playing and having fun, these children are living life of discrimination, fear, extreme poverty and injustice.  We have organised a project to support these children, so that they will be able to live a dignified life.  Now in this particular project, we have selected five children who are in upmost need, based upon family, economic, geographical and their health (HIV) status.

title: Quality Education for the poor.
description: This project will encourage rational and liberal thinking among the people who are mostly religious minded. The Official syllabus of Pakistan is religious cum gender based. The Schools for boys are separate from the Schools for girls. Every student Muslim or non-Muslim needs to adopt Islamiat/Ethics in the Examination. Religious tolerance can only be promoted by International Education syllabus, where no special religion study is compulsory.Educated mothers can make a Nation strong.

title: Help 30 youth in Mbale Uganda gain Farming skills
description: The project aims at putting up a farm that will provide free skills development and training in farming for the youth who are mostly unemployed and cannot afford formal education and help them become self reliant and responsible in the highly Agricultural Country. The Farm will keep 30 youths who will be trained in Agro-farming/business skills.These are mainly from poor families,street children and unemployed from the streets of Mbale Eastern Uganda.

title: Health care for10000 children in rural area of DRC
description: This project aims to provide health care against pneumonia, diarrhea and malaria for children less than five years old through community care sites and the access to family planning for youth 15-24 years in rural area of DRC. The main impact is the reduction of child mortality caused by those diseases from 80% to 20% and to increase the rate of family planning among youth from 4,3% to 9 after 24 months. To resolve the problem, the project will work with health provider and communities actors.

title: Rehabilitation 260 disabled children in Zimbabwe
description: Disabled children in Zimbabwe are amongst the most vulnerable children. S4S assists 260 children and their caregivers with sustainable rehabilitation programmes which lead to increased functionality and independence of the child. We do this through training of caregivers on how to conduct exercises with their child. In addition children are provided with the urgently and life changing medication and assistive devices, such as wheelchairs. Children participate in adapted sport in their community.

title: Business Training to Empowerment 20 Mayan Women
description: This project would provide business training to 20 mayan women who have the desire to start or improve a business to help them empower themselves as women and contribute to their family revenues. During the business training 20 mayan women will learn human development themes, gender equity, business management, marketing, finances, accounting, sales, customer service and corporate social responsibility.

title: International Experience & Field Study
description: The UDiON Foundation will be taking a small group of college students to Bangladesh where they will have the opportunity to gain international experience and leadership skills. While in Bangladesh, the UDiON Foundation and students will be opening a new Technology Center and Sewing Center for the people of Sylhet. UDiON will also be involved in the first safe and clean water project for impoverished people.

title: Empower At-Risk Girls as Peacebuilders
description: The Embracing Project has raised $8,000 toward the support of scholarships for 8 at-risk girls to participate in the "Serve with Us" program. This effort will allow us to complete the scholarships. In the program, the participants will: 1) receive coaching on personal identity and goal-setting, conflict resolution and peacebuilding; 2) travel to La Paz, Mexico, to volunteer with orphans, at schools, and in sustainable garden projects; 3) return home and "Pay it Forward" with local organizations.

title: Help 50 Maasai girls get education, not husbands
description: Nenkashe Education Centre works to help Kenyan girls in distress access opportunities for education and offer wide ranging services including mentorship, counselling, legal assistance, safe-house protection and child-parent reconciliations to empower girls.  We work in villages to promote health, sanitation and child rights issues to create vibrant livelihoods where leaders value girls and protect them from abuse, manipulation, forced female genital mutilation and early marriages.

title: Stratford Landing Elementary School - Virginia
description: Stratford Landing Elementary School is a special school located in Alexandria, VA. This school serves over 900 students. Like many schools it is overcrowded and underfunded. The purpose of this project is to provide funds to the school administration to supplement budget for technology, school programs, and to help fund the Care & Share program that provides school supplies, holiday food and gifts, and other essential needs to our children from economically challenged families.

title: Securing 20000 Garment Workers in Bangladesh
description: The goal of the project is to improve rights and empowerment of 20000 garment workers in 20 garment factories. The proposed project will contribute to improve working condition and legal compliance in the garment factory. The purpose of the project is to improve safety and occupational health practices at the garments factories. Worker's safety issues are expected to be addressed by the management through appropriate structural and institutional measures.

title: Cervical Cancer Prevention in Haiti
description: Thousands of women in Haiti are dying each year from a preventable disease, cervical cancer. Most women in Haiti have never been screened for the disease due to restricted access to care and a limited number of healthcare workers trained to provide screening and treatment. To reduce the number of deaths, Worldwide Healing Hands (WHH) is sending a medical team to Haiti to conduct much-needed training for Haitian OB/GYNs and staff in the methods used to screen and treat in a single visit.

title: Raising Rwanda: Women Farmers' Training Center
description: We work with an agricultural co-op of all women in rural Rwanda. After traveling long distances for training, the ladies of the co-op have self-identified a need for a training center and office space in their village. This builds their capacity and allows for development to come from and for a rural community. The co-op has already begin work, providing all labor, creating bricks, and gathering wood. Work with us to help them purchase the cement, windows and doors and support rural development!

title: Collect Rainwater for 700 Students in Uganda
description: Bishop Comboni College Kambuga has experienced a severe water shortage due to the increased population near the campus taking more and more water from the watershed.  The school students and staff spend an extraordinary amount of time fetching water for the myriad uses of the 700 students, plus teachers and staff.  The collection of rainwater at the boys' dorm during the rainy season is a way to alleviate this shortage and provide better quality water to the campus.

title: Fund a Home for the Pasadena Pride Center (LGBTQ)
description: PPC is a one-stop referral network for the LGBTQ Community of the Greater San Gabriel Valley and we need a home.   A physical location would allow PPC to host general educational community forums, activities, workshops and support groups for LGBTQ youth, seniors, adults and families. The number one need obtained from attendees of our Community "Listening Forum" was to find a home for LGBTQ services in the Greater San Gabriel Valley. This project would fill that need.

title: Boys and Girls Club of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
description: We are providing a fun, safe and educational after school program for children (6 years to 12 year olds) in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Our academic enrichment, sports clinics, entrepreneurial development for microbusiness, and community service outreach program will equip children to be positive youth leaders. Our goal is to expand Boys & Girls Club model into villages throughout Sub-Saharan Africa beginning with 450 R.A Padayachee students and 300 community children.

title: Quest for Quality Education at VIDYA
description: Over 33 years, VIDYA has made a difference to the lives of 3,50,000 people. We started with just a small center in Delhi, and now we're in 5 metros, with 70 projects across the country. We strive every day to provide high-quality education, empowerment, opportunities and second chances to the 12,000 children across 40 schools, 5,000 youth and 2,500 women we support.

title: Dignity for displaced women and girls in Lebanon
description: Women and girls displaced by armed conflict suffer most from not having suitable accommodation or access to a bathroom and fresh water.  Many live in shared shelters or abandoned buildings without a change of clothing or the means to attend to their hygiene needs.   A lack of sanitary pads and clean underwear prevents women and girls from going out and can also cause infections and skin disease. The project will provide clothing and a supply of sanitary pads to restore dignity and well-being.

title: Save 1000 Samburu girls from early marriage
description: The archaic cultural practice of beading among the Samburu remains one of the most dreadful exercises that recurrently exposes girls as young as ten to death and life threatening complications including excessive bleeding, sepsis, fistula, segregation and expulsion from society. We propose to increase knowledge and understanding around the dangers of the beading by targeting and working with Morans, men, women, boys and communities in Samburu County

title: Ultrasound facility for 10000 patients in Pakistan
description: This project will establish an Ultrasound facility at the LKMWT clinic MH 2 which is located in Bachal Village, Khokarapar, Malir, Karachi. Almost 10,000 patients visit the clinic every year. Large number of patients are women and children. Majority of the patients belong to very poor families with limited economic resources. Every year free ultrasound service will be provided to 1000 most deserving patients. A nominal fee of USD 2 will be charged from well to do patients.

title: Community Mobilization for Solar Energy in Gaza
description: The people of Gaza have less than 6 hours of electricity per day. They have decided to take things into their own hands, mobilize the community, plan a community solar energy project and raise funds for its implementation. Solar energy will provide Gazans with a reliable and sustainable source of energy that will supply the demand for electricity, helping to improve the quality of life on all levels. This is a project designed by the community and for the community.

title: Safe 500 Kyrgyzstani teens from extremists
description: Egalite will provide life skill building desk game, tutorial and mentorship to 500 poor Muslim teens in Southern Kyrgyzstan, who are likely to be recruited by religious extremists (including ISIS) because of poverty and unemployment. Egalite also plans to provide free consultations to their mothers on how to motivate and support their children on the way to better living.

title: Care against violence for 200 Argentine children
description: Lecheria provides care for 200 children and adolescents in situations of social vulnerability, in Buenos Aires, Argentina . Violence and discrimination are serious problems that require social educational work .

title: You can eradicate violence in Mexico!
description: By supporting our Peace Education Workshops in Mexico, you will give our children and teens the opportunity to practice tolerance, respect and gender equality to resolve conflicts peacefully. Shine a Light of Hope for Mexico!

title: Hire 4 Teachers to Keep Our Learning Centre Open
description: Good teachers are very special, and we believe quality education is of utmost importance in an individual's life. However, in many places of the world, as in Gbawe, Ghana, education comes with many challenges to no fault of the members of the community. We need to hire 4 (four) teachers now for the new school term to give courses in reading and writing, math, English, and job application and interview preparation.

title: HELP 44 ORPHANS IN LIBERIA STAY IN SCHOOL!
description: 44 orphaned Liberian children are currently cared for (basic housing, education and medical needs) on a one acre property with very limited space for them to thrive and grow. Your support will help fund a 26 acre campus that will provide a safe haven that completely cares for our 44 orphans traumatized by the civil war as well as the ongoing Ebola epidemic. Upon completion of all phases we will be able to care for over 100 orphans.

title: Revitalize Local Food Production in Afghanistan
description: The Samsortya partners are committed to replanting the forests, gardens, and orchards in their communities. Verdant forests and abundant gardens once made Afghanistan self-sufficient in food production and accounted for 50% of Afghanistan's GDP. Deforested landscapes, mudslides, destroyed farms, severe malnutrition and loss of basic human dignity is not the Afghanistan we accept. These courageous communities know exactly how to accomplish this. All they need is our support.

title: Health and food sovereignty for Ixil women
description: This project will give training to 200 women in food sovereignty and nutrition, developing education activities with groups of women.  Organized in 14 groups of  aproximately 20 to 30 women on 9 communities of the Ixil region at the North of El Quiche.  Our main objective is to improve life quality in the communities in the Ixil region by empowering women as leaders in their communities to promote reproductive health, food sovereignty, nutrition and natural medicine.

title: SCHOOL Project, serving 500 students in Liberia
description: The Charity School System is operated by the Charity Prayer Band, an organization established to respond to the spiritual and socio-economic needs prevalent in the Rehab Community, following the end of the civil war in Liberia. Charity Prayer Band continues to impact the lives and development of our community through the implementation of community based integrated projects targeting youths, women and children. This project will provide quality education and access to safe drinking water.

title: Support Potential Children in Rural Kenya
description: Potential Children living with HIV/AIDs are neglected and discriminated against, some are isolated hence unattended to. We are aiming at establishing an intervention facility in our center that will encourage and support children living with HIV/AIDs. Once identified, they will be registered, counseled, treated and guided on nutrition to improve their health. Inclusion and empowerment of these vulnerable group will enable them to live happily like any other child and contribute to the community

title: Mutual understanding Muslim - other religions Bdi
description: The basic study in the community  with the youth from different religions such us Muslims, Catholics and Protestants show that the bad values:suspicion due to religious affiliation the intolerance of each other on dogmas and religious practices and religious divisions are evidence as a bomb in delaying between those youth. 100young leaders age 10 - 27 years are trained 5 topics: Ubuntu values, trauma, conflicts resolution, leadership and governance and entrepreneurial.

title: EDUCATION IS HOPE(EIH)
description: This project proposes to initiate a three-year project" Education is Hope" (EIH) that will provide educational access to 200 orphan and vulnerable children in Adama, Ethiopia. The tragedy is that 75% of school-age orphan children in Ethiopia do not have access to formal education. We are delivering school materials,uniforms,nutritional support and tutoring.By doing so we will reduce the out of school orphans at least by 50% in Adama town in three years time of the project implementation.

title: Milford Hospice Specialised Palliative Care
description: Fundraising plays an integral role in helping to improve and develop our In-patient and community based Specialist Palliative Care Services.  As a Registered Charity we depend upon the support and generosity of the public to help fund our much needed services

title: Medical Care for 15 Romanian Roma Schoolchildren
description: This project is addressed to 15 children and young Romanian Roma immigrants living in Poland who for the first time in their lives have gained access to school but are not covered by insurance. Sight,hearing and posture defects are only examples of obstacles hindering learning and preventing the children from the full participation in the educational process. The project's aim is to give them access to health services and to supervise the treatment.

title: Medical Treatment for 100 Burn Children
description: The House of Charity is a tax-exempt organization of USA, that provides Surgical & Medical care to improve the life and health of Children around the Globe. All services provided  are free of charge & without any discrimination. In Pakistan, House of Charity has a goal to provide 100 surgical procedure to children suffering with severe burns & craniofacial deformities. These surgeries will not only save lives but also give children 2nd chance for leading a healthy normal life.

title: Allow empowerment education to 20 indigenous kids
description: This project enables 20 marginalized indigenous kids, that have been moved to San Cristobal de las Casas, to attend classes for a year. Your assistance will provide them educational and work tools for a decent and healthy future and you will contribute towards development of a better framework to facilitate a positive integration process with locals, to the benefit of people in need of protection, as well as for the San Cristobal de las Casas society at large.

title: STEAM Ahead - Preparing our kids for tomorrow
description: STEAM Ahead is a new, national education program that couples interdisciplinary STEM education with real-world, problem-based learning.  Research shows that STEM-science, technology, engineering, and mathematics-skills are increasingly necessary in our knowledge-based economy. However, like science and technology, art and design are also poised to transform our economy, encouraging the kind of creativity that enables innovation. With this in mind, we have added art to transform STEM to STEAM.

title: Office to Kickstart Community Development Zimbabwe
description: This project will create a green office with communication facilities at PORET's demonstration site in the lowveld of Chimanimani District, Zimbabwe, where ecological degradation and intensifying drought contribute to malnutrition and water scarcity. The greater connectivity afforded by this office will increase PORET's impact, helping it access funding and support to build on its limited but successful work towards the creation of sustainable socio-ecological communities through permaculture.

title: Maysles Cinema: Upgrade Uptown!
description: We are the Maysles Documentary Center. Every day we bring cutting-edge documentary films, enlightening post-screening discussions, and award-winning film making classes to our community space in Harlem where the local community and NYC at large can learn, share and get to know one another better! This project will allow you- filmmakers, moviegoers, art lovers- to help us upgrade our cinema equipment to provide the best film-going experience to the people of Harlem!

title: Empower Children in Sierra Leone
description: Share HEART in Africa places great emphasis on the importance of education in the transformation of a child's life.  By providing these children with this gift, we hope to inspire and empower them to become Sierra Leone's future leaders.

title: Community Education on Ebola Liberia
description: Eight nurses in Liberia are working to stem the tide of the Ebola epidemic by providing critical community-based education. Three have partnered with over 30 churches and mosques, others have gone door-to-door or trained peer educators. Each of them has disseminated lifesaving information about EVD's prevention, transmission, and management. They also distribute buckets and chlorine-based solution so community members can follow guidelines for proper sanitation and Ebola prevention.

title: Prevent Sexual Abuse by Educating Girls
description: Education prevents re-abuse and restores hope and dignity to survivors of sexual violence. This project will enable 10 girls who are survivors of sexual violence to attend high school for one year in a safe learning environment in Kenya. Freely in Hope provides holistically educational opportunities for our scholars which includes tuition fees, health care, psychological counseling, leadership development, and advocacy platforms.

title: provide solar cookers for 750 IDPs HHs in Galkacyo
description: The project intends to cut the link between rape &  firewood search through making & distributing solar stoves to 750 female-headed IDPs households in south Galkacyo to protect women & girls from SGBV subjected to them at outskirt of town as well as snake bites and hyena attacks in the course of the firewood search. Sexual & gender based violence eludes thousands of Somali women & girls who  suffer the consequence the dramatic impact on their economy, family &social wellbeing.

title: Help 1500 Women/Girls Lift Themselves from Poverty
description: This project will build boreholes, teach proper hygiene and sanitation practices and provide clean cook stoves in order to combat poverty, eliminate preventable water-borne and smoke-related diseases, reduce deforestation and provide micro-finance opportunities for women as stove vendors.

title: COLLECT 5,000 PINTS OF BLOOD TO SAVE 15,000 LIVES
description: 54,000 Nigerian women die every year in childbirth and 25% die due to lack of blood. We will change this. One Percent Project works to harness the power of young people to save lives through blood donation in Africa. In 2015 we want to collect 5,000 pints of blood to save 15,000 pregnant women so that they can live to raise their children.  Over the last 2 years we have collected 1,651 pints of blood with no funding, and we believe with global support, we can collect 5,000 pints in 2015.

title: PROTECT 950,000 ZAMBIAN CHILDREN FROM EBOLA VIRUS
description: Chikasika Child Care Institution is a Zambian Charitable organization providing basic services to vulnerable children in poor communities in Zambia. Zambia is one of the countries in Africa that is at a very high risk of experiencing an outbreak of Ebola Virus just like what is being experienced in Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea. Communities where the virus has broken out are struggling to contain the epidemic which is the first large scale outbreak of the virus in the region

title: Help Rural Mentally Challenge Student reach school
description: With this project funds we planned to buy a SCHOOL VAN which can transport upto 25 students in a single trip from the nearby villages. The existing mini van we have becomes 5 year old and we feel it is right time to go for the new one. School VAN is 100% essential to the special need students because the public transport system will not take care of their needs fully also it won't pick-up the students from their door steps.

title: Empower 50 Needy Girls in Meerut Through Education
description: Gramin Samaj Vikas Kendra is presently working in rural and urban location of Meerut, Bijnor, Gautam Budh Nagar, Aligarh and Bulandshahar of Uttar Prades working with poor marginalized community with focus of women,children's,scheduled Cast,small and marginal farmers,laborer. we are more focused girls to empower young girls and women by motivating them and their families to send their girls to schools.we provide skill training,life skill training and career counseling.

title: Reduce Type 2 Diabetes for DC area residents
description: The CDC reported that in 2012, 1.7 million US individuals 20 years or older were diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes and 5,000 youth were found to have Type 2 Diabetes in both 2008 and 2009.  Without treatment, complications to Eye, Kidney, Nerve Disease, Heart, Brain, and Blood Vessels may occur.  Healthy eating is the solution!  Our TV Style Cooking Show impacts over 5000+ individuals.  The show educates and demonstrates how to prepare healthy quick and easy but nutritional and affordable meals.

title: Help 2,500 Disabled Veterans with PTSD
description: Provide a free yard sign to 2,500 disabled veterans with PTSD that reads "Military veteran lives here. Please be courteous with fireworks," in time for Independence Day. Since we started the project in 2015 we have had a waiting list of thousands of veterans needing a sign. If you would like to sign up for a sign please register at http://www.militarywithptsd.org/involvedwithus/registration/ and check the box Firework sign.

title: Help the tiger Tikhon back to nature
description: Each year, poachers sell about 150 tiger skins, the annual turnover of the black market of hides and bones tiger is $ 5 million.Many tigers manages to escape, but they usually are in critical condition. And the orphan cubs are left alone, unprepared for life in the natural environment. So tigers in danger. Therefore, they need help in the recovery. Just this and Rehabilitation Center has been the Tigers.

title: Build a girl leader
description: Girl Determined is working to ensure that adolescent girls from conflict-affected areas have the chance to shape the course of their futures through weekly leadership and life skills programs.  Programs have been tried and tested over the past decade, and girls in communities across the country have demonstrated their desire to participate.  Help a girl out!

title: Support HIV+ teens for Jr. College in Pune, India
description: Since 1997, Manavya has been working diligently for the rehabilitation of born HIV +ve orphaned-destitute children and women. We believe that Education, nutrition and medication are the effective agents of change for HIV children. The toddlers, who came to Manavya at very young age, have entered adulthood. Due to this the needs of the children over the years changed with the growing age..

title: Rescue Horses to Help At-Risk/Disadvantaged in TN
description: Hope Reins rescues equine from anywhere in the United States, provides each with physical and mental rehabilitation, acts as their forever home and gives them each purpose.  Each horse serves as a "counselor" for children who are suffering from or have endured some form of trauma or difficulty. These amazing creatures encourage and give hope to those visiting the ranch as they, being rescued from severe neglect, abuse or abandonment, share a common bond. Our goal is to bring healing to both.

title: RURAL WOMEN/WIDOWS/GIRLS EMPOWERMENT PROJECTS
description: The marginalization of women in rural areas call for sympathetic situation due to high level of illiteracy, culture, tradition,religion,lack of skills and societal values for women,which resulted into infringing on women human rights, high unemployment, prostitution,HIV/AIDS explosion, malnutrition,inequality,absence in government positions etc.Our aim is to create employment for women and girls and reduce illiteracy. Over 3,000 women will benefit per year. Skills Dev./micro credits will be used

title: BUILD A MEDICAL CENTER FOR 33000 PEOPLE OF KALO
description: This project will build a medical center and wells at Kalo providing healthcare and clean water for people who hail from one of the poorest region in DR Congo. The medical center included maternity and nutrition center will serve more than 33000 people without counting children. There is no access to healthcare because no medical facilities and no wells for the clean water in this remote area.

title: Artisan Training for Women in Madagascar
description: A crucial part of our project in Madagascar is focused on financial and social empowerment for women. The artisan training workshops are the single most important component of reaching that goal. They provide an opportunity to work with women one-on-one, provide job training, leadership training and ultimately put financial power in the hands of women in rural households.

title: New Heights Educational Group, Inc
description: Our Resource and Literacy Center main office, along with our new Satellite Office/Curricula Library and Community Outreach Centers at which will be provided learning experiences, teaching resources for parents, tutors, and teachers, opportunities for youth leadership events, and community outreach/partnerships. Our Mission Statement can be viewed at www.NewHeightsEducation.org

title: Fostering Aboriginal entrepreneurship
description: Aboriginal people living in remote parts of Australia are asking for help to establish businesses to create new opportunities for themselves, their families and their communities. ELP provides capacity building support to enable people to learn about business and build the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to launch their own ventures. With ongoing mentoring and support, Aboriginal entrepreneurs are creating sustainable ventures that have widespread positive social and economic impacts.

title: Net@ Junior programmers
