description: Net@ Junior is our newest program, launched in 2014 with 350 participants ages 12-15 in eight different locations across the country. This year, the program expanded to 13 with 450 participants.  Net@ Junior aims to provide participants with the necessary technological background (programming) to succeed in a technological world, and increase the number of STEAM students .

title: Daily Bread Farm for malnourished children - Benin
description: The project consists in the implementation of a farm next to the hospitality center (C.A.R.F. Francesco Massaro) and the nutritional one co-managed by Aleimar and Sisters of the OCPSP (involved in socio-humanitarian purposes) for over ten years. The aim is to contribute to enhance the diet of the children and more generally to the self-sustainability of the two already existing structures. The beneficiaries are 130 children, in fact the project has not only a great economic value but  human too.

title: Nurture 75 vulnerable children in the RedLightArea
description: Children growing up in Mumbai red light area often stay under the bed or found lurking on streets unattended. From a young age they witness drug peddling, gambling dens, sexual acts and other illicit activities while their mothers engage in sex work. They're always at the risk of getting physically and sexually abused. A daycare & night shelter facility for these children would help them to grow in secured space with care and protection through healthy lifestyle, diet and hygienic conditions.

title: Economic Development for Minority Women in Georgia
description: The increasing share of low-wage jobs in today's economy makes it tougher for working families to afford necessities and nearly impossible to get ahead. As of June 2014, low-income families in Georgia represent nearly four in ten of all working families in the state. Our project aims to partner with local organizations, both in the metropolitan and rural communities, to assist these women to rise out of poverty through career development initiatives and workshops.

title: Preserve Strong Communities with Housing Mediation
description: Stable housing is one of the necessary foundations for a secure family. Thousands of people in Chicago struggle to maintain that necessity. Your donation to CCR creates an opportunity for tenants and landlords to talk, construct practical solutions and preserve relationships.

title: Improve Laws to Protect Corals in Latin America
description: It is estimated that up to 70% of reefs could disappear by 2030, including the reef-rich regions of Latin American and the Caribbean. Thanks to coral reefs, we have fish to eat, places to recreate, barriers from storms, and many medical cures. But this could change in the coming decades.  Corals reefs are threatened by human activities and impacts of climate change. AIDA provides much-needed guidance to implement effective laws and practices to preserve and protect reefs.

title: Free 28588 Children From Child Labour
description: All children have the right to enjoy their childhood and live a life of dignity. However, child labour is a reality millions of children in India face.   Your contribution will enable CRY and our grassroots partners to remove 28,588 children from the clutches of child labour and put them back to school.

title: Create Opportunity for Guatemalan Girl Pioneers
description: The landscape for unlocking the "Girl Effect" in Guatemala is extremely challenging, but Estrella de Mar's holistic approach to development is breaking barriers. Guatemala has the worst gender inequity gap in the hemisphere, and opportunities are especially limited for the indigenous population. Estrella de Mar empowers young Mayan women with education and also equips them with tools and resources to ensure their long-term success and infinite impact, ultimately breaking the cycle of poverty.

title: Touching Lives: Health Project
description: The purpose of this project is to: 1. Meet critical shortage of hospital facilities in Nigeria, 2.To meet the need of local people, 3. To provide high-quality care in a responsive way. 4. To train physician, nurses and health workers to be at par with colleagues in Europe and United States of America. Economic benefits are: 1. Access to affordable health care delivery. 2. Employment opportunity for health workers. 3. Improvement on level of awareness on health education.

title: Create 100 Jobs in Nigeria in 2018
description: Leadership Initiatives (LI) approaches the problems of underdevelopment by empowering communities to address their own needs.   LI partners with local government and business leaders to provide promising individuals with entrepreneurial, leadership and project management training. These young leaders then identify obstacles to development within their own communities, design workable solutions, and create sustainable business models to overcome those obstacles.

title: Create 56 Opportunities for Orphans Nigeria
description: Most orphans in Northern Nigeria today are unable to support themselves.  This is primarily because they are not able to attend school and learn a skill so they can become a full member of the local economy.  The Orphan Independence and Skills Program allows business owners to take in orphans and provide them with room, board and basic schooling.  These orphans can then go receive skills training or apprenticeships over the course of 18 months from other participating businesses.

title: Create 20 Community Owned Businesses In Nigeria
description: This Regional Business Education Program Center in Bauchi will offer classes to to teach leaders financial, personal and business management. It will also be able to serve as a resource for problems and questions that will arise. In essence this program will provide a 2nd year of regional business training allowing businesses that are currently successful to open up new shops in the surrounding region changes hundreds of lives.

title: Survivors of Gender-Based Violence Need Legal Aid
description: The Iraqi Refugee Assistance Project at the Urban Justice Center will provide free legal assistance to particularly vulnerable women in situations of sexual and gender-based violence in the Middle East, and help them safely resettle in third countries where they can restart their lives free of their persecutors. For these women, resettlement is the only long-term solution that will actually allow them to start new lives.

title: Uruguay against child sexual exploitation
description: We're inviting tourists in Uruguay to protect children and adolescents from sexual exploitation. We train youth promoters to reach tourists, local communities and tourism businesses to form a network of prevention against sexual exploitation.  It's time to believe and protect! It's time to see and act! It's time to listen and speak out! Would you join the network?

title: Shape the future of a child in rural Romania!
description: Children in rural Romania have twice lower chances to live a better life. The main cause is lack of quality education and teachers willing to go in vulnerable communities in Romania.  But you can shape their future for the better. Donate funds to continue the activity of 50 teachers recruited for the over 30 rural schools where Teach for Romania is present. Give these children the chance to learn, grow into a better life and contribute to the society!

title: Help Sierra Leonean Women Beat Breast Cancer
description: This project provides women in Sierra Leone the essential breast cancer information, early detection and breast cancer treatment they otherwise would not have access to logistically and/or financially.

title: Educate 50 Boy/Girl Scouts in the Galapagos
description: These camping trips help educate the youth of the Galapagos on the flora and fauna of this unique ecosystem, which in turn promotes the conservation of the island for many years to come.

title: Liberian Girls Books In A Bag
description: Since February 2014 all activities surrounding the reading rooms in Liberia have been on hold due to the outbreak of the Ebola Virus. Schools have been closed and large public gatherings prohibited.  The Liberian Girls Org would like to continue to encourage children to read while at home by providing book bags stuffed with books, school supplies, math and spelling activities, and printout of children-friendly guide on the preventing Ebola.

title: Global Mental Health Training
description: The Tributaries mental health team provides mental health training for service providers worldwide, focusing on low-resource countries where mental health services are scarce. Training increases awareness of the causes and symptoms of emotional trauma and mental illness, and can increase access to care, lower the cost of treatment, and reduce stigma and fear. Caregivers also learn about protecting children from abuse and how to care for themselves.

title: Ensure a Free Summer Institute for 200 Children
description: Summer Institute is an intensive 6-week training program for Teach For Armenia Fellows, and a fun, free-of-charge high-level learning program for 200 Armenian children from rural communities. The objective of the Institute is to effectively train our Fellows for their two-year teaching commitment, and to invigorate students from rural communities to benefit from such educational advantages.

title: What's Under the Tree in Wamunyu, Kenya?
description: Need a meaningful, memorable gift for someone with a generous heart and an adventurous spirit? Give a gift in your recipient's name to Kenya Connect. With our first-ever Holiday Collection, you can provide students in a rural village with computer skills, sports equipment, healthy hygiene facilities, or stacks of good books. Order one of these life-changing packages today. How many children will this benefit?  Kenya Connect works with 55 partner school with a total of 15,000 students!

title: Help Our Children's Library, Serve 10.000 Children
description: The Fundacion Rafael Pombo (FRP) is a non-profit organization geared towards building a culture that supports children's rights in Colombia. The Children's Library and Reading Room facility contains over 3.685 books and annually serves over 11.874 children. Our 28 years of experience can attest to the need for spaces that target the ignored and overlooked needs of children in Colombia. Help our Children's Library and Reading Room stay open for another year!

title: Supply Our Students
description: Glenwood Academy is a residential boarding school, located south of Chicago, that nurtures and educates at-risk and disadvantaged students. More than 50% of our population comes from underserved and marginalized communities that struggle with gangs, drugs and violence. This project, Supply Our Students, will help fund 20 students with education and extracurricular school supplies for one full school year.

title: Big Brothers Big SIsters of Central Mass/Metrowest
description: We provide needy, at-risk children with caring, reliable, and positive role models/mentors. Our program model has been proven to work through research and over 100 years of effective practice. We serve over 2000 children and volunteers annually across 40 communities in Central Massachusetts and Metrowest region. Our 1:1 mentoring programs are facilitated and supported by professionals trained within the Big Brothers Big Sisters of America network.

title: Harvesting Hope for Indigenous Women in Nicaragua
description: On the North Atlantic Coast of Nicaragua, Indigenous families confront extreme poverty and hunger. To combat these threats, MADRE and our longtime sister organization Wangki Tangni provide Indigenous women with the tools they need to survive, including training in organic farming and vegetable seeds. Women farmers are growing healthy foods to feed their families. And through MADRE-organized local farmers markets, women are selling surplus produce to earn much-needed income.

title: Get a Kosovan Kid to School
description: We're working with the poorest community in the poorest country in Europe. Kosovo's Roma, Ashkali and Egyptians have poor attendance at school (96% have not completed compulsory education) which is cause and effect of poor health care, low employment, and a rubbish start in life for kids. Over the past four years we've worked successfully at getting these children into school, by offering resources like book bags, winter transport, academic support and a skilled mediator from the community.

title: Transform 1,000 lives with clean water in Honduras
description: Help families in the Cangrejal Valley of Honduras to gain access to clean drinking water and improved sanitation to reduce the number of child deaths due to contaminated water. Your support will help local communities to develop a sustainable, community-run water system that also includes composting toilets, rainwater drainage and water reuse.

title: Radios: A Lifeline to Safety for Nicaraguan Women
description: In remote communities on the North Atlantic Coast of Nicaragua, Indigenous women are in danger. They suffer from high rates of abuse at the hands of their partners. They need information on the services available to them, including safe housing. But often that information is out of reach-too far away, or written in a language they don't understand. That's why MADRE and our sister organization Wangki Tangni support women's right to a life free from violence through an innovative radio project.

title: Empower Women in Uganda through Entrepreneurship
description: This project will establish a women's empowerment program through entrepreneurship training in Gulu, Uganda for women 18-24, building self-esteem and providing entrepreneurship and technology training to enable 720 impoverished Ugandan women to lift themselves out of poverty. Women will engage in self-esteem and team building exercises, learn computer and entrepreneurship skills, including writing a business plan, and gain valuable hands-on experience developing a cooperative business.

title: Healing for Sexual Violence Survivors in Colombia
description: Colombia's war has been going on for so long, most people don't remember what peace was like. MADRE and Taller de Vida, our local sister organization, are there for former child soldiers caught up in this violence. And we're there for girls who've survived sexual violence in the war. Through counseling and human rights trainings, these young girls receive the support they need to heal. They are able to rebuild from the traumas they've endured, to seek justice and to demand an end to violence.

title: Care in Crisis for Syrian Women and Girls
description: Syria is enduring one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. Women and girls are suffering widespread rape and forced marriage on top of the mass displacement, starvation and armed attacks threatening millions of civilians. In partnership with grassroots women's groups in Syria and surrounding refugee communities, MADRE is delivering aid and trauma counseling to women and girls. We're also training women to document and prosecute rape as a weapon of war and demand a voice in peace talks.

title: Empower Young Environmental Leaders in N. America!
description: The Brower Youth Awards (BYA) elevates the work of emerging environmental leaders in North America, celebrates their achievements, and provides them with the skills, resources, and relationships to further their work.  Earth Island honors six exceptional youth with a Brower Youth Award each year at a free community Awards Ceremony, and provides year-round support and leadership development to our 92 BYA alumni as well as hundreds of young environmental and social justice leaders in our network.

title: Teach Classical Music to poor kids of Talim Island
description: ANG MISYON's newest satellite is Talim Island, Rizal, Philippines, where the indigent youth are given free Classical Music education, instruments, uniforms, transportation/performance allowances, & meals. This project will provide 20 kids with these benefits for at least a year. Classical Music has the power to nurture upstanding citizens of humanity, aids in the eradication of poverty through social development, and "transmits the highest values: solidarity, harmony, & mutual compassion".

title: Eyenaemia
description: Through your donations we will be able to run field trials in developing countries and provide limited free monthly usage of its new non-invasive, easily accessible screening tool which makes screening for anaemia as simple as taking a selfie. Photos are sent to our servers via text, mail or other means. Preliminary studies in Australia show that we can detect up to 95% of cases of severe anaemia.

title: "Heal the Earth"- 1000 Young Farmers in Tamil Nadu
description: ISS has been involved in organic cultivation since its inception, and has its 31 acres farm certified as conforming to Indian NPOP standards of Organic and Demeter agriculture, by the  certification agency IMO control. ISS initiated the School of Bio dynamic Farming, given limits of using chemical fertilizer and pesticide and the need to heal the land. Proposal is to support the school to train and equip 1000 youth as next generation farmers and develop land in the next 20 years across India.

title: Gender-Equity-through-Education
description: The overall objective of this project is to improve the educational status of poor girls to meet the millennium development goals. The specific objective of the project are to initiate the community to Advocate for support and education of poor girls, to increase the enrollment of students in the school, to increase the access of girls to education, to change the life condition of poor girls through education and to empower the households of poor girls economically.

title: Protecting Pets In Domestic Violence
description: According to the US Department of State, 8 million Americans live overseas. While it is unclear how many of these families have pets, we know that approximately 30% of the victims we serve have pets in their homes while domestic violence is taking place. That is about 150 pets per year that are exposed to and experiencing violence in the home. Each year we provide food, shelter, airline flights, crates, medical examinations and basic needs for dozens of pets.

title: Clean Cook-Stoves for Rural Bolivian Schools
description: THINK GLOBAL, GO LOCAL -- CEDESOL will provide 11 schools in the impoverished Toro Toro municipality with clean biomass cook-stoves, working closely with 2,500 students, teachers and parents to equip them with stove training and environmental education that will empower women and children, promote students' educational access, prevent indoor smoke inhalation, and lower global carbon output.

title: Create a model for harmonious living in Costa Rica
description: In partnership with the National University of Costa Rica (UNA), IBREA Foundation will create a social model for peaceful living, through working with two rural areas in Heredia Costa Rica. Through providing brain-based holistic education to a focal group in each community, IBREA aims to establish the foundation for that process. Participants will go through a process of healing their body&mind to unleash their natural tendency for harmonious living & take action to make it a reality.

title: Feed our patients
description: With the South African hospital system not coping with the demand to care for terminally ill patients, our hospice is put under pressure more and more to take in terminally ill patients. We have started subsidising more patients each month and we are looking at a monthly food bill of over R5000 per month. Our request is to support us to be able to pay our food bill on a monthly basis over a year period.At Wide Horizon Hospice we believe ther is no end to carring and dignity in dying is a must.

title: Promote Healthy Aging in Finland
description: There is a growing aging population in Finland. By 2060 every 4th person will be 65+. Research shows that 62% of the Finnish aging population uses alcohol and 8% of these abuse it. Exceessive alcohol use in the elderly leads to loneliness, accidents, mixing with medication, binge drinking and using alcohol as self medication. The Finnish Blue Ribbon has created groups to train professionals and offer peer support, advice and information to the aging population.

title: Generate Income and Hope for Impoverished Families
description: This project helps 14 refugee families begin new lives. 5 men and 9 women in Central Region, Ghana, already trained in tailoring, soap making, bead artistry and carpentry, but without the means to start a business, will receive additional business training and start-up funds to establish their own small business to support their families.

title: Blast fishing awareness and quick response program
description: An increasing number of dolphins, turtles, sharks and fishes are appearing mutilated by blast fishery in and near three marine protected areas in the south pacific of Nicaragua, with is a biodiversity rich marine coral corridor which support local livelihoods. To address the blast fishing problem and to maintain livelihoods related with fishery we will develop an awareness program which include radio and TV spots, workshops with stakeholders and fishermen and fuel for 'quick response' patrol.

title: Fund a Warrior Canine Connection Service Dog
description: Warrior Canine Connection (WCC) supports recovering combat Veterans and their families through the healing power of dogs. WCC enlists Service Members and Veterans suffering from symptoms of Post Traumatic Stress (PTS) and Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI) in the critical mission of training service dogs for their fellow wounded Warriors with physical disabilities. These highly skilled, Warrior-trained service dogs are placed with Veterans at no cost.

title: Help Secure Permanent Emergency Shelter
description: Mary Open Doors (MOD) is committed to empowering and improving the well-being of women and children afflicted by domestic violence in Belize. The current project seeks funding to purchase the land and building now currently occupied by MOD and used as its shelter facility.  To date, Mary Open Doors have sheltered 130 women at its emergency shelter while providing education and human rights awareness for approximately 1650 drop-ins at its resource center.

title: CANOSA Fundraising 2015
description: CANOSA would be organizing the following programs/workshops in 2015. These programs   1. Android Programming Workshop for High School Students (Jan - Feb 2015) to enable youth for IT jobs 2. Odia Literature Discussion & facilitating upcoming poets (April 2015)  3. Regional Drama Festival (30 May 2015) with groups from Toronto, Ohio and Michigan 4. Celebration of Odia language, arts & culture on the Occasion of Kumar Utsav

title: Send Baru Students to Training School for a year
description: This project will allow Baru Students to study for a year technical careers such us Table & Bar, Cuisine and Accommodation, at the Training and Entrepreneurship School of the Island.  The Hernan Echavarria Foundation has partnered with other organizations to design, build, equip and operate a Training School for the Baru Island people which will train them in various skills related to tourism and construction, to attend the touristic and real state demand.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION IS A NECESSARY EDUCATION!
description: HELP US SEED FUTURE! We seek to provide different educational opportunities for children living in poverty, with environmental experiences, of urban cultivation of vegetables and fish crops in small areas (aquaponic system), recycling, own crops and gardens of plants, medicinal, edible and energetic, that arise from the need for have productive spaces and take advantage of the benefits of plants and fish. Looking to have food crops in their homes without spending money.

title: Help Haitian Family Farmers Keep Their Lands
description: Family farmers across Haiti have joined together to protect their lands from theft by tourism corporations,  mining, and seizure by large landholders. These farmers are some of the poorest and hungriest people in the world. Other Worlds supports Haitians in their struggle for their human rights and land rights through media, advocacy, education, legal defense, international support, and funds, so they can stay on their ancestral land, keep farming, and feed their children.

title: Build Workshop for Physically Disabled Burkinabes
description: In one of the poorest countries in the world, Tigoung Nonma (TN) provides a network of physically disabled Artists and Master-Crafts people that enables them to gain needed skills and to generate their own income. However, this negligible income is not enough. This project will help TN to build an accessible center where it can offer training, make and sell members' Art, and run its catering service. In April 2018, TN purchased a plot of land with a maisonette on it, ready to refurbish.

title: Educating 10,000 Children in India about Diabetes
description: It is estimated that 61.3 million people aged 20-79 years live with diabetes in India (2011 estimates). This number is expected to increase to 101.2 million by 2030. Behavior change--getting people to exercise and improve their diets--is the prime challenge in diabetes prevention. To be effective, we must reach young children before their lifestyle habits are fully established. We are committed to reaching 10,000 children with our two-year diabetes prevention program by 2019.

title: Annual Campaign 2014
description: ICEC is proud to have helped over 800 children this past year reach their developmental potential and provided their families with the tools and skills they need to parent their special needs child. We wake up every day passionate to "Treat Special Needs with Special Care."  We love what we do, but fulfilling our mission is not possible without the help from people like you - ICEC Friends & Families!   We are asking your help to refurbish, update and enhance our Therapy Clinic.

title: Support Sai Oo's Dream Of Attending Uni (ongoing)
description: After years of dedicated service to his community, Sai Oo wishes to advance his education by attending Mae Fah Luang University to complete a degree in Information Technology. During his years of selfless work, he has rightly gained admiration from fellow residents of the Koung Jor Shan Refugee Camp and friends from all over the world. Two very generous donors have committed to funding the majority of the total cost required, yet this is still not enough. Let's help Sai Oo reach his dream!

title: Save Infants' Lives by Promoting Breastfeeding
description: This project is to boost the cause of appropriate infant and young child feeding, of which breastfeeding is a crucial part.Breastfeeding needs protection,promotion & support as it is under threat.Vested corporate interests push breast milk substitutes (processed baby foods) and create disinformation campaigns to mislead mothers and deprive infants of the limitless benefits of breast milk.Infants are dying daily at the altar of greed, and we are fighting tooth and nail to stop this colossal crime

title: Rehabilitation course for children
description: The aim of the project is to improve cognitive and behavioural abilities of 8 children previously treated for brain tumors through a 3-month course of individualized neuropsychological rehabilitation sessions. During the course children will be offered motor and cognitive exercises that target the core processes underlying academic performance and psychosocial functioning.

title: Make Nonviolent Conflict Resolution A Reality
description: Brav promotes the ideals of nonviolence through conflict management on a state-of-the-art online platform. Through compelling education tools including games, and other visual interactions, we train all ages in resolution skills on our website's face-to-face platforms for use in organizations, schools, workplaces, and on an individual basis.

title: Vegetable gardens for children & woman in need
description: In remote rural areas of the Municipality of San Felipe, Guanajuato, Mexico 210 underprivileged children and women are struggling for food. SEBAJ is looking for donations to provide tools that guarantee these women and their children to cultivate enough food in organic gardens, to ensure their complete and healthy diet. Through workshops, the women will be empowered to learn how to maximize the benefits derived from these gardens and how to provide a proper nutrition for their children.

title: Urban Creative Factory for Deprived Youth
description: Urban Creative Factory - street art center will build capacities and provide opportunities to 200 deprived youngsters from Nis, Serbia such as juvenile delinquents, youngsters coming from socially excluded groups, youth living in poverty to empower them, integrate to the mainstream society and build their self-confidence through creative work and artistic workshops (graffiti, comics, hip hop music, break dance, photography, video) that would be free of charge and led by recognized artists

title: Rehabilitate rescued child slaves in Nepal
description: A quarter million children are put to work on carpet looms in India and Nepal. This project is devoted to replacing the tools in their hands with books. Hamro Ghar ("Our Home") is a center for children with no family to return to or for whom there is a likelihood of being sold or sent to work again. With your support, GoodWeave can provide these children with rehabilitation, education, and a safe home.

title: Agricultural /Animal Husbandry Center - Bobo
description: The Bobo Agricultural /Animal Husbandry Center will seek to address the issue of food security and low agricultural production through a non-formal educational medium. Although 80% of Burkina's population is involved in agricultural activities, food-producing farmers are unable to meet food demand for their villages let alone the entire country.  The center will educate rural farmers to create a sustainable source of nutrition.

title: Maintenance FUND for Accessible Nature Trail
description: The CDCT lead the coordination of the first accessible Nature Trail in the Dominican Republic with financial and technical support of the US government (USAID & USFS), along side the National Council for people with disabilities. Now that the construction is done and the trail is functioning, CDCT would like to start a maintenance fund in order to maintain the standards that are required in order to ensure that the trail continues to serve its purpose.

title: Teach 200 Middle & High School Students to Budget
description: When students visit JA Finance Park and face the challenge of budgeting for their fictional family situation, they make important financial decisions covering where their family should live to what the grocery budget is for the month. Volunteers, serving as budget advisors, guide students through the process of building a monthly budget with their assigned incomes and share their experiences

title: Center for Supportive Schools (CSS)
description: Center for Supportive Schools (CSS) inspires and enables schools to leverage the leadership potential of students so that they team up with faculty and staff to create the vibrant environments needed for academic, social, and emotional learning.

title: LightSail - Flying to Other Worlds on Sunlight
description: Help get us to the launching pad for LightSail 1! Support the LightSail solar sail spacecraft to reach space on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy launch in 2016. Technologies created for LightSail may enable other small, interplanetary spacecraft to achieve success. The creation and launch of CubeSats is within reach of universities and other organizations that could once only dream of flying their own missions. Longer-term, solar sailing holds the promise of propelling other larger craft to other planets!

title: Girls2Pioneers
description: Women are still underrepresented in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM), despite the fact that these fields are growing exponentially. The Singapore Committee for UN Women is implementing a programme to encourage more girls in Singapore to take up careers in STEM, especially those who are at risk or from low income families. Through day camps tailored by our curriculum developer Destination Imagination, we hope to engage the next generation of pioneers and innovators.

title: A New Compressor for Boulder Emergency Squad
description: This compressor will impact the lives of the 310,000 people in Boulder County by providing clean breathing air for Boulder County's Firefighters and Dive Rescuers for the next 20 years.  Additionally it will be used to compress air for use in vehicle extrication tools, air bags, rafts, and a multitude of other use cases.

title: Help Us Protect Our Native Seeds in Mexico
description: The project will be to protect native maize seeds in indigenous peasant communities in Mexico, strengthening farmers' knowledge plus have available native seeds for the production cycle and motivate peasant to continue working their land and integrating youth in the life peasant.

title: Healthcare for 500-1000 Ebola Orphans in Liberia
description: The objective of this project is to provide one year healthcare, nutritional assistance, and education fees and supplies for at least 500 to 1000 children, who have lost their parents due to Ebola.

title: educate and feed an orphan female child in india
description: Summary one more of our children became orphan, because of AIDS to their parents. She lost her mother and father for AIDS disease. And now she is suffering and fearing about her future. Her poor old grandfather is unable to look after her because he is too old. Educational support only can give her a better life and secured future. What is the issue, problem, or challenge? After losing her parents to AID s disease, this child is facing a lot of problems to go to school and for her daily bread

title: Build the First Inclusive Playground in Armenia
description: The aim of this project is to build the first inclusive playground in Yerevan Zoo for over 8,000 registered disabled children in Armenia who face public segregation. The lack of awareness for their special needs has left these children and their families at the margins of society. This playground aims to break these barriers and provide a space for integration. The interactions made possible by this initiative will help eliminate prejudices towards disabled children in all parts of the society.

title: Access to education for poor Romanian children
description: The project aims to facilitate the access of 600 children from rural, poor and isolated areas, in eastern Bacau county in Romania, to quality education, social care, counselling and guidance through 5 community centres named "Clubs with Glue". The services will be provided by local teams of educators and a mobile team of specialists travelling in the area from the city. We will provide scholarships to the best and poorest children to access high school education in the city.

title: Educate 300 underprivileged children in Bangladesh
description: FAIR plans to educate 300 children hailing from the socially outcast communities in Bangladesh who have no access to education due to financial constraints and negative outlook of the society. The project will build up a child animation centre in the community area providing reading materials, financial support, intensive coaching and necessary facilities to the target group through a skilled tutor who will bend his/her efforts to overcome all obstacles to ensure mainstream education for them.

title: Christmas gifts for 100 poor children in Pakistan
description: In our effort to ease more their pains even in a minute, we dream that before this Christmas end, we can provide them additional warmth on the coming nippy weather; additional clothes, blankets, slippers and to share with them their dream foods.

title: Help the disabled in Vietnam and Inner Mongolia
description: Eden Social Welfare Foundation plans to donate 100 white canes to persons with visual impairments in Inner Mongolia and donate at least 50 wheelchairs in Vietnam. The right to "mobility" is the first step for the disabled to get out of poverty in developing countries. This project will provide persons with disabilities a chance to participate in their communities and to better enjoy their lives. Also, wheelchairs will be purchased from a sheltered workshop to increase the income of the disabled.

title: Stop gender-based abortions. Give life to a GIRL!
description: Each year Armenia is losing around 1400 girls, in result of prenatal sex selection and gender-based abortions, which is already a demographic threat for the nation. Prenatal sex selection is deeply rooted in patriarchal structures of society that tend to favor boys. The objective of the project is to contribute to a reduction of gender-biased sex selection in Armenia. The project will result in at least 15% positive change and at least a 10% reduction in the number of sex-selective abortion.

title: Home for 100 Differently Abled persons in India
description: Arvind Saurabh is a Residential cum Vocational Centre for Mentally Challenged persons. Initially we will accommodate 25 persons &later enhance capacity upto 100 persons. The residents will be admitted under "Transfer of Parentage" which means once the person is admitted we will take care of them till their death. Besides providing residential facility we will keep the residents involved in various Vocational activities so as to make them productive.This will help in improving their self esteem

title: Educate 80 Girls in Pakistan
description: Zara studied Math in a Teach For Pakistan classroom in Lahore, and was the brightest of the lot. After 8th grade, Zara's parents took the life-altering decision to take her out of school to help out at home and get married. After a brief hiatus from school for a few months, Zara convinced her parents to delay her wedding until completing high school. Zara attributed this to the confidence and skills her TFP teacher instilled in her. Help empower girls like Zara get a quality education in school.

title: KYM Cataract Project
description: Following eye examinations in 12 countries, including Sudan, Cameroon, Chad, Niger, Mali, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Congo, Democratic Republic of Congo, Guinea, Nepal and Pakistan, 1000 people will have cataract surgery. After the operations, a certificate of appreciation with a photograph of the treated patient will be sent to benefactors who have made a full donation ($100).

title: 1000 Cranes Relief Fund
description: 1000 Cranes Relief Fund is supporting disaster hit areas with a focus on supporting projects working on long term recovery efforts in New Orleans, Japan, Philippines and Haiti.

title: Provide literacy skills to 500 women in Kenya
description: This project builds a Learning Centre in Western Kenya to provide for literacy skills to 500 rural women yearly.It also provides for learning materials such as books, pens, charts and provides for teachers.

title: June 1st School
description: June 1st School is the only school in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) District 4 that offers free elementary education from 1st - 5th grade. District 4 has a population of about 200,000. The June 1st school provides needed education to 200 disadvantaged, orphaned children and boat families, who have financial difficulties, who live in the streets and have to do labor work.

title: Educate a Girl, Educate a Nation
description: This project is basically designed to bring girls aging between 5 years to 10 years to mainstream education. The targeted children are those who have either never enrolled in schools or who left schools in early age due to domestic problems. The proposed project is aimed to improve quality of education for marginalized girls in the targeted areas by focusing on providing support packages to community schools such as incentive, books, uniform, and teaching kits.

title: Agroforestry the Peruvian Amazon
description: Alianza Arkana supports community-driven initiatives in Shipibo communities that address key issues affecting indigenous peoples in the rain forest. Through our  agroforestry initiative, we are reforesting 20+ hectares of land using medicinal plants.

title: Activities club for healthy lifestyle in Skopje
description: Our goal is to open a club where people can get inspired to live a more healthy and active life. It would primarily have an educational purpose, providing people with the necessary knowledge and motive to a positive change in their lifestyle, be more creative and to lead by example in their community.

title: Give  goats to 200 Widows in Uganda.
description: This project will give goats to 200 Widows of the Fumbira Community in Uganda,to improving on their household income.

title: Support rape victims ages 4 to 71 years old
description: Every 2 minutes someone in America is sexually abused. 44% of victims are under age 18. In 2013, the Center for Safety & Change provided more than 3,000 services to survivors of sexual assault, through the Center's counseling, advocacy, therapy and hospital and court accompaniment programs. The victims' ages ranged from a woman who was 71 years old, to three girls who were each only 4 years old. In addition the Center runs violence prevention programs for teens, designed to help prevent abuse.

title: Harper House Restoration in Columbus Ohio
description: Having once been a jewel of the community, the historic Harper House in Columbus Ohio has fallen into disrepair and is in dire need of renovation. Reversing the deterioration will remove the blight it has become on the area and allow it to be put back to productive use, while still preserving its rich architectural and historic significance.

title: Law+You: Ensure Responsible Citizenship in Liberia
description: Years of war and corruption have eroded Liberian citizens' trust in government institutions. This lack of civic engagement, combined with a 75% illiteracy rate, affects all aspects of life. Most recently, the impact has been manifested through the defiance of precautionary information about Ebola, leading to continued high rates of infection and death. Civic education is a way to empower children to know and protect their own rights.

title: Building peace for kids in Kenya, Mexico & Nepal
description: CWPO shares wisdom, where most schools in the world only teach knowledge.  We believe that when you combine knowledge and wisdom, real learning is achieved.  Our core curriculum covers areas such as:  conflict resolution/prevention, critical thinking, decision making, creativity, listening skills, imagination, concentration and cooperation (teamwork). We work with both private and public elementary/primary schools in Mexico, Nepal and Kenya. Our 35 week curriculum focuses on primary youth.

title: Support Health Education with you donation.
description: Vasco de Quiroga Univesity is expanding to other states within Mexico and Chicago in the US. We want to offer quality education at affordable tuition. Mexico has insufficient educational provision in health sciences and engineerings, which is why we seek to heal this need. In the city of Chicago, Hispanic people need education from their own culture to an accessible cost.

title: RENOVATION OF HOLY CROSS SCHOOL, CHENNAI,INDIA
description: Our trust has been running HOLY CROSS NURSERY AND PRIMARY SCHOOL-which is RECOGNISED AND APPROVED by the GOVERNMENT OF TAMIL NADU-and providing Quality Education at free of cost to the needy poor, neglected children.  We give proper care, food, clothes, protection and Quality Education and make them grow physically and mentally.Our scholl is now functioning in an Asbestos sheet covered building and we need genourous help from donors to Renovate the school building with a RCC roof .

title: To Provide Education for Needy Children in INDIA
description: This project will help children who cannot go to school because of poverty to study and get a job out of caste system in India. "MOTHER BABY SCHOOL" branches are largely set up in poor village. Also, another new project is that we support each individual student from elementary school to job hunting. It is  the education that their children would receive that would help bring them out of poverty. Through education, we are giving them chances to move beyond their caste and careers which they want

title: Building  God's Love School Classrooms
description: At God's Love Home we have some Land (50ft by 150ft)  and we want to put  six classrooms  block  building . This project will feed and educate the orphans, getting the full sum will ensure a sustainable future.

title: Teaching 6 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
description: This project will provide education and early intervention therapy to children with autism spectrum disorder and/or with pervasive developmental disorder. Six children who are diagnosed with ASP or PDD will participate with the special instructors, teacher helpers and speech language pathologist. Socialization is our main goal for teaching the life skills that will be needed for higher level functioning. This project being developed by the Pennsylvania Diversity Children's Organization.

title: ACTION FOR DEVELOPMENT OF RIGHTS -(ADR -UGANDA)
description: This Project Plans to build 3 classroom (Primary School)to support the education of orphaned and Vulnerable Children (OVC's) in Pallisa Uganda.   This Project Plans to support school dropout youth get vocational skills (Technical Education) for self reliance.   Additionally, it plans to be part of the fight against HIVAIDS, Malaria among the target communities and have access to clean water points.

title: Women Economic Empowerment through Skill Developm
description: RABT Development Organization is trying to empower 1000 young women through prevision of skill training in different trade like Office Automation, Garment making, beautician Trade. As well as provision of tool kits and course completion certificates in Office Automation, Garment making and beautician. Women are the marginalized segment of the society and often ignored when it comes to the benefits or facilities provided by the government or any other agency.

title: Give street children in Burundi a future
description: Our aim is to develop a new generation of leaders for Burundi through spiritual, cultural & socio-economic revival. We believe that children are the future and hope for Burundi. Our vision is to see every child & young person given the opportunities & chances they need to live a normal life. We conduct a wide range of programmes including leadership training, assistance to street children, health programs, skills training, and campaigning to raise awareness about the issues young people face.

title: Root cause treatment for 10 people for a year
description: Around 70% deaths globally are caused by non communicable conditions which are actually preventable. India happens to be one of the leading countries of this situation. To address this situation, Aashwasan Science offers spiritual technology that holds hope for the world as it connects people to their innate resources and unravels the root cause to bring cure, management and most importantly prevention - prevention not only in their lives but also for the coming generations.

title: Save Water and Live Healthy
description: The Spreeha Foundation and GraphicPeople - a subsidiary of AdPeople Worldwide - launched the "Imagination is Power" project to promote water conservation and healthy living for people in the urban slum community of Rayer Bazar in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The project has three objectives - to increase awareness, knowledge and practice. This is because last year a large number of occupants contracted waterborne diseases. The goal is to promote conscious and healthy living.

title: Help students experience their potential
description: Some youngsters who are educated dream & innovate less and are more concerned with survival. The acquired skills are many a time not relevant to the context. In India this can be seen in rising levels of unemployability, number of psychosomatic conditions, mechanical way of life & much more. Aashwasan brings forth an innovative program to help students experience their potential through long term engagement which helps them bring out their potential, imbibe people skills and become change makers

title: Braille books for 4000 visually challenged kids
description: This project provides Braille books for 4000 visually challenged students in South India.This will help them become independent and own personal copies of the books as that is lacking now.This will help in widening their horizons and gaining immense knowledge. Indian Association for the Blind (lAB),based in Madurai, South India, is a well-known non-profit organization working at the grass roots level for education, employment and rehabilitation of people with visual challenges from rural areas.

title: Run a 85-bed Child Cancer Ward in India
description: Treatment of children with cancer requires complex, intensive, expensive regimens administered over prolonged periods of time. Child requires an entire ecosystem of care in order to properly receive and benefit from cancer treatment .Almost 50% of children abandon care in the middle of their treatment due to the lack of family support and insufficient funds. IMPACT runs a 85 bed child cancer ward in MNJ cancer hospital to address all these factors and strives to provide optimal care.

title: Let's get together to educate these little joys!
description: Samarthanam has been striving towards working and advocating for the children with disabilities or from marginalised backgrounds.It isn't about the disabilities we work for,it is the abilities that we norture, the plethora of skills, talents and enthusiasm that we see in them, At the primary school,we see 150 of these little children full of life and looking forward to a brighter future which was almost a dream for them only a while ago.Let's give them their smiles,the tools for them to grow.

title: Let's walk together! Mangochi - Malawi
description: This project is aimed at children aged between 1 and 12 years with motor disability by mental retardation mainly caused by childbirth, and at children with hydrocephalus and affected with spina bifida regardless of their social, tribal or religious belonging.The project, with the contribute of Tiyende Pamodzi group, consist in a rehabilitation cycle for 5 children for the year 2015.The facilities involved are the Hospital of Mangochi and the rehabilitation center of Blantyre "Feed the Children".

title: MOSQUITO NET TO THE 600 POOREST FAMILIES IN NEPAL
description: This project will distribute and install 1,200 treated mosquito nets to the 600 poorest families in three malaria high risk villages where, currently we are working. Economic loss, particularly to the poorest is severe when the malaria mosquito infects them. This also affects the children's health and progress in their studies. Consequently, this project will prevent the families from economic loss and improve the school attendance of girls, we support through the Girls' Education Project.

title: Education to Protect our Natural Heritage
description: One of Latin America's most bio-diverse regions and a vital sanctuary for endangered animals, the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve needs ongoing protection. But in an area that is both rich in natural resources and inhabited by impoverished communities, this remains an ongoing struggle. We are therefore investing in the children of the Sierra Gorda, building understanding and respect for nature, and giving them the tools and resources they need to continue to protect their natural heritage.

title: China Leadership Summit 2015
description: The China Leadership Summit (CLS) is a three-day conference hosted each spring at Duke University and the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill. CLS aims to strengthen collaboration by bringing together undergraduate and graduate students from Duke, UNC, and other top universities with acute and demonstrated interests in US-China affairs. Boasting a DOB only five years ago, CLS already offers a stunning series of esteemed speakers, such as the World Bank's former country director for China.

title: "Opportunity to Dream: Yachana Future Builders"
description: For 28 years we at Yachana Foundation have put education as the key to a brighter future for Amazon youth. We are giving free tuition to community-oriented students this year. Our boarding students call themselves Yachana Future Builders [YFB]. Your contribution to offset YFB's tuition is your key to assure these indigenous and mestizo "builders" are equipped to reverse generations of poverty, practice environmental awareness, and act as stewards of Ecuador's rainforest.

title: Survivors: a portrait of the Ebola crisis
description: Through the eyes of Sierra Leonean filmmakers, Survivors presents an unforgettable portrait of the Ebola outbreak in West Africa. The team focuses their lens on unfolding stories of Sierra Leonean heroism all around them. Through the courageous stories of local Sierra Leonean nursing staff, volunteers, patients and their families, we see enduring humanity amidst the outbreak.  Banker White and Anna Fitch are collaborating with African filmmakers Arthur Pratt and Lansana Mansaray.

title: Livestock for Orphaned Children in Congo
description: This project will provide 135 AIDS orphans and their guardians with training, livestock, seeds, and counsel so they may become self-reliant. These children have suffered through the death of their parents...they don't need to fear for their futures and how they will pay for food, rent, clothes or food.  Through this project, these small orphaned families will receive the hand up they need to move forward.

title: Promote Conservation Education in African Schools
description: Education is limited and under-resourced in communities that have huge conservation on their doorstep. In South Africa alone townships up in the Kruger national park have never seen a lion and have no awareness of the issues the Big 5 face. Down by the Ocean communities see the sand but never stepped foot and again clueless the impact throwing a plastic bag on the floor can do to our planet and ocean. The only way to tackle this is Education & Awareness and you've helped us start our fight!

title: Mobile Bus for 400 Disadvantaged in Brussels
description: The Medibus is a mobile cabinet that offers paramedical care to the most disadvantaged people (drug users, sex workers, homeless people) close to tube and train stations. Yearly 400 consultations take place thanks to a group of 18 volunteers including 8 nurses. Besides its preventive care, part of the patients are referred to the care and orientation centre of Doctors of the World in Brussels. There the patient receives besides a more thorough examination, social and psychological assistance.

title: Operation Purple Healing Adventures
description: Operation Purple Healing Adventures are family retreats designed specifically to help families dealing with injuries, including PTSD or TBI. Healing Adventures offer a place to rediscover family-fun and togetherness, specifically for those families trying to adjust to a "new normal."    "It pulled us closer together and at the same time took me out of my comfort zone. Never made to feel like our sickness and challenges are handicaps." -Service Member dad

title: Education Support for Underprivileged Children
description: This project provide high-quality education sponsorship for 250 underprivileged children from poorest slum communities & studying V to X in Govt., Private Convent schools. These deprived children are good at studies but struggling for timely education support, due to children parents are working as daily wage labours in construction sites, scavenging, tobacco making, etc. With this project children will benefit immensely from SERUDS holistic approach to education & comprehensive support services

title: Help school dropouts earn a living
description: Currently in India, there are more than 300 million youth in the age group of 16 - 30 years who have not completed school and lack skills to attain a job or start a business. Through our Yuva Parivartan project, we will be providing basic vocational skills to disadvantaged youth across rural and urban areas in India. The training provided will lead to self and wage employment and further development of the economy.

title: Help Us Build Our School!!!
description: NEWS!!: We have FINALLY begun construction on our school. We have been running our school in temporary buildings for over 10 years and it is a very happy day to say we have materials to begin construction on one small building. This campaign will help us to construct a FULL PERMANENT SCHOOL that will be there for generations and generations to come. Please be a part of it!

title: Enteral Nutrition for tube-dependant children
description: We eat to live. It is one of the most natural things we do every day. Yet, there are people who are unable do it the usual way because of an illness. The only means for them to receive essential elements is to take them in through the tube.  There are 100 children between 0 and 18 under the care of Vera Fund, to whom enteral nutrition delivered through the tube is the only possible way to eat. To provide the nutrition in this specific form, we spend the average of 11,500$ per month.

title: Establishing Legal Aid in Post-Conflict Countries
description: The lack of access to legal counsel for poor men, women, and children accused of crimes is a serious problem in post-conflict countries. These people routinely languish in detention for months or years without trial, and face torture, coerced confessions, and wrongful convictions. This project will allow the ILF to expand into new countries with no functioning legal aid systems, and work to establish legal aid programs that provide effective, quality criminal defense services to the poor.

title: 100,000 meals for hungry Silicon Valley families
description: Did you get enough to eat? We've all heard those words. The truth is many of us aren't getting enough nutritious food to eat right here in Silicon Valley, despite the increasing wealth and low unemployment. It's easy to understand why. The cost of housing has skyrocketed with the booming economy, while wages have remained relatively flat for many of us.  Second Harvest Food Bank is serving more of us than ever before - 260,000 kids, families and seniors every month.

title: Growing our schools in Uganda!
description: Nyaka works to free children from the cycle of poverty by providing a high-quality, free education, both formal and informal to orphaned, abandoned or vulnerable children due to HIV/AIDS in order to counteract pervasive hunger, poverty, and systemic deprivation. Your donations will help us repair, maintain and operate two primary schools and a secondary and vocational school for these children in rural southwest Uganda, as well as providing extracurricular activities and extra tuition.

title: Preserving Chile's Ocean Treasures
description: Oceana has identified a unique opportunity to designate large marine reserves in the area around the Juan Fernandez Islands and the Desventuradas Islands (ie. the "Galapagos of Chile"). These marine reserves - 100K and 300K square km, respectively - would protect the livelihoods of artisanal fishers and those dependent on the tourism industry. To achieve this, Oceana will document biodiversity, mobilize national support and appeal to the Chilean government to implement the proposals.

title: Help kids with disabilities and highcost diseases
description: This project will benefit children and teenagers in Medellin, who were born with Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy or other deseases. The objective is to enable beneficiaries to develop personal and social skills that facilitate their training process and social adaptation through specialized therapeutic processes, speech therapy, physiotherapy, hydrotherapy, adequate stimulation, music therapy, occupational therapy, neuro psychology  and psychology.

title: Africa Responds
description: The Ebola outbreak has affected thousands of lives and strained fragile health care and social systems. An effective response to Ebola must strengthen existing community systems, including local organizations that provide timely, culturally appropriate, and lifesaving services. These organizations play a key role in rebuilding their communities long after the outbreak. Africa Responds is mobilizing funds to support grassroots organizations fighting Ebola in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

title: Empower East African Refugee Youth in Uganda
description: Soccer Without Borders uses soccer as a vehicle for positive change, providing under-served youth with a toolkit to overcome obstacles to growth, inclusion, and personal success. Our program serves over 1900 refugee youth annually from more than 6 countries. The majority of SWB youth do not have access to formal education. At SWB we offer English courses and educational workshops on a daily basis and continue our academics and social-emotional learning with our unique on-field program model.

title: A Tiny Toones Christmas
description: Tiny Toones engages, inspires and educates children and young people from the slum areas of Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Tiny Toones provides a unique combination of creative arts and non-formal education completely free. Thousands of children have benefited since 2005. Over 200 children attend classes every day, in dance, music, English, Khmer, math, art and computing. For many it is the only education they get. We are currently trying to raise $5,000 to help continue this vital service into 2015

title: Create a Nature Conservation Reserve on Lot 46
description: Lot 46 Cape Tribulation Road is in the heart of the Daintree lowlands rainforest (in far northern Australia) and is an incredibly special piece of land. It provides habitat for 19 endangered, threatened and vulnerable species. We have a chance to create a Nature Conservation Reserve on Lot 46 and protect it into perpetuity. By turning it into a permanently protected Reserve we will be changing not only its future, but the biodiversity of the area.

title: 1,000 vulnerable refugees access legal assistance
description: Your generous support allows Asylum Aid to help a thousand vulnerable women, men, and children who need protection from persecution and torture each year. This project will ensure vulnerable and traumatised refugees can get a lawyer who will take time with them and allow them to tell their difficult stories. The trust and confidence created between advisor and client, when the client feels respected and heard, are essential for making a strong case to get them the protection they need.

title: Grow Money on Fruit Trees! Help 288 Families!
description: Trees for the Future needs your help to grow thousands of fruit trees to help 288 farming families in Tawa, Kenya. A new juice factory offers an exciting market opportunity for these farmers, especially women. The trees will be planted in Forest Gardens, which enable poor farming families to transform their degraded farms into tree-based agricultural systems. Each family's Forest Garden will increase their market access, grow more foods, and bring farms into sustainable productivity.

title: Typhoon Hagupit Food, Sanitation and Livelihood
description: The project will provide immediate food security via vegetable gardening, basic food packs assistance, installation and or repair of toilets and rehabilitation of local livelihoods to the poorest of the poor severely affected by Typhoon Hagupit in Leyte and Samar provinces.

title: Palliative Care for Advanced Cancer Patients-India
description: Karunashraya, a 55 bedded facility extends free professional palliative care to advanced stage cancer patients who are at the end-of-life stage.Patients are at Karunashraya for an average period of 15 to 30 days before they pass on.These last days of the patients are made comfortable and free from pain- both physical and mental by our team of doctors, nurses and counselors. All food requirements, medicines and medical consumables are provided by us.The pleasant ambiance adds to their well being

title: Help disabled children to get art classes
description: The main aim of our project "Help disabled children to get art classes" is to bring a miracle to 88 children of the orphanage 4 in Pavlovsk, St Petersburg. All of us, employees and volunteers of "Shag navstrechu", want to give orphans life they deserve.

title: Train four builders in Haiti to build safer homes
description: Builders who lack formal training build unsafe houses. These unsafe homes are likely to collapse in earthquakes and hurricanes, putting families in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, at risk. We will provide training and certification in safer construction techniques to four builders. They will use this training throughout their careers, impacting the safety of dozens of homes and families. Certification also increases their income - a double win.

title: Come to Their Rescue
description: Helping homeless animals find forever homes is one of the ASPCA's top priorities. While we are making a difference, the sad fact is that every year more than 7 million animals enter shelters nationwide and almost 3 million don't make it out. Come to Their Rescue is a campaign dedicated to changing this situation by raising awareness and action on behalf of these animals in need.

title: Empower DC residents to grow healthy fresh food
description: To have good health, we need good food. But in many neighborhoods in the nation's capital, nutritious food is often not available. We want to ensure that everyone can eat healthy, local food, so we work to empower people to grow their own. We cultivate new gardeners and spearhead new community food projects and, in so doing, we broaden access to good food for everyone. In the process, we increase the health and resilience of communities, as well as families.

title: Support Mobile Ambulance Service for Wild Animals
description: Mobile Veterinary Service (MVS) project is one of the unique efforts of Wildlife Trust of India (WTI) to provide in-situ emergency relief to displaced or distressed wild animals. The project envisages placement of trained and equipped wildlife veterinarians in major protected areas across the country to ensure round-the-clock medical attention to wild animals in need. Each MVS comprises of a transport vehicle, a trained wildlife veterinarian, an animal attendant, equipment and supplies.

title: Story cards for 1.2 million Aanganwadi children
description: We want to tell you a story of a little girl.  Intombazanyana okuthiwa Ayesha othanda izithelo kanye nonina . Uma unina Ayesha yambuza yini umama do, waphendula - Mothers ukwakha amabhuloho.  This not a technical error.  Imagine if this was your first day of school.  For 1.2 Million children in Jharkhand, India, it is.  Language is one of the biggest reasons children drop out of school between Grade 1 & Grade 3.   We want to make 21 gorgeous story cards in 9 tribal languages.

title: Homeless pets need your help with medical care!
description: You can help homeless pets receive much needed medical and vet care to save their lives.  The pets at Warrick County Animal Control have no funding to help the pets become and stay healthy.  Sick animals are euthanized and we want to help them find homes by providing much needed medical and veterinary services with your help.

title: Songs of Peace from Orphans of Conflict in Manipur
description: Using music as a therapeutic tool, this project will bring emotional healing for children who have seen a lot of violence and trauma. Akhu (a grassroot musician) and his team will be providing music lessons to children of 2 orphanages in Imphal that shelter orphans of conflict. The project will help them channel their inner feelings and provide a creative outlet to release the trauma through music, and will release a music album containing songs written, composed and performed by these kids.

title: Ecological Ovens for 30 Families - Eritrea
description: The project "Ecological ovens" comes from the need to improve the efficiency of the traditional  Eritrean oven- the Mogogo.  Talking of facts, the energy performance of the traditional Mogogo is less then 10% and it is estimated that it consumes 50% of the Eritrean wood.  As it  has no fumes collection system,  these ovens can have serious  health repercussions,  causing respiratory and eyes diseases to people and livestock. The new ovens will provide a sustainable and safe way of cooking.

title: Changing lives in 40 child-headed homes in Rwanda
description: This project will improve the lives of 40 children head of household and their siblings in Rwanda. These children are orphaned or have been abandoned by their surviving parent and the oldest is forced to work to put food on the table, protect and support the younger ones going to school and get medical care when they fall sick. You can change a life by donating for their school material, pay health insurance or give the older one a means to make a living from hairdressing, sewing or farming.

title: Urgent medical care for the children of Chernobyl
description: This project will provide medical care to children affected by the 1986 Chernobyl disaster. The services CCI provides have reached out to almost 1 million children and their families. CCI volunteers have transformed the once frightening Children's Mental Asylum at Vesnova, 175 KM from Chernobyl, into a world-class child care centre from which CCI directs medical care programmes. A donation can underwrite care for a child like Igor who suffers from multiple heart defects.

title: Save Israel's Birds of Prey
description: Birds of prey are referred to in the Bible many times as a symbol of might and power but are declining in Israel today. Griffon Vultures (Gyps fulvus) are the largest birds of prey in Israel but less than 40 nesting pairs are left, as opposed to nearly 1,000 before the establishment of the state. The population of Egyptian vultures has also dwindled by nearly 70 percent, and two other impressive species, the bearded vulture and the cinereous vulture, disappeared more than two decades ago.

title: Kitchen Care- Kusina ng Kalinga
description: "Care Kitchen" is GK's flagship program to end hunger and malnutrition for children across Philippines. It is an in-school feeding program that aims to provide nutritious lunch meals over the course of one school year, improve school attendance rates and enhance children's learning capacities, and build a community that cares for the young by involving parents, teachers, and volunteers in the daily operations. Hunger ends where caring begins. Visit http://gk1world.com/kusinangkalinga for more.

title: Help for Families Impacted by Domestic Violence
description: Each year, Safe Horizon provides shelter to over 3,000 women and children who have left abusive homes. Many have escaped violence with just the clothes on their backs and whatever items they could grab as they fled.  This project will provide essential housewares (cooking supplies, cleaning products, bedding, etc.) for 1,000 families in Safe Horizon's domestic violence shelters, giving the women and children we help the comfort and safety of home.

title: MADD Victim Helpline - 24/7 help for crash victims
description: The MADD Helpline helps those who are impacted by impaired driving crashes when they need it.  We are there for those who have been injured in crashes, for the loved ones of those who have been killed, and for concerned citizens who want to help end the violent crime of drunk driving.

title: Saving Israel's Otters
description: The Israeli native Eurasian Otter (Lutra lutra) population underwent a dramatic decline since the 1960s due to illegal hunting, water pollution, depletion of water sources and the disappearance of wetland habitats. Recently the regional status of our otters has been categorized as "Critically Endangered". With less than 100 individuals estimated to be remaining in the wild, dramatic measures must be taken if otters are to be saved from extinction in Israel.

title: Support pregnant woman in Govt Hosp with nutrition
description: PSM is providing service to the poor people from several years. in that process we provide services to the poor pregnant women in project we visit to govt hospitals and take the list of pregnant women and for them We provide nutrition food the for that mother like fruits,bread etc and for infants we give Lactogen 1.

title: Establish School for vulnerable Girls in Kashmir
description: Phullawai is a remote access village with much vulnerabilities; having a population of 8500 people. The socio-economic status is under poverty line of the local community. There is no girl's school in the area, so the women are the most vulnerable group having literacy rate less than 2%. SDO has been working on education support since 2010. SDO will establish a Secondary level schools for girls. Through this school annually more than 200 girls will be provided free and quality education.

title: Sanitation and Infrastructure in Schools - India
description: Children from government schools in India often do not have access to toilets, clean drinking water and the basic minimum infrastructure to be in school. This project is created with the objective of providing the required infrastructure including clean toilets, stationery, library, safe drinking water and other fulfill other need-based requirements.

title: Animal Assisted Therapy for Special Needs Children
description: The Jerusalem Biblical Zoo's Animal-Assisted Therapy Program for children with special needs serves approximately 70 groups annually. Participants suffer from a wide-range of physical and cognitive challenges including autism; and this cross cultural project includes participants from all of Jerusalem's diverse communities - Jewish, Christian and Muslim, both secular and orthodox, from diverse socio-economic backgrounds, of various ages, and with disabilities of varying degrees.

title: Hands On Tokyo Youth Impact Project
description: Hands On Tokyo's Youth Impact is a group of student leaders from high schools and universities in the Greater Tokyo area that empowers and guides young people to realize their potential as empathetic leaders. Through opportunities to create, promote, lead, and participate in Hands On Tokyo activities, they can gain valuable real life experience. This is how Youth Impact is allowing passionate youth in Japan make a positive change within their own community and the world.

title: Assistive devices for 200 visually challenged kids
description: This project will help provide assistive devices such as computers/ laptops/ net books/ angel players for 200 visually challenged students. It will help in their gaining confidence and being on par with their sighted counterparts on the lines of computers and technology.

title: Gifted Students Environmental Education Program
description: The Zoo Bagrut High School Graduation Program allows highly gifted students from the 11th grade to participate in a sought-after and elite academic course presented at the Biblical Zoo and approved by the Israel Ministry of Education as a high school graduation credit. The goal of this program is to create the next generation of leadership in nature conservation by focusing on the exceptional students. Each year 15 participants from diverse backgrounds are selected to participate.

title: Help Save the Sumatran Tiger
description: The Jerusalem Biblical Zoo participates in the Sumatran Tiger European Endangered Species Program, the most intensive type of population management for a species kept in European Association of Zoos member institutions. This program plans the future management of this magnificent species, of which only around 400 remain in the world. The Jerusalem Biblical Zoo is home to a male and female pair - Avigdor and Hannah - who have successfully produced three cubs in recent years.

title: Scholarships for Ghanian Girls
description: This project will help Ghanian school girls beat the odds and continue their education. In a country where 30% of girls graduate high school, we are helping extraordinary female students go from kindergarten to university. Educating girls positively impacts their families, villages, communities, country, and the world.

title: Build the next generation of conservation leaders
description: SCA's mission is to build the next generation of conservation leaders and inspire lifelong stewardship of the environment and communities by engaging young people in hands-on service to the land.  Every day SCA unites young people with hands-on environmental challenges. Every day we create future stewards of our land, healthier environments and-ultimately-a better world.

title: Kidsave Sierra Leone: Reuniting Orphan with Family
description: This project finds families for children who lost their parents to war or Ebola; trains families and communities on the rights of children, monitors the children, helps with school, food and bed needs, creates supportive villagers where children are placed, and has a revolving microloan fund to increase families' income and food supply. Since Kidsave began this work in 2010, 1,092 children have been helped to find permanent families, usually kin and occasionally suitable non-kin.

title: Provide nutritious food for malnourished children
description: The recent Prime Minister  of India, Dr. Manmohan Singh described malnutrition in India "a national disgrace"  Many children in desperately poor villages here in Bihar are malnourished. A protein rich meal twice a week can do so much to restore health as part of our health care program. It is amazing how much difference this simple measure can make on Children's health and well being.   Help fill a hungry tummy today.

title: Social Entrepreneurship education in high school
description: Spain needs to turn the attention to social entrepreneurs and put a lot of effort into supporting the creation and development of more social enterprises.The project has aspecial focus in participants with fewer opportunities from fringe communities, rural areas, geographical and economic obstacles. These young people needs entrepreneurship education the most. In these communities the percentage of early school leavers is much higher arriving to to twice as much as in other communities.

title: Save Lives and Improve Transportation for NYC
description: Transportation Alternatives' mission is to reclaim New York City's streets from the automobile, and to advocate for bicycling, walking and public transit as the best transportation alternatives. With 12,500 dues-paying members, 115,000 supporters and a committee of activists working locally in every borough, T.A. fights for the installation of infrastructure improvements that reduce speeding and traffic crashes, save lives and improve everyday transportation for all New Yorkers.

title: A Bicyclist-Friendly Massachusetts
