description: We work for the cyclists across the state who see bicycling as a solution for the traffic, health, and environmental challenges we face in our communities. We can't do it alone. MassBike depends on people like you to continue our work improving the safety of bicycling as a healthy and more sustainable means of transportation and recreation.

title: Give-Only one borehole to 300 Children in Zimbabwe
description: This project will drill a borehole in Zimbabwe providing water for at least 300 orphaned and vulnerable children who come to Chiedza Child Care Center for support. We run a wet feeding nutrition program, pre-school, second chance education and psycho-social support activities for at least 300 children from vulnerable families at the center six days a week. Currently the center is struggling with shortage of water for supporting these children and want to drill a borehole.

title: Create A Bicycle Friendly Silicon Valley
description: Silicon Valley Bicycle Coalition (SVBC) exists to promote increased cycling in Santa Clara and San Mateo Counties. To accomplish this goal, SVBC advocates for improved and expanded bicycle infrastructure and other facilities, including bike lanes, paths, racks, lockers, accommodating traffic signals, capacity on transit, and more. Additionally, SVBC promotes bicycle culture through events and activities such as Bike to Work Day, Bicycle Friendly Workplace, and Valet Bike Parking at a variety of

title: Make SF a Better Place to Live, Work and Bike
description: The San Francisco Bicycle Coalition has been transforming San Francisco streets and neighborhoods into more livable and safe places by promoting the bicycle for everyday transportation. We are one of the largest and most effective bicycle advocacy groups in the country. Through our day-to-day advocacy, education and working partnerships with City and community agencies, the SF Bicycle Coalition creates safer streets and more livable communities for all San Franciscans.

title: Create A Bicycle Friendly Pittsburgh
description: Pittsburgh's bright future is built on an active transportation network that safely connects people to professional, commercial, recreational, residential, and cultural destinations. Well-designed bikeways and walkways will make riding a bike or walking easy, convenient and fun. Our embrace of an active and healthy lifestyle as reflected in Pittsburgh's commitment to providing safe, world-class facilities for biking and walking, is and will remain a key component of this transformation.

title: Open School
description: Children with disability, Roma children and children with special education needs are segregated from general education system in the Czech Republic. They are funneled into "practical schools",  primarily designed for children with intellectual development disorder. Our goal is to give these children a chance for quality education, integrated in the class with their peers from the neighbourhood.

title: Protect children from deadly Japanese encephalitis
description: PATH is bringing a lifesaving vaccine against devastating Japanese encephalitis (JE) to millions of vulnerable children in Southeast Asia and the Western Pacific, helping to stamp out the disease for good.

title: Get the clothes, get the confidence, get the job
description: At our London HQ, we dress and prepare women for interview.  This works: over one in two get the job.  We want to deliver this service across the UK. Women face tough challenges to get jobs.   They can lack confidence in their abilities and often face long gaps in their employment history.  We give a woman an entire outfit (to keep) and advice on her interview.   This transforms her self esteem so she can go on to succeed and get the job.

title: Construct a Workshop for Female Artisans in Rwanda
description: The community of potters in Cyaruzinge is a historically marginalized population that faces poverty and severe food shortages in Rwanda. To promote economic development in this community, HDI will construct a workshop to provide 30 female artisans with a space to safely create and store their unique products.

title: Bridging the cultural & spiritual gaps in AustinTX
description: ABBA takes a unique approach to the cultural issues that all communities face such as: child trafficking, 3rd grade illiteracy, cultural diversity and isolation. ABBA connects key leaders from across all four sectors (private, civic, church and nonprofit organizations) of our community and then convenes them in a neutral setting to discuss and determine the tipping points where cultural solutions can be shaped and executed. Through your donations we can leverage the power of community.

title: TEACHERS are the BACKBONE to EDUCATE GIRLS in Peru
description: Chicuchas Wasi(CW) School for Girls provides free primary education to underserved, indigenous girls. Our all female TEACHERS are specially prepared; to teach quality academics and Spanish to native Quechua speakers, make home visits to identify the home reality of the students and any family disfunction. CW provides education, personal development and empowerment needed for a secure future of economic independence, self esteem, confidence and become future leaders for gender equality.

title: Bring Safe Water to School Kids in Vietnam
description: Many children in Vietnam lack access to water that is safe for both drinking and handwashing. Water that looks clean may still have bacteria that is invisible to the human eye that makes it unsafe for drinking, and causes illness and disease. Hygiene education in schools is also lacking and diseases such as diarrhea are common. MEDRIX creates a healthy future for Vietnamese kids by installing water filtration systems for drinking water and handwashing stations in preschools and primary schools.

title: Dev. Disabilities:A Peaceful, Healthy Garden Space
description: Mental and physical wellness and nutrition are critical issues for adults with developmental disabilities seeking to live the most healthy and independent lives possible. 3LPlace, with your help, will create a multipurpose garden at our Life College Residence in Somerville, Massachusetts, offering space for quiet reflection and yoga, to teach about food production and gardening, and to engage in gently interrelated community activity.

title: Mission to Mars! Engaging young people in STEM
description: We ensure more young people from diverse backgrounds enter higher education, in particular attend the best universities, to study science, tech, maths and engineering - much needed skills for the UK economy. Our sessions, such as  'Mission to Mars', demonstrate how STEM subjects are applied to solve real world (and out of this world!) issues. These sessions engage and motivate young people, which we follow up with practical support and academic tutoring to ensure potential is fulfilled!

title: Emergency Vet Care for Street Dogs in Costa Rica
description: Dedicated volunteers are saving lives with your donations for emergency veterinary care for the street dogs of San Ramon, Costa Rica.  Check out our Before and After photos and help us change the world...for one dog at a time.

title: Provide 125 Students the Opportunity of a Lifetime
description: We will offer quality education and training to hardworking and appreciative disadvantaged children and youth in central Vietnam. In addition to the weekly English classes that we have been offering since 2011, and the Intensive English Course that was first launched in July 2014.

title: Provide bedding for 300 visually challenged kids
description: This project will help provide new bedding to 300 visually challenged children of Indian Association for the Blind (IAB). They will be able to have their own beds, pillows and blankets. All these kids are from rural areas and hence your timely help will be highly useful to them.

title: Healthcare for 500 mothers and children in Uganda
description: Due to the extreme poverty brought on by decades by war, famine and disease, many Ugandans cannot afford necessary medical care. Lacor meets this expansive need by waiving all fees for children less than five years of age and for pregnant women.  These subsidies dramatically increase access to health care for people in Gulu.  These subsidized fees to vulnerable populations come at a great cost to Lacor.  To stay open, Lacor must raise roughly 70% of its operating costs from external contributor

title: Give These Little Lives Hope for Tomorrow!
description: This project supports street children, orphan and destitute in Goa. There are so many run away children from different states, migrate to Goa in search of better livelihood options. In bargain of doing so they end up as child laborers, rag pickers and juvenile in conflict with Law. Children's home provides them an environment with all the basic necessities required for their healthy growth. El Shaddai has 6 homes, supporting 300, girls and boys, in age group of 2-17 years. We need your support!

title: School fees and uniforms for 14 Mammadu kids
description: This project will grant basic literacy for 14 orphaned and vulnarable children living in a township in Windhoek, Namibia. This is the only way to give them a chance for a better future.

title: Trucked Water Needed for Cite Solail School, Haiti
description: Fountains of Hope would like to provide 3000 gallons of trucked in water on a weekly basis to a school of 600 children located in the heart of the third largest slum in the world, Cite Solail, Haiti.  Donors would sponsor water that will fill two tanks every week.  There is a water purifier system at the facility which has been previously donated that can purify each tank in 20 minutes making the water potable for the children to use on a daily basis.   52 weeks x $60 per truckload = $3,120

title: Activating Empathy Through Play - Silicon Valley
description: "When Playworks came to our school, it changed Gabriel's world. From kindergarten to 4th grade, Gabriel was picked on and bullied . . . especially at recess. Then Playworks came to Castlemont School in Campbell, and Coach Michelle arrived. In a few days, with her gentle encouragement, Gabriel started playing . . . and rather than laughing and teasing him, the other kids were giving him high fives. Now he's motivated to go to school, to socialize and as a result, his grades have improved. Gabriel

title: quality education to 300 children at kishanganj
description: AIF will provide quality education to 300 children  in the age- group 6-14  through learning centers who are school drop outs  or never been to school.A local specific and contextual curriculum will be followed. The state government syllabus up to class V will be followed in the  centres as the emphasis is to help them join the mainstream education, however, the approach of teaching and learning will be different from normal regular schools keeping in mind the need of the children of this region

title: Save Birds from Kite-String Injuries
description: Hundreds of birds are grievously injured every year by glass-coated kite strings (locally called "Manjha") that are used for flying kites. The injuries are mostly related to the wings and range from fractures, ligament and muscle separation and, worst of all, complete amputation of the wing. This project aims to significantly reduce the number of birds injured due to use of manjha during the festive season in India.

title: Last Mile Health - Urgent Ebola Response Campaign
description: Over the course of this project, Last Mile Health will recruit, train, manage, supply and pay 300 Community Health Workers and 15 Community Health Worker Clinical Mentors to successfully respond to the Ebola outbreak in southeastern Liberia's most rural communities.

title: Chiguru-A Cultural Event for Govt School Children
description: "Chiguru", in the regional language Telugu, means "budding".  The project aims at providing a platform for the budding future citizens to showcase their cultural talents. Over 4500 children from government and informal schools in Hyderabad (India) will participate in various traditional/cultural/education/sports events. It helps facilitate the all-round and holistic development of underprivileged children and also kindles interest in volunteers from the community to engage with these children.

title: " 52 YEARS PROTECTING CHILDREN IN COLOMBIA"
description: Since COVID, Colombia has had an overwhelming increase in the number of children living in poverty. Since 1970, this project has been seeking to protect children at risk of abuse as well as help them and their families daily with education,food, psychosocial support,recreation,health,prevention of child pregnancy and guidance. We also work to keep them away from the dangers of being on the streets, child labor, and other forms of child abuse. Every year more than 200 children receive support.

title: Out Run EBOLA: awareness/protection for children
description: The EBOLA  Virus Disease (EVD) has sprinted across West Africa infecting over 20,000 people. Awareness and preventative training is the best way to outrun the epidemic. THINK (Touching Humanity In Need of Kindness) has been working with the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection to raise awareness in communities throughout Liberia.

title: Help 3-6 yr old children for pre-primary schooling
description: Nidan is running early childhood education centres providing pre-primary education to all children in the 3-6 years age group living in the slum areas of Patna. Nidan helps 5-6 year old children get enrolled in to Government primary schools wherein the mother teachers play a pivotal role in linking the children with pre primary centres and Government Schools and ensure that children are regular in the centres/schools.

title: Support most vulnerable & fight against isolation
description: Our purpose is to reduce poverty, bring hope and solidarity to poor communities or individuals in France and worldwide. We bring assistance to families, children and young people but also to the most vulnerable (homelesses, migrants, prisoners etc.). We fight against isolation, help them to find employement and we ensure their social reintegration. We provide emergency responses but also long term support, development aid and we work on the causes of poverty.

title: PROVIDE  EDUCATION TO AIDS ORPHANS IN RURAL UGANDA
description: The BCCBO AIDS Orphans Project  is working to free orphans from the cycle of poverty by providing a high-quality, free education, both formal and informal, to children aged 6-24 who have been orphaned due to HIV/AIDS in order to counteract pervasive hunger, poverty, and systemic deprivation. Your donation will help provide a student with a uniform, meals, medicine, and supplies for one school year. For your secondary students, your donation will also include transportation to their school.

title: Connect Fresh Water Pipeline to Rwandan Village
description: The community of potters in Cyaruzinge is a historically marginalized population that faces poverty and severe food shortages in Rwanda. They currently lack access to a fresh water source, and community members often go days without water. This negatively impacts hygiene and sanitation practices in the community and increases the prevalence of diarrheal disease. To solve this problem, this project will connect a pipeline from a nearby water table to a tap inside Cyaruzinge.

title: Help Women in Kenya Confront Climate Change
description: In Kenya, severe and frequent drought triggered by climate change is devastating rural families. People whose livelihoods depend on the land are left with nothing as their animals perish and their crops wither away. Families are going hungry. MADRE and the Indigenous Information Network are training Indigenous women to confront the impacts of climate change by conserving resources and adapting local ways of life.

title: Changing Young Lives with Dance, Music & Education
description: Tiny Toones engages, inspires and educates impoverished kids from the slums of Phnom Penh, Cambodia. We provide a unique combination of creative arts and education, reaching children who have dropped out or never been to school, and are at risk of falling into gangs, drugs, crime or lifelong poverty. Over 100 children attend dance, music, English, Khmer, math, art and computing classes daily. We must raise $30,000 to pay the rent and teachers each year, especially crucial during COVID-19.

title: Establish a Bicycle Exchange in Santa Cruz
description: Create a fully equipped workshop space with professional bicycle repair tools and an active schedule of twice-monthly bicycle repair events in Santa Cruz. As with our program in Silicon Valley, repaired bicycles will be distributed through local non-profit social service organizations that serve underprivileged clients in the Santa Cruz area. The goal of this new chapter is to become financially self sufficient within about 18 months.

title: Abolish Open Defecation from India:"Build Toilets"
description: Of the 1 billion people who have no toilets, India accounts for nearly 600 million. With the ever-increasing population of the country, everyone's health, especially that of women and children, is compromised in a major way due to unavailability of toilets. Nidan leads in providing solutions to this problem by helping communities in planning out the type of toilet facilities required including financing, construction, operation and maintenance responsibilities.

title: Bicycle Safety Education
description: Educate the recipients of donated bicycles about bicycle safety using instructors certified by the League of American Bicyclists.

title: Education for children in need
description: My Name is Kumar supports the education and welfare of nearly 80 children from the Londor begging community in Tamil Nadu.   We enable the education of children who would otherwise be forced onto the street to beg by providing them with school fees, safe school transport, equipment, uniform, after school homework support, healthy meals, and medical support. In addition to this we run out of school activities, trips and tuition for all the children in our programme.

title: Empowering Women and Girls
description: This project will support efforts to combat the incidence of sexual and gender-based violence in Liberia by providing awareness on the prevention of gender-based violence, including human trafficking against women and girls.

title: Rehabilitation for Kids from Wroclaw Hospice
description: Wroclaw Hospice Foundation is the only one in Lower Silesia which allows to provide care at HOME, since family itself is the best place for the sick child. Besides professional medical and nursing care, terminally ill  children require rehabilitation which many families can't afford. Our goal is to provide them with a free of charge, in-home physiotherapy.

title: Winterization Aid for Afghan communities
description: Afghanistan is a country prone to harsh weather conditions. Severely cold winters with extremely low temperatures and heavy snowfall impact thousands of people, especially in rural areas where communities already suffer from poverty, internal displacement and lack of access to basic necessities. Action for Development has been providing emergency assistance to communities in need across Afghanistan since 2012.

title: Secondary Education for Girls In Rural Tanzania
description: Secondary school graduation rates for girls in East Africa are dismally low but ASAP has created a holistic model to increase' graduation rates for girls to 80% or higher! The Kupanda Project includes safe housing, academic support, health/sanitation and leadership development. It is being implemented for 144 girls at a secondary school in rural Tanzania and will soon be replicated at other rural secondary schools, creating a paradigm shift in girls' education throughout East Africa!

title: Peace Hub in Jaffa
description: Israel is getting attention mainly for being the Start-Up Nation and for the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict. What if we could combine the two and harness the entrepreneurial spirit and the creativity to address the conflict? You can now support the creation of a joint space social initiatives and creative promotion of peace in Israel-Palestine. Now is the time to address the conflict in a non-violent and creative way. Please jin us in supporting the Peace Hub in Jaffa.

title: Help Bring Equine Therapy To 30 Children in 2015!
description: Borrowed Freedom provides scholarship based Therapeutic (Adaptive) Riding, Hippotherapy and Equine Experiential Education for more than 45 clients with physical, intellectual, developmental, emotional and socio-economic special needs. All sessions are delivered at no charge for those with demonstrated need through a comprehensive scholarship program. When this project is funded we will be able to help 30 children receive the life changing benefits of equine therapies and activities in 2015.

title: Reduce Gender Based Violence in Urban Communities
description: The project aims to help women, adolescents and children fight gender based violence empowering them with life skills, academic engagement, reproductive health, livelihood and employable skills, and encouraging community leadership to reduce Gender Based Violence and for access to citizenship rights including civic amenities.

title: The Genius of Caring
description: The Genius of Caring is an interactive project that presents documentary portraits of family caregivers and those impacted by Alzheimer's and other caregiving diseases. We're raising funds to produce a series of community-based events and update our website to include the feature length documentary The Genius of Marian, educational materials, and all Genius of Caring short films available free to the public.

title: Technology Refresh for Operational/Cost Efficiency
description: Ending poverty for 5 million families by 2024 involves people, process and technology to organize volunteers, staff and materials to build communities and support sustainability. The project helps optimize technology so that IT operations behind the scenes of GK can equip staff, volunteers and communities with technology at a lower operational cost. The project will fund 15 desktop computers for students at Toyota GK Village school and 15 for social entrepreneurs at the GK Enchanted Farm.

title: SUPPORT OUR RURAL AREA MEDICAL MISSION-2015
description: Rural dwellers in Central Region of Ghana suffer from adverse health conditions owing to mainly two reasons -first the lack of education and thus lack of awareness; and second poverty in area of standard of living, poor road network to the health facilities and rural settlement. The situation calls for timely care and diagnosis which can reduce the incidence of morbidity and mortality especially among children and pregnant women.

title: 2015 Sound of Hope Radio FM 96.1 Funding
description: Sound of Hope FM 96.1 is dedicated to provide value and service to to Chinese Americans in San Francisco Bay Area. We are the ONLY non-profit Chinese public radio that was founded by a group of hi-tech engineers, who shared the same vision of creating a truth-telling, public serving and learning-oriented public radio.  This is novice idea and can ONLY be viable through your support! We are running the first funding campaign in 2015 and wish to obtain enough fund to support this public endeavor

title: Help the flood displaced people of Kelantan
description: The East Coast of Malaysia encountered the worst flood in over one hundred years. Many low lying areas have seen houses or even entire villages completely being destroyed by flood waters. What is most needed now is temporary shelters, house hold items, construction materials, tools and furnishing for reconstruction of homes, school and health clinics. Town areas will slowly crawl back to life but the Orang Asli will find it very hard to get life back to normal if no help is extended to them

title: Provide advanced medicine for 25 orphaned babies
description: In Russia, more than 7000 children of 0-5 y.o. live in orphanages. Most of them have got different health problems. Computerised axial tomography (CAT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are advanced methods used in medical diagnostics. Due to relatively high cost of these technologies, only a few orphanages can afford them. Donations are needed to carry CAT / MRI for making precise diagnosis and assigning effective therapy for orphaned babies, and thus to enhance their chances for adoption.

title: Quality Education in Sierra Leone and Liberia
description: We enable disadvantaged children in Sierra Leone and Liberia to access quality education. In Sierra Leone, we support the only functioning primary school on the remote Turtle Islands, and provide scholarships to children from low income families to attend high quality schools in Freetown. In Liberia, we fund the LIFE for Liberia literacy center serving out-of-school children in Paynesville, outside Monrovia.

title: emergency help to victims of heavy rains
description: This project is shall be overruled by The Chinseu Community Based Organization but there is a special committee that is set to look for the help received and where it shall be distributed (logistic committee). This committee is comprising of different members of the societies like Member from the office of the Ward Councilor, Area development committee, Village development committee, Representative from the religious group and chaired by the Chinseu CBO - Disaster Program Officer.

title: Warm-Winter Package for Community Senior Citizens
description: 100 Warm-Winter Packages for 100 community senior citizens. Each package includes: 1 professional health examination, 1 professional service plan design, 8-hour integrated home care services, 1-year-free hot-line service, and 1 new-year gift. 100 packages will be delivered by the Leling, a Non-Profit Organization providing professional community care services for the elderly people with disabilities in poor families.

title: Help 30 first-generation learners begin school
description: This project supports a 2-year playgroup program for children ages 2 to 3 years old from impoverished "Denotified Tribe" slum communities in India. These children will be the first in their families to go to school. The focus of the playgroup is to acclimate the children to a school environment, improve school readiness through play, games, songs, and activities, while also imparting valuable parenting skills to the parents who accompany the children. Free meals and healthcare are provided.

title: Radios for Sierra Leone: information and Ebola
description: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, which has already claimed more than 8,600 lives in West Africa, is slowly coming under control. However, the need for trusted information for public health campaigns, information and news is still key to halting the spread of the virus, and to help people pick up the pieces of their lives. Through the distribution of our solar and wind-up emergency Polaris radios, people in Sierra Leone will be able to access news and health information 24/7.

title: Build 40 toilets for migrant workers in India
description: This project will improve sanitation for rickshaw pullers in Jharkand, India by building a total of 40 toilet facilities over 10 pockets in the city.

title: Share Light with Mexican Children with Cancer
description: Since 1990, we have helped more than 12,600 low-income girls, boys and young people who suffer from cancer in Mexico. With your help, we can continue to do so for the 1,200 children we have in active treatment and the 4,800 children we have in present remission.

title: Build a Bridge - Save a Life: in Vietnam
description: In America, parents are (understandably) concerned when their young children have to cross a busy street to attend school. In the remote areas of Vietnam, children literally put their lives in jeopardy to attend school. Especially in the monsoon season, which lasts for months,  students needs to cross rivers on perilous monkey bridges, or sometimes even INSIDE of plastic bags, - see our video. Sometimes these children die. We can build 5 Foot Bridges to allow kids a safe journey to school.

title: Shape the future of 70 orphan children in India.
description: Orphan children also have a dream for love, motherly-care,  education and to have bright future. Realizing these needs of orphan & abandoned children, NBJK has established an orphanage named LBHC in Bodh Gaya-Bihar.  There are 70 children in 7 houses in LBHC, one "mother" in each house taking care of 10 children.  We need support from kind hearted people for continuing our efforts to provide them quality food, best education, health care and making future of these orphan children very bright.

title: African Girls' Education and Empowerment Training
description: To generate peace, we must foster compassion and education, especially among girls in Africa. They are under threat of kidnapping if they try to better themselves. However, when girls are educated and empowered, they support their communities. Families are better fed, and their health improves. Girls' Education and Empowerment Training project in Africa, mostly Nigeria, provides programs that give young girls who are in fear for their lives a way to learn and empower building a better community.

title: Catch Your Dream Summer Camp
description: Crohn's and ulcerative colitis summer camps for young people and children  Project 'Esc' is an ambitious project led by EYG, with supervision from EFCCA, to provide annual summer camps for young adults, teenagers, and then children with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, IBD), across Europe.  By developing and sharing know-how, we will also support national IBD associations in holding their own summer camps.  The project is operated by EFCCA, Rue Des Chartr

title: Transport Patients from Gaza to Israeli Hospitals
description: The Road to Recovery bridges the political/cultural Israeli-Palestinian divide by rendering humanitarian services on a personal level.  Volunteers use their vehicles to transport low-income children patients from the West Bank and Gaza to Israeli hospitals for treatment that is unavailable locally.  We charter a minibus to transport groups of patients from Gaza to Jerusalem hospitals. Project proceeds will fund a 100% increase in minibus patient-trips from Gaza to Jerusalem hospitals for a year

title: A Collective Song: Music to Make Hearts Sing
description: Our journey began with a passionate intern and for two years, the much-anticipated music center in Al Aqaba was a dream coming true.  41 students gather after school to learn violin, viola and cello. Lina Karamali's hard work has created a Center, bringing together a community of people united through music, exploring the value of music in restoring spirit and heart. And after only a few months of playing, the young students were invited to perform at universities. Let's keep this going!

title: Your Help will Save a Cow
description: In india Cows are treated as God by Hindu Community.In Rural areas,People,Partially illiterate,Use to shelter the cows mainly for milk production.They are Practising the anncient method for providing food and health hygyne to those innocent animals.They trated them as a productive tools not as a creature.So when the cows get herted use to realease them quickly from shelter or sell them to slaughter house.Our organisation with the view to serve the animal has taken up a project to provide shelter

title: Enhancing  orphans and  needy children livelyhood
description: the target orphans and needy children lack support to acquire education, health and shelter. This project calls for a donor to change their status of living to a bright generation to come. the project target orphans and needy children disadvantaged to be in school, care and mentoring for a generation to come. We have 425 orphans and needy children in our school, child rescue academy integrated, and 230 of whom stay in our compassion orphanage home.195 needy children stay with their care takers.

title: Support Girls' Education in India
description: Studies have shown that educated women are more likely to have smaller and healthier families, lower HIV infection rates, and higher wages, yet out of the 121 million children out of school, 52% are girls.  Room to Read's Girls' Education Program seeks to reverse this reality by supporting girls to complete secondary school with the skills necessary to negotiate key life decisions. In India, the program has benefited 11,340 girls to date, and is enrolling 900 new participants in 2015.

title: SUPPORT AND EDUCATE 600+ ORPHANS
description: This project will build a school building in Liberia to accommodate 600 plus students. Since 2012, financial support from our organization has fostered the academic development and care for underprivileged orphans in Liberia regardless of tribe or religion. We are committed to building Liberia's future through a high quality education program for our youth which will propel them towards a brighter future. (UNESCO) 75% of our children have no education and 80% are girls and this must change now.

title: Delivering Health and Hope to Nigeria's Poor
description: GEANCO (www.geanco.org) saves and transforms lives in Africa.  We conduct complex surgical missions and run an innovative program to fight anemia in Nigeria.  Through our system of modern, solar-powered rural maternal clinics, we help poor, vulnerable pregnant women safely deliver healthy babies.

title: Restore the right to quality education in Colombia
description: This project will provide personalized and extra socio affective support to at risk children in Bogota's Egipto neighborhood by meeting their distinctive needs and building on the principles of child-centered, active, participatory and cooperative learning. This will be a 1-year pilot implementation of "Circulos para ENprender", a variation of our innovative and renowned Escuela Nueva Leaning Circles program.

title: Autism & Law Enforcement Education Coalition
description: The ALEC Program trains First Responders (Fire, Police and EMS personnel) on autism spectrum disorders and the best practices when involved in a crisis situation with someone diagnosed with autism.  The ALEC Program has been in existence since 2003, and the trainers are First Responders who have a loved one diagnosed with autism.  First Responders hear from a colleague who has the professional knowledge of the field, as well as the personal experience of having a loved one diagnosed with autism.

title: Detecting Potentially Dangerous Asteroids & Comets
description: The Planetary Society recognizes the threat that asteroids and comets--known as Near Earth Objects, or NEOs--represent. While an asteroid strike could have devastating effects, the good news is that an asteroid impact is the only natural disaster that is completely preventable. Our most important program provides small grants to astronomers who seek to discover, observe and track NEOs. We give these grants out through the Shoemaker NEO grant program.

title: "Education and opportunities for vulnerable youth"
description: Many vulnerable youth in Colombia need more education opportunities. The project provides professional guidance, financial support for education and a program to get employment for 60 Youth. They have lived in poverty and need access to education, work, and other tools in order to build a better future for themselves. This support allows them to break the cycle of poverty within their families and communities. If you dream of a better world, help these young people to change their future

title: Care for Orphans and other Vulnerable Children
description: Children in Malawi experience many challenges requiring psychosocial support. Factors like HIV/ AIDS, poverty, social conflicts and family breakdown have psychosocial consequences for children. Promoting psychosocial support helps to instill hope in children. The project is committed to creating a safe environment to protect children from abuse, neglect and exploitation while mitigating the effect of the death of loved ones to ensure that children grow and develop to their full potential.

title: Help NW Boxer Rescue provide one SPAY A DAY!
description: We take in JUST OVER 40 homeless boxers every month, and most have not yet been spayed or neutered. Who doesn't love the curious face and expressive eyes of a boxer puppy? However, at any given time we have so many Boxers in our rescue program that surgical costs add up quickly. We are dedicated to providing exceptional care for all our sweet wigglers, and we believe their best chance for a happy future begins with this simple surgery.

title: Help more South African children achieve in Maths
description: After the success of  "Help South African children achieve in Maths" GlobalGiving Project we are scaling this Project to support more learners. Education is the key to break the poverty cycle for children from underserved communities. In South Africa only 35% of learners age 12-13 pass Maths. We use a per-child, online Maths program to promote learning & to track children's progress from these challenged communities. This individualised approach allows teachers to provide support to each child.

title: TO SUPPORT 20 ORPHANS AND VULNERABLE STUDENTS
description: The proposed project seek to assist 20  bright orphaned and vulnerable students aged between 14 years -16 years in Muranga county in kenya and who have  completed their primary school to enroll for secondary school education.The vulnerable students will be assisted each with USD$247 to be paid as school fees for the first year for their secondary school education.

title: Educate & Give voice to HODI Girls in North Kenya
description: HODI works with girls to give them a voice/choice & ensure they are able to stand up for themselves overcoming FGM, Beading & Child marriages. The project will provide access to education, training and life skills through football. The girls learn her to how to say NO; they learn to be confident and know about their rights, their health while providing them with skills to transition to high school & universities. Giving 100 girls a chance to overcome poverty, illiteracy & become future leaders.

title: Give girls in domestic work a safe place in Peru
description: La Casa de Panchita exists because girls as young as 9 from the poverty of the Andes and shantytowns are forced to work cleaning, cooking and watching children in other people's homes. They are years behind in their schooling and often doomed to work in domestic service their entire life. Through workshops, psychological counseling, school support and recreational  and cultural field-trips, at La Casa de Panchita we help these girls and adolescents pursue a better and dignified life.

title: Food Security for 1,800 Villagers in Senegal
description: CREATE! will install a drip irrigation network in the women's cooperative community garden located at CREATE!'s training and demonstration center in Ouarkhokh, Senegal. The purpose of this project is to reduce the cost and time-intensive labor needed to grow vegetables using hand watering and to increase the size of the year-round irrigated garden plot by 75%.

title: Help prevent sexual abuse of children in India
description: The WHO reports, India has the world's largest number of sexually abused children.  Arpan's key project - Personal Safety Education (PSE) program addresses this issue by giving children age-appropriate information and skills to help protect themselves from sexual abuse. Children who report instances of having been sexually abused are supported with counselling and intervention to make sure abuse stops. Parents and teachers are made aware of the issue also.

title: Keepers of the Coast: 65000 km of coast to protect
description: The "Keepers of the Coast" program aims to allow all citizens to effectively invest themselves in their region by protecting coastlines, ocean, and their right to enjoy them. Since 2008, Surfrider fight against attacks experienced by the European coastline. Support the Keepers of the Coast program to give our volunteers the resources to fight on equal terms.

title: Be The Change - feed 50,000 impoverished monthly
description: In South Africa, it is not uncommon to met beggars at nearly every traffic light, asking for money to support them and their families. Upon this encounter, local motorist give an average of R10 ($1) per day. However many choose not to give because they're unsure of where their money will go. Love Story has created an opportunity for people near and far to give to the less fortunate with a guarantee that their donations are doing toward food and much needed items.

title: Health and education for children in Chiapas
description: We will provide early stimulation and nutritional attention for indigenous girls and boys between 0 and 4 years of age, of limited resources and in high risk situations. With the project we seek to contribute to a healthy development of the cognitive and physical functions. Also, we will provide them with birth certificates and help them to enroll in preschool.

title: Help Yellowstone-Area Youth Discover Nature!
description: The Montana Audubon Center, in Billings, Montana, connects people with nature, with an emphasis on under-served youth and  families. As part of our Center's programs, we are developing, promoting, and operating Montana's first public, ADA accessible Nature Play Area. This space will provide a safe, free place for children to play outside and connect with nature in an unstructured manner. This unique play area will mimic natural components found along the nearby Yellowstone River corridor.

title: Save the ruins of a Slovak monastery - Katarinka
description: Archaeological reasearch helps us to clarify and understand life in this area in the 17th century. Help us with our work with youth - we promote enagagement and active stance to the preservation of our cultural and historical heritage and protect nature.   We do not seek to reconstruct the church and monastery of St. Catharine, but to preserve it in a safe condition to future generations.  Help us cover the costs for engaging 6 x 12 people (6 camps for 12 volunteers) in saving Katarinka.

title: Relief for 1900 displaced families - Northern Iraq
description: It is estimated that around 11 million Syrians have fled their homes since the start of the Syrian civil war in March 2011. According to the UN Refugee Agency, there are currently 230,836 Syrian Refugees in Iraq and most have faced an additional hardship because of the war and political climate of Iraq. These communities as well as displaced Iraqis continue to have an urgent need for food and hygiene supplies.

title: Provide Scholarships for Adults with Disabilities
description: This project establishes a fund for adults with disabilities to attend SPARC without paying the monthly participation fee. We help participants with lifelong and vocational learning, and make it easy to attend vocational and like skills classes at low prices. Scholarships are awarded on the basis of financial need.  Month after month and year after year we have to raise $11,000 per month to close the gap between fees paid and actual costs.

title: Equine Therapy for 20 Veterans in Hopkinton NH
description: Ride UP, a program of riding and ground work with horses provides unique opportunities for Uniformed Professionals who serve our community to process experiences encountered at work.  Therapeutic interactions with horses have been shown beneficial in cases of P.T.S.D., which can affect anyone engaged in dangerous, life threatening activities, such as Veterans, Police, Fire, and Rescue Personnel. Non-judgmental, welcoming group activities allow processing of life events in a safe environment.

title: Hostel facility for Handicapped girls
description: Purpose of the project to build a residential facility for 16 "differently able" girls in Narasipur village, near Bangalore through a charity "Dharithree" registered in India. Currently the differently able girl students face enormous challenges to commute to Dharithree, This hostel will encourage more parents to send their girls to the "Dharithree" , an organization/s specifically built to cater to their special needs.

title: End Violence Against Women
description: The Trust Fund to End Violence against Women currently supports 78 initiatives in 71 countries and territories, with grants totalling US$8 million, and provides help for effective and sustainable initiatives to prevent, address, reduce, and ultimately eliminate these violations of women's human rights. Your donation to the Trust Fund will go towards an effective and long-term investment in building a world free from violence against women and girls.

title: Desperate need to increase hay storage
description: The United SPCA is able to buy a small amount of hay at a time due to limited storage of approximately four tons of hay. This hay storage is also in the same building as where horses are sheltered. Storing hay in the same building is an extreme fire hazard. If the water content of the stored hay is too high, it will combust. Please help us build a storage building safely away from the horses; and allowing us to buy bulk hay dramatically reducing cost, spreading your donations farther for horses.

title: Help Families with a Sick Newborn Baby in Hospital
description: Rainbow Trust has been providing emotional and practical support for families with terminally ill children since 1986. However, following publication of a report by the University of Leeds in 2011, we have identified an area in which there is currently little or no support for families, and aim to introduce our new neonatal palliative care service to provide specialist support for families with very sick new born babies.

title: Medical Training for Doctors in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone's health service  has recently been described as "stretched far beyond capability". Many of the senior doctors had succumbed to Ebola and junior doctors were on strike. Forty out of 60 students at the University of Sierra Leone's Provost of the College of Pharmacology, Medicine and Allied Health Sciences were forced to abandon their studies last year after they ran out of money. This fund will help medical student complete their studies.

title: Building a library for needy students in Nicaragua
description: This project will build a library in fishermen communities in Nicaragua, providing a rich supply of books to 600 needy kids.   The kids of these communities have never had a library and they deserve the opportunity of knowledge.

title: HYA Providing Aid for Syrian refugees in Jordan
description: With well over 100,000 refugees calling Zaatari home, among them more than 16,000 school aged children, education and healthcare resources are stretched to their limits. Around 200 babies are born in the camp every month and there is a shortage of milk for these babies and toys and school supplies for the children. We want to provide these necessities to the children, many of whom crossed the border into Jordan without their parents.

title: BUILD A MEDICAL CENTER FOR 33000 PEOPLE AT KALO
description: Kalo Telema plans to build a medical center and water wells to provide healthcare and clean water for people who live in this poorest and enclosed region in DR Congo. This project to build a medical center (maternity, nutrition center included) will provide health care and clean water to more than 33000 people. They do not have access to healthcare and clean water because there is no medical infrastructures and no water wells for the clean water in this area.

title: Grow an Indigenous Youths' Beekeeping Cooperative
description: An indigenous youth-run organic honey cooperative is struggling to stay in business, losing members to dangerous work in the city.  With some technical training in honey production technologies, sales and marketing, the "Bee Boys" will increase their honey production, sales and create stable, sustainable jobs for at-risk youth.  Learning-by-doing, the training sessions will leave the group with skills, techniques and materials to re-invest and grow their business.

title: Support Connections for Learning
description: Connections for Learning provides funding for individuals with bleeding disorders to attend the National Hemophilia Foundation Annual Meeting to gain the relevant experience and practical knowledge they need to better navigate life with a chronic illness.

title: Give Childhood a Chance and Keep Youth Drug Free!
description: Addiction destroys families, children and community livelihood. The International Blue Cross works with 41 member organizations to reduce substance abuse, especially among youth, and improve alcohol policies to protect our youth. We see a world where children can grow up in safe, healthy families and live free from addiction. We also see a world where people already harmed by addiction have access to treatment.

title: Support 100 Children With Special Needs in Houston
description: This is a day care center for children with special needs in Houston, Texas. Funds will allow Smartie Pants to provide free tutoring, therapy, and expand advocacy support services to over 100 children a year with special needs, 90% of which come from low income single parent homes.

title: Children in Motion:  Together is Better
description: In Russia, children with disabilities (CWD) are still isolated in their homes, segregated in special schools, and excluded from their communities.  The disability NGO Perspektiva aims to improve this situation by offering inclusive youth sports opportunities. 400 children, including 100 CWD; 10 physical education teachers at 10 schools; 80 schoolteachers; 150 parents of children with and without disabilities; and 50 disabled athletes will participate in trainings and inclusive sports activities.

title: 2015 Free Speech Film Festival
description: American INSIGHT's 2015 Free Speech Film Festival provides a beacon of hope to individuals around the world who seek freedom of expression in repressive societies. Our mission is to provide an apolitical online framework to practice, promote, and preserve the principles of free speech and the rule of law, through the power of film and social media; and to establish a vehicle of communications for youth around the globe.

title: Support Growth of 10 Social Enterprises
description: Grassroots Business Fund invests in social businesses that are making a positive impact at the base of the pyramid in communities around the world. MBAs Without Borders Advisors, recruits graduates of top business schools to grow and scale social enterprises that drive economic development, create jobs, and improve standards of living in dynamic global markets. MBAs Without Borders will partner with Grassroots Business Fund to provide pro bono consulting services to ten social enterprises.

title: Educate & Empower Children from Kibera, Kenya
description: RFS provides vulnerable children from the slum of Kibera, Kenya, with the opportunity to attend a boarding school where they receive a quality education.  Here they are provided an education along with three meals a day, clean water, medical care, a bed, uniform, and safety. "Most people look at the slum of Kibera and see a huge unsolvable problem. We see huge untapped potential."

title: Sewing Machines for Girls for Self-Reliance
description: Azad India Foundation is running stitching center in Kishanganj where 25 girls learn cutting and tailoring .A sewing machine to needy girls will help them to achieve economic self reliance and lead life of dignity.

title: Sponsor School kits for needy Indian children-2015
description: While trying to address the issues regarding enrollment of underprivileged children in Govt. schools in rural parts of India, we realised that despite Govt. education being almost free of cost, many children did not take the first step towards the school, simply because they did not have the very basic school supplies. As a humble attempt to change this situation we started a School Kit Sponsorship program

title: Free 200 Girls from Female Circumcision Nigeria
description: This project will be focusing on educating communities on the need to eradicate female genital mutilation in ikom & boki of cross river state. it will rescue 200 girls from 25 communities in an alternative rite of passage ceremony without the cut. through advocacy, open community dialogue/sensitization, and media awareness it will educate girls and boys about life skills, sexuality education, HIV, offer empowerment vocational training and seed grant to rural women.

title: Empower through Education for Poverty Eradication
description: The project aims to improve lives of child labourers, non-school going children and first generation learners by creating a model for the holistic education of the children of migrant workers. It aims to break the deep rooted generational cycle of unskilled labor through a holistic approach to education, recognizing that a 'well-rounded,' democratically-skilled child has an increased chance to work as a skilled laborer. The project will be implemented in 10 villages of Dahod district in Gujarat

title: Children's Heart
description: Since 2007, Mission Bambini has helped children with heart defects in underdeveloped countries. Our aim is to tackle the high rate of infant mortality caused by lack of swift medical care. The project has successfully implemented three intervention methods: medical missions abroad; helping to cover medical costs; providing surgery for children in Italy. In the last 8 years, 1,373 children have been saved by heart surgeries performed by our medical team, while 10,732 have been seen by a doctor.

title: Change makers in Colombia - Lideres de Cambio
description: This project aims to empower colombian young people to become change makers and contributes to build a peace community.

title: Build 40 homes for Haiyan Survivors in Cebu
description: Kinatarkan Island is one of the most severely devastated islands in the Northernmost part of Cebu Province, yet the least served in terms of humanitarian efforts because of its distance and the difficulty of crossing the open sea to reach the island. Over 700 houses were completely damaged by typhoon Haiyan, So far only  14 houses have been rebuilt and we want to do more.  Helping them to re-build more houses will help the community to slowly re-build their lives and their livelihood.

title: Alcohol-free spaces for children in Greenland
description: A staggering 30% of children in Greenland are victims of their parents' excessive drinking. The Blue Cross in Denmark has committed to supporting Blue Cross Greenland in their mission to reduce alcohol-related harm, especially among children.

title: Give Support to 800 Syrian Refugee Families
description: Focus of DKH in the countries of Syria, Jordan, Iraq, Lebanon and Turkey is the supply of refugee families, especially outside the camps, and support for host families and communities. Especially now, as winter sets in, people urgently need accommodation, clothing, blankets, stoves, and coal and food.

title: Computer Lab for 150 At-Risk Children in Thailand
description: The SOLD Project will equip the computer lab in the second building of the Resource Center with 10 computers. This will give the at-risk children of this poor rural community access to the internet and the opportunity to learn computer skills.

title: Ebola Prevention: Making Learning Safe in Liberia
description: With the Liberian government announcing the reopening of schools following the Ebola outbreak, many families lack the basic resources necessary to send their children to school. Many children cannot attend school due to deaths in the family and/or a severe lack of resources. To buttress the government's efforts to keep every school safe and prepared for future emergencies, the "Learning Safe Project" has been developed to provide immediate assistance to children to return to school.

title: WASH: Healthy Safety for children post Ebola
description: This project will build a new and functioning indoor toilet system with hand-washing stations, septic tank, and a hand pump for safe drinking water that will benefit over 200 children at a local school. Our WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) project is in line with the objective of UNICEF to contribute to the realization of children's rights to survival and development by increasing equitable and sustainable access to safe water and basic sanitation, and promote improved hygiene.

title: Yoga Stops Traffick 2016 - Fundraiser for Odanadi
description: YOGA STOPS TRAFFICK is a one-day global yoga event created to raise awareness and funds for Indian anti-trafficking organisation Odanadi Seva Trust.  Odanadi rescues and rehabilitates individuals who have been trafficked, prostituted, enslaved and abused in Mysore, India. Odanadi offers them a home, counselling, an education and career opportunities.

title: Sponsor a Special Education Student
description: Special education in Belize continues to prove a challenge. At Ambergris Caye Elementary School we create individualized educational plans for students with disabilities, promote inclusion, have a substantiallyseparate special needs class and resource room and provide a safe and accepting place to learn important educational skills and necessary life skills. Our goal is to provide options for children with disabilities whose parents cannot afford to send them to school.

title: Help us Spay/Neuter 1500 homeless cats in 2015
description: Our project is to spay/neuter 1500 homeless cats in 2015. This will help prevent thousands of homeless babies being born this year.  Homeless cats typically have a short life, starvation, being hit by cars, etc.  They will get medical care they need and no more homeless babies being born.

title: StandWithWomen in the Middle East to Create Change
description: CHIME FOR CHANGE and Equality Now will support local partners and activists to ensure that laws are equal, prohibit violence against women and girls, and provide equal access to justice. This project will empower and support activists from across the Middle East and North Africa (including Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Morocco, Palestine and Tunisia) to develop and execute national advocacy campaigns to repeal discriminatory laws that perpetuate violence against women and girls.

title: Free Yezidi Foundation Women's Center
description: The FYF Women's Center will open in late 2015. The Women's Center will be a safe space for Yezidi women, some of whom have endured unspeakable trauma. The Center will be run and operated by young Yezidi activists, and will provide a safe and nurturing environment with enriching and educational activities. In this context, FYF will also provide a pathway for post-trauma treatment by local practitioners trained by FYF's international post-trauma experts.

title: Free Yezidi Foundation Children's Center
description: The Free Yezidi Foundation Children's Center is designed to provide assistance to all Yezidi children suffering the traumatic after-effects of the ISIS attack against Yezidi populations in 2014. The Center will cater especially to those children whose parents were killed during the attacks, but will also provide services to children with access to the Center. The Center will provide enriching activities, basic needs such as shoes and food, and a pathway to post-trauma treatment if necessary.

title: Care Home for HIV Infected kids in India.
description: We are running care homes for HIV infected kids in Jaipur (Pink City) India. All civic amenities including food, education, health care, recreation and counseling services are provided by the organization. These care homes are run in rented accommodations and changing the house every 2-3 years is big problem for us because with the change in address their schools also get changed/  That's why we plan for constructing a care house building for our kids on the land donated by one well wisher.

title: Empower Women in Guatemala with Education & Income
description: Unmarked Streets teaches women in Guatemala skills like jewelry making, sewing, & quilting, and provides training/education on running a business. Participants earn money right away while building skills for the future. We work with a partner NGO which helps people find work - only 10% of women who come in are able to get a job. We will never see progress when 50% of the population is denied access to the job market. You can make a difference - donations go directly to the women in the program.

title: Provide housing for 100 Ebola affected orphans
description: Since the Ebola virus outbreak in 2014, over 4500 children lost their parents and became orphaned.  These children are now struggling to find food, shelter, medical care and the support they need to sustain themselves in the proper way. Taking them off the streets is very essential because if we don't they could be exploited in many ways for example the sex trade, child labor, arm robbery, and theft. Upon completion of the girls and boys dorms, we will be able to house 100 orphan children.

title: Support 200 Women SHG Micro Entrepreneurs
description: The proposed  project aims to provide seed capital to poor Women entrepreneurs to fulfil their credit requirements and thereby free them from the clutches of local money lenders, who charges exorbitant rate of interest. This project aims to achieve economic development of the beneficiary thereby attempting to reverse the age-old vicious cycle of "low income, low savings, and low investment".We will work through women's SHG groups as women are the most vulnerable section of the society.

title: Give 12 Cambodian Students 21st Century Skills
description: This project will ensure the ongoing wellbeing and education of 12 at-risk children in one of Cambodia's impoverished regions. 21st century skills, such as English and technology, will give these children the opportunity to break the cycle of poverty and become professionals and leaders in their community. This project provides access to public school as well as supplementary education, including computer, literacy, math, English, arts, soccer, and more.

title: Prepare 50 Underserved Boys for Summer Employment
description: Last year, the Ready Golf Caddies camp hosted more than 20 students from Maryland and the District of Columbia. Among those students were Niko and Tyrin. Niko, a first-generation college student, is on his way to college with scholarships and Tyrin, who came to the program seeking a mentor, is performing at the top of his 10th grade class. This program allows underserved children to increase their confidence, reach their goals, and explore new environments that were once inaccessible to them.

title: Help provide school bus for orphans
description: The horror of losing their parents to civil war, the Ebola Virus and extreme poverty has left many children out in the cold to fend for themselves for basic necessities such as a high quality education and food. Due to these hardships, they don't have the means to get to and from school safely. We need a school bus in order to transport 600 plus orphan students to and from school, field trips, sporting events and science project which are essential for their academic growth.

title: 5th Grade Science Camp Transportation
description: This project will raise money for buses to bring 5th graders to 4-days of science camp.  Each child pays for the camp, but we fundraise for transportation to keep costs as low as possible for the children.  Excess funds go towards scholarships so that every child can attend.

title: Support vocational school for 75 orphans
description: Our organization provides an open vocational school system to train, assist, and mentor orphans in various capacities such as Electrical, Plumbing, Sewing, Masonry, Farming, Janitorial, Certified Nurses Assistants (CNA) and other industrial training to prepare them for the workforce. These orphans are the byproduct of the deadly 15 year long civil war and the ongoing Ebola virus epidemic that has plagued Liberia and shut down schooling for a lengthy period of time leaving them uneducated.

title: Help Orphans With New Class Rooms and Desks
description: Launching a new campaign for needed funds for classroom construction of an orphanage, Sharon Children Home in India.  Sitting outside teaching students in harsh (difficult) weather makes it very important for us  to find a way to get support to build the new classrooms.Sharon Children Home is not supported by grants or governmental aid.  They are solely dependent on donations from compassionate organizations and individuals like you and me.  The home exists to care for 60 abandoned children.

title: Supporting Women in Science in Southern Africa
description: In sub-Saharan Africa, only 29% of STEM researchers (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) are female (UN Women Statistics). Faced with complex developmental challenges, southern Africa needs more scientific researchers. There is huge potential to develop a vibrant and diverse research community within the region to tackle these challenges head-on by encouraging women in the sciences.

title: Save Georgian Babies with Critical Heart Defects
description: Over 1,000 babies with potentially fatal heart complications are born in Georgia annually.They can be saved if screened and diagnosed within 48 hours of birth. Thanks to your support, the first phase of the newborn heart screening program in Tbilisi has now been fully sustained by the Ministry of Health! However, other infants in the country are still in urgent need of this life-saving screening program, particularly in the Kvemo Kartli region - an area where newborns are especially vulnerable.

title: Saving the honeybee one beekeeper at a time!
description: Spikenard Honeybee Sanctuary is raising funds for scholarships, children's programs, and new workshops so that more and more individuals can learn methods of sustainable beekeeping that contribute towards saving the honeybee.  While most blame collapsing honeybee populations on pesticide companies, lack of habitat, and invasive parasites, we recognize that if we, as beekeepers, do not change our ways, our children are likely to grow up in a world without bees, without flowers, without fruits.

title: Empower and Educate WISER girls in rural Kenya
description: WISER works with girls to transcend poverty, HIV/AIDS, and gender-based violence. We do this by creating environments that produce exceptional young women who drive change in their communities. We build self-esteem, provide access to health education and knowledge, and produce academic high achievers. This project will provide education, food, housing, clothing, psychosocial support, access to university-quality labs, computers, and hands-on learning opportunities to 240 girls.

title: Business skills & loans for BG Women Entrepreneurs
description: Breaking Ground's Women's Entrepreneurial Program (WEP) provides women with critical business skills through a seven-week business course that incorporates topics such as feasibility studies, basic marketing, cost analysis, and leadership. At the end of the program, women are invited to submit a business proposal to receive a loan from Breaking Ground. In 2016, Breaking Ground will distribute at least 16 business loans and provide business training to 50+ rural women.

title: Build a school for 200 street children in Ghana
description: This project aim at addressing illiteracy among underprivileged children by constructing a portable classroom to provide them with serene and healthy learning environment. Currently we have managed to mobilise these children under an open nature shelter where we meet  everyday to study. Situation on ground such as frequent bumping of people into the premises does not permit sound studies. With a portable classroom we guarantee these children right to quality education no matter their background.

title: Feed 1,800 orphaned children in rural Kenya.
description: This project will help feed 1,800 orphaned and vulnerable children every day. Malnutrition is an inherent problem throughout rural Kenya, which is further complicated by many political, social and economic factors. One nutritious meal a day will save a child's life. In as little as four months, a malnourished child can transform into a healthy child. A healthy, well fed child can then attend school and gain knowledge and skills for a productive and hopeful future.

title: Support 100 households to access safe  water
description: This project aims at reducing diarrhea  and other communicable diseases among children aged  between 3 to 10 years  from poor households due to  drinking dirty water , reduce on child and women abuse at water source points  which result from fighting for safe drinking water  in Mityana district of Uganda by constructing 5 water sources in to benefit 100 households

title: Building toilets for 300 poor families in India
description: Have you ever pictured a house without toilets? Well, in India, this is a reality. In the district of Cuddalore in which our organization is established, more than 60% of the population does not have access to toilet facilities. After the success of our former campaign to build 500 toilets in the district of Cuddalore; we decided to extend it and to build more toilet facilities for another 300 families. These families were chosen amongst the poorest Dalit and tribal communities of our district.

title: HOSPITALITY PROJECT, HOW TO START A NEW LIFE
description: This project aims at funding one full year of stay in a house with secret address for one woman who has escaped from home abuse and wants to start a new life. Starting a new life means learning to be independent, both psychologically and economically.  CADMI support abused women making available houses with secret address, where they can regain dignity and freedom.

title: Saving Lives of Snakebite Victims in Rural India
description: Every year 45,000 people in rural India die after being bitten by a snake. Anjali Health Centre (AHC) is a small 20-bed hospital in Pithora - Chhattisgarh providing medical aid to over 3000 families of mostly of tribal and native communities. Last year AHC received 126 snake bite victims. This project will provide AHC with crucial support in the form of antivenom serum (AVS), life support equipment (ventilators & hemodialyzers), training in snakebite treatment and expert medical advice as needed

title: Native American After-School Program
description: Fewer than half of the Tohono O'odham community's adults have completed high school, the lowest rate of all U.S. Native American tribes. The Gu Vo Youth After-School program establishes a safe, fun, active learning environment for the students, giving them the support and incentives they need to remain enrolled in school, improve their study skills, and increase grade point averages.

title: Communities Fighting Ebola in Urban Sierra Leone
description: The Welbodi Partnership works in some of the poorest urban neighborhoods of Freetown, many of them very hard hit by the Ebola outbreak. With this project, we will engage with community leaders and the staff of primary health clinics, who often know best what they need to stop the spread of Ebola and reduce its impact in their communities. We will provide funding for the most promising of these ideas, and will help community groups and front line health workers implement these initiatives.

title: WE HAVE BUILT IT - THE CHILDREN WANT TO COME
description: To provide a loving home for Ghanaian Orphans, Trafficked and Deserted children where they will be educated to grow with physical health, mental ability, emotional stability, vocational skills, good citizenship and multicultural expertise. Through this education and experience, they can learn to be responsible adults who can both care for their own families and pay forward what they have learned and achieved to help other.

title: Sponsor Fuel& Driver Maintenance Vehicle/Ambulance
description: We are organizing a home for the destitute older citizens, who have no one else in this world to support them in their last days. Regular medical check-ups are provided to the destitute older people to ensure they are healthy and happy.  In times of emergency when we need to take the aged people to the hospitals, now it is possible with our own vehicle. Here we request you to donate for Fuel and Driver maintenance for Vehicle

title: A Place for Peace and Ideas for Young Armenians
description: This project will provide young people with a safe welcoming place to explore, discuss and discover the language, art and actions that make for a vibrant, diverse and democratic society. Many live in a world of tradition except here at Peace Dialogue NGO where they can come with their friends to create a new dynamic community of ideas, growth and change . Here they can be free of the limits that bind the rest of Armenian society and dream of a world that they want to live in and build a family.

title: Pursuing new treatments for Neuroblastoma children
description: Cure First is tackling neuroblastoma (NB), a childhood cancer for which survival is poor and current treatments are overshadowed by side effects. Despite this,  NB has not attracted the focus of the pharmaceutical industry. Recently we were able to establish patient-derived organoids and to apply high-throughput robotic tools to highlight drug sensitivities. We are now raising funds to finance an in vivo study which will help validate our findings and prepare them for a clinical trial.

title: Build 3rd floor on Ebola orphanage in Sierra Leone
description: Due to crowded living at the Bonnie Memorial Children's Home (BMCH) for orphans of Ebola in Sierra Leone, it's time to expand! Construction is underway, but more funds are still needed to finish the project.

title: EFCCA
description: The European Federation of Crohn's & Ulcerative Colitis Associations represents 28 national patients' associations from 27 European states and 3 associate members. It aims to improve life for people with IBD and give them a louder voice.

title: Help us to Strengthening farm- School
description: With your contribution will buy the materials needed to bring them walls of our classrooms, and build a classroom workshop, benefiting 200 children and adolescents each year through programs of technical education and art that in those classrooms are free developed for poor people of Ciudad Sandino y Managua.

title: Social Enterprise Cafe for Georgian IDP Settlement
description: This social enterprise cafe will provide Georgian refugees from the 2008 South Ossetian War with professional training opportunities. The training room will provide professional skills training for local youth and host cultural events.  Social Enterprise Cafe became anopen space for everybody and young people are more involved in different non-formal activities. We want to keep the cafe as an open space to run different interesting meetings, but without paying rental costs, it will be difficult.

title: Eggs to feed hungry Grandmothers in Darfur
description: This Easter, please give a Chicken not an Egg!  Give a chicken to a Grandmother in Darfur and she will be healthy. Whilst our Goat Loans work miracles for children, herding a flock is too much for frail older people to manage, and so Kids for Kids provides chickens - easy to look after and the eggs are a brilliant source of protein. Reports are coming through loud and clear - Chickens transform lives. Grandma Afaf said: "For the first time in months I am eating good food"

title: Social football and education program in medellin
description: Social football program : An educational program that combines the methodology of football for peace and sport Football for the future.  Methodology: We impact children between 8 and 15 years and their families with programs in values education and educational workshops which are intended to provide them with tools for living. Beneficiaries : Children ages 8 to 12 years belonging to vulnerable community who participate in the program with his family.

title: Reconstruct 40 children with stoma in East Africa
description: The project raises fund to pay the cost of surgical and clinical care  for children with anorectal malformation in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda. In general, these child will need 3 surgeries to correct the anorectal malformation, as determined by the anatomy. Our aim is to restore health and give hope to these children so that they can go to school, provide for their families and contribute to the society.

title: Provide Computer Education for the Blind
description: Our motto is to make the visually Impaired become more independent in this competitive world.We provide dedicated support to the visually impaired and disabled by providing them the education in field of computer, independent living skills,provide braille books,free regular transport in and around Mysore throughout the academic year,help them in getting employment.This help as deterrent to deserving students to continue their education.so people with vision loss can achieve their full potential.

title: Enhance 200 Youth in IT In kenya
description: This project  will build a resource and training center to provide  training to 200 youths from Langas slum villages on IT.

title: Health for 45 indigenous communities in Mexico
description: Our foundation has been working with indigenous communities in Mexico for 42 years,helping to generate local development and to improve living conditions.The most impoverished communities in Chiapas are suffering the increasing difficulty of access to health services,because of this we intend to promote a project to generate alternative health services in the area to cover the health needs of 45 indigenous communities covering 15000 people and thereby decreasing the % mortality and malnutrition.

title: Give education & sports to 728 children in Bogota
description: Give the opportunity to 728 children to have a brighter future in Ciudad Bolivar, one of the poorest localities in Bogota, Colombia. We are looking to strengthen the program Goals for a Better Life, which has been developing School tutoring, recreational and sport activities, such as soccer, rugby, basketball, music, Etc. All with the purpose of improve the children quality life by providing an space for personal growth and showing them that they have opportunities to be happy and successful.

title: Provide Meals for 35 Children in Rural Cambodia
description: REDA Orphanage is home to 35 children in rural Svay Rieng, Cambodia.  By partnering financially with REDA, you can provide food, school and hygiene supplies, and access to education for these children.  REDA is a multi-faceted community development organization that supports families living in poverty.

title: Help 361612 girl children realize full potential
description: LET HER FLY. These three simple words have the power to set a girl child free.
