It plans to inspire and encourage parents, teachers, husbands, brothers, and colleagues to give the girl child the opportunities that she so rightly deserves. Through project 'Let Her Fly'  together let us make sure 361,612 girl children across CRY-supported projects in India, soar  high and realise their full potential

title: Mental Well-being through play for 56,000 children
description: 'Play is not a luxury. Play is a necessity.' Nothing is as innate to a child as play. Children who don't play miss out on a joyful & well-rounded childhood. Toybank envisions a world where all children are empowered through healthy play. We use our Conscious Play approach, mindful of its impact on a child's development, to keep at-risk children on-track with their mental & behavioral well-being. Toybank understands that intervention in a child's formative years ensures an equitable adulthood.

title: 100,000 Fruit Trees for El Salvador
description: The Fruit Tree Planting Foundation is striving to bring 100,000 fruit trees to the people of El Salvador. Together with the community, local non-profits, and municipalities, we will bring fruitful trees & horticultural training to areas affected by deforestation, violence, & poverty. Trees will be planted at schools, farmer's cooperatives & community centers, bringing sustainable nutrition & income to struggling families & communities, and training to provide information on planting aftercare.

title: GLOW Georgia Small Grants Program
description: Through the GLOW Small Grants Program we will provide funding for community projects planned and executed by Georgian girls throughout all of the regions of Georgia. GLOW Ambassadors, the most motivated leaders from our GLOW camps, will be eligible to apply for grants of up to 500 GEL to help support their community projects, enabling them to have an even bigger impact in their communities.

title: "Defying the Odds" for Students in Newburgh, NY
description: San Miguel Academy's (SMAN) population is underserved males at highest risk of dropping out in NY's highest drug and gang filled city. SMAN is a 5-8th grade, 11-mo. extended 6 dy/wk program. Working toward healing the  whole child is essential to the student's educational success. Place and Project-Based Learning, experienced outside of Newburgh, is a major component of our curriculum. Graduation rate is 100%, with 100% accepted into secondary & post-secondary programs through Graduate Support.

title: Fruit Trees For Uganda
description: FTPF is working hard on the ground and in our nurseries to provide fruit trees across Uganda that will increase access to sustainable nutrition, provide income for families in poverty, and help the environment. We distribute trees directly to households in low-income areas accompanied by knowledge exchange workshops on how to care for fruit trees long term. Orchards are also planted in schools, health clinics, community centers, and orphanages to promote community health and wellbeing.

title: Hope of Education For 100 Poor Children in SriLank
description: The purpose of this project is to provide educational facility for the 100 poor rural children. They belong to very poor families and their parents cannot provide them education. It is necessary to educate these poor children otherwise they will ruin their future by involving in sex trade, child labor, smuggling, and drugs. You can give them bright future. At the end of this project, we will be able to give them a new future and they will be able to live their lives as respectable human beings.

title: Rescue 90 child marriage victim girls in Tanzania
description: This project will rescue and provide full educational  scholarship  in primary, secondary and vocational training education  to 90 girls who are victims and at risk of forced child marriage and Female genital mutilation from rural pastoralist communities in Tanzania. In Tanzania the pastoralist communities  are marginalized  by their dominant culture, education is not a priority to them. Only fewer pastorolists get education especially males, while girls are less likely to go to school.

title: 700 schoolbag kit for girls in northern Nigeria
description: In 2013, about 200 girls where abducted from a school in northern Nigeria.This has added to the ever growing reluctance in the education of girls in the northern part of our country, Nigeria.This project is aimed at igniting the passion of getting an education in girls. We are targeting primary schools with the aim to encourage them to get an education and the importance of an education, at a very young age.A school bag with complete books and kit will be given to encourage excellent performer

title: SEED Junior Academy, Kibera.
description: SEED Junior Academy is a primary school located in Kibera slum, Nairobi, the largest slum in eastern Africa.  SJA provides an education and lunch to around 60 children who would otherwise not be in school due to a lack of public education in the slum. The school also employs three teachers and one cook who live in Nairobi.  SJA aims to empower its students to make changes in Kibera, and gain the skills to fulfill their potential.

title: Libraries for Poor Children in India
description: Imagine spending your childhood, without any story books. How dull would it be without the glossy, colorful story books to read. How do you dream about fairy tales without a chance to read one? This is the harsh reality at most village government schools in India. We believe that children have a right to dream and by filling the libraries with books at their schools, we give the minds of these children the opportunity to take wings. Join us to help these children get the magic of reading books.

title: Support Our Team of Therapy Horses
description: In 2014, DreamPower Horsemanship provided equine-assisted activities and therapies to more than 450 children, teens and adults with special needs. Sixteen kind and patient equine partners work in the DreamPower program. This project will support our horses, making it possible for them to keep up their good work.

title: Emancipation of the Girl Child Through Education
description: The projects seeks to provide education to first-generation school going girl children from the most backward communities, thereby providing opportunities to break out of poverty and illiteracy.

title: Gombe School of Environment and Society (GOSESO)
description: The Gombe School of Environment and Society (GOSESO) seeks to bridge human and wildlife prosperity through education for rural Africans with a focus on environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods. Based in western Tanzania, this project provides resources for teacher training programs in environmental education, service-learning for students, and the design and implementation of experimental courses in community-based conservation.

title: Access to clean water for P.A.C.E women
description: To date, 376 women have received life skills education through the Gap Inc. P.A.C.E. in Community program in Thimmampalli, India; however these women and their communities today face a shortage of water for their basic household needs. Through the funds raised on this campaign, we will temporarily provide clean water from a different source and establish a long-term solution to recharge ground water.

title: FREE  FACIAL DEFORMITY SURGICAL OUTREACH PROGRAMME
description: The scourge of facial cleft and craniofacial deformity in Nigeria is appalling with a prevalence of 1 in 1000 individuals. This results in social stigmatization leading to an increase in the 'out-of-school syndrome' in  children and adolescents. This project is targeted at providing free facial surgical treatments for 500 targeted persons ,drawn from 7 regions within NORTH-CENTRAL NIGERIA.

title: Paridi's Education: a role model for thousands
description: Paridi is the 4th of 6 children of a struggling family from Sragen, Central Java. Paridi had to struggle to pay his own school fees as well as helping the education of his younger brothers that made him to bury his dream of becoming an Accountant through University. Currently, Paridi works at YUM as a bookkeeper and he wants to improve his quality of life by enrolling at the Faculty of Economy. This project will help his university fees, books and study expenses for a period of 4 years.

title: Livelihood harnessing through culture cage
description: Green Youth Conservation Uganda seeks $12000 to fund an innovative cage culture tilapia project for the members and the surrounding community; the project will serve 90 people including their families; subsistence fishermen, women and youth groups in Entebbe municipality, teaching them to take advantage of the economic tools and opportunities presented by the water resources surrounding us. The project intends to produce a total of 90,000 Tilapia fish in a period of 12 months.

title: Solar Home Lighting to poor villagers in Rajasthan
description: This project will provides Solar Power System to light-up houses of poor rural people and will provide mobile charging facilities in 200 households in Rajasthan. This project will provide solar power to 1000 people enhancing environmental condition and enable villagers to work, children to study and eliminating kerosene lanterns (saving Rs. 10 million) and improving health while reducing CO2 emissions.

title: HELP 100 CHILDREN WITH DISABILITIES IN MUFULIRA
description: Mufulira is a mining town in the copperbelt province of Zambia. it has experienced the air pollution for quite some time now. The sulphur dioxide the common air pollution in the district has a negative impact to the human and environment. especially children who are mostly affected  and most of them are born with different  deformity . disabilities such as cerebral palsy, hydrocephalus and other disabilities. we have been helping the children by taking them to special schools and  physiotherapy

title: Prevent Cervical Cancer for Women in Oyo, Nigeria
description: Cervical cancer is a preventable disease that kills thousands of Nigerian women yearly. The Access to Basic medical Care (ABC medical) Foundation is committed to reducing the impact of cervical cancer in Nigerian women by providing accessible screening and treatment facilities in Oyo State. 20% of  women screened in a recent exercise tested positive for HPV infection. Further diagnosis of precancerous lesions and treatment  needs to be provided for these women.

title: Disciple 50 change agents to build Nigeria.
description: Apostles in the Market Place is a critical mentoring and discipleship platform from respected marketplace Christian leaders and professionals that identifies, selects, equips and deploys change agents to transform different spheres of the Nigerian society. It will raise 50 change agents to impact 10,000 people or more in governance, business, education, youth and sports, arts and culture and social issues by amplifying its message through its Series, publications and social media channels.

title: Make Oakland a Better Place for Walking & Biking
description: Oaklavia is Oakland's version of Bogota, Colombia's program where streets are temporarily closed to auto traffic and the community is invited to come play in the streets. Since 2010, Oaklavia has successfully encouraged tens of thousands of people to walk and to bike more. Oaklavia is produced by Walk Oakland Bike Oakland (WOBO), a non-profit organization whose mission is to improve neighborhood livability, vitality and sustainability by making walking and biking safe, easy, accessible and fun.

title: Land for Elephant Rescue and Care in India
description: The goal of this project is to buy 10 acres of land to provide a safe place elephants who were once abused or mistreated to call home.

title: Provide Education for Youth Sports Safety
description: This project provides education around recognizing, managing and preventing sports-related injuries to parents, coaches, educators and athletes. It offers educational resources and workshops on: 1) Concussion Prevention and Recognition; 2) Preventing Dehydration and Heat-related Conditions; 3) Nutrition in Sports Management and 4) Recognizing, Preventing and Managing Musculoskeletal Injuries.   Through appropriate education, youth athletes will be better positioned for safety and success.

title: Supporting the Healthcare System in Afghanistan
description: International Medical Corps has provided health services for vulnerable populations in Afghanistan for 30 years. We aim to improve the quality of life and health status of Afghans through integrated interventions and by strengthening the capacity of the public health system through an ongoing commitment to improving local infrastructure. We respond to immediate needs in the face of natural disaster or armed conflict but also focus on preparing local communities to respond to future crises.

title: Indoor Playground Project
description: We would like to, for the first time in our history, build an indoor playground specifically designed for working with young children who have special needs.  This space will be utilized for occupational & physical therapy for group and individual programs, and screening & evaluating children on those skill sets.  We have received a generous $20,000 matching grant from Pacific Life and need your help to raise the remaining $20,000 to get this sensory playground built!

title: Wheels to Africa
description: Wheels to Africa is a youth engagement project that collects bicycles for needy communities in Africa and provides leadership opportunities for American youth.  For the past nine years, teens across the Washington, D.C., area have organized events to collect used bicycles and to raise the money to ship them to Africa. Once in Africa, the bikes are transforming lives: helping college students make their way to classes, aid workers deliver medical supplies and farmers reach markets faster.

title: Help Provide Access to Education for Survivors
description: This project will provide education scholarships for tuition, textbooks, academic materials and vocational training for 4 survivors of sex trafficking.  Sex traffickers prey on at risk and vulnerable girls ages 11-14. They are tortured if they attempt to run away. This atrocious humiliation and degradation of girls demands immediate attention because the more we turn deaf ears and blind eyes the closer to home we may find its victims. Education empowers survivors to become economically viable.

title: Robotics, science, art and technology for girls
description: We have a permanent play centre available for girls and boys who are at risk of social exclusion: principally, children of single parent families, of those who have been victims of gender based violence, and of inmigrants. We do activities adapted to the ages of the children and the families' social and economic situations. We wish now to increase the quality and breadth of this play centre by complementing it with workshops on robotics, science, art and technology.

title: Solar ccokstoves for rural comunities in Peru
description: The project  is to strengthen access to energy for rural communities in Peru by spreading solar cookstoves.The equipement positively impact on various aspects of human development and of preservation of the environment. Smoke emissions caused by the burning of wood for cooking at home pose a  risk to the health of household members. Improving access to sustainable energy supply is an important contribution to development, in terms of poverty reduction, of fighting against deforestation and clima

title: Literacy 30 children with disabilities in Moldova
description: This project shall ensure literacy for 30 children with disabilities that are not transportable from rural areas of the Republic of Moldova (Straseni and Calarasi districts) with age between 6-11 years, who cannot read and write. Children shall be literate at home by teachers during an academic year (35 weeks, 4 hours per week). All these children are coming from poor families, so each child shall receive individual desk, textbooks, educational materials and school supplies.

title: Teach 24 Kyrgyz autistic children learning skills
description: 24 children with autism aged 3 to 8 from low income, single parent families do not have access to any type of rehabilitation. All are non-verbal, have behavioral problems, lack self-helping skills. You can help us train parents on how properly teach their children, have every child tested and given individual educational program, buy necessary set of teaching aids and games. This will give them a chance to attend kinder garden or school and avoid being placed in mental institution in the future.

title: Finding + supporting mentors for pupils in Berlin
description: Children, particularly in difficult life situations, need a constant companion, which they can confide in and who supports them. This is what the project "PaSch" (mentors for pupils) stands up for and professionally organizes the matching of an adult mentor and a child in need as well as supports them during their mentorship. PaSch develops long-lasting friendships over generations and cultures and supports children in their personal devolpement.

title: Safe care and adoption for Indian Babies
description: It is heartbreaking to even contemplate that a newborn baby could be abandoned into life threatening danger by being left by the side of the road or in a garbage bin. Sadly, our team finds these babies all too often, some badly injured, malnourished or suffering with mental and other health issues, including disabilities and HIV/AIDS. Our doors are open to all without discrimination to deliver the highest levels of support and medical care and find loving families for every unwanted child.

title: Organic Seed Bank Establishment in Philippines
description: The primary goal of this project is to develop a local sustainable source of organic seeds for farmers in the Northern Philippines. This will lower costs for farmers having to purchase seeds with each planting. This program will also improve the health of local soil by not having to use chemical fertilizers to grow hybrid and synthetic non-organic seeds. Friends of ENCA Farm will implement this program through comprehensive educational and training opportunities for participants.

title: Employ Two Indigenous Kuna Human Rights Advocates
description: We seek funds for one year of employment for two indigenous Kuna development professionals from rural villages in the rainforests of the Darien Region of Panama as they work to empower surrounding indigenous communities through advocacy and education in basic legal and human/indigenous rights.     Research proves  that greater legal security for indigenous communities leads to economic development for the world's poorest communities while also protecting the world's most bio-diverse regions.

title: Support Higher Education for 3 Teens in Uganda
description: This project will make it possible for Ice, Rebecca, and Joel to finish high school and attend university in Uganda. These determined and capable students are highly recommended because of their proven academic achievement and strong leadership potential. However, without outside help, completing higher education is impossible because of the high cost of tuition.  Investing in the education of these students will transform their lives and benefit the entire community.

title: Buy a Bale... of Hay for the Rescue horses!
description: With total of 44 horses currently in our rescues care, we are desperate to find and purchase hay as it is scarce in our area. The need for Hay and Support is ongoing. The funds we obtain will directly determine our ability to care for and help needing horses in the  upcoming year. With your help, IGP will not only be able to continue helping needing horses but also keep our barn open and available to state and local enforcement agencies take in horses that have been surrendered or seized.

title: Help support the young generations education
description: The Vasco de Quiroga University looks forward to help students by giving them access to a quality education at low cost and helping them reach their education goals.

title: Permanent Campus for Students
description: Palm Institute is growing at a rapid rate. When the new school year begins in September 2017, we anticipate even greater growth. Our short-term goal is to relocate to our permanent campus in the very near future to give our students the most convenient environment for teaching and learning. This would afford us the opportunity to provide quality liberal arts education (a missing ingredient in our higher education systems) to our students.

title: Assist 200 homeless-starved children in Bujumbura
description: Many children in Bujumbura do not have a roof over their heads and starve it because their fathers have abandoned them and their mothers are not able to pay rent and are hunted by the owners.  This project aims to assist 200 children homeless and hungry by empowering their mothers. Indeed, they will be sensitized and trained in the management of an income-generating activity. so they will be supported to initiate a small business that will allow them to provide shelter

title: Help Build a Climate Education Center in Nicaragua
description: The Nicaraguan Center for Forests, Energy & Climate will provide citizens of Central America with the tools and training needed to adapt to a rapidly changing climate. This regional hub for climate change education and natural resource conservation will build on Trees, Water & People's community-based conservation model, which empowers local people to solve social and environmental problems at the grassroots-level. Thanks to generous donors, every donation to this project will be matched!

title: Help Build Sports Academy For Kibera Youths
description: For the last 7 years, we have been developing athletes from the Kibera Slums, in Nairobi. The initial group of children between 8-12 years are now 15-19 years old and most of them are promising athletes. The Rising Stars Academy seeks to protect and equip the successful transition of our young athletes from amateur sportsmen to professionals. But most importantly, the academy is also a place to retain the athletes as they help mentor the younger youths in the program.

title: Catchers in the rye
description: We're Catchers in the Rye - we "catch" children, trying to make sure they have the best opportunities in life. In Russia, schools do not accept children with neurological disorders and other special needs. Our project of inclusive education lets them go to school, which is their basic human right. And including these children in classrooms also enriches the lives of teachers and other students, teaching them tolerance and empathy. Protecting somebody who is weaker than us makes us stronger.

title: Tutoring and Mentoring program
description: This program is for students in Kindergarten through 12th Grade.  We will be helping kids in the Riverview Kansas/South Memphis area.  This program will have a direct impact that will provide a fun and safe place for elementary to high school students before and after school, provide positive interaction with caring, respectable adult role models, encourage and develop life skills,having respect for others, positive social interaction, and engage youth in positive, potential life-long pursuits.

title: The Environmental Crisis on Native American Lands
description: Native American values, treaties, land and water are being threatened by big oil. In the Dakotas  fracking and pipelines have decimated once pristine landscapes, causing toxic damage , destroying ancestral burial grounds and now threatening drinking water. This campaign aims to bring world-wide attention to this environmental and cultural crisis through a feature film: A Different American Dream, a series of videos and a robust engagement campaign focused on supporting local grassroots programs.

title: Safe water for 50 malnourished children in Cusco
description: The Project is dedicated to improve the nutritional status of 50 children under the age of 5 from the peri-urban areas of Cusco by implementing water filters in each home. It will also train mothers to use and correctly maintain the filters while strengthening their skills in the following areas: health, family hygiene and healthy housing.

title: Extreme Sports for Children & Youth in Timor-Leste
description: All children have the right to play; yet opportunities for sports and recreation can be rare for children and youth in post-conflict Timor-Leste. With your support, between 30 and 50 at-risk children and youths can participate in extreme sports workshops, increasing their confidence and resilience while building stronger social relations.

title: Stop mass hunting of wildlife in India
description: Arunachal Pradesh, in north-eastern India is a biodiversity hot spot. Indigenous tribes hunt wildlife for meat, fur, bones, beaks, etc for consumption and traditional attire. Protected species like leopards, black bears and even tigers at times are hunted indiscriminately during mass ritual hunts. The project will work with the community to enforce a ban against hunting and build a community entrepreneurship model for synthetic alternatives to wildlife articles used in traditional tribal attire.

title: Prepare Women Leaders in Financial Management
description: This project will support 30 leaders of Women's Community based organisations from Bhavnagar, Amreli, Dahod & Mahisagar districts to be better prepared in Financial Management skills and accounting systems. This will prepare them to help their 4100 members to join a Gujarat State level Women's Credit Cooperative.  Having experience in micro credit, this linkage will provide them access to larger resource pool to meet their needs for loans for livelihood, sanitation, education and health.

title: Education for Marginalised Children in Lebanon
description: This project will provide education, through regular classes at Insan School, and psychosocial support for children of migrants, refugees and stateless Lebanese children; who are otherwise left without schooling opportunities, due to poverty, discrimination or the lack of appropriate documentation. Insan aims consequently to integrate them into the Lebanese school system, as the first step of integration into the Lebanese society, to give them better future perspectives.

title: After school for 100 children between 4-6 at Siloe
description: The after school program for 100 children at Siloe is an initiative that seeks to contribute to the reduction of social vulnerability and to encourage the proper use of leisure time with recreational and academic activities

title: bananafibre-equipments-children-120-Ugandans
description: This project targets children between 10-18 years,  there's high school dropouts, Child abuse,domestic violence, gender inequalities, communication gaps between children and parents/guardians. This project will help in purchasing banana extraction machines which will help children for alternative Change project to produce good quality and quantity products that can sustain the market demand and supply. This helps children to get money to go back school and mothers also earn from the trainings.

title: Help Recovery 5000 Sick Children in Crete, Greece
description: Crete's major hospital serves thousands of children from all over the island. Some are hospitalised for short periods but many, suffering from chronic illnesses, remain for longer stays, away from their families and friends. We would like to help them by creating better environment and reduce the negative emotional impact which may lead to anxiety, stress and depression. We plan to redecorate the ward, common parts and the rooms, introducing calming decor,donating TV sets and other entertainment

title: PLANT FOR SAFE DRINKING  WATER AND SAVE LIVES
description: Farmer to Farmers project water for life strategy to excavates four ponds for rain water storage and install 3 tube wells increasing the accessibility to safe drinking water to 120 households in the villages of Olaro, Awicere and Opyerodech in Olilim sub County Otuke district. Plant water for food security and Save Lives.

title: Smile a child. Renovate the Clinic in Poland
description: The project is run by the Association for Development of Child Surgery based in Wroclaw, Poland.  The building that currently houses the Children Clinic is in a very bad condition (i.e. the roof is leaking). Moreover the interiors and clinic furniture are in a deplorable state. The clinic is not properly adjusted to host babies. The Association is urgently looking for funds to renovate the building and by doing so, improving the conditions of hospitalized little patients and their guardians.

title: Helping grassroots projects to thrive
description: Talented, passionate GlobalGiving volunteers visit our project partners worldwide each summer. They spend 4-5 days with each project, conducting an in-depth organisational assessment. They also provide digital communications and fundraising support to help our partners grow.  The volunteers help us to fulfil an essential duty - checking how donor money is being spent on the ground; and to fulfil our mission - helping grassroots projects to thrive. They are entirely self funded.

title: Empower 500 young women in Southern Africa by 2017
description: Women make up over half the African population. Yet only 12% of these women have access to education and professional training. As a result, not only are these women deprived of the opportunity to fulfil their potential, their communities miss out too. Because when you teach 1 woman, you reach 100s, our African Women's Leadership Program (AWLEAD) is committed to empowering women aged 18-25 to achieve their professional goals and become the change they want to see in their communities.

title: Rural Area Development Trust - Mentally Challenged
description: The Manjari Day Care Centre was started in the year 2005 at Uthamapalayam,Theni district ,Tamilnadu,India. This centre provides therapeutic support to children who are  mentally challenged. Manjari centre consists of 30 children. Physiotherapy and special education are regularly given to the children. Physiotherapists help children with disabilities to develop or improve their motor skills. Service is in the form of exercise, education, consultation, or the recommendation of adaptive devices.

title: School2Skill Mobile App
description: Mobile Smart Phone Revolution in Africa is drifting students from learning and acquiring problem solving skills to sharing pictures "selfies" in social media. You can provide 1million Nigerian Youths and many more African students by 2017 a mix of knowledge sharing and social experience app thereby helping students to acquire problem solving skills in ICT trainings, leadership development, career guidance among other life skills that are completely absent in the traditional school curriculum.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening in Ethiopia
description: This project will provide free cervical cancer screening in the largest and poorest region of Ethiopia. Cervical cancer is the leading cause of cancer mortality among Ethiopian women over the age of 30. Records show that 7600 Ethiopian women are diagnosed annually with cervical cancer and of these, 6000 die of the disease each year. Cervical cancer screening has been shown as the most effective way to decrease cancer mortality among all women.

title: Better nuitrition for people with special needs.
description: The poultry project will address the rise in disabling conditions by providing quail eggs to supplement diets,  chickens for table birds and by employing some persons living with special needs. It will generate a little income to supplement the low fees charged for therapy sessions permitting maintenance. The lack of insurance schemes places a big burden for the individual who for the most part cannot afford therapy.Good nutrition for the > 2000 we see annually will permit social reinsertion.

title: School Ready Adopt-A-Backpack Program
description: School Ready Adopt-A-Backpack Program is an easy way to have a profound impact on students and their learning experience. Make school a better place for both students and teachers by the simple act of providing school supplies.

title: Provide Healthcare to 6000 K12 Students in Liberia
description: Access to affordable, reliable healthcare in Liberia is limited, resulting in high morbidity, mortality and dropout rates among K12 students. Healthy Nation provides affordable primary healthcare, including monthly screens, health education, and menstrual health and hygiene. Our work allows boys and girls to gain relevant knowledge about communicable diseases like Ebola. We served 2000 students in the 2013/2014 school, and project service to 6000 kids int he 2015 school year.

title: Helping street children to be Street Smart
description: Approximately four new children arrive daily on Kitale streets. Child Rescue Kenya (CRK) operates Street Smart, a street-based programme that supports the children to return home. The earlier children engage with Street Smart, the more likely they are to leave the streets successfully. The social work team identify new arrivals, encourage them to attend the Street Smart drop-in centre and build trusting relationships as the starting point for successful reintegration back home and into school.

title: People and Bees in Ethiopia
description: We are helping some of the poorest families in Ethiopia earn income through beekeeping. This income is essential to keep children in school, well-fed and pays for medicines when needed - and begins to break the cycle of poverty for households in northern Ethiopia. We are not giving equipment - instead we provide training, knowledge and skills so people can keep bees, earn money and not be reliant on outside help. Honey and beeswax can be sold as a reliable source of family income.

title: Teach Art to South African Youth
description: This project will provide help furnish our brand new Art Centre which will offer art classes to over 460 rural children and youth in our After-school Programme.

title: Provide education to 100 wastepicker children
description: The project seeks to enable children living in extremely violence-ridden, poor, and socio-culturally marginalized waste-picking community in India to reach their full potential through access to and retention in formal education. The learning centers work to enable communities to build capacity to educate children. As children enter schools, the biggest challenge is to retain them there, and to ensure they do not slip back into wastepicking. This proposal will target 100 such children.

title: Give Voice to Roma Genocide Survivors in Europe
description: Help Yahad-In Unum give voice to Roma genocide survivors and educate people on this virtually unknown history through our travelling exhibit, "Roma Voices." The exhibit reveals the unexplored history of the Roma genocide through encounters with 8 Roma people. Your donation will enable us to mount this exhibition, bringing this crucial history to a new public in Paris, Brussels, and other European capital cities.

title: Train 5 to 12 year-olds Against Sexual Abuse
description: Equip 1000 middle school Egyptian students & 200 teachers from 16 government schools with the first anti-sexual abuse curriculum. This will help improve the quality of life for Egyptian women & girls through the creation of safe neighborhoods free from violence. In training 200 students, the project will have reached approximately 12% of students, allowing them to act as ambassadors to the other students This gives them the opportunity to become part of a larger solution in their community

title: Eye Screening for Premature Babies
description: Retinopathy of prematurity is a sight threatening condition in premature infants, which has a disease course of 1 to 4 months post birth. It is a treatable condition when detected early. With improvement in survival rates of premature infants, this has become an significant issue. Medical condition of the infant, lack of skilled manpower and uneven spread of facilities are the major barriers to detection and treatment. We use a combination of technology and medical expertise to reach the infant.

title: Sanctuary helps Suriname's sloths back to jungle
description: Green Heritage Fund Suriname (2005) rescues sloths and anteaters from urban areas in Paramaribo, Suriname in tropical South America. Professional care in natural surroundings with quarantine and treatment room will minimize trauma caused by contact with humans, reducing rehabilitation time and thus improving survival chances for the sloths and anteaters. This professional shelter will also serve as an educational center to teach visitors about consequences of habitat loss.

title: Military Spouse Scholarship Program
description: The mission of the Joanne Holbrook Patton Military Spouse Scholarship program is to help prepare military spouses for meaningful employment and to better contribute to their family's financial security.

title: Computer Training Center for 100 Ethiopian Orphans
description: The International Organization for Adolescents (IOFA) is continuing its partnership with AHOPE Ethiopia to create a new computer and vocational training center. The project's goal is to improve access and usage of the internet for 100 HIV-positive orphans and other vulnerable children living in Ethiopia. By creating a computer skills training center, youth will have access to job skills training, English classes, and ICT literacy programs to facilitate their transition to adulthood.

title: Eye surgery for 50 people in southern Bangladesh
description: Friendship works with the most overlooked communities of Bangladesh in order to help maximize their potential. This project works with Southern coastal communities that fall victim to natural disasters frequently and have limited or no access to healthcare. Friendship's Rongdhonu Friendship Hospital works at meeting this need. The overall aim of the particular project is to restore eyesight for 50 individuals living in marginalized communities in disaster-prone areas of southern Bangladesh.

title: Education, Home, & Health for India AIDS Orphans
description: Agape's project will help orphans devastated by AIDS in India from cradle through college.  It will provide formula and diapers for HIV+ babies; home and medical care for 12 HIV+ orphans; educate a class of 22; and put 13 Agape school graduates through college. Together, we can give home, health, and hope through education in English to break the cycle of poverty and sickness these children were born into. Your life-changing investment in Agape's children will generate returns for years to come!

title: Help Ukrainian multi-child needy families
description: We collect money for the basic needs of 9 Ukrainian multi-child poor families with 7 and more kids each family. All raised funds will be spent for purchase of food, cloth, school appliances for children, payments for the kids studying and school coteries. Despite that fact that all the families live in terrible conditions below the living rate, the children are very talented and we want them to have good childhood and their future to be much better.

title: Make birth safer for 700 Ugandan women and babies
description: The Maama Project tackles high maternal and newborn mortality in rural Uganda by supporting pregnant women, mothers and newborns. The project educates and engages the community, distributes clean birth kits and trains community health workers to conduct home visits to pregnant women and mothers. To date, we have made 110 births safer with clean birth kits and doubled antenatal visit attendance. Support us to  provide 700 more women with a cleaner birth and 700 newborns with a safe start in life.

title: Restore Health to a Malnourished Child in Paraguay
description: This project provides a nutritious breakfast and lunch to 100 children in urban slums in Paraguay, enabling their recovery from malnutrition and securing human capital development in Paraguay.

title: Scholarships for Youth in Central Vietnam
description: In an area where nearly 85% of the land is still potentially contaminated with the explosive remnants of a war that ended forty years ago, kids often lack the resources they need to succeed in school. With your help, this project will support youth and young adults whose lives have been impacted by landmines and bombs in Quang Tri Province, Vietnam by investing in their education with scholarships for books, supplies, uniforms and school fees for primary, secondary and post-secondary schooling.

title: Environmental education to argentinean children
description: This project will provide environmental education through didactic workshops to 600 children from 5 to 8 years old in schools in  Argentina. Through these workshops the project will propose several activities in order to bring about such topics as the life cycle of plants and recycling and the relationship between them and the lives of children. The workshops focus its actions in promoting participation of children as agents of change in their homes in creating new habits of sustainability.

title: Save our Elderly & Kids in Crisis Feeding Center
description: We are at risk of losing our San Jorge Elderly & Kids in Critical Need Feeding Center. Nearly 60 elderly and 15 kids without primary caregivers rely on the center for daily nutritious meals in a safe, nurturing environment. Without this center,  these elderly and children will become even more vulnerable to malnutrition and other health dangers. By gaining the building, we can continue our feeding programs and expand to include other educational and community development programs.

title: Supporting five Mexican children with special need
description: We are seeking support for 05 children with special needs for a school year; they are deficient in the emotional, intellectual, language, motor skills, and vision and hearing areas. The children attend special education, Monday through Friday, from 8:00 until 13:00. Your parents and / or guardians are committed to rehabilitation; however, find it difficult to pay tuition due to the extra expenses that generates a sick child.

title: Food Security by Women in Rural Bolivia
description: This project aims to empower women eager to take action towards food security and food sovereignty in communities that are suffering from mineral contamination, climate change, poor crop production and high levels of migration.

title: Alzheimer Mexico - Learn and Act
description: Alzheimer Mexico, I.A.P. is a Mexican non-profit organization that provides comprehensive care to people with Alzheimer's or similar dementia, their caregivers and family members to improve their quality of life. Its care program includes access to comprehensive programs of physical and cognitive stimulation. We work to help people with dementia maintain their skills for longer, as well as to provide guidance and advice on dementia to families living the disease process.

title: Quality Education and health for girls in Uganda
description: This project will increase access, retention and quality education for girls in primary schools in Dokolo district through providing school fees, scholastic materials, provision of sanitary pads, and medical treatment for HIV affected children.

title: Educate 500 slum youth in Argentina
description: Centro Conviven promotes the social, cultural and educational development of at risk children from the slums of Buenos Aires, Argentina. We want to provide a physical and mental safe place to approx 500 youth of this community by providing educational, artistic and extra circular workshops. The educational workshops are developed to strengthen the self-esteem of the children and give them the tools to prosper through art, sports, technology, science & math..cementing & enriching their futures.

title: Healing Japan
description: "Just yesterday, she finally started to talk about that day - after almost 5 years.", our local partner psycho-therapist tells us about one of her numerous clients in Rikuzentakata. While more housings and infrastructure have been restored, the needs for mental health care services and resources in the disaster affected areas continue to grow larger. We support earthquake and tsunami survivors and care providers in their efforts to enhance the psychosocial recovery of the people in Tohoku.

title: Training Teachers in Ethiopia to Save Sight
description: Orbis is dedicated to the treatment and prevention of avoidable blindness. Through supporting this project you will enable teachers to educate children on the importance of eye care. Few people realise that, in Ethiopia, blindness can result from a disease easily transmitted between infected and healthy eyes by flies or infected clothing, and a lack of clean water to wash. Through educating children we can ensure the next generation in Ethiopia grow up without the threat of avoidable blindness.

title: Dreamland -  First Fun Center for sick children
description: All children have a right to play,they learn to live life through Play and it's essential to their all-round emotional and physical well-being especially for children with a disability. However in Ireland there is a total lack of play facilities for disabled children and this is heart-breaking for the disabled child, siblings, parent as having a disabled child is a disabled family.Now Share a Dream are going to build Ireland's first all inclusive Fun Center for special children called Dreamland.

title: 2016 Emerging and Innovative Environmental Leaders
description: ELP's Fellowship Program offers intensive leadership and skill training, regional networking opportunities, and time for personal and professional reflection. Consisting of three retreats and additional optional trainings, our curriculum helps emerging leaders hone their leadership styles, create learning organizations, and strengthen their outreach to diverse constituencies.

title: Help Bring Wildlife Back to Angkor Forest
description: This pioneering project reintroduces Endangered pileated gibbons and other species to Angkor Archeological Park. Angkor's wildlife was decimated by hunting in the 20th century, but its ancient forests are now a well-protected UNESCO World Heritage site. We aim to recreate genetically diverse wildlife populations by releasing a cross-selection of unrelated small carnivores, primates, ungulates, and birds. Released gibbons, muntjac and otters are all raising wild-born offspring in Angkor already!

title: Self-reliance & resilience in slum women's groups
description: Urban Health Resource Centre strengthens communities of 425,000 slum dwellers in Agra & Indore in India to access to maternal/child health services, address proof, education, improved living environment, Govt services. UHRC forms women's groups in slums and provides technical & confidence building training, enabling them to "pull" govt. resources & services from different departments through negotiation skills they learn, thus steadily developing collective self-efficacy & self-reliance.

title: 10 Burn children from Bolivia to Shriner's Hosp.
description: This project is to bring 10 Burn children from Bolivia to the Shriner's Burn Center in Galveston, TX for medical treatment. Your support will enable FANQ to pay for all the logistics, airline tickets, housing and medical expenses while in transit for the child and their guardian.  These children are burn victims due to fire/electricity and are indigent with no means of medical help in Bolivia.

title: Child right training for 60 community leaders.
description: This project will train 60 community leader in the context of child protection and aims educate families to better protect their children, it is surprising to note that despite the existence of protective laws of the child in Haiti, those  are still unknown for majority of the population and can be difficult to implement. therefore, provide training on the Law of the child protection law is a necessity for the community.

title: Safe Pregnancy for 200 Poor Women in India
description: The project will provide much needed healthcare for 200 poor pregnant women in India to enable them to deliver healthy babies under medical supervision. By contributing as little as $10, you can become a part of a poor woman's birth story.

title: Woodstock Community Development Project
description: this project will create space for community conversations and enhance the capacity of community leaders to stimulate stakeholder dialogues to re-imagine a more inclusive regeneration of the Woodstock inner-city area

title: Basketball wheelchairs to 60 disabled persons Bali
description: Yayasan Damai Olahraga Bali introduced Wheelchair Basketball to  Indonesia  .Now looking for more equipment to expand throughout Bali. Bali, and Indonesia as a whole, provides very little, if any, support for people living with disabilities,while Sport in many instances, can provide a disabled person not only with a recreational outlet, but many health benefits, both physical and mental YDOB supports disabled people in their desire to have some form of independence and to live a productive life

title: PROJECT "NO EXCUSES" SCHOLARSHIPS FOR 30 CHILDREN
description: Education is universally acknowledged to have a significant impact on future earnings. A good education is the foundation that a young person needs to be able to overcome societal challenges and become a valuable, income-generating member of the community.This project will keep 30 vulnerable children in school through a holistic scholarship scheme for a minimum of 5 years. It will cover the cost of educational, nutritional, health and social support to children aged 6 to18 years.

title: Equip Mobile Learning Lab for 450 Vietnam orphans
description: This project will equip mobile computer labs that will travel among 10 Vietnamese orphanages each month, providing relevant 21st Century Skill training to 450 orphans. This project represents an expansion of a proven model that has helped more than 1000 Vietnamese orphans over the past 5 years learn the skills they require to be prepared to graduate from the orphanage with valuable computer skills, self-confidence, and collaborative skills that are so important in today's job market.

title: Help UPO Help the DC Homeless
description: We are the eyes and ears of the city. Every day and night, UPO's Shelter Hotline team protects the health of people who live on the streets. We reach out so that people experiencing homelessness get the help they need. Last year, our team:   -  Responded to 92,000+ emergency calls -  Distributed 179,000+ life-sustaining items (i.e. blankets, socks, sleeping bags, long underwear, etc.) -  Gave free transportation to 112,000+ riders -  Distributed 28,000+ meals along with water

title: Transportation for a Rural Orphanage in Costa Rica
description: Children from Hogarcito San Ramon orphanage currently walk 45 minutes each way to/from public school daily, regardless of weather, on a two-lane road without sidewalks.  Children who require medical treatment are transported by taxi to facilities that are often an hour away, and the orphanage relies on donations to cover these transportation costs.The amount of money needed to purchase a vehicle is far beyond their means.

title: Youngsters challenge poverty through skateboarding
description: El Desafio SB is an innovative project that provides underprivileged youngsters with opportunities for education, leadership, and creative thinking that help break the cycles of poverty and exclusion. The safety in their streets is being challenged by drugs related violence. This project builds life skills like confidence, courage, trust and cooperation so they can reclaim their streets - and future - through skateboarding.

title: Send Children To School In Nigeria For A Year
description: This project will send at least 50 vulnerable children to school in Nigeria. These children are being exploited for hard labor in remote communities. And the only way to help them is to enroll them in school, provide school materials for them and empower their families economically.

title: Light up my candle . Girls.  150  girls. Nigeria
description: The insurgency situation in Nigeria has drawn all efforts put in by both Government and international development partners on girls education back.Girls in Northern Nigeria (Central) have lost the zeal to go back to school opting for early marriage as a safety bate.The few who are willing have got no support from home This project seeks to support indigent students affected by boko haram insurgencies  to complete basic education. Encouraging parents and guardians to release their girls to school

title: Breakfast for students at the Kuched Gaam School
description: The 130+ students at the Kuched Gaam government primary school in rural Gujarat, India are all from extremely poor families, many making as little as only $2 dollars a day. Since 2011, we have worked hard to increase regular attendance at the school from around 30% to now being nearly 100%.   Our continued success will allow us to make a meaningful difference in the lives of these children. Providing breakfast for the students has contributed greatly to our success.

title: Happy Chickens for Fiji Food & Climate Emergency!
description: The negative impacts of climate change, have caused a developing food emergency in Fiji.  Rural subsistence farmers have been severely stressed, as increasingly strong cyclones rake across the islands, destroying small farm plots and homes, and damaging coconut and other tree crops.  The coral reefs are also sustaining storm damage, and are being over-fished. We address poverty and hunger by providing islanders with foraging chickens as an alternative income and alternative protein to reef fish.

title: Beauty, Well-being and Dignity with Cancer
description: More and more women face cancer. The treatment is severe. The Mimi Ullens Foundation improve the quality of life of cancer patients during their treatments. By improving the well-being of cancer patients, we substantially improve their chances of recovery. Better within their bodies, they have greater strength to carry on the fight. Our help also makes it possible to combat loneliness and isolation through the warm welcome provided by specifically trained professionals.

title: Empower 100 vulnerable Colombian families
description: Bad family interaction produces abandonment, physical violence, abuse against women and children. In 77% cases of domestic violence in Colombia in 2013, women were the victims. This project will provide trainings to improve family dialogue and facilitate healthier interactions for 100 vulnerable  families in Santa Marta. It will also include training of government officials and local NGOs to help design new policies, which will benefit children and women, and create a Family Club in the region.

title: Response to Tropical Cyclone Pam in Vanuatu
description: Tropical Cyclone Pam made landfall on Vanuatu and the capital island of Efate with a population of 66,000. The capital city of Port Vila suffered a direct hit by the storm, which was the equivalent of a Category 5 hurricane. This is the strongest storm to make landfall since Super Typhoon Haiyan hit the Philippines in 2013, and the humanitarian impact is expected to be high. UNICEF is reporting that the full force of Pam was dramatically worse than had been initially predicted.

title: Vanuatu Communities Support - Cyclone Pam
description: On Friday, March 13 2015, Cyclone Pam seriously affected Vanuatu with especially the central and south parts of the archipelago leaving thousands of people without home and resources.  80% of the rural communities live on the subsistence agriculture and in the coming weeks the situation will become more dramatic with a shortage of food. We need some support to be able to assist the communities surrounding our centre in Port Vila and our members from the islands.

title: Help Students Catch Up After Ebola
description: Ebola isn't over yet. After being closed for 7 months, the MTM Academy finally reopened in March, but students are severely behind. In mid-March, a new case of Ebola was confirmed. We know that ALL of our students are safer somewhere they can be monitored with hand-washing stations and access to medical care and psychosocial support.

title: Improving & Protecting Lives of Syrian Refugees
description: The Women's Refugee Commission (WRC) has been working with Syrian refugees in Jordan, Iraq and Lebanon in multiple capacities to improve their lives and protect their rights. The horrific violence has created a desperate humanitarian situation. In response, the WRC has initiated a series of activities to address some of the gaps and challenges experienced by those women and girls most affected by conflict and displacement.

title: Support 35 students in Grade 2 classroom in India
description: The broad scope of the project is to provide education to the students of the Laxmi Nagar Mumbai Public School in Mumbai, India. The school is being run under the Public Private Partnership Policy as a part of Akanksha's School Project and aims to create a model for high-performing schools that redefines what is possible for children from low-income communities to achieve, and that drives wider systemic reform in the Indian educational system.

title: Emergency Relief for Vanuatu after Cyclone Pam
description: Cyclone Pam has caused widespread devastation to the tiny islands of Vanuatu affecting over 200,000 people. GVI has close ties with Vanuatu and its people, following 7 years of working with local partners in this incredible country. The full extent of the damage is still being assessed and all donations to this fund will be used directly on the ground by the partners of GVI in their emergency support and relief efforts.

title: Safe Childbirth in Rural Tibet 2015
description: Most women in Tibet give birth at home without access to emergency care or materials and training needed to prevent infection and hemorrhage. We have been working for 11 years in Eastern Tibet to provide a clinic, trained doctors and midwives, and community health educators who teach safe home birth messages, give out clean birthing kits and document birth outcomes. We will pay health workers' salaries for 1 year, provide training and supplies to reduce infant mortality & purchase an ambulance.

title: Provide food&care for ALL our animals for 1 year!
description: The mission of DAKTARI is to inspire, develop and educate underprivileged children to care for their environment through an immersive experience at a wildlife orphanage. All the animals at DAKTARI can not be reintroduced into the wild either due to injury or because they are too used to humans and could become a danger to local farms. The maintenance of the animals is crucial not only for their wellbeing but also because of the huge support they provide in teaching children about nature.

title: Looma ~ interactive A/V education for any school
description: VillageTech Solutions is designing and field-testing Looma. A single 85 watt unit will bring the best educational content of the Internet to any classroom, anywhere on Earth. Looma has a bright LED projector, fast computer, good sound system, webcam and microphone to record students or teacher, massive storage, wifi/bluetooth/USB connections. Looma does away with the keyboard or mouse by using an aerial "wand", making it easily controlled by teacher or students in a shared environment.

title: Lekari bez hranic - Medecins Sans Frontieres in Cz
description: Doctors Without Borders/Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) is an international medical humanitarian organization created in France in 1971.  MSF provides independent, impartial assistance in almost  70 countries to people whose survival is threatened by violence, neglect, or catastrophe, primarily due to armed conflict, epidemics, malnutrition, exclusion from health care, or natural disasters.

title: Save Lives with Emergency Care in Uganda
description: Global Emergency Care (GEC) trains healthcare providers in emergency care to save lives and prevent unnecessary deaths in Uganda. Due to a healthcare worker shortage in Uganda, many patients die from treatable diseases and injuries such as pneumonia, diarrhea, and trauma. GEC developed a sustainable, train-the trainer model that educates Emergency Care Practitioners (ECPs) to provide quality acute care in order to save lives.

title: Purchase Motorbikes to Reach Remote Villages
description: One of the key areas overlooked in the Ebola eradication process has been the difficulty of accessing remote towns and villages along Liberia's vulnerable borders. Most groups cover only those areas accessible by car, neglecting key communities requiring arduous travel by foot or motorbike. We need two motorbikes so that our Mobile Peace Teams can reach remote villages to work with elders, ex-combatants, and women working to build stability and resilience in these strategic, underserved areas.

title: Bring Clean Water to 40 Families in Nicaragua
description: This project will provide a year-round supply of clean and safe drinking water to our local community of El Manzano Uno in rural Nicaragua.Currently, there is a lack of access to sufficient water and the groundwater is contaminated by human and animal waste, plus excessive pesticide usage.  The project entails drilling a Deep Water Community Well, installing a Community Water Tower and putting in the Pump and Filter.Water lines will then be established throughout the community for all to use.

title: Enable Sharon Go To College and Mentor Other Girls
description: Sharon is a young girl, born and brought up in the slums of Kibera. Her father died while she 11 and she quickly took up the role of a mother for her 6 younger siblings as her mother fended for the family. She was awarded a high-school scholarship, and she is to join College in May 2015 to pursue a degree of her choice. This page seeks to raise funds to enable Sharon complete 4 years of college education and continue to mentor and reach out to other young girls through our Rising Stars Project

title: Help For Amos -Veterinary Hospital Costs
description: On March 20th Amos one of our Sanctuary Horses here at IGP had been admitted to the University of Georgia Large Animal Teaching Hospital for Chronic Pneumonia.  Without extensive professional treatment Amos will not survive.

title: Training the Church to respond to domesticviolence
description: Restored is developing in partnership with Paz y Esperanza Int. an On-line course for pastors and church leaders to address domestic violence and support victims & survivors. This is an exciting opportunity to challenge and bring positive change to a culture that allows domestic abuse across Latin America.It has been internationally recognized that faith organization have a key role to play not only attending survivors; but also influencing the local communities where no other actor has access.

title: Cancer in Kenya: Giving a real chance of recovery
description: Faraja staff have a vision.  For all adults and children, diagnosed with cancer in Kenya, to be able to access the right medical treatment at the right time. A big problem needs a big solution. The goal is to raise at least 100 million Kenyan Shillings within 2 years. A powerful pool of funds, called the Faraja Cancer Support Fund, invested to generate life-saving medical grants for generations to come. Giving hope and a real chance of recovery to thousands. Forever

title: Find Solutions to Extreme Poverty in India
description: Fundacion Vicente Ferrer is a NGO which helps to find solutions to eradicate extreme poverty in rural areas of southern India, at states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Thanks to over 40 years of tireless and constant efforts, the organization has become a deep-rooted part of society, respecting the environment and local culture, contributing to the process of social transformation. Our goal is to ensure sustainable development with the active involvement and leadership of the communities.

title: Support  Rural Schools in India
description: This project will bring back smile on the faces of children living in most inaccessible areas of Karnataka, India. Through this project we aim to provide basic needs of school going children. They include Uniform , Rain Coat, Pair of Shoe, Note Books, School Bag, Nutritional Supplements, Field trip once a year and last but not least  provide school  'TEACHER'. The uniqueness of this program is that the leads of this project have studied in these schools and faced very same challenge

title: Disadvantaged youth supports street children!
description: This unique project is building the first professional cultural studio in the world. With a unique methodology many disadvantaged youth from 8-27years are trained to be a helping artist for streetchilderen in Indonesia. Our students receive music education in singing, guitar, piano, producing, drums, theater, rap or songwriting. They learn how to make their own songs and with those songs, we create wonderfull music albums. The proceeds go to the street children. Two charities in one!

title: Saving Lives - Improving Health in Rural Guatemala
description: The 100,000 people living in rural villages in San Martin, Jilotepeque lack even the most basic health care.  Most have no access to treatment or medicine. Our health team is sensitive to the indigenous culture.  We focus on educating patients about nutrition, hygiene, how to manage chronic and acute diseases, prenatal care and child development. Without our care men, women, and especially children will go untreated because families lack resources to see doctor

title: Haverim: Distributing free medication in Israel
description: Our 'Free Medicine' Project supplies over 7,000 people with free medication every month. People that without our help are forced to choose between food - and medication. For them, this life-saving medication is sometimes the difference between life and death.

title: Inspire a love of reading for 700 kids in Turkey
description: This project will fund the creation of a library space for children in one of Turkey's most disadvantaged regions, Siirt, Kurtalan. In Siirt, no other comparable spaces exist.  This project aims to create a space that will be a central resource for kids in the community, inspiring passion for and interest in reading.

title: Empower Women to Feed their Families
description: Oxlajuj E is a women's organic amaranth cooperative of 110 members who grow, cook and sell amaranth, a high-protein traditional Mayan grain, to feed their families. They support their families' from selling their grains through the cooperative bakery and export to the city. However, they must harvest the grains by hand, a tedious task that takes women and children 3 days to clean chaff from grain, in what would take 3 hours with our new mechanical winnower.

title: Make Motherhood Safe in Ebola-affected Countries
description: With health systems in parts of West Africa devastated by the Ebola outbreak, 1.1 million pregnant women in the region may have nowhere to turn. Without proper access to prenatal care, emergency obstetric services, and trained healthcare professionals, maternal deaths will rise dramatically. UNFPA, the United Nations Population Fund, is helping by training and deploying midwives, distributing emergency birth kits, and increasing access to family planning.

title: Educate Bolivian Mothers to be Dental Hygienists
description: The Smiles Forever Dental Hygiene School in Cochabamba, Bolivia provides vocational training for  indigenous mothers.  We afford them a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to change their lives and the future for their children.  These women are enrolled in a fully accredited 2-year program, requiring a huge commitment. The challenges and rewards are great for these mothers.  They love giving back to their community at free clinics. While they accrue internship hours they assist dental professionals.

title: Sustainable Nutrition for 823+ Families in Peru
description: Through participation in a sustainable farming program, 823+ rural farm families in the Piura region of Peru will develop a buffer between themselves and starvation. Participants learn to provide their families with complete nutrition by planting sequential gardens, raising small livestock, growing field crops, learning proper hygiene practices and money management. Families participate together and are encouraged to pay it forward, creating a lasting impact on their community for generations.

title: Emergency Aid for Vanuatu After Cyclone Pam
description: This project will enable IsraAID to continue to distribute basic food and supplies to remote islands in Vanuatu, essentially saving the lives of thousands who have no access to food or clean water. The project will also include Psycho-Social Services (PSS) and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) programming to help populations cope, as well as potentially Medical Teams to mitigate health concerns resulting from the disaster

title: Rural Assistance Program Prey Veng (RAP), Cambodia
description: Small farmers dependent upon a single annual rice crop live a subsistence life and  face financial disaster and forced  economic  migration  when  the rains and rice crop fail. Since 2000, to combat this, RAP has educated farmers in the benefits of diversification for income stability,chemical free farming techiniques to increase yield  and reforestation. RAP has also drilled nearly 500 water wells to provide reliable access to drinking water for farming families in the months long dry season.

title: Provide healthcare and medicines in Oyo, Nigeria
description: The Access to Basic medical care Foundation was created in recognition of the challenges faced by the masses in accessing affordable and quality healthcare. The foundation provides free healthcare and medicines to residents of Oyo State in Nigeria through primary healthcare clinics in different areas of the State. There are 13 clinics and we have provided care to over 250,000 individuals since establishment in 2011.

title: Blind Sports Equipment for 30 Blind children
description: Yayasan Damai Olahraga Bali introduced Blind Judo  to  Indonesia. We are now looking for support for equipment to grow our Blind Sports Program with Goalball and Blind soccer. Bali, and Indonesia as a whole, provides very little, if any, support for people living with disabilities. Sport in many instances can provide a disabled person not only with a recreational outlet but also many crucial health benefits, both physical and mental. Please help us reach more people people.

title: Create Dignified Service Space for 5000 Immigrants
description: Nationalities Service Center (NSC) prepares and empowers immigrants and refugees in the Philadelphia region to transcend challenging circumstances by providing comprehensive client-centered services to build a solid foundation for a self-sustaining and dignified future. We are currently seeking funds to create a dignified service environment that protects the safety and health of our clients.

title: Introduce 30 Blind Youth to European Values
description: This project will empower visually impaired youth leaders aged 14-24 to fight for their rights and European values through bringing 30 youth leaders to Bulgaria to get acquainted with European social policy and living standards for people with disabilities.

title: Support Training for South Sudanese Social Workers
description: This project will allow two of the first social workers in South Sudan to attend a 3-week training on women empowerment and economic development in Israel. The training is fully funded, but they need to purchase their own flight tickets. Through this training, Lily and Judith will be able to bring new skills and knowledge back to South Sudan and integrate it into their existing projects and work in general, reaching over 200 households every week.

title: Nutrition & Fitness for Immigrant Community
description: Fitness and nutrition is very important for all ages in African immigrant communities; particularly for women and girls. However, lack of education regarding nutrition and healthy cooking, better eating habits and a more active lifestyle leads to unhealthy lifestyles in immigrants. Fitness has not been traditionally recognized as it has not been a part of their regular routine, education or background in Africa.

title: Native American Academic Summer Program
description: The goal of our summer enrichment program is to promote education, build our youths' self-esteem, spark curiosity, and shape strong, healthy, contributing members of society. The program focuses on teaching reading, math, technology, and health education. Also incorporated are the teaching and development of traditional Tohono O'odham art, handcrafts, language, gardening, and cultural history.

title: Bella's Memorial fund
description: 2015 we were notified of Bella, an owner surrender to be euthanized due to an an ACL tear.  We rescued her and during her ACL surgery cancer was found.  During a following procedure Bella lost her battle.  There was something about her way, her sweet face. How her foster sib would lay diligently beside her. The amazing care her foster Father gave her. So moving. We see many Boxers come in with cancer. Quick treatment allows them to live out a happy life in a forever home.

title: Making profitable the boat of Glenn Paige School
description: The project will provide the boat with an appropriate engine of 75 horse-power, petrol reserve and life vest.

title: Unite Inter-Faith Children via Education and Water
description: In the Philippines, religious conflict and natural disasters have caused suffering for millions of Filipino children. This program empowers elementary school children who are the victims. Interfaith education teaches students the value of cooperation and diversity. We provide books, school supplies, clean water, and hygiene supplies for 20,000 children. We also provide hand-washing supplies and nutrition programs for more than 3,000 children.

title: Help Blacky Walk Again!
description: Blacky was rescued with a broken hind leg and other fractures. He was found lying by the side of road, weak and unable to move. He needs surgery to make him walk again.

title: Retain Orphan Girl Children in Schools in Uganda
description: Girl Children of 12 - 24 years in Uganda dropout of school due to failure to manage menstrual health hygiene and lack of support like adequate food and school items. As such engage in child marriage, prostitution and are exposed to HIV/AIDS. The project will enhance retention of 1200 orphan girl child in school by empowering them with knowledge and skills in menstrual health hygiene practices and strengthening the economic power of caregivers through provision of improved agricultural inputs.

title: Help Build a Home for a Lakota Family
description: Trees, Water & People (TWP) will help build an earth-friendly home using compressed earth blocks for Paul Shields, his wife and three children. Paul is the son of Oglala Lakota political prisoner, Leonard Peltier, and is carrying forward dreams of a better future. "My dad will be happy I finally have my own home and can pass it on to his grandkids after I'm gone."  With your help, we will work with builders, volunteers, and Lakota Solar Enterprises to construct Paul's new home this summer.

title: Connecting Kenyan Schools to the World
description: Technology serves its greatest purpose when it connects people to each other. When we work with schools in Kenya to build computer labs and provide internet access, human connections, ideas and collaborations happen. Work with us to connect Kenyan students to their peers in Colorado and watch as they build the future!

title: Help 3 Unemployed Women to Train for a New Job
description: We want to fund the scholarship of 3 unemployed hairdressers to offer them a training to become a social hairdresser and be able to work in hospitals or retirement homes where a lot of help is needed. This way we're in fact helping more people in addition to these 3 women who will find a job and be useful to the community. These women can also be youth people too who just have finished their training as hairdresser and do not find a job and would like to become social hairdressers to find a job

title: Help renovate the school for 500 students in Kalo
description: Project involves renovation of this school made with wood, stubble covered. It will allow 500 students to learn and grow in the best conditions. Building is in deplorable sanitary conditions, many openings in the walls; alarming safety conditions, no toilet facilities. Constant risk of collapse for cracked walls. Heavy rains often outweigh the roof.  Children pass the week in this unsafe building. The funds will help to buy materials construction and for labor (budget attached)

title: Expanding: Child Trafficking Prevention Program
description: SOLD has identified key factors that place a child at risk of exploitation - like poverty, lack of education, and the absence of positive role models - and has developed a holistic model to address those risk factors. We are now launching our second location to provide these programs to our High School and University students in Chiang Rai, a trafficking hub in Northern Thailand.

title: $10 to keep a kid warm for one year
description: To order two sets of school uniforms for a kid from factory (one for summer and one for fall), it takes only 65 RMB / 10 USD. After delivering school uniforms to close to 4000 poor students in Guizhou province in 2014 and we will increase the number to 4700 in 2015. CTEF needs 47,000 USD to complete the project in 2015. We can allocate 23,000 from the fund we have but we still need 24,000 for the project. Please save a lunch to keep a kid warm for one year! Thank you for your support!

title: Early Childhood Development in South Africa
description: Thanda's After-school project starts with five-year-old's, but by this point 90% of brain development has already taken place. In order to support their development from an earlier age, we started an Early Childhood Development (ECD) program in 2016 with 20 children.  In 2017 we are expanding our ECD program to 60 children and need additional equipment and support. Your donations will enable us to extend our services to these youngest members in our community and make a lasting impact.

title: Girl Power Project - GPP
description: Give power to rural poorest girls to help girls, break the cycle of poverty by accessing education, skills and child protection services. Your end of year donations, will help our girls left behind and trapped in marriages, provided with free tuition, mentoring, healthy meals, clothes, school supplies, healthcare and family support services. Your donation will address both the drivers and consequences of girl-child poverty and those left behind. Join us to send more Girls to schools.

title: Fund clown performance in children hospital rooms
