description: Eight young people with financial need and a deep desire to continue and complete their education, in spite of overwhelming personal and social hardships will obtain a scholarship, individual support and mentoring, and enrichment activities. This will enable them to achieve a well-rounded education that otherwise may be unreachable.

title: Help feed hungry kids in Denver, Colorado
description: This project will provide "PowerSacks" of food to 1250 low-income Denver, Colorado elementary students at 8 schools to help bridge the hunger gap these kids experience over the weekends.  Each PowerSack a student takes home on Friday is designed to serve two meals to a family of four.

title: Give Colombia street children a life worth living
description: The project will provide much needed housing, healthcare, nutrition, education, spiritual/human formation, for 50 (150 every year) street kids in Barranquilla, Colombia, to enable them to live a life worth living and to become change agents in our world. By contributing as little as $10, you can become a part of an amazing life story.

title: Free Accommodation for Kids with Cancer in Ukraine
description: This project guarantees free accommodation for families with children affected by cancer and other severe diagnoses during times of war. The construction of the New Dacha Center will provide 15 families with free accommodation for extended treatment periods. Currently, there are no similar centers in Ukraine. Cancer therapy can take several months, and families with ill children require a secure place to live during this period to properly care for and support their children.

title: Provide Education for Refugee Children in Lebanon
description: Insan Association will provide Access to Education at Insan School, as well as Psycho-Social support for the most marginalized children in Lebanon. Children of refugees from Iraq and Syria, children of migrants, as well as vulnerable Lebanese children, have no access to schooling due to poverty and discrimination. Accordingly, Insan aims to help these children to fully live out their childhoods, and continue to play, learn, discover, and laugh, despite the hardships they face

title: Palliative Care in Hyderabad
description: Palliative Care seeks to improve the quality of life of people with advanced life threatening illness. It involves physical, psychosocial support to the patient and the family to cope with illness and bereavement.    Every year: - ~200,000 people in Telangana & Andhra Pradesh are diagnosed with cancer -70% are diagnosed with advanced cancer and need pain relief and palliative care -Less than 1% has access to any palliative care or a pain relief program  We are here to make a difference.

title: 21 Child Soldiers Need Vital Help
description: Rescuing child soldiers, returning them back to their families so they can have safe, happy childhoods.  Giving them an education and a future free from violence and poverty like every child deserves.

title: Help Educate 500 Deafblind Children in India
description: Deafblind children have limited access to basic services like education, health and training in India. Sense India is the first national NGO working exclusively for deafblind children in India. Through this project, 250 deafblind children will be provided with education and assistive devices to help them to be independent.  Apart from deafblind children, their families will benefit through training and counselling about this rare disability and helping them collectively live a fulfilling life.

title: Help 500 Rape Survivors Get Psychosocial Services
description: Rape in Nigeria is endemic. People who offer psychosocial services to survivors do it at a cost. We aim to leverage on technology to build a mobile application where cases of rape can be reported; survivors can connect with (trained) law enforcement agents and caregivers for social reintegration at NO COST. The project will also help reintegrate survivors who drop out of school due to teenage pregnancy or unmasking of their rapist that could possibly be a relative, guardian or financial sponsor.

title: Building a college for natural medicine in Zambia
description: Since 2007 ZINARE has established a naturopathic medical course with the support from the World Health Organisation (WHO), which provided a grant to establish a curriculum in naturopathic medical education in Africa, and to develop training to help bridge traditional and conventional medicine. ZINARE has also conducted research in traditional medicines, as well as training in biodiversity in health. However, reduction in government funding has led to challenges in continuing ZINARE's work.

title: Safe and Clean Water for Mafwasa Community
description: This project will sink 3 boreholes for 325 households who draw water from unprotected shallow wells, rivers and streams. It will result in reduced incidences of waterborne related diseases, and will further reduce time and energy expended - especially by women and girls who are traditionally responsible for fetching water. The project will therefore contribute to the wellbeing of children and their families.

title: Suppport children with tuberculosis from Ilisua
description: Children with tuberculosis in Ilisua are coming from poor families and have the basic needs not fulfilled. Most of the children are at high risk to get sicker and die. Families cannot provide food, sanitation, proper shelter. For this reason children live in the hospital , from there they get to school. Unfortunately , the state itself provide not too much for the children. They have 2 dollars per day for food, sanitation , educational materials. Ecce Homo come in support of basic needs.

title: Engage 100 Out-of-School Nigerian Youth in farming
description: Antof Rural Resource Development Centre plans to establish piggery, goat farming, poultry and farm-produce processing for 100 Out-of-School youths in Akwa Ibom State in 12 months. Targeted youths are between 18-35 years of age who did not complete their high school and have not acquired livelihood skills, and therefore, are not gainfully employed. The project will support 60 females and 40 males to generate income for themselves, take them out of the street and contribute to food security.

title: Restore Mental Health of 1500 persons-Rural India
description: This project mobilizes the community to provide mental health via development, empowerment [where the persons with mental health problems are not objects of charity but subjects with rights], building the client's capabilities, awareness creation in society, providing treatment and access to livelihood options plus advocacy to 1500 people with mental health problems and epilepsy in rural Karnataka. GASS equips them  to recover and lead quality lives with respect and dignity in their communities.

title: Restore livelihood in 10 villages in Liberia
description: AIFO will support the Self Help Groups of 10 villages in Liberia to restore livelihood after the Ebola virus disease emergency, boosting their income generating activities

title: Robotmania at the Pico Rivera Libraries
description: The Pico Rivera Library has about 160,000 visitors/ year and 226 program participants a month. Children and adults will learn how to program and design functioning Mindstorm robots using instructions and incorporating their creativity. Teams use the robotics system to design a robot that can solve challenges and complete missions on a LEGO-based playing field.They will discover the fun in science and technology in addition to building self-confidence, knowledge, and valuable life skills.

title: Expand health access in 13 rural villages in Peru
description: In the rural areas surrounding Cusco, 54% of children under 5 suffer from anemia. This project trains Community Health Workers to address the underlying issues that cause anemia and other health conditions in 13 often-neglected villages near the tourist hotspots of the Peruvian Andes. Our goal is to expand access to care and provide culturally appropriate education to improve poor health outcomes.

title: Solar Electrify 750 Villages Across The Globe!
description: The Barefoot Solar Initiative trains illiterate and semi-literate women to become Barefoot Solar Engineers, enabling them to solar electrify their communities. This demystification of technology skills is coupled with a strong focus on enterprise development, financial inclusion skills, and women's empowerment.  This financial support helps to train more engineers, ship more solar equipment, and found six regional training centres in Africa.

title: Peace through Arts for 1000 Pakistani Children
description: For nearly a decade and half now, people of Pakistan have been enduring the contingency of a bloody conflict as a result of war waged against terrorism. The state of violence has badly affected the lives of children at all levels including physical, psychological and social. We want to engage children in the narrative of peace using visual arts & photography for creative self-exploration and critical thinking using the arts, especially less-privileged studying in public and charity schools.

title: Breast Ironing and the rights of the girl child
description: Breast ironing in girls is highly prevalent in many different regions of Cameroon, yet there may not be specific laws to address them or if there are laws, they may not be implemented properly. In order to fill this gap, Health Services Partners Global Inc can make an intervention here to effectively reduce this type of violence against women and girls. The objective of the project is to reduce cases of violence against women and girls caused by breast ironing.

title: Help Villagers in Benin Access Safe, Clean Water
description: Villagers in northern Benin are in dire need of clean, safe drinking water. Families rely on water from streams and open wells that are easily contaminated, leading to the spread of water-borne disease which accounts for 19 percent of deaths annually.  Children are especially susceptible. SELF is installing a new solar-powered water pump in Kalale and needs your help.

title: Slavery in Brazil - The voice of those excluded
description: Over the past 20 years, almost 50,000 people were freed from slave labor on farms and coal plants across Brazil. Reporter Brasil is recognized as the most important source of information on slave labor in Brazil, both within and outside the country. Its reports, research and educational methodology are used by government, businesses and civil society as instruments of daily work. With this project, we want to produce 100 reports and analysis on cases and complaints of slavery in 2015.

title: Jaguar Rescue Center: helping injured wild animals
description: We are a busy rescue center located in the South Caribbean side of Costa Rica. For more than 10 years our main goal has been the rehabilitation and release of all kind of orphans, sick or injured wildlife. We attend to more than 500 patients every year, including monkeys, wildcats, sloths and all kind of small mammals, birds and reptiles. Without government funding, this project will fund essential supplies, new equipment for the facility and care for our wild guests.

title: Hope for Darfur Education for Genocide Prevention
description: Darfur Women Action Group deeply appreciate the opportunity to participate in this global giving's challenge.  Our project is intended to provide education for 500 elementary students among  the internally displaced children in the camps  in Darfur who have been systematically victimized and deprived from having access to education.

title: Empower Healthy Communities in 3 Countries
description: Health education and professional training are the backbones of healthy communities. NWB's unique expertise on plants as medicine, nutrition, exercise, acupuncture and stress relief are vital but need boots on the ground among our communities in Haiti, Mexico and Arizona via Community Health Workers and training professionals in advanced techniques. We have the knowledge and the model, but now we need to hire 3 CHWs and train 12 more doctors, nurses, midwives and physical therapists!

title: Obesity Prevention-1600 Washington DC residents
description: The CDC reported that in 2012, 1.7 million US individuals 20 years or older were diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes and 5,000 youth were found to have Type 2 Diabetes in both 2008 and 2009.  Without treatment, complications to Eye, Kidney, Nerve Disease, Heart, Brain, and Blood Vessels may occur.  Healthy eating is the solution!  Our TV Style Cooking Show impacts over 5000+ individuals.  The show educates and demonstrates how to prepare healthy quick and easy but nutritional and affordable meals.

title: Peace Day Austin
description: Peace Day Austin is a collaborative grass roots initiative to promote meaningful city-wide participation in the UN's International Day of Peace, 21 September.  We're using the platform of Peace Day as a global time of local opportunity to come together in spirit and action for greater peace in ourselves, our communities, our world.  Community, faith, educational, tech and arts groups -all ages and races - will engage in peace-related activities every day from 9/11 to 9/21 (Peace Day.)

title: Be the lifeline of a 1000 children in India
description: This project will ensure nutritious food, quality education and desired health to 1000 children, through our 7 Children's Homes for the orphan, neglected & abandoned children in the streets, 3 Day Care shelters & 4 community centers in the poorest sections of the society for the children of the slum dwellers to have a fair chance in life to grow out of the crude hands of exploitation.

title: Vegetable farming for poor women of 10 rural areas
description: Through this project we want to initiate a business model for poor rural women of 10 areas based on organic and commercial kitchen gardening to transform the low income women lives from poverty to prosperity.  Women Vegetable Clubs (WVC) is an idea to club rural women for collective entrepreneurship through organic commercial kitchen gardening. As the project is highly sustainable therefore it will be initiated from from 1 rural area and will move towards the next 9 areas after the completion.

title: Help families end Domestic Violence in India
description: My Choices is funding 15 PeaceMakers (fieldworkers) for 1 year to provide free Counseling, Rights Education and Legal Aid to victims of domestic violence and work with students and families to bring about holistic change.   Between 40-80% of married Indian women face domestic violence. In India, it is seen as a sign of masculinity for men and a right of passage for women. We work to provide victims of violence choices that include working with their families to the break the cycle of abuse

title: Brixton People's Kitchen
description: Brixton People's Kitchen is your local community food project that aims to tackle food poverty throughout Lambeth and beyond.   In an often intense battle against food waste and nutritional inequality, we pride ourselves on knowing the needs and wants of our community. Our community shop goes hand in hand with our community cafe. Meaning everyone has a safe space in which they can come together, eat, and do their weekly shop for just 5- as well as going away with many goodies for free.

title: Young teachers for the kids in North East Bulgaria
description: The project aims at fighting the illiteracy and the vast school drop-out rate in Razgrad region. We will achieve that by providing young and dedicated teachers in 3 schools in the region. Teach For Bulgaria teachers will work with students, help them overcome academic deficiencies and motivate them for better results. The funds will cover teachers' recruitment, training, development and support. Every dollar raised will be matched with an international grant.

title: !Ya Basta! Healing Wounds of History in Colombia
description: Over 12 months, ICRD will mobilize and train 100 female religious & community leaders to conduct local reconciliation (and prepare them to train 400 more) in support of the Colombian Government's (GOC) reintegration of former fighters into conflict-affected communities. Designed in collaboration with the GOC, victims groups, ex-combatants, and others, the project integrates local skills to build on the unique strengths of women and faith actors to break a 100-year cycle of violence and revenge.

title: Job Training for poor mother- sick children Brazil
description: Help poor mothers with sick children currently undergoing hospitalization or treatment far from home. Help the mothers  to be near the children, generate income and to find jobs.

title: Flood Relief for Affected Families in Texas
description: This project aims to support the communities affected by flooding in Texas through debris removal, focusing on those unable to complete the job themselves.

title: White Canes For 100 Blind Children In Ukraine
description: Our mission is to improve lifves of 1000 Ukrainian children which struggle with impaired vision. We want to supply over 100 youth with white canes - essential for their orientation and mobility.

title: EMPOWER: 500 Masaiti District orphans with solar
description: We aim to provide 500 solar lamps to orphans in Zambia who do not have electricity at home, because without these solar lamps, children will not be able to complete their school homework during the evenings. This is a follow-up to the donation of solar lamps we gave out in Zimbabwe last year. Fortunately, this year, we have been working with a Design Student of Northumbria University (UK) and we have designed a cheaper and effective solar lamp which will be affordable to most families in Zambia.

title: Give wings to our dreams
description: The inclusive theater "WE ARE" unites more than 40 children, both with and without special needs. Over the past 11 years, the children staged five plays, and gave numerous performances in Yerevan and the regions.The inclusive theater is a powerful tool that gives children with special needs a sense of belonging, helps build their confidence, gives them new skills. But the theater has no special funding and solely relies on the generosity of sponsors to continue its operations. Donate now.!!!

title: Life-Giving Nutrition for Vanya
description: Vanya Balabonin, 10, a radiant and charming boy, has a rare disease that has no name yet. He can't digest normal food, and eats once a night, through intravenous infusion. A daily package of parenteral food costs about $28, monthly - $840.  He needs that food to grow, gain some weight, play and just be - just like other kids. He is a very curious guy, eager to learn and discover the world. We make sure he gets this nutrition mix on time and on regular basis.

title: Improving Adolescent Girls Access to SRHR
description: GPI's weekly safe space lessons provide an opportunity for hundreds of 10-18 year old Nigerian girls to become empowered with factual information on gender, life management skills, adolescent sexuality, and sexual and reproductive health and rights.  Girls graduating from the three year program use the information gained to carry out social work interventions in rural communities on issues of early marriage, teenage pregnancies and FGM which have led to a reduction in these practices.

title: Clean drinking water and prevent CKD in Sri Lanka
description: North central region of Sri Lanka is ravaged by Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD). Over 100,000 people are currently affected (up to 10 to 15% of people in certain villages) with approximately 5% deaths among the affected population per year. The cause of the disease is polluted drinking water. This project aims to prevent the disease by providing easy access to safe and clean drinking water to the school children.

title: Educate 155 homeless Maasai girls in Kenya
description: This project keep in school girls who are victims of retrogressive cultural practices like early marriages, Female Genital Mutilation (FGM), stigmatization due to teenage pregnancies and HIV and AIDS, sexual molestation by close family and relatives or dropping out of school due to financial difficulties in their respective families. We provide our girls with a place they can call home whenever they are out of school, pay their school fees and stationery, food, clothing and sanitary pads.

title: Climate Change Adaptation
description: The vulnerability of people and economic sectors to climate variability and subsequently climate change varies across the society as a result of differing capacities to cope, recover, and to take adaptive measures. In Bihar, two of the major barriers to implementing climate change adaptation are: (i) prevailing weak socio -economic conditions and (ii) cross cutting issues such as the availability of capacity (resources - human, financial, and technical) and the practice of good governance .

title: Playground for Disabled Children in Kyrgyzstan
description: This project will install a playground designed for disabled kids in Osh City's Children's Rehabilitation Center which is visited by over 3,000 children every year. Such infrastructure is especially important in Kyrgyzstan where even parents marginalize their disabled children in society. As people see disabled children playing and gaining the same social skills as normal children, this project will help prove to the Kyrgyz people that disabled citizens can become effective members of society.

title: Save the Negev Desert Tortoise!
description: Testudo werneri is one of the smallest tortoise species in the Mediterranean region, with a historical distribution in northeastern Egypt, Sinai, and parts of the Negev desert in Israel. Populations in Egypt are already practically extinct due to factors affecting their habitat and collection for the pet trade. Currently, T. werneri has a national Israel Red List status of Endangered and in 2003 it qualified globally for listing as Critically Endangered under current IUCN Red List Criteria.

title: Temporary Housing for Homeless Youth
description: A pioneering project that secures Temporary Housing on a weekly basis for the homeless youth in the streets of Athens. Our Street Work teams daily roam the streets and neighborhoods of the greek capital and provide support through intensive counseling, social and employment advisory for the youth that lives or spends most of their lives on the streets (rough sleepers). Providing Temporary Housing is the foundation of the long journey towards rebuilding their lives, offering them a 2nd chance.

title: Overcoming poverty through community development
description: In Techo we believe in people, we work hand to hand developing projects from the voice of the habitants of the slums in latin america.    We make projects for education, productive development, health, microcredits and work focusing in women and children.

title: Let's Plant Trees in Haiti, Together!
description: Almost completely deforested, Haiti is vulnerable to landslides, erosion, and climate change. Let's Plant Trees in Haiti, Together! will partner with grassroots partners in rural Haiti to plant trees and stopping soil erosion while producing food.

title: Give 60 kids in Angola the chance to go to school
description: Every child should have the chance to go to school, to learn to read and write. 4 million children in Angola do not have access to primary education. RISE builds primary schools in rural Angola to educate children, empower communities and contribute to the rebuilding of the country. Through GlobalGiving, we met our original goal to give 50 kids a chance to go to school, so we've increased the goal to give another 10 kids in Angola the opportunity for education!

title: Reaching the lost & lonely in Belfast #SOSBuyaBus
description: SOS Bus support people in their time of crisis on the streets of Belfast in the early hours each weekend. Minibus teams provide caring services reaching out into the dark streets. When vulnerable people need to be taken to hospital our Response Team minibuses can be tied up for up to 40 minutes. Often we miss a call from someone in desperate need as vehicles are in use leaving the caller on the streets vulnerable and exposed. We need a third minibus to fill the gaps and help more people in need.

title: Urgent call to action Indonesian children need you
description: Thousands of underprivileged children will be back in school if you help, please do not sit idly  by! join with us by donating to our cause, a future generation needs your help NOW.  To bring to the wider public's notice one man is riding a rickshaw 2600km from the tsunami museum in Banda Aceh to Jakarta Indonesia. Support his efforts to do good in the world by donating, don't let him do it alone.

title: Feed and educate 45 street children in Narok Kenya
description: This project will help support street children in Narok Kenya to have access to food, education and shelter. Children from poor families will be supported to join school through funds donated by organizations, individuals and religious organizations

title: Save Child Marriage Victim Girls in Pakistan
description: This project will create momentum for preventing child marriages in Sindh province of Pakistan. Faith leaders and journalists will be trained. Awareness will be raised through interesting theatre stories about the harmful effects of child marriages and about new laws passed against child marriages would be imparted to adolescent boys and girls students and their teachers, parents. Social, electronic and print media campaign and utilization of IEC material would also complement the campaign.

title: Raising Queer Workers' Rights in South Korea
description: This project aims to raise awareness on LGBTAIQ workers' rights within the queer community and workplaces in South Korea. Solidarity for LGBT Human Rights of Korea plan to interview queer-identified workers and collect discrimination cases. Alongside with these peer-to-peer activities, the project includes community education (e.g., holding workshops and publishing guiding materials) on queer people's labor rights for the broader field of labor activism.

title: Save Baikal: ecological tourism development
description: Save Baikal is a project aimed at researching, developing and introducing efficient methods to clean and protect Lake Baikal's coastline. This includes waste management at specially protected areas frequented by tourists. We aim to build cooperation with the public, government and companies to save the unique beauty of one of the most ancient lakes in the world, which is especially endangered in times of growing economic and tourist potential

title: Kids shall forget war!
description: The armed confrontation in the West Ukraine violently hammered lives of dozens of hundreds of civilians. Many kids were killed in this war, and many were wounded, lost their families, close people, lost their homes, and were displaced from what they loved. With $5000 this project will provide help to ten children, who suffered from fighting in Ukraine. We will cover their emergency and basic needs, provide with medical and psychological care, buy them food and clothes and school supplies, etc.

title: Stop Loss of Cash-Transfers Meant for Most Needy
description: This project will develop a databank monitoring system to stop loss of payments from Kenya's Poverty Fund. According to 2014 government audit, the Fund paid Sh 600 million (over $6m) to "ghosts" and "beneficiary organisations diverted the money to private use". Since June 2009, monthly payments of 444,000 orphans and needy persons are paid to people whose identity and existence are unknown. This databank, using mobile phone applications will ensure 1 million vulnerable people receive their help.

title: Chez Wa
description: The farm " Chez Wa" is an agro-pastoral initiative of the Association in memory of Prof. Walter Albisetti . It is located in a fertile area Adeta ( Kpalime ) and a provisional area of over 6 hectares of cultivable land. The project involves planting fruit trees, other trees  and breeding pigs for the purpose of generating activities to make funds available to poor people supported by Afagnan -Project Association. Beneficiaires of the projects will be the sick and the poor.

title: Save a Child: Reduce Malnutrition in Bolivia
description: Within Latin America and the Caribbean, Bolivia has the third highest rate of child mortality for children under age five with 30% of children under age three being chronically malnourished.  MAP International integrates  child survival and early childhood development into it's Focus 1365 Project to impact the highest amount of vulnerable children.

title: Bring Back Native Stingless Bees, Empower Women
description: We aim to train 30 local Maya women to raise melipona, native stingless bees that live in hollow logs, produce rich, curative honey, and have historically been an object of worship and a staple of the local economy. In the past 25 years, more than 90% of stingless bee colonies have disappeared, due to deforestation and the introduction of African bees. Our goal is to donate hives to 10 communities and train women in beekeeping. If we lose the melipona, we lose a cultural and financial treasure.

title: Female Friendly Spaces in Post-Quake Camps - Nepal
description: This project provides a travelling shelter for women and girls living in post-disaster zones. The roving Female Friendly Space (FFS) travels to various post-earthquake camps in Nepal where women and girls can go to report incidences of violence, seek services, be referred to medical or trauma counselling, attend awareness workshops and feel safe. The FFS also provide income generating activities, education, shelter and 24-hour protection for women and their children.

title: Business and Education Micro-lending for Youth
description: Young adults need opportunities to work or get an education.  By allowing them to access affordable loans for businesses or education, we give them options!  Typically, young adults have less experience and fewer resources.  With a micro-loan, they have real choices.  We will create a fund to Youth Fund to help fund loans on our usual lending platform.  Repayments will be used to make additional loans, so this is a donation that gives more than once.

title: Narrow the Gap - Help Nonprofits in Vietnam
description: Every year, local not-for-profit organizations (NPOs) in Vietnam continue to fight an uphill battle to build a better future for their communities and bring equal opportunity to disadvantaged groups, but who is fighting to make sure the NPOs have the knowledge and resources they need to stay afloat? Since 2009, LIN's Narrow the Gap Community Fund has brought together resources to support projects that address the most pressing issues. Will you join us in creating a brighter future for Vietnam?

title: Ama Ghar Displaced Children Fund
description: Many children were orphaned or displaced by disastrous 2015 earthquakes in Nepal. Ama Foundation worked with anti-trafficking organizations and the Nepal government to help find these children a safe home. Since 2015, we have taken 30 new children into our home, which can house 75 children - but we currently only have funding for the 46 children who currently live there. Your contribution helps us to take in more children and give them a loving home, an education and a future.

title: Help US Youth Advance Justice and Sustainability!
description: Last December, SustainUS delegates traveled to Paris for the COP21 climate talks and fight for a just and meaningful deal at the UN. Now, we're working to keep up the advocacy. By covering travel costs and providing small stipends to key SustainUS leaders in 2016, we can build a lasting advocacy team to keep the pressure on our leaders to implement and improve the agreement reached at Paris. Donate to support our work for climate justice!

title: Technology Training Center for Ethiopian Israelis
description: The high-tech industry presents one of the most attractive and financially rewarding career paths in the Israeli job market. Unfortunately, many young Ethiopian Israelis are confronted with obstacles which deter their integration into the industry.

title: Fundraising for our Jazz Programme
description: World Heart Beat's mission is to make quality music education accessible to every child. We are fundraising to continue to support the 49% of our students who study through our bursaries - without your continued support our academy wouldn't thrive with the same multitude of young, talented musicians who we get to teach.  Our Jazz programme is totally free, and we would like keep it that way, so we need your help - we are so grateful for any support which you can offer!

title: Empower 175 students for food security in Kenya
description: With your support the rural youth of Nakuru County in Kenya will be empowered to ensure sustainable food production and food security for future generations. At least 175 students will develop skills on sustainable farming, animal husbandry, food processing and marketing, and will further disseminate these skills within the local communities enabling the small-scale farmer fully utilize the good agricultural potential of the County.

title: Relief rebuilding to 25 communities in Nepal
description: Women and children are hard- hit in Nepal earthquake. Tewa is supporting community based women's organisations working in 14 severely affected earthquake districts to rebuild communities and lives, enabling  grantees to use their local skills,knowledge in supporting pregnant, postnatal, physically challenged, indigenous,marginalized and most vulnerable communities. Peace and philanthropy centres as a pilot initiative,with psycho social counselling, barefoot volunteers/grantees will be mobilized.

title: Educate African Children to Save Their Environment
description: Through the medium of a wildlife orphanage and our location in the middle of the bush, our mission is to inspire and educate underprivileged South African children to care for their environment, while creating awareness about environmental job opportunities. DAKTARI works with volunteers from all around the world to teach children and provide care for our animals. Find out more and sign up to volunteer through the links below!

title: Girl Power, Stop Child Marriage
description: This project will form ten girl's clubs in an island in the southwestern part of Bangladesh to improve the life skills of 500 adolescent girls where child marriage is usual. Those girls will protect their peers from child marriage.

title: Motorcycle training for health workers in Gambia
description: Riders for Health are mobilising health workers across 8 countries in Africa, enabling them to travel to and distribute healthcare to the most rural communities. Millions of men, women and children don't have access to life-saving healthcare due to the fact that transport is simply not available. Riders provide the missing link and your donation could provide training for a health worker, equipping them with the skills to ride a motorbike and reach those that have, until now, been unreachable.

title: Motorcycle training for health workers in Nigeria
description: Riders for Health are mobilising health workers across 8 countries in Africa, enabling them to travel to and distribute healthcare to the most rural communities. Millions of men, women and children don't have access to life-saving healthcare due to the fact that transport is simply not available. Riders provide the missing link and your donation could provide training for a health worker, equipping them with the skills to ride a motorbike and reach those that have, until now, been unreachable.

title: Excellent education for 2500+ students in Chennai
description: Solving India's education crisis needs the best minds & hearts as leaders in education. Teach For India Chennai's movement of 100+ Fellows join us from colleges & corporates to work as full-time teachers in 32 high-need, low-income schools across South, Central and North Chennai. Teachers being the most important school-based factor impacting a student, our Fellows lead classrooms to directly impact 2500+ students & 10000+ community members.

title: Help A Vulnerable Child Learns Life-Skills Now
description: We currently run literacy and life-skill projects with indigent young people from 43 schools, empowering them with reading and writing skills through exchange programs. We propose a skills learning center to offer basic literacy and vocational skills to less-privileged children in Jos, Plateau State Nigeria, who are mainly from few poor of the poorest families affected by the various crises - to prepare them for professional life and make them self-reliant to cope with the challenges of poverty.

title: Help 500 elderly lonely people in Greater London
description: This project will look after 500 lonely housebound, blind, wheel-chair bound disadvantaged pensioners in Greater London, providing seaside coach trips, boat trips on Thames, afternoon tea parties, and Christmas Parties.

title: Send Laura to college
description: Do you remember Laura? Her story touched many people's hearts. In 2011, Laura was one of our students when we implemented brain education in El Salvador for the first time. Her changes were transformational and she made her mind to create a better life for herself and her child. Now she wants to go to college.  There are many Lauras in El Salvador and in other countries. Let's help one girl who can be a model for many others because of her determination and will to overcome her limitations.

title: Supply SOLAR power to 77 families in Qinghai
description: In a remote village in Qinghai, 130 children and their families use wood and dung as their fuel for cooking, heating and boiling water.  In a barren environment, collecting these items is time consuming and a burden usually for the women and children.  In the evenings, children study using butter or kerosene lamps, and candles. The local government has done much to help remote villages with infrastructure, but it is agreed SOLAR PANELS will improve health, save time, and help the children study.

title: Train Primary Teachers in Conservation Agriculture
description: We urgently need your help to teach climate smart agriculture in primary schools and help tackle food insecurity while building climate change resilience. We develop lived experience as schools manage crop plots and nutritional gardens.

title: Sponsor Francine's High School Education in Zambia
description: Kucetekela Foundation (KF) provides a five year scholarship program for impoverished youths in Zambia. By donating to this project, you will help provide for Francine's various needs as she continues working hard to complete her secondary schooling at Chalo Trust School. As Francine works on completing school, she also improves her community through various service intiatives.

title: Advent International for PIH: Reach the Beach
description: We will be running the 200 mile Reach The Beach Relay New Hampshire from Bretton Woods to Hampton Beach taking place 18-19 September 2015.  We are again collectively raising money for Partners In Health, to revitalize rural health clinics and train the next generation of Mexican doctors in the Sierra of Chiapas, Mexico-one of the most marginalized areas of the country.

title: Save mothers and children in the Mediterranean Sea
description: Since 2013 the Foundation's medical teams have worked on board of the Italian Navy's ships to save and rescue migrants adrift  in the Sicily Channel, providing first aid to 70,000 people and focusing on mother and child emergency healthcare: to date the Foundation's pediatricians, gynecologists and midwives assisted 10,000 women, 9,000 children, 500 pregnant women, several of them during labor and delivery. An estimated 2,000 women and 1,500 children will need help in the next months.

title: Help 1,400 Children in Nepal to Go Back to School
description: The unimaginable devastation caused by the earthquakes in Nepal has left many communities without homes, schools, livestock, food, and supplies. PHASE is deeply rooted in these local communities and is in a good position to provide both immediate and long-term support. We are on the ground in these isolated areas, helping to rebuild lives. This project aims to bring a much-needed sense of normalcy to the lives of school children by providing them with educational materials.

title: Provide Social Services in Hong Kong
description: Protect the young and the innocent, care for the elderly and the underprivileged, aid the poor, heal the sick, educate the young, nurture their morality, provide recreation to the public, care for the environment, pass on the cultural inheritance and bring goodness to the community. PLK currently runs over 260 units throughout the Hong Kong Special Administration Region, providing welfare, educational, recreational and cultural services to the community.

title: Talent Award for 5 students per year in ECUPL
description: Ge Jun Talent Award, five students will be assessed and selected as prize winners per academic year (three undergraduates, one Master student, and one PHD student) and each will be awarded 20,000 RMB. Jun Ge will donate 100,000 RMB each year to full-time undergraduates and post-graduates majored in law from 2013 to his retirement.

title: Jalambang Nursery and Youths project Association
description: The community of Jalambang, located in West Coast Region of The Gambia, has about 350 to 400 households with an estimated population of about five thousand to six thousand people. Currently, the children of Jalambang have to travel 6 kilometers each day to Brikama to attain school. Because of the danger, many parents keep their children at home. This project will help establish a school in Jalamba, ensuring the education of our youth and expanding livelihood options for parents.

title: 500 Nanofilter Stations for Mwanza, Tanzania
description: After an impressive achievement in Arusha, of which the government reports the reduction of waterborne diseases by 42.9% due to Nanofilter, now we are expanding to Mwanza where people depend on water from Lake Victoria contaminated with microorganisms causing BILHAZIA. We are determined to establish 500 water stations. Your donation ($1,000) will help build a station that serves 100 families. For more information please kindly contact the inventor of Nanofilter, Prof.HILONGA: hilonga@gmail.com

title: Enable 4000 leaders drive lasting change in Kenya
description: Tatua Kenya supports individuals and organizations by providing access to a training course. The fellowship builds the leadership capacity of participants through the skills of community organizing in order to create a sense of responsibility and ownership amongst community members, and sustainable change. Through 15 Tatua Fellows, the program reaches over 4000 community members in meaningful campaigns and projects ranging from education to taking care of the elderly.

title: Champion Her Right to an Education
description: ZanaAfrica Foundation provides adolescent girls in East Africa with the resources they need to live more healthy and informed lives. We are showing girls they are powerful agents of change in their own lives through supporting them in mind, body and spirit. This holistic approach includes sanitary pads and underwear that girls need and want, standardized and aspirational health education, and safe spaces and mentors for girls in their communities.

title: Biodiversity for All in Mexico
description: As home to one of the world's most endangered ecosystems, the Cloud Forest, El Triunfo Biological Reserve must be protected so carefully that few may visit each year. Now, through the play Guardians of the Mist at the Chiapas Zoo, audiences are introduced to issues affecting this environmental treasure. The show follows the heroic efforts of an animal kingdom protecting itself from habitat destruction and serves to build empathy and emotional connection to the forest and its diverse species.

title: Mental Health and Trauma Training in Nepal
description: Two major earthquakes rocked Nepal in a two-week period, killing nearly 9,000 people. The psychological effects of this sudden widespread death and destruction remain long after the quake. We're training local community workers so more people can get help as they  cope with tremendous losses.

title: University Scholarships for Students in Palestine
description: Palestinian students face many obstacles in obtaining a university degree. They cross checkpoints en route to lectures, study at home by candle light, and work side jobs to pay their tuition. Our scholarship pays for students' tuition at local universities thereby enabling talented and ambitious high school graduates to obtain degrees and the skills to make important contributions to their communities and their country.

title: Open a House of Hope for abused kids in Cambodia
description: We need to open the first crisis center for families with abused children in Cambodia, a home of healing for 700 hurt children next year. For kids from traumatised and abusive families, the only answer now in Cambodia is orphanages, shelters and jail. But we've seen little miracles when our dedicated team works with a family, relatives and communities to build love and support for their children. Last year, Global Giving helped feed more than 600 children - this year, help them go home.

title: Disaster Recovery through Art for Nepali children
description: Children in Nepal are struggling through tough times, whether they are recovering from a devastating earthquake, or economic hardships, or an uncaring environment. Our project aims to build up hope and resilience in these children through the medium of art. Art is an amazing way for children to express themselves, share their emotions, build self-confidence and feel joy. Through our project, we want to bring this experience to as many Nepali children as possible.

title: Entrepreneurship for 27 Prisoners in South Africa
description: We believe every young person has the God-given talent & potential to flourish. Young people in South Africa face enormous socio-economic challenges such as high rates of unemployment, crime & gangsterism. This results in many young people ending up in South African prisons & losing purpose for their lives. MEP is a holistic 1 year entrepreneurship programme that works with juvenile offenders economically, spiritually, emotionally and socially, preparing each offender for pre and post release.

title: Rural Girls Quality Education in KPK Pakistan
description: Zarbaig school in Dir has been recently constructed with the generous help of DIL supporters. The first purpose built girls school in this rural area, Zarbaig has 9 classrooms and 4 washrooms. Girls could not access education in this area and families have had to survive on meagre earnings primarily on daily wage labourers' income. The 218 students attending Zarbaig come from poor households where literacy barely exists and job opportunities remain extremely restricted.

title: Stray Dogs become "Therapy Dogs"
description: This project save the lives of stray dogs, and train them to Therapy Dogs. We  will continue this activity continuously and save as many lives as we can.

title: Educate 100 Dalit girls
description: For $10,000 we can add 100 girls to our child sponsorship programme immediately. Our sponsorship programme is quite unique as we open a bank account for every child and this account is managed by the child's mother. This teaches the mother how to manage money. When we add a child to the programme, the mother also joins our self-help group programme. She will benefit from our micro finance programme so she can purchase a cow or a sewing machine to generate much-needed income for the family

title: Afghanistan Earthquake Relief and Recovery Fund
description: On October 26, 2015, a powerful 7.5M earthquake caused significant damage in Afghanistan and Pakistan. Survivors need access to emergency supplies like food, water, and medicine in addition to longer term recovery assistance.  All donations to this fund will exclusively support local relief and recovery efforts from this earthquake.

title: Safe Shelter for 16 Children and Woman in Thailand
description: The shelter home and education support program in Mae Chan consists of two sites. The Swimming Home shelters 14 children suffering from abandonment, abuse, or neglect; while the Ban Klang Na Shelter is the home for victims of human trafficking for the duration of rehabilitation and preparation for their return home. The children and woman receive shelter, protection, life skills development training, nutritious home made meals, family outreach services, and government school education.

title: Improve Nutrition for 60 IP Filipino Children
description: The indigenous people (IP) in the Philippines are among the poorest sectors in the country.  They are hardly  reached with the basic services due to accessibility factor and neglect.  As a result IP children generally have poor nutrition because of parents' lack of awareness and financial difficulty to buy foods rich in nutritional value.

title: Support 25 Transformative Evening Village Schools
description: To address the problem of school dropouts and children related to their studies, Agastya Volunteers visit Community Centres in the evenings and provide remedial lessons.  The children are also provided with interactive learning sessions through, singing, dancing, hands on experience on Science, Maths and Digital literacy which makes learning a great fun for them.

title: Put Solar Power to Work in rural Ghana!
description: SOLAR POWER INITIATIVES should be a 'No-Brainer' in Ghana! To replace toxic kerosene use in homes without electricity; to provide a 'clean' lighting 'solution' for Ghana's chronic (daily) "light off" power outages....for homes, small businesses, schools; to explore the potential for low-cost solar to drive irrigation systems.  4SROGBOE's goal is to bring SUSTAINABLE Solar Energy Projects ...IN AS MANY USEFUL AND COST-EFFECTIVE WAYS AS POSSIBLE. Using available technologies..and the sun is free!

title: Help 500 Filipino Children be Literate in Computer
description: Based on the data, 60% of the public schools in the Philippines have at least one computer unit.  The rest of the public schools in the Philippines have not even a single computer unit.  This is true in poor communities and inaccessible barangays. That is why many of the public schools students living in these communities are far behind in computer knowledge compared to their counterparts who are studying in private schools in the cities and well-funded government learning institutions.

title: The Mentoring Club, Uganda: Making Education Count
description: ADOVIC, a grass-roots social change organization based in Jinja, Uganda recently completed a successful six month pilot programme, mentoring 22 high school students. ADOVIC now seeks funding to make their programme, 'The Mentoring Club', available to schools across the Busoga Region.  You can help make a difference to students' long term emotional wellbeing and educational success while also providing opportunities for local youth and social worker university graduates. Join us now at The Club!

title: New World Possible for 10,000 Ndia Women, kenya
description: HFAW in collaboration with Jiinue Network and other women who recently participated in Global Women Leadership Network (GWLN) will raise awareness among rural and marginalized women to refuse selling their votes, avoid electing corrupt leaders, vote for more women for elective seats and choose leaders of integrity come 2017 election. We are planning an urgent 10 kilometer walk, first  one in Ndia Constituency in Kirinyaga County, scheduled for October 10th, 2015.More Counties walks will follow.

title: Rescuing Girls Sexual Exploitation in India Nepal
description: Free a Girl is dedicated to rescuing girls from situation of sexual exploitation. We believe in creating a safe environment for children and young people, protecting them from sexual violence and exploitation. This project seeks to rescue girls who are victims of sexual exploitation in India. The rescued girls will receive rehabilitation and reintegration support as well as legal assistance to ensure their best interests are being advocated before judicial authorities.

title: Help 25 Colombian Indigenous Women Grow Leadership
description: The Solidarity Foundation in Medellin, Colombia will use its 26 years of experience to help Embera Katio indigenous women in their reservation in the municipality of Dabeiba-Colombia, to empower them as entrepreneur leaders and generators or their own incomes, through the elaboration of arts and crafts.

title: Give 420 Girls in Tanzania Their Own School
description: Africa Schoolhouse's newest project is an all-girls boarding school, the first in the Misungwi District.  This school will allow 420 girls to receive and complete their secondary education in a safe, nurturing environment.  In addition to the standard Tanzanian academic curriculum and teachers, the school will also promote leadership, STEM, entrepreneurship, social justice and care for the environment. $33,000 will help us renovate and modernize two classrooms, and let 100 girls start schooling.

title: Empowering Entrepreneurship through Technology
description: This project will expands U-TOUCH entrepreneurship training in digital centers in Uganda providing entrepreneurship and technology training to enable 400 Ugandans to lift themselves out of poverty. Youth will engage in self-esteem and team building exercises, learn computer and entrepreneurship skills, including writing a business plan, and gain valuable hands-on experience developing a cooperative business.

title: Help 300,000 kids realize that Math can be fun
description: Ganitha Kalika Andolana (GKA) - A Math Movement launched by Akshara Foundation and the Karnataka state Government, aims to improve basic Numeracy skills and facilitate classroom learning of Mathematics in Government primary schools of Karnataka. GKA will help over 300,000 children studying in grades 4 and 5 of 7800 Government-run primary schools attain mathematical fluency. It will also build capacity of over 8000 teachers to enable them to teach Maths creatively inside the classrooms.

title: Help Veterans Who Struggle with Fireworks
description: You can provide a free yard sign to veterans who struggle with Fireworks. In 2015, over 4,000 signs were given out to veterans, but it is not enough. There are still thousands of veterans waiting for a free sign.  If you would like to sign up for a sign please register at http://www.militarywithptsd.org/involvedwithus/registration/ and check the box Firework sign.

title: Helping More Young Australians to Succeed in Life
description: The Beacon Foundation is working towards an Australia that understands, cares and is motivated to support young people to successfully transition from education to employment.  With your help, and through programs that actively involve industry in education, we bring learning to life, increasing student engagement in education, introducing students to a range of jobs and employers, and providing the skills and inspiration necessary so they transition successfully from learning to earning.

title: HER Sparkles - Young Women-Led for Social Change
description: HER Sparkles aims to empower young women who dare to make changes, and to encourage them to put their ideas into actions with youth and gender perspective. A total of 8 young women-led projects which are issues that happened around us, yet, much hidden or invisible in mass media discussions. Topics include teenagers' sex education, menstruation taboo, youth sexual desires, etc. Your support means a "YES" to young women's empowerment - that enables them to take a lead in making social changes.

title: Help End #MaternalHealth Disparities in the USA
description: Did you know that 3-4 times as many African Americans are harmed or die during pregnancy or birth compared to European Americans? America ranks 60th amongst other nations for maternal mortality. Shut out by a system that literally denies them healthcare, this project gives access to FREE midwifery care for 500 pregnant women per year; connects them to essential support and resources; and educates and empowers them to acheive the safe outcome that is EVERY woman's dream. #MaternalHealth matters!

title: Give Clean Water to Kids in Africa
description: The capital city of Ethiopia, Addis Ababa, is one of the fastest growing cities in the world. More than 374,000 poor children attend government-funded schools in Addis, where the water and sanitation conditions are appalling. Only 6% of schools have reliable access to water, 35% have useable toilets, and of schools that had taps for handwashing, only 66% worked. Soap is present for handwashing in just 10% of schools. Splash's goal is to ensure every school in Addis has safe water always.

title: Family to Every Child
description: Within the Stick together project, our organization work in Smolensk region, in Russia. In "Stick together. Smolensky region" we re-establish the orphaned children links with their blood relatives and help families to reunite with their own children.

title: Help Young Children in Kindergarten!
description: We have supported the reconstruction of the school in Bulqize and have a new kindergarten for 50 children 5 to 6 years old, but unfortunately it is empty of resources!  We wish to equip the kindergarten with toys, games, books and didactic materials to encourage the young children's development through exploring and investigating their environment and mastering skills.  A short mentoring program for preschool teachers will assist in the interactive learning program.

title: You Can Give Kids in India Clean Water
description: Splash is at the forefront of a growing movement to ensure that children in urban poverty have the resources they need to thrive and realize their full potential. We provide water, sanitation, and hygiene hardware (water filters, handwashing and drinking stations, toilet construction) and custom hygiene education to students, staff, and local communities. Your generosity brings dignity, good health, opportunity, and joy to kids in Kolkata and others just like them!

title: Legal Help for Domestic Violence Victims
description: This project will help make WomensLaw.org mobile-friendly, making legal information and help available to domestic violence victims through their mobile devices.

title: Young Epilepsy - New School, Classroom Appeal
description: The children in our school - some as young as five - are living with the most severe epilepsy and associated conditions, experiencing up to 40 seizures a day. Our current school is becoming unfit for our students complex needs and desperately needs replacing. As a result we are having to turn young people away, some of whom have nowhere else to go. We urgently need your support so we can open the doors to our New School in time for the first day of term in January 2016. Join our Galaxy of Stars!

title: Connecting Forests Across Generations
description: This project will expand an existing biological corridor along the Rio Sol and provide an indigenous grandmother an opportunity to supplement her income and pass along her forest ethic to her children and grandchildren.

title: Clean Water For 50+ Rescued Kenyan Infants
description: In Kenya, contaminated drinking water is still a reality for many people. For this reason, New Life Home Trust has installed a water tank or borehole at each New Life home over the years. With the help of these tanks, once abandoned infants are offered quality care without fear of contracting preventable diseases. Additionally, we keep our overall costs lower by relying on our water tank rather than an outside source. New life for rescued infants requires clean, safe drinking water daily.

title: Moving Beyond Surviving Human Trafficking
description: Our program applies proven curricula to teach survivors of human trafficking computer programming and other skills demanded by today's technology companies. We provide survivors with viable means of ongoing self-support - something absent from today's anti-trafficking movement.  We will train up to 26 survivors living in the Bay Area in this pilot and help them find work after completing our program, which is customized to each survivor's aptitude and interest.

title: Summer Enrichment Program
description: The Summer Enrichment Program is offered to students in grades 2 through 8 who lack an adequate foundation for learning to read and write effectively. There are 2 three-week sessions that run during the summer to help new students get acclimated to the school and helps existing students make academic gains while they are out of school. The program provides experiences in reading fluency, expanded vocabulary, phonics, poetry and reading for pleasure.

title: FOCUS-Breaking the Cycle of Homelessness in Toledo
description: (FOCUS) Family Outreach Community United Services was founded in 1982 to help the homeless population in Toledo break the cycle of homelessness.  FOCUS takes a long-view of our clients' lives and futures.  We take children & families out of a shelter and find them a home.  We help the parents find jobs, learn how to budget and become stable to ensure they remain in their homes once FOCUS subsidy ends.  Many of our families are single mom households who have nothing to support their family.

title: Save the Life of a Malnourished Child
description: Malnutrition accounts for almost half of the deaths among children under five globally. Within approximately seven weeks the ready-to-use therapeutic food we make in our factory, Plumpy'Nut, can bring a child back to good health. Your support can save the life of a severely malnourished child.

title: Proud to Be a Girl: Empowering Girls in Cambodia
description: In Cambodia it is sometimes hard to be a girl.  It's dangerous to be a girl. It's scary to be a girl. It's even shameful to be a girl.  Hagar Cambodia provides healing and restoration through aftercare to girls who have experienced the most violent and severe forms of abuse and exploitation.

title: Help Harness The Power Of Equine Assisted Wellness
description: The Center For Equine Assisted Wellness specializes in equine assisted learning and wellness programs that promote healthy life choices and self-compassion, and help those with special needs lead happier, more productive lives. Each person who comes to the farm will have a unique experience that builds on their personal goals and desired outcomes, as they dig deep to find their own path to personal wholeness. They are able to go out into the world and be the very best they can be.

title: Nuevas Novelas: Media Literacy to Prevent Violence
description: Telenovelas tend to replicate intimate partner abuse, and this is your invitation to become part of a project that provides young women with the tools to re-envision the world they wish to live in. In our workshop series, thirty (30) young women from South Los Angeles ages 15 - 18 will rewrite scenes from TV shows in collaboration with their counterparts from Guatemala. They will then produce short videos that normalize healthy relationships and later obtain internships with their new knowledge.

title: We are India's children
description: In India, children are forced to drop out of school because their parents cannot afford to pay their school fees, but for some children the situation is much worse. They are ostracized simply because of the profession of a parent. Children of sex workers are one of the most vulnerable and marginalized groups in our country, and it is through absolutely no fault of their own.

title: The Emerging Entrepreneur Competition
description: The young girls studying in the technical institutions of Punjab are among the most vulnerable in the province, with almost all of them living below or just above the national poverty line. The proposed project will provide greater opportunities to disadvantaged young people studying in the vocational and technical institutions of the Punjab province of Pakistan through advancing enterprise and social entrepreneurship education and opportunities and creating sustainable enterprises.

title: Empowering Mayan women through ancient textiles
description: impacto textil is now starting to replicate and scale methodologies and tools as to serve 500 to 1000 artisans in a two-year timeframe (having worked with 85 Mayan women to improve production of textile handicrafts). Our work helps women to expand on their craft, teaching them advanced design principles and technical skills. With improved products, artisans gain increased access to ethical and fair trade markets and a secure income to support their families, mainly children and their community.

title: Makerspace
description: Chimera will be moving from a small office space to a much larger warehouse facility, allowing us to continue striving toward our mission of education and providing resources to makers and artists in the North Bay.  We'll be able to teach larger classes. Our community will have access to metalworking and woodworking tools. We'll still have our 3D printers, laser cutters and CNC mills!

title: Kindly Help Buy Land and Build a Training Center
description: This project will empower underprivileged youth to train in hands-on skills that will help them to be self-reliant. Most of the developing countries have since many years suffer from unstable sources of income. This has resulted in many challenges not only to the youth but also among the rest of the population. Once this project is fully funded,we are to release improved levels of income among  the youths in our catchment areas.

title: Improving Health for People of Kilimanjaro Region
description: Pamoja Tunaweza Women's Center (PTWC) provides quality and affordable health care to the people of Kilimanjaro Region. Our locally staffed clinic provides primary outpatient care to over 250 patients each month and our bi-annual two week medical outreach activities provide free care for 300-600 patients each day. We also provide support to the most vulnerable through income generating projects, payment of school fees, and health education to address the social determinants of health.

title: Help 50 Elderly People Not Lose Their Home
description: San Jose is a home for elderly people who have found themselves lonely and lacking the necessary care for everyday life. Unfortunately, we are facing an emergency: urgent repairs and installations must be completed, and we do not have the necessary funds. Most of the residents, who are over 90% women, have no other family. This place is and has been their home for over 10, 15, or even 20 years, and we cannot look away.

title: Mushroom project expansion for women in Uganda.
description: We hope to raise $10,000 toward supporting Epaphroditus Savings and Credit Cooperative Society, a registered co-op located in the Wakiso District of Uganda, about 30km from the capital city Kampala. It currently has 20 active female members whom Africa Development Promise is supporting to start a mushroom growing project. The women need assistance with both communal and individual farm set-up, as well as training associated with identifying and understanding value chain.

title: Help Mentor 100s of  U.S. Middle School Boys
description: CBM CARES is helping hundreds of African American boys across the nation, in late elementary and middle school, to develop an attachment to school (less truancy and suspensions, and greater high school matriculation); achieve academically and improve their behavior by connecting them to a responsible male mentor. These relationships are helping them to mature, grow and prosper in life. Our program works in CA, DC, IL, MA, MD, PA, SC TX, and VA.

title: PAL Harlem Center Family Day for youth & families
description: Heading back to school is a financial burden for many PAL families, especially those with more than 1 child. Many of the Harlem Center parents struggle to provide their children with the required school supplies necessary for academic success. We intend to provide our participants with backpacks and other school supplies, helping them to approach their new classrooms prepared and confident.

title: Educate Former Street and Slum Kids
description: Education is the only way for street and slum kids -- many of whom have no parents or who have illiterate parents -- to lift themselves out of the devastating poverty that they face. The former street and slum kids at our children's home receive quality education and are thriving in this stimulating environment. We provide private school education, daily after-school tutoring, and fun and enjoyable extracurricular activities, and we monitor performance.

title: Provide Surgery for Children in Ethiopia
description: Most children in Ethiopia do not have access to complex pediatric surgery and thus live with their disability or die from it. The only pediatric surgical center in the country is in Addis Ababa, but most families cannot afford the cost of surgery, medication, or hospital care for their children.  This project will allow children with life-limiting disabilities to be operated on by trained pediatric surgeons and be restored to a meaningful and productive life.

title: Empower Refugee Youth Through Dance
description: "Before I started dancing, I was always thinking about the problems and stress I face. It was hard for me to think about my future. Dance has helped me to focus in a way that I was never able to before." -Eric, MindLeaps student. MindLeaps uses dance to help at-risk youth and refugee children build essential cognitive and behavioral skills. Through participation at MindLeaps, these youth show an increase in responsible and healthy life choices, greater school success, and community integration.

title: Digital Literacy: IT for Street Children
description: "When I first came to MindLeaps, I didn't know how to turn on a computer. Now I can write emails and soon I'll learn to tweet!  I believe in myself. I think one day I could set up my own IT institution." - Prince, a street child in Rwanda.     At the MindLeaps Center for Street Youth, children, who have never touched a computer, become digitally literate - giving them tangible skills and a chance to earn a living in Rwanda's developing tech community.

title: Provide Water Purifiers to 100 Households
description: The majority of communities in Uganda are forced to drink untreated water, which results in widespread illness and disease. With your help, we can buy 100 water purifiers for impoverished households in Rural Uganda. By doing so, we can promote treated water in areas and an increased focus on health care.

title: Give 2500 Therapies to Disabled Kids in India
description: Children from low income families are worst affected when they have disability as the parents have hardly any money to even support food, shelter and clothing for them.  This affects these children long term.  The project is helping these children by providing subsidized therapies like Speech, Physio, Remedial, Occupational and psychologist  in Mumbai.  The children also receive counseling and support during these difficult times.  We have provided more than 10,000 therapies to over 300 children

title: Provide 150 at-risk students with computers in TX
description: Katherine Anne Porter School, a Title 1 (high poverty) charter high school in Wimberley, Texas, will provide 150 Chromebooks to their majority at-risk, economically disadvantaged student population that does not otherwise have access to computers.  We believe that technology should not be elitist and only available to those who can afford it - every student deserves to have the tools and experience that will help them compete and succeed in life after graduation.

title: Bridge the technology gap for 1000 students
description: This project will bridge the technology gap that exists between schools and disadvantaged students. By building a cloud-based computer lab for high schools that lack the funding and staff, students will gain hands on experience with real world IT components. Yellow Circle labs promote increased learning by allowing students to build their own information technology projects without having to worry about costs. Students with financial needs will be provided laptops for use during their education.

title: Forests for the most endangered primate in Peru
description: Deforestation is leading the San Martin titi monkey to extinction. The expansion of agriculture has already eliminated 60% of its habitat, forcing the remaining populations to live in isolated patches with limited resources of food and habitat. This locally-managed fund will allow the reforestation of critical areas for the species, contributing to its survival and benefiting almost 18,000 local people with the many associated forest ecosystem services such as pollination, or climate stability.

title: Build Classrooms and Desks  for Orphans in India
description: This Project will build New class rooms In South India ,where 60 kids are learning under trees and in dark and inadequate rooms of a Old building ..Which also will help the kids to have school desks.

title: Estudio Damgo IV: A Filipino Design+Build Studio
description: Foundation University architecture program, Estudio Damgo, enters its fourth community project.   Fifth year architecture students address the needs of the community at a macro-scale at Dumaguete City's Port Terminal. The project is a Welcome Center, which is part of the port redevelopment master plan addressing the growing needs of city.  The Welcome Center will serve as a gateway landmark for seafaring travelers by orienting visitors to Dumaguete City and Negros Oriental province.

title: Help Women Affected by Cameroon Anglophone Crises
description: This is extended to support women and families who have been affected by the crisis in Bui Division. We want to buy at least 400 3 week-old chickens and give them to 50 women who have been severely victimized by the current socio-political unrest in the North West and South West of Cameroon. The situation is very bad and these women need help by way of being re-integrated. This project is because they lost all they had to the displacement, homes burnt and properties damaged.

title: Save  Women & girls from Violence-India
description: Crime against women, especially rape, incest rape are on the rise over the last three years in Tamil Nadu, there had been 7,475 crime cases against women. Tamil Nadu accounted for 923 rape victims and 90% rape cases go without reporting because of Scandal, Disgrace, shame and indignity. CHHASE provide legal aid and awareness to all including schools to stop violence & to keep gender equality. This project aim to change mentality of men to give due respect to women to live safely & respectfully.

title: Transform the lives of 3200 children in Hyderabad
description: From 46 Fellows impacting 1250 Students in 2012, today, Teach For India Hyderabad has 82 Fellows serving 3250 Students across 33 Govt. and low-budget private schools. We've made headway in regional educational reform with over 200+ Alumni working in various roles to push the needle in the education system, from entrepreneurial innovation to policy reform. Our focus rests squarely on building proof points of excellent schools, supporting social entrepreneurs, and infusing talent into the System.

title: Cumbria Talented Athlete Fund
description: The Cumbria Talented Athlete Fund supports talented athletes from across the rurally isolated county of Cumbria, to help them reach their potential in their chosen sport. The fund provides grants to amateur athletes to help towards training and competition costs. Given the large distances needing to be travelled by athletes competing at regional level or above, this fund provides a essential support to ensure that Cumbria remains well represented on the national and international sporting stage

title: Support 100 Girl Survivors of Sexual Abuse Zim
description: This project will rescue girls from abuse and provide support to survivors. Vulnerable girls are often whose parents have died mostly as a result of AIDS. TaLI provides such survivors with medical assistance to prevent HIV or to provide support where they are  HIV positive. We provide Counselling to victims and their parents, We rescue them from abusive environments, We report and follow abuse cases with police and support through justice system/courts and  Reintegration with families.

title: Save a Girl from Child Marriage with a Scholarship
description: In Bangladesh, poverty is forcing girls as young as 10 to become child-brides. Though parents believe this is a viable way of providing for their daughters, it usually means a life of abuse, poverty, and loneliness. And it often leads to the girl being trafficked. This project provides a girl with a scholarship to stay in school, which is the best way to prevent child marriage and give her the chance to become educated and rise above poverty.

title: Healthy Start-Ensure immunization to 30513 babies
description: The first 5 years play a significant role in a child's life. But, for thousands of children, growing up well continues to be a distant dream. Long before they turn 5, their physical, emotional and cognitive growth is irreversibly hampered by lack of adequate nutrition and healthcare. You can make a difference by giving them a 'healthy start'. 'Healthy Start' initiative will ensure 30,513 babies under the age of 1 year across CRY-supported projects receive access to all lifesaving vaccines

title: Protect girls from human trafficking in Laos
description: SENGSAVANG offers protection and assistance to victims and girls at risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation in Laos. Our shelter in central Laos provides a safe home where the girls receive holistic care during their rehabilitation process and are given hope for a better future. Through education, vocational trainings and micro-business starter kits, we transform their lives and ensure a sustainable socio-economic community reintegration as an active support for their families.

title: Renewable energy to rebuild villages in Nepal
description: The NGO atmosfair will provide families, schools and health centres in two earthquake struck villages northeast of Kathmandu with solar lanterns, solar home systems and efficient cookstoves. Being forced to live and work in temporary shelters until the end of the monsoon season, those energy devices will improve the earthquake victims' living conditions, study opportunities and health treatment.

title: Give education & training to Zimbabwean girls
description: Addressing huge gender disparities our programme invests in education, vocational training and psychosocial support for vulnerable young women in Zimbabwe. We need your help building their skills, confidence and independence to live a full life.

title: Transform lives of children through human values
