description: Our goal is to help the development of underprivileged children by promoting core values such as friendship, respect, honesty, and solidarity. We provide social, cultural, and recreational activities in which children interact with volunteers who serve as role models. Volunteers provide leadership, inspiration, and encouragement for children to develop into productive and healthy members of society.

title: Provide theater to 2,500 under-served children!
description: AFA is thrilled to present "Voice Power!" written & performed by Darian Dauchan, directed by Jennifer McGrath, our 2015 Audience Project Tour. We will bring this exciting production, free of charge, to over 2,500 under-served NYC children this fall, many of whom have never seen professional theater. Poet/musician Darian guides young audiences on a vocal odyssey through rhymes, beat-boxing, & acapella melodies in search of one of civilization's most valued treasures - the power of the voice!

title: Feed 30 malnourished young children in Kenyan slum
description: Macheo feeds and provides daily care to 30 malnourished children under the age of 4 in the slums of Thika, Kenya. They administer nutritious meals, basic healthcare, child development activities and parental training, to effectively change the future of these disadvantaged children. Malnutrition during the first 1000 days of life, irreversibly stunts a child's body and brain development, permanently limiting their potential. Therefore, give hope to the hungry and a future to a child.

title: Helping Flood Affected Youth to Help Themselves
description: The recent floods in many parts of Pakistan have rendered thousands of people homeless, forcing them to leave under the open skies amid the surging water levels in rivers and other water resources.  Chitral as well as Gilgit-Baltistan among the worst-affected areas.  Several hundred thousand people have no access to food, water, shelter or healthcare and the situation will undoubtedly deteriorate as rains continue and more rivers flood.

title: Help Uganda's poorest: Bududa Learning Center
description: We help the poorest of the poor in rural Uganda. We have a vocational school teaching them marketable skills, an orphan's program providing support and lodging, and a women's micro finance initiative. Your donations keep our initiatives running.

title: Empower the Slum Woman for Sustainable livelihood
description: Institute for Development Welfare Services (IDEWES) main goal is to develop and empower the women in the slum areas for sustainable livelihood. We create sustainable solutions to economically empower the women to have a healthy livelihood to support their families and communities as a whole.  Bridging the gap to solve the issues of inequality amongst the men and women who have been constrained by the customs and traditional norms holding them back from economic stability.

title: Enabling People with Disabilities to Have Equality
description: RespectAbility works with leaders, employers, media, faith-based organizations, nonprofits, and the disability community to enable and empower people with disabilities to have a better future. This includes educating employers about the fact that people with disabilities can be extremely talented and loyal employees, non-partisan voter education and political participation, and advocating that negative stigmas against people with disabilities - and the hate crimes against us - should stop.

title: Empower Orphans in Kenya with a Quality Education
description: The Margaret Okari Children's Foundation is dedicated to educating and caring for orphans in rural Kenya. We operate a residential school in the Kisii hills where we serve more than 220 orphans and vulnerable children from preschool through 8th grade, providing them with a nurturing home, food, medical care, and one of the best academic programs available in the region. We have also helped dozens of children attend secondary school and have two university graduates.

title: Psychosocial Recovery. - Nepal Earthquake
description: Beneficiaries: 500 Dalit and Janajati households in Nuwakot, and the surrounding schools. We will hold one to one family counselling and communication sessions, creative therapy classes within schools, and education (on reproductive health, human trafficking, nutrition and domestic violence.). This will create a platform to the affected to overcome their anxieties, and move forward to create a sustainable future for themselves.

title: Empower 100 displaced and victimized Women
description: This project will empower 100 women as leaders by promoting their fundamental rights and improving their quality of life  with human and psychological support that ultimately will lead them to participate in economic life. This year project will involve displaced, victimized by the conflict or violent victimized women who live in neighborhoods Patio Bonito and San Bernardino, urban neighborhoods in Bogota. Women here are facing serious vulnerabilities such lack of basic household services.

title: Ositeti School need a drinking water well!
description: This project will be used to help build a drinking water well in Ositeti School in Maasai Mara (Kenya) The "Amigos de Ositeti" ONGD is an organization dedicated to increasing services of the school, students and teachers. One of the most important things is to get drinking water for the community of this village. First, there were only 35 children in school but they are now than 400 and the build is very important for they.

title: Help 2500 Girls In Ghana at Risk of Child Marriage
description: This project is to send 2500 girls to school who are at risk of Child Early and Forced Marriage in Karaga District Ghana. Child marriage undermines a child's right to education and entrenches gender inequality. Ending child marriage will enable girls be in school to achieve their full potentials in life. It will reduce child mortality and improve maternal health since child brides are under social pressure to prove their fertility, thereby experiencing early pregnancies or death in childbirth

title: PsyCareMobile Clinic for 250 mentally ill in Togo
description: The PsyCareMobile (PCM) Clinic project will provide basic community mental health services and restore dignity for 250 mentally ill children and adults often  homeless, abused, shackled or abandoned by their relatives on streets or at psychiatric centers through an ambulatory service delivery system in Lome, Togo. Your donations will help provide a mentally ill with meals, medicine, psychotherapy, train grassroots-level mental health workers, raise awareness and support our providers.

title: Improve education of under-served Thai children
description: This project aims to increase quality of education for children attending underserved-childcare centres in rural communities & bordering province of Nong Khai, Northeast Thailand. We will provide teacher training for early childhood educators, many of whom have never had formal training. This project will affect 4000 children, 206 educators and their communities. Through training, study trips and community education we hope to reduce the gap in education quality between urban and rural centres.

title: Flying Free: Save the Amur Falcon
description: Every year, Amur falcons (Falco amurensis) fly 22,000 km from Mongolia to South Africa-the longest migration of any raptor. Nagaland in India is their last stop before a 3000 km-long flight across the Indian Ocean. The birds have traditionally been hunted in Nagaland during their roosting period, but last year, reports of mass killings caused consternation across the world. Addressing this issue, WTI has initiated activities involving local villagers to protect the falcons.

title: Free School meals for 554 Children in Spain
description: As a result of the economic crisis the number of children living below the poverty line has increased dramatically in Spain. Free School meals is a program that enables 554 children at social risk in Spain to have at least one meal at school with the necessary nutrients, improving their health and helping them to follow a normal life.

title: Support 169 families with terminally ill children
description: Because many palliative care needs are excluded from state healthcare or social programs in Russia, families with terminally ill children are left with no aid. Yet, it requires significant spendings to support a child with a genetic, neurological or other life-limiting condition. An average Russian family cannot afford to pay for what it takes to provide proper palliative care. Vera Hospice Charity fund has been providing these families with essentials for  years. We ask you to join us and help.

title: School Outreaches and Sensitization Project
description: School outreaches and  sensitization project aims at equipping  students in main stream primary and secondary schools with intellectual and practical skills. The project will be implemented through vocational clubs established in five schools. the students will then be trained in selected soft and hands on skills. Competitions will be held where the best vocational club and school will be rewarded. This acts as a motivation to other students hence  promotion of vocational education.

title: International Veterinary Outreach: Nicaragua
description: U.S. veterinary students & veterinarians, as well as Nicaraguan veterinary professionals, have come together to organize veterinary outreach clinics in underserved Northwest Nicaraguan communities and in the process, inform the public of proper health protocols, all while getting worthwhile experience in the field. We hope to grow as an organization and spread our outreach to other locations around the world.

title: Model School in Sundarban
description: Sabuj Sangha intended to ensure quality education of the underprivileged children in Sundarbans; .  The school is affiliated by the Government of West Bengal, but un-aided. Total 187 children are presently reading in pre-primary to upper primary classes up to class VIII and the students are taught by 13 teachers (male 8, female 5) . Proper teacher pupil ratio (1:25), Use of TLMs is aiming at creation of a positive fun that is imperative of modern scientific approach of joyful learning.

title: One Girl,One Pad, One sucess story at a time!
description: Mfariji Africa supports disadvantaged Kenyan girls to stay in school and finish their education through provision of  sanitary products,menstrual hygiene training and mentorship.

title: HELP TO CHANGE YOUR LIFE FOR A CHILD
description: This project benefits 50 children who come into our care after being abandoned by their parents or removed from their home due to neglect, abuse, or other forms of violence. Our project provides them with shelter in a family-like environment where we provide the children with holistic services including education, shelter, food, medical care, play time, and psychological help.

title: Community responses to mitigate child malnutrition
description: This project will train local self help group women in 100 North Karnataka villages to identify underweight children below 5 years and follow a 5 step tracking model to track and treat these children.  The 5 steps include referral for a health check up, micro nutrient supplementation, making and providing a high protein, high calorie ready to use mix ( using local ingredients) , intense one on one counselling of the mother on diet chart, personal hygiene and regular monitoring using growth chart

title: Support 50 Deprived families in Cholistan (Desert)
description: Technical education /skills are the only way to cope the mass problems of Poverty and Unemployment. In Distt. Bahawalpur, there is only 4 technical institute which is insufficient for this region. we are going to offer training at real work environment with full practical hands on experience. we will initially train only 50 females from rural areas. They will be able to get on hand experience and will be able to start their own small business to support their family financially.

title: Help Us Rebuild School Toilets In Baljevac, Serbia
description: Elementary school Josif Pancic in  a small mining town of Baljevac, in Central Serbia is attended by 210 pupils. The school is very old  and  In the worst condition are toilets throughout the building that need urgent reconstruction, because they are below minimum standards of use. It is necessary to replace toilets, tiles, sinks, lavatories, and painting. It is necessary to raise funds in a short term so that the school would be reconstructed before the beginning of the school year September 1.

title: Train 60 girls in computer coding in Afghanistan
description: 87% of Afghan women will experience gender-based violence. There are strong gender stereotypes that limit women's choices, both within the home and their communities. Girls Can Code raises the status of women in Afghanistan by giving them much sought-after skills in computer literacy, coding and English. We also secure internships for our students so they can gain invaluable work experience. With your support, we will train 60 young women in vocational skills and help transform their lives.

title: Help Homeless Women Get Back Into The Work-Place
description: 'Women into Work' is an employment, training and education programme to engage and support 110 previously homeless women living in London. Participants on the programme are seeking to secure employment, some for the very first time. The programme aims to train, support and guide them on their journey into the work-force.

title: Supporting 55 Saltpan Workers' Children Education
description: This Tuition centre aims to support education and protection of 55 semi-orphan saltpan workers' children. These centers provide Tuition, nutrias, uniform and recreation. The centre has 4 part time teachers cum care taker. The children are studying from Ist to VI th std and continue school going and their education progress are followed and reviewed. Monthly test and parents counseling are taken every month

title: Business empowerment for 20 women of Yucatan
description: With your support will be provided business training with the Emprende Workshop to 20 mayan women of Yucatan engaged in developing various crafts and office items with recycled materials. The training will be useful, to strengthen their value as a person and to recognize the skills and abilities as entrepreneurs who have to make the right products to market at a cost that will generate profits and especially to support sustainability environment.

title: Let us touch the sky - Dreams of sick children
description: This project will help sick children to take time out from hard Treatments and fulfill their dream of being once overseas Like a normal and healthy child .The average family cannot afford financially and medically to take a sick child for a vacation .The purpose of the project is to fund a vacation for children suffering from the disease, accompanied by medical staff and medical equipment that match their needs

title: Community Health Worker Program
description: Children with AIDS/TB-Treatment/Prevention. Since 2001 HOPE Cape Town has worked to reduce the AIDS/TB epidemic in the Western Cape region of South Africa through a multi-model approach involving Clinical, Social, Educational & Nutritional direct care service to infected children & their families.  25 Community Heath Workers provide counselling, facilitate access to healthcare, provide community support, assist with medical procedures, track patients, conduct home visits as 1st line of contact.

title: Sponsor a Young Person with Mental Health Issues
description: This project will provide free counselling, art and drama therapy, mentors and support groups to help young people with mental health issues to recover and have brighter futures. Children and young adults report a sense of hope for a positive future after coming to us; feeling less lonely, with greater confidence in themselves. We empower them to take control of their mental health and lives, and stop them becoming another tragic statistic.

title: Feed 500 Argentinean children for one year
description: Help children that suffer from hunger in Buenos Aires, Argentina. For every dollar you donate we will feed one children for a month. Our goal is to feed 500 children during one year ensuring nutritious meals to help them grow happy and healthy. Join us in our fight against hunger.

title: Give Light to Mothers Giving Birth in Darkness
description: Maternal mortality is the second leading cause of death of girls age 15-19. And preventable newborn deaths account for 44% of deaths in children under the age of five worldwide, resulting in 2.9 million lives each year.  In more places than you can imagine, mothers are giving birth to babies in darkness.  This contributes to high infant and maternal mortality rates in impoverished regions.  That's way we are doing everything we can to support infant and maternal health in Vietnam.

title: Emergency Support for Syrian Refugees in Serbia
description: Millions of people are leaving their homes on Middle East escaping from the war and disaster. They are travelling thousands of miles on their path to better life, and Serbia is one of the transit countries and last before they enter the EU. Since January 2015, over 100.000 forced migrants have entered Serbia. Throughout the country, families with their children spending days and nights on the open space, in the field, but soon coming the cold days, and that will not be possible any more.

title: Give Rescue Cats a Safe Future
description: Lanta Animal Welfare (LAW) in Thailand continues to work hard to relieve the suffering, trauma and pain of local animal populations. We have now outgrown the current cat house.  A new cat compound (see plans) and a 'meet and greet' area for visitors, and potential adopters is now essential.    A fun interactive education area is also needed for our Animal Welfare Education Program.  This will enable us to host more local kids and teach them to respect and understand animals and their needs.

title: Educate and empower children on online privacy
description: The internet offers children tremendous opportunities to learn and to explore new ideas. However, children's freedom to explore and develop should not be limited due to lack of awareness of  privacy-protecting strategies. We will develop a textbook to help kids both become more aware of risks and of tools for privacy protection as they explore and learn online. This represents a crucial step to help kids make safer and informed choices, what to share and how to share online.

title: Help Educate Poor Slum Children In India
description: AROH Foundation plans to improve learning outcomes of poor and underprivileged children in slums. These children suffer from extreme disparity and deprivation and are engaged in rag picking, waste picking or other small jobs. These children are not attending school regularly and are likely to drop out of school. The project aims to provide care and education facilities to 500 such children in the age group of 6-10 years and remove them from shackles of child labour and poverty.

title: Empower 50 Panamanian Youth through Education
description: Cambio Creativo provides academic reinforcement, leadership development, supplemental nutrition, and life skills to children from the underserved communities of Coco Solo and Buena Vista. We offer young students a safe public space where they can cultivate the skills and confidence to pursue higher education and gainful employment. Your donations provide students with after-school tutoring in math and literacy, creative educational experiences to develop critical thinking, as well as workshops.

title: Building Agribusinesses to end Poverty in DR Congo
description: Mavuno is now 100% locally led!  If you would still like to donate, you can now do so directly to the Congolese organization via the "Mavuno's American Friends Fund" through the King Baudouin Foundation - please donate here: https://kbfus.networkforgood.com/projects/53132-m-kbfus-funds-mavuno-dr

title: Micro-credits for Baru Island entrepreneurs
description: This project will give micro-credits to low income entrepreneurs of Baru Island, who have a business idea, experience in a activity and lack of financial support.  The project objectives are to 1) identify the young entrepreneurs and 2) provide them with technical and financial support (training and credit) to improve their business and increase their only source of income.

title: Help rescue wild animals and birds in India
description: The Mobile Veterinary Service (MVS) is one of Wildlife Trust of India's unique efforts to provide in- situ emergency relief to displaced or distressed wild animals.Animals can be displaced due to natural or man-made factors. Often, affected animals succumb to their situation due to inaccessibility and other challenges like getting trained wildlife professionals armed with essential equipment to the site of the emergency. Our MVS team works around the clock to rescue and treat these animals.

title: Teach the jury system to 7 million Filipinos
description: The Filipinos are unaware that there is an alternative to the Single-Judge system that has failed to enforce the country's laws .  The teaching of jury system to university students, who will pass on the knowledge they have gained in all of the 17 Regions of the country, will help empower the Filipinos in enforcing equal justice to all _ whether rich or poor Filipinos.

title: Save Sick, Injured and Abused Homeless Pets!
description: Animals often come into shelters suffering from severe illness or injury as a result of abuse or neglect. Thanks to the Petfinder Foundation's Emergency Medical Fund, these pets can get lifesaving care, stop suffering and find forever homes rather than being euthanized.

title: Hospice Care for the Terminally Ill
description: This project will provide home hospice care to 10 terminally ill patients in Nepal every month. Currently,  terminally ill patients in Nepal do not have an option to have hospice care at their homes. Only a couple of hospice care organizations in Nepal currently offer in-patient hospice care.  A large majority of terminally ill patients do not receive any kind of  end of life care. With this project, we will be able to provide peace, comfort, and dignity to the terminally ill patients.

title: Send A Disadvantaged Woman to Univ in Burkina Faso
description: Chance for Change works to help young women receive a secondary education in one of the world's poorest countries: Burkina Faso. Candidates for aid are proposed by local associations, and selected in consultation with university women's groups. The average grant is about $1,200, but every dollar makes a difference. A donation of just $25 can provide essential school supplies. Beneficiaries' families share in the financial burden to, along with CFC, provide these women with brighter futures.

title: Provide Rehab Care for Sea Turtles in Osa
description: This project aims to attend to 100% of green, hawksbill and olive ridley turtles that arrive at the rescue center with health problems or injuries by improving its facilities. With the necessary medical and technical equipment, sea turtles get the chance of rehabilitation and will be re-released into their natural environment after a successful treatment. Collected scientific data about health status and threats will improve long term conservation and survival of the endangered species.

title: Educate 250  students in northern Uganda
description: This project will build a biogas kitchen for the Children of Hope Uganda nursery school and vocational school in Barlonyo, northern Uganda, site of the Feb 21, 2004 massacre of 301 villagers by Joseph Kony's Lord's Resistance Army.

title: Support Children with Cancer & Blood Disorders
description: Each year, over 500 patients receive consultations and treatment during 8,000 visits to the Division of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology at New York-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center. Many of these patients are unable to afford costly medications and treatments not covered by insurance. Our project will help provide life-saving medication, treatments, and support for families who could otherwise not afford to do so.

title: Adopt-a-Rescuer!
description: EMPACT Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) Task Force is an all-volunteer, non-governmental team that provides specialized rescue and medical services after disasters. This includes locating and extricating victims and providing emergency treatment to those who have been trapped in collapsed structures, or otherwise affected by disaster. The team meets FEMA and UN training and equipment standards, and provides technically specialized response personnel to all who benefit in times of need.

title: Feed 4,500 children in 15 schools in Kilimanjaro
description: Over 4,500 school children will benefit from this initiative and over 10,700 community members will be provided with skills on modern farming.  By growing grain and vegetables on school farms, schools are able to provide lunch and improve the children's nutritional intake. Sustainable farming techniques are also taught to parents and the community, which are then applied in their own small farms.

title: Mental Health Services for Children in Kibera
description: Violence against children is a serious problem in Kenya today. Approximately one-third of children have experienced physical or sexual violence by the time they are 18. Despite the great need, due to funding limitations and capacity, counseling and support services are nearly non existent for children. This project will address this gap; providing routine, quality counseling services to 20 orphans and vulnerable children living in our rescue center in Kibera - one of Africa's largest slums

title: Ebola Orphans Aid
description: The Ebola virus has orphaned over 10,000 children in Sierra Leone, thereby causing a huge economic burden on the country. These orphans are in dare need of food, shelter, clothing, medical, psychological and other livelihood support and our organization is committed in providing such supports. Our ultimate goal is to help Ebola Orphans rise above stigma, marginalization, hunger and abuse.

title: "The Lucky Specials": Helping People Respond to TB
description: Tuberculosis (TB) is now on par with HIV/AIDS as the greatest killer worldwide due to a single infectious agent (World Health Organization). To address this health epidemic, Discovery Learning Alliance is creating "Inside TB," a film for audiences across sub-Saharan Africa addressing how TB works.

title: Assistive Technology Program at Al Noor
description: The Assistive Technology program at the Centre was recently implemented to enhance the quality of life of children with Special Needs in the UAE. Assistive technology, often abbreviated as AT is any piece of equipment or product system that is used to maintain, or improve the functional capabilities of individuals with disabilities. In alignment with our Mission, it is important for the Centre to deploy such enabling technologies that allow all our students to realize their full potential.

title: Home for 50 Challenged Girls in Bangalore, India
description: Margadarshi is providing Home, with all amenities for 50 neglected girls with disability hailing from the poorest sections of society in Bangalore, India.  These girls are are capable of leading their own own life, as every disability is just physical and it is their Mental Ability is what counts.  With proper and timely support these 50 girls with disability will be empowered to lead independent life socially and financially. Margadarshi helps them to achieve this.

title: Live&Learn in Kenya School Classroom Construction
description: We are building a high standard education center in the slums of Nakuru, Kenya so that through free, high-quality education very needy children will be able to break out of the vicious circle of extreme poverty from the young age of 3. We are presently constructing a library, medical/dental clinic and LLK/social service offices and finishing the kindergarten construction. Our next endeavor is building a vocational training school with training rooms for hairdressing, car mechanics and tailoring.

title: Support 32 burned Children in Mongolia
description: Every year, more than 5,000 people are suffering from forest fire or stove or hot water since there are cold and dry weather in Mongolia. Most of them are children so under this project, we will support about 30 burned children in Mongolia by the services such as medical fees, emergency medical treatment, ointment, and especially skin graft surgery.

title: Raising Boys to uphold Women's right to safety
description: Men Against Violence & Abuse (MAVA) is India's first voluntary organization engaging Boys and Men to stop and prevent gender-based violence against women and advocate for a gender-equal society. At Project Umang (meaning Aspiration), MAVA is sensitizing and mentoring 45 adolescent boys, from 3 disadvantaged communities of Mumbai, who are aspiring for a society where girls / women are not subjected to any kind of violence or where girls / women do not live in fear of violence.

title: Educational Center to Empower 500 Rural Ugandans
description: This project provides educational and economic opportunities that will empower a vulnerable community. In the rural Iganga District, the poverty rate is twice the national average, 40% of people lack access to clean and safe water and 80% rely on subsistence farming.  S.O.U.L. is building an Educational Center to expand its successful Student Sponsorship, Mentorship, and Technology Programs, Women's Empowerment/Agriculture Cooperatives, and Maternal Health Network, impacting 500 Ugandans weekly.

title: Myanmar Flood Relief
description: Save the Children has been working in Myanmar since 1995 and is well-positioned for a response. We have ongoing programs in the Chin, Magway and Takhine states, expert staff and pre-positioned stocks of relief materials already in the country.

title: School bus for Umoja students
description: Umoja provides education and well-being support for vulnerable young Tanzanians. We need a school bus to get our children to and from school every day, for school trips, transporting donations or purchases of educational supplies and more!

title: Addison Pediatric Transplant Research Project
description: Organ transplantation is an incredible second chance at life, but it isn't a cure. Children face many challenges because they have an entire lifetime ahead of them, yet much of their care is based upon clinical trials and studies conducted on adults. The goal of the Addison Pediatric Research Project is to ensure pediatric transplant recipients have a long and healthy life by funding research focused on the unique and challenging issues facing children who require organ transplants.

title: Hong Kong Pride Parade
description: The Hong Kong Pride Parade promotes equal rights for and anti-discrimination against the LGBT community. By showing the different faces of our community, it facilitates respect for diversity in the society. We host the annual parade in the busiest streets of Hong Kong, along with mass assemblies at both the commencement and conclusion venues of the parade. This parade is the largest event in Hong Kong advocating for equal rights for the LGBT community.

title: Nonprofit Grocery Store Startup
description: More than enough food is produced each year to end world hunger however as of 2012 according to the USDA, 17% of U.S. households were food "insecure" which means that they occasionally run out of money for food or food entirely.  By opening a nonprofit grocery store in partnership with businesses, healthcare, higher education, government programs and other nonprofit organizations; we can create a framework to end food inequality that can be scaled to address this global problem.

title: Send girls to school in Ethiopia
description: This project will send adolescent girls from very poor families to school and provide them with supplemental nutrition.  These girls, whose families earn less than $2 a day, cannot afford the mandatory public school uniform and materials. Without an education, they will repeat the cycle of poverty. By sending them to school -- and away from child marriage, poverty, trafficking and gender-based violence -- we're creating a safe passage from childhood to adulthood for a group of girls in Ethiopia.

title: Click for the dreams of 100Colombian Entrepreneurs
description: Clicks for dreams will provide income generation opportunities to 100 entrepreneurs living in vulnerable situations and victims of the armed conflict in Colombia through the creation and strengthening of their small businesses.

title: Thailand's "Flying Library" for over 500 children
description: The growing construction sector in Thailand is bringing many migrant families from Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos.  Children from these communities grow up in precarious and isolated construction areas with no access to education. Kids Home Foundation's Flying library brings reading sessions directly into these communities. Our library not only improves literacy and expands children's knowledge, but it also facilitates and encourages school registration playing a key role in children's development.

title: Build Centre for disabled children in Uganda
description: The Special Children's Trust  aims to build a One Stop Centre for children with special needs in Kampala, Uganda, including a school, therapy, sensory and play centre. We aim to provide services in inclusive and special education, Physio, Occupational, Speech Therapy and assessments, sensory play, outdoor activities, teacher/therapy training and awareness building to reduce stigma and provide a place for children with special needs and those without to have fun, learn and flourish together.

title: Flood relief for displaced communities in Myanmar
description: This project will provide food/non food items distributions and other forms of emergency relief for displaced communities in Myanmar's flood-hit Rakhine, Magway, Sagaing, Mandalay, and Chin states.

title: Bus for 83 children in Guatemala with disabilities
description: Our project will provide the possibility for 83 children with disabilities in Santiago Atitlan and Cerro de Oro to attend our school, Escuela de Educacion Especial, and get the treatments and medicines necessary. The shuttle bus will provide secure transportation to and from school every day and to the necessary medical appointments in Guatemala City every other week. The shuttle bus will be adapted to the special needs of the children which is crucial for them.

title: Sexual Assault Crisis Response for Ugandan Orphans
description: The Nyaka AIDS Orphans Project uses education and empowerment to help HIV/AIDS Orphans escape poverty. After a 9-year-old student at one of Nyaka's schools was raped by a 35-year-old man, the organization mobilized to protect the children of Uganda. This project will work to increase understanding about sexual assault among students and community members, influence attitudes about sexual assault, and work with local authorities to get justice for sexual assault survivors.

title: Transforming People With Disabilities in India
description: You can empower youth, 18-24 years old, with disabilities to learn computer skills so they can get a job or start a business in India. This project will equip about 28 students with disabilities with computer skills each year. The education you provide will give young people with disabilities the opportunity to succeed in a career in the IT field, support their families, and create a strong sense of self-worth.

title: Evidence for Child Health - Podcasts for Parents
description: As a parent you  want to make the best decisions about your child's health, but there is so much information and it can be confusing.   Your donation will help improve children's health and empower parents to make sense of information about common childhood illnesses. Your support will result in a series of high quality Podcasts, created by Cochrane Child Health intended to support families to understand and make informed decisions about children's health.

title: Food for 500 children in our art camps in India
description: Kanavupattarai (Workshop of Dreams in Tamil) is a 3 days residential art camp organized for adolescent children suffering from depression and disruptive behaviour. A combination of theatre activities , creative games, sand therapy, yoga, dance, music and peer-to-peer conversations are used to bring about behavioural changes. We need your financial support in providing food and refreshments for the children.

title: Sensory Garden for Disabled Children in Thailand
description: In Thailand over 2milion people are living with a disability. Despite Thailand's progressive laws encouraging access to education the reality is very different. In many cases the stigma associated with disability leads many to being abandoned or confined to a world of social isolation in their own homes.  CCD's  aim to eliminate this injustice by providing day care services which are educational, therapeutic & fun. Enabling disabled children to achieve their potential and integrate into society.

title: Life-Saving Treatment for Kids in Ukraine
description: Childhood cancer is not a death sentence. In Ukraine, 1000 kids are diagnosed with cancer every year. 7000 kids are hospitalized annually, including new patients, those continuing treatment, and those experiencing a recurrence. Their chances for survival depend on the availability of medication, facilities, and emotional support. Zaporuka's project provides these kids with necessary treatment (medicines, rehabilitation, and equipment), and relief (psychological support and leisure activities).

title: Bringing Baltimore Girls and Their Moms Together
description: The Girl Scouts Beyond Bars Program gives daughters of incarcerated mothers access to community activities that foster team-building and healthy decision making skills.  GSCM provides regular Girl Scout troop meetings with their moms at Maryland Correctional Institute for Women, an annual sleep-over, educational sessions to build self-esteem and empower them to reach their full potential.  Girl Scouts of Central Maryland operates the first and longest running Beyond Bars program in the nation.

title: CREATE A YOUTH-SPACE FOR SLUM DWELLERS IN ABUJA
description: The Project will Create a youth space(The HUB) in Mabushi where 200 underserved youths from Mabushi Village, and other urban slums in Abuja will be trained in computer and entrepreneurial skills with a focus on digital Jobs.

title: Help American LGBTQ Victims of Violence Overseas
description: This project will enable us to provide 24/7/365 support to LGBTQ Americans who have experienced violence in foreign countries including sexual assault, domestic violence and targeted hate crimes. Support includes funds for emergency needs, transportation expenses, medical expenses, counseling and legal support.

title: After the Earthquake: Rebuilding 5000 lives
description: Magnitude 7.9 earthquake left Nepal devastated with millions homeless and uprooted from their lives. The scale of devastation is beyond Nepal government's ability to lift people out of crisis. This project will support building of resilient houses and providing livelihood training and support for 1292 households in 3 VDCs in severely affected districts of Nuwakot and Sindhupalchowk. Support BPW in working with local women's Coop's and technical organization to help Nepali's rise to independence.

title: Help 2000 students from US & Japan connect online!
description: Traditional foreign language learning that lacks opportunities for communication with foreigners and the prohibitive cost of international travel continues to limit students' ability to engage in international exchange. Our Global Classmates program connects thousands of high school students in the U.S. and Japan online for a language and cultural exchange and turns them into lifetime cultural explorers who not only strengthen ties between the U.S. and Japan, but solve global issues together.

title: Educate Nigerian girls for one year
description: This project will provide a one year sponsorship for 20 school girls in Nigeria who are at-risk of dropping out.  With your donation, 20 vulnerable girls would be able to stay and succeed in school and beyond. GEM will provide Scholarship  fund, school supplies and sanitary pads to 20 girls from the northern Nigeria. GEM plans to further enhance awareness and mobilize broad support towards the education of girls by advocating with parents, schools, community members and local leaders

title: Chiguru - a cultural event for the underprivileged
description: "Chiguru", in the regional language Kannada, means "budding", and the project aims at providing a platform for the budding future citizens to showcase their cultural talents. Over a 3000 children from government and informal schools across Bangalore (India) will participate in various traditional/cultural events. It helps facilitate the all-round and holistic development of underprivileged children and also kindles interest in volunteers from the community to engage with these children.

title: Provide Education for Underprivileged Children
description: SHARE NGO, Nonprofit Organization was formed to help underprivileged children. Children are entitled to a free, quality basic education. Recognizing this entitlement, world leaders made the achievement of universal primary education by the year 2015 one of the Millennium Development Goals. In 2004, this goal appears to be out of reach for many poor countries. School attendance, especially for girls, is far from universal,many children drop out of school before completing their primary education.

title: Provide Clean Water for Amazon Youth Livelihoods
description: The Rural Family Home (CFR) is a three-year vocational program for rural youth in the Brazilian Amazon that offers them opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods in their home communities rather than having to migrate to cities. To realize its potential and to become fully sustainable, the CFR needs improved facilities, particularly access to clean drinking water. The addition of an well, which students will help to design and to construct, will enable the CFR to thrive for years to come.

title: Provide Nutrition for Poor People in Mexico
description: Why do people have to die of hunger while in the same state a lot of food is disposed by supermarkets, production facilities and restaurants because the demand on certain products was not as high as calculated? We,  the Food Bank in Merida (Banco de Alimentos de Merida A.C.), give the mentioned facilities a break to donate these products and by distributing them we can contribute to decrease the amount of starving people in the Yucatan.

title: Academic schooling in a refugee camp in Kenya.
description: This project provides access to a Bachelors degree through an online program for eligible refugees from Kakuma refugee camp and members of the Kenyans from the underdeveloped community adjacent to the camp located in northwestern Kenya.  The first and current cohort is made up of 17 students, who are registered to two majors- Business Administration and Computer Science. Upon finishing their studies, the students will acquire a B.A or an associate degree in their fields.

title: Train 20 Vulnerable Bulgarians in Entrepreneurship
description: This project will help break the cycle of poverty and boost economic development in Bulgaria by providing aspiring entrepreneurs from socially vulnerable background with business management training and financial assistance to start and grow their small businesses in the least developed and socially challenged areas.

title: Send 25 multidisabled students to school in Chile
description: This project is focused on helping the blind and multi-disabled children by providing them with an education. We are focusing our efforts on raising money to purchase a minibus as many of the students live far from the school and their families can't afford to take them to this special needs school. Without this bus children will stay at home. Every child deserves the right to an educationI and this project will focus on those who need specialized education that they can't get anywhere else.

title: #ProjectBaon: School Meals for Filipino Kids!
description: "Baon" is a Filipino word for packed meals prepared by parents for their kids going to school.  Sadly 1 out of 3 kids in the Philippines don't get the food they need every day.Since learning depends on good nutrition,these kids may never reach the same potential for learning as well-nourished kids. Since 2015, #ProjectBaon has been providing healthy "baon"- packed lunch & snacks  to kids who has no access to nutritious meals and are living in  poor communities in the Philippines.

title: Rebuild orphanage for 20 Colombian girls
description: This project seeks to remodel the bathrooms and buy new dining room furniture and computers for an orphanage in Antioquia, Colombia. The Orphanage provides education, food, shelter and love to orphaned girls. Your support will allow us to improve living conditions in the orphanage to provide the girls with a dignified life. Thank you for believing we can change the world together. Every gift makes a difference

title: "Children education in the prostitution zone"
description: Bandar Baru is a village consisting of a large number of brothels and (nobody knows since when) has gained the dubious title as a "commercial sex zone". We have decided to rent some land and set up a Slow Loris rehabilitation center, and also an educational site and a mini library for the kids.

title: Don't Spoil My Future:End Early Marrige Now in S.O
description: In  South Omo Zone is the top prone area where Early Marriage (South Omo Zone WCYAs, 2015). The percentage occurrence of Early Marriage is the highest in the Zone which is 11.2%. Low educational background,low awareness, interference of community leaders, Social Norms, Isolation of the community from outside world and loose coordinated system are the factors. Thus, this project will establish network and referral  linkage, create awareness, facilitate legal protection and rehabilitation ofvictim

title: Help 2000 children with congenital heart defects
description: We are aiming to provide patients of Kyiv Children's Cardiac Center with an opportunity to undergo surgery and live a full life after their congenital heart defects have been cured.  For this purpose, we want to fix an expensive and extremely important ultrasonic machine that has failed to function.  Doctors use it for carrying out more than 2000 operations a year.  We are collecting money to buy a new motherboard and replace the broken one.

title: Transport disabled children to school
description: We will buy a new minibus to transport disabled children to special schools in Eastern Hungary. We already have a running transport service with experienced specialists.

title: Support a patient Save a Life !
description: Support a Patient Save a life.. is an initiative by RVM Foundation a unit of FOSA Humanitarian Hospital that encourages the helping hands in our society to support a poor patient by aiding their basic and medical needs.  RVM Foundation believes and promotes the idea that positive community support is essential to realize its vision of "Reducing Pain and Suffering". Hence, we seek and welcome financial and non-financial support from individuals, corporates & institutions to take forward our work

title: Earthquake;Encouraging Miyagi by a community space
description: This project aims to promote to exchange people all over Japan by offering lodging facilities and community space in Active Life YADO that we has built. (http://www.globalgiving.org/projects/build-ishinomaki-multi-purpose-recovery-base-project/)  A mental care of an earthquake victims is still needed. We are going to support them with local people by a community-rooted way.

title: Permaculture Teacher Training in East Africa
description: PRI-Kenya offers a professional and comprehensive education programme in permaculture design and related subjects. Our Teacher Training provides skills in teaching permaculture for those who have already completed their PDC and who already have some experience implementing permaculture. As part of our TOT and together with International Permaculture facilitators, we focus on giving students an in-depth insight into the permaculture design process alongside.

title: Poverty Alleviation1080Internally Displaced People
description: The Project will take place  outskirt of Mogadishu-Somalia where most vulnerable Internally Displaced . This project will Support 1080 IDPs (180 HH) through engagement of Micro Enterprises per family entrepreneurs .They will provide Business Training skills The grants will be given  First Installment USD$ 150 as start-up Micro enterprise per IDPs family Each IDP Family Enterprise  must reinvest 20% in their business in  4 Months After  4 months of profitable enterprises will be provided USD $150

title: Educating the Thabang Children
description: Our children come from rural,  very poor and abusive backgrounds. With your aid we provide a safe haven, send them to school and empower them with life and vocational skills to become independent citizens and future role models for the South African community. Through a Child & Youth Care Centre and a Drop in Centre, we directly support about 100 vulnerable children as identified through the Social Welfare. Indirectly we impact at least 500 needy people, the majority being children.

title: Sponsor school uniforms for visually challenged
description: This project helps provide new uniforms and new sandals for our 120 visually challenged beneficiaries from rural areas. They are all between the age groups of 12- 20 years. This project aims to help students pursuing grade 6-12. Through this project, each visually challenged student will be able to get the pleasure of having their own set of uniforms and sandals.

title: Save lives of family violence victims in Serbia
description: This project will provide free legal aid to the victims of family violence considering that researches show that legal aid to victims is the most influential support service in lowering the rate of domestic violence. Considering that our or organization has established network of lawyers in Serbia and has provided this kind of support this is proven to be effective. In addition, our organization will continue to to save lives by sheltering women and children that are escaping for severe violence

title: Surgery help for 35 hurt homeless dogs in Pernik
description: The project will help 35 injured homeless dogs in Pernik which have been hurt by car accidents or domestic violence. Animals need scanner, blood tests and surgery to solve their problem and ensure independent life and a second chance to find a new and caring family. Thus we show humane attitude and remove from streets and playgrounds the heartbreaking view of cripple animals scaring everyone. The improved healthy status of the dogs can give them a new life and owners to love and care about them.

title: Eastern Ukraine Relief & Emergency Kids Aid Appeal
description: The violent armed conflict in Ukraine continues not intermittently but constantly. This has, and is, having a devastating impact on the country and on children and families. The economic situation is dire with Ukrainians 20% poorer now than they were at the end of the Soviet Union era. Inflation has reached 45% and the local currency has plummeted. The war in the provinces of Donetsk and Luhansk in the east of the country has compounded an already fragile situation.

title: Yearly camps for 80 children with cancer age 6-18
description: We provide children an environment that normalizes relationships and experiences, helping them in the healing process and enhancing their quality of life. We give them the opportunity to share experiences & feelings, see new challenges & push their limits & cope with their circumstances in a positive way. They grow, support and challenge each other. The stories children share are emotional and special: 'Half a word is enough', 'Everything is possible', 'Everybody accepts me as I am.'

title: Life skill training of 350 girls in Madurai slums
description: The project will develop and enhance life skills of 100 poor girls in slum areas of madurai  by creating opportunities for improving status of health and, education. 200 more will be reached and motivated by fairs, discussions and other events. 5 Girls' resource centers will provide safe spaces to provide training in skills and help them organize to become change agents. Mobile library, workshops, educational visits and health camps will lead to their capacity building

title: Help 500 at risk youth receive education & mentors
description: Centro Conviven promotes the social, cultural and educational development of at risk children from the slums of Buenos Aires, Argentina. We want to provide a physical and mental safe place to approx 500 youth of this community by providing educational, artistic and extra curricular workshops. The educational workshops are developed to strengthen the self-esteem of the children and give them the tools to prosper through art, sports, technology, science & math..cementing & enriching their futures.

title: Empower youth through technology in Costa Rica
description: Collaborate with us for social innovation in Costa Rica. Empower youth. Promote the integration of education and technology. Encourage entrepreneurship. Put your Ideas into Action. | Colabora con nosotros por la innovacion social en Costa Rica.  Empoderamos a los jovenes. Promovemos la integracion de educacion y tecnologia. Fomentamos el emprendimiento. Solo la idea de hacer una diferencia no es suficiente. Es hora de poner las Ideas en Accion.

title: 'After the Quake' work for CORE
description: CORE has had ongoing programs in Nepal since 2006. We are focusing on longer-term activities to enable the survivors of the powerful earthquake on April 15, 2015 to recover from the damage to their homes, well-being, and livelihoods.  CORE provides support to rural communities in Dolakha district, literacy for women in IDP camps, and our ongoing work with non-formal education and micro-finance for urban migrants and the very poor in Kathmandu and rural communities in the valley.

title: Empower 50 Survivors of Sex Trafficking in Rwanda
description: This project will provide short-term room and board, emergency healthcare, counseling, advocacy, and financial aid to 50 girls and women victims of sex trafficking in Kigali, Rwanda. The project will help to transition these girls and women from their past life of controlled abuse to stable independence.

title: Promoting non-violence with 200 Brazilian families
description: The objectives of this project are:to provide physical,psychological and social monitoring to children,adolescents,women and families in a disadvantaged community in Northeast Brazil;to supply or supplement the necessary assistance that these victims need using integrated therapies with a focus on education, prevention and self-care;to educate and promote a culture of peace and attitudes based on non-violence and human rights through parades for peace and talks on self-care and access to justice

title: Antibiotics for 300 Very Sick and Needy Cambodians
description: You can provide life-saving, powerful antibiotic medication for at least 300 people a year. Impoverished people come to Sihanouk Hospital Center of HOPE with complex, drug-resistant infections that require hospitalization and rigorous medical treatment. Patients are admitted after seeking unsuccessful treatment from drug sellers and suffering from symptoms for a long time. Their infections are severe and require laboratory testing and appropriate medication. Your gift saves lives.

title: Support 100 children to sit and stand
description: More than 15% of children in India experience Developmental Delay.  They do not get the appropriate developmental aids, due to lack of awareness and the financial hardship.    Mobility India provides assistive devices like Ankle-Foot Orthosis, Standing Frame, Sitting chair, Corner seat to aid the child to have enough freedom to move, explore, walk and have the correct  feet posture.

title: Empower Marginalized Women to make it on their own
description: This project is enabling marginalized young women from multi-ethnic communities in Sandzak and South of Serbia to get education in IT. Obtained skills will empower these woman  to get employment, start their own businesses and set an example that women can be leaders in communities.

title: Free education for 60 deprived children in Peru
description: Picaflor House is a community project in the village of Oropesa, in a deprived area of the Peruvian Andes near Cusco. Although millions of tourist dollars flood into Peru every year very little reaches remote villages of the region. Here, the poorest children would normally be destined for a lifetime of poverty and hardship. While villagers work hard to feed and clothe their children, we provide a safe space for children to play and free education to help them break out of the cycle of poverty.

title: Help Children from Ukrainian East
description: This project will launch a database of children (age: 0-18), who have lost father/mother or both in ATO, who are forcibly displaced or suffer from ATO in any other way. Children of the project (for a present moment 55 children) will undergo free psycological and social rehabilitation, will receive free legal aid from the Center of Social and Legal Aid to ATO Participants. Main aim of the project: integrationof the family abroad with the family, who has suffered from ATO.

title: Stop Violence Against Women's in India
description: 27,933 cases Approx of violence against women are registered in police station yearly in Rajasthan,  The main objective of this project is to bring gender equality within the male dominated society, respect for women, end social malpractices, decrease in dowry system, END child Marriage and women should also have equal rights in society.

title: 1800 young in Medellin sensitized to HIV: a hope
description: The purpose is to reduce HIV infections and improve the acceptance of infected people, decreasing stigma. We intend to: 1. build an artistic exhibition with educational content, collecting expectations of the youth and transmit the experience of infected adolescents, promoting adoption of healthy lifestyles; 2. lead a campaign with pedagogical elements on the importance of self-care; 3. carry out educational actions to strengthen the ability of youngs to make responsible / autonomous decisions

title: Help provide urgent surgical care in rural Haiti
description: St. Boniface Haiti Foundation is establishing a surgical program that will set a new standard of surgical care for Haiti's South. On the southern peninsula of Haiti, home to two million people, too many have no access to life-saving surgical services. SBHF is committed to providing safe, quality healthcare to the most vulnerable, and this includes providing increased access to surgical services. SBHF aims to provide high quality health and surgical care for all, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Give Support to Orphaned School Children -Uganda
description: About 60% of all children in rural  Pallisa are vulnerable and out of these, 20% are moderately vulnerable while 40% are critically vulnerable. Some of the reasons that expose children to vulnerabilities include poverty, HIV/ AIDS, inadequate social welfare and ineffective implementation of the existing laws as well as high population growth rate.

title: Teenage Pregnancy & Girls' Education Access_Malawi
description: This project will recruit, train 300 teenage pregnant mothers over 3 yr period become peer educators for 20 rural schools reaching 6705 girls,  the 300 girls will be encouraged to return to school after first delivery to reduce teenage pregnancy, increase girls' education access, reducing literacy gap between boys and girls in Malawi. The project will also help to change social/cultural values in community and schools to support girls' return to school through active community engagement.

title: Restore 10 water springs for 7500 Kasese villagers
description: Africa Community Connect plans to construct 10 water springs to provide free and clean water for women, children and youth who hail from the poorest & isolated sub county of Kitholhu Uganda; also training girls about sanitation and Hygiene skills.

title: Send a street kid to school in Nigeria for a year
description: Home and Street Kids Welfare Initiative plans to build five classrooms to provide free education for the street kids who hail from the poorest sections of society in Kwara State Nigeria, also providing the kids free meals. This project runs a free school in Ilorin, Kwara State for the used to be street kids, providing a one on one structured learning to 32 street kids both from Nigeria, Niger Republic and Mali.

title: Inclusive fitness for people with Spina Bifida
description: The implementation of this project will allow the integral development of people with spina bifida of the Monica Uribe Por Amor Foundation. Spina bifida is a disability that affects the musculoskeletal system, so these people need a tailored fitness. We will build an inclusive gym adapted to the needs of this people. .It will enable significant progress in the following areas: development of motor skills, health promotion, acquisition of healthy habits and behaviors and self-care.

title: 30 Children need a home in Colombia, help us!!!
description: The project will provide a shelter for 30 girls at high social risk in Medellin, Colombia.

title: Teach 250 Students Farming Skills in South Sudan
description: The food crisis in South Sudan has resulted in millions experiencing acute malnutrition. By teaching farm management, students at Abukloi School in Rumbek, Lakes State are learning the skills to plan for, grow, harvest, manage and market crops to feed hundreds of people and earn income to support their school. Our rapidly growing secondary school of 250 students has land to expand the farm program to further develop this self-sustaining program and end the cycle of malnutrition.

title: Vocational skills for 24 orphans in DR Congo
description: The project will support 24 orphan girls and teenage mothers in DR Congo to uplift their social and economic status and achieve a financial stability in their care-families. The project will provide a 6 months  training in tailoring, in addition to the nation of small business management, self-employement and entrepreneurial concepts. We will guide trainees to form 4 groups of 6 girls each, develop business plans and give each group 3 sewing machines as kits to start up their own business.

title: Fund 1000 Scholarships in Rural China for a Year
description: Some 200 million rural Chinese live below the poverty line by the World Bank definition of $1.25 per day, implying that 40 million school-aged children are at risk of dropping out of school before their high school graduation. In order to combat this huge waste of human capital, the SOAR Foundation, for the past 25 years, has provided 30,600 merit-based scholarships to more than 13,000 impoverished yet gifted students across rural China to finish high school and achieve success thereafter.

title: Skills Training for 300 Out-of-School Youth
description: The project will train 300 out-of-school youth who are sons and daughters of the sugarcane labourers in Silay City, Negros Occidental, Philippines. These youth ages 20 to 27 years old are always sourced of family and community problems since most of them are idle, low educational background, juvenile delinquency and unemployed. Based on the study of SIMAG, these youth are very eager to acquire vocational skills that they can use for their employment and liberate them from the bondage of poverty.

title: Add Marrow Donors: Eliminate Leukemia Worldwide
description: In thousands of cases marrow transplantation from an unrelated donor is the only way to save lives of patients, in particular, kids and teenagers, who suffer from leukemia and other deadly blood diseases. The main goal of the Karelian Registry is to dramatically increase the number of bone marrow donors in Russia.  Funds raised through this project will allow us to add 2500 more donors in the Registry. Our mission is to give hope!

title: Art & Dance lessons for 300 Children in Cambodia
description: Epic Arts is an inclusive arts organization based in Cambodia. We use the power of the arts to bring together people with & without disabilities. "Creative Schools Cambodia" is an ambitious new creative learning initiative that aims to change attitudes and inspire creativity amongst the next generation of Cambodians by connecting young children and disabled artists through a structured program of arts activities in schools.

title: Sight for the poor- restoring sight, change lives
description: We believe that sight is priceless and we want to deliver good eye care to 500 less privileged  and needy members of the community in Ajegunle, Lagos. It is a known fact that blindness is an important cause and effect of poverty. The project goal is to work with poor and marginalized communities to ensure that People do not go blind unnecessarily. "Sight for the poor project" will ensure that we prevent, treat and cure avoidable blindness and promote eye health.

title: The kids kitchen: daily meals in the wake of Ebola
description: The project will build a small kitchen to provide daily meals to the children of the We Are the Future kindergarten and primary school in Freetown, Sierra Leone. These children come from poor fishing communities where families have lost most of their income due to the Ebola outbreak that has devastated the country and its economy.

title: Help Ksenia and 11 children with rare skin disease
description: Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB) is a rare inherited connective tissue disorder that affects 1 child out of every 20.000 births. It seriously affects skin, internal organs and bodily systems. It is incurable, but proper medical care may significantly reduce the risks of complications and prolong the life of those, suffering from EB. This project aims to support 12 children in Belarus with severe form of the disease to purchase necessary lifesaving medical supplies.

title: Help 40 Women in Nigeria build small businesses
description: This project will train 40 women doing small businesses in a rural community in Nigeria, providing micro loans to expand their existing businesses as well as business mentoring and business linkages.

title: Provide  Education to 143 Vulnerable Children
description: The percentage of vulnerable children in Hoima district is 42.5%. Buhimba Child Care Initiative provides education to 143 children in Buhimba Hope Academy of this category who lack basic scholastic materials and school fees. Classroom space is also limited due to increasing numbers. Help us construct one classroom block and to pay for school fees and scholastic materials so that these needy children can remain in school. One dollar makes a big, big distinction!

title: Bathroom facility for disabled children in Moldova
description: Steaua Calauza NGO for Children with Disabilities aims to support the disabled children and families throughout the Gratiesti town, Republic of Moldova and to facilitate access to therapy, recovery and treatment methods appropriate for the disabled. The local administration gave Steaua Calauza a facility that does not provide adequate sanitation facility for disabled children. The objective is to provide Steaua Calauza an adequate, disabled accessible and safe bathroom with flush toilets.

title: Join Hands to promote Physically Disabled Cricket
description: Pakistan Cricket Association for the Physically Handicapped is well on its way to bringing back the Physically Disabled people in the main stream of life as they are neglected physically, and emotionally.  Most are reduced to a life of begging because they are seen as useless. Our main mission is to act and promote Cricket Activities between Physically handicapped to boost their morale.  In this regard we are organizing Cricket Event in Pakistan for the betterment of this neglected Society.

title: Give Health care to 65 Disabled Children in Uganda
description: This project will provide health care to children with Special Needs. This health care support will be done in collaboration with the SEBBI MEDICAL CENTER which is a geographically nearby health clinic with the organization. The project will provide primary health care to children with Special Needs to attain better health services through promoting health and preventing illness.

title: 2000 ear test to Colombian children of low income
description: Help us to make 2000 ear tests to Colombian children with low income; in order to we detect hearing loss at an early age. If a hearing loss is detected and treated early, people can improve their language, communication and social skills, to make them productive citizens in society.  The Oyeme Foundation will guide children and their families to improve their quality of life.

title: A seat at the table for 80 producers in Swaziland
description: This project will gather 80 Fairtrade small producer organizations and workers from the Southern Africa region, Madagascar, Comoros and Mauritius in celebrating 10 years of producer empowerment and Fairtrade impact. Producers will share their experiences and receive training on governance, business management, Leadership and Advocacy to enable them increase their levels of participation, collectively advocate and influence decisions, improve and strengthen their functioning as businesses

title: Support the flood relief efforts in Argentina
description: Earlier this month unseasonal torrential rain across the Buenos Aires region has caused several rivers to flood their banks, leaving severe damage to homes and belongings. It has also lead to the evacuation of thousands from those areas most affected - Lujan, Salto, Areco and Mercedes.

title: Over 500 Children's Lives Changed in Colombia
description: Beisboleritos (little baseballers) began in Medellin in 2009 as an initiative to counter the presence of illegal groups affecting children and adolescents in Colombia. These children become a target for illegal armed groups (guerrilla) through armed recruitment, making them child soldiers. Beisboleritos works in highly vulnerable communities to help children and adolescents develop and strengthen skills to resist and assertively respond to these threats. Info: info@gipcolombia.org

title: SUPPORT SPECIAL NEEDS SCHOOL BUILDING PROJECT
description: Each youngster deserves a normal childhood- a chance to dig in the dirt, to sing off key, to explore the world, and to discover new things along the way. The lives of certain children by virtue of illness or disorder are anything but normal. Sadly, these youngsters are suffering physically and emotionally not only from coping with the treatment necessary to sustain life, but also from coping with the loss of their childhood. First Intervention Ghana provides a befitting environmental experience

title: Strengthen WASH in schools in rural Liberia
description: FACE Africa is conducting a WASH in Schools program to improve the future of children in remote Rivercess County, Liberia. Strengthening WASH provision in schools is a key first step to recovery from Ebola. By expanding our safe water point and sanitation network to schools across the county, and by providing comprehensive hygiene training and education, we can keep children safe and healthy so that they can learn, grow and prosper as part of resilient communities.

title: Send More Girls to School!
description: 49.8% of Turkey's population constitutes of female population.  While the numbers of women who receive education have increased in recent years, the proportion of female illiteracy is higher when compared to male illiteracy.  As for high school graduates and equivalency, the number of females who are high school graduates constitutes a mere 14.4%.    TPF plans to send more girls to high school and make the greatest impact in lives of many young women by providing them with scholarships.

title: Healthcare Training for 15 Underserved Youth in NY
description: This project will fund a Health Care initiative program for 15 low-income students, enabling them to obtain training for a career in healthcare. Students will start by pursuing Basic Life Support (BLS) certification with the American Heart Association. The students will then have a year of lectures, lab exposure, and weekly clinical volunteer experience. The program then culminates with students picking one of two capstone projects: EMT certification or a research assistantship.

title: Reusable Sanitary Pads Dignity for School Girls
description: Many girls in rural Kenya are missing out on a good education because they cannot afford disposable sanitary pads hence have to be absent from school about 40 days a year. Our solution is the Neema Reusable Sanitary Pads made from easy to clean and comfy fabric. A pack of 10 pads will serve for 2 years and costs 50% less compared to disposable pads; a sustainable, hygienic and cost effective menstrual management solution for the vulnerable. Over 300 girls have benefited to date.

title: Her Farm Films. Stories by and for Women in Nepal
description: Her Farm Films is the name of our production branch at Mountain Fund.  The mission of Her Farm Films is to provide the training and equipment needed for Nepali women to produce short films about life in Nepal for women.

title: who care the caregivers of visual disability child
description: For 22 years the foundation serves children multis girls and disadvantaged youth with visual impairments , deafblindness and multiple institutional and community through the strategy of Community Based Rehabilitation (CBR ) with the participation of families programs, networks support and programs that are born of their own needs, where they themselves become the protagonists of their own transformation.

title: Replace a School in an Earthquake Zone in Bolivia
description: Click ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTATION abajo para ESPANOL. MMB is working on its 54th school construction project with the community of Tunas Pampa, in Aiquile, Cochabamba, to replace a school in danger of collapsing on its students and teachers due to strong seismic activity. MMB will also fully equip the new school and replace the dilapidated teacher housing and communal bathrooms.

title: New Windows and Furniture  for Hospital in Moldova
description: NGO "PHOENIX"  plans to change the windows  and furniture in the Ward of Respiratory Diseases of the Mother and Child Institute, a national hospital where the most complicated cases from all Moldova are treated.  The bad condition of the existing windows does not allow a proper ventilation of the spaces, neither to reduce heat loss in winter.  Furniture is too old and may not be restored. Under these circumstances, this infringes upon sanitation rules to be observed in the hospital.

title: Train 200 Women Caring for AIDS Orphans in Kenya
description: Uzima Women Relief Group International plans to train 200 women taking care of AIDS orphans and their families in rural Kenya to improve home-based care, better farming methods, nutrition, education and income generating activities. Train-the-Trainer model will be used. Workshops will be facilitated by professionals in the above areas who will engage women in hands-on participatory approaches. Informal training will be done on a continuous basis through home visits and community events.

title: Help Support Kids 4 Afghan Kids Schools
description: Kids 4 Afghan Kids (K4AK) was founded in 1998 in Michigan by teacher Khris Nedam, and her sixth grade students, to help kids in rural Afghanistan.   Since then, the US students have helped raise the money to build four schools, a deep water well and a medical clinic.   Due to this success, many more Afghan children wish to attend school.   They need your help to raise the funds!  Kids 4 Afghan Kids is 100% volunteer, so your 100 % of your donations are used to educate children.

title: A gardening program for 250 orphans in Zimbabwe
description: This project will provide a training garden, tools, seeds and essential skills training for 250 poverty stricken orphans and vulnerable children in rural Zimbabwe.

title: Support people in mental distress in Tuzla, Bosnia
description: Association for mutual support in mental distress runs a daily centre for people who face psychological problems and stigma in society. Around 30 people uses daily centre and participate in different activities for social inclusion and rehabilitation, and lot more are affected with our human rights and anti-stigma work. With your support TK Fenix will renovate and equip daily centre with necessary materials for support groups, occupational therapy and life skills activities.

title: Send 40 vulnerable children to school in Tanzania
description: The project will help the 40 vulnerable children from poor families in Morogoro Municipality in Tanzania to access primary education by providing free books, uniforms and sports equipments. These kids are above average age of starting primary education (they are between 9-14years old) so they need special extracurricular program like sports to get them involved

title: Help 150 Mbororo women in Cameroon earn an income
description: WAA Cameroon wants to offer trainers training support on livelihood development in Mushroom and dry fruits, to 150 indigent Mbororo women facing integration difficulties due to their poverty and nomadic lifestyles. This will take place in three regions of Northern Cameroon considered the poorest. WAA will equip trainers with start off material and equipment while supporting their young children to attend free informal literacy classes to enhance their access to education.

title: End child marriage for 750 at-risks girls & family
description: The project goal is to increase the self protection of 750 adolescent girls who are at-risk of early marriage living in communities prone for child marriages and sexual violence in the North West Region of Cameroon. The project also intends to improve prospects to education, economic growth and employment opportunities for rural women and their children. It shall work to foster partnerships with local governance structures to create enabling environments for defending women and girls' rights.

title: Send Ugandan Ex-brides back to school
description: Child Care and Youth Empowerment Foundation plans to extend financial support to 20 more vulnerable ex-brides in Uganda returning to school to better their lives and the lives of their babies. They presently can't pay for it, yet their parents kicked them out of their homes and rejected them due to pregnancy. With this education, they will be literate and secure better jobs.
