description: Due to poor hygiene conditions characterized by dirty and inaccessible toilets in local schools leading to school drop out and infectious diseases among pupils with disabilities . This project will provide accessible toilets and access to clean and safe water in 15 schools. This will improve on the hygiene conditions of 500 pupils on wheelchairs and the blind who crawl and touch in filthy material in order to reach the toilet openings. "A disease free environment  accelerates quality education"

title: Help fund a classroom for kids in rural Angola
description: Every child should have the chance to go to school, to learn to read and write. It is estimated that between 513,000 and several million children in Angola do not have access to primary education. RISE builds primary schools in rural Angola to educate children, empower communities and contribute to the rebuilding of the country.

title: Compassionate Programmes for 30 children in Kenya
description: The Bouncing Ball Trust provides funding for Compassionate Programmes for disadvantaged children in Kenya, enabling them to receive a primary education that would otherwise be denied to them. These children often come from families that are struggling to feed and clothe them never mind sending them to school (there are very few free education opportunities in Kenya)

title: A Christmas Rewards Night for Young Care Leavers
description: Drive Forward is organizing a Christmas event to celebrate the success and accomplishments of young care leavers in London. Throughout our employability and life skills training programme, we have seen young people making great efforts, developing new competences and gaining confidence and self-esteem. Some of them have already found a job, are doing an internship or got into higher education. We want to recognise their hard work with a community Christmas dinner and some fun rewards!

title: Donkey library for 1000 rural Ethiopian children
description: The Donkey Library will bring books and reading to over 1,000 Ethiopian children living in rural areas. Schools in remote parts of Ethiopia often do not have libraries, and so thousands of children don't get the chance to read outside the classroom. The donkey librarian travels from school to school with books in panniers on the donkey's back, giving children the chance to read, learn and discover in an exciting event.

title: CARE: Lasting Support for Refugees Worldwide
description: There are 43.7 million refugees in the world today. Refugees have well-founded fears of persecution for reasons of race, religion, nationality, and other factors. CARE places the needs and rights of women and refugee girls at the forefront, reflecting CARE's experience that empowering women and girls is a critical pathway to reduce vulnerability and long-term poverty. CARE provides short and long term assistance to refugees- from shelter, food, water as well as education, health and security.

title: QUALITY OF LIFE ROAD TRIP - 2016
description: Marin City Health and Wellness Center understands that to address the needs of teens in our underprivileged community we need to expose them to multicultural experiences and allow them to strive for their greater self. This project will fund a cross country  tour including many different states to show and teach the kids about their heritage and the history of this country. It will open their eyes to a whole new world full of experiences, hope and possibilities.

title: Protect Lao Girls From Human Trafficking
description: SENGSAVANG offers protection and assistance to victims and girls at risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation in Laos. Our shelter in central Laos provides a safe home where the girls receive holistic care during their rehabilitation process and are given hope for a better future. Through education, vocational trainings and micro-business starter kits, we transform their lives and ensure a sustainable socio-economic reintegration as an active support for their families.

title: Safe clean water for 6,000 people in rural Uganda
description: The project aims to alleviate rural poverty and water-related ill-health in Mityana and Mubende Districts in Uganda. The project will benefit about 6,000 people through increased access to clean water, better sanitation and agricultural production. This will be achieved by providing low cost manually constructed boreholes, hand-dug wells with pumps, and  training community members in environmental health.  As a result rural communities will have a better quality of life and greater productivity.

title: TIGER Girls-Educating Syrian Refugee Girls
description: Adolescent girls in Zaatari are dropping out of school at a dangerous rate; only 20% achieve a secondary school certificate. TIGER Girls (These Inspiring Girls Enjoy Reading) will enable 1,200 Syrian girls, supported by Syrian female coaches, to participate in team-based learning, increasing their personal sense of agency, meaning and connection. Using an open source multimedia library, this community-based program will motivate adolescent girls either to stay in or to return to school.

title: Establish Girls' Empowerment Centre in Rural Kenya
description: NIGEE is a Kenyan-based non-profit organization that helps school girls who dropped out due to teen pregnancy or child marriage. About 200 of these girls have completed high school and need vocational training to join the job market, and about 300 girls in school need a facility to convene during school holidays and be tutored on sciences and educated on reproductive health. The Girls' Empowerment Center will offer these services to 500 girls and host 50 victims of sexual violence.

title: Help 400 Children/Teens with Autism in Venezuela
description: Provide assessment services for 300 children and adolescents with autism and much needed specialized and comprehensive education to 100 students with autism in Venezuela. We aim to develop their skills and abilities to allow them to integrate effectively within their communities. In Venezuela, specialized programs and professionals scarcity combined with hyper-inflation is severely restricting the access to and the provision/operation of non for profit special education/services.

title: Trauma-relief for 600 Women through Sport and Play
description: The Women on the Move Project is a psychosocial intervention which uses sport and play activities to enable women traumatized by civil war and violence to better cope with daily challenges, increase their self-confidence and improve their future prospects. Core elements of the program are group sport and play activities that improve life skills, including team sports to develop social cohesion and trust. Through income-generating activities, women are empowered economically.

title: Affective sponsorship to sheltered children Brazil
description: The project aims to provide familiar and communitarian conviviality for sheltered children between age of 7-17 years old  who have fragile or broken family bonds,  remote chances of adoption or family reintegration, enabling and encouraging the formation and maintenance of individualized and long-lasting emotional bonds between them and previously selected - qualified volunteers. Offering them a chance to experience family and social life which will help them to build an autonomous life

title: Personal Ponies "Senior Citizens"
description: As PERSONAL PONIES heads into our 30th year of providing small UK Shetland ponies to children and adults with special needs, we are launching a new project to help us update one  of our volunteer farms specifically for our "Senior Pony Citizens". Our retired ponies hold a special place in our hearts and having the funds to make sure they receive the best we can provide in their later years is a very small thank you for all they have given to our program.

title: FEED A FAMILY IN RURAL MALAWI FOR A LIFETIME
description: This project will provide ten desperate families in southern Malawi - an area of plagued by drought and flooding - with an ongoing supply of fresh vegetables.  Through a home treadle pump system.   Your donation will give food security to families in need.

title: Inclusive learning for 50,000 children in India
description: Disadvantaged children in rural India can benefit most from more enlightened, inclusive teaching. This project aims at empowering 125 school teachers in the poorest areas with an intensive, inspiring program. It consists of a 5-day workshop and powerful school-based support sessions using proven methods to enable teachers to bring in the last child into engaged learning. Every teacher impacts on average over 400 children in his/ her career, so the program has potential to impact 50,000 children.

title: Build A School for 200 street children in Ghana
description: The project aim at addressing illiteracy among underserved children by constructing three classrooms to provide them with a serene learning environment. Currently, we managed to mobilise the children under an open nature shelter where we meet everyday to study. Situation on ground such as rainfall and frequent bumping of people into the premises does not permit sound studies. With portable classrooms we guarantee these children right to quality education no matter their socio-economic background

title: Alternative livelihoods for 500 ragpicker families
description: This project will help 500 of Kolkata's most vulnerable families to lift themselves out of poverty and provide a better future for their children.  Tiljala Shed will provide seed funding, advice, vocational and business skills training for women from rag picker families and others living in the city's most deprived slums and squatter camps.

title: Empowering Women in Sierra Leone
description: PROJECT GOAL  To strengthen  cooperation, rights and equality  for women  Specific objectives:   The main goal of this project is to address heightened levels of discrimination and violence against Women by enhancing advocacy and networking capacities among Women groups and promoting coordination for increased success in anti-discrimination and violence campaigns in Sierra Leone.

title: Empowering Youth through Life Skills
description: The targeted project areas consist of large school dropouts who are victims of many unfortunate circumstances, the very awkward situation in which these youths find themselves need immediate special attention most certainly if given an opportunity by offering them special training for jobs and some skills to enable them to become self-reliant. The expected result is that these youths will be of service to the nation and the problem of unemployment and poverty will be greatly curbed.

title: Chalantika - education slum center
description: Chalantika is a slum center for education in Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka. It provides free educational support to 80 children and their guardians. There are two kinds of classes: first help students with their classes, which reduces high drop-out rate. Second prepare pre-school children to enter the first class, which is mandatory and paid in Bangladesh. Also, there is a close contact works with all the childrens guardians, mostly women, during literacy and sewing courses.

title: Support Homeless Youth in New York
description: The Streetwork Project youth and teen homelessness program was formed in 1984 as a response to the growing number of homeless teens in New York City. Today, Streetwork Project makes more than 21,000 contacts with homeless young people, serves more than 65,000 meals a year, and provides forms of housing to homeless youth, teens, and runaways. Show your support by making a donation today, and help us combat youth and teen homelessness.

title: Provide Transportation for Sick and Hungry Pets
description: Your investment in this project will help us purchase our first van that will save lives. This van will enable us to provide more life-saving pet food and veterinary care, transport more sick and injured pets to the veterinarian and deliver a pet into the loving arms of a safe foster home.  Your investment will keep pets happy, healthy and home.

title: Educate in Competences 3750 Taxi Drivers in Bogota
description: Fundacion Ciudad y Transporte plans to provide 15 free training programs throughout the year to educate at least 3.750 taxi drivers in Bogota City, in citizenship and labor competences, seeking for the improvement of their educational conditions and the enhancement of their quality of life and service. This project will help them to face efficiently the new challenges that the globalization has brought to the cities this new century and to professionalize their field.

title: Support Food Security in Kigutu, Burundi
description: Village Health Works (VHW), located in Kigutu, Burundi, offers community, clinical, and school-based programs with an impact on more than 200,000 community members in the last year. To relieve Burundi of the title, "Hungriest Country in the World," according to the 2014 Global Hunger Index, VHW addresses sustainable agriculture and livestock care through supporting on-site and household gardens. Increased harvests provide local families, patients, and school children with nutritious meals.

title: Conscious Club After-school Program - Tanzania
description: The Conscious Club is an after-school program established in government primary schools, focused on developing leadership skills, building confidence, and teaching sexual and reproductive health. Each school's club comprises 60 students, divided equally between girls and boys across grades 3-7. Meeting twice per week, the curriculum was developed in partnership with a local, youth-run NGO. These clubs provide valuable skills and knowledge not typically covered in the school curriculum.

title: Empower Deaf Women to  Build a Business in Mexico
description: The students of this school for special education, all of whom are deaf or hearing impaired, are asking for your help to start a business on the school premises where crafts and bake goods, handmade by them, will be showcased and sold to the public. This co-operative venture will provide opportunities for the students to learn entrepeneurship skills and create employment for them, allowing them to become more independent and self-sufficient while making the school itself more sustainable.

title: Kalimantan Haze Emergency Appeal
description: Because of continuous forest fires, the people of Central Kalimantan are suffering from the worst haze in history. The air pollution level has reached 3,000 - more than 10 times the hazardous level!  The air has become a yellow color. People have difficulty breathing, suffer from constant headaches and more and more babies, children and pregnant mothers are experiencing acute respiratory infections. This project aims to distribute oxygen tanks, masks, eye drops, milk and vitamins to 7 villages.

title: Education for Every Girl in India
description: This project will provide educational stuffs (uniform, school fees, books, sweater, notebooks, pen, pencil, stationary, etc.) to more than 1500 underprivileged poor Girls students of rural regions in Rajasthan so that they may be able to develop their educational standard. This project will help the marginalized children to get better opportunities to be educated and to contribute in the development of society.

title: Launch a peer support forum for burn survivors
description: People with burns or trauma scarring can often feel isolated because they do not get opportunities to meet others with similar experiences. Our aim is to launch an online forum to create a safe and supportive environment to share experiences,  get scar advice and gain access to our other charity services which aim to make it easier to live with burns and scars. Our vision is a world where scars do not limit a person's function, social inclusion or sense of well-being.

title: Providing Bilingual School to 200 Honduran Youths
description: This project will provide a bilingual education focusing on improving  math and reading literacy to 200 poverty stricken Honduran children that would not be able to afford a private school education without us.

title: Empowering Resource Poor Women Through Micro-loan.
description: The project will provide micro-loans to resource-poor women in Mandera County, Kenya. Mandera County is the second poorest county in Kenya with 89% of the inhabitants living below the poverty line. Women are affected the most by poverty due to their role in the family. They are in the frontline dealing with the impact of poverty. When there is no money to buy medicine for a sick child or buy food for the children, the mother is often the person to find ways and means to alleviate the problems.

title: Educate Girls in Tanzania
description: Creating the education infrastructure needed to make a meaningful difference in the lives of young girls requires a multi prong approach with efforts lasting years, if not decades. Our first priority will be to support girls in Tanzania by providing them with much needed resources to acquire quality education from primary up to university levels. We shall focus on less-privileged girls, especially those in rural areas as they face the greatest challenge in acquiring any form of education.

title: The Faraja Medical Support Fund
description: Faraja's main mandate initially was to provide information and therapies to aid patients through their chemotherapy and radiotherapy treatments. However, with an increased cancer burden in Kenya ( mortality currently at 32,000) there is a higher demand for financial assistance for patients. The Faraja Medical Support Fund aims to give the right treatment at the right time to up to children and adults with cancer in Kenya.  The fund offers support to cancer patients in Kenya.

title: Shelter and water for earthquake victims in Nepal
description: This project will build up to 500 temporary homes and rehabilitate broken water supply infrastructure in the earthquake ravaged Kavre/Sindhupalchok area of Nepal.  500 families who lost their homes, their grain stores and their belongings to a devastating earthquake in May of 2015, will have shelter and  clean water again. Protected from the winter cold these families will then be able to focus on rebuilding the livelyhoods they lost.

title: Give the Gift of Education in Nepal
description: On April 25, 2015 a 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Nepal. The country was still reeling from the disaster when a second earthquake struck on May 12. The earthquakes destroyed or damaged over 36,000 classrooms leaving 1 million children unable to return to school. We've already given 2,177 kids the "Gift of Education" by rebuilding classrooms, providing school furniture and learning materials, and by making schools safe and fun places to learn. But we need your help to do even more.

title: Urban Youth Skill Support for 2000 Nigerians
description: The Project will train 2000 vulnerable urban youths in various skills in Nigeria such as video/photography production, hair dressing, horticulture, woodwork, painting, poultry/livestock farming, computer training, carpentry, welding and interior decoration. For sustainability and replication, they shall be mentored on entrepreneurial skill and given a start up grant in the form of revolving loan. These will improve their living conditions and harness their talents for society growth.

title: Creation of Community Mushroom Cultivation Center
description: In order to address malnutrition and unemployment in semi-rural Cameroon, we cultivate mushrooms and train subsistence farmers as well people living with HIV. To accomodate the increasing pressure from communities to learn mushroom cultivation we are expanding our farm and training center. Not only are mushrooms a cheap source of protein and an environmentally friendly agriculture product, there is also a strong mushroom market that presents opportunities for employment in an impoverished area.

title: Provide a Loving Home for Street Girls in DR Congo
description: Street Girls in Congo are vulnerable to sexual exploitation, violence and addiction, and are often invisible on the streets. The Kimbilio projects offer support and provides a loving home for up to 20 street girls, where they live in a small family setting and receive one-to-one support from our carers. The girls enjoy a range of activities such as sewing, art and sports, as well as attending a local school. Ultimately, we try to reunite each girl with her family.

title: Support over 5,000 children through treatment
description: The Oak Centre for Children and Young People is one of the largest comprehensive children and young people's cancer centres in Europe. Over 5,000 day patients and 600 inpatients will receive treatment there every year.  The Royal Marsden strives to ensure that the hospital environment is a real home from home setting for our younger patient. This project provides materials and activities to provide entertainment and distraction for the children as they undergo treatment.

title: Provide Social Services for Exploited Cambodians
description: Justice and Client Care Social Work Project provides essential counselling and social services for survivors of trafficking and sexual exploitation living in their communities to rebuild their emotional well being and resilience in a long-term setting. The project also supports the families of survivors, providing them family counselling, family conflict mediation and life skills education to address the social causes of exploitation and prevent future abuse of family and community members.

title: End Child Abuse in Slums of Kampala & Arua
description: Restoring the Village is a campaign sponsored by the World Action Fund (Uganda) that celebrates the belief that the life of every Ugandan girl and young woman MATTERS.  Our vision is to restore life to 900 girls trapped as sex slaves/prostitutes in Kamapala and Arua Town while creating a sustainable village that will be a model for healthy and violence-free living and vibrant economic development.

title: Menstrual Health Equity for Women in Lebanon
description: Days for Girls (DfG) Lebanon is bringing locally made, washable menstrual Kits and health education to women. Since 2011, Lebanon has experienced an influx of refugees of which women and children comprise 1.5 million of the overall population. With protracted displacement, refugees have multiple humanitarian needs; among them are the challenges of managing menstruation with privacy, dignity, and safety.

title: Rescue Van for Homeless and Injured Animals in HK
description: We rescue, rehabilitate and rehome homeless animals in Hong Kong. LAP rescues and rehomes over 600 animals a year. All of which are either stray colonies/abandoned animals/unwanted pets. We would like to bring about the conditions where every animal has a good home. Currently our constraints are that we don't have the flexibility of when to do rescues as we rely on rented drivers and vans. With a van we will be able to cut cost of rental and rescue more animals as and when its needed

title: Provide Science Labs for Tanzania Secondary School
description: Secondary schools in rural Tanzania often lack science laboratories that foster a deeper understanding of biology, chemistry and physics. The students we work with in the villages surrounding Kigoma town often lament that they don't have the same opportunities to learn science as their peers in larger towns and cities, who have access to fully functioning labs. Hands on experience with scientific knowledge will increase educational and career opportunities for these bright students.

title: Centro COMParte: social economy & peace in Bogota
description: After a field research work started in 2007, PSF opened in 2013 "Centro COMParte", which is a place conceived in order to build a model of social and economical actions in a post-conflict context in the marginalized boroughs of the South of Bogota. Centro COMParte aims at contributing to the building of a sustainable peace by the support of life's projects of an uprooted population thoughout education, culture and entrepeneurship.

title: Train 100 poor Mumbai women in entrepreneurship
description: This Project will train groups of 10 poor single mothers, widows, divorcees, school & college dropouts in different nodes of Navi Mumbai in designing jute woven bags, home linen, ladies dresses and the manufacturing process of paper artifacts. Empowering groups with stitching machines, entrepreneur workshops and making them financially independent contributing members of their family and community for an enriched happy society

title: Education support to underserved inner-city kids
description: Volunteers work towards funding economically backward children with education opportunities. Children benefit from a high standard of education, nutritious meals and mentorship provided by NGO partners to help them with higher studies and career options.

title: help 400 children in Palestine improve their lives
description: FGHA is providing humane, financial, emotional, psychological, and social support for 400 children and their families. Palestinian children are deeply affected by the ongoing fierce conflict, which has led them to a behavior characterized by distrust and hostility that, in the long run, can tremendously affect their social development.  Our project will provide financial and psychological support for 400 children throughout the whole year in Nablus city.

title: Support The ChangeMakers
description: We, the dance4life ChangeMakers, are a completely youth-led group that advocates for the sexual and reproductive health and rights of young people. We envision a world in which young people enjoy health care and well-being, free from coercion, discrimination, and violence. We demand the rights of young people to lead a healthy, joyful, safe and meaningful life free from unsafe sex, unintended pregnancies, dangerous abortions, gender-based violence and other related problems.

title: Gearing Up for Great Streets: A Bike-Friendly PGH
description: The streets of Pittsburgh do not have enough safe places for people to walk and bike. People cannot get where they need to go without risk of serious injury or even death. BikePGH is transforming our streets by making them safe and accessible for everyone to bike and walk!  Advocacy. Education. Community. This is how we get things done.

title: Save dugongs & sea turtles in the Indian Ocean!
description: Artisanal fisheries need tools to prevent trapping of dolphins, sea turtles, and dugongs in their nets.  We work with conservationist NGO C-3 and communities in the Philippines and elsewhere. We are providing practical solutions which protect endangered species, and sustain local livelihoods and eco-tourism. Using our smartphone app, fishermen are already monitoring dugongs. Next we are developing devices to attach to their nets to reduce the by-catch of large and endangered species.

title: Teach Thai Youth to Report Human Trafficking
description: Traffickers use technology every day to outsmart law enforcement, non-profit organizations, government agencies and concerned citizens around the world. We want to make it easy for everyday youth to join the movement to report and prevent human trafficking using a device with which they are totally comfortable.

title: CARE: Help Afghanistan Earthquake Victims Today
description: Your help is urgently needed to provide critical relief to families after a 7.5 magnitude earthquake struck northern Afghanistan, with tremors felt as far as Pakistan and India. CARE is already on the ground preparing for the relief effort.

title: Response to Afghanistan/Pakistan Earthquake
description: A powerful earthquake struck Badakshan Province in Afghanistan on October 26 and also affected a large area of Pakistan. According to the US Geological Survey, the magnitude 7.5 quake struck at 1:39 pm local time and was 121 miles (196 km) deep. Initial media reports indicate at least 177 people have been killed in Pakistan, with the majority of the fatalities occurring in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa or KPK. Some 33 were reportedly killed in Afghanistan. An additional 1,000 are reportedly injured.

title: Community Based Rehabilitation
description: Vidya Sagar's CBR program ( since 1990 ) aims at sharing the technical knowledge and skills on rehabilitation( capacity building ) and reach out to as many persons with disability, irrespective of their location and socio - economic background ,ensuring access to appropriate services. The CBR team with 7 projects reaches out to 28 community workers, more than 275 persons with disabilities, their families and the community.

title: Bringing children's palliative care to Bangladesh
description: With an estimated 29 000 children in Bangladesh needing specialised end of life care each year, there are presently just 2 doctors providing children's palliative care in this impoverished country. This project will provide training for 20 doctors and 10 nurses in the basics of children's palliative care resulting in a massive improvement in the quality of life and relief of suffering of an estimated 1,200 children and their families.

title: Help children prepare for disasters in Pakistan
description: More than 200 people have died in Pakistan and Afghanistan after the recent devastating earthquake in the region. A further 1,500 have been injured. RedR UK is training local schoolchildren and teachers in essential skills that will help to minimise the impact of disasters like this in the future.

title: Earthquake Recovery for Students in Badakhshan
description: A 7.5 magnitude earthquake hit northeastern Afghanistan in the Badakhshan province on Monday, October 26th, claiming more than 300 lives in Afghanistan and Pakistan, destroying many buildings, and displacing thousands of people. At least 4 AAE schools in northeastern Afghanistan have been affected and we have a list of 50+ families in need of immediate aid.

title: Shelter for Victims of Domestic Violence in Uganda
description: Due to the overwhelming amount of abuse women face in Eastern Uganda and the lack of facilities available to them, WORI Uganda wishes to construct a shelter to provide temporary refuge and basic necessities for victims of domestic violence. In addition, it will provide psychological counseling and emergency medical care to the victims of domestic violence, as well as providing legal aid for the victims, whilst raising awareness on domestic violence

title: Help Victims of 2015 Afghan Earthquake
description: On 26th October 2015 there was a devastating 7.5 earthquake centered in the Hindu Kush mountains in Afghanistan's Badakhshan Province, which borders Pakistan. Many people in the area around Peshawar, Pakistan have lost everything. AIL's Peshawar office has worked with people in Pakistan for decades and has extensive contacts in the area and frequent experience of helping with natural and other disasters. Staff have identified 1,000 earthquake victims they can help in the Peshawar area.

title: Send 200 preschool children to the farm in Oregon
description: Studies show that when kids are involved in gardening, it increases their consumption of vegetables. We know this to be true, since out on the farm, kids will taste and like almost everything they harvest themselves. Eating more vegetables puts kids on track to become healthier adults.

title: Share Hope with Refugees at Camp Oinofyta Greece
description: Thousands of Syrian refugees have traveled to Greece fleeing a civil war that has raged since 2011 and displaced millions. Through a new agreement, the EU has closed the borders from Greece into the rest of Europe in hopes of better managing the crisis. The local Greek government is stretched thin, so it is imperative that volunteer organizations like Do Your Part receive funding to help support the refugees and ease the burden on the Greek people while refugee asylum applications are processed.

title: Training 130 women youth health leaders in Gujarat
description: 88% of India's 355 million women do not have access to sanitary pads. Lack of awareness and affordability means that sand, ash, rags or dirty cloth are used instead of sanitary pads, leading to blistering, soreness, infections and long-term health issues. This problem can be solved with our health and hygiene awareness project, training young local women leaders to raise awareness about menstrual health and hygiene and generate income through selling low-cost sanitary pads locally.

title: Save Baikal: preserve the purest lake on the Earth
description: Baikal Lake in East Siberia is the deepest, purest and most ancient lake on the Earth. It contains 20% of the planet's surface water reserve, 3/4 species found there are unique. Ecological situation got very hard there today. "Save Baikal" is aimed at researching, developing, and introducing efficient methods for cleanliness preservation and protection of Baikal Lake coastline, incl. waste treatment in the specially protected nature areas frequented by tourists. We engrain solutions that work.

title: Cambrian Wildwood - Rewilding an area in Mid Wales
description: Imagine walking through a truly wild landscape, abounding with wildlife, right here in Britain. Visiting the wildwood, in the Cambrian Mountains of Wales, you will see red squirrels in the trees, wild horses grazing, and many other mammals and birds. You might even spot the elusive pine marten. You will be able to follow trails throughout the wildwood and camp wild in beautiful sites, immersing yourself in nature. You can make this vision a reality by donating to help us continue the work.

title: Help Rebuild a Nepal School after the Earthquake
description: After the devastating Earthquake in Nepal in April 2015, many schools have been flattened.  Help us to get the Nepali children back into education by rebuilding their schools in the remote area of Makwanpur. This area currently has one of the lowest rates of school attendance in Nepal and Nepal already has one of the worst literacy rates in the world - only 45% of Nepalis complete primary school. If the children have no school to go to, this problem will just get worse.

title: Secondary education for 30 girls in rural Kenya
description: We wish to secure a year's secondary education for 30 girls in Msambweni, Kenya.  Girls who achieve well in primary school and have aspirations are rarely able to progress to secondary school;  the cost is prohibitive.  This project will, in particular, assist orphans or girls who are being raised by a woman living on her own.  Education will transform the life of each of these girls, provide hope and security to the whole of her family and improve the quality of life in her community.

title: Enable 500 Tanzanian youth to feed their families
description: We believe everyone has the right to life's basics. A roof, enough food to eat, clean water to drink and the education needed to build a brighter future. What we take for granted can only be dreamed of by communities in extreme poverty such as Zeze. But his dream isn't impossible. It doesn't take years of research or huge multinational organisations. It only takes the hard work of MVG, the villagers of Zeze and your donation. Will you help us to bring life's basic needs to the people of Zeze?

title: Aid Widows and Orphans of Afghanistan Earthquake
description: 350 persons have already been reported dead and several more injured from 7.5 Afghanistan earthquake. These numbers are sadly growing and victims need your help.  Give aid to widows and orphans of this earthquake, who are the most vulnerable of those who are suffering. The aid will provide food, clothing, shelter and help them get back on their feet.

title: Chacala Music & Art Festival
description: This project will continue to support the children of the Chacala Village who attend classes in music and art prior to the Chacala Music & Art Festival and then exhibit their work and/or perform at the festival. We have been fortunate enough to reach over 200 children each year. Funding will provide scholarships for many students at the Chacala Mariachi Institute.

title: Empowering 200 Girl Leaders in India
description: Empowered girls are a powerful catalyst to change development outcomes. The Girl Icon Program is a leadership  development program that works with girls between 12-18 years from low socio-economic communities in India to empower them through experiential life-skills based journey, providing safe spaces to amplify their voices of change and opportunities to sensitize and mobilize communities through collective social action.

title: Give qualified teachers to 150 children in uganda
description: We started Christ Towers Junior School project in February this year renting class rooms. Since the school was a dream, payment of qualified teachers has been  an outstanding challenge. With friends in the US and Global giving donors we are creating a modern environment for intellectual learning for poor girls in Kiboga. Hiring class rooms and paying the teachers so far makes 'Starting a school' a challenge for the beginning School years.  Allied Organization offers to help build this s

title: Support Shipibo-Konibo Change Makers
description: Palm oil,  oil and gas company activity is increasingly affecting  Shipibo-Konibo communities on and around the Ucayali river - one of the main tributaries of the Amazon in Peru. Support educational workshops and professional development opportunities to equip them with the skills necessary to defend their rights and make more informed decisions regarding sustainable economic development.

title: Build Homes for Earthquake Survivors in Nepal
description: When a powerful earthquake rocked Nepal, people lost their homes and their way of making a living. This project will provide homes and hope for families in hard-hit areas close to the epicenter of the April 25 quake.

title: Meet Aspen!  Certified Therapy Dog.
description: A review of the scientific literature indicates that the presence of a friendly dog has a positive impact on ones emotional and physical well-being. Aspen will assist victims of sexual assault by: providing stimulation for conversation, improve the victims physical, social, emotional and/or cognitive function and elevate the mood of both client, staff and the facility in general.      Additionally, Aspen will educate children on anti-violence through our unique prevention program "Paws Off"

title: Help child victims get justice
description: Orphaned girls in Kenya are extremely vulnerable and at high risk for sexual assault. Makindu Children's Program offers legal counsel, advocacy, mental and physical healthcare,  and trauma support to child victims of sexual assault. This project will help provide much needed social support to Sofia and other victims like her, in navigating through the slow and painful legal process to bring perpetrators in Kenya to justice.

title: Improve literacy for Ugandan rural children
description: Over 70% of Uganda's primary school children do not finish primary school on time or even at all. This is a huge problem because over half of Uganda's population (52%) is children below the age of 15 and the future belongs to them. Our focus is to help children improve their literacy and develop key life skills through spelling competitions and in-service teacher trainings.

title: Refugee & Migration Crisis
description: Since the beginning of 2015, more than 705,200 people have moved or are moving through Europe. More than 3,200 people have died or gone missing at sea. The most common countries of origin are Syria, Afghanistan, Eritrea, and Iraq.   28 National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies are responding across Europe and addressing immediate needs in Health, Water & Sanitation, food and non-food distribution, psychosocial support and longer-term needs.

title: Conquer Childhood Cancer-Build a Lab Bench!
description: We are committed to making all childhood cancer survivable, no matter the diagnosis. We connect research with the discovery of new therapies for children's cancer. Be a part of our new lab by making a donation to build a lab bench.  We have two new clinical trials starting soon and the opportunity for more with your help.

title: Improved Cookstoves for 25 Liberian Village Homes
description: Village Improvement Project, Inc. (VIP) seeks to replace three-stone open fire cooking method with improved cook stoves for rural village communities in Liberia. Village Improvement Project, Inc. project aims to design and produce cleaner burning stoves to reduce household air pollution for 98% of the population in Liberia, West Africa who use solid fuels for cooking.

title: Rebuild Women LEAD's Home in Nepal
description: This project will rebuild Women LEAD's home (our office), which suffered critical structural damage in the April 25th earthquake. Our on-site training hall is where hundreds of young women are trained and mentored each year through our leadership and empowerment programs. We urgently need a safe, earthquake-resistant venue in order to continue developing the next generation of female leaders and change-makers in Nepal.

title: Help girls in Uganda to stay in school
description: Help girls in Uganda to stay in school is a project that is aimed at helping marginalised adolescent girls to thrive in a changing world by building their 'skills for life': their ability to protect and look after themselves, make a living and make informed life choices. The project's focus is on adolescents aged 10 to 18, and on girls in particular. Promote the role of girls' education in development and provide equipment,  and  training to enable more girls stay at school.

title: Language Course & Recreational Events for Refugees
description: Together with you, we support organizations and initiatives in the recording, management and integration of refugees .

title: 10 Computers Educate 40 Bangladesh Orphans
description: This Bangladesh project teaches computer skills to thirty orphanage children, preparing them for advanced schooling or future jobs as well as familiarize small children with the taste of the modern technology that began happening in this country.

title: end|NS Campaign: Hope for NS Afflicted Children
description: Hope for Humans' goal is to give life back to children afflicted with Nodding Syndrome, a devastating neurological disease. For $10 per day you can provide a child with NS 24 hour health care, special needs education, nutritionally supplemented meals, access to clean drinking water, agricultural training, and community empowerment, awareness, and advocacy. We are raising $19,000, the cost to provide our services to 21 children for 3 months.

title: Help SOS save Madagascar's Lemurs and Communities
description: SOS Lemurs is a special initiative of SOS - Save Our Species, working to save lemurs and help the communities who depend on their survival. Only found on Madagascar, over 90% of  lemur species are threatened with extinction due to slash-and-burn agriculture, illegal logging and hunting. Implementing projects aligned with the IUCN SSC Primate Specialist Group's Lemur Action Plan is our best chance to save them. It identifies 30 key sites and what to do. SOS lemurs is acting on that plan. Join us!

title: Supporting Women and Girls After the Nepal Quake
description: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Nepal in April of 2015. Another devastating earthquake struck only days later. Thousands died and millions were affected. Hospitals were overwhelmed and supplies were depleted. 2 million women and girls of reproductive age were among those affected and are now those most vulnerable. UNFPA, the United Nations Population Fund, will focus on their needs and rights throughout the recovery process.

title: Support 30 young people off the streets of Mombasa
description: Glad's House wants to support 30 of Mombasa's most challenging young people off the streets of and move them into our Transitional Home and Boxing Programme. Some of these young people have been on the streets for 10 years, some for even longer. There are no options for them any more. We want to give them back those options and work with them to turn their lives around through sport and education and to move into independent living and education, employment and/or training.

title: Support 100 Women In Poultry Farming In Lusaka
description: This project will increase the economic empowerment of HIV Positive women with skills in poultry farming in Lusaka, Zambia. 100 HIV Positive women will be provided with skills and  capital input to carry out poultry farming .

title: Water Basins for 8,000 Villages using Solar Power
description: Village residents plan and build a Rain Water Catchment Basin (RWCB) to have water all year round even in the dry torrid conditions of the Sahel.  With water, the transformation of villages from 'dry and dying' to green and vibrant is amazing! The basin taps into the existing water aquifer, raises the water table, filling dry wells. Thanks to generous donations, two villages now have market days 3 days a week all year.

title: Birunda Shelter for 300 Street Children
description: We break the cycle for children living dangerous lives on hostile streets and take them to safety. The Birunda Shelter provides a chance for some of them to grow up.  Birunda provides accommodation for up to 6 months for 300 of these children aged 2 to 16 including basic needs, food, vaccinations, informal education, and the opportunity to be reintegrated back with their family.

title: Forests4Water Brazil: Community Climate Action
description: If there's one thing that the pandemic has taught us, it's how interdependent we all are, and how what happens in one place can affect others, thousands of miles away. Take rainforests. Home to half of the biodiversity on earth, they store carbon, produce oxygen and play a crucial role in regulating the water cycle and stabilizing weather patterns over huge areas. Global warming demands that we take urgent action to protect and restore the ecosystems on which all our lives depend, starting now.

title: Support  300,000 DC residents to reduce Obesity
description: Battle of the DC WARDS is a competitive dancing Flash mob battle between all 8 Wards, online voting along with a panel of judges. Each participant in the winning Ward receives a $25 food voucher to be used at a Fresh Farm Market.  This project is an exciting avenue to eradicating obesity which is the leading causes of death in the U.S. and worldwide.  The project will provide continuing education on healthy eating and increase physical activity for over 300,000 obese DC residents.

title: Operating an Education Center for 60 Children
description: The Integral Heart Foundation has been working full-time in Guatemala since 2010. Having successfully funded the opening of our center, we will now focus on fundraising for the operating costs of between $25-30,000 annually. We support the lives and education of 60 children and teenagers and their families. The education programs happening at 'La Academia' are Critical-Thinking, English, Spanish, History, Psychology, Homework Study, art, playtime and we provide breakfast, lunch and snacks daily.

title: Rise Now for the Syrian Refugee Children
description: Today, more around 2.5 million Syrian Refugees are living in Turkey. Around 50% of this population is children. Bridge to Turkey Fund's project will help refugee children to achieve developmental progress and will provide continuity in their education.  Our project will raise funds to provide the Syrian Refugee Kids with backpacks and education kits; to sponsor their language education & social development; to build libraries for Syrian schools; and to empower these children's mothers.

title: Breaking Chains of Poverty through Dance.
description: This project enables youths in Rural Rwanda to earn a living through traditional Dancing and create a source of income to fight poverty in their families. The income earned is used to pay school fees for their younger ones, health insurance and basic needs as their parents are not able to do pay for them because of poverty and some are orphans. We believe dancing will not only transform their lives but will also resonate in the community as it engages more youth.

title: Make Oakland a Better Place to Bike and Walk
description: In 2015, WOBO successfully executed the popular Bike to Work Day and THREE Oaklavia (oaklavia.org) events, continued to host free monthly walks with our sister organization Oakland Urban Paths, grew our social rides/classes to showcase local murals, facilitated local businesses in expanding Parklets across the city, coordinated a winning road diet campaign along Telegraph Avenue & Grand Avenue, and supported Mayor Schaaf's proposed Department of Transportation. Help us make 2016 even better!

title: Strengthen the training system in Shenyang
description: This project will address one of the major problems in blindness prevention in China: lack of quality eye care personnel in the rural areas where they are most needed. Through this project, we target to strengthen the training system in Shenyang He Eye Care System (SHECS) to address the lack of high-quality eye care service personnel identified in the current China Blindness Prevention (PBL) Plan, particularly in rural areas.

title: Help for Refugees
description: In order to help the millions of people who have been displaced due to armed conflict, persecution, or other dangers, the member organizations of Aktion Deutschland Hilft are implementing numerous projects for refugees worldwide. These projects cover areas such as the provision of emergency shelters, psycho-social support for traumatized children, distribution of food and hygiene articles, assistance for unaccompanied refugee minors, and medical care.

title: Give a job to 25 discriminated people in Bucharest
description: Ateliere Fara Frontiere provides a job and an empowerment program to 25 disadvantaged people. Men and women with a disability, chronic diseases, family or justice related problems, addictions. We give them a fresh start in life, in Bucharest where exclusion and discrimination are fierce.  Our employees are people who, despite a wrong start or a life accident, are working hard towards rebuilding their lives. Through their work, reusing and recycling waste, they also make the world a cleaner place

title: I Speak Football
description: I Speak Football is a project led by young leaders that uses football to connect isolated young people in Melbourne. Offering football sessions to boost language skills and social networks, we aim to help 300 young people from marginalised cultural backgrounds to make friends, boost their self-confidence and self-esteem.  Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help I Speak Football to help the young leaders support even more young people in Melbourne.

title: Emergency Appeal Earthquake Badakhshan Afghanistan
description: Help to bring support to the victims of the earthquake in northeastern Badakhshan province of Afghanistan. A 7.5 magnitude earthquake centred in northeastern Afghanistan struck on 26 October, causing significant loss of life and widespread damage to about 7 600 households. These families who have lost their homes need support to survive the freezing cold season . In order to face the severe winter weather our project aimed at providing winterization support to the victims.

title: Starfish Impact School
description: Just 10 percent of Guatemalan indigenous girls who live in rural communities are enrolled in secondary school, and less than 1 percent continue on to university. Starfish has embarked on a new journey to launch our first all-girls' secondary school in January 2017. We believe that by combining our intentional, holistic program with highly trained educators and a rigorous academic model, our Girl Pioneers will truly be able to realize their infinite impact and create long-lasting change.

title: Empowerment workshops for 30 young girls - Bolivia
description: We work with 30 young girls (from 5 to 18 years old) in a centre for victims of sexual abuse in Bolivia. Our project aims to help these girls regain confidence in themselves, empower themselves and remain strong against the adversities life has thrown at them. We need your help to continue running micro-business workshops in order to help these girls overcome their traumas, find the will to survive and become independent and healthy adults.

title: Food Angel- Food Rescue & Food Assistance Program
description: With the mission of "Waste Not, Hunger Not", the program rescues edible surplus food from the food industry that would otherwise be disposed of as waste. The rescued food items will then be prepared as nutritious meals in our central kitchens and be redistributed to serve the needy in Hong Kong. Currently, Food Angel rescues 35 tonnes of edible surplus food each week, producing over 15,000 nutritious meals and helps distribute over 9,000 other meals and food packs daily free of charge.

title: The Tafel Refugee Integration Project Fund
description: The number of people, especially refugees, seeking help at the Tafel has sharply increased. Local Tafel initiatives have a variety of ways to address the challenges like language barriers, food and volunteer shortages or increased conflict potential, and this fund offers financial support for the best concepts.

title: Help Orphans & Needy Children in Kenya
description: This project, the Diani Children's Village, helps orphans, abandoned and abused children in Kenya and provide them with a home, education and basic needs. A good education will provide a proper foundation for an independent and successful life. Apart from formal education we also personally engage with the children to teach them the necessary life skills through our self generating income projects like our workshop and poultry project.

title: Build the Caladesi Discovery Center on the island
description: This project will create a learning center on an unspoiled barrier island that focuses on the ecology, history, geology of barrier islands in the Gulf of Mexico

title: Promote Child Nutrition & Welfare in Akwaya
description: Many children in Akwaya are living in households where food is a luxury.  Many are taken to orphanages as vulnerable children; however, even the orphanages do not have enough for the children.  Some die before the caregivers can do anything to revive their lives.  It is for these reasons that FORUDEF, as an extension to its nutrition programme, has decided to support 500 malnourished children in Akwaya over a three year period. The program will also focus on prevention and nutritional education.

title: Boots & Beats
description: Boots & Beats is a project led by young leaders that uses the passion for football and music to address youth unemployment and engage young people, connecting them to work-related training and volunteering. Offering high quality football coaching and music workshops, alongside job skills courses, we aim to help 500 young people.  Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help Boots & Beats to continue the work of our young leaders and help even more young people in Manchester.

title: Resilient Homes for Nepal Earthquake Survivors
description: This project seeks to provide secure, dignified, earthquake resilient transitional homes for people displaced by the Nepal earthquakes who lost their homes during the 7.8 magnitude earthquake on April 25, 2015. The project also incorporates self-recovery and disaster preparedness objectives by educating affected communities in shelter safety issues and training local workers in build back safer methods.

title: Early Education Program in Tajikistan
description: In Tajikistan early childhood development programs - the equivalent of Head Start programs in the U.S. - are broken-down remnants of the Soviet era, more daycare services than opportunities to get ahead. But CAI-Tajikistan is looking to change that by creating a model, holistic program that could be replicated by any school in the region. The program includes the latest teaching methods for instructors, a safe learning environment, and unstructured playtime.

title: Broadening housing requisites:1000 Bihar villagers
description: It takes thousands of years for nature to build fertile Topsoil, but it takes minutes for brick kilns to decimate the top 6 inches of life giving soil for being used in construction. Thousands of villages in India have become infertile. Drishtee is offering sustainable housing solutions for marginalised rural dwellers. Designed by rural women, the house is built with compressed eco bricks and bamboos. 1000 such houses in clusters of 20 each is needed for demonstrating an alternate solution.

title: Healthy Goals
description: Over 60% of India's population lack access to adequate sanitation, increasing health risks from preventable yet deadly diseases. Healthy Goals uses football sessions to engage young people  from Kolkata's slum communities in educational games to teach them about health, sanitation, and how to access clean water.   Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help us reach even more young people in Kolkata.

title: Supporting People with Down Syndrome in Africa
description: Many people with Down syndrome in Africa face low life expectancy, abuse, stigma, segregation and limited life opportunities, both as children and adults. Society's negative attitudes prevents them from reaching their potential, living valued lives and contributing to society.     This project will provide capacity building training for small Down syndrome charities in Africa, putting them on a sound footing with tools to improve knowledge, attitudes and empower people with Down syndrome.

title: Feed the Homeless Project
description: This project is about feeding homeless children and women who are living in the streets in Cameroon-Africa.

title: Empower 200 Students' Rural Community Projects
description: This project empowers over 200 students by training teachers, who will help them use community resources and connect their school content with transforming their communities.

title: Educate and Empower 44 East Bali Mountain Children
description: Your donations enable East Bali Poverty Project (EBPP) to continue providing quality education in 2023 for all 44 students in EBPP's Jatituhu & Pengalusan schools, located in remote hamlets on the steep Mounts Abang and Agung slopes in Ban village. Government schools are too far away and no public transport. We've already sponsored five children to university and need your help to continue their education so they can graduate, realise their dreams and lead their communities to a better future.

title: Help Educate the Underprivileged - Round Table 123
description: This project will provide 5 classrooms in Southern India at Siragu Montessori School in Chennai, India. The school believes in providing more than education , enabling students to be employable on completion of their education. Personality Development,  value systems , and vocational training are provided to students living on pavements, rescued from Child Labour and poorest children and ZERO fees is charged for their education and stay.

title: Help 253 Children Receive a Rural School Library
description: This project will provide two primary libraries in rural Vietnam, providing a rich supply of books and critical literacy support programs to 253 children.

title: Save a Turtle by Reducing Marine Litter in Kenya
description: Over 100 million marine animals are killed each year due to plastic debris in the ocean. Sea turtles around the world are eating plastic at an unprecedented rate, plastic bags can bear a striking resemblance to jellyfish underwater and have a tendency to confuse hungry sea turtles.  In our own little way, we would like to save turtles by cleaning up beaches along Kenya's coast while removing garbage dumps and transforming them into Mangrove forests, perfect habitats for some turtles

title: Help build a playground in Guatemala
description: School the World aims to improve education in the developing world. We build schools, train teachers, drive a sustainable supply of books and empower parents as "first educators".  We have introduced a new pillar to our strategy around PLAY and its importance in childhood development. Our goal for 2016 is to provide a playground at each one of our 38 schools in Guatemala and Honduras so that our students have the opportunity to practice what they are learning.

title: Access to maternal health services in Liberia
description: Emerging from the recent Ebola outbreak that destroyed its already fragile health system, Liberia is now faced with numerous challenges in improving health outcomes and the greater health system.  These issues are particularly grave in the areas of maternal and child health, as evidenced by the high infant, child and maternal mortality rates. Our program will benefit 62 health workers and a total of more than 100,000 community members through improvement of services at 3 health facilities.

title: Maasai Olympics: Ending Lion Killings In Kenya
description: Iconic predators of Africa are disappearing before our eyes. Wild African lions have declined by 75% in 20 years. Predators are critical to healthy eco-systems in East Africa. In Maasai culture, it is custom for males to kill lions as a rite of passage into manhood. Maasai leaders asked for assistance from Big Life to eliminate lion hunting from their culture. In response, the Maasai Olympics and conservation education initiative were created to provide a transformative alternative.

title: HELP NEGLECTED VULNERABLE ELDERLY PEOPLE IN KENYA
description: Purity Elderly Care Foundation was established to take care of the neglected, abandoned and the lonely elderly persons in our society. From providing them with food, shelter and clothing, we also assist with medical assistance by taking them to hospital, repair dilapidated shelters, support those with Orphans and Vulnerable Children and give compassion to to the lonely. We observe International Days and also lobby and advocate for the plight of this marginalized group. We are gonna get old too!

title: Influence Africa's Future, Invest in Young Leaders
description: Join the Revolution of Hope! GOLD empowers vulnerable children to develop as young leaders and activists of social change by equipping them with the skills to mobilize their peers to reach their full economic and social potential.  At the heart of the GOLD model is the belief that the message giver is the strongest message - It's not what you say, it's what you do. GOLD helps youth develop a values framework that promotes healthy life choices and critical decision making skills.

title: Building a Movement to Save 2 Million Lives
description: In Nigeria 26,000 women, 50% of children with malaria, accident victims, cancer and sickle cell anemia patients all die because of blood shortage. One Percent Project is creating a movement to inspire thousands of young Nigerians to give blood to save all these people. We are harnessing the power of technology and media to get 2 million young people registered on our donor database. To do this, we need to go where people are and we need a mobile blood bank.

title: Give girls dignity with reusable sanitary pads
description: By providing 350 girls access to sanitary protection during menstruation dignity will be restored to girls, and the cycle of poverty will be interrupted and gradually broken. Your donation will provide a girl with sanitary protection for 5 years, her entire high school career.

title: Help Build Outdoor Aviaries for 100 Parrots in NJ
description: This project calls for building several outdoor aviaries for the 100+ parrots, cockatoos, macaws, and other psittacines cared for at Under My Wing Avian Refuge in Wantage, NJ. The aviaries will be built on our 10-acre wooded property, close to the birds' indoor quarters. They will allow the birds to spend time in the fresh air and sunshine, and enjoy some free flight. Also, both the indoor and outdoor aviaries will be used for hands-on avian educational community programs for adults and youth.

title: Give Opportunities to 150 Kids in Bogota
description: Your donation can improve the life of 150 kids between 5 and17 years old, who have experienced the problems of  Colombia's big cities.  Now we want to provide a space in which the kids can have activities of culture, sports and preparation for their future. They come from low income families neglecting their children, who spend a lot of time on the streets expose to drugs, often with physical, psychological, and/or verbal abuse. AIMY has been working for 58 years with this vulnerable population

title: #JADHero
description: Starting this December 1, 2015 on #GivingTuesday, help Junior Achievement of Dallas achieve our focus to provide business role models, basic business skills, and financial literacy to 100% of the most at-risk students in the Dallas community. Our programs give K-12 students the essential financial literacy and business skills necessary to be successful in the global economy of today.  Help us reach 50,000 students during the 2015-16 school year!

title: Vision Care for 353,169 children in  Sri Lanka
description: Sri Lanka's 2nd largest population of 2,294,641 is residing at Gampaha District. . 353,169 children are studying at 531 Schools. According to the statistical calculations of vision 2020 program of Ministry of Health Sri Lanka  minimum of 4000 students from Gampaha district is studying while suffering from vision problems. Most of these children are unable to afford to purchase an eye glass due to their financial difficulties in their families.

title: Helping Cambodian Children at M'Lop Tapang
description: This project in Sihanoukville, Cambodia helps vulnerable children, youth, and their families.  M'Lop Tapang offers access to education, reintegration with families, life-skills training, creative and recreational activities, while ensuring protection from all forms of abuse. Our efforts allow underprivileged children to embrace their childhood so they can become responsible adults as well as positive, independent members of society.

title: Ububele Mother-infant Home Visiting, South Africa
description: Healthy brain development starts with positive life experiences in the first 1000 days (conception to 2 years). Ububele's Umdlezane Parent-Infant Programme, in impoverished Alexandra Township in South Africa's Gauteng,  supports the mother-infant relationship. Umdlezane is an Nguni term that refers to the time, post-partum, when a mother's relationship with her baby is prioritized by other women in the family, who take care of other concerns in the home so that the mother can focus on her child.

title: HELP TO BUILD A LEARNING RESOURCE CENTRE IN NEPAL
description: This project will build a learning resource centre in the Bhagawatpur villages of eastern Nepal. The centre will have facilities of  a library, computer learning, life skills training, after school club, newspaper and telephone.  The villages are isolated and they do not have an access to reading materials (newspapers and books) and facility for online courses. Consequently, this project will improve the reading and writing skills of the people and connect the villages with the global society

title: Goal in Three Parts
description: Sao Paulo is a thriving metropolis but inequality means that many struggle to break the cycle of poverty, especially young women. Goal for Equality seeks to empower marginalised young women in Vila Albertina, a favela located in the north of Sao Paulo, by training female coaches to deliver mixed football leagues and education on gender issues to other children and young people in the community.  Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help even more young people in Sao Paulo.

title: School gardens for 200 kids in Nicaragua
description: Low coffee prices and diseases like leaf rust are hurting small farming families in Latin American  rural coffee-growing communities. Farmers have seen their coffee production decimated, with yields declining by over 60% in many places. We're working with the 650 coffee-farming members of Nicaraguan coffee cooperative SOPPEXCCA, to help them build long-term food security programs so they can grow nutritious, fresh food for the community and reduce their dependence on coffee for all their income.

title: Purchase land for a school in Togo
description: In the school Yanfouom in Togo there is a lack of space : we had 40 students in 2000 and now in 2015 over 900 !! So we need to purchase land for new buildings and to have an appropriate schoolyard.

title: All Equine Services Free to Clients at BITS ETC
description: Hippotherapy: using horse interactions to leverage gains made by physical, occupational, and speech therapists, as well as mental health practitioners increasingly moves into mainstream medical practice. At BITS ETC we can make a difference by offering these interventions free of charge to all clients who could be positively impacted by spending time with our therapy herd. Our two most utilized programs target those with autism, or Uniformed Professionals..Veterans, and First Responders.

title: Recycled 1956 Chevy Truck Become 3-D Teaching Aid
description: For over 30 years Yachana Foundation has seen that more hands on learning aids entices students to want to learn. Large-scale physical aids give students the opportunity to use their sensory abilities to enhance the learning by being able to touch, feel, a real engine cutaway. Your contribution to the Recycled Chevy Truck Project will assure that students in our Agricultural Education curriculum will be better prepare in the mechanical systems needed to sustain the agriculture industry.

title: Marnie's Old Pals at the ASPCA
description: Marnie the Dog - a 13 year old rescue, social media influencer, and senior pets advocate - has started a special fund with the ASPCA to help senior pets. Marnie's Old Pals at the ASPCA Fund was created to help older cats and dogs at the ASPCA Adoption Center in New York City to receive the necessary care to get them adopted into safe, loving homes.

title: Together
description: The main idea is to reconstruct the square in Vorniceni village, Republic of Moldova, in the way to create a beautiful place for rest and to provide new work places.  The long-term goal is developing of a green area with an international importance.

title: Digital literacy to empower urban slum children
description: There is no such industry which works without computers in modern times. Imagine in this context, what it means for the person who has never used a computer- the possibility of finding work? At Humana's Academy for Working Children, we provide access to computer from an early age to children. We need to re equip 2 computer training centres in Jaipur, Rajasthan. Help us in making both children and youth gain skills & confidence to help arrest the problem of unemployment in our country.

title: LiftUp 200 Dalit & Minority YoungStars
description: The new LiftUp YoungStars Initiative aims to "lift up" 200 of Nepal's most vulnerable youths. The Dalit and youth populations have been impoverished by natural disasters and suffered severe discrimination based on their social status. We hope to raise $5,000 to partner with local organizations that will provide skill-oriented vocational training for 100 Dalit YoungStars and public service preparatory classes for 100 more. This project will be managed and documented by the ICDR office in Nepal.

title: The International Back-to-School Hackathon
description: The International Back-to-School Hackathon teaches students around the world important computer science skills, collaboration skills, and how global human issues can be solved with teamwork and technology. This program brings access to education and technology to all of its participants the world over, providing student to not only learn coding and design, but to gain perspective from their peers in other countries.

title: Fostering Inquisitive Learners
description: ASIJ is a non-profit institution. Donations allow us to continue offering the many important cultural and academic programs that make an ASIJ education so special.

title: help mothers  fight malnutrition among children
description: after differences in meetings (regal) between those who are involved in the project (mopab, city hall, casec,asec,mspp civil society) all the population hopes to find funds to run the project (help mothers fight malnutrition among children ) in order to improve the situation of life in haiti, where food insecurity is rage. of these project will allow 3500 people combat malnutrition. the mairie,mspp, mopab,civil society in petit-goave are seekers  of this project and we asked comprehensive of all

title: Help Us Plant 10,000 Longleaf Pine Trees in 2017
description: Longleaf pine trees are one of the most ecologically important tree species to the southeast United States, supporting over 900 unique species. Due to over-use, there is now only 3% of the 90 million acres of longleaf pine forests that once spanned the southeast. LET'S PUT THEM BACK! During last year's planting season, we planted 12,000 longleaf pine trees on conservation land with your help (we only planted 4,500 the year before). Please help us plant another 10,000 in this planting season!

title: Stop Child Marriage Through Education of Girls
description: The goal of this project is to end gender gap in education of 89,000 girls in Kajo-Keji, South Sudan by providing access of education to young girls.  Only 6% of 13 year old girls have completed their primary school. The lack of educational opportunities for girls leads to economic disadvantage which is a precursor to marrying before the age of 18 years.  Early marriages of girls in South Sudan is eroding the future backbone of the community.

title: Medicine and Care for 2500 Ugandan Orphans
description: Bambi Uganda Orphans hopes to expand its Mobile Health Clinic (MHC) program and provide medicine, health care items and training in hygiene and sanitation to 2500 orphans and their care givers in 15 remote villages in central Uganda.

title: 1 years swimming for a 100 disabled children
description: Bali Sports Foundation uses the power of sport to change the lives of people living with disabilities in Bali and East Indonesia.  With this campaign we can provide swimming programs for 100 children/youth living with disabilities for one year.

title: Because She is a Leader...
description: Because She's A Leader... is about celebrating the incredible power women have to affect positive change in Myanmar when they are in leadership roles! Our campaign aims to raise awareness and funding for women in Myanmar that aspire to step into leadership roles within policy-making and influential organisations, and to establish themselves as entrepreneurs. We need female leaders as it has a positive ripple on effect both economically and socially throughout communities and the country!

title: Puberty Education and Sanitary Kits for 350 Girls
description: Our data shows that most of the girls don't learn about puberty and menstruation from their mothers.  CCDO initiated a puberty program for girls and boys to learn about their growing bodies. CCDO is proud of this comprehensive 6 week program which teaches puberty as well as respect, communication, anti-domestic violence, human trafficking and healthy relationships. We give sanitary kits to the girls so that they can continue going to class during their periods.

title: Help communities through sustainable aquaculture
description: This project will empower fishers from marginalised fishing communities and enable them to maintain their livelihoods, while protecting and conserving Indonesia's marine environments.  At the LINI Aquaculture and Training Centre in North Bali, fishers will gain practical knowledge and skills in sustainable aquaculture practices for marine aquarium fish, best practice in fishery management, and coral reef restoration.

title: Support 15 Young Journalists in Bosnia-Herzegovina
description: Balkan Diskurs is a non-profit, multimedia platform created and run by a regional network of journalists, bloggers, multimedia artists, and activists who came together in response to the lack of objective, relevant, invigorating, independent media in the Western Balkans. We aim to train 15 aspiring journalists each year to produce high-quality articles, photo essays and documentaries to set a trend of journalistic integrity in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This campaign will support this year's trainees.

title: COLD TEMPS. to WARM HANDS - REFUGEE WINTER AID
description: Ilyas, Marvan and 7-months-old Halil are just 3 of all the children who fled from their homes with their families due to the conflict in Syria and the surrounding region. Ilyas (9) and Marvan (7) arrived to Turkey with minimal supplies and clothing. Putting their childhood aside, they now have to take care of themselves as well as their brother. Currently, Turkey hosts the most amount of refugees in the world: 2.2 million Syrian and 2800 Yazidis. THIS FUND WILL PREPARE THE REFUGEES FOR WINTER.

title: 10,000 VICTIMS: Unprecedented Case of CSA
description: Publishing a book and writing a script, revealing detail description of the most shocking case of child sexual abuse, will help to make the truth come out. The book will collect exclusive facts, evidence and testimony of witnesses who now prefer to keep silence

title: Help 50 disable children complete school in Tumu
description: the project will build a rehabilitation center in Tumu, This will rehabilitate 50 disable children per a year and means-trim into the regular school under the inclusion education policy. this will also give the confident to parents of  disable children the need not to discriminate / stigmatize them. it will also give them basic understanding to be able to coup with the regular school.

title: A MEAL-A-DAY FOR 200 NIGERIAN IDPs
description: Markengee Home for Orphans and widows plans to feed 200 Nigerian IDPs (Internally Displaced Persons) camping in Abuja, Nigeria between the month of  January or February 2016 as the case may be. This project aims at encouraging other foundations and the world at large to pay attention to the plight of these orphans and widows affected by the insurgency in the north-eastern part of the country.

title: Reduce work hours for Ecuadorian street children
description: This project gives attention to those children and adolescents who are at risk due to child labor. We aim to achieve the restoration of the rights of our children, such as the right to education, the right to health care and the right to identity. We do so by giving educational workshops in order to address the importance of education and to promote the reduction of their children's working hours.

title: Education & Nutrition for 200 children in Rwanda
description: The Kuraneza Early Childhood Development (ECD) project plans to provide care and basic education to 200 vulnerable kids of 3-6 years. The Kuraneza nursery supports underprivileged kids of underage and single mothers, orphans and from families living with HIV/AIDS in poverty-stricken Gasabo district.
