Effective Early Childhood Development helps kids at risk of poor development due to a lack of parental care and learning opportunities to break free from the poverty cycle in Rwanda.

title: Emergency medical clinic in rural Uganda
description: Basic emergency medical care is not available in our area of southeastern Uganda; the nearest clinic is over a day's walking distance.  Our clinic would offer first aid, immunizations, treat minor illnesses, and evaluate needs for further treatment on a local level for a large impoverished rural community that has no transportation options other than by foot.  One of our orphans who graduated nurse's training will manage the clinic. It is a life saving project for many who lack resources.

title: Connecting Detroit Youth to a Brighter Future
description: Despite the challenges in Detroit we have been able to reduce youth substance use.  90% of the students The Youth Connection serves graduate from high school and either go on to college, pursue a career, or enlist to serve our country. We expose youth to new opportunities to grow, learn and serve their communities that encourage them to see beyond their neighborhoods. We encourage, engage, and support families and our results speak to our passion for helping youth connect to a brighter future.

title: A Yellow School Bus for Rural Morocco
description: This project will establish a network of school buses to provide safe, accessible, and affordable transportation to and from local secondary schools for 660 children in Morocco's High Atlas Mountains, where more than 70% of the population lives in poverty. The first phase of the project will require two minibuses and the resources to manage and track the progress of the project throughout 1 year. The local commune and Morocco's Ministry of Education will join us in managing the bus systems.

title: FEMALE SHEEPS FOR 50 WOMEN IN THIES SENEGAL
description: This project is to provide women in the rural community of Thienaba sheeps for them to start a micro livestock. It is a project that we have already started since 2011 with the award of 76 sheep. The original idea was to make goats available to every woman, for two reasons, first the goat is less expensive to buy and reproduction is faster. Having this in mind, a project team moved to the village to discuss the feasibility with women.

title: Brighter Future For Haiti
description: Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day. Teach a man to fish and you feed him for lifetime. ~ Chinese proverbs. As of the today we have 250 students enrolled into our school. We currently teach our students in tents. We would now like to break ground and build a school building. This building will have a capacity hold over 600 students, have over 20 classrooms, a library, and a technology room.

title: Train refugees and stop xenophobia in South Africa
description: This project will build positive relations and reduce violence between refugees and South Africans. This will be achieved by training 24 refugees to become agents of social change; providing civic education training workshops, community dialogues, round-table discussions, and advocacy activities in local host communities.

title: Empower women and children in Pakistan on violence
description: Rozan House, where every brick counts.  A combined counselling and community centre and residential training facility for the empowerment of women and children in Pakistan on issues of violence.   Since Rozan's birth 15 years ago, we have been steadily raising an endowment fund with the aim of building Rozan House.    The donations would help to provide sustained and life transforming assistance to women and child survivors of violence and contribute to promoting peace and harmony in Pakistan.

title: Bring Clean Water to 1000 Ghanaian Villagers
description: This project installs hand pumps well and a complete solar paneled water pump  in the Upper East Region of Ghana, providing safe drinking water to benefit 1000 villagers in Nyorugu; an underprivileged village, where children are dying from  diseases caused by contaminated drinking water. It  empowers 200 women to  increase productivity through irrigation . It introduces health and sanitation by building 7 latrine pits, sponsors 7 orphans and keeps 31 girl- child in school.

title: Promoting social inclusion and fighting terrorism
description: The recent terrorist attacks in Paris remind us how important it is to promote tolerance and fight obscurantism. One of the root causes of such acts of violence is social exclusion in underpriviledged neighborhoods. Education is a powerful leverage for social change.  Today, PL4Y International intends to launch a sport based project to help children learn tolerance, empathy and develop life skills in 10 districts in the Paris region where poverty and social exclusion is strong.

title: Send 204 children with disability to school
description: East Eagle Foundation plans to build six classrooms, two latrines and one school office to provide  free education for children with disability. the primary beneficiaries of this school are 204 disabled children of Nsele City, in Kinshasa-DRC. The project will contribute to solving the problem of school exclusion suffered by disabled children  and wants to mitigate the risks associated with human rights violations for children with disabilities and barriers to access to quality education.

title: Train Kenyan Educators to Empower Youth
description: Support Youth Resilience! Help us train Kenyan Educators & continue to empower youth at the same time!   Building on the successful Kenyan pilot of our Transformative Citizenship Program (TCP), we are now training educators to lead this program. More students will also be served. TCP teaches the skill sets required for economic & social resilience. It includes: 1) course study, 2) work placement (e.g. farming) and 3) mentored economic enterprise.  Help us take TCP online - accessible to all!

title: Addressing Health Disparities for Kachin Women
description: GlobeMed at Dartmouth aims to improve the health of Kachin women and children who have been internally displaced due to ethnic conflict in Burma. We work with our partner, the Kachin Women's Association Thailand. This year, we will focus on creating an emergency fund for mothers who require surgery or hospitalization due to complications during childbirth. We will also continue to fund reproductive health trainings for adolescents and mobile medical care visits to IDP camps in Burma.

title: Guiding Costa Rica towards development by 2050
description: Association Strategy XXI Century designs a roadmap with the goal of advancing Costa Rica (C.R.) towards the level of a developed country by 2050. We facilitate a variety of science, technology and innovation (ST&I) proyects that foster the production of groundbreaking knowledge. In order to dynamically assess/adapt to the specific needs of C.R, we monitor and analize indeces on the status of these areas, stimulate engagement between key players and champion concrete actions that generate change.

title: New American Africans Youth Program
description: New American Africans is a community-based organization providing supportive services to recently arrived refugees in the greater Concord area and throughout the state.  Our goal is to help newcomers to feel welcomed and secure in their new community, particularly during the "post-resettlement period" when much of the federal-funded refugee assistance has ended.  We work with community members to address ongoing needs for English language learning, jobs, decent housing and successful schooling.

title: Clothe 500 Girls For School in Northern Nigeria
description: This project aims at encouraging and supporting girl-child education in Northern Nigeria and in the process stop early marriage, child labour, violence against girls and reduce poverty. Five hundred disadvantaged girls from the poorest homes will be empowered with school kits including school uniforms, schoolbags, socks, school shoes, water bottles and writing materials in order to encourage their parents and caregivers enrol them in schools so that they can take charge of their own destinies.

title: Send 210 orphan to school in Sierra Leone
description: This project will provide orphans permanent family home, quality education and healthcare in the community. Today, 210 sponsored children are benefiting from our education programs. You can sponsor a child growing up and ensure they receive all they need to prosper.

title: Help for educational support to 200 slum students.
description: Ahilya Bahuddeshiya Shikshan Prasarak Mandal is working for the uplifment of the poor students. We provide technical, vocational education and health awareness. Our target group is poor and needy students and backward people from the slums of Latur city from India. We are running shelter home for the women in distress.

title: Taking Care of 50 Vulnerable Sri Lankan Children
description: This project takes care of 50 vulnerable children living in eastern Sri Lanka by providing them with day care facitilies, creative opportunities, educational and learning tools, pharmaceutical drugs like vitamin and iron, worming treatment, footwear to prevent worm infection, one nutritious meal, uniforms and a committed and trained staff.

title: help nurture 1,200 young entrepreneurs in kenya
description: Hand in Hand Eastern Africa plans to inculcate an entrepreneurial culture among youths who are in primary schools within 23 Counties in Kenya by training them on entrepreneurship and helping them embrace self employment thus addressing issues of unemployment, drugs and substance abuse as well as being radicalized into terror groups

title: Educate deaf families/children in Vienna
description: kinderhaende (children's hands) is an organization devoted to deaf children and their families who intend to learn Austrian sign language (OeGS) and thus take the opportunity to use a language which perception does not depend on the ear. The project's goals are to fund five classes where children (6 months - 7 years) and parents learn OGS, get an affirmative perspective on deafness and grow a positive image of signing people.

title: Girls voices matter in Chicago and abroad
description: For 22 years, Global Girls, Inc. has provided arts education and presentation opportunities for girls ages 5 to 18. Through rigorous performance training, youth develop essential life skills: resilience, self-analysis, self-discipline and grit. They learn ensemble, negotiation and critical thinking skills helping them succeed on stage and in life. The mission is building personal capacities that nurture individual growth and inspire girls to use their talents for positive change for all girls.

title: Bulgarian Creative Writing Competition
description: The Bulgarian Creative Writing Competition in English aims to encourage and expand the creative thinking among Bulgarian students, as well as to enhance their English language writing skills. The goal is to create their own unique pieces of writing and to think "outside the box". This will be the 8th edition of the competition and each year more than 4000 students from the whole country take part.

title: Education for 50 disadvantaged Romanian children
description: The daily Socio-Educational Centre Pinocchio (Panciu, Romania) provides scholastic support and education to 50 children and youngsters of the most disadvantaged brackets of the local population, paying a special attention to the Roma minority. This project will support the formal and non formal educational activities (afterschool, literacy, creative workshops, education to hygiene), as well as the canteen service in order to foster a proper children's nutrition.

title: Train 100 Nepali youth monitors so aid saves lives
description: We will train 100 Nepali youth to become rapid response integrity builders. In 5 of the worst affected earthquake districts, these young people will access information on the relief effort to understand who is entitled to what and raise community awareness so they know how to access these vital services. With our oversight, the young people will be able to ensure that those most in need will receive the homes, healthcare and education they deserve and are entitled to.

title: Proudly Pushing the Global Sexual Rights Agenda
description: This project is no longer accepting donations. Please visit the SRI website for contact information.

title: Bees for pollination to improve lives in Ghana
description: Bees are amazing! They can help to solve poverty in more ways than one. In Ghana cashew farmers struggle to make ends meet. Bees can change this - twice over! They can give farmers honey to sell AND they can improve cashew nut yields through pollination. Research has shown that bees can increase cashew yields by 100%. This project will train some of the poorest farmers in Ghana to start beekeeping and secure a better future for their families - with the help of the honey bee.

title: Provide clean water for Akili Girls School, Kenya
description: Akili Preparatory School for Girls provides free quality education for underprivileged girls from Obunga Slum, Kisumu, Kenya. Deeper Missions Org, USA is matching all funds raised upto $10,000 to enable us to drill a permanent well 110 meters deep  to provide clean and safe drinking water for 30 underprivileged girls attending a boarding school in its Obambo Campus as well as over 300 households living in Obambo village, Kisumu, Kenya.

title: Train 5000  Farmers on Climate Change Agriculture
description: Edom Development Group Plans to train rural peasant farmers on climate change Agriculture using agro- forestry and conservation agriculture, providing free training and improved planting materials to 5000 rural farmers practicing traditional agriculture characterized by serious problem of land degradation, soil erosion, low-crops yield and falling soil fertility.

title: Support Innovation in Vulnerable Schools
description: In recent years, we have integrated classroom innovations from around the world into our work on the ground. Our Center for Educational Leadership recently launched successfully the "Redes de Tutoria" ("Tutorial Networks") and we have proposed to scale this innovation into 50 Schools from Chile of different contexts and show to Policy Makers "Yes, we can innovate and this is the way to do it". We invite to our donors to sponsor a vulnerable school in Chile to help us to implement this initiative

title: Veteran Scholarship Awards @ Literacyworks Center
description: The purpose of The Literacyworks Center is to assist underserved, below-basic-skills students in solving the many educational, personal and logistical challenges they must face to stay in school and succeed in work. The Center will provide advising support and need-based Adult Literacy Awards to our Veterans that will help them break their persistence barriers such as transportation, childcare and tuition. This will help to ensure our Vets complete their educational and career goals.

title: Sustaining Matses Indigenous Medicine - Phase II
description: The health of Amazonian peoples has always depended upon the wisdom of their elders. Passed down through the centuries, their knowledge of medicinal plants is a product of deep spiritual and physical ties to the natural world. Now with cultural change destabilizing even the most isolated societies, that knowledge is rapidly disappearing.  Acate and Matses indigenous elders have developed a three-point plan of action to maintain their self-sufficiency in health as they adapt to the outside world.

title: Education for 40 displaced indigenous Filipinos
description: The Bajau of Zamboanga, Philippines are among the last seafaring indigenous communities in the world. Their homes were burned to the ground due to armed conflict in their area in 2013. As they await permanent relocation, the Adult Capability Building Program of Cartwheel Foundation gives Bajau adults access to peace-advocating and culturally-relevant education in response to their expressed desire for continued learning of functional literacy and life skills.

title: Provide Washable  Pads for 4000 girls in Nigeria
description: The stigma and taboo of menstruation is a human rights issue. Lack of sustainable menstrual hygiene solutions push menstruating girls out of school leading to school dropout, Child Early Forced Marriage and gender inequality which is an obstacle to SDG 5.We are providing washable menstrual hygiene kits that last 3years and bathing soap that last 6months. We also talk to them about reproductive health education, rape, HIV/AIDS, contraceptive usage and also dispel the myths surrounding the issue.

title: Help 200 families defeat malaria in Ikota, Nigeria
description: Your donations will provide long-lasting insecticidal nets (mosquito bed nets), malaria testing using rapid diagnostic test kits and treatment for those who test positive, treatment courses for pregnant women to help prevent malaria during pregnancy, and training on malaria prevention and awareness for key community agents. The programme will target low-income families in the traditional community of Ikota, with a focus on the most vulnerable groups of pregnant woman and children under 5.

title: Rural outreach to 100 children with disabilities
description: KCDC is the only organisation providing physiotherapy, occupational therapy and speech therapy to children living with disabilities in Western Uganda. This project will provide outreach rehabilitation services to 100 children living with disabilities in the rural villages who would otherwise be unable to receive therapy, allowing them to reach their full potential by supporting and teaching them to become more independent, improve community inclusion and promote access to education.

title: Project Mosquito Net
description: Join us in providing insecticide-treated mosquito nets to protect Kenyans, especially young children, from mosquito bites. Malaria is caused by parasites that are transmitted through the bites of infected female anopheles mosquitoes.Prevention of malaria through the use of treated mosquito nets has been proved to be an effective control.

title: Urgent: Winter cold relief for refugees in Lebanon
description: This project will provide winter relief to Syrian, Palestinian and Iraqi refugees in Lebanon.  With your support, we will provide thermal gloves, hats, thick socks, hand and foot warmers, and coloring books/crayons/small balls for the children. Last year's winter brought severe cold and unlivable conditions with snow, high winds, rain and freezing temperatures. This program provides essential items, particularly for children and the elderly, who are most vulnerable.

title: Provide Clean Water in Northern Uganda
description: Lifeline seeks to transform the lives of rural Northern Ugandans through a holistic, highly replicable model for service delivery and the long-term sustainability of water points. This project will rehabilitate boreholes, teach proper hygiene and sanitation practices and provide income generation training in order to combat poverty and eliminate preventable water-borne diseases.

title: Help 50 HIV children to go to school in Uganda
description: childline Uganda is helping  HIV/AIDS positive children in Mityana Uganda.  This project will help in providing school dues and basic needs to 50 HIV/AIDS positive children in Mityana Uganda in order to improve their well-being and also to provide income generating activities to their households such that they can buy for themselves in the future. They also need transport to help them go to the hospital and get treatment since they move long distance to the hospital which reduces their life.

title: Bridging the Technology Gap in Kenya and Denver
description: Students in Kenya and at-risk students in Denver have the right to a high quality education and resources. Technology education teaches tools to communicate and collaborate. Through our Learning to Connect and Connecting to Learn program, students in Kenya and at-risk Denver students are working together to learn STEAM skills. The work they do is building critical thinking skills and letting them learn how to work with a diverse group. These are necessary for 21st century learners

title: Send 50 children to school in Guatemala!
description: This project will allow 50 children to go to school in Guatemala for 1 year, including all stationary, school activities and healthy meals under the supervision of certified and friendly local teachers.

title: Conserve orangutans near four Sumatran villages
description: Sustained conservation education is vital to save wild orangutans that are critically endangered. This project will build an education center for sustainable living near the Gunung Leuser National Park in North Sumatra, Indonesia, to provide a venue for hundreds of villagers near the park to learn about ways to conserve the many wild orangutans living nearby, reduce primate-human conflict, and obtain training in sustainable agricultural techniques that are less destructive to the environment.

title: Provide good education to Brazilian poor students
description: The project impacts on public school students from Vitoria, Brazil, with low family income. These students receive cost-free elementary Portuguese, Mathematics and English classes in the NGOs facilities. This way, they get far more opportunities by being involved in the Project that any other students from public schools in Brazil, even making it possible for one of them to earn a full-time scholarship in the best private school of our State.

title: Help Jamaican Students Become Organic Growers
description: Through our 'Young Soldiers for Food Security' program, Farm Up Jamaica gives students, from many agriculture schools the opportunity to gain practical farming experience by working on Organic farms. We provide them with transportation, room & board, and a stipend to inspire them to create a vision that can positively impact their communities while preparing them to become Jamaica's next generation of environmentally-conscious farmers.

title: Teaching Children Human Rights in Liberia
description: What good are your rights if you don't know you have them? Our program to teach civics, rights awareness and conflict resolution in selected schools and communities is already funded, but we need help printing copies of the Constitution for the students. Liberia is a country still recovering from more than a decade of civil wars and EBOLA outbreak. Help us give citizens the tools to rebuild their own democracy by bringing civics and rights education to every school in Liberia by fall 2016.

title: Training 20 Adults in the Poorest Area of Bulgaria
description: Phoenix Inspire is a proactive charity based in Vidin.  P.I. strives to teach and develop  skills to disadvantaged young adults through two social enterprises in north west Bulgaria.  By working and learning in one of these social enterprises our trainees will learn and understand how to make a wide range of food products and how to serve customers correctly so that when they leave the training program they will have the skills and knowledge to enable them to progress into employment.

title: Rehabilitate & Reconstruct Nepal Handicraft Sector
description: This project will help develop handicraft sector in general and undertake rehabilitation of artisans, painters, workers, members of handicraft family and reconstruction cultural heritage sites in particular.

title: Clean water & Toilets to 100 Children in Nyalenda
description: SLEC will connect clean water and two 10,000 liter tanks, construct five toilets and five bathrooms for 100 children, installation of electricity,  construct three classrooms and cooking area, purchase books and furniture.  Construct a sleeping area  for 30 toddlers   The Children in Nyalenda slum will be healthier (free of water borne diseases) receive nutritious meals and quality education.

title: Build a School for 200 Children with Albinism
description: 90% of people with Albinism in Uganda live in rural areas where they can't grow their own food because of the danger from the Ugandan sun. They also face danger from Albino hunters who use them in ritual sacrifices. This project will set up and equip a vocational school to provide vocational education and life skills training to 200 young people with Albinism in rural Uganda. The training will help these vulnerable Ugandans develop skills to run their own businesses and become more independent

title: City in the Community Soccer Program
description: One third of children in New York City's public elementary schools are obese or overweight. The City in the Community Soccer Program combines soccer with education about health and nutrition, in order to help young people to improve their fitness and live healthier lives.   Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help City in the Community Soccer Program to continue the brilliant work of the leaders and give them a platform to help even more young people in New York City.

title: Save Malnourished Mother & Children In Sunderban
description: BTS aims to save 500 malnourished mother and children by supporting nutrition food supply and medical care for safe delivery. The project aims to improve awareness on exclusive breast feeding and child caring among young mothers between nineteen and twenty five years of age group. It will impact on reducing IMR and MMR rates among the mothers from fishermen or forest-fringe community people living deplorably in Sunderban.

title: Build 5 houses in rural Nicaragua
description: This project will help build 5 houses near Leon, Nicaragua. Families interested in having a house built complete an application and must assist in the construction, provide lunches to the foremen and pay 25% of the cost back interest free over 4 years to ensure the programs sustainability and help to fund more houses. Most houses are built with the help of high school and college groups traveling to Nicaragua to learn more about the culture and history of this beautiful place.

title: Give Hope to Mexican Children with Cancer
description: Since 1990, we have helped more than 12,600 low-income girls, boys and young people who suffer from cancer in Mexico. With your help, we can continue to do so for the 1,200 children we have in active treatment and the 4,800 children we have in present remission.

title: Improving Health Services for People of Kilimanjar
description: Pamoja Tunaweza Women's Center (PTWC) provides quality and affordable health care to the people of Kilimanjaro Region. Our locally staffed clinic provides primary outpatient care to over 250 patients each month and our bi-annual two week medical outreach activities provide free care for 100-200 patients each day. We also provide support to the most vulnerable through income generating projects, payment of school fees, and health education to address the social determinants of health.

title: Reclaiming Radicalized Youth in India
description: Gandhian dialogue on radicalization, education and training in his vision and methods of nonviolence; visiting human suffering with love and compassion in the conflict zone of Jammu & Kashmir and in radicalized tribal belt of eastern India has built community peace-infrastructures in 16 districts; motivated youth away from ideologies of hate and violence; 100+ dedicated Gandhi Peace-Makers resolved this year 21 violent conflicts. Radicalization tended at its root can stop breeding extremism.

title: Integrate 300  Deaf children in Addis Ababa
description: This project plans to provide educational and psycho-social support for 300 Deaf students who are deprived of socio-economic opportunities in the society they belong.  The project will benefit Deaf children and youth through tutorial, sign language training, socal work skills training and provision of educational materials.

title: Virtual school for children in Ukrainian
description: We are working to make good things happen.  This project will create short educational videos in Ukrainian language for children, in order to simplify teachers' work and free parents' time. Teachers can use them as supplementary material to explain the topics in the classroom. They briefly reveal a topic of the main subjects of the school curriculum. Videos are created with the help of the latest software that allows to make high quality picture and clear sound.

title: Female Adult LIteracy Classes in Timbuktu
description: Fund a Female Adult Literacy class in the village of Tourari so that the women of this village can enjoy the hope that comes with reading and empower their children to prioritize education.

title: Educate 300 Girls in District Malakand KP Pakistan
description: This project will help the poorest girls in district Malakand Khyber Pakhtun Khwa for getting their basic education.This project will provide uniform,bags,books & stationary ,shoes and other educational materials as well.Due to poverty and rigid religious community most of  the parents neither afford nor allow their girls to send them to school.They prefer early marriages.This project will not only educate these 300 girls but will help in solving the social problem of early marriages.

title: Support for destitute children
description: Sunils Social Services Home starts in the year 2006 with a sole aim to serve the destitute and starved children and made its holy efforts to bring the children's on to the requirement of the society either in educational and competitiveness so as to further progress the society.since 2006 more than 200 children were benefited through our organization,many children's were graduated.Our main aim is to provide quality education in English medium for orphan children to fulfill their ambition in life

title: Give a Gift to Children Living in Poverty & Crisis
description: You can make a difference in the lives of people who are fighting to escape poverty and recover from crisis. What can your holiday gift do? Concern helps people fleeing conflict, persecution and poverty in 29 of the poorest places across the globe. Gifts like warmth, health, and opportunity, often taken for granted, are essential and urgently needed.  You can help children and their families do more than just survive this winter - you can give them the hope and resources to thrive.

title: Prevention of armed violence 500 adolescents Peru
description: This is an initiative driven from Grupo de iniciativa Nacional por los derechos del Nino (GIN) focused on teenagers victims of crime violence in Callao. The project provides: Community Empowerment, urban interventions and economic entrepreneurship for either teenagers or single mothers suffering from violence at high-risk sectors of Callao, Lima, Peru. They do not have access to work training nor basic employment.

title: Women Empowerment in Sierra Leone
description: IBREA will work with the Ministry of Social Welfare, Gender and Children Affairs to provide our brain-based holistic education training to selected groups of women as well as to social workers who are working with women. In the aftermath of the ebola crisis and the recent floods that damaged the country, on top of the already existing scars left by a long war, Sierra Leonean women are particularly  in need of support to grow their confidence and strengthen their role in society.

title: Train 50 women teachers in Uganda to educate 1000s
description: GWI is working to increase the number of girls that go to school. In rural areas of Uganda, a huge number of girls are not enrolled in school or forced to drop out, in part due to a lack of women teachers. Our project will support 50 young women from rural Uganda to become qualified secondary school teachers and ambassadors for girls' education. This will provide access to quality education for 2000 children per year and vital role models to improve girls' enrollment.

title: Build School Gardens for 1800 Youth in Burundi
description: This project will start 4-H youth school gardening programs at 9 elementary schools in rural Burundi, a country that is the 3rd poorest in the world and working to heal from decades of civil war. Teachers, administrators, and community members will be trained in 4-H, Play for Peace, and using school gardens to teach students. Youth will develop leadership, conflict resolution, and science skills through this hands-on 4-H programming while also growing food to address poverty and hunger.

title: Help Rescued Monkeys in Arizona
description: This project is to renovate and expand habitats for rescued monkeys.  The structures in Monkey Village have provided a safe and secure home for several years. However, it is time to make necessary improvements and expand existing structures to provide the best home possible to these deserving primates. The majority of these primates were rescued from one of the worst animal hoarding cases ever witnessed in Arizona.

title: Yachana Foundation Fund
description: Yachana Foundation is a non-profit organization that promotes education and sustainability in the Ecuadorian Amazon. This institutional development fund allows donors to contribute to a general fund that will be used to provide funding to sustain education enrichment and development projects that are the mainstay of the foundation.

title: Provide 50 kids a future and education in Nepal
description: We are installing Mini-Schools in the villages of the Yangri Valley. The goal of these schools is tri fold: (1) recommencing the children's schooling and thus simply reintroducing the daily structure and rhythm of school into their lives, (2) preparing the children academically to enter quality schooling within a year, (3) to keep the children from child-labor and positively impact their families and communities. Students are taught by a HimalayanLife teacher, ensuring entry-level knowledge.

title: Improving HIV Treatment with Nutrition Support
description: Food security and nutrition are crucial for successful HIV support and treatment programs. This project will dually benefit Alive Medical Services' Organic Gardening Program and Nutrition Support Program, which work in synergy to support thousands of our clients with access to well-balanced nutrition and livelihood skills.

title: Help provide healthcare for 50 vulnerable in Abuja
description: Nasiru, a laborer needs to go to the hospital for an injury he sustained while breaking granite rocks into tiny stones. He has no money and no insurance. His family depends on sales from the stones. He resorts to traditional herbs and self medication. With little contributions Nasiru and his family can access healthcare without paying cash. Many people die because they cannot pay hospital bills. TPL want to change that for individuals and communities using micro-health insurance.

title: Poultry farm for improving incomes and nutrition
description: The project overall objective is to improve the health of orphans and children living with HIV through promoting community/home based incomes and nutritional education and care through poultry farming.

title: Preventive oral health program for rural children
description: This program will benefit more than 6,000 children between 6-12 years old in rural areas of Guatemala, providing preventive dental care to children without access to dental services. These children in poverty and extreme poverty have mostly never visited a dentist and have high rates of oral diseases. Not carried out this program probably they will never have the opportunity to attend their oral problems.

title: Alo, prematuritate! / Hello, prematurity!
description: The project addresses to a serious social problem, found both internationally and especially in Romania, namely, infant mortality and prematurity effects on the newborn and his family. In Romania, 1 in 10 children is born prematurely, so we could help 20.000 children and their families, yearly. We'll give professional advice, information and moral support to parents of premies via free phone line, within the project "Alo, prematuritate! / Hello, prematurity!" (Call Center).

title: Empowerment through Technology Training in Uganda
description: This project will expand U-TOUCH technology training in Uganda to enable 200 Ugandans to lift themselves out of poverty. Youth will learn computer, life skills and entrepreneurship skills utilizing laptops and mobile devices. Computer skills training is required in schools and for employment.  A certificate of completion from U-TOUCH helps applicants move to the front of the line. Smartphone and tablet use is increasing and specific training is needed for their use business.

title: Empower a Girl in Long Beach and Anaheim, CA
description: 4GIRLS conducts two workshops in Southern California, bringing together middle-school girls from diverse backgrounds and experiences for a weekend of inspiration and empowerment.  Our 2020 workshop is structured around the theme "Bold" and our quarterly empowerment events reinforce the workshop theme. At a critical time when building self-esteem is paramount, 4GIRLS provides young girls opportunities to access their strengths and voices, and to develop their identities.

title: Reducing Child Labor through education
description: The project is centered at child labor, specifically children bonded in brick kiln industry. The proposed idea is the result of the applicants' experience of three decades which shows that when bonded children get education, they become aware of their rights, are able to handle basic accounts (i.e. calculate income, interest, and other information which is critical to reduce bondage). So, IDA will strive in escaping the bonded children from slavery through providing education at their doorsteps.

title: Get emergency help to injury victims in Bangladesh
description: In Bangladesh, there are no emergency medical services (like 911), and as a result more than 82% of critically injured people die before they reach a hospital. Children and vulnerable populations such as those living or working in the streets (rickshaw-pullers, informal laborers, food vendors, etc.) are disproportionally affected. CriticaLink trains local volunteers as emergency First Responders and uses mobile technology to help them respond quickly so they can save lives in their community.

title: Educate 200 Visually Challenged College Students
description: The Project Vision is an initiative of the HOPE Society to help the visually challenged persons who constitute 39 Million people in the world out of which 15 Million are in India. Our Vision is "Let Everyone See" and the Mission is "To provide opportunity for every visually challenged to gain sight and for the permanently visually challenged to live a full life". To realise this mission Project Vision is focusing on the higher education of the visually challenged through the present initiative.

title: Pregnancy Prevention for 6,000 Refugee Girls
description: This project will provide accurate and relevant sexual and reproductive information to at least 6,000 adolescent youth in Kakuma Refugee Camp. The project will also facilitate youth-friendly access to secure HIV testing and family planning services. SAVIC will train 60 community peer educators, and provide Curriculum-based sexual and reproductive health Training for 600 refugee youth. The project will also train 240 parents and community leaders on adolescents' reproductive health.

title: Needs of Destitute Home
description: Destitute Home For Children of age group 06-18 we are running from 2002.Home is running from Permission of State Government.Children are getting all the facilities like Food,Shelter,Cloth and Educational Material with facility of School we Provide them.Destitute children are comes from poor family in Home.we Provide them all facilities and make them a self Reliant in their life.200 Children are living in home.

title: Train 50 young transgenders of Khulna, Bangladesh
description: 50 young transgender will receive skill training on beauty parlor, embroidery and cattle fattening works for alternative livelihood means. They are habituated by taking food and household materials forcefully from the local market and dance and sing from door to door with new born baby at their lap. They have no alternative opportunity to be rehabilitated. Though they are recognized by the govt. as the 3rd gender but no step has taken to bring them back to the main stream of life.

title: Protect, feed, and educate 114 rescued children
description: Grandsons of Abraham is feeding, educating and providing a safe environment to over 114 children rescued from the streets of Mombasa, many of whom have been victims of abuse - sexual exploitation, trafficking and child labour.

title: DREAM Mentoring Program
description: This project will ensure that our youth succeed in education and life through mentoring, cultural activities and community outreach. The project also helps to alleviate child hunger, by providing free nutritious after-school meals and snacks daily.

title: 1,000 Who Care: Giving Kids Hope For Their Futures
description: The only place to help kids in our city has been ruined. So Kids are surrounded by loss, violence,  hopelessness and no organizations to help guide them through the problems they face in today's time. With bullying, peer pressure, suicide and other issues on the rise, there is one center that does save and shape kids lives through the arts and education. With your help, Future World can stay open and continue the great work they do with teaching kids to be confident builders of their futures.

title: Support 2000 Children with Medical care in Busoga
description: Busoga Yaiffe plans to build medical center and find ever lasting solution, when the vulnerable chidren get free medical care it reduces on infant deaths and also mulnutrition. By the end of our project we should have postive impact on community by the mothers. the benefiacries are children between 0 to 14 years. we shall purchuse drugs and medical equipments and after we shall build up a medical center with time.

title: Mainstream 350 IntellectuallyChallenged Youngsters
description: Jeevoday  Special School for the Mentally Handicapped runs by Jeevoday Education Society. It is a Registered Educational Institution imparting education to the mentally challenged children of Nagpur and adjacent areas. To bring about awareness among the people regarding prevention, early detection, intervention, and rehabilitation of persons with disabilities we established the special school for the mentally challenged on 2nd October 1989.

title: Empower Hundreds of Queer Youth in California
description: LGBT youth are disproportionally disenfranchised in all aspects of American society, including education. To combat that, this year, Bay Area Youth Summit plans to host a pay-what-you-can summer class series taught by LGBT* youth for LGBT* youth. Our class will give youth in the queer community the opportunity to get paid to educate their peers, while giving other queer youth the opportunity to extend their academic pursuits outside of the classroom, at little or no cost.

title: Help Ukraine's refugees to make a new start
description: Psychological integration workshops, art-therapy, humanitarian aid and other rehabilitation and practical help for more than 200 Ukraine's refugee families. The project is aimed to help more than 1000 internally displaced people, basically children and women, from different parts of Ukraine who have been facing the horror of war.

title: Snorkeling Shop for Oracabessa Bay Fish Sanctuary
description: The Oracabessa Bay Fish Sanctuary is helping to ensure the sustainable livelihood of local fishers.  Since 2011 we have seen a 1,300% increase in fish biomass and fishers are now catching more pounds of fish outside of the sanctuary than they were before within the Bay.  Our snorkeling project will purchase equipment needed in order to establish an income generating snorkeling tour business which will support Sanctuary operations.

title: Helping Women Survive Cancer
description: Expand the services of the Women's Center of Greater Lansing by creating a program that will focus on psycho-social, holistic, person-centered support during and post-treatment to cancer survivors and their families. Offered in a warm and inviting setting outside of a hospital and nearby the main medical facilities in the area, this kind of support from professionals is shown to improve health outcomes and quality of life for cancer survivors and their families by going beyond medical treatment.

title: Build an environmental training center in Moldova
description: This project aims to construct an environmental training center in an emerging Eco-village in Moldova. The center will serve as a regional hub for practical education in the fields of organic agriculture, energy efficiency, eco-construction and community development. It will include a kitchen/dining area and meeting space to accommodate up to 60 individuals at a time.

title: Protect 84 children through summer camp- Argentina
description: This summer camp will protect 84 argentinian children who face economic hardship, marginalization and vulnerability. It will give them the opportunity to break away from their difficult life circumstances, even temporarily, and to be able to enjoy their childhood , learning and having fun in a safe and respectful environment.

title: Support Nearly 2,000 Homeless Women in DC
description: N Street Village serves nearly 2,000 homeless and low-income women each year. We aim to help these women claim their highest quality of life by offering a broad spectrum of services, housing, and advocacy in an atmosphere of dignity and respect. We help women achieve stability and make meaningful gains in their housing, income, employment, mental health, physical health, and addiction recovery.

title: Support Social Care Center for Ukrainian refugees
description: Just in one day their lives were turned into hell ... Hastily having collected the most precious things, crying children woken up at night by tears of fear and horror in the eyes of their parents... that's what the war in Ukraine did with 1.5 million people who, according to the statistics of United Nation Office, suffered from the hostilities in the South-East of Ukraine.

title: Help to spread Terrorist attack Victims Stories
description: Renaissance Foundation for Social Innovation, Pakistan works to counter Islamic Extremism through creating digital content. Every day young people are becoming prey to extremist ideology. There is a need to save younger generations. We believe that extremism can only be challenged through raising awareness among youth and general public in Pakistan. Keeping in view this context, we are launching a campaign to collect stories of former extremists and those who survived. Please join campaign

title: Refugee Crisis - Haiti Returnees and Deported
description: A critical humanitarian situation is occurring in Haiti caused by the deportation and returnees from the Dominican Republic.  A large group of the refugees (men, women and children) in the South East department have no where to go and are living in temporary camps.  Heart to Heart International is needing your help to supply food, water, shelter and medical attention to those in crisis.

title: Prevention of child trafficking
description: Trafficking unfortunately concerns many children. The main factors are poverty, problems faced by children at school or in their families, the ignorance of the laws on trafficking and its reality. This projet takes place in Togo (District of Tchamba) and concerns 62 villages. It will help 34.000 children and 26.000 adults. It consists in : raising awareness among the communities and families; the enhancement of the family and youth economic security; providing support to children victims...

title: Invest in the Future of 20 New Youth Leaders!
description: Our Fly By Light youth program provides supportive and positive spaces for young people to learn how to peacefully resolve conflict. Fly By Light focuses on education, social justice, and artistic expression as a means for changing communities for the better, and places the onus on youth participants to take leadership roles in doing so. Funds raised for this project will help us create a new program site in Washington D.C. where we will help more students find and shine their light.

title: Support to 20 SMART girls in rural areas of Bosnia
description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is known for having a lot of smart young people, but all of them do not have the same possibilities for advancement in education and life. This applies in particular to young girls in rural areas. The most effective way to assist vulnerable and disadvantaged girls in rural areas of Bosnia and Herzegovina is by providing them with a quality education, mentoring support, and educational packages. This is what CCSP is doing for women and girls through its Mentoring program

title: Recovery Support for Chennai Flood Survivors
description: In the completion of 6 months on Chennai and Cuddalore flood hits, ROSI has implemented the relief works successfully in both areas and rehabilitation works as House repairing, tuition centres and educational materials, Alternative livelihood training  and Income generation are continued.

title: offer work out sessions for 225 mentally disabled
description: Mentally disabled people tend to have a more fragile health condition than the average population, which hinders their full and effective participation in society. Regular physical exercises can help improve their overall condition but those belonging to socially disadvantaged families can not afford the costs of a health club. This project will provide 225 mentally disabled people with biweekly work out sessions in an adapted fitness facility and under the guidance of a qualified professional.

title: One Love's Mission to End Relationship Violence
description: The One Love Foundation's mission is to end relationship violence by educating, empowering, and activating young people in a movement for change.  Created to honor Yeardley Love, a UVA senior who was beaten to death by her ex-boyfriend just weeks before graduation.  After her death, her family and friends were shocked to learn the statistics that 1 in 3 women and 1 in 4 men will be in an abusive relationship in his or her lifetime. One Love's work today is dedicated to changing those statistics.

title: Hope of Education For 100 Poor  SriLankan Children
description: The purpose of this project is to provide educational facility for the 100 poor rural children. They belong to very poor families and their parents cannot provide them education. It is necessary to educate these poor children otherwise they will ruin their future by involving in sex trade, child labor, smuggling, and drugs. You can give them bright future. At the end of this project, we will be able to give them a new future and they will be able to live their lives as respectable human beings.

title: Sustaining the Great Colorado Springs Conservatory
description: The Colorado Springs Conservatory is the Pikes Peak region's preparatory school for the performing arts. It was founded 21 years ago by Linda Weise, a graduate of both Oberlin and Julliard, with the goal of creating access to the arts for all students, ages 3-19, among various other populations. Currently, we offer programming in, but not limited to, voice, theatre, orchestra, instrumental music, music theory, dance, recording arts. Our courses are a leadership program disguised as the arts.

title: Filipino Youth Leadership for Community Resilience
description: R3ADY Asia-Pacific, a project of the New Venture Fund, will partner with Central Visaya Net and Corporate Network for Disaster Response to implement a project in Haiyan affected communities to build disaster-resilient communities with zero casualties through trainings, workshops, and development of contingency plans.  The project's key focus areas will be developing Community Youth Leaders to promote and build communities' capacity to become more resilient in the face of the next natural hazard.

title: Where Angels Play - Playgrounds Coming in 2016!
description: Where Angels Play provides children with safe and fun places to play in communities in need.  The playgrounds serve the additional benefit of being built to honor the lives of those that have left us much too soon.  We endeavor to create joyful places to play... to provide hope, recovery, and a return to family values in the wake of tragedy and violence.

title: CityArts Creative Urban Arts and Youth Program
description: Providence CityArts helps over 900 kids find their creative pathway to a positive future and a just society.  For our Southside youth, where 1 out of 3 children live in poverty, arts access can be life changing.  CityArts is a NAHYP award-winning agency, with free classes that help youth develop lifelong skills and habits of inquiry--to explore ideas through art/design, media, music and dance.    Creativity, imagination and innovation are the tools we provide to succeed in school and in life!

title: Help Sustainable Reforestation in Costa Rica
description: Farmers on the Caribbean Coast  are becoming succesful for the first time  in their reforestation efforts thanks to technical asistance and training offered by ASIREA. Without this support,  most farmers prefer to invest in other productive activities  that cause deforestation and degadation of the tropical forest. Help us to help farmers improve their income while reforesting the world.

title: Serve 2000 meals to those in need in Silver Spring
description: Shepherd's Table provides help to people who are homeless or in need by providing meals, social services, medical support, clothing, and other assistance in an effective and compassionate manner. The food services program is at the core of our mission, and this ongoing project ensures that we can continue to provide nutritious meals to our community.  During the pandemic, we continued serving meals every day, and started a new program to distribute meals to families and children in need.

title: Green Jobs for Girls Sexual and Reproductive Right
description: This community project intends to tackle development challenges facing girls in Cameroon by giving an adequate educational training and information on their sexual and reproductive rights. The community project is designed to empower young women through multidimensional training and education opportunities in a way that help them moving out of the existing abject poverty. It is expected to enable young women to recognize the potential, possibilities that exist

title: MADD Help Line - helping 3K drunk driving victims.
description: Drunk driving kills 10,000 people in the United States each and every year and injures 290,000 more. The MADD Help Line helps those who are impacted by drunk and drugged driving crashes when they need it. We are there for those who have been injured in crashes, for the loved ones of those who have been killed, and for concerned citizens who want to help end the violent crime of drunk driving. We want to raise $13,535, the annual cost of running the Help Line on nights and weekends.

title: Provide holiday gifts to 500 foster youth
description: For foster youth, the holidays can be a very somber time. Seeing families enjoying the season can be a painful reminder of the holiday celebrations they never had. Every year UFC offers several hundred foster youth a warm and welcoming environment to celebrate the festive season. We need your help to ensure that the youth in our programs receive something during this special time of year, just like the children in our own families. Yours may be the only gift they receive.

title: Access to clean water for 2500 villagers in kenya
description: The project will install 8 water hand pumps in Tsiekuru Village. This is in addition to 5 pumps installed in phase I.   2,800 individuals plus 1,500 herds of cattle and 4,000  goats which form the prime livelihood in this arid and semi-arid region will enjoy  access safe drinking water.  Women will be saved from walking long distances, outbreaks of cholera will reduce and young girls will concentrate in their education.

title: Empower 19 youths living on the streets in Mexico
description: This project will help JUCONI Foundation purchase a facility where a permanent Youth House can be established for young men aged 14-18 affected by family violence, who experience marginalized situations, extreme poverty and/or live on the streets in Mexico. Within the Youth House, JUCONI will provide youth with long-term personalized educative-therapeutic interventions that will prepare them to live an independent life free of violence and become fully integrated into society as young adults.

title: Help 600 homeless Peruvian children
description: Your donation will benefit more than 600 children and homeless teenagers with drug problems , social risk and with family problems through sport of Lima Kids Futsal League. Help us continue this turorial vulnerable children from Peru to better life skills , better opportunities and a better future through the lessons learned as part of a team.

title: Support Oregon Athletes with Physical Disabilities
description: Oregon Disability Sports provides loaner equipment for 200+ Oregon and SW Washington State youth (aged 7-18) and adults with physical disabilities resulting from spinal cord injury, amputation, polio, and cerebral palsy and other illnesses so they may participate in adaptive sports. Additional equipment is needed so more athletes can participate in wheelchair basketball, wheelchair rugby, hand cycling, swimming, kayaking, goal ball, and track & field.

title: Provide Education in Rural Communities of Morelos
description: El Penon and Montefalco schools provide integral education to children of rural communities of Morelos, Mexico. The Model develops 3 main aspects to achieve superior educational level and personal development; extracurricular activities, parenting school and mentoring program. Through these aspects, we change the way children learn and interact with their with their communities, hence becoming a change agent and social development catalyst.  This project aims to provide funding for scholarships

title: HIV Services for 300 Myanmar Gay Men & Sex Workers
description: Our project, run by and for gay men and sex workers in Myanmar, will provide free, rapid HIV tests for more than 300 gay men and sex workers in Yangon, Myanmar. Myanmar is one of the poorest countries in the world, and homosexuality and sex work here are still illegal. For the approximately 30 of those 300 people tested who will find out they are HIV+, the project will support them to initiate and stay on HIV treatment for a year.

title: Vonk
description: The project  The Vonk project has been founded to help food bank clients or people receiving debt relief support. Vonk focuses on support in dealing with clients' financial problems and support in the organization of their money situation. For instance, clients can receive support in administration, filling in tax papers or other institutional forms. Getting your financial situation back on track will create room for other things in your life. Vonk helps people gain control over their lives.

title: A Village at a time in Malawi: Assets for Incomes!
description: We want to adopt simple mechanization through productive assets to increase productivity in response to identified domestic and regional markets for staples. The initiative, will fast-track commercial farming of ongoing smallholder farm enterprise efforts through selected farm implements. We target social villages that and graduate them into trading-blocs; Commercial Villages. Farmers are equipped as market players and women or youth are also suppliers for direct payment by various buyers.

title: Help children at risk develop their talents.
description: Our organization is fighting the lack of education for children at risk of poverty. We have created a unique School of Arts and Crafts where we educate gifted children from the most neglected and marginalized sections of society. We aim to overcome children's deficits and traumas accumulated in them from their previous way of life. We also aim to provide high quality education and individual training in the arts - theater, music, dance,

title: Education & shelter for homeless children in India
description: Help 4500 homeless children in India reclaim their childhood through the Rainbow Homes Program. The concept is simple: unused rooms in government schools are refurbished and converted into Rainbow Homes, where all needs of the children are taken care of - schooling, recreation, shelter, nutrition, tuition, healthcare, and most importantly, love and care. The idea is to ensure a safe and happy childhood for these children. We are supporting 2600 girls and 900 boys through separate interventions.

title: Help 8 disabled ophans to have a real Christmas
description: This project will give disabled children a chance to pass Christmas holidays outside the orphanage in a homey atmosphere. All children will have various workshops including art, theater classes and music sessions. All of them will be surrounded by the personal care of a volunteer. But the most important thing - all of them will have a real family holiday with people who love them and care about them.

title: Kicking for Change
description: Kicking For Change will use football as a catalyst to get able-bodied and disabled children back into education. Children will be engaged in a 48 week programme combining football sessions with literacy, numeracy and life-skills, with the aim of giving 500 children the skills and support they need to get back to school.    Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help us reach even more young people in Cape Coast.

title: The Mobile Solar Computer Classroom
description: The Mobile Solar Computer Classroom is helping bridge the digital divide in Uganda by taking computer skills to remote schools and libraries across Uganda.  Maendeleo Foundation crisscrosses Uganda taking computers and computer training to rural areas where most children and youth have never experienced modern technology.    Through a digital literacy curriculum, our training builds; computer, basic literacy, critical thinking and creativity, skills of children, youth, teachers and librarians.

title: Redcross Amsterdam: Support Refugees
description: Since september 2015 thousands of refugees entered the Netherlands seeking safety.  The Redcross Amsterdam provides emergency  shelter, medical assistence and basic needs like warm winter clothing, blankets, toiletries.   Our support doesn't stop with relieve aid. In the coming years we will support these people any way we can in picking up their lives and  trying to make  a future for themselves and their children. Finances needed depend on accurate needs  and the precarity of the situation

title: Bringing the Girls Inc. experience to more girls
description: Serving girls in the United States & Canada with intensive, holistic, long-term programming that treats each girl as an individual, your investment will help bring the Girls Inc. Experience to more girls, whose needs are not currently being met with a deep level of support. Across the U.S. & Canada, Girls Inc. is providing real solutions to the unique issues girls face. The Girls Inc. Experience consists of people, an environment & programming that together empower girls to succeed.

title: Monthly Support for Food and Shelter
description: During 2015, several children have graduated 12th grade and gone on to higher education or vocational training. We seek continuing support for food and shelter for the remaining 10 children.

title: Furnish a Home with A Wider Circle
description: You can make a difference by assisting in the furnishing of rooms or entire homes for families living in great need in this region. Our goal is to furnish 100 homes through this project!

title: Build new bathrooms for a village in Uganda
description: KUZA Leadership students will construct new bathrooms for an impoverished village in Eastern Uganda.  50 Ugandan high school and University students will clean the community health center and visit and encourage the sick.  They will conduct workshops for the youth in the village to encourage kids to stay in school and not get pregnant.  Cleaning the village wells and paths and constructing new, clean toilet facilities for the community will be completed in January 2016!

title: Feeding America Fight Hunger in US
description: The Feeding America network is the nation's largest domestic hunger-relief organization. Together with individuals, charities, businesses and government we can end hunger. Through a network of 200 food banks and 60,000 food pantries and meal programs, Feeding America provides meals to more than 40 million people each year.

title: Use Soap to Empower 60 Rape Survivors in Mali
description: This project will help 60 survivors of the brutal conflict in northern Mali to recover by producing and selling soap. Our Malian partner, Sini Sanuman (Healthy Tomorrow) in Bamako will purchase the ingredients for 5,000 bars of high-quality shea butter soap. The women will then learn how to make and sell the soap at Sini Sanuman's center in Bamako. This will bolster their confidence and earn them a living. It will also show Malians how women can contribute to peace in their war-torn country.

title: Give a worthy old age to 300 elderly in Colombia
description: Fundacion Nino Jesus plans to offer a better quality life for the elderly in Bogota, especially in Engativa. The main purpose is to provide them with the tools so they are able to develop their skills whilst being in a medically supervised environment with a professional team providing them healthy snacks in accordance with their nutritional requirements and medical conditions.

title: Help Protect 75,000 Acres of Congo Basin Forest
description: Often described as the lungs of Africa, the vast forest expanse of the Congo Basin is the world's 2nd largest tropical rainforest. Spanning 8 countries, the forests are home to an array of wildlife, including forest elephants and mountain gorillas, as well as numerous indigenous groups. Yet, mining and agricultural interests threaten wildlife, forests and people. Your support will enable us to train communities in Cameroon to manage these lush landscapes, conserving them for future generations.

title: Ecological  school produce food and trees for life
description: Establishing school gardens and reforestation plans are implemented in 10 rural communities from Nicaragua, as a teaching strategy to improve education, develop ecological awareness and improve food security .  Teachers and children are trained and learn to cultivate the land. They produce nutritious food and improve their nutritional status that allows them to learn and improve concentration.  They learn to value the environment and reforest the communities to protect water sources.

title: Help 500 At-Risk Costa Rican Youth Finish School
description: This project will help empower 500 low income, at-risk students to finish their high school education. Through tutoring, robotics and psychological support, we aim to give at-risk students the tools they need to graduate from high school and have hope for the future.

title: Give 100 Bicycles to Students in Rural Guinea
description: The Guinean Alliance for Education and Development's (GAED) Bicycle to School Initiative has provided 40 students in rural communities in Guinea with brand new bicycles to help with their commute to and from school. Your financial support have made this possible. We are Seeking your support to reach our goal of 100 bicycles for Guinean student who have to walk 3 or more miles to and from school each way. Your donation at any giving level is greatly appreciated and will change a child's life.

title: #GivetoGOAL this Holiday Season
description: Help GOAL continue it's lifesaving work, this #GivingTuesday and throughout the holiday season. Be sure to help spread the word!

title: Mobile technology to underserved - 1 million kids!
description: This mobile technology bus will bridge the digital gap by providing technology access to underserved children across the United States, and eventually the world, one neighborhood at a time.   We will empower children and families by strengthening their literacy skills, enhancing academic studies, and  providing  life long learning skills.

title: Marymead Christmas Appeal 2015
description: Marymead supports nearly 2,000 children, young people and families by providing a range of high quality, innovative support services. Christmas is a special time, and many of the families we support will experience significant challenges over the Christmas period.  We exist to support those who have experienced the trauma of family violence, child abuse and neglect. Your support this Christmas provides essential items such as gifts and non perishable items for children and families.

title: Protect the Protest in Palestine & Israel
description: The goal of #protecttheprotest is to raise US$ 100,000 to protect the right of Palestinians to protest institutionalized racism and the Occupation, and to mobilize for freedom and justice. Popular protests have shaped the world as we know it & protest *can* catalyze change for Palestinians; but first, protest needs to be protected. As protests in Israel/Palestine are being violently suppressed, Adalah is on the streets & in the courts to protect this democratic right. Join Us!

title: Naked Heart Foundation
description: Our main mission is to help build an inclusive society that is open to people with disabilities and special needs, through play and the creation of free support services for disadvantaged families.

title: Sponsor  Education for Children in Rural Uganda
description: This project will  support primary education, provide supply of scholastic materials, nutritious meals for children and critical literacy support to 358 disadvantaged children living in peri urban communities of Matugga in Wakiso  District, Uganda.

title: Oral Immunotherapy for Food Allergic Patients
description: Assaf HaRofeh Medical Center (AHMC), is a Joint Commission International accredited medical institution, located in Zerifin Israel. This project will support the efforts of the Center for Food Allergy at AHMC to advance its groundbreaking work and research in oral immunotherapy (OIT) for the treatment of food allergy.  The OIT program is unique within Israel , and in the last five years has positively impacted on the lives of hundreds of patients and their families.

title: Winter Woolies - Keep street kids cosy
description: With the winter fast approaching in Nepal and no proper heating available, we need to do all we can to keep our children warm and healthy at our Birgunj and Dhading children's homes. Fuel and gas shortages and regular electricity cuts mean that we have to use wood for cooking and can only keep warm by campfire. To keep everyone safe this winter we need to buy electric heaters, warm clothes and blankets for all the children and for our baby buffalo that is joining our team very soon.

title: SAVE THE NEXT GENERATION,GIVE HOPE TO THE HOPELESS
description: KATHY LIFE BUILDER FOUNDATION PLANS TO IMPROVE ON ASSISTING 1,500 FAMILIES LIVING WITH SICKLE CELL DISORDER, WITH FREE SUPPLEMENTARY DRUGS IN THREE STATE, GIVING SCHOLARSHIP TO 30 ORPHANS, CARING FOR THE POOR AND AGED.ADVOCATING FOR THE GIRL CHILD/PRO-LIFE AND FIGHTING AGAINST HUMAN TRAFFICKING.

title: Prevention of HIV/AIDS Transmission of 56000 Women
description: Very few HIV/AIDS programs have targeted the fishing community of Namayingo district, prompting to the escalating infection rates that has seen many children born HIV positive. Prevention of HIV/AIDS among 5600 women of child bearing age through prevention of mother to child transmission, Care and support for People Having AIDS, and mitigation of the adverse effects on the infected and affected persons is going to be implemented in the district

title: Provide Patients Comfort at End-of-Life
description: Patients experience unnecessary pain and suffering during treatment of disease and at the end-of-life.   Palliative Care Network addresses pain and suffering more effectively through education by providing a FREE, online, educational platform for palliative care professionals to remain abreast of palliative care trends.

title: Mindanao Safe Sanitation Project
description: The project will provide hygiene kits, toilet bowls, toilet repair, construct new toilets, provide communal hand-wash stations and build giant rainwater harvesters for dirt-poor families in Mindanao in order to prevent open defecation, promote sustainable sanitation and hygiene practices and prevent the spread of water-borne diseases.

title: Safe drinking water for 12,000 in rural Malawi
description: This project will help 11 villages in rural Malawi have a safe water supply by drilling a borehole and provide a hand pump centrally in each village.  This project will impact over 12,000 people in the community and a School of 3000 children where there have been deaths of children due to drinking unsafe water from open ditches.

title: Gift of Sight to 1000 needy people of rural India
description: The aim of this project is to provide free cataract with IOL implantation surgery to 1000 patients from remote rural and tribal regions of Southern Rajasthan in India. This project will aid in reducing the backlog of blindness through identification and treatment of blinds at primary, secondary and tertiary levels. It will help patients regain their vision leading to a better quality of life.

title: Provision of safe water for 700 inhabitants
description: About 700 inhabitants in the Mudagammana village in Kandy district in Sri Lanka  face acute shortage of clean water for drinking and domestic purposes. This water shortage has an impact on the well being and economic activities of the community leading to poor sanitation and recurrent health problems. In this project, we propose to construct a sustainable s water supply system to bring down water through gravity from a perennial water stream located at higher elevation.

title: Scholarships for 50 Girls in New Delhi
description: CSR will provide extra tuition, additional nutrition, and other costs associated with school (such as: uniforms, books, and school supplies) to girls who are attending free government schools.  We need to raise an additional $6,300 by March.

title: Emergency Relief for Refugee Families in Greece
description: There is a refugee crisis at Europe's door. The reason we talk about a "crisis" is not because of the number of refugees but because of the incapacity of Europe to deal with the problem in an organized and predictable way. There is a need for all European countries to cooperate with solidarity in order to confront this problem with cooperation and goodwill. The Greek islands receive 2.500 refugees every day. Source:  The Greek Police Site and the UNHCR

title: Save 100 girls from FGM and HIV in Kenya
description: This project will provide life skills training to 100 girls aged 9 -15 years olds who hail from the city slums old, provide basic needs and pay school fees to keep them in school for a year.  The Life skills training will help girls to understand their bodies, know their rights undergo alternative right of passage and prevent infections.

title: Teaching farming to over 1,000 families in India
description: Shivia helps very poor families in West Bengal work their way out of poverty through farming.  We offer our beneficiaries the chance to turn small plots of land into fertile areas where they can grow valuable crops. We train our farmers to adopt new farming techniques and organise them into groups so that they can benefit from reduced costs for seeds and fertilisers and have better access to the marketplace.  We aim to work with over 1,000 farmers helping them gain a much needed income.

title: Protect Congolese Forests and Peoples
description: This project will help support practices that safeguard the forests, ecosystems and inhabitants in the Eastern Provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo. As a collaborative group of concerned individuals and groups based in South Kivu, the Congolese Foresters Network strives to improve the lives and environment of this region.

title: Healthy Ladies, Healthy Babies Project
description: Roots of Health empowers women and girls in the Philippines to secure their right to health and freedom from violence. We support women's health and the well-being of their families and their communities. The GlobalGiving Challenge will help us expand our work and fulfill our mission.

title: build 3 classrooms for 200 orphans in Cameroon
description: our orphanage is named Cameroon foster care orphanage  situated in mokindi village Limber cameroon, at about ten miles from the nearest school. It is therefore very difficult to the orphans to attend school in tawn; our aim is to build three classrooms before the academic year 2016/ 2017 beside the orphanage; in order educat these children. this school will help orphans and the neigboring homes to educate their children. this school will solve the problem of distance and early specialization.

title: Support Set Her Free: Empower Ugandan Women
description: GlobeMed at The George Washington University partners with Set Her Free, a non profit based out of Kampala, Uganda. Their mission is to empower young women of Uganda to lead live self-sustaining lives. SHF does this by providing a safe environment, education, and rehabilitation services. Currently, Set Her Free is working on building their Angel House which will help them become more sustainable. Please consider donating to help with this project.

title: What's Under the Tree in Wamunyu 2015?
description: Need a meaningful, memorable gift for someone with a generous heart and an adventurous spirit? Give a gift in your recipient's name to Kenya Connect. Through our Holiday Collection, you can provide students in a rural village with computer skills, sports equipment, healthy hygiene facilities, or stacks of good books. Order one of these life-changing packages today. How many children will this benefit?  Kenya Connect works with 55 partner school with a total of 17,000 students!

title: Save Snakebite Victims in Rural India
description: Every year 45,000 people in rural India die after being bitten by a snake. Anjali Health Centre (AHC) is a small 20-bed hospital in Pithora, Chhattisgarh providing medical aid to over 3000 families of mostly tribal and native communities. Last year, AHC received 126 snake bite victims. This project will provide AHC with crucial support in the form of antivenom serum (AVS), life support equipment (ventilators & hemodialyzers), training in snakebite treatment and expert medical advice as needed.

title: Send 5 Youth to College
description: The project will support 5 aspiring vulnerable youth from Kibera to obtain a college education - an extremely rare opportunity for youth here where the population lives on less than $2 per day and just half of school-age youth reach secondary school.
