The model Unique Star uses revolves round small business set up loans with sustainability within the business model. We aim to impact families and thus children's health and education and bring about access to viable and sustainable employment. This is not a 'hand-out' but a 'hand up' helping families to empower themselves.

title: Education Support for 60 disadvantaged children
description: Development of Village Education (DOVE) intends to provide education support for 60 children from marginalized families in the backward villages of Thoothukudi District of Tamil Nadu in India.   The area is typical rural one with more number of villages located around. People are mostly daily wage earners. Hence this project covers the entire education cost of 60 disadvantaged children from this area for one year.

title: Ocean Debris Art Exhibit at the Smithsonian Zoo
description: The Smithsonian's National Zoo is bringing 16 larger-than-life animal sculptures made entirely of marine debris collected from beaches. The sculptures graphically illustrate the tragedy of plastic pollution in our waterways. The Washed Ashore exhibit is completely interactive and will span the Zoo's main walkway. We are expecting 1 million visitors during the exhibition and are creating extensive educational curriculum to inspire people to make better choices for ocean health.

title: Free Climbing Camp for 18 Bronx Children
description: This project opens up an enchanting outdoor portal to the children of the South Bronx growing up amidst the highest rates of asthma, diabetes, and poverty. Through rock climbing, hiking, and camping, children and their families grow in trust, responsibility, and self-acceptance. Once home we proceed to green the Bronx and spread the seeds of justice.

title: Children - The Change Maker
description: This project aims to address the issues of child rights and child protection through active participation of disadvantaged children. We intend to strengthen the children and adolescents of underprivileged communities of Bhavnagar, India by forming their own collectives called Balsena. Balsena children would be engaged with various capacity building programmes like leadership training,  exposure visits, children seminars, participation in national forums.

title: Climate Crisis: Tackling Our Carbon Footprint
description: The Climate Crisis is a hot topic across the globe at the moment and that is because this really is our last chance to act now otherwise the future of our planet is not going to be the same ever again. As a charity, we work on over 75 projects across global communities and this project is to install education, awareness, systems and resources to ensure every project no matter the focus is carbon responsible. Helping everyone do their bit to tackle their carbon footprint.

title: Education sponsorship for about 238 children
description: Our project transforms nearly 238 street kids into valuable members of society in education sponsorship  through provision of formal education and vocational training opportunities as well as job orientation for about 250 students reintegrated in families before August 2020.We as EDD, will empower youth and children in order to sustain themselves and their families as well as eradicating root cause that push kids to join street life.

title: Sexual and reproductive health in Hisar, India
description: Childreach India's Sexual and Reproductive health (SRH) project aims to improve women's access to, and the quality of, SRH services in Hisar, Haryana, through combatting discriminatory gender norms which limit women's ability to access such services and connecting disempowered women to these services.

title: Restore Dignity to Women in Mali
description: This project provides surgeries for women and girls in Mali who live with obstetric fistula. It also provides the social, psychological, and economic skills and resources women need to rejoin their communities once they've been undergone the procedure. Fistula can occur when girls become pregnant before their bodies are fully developed, and when women do not have access to skilled health care during obstructed or prolonged labor. The results are debilitating and the infant is often stillborn.

title: Rebuilding Communities of Sanriku Coastal Areas
description: 5 years after the powerful tsunami which destroyed nearly 400,000 houses, many victims are still continuing their endless  journey to find a new "home" where peace can be found. Whilst they struggle to adjust to a new environment, they are placed under extreme stress, and suffer isolation and depression. It is thus crucial that the residents of each new community can develop strong bonds with others. Through this project, JISP aims to support the local efforts to build a resilient community

title: Reducing violence in a Rio favela using football
description: This project will work with 294 children and 20 families to combat violence and improve gender norms within the Mangueirinha Favela in Rio utilising sport as a way of transforming lives. Through the project, violence and discrimination within the community will be reducing, and community members will be united through the power of football. This will result in an improved social environment for hundreds of children, and will lead to them having a positive outlook on their lives and futures.

title: DIL Trust UK Orangi School
description: DIL schools provide children, especially girls, in remote marginalized areas with access to quality education. Besides the academic learning, DIL also makes great efforts to provide a holistic school experience to its students through a comprehensive co-curricular program; well-stocked libraries and computer labs; engaging with the parent body; and strong teacher development throughout the year to make this goal achievable.

title: Saving the Symbol of Nias (Beo Nias)
description: Our mission is to conserve Nias Hill Myna (Gracula robusta) population, an endemic bird of Sumatra, who is on the red list status. The Nias Hill Myna is a distinctive large bird that is restricted to hill forest of Nias and Banyak Island off western Sumatra, Indonesia (Feare and Craig 1998). Famous for its ability to talk, Nias Hill Myna has been extensively trapped for the cage bird trade which has almost certainly caused its extinction in the wild.

title: Mental Health counselling for Adolescents in India
description: Every 90 minutes a youth commits suicide in India. Mental health is highly stigmatized in Indian society and has therefore become a burning issue affecting adolescents predominantly. Mental health problems amongst children can lead to catastrophic consequences such as suicide, depression,substance abuse,failure to complete schooling and health problems. AWAG aims to provide free expert counselling to 750 vulnerable children of 5 Government schools of Ahmedabad in 1 year.

title: Rebuild a Secondary School for 250 Kids in Nepal
description: The Shree Bhumimata secondary school was forced to close its doors after being badly damaged in the 2015 Nepal earthquake. Its 250 students, most from disadvantaged families, were forced to attend class in a temporary space which is crowded, cold and ill-equipped. This project will rebuild the village school, providing quality education in a safe space to a community which is in dire need of an opportunity to rise out of poverty and combat gender inequality and discrimination.

title: Repair a Madagascar School to Educate 281 Children
description: We are working to renovate four dilapidated and dangerous classrooms at a remote primary school in rural Madagascar, creating clean, safe conditions for 281 children to learn in.

title: Protect Children in Latin America from Zika Virus
description: The Zika Virus is affecting at least 26 countries in Latin America and the Caribbean.  It was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by the World Health Organization (WHO) given the suspected linkage to birth defects and potential to infect up to four million people in a year.  UNICEF is scaling up its support using its network of 24 local offices. UNICEF is working to slow the virus' spread, mitigate its impact, and drive rapid diagnostics and vaccine development.

title: Empower girls in rural India to be Champions
description: Mann Deshi Champions empowers rural girls in India to redefine winning: equipping them to be successful through nutrition, education and athleticism. With unprecedented access to sports facilities, equipment and nurturing coaches, our Champions build communication and leadership skills, practicing dedication and teamwork. Altogether, they are encouraged to be brave and bold no matter the arena or opposition their future presents: police officer or gym coach, nutritionist or professional athlete.

title: Emergency Support to Drought-Stricken Ethiopia
description: With the consequences of climate change becoming increasingly seen across the African continent, cyclical droughts will become more and more destructive. According to the World Food Programme, up to 15 million people in central and eastern Ethiopia "will face severe acute food insecurity and require assistance in 2016, making Ethiopia the country with the largest acutely food insecure population in the world".

title: Support Taiwan Red Cross
description: The Taiwan Red Cross responds quickly to assist in domestic or international disaster relief efforts, helps those affected to get back on their feet, provides first-aid training and certification, and leads volunteers of all ages in giving back to their communities.

title: Support Day Care in Guatemala!
description: This project funds a full Day Care Program in the rural area of Guatemala for kids from 9 months to 5 years old.

title: Support  Senior Citizen Day Care Centres in Mumbai
description: India is an old country which has venerated its seniors. But the scene is rapidly changing.  Among the low income groups, close to 50 million senior citizens  cannot afford even two square meals a day. BCPT's day care centres provide emotional and social support, medical assistance, recreational programs, legal awareness and health & nutrition support to an average of 50 elders per centre. Currently BCPT partners 13 centres and aims to include 5 more centres in the next financial year.

title: Loan Scheme for Disadvantaged Young People
description: For years Jopa had been equipping young disadvantages people in the Buwenge area with skills in carpentry, tailoring and knitting, hair dressing and mechanics to allow them to gain employment or set up their own businesses.  There is a problem in accessing start up capital for this group and there is a clear need to support these people further to allow them to set up their own businesses and become financially independent.

title: House of Hope for 100 Orphans in Kalo DRC
description: Kalo Telema operates an orphanage which aims to give love, compassion and care for orphaned and abandoned children, the extremely vulnerable children. We provide them with food, clothing, and we intervene in the payment of the costs for their medical care. The situation is extremely difficult due to lack of adequate resources; we cannot accommodate all the children that we take.

title: Solar lighting for remote communities in S.E.Asia
description: Building on our past renewable energy projects, we aim to continue our work for marginalised communities. This project ensures sustainable and environmentally friendly solar power for the most vulnerable, those that do not have access to the main power grid. Many people rely on expensive kerosene lamps and candles, which pose fire risks to their thatched homes, increase health problems and prevent students from studying after dusk. Help us today by bringing light to those who need it most!

title: Provide Music Education for Children in Guatemala
description: We transform the lives of low income children in Guatemala through music education. Our programs help kids develop important life skills and a positive self image so they can begin to believe that they have the ability to achieve whatever they want in life. Guatemala has suffered greatly through a very long civil war but we can help rebuild civil society by giving our children, among other things, the opportunity to have music in their lives.

title: VOCATIONAL EDUCATION CENTERS
description: The speed of a nation's development is directly related to the quantity and quality of vocational skills possessed by its workforce. The wider the range and higher the quality of vocational skills, the faster the growth and more prosperous the society.

title: Football meals
description: We provide two afternoon football sessions per week followed by a great meal for around 300 street children per week.

title: CreatingSTEAM 2016: Experiential Learning Program
description: This project provides a 10 day project-based, experiential learning program for high school students which focuses on STEAM disciplines and 21st century workforce skills. WCTD will be working with several under served communities to ensure students who lack economic mobility and resources will have access to the program and the technology needed to participate in activities across the 10 day program.

title: Send a Girl to High School with a Bicycle Gift
description: This project is supporting a bicycle each & other educational support for higher secondary education of 1000 girls in Nepal who are forced to walk at least 4-12 KM for the nearest high school. With a bicycle in hand, a girl is more secure on the way, regular in school saves time & energy for better performance that helps fill the gap/pass out between boys and girls. A girl's regular engagement in school means fewer chances of her being a victim of a child, early or forced marriage at home.

title: Medications for Children`s Oncological Units
description: Tabletochki Charity Foundation supports Ukrainian hospitals by purchasing necessary medications and medical supplies. With your help, children can receive the most effective medicines, even if they are possible to find only abroad.   Your charitable donations make the children's treatment more effective and bring children closer to recovery. You can read about the impact you make in our regular reports and on social media.   Ukrainian children are brave in their fight against the disease. But th

title: Reunite Children with their Families in Congo
description: There are thought to be thousands of street children in Lubumbashi alone, and since 2009 Kimbilio has been helping to reunite these children with their families. We take the time to get to know each child on a personal level, before locating their family and helping them to rebuild their relationship. This is a challenging and emotional process, but giving children this second chance can be life-changing.

title: Support a Local Girl's Empowerment Leader
description: GLOW Georgia is growing and we're ready to hire a local Georgian project manager to help! The project manager will be an essential team member working to educate and empower girls, particularity in under-served communities, to develop their leadership skills and become agents of change in their communities. The project manager will oversee 2 week-long camps, a year-round volunteer program, and organize a project design and management conference for exceptional young female leaders in Georgia.

title: Relief for Taiwan after the 2016 earthquake
description: IsraAID is responding to the February 6th earthquake by supporting the local government and civil societies with expertise in the field of grief care, psychological first aid, psycho-education, and resilience building for the small community in the Tainan that was most affected.

title: Give Seriously ill Children their Childhood Back
description: Hospitals treat the illness, Barretstown treats the child.  Barretstown offers free, medically endorsed camps and programmes that are designed for children and their families living with cancer and other serious illness - all supported behind the scenes by 24 hour on site medical and nursing care. Our programmes are designed to rebuild confidence and self-esteem through activities that foster growth, development, and independence.

title: Rebuild Earthquake Resilient Schools in Nepal
description: In 2015, two violent earthquakes struck Nepal affecting 5.4 million people. AHAH arrived 72 hours after the first, to see how we could help. After six+ months of rubble removal and constructing camps, clinics and homes, we began to focus on rebuilding resilient schools. This program, now entering its fifth year, is our holistic approach to helping as many overlooked rural communities as possible recover -- and recover stronger -- by rebuilding the schools at the center of community life.

title: LGBTQ Middle School Support Group
description: Currently, there is only one LGBTQ support group for middle school-aged youth in Massachusetts, and it does not serve the metro Boston and North Shore region. A new group serving our area is desperately needed, as youth are coming out earlier and earlier and need to overcome the feelings of isolation and depression which accompany this time in their  lives.

title: Equipped for Success!
description: CEO's first equipment drive will provide boots, tools, and training for participants to successfully enter the workforce. CEO's transitional work crews employ over 4,200 formerly incarcerated individuals each year, providing maintenance and beautification services in the cities and states where we work. Participants in transitional work receive daily paychecks, learn hard and soft skills on the job, and develop the tools they need to rejoin the workforce, begin a career, and remain crime-free.

title: Help fight child abduction and sexual exploitation
description: Our mission: To help law enforcement find missing children, reduce child sexual exploitation and prevent future victimization. As the nonprofit leading the fight to keep children safer from abduction and sexual exploitation, NCMEC is dedicated to the victims of these crimes and their families. Co-founded in 1984 by missing child advocates John and Reve Walsh after their son Adam's abduction and murder, NCMEC's role has grown to respond to evolving threats against our nation's children.

title: 4000 out of school children in 40 Community School
description: YIAB is going to establish Community Model School in areas, where, there is no govt. school or private school or communities have limited access to govt. schools. Community takes up central onus by donating land/space and teachers. Through this campaign YIAB is going to establish 40 community model schools in rural areas of Naseerabad District in Balochistan Province to enable 4,000 out of school poor children to have meaningful access to education.

title: Create income for 100 displaced Batwa in uganda
description: This project provides knowledge of working hives, management skills of bee products, skills  in creating an alternative source of livelihood for Batwa pygmies evicted from their indigenous home in the Bwindi forest when the area was conserved as a national park.  Through training on the demonstration apiary and home to home extension services, the Batwa will be supported with tools, knowledge of production and value addition and helped to access market of their products thus generating incomes.

title: Stop Child Marriage Through Education of Girls
description: The goal of this project is to end gender gap in education of 89,000 girls in Kajo-Keji, South Sudan by providing access of education to young girls.  Only 6% of 13 year old girls have completed their primary school. The lack of educational opportunities for girls leads to economic disadvantage which is a precursor to marrying before the age of 18 years.  Early marriages of girls in South Sudan is eroding the future backbone of the community.

title: Train 90 Teachers in Rural China to Create Future
description: Train teachers from rural areas in China to unleash their students' potential and creativity in building their communities and preserving their culture.  Donations in 2016 sponsored more than half of the 90 teachers in Conference:  Makerspace: Creativity in the Library.   Design Thinking workshop in 2017 will strengthen their experience to build their respective schools foundational capability.

title: Tohum Autism Foundation Turkey
description: The project aims to create an environment where teachers and other employees of our school and foundation gain technical know-how at the school and foundation,

title: Support Young People to Lead Social Change
description: The YP Foundation equips young people with knowledge, perspectives, leadership and technical skills to lead community programmes on critical issues of health, gender, sexuality, education, active citizenship and human rights. Our training programmes reach out to poor and vulnerable young people, especially young women and girls from urban and rural areas to improve their confidence, negotiation skills, access to information and services and overall quality of life.

title: Educate 500 needy Children in Dirakho Village
description: This project will constructs Early Childhood Development Center to provide free education for the needy children, tap and nurture talents and establish a community library to provide a rich supply of books and easy access to information for improved student performance in schools. It will raise funds to provide free meals , daily up keep and support education for needy students from the community.

title: Vincent's Mobility
description: This funding will help buy Vincent an adaptable Wheelchair. Vincent is a 10 years old boy with a physical disability living with his grandmother, his father succumbed to cancer and his mother an HIV victim passed on last year, The grandmother cannot raise money to buy him a wheelchair. When we identified him during our outreach program he said "I have not been able to go to school because schools in my community have a rough terrain making crawling down to access school facilities impossible."

title: Help students advance with a better instrument!
description: The Virtu Foundation has received, by donation, a fine 18th century cello by celebrated Parisian maker Andrea Castagneri.  His instruments have commanded lofty values at auction.  The challenge is that this rare instrument needs $8,000 in restoration work to allow it again produce the glorious sounds that has caused unknown generations to care for and cherish it.  It will then go, by Scholarship loan,  into hands of a talented young musician in need of a better instrument.

title: Education Brings Renewed Hope for Kids in Kenya!
description: Every child dreams of what they will be when they grow up, but when you live in extreme poverty, that's all they are, just dreams. A key to breaking the cycle of poverty is education. Many kids in Oyugis, Kenya are hoping someone will begin the dream with them by paying for their Secondary School (H.S.) Education.  Others who were forced to leave school when their family could no longer pay tuition, yearn to return to complete their education. They can with your help! Give Hope-start the dream!

title: Give Sight to 5000 School Children in Sri Lanka
description: So Others May See Inc. is planing conduct Vision screening for 353,169 school children studying at 531 schools in Gampaha District of Sri Lanka and donate 5000 custom made spectacles to correct their vision.  Majority of the Children  are suffering from blindness due to preventable causes. Vision screening and providing custom made spectacles to correct vision at early stage in a child life will restore his vision for a bright future. Giving sight is Giving Life.

title: YOU are the KEY
description: CHILDREN are losing their education. We must get them back on track at all costs. The Pandemic has closed schools. Schooling online costs $10 a month for internet and with families only earning $60 a month for all of life's basics, something has to give, a generation will be lost. We cannot let this happen, You are the KEY to their success. UNLOCK a child's potential and Donate today. Help us reach our target amount so we can give 1,250 children FREE internet schooling for Four months.

title: Chain of Courage for Children with Cancer
description: The treatment of childhood cancer usually takes a long time and is hard. As the treatment continues a child might become more reluctant to co-operate with the necessary procedures. Knowing that there is a reward waiting at the end of the procedure improves the child's attitude.  This is where the Chain of Courage (KanjerKetting) comes in. The Chain of Courage is a system that is used during the entire course of treatment. Children receive a special bead after every treatment, intervention

title: loveisrespect
description: love is respect is the national resource to disrupt and prevent unhealthy relationships and intimate partner violence by empowering young people through inclusive and equitable education, support, and resources. A project of the National Domestic Violence Hotline, love is respect offers 24/7 information, support, and advocate to young people between the ages of 13 and 26 who have questions or concerns about their romantic relationships. love is respect is a safe, inclusive space for young people

title: Operation Dog Food:  For Service Dogs of Veterans
description: We are solving the problem of Disabled Veterans not having any Government support for maintaining their Service Dog.  The VA does not allocate any funds to support the costs of feeding or maintaining a Service Dog that's helping a Veteran with a Service Connected Disability.  The expenses of the dog's service equipment, ongoing service specific training, dog food, veterinary care, insurance, grooming, etc. come out of what's left in the Veteran's pocket.

title: Participation of Males in Family Planning Project
description: There is a very strong need for more options that men can use as a way to become more involved in family planning. CCDO works to educate the community to have the proper programs that could find better ways to reach men as individuals and as members of couples using contraceptives through educating couples, information dissemination and discussion on families. Project impacts will include enhanced awareness and knowledge on family planning issues

title: HOPE Cape Town Community Health Workers
description: 25 Community Health Workers serving 22 communities and clinics in the Western Cape, South Africa supporting those infected and affected by HIV/Aids and related illnesses.

title: Sports Fields of Dreams and Champions
description: KYFA sees sports as a way of developing the talents and self-esteem of girls. Through a soccer tourney, girls are given the chance to showcase talents that are not usually recognized. While in the field, they get out of the 'social construction' that would ordinarily bar them from participation in football and in public events. KYFA also believes that these disadvantaged girls will get inspiration, learn life skills and excel in school by connecting with motivational speakers and role models.

title: Empowering children to realise their Human Rights
description: Amalungelo Abantu Project (Human Rights Project) will help South African children from marginalized communities to realise their Human Rights, build their confidence, and give them the tools needed to exercise their rights as children.  The Amalungelo Abantu camp (15 - 17 April 2016) will focus on developing an increased sense of self-worth, confidence, and hope in individuals often living in poverty, with food insecurity, overcrowding, violence and abuse at home. We empower these children!

title: Cycling to Success!
description: The Mariposa Cycling Program educates, empowers, and employs girls living in extreme poverty in the Dominican Republic-putting them on the path to healthy and independent lives. Our cycling program  will empower the Mariposa girls through knowledge of bike safety, maintenance and repair, the skills to engage in fun outdoor activities, and freedom of movement within their community.

title: Send a Poor Child to School in India
description: VETNGO provides high quality education for poor children who hail from the poorest sections of society in and around Kanjanur village, Viluppuram Disrict, Tamilnadu and also providing the children with free meals.

title: Support Young Aspiring Mexican Tech Inventors
description: Throught this project, thousands of youth learn how to be a creators or inventros. Support them to get to their goal

title: Improve English skills for 100 Immigrants in IL
description: This project will assist 100 immigrants to learn how to speak, read and write English to integrate into their new homes.  The greatest barriers to integration and increasing household income for immigrant communities is the lack of English skills.  The Indo-American Center works with community members by providing literacy and civics classes, enrolling individuals in our workforce development program and assisting with job search and job placement at no cost to the individuals and families.

title: #savethebabies: Help Children Rise out of Poverty
description: Jake's Diapers serves babies around the world living in devastatingly difficult situations, where sometimes a choice has to be made between food and diapers. Jake's donates cloth diapers at no cost to orphanages, rescue centers and missionaries so these organizations can afford basic living expenses and focus on a solution for problems such as malnutrition and starvation. Cloth diapers provide a long-term solution from birth through potty-training, truly changing the lives of these children.

title: Unlock the child's technology future
description: Technology is reinventing the world but the kids in Ghana are not exposed to any digital making activities. Knowing that digital skill set is going to be a requirement in future work force, action to empower school  children now with digital skills is a must. Healthy Career Initiative is set to solve this problem through coding clubs in elementary schools. Yes, it is our responsibility to equip future generations with the skill set they need to thrive in the 21st century workforce.

title: Ensuring Girls in Ethiopia Receive Basic Eye Care
description: In Ethiopia, more women than men are blind due to eye diseases such as trachoma. This blinding eye disease is spread from child to mother through direct personal contact. Without treatment, trachoma leads to blindness. It's a sad reality that 50% of children who go blind in Ethiopia, will die within two years.  Orbis is working to change this by eliminating this disease in Ethiopia. With your help, Orbis will ensure the next generation of women and girls grow up without the threat of blindness.

title: Bring Fruit Trees to Native American Reservations
description: Trees for Tribes supports Native American communities' efforts toward food sovereignty & food justice by planting fruit tree orchards that provide abundant harvests of nutritious fruit. Tribal members also build their skills, (re)learning important techniques on how to care for their orchards & preserve the harvests. Through this program, FTPF has planted dozens of orchards filled with hundreds of fruit trees & provided arboricultural training for tribal communities all across Turtle Island.

title: Help 300+ Zimbabwean Orphans Return to School
description: BEAT AIDS Project Zimbabwe (BAPZ)'s Guardian Angel Programme helps to return more than 300 Zimbabwean orphans and vulnerable children (OVC) affected by HIV/AIDS, especially young girls, back to school by covering annual tuition fees and the cost of books and school uniforms. Education is an integral part of BAPZ, and the Guardian Angel Programme picks up where UNICEF BEAM funding ended in 2014. We invite you to do your part for more than 300 of the most vulnerable children in Zimbabwe.

title: Provide Instruments for Vulnerable Colombian Youth
description: Fundacion Nacional Batuta works in the most vulnerable and conflict ridden areas of Colombia, providing children and youth with the opportunity to learn and practice music in a group setting which gives them a sense of place and a nurturing community.  This project will fund one of our most urgent needs: instruments! Instruments are the cornerstone of our program and play a key role in teaching responsibility and ownership.

title: Improving Education for 5,200 Brazilian Children
description: This Project will offer twice monthly sessions of Story telling, puppet theatre and reading mediation to 5,200 elementary school children to improve the quality of their education. It will be delivered by 20 specially trained local high school children.

title: Kitchu Community Water Project
description: Water supply is a major problem in Kitchu as the pictures show.  Specifically, the Kitchu Community Water Project is designed to provide this Community with dependable, clean water throughout the whole year by: 1) Purchasing a very powerful water pump from a Water Supply Company; 2) Paying this Company to: a) Drill and construct a deep well; b) Construct a big water storage tank; and c) Connect plastic pipes from the water storage tank to four main water supply supply points in Kitchu Community.

title: Build a pre school in rural Uganda
description: Sprout Care Foundation plans to build a two classroom block to provide free education for children from the poorest of poor families with no access to safe, high quality early childhood education. The school will target children from 3 to 5 years by investing in their early childhood education as the most effective way to break the cycle of poverty. It will lay the foundation for success in school, career and life.

title: Solar Energy Light in the Life of Rural People
description: Provision of 500 mini solar sets to low-income households and 150 solar power stations to public facilities (rural clinics, schools and libraries, community centers and mosques). with the purpose to bring light in the lives of poor ones

title: Improve Education & Health of Cambodian Families
description: This project will provide daily nutrition to stop the cycle of malnutrition, maternal health classes to reduce rates of mortality, and community education training and support for 253 families in the villages of Sre Robong, Trapieng Tmar, and Arak Svay, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia.

title: Treat Chronic Leg Ulcers in 50 Nigerians
description: Leg ulcers, the most debilitating and stigmatizing complication of sickle cell disease can remain unhealed for years. Very painful, they render patients incapacitated, confined indoors and preclude them from leading normal, productive lives. Sickle Cell Foundation Nigeria has identified a wound dressing solution more effective for healing these ulcers than commonly used solutions. This project will be providing FREE wound dressings for 50 indigent patients in Nigeria over a 6 month period.

title: Help 2000 kids conquer violence in El Salvador
description: This project will bring 2000 children from violence riddled villages across El Salvador to Tin Marin, the children's museum in San Salvador the capital city. School children will experience how fun can conquer fear of violence and how safe environments can be created by children, teachers and parents working together. Tin Marin knows how to help children learn through play.  The new challenge is to use that knowledge to impact the biggest problem facing Central America - social violence.

title: New CancerLink support centre in the community
description: We are opening a new cancer care support centre in the community, in Kwai Chung, Hong Kong where we will provide free professional cancer care services that covers 1.5 million population in the area.  Services we provide include practical, psychological and physical support, including symptom management, nursing & dietetic consultation, emotional support & relief fund. Run by the Hong Kong Cancer Fund, our one-stop free cancer support service is unique in Hong Kong.

title: Changing the Culture of Violence in Fiji
description: With the economic impact of covid 19 in Fiji bringing job losses and depression there has been an increase in violence against women and children. The youth, trained with the virtues project and puppets, continue to make a huge impact visiting communities and teaching government officials about how the virtues project operates to change the way people respond to their messages and each other. In recognition the Red cross and other agencies request their voluntary support for their programs.

title: Peace Schools for Children - Pakistan
description: The project will help sustain children in Lahore, Pakistan. Currently there are 1050 students studying in school and funds are required for their education, teacher's salaries and supplies.

title: Famine support for 1700 Ethiopian students
description: Sitting in class when you are hungry is not easy; eventually the student will prefer to stay home and sleep to escape the pains of hunger. Abraham's Oasis has already provided one month of complimentary feeding for school students in order to encourage them to 'stay in school' during this time of famine. We plan with your help to continue this until the rainy season and harvest time or another five months when school ends.

title: Emergency Relief for Fiji After Cyclone Winston
description: On 20 February a category 5 cyclone  tore through the island nation of Fiji. Cyclone Winston has cut a path of destruction to the largely rural nation. Homes have been destroyed, rivers have flooded, power lines have snapped, trees have been uprooted and access to safe drinking water has been compromised. Fiji needs our help.

title: Support victims of human trafficking in Serbia
description: Serbia is a poor country with dominant patriarchal values which contributes to the mistreatment of young women in society and the human trafficking is just one of the causes of this problem. ASTRA's goal is to contribute to the eradication of human trafficking. Until now, ASTRA has assisted 507 victims of human trafficking during their recovery by providing legal, medical and psychological assistance as well as accompanying our clients through institutional procedures.

title: It's Hard to Learn When You're Hungry!
description: Hunger should not be a barrier to education in 2023. Many of the children and young people attending our partner centres have lost one or both parents and many live with an elderly guardian who does not work. Lunch provision at the projects benefits the students and their families - many parents and carers will only have something to eat themselves if they know the children have already eaten. A regular healthy lunch improves attendance and concentration, as well as health and wellbeing.

title: Tutoring program for 15 hard of hearing students
description: This program is aimed at providing after-school academic tutoring to 15 hard-of-hearing students who attend ordinary school at the age of 7-15 years old . Special education teachers teach them Mandarin Chinese and Mathematics with methods like writing, Q&A, and practice with repetitions that help and enhance hard-of hearing students' understanding.  There will be a social worker who is responsible for case management , and  will teach them social skill and emotional behavior management.

title: STEM CELLS Summer Program
description: STEM CELLS is a free summer program offered for 7 weeks. The first week is always a leadership training for our volunteers. Followed by three 2 week sessions of STEM camps. We try to serve up to 60 youth participants not including the youth counselors/volunteers. We provide fieldtrips to laboratories and other STEM related jobs along with classes from leading specialist in various fields. We also design service learning projects  weekly and Swimming lessons and weekly pool trips.

title: Local Action - Global Impact
description: The main idea is to reconstruct the square in Vorniceni Village in the way to create a beautiful place for rest and to provide new work places. The long-term goal is developing of a green area with an international importance. The short - term goal is to make an ecological inspection to cut the old and damaged trees and to plant the new ones (autumn). The global idea is to create an example of a square, having as a back fought that creating such squares in the entire counties...

title: Rescue & Justice for Trafficked Victims in India
description: According to government figures, there are 3 million commercial sex workers in India, of which an estimated 40% are children, so the need for anti-trafficking work is huge. In Madhya Pradesh, entire communities practice and perpetuate forced prostitution of children. These young girls grow up believing that their identity and fate is linked only to their sexual exploitation. Freedom Firm seeks to combat this problem by providing rescue, restoration and justice for trafficked victims.

title: Young Biodiversity Artists- Tropical Forest Brazil
description: Our program gets youth from our local Atlantic Forest community in Brazil to transform knowledge into art. What better way to "leave a healthy planet to our children" is there than to get them involved in earths recovery! 15 students will enter their classroom, the Atlantic Forest, for a 3-week course on biodiversity, history, culture and use this knowledge to transform it into digital art, through photography and editing. All art will be online taking their environmental advocacy international.

title: 1000 days - Education & Support for Mother & Child
description: From a woman's pregnancy to her child's 2nd birthday there are 1,000 days. This time is important for setting the foundations for the rest of life. The support and education a mother receives during the 1,000 days can have a very real impact on the care she gives, influencing how her child grows and develops. RED International has worked with various partner projects but now focuses on India offering education, support and services to mothers and fathers so that they are well prepared.

title: Building a Home for the San Antonio Preschool
description: After operating a Preschool Nutrition Center in the small town of San Antonio Palopo, Guatemala since 2010, we need to establish a permanent building to house the over 50 preschoolers that rely on the center for daily nutrition and education. Currently the preschool operates in a temporary shelter which is dark, cramped, and not conducive to learning and growing.

title: Clubs at Clara Luna
description: There are four clubs at Clara Luna; kids, youth, reading, and GLOW club, which engage youth in themes about environment, health, art, leadership, and reading. Clara Luna inspires youth in Puerto Lopez through these clubs in a creative and educational space. With the donations, Clara Luna will be able to host these clubs for a year.

title: Protecting the Youth of Ushpa-Ushpa
description: Proyecto Horizonte has established a psychology and social work clinic that works to help the youth of the community of Ushpa-Ushpa overcome various vulnerable situations that they may face. We also designed a personal development and skills program with the objective of teaching young boys and girls of our community to make relevant, positive and effective life choices through informative workshops and classes.

title: Clean water for 4,250 villagers in the DR Congo
description: This project will bring a vital supply of clean drinking water to a population of 4,250 living in the village of Kimbobolo in Madimba Territory of the D.R. Congo, and to a 30-bed medical centre that serves over 8,000 people in the rural area.

title: Educating & Supporting Adolescents on HIV/AIDS
description: Help adolescents, especially girls, in sub-Saharan Africa stay healthy and HIV negative through peer support and education.

title: Farm Talk Radio Educates Farmers in Zambia
description: Farm Talk, is a wildly popular radio program produced by our partner COMACO, which has 165,000 registered small-scale farmers in Zambia's Luangwa Valley, home to many wildlife parks and forests. Farm Talk provides farmers with information on production techniques, climate change, habitat preservation and wildlife conservation. Farmer listener groups rely on our solar Prime radios and Lifeplayers to listen to Farm Talk and, in turn, derive many benefits from group listening and discussions.

title: Tailoring store for Indian women
description: The project that  we are proposing is the construction and management of a tailoring store for one year. A real shop, it can be the natural outlet for women who are working for years with professionalism and desire growing. Women become masters of their own future, their own well-being, their own independence: the married can take care of their children by providing them the opportunity, with education, adequate nutrition, creating a greater independence from the family of origin.

title: Creating a Monarch Butterfly Habitat
description: Back to Natives is raising funds to restore the habitat for monarch butterflies at the Back to Natives Native Plant Reserve in Dana Point, CA. The project will focus on planting and/or seeding with locally native milkweed species.  Numerous locally native nectar plants will also be included with the goal of creating a monarch breeding and migration habitat. The project will be carried out by high school and college volunteers participating in a service learning program.

title: Mamare - home for 38 orphan children in India
description: Mamare Home for orphan children in India (rural area) was established in 2006. Now, 2016, 38 children are living as a family in this home. Love, care and educate is our slogan. Education is the main factor to make a difference for these children, to break the vicious circle of illiteracy, ignorance and poverty. For the academic year 2016-2017 (june-april) we need 8000 $ to cover schoolfees, transportation, notebooks, textbooks, school supplies and uniforms.

title: Health for 1000 women and children in Tanzania
description: Impoverished women and children of Tanzania are without needed dental, vision and medical care.  This annual project impacts the lives of hundreds by bringing on-site healthcare clinics and solutions to address village needs for clean water,community sanitation, education and business development.  Washable feminine hygiene kits and sexual education are provided to women and girls, helping prevent new HIV infections, keeping girls in school and offering entrepreneurial opportunities.

title: Provide Free Healthcare to Needy in Rural Cameroon
description: The project is to raise at least $12,000 annually to fund the salary of Ascovime support staff helping Dr Bwelle to reduce the suffering, and thereby put a smile on the face hundreds of thousands of underprivileged people in rural areas in Cameroon. In weekends, Dr Bwelle and his teams of national and international volunteer doctors conduct large mobile missions to rural areas to provide free medical consultations and carry out surgical interventions, tooth extractions and dental care.

title: Drinking Water for Humans,Animals of Thar
description: With your kind support, Customs Health care society will provide clean drinking water to the drought hit villages of Thar in Pakistan. Thar is part of Pakistan which is often hit by drought as there are no rains over the years and shortage of  water is the main concern. In the wake of this, we have embarked upon to dig 40 wells in 40 different Goths ( villages ) of Thar which on completion will not only provide clean drinking water to almost 12,000 humans but also to animals and birds.

title: Increase Slovak girls participation in technology
description: Project is aimed to young girls, aged between 14 and 18 years, who are currently not very motivated for technology and computers science. Project's activities will happen on high schools in whole Slovakia and we can reach more than 2000 Slovak young girls per year. We inspire and encourage young girls to be more interested and consider careers in technology through our outreach programs, workshops, mentorships and other resources.

title: Empowering 50 rape survivors through bee-keeping
description: This project will help 50 survivors of wartime rape from Gjakova region to overcome poverty and the consequences of war trauma. The project will supply the survivors with bees and bee-care supplies and develop their capacities in bee-keeping and honey production.  Due to war trauma affecting their psycho-social functioning, the project provides in addition psychological support to the survivors involved.

title: Alive and Smiling - Nutrition for Premature Baby
description: Children and teenagers who were prematurely born have high risk of nutritional disorders; small stature, anemia, malnutrition, metabolic syndrome as well as mental, visual, hearing and coordination disorders.  Behavioral change is also a factor. Our goal is to give proper formula to all preterm babies who will come to EPM's Outpatient Care of Premature Infants. The formulas will be given for one year after breastfeeding ceases or to children who lacked breastfeeding.

title: Support Widows Dairy Goats Project in Kitui, Kenya
description: Gender disparities imposed by cultural and traditional practices keep women in subordinate positions in all areas of life in the Africa rural society. Cultural practices contribute to undermining the women's position. It increases their vulnerability to HIV/AIDS, and impacts negatively on livelihood resources such as natural capital, economic capital, human capital, social capital and physical capital. Yet in many cases women are left to take care of the children and grandchildren.

title: Empower Women Survivors in Mid-Michigan
description: Our mission is to guide, empower, and heal women. As the only non-profit organization of our kind in the area, we have helped over 7,000 women move toward financial independence after surviving soul-crushing events. No one is turned away by the inability to pay. We start where a woman is when she walks through the door. We provide counseling, support groups, job search tools, a professional clothing & personal care closet, and help women get out of violent situations. We save lives.

title: Out of Home and School in Northern Nigeria
description: This project gives out-of-school children a chance to have access to educational materials, establish community reading clubs across 10 IDPs camps in Borno and engage children in activities that facilitates learning and encourage term work. Boko Haram draws its members mainly from disaffected youths, unemployed and destitute children. Displacement camps without education facilities and children's alienation will help provide more cognitive opening that extremist will exploit in recruitment.

title: Help  Displaced People Become Self-reliant
description: Conflict in eastern Ukraine has left many without the means to feed their families. This project will enable families displaced from their homes to obtain livelihoods by providing them with seeds, poultry, pigs and fodder. They will have the opportunity to establish their own farm and support themselves while starting their life from scratch in a new region after fleeing violence.

title: Financial Assistance for Holistic Cancer Therapy
description: Cancer is a major public health problem in the United States and many other parts of the world. One in 4 deaths in the United States is due to cancer.  Natural medicine cure rates are more than 30 times higher than the cure rates of those who use chemotherapy, radiation and surgery.

title: Media Assistance for Small Nonprofits
description: We are increasing the capacity of nonprofits to tell their story in a way that generates support and stimulates new and more impactful projects. Funding will be used to provide a team of media and technology professionals to create, design, and implement a program of professional media assistance for small nonprofits, extending the reach of the organizations' message, spurring investment in their cause .

title: Teach Tech to 1500 low income girls in Bay Area
description: Project will provide 1500 low income youth, with an emphasis on women and girls, with free lessons in computer programming and computer literacy through keyboarding, and provide free meals during projects.

title: Economically Empower 7800 Rural Women in Uganda
description: 7800 Rural women of Mitooma district in Uganda are helped to improve their household income through giving and training in keeping dairy goats for milk production and selling them to earn income to help them save, invest to meet their future goals and be able to meet their household basic needs of life like health care, better housing facilities, education, food and water. The goat droppings  help in malaria prevention through burning their dropping in mud container at night.

title: House of Hope Orphanage and School
description: House of Hope is a Ugandan orphanage, school, and child empowerment center catering to vulnerable children in Uganda. The children are predominantly orphans, HIV+, abandoned, neglected, or abused children who have been removed from a harmful environment and brought to HOH for safety and love. When possible, children are placed with host families in the community, and HOH caters for all the child's needs such as education, clothing, hygiene, medical, food, emotional, and so forth.

title: Emergency Disaster Relief for Moturiki Fiji
description: A severe condition 5 hurricane plowed through Fiji on 19-20 February, killing at least 42 people and destroying thousands of homes, rendering over 50 thousand people homeless.  The community-based coral reef conservation sites on Morutiki Island, where we have worked since 2004 were very badly hit, with 90% of the houses destroyed by fierce winds and a two meter storm surge that swept into the villages. These people have given so much for conservation.... and now they need our help.

title: Art Therapy Workshop for Rehabilitating Soldiers
description: For the last 9 years, every Wednesday our volunteers gather at the Rehab. Dept. at Tel Hashomer hospital, to offer war veterans a free Art Therapy Workshop.  Our 'art students' are hospitalized for  months on end, far from home, struggling daily to return to their mental and physical abilities. They repeatedly tell us how the weekly art workshops are like a ray of sunlight in the hospital routine. We are seeking funds only for the purchase of the canvases, paint, brushes & easels.

title: Saving Belize's Birds
description: Belize Bird Rescue is the only multi-species avian rescue facility in Belize, rescuing orphaned, injured and illegally trafficked parrots and other wild birds of the Central American Rain-forests.

title: Hot Meals for Destitute Elderly Women
description: This project will bring nutritional support for a six month period - July through December 2016  - to sustain the destitute elderly women, who do not have family or long term care support. Twenty destitute elderly women will receive fresh, nutritional food support from WD every day.  With these hot meals the destitute elderly women health have improved health and quality of life.

title: Build a Photography Center For Refugees in Kenya
description: Gizzim Youth Group plans to build a photography and arts center in Nairobi/Kenya to cater for children who are refugees,street children and those at children's homes who are orphans and who come from the poorest sections of the city. We provide photography lessons to enable the children to stay away from crime, alcohol, substance abuse, and unwanted pregnancies.We teach a group of 300 children particularly the refugees who feel that they have lost their identity and sense of  belonging.

title: Empower Women to Change 2 More Sri Lankan Villages
description: When women take over the economy of their village, everything changes. Family life, health, education, social and civic life all are strengthened.  The YMCA village women's program is a mix of micro finance, empowerment, and community organization.  For a decade, groups of 20 women have been organized in east Sri Lanka - one village at a time.  You can support expansion to one of the next two villages.

title: Cuido terapeutico para madres solteras y sus ninos
description: El acceso a la atencion terapeutica proporcionara servicios terapeuticos a 25 ninos y sus madres solteras, jovenes y vulnerables en las siguientes disciplinas: Para ninos de 1 a 5 anos de edad, Terapia del Habla y Psicologia Pediatrica. Para sus madres: Servicios de consejeria clinicas y talleres sobre estilos de vida saludables y la autoestima.

title: DISHA & DOSTI - FREE Diabetes clinic for the Poor
description: Project DISHA which supports Type I (insulin dependent) diabetes children and youth through FREE Childhood Diabetes Clinic and free Insulin for every child.  Project DOSTI aims to foster optimal health, well-being and longevity of people suffering from diabetes mellitus, in a cost effective manner in  Bangalore urban and rural, State of Karnataka with free / subsidized Diabetes Clinic, medicines, tests and treatment.

title: Shammah School for Orphans and Street Children
description: The school was started in response to a critical need for education for orphans and street children. Children are forced to travel hundreds of miles to continue with their secondary education forcing many to give up from pursuing their educational dreams, especially children who lack financial resources. The school will serve approximately 720 students (boys and girls), in particular orphaned and street children. The school is located in Segese village, Kahama District in Shinyanga Tanzania.

title: Support 50 Muslim Girls to Become Nurses
description: Globally, Muslim women have lacked educational opportunities to benefit their communities even though nurses are the framework of public health. In 2015, AAI began supporting a Nursing program in Sulu Province, Philippines; a region of 19 island districts, a population of 1 million, and only 16 medical doctors. Our goal was to provide 50 female students with a quality education to launch their nursing careers. Thus far, AAI has helped 240 young women to become nurses.

title: Contribute to a solidary economic system
description: Banco de Tiempo contributes to an alternative economic system based on the exchange of services and activities, with time as the only form of payment. By facilitating a network of exchanges for people  living in the metropolitan area of Costa Rica, we help to create a community based on solidarity, honesty and trust. The activities and services provide a  possibility of learning, developing and enhancing well-being among our members without the use of money.

title: South Taiwan Earthquake Emergency Relief
description: World Vision Taiwan is raising money for assisting those families affected by the earthquake in rebuilding homes and hope. One of our major plans is Education Aid Program. This a three years program which will provide education materials, tuition aid, afterschool program to children from disadvantage families affected by earthquake.

title: Give 1000 Persons with Disabilities an Identity!
description: NOWPDP is facilitating the issuance of Special Computerized National Identity Cards (SCNICs) for persons with disabilities (PWDs), enabling members of this disenfranchised group to have access to their rights as Pakistani citizens and avail benefits offered by the public and private institutions for PWDs. Through this project, NOWPDP will organize five registration camps to facilitate the issuance of 1,000 SCNICs of persons with disabilities.

title: Training the Next Generation of Conservationists
description: This project will identify, train and encourage the next generation of 15 local conservationists in 10 countries (Costa Rica, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Malaysia, Maldives, Oman, Peru, Slovakia, South Africa, UAE) and host them on our expeditions.  We want to raise $7,500 for 15 placements in 2016 + $1,500 for a nascent community-based coral reef conservation programme in Oman, which is driven by past placements. TOTAL $9,000.

title: Support Over 100 Brazilian Social Innovators
description: This project will support the Social Good Brazil Lab; a social innovation incubator for early-stage, technology-related social initiatives that annually helps upwards of 100 Brazilian social entrepreneurs (Labbers) bring their ideas to fruition.|Este projeto ira apoiar o Social Good Brasil Lab: um programa de aceleracao para iniciativas sociais em estagio inicial que usam a tecnologia. Anualmente o Lab ajuda cerca de 100 empreendedores sociais brasileiros a tirarem suas ideias do papel.

title: Fiji Cyclone Disaster Response
description: For over five months All Hands Volunteers has been working hard to provide immediate assistance to communities in Fiji affected by category 5 Cyclone Winston.  To date we have been able to provide household emergency hygiene and sanitation solutions in over 18 different villages. This intervention is crucial in order to prevent the spread of life-threatening disease, but with 28,000 homes damaged or destroyed, the needs are still great.

title: "Ofarim" - School for Autistic Children
description: Ofarim is a developing school for Jewish, Muslim, and Christian children with severe  autism. It combines technological teaching methods and innovative treatments. The school opened in 2014 due to the distress of children with autism who did not have a place in any existing school.  The school is working to develop cognitive abilities, emotional, and social functionality of the students. Ofarim thrives to find unique ways for teaching the students despite the complex difficulties.

title: Sustainable Skills and Empowerment for the Youth
description: Another Hope Children's Ministries would like to reduce vulnerability and dependency among the young people by 20% in 5 Districts of Central Uganda (Kampala, Mpigi, Wakiso, Mityana and Mubende) through vocational skills training. This project will benefit 12,000 Youth in the 5 Districts of Central Uganda hence reducing  the unemployment rate among the youth and increasing the number of youth joining Vocational schools rather than Degree courses that have no ready jobs.

title: Waiting for New Premises
description: Our association currently helps people in need with meals every evening in winter in a corridor of a metro station downtown Brussels. We aim to improve this by moving to new premises, close by, and fitting them in order to improve preparation / delivery of meals and ease the work for our teams. To make this possible, the more we manage to save on our yearly ordinary expenses (rent, disposable, food etc) the sooner we can start looking for new premises and a new kitchen, new kitchen utensils etc.

title: Healing for 70 Trafficking & Abuse Victims, Kosovo
description: RED International's partner in Kosovo is Operacioni i Mekembjes (Operation Restoration). They are the only organisation providing long-term support to victims of domestic violence and trafficking, as well as combating the conditions which lead individuals to become victims or aggressors through education and training programmes for vulnerable young people. Through an individualised programme of psychotherapy, emotional therapy and vocational skills training, more than 70 women and young peop

title: Build Water Stations for the Donkeys
description: Donkeys are the most worked animal at difference areas of Kahama district, with more than 10.000 donkey's populations being present  The donkeys working  system is constrained by lack of proper place for drinking clean and the owner have no means of giving water for their animal rather than left themselves to find water. donkey are worked more than 8 hours without rest or cool their thirsty  and many donkey become exhausted .The project will build ten donkey water troughs at local villages

title: Plant & protect 10000 trees in San Luis Potosi
description: This project will plant and protect 10,000 trees in San Luis Potosi City, Mexico, in order to restore, enhance and protect the tree canopy of the city. Proforestal, A.C. is a non-profit organization leading the effort to build healthy, livable communities in San Luis Potosi region.

title: Primary Pro-Health Programme for  Women
description: Our project focuses on health. We give a village woman knowledge and basic tools and training to take responsibility for her own health, then that of her family's and then the health of the community.

title: Support 200 women coffee farmers
description: This project led by the Kahawatu Foundation helps rural women in Burundi to earn sustainable income from coffee production. It also supports women coffee farmers to secure food supply for their families. This project promotes new gender roles, encourages both men and women to question existing patriarchal customs and increase their collaboration and respect in, and outside the field.

title: End Human Rights Abuses Against Alleged Witches
description: This project will work to safely return the hundreds of women living in the Kukuo camp for alleged witches to their original communities after being violently banished due to witchcraft accusations.

title: HUMANITARIAN WATER RELIEF PROJECT
description: The increasing threat of clean drinking water shortage constitutes one of the biggest challenges to Pakistan's survival. This threat is not less dangerous than that of terrorism because it has been taking millions of lives, especially those of children, every year. District Tharparker has been on top risk due to drought situation no drinking water no food etc. FRDP will help the poor people through this project to provide them safe drinking water through the installation of Hand Pumps & Dug well

title: Helping Children &Families Living w/CysticFibrosis
description: Claire's Place Foundation is a  non-profit organization providing support to children and families affected by cystic fibrosis (CF). Claire's Place Foundation is named in honor of Claire Wineland, now a teenager, who has been living with CF her entire life. We provide Extended Hospital Stay grants to families experiencing hospital stays of at least 14 consecutive days, offering both emotional and financial support.

title: "Hey kids-Check Your Water Before You Drink"
description: The project has been prepared with the objectives of Environmental Awareness among School Students as well as community; this will not only give them an experience of team work, but will also make them Environmental Aware.

title: Protect Filipino Kids From the Deadly Dengue Virus
description: About 3,174 Filipinos, mostly children and teenagers have already died from Dengue (2,576 from 2011 to 2014 and 598 in 2015) and the number is growing exponentially every year. The Philippines is one of the 4 countries in the Western Pacific with the highest dengue incidence in recent years and the Health Department is in dire need of funds to sustain its school-based dengue control program that includes the installation of insecticide treated nets (ITNs) in windows of public elementary school.

title: Provide Washable Pads for 4000 girls in Nigeria
description: The stigma and taboo of menstruation is a human rights issue. Lack of sustainable menstrual hygiene solutions push menstruating girls out of school leading to school dropout, Child Early Forced Marriage and gender inequality which is an obstacle to SDG 5.We are providing washable menstrual hygiene kits that last 3years and bathing soap that last 6months. We also talk to them about reproductive health education, rape, HIV/AIDS, contraceptive usage and also dispel the myths surrounding the issue.

title: Transform 200 children through music in San Juan
description: The project seeks to increase the impact of the Center for Children Artistic Development -CDAI- in San Juan Sacatepequez. CDAI has brough a life-transforming musical education to 1,300 children and their families in San Juan, one of the most violent municipalities in Guatemala. 200 children have asked to join the parent's school, early stimulation and musical programs of CDAI, so the project looks for allowing these kids to join the Center in order to transform their lifes through music

title: Support UPO's Foster Grandparents Program
description: Before COVID arrived, 200 UPO "Foster Grandparents" (senior volunteers) were annually serving 6,000 socio-economically disadvantaged children in Washington, DC. They engaged in-person tutoring, mentoring, and social emotional support assisting students in classrooms. Proven outcomes were improved school readiness and K-12 success. During the pandemic, the switch to virtual learning changed our operation: We focused on computer literacy education for the Foster Grandparents.

title: Help Us Get 30 Marginalized Women Into Business
description: These funds will help us to give small business loans to women who have very poor life background who would not otherwise get loans from any other financial institutions, because they don't have the loan security and other loan requirements.   These women, regardless of their poor life backgrounds, they have a lot of faith in their competence to run small business and have the right altitude and willingness to do change their lives for better.   Your donations are going to make this happen!

title: Educate and Empower Women in South Kivu
description: Together we can provide educational and income-generating opportunities for single women and women as head of households living in the Kalonge Bitale region of the Kalehe territory, South Kivu Province, Democratic Republic of Congo. Many women in this region face immense inequality and dire poverty. This project will provide women with the literacy and finance training with counseling and support resources to start small businesses to help them become self-sufficient.

title: Mealewya Water Project
description: Your donation will provide  access to clean water for rural communities  that has been victimized by persistent drought.   Clean water helps keep  the community healthy. Women and girls will spend less time fetching water and will have free time to attend school. Having toilets at school means teenage girls don't have to miss class when they have their periods.  Clean water enables the community to grow ample food and generate more income to improve their living condition.

title: 400 Youths Combat Teen Pregnancy in Thailand
description: "Combat Teen Pregnancy" project builds capacity of 400 youths to campaign on teen pregnancy prevention in 5 provinces of Thailand where births to adolescent mothers doubled from 2000-2012. In 12 months they will advocate sexuality education with 8,000 peers in 25 schools and with 10,000 families through radio, newspaper, video clip, and fun activities such as puppet theatre, role play, and skits.

title: Help 30 Tanzanian girls on Vocational Training
description: This project intends to give skills training in tailoring & embroidery courses for sustainable livelihoods to vulnerable girls in Kilombero District in Tanzania. With this vocational skills training girls live with dignity by earning themselves. During this training, beneficiaries will learn and develop skills in tailoring & embroidery work on sarees, blouse pieces. We provide Sewing Machine, Tool Kit to survive on their own and live with Dignity.

title: Build  classrooms for 500 poor children.
description: This project will build five classrooms to provide free education for poor children and orphans who hail from the poorest communities in Mulanga Village. We hope to secure the materials and resources necessary to build and operate a primary school in Mulanga, going some way towards lifting the community out of poverty. The Community has already donated 2 acres of land to support this cause.

title: Feed 125 vulnerable pregnant and lactating mothers
description: Diamond Mothers Centre (DMC) seeks to provide nutritious meals to 125 pregnant and lactating mothers from vulnerable households within Mathare Slums in Nairobi, Kenya.  Under the auspices of St Teresa Catholic Church, DMC holds weekly meetings with mothers and provides them with appropriate information, training, and raises general awareness about exclusive breastfeeding, continued breastfeeding with complimentary feeding for up to two years and child health.

title: Empower dropouts & school children in South India
description: BWDA Vacation Schools are week-long summer schools for rural children (ages 6-14) in 100 centres in Tamil Nadu, Pondicherry & Andaman Islands in South India. The aim is to encourage school dropouts and poor children to start or continue with primary education. The lessons offer a creative, cultural & community based outlook for children, cultivating in them a desire for stable education. Till date, the vacation schools have benefitted 185,896 children in 2208 centres, including 20,000 dropouts.

title: Care Center for abandoned cats & dogs in Turkey
description: In Turkey, everyday thousand of puppies and kittens are sold in the pet-shops just like stuffed animals and most of them found themselves abandoned on the streets within couple of months in miserable conditions, all breeds and age, these pets are starved to death, got run by a car or beaten by people. This project will help us to develop our care centre properly  for these pets including handicapped ones so we can keep them safe, treat the sick ones and finally place them with a loving family.

title: Build School Toilets To Save Lives And End Poverty
description: This project aims at providing adequate toilet facilities and clean, potable water to the 1000 pupils who attend Abiola Nursery and Primary School, a low-income school in Mushin (a slum) in Lagos State, and in the process save lives, improve child health, ensure greater dignity, privacy, and personal safety, particularly for girls. We hope to build a toilet facility comprising 5 well-equipped toilet stalls and also install a borehole that will enable pupils get easy access to clean water.

title: Equal Access to Global Citizenship Education
description: SIMA Academy, known as the"Netflix of Global Education" allows students to experience current affairs through the eyes and stories of those on the front lines. By providing learners with carefully curated award-winning documentaries and VR/360, paired with dynamic teaching resources, students cultivate vital critical thinking skills to help inspire empathy and guide each student through emotion to action. We want to ensure equal access to all students regardless of their economic background.

title: Revenue Creation for Women in Rural Haiti
description: Haiti has upward of 65% unemployment. The rate is even higher among women in the rural areas.  Lambi Fund in partnership with local organizations will reinforce micro credit funding for women to build and maintain their small business enterprises.  They will also receive training on managing their selected revenue streams.  This project will create revenue for members of women-led grassroots organizations.  It will increase their capacities to care for their families and build their communities.

title: Youth Cleanup Campaign for 3 Communities in Ghana
description: This project aims to rekindle a sense of community engagement through conservation education, training, organizing and assisting in massive cleanup activities for youths in 3 rural communities in southern Ghana on the need to keep clean communities  and reduce, re-use, recycle and compost waste.

title: Feed Marginalized Families Through Gardens
description: The community of potters in Masoro is a historically marginalized population that faces poverty and severe food shortages in Rwanda. To promote food security and economic development HDI will construct sac gardens and conduct trainings in order to empower women to provide food and income for their families.

title: Empowering 100 vulnerable children in Kiambiu slum
description: The main goal is to support the Glory center school located in Kiambiu slums in Nairobi in order to provide free education to around 100 children who hail from the poorest in the informal dwellings. It will also support them with other basic needs which will create a conducive learning environment.

title: Save women from breast cancer in South Africa
description: Hoedspruit Training Trust, now formally Hlokomela is based in Limpopo, South Africa. Limpopo is one of the worst areas in South Africa for poverty, whilst lacking basic facilities in the local villages such as running water. Hlokomela is an established non-profit clinic committed to serving farm workers and their families. Our goal is to provide a cost-effective and sustainable way to screen for and treat breast cancer, preventing hundreds of deaths each year.

title: Eradicate Jiggers Among 500 Children in Bungoma
description: This project will hold 8 treatment camps in Bungoma County to sensitize 8 target communities on child healthcare, treat at least 60 jigger infested children in every target community, spray 250 jigger infested homes and offer shoes to 500 bare footed kids.

title: Celebrate National Kidney Month with a gift to NKF
description: The National Kidney Foundation (NKF) is calling on you to join the fight against kidney disease.  Over 26 million Americans have kidney disease and most don't know it. Early detection and treatment can slow or even prevent the progression of kidney disease. That's why NKF's community based initiative, KEEP Healthy, offers free kidney health screenings to those at-risk of kidney disease.  With the support of people like you, we can continue advancing our mission.

title: Empower 200 children and their guardian in Nigeria
description: This project seeks to eradicate the problems of children in difficult circumstances in Nigeria i.e HIV/AIDS affected and infected children, malnourished children, Child workers, Abandoned and neglected children, Street children. This project will provide Family and Community-based care, Household Economic Strengthening, Food Security/Nutrition, Health care, Education and Psychosocial support for 200 children that are vulnerable. Their guardian will be empowered for sustainable livelihood.

title: Build a Safe- Eco Friendly House for Girls at Risk
description: This project will provide a permanent home for orphans and vulnerable children, basic healthcare, formal and informal education. Your donation buys materials to construct a safe and eco-friendly house for girls that are living in a small rented house downtown the city of Medellin, Colombia which is in precarious situation.

title: Send a girl to school in Nigeria for one year
description: It is no longer a breaking news that Nigeria is in security and economic meltdown. Consequently, there is widespread poverty in the communities making it difficult for parents to prioritize the education of girls. Girls Education Mission International is on a mission to defend, protect and promote the education of girls who experience violence and are denied chances to enroll, stay and succeed in school and beyond. The education of 15 girls in significant financial need will be supported.

title: Feed 300 Wayuu in drought-stricken Guajira
