title: Maternal and Child Health Clinics
description: The aim of HopeCore's Maternal and Child Health Clinics is to improve the health of the women and children in our communities through education, prevention, and curative services.  Children are monitored for growth, given Vitamin A and dewormers, and referred to the nurses if they are in need of any further clinical services. Mothers are lectured on topics such as family planning, nutrition and breastfeeding and clinically treated when necessary.

title: Fight Against Violent Births in Brazil
description: One in four Brazilian women reports suffering from obstetric violence during pregnancy or birth: abusive medical procedures which infringe on mother and baby's basic human rights and can lead to serious health consequences. The Golden Hour is a national network of birth professionals working together to fight against such violence. The project contributes to the empowerment of women by providing quality information, enabling them to make conscious and autonomous choices.

title: Equip 200 Jamaican Youth to Combat Climate Change
description: With your support, international development nonprofit ACDI/VOCA will conduct a one-day, educational Climate Camp this summer in Kingston, Jamaica. The camp will prepare 200 Jamaican youth ages 8-17 to become change agents in their communities. Climate Camp will feature age-appropriate training sessions, multimedia presentations, small-group discussions, hands-on activities, games, and competitions, which will provide participating youth with strategies to combat the effects of climate change.

title: Transform Consumerism in Sao Paulo, Brazil
description: Rede Rizoma (Rhizome Network) is an online platform that aims to help consumers and producers of perishable goods in Brazil. This project will first be implemented in the 96 districts of Sao Paulo. It connects consumers directly with local producers according to locations and interests, making purchasing collectively possible. By buying collectively, consumers can enjoy lower prices and producers better remunerations since there are now less transactions and actors in the production chain.

title: Foundation Preparatory Academy Science Wing
description: Foundation Preparatory Academy Science Wing aims to address the current challenges in the field of Science education more specifically in the elementary and high school levels. This can be done through advanced technology and with the aid of laboratories and equipment for enhanced academic learning.

title: Protect a brand new mouse lemur in Madagascar!
description: Extreme poverty is contributing to already catastrophic forest destruction in Madagascar. The habitat of endangered animals like mouse lemurs is fast disappearing. Project Microcebus will help ensure the long-term survival of mouse lemurs, engaging communities through environmental education, tree planting and encouraging them to protect its threatened habitat. Research will alert the global community to a new candidate species and strengthen the case for the protection of these forests.

title: Lawyers For Change (LFC)
description: LFC is a learning platform that seeks to build a resource & support base for social justice lawyers to galvanise a movement across India by connecting them. We hope to pioneer as the go-to place for social justice lawyers negotiating the labyrinth called Indian judicial system. We believe this will fundamentally subvert how we use the law as a tool for empowerment & ensuring access to human rights for all. Join us & contribute to creating a just and vibrant society.

title: Protecting Tigers in Thailand
description: Over 95% of the world's wild tigers have been lost in the last 100 years and with as few as 3,500 remaining it is vital that we act now to protect them and their vital forest habitats. Thailand is home to a significant population of c.200 tigers. Working across five national parks, our primary aim is to build anti-poaching capacity among park rangers and to break the poaching cycle by engaging with local communities and children of poachers to change attitudes towards tigers and wildlife.

title: Feed 20 Neglected Tuberculosis Victims in India
description: In 2014, there were 9.6 million cases of active TB which resulted in 1.5 million deaths. If left untreated, TB kills about half of those infected. Medication is issued by the Indian government, however most of the victims, being laborers or farmers, have no means of support while they are sick. The treatment often fails because the sufferer does not make a full recovery due to malnutrition. They  either die or continue to spread the disease. This project aims to break this cycle.

title: Protecting Snow Leopards
description: The mysterious snow leopard is known as the ghost of the Asian mountains. The biggest threat to them, is us, and our impact on their habitat. These elusive cats are threatened by habitat fragmentation as human populations continue to grow and the climate crisis intensifies.  By funding holistic initiatives, DSWF works alongside communities, governments and law enforcement experts in Asia to provide snow leopards with the greatest form of protection.

title: Become a Magic Maker this Christmas
description: Let's Make Even More Magic: Help make our big plans a reality and bring the magic of Barretstown to even more children like Amanda With your help in 2017 we will deliver our life transforming programmes to more children than ever before!

title: Build a Birthing Center in Uganda for 1,000+ Women
description: This project will build a Birthing Center in the Jinja District of Uganda, providing a safe, clean, and dignified environment for expecting Ugandan mothers. Ugandan woman and their newborn infants continue to die needlessly from preventable causes as a result of poor access to and quality maternal healthcare in facilities. The Birthing Center will be a state-of-the-art facility that works in partnership with local communities to empower 1,000+ Ugandan women to deliver with dignity.

title: Fight Hunger in Brazil Using Food Waste
description: Connecting Food is an online platform that aims to help NGOs in Brazil improve and innovate their current food collection system, which will in turn fulfill the needs of thousands of Brazilian people who struggle with hunger. In order to accomplish this, Connecting Food brings together technology, education and a system of "social franchise" to connect large retailers with Brazilian NGOs and reduce the social, economic and environmental impact of food waste in Brazil.

title: Technical Aid to 25 Cochabambinos w Disabilities
description: Tukuy Pacha aims to improve the independence of people with serious disabilities in 5 municipalities of Cochabamba, Bolivia by endowing them with assistive equipment for their daily activities. Technical aid allows people with disabilities to become active in their community, move more freely, and feel safe when they leave their homes. An extensive medical and social analysis ensures that each case will be provided the correct tools to boost their quality of life.

title: Empower 2,200 Deaf in Brazil with Education
description: Many Deaf children in Brazil do not have access to quality education, resulting in an inability to master their own language - the sign language. Surdo para Surdo is a Brazilian tutoring platform designed to help the Deaf community in Brazil by connecting Deaf who want to learn with Deaf who are interested in teaching.

title: Help 48,000 People in Brazil Combat Mosquitoes
description: Communitor aims to help the residents of Aglomerado da Serra, the largest slum in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil fight the battle against mosquito-borne diseases, such as Dengue Fever, Yellow Fever, Zika and Chikungunya. It creates a map of the distribution of mosquitos and occurrences of disease cases, which is then used to predict disease outbreaks and plan resource allocation. Such geographical information significantly improves the effectiveness of vector control.

title: Run RTFs American Wild Horse Sanctuary for a Year
description: Now in its 25th year, Return to Freedom's American Wild Horse Sanctuary cares for over 500 wild horses and 42 burros, using minimally intrusive population management techniques that can be applied on and off the range as an alternative to government roundups. The sanctuary provides educational programs, reunites wild horse families, safeguards their quality of life--with medical care and a forever home. RTF advocates for policy reforms to protect their brothers and sisters on the range.

title: Cultural education without disparity
description: RASA is an organisation serving the cause of empowering people with differing abilities for over  27 years and has successfully enriched the lives of several thousand beneficiaries  . RASA provides  for  empowerment of individuals with every need and includes individuals with mental and physical challenges in its ambiance , Rasa's integrated approach to development is  one of its kind.  The development at Rasa happens through the experience of Indian Theatre Arts.  RASA 's work is honorary.

title: Biodiversity Restoration Along the Tsurumi River
description: Green belt 1km along the left bank of the Tsurumi River, Tsunashima, Yokohma, Japan has been invaded by foreign plants causing pollen allergies, degrading the amenity of the otherwise popular area . We plan to restore the vegetation to the one composed of a native grass, Ogi that produces a safer and biodiversity rich area. To attain this we need financial support for three year's work of rearing Ogi displacing invading plants .This will benefit thousands of citizens and native biodiversity.

title: Hands Off Our Grants Campaign (HOOG)
description: This project is protecting the rights of millions of social grant beneficiaries, who are dependant on Social Assistance for their livelihoods. Unlawful and unjust deductions by various corporate companies have depleted thousands of grants, including the child, foster and pension grants. The HOOG Campaign is about stopping these unlawful deductions and bringing recourse to the victims.

title: Improve the Health of Mother and Child in Nzega
description: The campaign goals is to increase the rate of nutrition and breastfeeding babies exclusively breastfed for at least six months in Nzega Tanzania. Our Specific goal is to provide nutrition education and breastfeed babies exclusively breastfed for at least six months earlier, among young mothers, nurses, volunteers and conducting quarterly meeting to District Nutrition Steering Committee in Nzega District.  Project will train 53 on nutrition and breastfeed babies exclusively breastfed.

title: Support 500 Students to Pass Year 10 Examinations
description: The students part of this program come from an economically poor background and are forced to work during the day in order to support their families. They attend night school in order to obtain their education. Masoom is supporting beneficiaries through Material Distribution Drive - a provision of extra classes and study materials to prepare for Secondary School Certificate (SSC) exams to enable them to complete their basic schooling with good grades that can help them in building a good future.

title: Empower 300 Bal Sansads in Bihar To Drive Change
description: The Anandshala program strives to help students stay, engage and learn in school. Through capacity building and advocacy, it works to drive leadership for change at various levels of the education system: school coaches, headmasters, teachers and student parliaments. This project under Anandshala is designed to strengthen the system to tailor its own solutions to the problems of student retention and engagement. It will cater to 90,000 students through student parliaments in 300 middle schools.

title: Help 2.1m Children of Prisoners in Europe to Cope
description: Not my crime, still my sentence: Across Europe, some 2.1 million children have a parent in prison. They suffer emotional, social and economic difficulties and need targeted support. Regular contact with a parent in prison promotes resilience in children. Our teams accompany children on prison visits; provide advice and psychological support; train prison staff; listen to young people. We raise awareness in communities and schools and support the rights and needs of these hard-to-reach children.

title: Scholarships for Youth Social Entrepreneurs
description: SINAL seeks to reduce youth unemployment in marginalized communities in Brazil through creating an apprenticeship program in the new professions of sustainability. With our partners the Do School,  next year for 10 weeks 20 young social entrepreneurs from around the globe will come to SINAL for the "Apprenticeship Challenge" - where they will work on this real-life innovation challenge to develop new economic opportunities for youth around the country and create a more sustainable future.

title: Build Development Center for 300 Colombian Kids
description: La Fundacion Las Golondrinas has built one-third of a new center for early-childhood development but requires additional funding to continue construction.  The early-childhood center will serve young children in Llanaditas, Medellin, a marginal neighborhood where many families live in poverty and have been forcibly displaced by violence and conflict.

title: Promoting Human Rights of Refugees in Europe
description: We believe the humanitarian crises unfolding across Europe require a strategic and long-term advocacy approach and sustained pressure from civil society actors. We furthermore believe a regional, national and international response to asylum and migration that upholds the human rights of people seeking refuge in Europe is perfectly possible. In 2020, we will continue calling for change, from ensuring humane living conditions in transit points to stopping the obstruction of asylum procedures.

title: Hot meals 1500 Children 3x a Week in Gaza KGs
description: KinderUSA's Nutritional Meals for Kindergartens provides 1500 children attending 12 kindergartens (aged 4-6) in marginalized and war-torn regions of Gaza with nutritious meals at school three times a week during the spring (February - May)  and fall (September - November) 2017 school semesters. The project simultaneously provides training in food production for 23 female heads of household,  employing 5 hearing impaired women as trainers in the project  to prepare the meals,

title: Unleash the skills of 1000 global problem solvers!
description: Support the skills development of global innovators and entrepreneurs working primarily in low income and resource-strapped communities to bring their ideas to fruition and elevate their communities out of poverty. The Global Knowledge Initiative brings advanced, intensive training programs to problem solvers around the world. Our program enables individuals to collaborate and garner the tools and resources needed to affect long-term change in fields such as agriculture, health and education.

title: Reconstruction of schools in earthquake areas
description: The earthquake of Augiust 2016 in central Italy has left many populations without homes, schools, hospitals etc.. we are funding the reconstruction of the schools in Arquata del Tronto.

title: SavingOurVets Survival Packs for Homeless Veterans
description: The American Homeless Families Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit committed to feeding homeless Veterans. Food and warm clothing are essential for survival during a time when shelter has become a grave situation. Through the Gift of Giving our exclusive Survival Packs to homeless Veterans, you give each Veteran food for 30 days and winter clothes to stay warm. By supplying a full month of food and warmth, we are greatly impacting survival rates of homeless Veterans in our communities.

title: Emancipation Weeping Girls from Sexual Abuse
description: Release , resettlement of girls, victims of human trafficking sold for forced prostitution. Virgin Girls are underprivileged & deprived of human rights. We deliverance them in respectable community and will give the secure future with needy tools and skills with information.

title: Infant & Mother Health in Nepal's Arsenic Areas
description: Neonatal mortality in Nepal's high arsenic areas is 12.4 %. Safe water filters and good nutrition for these families will significantly decrease the mortality rate and increase the number of healthy children. Our target is to conduct 4 workshops for 60 women in early 2017, providing filters to each family, Nutrition and Hygiene Workshops, training to Health students and Female Health Volunteers. The Female Health Volunteers will conduct the 2 year monitoring program. This project will help  >480

title: Inspire 60 Girls in West Baltimore Thru Mentoring
description: We Inspire Girls to Embrace a 'Life of Promise' through long term one-on-one, group and peer mentoring relationships for 60 middle school girls in Baltimore City through after school programming and youth development activities that focus on the "total" girl - social, academic, spiritual, physical, emotional, relational, behavioral, etc.

title: Support 200 Women Caring for AIDS Orphans in Kenya
description: Impact: With time there will be tangible changes in some of the customary laws that impose on women and deny them the right to access good education. Training women to know their rights will eventually impact positively the HIV Prevalence and Incidence rates in the regions and nationally. Who we are helping:  Women, girls and men  How we are solving a problem:  Women will be taught their rights to own, inherit, and control property amidst unchanging discriminatory laws and customs.

title: Health Education for 100 Youth with Disabilities
description: Healthy Lifestyle Education And Practice (LEAP) increases healthy behaviors (exercise, nutritious foods, hydration, sun safety) and decreases unhealthy habits (screen time, sugary drinks, empty calories) in children with intellectual disabilities.  This project will provide Healthy LEAP curricula, sports equipment  and all related materials for 100 special needs Preschool children in Arizona schools in 2017.  These children will be empowered to overcome health risks inherent in their disability.

title: Bring Music as Therapy to Struggling Youth
description: My Voice Music brings all the instruments, instructors, and recording equipment needed to run songwriting and recording programs to youth in lockdown mental health treatment centers and jails.  This project will support our work with over 20 separate programs in the Portland area that serve incarcerated youth, immigrant youth, and youth facing extreme mental health challenges.  When youth are given the opportunity to share their voice through music it can be a transformative experience.

title: Help Keep 15 Aspiring Ugandan Girls in School
description: This project will help keep 15 Ugandan girls in school by helping to pay for necessary costs like tuition, exam fees, books & boarding costs.  Most girls are in secondary or vocational school (grades 7 - 12) which is unaffordable for most of their parents/guardians since the girls come from very poor families.  In some cases, the child may have 1 sponsor who can pay 50% of the schooling amount but the family is unable to pay the balance.  Most girls cannot continue beyond 6th grade without help.

title: Educate & Feed 130 Children In Red Light Areas
description: South Kolkata Hamari Muskan works primarily with the children in red light areas of Sonagachi, South Asia's largest red light district, and Bowbazar. The children born in the red light areas are always under the heightened risk of child trafficking and child sexual abuse. South Kolkata Hamari Muskan's day and night creches provide education, psychological support and nutrition to 130 children in these areas.

title: Free Veterinary Clinics
description: We offer free veterinary care to the pets of people experiencing homelessness or living in extreme poverty. By offering these services, we save lives and alleviate suffering .

title: Restoring 10 Mangrove Forests in Kenya
description: Through the #TwendeGreenCampaign, the project will restore livelihoods to 1000 households along the Kenyan coast by planting over 1million mangroves and  training 10 community groups on alternative income generating projects. These are households whose main source of income is obtained from beach and ocean operations including artisanal fishing, all which have been affected by climate change forcing them to embark on charcoal burning and hence the loss of mangrove forests.

title: Create a Library for 350 Kids in Rural Nicaragua
description: From Books to Brilliance will create a village library in the impoverished rural community of Paz y Vida, Nicaragua. This lending library will be located in a newly built community  center.  From Books to Brilliance volunteers will purchase all books and educational materials in Nicaragua.  Aligned to Paz y Vida's specific requests, these resources will serve approximately 350 children who live in Paz y Vida as well as in the surrounding villages.

title: Empowering 200 Awajun Youths to Prevent HIV
description: The Awajun are Amazonian people with one of the highest HIV infection rates in Peru, due to a lack of understanding of the disease and the continuity of cultural practices that favor its transmission. This project aims to empower 200 Awajun youths by providing appropriate HIV information, which will be recreated by them and shared with their peers using an understandable language with adequate allusions bridging the communication gaps that exists between health services and indigenous peoples.

title: Give 110 Nepalese Families the Gift of Clean Water
description: Clean water at the local school and in the village wards will provide immediate and long-term impact on health, improved sanitation, and hygiene for 572 residents and 437 students in rural Nepal.  Water delivered from a remote safe water source reduces women's chore of fetching water up steep mountains and carrying it down challenging trails, greatly improving quality of life, improving health, and giving these people time and energy to create and operate businesses to improve livelihoods.

title: Girls: Better after quake
description: A 9 months mentorship program aimed at unleashing the social leadership of 15 adolescent girls of earthquake affected area of Nepal. This project will reach out to the girls in an individually tailored, empowering them with diverse skills.  Nuwakot is a district with one of the highest destruction caused by earthquake in 2015, labor migration among adults and highest rate of girls trafficking. Hence, the need to enhance the leadership of adolescent girls is not only necessary but imperative.

title: 80 children in poverty to play sports in NL
description: The Jeugdsportfonds foundation creates opportunities to participate in sports for children and teenagers under 18 years old who otherwise would not be able to join sports clubs because their families lack the necessary financial means. Being able to participate in team sports is important for children's physical, intellectual, and social development. It costs 250 to allow one child or teenager to participate in a sports club for one year. Let's try to help 200 together with Nike.

title: Empower 400 young leaders in Permaculture, Bolivia
description: Our Permaculture Practitioner Young Leaders Program provides practical training for 400 middle school students from agricultural areas. The Permaculture techniques we teach will be aimed at improving soil fertility, harvesting water, and building living interactions that save time and increase productivity. Hands on instruction will give practicioners the tools needed to go back to their communities as leaders in sustainable development and healthy living.

title: Support Bilingual Musical Theatre in Paris
description: Help create the first bilingual Musical Theater Center in Paris. In our new space in the heart of the city of light, interdisciplinary artists will hone their crafts while fostering collaborative, international exchanges in a welcoming, bilingual environment. Our non-profit association invites all to enjoy quality performances and educational opportunities in a space dedicated to cultural exchange.

title: LightUp Lives Early Ed for 75Marginalized Children
description: Freedom for You runs a Child Learning Center 'Bal Niketan Vidyalay' in slums of Rabale, Navi Mumbai provides crucial early education to tiny-tots, age 2-5 years, of rag-picker/daily wage-earner parents. For these parents struggling to make ends meet, sending their kids to school takes second priority, able to feed them being the first. CLC provides mid-day meal; Infra cost of  additional room, play equipment, educational aids, one-set uniform/shoes and first year operational cost totals USD7500

title: Technology to Tap Toddler Talk
description: Children who are deaf or hard of hearing are not able to develop the ability to listen and talk without appropriate technology and specialized supports. This project will provide technology that measures the quality and quantity of interactive talk. This, in turn, will help families enrich their child's listening environment and communication and better enable their child who is deaf or hard of hearing to develop rich spoken language and listening skills for learning.

title: Empower Tanzanian Girls Through Education
description: Help us empower 1500 of Tanzania's Maasai  girls and young women through education for them and their communities. Goal one is to free girls from harmful traditional practices and attitudes that deny them education, while exposing them to abuse such a Female Genital Mutilation, child labour and child marriage,  early teen pregnancies (with their appalling maternal and infant mortality rates), and from HIV/AIDS, which is often the result of rape.  Our second goal is to disrupt the poverty cycle.

title: Gift a Smile to 54 Cleft Children in Karnataka
description: Trinity Care Foundation plans to provide free surgeries for Cleft children who hail from the poorest sections of society in Karnataka State, also providing the children with speech therapy and further treatments. Your donation helps to provide free reconstructive surgeries and emotional counseling to support these children and their families.

title: Toys for Cambodian Children
description: Celebrate this holiday season by purchasing a toy for a disadvantaged Cambodian child. Not only will you be making a child smile, but you will also be helping vulnerable families in the local community; all the toys are made by parents in our Home-Based Production Program, a program that helps poor families develop a steady, safe source of income generation.

title: Build School Without Fear for 1000 Children
description: Violence in schools existing, each year about 246 million children suffered from violence or abuse in schools or nearby areas in global level. For lacking of a comprehensive and effective child protection system, especially in schools, children facing risks brought by violence/ abuse, which leads negative effect self-depreciation, aggressive behavior, and unplanned pregnancy etc. The program plans to build and pilot child protection system in 2 schools which is expected to impact 1000 children.

title: Investing in Women Leading the Change
description: Unlock the leadership potential of women in Asia by providing mentorship and scholarships to complete higher education and become change-makers in their communities.  We currently serve over 300 Rising Stars and as we scale up to reach our goal of supporting 1,000 by 2018, we are fundraising to provide more scholarship funding and leadership development than ever before.

title: Support Women & Children in Armenia Fleeing Abuse
description: The Women's Support Center runs two shelters to support women and children from all across Armenia who are fleeing violence. In the absence of State support, this is a service that is desperately needed in the country. Your support today will go toward rent, utilities, food, hygienic products, and medical care for 50 women and children to help them regain their dignity and rebuild their lives in a healthy, supportive, and safe environment free of abuse.

title: Lisanga, houses for unaccompanied minor refugees
description: There has, understandably,  been a lot of attention for the youngest unaccompanied minors arriving in Europe, we have also opened extra places to accommodate those under the age of 12. However we feel that we should not forget those older than 12. There are a lot of unaccompanied minor who, once they have been recognized as refugees, have to leave their provided housing. We have therefor decided to provide housing and care for 20 youngsters (15y-18y) in houses rented by us with daily care.

title: Threads of hope: empower women from Tamil Nadu
description: The project stems from the need to increase employment opportunities for women in an extremely poor region of India. It promotes the achievement of a high-school diploma through courses of dressmaking or IT skills and it supports these young women to start their own business.  The project is aimed at women living in Nagercoil and neighbouring villages.

title: A Wheelchair Bicycle Tandem for Aksi
description: Access to sports, moving and fresh air is a boost for all people, but not always easy when you have a physical disability.  A wheelchair bicycle tandem is a perfect tool to combine all three and will improve the spirit, physical condition and connection of cyclist and wheelchair athlete.

title: Love life. Fight cancer. Support our fellows!
description: Only together we can make a real difference to help Fight cancer. Out of love for life, we want to make this happen, together with you! We support cancer research through the Dutch Cancer Society. Specifically, we support fellows: young talents in the medical world, whom we believe will be our heroes in the future when it comes to cancer research. With you support, we can finance fellowships, which enables these young talents to pioneer at the best research centers worldwide and develop knowledg

title: Domestic Violence Education Program
description: My Sisters' Place promotes safety and social change by providing opportunities for middle school-age students, teens, and adults to increase their knowledge of the warning signs and dynamics of dating/domestic violence. The aim of the project is to help the next generations create relationships based on respect and equality and to increase the number of youth-serving adults who are better attuned to identify and assist victims.

title: Making a House a Home for Domestic Abuse Survivors
description: When women and children flee domestic abuse to live in one of Solace Women's Aid refuges, they often leave with nothing except the clothes on their backs, feeling traumatised and afraid. Our project will provide practical and emotional support in the refuges to help them on their journey to recovery.

title: Health and Social Care for 2500 kids in Nairobi
description: Our project creates a high potential clinical service in Nairobi slums for 2500 children and their families affected by the COVID emergency. We provide medical care through home visits with community health workers, nurses, doctors and social workers to assist children in all their needs, especially those with chronic diseases such as HIV and sickle-cell anemia who can't interrupt their treatments, distributing medicines and food packages to ensure the well-being of the whole family.

title: Refugees Fleeing Terror of ISIS
description: To save the lives of their children and families, the Yazidi families fled their homes to Northern Iraq (Kurdistan).  Now, they are living in empty containers, tents or abandoned buildings.   Some, while fleeing, experienced the murder of friends and family.  Many of the women and girls are suffering PTSD from the horror of rape (some as young as age 9) by ISIS militants.  GHNI teams are working to help families find safety, healing from trauma and the ability to rebuild lives.

title: Student ACES Leadership Initiative
description: Student ACES was founded to create a pathway for high school athletes to achieve the highest standards of leadership. The inspiration is derived from a desire to see every student achieve a foundation of leadership that will generate positive outcomes and tremendous success in their lives. The end goal of Student ACES is to help student athletes optimize their leadership potential and experience a high level of drive and inspiration. We would like to offer the free program to more students.

title: Help Gift Disabled South Africans a Wheelchair
description: The sweethearts Foundation aims to provide wheelchairs to men, women and children from South Africa in need.

title: Hip Replacement for 12 Nigerians with Sickle Cell
description: Nigeria has the highest number of people with sickle cell disease globally. A blood disorder marked by debilitating complications and a short life span, it causes breakdown of the hip joint. Affected persons live daily in constant pain and are rendered immobile. The only treatment that brings them reprieve is hip replacement surgery. Sickle Cell Foundation Nigeria wants to provide free hip replacement surgery for 12 indigent persons with this condition over a 1 year period.

title: Nutritional support for integral development
description: Bola Pra Frente Institute assists children from a poor community in Rio de Janeiro.  We use sport as a tool to facilitate and promote learning at the same time. For that, we need one of the most important bases for the proper functioning of the body, food. It can improve our body's defenses and the performance of physical and academical activities. Therefore, this project aims to give 100 children a nutritional support in order to improve their integral development for one year.

title: Increasing Access to Safe Drinking Water in Layyah
description: Participatory Welfare Services (PWS) proposes a project with an overall objective to provide safe drinking water sources and health & hygiene awareness focused in district Layyah. The project is intended to target villages of layyah. PWS will work on two key interventions: (i) installation of 100 hand pumps; (ii) conducting 12 health & hygiene sessions.

title: Safe Motherhood - Improving Maternal Infant Health
description: The maternal mortality rate in Gambia as estimated by the WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA and the world bank from 1990 to 2013 was 430 per 100, 000 with a neonatal death of 2168 per 100,000.  This project will provide state of the art maternity tools and supplies, it will also mobilize local networks of midwives to improve household and community practices. Studies have shown that improving knowledge and capacity of skilled birth attendants through training can lead to a 54% in mortality at birth.

title: Next Generation Lideres (NGL)
description: The LatinoJustice Next Generation Lideres (NGL) program recruits and trains young Latino lawyers to serve as mentors for high school and college students considering law school. NGL mentors will help Latino students prepare to get into law school, access services and programs designed to prepare them for law school entrance exams, figure out financing options, and become tap a greater network of Latino lawyers who can help them access internship and job opportunities after they become lawyers.

title: Arts Program for 50 At Risk Youth in Chapel Hill
description: The goal of this pilot after school project is to build resilience in youth - who have experienced trauma - through artistic self-expression, using a range of media, including text/spoken word, still images, audio, and video. By giving voice to their experiences,they build independent thinking skills, gain ownership, and learn from one another as they engage in creative challenges. This journey of self-discovery and confidence building reduces their involvement in high risk behaviors.

title: Support quality education of underprivileged kids
description: The project will help support overall development and high quality education for children of daily wage workers in Chandauli, India. This project will help provide technology based affordable high quality education in rural areas at minimal cost, Free Tuition fees for children of daily wage workers, Scholarships in the form of reduced tuition for children from disadvantaged background.

title: Local Action - Global Impact
description: One of the most stringent problems of the Moldovan society at the moment, especially of the rural society is the absence of the access to information or limited access to the public information. While the price of subscriptions to periodicals is very high for the majority of the village people, and the Radio and TV are at the disposal of the power, the population from the rural regions stays uninformed about different fields of general interest.

title: Using Sport for Social Change to Empower Chicago
description: Urban Initiatives teaches students the importance of learning and making positive choices through sports-based youth development programs. 15,000 students in 51 schools across Chicago experience the benefits of UI's programs every day. Of the children we serve, 93% come from low-income families.   Your donation will allow us to sustain our work and help create stronger, healthier, and safer Chicago neighborhoods.

title: Dog Food for Service Dogs that Serve Disabled Vets
description: The costs to obtain and care for Service Dogs are not supported in a Veterans disability pay.  Therefore, the expenses to maintain a Service Dog with dog food, grooming, veterinary care, training and supplies comes out of their own pocket.  We, at Feed the Dog, Inc. believe that this poses an extraordinary burden on a Veteran's already limited finances.   Your support will ensure that Service Dogs across America in the Feed the Dog, Inc. program receive quality food and the care they need.

title: Change the Script for LGBT Youth
description: Mythic Bridge is raising $15,000 to provide continued support for LGBT and other youth by producing a series of short films that tell the LGBT youth experience in an authentic and positive way.  These films will showcase how people deal with the issues of being young, while also being LGBT and finding a balance and normalcy in the face of current societal, social, and political challenges.

title: Empowering Indigenous Youth for a Healthy Future
description: Based on comprehensive community health profiles, Rising Minds has designed a multidimensional, action-based health training initiative targeting the most at-risk population in Guatemala- indigenous children. This initiative will work across five schools to provide weekly trainings surrounding health, nutrition and illness prevention to over 200 indigenous children between the ages of 2-13.

title: Helping Abused Girls, Sierra Leone
description: We have built a shelter for young female victims of violence (gender-based violence, female genital mutilation, rape, etc). We provide the necessary medical and psychological treatment, legal aid, education, and basic needs (food, water, clothing, hygiene) to help these girls heal and return to their families and communities.  We need additional funding to continue operating our shelter and providing prevention and intervention programs to address the source of the problems.

title: SOS Siria
description: Since the conflict began, SOS Children's Villages has been able to help over 100,000 people. We have provided shelter for unaccompanied children, as well as new mothers and their babies in our Interim Care Centres. We have provided warm clothes, bedding, blankets and meals to families who have been forced to live in poor accommodation without basic food or water. We have created Child-Friendly Spaces where children have the chance to play and receive counselling.

title: Livelihood Opportunities for Women in Rural India
description: From March to April 2021, rural Indian women in informal jobs accounted for 80% of job losses (Financial Express). The Desai Foundation is working to rebuild and empower the lives of women in rural India. These livelihood programs help recover and restore a support system, an income, independence, and empowerment. These programs equip women with skills and engage them into the workforce so they can independently provide for themselves and their families, cultivating confidence and dignity.

title: Help Tanzanian Farmers Get Water!
description: Tanzanian communities in Iguguno and Tumili have experienced an incredibly dry year & the rainy season has not started on time. The changing climate has forced local farmers to purchase their water, which places an enormous burden on them as impoverished subsistence farmers. These farmers can not afford to cover the basic costs to water their tree nurseries to grow a better future. With your help, 488 families will stay on track to grow resilient Forest Gardens & continue to change their lives.

title: FNPW Creating Healthy & Connected Communities
description: Refugee and humanitarian entrants face many specific barriers in the community - this program aims to grow the confidence and life skills of the participants while they also contribute to National Parks by undertaking volunteer work. This is an innovative project to  proactively engage refugees and asylum seekers in a healthy and positive program that supported new skills development, cross cultural exchange and provided the avenue for the target group to more easily integrate into work.

title: Giving Tuesday - Project FLIGHT
description: 12+ partners with high schools in underserved communities to provide ALL of their students the individualized college, academic, and social support needed to unlock their full potential. Every dollar from "Project: FLIGHT" will go directly into programming for our students on their road to post-secondary education. This campaign will fund the essentials that every student needs on this journey, from college visits to a dedicated, in-school 12+ advisor to walk with them every step of the way.

title: Family Caregiver Respite
description: Over the years, a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease takes a toll. For the person with PD, the changes are slow, yet unrelenting requiring constant adjustment and adaptation to diminishing independence.  For the families, this steady progression also takes a toll.  Spouses and other family members too often find themselves the single source of help and support for their loved ones. The Family Respite Program provides funds for qualified families to hire help so that they can safely receive help.

title: The Gift of Water to an Entire Village in Ghana
description: For the  3000 villagers in Mankoadze, a small village in Ghana, clean fresh water is a luxury.  Water is something many of us take for granted every day accessible by the turn of a tap.  Currently, children as young as 5 have to carry water for over 8 miles to bring it to their families for drinking, washing and keeping livestock alive. Be Enriched in partnership with the Rotary club of Tooting and TEABAG has been fundraising and building a well, but we need your help

title: Give a Better Life To An Elderly Widow
description: This project will help offer Daimilia (an elderly widow) a better housing opportunity. One that is dignified and protected from pests.

title: Supplementary Feeding with Boiled Egg
description: The majority of children who are attending our childcare centers and village preschools (total 359 persons) are from poor working families with 40 % under nourished. In order to improve the nutritional standard of children we have come up with a new campaign for supplementary feeding with boiled eggs.

title: Access to Clean Water in Remote Cambodian Villages
description: The lack of clean drinking water poses a real health risk for remote villages in Cambodia. With a water tank at school, the rainwater runoff from rooftop gutters gets collected in the rainy season and stored for the use during the dry season. Students, teachers, and other community members can use the water for drinking or their personal hygiene.

title: Technology Support - 100 ACPC's Pan India
description: AMBA is a Training & Business Hub for adults with moderate to severe intellectual disabilities using ICT. Our ecosystem of learning & earning is adaptive, visual & functional. Their lack of social skills limits them from working in mainstream companies, so AMBA's scaling model is within collaborations with AMBA Certified Partner Centers (ACPCs) pan India while helping them evolve into hubs for learning & earning. We are currently within 300 collaborations impacting over 8000+ youngsters.

title: Friends Rehab and Institute of Technical Education
description: Support Aid Ministry (SAM), intends to set up a facility on the land to be referred to as Friends Rehab and Institute of Technical Education (FRITE). FRITE is bringing out various interconnected projects on this land to support drug addicts, street children and other vulnerable populations, mainly the poor. The Vocational Training Centre will be the key project with its own building, infrastructure, equipment, staff and maintenance.

title: Help 200 orphans children to get education
description: This project will build 6 rooms in the city of Nsele in Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo, providing basic education and support services for critical literacy to 200 AIDS orphans

title: Quality Healthcare to70000 patients in Rural India
description: Set up on the 30th of September 1996,in the wake of a devastating earthquake, the SPARSH rural hospital (of the PRIDE India) continues to be one of the only source of quality healthcare to villagers from Marathawada region, especially Osmanabad ,Latur districts in Maharashtra, India.  The hospital provides primary healthcare with its 40-bedded high specialty facility, support and care to people living with HIV/AIDS, Maternal and Child Healthcare and Outreach activities through Mobile Medical Van

title: Harmony Preschool_Invest in the Next Generation
description: Harmony Preschool, established by Ready for Reading and housed in their community library, is located in a poor area of eastern Rwanda. The project will continue to build on Harmony's book rich, hands-on learning curriculum for its 40 students, increase the number of preschool teachers receiving training and parent education workshops. Learning through play practices will be integrated into children's programs and activities at the library providing access to any child in the community.

title: No Violence Against Women and Girls
description: The programme supports survivors of domestic violence and gender based violence in Patna district of Bihar, India. The programme is aimed at contributing to reduced prevalence of violence against women/girls and lead improved efforts to provide necessary services to survivors of gender-based violence. Sahyogi make the community aware on GBV, educate women to identify GBV/DV and respond, provide counseling and legal aid support to the survivor and link them with existing govt. services for justic

title: Right to School
description: The projects aims at providing children access to equitable and quality education, ensuring that the schools in this area are compliant with Right To Education norms. This project aims to work with 2,061  children from 15 villages (in Telangana State) the school they deserve, so that they are on the path to complete their education and take the first step towards a successful future. By creating healthier learning environments in schools and raising awareness among all stakeholders.

title: Steering 500 Women Away from Prostitution, Mumbai
description: This fundraiser will seek to empower women living in the Kamathipura red light area of Mumbai by providing them necessary resources and tools to develop long-term skills so they can leave prostitution. In past 18 years, AAWC has provided more than 2200 women with vocational training, financial & adult literacy sessions, assisted them to obtain essential documents for availing government benefits and schemes, which has helped them to gain skills for generating income from the alternate resource.

title: Arts & skills workshops for 100 youth in Zimbabwe
description: Economic challenges in Zimbabwe have left young people frustrated and discouraged, turning to dangerous coping mechanisms (alcohol, drugs, crime). Engaging 100 youth (30 boys, 70 girls) in Arts workshops (dancing, acting, visual arts) will give them a platform to express and work through their frustrations, while providing social entrepreneurship skills to earn a living and impact their communities.

title: Help MAKNA with treatment access to 450 patients
description: Cancer is an expensive disease, but the battle against cancer is considered niche. It doesn't help that there is a stigma associated with it and society shies away from it.  We target 350-400 patients each month. Each approved case means that MAKNA support is guaranteed to be ongoing for the next 12 month period for that case, regardless of scenarios. In particular, for November 2016, the number of approved cases is 450.

title: Planting a Forest to fight pollution in Sofia
description: Sofia is Europe's most polluted capital and World Health Organization alarmed that Bulgaria ranks second in the world in terms of deaths due to air pollution. We want to buy neglected urban land and plant an Urban Forest to restore the green passes that lead the fresh air from the mountain to the city.

title: Educate, Equip, Empower Girls and Women in Nigeria
description: The project will tackle issues of poverty, girl child education, networking and access to opportunities. This project targets girls and women of four different profiles in Kaduna in northern Nigeria. Through the project, we aim to subsidize the education of ten girls in public secondary schoosl over two years, train and mentor 120 indigent rural women (mostly widows and heads of households), engage 100 adult females in two tertiary institutions and empower 2 female artists.

title: Empowering 300 Women/Girls in Northern  Pakistan
description: Gilgit-Baltistan is a remote, economically backward and one of the impoverished regions of Pakistan.  Women of the area are restricted to the household work in the mountains  and no avenues of women employment and economic empowerment are available. KIDF Pakistan has started training these poor women in  skills of cloth stitching, handicraft, dress designing and connected them with the market for small scale entrepreneurship to make them financially independence and an income generating member

title: A little goes a long way
description: CityHope Disaster Relief provides relief aid to the most vulnerable of human beings at a time when disaster strikes.  Whether it's a flood; a drought; social & politically motivated unrest, we are here to provide a measure of comfort and dignity to those worst affected.  HELP us today by donating funds which are used to ensure that each victim receives a relief kit which comprises of food, sanitary provision and hygiene products to help during the height of the catastrophe.

title: SAVING PETS IN TOWNSHIPS - EMPOWER DISADVANTAGED
description: PETS is a PRO-Life, PRO-Active Animal Rescue organisation that was officially registered as a PBO in 2007, although we had been operating before that. WE try and save, maintain and improve the living conditions of animals in their immediate surroundings. We empower animals in townships and poor communities. Pets living in such areas do not have the same privileges as other animals such as daily meals, warm shelters, regular inoculations, sterilisations and vet care in emergency situtuations.

title: Improve Health for Mothers and Babies in Myanmar
description: This project will provide 2,400 new mothers in Myanmar, with a baby kit that contains essential health and hygiene items to give their babies a healthy start in life. These kits help improve the mothers' and babies' lives in Karen State, which has one of the highest rates of maternal and newborn mortality in the world.

title: Help Ukrainians Displaced People to Begin New Life
description: The project will address humanitarian and rehabilitation needs of internally displaced people (110 families) who have migrated to Brody from war areas of Eastern Ukraine. The  project will address following areas. 1. Psychological treatment for improving mental health of IDPs. 2. Empowering displaced women to earn livelihood by conducting tailoring and cooking courses. Children development  program focusing on educational needs, mental and physical growth. Healthcare for older displaced people.

title: Play Center for 82 children with cancer in Mexico
description: The procedures that patients undergo (children and teenagers), the undesirable effects of chemotherapy and its life expectancy lead to stress in children, which manifests in anxiety, fear, behavioral changes, irritability, and withdrawal behaviors. The goals of the play center are: Use positive reinforcement techniques for enhancing patient motivation, To improve their mood and reinforce their immune system, To preserve the health and satisfy special education needs of oncological patients

title: Build a Health Center in Katoyi-Masisi (DRCongo)
description: The aim of this project is to build a Health Center that will provide primary health care to approximately 62,500 inhabitants  in  Katoyi - Masisi and surround areas. It should be noted that the nearest health care facility is at 50 kms. I addition to improve health care for all inhabitants in general, this project will reduce maternal and neonatal mortality in this area, where 80 % of women die on their way (rudimentarily and dangerously transported) to a nearest health facility to deliver.

title: Promote agroforestry to improve climate change
description: Philadephia Foundation shall pay community men and women to plant 30,000 trees (of different species) in all farms owned by peasant farmers that are along Mfulanjobvu river bank covering water springs and bare mountain where there are source of rivers in Balaka district .These trees shall prevent soil erosion that is taking place along Mulunguzi, Mfulanjobvu and other rivers.  The species of trees planted shall assist to combat climate change through permanent capturing of 30,000 tons of CO2.

title: Give a Home to a Child in need from Cartagena
description: With your help we will protect 25 children who are in street life situations, they will be emotionally and physically rehabilitated to start a new life. We wish to continue providing services in the house of Dones, where we have changed many lives. The house has been adapted to accommodate our children; it includes a kitchen to prep freshly cooked meals, a spacious outside area to play, a psychology office, two comfortable bedrooms, four bathrooms, a living room, and classroom/computer room.

title: construction of a library for 800 people in uganda
description: We plan to  construct a 2 storeyed  community library  using plastic bottles as a way of educating children as well as   cleaning and improving the sanitation of the dirty community, there is  plastic bottles  everyone  so we want to show them that waste can be turned into something  valuable. this will be the 1st community library in Bukomansimbi district which has a population of more than 200,000 people

title: International Back To School Code-a-thon 2017
description: The IBTSC is a FREE 48 hour program that gives students an opportunity to use technology, research, and collaboration to address issues and problems confronting the human race on a global scale. Students will work together to learn to code in HTML5, Java Script, and CSS. Students work in teams of 4 to build a website that reflects their ideas and commitment to problem solving.  Teaching students to code can be life changing for a child in an underserved community.

title: Help 429 children go to school in Afghanistan
description: This school in Nangarhar province offers co-education for boys and girls, which represents a major progress especially in an Afghan rural area, where girls rarely attend and even complete school education. It has greatly enhanced the prospect for jobs and the general economic situation of the population. Because of its rural location, the next Government school is too far away for young kids. When they finish class 6 and then transfer to a Government School, they usually take top places.

title: Medical Relief for Refugees in Greece
description: The SAMS Global Response program was founded in 2016 with the aim of providing medical relief to vulnerable persons and refugees. Our first project is in northern Greece, where we provide primary healthcare for 3,500 refugees in four official camps. Additionally, SAMS-GR provides transportation for referrals and builds local capacity through community health programs.

title: Build a Home for Former Child Beggars in India
description: In 2017 My Name is Kumar plans to build a permanent home for over 50 former child beggars in Tamil Nadu, India.  A new home will mean we can help more children facing a lifetime of begging and allow brothers and sisters to grow up together (boys and girls cannot sleep in the same building according to state law).   It's time to build a permanent home for Kumar and his friends to grow up together!

title: Giving Emergency aid to abused girls and children
description: The project will provide Emergency health and pay school fees for 20 girls and 6 boys who are survivors of Sexual abuse and physical violence who are currently sheltered in our facility in Ngong town. We seek to provide Psychological support through counseling therapy for both the survivors and their family members in order to reduce the long term impact of Post traumatic stress disorder of the survivors and integrate them back to the community. We also seek to provide school fees to the victims

title: Give EPI Experience to Oyacachi Students!
description: Help send 10 Ecuadorian students on a 5-day environmental education course with EPI!  Students will work with scientist Armando Castellanos to monitor wild populations of mountain tapirs and Spectacled bears, listed by the IUCN as vulnerable species. This project will inform wildlife management decisions protecting these charismatic mammals, and empower youth to take an active role in conservation. Donate on our website: www.ecologyproject.org/give/support-ecuadorian-students

title: Empower Syrian women and children in Turkey
description: With our project we aim to empower Syrian refugee women by increasing their employability and support their emotional and cognitive well-being. In addition, we also aim an increase in the mental well-being of Syrian refugee children in Turkey through psycho-social support and non-formal education.

title: Protect Globally Rare Plants in New England
description: Today, 17 percent of New England's native plant species are on the brink of being lost and another 5 percent have already disappeared from the region. Seed banking is one critical strategy for conserving at-risk plant species. We aim to secure seeds from at least 2,000 of the 3,300 populations of these rare plants, which will enable us to preserve the range of genetic diversity and each species' ability to adapt to changing conditions.

title: Women Empowering Women in Africa and Asia
description: A life-changing training program for women in developing countries - Women's Mentorship Program (WMP). A unique opportunity for women to learn management skills and financial best practice from other women managers, and expand their professional skill set in areas of employment normally dominated by men. The experience promotes gender equality. It transforms careers, credit unions and communities by teaching skills that enable women to be successful managers of co-op financial institutions.

title: Mujer Adelante
description: Our Project, "Mujer Adelante" has the general purpose of providing 20 young, single and low-income, single moms, heads of families the tools to develop greater self-esteem and self-reliance. The main goal of the project is to provide our target population, basic tools to help them propel above risk factors and thus achieve to be independent and productive women and mothers.

title: VETOGA 200 Hour Teacher Training Program
description: VETOGA's mission is to provide yoga, meditation, and healing arts to military, veterans, their families, and communities. We accomplish this by holding FREE monthly yoga classes that help veterans build sustainable communities. VETOGA will be hosting the first ever 200 hour Yoga Teacher Training program that is specifically for veterans to become yoga instructors. This teacher training will equip veterans with the holistic tools and teachings to continue to pass on the healing benefits of yoga

title: educational support for 1000 poor children
description: There are millions of poor and vulnerable children spread across the streets and slums of North-Central Nigeria. They are victims of prolonged ethnic, religious and other social conflicts.  These children will, naturally, grow into the society and seek to benefit from it. Without an education to help them compete, they have no opportunities. Without those opportunities they are a threat to society. This project intends to take at least 1000 of those children off the streets and into school.

title: Soccer & life skills for kids in Haiti - Season 2
description: In 2016, Futbol Mas ran social-sports programs in 2 disadvantage schools of Canaan, a slum born after the devasting earthquake in 2010 in Port-au-Prince, Haiti. With this campaign we want to continue to sponsor our intervention during 2017. As second consecutive year, 269 children will receive soccer and life skills workshops taught by a sports coach and a social science professional, over a period of 9 months.

title: PURESchools - Rural School Adoption - India
description: PURE School Adoption - Hanmanjipet  A school in the backward rural region of Karimnagar is in need of care and development. Students hail from under poverty line households. The high school and the primary school are in the same compound. The dilapidated compound of the building and lack of basic amenities need to be addressed immediately.  With water, toilets and building repairs(compound wall construction) in the first and class room amenities once the construction & repair work is completed

title: The Rehabilitation Commonwealth of DC
description: DC's homeless family shelters are home to nearly 800 most vulnerable families. Sometimes, it is more than 460 children living there who suffer the most. Shelters are due to be shut down by the end of 2016 with no alternatives in sight. I want to help at least 100 of the 800 families have shelter, job training, support and transportation for 30-days this Winter.

title: Help Purchase a Facility
description: Our organization is in desperate need of their own facility.  The facility will enable us to stop renting from other businesses and it will help place that money back into helping the community.

title: Free Shakespeare and classical theatre in NE Ohio
description: Rubber City Shakespeare Company's "Free Shakespeare" project stages Shakespeare and other classical works that are accessible for everyone. The "Free" Shakespeare project includes free staged reading throughout the year, and Pay-As-You-Like-It performances for each production. Using Shakespeare's plays and other classical drama, we strive to inspire the next generation of theatergoers and performers, while also providing entertaining classical theatre for free or an affordable rate.

title: Housing a Homeless Family This Holiday Season
description: The trauma of homelessness on families, particularly children, is most acute during the holiday season. Cornerstones tries to rapidly-rehouse families into permanent housing within 30 days of entering the shelter by covering the cost of the first month's rent, a security deposit and other moving expenses.

title: Provide for 300 Vulnerable Kids in Kibera School
description: The lives of 300 vulnerable children in Kibera, Kenya slum are impacted and given an opportunity for education. These little ones would have to resort to begging, early marriage or selling themselves in order to make it in the slum. Education will help them have a better outcome and inspire them to pursue their dreams.

title: DC Area Teen Songwriting with Service for hundreds
description: Now more than ever, teenagers need positive role models. By studying and writing songs about people of particular courage, students are inspired to perform acts of STEPPING UP! (community service) in the spirit of the person about whom they just wrote a song. And they are empowered to take leadership roles to get others to join them in their efforts. Each song reaches hundreds of people.  Created by Chords of Courage, a charitable organization that inspires kids through music.

title: Food to 10 moms in recovery & kids in Norwalk CT
description: This project will provide three meals a day for a year for ten pregnant or parenting women (and their children) in long-term inpatient treatment for addiction. We have a successful completion rate for people in treatment that is 18% above state average . FIRP is one of the most highly subsidized programs we offer. Almost two-thirds of the women served do not have benefits that will cover inpatient treatment for substance abuse and come into the program with little more than they can carry.

title: Maternal Hospital Opening in Iganga, Uganda
description: The brand new Hearts 4 Africa Maternal Hospital will serve a densely populated area where 700,000 people are living in extreme poverty. According to The World Bank, the Iganga region has the highest rates of maternal mortality in all of Uganda. Plans for the brand new facility include private delivery rooms, an operating theatre, water wells, and even a chapel and clinic to serve the greater community. $25,000 is all we need to complete our first building and begin offering maternal healthcare.

title: #StandWithGirls in the Philippines!
description: Over 100,000 girls aged 12-17 are victims of child sex-trafficking and/or sexual exploitation in the Philippines every single year.   GirlsGotThis is an action-led movement to protect girls by using the power of play; creating community safe-spaces to protect and provide equitable participation for girls and to capacitate teachers and communities to identify and report signs of abuses.   We are #StandingWithGirls by harnessing the power of sport to unleash the potential of girls!

title: Livestock, Livelihood and Environment Conservation
description: The project proposes to develop agro-forestry over the forest fringe villages reclaiming grazing lands so to provide nutrient fodder for livestock, increase income/livelihood of resource poor SC/ST/BC ruminant rearing families, reduce forest pressure/land degradation pose by overgrazing, eco-restoration, undisturbed wild animals'/tigers natural habitats etc. over the NSTR Tiger reserve areas. In nutshell balancing Livestock, Livelihood and Environment through multi-stakeholder initiatives.

title: IceCream for Adolescent Sexual/Reproductive Health
description: For every ice-cream we sell to an adolescent girl, she also benefits a comprehensive package of sexual and reproductive health services including free HIV screening, and family planning services on our mobile truck. This project won the "Making Quality Matter in  Family Planning Challenge 2013"

title: Make the Christmas of Elderly People Special
description: In Pakistan, the lack of social protection to elderly people (age 60-85) makes them extremely vulnerable in the family and societal structures. At average, there is one elderly person in each residing family of Pakistan and they are treated as burden in majority of the families. A Small Christmas Package can make their Christmas special. AWARD will provide Surprise Christmas Packages to 150 elderly people whose hope for happiness and care are vanishing.

title: A GAME House in Beirut's youth to do sports
description: GAME Lebanon is using street sports as a vehicle for social change, empowering and inspiring youth to engage in their local communities. However there is a vast need for more public street sport facilities in Lebanon. The GAME House will be an innovative indoor street sport facility to enable children and youth to meet on equal terms through sports. On ground level, it will ensure that more children and youth will have access to do sports as well as creating a local based hub for the community.

title: Cleanup at areas of the venues for 2020 Olympics.
description: We are an NPO based in Japan and carry out cleanup activities by 85 teams all over the world.  In order to boost the momentum of the Tokyo Olympic Games and the Paralympic Games in 2020, We want  to recruit volunteers from inside and outside Japan and to form 37 teams of clean-up activity. Then we clean up at areas around the 37 venues from now on.  While spreading Japanese cleaning culture to many places, we want to make the most beautiful Olympic Games ever with local communities.

title: Unified Schools Football Program in China
description: Children with intellectual disabilities are the most marginalized group and the students in regular schools are hardly aware of the existence of such a group who are at the similar age. Unified Schools Football Program uses the power of football to improve health, build friendships and create an inclusive environment for children with and without intellectual disabilities. Already supported by Citizens Giving, your donation will help even more young people in China.

title: Conserving 80 globally endangered Francois Langur
description: This program empowers local ethnic (Tai, H'mong, Dao) communities' direct involvement in conservation of the endangered Francois Langur (leaf monkey) and its habitat in northern Vietnam, by establishing the first community-based conservation area in Vietnam.  Villagers are involved in conservation management and monitoring of the langur and other species in the landscape.  The program provides training, mentoring, and technical and financial support, including  livelihood development activities.

title: Futbol Matters
description: Futbol Matters is a project that will create a safe space for 400 children to play football in Gustavo Madero, Mexico City. 40 young leaders will be trained in construction and management, supporting them to build the community football pitch and teach them skills to support their future employability. Already supported by Cityzens Giving, your donation will help Futbol Matters to continue the work of our young leaders and help even more young people in Mexico City.

title: Send Harlem Students to World Peace Leadership!
description: This January, the IBREA Foundation is hosting a World Leadership Program! Since we have been working closely with students at the A. Phillip Randolph High School in Harlem NYC, we have selected 3 exemplary students to participate in the program. With your contributions we will be able to fund the costs of their participation so that the students can fully immerse themselves in the program.

title: Arkansas Women's Business Center - Tuesday Giving
description: When women entrepreneurs are provided the right tools, their small businesses can be a success. AWBC provides the necessary resources and tools to build our communities with strong entrepreneurs. We have a big goal to raise $5,000 dollars this year, supporting 5 new business start-ups in the upcoming year.   You can sponsor a Arkansas woman entrepreneur today, we can't do it without your support! The important thing is to give what you can. An entrepreneur in need will appreciate it more than

title: Support Hospices in Moscow
description: "Someone who can't be cured can still be helped".  This Vera Hospice Charity Fund's motto may seem like common knowledge, but 10 years ago, when the foundation first began supporting hospices and terminally ill people, very few members of Russian society would agree. Death and dying have been taboo subjects for decades. As a result of this negligence, children and adults with different life-limiting illnesses and their loved ones were left with no professional care, in pain and despair.

title: Menstrual Dignity for Refugee Women
description: Women refugees and internally displaced persons (IDPs) around the world have multiple humanitarian needs; among them are the challenges of managing menstruation safely, privately and with dignity. Days for Girls (DfG) meets the needs of displaced people who menstruate by providing washable, long-lasting menstrual Kits and vital health education. Prioritizing areas with the highest need, our refugee outreach began in Uganda, expanded into Lebanon and Chad, and now also includes Jordan.

title: Youth Robotics Programs in DC, MD, VA - FIRST Rob
description: Join FIRST Chesapeake in shaping tomorrow's leaders. Our dynamic robotics programs across DC, MD, and VA infuse students with STEM skills and life-enhancing abilities. But we need your support. Each donation isn't just a gift-it's an investment in the architects of our future. Stand with us to empower the young, innovate dreams, and create lasting impact. Support the future, today.  Because of you, every kid can go pro!

title: Help 20,000 Girls Escape Forced Marriages
description: Helping end gender gaps in school enrollment and widespread child marriage in South Sudan and gender gaps in school enrollment, contributes to soaring maternal mortality rates, and violates the right of girls to be free from violence and to marry only when they are able to give their free consent.

title: Feel Free: Give Play to Girls Who Need It
description: How do you feel when you are running on your favorite trail, playing ball with your team or surfing big waves with your friends?   You feel free.   1 in 3 girls and women worldwide experience gender-based violence - rape, abuse, harassment, early pregnancy, forced marriage.   They deserve to feel free, just like you do.

title: Problem Solving for 200 Traditional Leaders
description: When Timorese people have conflicts, they turn to a traditional leader in their community for help. Ba Futuru trains these traditional leaders to solve conflicts without violence and respect the rights of women and children. Using real-life examples, Timorese trainers will demonstrate non-violent problem solving techniques in a collaborative setting with traditional leaders, local and district authorities and government officials.

title: Eye Care for Disadvantaged Children in China
description: Eye problems severely affect the quality of children's life and pose impediments to their learning prospects. Migrant and rural children in China that are beset by eye problems mostly go untreated mainly due to lack of  resources and medical insurance coverage, leading to the future deterioration of the children's vision. To respond, our "I Care" project provides free eye tests, eye glasses and eye operations to disadvantaged primary school children.

title: MinaCup - Keeping Our Girls in School
description: MinaCup is a sustainable, life-changing solution that keeps young girls in school for up to 5 years. Improving levels of education in girls means lower rates of unwanted teenage pregnancies and reduces the risk of cervical cancer. Educated mothers are less likely to die during childbirth and tend to only get married and have children when they are ready. Educated women contribute to the work force and keep hunger pangs away in their home.

title: Training 100 Female Led Artisans in Swaziland
description: Help create income opportunities for women to stem the tide of HIV/AIDS and elevate the status of women in Swaziland. Swaziland Fair Trade will train and mentor 100 female led producer groups to facilitate income generation and job creation.

title: Supply re-usable sanitary towels in rural Kenya
description: This project will make and distribute re-usable sanitary napkins to women and girls in rural Kenya at a cost of USD 2 for an annual package saving them USD 10 every year.  The project will improve the self esteem and bring back their dignity they deserve as humans enabling girls go to school and women go out to fend for their families uninterrupted.  At every distribution centre, education on menstruation hygiene, growing up, pregnancy, family planning and sexual related diseases will be given

title: Rehabilitation of 64 Vulnerable Women in  Ethiopia
description: This project will assist traumatized women through self-help groups to regain their dignity and to encourage them to become self-supported by assisting them to start a small scale business.

title: 1000 Entrepreneurship Apprenticeships in Nigeria
description: In August 2010, the International Labor Organization warned of a "lost generation" of over 300 million youth. These youth are eking out uncertain and unsustainable livelihoods on the margins of society and facing reduced life opportunities.    Just $100, means Generation Enterprise and its social mobility enterprise, Zest, can provide 3 months of paid formal economy job training to a "lost" youth in Nigeria. If  that youth is successful,  they are guaranteed at least 1 years formal employmen

title: Warm Touch (Lamset Dafa)
description: Campaign's immediate goals (KPI's): - collecting minimum 120 tons of clothes and blankets. - Securing minimum 100,000 liters of heating fuel Campaign long term goals:  - Affirming youth involvement and their ability to work together. - Showing solidarity with people inside Syria. -      Networking and Connecting people together.

title: Give English Text books to 300 students in N. Kivu
description: In North Kivu (Kiwanja - DRC), this project will aide students displaced by conflict, who have shown increasing enthusiasm to learn English language in a region. East African French speaking countries are supplementing it with English. It will enhance students to teach themselves english to ease communication & education since the region is French & Kiswahili speaking. Various beginners 'teach yourself' english books, CDs, etc will be supplied and an English language club facilitated

title: Scholarships to College Students with Disabilities
description: This project's goal is to provide scholarships to contribute to the increase in employment opportunities for college students with disabilities. This project will provide 8 general scholarships to full-time college students who have documented disabilities of any type. The qualified student must be a full-time student currently attending a four-year college or university during the year.  In addition, must have already completed 24-credits and a GPA 3.0 or above.

title: Promoting Healthy Student Diets and Local Farms
description: This project will initially benefit the students of Westerly, Rhode Island and ultimately many more. Administrators need data to support transitioning to purchasing local food. Our aim is to show that students prefer salad bars laden with fresh produce. We will promote local farmers and highlight nutritional facts; subsidize purchases; track student buying, and evaluate the experience.
