The design and construction is led by the Senior Architecture students under the Estudio Damgo program of the Department of Architecture and Fine Arts.

title: Emergency Relief Aid for Needy Ethio-Somali IDPs
description: The proposed project will target a total of 2,500 vulnerable hard to reach community including women, children, old ages, and marginalized groups through a wide range of interrelated interventions in 5- Villages/Kebeles of Gode woreda/district, Shebelle zone of Somali region. These include: 1) Short term water trucking to 2,500 vulnerable communities based 5 target village/Kebeles in Gode woreda/district.  2)Provision of Food supply to 6 Kebeles with each most vulnerable 1,500 HHs (IDPs & HOST)

title: Provide Antibiotics to Children in Need Globally
description: Antibiotics, so easily available for most of us, are often difficult to find in resource-poor countries. When infections occur, antibiotics are often the difference between life and death. This project will provide antibiotic treatments to children in resource-poor regions around the world.

title: Help 5000 Nigerian Girls with Pad for Menstruation
description: Sanitary pads assistance is about helping poor girls in our focus communities, Sogunro slum of Lagos state and ungwa hausa cable point Delta State of Nigeria with menstrual materials. They use all sorts of dirty materials to hold their menstrual flow because they cannot afford sanitary pads. Such materials like rags from dustbin is unhygienic and often gives them infection. We stock pads for their monthly collection and teach them how to make/take care of reusable pads which is cheaper for them

title: Literacy for Adults: Reading the World (Mexico)
description: This year the Tihueliske We Can! Education Program for Women and Youth will help a minimum of 30 people living in acute poverty to gain skills for life in Tlamacazapa, Mexico. Village women gain literacy while learning about human rights, equality and personal development. Local young educators use newly developed modules to guide the classes, complete with exercises and drawings relevant to rural life. Each class provides opportunity for good progress and stimulating discussions.

title: Help eradicate malaria in South Africa
description: Hoedspruit Training Trust now formerly Hlokomela, aims to provide each farm worker with the opportunity to be tested and treated for malaria. This will identify both positive malaria cases as well as carriers and help save lives. This is particularly important because of the large number of migrant farm workers who are either carrying the disease in from endemic areas or are silent carriers of it.

title: Medical Clinics for Rohingya Refugees
description: Bruised and beaten, desperate and despairing, Rohingya refugees escape the violence of Myanmar and find themselves in a refugee camp the size of a city without enough food or water to sustain them all. In these squalid conditions, contamination and disease are rife and outbreaks are deadly. Help us fund ten medical clinics to service 250 patients per day. Just 2.50 will pay for a consultation and treatment.

title: Dignity Kits for Rohingya Refugee Women
description: Millions of refugee women are currently living in dire conditions in camps without basic everyday essentials like food, clothes and warmth. For these refugees, being a woman means that they are also deprived of feminine hygiene products to manage their period, which adds to the hardship. Global One is providing essential Dignity Kits complete with a menstrual cup/pack of sanitary towels, soap and shampoo to female Rohingya refugees.

title: Earthquake Relief for Southern Peru
description: On Sunday, January 14, 2018 at 4:18 AM, an earthquake of magnitude 7.1 was recorded near Acari in the Arequipa region of southern Peru. One person is confirmed dead, dozens have been injured, and homes and roads collapsed. Based on RMF Peru's 11 years of experience in earthquake and flood relief, this project will provide mobile medical outreach care for affected communities, while providing emergency kits for 3,000 people displaced or most vulnerable after the earthquake.

title: Support and training for parents in Guatemala
description: The project will provide training and emotional support to parents of babies and young children with Down syndrome. This will enable them to ensure they can give the best possible support and care to their children during early development.

title: Help Provide Education to 200 Children in Need
description: This project will help provide both academic and vocational education to 200 children in need at Fortune Community School in Solwezi District of Zambia. Charity Centre for Children and Youth Development has constructed a 1x2 classroom that is providing basic education to the less privileged children in the community. The project will help raise money for payment of salaries for teachers and tutors, school uniforms, Books, food, sanitation pads for girls etc.

title: Give Mobility to 20 Kids in the Developing World!
description: This project will provide free orthopedic care to 20 children with untreated limb disabilities in the developing world whose families cannot afford care. For these kids, mobility is more than movement. Mobility is hope, access to education, and the chance to live-self sufficiently.

title: Provide trauma relief to workers in South Africa
description: Formerly Hoedpsruit Training Trust, Hlokomela runs TRE appointments (Trauma and Tension Relief Exercises), to help rural farm workers deal with trauma and stress in their lives.  This project aims to support 20 community workers in rural Hoedspruit to be trained in TRE.

title: Safe Water and Good Hygiene Campaign in Uganda
description: This project is intended to enhance the health status and productivity of  vulnerable communities  in Nangabo Sub-county,Central Uganda. These  communities rely mainly on unprotected springs as a source of water as the safe water coverage is  49% . The water is usually full of diseases causing germs. Worse still the sanitation conditions and hygiene practices in  the household /schools, are  inadequate. This project will ensure access to safe and clean water as well as better hygiene practices

title: Herding for Sustainable Futures
description: RAIN's mission is to empower people to choose the lifestyles of their dreams. RAIN's mentors are traditional women rural and nomadic with little or no formal education. Goat herding is a core part of their identities and incomes. Yet many are unable to buy the foundation animals for developing a herd. RAIN's Mentor Herding Program puts women on a sustainable path with one more tool for generating food security and income.

title: Housing for Women leaving the Sex Industry
description: We are raising funds for the costs of the housing that we provide for the women that want to leave prostitution in Pattaya. Most women do not have a place to stay once they leave the bars and because of that we offer the accommodation for free until the women start working.

title: Parkinson day 2023-Donate for 80 Latrine Building
description: This is a project aimed to build raised Latrine for 50 poor PD patients in Ethiopia. It will help the patients defecate smoothly while in latrine. Parkinson's Disease creates Stiffness and many of our patients are suffering from failure to easily use common latrine.   By donating money to this project you are becoming hand & feet to patients.  You are giving away your resources, but will harvest satisfaction.

title: Empowering the Future - Auroville
description: Auroville is a leader in evolutionary regenerative design; a project with 3000 people from 53 countries dedicating their lives to the future of humanity. Integrating conscious living, sustainability, alternative energy; acting as a green demo site and training center for 50 years, it's a unique place for progress and creating change locally, regionally and internationally. Although endorsed by UNESCO, PM`s, Presidents of India and the Dalai Lama, Auroville's potential is severely under threat.

title: Changing the Lives of At-Risk Youth in St. Croix
description: It's obvious to many at-risk youth in St. Croix that their future prospects are bleak. They're living in poverty, doing poorly in school, and lack positive role models and the tools to make good decisions. Add in the impact of Hurricane Maria one year later many children are still dealing with the trauma of losing their homes, possessions, schools, and, often, the family's source of income and things look even bleaker. It's no wonder so many of these youth give up and turn to risky behaviors.

title: Stop Ugandan women & children dying at childbirth
description: In Uganda people rich or poor can lose a wife, sister, mother, daughter or son at childbirth due to the very low standards of care at hundreds of private and government maternity facilities. Whisper has an opportunity to put a big stop sign to everything wrong that pregnant women are experiencing and bring our own values, endless love and hope to every single pregnant mother and newborn child. Help us and donate to this needed cause. Thank you

title: BPO - LEARN AND EARN AT VIDYADHIRAJA
description: BPO - BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING TRAINING AT VIDYADHIRAJA SCHOOL, children from TATA NAGAR, a slum pocket of Mumbai will be able to work in call centres and enrich their personalities, financial status, continue academic learning and socially uplift themselves from the throngs of a community surrounded by violence and vices.  Providing a BPO training to these students can make them skilled in communications, teamwork while strengthening their job-oriented IT and networking.

title: Vocational Training for Freed Child Slaves, Nepal
description: We are offering girls and women, now freed from domestic slavery, a new life through vocational training.  We train these girls in relevant and marketable trades and help them start their own business or gain employment, leading to social and economic independence for the first time in their lives. Without our help these girls face being marginalised and caught in a cycle of poverty in one of the world's poorest countries.

title: Rehabilitation of children from prison
description: The project will help children who were imprisoned to get back into the society. These children would have committed crimes and are arrested and subsequently put into prison. the aim of the project is to help them move on with their lives after prison. children will be trained in vocational skills with some going back to school. This will help break the cycle of graduating children into adult criminals. children will receive counselling and support from CATCH

title: St. Cyril Initiative for Patients' Support (SCIPS)
description: This project will treat  patients who may otherwise die from the cancer because they have no money. St Cyril Initiative for Patients' Support (S.C.I.P.S.)

title: Supporting Children with Disabilities in Pakistan
description: MAITS' award-winning Community Healthworker training teaches life-saving techniques that improve disabled children's health & well-being, through expert volunteer trainers in Pakistan. We will equip local community workers with the skills to support families in their own homes. Piloted in Jamaica we taught simple techniques to carers of disabled children. Before our training, there were serious case reviews with children dying or very ill. After, there was not one serious case review or death.

title: Build a Cafeteria to feed 150 children in Mexico
description: We are building a cafeteria for a public kindergarten in Acuna, Coahuila, Mexico where 150 children between 4 and 6 years of age living in poverty will be fed. A cafeteria in good condition providing a nutritious diet is essential in schools because a poorly nourished child learns slowly and likewise healthy eating should start from the early years and is basic as they can mark the difference between  a healthy life and the risk of suffering diseases in later years.

title: New Instruments for 200 Chicago Youth!
description: This project will build and restore music and band programs in underprivileged Chicago land schools lacking or at-risk of losing their music programs; providing band directors, new instruments, scholastic field trips, music intensive workshops with industry professionals and performance opportunities.

title: Help Prevent Child Brides in South Sudan
description: Teenage girls in South Sudan are being forced into marriages with much older men. Girls that drop out of school are the most at risk of becoming child brides.  Drop in the Bucket has worked in water & sanitation in East Africa since 2006. We recently expanded our program to include scholarships to girls who are good students but lack family support. We want these girls to get an education, so they have a choice in who they marry. Educated girls earn more money which breaks the cycle of poverty.

title: Old Aged Home for Needy Older Person
description: Although the constitution of India defined as welfare state and Indian family as a social institution is well known for the emotional and physical support that it provides to its extended members, many a time it fails to respond to the needs of older people in the age group of 60 years and above in difficult circumstance specially in the metropolitan cities. Immediate support and care of the family are not available due to many reasons ranging from economic instability of the family

title: Give free medical to orphans and street families
description: NJIWA Medical  currently operates as a self-funded clinic combining general practice and maternity. Treatment of needy, orphans & homeless is funded by the proceeds from paying clients, who may also receive a discount depending on their circumstances. Mtaa Safi is supporting the efforts of NJIWA MEDICAL with labour and financial support. The clinic building needs work, medical equipment is required, and medicines always need replenishing. Every little bit helps.

title: Gift a Smile to 81 Cleft Children in India
description: Trinity Care Foundation plans to provide free surgeries for Cleft children who hail from the poorest sections of society in Karnataka State, also providing the children with speech therapy and further treatments. Your donation helps to provide free reconstructive surgeries and emotional counseling to support these children and their families.

title: Help schools address mental health and suicide
description: Many schools struggle to talk about mental health. Some schools ban conversations about suicide altogether, fearing 'suicide contagion.' Unsilence's TOMORROW is an online learning experience and classroom program. It uses interactive storytelling to help teens and teachers build the skills to talk about suicide, depression, and mental health in appropriate and effective ways. Help us make a difference in our school and communities TODAY.

title: Restore Ecosystems to Conserve Environment (RECE)
description: Most wild animals and plant species are nearing extinction in refugee camps where over 1.4 million South Sudanese refugees are settled along host communities, the project will create an additional zone and engage communities to participate in conservation of both Fiona and Flora. Engage  government and humanitarian organizations to support conservation measures to protect the wildlife species who originally had a permanent home, and suddenly they have been tempered for human settlement

title: Help support 1 million sexual violence survivors
description: Less than 13% of sexual violence survivors feel safe speaking up or getting help. That equals 1.14 billion survivors worldwide suffering in silence. MapYourVoice offers survivors a safe and therapeutic place to have their voices heard and validated.  Survivors gain easy access to local support -- and are encouraged to reach out for needed protection and care. Each survivor's anonymous report adds to valuable new data that can be used to help prevent and combat further sexual violence.

title: Atlas Corps: Empower Women Globally (#GivingToday)
description: Celebrate #diversityandinclusion! Let's inspire female leaders! WEF's 2017 Global Gender Gap Report found that the presence/participation of women in leadership roles is a crucial factor in closing the opportunity gap. Atlas Corps empowers women globally by engaging social change leaders in 12-18 month Fellowships. Join Atlas Corps as we focus on empowering women to tackle the most critical social issues at home, in USA, and world!

title: Clear Eyes and Jobs for Women in Rural Bangladesh
description: Women-run vision centres benefit the community in many ways. Training women to run these centres gives them on-the-job skills, independence and confidence. Bringing women-run vision centres to the doorsteps of female living in rural Bangladesh encourage these local women to have their eyes checked and treated. With healthy eyes and clear vision, they can then study or work better, take care of their families better and enjoy the beauty of life to the fullest.

title: Kids Saving the Rainforest
description: The vision of Kids Saving the Rainforest is to use every avenue available to rehabilitate wildlife, conduct original scientific research, train volunteers, plant trees in the rainforest and promote conservation. Your donations make our conservation work possible.  We know that it is thanks to you that we can make a difference in our rainforest and the wildlife's lives. Help us continue our work, please make a donation.

title: Responding to Deadly Conflicts in Western Kenya
description: Transforming Community for Social Change responds with effective programs at the grassroots level to political, tribal, and other conflicts in western Kenya. These responses include alternatives to violence, trauma healing and reconciliation, non-violent direct action, mediation, community dialogues, and listening sessions. The goal is to keep conflicts from escalating through retaliation and revenge. Thousands of Kenyans are involved in these peace sessions.

title: Drinking water for 350 students in Telangana India
description: Absenteeism due to water borne diseases steals precious learning time for students in government schools across India. Jaldhaara aims to provide a reliable and high quality service of providing purified drinking water to schools across its footprint, thereby reducing the number of days that students are absent due to this issue. This service will be reinforced by awareness creation programs that will educate and familiarise the students with good Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) habits.

title: Quality education for kids of disadvantaged group
description: The project is run in a highly remote area called sundarbans, the southern most part of West Bengal where no proper facility of education is available. this project will build up school building and other infrastructure for education like environment with other facilities for 500 students for deprived group of Sundarban area of West Bengal, India and a part of ongoing project.

title: Add more shelter for rescue horses in Dunkirk Md
description: Lilly Pond Foal Rescue will be able to house 2 more needy horses with the addition of 2 more stalls. That's 2 more horses or foals that won't have to suffer anymore neglect or abuse. We are located in Maryland and rescue 40-50 horses and foals per year.

title: Scholarships for At-risk Youth in Afghanistan
description: This project will provide at least 100 yearly scholarships to at-risk youth, particularly girls and victims of terrorism, in Afghanistan's most impoverished and marginalized Hazara communities. Through partnership with reputable schools in Afghanistan, the Foundation has designed a low-cost merit and need-based scholarship program to provide quality education with emphasis on critical thinking.

title: Help Renovate 100 Damaged Houses.
description: This project is helping Renovation of housing for 100 Tribalas in india living in Rural areas . They have own Registered land but no proper houses. Mostly living under difficult circumstances , at present their houses which are Hut or semi Roofs i.e. foundation and walls with bricks and cement and roof with coconut leaves. Because their building is totally collapsed , roof, flooring and walls were damaged.We would like to Alter this semi huts for their welfare .

title: Help 50 girls stay in school & watch them excel
description: This project will assist 50 girls in vulnerable communities in Cape Town & Gauteng to stay in school, provide them with an internationally recognized skills development program while supporting their basic needs for nutrition and re-usable sanitary towels.

title: Enable Food Security with Storage Bins in Kanpur
description: In Shivrajpur Block of Kanpur, the  Food security Problems are intensified because the farmers tend to be small/ landless laborers. Any natural calamity or unforeseen situation can reduce them to miserable & reduced situations.  This vulnerability is due to their incapacity to store grains beyond harvest trapping them in a vicious cycle of starvation, debt, & poverty during his lean season. Our project aims to support retaining capacity with low-cost Storage Bins.

title: Retain 150 MSM in HIV/STI services in Nigeria
description: In Nigeria, LGBT who are also living with HIV face stigma, exclusion, harassment and violence because of both their HIV status and socio-cultural, and religious perceptions. This support will  retain more than 100 MSM tested positive to HIV from the Global Fund ( New Funding Model) HIV intervention in Edo state, Nigeria and others who have tested HIV+ after the end of the project support cycle. MSM friendly centers will promote access and uptake of appropriate HIV/STI management services.

title: Support  Leadership  Project for Girls in Bongo
description: Girls and young women in Bongo- a  village in the Upper East Region of Ghana are from low income families and face a myriad of harsh challenges daily yet they have big dreams for themselves, their families and  community.  Since 2009, Greight Foundation has implemented 'Train-Coach-Mentor' Girls Leadership  Project for  girls and young women including visually impaired girls.  This project will  train, coach and mentor girls in personal development,  basic leadership and entrepreneurship skills.

title: Empowering Resilient Women Pilot Program
description: The CLEO Institute, focused on climate change science education and advocacy, will implement 'Empowering Resilient Women', a pilot program based in South Florida to help women & girls of under-served communities connect the dots between climate change, public health risks, & emergency preparedness.  Miami/South Florida ranks among the top US cities for income inequality. As the heads of their households, these women are in urgent need of this education, to become more resilient.

title: Help 10 Public Schools to access internet Tanzania
description: Help to avail study materials to poor student(s) who otherwise would have found it difficult to access this material These project will help in improving the educational standards of our country through the use of ICT.

title: To Provide meals to childrens with disabilities
description: This micro project will change the dire state of malnutrition faced by some students studying at the Sigaram special school for children with disabilities and Early Intervention centre for Cerebral palsy children. This is done by cooking nutritious noon meal with essential ingredients at a subsidized cost to the deserving students, thus helping them develop their body and their mind and their immunity power so that they can live happily without a worry about their health or the food.

title: CAPE TOWN DROUGHT RELIEF FOR THOUSANDS OF ANIMALS
description: Cape Town is experiencing the worst drought in recorded history. Our taps will run dry within the next 80 days which means we must act urgently to provide an alternate source of water for animals - both here at the SPCA and in the wider community. When there is nothing left for them to drink, they'll start dying in their thousands within a matter of days. The video shows how shrinking river beds are becoming death traps for animals, we have the solution but we need your help.

title: Opportunities & Hope for Guatemalan Maya Women
description: The Association of Highland Women will mentor 250 rural young women for success through the women's circle program that organizes mutual support groups that meet weekly.  Programming includes peer-to-peer counseling, literacy,  health and nutrition education, civic participation, leadership,  and enterprise development.     The process starts with improved cookstoves that provide women with the energy and free time to participate in empowerment programming facilitated by local social workers.

title: We all love a shower
description: Restoring dignity and safety to thousands of women and children trapped on Lesvos Island with a simple solution: adequate showers

title: UWC Costa Rica Sports & Cultural Festival 2018
description: The UWC Costa Rica Sports and Cultural Festival brings together 500+ people from around the country, especially students from different public and private schools. It is a space where everyone can live the UWC mission for one afternoon. As UWC we are the example that living together in tolerance, with different nations and cultures, for a better future is possible. We aim to overcome the lack of interaction between people from different socioeconomic backgrounds that Costa Rica faces every day.

title: Help Saved by Music Foundation children get a home
description: Saved by Music Foundation is a registered non-governmental organization (NGO) based in Mbale, Uganda. Our organization is lead and run by volunteers and we rely on donations from the public to ensure that we can continue to provide the support and care that the children of Mbale need. Saved by Music Foundation is dedicated to helping vulnerable children. Street children and children that come from the poorest families within our community are our main focus and priority.

title: Robotic Project for 60 students in Cundinamarca
description: Foundation vision 20/20 Colombia is planning to develop a robotic initiative for 60 students from the municipality of Cachipay and La Mesa Cundinamarca. Rural students that have a limited access to technology will be given the opportunity to develop new ways of learning about problem solving, math, physics, and software programming. This opportunity gives the students a brighter hope for the future knowing these skills will help them grow.

title: Clean water for 1 new person every 10 seconds
description: Nearly 1,000 children under age 5 die every day from diarrhea caused by contaminated water, poor sanitation, and improper hygiene. But World Vision believes the global water and sanitation crisis can be solved within our lifetimes. That's why we're focused on providing clean water and sanitation to every person in every community we work in, including the most vulnerable populations in the hardest-to-reach places.  World Vision is providing clean water to one new person every 10 seconds!

title: Change the lives of dogs and cats in Venezuela
description: We want to continue helping dogs and cats in Venezuela, by preventing new ones from being abandoned by families that no longer have the resources to feed them, and by improving the life quality of thousands of animals that live on the streets of our country.  The requests for our help have exponentially increased in the past few months and will only continue to do so in a country with an expected inflation of 13,000% (according to IMF estimates) so we are urging you to help us help them.

title: Empower women through financial access & service
description: Around the world, mothers and other women who care for children work tirelessly to provide them with brighter futures. Research shows they can do it: Increases in women's income result in direct improvements in their children's lives. Yet women, especially those in rural areas, remain disproportionately represented among the poorest of the poor, making up 70 percent of all impoverished people. The Women's Empowerment Fund is a bold vision to raise $25 million to financially empower 2 million.

title: Get cooking in Nepal with Solar Cookers Intl.
description: In Nepal, usually it's women who cook. They face blockades, fuel crises and poverty. Cooking fuel is often unavailable. Free solar thermal energy is abundant. Goals:   Build solar cookers from locally available materials  Train/empower primarily women: elderly, orphans, disabled and others to obtain cooking/fuel security Protect family health from diseases due to indoor air pollution Reduce environmental and forest degradation  Encourage women to set up micro-businesses.

title: Help end hunger in the poorest part of Mexico
description: Guerrero is the second most marginalized state in Mexico, 64% of its population lives in poverty and 23% in extreme poverty. The poorest municipality in Mexico is here: Cochoapa el Grande, an indigenous region. According to the United Nations, Cochoapa has the lowest Human Development Index in Mexico, similar to such African countries as Liberia and Guinea-Bissau.  Our training and bioconstruction program improves the quality of life and combats hunger in Cochoapa, bringing sustainable change.

title: POWER Lunch!
description: ESPANOL: https://issuu.com/nexoscomunitarios/docs/descripcio_n_de_almuerzo_power POWER Lunch is the new version of our successful Lunch Program in the High-Andes of Peru! We aim to combat malnutrition by: - Providing 5 nutritious lunches per week. - Implementing workshops and experiments based on Active Learning Methodology  - Will use PhotoVoice and medical check-ups for monitoring and evaluation. We will continue developing our Sustainable Homes Project to promote sustainability in nutrition

title: Provide Desks and Chairs to Students in Tanzania
description: This project will fund the purchase of 320 desk/chair sets for a secondary school in Western Tanzania. In 2015, we opened Amahoro Secondary School. As enrollment numbers grew, so did the demand for desks and chairs for the students. Presently, 320 students are still sharing seats or sitting on rocks on the floor. The government funds for this school are not meeting the needs. This campaign aims to support the community and school to make sure that each student has his or her own learning station

title: Ruadt Village Rehabilitation Therapy Centre
description: 1. Project Title : Village Rehabilitation Therapy Centre  2. Background of the Organisation :   The Rural Area Development Trust (RUADT) is a voluntary social service organization exclusively working for the rehabilitation of differently-abled people. It was set up in the village of B. Dharmathupatti in 1991, with the mission of identifying needy differently-abled children in the area and of creating awareness about disability and its implications for affected families and individuals in 10.

title: Build a fish farm, save Nigerian women from Penury
description: The purpose of the project is to establish a 3000 capacity catfish farm each for every 100 rural poor women in 10 rural communities in Nigeria.  These women will be equipped with sustainable skills and knowledge in fish farming, fish feed making as added value, business and entrepreneurship skills needed to run the fish farm as a joint business. The goal of the project is to empower 1000 rural poor women to become economically independent and lift themselves and families out of poverty.

title: Marche's earthquake: give kids a new civic center
description: Caldarola is an Italian municipality which is still trying to recover after the serious damages caused by the earthquake that hit Central Italy in 2016. The aim of the project is that of supporting and promoting the rebirth of community life through the rebuilding of a center that can host activities, events, and workshops. Children and young people, in particular, will have a safe place where to meet and stay together, refinding hope and trust in their territory again.

title: Home away from home.....Support the old age person
description: Ageing is a time of multiple illness and disabilities. The aged parents are now-a-days undergoing great difficulties and are always subjected to mental stress due to negligence made by their children. And as they become unproductive at that age, they don't have the basic needs of life like food and shelter. In this context, our Shakti organization has started managing an Old age Home since 2006 to provide food, shelter, clothing and medical aid to the destitute grandparents/ old age persons.

title: Develop 100 Women Entrepreneurs in Indian Villages
description: Pipal Tree Foundation plans to provide training to 100 women from poorest part of Ranga Reddy district in Telangana. The training would be provided in Seri Culture (silk production) and Goat Farming. The project provides complete training to 100 women to enable them to start their own business in the field. The project plans to provide financial assistance to  these women for tools, plants and goats after successful completion of training. It also plans to support these women for next 18 months

title: Healing for 20 Trafficking & Abuse Victims, Kosovo
description: O.Mekembjes (Operation Restoration) is an affiliate of Operation Mercy in Kosovo. They are the only organisation providing long-term support to victims of domestic violence and trafficking, as well as combating the conditions which lead individuals to become victims or aggressors through education and training programmes for vulnerable young people. They achieve this through an individualised programme including therapy and skills training for up to 20 participants at one time.

title: Help 100 traumatized Palestinian children succeed
description: Since 1925 the Spafford Children's Center (SCC) in East Jerusalem has served the Palestinian population. Currently, SCC provides treatment for trauma reactions in children who have experienced violence in their communities as well as family stress. For decades children struggling in overcrowded schools have received SCC's individualized tutoring in Arabic, English, and math. The SCC also provides speech and occupational therapy, plus art, dance, music, and recreational programs.

title: Empowerment for disadvantaged girls and women
description: This project is providing vocational training skills (tailoring & crafts) to school dropout girls , and micro loan to single mothers in northern Uganda, to empower them to start small businesses and create a better life for their families and to be financially independent , This micro project will support 5 groups (100 women) with interest free micro loans and 100 girls this year to enable them expand their businesses and be self reliance.

title: Help Ugandans Obtain Vital Health Services
description: In Uganda, vital healthcare for vulnerable people is often compromised by corruption. Life-saving medications go missing, funds to pay nurses disappear and patients are forced to pay bribes to save the lives of their loved ones. We created the Citizen Action Platform (CAP) as a means for patients to report and eliminate the maltreatment they confront. Now, people are able to stand-up to injustice and improve their communities through a simple text message.

title: Empower & Support Nonprofits in Southeast Asia
description: My name is Cedric Yumba, a GlobalGiving Representative in Southeast Asia for the year 2018. I will be traveling to Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia to visit more than 50 GlobalGiving nonprofit partners addressing a variety of community issues. My impact includes meeting communities change makers to discuss ways we would support their organizations, running 8 workshops to train our current partners, acquiring new strategic partners and much more.

title: Support 200 volunteers to prevent Hepatitis E
description: This project will raise funds to support 200 volunteers involved in a health education campaign educating the community how to prevent and manage Hepatitis E at the community level in Ohangewana, Oshikoto, Khomas, Oshana and Omusati regions of Namibia. The campaign is in response to the outbreak of Hepatitis E in the Khomas region since October 2017 with over  900 cases confirmed and six deaths registered thus far. The outbreak has caused huge anxiety and panic in the communities.

title: Educare for 150 underprivileged children
description: This project will provide school items (school dress, monthly stipend and educational materials) and develop big brother/sister initiative for 150 underprivileged children who comes from the most climate vulnerable place in the world and belong to poor, marginalized and Dalit families in Tala Upazila of Satkhira district in Bangladesh. By providing these items we can increase the attendance of school students, encourage them to do better, reduce drop out rate, child marriage and discrimination.

title: WCC water project (Sierra Leone)
description: WCC water project is  to provide clean drinking water to communities in the Eastern of (Freetown)Sierra leone. There is a desperate need of water supply in Sierra Leone. Young people have to walk 3 to 4miles everyday just to fetch water needed for their households. This will also help children and parents to enhance healthy child development, safe drinking water and strengthen community partnerships. The water Programme adds value to the overall development context by offering an alternative .

title: Help 200 Orphans get Health Insurances in Tanzania
description: Community Development Watch (CODEWA) plans to provide health insurance cards to help orphans and vulnerable children in Tabora -Tanzania to get free hospitalization and treatment for one year.  This project will cover all hospitalization and treatments for free in all public and private hospitals in Tanzania. It will enable orphans to stay healthy, feel safer and increase their school attendance to get better results.

title: Empower & Educate the Girls of Rural Kisumu
description: A study by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation found nearly 65% of women and girls in Kenya are unable to afford sanitary pads. Other studies show that many girls drop out of school when they hit menarche, with many missing up to 5 days of school every month.  Furthermore, many girls are cornered to engage in 'sex for pads' that leads to 13,000 teenage girls in Kenya dropping out of school annually. Our program makes Sanitary Kits and SRH workshops accessible to girls so they stay in school.

title: Empower 50 Nigerian Trafficked Victims
description: This life transforming project will help to strengthen the rehabilitation of victims of human trafficking in Nigeria, who often get more frustrated after their rescue, due to lack of sustainable empowerment. With this project, victims will be provided with resources to: a. Start their own businesses  b. Enroll in schools  Recently, we provided resources to open a business for a Nigerian victim we rescued in 2017. There are many of such victims who are wandering in Nigeria, and are at risk.

title: Constructing WCC Academy
description: As an organisation, WCC supports research on child poverty and education in Africa. Intuitively, the main means of escaping poverty is education, taken in its broadest sense (formal and informal schooling, skills training and knowledge acquisition). WCC aims to give the children and young people in Sierra Leone a health service fit for the 21st century. This exists partly as an advisory service with plans to improve the capability in the near future.

title: WCC Healthcare project
description: The main purpose of this project is to help provide necessary and effective health care in Sierra Leone in order to assist mothers and children. There are three pillars that this project is based on:  Health information - Family planning is commonly regarded as cost-effective health intervention with social and economic benefits. For every dollar spent on family planning, Sierra Leone is estimated to save U$ 2.1 dollars, in particular to rural communities (Keen, 2017);   Equality healthcare

title: Restore Health To 5000 Ibadan People With Diabetes
description: This project will raise awareness, provide training to volunteers and experienced hands from the various communities to act as health champions, sharing vital information on hypertension and diabetes through peers group, meetings, and through other health campaigns. We will provide support in terms of medical screening, medications (medical drugs), and other nutritional supplements and advice that will aid them to cope and live a healthy

title: Enable young Girls through Life Skills and Sports
description: The project KOUSAL - Knowledge on Utilizing Skills and Leadership would help in capacity building of adolescent girls who are resident of Bhaskar Nagar, a notified slum of Guwahati city, Assam. The project aims to work on the different life skills through sports as a medium of developing confidence, self respect and enhanced communication. The project will also aim at developing peer leaders from among the girls for creating future leader and work on scale ability and sustainability.

title: Support Greek farmers,Shepherdog breeds & wildlife
description: Shepherd dogs are the most important measure for the livestock breeders to protect their flock from bears and wolves. In Greece the breeders do not receive subsidies for the acquisition and raise of a shepherd dog. So Callisto founded a Shepherd Dogs Network to donate puppies to breeders that face losses from large carnivores. This way the network contributes to the conservation of the Greek shepherd dog breeds and protects the large carnivores by improving their coexistence with the farmers.

title: SWATT-TEAM: sexual violence responders in Zimbabwe
description: 1 in 4 women in Zimbabwe have experienced sexual violence since the age of 15, causing long-term emotional and psychological trauma which impacts on women's ability to care for themselves and their families. Oasis Zimbabwe is training 1000 community sexual violence responders, to help survivors to access immediate medical and legal support, and to process and recover from trauma in the long term, so they can build hopeful and sustainable futures where they can pursue their dreams.

title: Mission: Tuition! 2019
description: While fulfilling the educational needs of the children in TLC's care, those awaiting placement into permanent families, TLC also supports the children who have, due to difficult circumstances, been adopted into the founding family over the years. This support is a vital aspect in helping them as they work towards becoming independent. You can help support our home as all these lives (little and not so little) continue on the road to achieving their dreams!

title: SLOW LORIS & WILDLIFE NEW REHABILITATION CENTER
description: Since the establishment of the Slow Loris rehabilitation center in 2016,ISCP has saved 100 lorises and 94 of them have been released in forest,24 leopard cats,5 longtail macaques,4 gibbons,11 binturong,1 sun bear,13 raptors, songbirds & others wildlife in cooperation with local wildlife authorities & other local NGOs. Currently,the Sumatran Kukang rehabilitation center,which was built in 2016 by ISCP will plan move and renewbuilding.currently center can be seen here: https://youtu.be/fPj2TfJ8Et0

title: Tsharka Tibetan Elem/Middle School, Dolpo, Nepal
description: Support the expansion of Tsharka Elementary School to serve all the children in this Tibetan village located in the remote Himalayan region of Dolpo, Nepal. Currently, the school is filled to capacity with 60 students. There are 120 children in Tsharka Village. New classrooms are being built and more teachers must be hired. The International Community Development Foundation seeks money to complete four new classrooms, improve the existing school buildings, and pay salaries for new teachers.

title: "Youth Peace" Campaign U.S.A. & International
description: Our Campaign's core beliefs: All youth are "equal" in importance, meaning, value, and worth, without exception.  All youth's "destiny" is to live a long and healthy life. Every youth is special, unique, and "one-of-a-kind."  Violence, bullying, and abuse (VBA) are the "Head of the Snake." This is the number one root "problem" of humankind. We aim to "stay ahead of the curve," meaning violence and conflict "prevention." Youth's no. one job is to "survive" their youth.

title: ADOPT AN ADVOCATE
description: Roughly one million victims and survivors have leaned on, counted on and received support from a Mothers Against Drunk Driving victim advocate. That means that victim advocates serve as a vital and critical component. That's why we are asking you to "Adopt an Advocate".

title: WeSurvive: Stories of the Ebola Outbreak
description: WeSurvive: Stories of the Ebola Outbreak is a web-based, oral history database that allows users to access a substantial collection of personal video testimonials from Ebola survivors, their family members, and other community members affected by the 2014 West African Ebola outbreak.  We believe it is vital that West Africans contribute directly and significantly to the historical record and deepen both how this catastrophic Ebola outbreak and the region are understood.

title: Pass the Mic! to Kibera Girls  Literacy project
description: In Kenya, 6/10 out of school children come from poor families. In the Kibera Slums of Nairobi, Kenya, they are the poorest of the poor. And girls are at the greatest risk of dropping out. Pass the Mic! is unique, four-year leadership development program for primary school and secondary girls studying in the informal schools in Kibera. Pass the Mic! will target girls, who are most at risk  due to academic challenges, and provide them with holistic support daily after school.

title: E-Libraries for Post-Earthquake Ecuador
description: In 2016 a powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake severely affected Coaque, an under-resourced Ecuadorian community. In 2017, Tufts International Development, partnered with Libraries Without Borders and Avanti, created learning spaces where we set up digital servers and laptops and trained local residents on how to use the technology to lead capacity-building activities. We are currently focused on the sustainable continuation of this pilot program as well as beginning our search towards expansion.

title: Mainstreaming 200,000+ street children
description: Save the Children, through it's on the ground work in the states of Delhi, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, is trying to create an enabling environment for vulnerable children living on the streets of India, thereby strengthening their access to identity, leading to right to survival, development, participation and protection by: Facilitating the process of securing an Aadhaar card for each street child, post which they will get to live in a shelter home or be reunited with their pare

title: Train 20 Women to Make Soap & Prevent Trafficking
description: In order to combat child trafficking, 20 women will learn how to make soap and other skin care products. Poverty is one of the main root causes of trafficking in Ghana and women are disproportionately affected by poverty. This training will enable these 20 women to become economically independent and secure. Participants in the training will set up a cooperative, ensuring collective success and support.

title: Providing health care to 1000s in Bujumbura slum
description: The Ntaseka Clinic in Kamenge slum of Bujumbura provides health care for survivors of rape and gender based violence, support for 330 HIV+ individuals, trauma healing workshops for raped and abused women, and health care for children and the general population.  This includes AIDS testing and support for those who are HIV+. Founded in 2002 with a fulltime staff of seventeen, it services more than 10000 people each year.

title: Empower 100 Pakistani Women through Sewing Skill
description: The Society for Human Development (SHD) will establish one (donations permitting, two) Sewing Centers in Central Punjab, Pakistan to provide an opportunity for rural girls and women to learn a valuable, income-generating skill, enabling them to lead a life of self-reliance and dignity.

title: The Man Who Built Peace - UK Launch
description: Frank Buchman was a revolutionary thinker and leader whose trust-building, reconciliation and peace efforts greatly influenced the 20th century, and offer a powerful solution to many of the issues facing the world today. The Man Who Built Peace is his story. Your donations help Initiatives of Change share this powerful documentary to showcase his life-story and raise awareness of his impactful work. We will launch the film in London on June 7th, followed by a regional tour of UK cities.

title: WCC Football Team (Sierra Leone)
description: "Football for all" creates avenues for healthy living and active lifestyles. This preventative health approach will help to improve the health status of the communities. It provides sporting activities as an alternative to anti-social behaviour. Football for all will target groups and areas, where there is a recurring pattern of crime and violence to preach peace in the name of football.

title: Rescue 100 Abandoned Dogs in Mexico
description: Our Dog Rescue Center plans to provide medical care, including vaccinations and neuter/spay operations, for 100 dogs in Santa Rosalia, Mexico. Abandoned dogs roam the streets and the number will continue to rise unless we shift the trend by providing veterinary care, promoting adoption, and increasing education about the treatment of animals. We will improve the health and safety of the community by improving the health and well-being of the stray dogs.

title: Help giving for Cassava-Grater Machine
description: The organization's aim to contribute to a sustained improvement of living conditions, stability, health, education and economic growth in the rural population of four communities in Gbinle-Dixian chiefdom in Kambia District Sierra Leone West Africa. Harvesting cassava farm is now in progress after 1 year 6 months in field. Thanks for your donations. The project activity is designed to focus on buying a machine for cassava-grater and enhance them to produce enough food which becomes available.

title: Children and Youth Health and Nutrition Project
description: Children and youths living in remote areas in Mindanao are severely disadvantaged and most of them are severely malnourished. Most have difficulty going to school or completing the school year. The reason for this is poverty and lack of farming inputs in order for their parents to develop their farms and earn decent income from their harvest. Coupled with this is the frequent occurrence of severe storms which destroys farms making the farmer more poorer.

title: Develop character & provide leadership education
description: The Boy Scouts of America's (BSA) mission is to prepare young people to make ethical and moral choices over their lifetimes by instilling in them the values of the Scout Oath and Scout Law. Our priority is to bring the benefits of Scouting to more youth while remaining true to our mission. Both girls and boys have access to the character development and values-based leadership training that Scouting promises to help them be better prepared for future success.

title: Creating a Safe Space for Women and Girls in India
description: Sexual violence is a global pandemic. Women and girls find it difficult to report these acts, resulting in a lack of actionable data. We encourage women and girls to report their experiences of sexual violence, anonymously on our crowdmap. This project will allow us to create digital toolkits which explain the spectrum of abuse, legal rights, how crowdmapping works, and how to engage communities to take action. We will use these tools in community workshops and with our partner organisations.

title: Let's support kids with hearing disabilities
description: The project supports children with hearing disabilities who attend the Bethlehem Ephpheta Institute where,through specialized educational and scholastic paths,they can receive an adequate education, thus being helped in the process of social integration. Many children,living away from school,have difficulty attending classes regularly so we have also activated and contributed to transport service to guarantee them the possibility of reaching the institute.

title: Educate 600 girls in Faisalabad Pakistan
description: The educational opportunities for a girl child and career oriented skills; the girls have always been dependent on father, brother before marriage and upon her husband after marriage. Most of their time and efforts are devoted for family welfare in on-forms and off-forms duties but their contribution is not economically valued. This is the overall scenario of average women. Thus without education and career oriented skill their dependency increase, making them unemployed & doing household chores

title: Support literacy program for children in Tobago
description: EARC will provide books, clothing, school supplies, food, and access to technological devices for the children in Tobago to support literacy and personal development.

title: Help 60 Rwandan Students Fight Poverty with Trees
description: Rwandan charity Compagnie Agricole Environment (CAE) will train 60 local students to plant and protect 60,000 life-giving trees. These trees will provide food, water and income for their families by bearing fruits to improve nutrition, protecting their cattle's water supply from evaporation and boosting their crop harvests by enriching the soil.

title: California Fires & Debris Flow: Relief & Recovery
description: The devastating fires in December 2017 and debris flow in Montecito on January 9, 2018, destroyed families and livelihoods with incredible loss of property and life. It also dramatically impacted the local economy. Our nonprofit organizations activated immediately to provide food, shelter, emotional and spiritual care, and case management to navigate recovery from consecutive disasters. The Community Disaster Relief Fund supports those critical service providers in relief and recovery.

title: Chance For All in an African Magical Classroom
description: Volunteers will teach the French language and mathematical skills to street children in San Luis Senegal. This is a grassroots project started by the Senegalese called Chance for All. Using three rooms in a home provided by a local family. They will supplement the meager supplies they have acquired with equipment, books and materials provided by Magical Classrooms. They have already been been shown how to use them and the director of the project has been trained to oversee their use.

title: Empower India Rural Girl Children with Education
description: This project empowers the rural, underprivileged girl students studying at Isha Vidhya schools in India, by funding their education, noon meal and transportation. Girl students benefited by this project can focus on their studies without a worry about their fees, food and safe transportation to the school.

title: Construction of Menstrual Hygiene Toilet for Girls
description: Menstruation is considered dirty and impure and during periods. Girls are discouraged to attend school and interested to stay at homes. The unavailability of sanitary pads, inadequate sanitation and absence of separate toilet for girls in schools, Hostels, College compounds. The problem and has a huge impact on girls school attendance and is a major reason for dropouts of girls from schools, Hostels, Colleges, e.t.c.We are ready to construct 25 Toilets for 25 Schools particularly for Girls only.

title: Build 6 toilet facilities for 300 people of Swada
description: Despite the effort to end open defecation by 2030, Swada, a village considered as the most deprived village amongst 160 villages in Ga South Municipality has no single toilet facility. This has resulted to the practice of open defecation which contributes to the contaminating effects of open defecation particularly on women and children. The project would improve access to sanitation which is a critical step towards reducing the impact of diseases and making open defecation unattractive.

title: Build libraries for 2 deprived schools in Akweley
description: This project will build two libraries which is integral to the teaching learning process. The libraries will benefit 500 basic school children in the Akweley community where there is a high rate of illiteracy due to poverty. Book to Read Foundation in pursuit of one of our aims towards bringing to the barest minimum the high illiteracy rate has so far donated over 1000 reading materials ,stationery , desktop computers and organized spelling bee competition for the pupils in the community

title: Help free 50 Surrey women & children from abuse
description: Women and children who are experiencing domestic abuse live in fear and use all their inner resources to get through each day. Once women make the decision to leave abusers, short term accommodation is available in one of our two refuge houses. We offer a 7 days a week helpline and support and assistance to rebuild lives free from abuse. Donations help secure housing, furniture, essentials and offer outreach services, which are so vital to the emotional and mental recovery of women and children.

title: Promoting Women's Leadership in Pakistan
description: The project aims to promote women's leadership role in development in the face of extremism and conflict in KP. Women are underrepresented at all levels of decision-making processes in all most every sector. Facts and findings in the education, health and employment sectors show that women needs and challenges are not being sufficiently addressed, because the majority of the leadership is male-dominated.  This project will invest in building & strengthening women's leadership.

title: Hope for 500 UK women affected by trauma & abuse
description: Every day in the UK girls and women as young as 8 and as old as 80 turn to self injury to cope with abuse, trauma, loneliness and despair. This project will allow Self injury Support to expand our specialist services, reach more women at risk of harming themselves and provide self injury training to other services and improve support across the UK . Expanded services will reach at least 500 more women affected by trauma, sexual violence and self injury who deserve our care and compassion.

title: TEACH CODE LITERACY TO THE RURAL YOUTH IN VIETNAM
description: Learning to code will help prepare the kids for the world they live in today. Programming is too important to be left just to computer science departments - it can be taught effectively outside of computer science. Beyond the practical reasons for learning how to code, there's the fact that creating a game or animation can be really fun for kids. The Dariu Foundation recognizes the importance of code literacy and we plan to provide the youth with coding skills in our own mobile schools.

title: A museum to tell the story of St. Martin
description: The building that housed St. Martin's first natural history museum was destroyed, but we're creating a new one! Amuseum Naturalis at The Old House will be a museum for local nature and heritage, and a space for community projects. During the first half of 2018, we will be repairing the buildings in our new location, cataloging our historical collection, preparing our exhibits and launching community projects like our native plants nursery which will distribute native tree seedlings for free.

title: Transform teens who have family in prison
description: This project supports teenagers who have incarcerated loved ones. One in 14 children in the US a parent who is or has been i prison. POPS (Pain of the Prison system) transforms the stigma these young people have faced and the shame they too often feel into hope and healing and a sense of justice that they earn by awakening to their own power and resiliency. The POPS publishing program amplifies the students' voices and visions in annually published, award-winning anthologies.

title: Help 36 needy Children go to school in Uganda 2018
description: By meeting  Children's Education rights/needs we are giving them the opportunity to reach their full potential and the power to transform their lives, families and communities; empowering them to be more responsible citizens and independent adults accountable to the societies they live in, reducing high illiteracy levels in the country  thus breaking the chain of vulnerability so as to have transformed communities in Uganda.

title: Empowering women in Afghanistan
description: To meet one of the greatest needs in Afghanistan - to help women - GHNI teams will launch empowerment centers to provide training and opportunities to produce and sell handicrafts.  We will also teach women how to plant and nurture a family garden.  This allows the women to provide diverse vegetables to feed their children healthy meals.  We have one center where women have been meeting and they are seeing great success in growing food and earning an income.  GHNI will be adding 2 centers!

title: Let's give girls training for a vibrant future
description: AFCA will set up 3 greenhouses for orphaned girls who were abused by their guardians. Girls will gain incredible skills for their future: set up the greenhouse, set up an irrigation system, mulch, grow seedlings, plant, fertilize, harvest, market, and sell produce. They also learn traditional field farming.   With a little under half the proceeds going into their personal bank accounts, the girls have funds for the day they leave the orphanage! They leave with skills, a savings account and hope.

title: Improve Disaster Readiness to Solve Hunger
description: Feeding San Diego's mission to end hunger in our area is rooted in our early work supporting victims of the 2007 firestorms, which displaced hundreds of thousands of residents. We remain dedicated to supporting our entire region in times of extreme need, and effective preparedness begins by building the capacity of our organization to escalate our hunger-relief services at a moment's notice.

title: Flowers in bloom: support 40 abused kids, Ethiopia
description: The "Flowers in bloom" project aims to improve the reception conditions of sexually assaulted minors in Addis Ababa. Aleimar joins a project that Il Sole Onlus and Integrated Family Service Organization (IFSO) are carrying out since 2002 providing medical, psychological and social assistance to abused minors and their families, guaranteeing adequate nutrition and hygienic conditions, enhancing psychological support. The project aims to strengthen the reception services of two family houses.

title: Education for Underprivileged Children in India
description: Shiksha will provide a free and quality education to 1,000+ children of migrant labourers in Gurgaon, Haryana, India. In addition to a completely free education, all students will be provided with free books, stationery, uniforms, and a nutritious mid-day meal.

title: Tomorrow Now:  Education for South Sudan Girl's
description: It's been 4-years since the outbreak of major conflict in South Sudan.  The country has the highest rate of children missing out on schooling in the world, 72% according to UNICEF in 2017.  Less than 1% of girls here will complete their secondary education.  HDC is a national NGO, working across the country to help those impacted by conflict & displacement.  Through Tomorrow Now, we provide scholarships & supports to girls to achieve their dream of obtaining an education.

title: Help Provide Hay for 82 Rescue Horses in the US
description: This project will provide 82 rescue horses with quality hay for one month.  Many of the horses at  The Foxie G Foundation come to us from neglect situations or have been saved from being slaughtered in Mexico and Canada. With good care and  nutrition, most are able to be placed in loving, adoptive homes.  Horses that can not be adopted live out their days on our farm in a sanctuary setting.

title: Support Maternal Health in Rural Haiti
description: Project Medishare aims to reduce maternal and infant deaths in rural Haiti. To encourage pregnant women to seek continued prenatal care at our maternity centers, Project Medishare will distribute newborn welcome kits to 75 moms. The kits will include a baby box to provide a safe space for infants to sleep, along with essential health and hygiene items to help keep mom and baby healthy.

title: Empowered Camping
description: Due to the many stresses that single parents deal with, it is vital that they find a healthy way to relax, recoup, and revitalize. Many families take a vacation in order to let go of their day to day demands. Unfortunately, many single parents are unable to afford traditional vacations. At the Empowered Camping event, we teach families how to disconnect from electronics and reconnect with each other. Mentors teach the families how to put up a tent, build a fire, and cook over the fire.

title: Feed 1,530 Kenyan School Children with Porridge
description: Hope Alive Campaign seeks to provide a daily cup of Porridge to school children in Kenya, from extremely poor backgrounds, who cannot afford three square meals a day. This project in Kenya, shall provide 1,530 orphans and vulnerable children, with a nutritious cup of Porridge, every school day, in the morning, from Monday to Friday, to help them fight short term hunger, concentrate in class, actively participate in classroom activities and lead to improved academic performance.

title: Training Ugandans in Trauma Informed Care
description: This project equips local leaders in Uganda with mental health and trauma informed care knowledge and skills, so they can support survivors in their communities, disrupt cycles of trauma and violence, and break the stigma around mental health.  Trainings are designed for everyday community leaders who may have little to no prior mental health knowledge - including teachers, health workers, faith leaders, local government leaders, and more.

title: Teach reading and writing to 450 illiterate Uganda
description: Change African Child Int. will teach 450 women living in poverty the basic skills of reading and writing in the mother tongue, numeracy and English. The project is in Wakiso District, Uganda. Groups of 25 meet twice weekly for six months with a trained group leader and learn by discussing their life challenge and create their own texts. The aim is to make the women able to take charge of their own livelihood, understand their rights and provide a good future for their children.

title: mamare children home
description: support inmate girls in the children home with care and education.

title: Send Dalit Girls to Nursing School
description: The Veera Project offers young women graduating from secondary school the opportunity to pursue a higher education and enter a variety of professions.  Women in India need to be educated to become independent. Our girls come from very poor villages of the Thar desert around Jodhpur. Nursing is one particular job they care to train for to help their people in the villages or to work in a hospital with a good wage.

title: Project for the Empowering Various Affected Women
description: This project target rural people, who are the affected previous 25 years of war, armed terrorist, ethnic conflicts, and flooding, landslide, drought, disaster vulnerabilities. The most of widows' family, women, young women and affected from their daily nutritional foods, health care, children education and family need are have problems. Unemployment has become a major issue across the region. To improve the income of 900 rural women through 150 groups self employment.

title: Compost Pit for Food Security of a tribal Family
description: The indigenous communities Gond and Baiga, 99% of these family lives in below poverty line, identify as small and marginalized farmer. Their livelihood depends on small piece of land which they use for maize and paddy cultivation, they do not have any irrigation facility. Per acre production is very much low. They are actually saving world from climate change, they never use chemical fertilizers for more crop production. Another reason is they do not have money to purchase costly fertilizers.

title: EVENING STUDY CENTERS FOR POOR CHILDREN
description: Evening Study Centers will be organized in 10 rural villages. 40 primary school children will be admitted in each center. Qualified persons will provide guidance and support to the children to improve their academic performance. The methods used will be participatory and learning by doing. A nutritious snack will be given to the children. There will monthly growth monitoring and annual health check-up of children. Feedback and motivation will be given to parents in monthly meetings

title: Women Economic Empowerment: Snail Farm in Ghana
description: Many African women are faced with a heavy burden as a result of still existing patriarchal structures. They often experience great difficulty buying or renting land, finding good jobs, and accessing financing. AYPAD created the Snail Farm in Ghana to assist at-risk women in raising the African Giant Snails to alleviate poverty and malnutrition, and provide economic opportunity and education through a sustainable farming program.

title: Help Mothers and Girls Earn a Brighter Future
description: An income gives women in rural Darfur villages freedom of choice and ability to make decisions for their families. Almost invariably village leaders are men.  Our sustainable projects give women a voice in their communities. Goat Loans, Donkeys, and Midwife & Paravet training give women incomes and change their status. Your help will enable women to build better, life-changing  futures for themselves and their children.

title: Youth  Awareness to End HIV/AIDs and Hepatitis B
description: The mandate of our organization is to restore hope in the lives of the need and give information to people in our communities that will help them make healthy decisions for themselves and their families. We will be working with the local schools, youths and health centres on this Project. We will use participatory storytelling, videos to create awareness and break down stigma surrounding HIV/AIDS and Hepatitis B in Uganda. Participants will attend a multi-day training led by local professionals.

title: Hope Alive for 100 Victimised Women in ibadan
description: Help us keep hope alive, project to empower 100 victimised women(victim of domestic violence and single mothers)  in Ibadan to be self reliant, Ibadan is a largest ancient city in Nigeria, had been the centre of administration of the old western region since the days of the British colonial rule, women shoulder 2/3 of the world's problem and that's why we'r given our nurturing supports to the victimised women to be mentored by experts in diverse fields such as, fashion designing, hair making,

title: HepC Medicine to 500 villagers in Myanmar
description: The project will provide free hepatitis C medicines to 500 villagers in the poorest rural areas of Mon State, Myanmar.  A treatment course of generic hepatitis C drug costs 300 USD per patient. 75% population in rural areas cannot afford the drugs. The project will start in July 2018. The project provides free hepatitis C generic drugs to the high risk patients by working with local charity hospitals and pharmaceutical manufacturers to tackle the high cost of the drugs.

title: Restore a house to mobilize 100 ignored labor pool
description: This project will positively influence ignored labor pools: chronically unemployed, marginalized communities, orphans, recovering addicts to address staff shortage to serve Madagascar hospitality and tourism industry. Travel to the capital to polish foreign languages will diminish. The renovation of this historical landmark will also signify the preservation of the architectural ensemble of the Old Town Fianarantsoa. We include lemur identification in our curriculum to reduce human-wild conflict

title: TRAIN 200 NIGERIAN YOUTHS TO BE SELF-RELIANT
description: This project is a Free Skill Acquisition Program, to be held in Southern Nigeria. It aims at training two hundred (200) indigent and unemployed Nigerian youths in skill areas of interest and empower them with the necessary tools to begin their own trade and be self employed.

title: CareCraft
description: Empowering marginalised women and men living with epilepsy through income-generating and self-management skills for sustainable livelihoods through training and financial support and help them become an expert artisan in a specific craft.

title: Give 150 Peruvian babies a safe start in life
description: Kira is a social enterprise focused on crowdfunding and delivering survival kits to low income mothers, guaranteeing an equal and safe start in life. Our survival kit is call Kirawawa, a cardboard baby box that serves as the baby's first crib. This project will allow us to fund our operations to attend 150 mothers and babies this year; and, more importantly, start with our preventive health coverage pilot. We will monitor the development of the babies, preventing further diseases.

title: Increasing Digital Literacy to 100 More Children
description: Young people's futures will be determined by their digital literacy and skills, yet the gap between the digital-haves and digital-have-nots is getting wider. We will close the gap by supporting communities to run their own tech clubs, delivering grass roots access where it is needed most. Your support will provide laptops & volunteer coordination for those communities. We are already working with 16 clubs across the West of England but want to double that with your support!

title: Raise the Girlz to be Future Leaders in Jamaica
description: The program empowers girls to believe they are capable of achieving any goal they set for themselves.  Our programs teach girls to manage money, develop healthy relationships, deal with peer pressure, critically examine global events, be physically active, and develop a love of learning.  Girls have significantly less access to safe public space in Jamaica as compared with boys. Therefore, our program provides girls with a place to gather learn and grow while supporting emotional development.

title: Protect 50 street children from abuse in Quetta
description: This CPRT centre will take 50 children off the streets in Balochistan protecting them from abuse, slavery and a life of crime. Our project has been successful in 13 centres in 9 cities across the country and already transformed the lives of our children in CPRT centres by inspiring them to leave the streets and join main stream education.

title: Native Language Story Books for Ladakhi Children
description: 17000 ft Foundation, an Indian non profit has been working tirelessly to improve the lives of children living in the toughest inhabited regions of the world, the high altitude Himalayan region of Ladakh, India. The Foundation has setup 250 school libraries, 140 playgrounds and trained  over 1000 teachers. For the 30,000 school going children in this region, there are no story books in their mother tongue, Bhoti. This project will translate, contextualize, print and distribute 15,000 story books.

title: Medical care for abused, pregnant girls in India
description: Tejus Home is the first, and as far as we know only, home for abused, pregnant teenagers in India. So far we have welcomed 52 girls aged 12 to 18, generally half way through pregnancy, socially stigmatized and rejected by the family. Along with our partner, Birth For Change, DIL SE offers the possibility of a healthy pregnancy thanks to quality and respectful maternal health care with midwives, other medical professionals such as Govt. and Pvt. sector hospitals and Ultra sound scan centres.

title: Bosnian War: Support 375 Victims Tell Their Story
description: Without a publicly available record on war detention camps in Bosnia, the victims remain unable to realize their rights and reparation for the sufferings they endured. All this creates a context in which the victims who were illegally imprisoned during the war become de facto discriminated group. We work to record stories of former war camp victims to empower the future of the process of reconciliation in the country.

title: Help Investigate Eco-Crimes in Southern Africa
description: Like the colourful Oxpecker birds that remove parasites from wildlife in Africa, our investigative journalists target problems in the environment and peck away at them until they disappear. You can help reduce environmental crime by supporting the dedicated journalists who expose and track the villains.

title: 10000 Washable Sanitary Pads for African women
description: In Limpopo, South Africa, young girls skip school during their menstrual period because they can't afford hygiene products. We provide washable, reusable pads to these girls so that they can stay in school. Longterm, we will help limit the ecological damage caused by disposable pads being thrown into rivers and on the streets in rural areas where there is no municipal trash collection. This project will also create jobs and seamstress training for local women in our Sewing Project to make pads.

title: Constructing a Craft Center for 500 Women in Ghana
description: ASIGE women baskets is the innovation that uses straw  and dye to design colourful baskets for local and international markets. This project will will create sustainable employment for over 1000 women the value chain and contribute to eliminating poverty  completing. AWB,  therefore wants to build craft centre/park where we can produce quality baskets/crafts and also serve as an International tourist destination in Ghana. This project is the future of the rural women of Bolgatanga Ghana

title: Help Provide Education for 1200 Orphan in Cameroon
description: This project will provide 1200 orphans with basic education including School building construction in  Cameroon. O.A.A is working to free orphans and vulnerable children from the cycle of poverty by providing free education for orphans, street children and destitute children. Your donation will provide children with free education, nutritious food, medication, scholastic materials, uniforms, socks and shoes.

title: Give a Gift of Home to a Homeless Family in India
description: Give a homeless family in India protection and a home. weatherHYDE is a life-saving shelter designed to protect homeless families from extreme weather and to offer women and children privacy and a safe space. Beneficiaries are carefully selected by billionBricks' community partners working on the ground in homeless communities in India. Every weatherHYDE is geotagged and tracked, so that we can share detailed information on the impact your donation will make on https://weatherhyde.org/impact/

title: Engaging Communities to Conserve Giant Manta Rays
description: We aim to empower coastal communities in marine and manta ray conservation.
