Through this initiative, we not only help improve schooling conditions in the country, but also positively impact the environment.

title: Empower 100 At-Risk Students against Child Abuse
description: PEaCE will train 100 students from 10 different at-risk schools to be change makers with the knowledge of how to protect themselves and their peers from sexual abuse and exploitation. They will each go through one 2-day workshop and one 1-day workshop as an essential part of this training. After completing the training, these students will each train a further 20 students from their schools within a year, spreading the message.

title: Dental Mission for Tibetan Nomads of Yushu
description: The nomads of Yushu Prefecture in Qinghai Province have very little access to healthcare, and they live hundreds of miles away from proper dental care. A group of dentists from Temple Dental School are donating their time and skills to give these people their beautiful smiles back! Please help us in supporting these communities, which the Pureland Project has been working with for over 13 years, by helping us bring these talented dentists to those in need!

title: Support 673 Nigerian girls to end silence on SRHR
description: This project will provide mobile health service that bridges the educational divide in Nigeria on Sexual Reproductive Health topics.Using a combination of monthly education series via SMS & informed peer education via health-in-a-bag tool kit,673 adolescent girls from 6 rural schools will be educated & empowered to create a supportive environment for open discussions;increase access to health information for out-of-school girls in their locality & referral for Sexual Reproductive Health services

title: Build Child Friendly School in Indonesian Village
description: This project will fund the renovation of a child-friendly school in Central Java, Indonesia. Your donation will help provide two furnished classrooms, a teacher room, a children's playground, two toilets, one pantry, a clean water supply system, and Green facilities: rainwater harvesting, vertical garden, water absorption holes, trash management, and school recycling center. The whole facility will have a sustainable impact for 30 years (or more) worth of school year (50 children per year).

title: Donation of Educational Material for 131 Students
description: This project is set up in order to provide educational material for 131 poor students between the age of 5 and 12, who are lacking access to adequate school material in O Roong and O Ta Kok Primary Schools. The schools are located in a rural area of Svay Leu District, Siem Reap Province, Cambodia. We help them to improve and develop their skills by providing educational necessities. This project will give the students a good opportunity for their own and their community's future.

title: Sponsor An Orphan Education-Make A Better Future
description: This micro-project will change the life of an orphan girl by providing her education in one of the best educational institutions in Mirpurkhas, Sindh, Pakistan. Sponsored orphan girl will get school books, shoe, bag and dress. Orphans are a vulnerable segment of our society and according to UNICEF report, Pakistan is home to 4.2 million orphaned children who are unattended and abandoned children, waiting for provision of facilities to them including housing, education, shelter and healthcare.

title: Sustainable E-Classroom Education of Autism Baby
description: E-classroom is a format of education on constructivist teaching and project-based learning. This project needed a digital tool that encouraged autistic students to learn faster and easier, removing traditional learning barrier for special needs education. The greatest benefit is that it is tactile. It is such a visual method.In general, this type of student has coordination problems and the simple action of using their fingers or a tennis ball to trace shapes or to write helps them enormously.

title: Give HOPE & SUPPORT to 100 children with cancer
description: Every child diagnosed with cancer deserves HOPE for a brighter future.  Our mission is to raise awareness of the early warning signs of childhood cancer & funds for kids with cancer who are in need of medical & financial assistance.  Just having your child sick for a day is hard. Imagine sitting at your child's hospital bedside & not being able to pay for the treatment or procedure they desperately need to save their life or even ease their pain. For many South Africans this is their reality.

title: Health Care for 10,000 Nicaraguan Campesinos
description: Our project has trained 14 local health care providers called brigadistas to provide basic health care to campesino families in 11 remote mountain villages. Brigadistas administer first aid and medications from mini-pharmacies called botiquines. Each month, our Nicaraguan doctor visits each village for consultations. Our nurse refills the botiquines and meets with the brigadistas. Each brigadista sees 50-80 patients per month, in 11 villages: in 2019, we had over 13,000 patient visits.

title: Summer Camps for Youth Empowerment in Kosovo
description: Support young Kosovars from underprivileged backgrounds to realize their full potential with a SCHOLARSHIP to a summer camp. The benefits of the summer camp experience stretch well beyond the camp week by providing youth with practical, leadership and community service skills that they use throughout their lives. We are asking for your support to provide 50 Kosovar youth with scholarships to attend TOKA's summer camps in 2019.

title: Build a Disability Centre in Uganda Refugee Camp
description: The refugee crisis in East Africa is already affecting millions and still growing. But it is the most vulnerable who suffer the greatest. The creation and running of a new disability centre in Palorinya Refugee Settlement, Uganda, will mean some of the most vulnerable people will receive dignified disability care and rehabilitation.

title: Thalassemia Management of 50 Children (Karnataka)
description: Our project aims at making available affordable and reliable care locally to children suffering from thalassemia by making use of technology and management. Thereby restore normalcy of their lives while the option of permanent cure for them is realized.   We want to ensure last mile delivery at our centres so that every child who comes to the centre gets highest quality of treatment irrespective of the families financial background.

title: Re-Educate 100 Teen Mothers in South Sierra Leone
description: This project will not only help support 100 victims of teenage pregnancy who have dropped out of school to go back to school, but also sensitize 500 school going girls in five communities in Kenema and Bo districts about the dangers of teenage pregnancy. It would Provide three-year scholarships and school materials for 100 teenage pregnancy victims in Bo and Kenema districts and support 500 girls in five schools in Bo and Kenema districts to prevent them from becoming victims themselves.

title: A Life-saving Mission on the Air Ambulance
description: Unlike the average land ambulance, our helicopter is manned by a paramedic and doctor team. With a doctor onboard, we can bring the skills and expertise of a hospital to the scene of an incident. Our pilots, paramedics and doctors work together as a team, along with other emergency services, to deliver the best care for patients. Speed is imperative for survival with major trauma incidents, and we can be anywhere in the Thames Valley within 15 minutes.  SUPPORT OUR LIFE-SAVING CARE!

title: Educate, Equip and Empower 230 Girls and Women
description: The project will tackle issues of poverty, girl child education, networking and access to opportunities. This project targets girls and women of four different profiles in Kaduna in northern Nigeria. Through the project, we aim to subsidize the education of ten girls in public secondary schoosl over two years, train and mentor 120 indigent rural women (mostly widows and heads of households) and engage 100 adult females in two tertiary institutions and empower 2 female artists.

title: Provide Rehabilitation to 500 children in Haiti
description: Many children in Haiti are in need of physical rehabilitation; some are born with disabilities while others experience trauma, amputations, neurological problems, or have orthopedic needs. Tous Ensemble is a rehabilitation center in Southern Haiti working to help these children, and the only one that provides physical rehabilitation, prosthetics and orthotics, free clubfoot treatment, wheelchairs, walkers, crutches, etc. Every year 500 children receive therapy or other services at Tous Ensemble.

title: Bring America Home Now
description: The National Coalition for the Homeless is spearheading the launch of Bring America Home Now:  A Comprehensive Grassroots Campaign to End Homelessness in the U.S. Led by people who have  themselves experienced homelessness, we will focus on the passage of federal legislation aimed  at addressing the interconnected solutions to the decades-long epidemic of homelessness in the  United States.

title: Help dignify a child,build a sanitation facility
description: Kiini Sustainable Initiative plans to construct modern and use friendly toilet block units to improve sanitation in primary schools in Kenya that are attended by  children from poor backgrounds across Kenya,faced by a major sanitation crisis with average ratio of 30 pupils to 1 toilet.The sanitation project will create a confident and healthy school community.

title: Education+care+mentorship for 100 Nepali children
description: HCC's Rural Education Scholarship Program (previously Earthquake Orphan Scholarship Program) was established in 2015 following the devastating earthquake that left many children in Nepal orphaned, homeless, and at high risk for trafficking. This program aims to keep children with surviving family members and runs supplemental programs to help strengthen local networks and rebuild rural communities while providing a pathway out of poverty and into leadership for at least 100 children at any time.

title: Help 100 Poor Rural Nigerian Women Feed their Kids
description: Eka works with her husband on a small plot of land, where they farm all they can grow. According to Eka "Everyone farms similar crops and sometimes it's difficult to compete with  the other big farmers - so we sell at lower prices". Most times it is difficult to feed our 4 children and send them to school.  If I can get an additional income from rearing chickens, I can support my husband with more income, and my children get to eat eggs too. All Eka needs is $335 to start a poultry egg business.

title: Support Minnesota's BUY NATIVE Education Campaign
description: The practice of exchange and trade is deeply rooted in the history and cultural practices of indigenous communities and contributes to the diversity of a strong tribal economy.  This project will launch a Buy Native educational campaign targeted towards the eleven rural tribal and urban communities of Minnesota. Materials will include: events, marketing and outreach, community training to implement a strong Buy Native campaign, new equitable procurement policies and tools for Tribal Governments.

title: Creating a safe haven for Abuse and GBV Survivors
description: Shamwari Yemwanasikana will establish a One Stop Empowerment Center (OSEC) in Seke district as a halfway home for vulnerable girls. Our intervention strategy will cater for the emergency health examination and prevention against STIs and HIV transmission by ensuring the administration of Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) as well as provide legal aid, psycho-social support, counselling, economic empowerment activities and safe shelter to girl child survivors of abuse and GBV.

title: Transform the lives of 75 teens in New York
description: YVC plans to transform the lives of 75 teens through interactive workshops, helping them to realize their personal worth, build positive values, breakthrough barriers and move towards a bright future.  Through the safe and supportive environment of the Power of Peace workshops, teens will move beyond their history and become positive, contributing members of their schools, communities and families.

title: Fresh, Local Food for North Carolina Students
description: For many kids in North Carolina, the breakfast and lunch they get at school are the two daily meals they can count on receiving. So it's essential that these meals contain the freshest, most nutritious food possible. Supplying locally grown food to schools and encouraging kids to taste and learn about how it is grown has a dual benefit. It ensures that kids eat well now and in the future, and it provides local farmers with a large, dependable market for selling what they grow.

title: Support Montessori Communities in Puerto Rico
description: Maintaining Montessori Guides' Assistant position is vital for the strengthening of educational services and the reconstruction of the social fabric of the communities we serve. We have 194 Assistants serving around 5,500 children. They contribute to the social transformation of their community through work with children, providing an optimal environment for learning and growth of the child and youth, through their training as assistant and their integration into work force of our communities.

title: Empower 100 nonprofits in the reconstruction of PR
description: This project want to train and assist 100 nonprofit  in themes related to administration, accounting and compliance so they can keep reconstructing Puerto Rico providing services related to health, education, social services and food.

title: Sustainable livelihoods for rural Andean farmers
description: The EcoHuella Farm supports indigenous farming communities in the Andes of Peru. We welcome and train hundreds of farmers in ecological production so they can grow healthier food, earn more money, and continue to be stewards of the land. Farmers take part in workshops that help them grow food more sustainably and sell their organic products to better markets. The demand for the educational opportunities at the farm are more than we can supply.

title: Stand with displaced people in the DRC
description: Political and military conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed thousands, destroyed homes, and displaced more than 1 million people since 2016. In partnership with the United Nations Refugee Agency, ActionAid is supporting 26,450 displaced people through women-led programs addressing the most urgent needs: gender-based violence, food insecurity, health, and basic survival.

title: Send Vulnerable Filipino Children to School
description: Opportunities for schooling taken for granted elsewhere are not always available to children in remote rural areas in the Philippines. FPVI enables vulnerable high school-age children in Tunga, the smallest town in Leyte, to continue with their schooling by helping with school-related costs, plus mentoring & monitoring of their general well-being. In this pandemic time, FPVI provides them with tools for online group tutorials & activities, & projects in aid of mental & emotional wellness.

title: ASH Fighting 4 Health @ Tobacco Treaty Negotiation
description: ASH will push for stronger public health measures worldwide by participating in and influencing global negotiations of the World Health Organizations Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) a platform to advance tobacco control measures worldwide. Your support will ensure that ASH will be in attendance and reach 181 parties to push for best practices in our field, influence decisions on the standards governments should meet going forward and ensure accountability measures are in place.

title: Build a Farm settlement for 50 Farmers in Nigeria
description: This project aims to reduce hunger and poverty amongst a group of 50 farmers and their families in the rural communities of Delta State,Nigeria by providing farmland,seeds,livestock,training and equipping them with tools for sustainable agricultural practices that would help them farm their way out of poverty.

title: EMPOWERING THE POOR WITH EDUCATION AND SKILLS
description: This project aims to provide education and job training skills to those who have no education. In the morning, the participants will have the opportunity to learn to read and write in Thai language as well as develop basic numeracy skills. In the afternoon they will have the opportunity to learn skills such as cooking, furniture making/restoring, growing food, bead making and sewing. A combination of education and skills training will enable them to apply for jobs in the short and long term.

title: Hooping To Make A Difference In Our Communities
description: Since 2000, the Annual Metroball New York Ave Classic has become a renowned FREE Summer Youth Streetball League highly anticipated each summer in the Washington DC metro area.  Over 600 Youth from the surrounding neighborhoods in DC, MD, & VA through competitive basketball competition. This positive interaction has proven to reduce violence & deviant behavior among the youth living in the neighborhoods surrounding the New York Ave Playground & unite many youth of all ages in the region.

title: Educate Quarantined Children!
description: COVID-19 pandemic has severely affected the educational systems in Afghanistan, leading to a total of 11 million children out of school. The government has announced online teaching through TV and radio, but unfortunately most of the children do not have access to smart phones, Radio or TVs to watch and learn through. Teach for Afghanistan Organization (TAO) has prepared easy to understand curriculums to pass to all children at their homes, so, no child is left without learning.

title: Economic Empowerment for Women in Tanzania
description: This project will help 24 widows and vulnerable women in a village in northern Tanzania's Hanang District start small businesses raising livestock and producing grass seed.

title: Help 300 Women in WASA Settlement learn a skill.
description: This project will train and empower women in WASA IDP Settlement in Abuja, providing quality income generating activities to 300 disadvantaged women who fled from Northeast and Northcentral as a result of insurgency, also support them with start up fund.

title: HELP CHILDRENS SPECIAL NEEDS SCHOOL IN CAPE TOWN
description: With very limited resources Parow Inclusive School in Cape Town accommodates the needs of learners with special educational needs.  These learners have barriers to learning and require an extra level of support.  Parow puts the needs of the learner first and do everything possible to facilitate the learning experience in a way that addresses the child's special needs.   Some of children come from very poor backgrounds others are foster children, some from Orphanages and some refugees

title: Send Girls Victimized by Violence Back to School
description: In Kasese, years of tribal and political unrest have sent many children out of school due to high rates of poverty and cultural biases. Many girls have dropped out of school due to parents dying in violence or being arrested as a result of conflict. Others have dropped out due to teenage pregnancy that has resulted from engaging in commercial sex work in order to raise funds for school fees. Our project will provide school fees and scholastic materials to help these girls return to school.

title: Help protect 5000 children through 180 activists
description: Despite years of intervention, India has 43 lakh child labourers, 27% child marriages & 1,06,958 crimes against children reported annually. We have e a moral duty to protect the rights of children, particularly the most marginalized in society. (Census 2011; NFHS 2015-16; (NCRB 2016). Since 2003, CRT is working to ensure 'Every Right for Every Child' through its training, campaign & advocacy initiatives. We need your support to protect the rights of around 5000 children by training  180 activist

title: Irish Red Cross Services in Ireland and Overseas
description: We provide emergency services as well as a variety of community services including youth work and care for the sick and the elderly. The Irish Red Cross voluntary ambulance service is active in communities across Ireland, providing support at community events and to the Emergency Services in times of need. There are a range of programmes providing support to vulnerable community groups. Overseas,  Irish Red Cross has earned a distinctive reputation for the skill and commitment of our delegates.

title: Provide Laptops to 30 Tribal Youth of CentralIndia
description: Bharat Rural Livelihoods Foundation (BRLF) plans to provide laptops to 30 tribal youth who will undergo the third batch of Certificate Program in Rural Livelihoods (CPRL) beginning in the last week of July 2018. The six-month duration certificate program addresses  the capacity building challenge for existing and aspiring rural professionals who would potentially engage at sub-district levels in the rural development sector; be it through NGOs, Government Institutions, or, as elected reps

title: Educate a Girl Child, Empower a Nation
description: Despite India's push to guarantee education to all children (RtE Act, 2009) only 33% of girls complete Class XII (Ministry of HRD). Education is one of the key areas for girls/ women empowerment. We, at VRDS, have been promoting girls' education, to prevent child labour, child marriage and other abuses, and promote gender equality as part of our holistic effort towards community development in Haveri district of Karnataka. We seek your support to educate 100+ girl children through our project.

title: Saving Rhinos with Solar Energy
description: Kenya's Ol Pejeta Conservancy is the largest black rhino sanctuary in East Africa. Ol Pejeta has made a commitment to ONLY be using renewable energy by 2023. This task begins with the conversion of our diesel-powered boreholes to solar. Each borehole once converted to solar - we have 10 of them - will save US$7,000 per year in fuel. All our savings from going solar will be put straight back into wildlife conservation and community development.  By going solar, we save rhinos!

title: Youth Services Matter
description: Youth services are fundamental to enriching the lives of young people in the borough of Hammersmith & Fulham. From supporting with employment, mental health, education and prevention of crime. This appeal will enable us to provide much needed support to the youth sector in order to keep it thriving. We are aiming to raise an additional 10,000 for our grants pot, in order to  distribute these funds to the youth organisations which enable the development of young people into powerful adults.

title: #strongerforlonger - Muscular Dystrophy therapies
description: Most people with muscular dystrophy (MD) cannot access regular therapy for their condition. Yet effective therapies exist, like physiotherapy and osteopathy, which could keep them stronger for longer and significantly improve their lives.   Building on the success of our UK centre, we will create a toolkit that shares our model freely across the MD community, to spark action and empower others to launch their own clinics. The first tool in the toolkit will be a film demonstrating our programme.

title: Give more medical options globally across species
description: The Humanimal Trust drives collaboration between vets, doctors and researchers so that all humans and animals benefit from sustainable, medical progress but not at one another's expense. This is One Medicine.   This project will raise understanding on a global scale of the huge positive impact equitable access to medical advances using a One Medicine approach could bring amongst professionals, the professionals of the future, and the general public, plus provide opportunities for collaboration.

title: Empower Syrian Girls to Dream Big
description: In Syria today, over 1.75 million children are out of school, and many schools have destroyed. Girls are disproportionally affected. NuDay is countering this with our Future Generation Initiative (FGI), which prioritizes education and livelihood trainings for young women. Through your support, the initiative ensures that girls are able to build their futures - as they want it! Support Girl (Em)Power(Ment)!

title: Create music for looked-after children in Scotland
description: Track will use song-writing and music-making to build trust, confidence, belief and skills for learning and life with care experienced and looked after young people in Scotland.  Using their innate creativity we will support children from chaotic backgrounds to unlock, celebrate and amplify their potential.

title: Literacy for 500 rural children in Mindanao
description: This project aims to provide quality instructional materials, language, and literacy teachers and build a conducive place for 500 rural children learners or indigenous peoples' children, teach reading and writing to these children in order to strengthen their functional literacy making them more confident in proceeding to higher levels of learning.

title: Sponsor to Educate & Empower Children in Zambia
description: It is estimated that over a million children are out of school in Zambia. Many parent/guardians  fail to take their children to school. We enroll these children from poor  communities and provide them with both primary and junior secondary education. 450 students are currently enrolled with Destiny Community Schools in Matero.  It is our goal for the orphaned and vulnerable children  to be given an education which will empower them to break out of the cycle of poverty.

title: Safeguarding: Protect 1,000s of Children in Africa
description: Our Safeguarding & Protection Programme trains leaders and teachers in community projects and schools within our 40 partner organisations across East, West & Southern Africa. This training and monitoring will benefit 92,000+ Children & Vulnerable Persons by 2020. Changing the dynamic in society, it protects, empowers and strengthens their rights within their families, schools, communities and the law through our Advocacy, Positive Discipline Programmes and Childrens' Rights Clubs.

title: Liberate Devadasi families from exploitation
description: The Karnataka State Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act, 1982 outlawed the Devadasi system. But the state reports 46,660 devadasis (Women and Child Welfare Department, National Commission for Women); realistic estimate suggests the number to be 100,000 (International Labour Organisation, 2015). Sakhi Trust works to rescue and rehabilitate those women and girls forced into the Devadasi system. We seek your support to help them and their families to live a decent and dignified life.

title: The Reusable Sanitary Towel Manufacturing Project
description: This project will produce washable sanitary towels mainly for rural school girls and provide employment for 3 to 10 women.

title: Educational Support to 20 Needy Children
description: PNCC, an organization for migrants workers, under this project aims to provide scholarship support to 20 helpless children of deceased and missing migrant workers from across the nation enabling them to attend good private schools that offer quality education. The support will cover the cost of their tuition fee, books, stationery, school uniform and day meal. With the help of this support, they will be able to acquire quality education which in long run can change the context of their life.

title: Rebuilding Palestinian Livelihoods in Yarmouk Camp
description: Despite being the 'Capital of Diaspora' the political, economic and cultural weight of the Syrian crisis has significantly weakened Yarmouk camp and its people. The suffering has been widespread due to military action, displacement, besiegement, domination, detention, destruction and death of Palestinians in Syria. Jafra aims to provide these people essentials -  food, safe water, shelter - a means to pave their way to return to Yarmouk.

title: Creating a world without childhood cancer!
description: The Gold Hope Project is on a mission to end childhood cancer. This project will fund innovative research grants for a devastating brain tumor that affects children called Diffused Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG). DIPG has no cure and has had no new treatment options for the last 40 years. Children diagnosed with this cancer are given 9-12 months to live. With your help, we can change those grim statistics.

title: Give prevention tool to 10,000 indigenous children
description: We created this proyect because we need to translate to 3 indigenous languages: mixteco, zapoteco and amuzgo, the"Filipons T-Shirt" tale. Filipon helps children to be aware of the importance of learning how to take care of their bodies and to seek for help when they need it. Throughout the story, they will understand that there are some people's actions that "stain" the brightness of their hearts and hurts their "self-esteem," but it also teaches them how to identify their protective adult.

title: Provide vehicle for abused girls home in Argentina
description: Hogar San Jose Home provides shelter, food, emotional support, education and love to more than 100 girls that go through our Home during the year. A judge has taken them away from their home because they were sexually abused by someone in their own family.  We urgently need a van or minibus to be able to transport them to their different after school activities, doctors appointments, meetings with the judge, etc. Today we rely on volunteers and public transportation which makes things difficult.

title: Help build dormitory for 60 rural nursery pupils.
description: When we work together we do great things. Uganda needs strong children, educated children, successful children to grow to become the next generation business owners, artists, doctors, and community and national leaders.  We, you and the Memorial School - build our country one student at a time. Our project is to help build a 30 bed dormitory that will be accommodating 60 rural kindergarten pupils each school period.

title: Economic empowerment of 50 women in Soma,Turkey
description: After a devastating mining disaster in coal mining town of Soma, Manisa, Turkey 301 miners were killed and nearly 3000 miners became unemployed. Their female relatives suddenly found themselves as the sole breadwinners in their families. Anatolian Artisans has organized the women to start a cooperative where they can make products using their traditional skills. They need funding to include more women expanding their workshop.

title: Entrepreneurial Workshops for Nicaraguan Students
description: Vayando is an Atlanta based social enterprise operating in East Africa and Central America. Our platform markets motivated entrepreneurs as a way for travelers to book directly with local people to learn about their livelihoods. Social impact is central to our model. In Nicaragua, we are piloting an entrepreneurial development program for local youth, where classrooms of rural and urban high school students are taught small business development skills by successful Nicaraguan entrepreneurs.

title: Sreyassu
description: Sreyassu is a community-based organization located in Chillakallu, Jagayyapeta Mandal in Krishna District of Andhra Pradesh State. It was started in 2006 as a Project to support the people living with and affected by HIV/AIDS. Slowly, the registered members in the Project were educated and empowered in a way that they grouped together and formed as a community based Organization. The aim of the project is to help 100 HIV affected children with foster care, education, and nutrition.

title: Reading Centre in Congo (DRC)
description: This project will build a reading center in eastern Congo to teach basic reading and writing skills to children, mostly orphans who have been left behind after 15 years of civil war that killed over 5 million people.  3.5 million children in Congo are not attending elementary school.  IWOF will build a reading center on land owned by Grace Orphanage. Many widows in the area cannot read, and classes will be offered to these women who care for children, some not even their own.

title: Education before work
description: In Ednica we keep working to provide better conditions for children in vulnerable situations. We have three community centers in where we provide to the children educational, medical and psychological support in order to help them to build a project to live better and know their rights.  The last past year and half all the education change and our children are having online classes, we really need you support for cover the expenses of the internet service.

title: Improving life of 200 youth living with HIV.
description: A three day Conference of young people living with HIV is important in order to have a forum to discuss Positive prevention, adherence and how to maximize treatment outcome. The conference will also address causes of treatment failures and drug resistance related to poor drug adherence.  The conference will also address issues of livelihoods among the young people living with HIV

title: Training Service Dogs for Veterans!
description: Operation Freedom Paws empowers veterans & individuals with disabilities to restore their freedom to live life.  Being able to purchase training equipment helps our service dog teams build their confidence not only in training but also in life. On days that may be difficult for our teams, accomplishing training tasks can be a big win. This equipment helps train both members of the service dog team for unique circumstances in a safe place, giving encouragement to go out in their community.

title: Invest in rural residents building their future
description: Rural central Wisconsin was hit hard by the economic upheaval felt by many midwestern communities. In unprecedented fashion, residents united to rebuild their lives, livelihoods and their community. Together, 2,000 residents designed the Tribune, a social enterprise unique in both its development process and resulting purpose, as a resident-led, community-owned source of good jobs and great lives. Support for the Tribune's renovation will launch this powerful symbol of renewal in rural America.

title: Send destitute kids to school and save chimpanzees
description: We are providing scholarship for 30 destitute kids from remote villages into secondary school. Our beneficiaries include orphans, school drop outs and kids from the poorest households for whom this is the only chance. Your support will help pay for accommodation, fees, food and school needs thereby providing these kids especially girls with a life changing opportunity, increasing literacy, relieving the poor of educational cost and taking off hunting pressure on our endangered wildlife heritage.

title: Chamany, health care for 20 children in the street
description: "Chamany" was given birth in the streets and she's been living there since then. She has lack of identity documents, does not go to a school, receives little or zero attention towards her health, does not live in a safe place and has no access to psychological or psychiatric treatment. She requires specialized care, neural stimulation and psychological treatment for strengthening her brain maturation, improve her mental health so that she can count with better tools for accessing a school.

title: Knot Undone (An Anthology of Mental Illness)
description: Mentally Aware Nigeria Initiative is proud to bring you Knot Undone: An Anthology of Mental Illness in Nigeria. Featuring seventeen stories that portray what it's like to live with a mental illness in Nigeria from the eyes of those that have lived out this grueling reality. In a country where mental health stigma is a culture, where do people that cope with these illnesses hide? In Shame or in denial? And right in front of our very eyes?  This will be the first collection out of the series.

title: Christmas in July
description: Give the gift of Christmas this July by sending a care package to a family in need. The unexpected joy you will give these children can only be captured in their own words. Thus, we will include a return postcard with each package so that they can communicate with you.     Total costs to deliver a package is $15 and will provide about $120 worth of food. An unexpected gift by Santa will bring a smile to any child.

title: Secure LongTerm Care for the Healthy but Unwanted
description: In a perfect world, Animals will have the same rights and live past their prime in peace with the care they need to continue to live a life of quality.  Unfortunately, that isn't the case in this world.  We are a sanctuary which is different from a rescue.  For 15 years, We have been providing a safe and loving forever home to every animal that we rescue and we do not discriminate against age or illness.

title: Train 100 young Kenyan entrepreneurs
description: The latest United Nations Human Development report revealed that youth unemployment in Kenya had risen to 22.2 per cent, significantly higher than neighbors Tanzania, Uganda and Ethiopia. Lack of opportunities creates vulnerable youth, and has a destabilizing effect. This project will train 100 youth in socially responsible business practices and leadership skills. A pitch contest will follow, with 10 selected to receive access to seed capital, leadership training, and mentorship.

title: IGNITE Lecture Series 2018 (GESL)
description: GESL is a feminist-based org in Sierra Leone that nurtures & enhances the leadership skills of young girls to become effective advocates & social change agents in their communities. Our IGNITE lecture series is a blended-format series focusing on Violence Against Women & Girls. Through local events, podcasts, videos, and print, we aim to enhance the advocacy & activism skills of our participants.

title: Build a Childhood Development Centre for 400 Kids
description: IREAD plans to build a pre-school with a resource center to provide needed high quality early childhood education (ECE) to 400 children aged 3 to 6 years in the village of Marracha, NW Uganda.  Research has shown that well-conceived ECE programs are the most effective way to break the cycle of poverty and lay the foundation for lifelong success in school, career and life.

title: Capacity building training to health workers
description: We will deliver the capacity building training package on Mental health and Psychosocial programme to the mid level health workers (Health Assistant and Community Medical Assistants) of seven village development committees of Makawanpur district. BNMT Nepal will follow the 9 days training module of MHgap which is approved by National Health Training Center (NHTC), Nepal government. The training will be facilitated by the psychiatrist and psychologist.

title: Help 100 Mexican Children Stay in Secondary School
description: In response to the violence and drug war in our country, HECAT was opened in the Northern Mexican city of Torreon seeking to provide better chances to children from low-income families through high quality education.  With your help, this project will expand our middle school program by building three new rooms on our roof to continue to provide education, nutritional and medical support for children who hail from some of the poorest areas of our region.

title: Set 2,500 young people on a path to career success
description: Opportunities Ahead, our annual careers fair, will inspire teenagers about the diverse range of careers available in our region, opening their eyes to opportunities and motivating them to aim high. Meeting professionals from 50 leading businesses will enable them to learn about different career pathways and what skills they'll need to succeed in their futures. Schools struggle with the cost of transport to bring students to the event, so we need to raise funds to support them.

title: Give 1600 people access to water in rural Vietnam
description: Clean water is a basic need but 97% of the poorest households in rural Vietnam have no access to piped water. This project will connect 400 rural households (1600 people) in Chau Thanh district of Ben Tre, Vietnam to safe water. Thrive's unique approach incentivizes the private water sector to establish water connections in rural areas while involving government and communities in the process to ensure sustainable, efficient water supply delivery that continues even after Thrive's involvement.

title: Educate & motivate Girls in Rural Schools
description: Smart Ladies Society is an organization that helps high school age girls in Lesotho rural schools become the best versions of themselves. We provide a support system that imparts life skills, instils hope, and empowers girls in vulnerable environments.   This project will pay for a year's school fees for our neediest, and also provide access to life skills programs to over 100 girls. Our programs are design to expose the girls to positive experiences they would not otherwise have access to.

title: Help renovate a Community Health Centre
description: This project will renovate a Comunity Health and Development Centre of Solidarity Community Care Organization at Etope laShilongo village in Omulonga Constituency, Ohangwena Region of Namibia. The Centre houses and kindergarten for 30 children and is the second headquarters of the organization catering for the northcentral regions of the country where the organisation implements its community-based care and development services. It needs urgent renovation since it was built in 2009.

title: Help build a facility for slaughter bound horses
description: Voice For Horses Rescue Network has helped over 500 horses since 1999, the cost of caring for horses who have been abused, neglected, abandoned, injuries, sick or who have been thrown away because they can't race any longer as well as owners who can no longer financially care for them is overwhelming.   The cost of feed which depending on the horse is around $15 per day and with 10-12 horses to feed it runs $5000+ a month,  Horses are in need every day, and we cannot help without you

title: Ensuring people are the heroes of their own story
description: Aid, philanthropy, non-profits and government, often, make decisions for people, rather than with them. At Feedback Labs, we believe people are the best experts in their lives and should drive the policies and programs that affect them.   Feedback+ events invite feedback proponents from across the world to share their strategies for putting people and communities at the forefront of decision-making. This project seeks to sponsor attendance for more of these change-makers to our Summits.

title: Train 30 Neurosurgeons in Uganda by 2030
description: This project seeks to train 30 neurosurgeons in Uganda by the year 2030, and provide financial relief for financially disadvantaged patients in need of neurosurgery. The donations will cover the living expenses, training materials, equipment and test fees for Ugandan neurosurgery residents as they go about their neurosurgery training and rotations.

title: Psychosocial support for 300 Cambodian children
description: The sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism continues to be a major issue in Cambodia and there are not adequate psychosocial services for child victims. We will provide immediate psychosocial assistance and care at the crisis intervention stage after a child has been rescued from a situation of sexual exploitation.

title: Promote Safe Delivery for 250 Mothers in Gulu
description: Promoting safe delivery; is a project that supports access to proper healthcare services for expectant mothers and their new born babies in Aswa County, Gulu District, Uganda.   This project therefore conduct community health promotion through the use of the village health teams and aiding mother access facility delivery through providing voucher to every expectant mother for motorcycle transport to the nearest facility during labour or any health complications.

title: Give Hope to Kenyan Orphans Through Peer Mentors
description: The Mentorship Program is aimed at empowering and giving hope to orphaned and vulnerable children by giving them a trusted peer mentor and friend.  A relationship with a non-parental adult influences positively the child's perception of their own strengths and abilities, enhancing self-esteem and giving them a different perspective to life's challenges. Under the Program, a support network of volunteers will dedicate their time to spending it with the kids and carrying out various activities.

title: Support Mounted Rangers Fighting Rhino Poaching
description: Mounted rangers constantly put their lives on the line while protecting our rhino populations from well-equipped and organised poachers. A staggering increase in poaching has devastated the South African rhino population, with almost 9,000 rhinos killed for their horns in the last decade. KZN's mounted rangers and loyal horses are part of the last stand in this war.

title: Gift Life to 1000 water starved families in India
description: Erratic rainfall, long dry spell, severe water-crisis has made life full of distress and despair for 1000 poor families in Kalahandi. Hunger, malnutrition, crop failure is forcing people to migrate. The project will help to revive defunct traditional water harvesting structures & build new ones ensuring year round availability of water for drinking, household use, irrigation. It will lead to good health, more income, good yield to farmers, ground water recharge & hope for a good LIFE for kids.

title: Using AI to Protect Community-Driven Development
description: Large-scale commercial development projects disproportionately affect people with limited political and economic power.  A number of humanitarian organizations are hard at work trying to ensure these affected communities have access to information early enough to mobilize and influence the legislative decision-making process, but much of the work remains extremely manual, which slows the process.

title: Where is YOUR Happy Place
description: We wish to create a virtual digital platform that will link 45 million adult American immigrants as well as their 36 million offspring, in a path breaking digital website and app.

title: Nutrition Champions
description: The project Nutrition Champions works on essential nutrition actions to end malnutrition in urban slums of India because malnutrition is a major contributor of mortality and morbidity among young children. In 2016-17, Matri Sudha created 11 Nutrition Champions and aims to create 50 Nutrition Champions in 2018 from among women, men, health and nutrition workers who champions the cause of malnutrition free community. Matri Sudha aims to create 10000 Nutrition Champions by 2030.

title: Project Voice: Advocacy Training for Refugee Youth
description: Project Voice capitalizes on the skills of young refugees in an effort to promote effective advocacy, engage and develop skills of marginalized youth, and reduce vulnerability to extremist narratives. We support and train refugee youth to conduct research, produce policy recommendations, and disseminate their findings on community issues, empowering them to direct their own advocacy agenda.

title: Dig a Well, Plant Trees, Buy a TukTuk
description: Help dig a fresh water well & build a water storage tank for a small sustainable palm oil mill cooperative to support 300 widows & single mothers in Nigeria.  Your donation also goes to plant 1500 palm trees on family farms, so that the environment is preserved. Then your donation will help widows buy 2 Tuk Tuks, which will help them transport their seeds to the mill, & pressed oil to the market, maximizing their profits. Water well, a tank, 1500 trees, & 300 lives changed

title: Avoid maternal and neonatal death in the Dominican
description: The National Institute of Health works on the prevention of maternal and neonatal mortality, through prevention programs, training, advocacy and promotion of public policies through a network of organizations at the national level. The objective of the project is to train women on the right to receive information and timely and quality health services.

title: Rwanda : Nyumba School Rehabilitation Project
description: The ACAPE  TRUST (Cecile AHOZEREYE Association for Childhood and Education) was set up to initiate, develop, and encourage all projects and accompanying activities which favor children, and especially the education of children, adolescents, and young adults. ACAPE is focusing its main efforts towards the rehabilitation of damaged and dilapidated school facilities, and the first one is the School of Nyumba.

title: Education Kits for 21,000 children in Pakistan
description: We run community-based SABAQ Centres for highly marginalized and remote communities in Pakistan where children learn only through digital lessons using the SABAQ Tab. However, technology alone can not facilitate the skills development in the children. SABAQ will provide education kits to 21,000 students in 500 Centres in Sindh. Each kit will have English and Urdu readers, practice workbooks and other classroom resources for a holistic classroom experience in a non-formal education set-up.

title: Help Refugee Youth in Uganda Find A Future
description: Uganda hosts more refugees than any other country in Africa, fleeing from conflict and famine. In the capital, Kampala, MindLeaps offers urban refugee youth energizing, fun dance classes in a safe space. MindLeaps' program develops cognitive and life skills, which help youth gain knowledge, confidence and hope. Through participation at MindLeaps, these youth show an increase in responsible and healthy life choices, greater school success, and deeper integration into the community and workforce.

title: Community & Economic Development with Youth Rugby
description: Summary Rugby Idaho looks to provide safe and affordable programs to all kids (1st-12th) in Idaho throughout the year. We look to sustain legitimate programs that teach core life skills that pertain to developing leaders within the community. Our major focus is developing partnerships with local Parks and Recreational. This year we are hosting a very important regional tournament where kids have the opportunity to speak to college scouts and youth Olympic selectors.

title: Reaching adolescent girls in humanitarian settings
description: Our goal is to strengthen adolescent girls' access to comprehensive quality sexual and reproductive health (SRH) information and services in emergencies. WRC will review existing tools, approaches, and projects pertaining to adolescent SRH, and will engage with adolescent girls to understand their needs and priorities. This research will enable us to formulate evidence-based program approaches and recommendations for policy-makers and humanitarian practitioners.

title: Unlock the world: STEM Brasil
description: STEM Brasil is different. It inspires, engages and support public school science and math teachers through training sessions of 21st Century Skills, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Math subject areas. Over 4,500 trained teachers impacted more than 570,000 students, with world-wide quality STEM classes. The teacher plays a facilitator role and proposes project-based learning exercises, where students collaborate on projects and work together to solve problems connected to Real-World-Challenges.

title: The Island Spirit Fund
description: The Island Spirit Fund is dedicated to awakening the Island Spirit across the U.S., USVI, and where our partners live and work to ensure no one weathers a storm alone. It pursues this vision through relief efforts, helping rebuild and renew communities impacted by hurricanes. Grants are focused on awakening the Island Spirit on St. Croix in the aftermath of Hurricane Maria, and in other areas where our partners live and work, building resilience for future storms.

title: DONATE A CUP OF PORRIDGE MEAL FOR A NEEDY CHILD
description: There are over 1,600 children at Kako, Kiyumba and Ssunga Primary Schools in Uganda who miss out on anything to eat at lunchtime, and many will have had no breakfast, and find it difficult to concentrate and gain an education. Malnutrition affects their health, development and ability to learn. Youth With A Vision seek to provide food for a lunchtime meal-a cup of high protein maize flour and sugar and also work with the schools to establish gardens to sustain the lunch meals for needy children

title: Sustainable holistic education for 30 at-risk kids
description: The programs & services provided by Kids in Need of Direction provide opportunities for advancement to children  from the most disadvantaged areas of Trinidad & Tobago. This project will allow 30 at-risk children to participate for one year in our educational programs.   Our programs address the physical, mental and emotional needs of children, and include literacy & remedial education, martial arts, exploratory learning and social education. We provide children with all essential materials need

title: Recovery support to flood victims in Somalia
description: Heavy rains and flooding have continued to compound an already fragile humanitarian situation in the southern and central parts of Somalia, worsening conditions for communities who recently endured a long period of drought (OCHA 25/05/2018). The floods have resulted in the destruction of homes, critical infrastructure, latrines, and the loss of livestock and crops. There is need for shelter and Non Food Items (NFIs), as well as WASH assistance.

title: Uniforms, Tablets & English Classes for 20
description: With rapidly changing technological advances, youth growing up in the Dominican Republic need additional educational and vocational training to compete in the global workplace. InnerStar provides programs that encourage young people to embrace innovation, overcome challenges & inspire others around the world. InnerStar promotes cross-cultural learning experiences that cultivate creativity, leadership & technical skills. With the proper tools, students will be able to embrace their "InnerStar".

title: Digitally Empower the Unconnected in Afghanistan
description: NetFreedom Pioneers (NFP) has created satellite tv filecasting, a way to distribute offline digital content (including current events, educational tutorials, minority community resources, health information, and other media) to the public for free, thus expanding the right to access information. NFP will implement and localize this system in Afghanistan where the common individual is disadvantaged because of lack of infrastructure, remote geography, and high cost of the Internet.

title: Theater as an LGBTI empowerment tool
description: We propose to explore the potential of the dramatic arts that allow the LGBTI population of the center of Bogota and belonging to the project, to potentiate social skills that allow to improve the confidence, the self-knowledge, the self-esteem and the transfer of corporal techniques to our daily life to mention only some . It seeks to sensitize, to promote the culture of respect and acceptance of the population with sexual orientations and diverse gender identities

title: Makerspace  - Learning through Innovation
description: Mantra4Change aims to build Makerspaces at schools as a place where students can gather to discover, explore, tinker and create using a variety of tools and materials. This would be a space that encourages students to design, experiment, build and engage in various fields like art, science, technology, music, food, environment and more. It is a rich learning environment which enhances a student's critical thinking, scientific temperament and curiosity on how and why things are made.

title: HELP ME SHINE: Transforming disability to ability
description: People with disabilities have AMAZING abilities.  In fact, all human beings should have the opportunity to SHINE and find their purpose in life, regardless of their metal or physic limitations.  With your support,  people with disabilities will foster and showcase their talents to the world.  This project will give meaning to life to 80 individuals with intellectual disability in Puerto Rico by developing entrepreneurial skills, artistic skills and sports skills.

title: Educate young girls to prevent sex trafficking!
description: This project will build a 55-bed dormitory for a Secondary School in the remote access Nepali Himalayas, providing equal access to education and accommodation for girls who live over a 3-hour trek from the school and are at-risk for child sex trafficking.  A dormitory has been identified by communities in this District as a very clear way to ensure girls can attend school and supports the Nepal Government National Plan to eliminate child trafficking, outlined by the United Nations IOM division

title: Water well 1300 people in Chargel village - Gambia
description: To provide safe drinking water for a highly populated rural community in Central River Region of The Gambia. 1300 people shall benefit from this project

title: HELP 3000 HOMES  COOK SAFELY WITH MIRACLE STOVE
description: This project will provide Miracle Rocket cook stoves to 3000 poor rural households in Nyeri  County of Central Kenya where over 80% of the population use traditional three stone fireplace for cooking which expose them to indoor house pollution, spend a lot of time gathering wood and exerts pressure on local forests leading to forest degradation. Stove will reduce wood consumption, saving lives and environment and is Cheaper to Produce locally.

title: She-Advance: Girls Mentorship Center
description: She-Advance program will improve girls effective participation in decision making and leadership at school, household and community through a blended approach comprised of holiday centers where 100 girls are engaged in off school scheduled girl mentorships with motivational speeches and dialogue; Girls are encouraged to volunteer at community events and learn about the importance of giving back to the community.

title: Bal Chetna - rehab of differently abled children
description: Bal Chetna is a program for the rehabilitation of mentally challenged children. Established in 2002 as a residential and day care facility in response to a growing number of mentally challenged children being abandoned at our children's home PALNA. The day care program started when our creche workers found many children with mental and multiple disabilities living in slums and resettlement colonies. Today we have 150 challenged children in our 3 day care centres and one residential facility.

title: Creativity StARTS Here
description: Creativity StARTS Here means that ARTS and CULTURE is the origin of all innovations.Creativity StARTS Here is a project that focuses on establishment of a Cyber Cafe that will be managed by the Mathare Foundation. Computer Aid, our partner has offered us 5 computer and a laptop with only one condition we need to have 5 sockets (for power connection) and 5 desks where will place the computers. The sockets will cost us $ 80 The desks will cost us $ 500. We are therefore requesting for $ 580.

title: Baboons need us - Help us get to them
description: Baboon Matters is working across South Africa to conserve baboons through our education, job creation and advocacy work.   In 2017 we drove 15 000km across South Africa to work in rural areas, helping subsistence farmers and communities learn how to manage their properties to reduce losses and conflict with their wildlife neighbours.  We travel widely to help injured or trapped baboons and get orphaned baboons to places of safety.  We urgently need a strong reliable vehicle to continue our work.

title: Powering youth energy changemakers in Kenyan slums
description: LivelyHoods works with disadvantaged youth and women in Kenyan slums to provide them with training, skills and support to transform them into clean energy ambassadors in their community, earning a safe, sustainable income. We will provide 70 youth and women with a unique opportunity to work their way out of poverty and become changemakers in their community by bringing affordable, life-changing clean energy to low-income households in their slum communities.

title: Learning to Give Bulgaria
description: This project works to develop the giving environment and culture in Bulgaria by promoting and teaching giving among students in Bulgarian schools, through developing and introducing a model for civic education.

title: Syria: Aiding Kurds and other vulnerable refugees
description: The crisis in Syria forced hundreds of thousands of Syrian families to flee, many to neighboring Iraq.  Peace Winds has been assisting families providing shelter, infrastructure, schooling, and livelihoods in northern Iraq/Kurdistan for more than 20 years.    The "present Turkey/Syria border crisis" has greatly increased the flow of Kurdish and other refugees.  The anticipated 250,000 refugees will need shelter, food, water.  Peace Winds is responding.

title: Building Project for Volunteers in Pretoria
description: South Africa Volunteer Work Camp Association plans to build a volunteer house to provide accommodation & classrooms for free services to community of Soshanguve, Pretoria. We support with free afternoon after school lessons for children from primary to secondary school especially orphans, less disadvantages children in the community. Help make this project a reality with any help even purchase of bricks, sand, roof material, fence or anything possible.

title: Inspire Rohingya Refugees through Art
description: Artolution started working with refugees impacted by the Rohingya Refugee Crisis at the end of 2017. Lead artists and Artolution Co-Directors, Max and Joel, have traveled to the Balukhali refugee camps in Bangladesh, the largest camps in the world, among other camps, to create community art projects with refugees, as well as to bring joy and hope to the lives of children. Artolution was the first organization to bring community-based arts programming to the Balukhali camps.

title: Comprehensive Project of Agro-Industrial Forestry
description: Promote the establishment of integral agro-industrial forestry development systems, as a sustainable activity in 100 Has., In the period of 2018, 2019 and 2020, with the participation of the organized population and organizations related to the activities of the project.  * Constitute an ecologically stable and economically sustainable development model for the region, in accordance with harmonious development policies of the Loreto region.  * Promote agro-export crops.

title: Seeding Hope of Education in Haiti
description: The Seeding Hope Program is a cooperative initiative initiated by local community members in Haiti. Its purpose is to increase school attendance among struggling children and families. The impact of this program goes beyond just tuition fees. It reflects our philosophy of partnership with other organizations, and our vision for sustainability. While supporting the education of those kids, we are empowering local leaders to serve and promote change in their communities with the leadership develop

title: Semi-Permanent Roofing and Apprenticeship Program
description: ConPRmetidos, along with Heart 9/11 and the University of the Sacred Heart, have agreed to partner in a project to repair or replace damaged roofs in the communities of Playita and Cantera Peninsula in Puerto Rico using volunteers provided by HEART 9/11 and apprentices recruited by Sacred Heart. The Program contains three components: (1) damage assessment and inventory; (2) recruitment, training, and management of fifteen apprentices; and (3) installation of fifty semi-permanent roofs.

title: Tibetan refugees in exile in Tezu, India
description: The Tezu-Dhargyeling Tibetan refugee camp in the isolated region of Tezu, India has requested a noodle-making machine to start a business, in addition to a generator and power inverter for their middle school and day care center. A noodle business, which was very successful in a neighboring camp we support, will provide economic opportunity and food for the entire community. The urgently needed generator and inverter will keep young Tezu students in school during power outages.

title: A Call to Action and Leadership for Myanmar Youth
description: DEPDC plans to train 100 Myanmar youth on leadership skills, survival techniques, non-profit structure, and safe migration, so that these future leaders can return to their hometowns and initiate their own projects. The goal is to begin a larger grassroots movement that can reach more people and can inspire young, creative leaders to combat the most concerning problems in their own areas, especially with the recent rise in undocumented migration, which has led to an increased trafficking risk.

title: Give books for the kids of conflict-torn Marawi
description: PBSP plans to give 3 storybooks each to 12,000 Maranao children who are victims of the five month-long Battle of Marawi in southern Philippines between the government and ISIS-inspired terrorists.

title: Goat for livelihood support for poor women
description: This project will provide goats of local good breed to 25 poor marginalized women especially the widows of rural areas of Kishanganj for improving their livelihood choices so that they increase their living standard. This gives them the ability to begin raising a small herd of goats to provide them with source of income. Goats can be a source of ready cash for the women during emergencies.

title: Urgent relief for victims of Guatemalan volcano
description: This project will directly fund the urgent needs of children and families devastated by the Fuego volcano eruption. This historic disaster has left at least 69 dead, dozens missing, and nearly 300 people injured. GFC's local partner ASOGEN opened a shelter and is providing emergency supplies like food, clothing, toiletries, and emotional support to children and families experiencing unimaginable trauma, and their numbers are increasing. They need our help now.

title: Student Sponsorship: Help Malawi Students Thrive
description: At EKARI, we believe in the singular power of education to break the cycle of extreme poverty. In support of this mission, we provide direct tuition support - in addition to a range of comprehensive support programs - so students can excel throughout their high school and college educations.

title: Empowering Our Immigrant and Refugee Neighbors
description: The Village Exchange Center (VEC) is a community center and multi-faith space established to support and empower the immigrants, refugees, and other community members of northwest Aurora as they navigate the challenges of a new country and culture.  VEC's mission is to celebrate religious and cultural diversity with the overarching goal of empowering newly arrived and hosting communities by creating opportunities for social, cultural and economic exchange.

title: Living Prevention TV Presented by AlternaCare
description: Welcome to Living Prevention TV! A first of its kind making TV history, LPTV is a refreshing new series bringing prevention truth mainstream. A #PreventionNotPrescription movement, Living Prevention TV is advocacy for people exploited by pharmaceutical corporations promoting a 'pill for all ills''. Hosted by 30-year terminal cancer survivor Kari E. Gray, 'paying it forward' is LPTV. Making the truth in health known is an independent TV series funded by donations to keep the show about you.

title: Guatemala Volcano Relief Fund
description: The Fuego volcano in Guatemala erupted on Sunday, June 3, 2018, killing at least 190 people and displacing thousands from their homes. This fund will provide relief to people impacted by the volcano in the form of emergency supplies like food, water, and medicine, in addition to longer-term recovery assistance to help residents. All donations to this fund will exclusively support disaster relief and recovery efforts in Guatemala.

title: Help Us Teach English to Underprivileged Adults
description: Action10 in collaboration with SpellAfrica in Nigeria with this project aim teach English to over 1,000 adults and youths with little to no basic education who operate their small personal businesses, who are jobless or who have low-income jobs. The goal is to reduce the number of 3 million illiterates in Lagos, demonstrate the relevance of literacy in the development of social and economic lives of people in Nigeria and show how it can improve our economy.

title: Guatemala Volcano Emergency
description: On June 3rd volcano Fuego erupted sending molten rock, ash and toxic gasses cascading through villages killing dozens and trapping families in ash covered homes.  We have boots on the ground to aid families with solar power and water filters.

title: Vaccinate and Sterilize Cats and Dogs on Trinidad
description: Animal Balance will be heading to Trinidad for the first time this month to sterilize and vaccinate cats and dogs on the island. This project is close to our hearts, as it is the first time we will be working on the home island of our dear friend, veterinarian and Board Member, Dr. Raymond. We are joined in this project by local group, Animals 360. There is a great need for these services on Trinidad and we are eager to help improve the lives of animals there.

title: HELP US SAVE OUR WILDLIFE ORPHANAGE!
description: DAKTARI is a home for wild animals whom, for most of them, cannot be rehabilitated because of injuries or being tamed by people. DAKTARI is giving them a second chance in life while being a tool to educate underprivileged children.  The wildlife orphanage started with a blind donkey and a bushbuck. Today, more than 30 animals call DAKTARI home, including two lions, a cheetah, ostriches, mangooses, owls...

title: On The Ground with the Guatemala Volcano
description: Integral Heart Family has been working in Guatemala since 2011. Our school, which is hosting classes for our 85 sponsored kids is also operating as a drop center for supplies for the main rescue center for the victims of the volcano. We are sending medical supply and food deliveries to one center which has 676 refugees in Alotenango, Guatemala. Our plan is short-term support while this center is occupied and longer-term support in helping the affected persons relocate to their new homes.

title: Guatemala Volcano Relief: Helping Children in Need
description: Fuego Volcano has affected over 2 million people. Our Diaper Drop, Casa Jackson of The God's Child Project, is treating children with 1st, 2nd, & 3rd degree burns, as well as children separated from families. This is the greatest disaster Casa Jackson has ever faced, and this project will help supply diapers to families in need.

title: GUATEMALA - TECHO Emergency Response
description: TECHO is channelling funds to build new homes for the thousands of families and communities affected by the eruption of the Volcano de Fuego. Firstly, temporary housing models will be built for families currently living in tents. Thereafter, TECHO will provide more than 800 definitive homes together with other NGOs and authorities in the field, focusing on the long-term approach of our emergency response.

title: Charlie's Fund: Saving Lives Through Technology
description: On June 5, 2018, Charles Farrell--father of CriticaLink Founder Jennifer Farrell--died suddenly from complications of an Aortic Dissection- a rare but often fatal emergency of the heart. In his memory, we are starting Charlie's Fund, which will be used to improve access to rapid, life-saving medical care all over the world. This fund will go to projects that focus on innovative use of mobile technology in medicine and empowering women in STEM, with the goal of saving MANY lives in the future.

title: SOAR Mobile Eye Care Project for ArmenianChildren
description: Armenia's children in institutions or in poverty-stricken regions lack health care services and access to vision care. SOAR Mobile Eye Care Project will provide that care for them.  A completely outfitted Mobile Eye Care Center will travel to all SOAR-supported facilities plus remote villages in Armenia to conduct routine vision screening, eye exams, and treatment for children and families.

title: Provide Lifesaving Support for Guatemala
description: CARE has strong community connections throughout Guatemala, having worked in the country since 1959, enabling us to mount a quicker and more effective response. Your contribution is a crucial source to help us position and deploy needed supplies and staff, make funds available to emergency-affected communities for immediate assistance, strengthen our ability to respond to future emergencies, and provide overall program oversight to ensure the highest-quality response.

title: No one should die of malaria today
description: The Amazonian Indigenous Peoples' Health and Wellbeing Initiative will address the unprecedented rise in malaria in Venezuela by facilitating purchase and transportation of mosquito nets impregnated with insecticide, essential medicines, and supplies to three remote Indigenous communities - Joti, Enepa and Piaroa - who have urgently requested these supplies to prevent further spread of malarial infection and catastrophic loss of life. They ask for your aid in their own words in the video above.

title: Volcano Disaster Long-term Recovery Fund
description: On Sunday June 3rd, Guatemala's 'Fuego' volcano exploded affecting 1.7 million people, displacing thousands, and with a death toll of over 100. This fund will provide relief to individuals who have been impacted by the disaster in the form of long-term recovery assistance. We are partnering up with other local vetted organizations and private entities to give recovery support to those affected by the volcano.

title: Empower Girls through STEM Education
description: According to UNESCO, the careers with less demand for women are Engineering, Communication, Information Technologies and Manufacturing. In Mexico, only 30% of the graduated from STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) or related fields are women. In addition, the  reason why women do not have access to digital technologies is the gender gap. With your donation, you will support and encourage girls in Mexico to start studying courses in computing, coding, electronics and robotics.

title: Disaster Kits for Guatemala Volcano Survivors
description: Guatemala's Fuego Volcano erupted on Sunday, June 3 killing 99 people & causing thousands to lose their homes. More than 12,000 people have been evacuated. Over 1.7 million people have been impacted. MAP International relief supplies are being used by first responders providing care for survivors. Your donation will help us provide MAP Disaster Health Kits, supplies for burn injuries, personal protective equipment such as masks, and more to victims of the volcano eruption. Please help today.

title: Storm Eta Emergency Response in Guatemala
description: This project will distribute essential relief items, such as hygiene and baby care products, to meet urgent needs identified by the affected communities in Guatemala. IsraAID's Emergency Response Team will also assess Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Mental Health and Psycho-social (MHPSS), and Medical needs.

title: Guatemala Disaster Relief Fund
description: Sunday June 3rd there was one of the most violent volcanic eruptions in decades in Guatemala. Fuego Volcano has affected thousands of people in the surrounding area, more than 3,265 people have been evacuated from their homes. Now is the time to help the people that have lost everything.

title: Recovery of Puerto Rico through Youth Leadership
description: This project will help the recovery of Puerto Rico by establishing a "community leadership incubator" to prepare youth who were challenged to assume community leadership roles for which they had no training and/or experience, following the physical and social devastation caused by Hurricane Maria. This project's objective is to expand the social capital of a group of volunteer youth by designing and delivering a theory and practice "Community Leaders Training Module" through a one-year period.

title: Volcano Ash Clean-Up at The School of Hope
description: The School of Hope in Jocotenango, Guatemala has, thankfully, escaped serious damage from the eruption of Volcan de Fuego. Most importantly, all of our students, staff, and families are safe.   The school has suffered some roof and water drain damage. In addition, the clean-up to remove the ash at the school has taken much time and effort. In order to cover the costs of repairs and cleaning, we need $1725.00. We have already received donations of $300, leaving us $1425 to raise.

title: SummerProgram: Inspiring & Keeping Girls In School
description: Las Claras Summer Program ("Veranito Las Claras") is an initiative that started on 2018 to involve young girls (7 to 14 years old) in the community of Felipillo so that they could receive several workshops and classes on vital and empowering life skills.   Furthermore, it is an initiative where our very own teen mothers at the Las Claras Program (main project) involve themselves as leaders, guiding and supervising the girls in their daily activities, in this way giving back to their community.

title: Child Sexual Abuse - If u don't stop it, who will?
description: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is a universal problem with grave repercussions & Five years ago Sahyog embarked on its journey to respond the issue. It was a path less tread upon & consequently more Challenging route. It was a world defined by the language of silence, a silence which speaks & a silence, to which, we at Sahyog try to give strong voice.Sahyog feels humbled & proud that we have touched directly  almost 1 lakh Children, assisted them to overcome their trauma & move enriched life.

title: Improve literacy skills for 3000 Kenyan pupils
description: PACE provides reading and numeracy support for students from schools in rural and slum areas. We help children move from learning to read to reading to learn. With this afterschool support, students develop a love for reading and gain the confidence to drive their own learning. This project will enable 60 of our fellows to provide eight months of literacy coaching, math support and academic enrichment for 3000 students in rural and slum areas.

title: St. Croix Long-Term Recovery Group
description: The St. Croix Long-Term Recovery Group (LTRG) is a cooperative body that is made up of representatives from faith-based, non-profit, government, business and other organizations working within St. Croix to assist individuals and families as they recover from Hurricane Maria. The goal of the LTRG is to unite recovery resources with community needs in order to ensure that even the most vulnerable in the community recover from the disaster.

title: Rebuild Homes in Guatemala after Volcano Disaster
description: Habitat for Humanity Guatemala has activated a Disaster Relief and Recovery program to help families affected by the Fuego Volcano eruption of June 3rd, 2018 to rehabilitate and reconstruct their homes. The program will provide families with Emergency Kits and water filters as well as the construction of new homes, sanitary latrines, and smokeless stoves.
