We have 3 strong and incredible rhino survivors in our care that still need our support, commitment, love, and most importantly, protection. This comes with great financial costs that keep rising, and we can't do it alone. We need all the help we can get.

title: Train 250 English teachers in Cambodia!
description: The Angkor Tree Project provides free teacher training to 250 young Cambodian teachers.  Located in Siem Reap, we target teachers in informal schools (NGO's and community schools) to improve the teaching skills and language proficiency of local English language teachers.

title: CAMPAIGN TO RE-OPEN THE ARK SHELTER.
description: In December 2016, the Ark Foundation's Shelter for Battered Women & Children closed its doors after 17 years of operation. This was mainly due to lack of funding. The Shelter was the only functional shelter for domestic abuse victims (both women and children) in the country, and since it's closing, it has been a huge challenge to protect and reintegrate woman and children who are victims of domestic violence.  Currently in Ghana there is no domestic abuse shelter in operation, resulting in women

title: Saving lives of 25,000 Households in Rwimiyaga
description: Agro Action Rwanda plans to install-construction of 4  water well-boreholes as clean water system using a rotary drilling rig enabling as many 25,000 households (1Household or family is about 7 persons average) to extract clean and safe drinking water directly from the ground and distribute First Aid Hygienic and Sanitation materials for 500 vulnerable children and women.

title: Promote Nutrition Therapy for 27 Tanzania's Region
description: Youth 4 Social Economic Development Organization enhance health promotion on nutrition, WASH and access of Nutrition Therapy for local society in Tanzania, who are in danger on Poverty, marasmus and malnutrition effects especially young children of age 0-15, martenal mother and lactating mothers in Tanzanian's society. The project is also Providing a supply of food substance and set diet plates for young and finally building 4 nutrition clinics.

title: Protect 800 Children from Child Labour
description: Millions of children across India have to work for a living. YOUR support will help 800 children get out of child labour and get back to school.

title: Give Early Education & Hope to Ugandan Children
description: Give young children living in poverty in Uganda, the best start in life at Act4Africa's ground-breaking Kindergarten in rural Mayuge, Eastern Uganda. Kathy's Kindergarten gives vulnerable children, aged 3-6, vital early years education, daily nutrition & health checks. Disadvantaged, at-risk children receive subsidised education and hope of a brighter future.

title: Give health to 60,000 sick children in Colombia
description: By donating to this project, you contribute to the purchase of medical equipment, hospital furniture and the improvement of the physical infrastructure of the Children's Hospital of San Vicente Foundation. Thus, every year, 60,000 children in Colombia, with serious illnesses, will continue to receive the best specialized medical care.

title: Creating a safe haven for Abuse and GBV Survivors
description: Shamwari Yemwanasikana will establish a One Stop Empowerment Center (OSEC) in Seke district as a halfway home for vulnerable girls. Our intervention strategy will cater for the emergency health examination and prevention against STIs and HIV transmission by ensuring the administration of Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) as well as provide legal aid, psycho-social support, counselling, economic empowerment activities and safe shelter to girl child survivors of abuse and GBV.

title: Reconstruction and Adequacy of Rural School
description: For more than four years, the children of the village Arenal, receive their school classes in a community room, due to the affectations that the fall of a tree left. We want to raise funds for the materials needed to: - Change roofs - Clean and paint - Make wooden paths to facilitate entry and transfer from the school to the bathroom and dining room - Improve teachers room

title: Help 50 Disadvantaged Kids Experience Preschool
description: Opportunities of attending early childhood education - Lower and Upper Kindergarten, are missing for children of families financial hardship. There is no facility in government schools for pre primary education currently.  The Avasar Foundation is building pre primary schools in government schools and this project will provide free pre primary education giving free uniform, books and stationeries for 50 Kids.

title: Promoting Girls' Education & Equality in Guatemala
description: Building on the 2019 pilot with 230 girls in Solola, Guatemala, in 2020, GR is expanding the project to reach 500 boys and girls through partners implementing the GR curriculum and tools to build the confidence, skills and mindsets girls need to persist in school and to change attitudes so that entire communities--girls, boys, parents, teachers and leaders--stand up for girls and against gender discrimination.

title: TAILORING WIDOWS
description: Tailoring widows' project plans to implement vocational training programs to provide free training in Tailoring and Dressmaking for 200  disadvantaged and venerable girls and women in Kisumu County Slums, Kisumu City in Kenya.  The support requested is to equip our vocational School with modern machinery to provide value added and market focused training to make the vulnerable group economically empowered.

title: Project Rhino K9 Unit: Defending African Wildlife
description: The greatest threat today to two of South Africa's most iconic species - the Black and White Rhino - come in the form of furtive raids by poachers armed with high-calibre rifles, night-vision equipment, getaway vehicles and backed by a vast, well-funded international criminal network. With their superior sense of smell, hearing and unique physical capabilities, well trained canines are a valuable supplement to law enforcement and a critical tool in combatting this war against rhino poaching.

title: Improving lives of 500 rural farmers in N. Uganda
description: This project will support 500 direct subsistence farmers in Northern Uganda to grow cotton, chickpeas, mung beans & different fruits while linking them to international buyers who can offer stable markets with higher prices. The market linkages & use of organic farming will help farmers reduce their impact on the environment & open doors for them to access broader markets for their produce. These farmers will increase their income from about $20 dollar on average per month to $80 by March 2019.

title: Strengthening Internally Displaced Persons
description: This project will provide: - Food items/parcels to address the immediate needs of 1500 IDPs  affected by the crisis in Buea, Muyuka, Kumba Town and Mamfe  Hygiene kits to support 1000 women and girls to maintain dignity and to meet their basic health and hygiene needs    Emergency birth kits to Four hundred Women  to meet the specific needs of women in emergency situations of delivery   Train 100 internally displaced persons with knowledge on balanced diet and business life skills for income

title: Flood Relief in Okayama
description: The team will distribute urgent relief items and assess the immediate medical and post-trauma psychosocial needs.  IsraAID's professionals will also provide Psychological First Aid and mental health support to those evacuated.

title: Attika wildfires 2018: Recovery support
description: The disastrous fires that hit Attika's coastal region in July 2018 have left the area devastated and its population in deep shock. With many lives lost and homes destroyed, communal life has come to a total standstill and it is only now, six months later, that people are slowly starting to move back into the area. In partnership with the DESMOS Foundation, Echo100Plus has decided to raise funds to start the reconstruction and furnishing of some of the playgrounds in the afflicted municiplities.

title: 1 Project. 100th Fellow. 1 Million Conversations.
description: We're seeking your help to create one 10-week Logan Nonfiction Program fellowship position at the Carey Institute for Global Good in upstate New York. We give independent investigative journalists the time, space, and support needed to produce groundbreaking books, long-form articles, documentary films, and podcasts that change public discourse. You will be directly contributing to deeply reported, independent journalism that otherwise will not be done.

title: SEND A CHILD TO SCHOOL IN UGANDA FOR A YEAR
description: For the past 20 years northern Uganda suffered severly from Lord resistance Army (Kony) war .the war left the people highly improvished and many infected with HIV /AIDS .the level of poverty is very high compared to the others region in Uganda and most of the children lost their families to war and diseases therefore,there is needs to provide them with a family,a home an education as an opportunity to become a part of a large solutions for their community.

title: Climate Action Now
description: Climate Action Now addresses the issue of climate change, by facilitating reduction in personal carbon footprint and increasing general awareness of climate change among the public, to provide a better future for everyone. This project is planting trees with a goal to 1,000,000 trees to offset carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions of more than 560 UK residents for 20 years.  The tree planting is done in Tropical reforestation sistes and provides employment to villagers lifting them oout of poverty.

title: Bikes for village Girls
description: We are giving rural poor village girls bicycles to help them get to school this September 2018. These girl-children walk one or more hours to and from schools. At times, these long distances often keep them from attending regularly. This get them tired and sleeping in schools. Since they are always the target for raping, trafficking, abuses, etc, protection and safeties is another reason why bikes should be given to young girls bikes, Bicycles are the first simple answer to access education.

title: School Gardens & Skills Training For 400 Gambians
description: Grace Foundation Gambia provides free meals, school gardens and skills training in schools to mainly 400 poorest girl children and youths in the West Coast region who come in schools daily on hungry stomach and made to engage in street trading where they face child trafficking, girl marriage, teenage pregnancy etc in order to feed at home. Your donations will go into very needy infrastructures like school gardens, kitchens, starter packs, learning materials, dining hall etc.

title: Children of Akplamafu Primary School
description: Over 1 billion children live in poverty. Education, which gives them vital knowledge and skills, is key to escaping poverty. But, millions of children don't have access to education, leaving them at greater risk of an inability to thrive and exploitation. That's why we're working to crowdfund $7000 so that the Children at Akplamafu Primary School, Ghana, can thrive. Your contributions will provide meals, laptops for teachers, books, school furniture, art supplies, and even sports jerseys.

title: Recovery for Those Affected by Flooding
description: This project will provide vegetable seeds, organic fertilizer and garden tools to 350 poor farmers affected by the recent flooding in the Philippines especially in Bataan and in other parts of the country in order for them to secure immediate food since some selected vegetables can be harvested in a short time.

title: Vocational Training for 100 Female Victims in Chad
description: Corridors of Peace plans to provide free vocational and literacy training for girls and Women who were victims of the clashes between the Zhagharwas and the Tamars. Also to provide free meals for their children who hail from the poorest landlocked sections of the society in Guerida,  The project would build a vocational center in North Eastern Chad, to provide a rich supply of vocational skills, like Sowing Machines, Solar Water Pump for Agriculture and Solar Powered mill for income generating.

title: Create Environmental Education Program in Ecuador
description: Help us create an environmental education program for 115 elementary school students, boys and girls.  This program will get them hands on experience walking in nature, doing beach clean-ups, planting trees, building community gardens, recycling, and making compost. Through project based learning, we hope to empower our students to be part of the global effort to protect our planet for future generations.

title: Integrate 500 patients of mental health  in Rwanda
description: Mental illness support in Rwanda is left behind. Many of patients have no access to proper diagnosis, long term treatment, care or counseling and social integration. This project will allow NDUHURA Organization to integrate 500 of mental health patients in their social environment and advocate for their rights and raise awareness to reduce stigma through a community-based network of trained health professionals. With this help, we can change the lives of many of mentally ill patients in Rwanda.

title: EMPOWER ENTREPRENEURS IN UNDER-SERVED COMMUNITIES
description: Somo is an accelerator that works with impact entrepreneurs from low-income, urban communities. Our programs include long-term support in the form of training, advising, funding, and increased market access. We believe that people from low-income communities are in the best position to create change in their own communities-they understand and see the problems themselves, their families and neighbors are dealing with.

title: No excuse for child rape
description: LITSAM Youth Awareness Initiative plans to sensitive five hundred (500) young parents in Kano State on how to protect children from rape, stop the stigma and discrimination of victims of rape and report cases immediately when they happen. The 2017 Police report of child rape cases in Kano stands at 334. Rape cases are mostly under reported due to fear of stigma and discrimination, ignorance of reporting procedure etc. LITSAM will work with 20 volunteers, 5 Police Officers and 5 legal experts.

title: Supporting Syrian refugees with disabilities
description: MAITS will train local outreach workers in Lebanon supporting Syrian refugees, to help families with disabilities such as autism. Our partners outreach team is working with 398 people in refugee camps, including 123 children. 42 of these have a diagnosis, others may be undiagnosed. The outreach workers want disability training to better support these vulnerable families. We have a volunteer trainer and need your help to make this happen. We will translate and share the resources in Arabic.

title: Emergency response to devastating floods in Laos
description: Laos is experiencing the largest floods in 10 years, caused by the sudden collapse of a hydroelectric dam. Health Poverty Action works in Attapeu, the most severely affected province, now declared a National Disaster Area. Flash floods have submerged homes, hospitals, schools, roads, bridges and fields. This will have a devastating long-term impact on peoples' livelihoods and well-being. HPA is one of the few organisations providing emergency and long-term assistance to affected communities.

title: WiFi Learn
description: Join Sosua75.org, in collaboration with Fundacion Software Libre Dominicano (FSLD), and their wifilearn.org program, in our mission to provide EQUAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES to the children of Sosua and Cabarete, Dominican Republic. Our hotspot WiFi technology securely serves high quality educational content to the following sites/resources: Khan Academy, Coursera, Wikipedia, Duolingo, and others, guaranteeing social inclusion to members of poor communities where WiFi access points are installed.

title: Help Stateless children achieve Thai citizenship
description: Citizenship provides belonging, a sense of identity. It provides access to education, health care, and careers. But for many children born in the mountain villages of Thailand, it is a difficult thing to acquire due to lack of knowledge, lack of education or poverty. Help us provide resources to families going through the process of applying for citizenship for their children so those children have no limitations to success.

title: We Need a Kitchen Ventilator Hood!
description: Our cooks work hard to provide nutritious meals to hundreds of students daily. Their ability to do this will improve with the addition of a kitchen hood ventilator. This hood will remove grease, combustible materials, smoke, odors, and heat from the kitchen, leading to a cooler, fresher, and healthier work atmosphere. It will also benefit our students by improving the hygiene of the kitchen, leading to even cleaner food. Three quotes from local businesses indicate this will cost us $1,150.

title: Help rebuild the homes lost in the fire in Athens
description: On Monday, July 23rd, multiple fires erupted near Mati and Rafina, seaside areas of Athens, Greece. Fanned by winds of up to 60 miles per hour, the fires quickly grew into raging infernos claiming the lives of over 90 people, completely destroying over 1,200 homes and leaving a whole country in a state of shock.   This project aims to humbly help families rebuild their homes.

title: Hair Comes Your Future
description: Build self esteem in over 2000 at-risk students through beauty and barber services. Each student will receive one free full service every month for twelve months. Full service consist of shampoo massage, scalp conditioning treatments and a haircut/hairstyle.

title: Computer Literacy and Practice
description: Millions of children lack basic computer literacy, lack of access to information and how to communicate. Children who go to schools in poor and rural areas do not have basic hands on computer practice. Our partner World Computer Exchange can offer a solution - mobile libraries equipped that can be used in schools for accessibility. This project will provide 1,800 school children access to develop their vital technology skills and opportunities.

title: Changing children's lives in the home
description: This project will help parents to enable their children to have a great start at school. Many parents do not have the skills or resources to help their children on their educational journey at home. But they have passion and a desire for their children to succeed. The workshops will provide parents with skills and resources so that they feel empowered and encouraged to help their children avoid the education poverty trap and secure a better future. 1000 children will benefit from this project.

title: Bringing potable water in Babli's village in Mewat
description: Babli is a resident of Mewat region of Haryana, Hathin Block, district Palwal. She treks several miles daily to fetch water. With scorching Sun, parched land and rapidly depleting source of water, she does not know how long she will get water. She and many like her have abandoned their cattle as there is no water or fodder for them. She is not very old but due to drinking contaminated water day in day out her hair is almost grey, her joints are swollen and her gait is slow and laborious.

title: Help improve blind people's lives in Brazil
description: Dorina Nowill Foundation for the Blind (Fundacao Dorina Nowill para Cegos) is a nonprofit philanthropic organization that for 72 years has been dedicated to the inclusion of the visually impaired in Brazil. We supply special services for the visually impaired and their families free of charge, in the areas such as education, rehabilitation, low vision health and employment. We provide them with a one-year rehabilitation program with transformative solutions.

title: Give Guyanese Students Access to University
description: SAGE is the only non-profit post-secondary scholarship fund in Guyana, offering low-income students the opportunity to complete their degrees locally without the burden of loans. SAGE began with a single scholarship for the 2009-2010 school year and continues to grow. To date, nineteen deserving students have received full scholarships to the University of Guyana (UG), with majors including law, medicine, agriculture, international relations, education, computer technology and tourism.

title: Biogas for Better Lives in Rural Thailand
description: This project will enable 400 hilltribes in 80 households at Yamokee Village in Tak Province in Thailand's very remote area to turn waste from pig farms into biogas plants for cooking, lighting and organic fertilizer. Households will no longer depend on trees/ firewood for cooking. The community avoid diseases from the pig waste, save time for collecting firewood, save money from buying chemical fertilizer, and there are global benefit for climate change mitigation.

title: Help Haitian Families Rise From Poverty to Dignity
description: You can help the very poorest families in rural Haiti permanently escape extreme poverty. Beyond Borders Family Graduation program is an 18-month asset-building initiative that equips families with the resources and skills they need to begin earning a living so that they can provide for themselves, send their children to school, and live with independence and dignity.

title: Cote d'Ivoire Rising-STEM Scholarship for Females
description: In Cote d'Ivoire, only 1 in 16 students are in college, and less than half are female. This disparity is even greater in science, technology, engineering and mathematics programs. Cote d'Ivoire aspires to be an emerging economy in 2020. This aggressive goal demands educational gender equity in STEM. This program will provide scholarships to well-qualified female students from rural areas to attend IUGB in Cote d'Ivoire to build a diverse workforce.

title: Sustainable Livelihoods for 100 Families
description: EcoLogic aims to support rural Guatemalan farmers with the development and expansion of beekeeping and honey production that benefits both their families and the environment. Beekeeping can also help build sustainable, resilient livelihoods. By providing supplies and technical assistance we are improving the ability of local families to maintain sustainable beekeeping. With this project, we seek to establish 200 new beehives and provide supplies and technical support to 100 new beekeepers.

title: Create a future for Kenya's disadvantaged girls
description: Starehe Girls' Centre and School is a national boarding school in Nairobi, Kenya, that gives access to quality secondary education and leadership opportunities to disadvantaged adolescent girls from all the counties of Kenya. The Centre provides a supportive environment where the girls develop their full academic and personal potential. The Louise Martin Memorial Scholarship provides girls access to education for all four years of secondary school.

title: Provide School Supplies to Girls In Need
description: This project will provide 350 girls in need of school supplies with the tools necessary to be successful in the classroom in deprived communities of Ghana. Money raised will go towards purchasing pencils and notebooks, school uniforms and school bags for at-risk girls.

title: MAKING HEALTHCARE A HUMAN RIGHT
description: In today's era, medical science has advanced tremendously and progressing however the irony lies in the fact that affordability of medical treatment is often a  question of distress to society, specially for people living below poverty line. In such cases, Abhilasha Foundation sponsors surgery and treatment for the children by working voluntarily with hospitals such as Reliance, Jupiter, Nanvati Hospital and many more to fund critically ill patients so that they are not deprived of medical help.

title: Sustainable Livelihoods - Overcoming Poverty
description: SWIFT understands that eradicating poverty will lead to the eradication of societal problems that we face in the world today. The Covid 19 crisis has caused untold misery for thousands of our members who are now without any form of income. With not social support available in Eswatini the need is great, we now need to keep people alive.

title: Providing Safe Spaces for Homeless Children
description: Street and Outreach work is at the heart of Glad's House - in 2006 we started as a street based Organisation to ensure that every child and young person could access support, not just those that were able to move into residential units. Our Project will ensure that every child and young person living on the streets of Mombasa has access to space and activities to play, get school support where needed,  alternative family care and also support from Glad's House staff if they want it.

title: Help Girls to End the Cycle of Poverty & Violence
description: The growing urban poverty and disparity have adverse impact on lives of women. They face multiple disadvantages due to poverty, gender discrimination, and lack of access to higher education. The present project aims at empowering  young women staying in urban settlements through employability skills training, critical life skills and linking them to jobs and other income generating options like enterprise development leading to financial independence and greater control over their own lives.

title: Spring water source maintainance for 300 in Uganda
description: This project is protecting a community water source in a village in Uganda.Safe and acceptable water for human consumption that is available in sufficient quantity, physically accessible and affordable is a crucial prerequisite for human wellbeing. Access to safe water is not only fundamental to good health but also to satisfactory livelihoods, dignity and prospects for economic growth and education.

title: Support Education of Children With Special Needs
description: In India a child born with special needs is destined for a life of dependency. For the poor this situation is extreme. The children with special needs are considered to be a social, financial, mental and physical burden to their families. Special Care Center annually reaches out to children who are hearing and speech impaired and mentally challenged and living in poor socio economic condition and is attended by 300 children who lack affordable education facility for their special needs.

title: Build A Primary School for 300 students in Uganda!
description: Rukundo Preparatory School (RPS) offers a premier education experience. Small classes, dedicated teachers, & new facilities, including flushing toilets, make our school stand out among other rural schools with overcrowded classrooms & unsanitary conditions. In addition, we provide two nutritious meals each day-for some students, the only meals they rely on. To help support more children, we need YOUR help to raise $45K to complete the construction of our primary school's first-level foundation.

title: Keep 500 South African Girls in school
description: The Diepsloot community school-based outreach project exists to educates, raises awareness about social ills. Offers skills development as well as problem-solving solutions to over 1000 school girls to date. The BEAR Foundations secondary school activities enable girls to exercise their potential and explore options to better improve their lifestyle and to help them focus and complete school through t Which in turn helps to fight against the challenges of poverty, teenage pregnancy, and HIV/Aids

title: DONATE TO MAKE EDUCATION A REALITY
description: Justice and Development for All is committed to support the government in improving the quality of education of primary schools at Nguruka Ward which has  more than 5500+ school pupils. The primary schools  face shortage of important teaching materials , text books, and teaching aids are not sufficient to meet the need. Currently, the book ration is 1:4 pupils, forcing some of pupils to be demoralized as they don't perform exercise nor get time to perform assignment given by teachers .

title: Offer holidays to 30 refugee children in Greece
description: This project will provide 3 days of outdoor activities in a farmhouse located in the region of Karpenisi to 30 refugee children living in refugee camps in Greece, offering them the chance to escape from their difficult everyday life by sharing moments of joy, adventure and revitalization.

title: Increasing Access to Safe Water in Sudan
description: Hygiene and sanitation trainings and hygiene kits, cleanup campaigns, construction tools and training for building latrines, teaching hand pump mechanics (to men and women) and pump repair kits, building wells. These are just some of the basic but life-saving interventions that NEF is implementing South Kordofan and Central Darfur in Sudan to help remote communities safely access clean water and prevent the spread of disease. We need your help.

title: Reduce Pain and Hospital Stay for 5700 kids/ year
description: For over 93 years La Fundacion Clinica Noel has been changing the lives of thousands of kids with different problems such as cleft lip & palate and osteogenesis imperfecta.  Nowadays we give surgery to 2892 kids per year and the pain they have after de surgery can be unimaginable, as the nausea they feel but will be solved using an ultrasound machine when the kids are getting the anesthesia during the surgery.

title: Partnering with Young Mothers in Nepal
description: Over the last two years FFF has held Neonatal workshops in four villages in Nepal, three in Nawalparasi and one in Bara. In each village there were a notable number of babies (32% to 46%) that were underweight. To better serve the young mothers and children,  we propose quarterly meetings with the mothers to continue discussions regarding healthier food choices and kitchen gardens. We will also track the health of the mothers and babies and suggest medical followup if needed.

title: Help Save Newborns in Haiti
description: Konbit Sante partners with health-care facilities in northern Haiti to improve the quality of care provided to the large population there. One partner is the neonatal service at Justinian University Hospital in Cap-Haitien, the second-largest public hospital in the country and the public referral center for more than 1 million people. This project focuses on the procurement and management of essential emergency medicines and medical supplies needed to save the lives of newborns.

title: Preventing 800 Sindhi children from sexual abuse
description: Imagine our 6 years` innocent school going daughter is gang-raped, killed and thrown onto garbage! imagine we saw her off at school gate and we receive her dead body in rages with her body bleeding all over!   Zainab Ansari was a six years old innocent girl from Kasur Pakistan who was raped and brutally killed. there are thousands of Zainabs who are assaulted mentally or physically each year. Through this project REACH will conduct 40 awareness sessions to 800 female children in schools of Johi.

title: Inclusive entrepreneurship program
description: Kadiwaku Family Foundation wants to help 650 individuals with disabilities living in rural areas in Democratic Republic of the Congo to participate in entrepreneurship training and will provide them with accommodation and devices designed to assist a person to perform a particular task or run a business activity, such as wheelchair, hearing aids, white canes, tape recorders so that they live live independently and be economically and socially included into society.

title: Boost The Learning and Education of Kids in Ghana
description: In Ghana, children are involved in the worst forms of child labor. This includes gold mining, fishing, and cocoa harvesting. Because of poverty, ignorance, and child labor, hundreds of kids do NOT go to school. Tragically, many of them drop out of school every year. We are helping to change this by providing scholarships, school supplies, school meals, and uniforms. Computer training is helping to provide the kids with the needed competence for a digitally-connected world.

title: Help Girls Live Healthy with Effective Pad Usage
description: Chhaupadi, the traditional act of banishing women (during their periods) from houses, schools, etc. is still widely practiced. Nepalese people lack the adequate knowledge and information regarding the need to maintain menstrual hygiene, which may lead to serious reproductive health issues. Our project has a clear goal. We will provide the production of low cost pads and transformational hygiene education to 5000 young women.

title: Give a future for 950 Indian kids living with HIV
description: Our HIV-positive Women's Networks provide essential care. Many children & adolescents are traumatised by loss of at least one parent to HIV/AIDS and by the knowledge that they carry a life-threatening virus and are now also exposed to Covid-19. They need counselling and support to cope with the medical, social and psychological impact of HIV combined with all the usual teenage concerns. We support 950 vulnerable children living with HIV in south India and now provide medical assistance directly.

title: SEND 1000 ORPHANED  CHILDREN TO SCHOOL IN NIGERIA
description: This project will help to provide educational support and access for 1000 orphans traumatized by insurgency and Herdsmen attacks in Northern Nigeria. Sending these orphans out of the streets to schools will help to reduce their vulnerability\exploitation and help them to secure a better life and a future, given that basic education serves as a spring board for continued education.

title: Lombok Earthquake Relief Fund
description: A 7.0 magnitude earthquake on the island of Lombok, Indonesia caused extensive damage on Sunday, August 5, 2018, killing more than 98 people and displacing more than 20,000 from their homes. This fund will provide relief to people impacted by the earthquake in the form of emergency supplies like food, water, and medicine, in addition to longer-term recovery assistance to help residents. All donations to this fund will exclusively support disaster relief and recovery efforts in Indonesia.

title: Champion rural primary education in Mulshi, India
description: Akshara's Khelghar program provides children in rural Maharashtra with access to high-quality primary education in a contextual, creative & interactive manner. By bolstering a weak village schooling system, Khelgar gives young learners an educational grounding that overcomes socio-economic disadvantage and minimizes the urban-rural attainment gap. Akshara is the local social-impact initiative of UWC Mahindra College, providing community interventions to a community of 2500+ in the Mulshi valley.

title: Mentoring Young Adults in Uganda into Innovators
description: Mentoring 15 Ugandan young adults into innovators who are highly skilled and who have experienced positive life-changing awakening processes that will lead them to rational  analyses of their own attitudes and actions; and of the existing social, cultural, economic and political relationships in their communities. Their experiential learning from the analyses will motivate them to take action against poverty and improve standards of living for at least 150 people living in 30 Ugandan households.

title: 100 Smiles in 100th Mission
description: For the last 16 years we have gone to the remotest corners of India to bring Smiles to around 10,000 kids and adults through our medical mission. After 3 months we would organize our 100th MEDICAL MISSION IN INDIA. And, what better way to celebrate than bringing the gift of Smiles to 100 more children. Support us and join the celebration of Smiles. Select a Donation option that suits you or start a Recurring Donation to JOIN THIS SMILE MOVEMENT.

title: Protect Bandhavgarh's Tigers From Poachers
description: 97% of the global wild tiger population has been lost in 100 years. Only 3500 remain so it's vital we protect them & their critical habitat. 2967 wild tigers are in India. Poachers have jeopardised wild tiger survival for years with snares consisting of anchored wires with sliding nooses camouflaged along tiger trails. Our Anti-Poaching Patrols aim to eradicate snares around Bandhavgarh so tigers can walk safely, & to educate local communities to change attitudes towards tigers/other wildlife.

title: Build an Early Childhood Education Centre, Uganda
description: Early Childhood Development (ECD) programs are a highly effective means of strengthening society by ensuring that its individual members live up to their full potential. Children who participate in these programs tend to be more successful later in school, are more competent socially and emotionally and show better verbal, intellectual and physical development than children who are not enrolled in such quality programs.

title: Stand #ByHerSide in Afghanistan with WAW
description: Women for Afghan Women's (WAW's) #ByHerSide program in Afghanistan provides access to critically-needed health services including life-saving treatment and surgery for survivors of rape, incest, physical abuse, or violence by family or community members; OBGYN services for pregnant women (including supplements to reduce incidences of malnutrition); and birth and after-birth services in proper medical facilities. For a full scope of WAW's life-changing programs, visit womenforafghanwomen.org.

title: Women's Health Champions
description: This project will bring inclusive, comprehensive women's health education to women in rural communities around Santiago Atitlan, Guatemala. Staff will train peer health educators, or "Champions", to lead informational sessions in their own communities. The project will also empower women with the economic resources they need to advocate for their own health by equipping participants to distribute locally-manufactured reusable cloth menstrual pads as a source of personal income.

title: California Wildfires
description: Do Your Part is responding to the devastating wildfires in both Northern (Camp Fire) and Southern California (Hill Fire/WoolseyFire) with critical emergency relief supplies, and assisting displaced families with disaster case management and financial grants to help them begin their lives over.

title: supporting 100 Farmer suicide families in India
description: Farmers, the food producers are victims of perpetual agrarian crisis. Widows become farmers when husbands commit suicides, forced to shoulder family responsibilities to take care of children education, aged family members and survive in farming. In addition gender discrimination and sexual abuse is facing very often. FIAN empower and council widow farmers community to rehabilitate ,  face challenges and stand on their own in finding livelihood and compensation from the Government.

title: Say no to Malnutrition to Poor Children in School
description: In Kenya Africa, hunger is a constant crisis that prevent children to go to school, chronic pain gnawing away at hungry children. We must put an end to starvation in Kenya and we can't do it without you. Right now, millions of children in rural schools from poor families need emergency food assistance to survive and continue with education. YIDP has many proven ways to help stop hunger in Africa and beyond.

title: Help End Violent Disciplining of Children in Haiti
description: Help ACESWorld empower Haitian parents and teachers to uphold the right of children to be free from violent discipline. Violent discipline is the most common form of violence children experience in Haiti. This project will give 300 Haitian families nonviolent strategies and resources to discipline their children. It will also help them develop an understanding of the long-lasting harm that violent discipline can cause children.

title: Workshop Tour for children in Dutch refugee camps
description: With this project we stimulate trauma relief on a physical level through dance, basketball, rap and boxing. Are coaches are role models from diverse cultural backgrounds that will support, inspire and motivate child refugees without a home to move and become physically and mentally healthier. Every year we try to raise money through grants and this platform to give 150-200 workshops in emergency shelters and regular shelters to child refugees.

title: Increasing social projects impact in communities
description: This project will support the development and innovation of initiatives with social impact, making possible the professionalization of non-profit organizations. This will be achieved by mentoring  in five areas: strategy, management, marketing, business, technology. Through mentoring, social leaders will be able to develop high quality projects with greater social impact, increasing the likelihood of positive changes in the life of 2,000 children and teenagers in risk and vulnerable situations.

title: Move Forward Suriname 2023
description: Sunny Point is a neighborhood in Suriname without police control where children live in poor conditions. In 2017 and 2018 we launched a dance, sports and rap community projects in Suriname for teenagers from this area and other neighborhoods.The talented children in Sunny Point stole our hearts and with your donation we can go back. Summer 2023 we want to organize dance and sport activities for the children growing up in this tough area close to Paramaribo. The more we raise the more we can do.

title: Support for child victims of sex trafficking
description: This project will provide aftercare support and reintegration services for up to 100 girls aged 1-18 who have been victims of sexual exploitation and forced labor in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The young girls will receive access to safe short-term shelter, healthcare, education, legal support and family reunion or community-based care support.

title: Lions/Lioness-Serving The Visually Impaired
description: This project will provide funds for the charities we support for the visually impaired.  We support Leader Dogs for the Blind, Eversight Vision, Lions Bear Lake Camp, Penrickton Center for Blind Children, Project Kidsight, Seedlings (Braille Books for Children), as well as charities for the hearing impaired.

title: Work Readiness Training for Disadvantaged Youth
description: Beacon focuses on disadvantaged communities and areas of high youth disengagement and unemployment, where the risk and the need are greatest. We work with schools, businesses and communities to help bring relevance to the curriculum and inspire young people to think about careers and experience the workplace, long before they leave school. This helps school retention rates and teaches real-life skills, preparing them for the workplace.

title: Holistic Development of 300 Women in Gujarat
description: The Information centres will offer women and adolescent girls building their capacities and make linkages to the required services of local government as per their need through our information centre. It includes getting prepared for documentation to avail the govt. welfare services for food, nutrition, vaccination, health and livelihood. Make sure that every child in the community goes to school. The centre will provide life skill related training and linkages for holistic development.

title: Care & Support Home for 20 OrphanChildren in India
description: According to UNICEF, children worldwide lose their parents in conflict, or due to poverty, disability, HIV/AIDS. Hence there is a large population of children that grow up without one or both of their parents. Children without parental care are at a high risk of abuse, exploitation, and neglect. Large numbers of children end up in institutional care. Inadequate individual care of institutions can socially and emotional impair children.

title: Empower and Protect Cambodian Women
description: 49% of Cambodian women believe men are sometimes justified in hitting their partners. NGO-CEDAW is working with the government to strengthen the law against domestic violence. We are building popular support for this change by engaging youth through workshops, debates and art exhibitions to challenge their beliefs about gender roles. We have contracts with donors for specific activities, but with no reserve funding, we still need your help to fund our much-needed work!

title: Give poor teen mothers of rape a hope and dignity
description: Care and education prevents abuse&re-abuse, restore hope and dignity to survivors of sexual violence and give bright future. This project in action in rural Rulindo District of Rwanda assists teen mothers of sexual violence from poor families with clinical care, safety, psycho-Social therapies, education, economic well being and ability to influence the decisions that affect their lives.

title: Ending extreme poverty? Focus  on children & Educ.
description: This project aim at building a three unit classroom block for 150 children in Ghana Akura a highly deprived community in Northern part of Ashanti Region (Ejura) in Ghana.  Our goal is to provide quality education for children of school going age between the ages of 5-15yrs in six deprived communities who lack basic schooling. Provide them with critical literacy support programmes for all the children who lack basic needs in the selected communities including teaching and learning materials .

title: Help children become book lovers in rural Mexico
description: Books can change the lives of children and developing the habit of reading at a young age will become a lifelong tool. When children read, they learn to become creative, empathetic and critical thinkers.  In the spring of 2019, we wish to implement a large scale reading campaign in Mexico that unites 700 children from over a dozen rural villages. Children, teachers, and parents read a selected book together and then the author personally meets them in their villages. This will be our 6th year.

title: Help Feed 800 Venezuelan School Age Children
description: Research* shows that 3 out of 4 children are unable to attend school regularly due to hunger and malnutrition. Foundations Pabellon con Arepa and Oportunidad y Futuro have partnered to buy groceries and ensure they are efficiently used by school pantries in La Vega, one of the poorest sectors of Caracas, Venezuela. Your contributions will provide daily meals to over 800 children. This will significantly decrease drop-out rate and keep children in school. *Encuesta Condiciones de Vida 2017- UCAB

title: WILDFIRES IN GREECE- HELPING PEOPLE IN NEED
description: This project will give emergency help to kids & families, fire victims in Attika, Greece. We will create Help Stations to cover the Fire Victims with food, clothes, psychological support, and medicines. At the areas with no electricity, we will provide energy banks and internet sticks. We cover Mati, Kinetta and the kids Camp.of Rafina.  H.U.G. POINTS will provide in person  psychological support in this dark period, as well as, nutrition, tools and essentials on a daily basis.

title: Wheelchair repair program & assistance center
description: Nepal lacks the skilled manpower to repair wheelchair and don't have a repair center. So this project aims to generate manpower and provide basic service to the wheelchair users. Along with awareness to caregiver, health support, assistance & other for proper care and maintenance of wheelchair. The trainee will be wheelchair user, representatives of organizations of PWDs so that after training they can set their small workshop with tool kit provided by CDCA and provide service to the community.

title: POSITIVE KIDS-50 HIV infected orphan children
description: FF functions from the belief that 'no child needs sacrifice quality of life to an illness'. The Foundation endeavors to ensure that the basic rights of all children accessing care through the centres at Bangalore & Hyderabad are protected. This is an orphan care residential program where FF plays the role of guardian providing shelter, educational & medical support for HIV +ve children

title: Little Sofia struggling with leukemia
description: Beautiful girl with big gray eyes and sad smile - Sofia from Ukraine. She is only 5 years old and for several years Sofia has been struggling with leukemia, which can take her life. To treat the girl constantly need expensive medications. Mom alone brings up Sofia and works as a teacher in a rural school. She asks to respond to all not indifferent people and help her daughter to be healthy and smiling again!

title: Build 2 Classrooms to Support Disadvantaged Child
description: This project will build two Nursery classrooms for 100 Disadvantaged Children in Bukasa village a poor community to support Early Child Development. Besides providing a strong education foundation, the Nursery School will provide a noon meal to the children since their parents are poor and some stay with their Guardians.

title: Guinea: Building health center for a village
description: Kahere is a village located to 35 km of Labe town, which is about 450 km from the Guinean capital Conakry. More than 200 families of 400 people live there without a health center. To take health care, these villagers have to walk 15 KM everyday to get to sub prefecture called Sannou. This is very tough and painful. Especially in the case or emergency patients.  That's why building a health center in this village will help the inhabitants to have better life and care.

title: Cats in Need: Provide Shelter & Care for 121 Cats
description: The Foxie G Foundation is a 501c3 organization that currently caretakes 12 free roaming cat colonies and provides sanctuary care (longterm/lifetime care) to approximately 121 cats.  The need for low cost spay/neuter programs has increased substantially with the economy and rise in outdoor and stray cat populations.  The monies raised in this campaign will go to providing funding for no cost spay/neuter in our area as well as refurbishing our current outdoor cat feeding and housing stations.

title: Provide Jobs for +50 young people in Mexico
description: Motivate young people in Mexico with a high degree of vulnerability to experience a form of self-employment that proves that they are their own skills and a project to try, enough elements that could greatly improve their living conditions no matter they have not finished their studies, whether single mothers or young people who do not work, for people who are eager to learn and get ahead... It's always possible!

title: Be a kid, that's their job
description: "The education is the most powerful weapon to change the world" - The student population that attends public schools in Venezuela comes from low-income families. These are children of parents who work as unskilled labor, housewives, domestic workers and unemployed, so buy shoes and clothes isn't in their priorities. They attend classes almost barefoot and this puts them at risk of infection and death from soil- transmitted diseases that enter their bodies through cuts in their unprotected feet.

title: OPEN YOUR HUG TO FIRE VICTIMS. GREECE NEEDS YOU
description: This project will give emergency material help to FIRE VICTIMS in Attika, Greece. We ll run MOBILE HELP Stations to provide fire victims with food, clothes at the 3 mostly destroyed areas, MATI-KINETA-RAFINA still without electricity or any gov. plan. We'll provide to H.U.G. help POINTS all fire victims in person, "Emergency Packages" with essentials described in our action planing and our Mini vans of Distributions we need your help to get them basically equipped to give help to families.

title: Friends of Ocean Academy, Belize, 2018-2019
description: Most Caye Caulker children were forced to quit school at the age of 12 until Ocean Academy opened as the island's first high school offering an education to all children who want to learn.

title: Danny Michel Ocean Academy, Belize, 2018-2019
description: Ocean Academy, Caye Caulker's first high school, opened in 2008 and provides academic and job skills programs that enable children to break free from systemic poverty. Canadian singer/songwriter Danny Michel and his fans support students who are the first in their families to attend high school which is not free. Building on the momentum of $75,000 raised to date, Danny is close to his $100,000 goal.  Danny makes regular site visits to Belize for transparency and to reconnect with the community.

title: Provide a Hostel School in the Hidden Himalayas.
description: Humla is the remotest district in Nepal situated in the far NW of the country. It is very poor with little or no basic infrastructure and a third of children die before their 5th birthday. Our aim is to help bring some stability by providing better education facilities especially for those children who live too far away from existing government schools and cannot travel on a daily basis and in the bitter mountain climate

title: Build a school for 150 children in Uganda
description: Humura Vulnerable Children/Youth Support Organization, plans to build a 3 classroom block to provide free education, meals and counseling services to children living with HIV/AID's for 150 vulnerable children who stay in the poorest and marginalized areas of Kicwamba sub county in Kabarole district. These are orphans and other vulnerable children whose parents died of the scourge of HIV/AID's.

title: Assist 20 women producing 100% biopads in Cameroon
description: Through False Labels Global Inc.we will help 10 million rural women and girls in overcoming the social barriers linked with menstruation by providing them with low-cost sanitary pads (KujaEcoPads),an innovation that produces 100% biodegradable sanitary pads from locally sourced banana stem fibers.We plan to buy land and build a production center for the 20 who are currently working in a very small rented space.

title: Provide safe drinking water,tens thousands-postwar
description: Rural Women & Youth Coordination's water recovery-Links plans to provide sufficient safe, healthy water supply near villages hard-hit by water crisis in a post war ravaged northern Uganda, that recently suffered  prolonged drought ever, due to climate change. Putting the poorest families, orphans, widows and other vulnerable children at a high risk of serious outbreak of water-borne diseases, due to sharing dirty water sources with animals. To get scare safe or clean water one needs a bicycle.

title: Launch our School for 400 Children in Rural India
description: Education empowers young leaders to establish successful careers and give back to their communities. FOREFRONT is constructing a primary school in Kolluru, Andhra Pradesh, India, that will serve 400 local children per year with a focus on building skilled and active change makers in their communities. FOREFRONT's primary school will support students in realizing holistic success in the short and long-term by fostering their critical thinking skills, socio-emotional skills, and healthy habits.

title: Help Nicaraguan Parents Build 5 Rural Preschools
description: Parents will build 5 preschools in 5 rural communities in eastern Nicaragua. Their preschoolers are currently being taught under trees, in borrowed spaces, family kitchens, & churches. In these isolated communities outside of Mulukuku, parents have already given land,but they lack building materials. Their children, need early attention in education & they want to build schools for them. Teachers also need basic educational supplies for these poor rural children to get a head start in education.

title: THRIVE IN WORK YOUTH FUND
description: We provide support & small but life changing bursaries to enable disadvantaged young people to secure valuable employment, changing the shape of their future & the quality of their lives

title: Sponsor food for 60 orphan special needs children.
description: This project will help us to provide nutritious meal for 60 orphan children with special needs which help us in improving their survival. The children struggle with Cerebral Palsy, Downs Syndrome, Physical Challenges, Cognitive Challenges, Speech and Hearing Impairment. The children are primarily abandoned disabled orphans with a few from underprivileged backgrounds.

title: Read Library Project
description: Having setup 150 libraries in underprivileged schools & communities across the length & breadth of India, 15 libraries in Kenya and 3 in Nepal, the Project IAHV Read Library encourages school children to develop the habit of reading widen their knowledge, skills and imagination beyond curriculum text books. Books availed in many languages: Kannada, Gujarati, Hindi, English, Urdu, Bengali, Marathi, Malayalam, Telugu, Tamil, Swahili, Braille & Digital books.

title: Indonesian Earthquake and Tsunami Response
description: An emergency response team from Save the Children's local partner has deployed to central Sulawesi in Indonesia after an earthquake struck on September 28th.   The magnitude 7.5 quake triggered a tsunami with waves reportedly up to three meters high near the island's capital Palu. More than 1,400 people have been confirmed dead, including hundreds of children, and more than 65,000 homes are destroyed.  Save the Children's national entity has a team on the ground preparing to distribute aid

title: Kadam Resource Centre and Home for Girls
description: Introduction Kadam Education Initiative, which emerged out of the interventions of Centre for Development, Ahmedabad city for children who have dropped out of schools with special focus on girls. Almost 25-30 children a month, arriving at the Ahmedabad Railway station rescued by CfD associated with the Child line and and eventually sent to ill-equipped shelter homes. KEI intends to build a Resource centre and Home, which will also serve as one stop emergency shelter.

title: Helping NPO support centers in disaster relief
description: Historic rainstorms caused floods and landslides in western Japan. Damages in Okayama and Hiroshima are particularly severe. With a network with local nonprofit organization (NPO) support centers across Japan, Japan NPO Center has been coordinating staff dispatch to the support centers in affected communities to help out the necessary operations. Your support compensates the staff's transportation to and accommodation in Hiroshima & Okayama which are currently done with out of pocket expenses.

title: Empowering Communities to Conserve Dry Forests
description: With only 2% remaining, Peru's dry forests are one of the most endangered ecosystems in the world. Native trees are heavily logged yet are crucial to the survival and wellbeing of local communities and endangered wildlife. Located on Peru's northern coast, this project will work with low-income farmers and community members to reforest this threatened landscape. Local people will be trained on how to restore and sustainably manage dry forests in ways that boost their income and conserve habitat.

title: SOFT SKILL TRAINING FOR 450 CHILDREN FOR A YEAR
description: This integrated program of soft skill training uses the medium of creative arts and has impacted the lives of more than 4000 children and youth from marginalized backgrounds in Mumbai. We now need to expand and reach out to 450 additional children.

title: Access to Sanitary Wear for 1000 Girls in Matobo
description: The Project seeks to assist the adolescent girls and young women in both urban Bulawayo and rural Matobo disadvantaged by the COVID-19 pandemic and effects to contain it.  The project will provide each participant with 2 packets of 10 hypo allergic sanitary pads, 1 bar of bathing soap and 1kg of washing powder. In its inception the project will also provide each participant with a cotton washing towel and 2 cotton under pants.

title: Gift an Education ... be the agent of Change !!!
description: Chaithanya Mahila Mandali Non-profit, founded by an Orphan-Sex-trafficked survivor born again to change the fate with you, of the many Children and girls living/affected by Sexual Slavery in India( since 1999).CMM's home away home, takes care of such daughters of Victims, aimed at preventing them early from the possible risk of getting into the same life as mothers. At CMM's home they receive Quality Education, Psychological support, Self-Defence Skills, Food and Safety from neglect and abuse.

title: Healthcare Access to the Poor in Afghanistan
description: Make healthcare accessible to disadvantaged and poor Afghans who cannot pay for the care they need in a war-ridden country with under-resourced healthcare system.  FMIC believes that cost should not stand between families and the medical care they need.  The Patient Welfare Programme at FMIC helps treat patients who do not have the means with no or minimal cost through patient welfare funds. With the growing demand every year, the hospital needs support to continue this life-saving effort.

title: No walls 4 education! 3500 PC for Mexican students
description: Help us break down the walls of inequality in Mexico that prevent a fair access to opportunities by providing personal computing to 3,500 students in La Paz, Baja California, Mexico who have been denied a proper education due to the lack of technology in vulnerable communities.

title: Reduce Clashes Between Jaguars & Farmers in Belize
description: The jaguar is an iconic wildcat species in Belize. Jaguars are increasingly losing critical habitat and coming into conflict with livestock farmers due to expanding agricultural areas, including livestock farms. Ya'axche's previous collaborative work with farmers has yielded positive results to address this conflict. Ya'axche will assist 2 farms in becoming "jaguar friendly" and conduct 2 community/national workshops and outreach to preserve the harmonious coexistence of humans and jaguars.

title: Nourishing 1100 children of the Wixarika Community
description: We have 17 years working together, with the Wixarika Indigenous Community, delivering our nutritional complement, named "ONIformula", to 1100 beneficiaries, which is designed  especially for children with low weight and size. In addition, of the delivery we provide nutritional follow up to the children that receive it, we measure and weight them to know their nutritional state. Also, we diagnose and treat anemia, and give nutritional talks to parents to change alimentary and hygene habits.

title: Tote Me Home - Food for Kids!
description: Do you know that there are children in the United States that do not have enough food at home?  The families rely on the schools to provide the majority of their meals.  But what happens when they go home for the weekends?  The Collinsville Food Pantry has a program called Tote Me Home that sent 4,444 bags of food home during the 2017-18 school year with children who have been identified as food insecure by social workers.

title: Help Heal Children in Hospital - Jabulani Kingdom
description: "Laughter is the best medicine", particularly in hospital wards. Our Jabulani therapeutic clowns aim to relieve the stress and anxiety that children suffering from life threatening illnesses in hospital face. Through using arts-based activities, which include comedy, juggling, magic, mime & story-telling, our therapeutic clowns help restore and improve the mental, physical and emotional well-being of each life-threatened child in hospital.

title: Fire Emergency Response in Attica, Greece
description: This project will provide direct emergency relief to families affected by the recent Attica wildfires in Greece, by providing the means for volunteers to continue carrying out their physical work of rehabilitating fire damaged homes. Support to these families who have lost their homes and possessions is critical in helping to rebuild their lives.

title: Free Education & Mentoring for Mumbai's Slum Kids
description: At AXF, Mumbai's educated affluent interact with slum children who attend government schools that fail to deliver, to bring about transformation. 1600 children aged 6-18 years receive numeracy & literacy skills, life skills, aptitude testing & vocational guidance at 16 community-led learning centres across Mumbai. The resulting resource redistribution creates a more equal society and opens up opportunities for the underprivileged, enabling them to be gainfully employed and attain prosperity.

title: Urgent Relief to Flood-hit Kerala
description: Monsoon fury has once again descended on Kerala. Many areas, yet to recover from the devastation of the 2018 floods, have been hit badly, while some new areas, too, are affected. This project aims to provide urgently needed relief & rehabilitation support to people and communities affected by the flood, while continuing the programs already initiated last year.

title: Enable 60 Cambodian children to go to school
description: Imagine your parents asking you to work instead of going to primary school. This is reality for many Cambodian families whose children work in the fields or at home to help the family survive, missing weeks of school and being at high risk of dropping out entirely. SeeBeyondBorders' Conditional Cash Payments programme offers a lifeline to families, providing small payments conditional on attendance and bikes to encourage attendance, to make prioritising their child's education a viable option.

title: Life-saving primary care for 5,000 rural Rwandans
description: This project will enable OFH to train and equip a nurse to open and run her own clinic, providing quality healthcare that will transform the lives of 5,000 rural Rwandans by bringing healthcare within walking distance. Since 2012, OFH has been empowering nurses to run clinics that save lives through prevention and treatment of common illnesses. With your support, the new clinic will serve 7,500 patient visits per year. 2020 gifts will primarily fund new equipment needs for COVID response.

title: Build a senior center for 500 South Asian seniors
description: India Home plans to develop New York's first community center for South Asian seniors that would provide culturally sensitive and linguistically appropriate programs for South Asian seniors. This center, the South Asian Community Home (SACH), in NYC, will serve the needs of the growing South Asian senior population with culturally-specific programs, including a Creative Aging Center, Case Management Center, Social Adult Day Program for older adults with dementia and intergenerational activities.

title: Empower residents affected by the fires in Greece
description: Only hours after the fires, Emfasis Foundation streetworkers visited the local community, documenting meticulously the findings after talking with its members, in order to establish effective ways to empower them to withstand the tragic & sudden loss of property, job, and neighbors, the destruction of their natural environment. We have gathered cases concerning individual and families, and we empower them through employment (minimum 12 months), psychosocial support, community discussion forums.

title: TRAINING OF IT,INTERNET,SOCIAL MEDIA FOR THE YOUTH
description: This project will provide Training of IT, Internet and Entrepreneurship for the poor, marginalized & disability youth with gender equality. Trainees about  480 persons from five districts in Sulawesi Selatan, Indonesia. Duration of projects are ten (10)  months,  with eighteen hours per week & divided into several groups. The target of this training is the youth who have interests, desires, creatives & talents in improving their potential & skills to improve their better life

title: Lights On! Empower Kamarata with the Sun
description: In Eposak, we transform lives through sustainable tourism in unique, remote and underdeveloped tourism destinations in Venezuela. Lights On! is a project designed to provide solar power to the indigenous community of Kamarata (near Angel Falls - the highest waterfall in the world), in order to help them to be better prepared for tourism activities.  Let's start with the schools and the rural hospital!

title: Economic empowerment for tribal women -Role Models
description: The key objective of the project is to develop, train and empower hundreds of tribal Indian women from  Dadra Nagar Haveli & enable them to become self-sufficient through livelihood activities viz. Animal Husbandry, Organic Farming, etc. Capacity building training and access to market links will also be provided to ensure that Year 1- leading 40 super performers have the necessary resources and guidance of their supervisors to run a successful micro business and generate non agricultural income.

title: Rung Do Pakistan
description: The RUNG DO campaign brings an opportunity for individuals to play their part in contributing positively towards protecting our ecosystem! WWF-Pakistan and Call the Band, are collaborating for the country's biggest videographer collaboration that features the beauty of the country and its people. The videos highlight the diversity of Pakistan and encourages individual action to plant trees in cities and villages across the length and breadth of our homeland.

title: Kerala Flood Relief
description: The recent rains in Kerala state have resulted in large scale damage. Almost everyone in Kerala had been effected one way or the other by the devastating floods caused by torrential rains. Torrential rains, overflowing rivers and a series of landslides have resulted in death of 79 people in the state and thousands of people lost their houses and belongings. Still 13 districts are on red alert. Learning Links Foundation is in the process of extending help in small ways to mitigate the sufferings

title: Improve nutrition for 1000 children in Lukulu
description: Lukulu district in Zambia has 86% of people in the rural areas who solely depend on rainfed crops. Loss of food crop means loss of food and income and it severely  affects  some female headed households. Most of these female headed households struggle to have balanced diet for their children. This project gives out goats to vulnerable rural female headed households as a source for food nutrition and income to improve wellbeing of 1,000 children.

title: 10 school farms to feed 1,750 rural poor children
description: The rural primary schools in Uganda are often  overcrowded yet government does not provide lunch to children during school lunch time; hence poor performance, high school drop-out rates, high crime rates. The project will ensure the establishment of 10 school farms to feed 1,750 poor- hungry children during lunch time to support their education, develop entrepreneurial minds and skills in sustainable agriculture in Bukedea District.

title: Housing & Rehabilitation flood affected
description: Many states in India are battling floods and Kerala is especially affected with over 50,000 people needing immediate help. There is an urgent need for civic participation to bring timely relief to them.

title: Kerala Floods Relief Fund for 500 Poor Families
description: The 2018 Kerala floods were a result of the unusually severe amount of southwest monsoon rains. 35 out of 39 reservoirs in the state were opened for the first time in history. The calamity has has caused immeasurable misery and devastation. Many lives were lost.Hundreds of homes were totally destroyed and many more were damaged. For the first time in history, 27 dams in the State had to be opened. 70 deaths till August 16th.

title: Help Nicaraguans Affected by Political Unrest
description: Nicaragua is engulfed in a political conflict which is adversely affecting the poor borrowers we work with. People living in remote, rural areas of Nicaragua have had their businesses disrupted by road closures, products not getting to market, and school closures. WCCN is cooperating with a local microfinance institution to provide financial relief to its poor borrowers, to help get people back on their feet.

title: Empower Colombian leaders through higher education
description: All the population have the privilege of studying at many countries, however in Colombia most people don't have the opportunity to continue their studies and thus are not able to improve their quality of life and help others. That's why we are a foundation that bets on those young leaders who want to improve their knowledge to help their communities and thus contribute to make this country a better place, where study and effort are a mean to achieve great things.

title: Provide School Supplies for 2,500 African Students
description: This project will provide 2,500 students with school supplies so that they will be well-equipped to receive a quality education.

title: Give Hope to 300+ South Sudanese Refugee Women
description: South Sudanese refugees in Bidi Bidi camp, Uganda, are dependent on aid with few job opportunities. Despite the horrifying conditions that led these courageous people to flee their country, hope remains. An extraordinary refugee, Rose, has a long-term plan to create economic freedom in the camp for 300 women every year. This project funds machinery, materials, & training to kick-start Rose's embroidery business, an inspired vision that will provide vocational training and jobs for her community.

title: Educate a Girl in Kashmir
description: Pakistan is one of the few countries in the world with a rising illiteracy rate. In a country where 60 percent of youth are illiterate and only 1 in 3 women can read and write, HOPE has been working hard to reverse this trend. HOPE has implemented an innovative solution to helping girls in Pakistan's rural and remote areas such as Kashmir - HOPE home schools - whereby girls who ordinarily face multiple obstacles to obtaining an education are becoming teachers and role models in the community.

title: Equipping Hands for Effective Communication
description: The project will provide affordable high-quality physical and virtual on-demand sign language acquisition learning devices to hearing-impaired children and teachers through Interactive-Board Game devices, and a virtual mobile app. We endeavor for a just world that advances children's rights and equality for deaf children. With the aim that no child should be left behind.

title: Help Orphans from South Ukraine Find a Family
description: The project will assist 20 orphans from South Ukraine to find a new families by producing short and qualitative video profiles about them. The videos transmit an objective and comprehensive view of the child. The profiles would be promoted through social medias, mass media and the adoption communities in order to speed up the search in finding a family for these children. Your donation would change the lives of 20 orphans and would fill 20 homes with joy, love and happiness.

title: Help Orphans from Western Ukraine Find a Family
description: The project will assist 80 orphans from Western Ukraine to find a new families by producing short and qualitative video profiles about them. The videos transmit an objective and comprehensive view of the child. The profiles would be promoted through social medias, mass media and the adoption communities in order to speed up the search in finding a family for these children. Your donation would change the lives of 80 orphans and would fill 80 homes with joy, love and happiness.

title: Solar for Education
description: Solar for Education program is an initiative aimed at powering schools in rural communities in Nigeria without electricity with solar to enable the students read and do their homework at nights. The program will also train the students with skills in installation and maintenance of simple solar systems while providing educational benefits for students in learning about renewable energy and environmental stewardship.

title: Green Corridor's Learner Safe Space
description: Our charity provides support to young people who have special needs, who are more at risk of health problems such as obesity due to their special needs. Research shows they can learn better, improve their memory and alertness just by being well nourished. We want to be able to provide our learners with an all season space, adjacent to our kitchen, that provides a place to eat their healthy lunch, to go to when they are feeling stressed or anxious and somewhere they can learn vital social skills.

title: Empower Families of Children with Special Needs
description: Doman International helps children with special needs reach their full potential. By teaching parents about child development, Doman International empowers families to help their children. In the past, this team has only taught live conferences to families. Giving to this project will help take this life-changing information and put it online, so it can be accessed by all parents worldwide. This project will help parents help their own children - and help children get better.

title: Kerala devastated by floods
description: The southwestern Indian state of Kerala is facing the worst monsoon season since 1924, causing severe flooding and landslides. At least 364 people have been killed and more than 200,000 people have been displaced. ActionAid is responding immediately, including providing food, temporary shelter, reconstruction support, and health kits, for as many as 45,000 people. Will you help?

title: 3,000 Guatemalan Farmers Graduate from Poverty
description: We are a small, but impactful U.S. nonprofit that provides technical assistance and business training to help farmers graduate from poverty. SID's Guatemalan project will directly assist 3,000 coffee-farming families.   Every dollar contributed will help these farmers and their families build a sustainable livelihood. Please reference our 'Reports' page for more information regarding the success of our current program and our values of gender-equity and environmental stewardship.

title: Roots Community Market
description: Roots Community Market provides a variety of free nutritious foods and hygiene products to community members in need. We offer members a dignified way to shop for food by using a point system that encourages eating fresh produce and healthier versions of favorite foods, creating a non-stigmatizing food distribution method. In 90 days we have distributed 3,378 lbs of food to 320 people. We need your help to ensure the market remains a dependable resource for our most vulnerable Oakland residents.

title: Urgent SOS For Flood affected People - Kerala
description: #DoforKerala #KeralaFloods   Kerala is staggering under the worst floods in its history since the end of July. The devastating floods have paralyzed normal lives of people. IGSSS is on the ground, coordinating with State Inter-Agency Group (IAG) and Government of Kerala, providing the best assistance to the affected people in Wayanad district of Kerala. Let's all join together to Save Kerala - God's own Country, by generously donating to IGSSS in order to reach out to the most affected people.

title: Help Right a Wrong!
description: A number of trusting families have been taken advantage of by a dishonest service dog trainer and we would love to be able to help make their dreams come true.  These families, and more, have fund-raised and paid thousands of dollars for fully-trained seizure-response service dogs, only to have their funds taken with nothing to show or in some cases have received untrained service dogs. These families are defeated as it would be impossible for them to raise funds again in their own communities.

title: Emergency Relief : Flood Affected People in Kerala
