description: Incessant rains and massive flooding are rendering thousands of people across the State of Kerala, India homeless this year too. Hundreds of thousands of people are in Relief Camps. Rains are still lashing different areas of the state and people do require lots of help in relief camps with supply of essentials and long term interventions are necessary. Your help is needed to reach many who are affected.

title: Drawing a smile for disabled children in Bethlehem
description: Many children in the Bethlehem Refugee camps suffer from several different types of disabilities such as cerebral palsy, autism, west syndrome, down syndrome, speech disability, learning difficulties, and many more. There is a lack of support for them and their families in our area, so we are providing services to rehabilitate and improve their way of living and to achieve self-sufficiency. Ultimately, we want to draw a smile on their faces and boost their confidence for future hopes and dreams.

title: Giving skills to the needy and unemployed youths
description: Many youths have no trustworthy adults in their lives. The youth are the future generation of the world and thus equipping them with skills. Save a Life is committed to transform the youth into responsible persons. Save a Life believes in the potential of all children, as well as ensuring that the rights of all children as described in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child ("UNCRC") should be guaranteed to them. We rescue street children and train skills to the youth in slums.

title: Kerala Floods- Relief and Rebuild for 400 families
description: The Indian state of Kerala is facing the worst monsoon and causing severe flooding and landslides. As of 18 August 2018, Eight districts remain on red alert.  More than 324 people have been killed,  85,000 people have been displaced and more than 223000 people are evacuated and live in relief camp.  BASS India is responding immediately with local volunteers and wish to help at least 400 families with drinking water,  food supplies, clothing and  continue with rebuild activities. will  you help ?

title: Relief - Rehab supports for Kerala Floods 2018
description: Intermittent rains from beginning of August 2018 led to massive floods from 8 August in many parts of Kerala state including Idikki District. Around 2400 families are taking refuge in Adimali and Cheruthoni flood relief camps. Food supplies given from 9 August. Government is providing cooked food. They need new clothes, cooking vessels, 1 month food - stay family needs, water drums and educational supports for 600 school going Children.

title: Flood relief for Kerala, India
description: Kerala, a southern state in India has been struggling with floods for past 10 days, leaving people in couple of areas at the relief camps with no food, clothing and Shelter. Prime Trust is trying its level best to provide support whatever is possible from their end. We are eagerly awaiting to help those people with basic and immediate support.

title: Help 39 children get school supplies
description: This project will help provide scholastic materials to 39 most vulnerable in Manywa village who needs it most. Having noticed that many children in this village delay to return back to school after school holiday due to total lack of scholastic materials since they are highly needed at school at the beginning of the term. Many children go to school bare footed which makes them in a big risk of getting waterborne diseases. Also many girls do not settle in class due to lack of pads.

title: Caregivers 2 Breadwinners Sri Lanka- jobs for moms
description: In Sri Lanka, mothers of children with disabilities are usually limited to the role of caregiver, which severely limits the household's ability to earn much-needed income. Strong families with adequate resources can provide their children with needed support and thus keep them out of institutions. This project aims to employ such mothers by providing them with the training and resources necessary to create re-usable grocery bags to replace single-use plastic bags.

title: Nourish 1000 Malnourished Children 4 Cleft Surgery
description: Mission Smile nutrition team has supported 1000 cleft children in North east India and helped restore both health and smile of the malnourished children. Currently another 1000 patients are enrolled in the program. The Nutrition Programme mandates to provide free counselling, medicines & food supplements to such children but is not being able to due to paucity of funds. With help of kind donors  we plan to help the malnourished  children attain the perfect health for cleft surgery.

title: Educating dropout & out of school adolescent girls
description: Adolescent Girls Education Project will provide relevant and holistic education to girls who have remained excluded from school education. 50-60 girls will receive quality education belonging to poor economically background families majorly from minority and Dalit communities. 45-50% out of school/dropout girls will enroll into mainstream schools and complete their elementary education. 30-40% Girls of VIII to X grade will also get subject specific support & write their elementary exam.

title: Housing & Rehabilitation for Kerala flood victims
description: Over 2 million people are displaced from their homes, caused by one of the worst floods ever been seen in over 100 years.  The Torrential rains causing floods and landslides have taken the lives of more than 400 people. Warrier Foundation will provide rehabilitation and housing to the flood affected victims in Kerala including special attention towards children from orphanages and destitute homes by giving them shelter, food and basic healthcare.

title: Support Middaymeal for 5000 underpriviledged kids
description: Annamrita believes in providing children with the right nutrition to support their education.  We serve 1.2 million meals every single day, through our 20 kitchens across India. Our aim is to Promote Education One Meal at a Time by providing nutritious, wholesome, hygienic meals prepared in hi-tech kitchens which not only nourish the body but also nurture the soul. Our program is based on the belief that 'you are what you eat'.

title: Vacation Groups for Abused Children
description: This project will provide vital emotional, psychological and practical support during vacation periods for c.30 of Israel's most traumatized and neglected children. Sadly, some children in our care have no family or their home situation is too destructive for them to return during the holidays. Our programming and staff adapt to the specific needs of these children at such times, so they do not develop strong ongoing feeling of rejection, that can negatively affect them now and into adulthood.

title: Enhance Education of 400 school children in India
description: This project will prevent 400 disadvantaged students  from dropping out and becoming child labour. It will  provide them coaching, nutritional support, text book,  note book, pen , pencil, dress and facilitate them  through joyful learning. It will equip them with 21st  century skills  so that they will be interested in learning and get all round development through extra  curriculum activities.

title: Cashew  Processing Unit for 500 farmers
description: The Project focuses on helping Farmers to get better prices for their produces. Farmers lack technology and know how to process their harvest. Farmers sell Paddy 21$ per Quintal as compared to rice which is available at 60$ per quintal. In the same way Farmers are selling Raw cashew @ 145$ per Quintal and processed Cashew is sold for 1500$ per quintal. The project will enable farmers to process, package and market their produce and develop sustainable income practices.

title: Hope, Opportunity for 2,500 kids in Eastern Europe
description: War will have a devastating impact for children and families across Eastern Europe economically, practically and emotionally. Over 2,500 vulnerable children will be given hope, opportunity and security with initiatives to prevent family breakdown, support the abandonment, transform lives of those affected by disability and offer firm foundations for those severely impacted by war and living in precarious conditions.

title: Kerala flood relief program
description: Mass floods has damaged severely the state of Kerala. Torrential rains, overflowing rivers, dams and a series of landslides have resulted in death of 354+ people in the state and thousands of people lost their houses and belongings. Monsoon rains continue to batter many districts of Kerala. CHHASE extending humanitarian relief to the affected families.

title: Educate 1000 kids on Conscious Consumption Brazil
description: Edukatu is a free access website already available to educate for conscious consumption. Based on Edukatu platform this project will raise awareness of 100 teachers and 1000 students from 6 to 15 years old from Brazil public school through the completion of a knowledge acquisition path on natural resources as a way to change the behavior of teachers, students and surrounding community towards conscious consumption as a way to contribute to sustainability through the change of lifestyles.

title: Keep 100 girls at school in Rwanda-GirlsEducation
description: The Rwandan government enacted a policy that provides all Rwandan children with Twelve years of fee-free education. Yet, girls are still dropping out of school at far higher rates than their male counterparts. YOMADO hopes to eliminate this gap through its threefold approach, which pairs girls with mentors, organizes savings and loans groups, and implements community community score cards to keep girls at School

title: Support Students Creating Peace Culture
description: In support of the change-making force of young people, PEAC Institute, a partner organization of ICAN, will take part in a youth forum on the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons in Auckland, New Zealand from December 4 to 7. PEAC understands the necessity of youth involvement in high-level security discussions which implicate the safety of their future world. The participants will include young people from the Pacific Islands and international relations students from the US and Europe.

title: Harvesting honey saves forests and lives
description: The coastal villages of SW Thailand were once home to thriving mangrove forest ecosystems that preserved the shoreline, sequestered carbon, sheltered fish, and sustained communities that relied on small-scale inshore fishing. Today, these communities are among the poorest in the region as mangroves are lost to aquaculture, logging, and urban expansion. MAP will help 4 communities develop sustainable sources of mangrove-based income through harvesting high-quality honey from mangrove flowers.

title: AWARENESS CAMPAIGN FOR CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING
description: This project on awareness campaigns on cervical cancer screening is centered on promoting and building the capacity of 3,000 females in Northern Province of Zambia, within a year so that they get to understand their medical status on cancer as early as possible so that any intervention to safe life and seriousness of the disease is done earlier.

title: Enable an encounter with a rare Pterocarpus Forest
description: The project greatly expands the open-air classroom role of an extremely rare 51-acre Pterocarpus Swamp Forest at Palmas in Humacao through the creation of an app that provides information to visitors about the Forest's functions, flora and fauna, and the slow process of recovery from Hurricane Maria, as they meander along the 3/4-mile, elevated boardwalk that winds its way through the Forest interior. The project also provides new interpretative signage within the Forest's facilities.

title: Help a Thai student achieve their dreams
description: Kids outside of Thailand's urban centers face a bleak future due to poor quality education, with under resourced schools and poorly trained teachers, leaving them trapped in poverty with little hope for a better future - a situation that is only getting worse. By delivering 21st century learning directly to students, providing resources to disadvantaged schools and training teachers on high-impact practices, we're transforming education in Thailand so that all kids can achieve their dreams.

title: Educate 89 inner-city youths and adults in Panama
description: The students of our evening and night school hope for a different future than the one offered in the streets of Curundu. These students were not able to finish middle/high school due to environmental factors such as poverty, parental ignorance or negligence. You can help brighten their hope of a better life by encouraging them through academic scholarships and securing a meal for the day - let them know that out there in the world somebody else believes in them. Together we can!

title: The Clock's Ticking: Save 100,000 lives in Kerala
description: Unprecedented rains in Kerala have wreaked havoc. As the rains retreat, scores of dead bodies of humans and animals appear, sewage and drinking waters mix. People are clearing the waste, debris and dead bodies, exposing them, their families and others to contagion. A second wave of havoc is underway through outbreak of cholera and typhoid. Swasti and CMID will provide safety kits for the critical 10 day period that begins now. We want your help NOW to prevent these outbreaks and save lives.

title: A WATER WELL for the Community of Bretagne - Haiti
description: This project will build a Water well  in Northern Haiti, providing water for a village where there are orphans traumatized by the continuous popular revolts, earthquake 2010, hurricane Matthew, causes for which most of them are orphans. In that Village 7.000 people live there and they don't have water and even drinkable water. Later will be possible to supply drinking water to the village with the construction of a dedicated point and equipped suitable machinnery for potabilization.

title: Help Rebuild Kerala
description: Monsoon has ravaged Kerala and has wrecked havoc across the state with over 350 people dead, lakhs of people rendered homeless, over 3 lakh people in relief camps and and an estimated 20000 crores (200 billion) worth damages.  This project is aimed at providing emergency relief support as well as help to provide long term rehabilitation in terms of help to rebuild homes, provide furniture, provide medical and psychological help, help to get back lost documents and in short to help rebuild Kerala

title: Save Dogs from Gas Chamber Executions in Japan
description: Tens of thousands of dogs are killed each year in Japan, many of them through "dream boxes," execution by gas chamber. This project will provide funding for Peace Winds Japan to continue rescuing these dogs and caring for them in our facilities. Take part in saving these dogs from a cruel and inhumane death.

title: Empowering Young Women in Nairobi's Slums
description: Our Project aims to provide skills training and job placement for 2,000 poor and vulnerable Adolescents Girls and Young Women(AGYWs) from the slums of Nairobi.We provide integrated training to beneficaries and subsequently place them into employment as nannies,house-helps,cleaners and tea-girls where they earn a decent salary.

title: Flood Relief for Kerala and Karnataka
description: The torrential rain caused havoc in Kerala and parts of Kodagu (Karnataka) leading to heavy mud flow due to landslides, opening of the shutters of the dams causing heavy flow of muddy water through medium and large streams resulting damage on the sides of the streams/rivers. Most of the families have lost all their belongings as they were evacuated and moved to the relief camps.   Immediate requirement is to provide food and basic support to family and children

title: Save 1,000 Youths from Stress & Addiction in India
description: We INSPIRE, EDUCATE & FACILITATE Indian (esp. U.P.) Youths & Children to live Value Centered - Stress & Addiction Free Lives by --- Over 50 Workshops & Seminars - to impart values and techniques --- Our 6 Hostel Facilities, Counselling & Scholarships - to provides free accommodation, meals and study facilities with a hygienic, encouraging and caring environment with positive association for needy youths --- Yearly 3 Skill Development & Career Guidance Programs - to help professional growth

title: Expand the Impact of South African  Black Leaders
description: We will share the stories of 6 black community leaders who are making a difference at the grassroots level in Johannesburg. Through short biographical videos, articles and photography, as well as targeted marketing and social media exposure, we will highlight their work and help facilitate partnerships and collaboration that grow their impact locally and nationally.

title: Saving Children's Lives in Sierra Leone
description: 1 in 8 children dies before their fifth birthday in Sierra Leone, with 161 deaths per 1,000 live births. A primary reason for high child mortality rates is an under-skilled and under-resourced workforce. Welbodi Partnership works to upskill and empower local workers to ensure long-term impact on child health outcomes in Sierra Leone. We do this by recruiting expert Paediatric Nurses and Doctors to train and mentor the local workforce and provide critical clinical support.

title: Send 10 orphans to a vocational training in Kenya
description: This project will  support and empower 10 young adults orphaned by  HIV/aids through vocational training for six month in Kiambu sub-county Kenya. The training will provide the orphans with carpentry, hair dressing, tailoring, painting and driving skills. This will enable them become self-reliant and support their families.

title: Educate/Rehabilitate 130 children- Northeast India
description: Bethany Society aims to provide safe accommodation and opportunity for quality inclusive education to 130 children and young persons with disability belonging to marginalized and remote areas of Meghalaya, India where they are deprived of access to education or skill-training. These children come from extremely poor & deprived backgrounds. The goal thus is creating equal access to opportunities for education and employment for these 130 young people with disabilities living in Bethany Society.

title: CareerSupport&information access to 10,000TZ Youth
description: The programme implements a career hub (physical venue plus e-space) for career planning that provides 10,000 Tanzanian youth with access to quality information and mentorship. It delivers training and facilitation on 21st-century skills to 120 public schools, while its online platform enables more than 150,000 young people to make informed decisions about career planning and access consultation services. Through its physical space, it provides on-site mentorship and coaching to 3000 youth.

title: Seeds and Support for School Gardens Worldwide
description: School gardens grow vegetables and also grow future leaders to counter hunger and poverty in their communities. In many locations, a garden-supported school lunch is the only healthy meal of the day and motivates parents to keep their kids in school.  SPI programs give vegetable seeds for 20+ vegetable varieties. SPI's partner schools become hubs for providing seed, seedlings, and training to kids' families. With your help, we're growing gardens in 9 countries!

title: Shelter Homeless Orphans of the crisis in Cameroon
description: This project will provide the first-ever shelter and a comprehensive package of care & support to a cycle of 100 of the thousands of homeless children orphaned and displaced by the ongoing arms conflict in the English speaking part of Cameroon, with the aim of reuniting them with their families in the short and long runs.

title: VOCATIONAL TRAINING FOR 58 TEEN-MOTHERS IN HOMABAY
description: This project will equip Teenage Mothers from families of deceased people due to HIV/AIDS with vocational training and skills development which will enable them to become self-reliant in life, to evade the of sexual exploitation, lack of proper integration in families and and unemployment among others. It is also geared towards making the Teenage Mothers become tools of grate change  among young girls and fellow youth in the community of Kanyabala in Homabay/ Kenya.

title: Vocational training in rural Burkina Faso
description: We offer vocational training to youngsters in the rural areas in Burkina Faso. With a technical degree these youngsters will be able to open their own workshops and earn their own money. In that way they will be self-supporting and less dependent on aid from abroad.

title: Support Learn Fresh and NBA Math Hoops
description: NBA Math Hoops is a community-based education program serving students who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM, helping them build fundamental math and social emotional skills. This project will support NBA Math Hoops program events through the 2019-20 season, bringing together students for competition, STEM and cultural learning, and fun educational experiences.

title: Give the learning power of play to 1000's of kids
description: Our project focuses on engaging 1000's children, from 30 primary schools across the Pafuri Node of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Conservation Area in Southern Africa. By engaging children through soccer we are able to harness their energy, create safe spaces to allow them to discuss and learn how to tackle social issues affecting them and the environments in which they grow up in, from HIV, gender equality, poaching and substance abuse.

title: India Flood Relief
description: Heavy rains and flooding have forced families from their homes. Emergency support needed!  Villages are submerged underwater, and families have lost everything. They have an immediate need for rice, oil and vegetables.    Can you please provide much-needed relief aid right now?  They are hungry, thirsty, and were forced to leave their homes to escape the floodwaters.  Please help these flood victims in India today!

title: Protect 500 Disabled Children From Sexual Abuse
description: This project will protect children living with disability from sexual abuse .ICCF research gave a high rate of sexual abuse on children with disability .Child abuse is a national tragedy taking the lives of one to three disabled children every day.The project will help to protect and give all round support in Awareness -  Raising Campaign, Education, Training,Security,Legal and Development for  500 disabled children in Lagos state.They will benefit from psycho-social workshop/training programs .

title: Garden to Market- Helping the poor to grow food!
description: 'Garden to Market' is a project aimed at helping people living in poor communities in Pattaya, Thailand to grow their own food to feed their families and also earn an income through selling produce at market. These trained growers are then empowered to set up community gardens in slum areas around the city empowering more families and overcoming hunger.

title: Relief Fund for Disasters occurred in Japan 2018
description: The record-breaking torrential rain which began to fall on July 5, 2018  has caused significant and widespread floods damages in western Japan. Also on September 6, an earthquake with a seismic intensity of 7 with Hokkaido epicenter occurred. Many dead people missing, houses collapsed and landslides occurred.We have begun an emergency relief fundraising effort, with the aim of supporting emergency rescue operations and reconstruction.

title: Support School Education of Children in India
description: Poor quality of education in government schools where economically weaker students study leads to unsatisfactory "learning outcomes". We at LOKMITRA 1) Enhance capacity & motivation of teachers through peer learning & hands-on support 2) provide apt learning materials to improve teaching 3) Capacitate School Management Committees, leading to improved learning. This appeal is to enable LOKMITRA to be synergetic in impacting 1000 school directly and indirectly in four districts of Uttar Pradesh

title: Gift 40 babies with the best start in life
description: The first six weeks after birth are the most critical. You can help save lives by giving a new mother the essential things like a bassinet, cloth diapers, blankets, a container for clean water, and soap. Your gift also provides regular visits from our midwife and social services. Our tuk-tuks are also available to take our women and babies to medical facilities (ambulance services are very limited in Cambodia).

title: Promoting women rights in rural areas
description: Rural women are key agents for achieving the transformational economic, environmental and social changes required for sustainable development. But limited access to credit, health care and education are among the many challenges they face, which are further aggravated by the global food and economic crises and climate change. Their basic rights are ignored compared to their fellow men. Empowering them is key not only to the well-being of individuals, families and rural communities.

title: Deliver information and access to end-of-life care
description: End With Care, is a free educational resource that provides and promotes awareness of end-of-life issues. We gather and present information assisting individuals, families, and caregivers with end-of-life needs find answers, resources, care, and support.

title: Save 1 million lives
description: DTI helps people waiting for an organ transplant to receive the gift of life! Your donation empowers doctors and nurses from Africa, Asia and South America to implement and operate organ donation programs in their respective countries to rescue millions of lives, help people avoid lifelong dialysis and dramatically reduce healthcare costs. Giving your loved ones a second chance in life is our passion. We'll save one million lives by training thousands of medical teams on how to do it!

title: Make a dream for a street child in Uganda
description: The project addresses social, emotional and economic needs of 50 streets children education issues by developing a Community Volunteer mentorship model (training, financial literacy, food security). It provides beneficiaries with the resources and knowledge to initiate their own projects based on dream drawing/family plan to meet the basic costs of attending school. It promotes team building, collective action, builds confidence and social skills for vulnerable children in Kabale District Uganda

title: EMPOWER WOMEN WITH DISABILITIES IN TANZANIA
description: TEPDGHO intends to work help women with disability in Tanzania so that to empower them economically. We have worked with some groups of women with disability to do some productive works. They have proved to be committed as long as the work they do tailors their disability.  TEPDGHO provided different supports to the women with disability and they engaged effectively and productively in those areas. The only challenges they face is resources and the community support.

title: Provide Clean Water to 270 Refugees in Uganda
description: Bugema Community Based Child Based Organization plans to provide clean and safe drinking water to 270 refugees who hail from the current civil unrest in South Sudan and Democratic Republic of Congo flooding across the borders into Uganda. This project is working towards saving refugees from suffering from typhoid, malaria, Diarrhoea, cholera and filariasis as a result of drinking dirty water and bathing in dirty water.

title: Education to empower girls and women
description: We will train, coach and mentor 500 underserved head of household unemployed women to create and develop their own businesses in the food industry. Cocinando Suenos our experiential education program, equips women with the needed entrepreneurship, management, culinary and personal development skills to launch and propel their own social businesses in the food industry, doubling their income and significantly improving their livelihoods and that of their families.

title: New Lease For Husky Rescue KZN, ZAR
description: We are deeply passionate about the rescue and rehabilitation of the Siberian Husky. Sibes are one of two breeds in trouble world wide. Next to the pitt bullterier they are the most overbred, misunderstood, surrendered and sadly most euthanized breed of dog in shelters as a result. Media programs like Game of Thrones are singularly responsible for this situation. And yet they are one of the most amazing breeds with an extensive history dating back as far as 3000 years according to some experts.

title: Build School Library & Storeroom for 650 Students
description: This project will construct a library addition to an existing school classroom building in northern Uganda. The library will provide a secure place for 650 primary students to access literacy and technology support.   The room will provide storage for 1500 books, 3 solar-powered laptop workstations, plus a small storage area .  It will also fund the purchase of 100 Uganda textbooks. The school is in northern Uganda in an area that was devastated by a 20 year old civil war that ended in 2006.

title: Believe. Challenge. Grow.
description: Nor Luyce is a 3-phase mentoring program that aims to empower adolescent girls in Armenia, ages 13-18, from orphanages and low-income families to lead self-sufficient lives. Nor Luyce strives to build a community of strong, thoughtful, creative young women. We encourage our participants to work hard and dream big and help them reach their desired personal and career goals.

title: Access underprivileged youth with reading material
description: This project will access the youth with fewer opportunities with books for reading and researching as well as promoting reading culture among them. UYSTO plans to ship the books donated to us by books2africa and put in place a container that would be modified for a safe  place to sit in and read. The youth will be accessed  with readily available library services and hope that this will address the question of  "The best way to hide something from Black people is to put it in a book" by Malcom X

title: DRUG ABUSE CAMPAIGN IN 300 HIGH SCHOOLS IN NIGERIA
description: The Campaign for drug abuse will engage approximately 300,000 youth in Nigeria, 11 to 16 years of age, to reduce their involvement in high-risk and criminal behaviour. The project is based on Life Skills Training program with additional cultural and recreational components. The  Skills Training program is a school-based prevention program that targets drug abuse among youth. It helps youth build the knowledge and skills they need to resist peer pressure and will also strengthen positive attitude

title: A New Chance for 50 Refugee Families in Serbia
description: The Project plans to create a social enterprise that will integrate refugees in Serbia on the supply side as distributors, suppliers or employees, supporting their potential to secure sustainable monthly income for themselves and their families. By providing training, basic tools and equipment, as well as building up capital and social network, this project will economically empower and socially integrate at least 50 refugees in 6 municipalities in Serbia.

title: School fees for 500 Djugu Displaced Children
description: We have 500 displaced children who do not attend school. The money granted by the donor will help to pay school fees for these children. These children fled the ethnic conflict from Djugu territory between Hem and Lendu since February 2018.   - They are in Bunia and don't have any assistance as their parents lost all they had during the conflict: gardens, livestock and all properties. They need good will people to continue with their studies.

title: Support Kerala Flood
description: Kerala floods claimed overall death toll to 370, more than 7.8 lakh people are in relief camps, 8000 houses have been washed away and around 26,000 are partly damaged.  The rain has ripped the roofs off homes, uprooted trees, brought down power lines and many areas are underwater. People have lost everything they had and are now struggling just to stay alive. A number of Immediate Response Teams have been deployed all around to carry out the rescue work but still the situation is far from over.

title: Love barter, education for 150 Colombian children
description: Laudes Infantis plans to adequate three communitary centers and offer school kits; as well as library spaces, homework support, art, culture, psychosocial assessment for 150 children (and their families) in vulnerable or forced displacement conditions in the southern periphery of Bogota. In order to accomplish this, parents must generate co-responsibility with the services received with love barters (commitment to build strong affective bonds in the family).

title: Help us to build a Mexico in Peace
description: Otro Tiempo Mexico plans to build the National Observatory of Peace and Human Rights, composed by people and civil organizations defending Human Rights, to attend the crisis of violence in the country and the multiple violations of the rights of victims and groups such as women, indigenous peoples, LGBTI + population, people with disabilities, elder people, cultural minorities, among others, providing legal and psychological support; and monitoring public policies on Peace and Human Rights.

title: Supplies for Orphans at Reteti Elephant Sanctuary
description: Reteti is home to the first community owned elephant orphanage in Africa.  Designed to rescue and release orphaned and abandoned elephant calves, whilst creating much needed benefits to the Samburu people that live alongside them, the Reteti Elephant Sanctuary is the representation of  communities standing up united for wildlife, in recognition of their inherent value.  Silent Heroes will visit the Sanctuary in October to hand deliver supplies.    Thank you for being a Silent Hero!

title: Kerala India Floods
description: Over 300 people have died from massive, historic flooding in India's Kerala State-and hundreds of thousands are now displaced as farmlands, livelihoods, homes, and more have been destroyed. This is the worst flooding in the area in nearly 100 years.  Your partnership is critical! Together, we can scale up efforts to help families who have lost everything. Please join us in support of those devastated by flooding and landslides, and know your gift will support urgent relief efforts.

title: Rural Educational Advancement Project (READ)
description: Bulla Afya Primary school is located in Bulla Afya location, Mandera County, Kenya.  Until early 2018, the 25,000 residents of Bulla Afya location did not have a school. This project will build three latrines, dig a shallow well, construct an underground water tank & supply 30-three seater desks to Bulla Afya Primary School. Also, the project will provide school uniforms  & storybooks to 100 orphaned & vulnerable girls in addition to 8 hours of remedial lessons per month for two years.

title: Give the Gift of Education to Bolivian Girls
description: The Helping Hands Project provides support for marginalized and disadvantaged youth, especially girls at-risk and in extreme need, in the department of La Paz, Bolivia. With help from the Project they can access a high school education and post-secondary training. By providing school materials, school fees, transportation, uniforms and lunches, as well as counseling, the Project enables our girls to finish a secondary education and go on to post-secondary training.

title: Fight plastic pollution in the bay of Cartagena
description: This project seeks to generate positive changes in environmental habits of dwellers in the island of Tierra Bomba in order to improve their quality of life and help ward off plastic pollution at sea. How? By empowering local organizations, strengthening environmental education, providing technical assistance for the implementation of "sustainable actions" leading to better use of resources, conservation of ecosystems and biodiversity, reforestation, better residue management and recycling.

title: End #metoo stories in Swaziland by mentoring men
description: Women and girls in Swaziland are suffering and dying everyday from physical and sexual violence at the hands of men. Much of this is avoidable. This project will mentor and educate 600 men and boys in Swaziland to be peaceful and respectful men. Through 3-day intensive mentorship camps, participants will be encouraged to challenge negative social and cultural values that view women as sexual and expendable objects or as less than equal. Let's put an end to #metoo stories in Swaziland.

title: Scholarships for 20 sustainability young leaders
description: The world face many socio and environmental challenges like loss of biodiversity and forests, high pollution and diseases. Young students in Brazil have transformative ideas for these challenges, but many don't have opportunity to develop it due to lack of resources to seek more knowledge and guidance. ESCAS - School of Conservation and Sustainability, is a place to them. With a Scholarship Fund, we will benefit students with education for sustainability to them change the world.

title: Child Safety Protection and Youth Development
description: - Focuses on the prevention of sexual violence,  corporal punishment and bullying, conviction of perpetrators, and the creation of safe spaces. _ Focuses on the many challenges that young people are confronted with throughout South Africa. - Creating space for young people to engage with issues affecting them  - Target beneficiaries - young people from 12 to 22 years

title: Help 1100 Students affected by Flood in Kerala
description: Kerala floods has claimed 400 lives while displacing lakhs of people. People lost their belongings; houses damaged very badly ; health condition of many , especially old people are very bad. Tiny tots & older children are left heart-broken to see that their favorite storybooks, school bags etc. have been washed away. The project will support schools, help students to meet their educational needs and also families to buy cattle or fishing net or boat or to start small business.

title: Sustainable Livelihoods Project
description: Helps poor communities to work their way out of poverty and supports self-help groups (SHG) to establish income-generating activities. It has already reached 3 346 families, and through the efforts of SHG achieved cumulative savings of over R5.1 million. A ripple effect of this achievement is that families who participated in the programme were able to support over 50 young people to attain a tertiary education and graduate in areas of education, social work, engineering, and nursing.

title: INCLUSIVE YOUTH DRIVE AT BINDURI IN GHANA
description: The project objective is to challenge the problem of socio-political-ethnic violence which has become more entrenched among the youth in Ghana as a result of social process. It is to prevent and counter narratives by providing platforms of discussion through an interfaith/socio-cultural exchange platform strategies on the essence of peace and security for development in the selected communities to educate, sensitize, train and empower the youth in rural/urban communities.

title: Muslim American College Scholarships Project
description: School's In...  And MALA is gearing up for college scholarships - with your help!  The Muslim American Leadership Alliance (MALA) is dedicated to leadership through integrity, and as such provides a platform for people to share their individual stories and to speak for themselves. MALA nurtures emerging community leaders, and unites Americans of all backgrounds. MALA is open to choice and creed, and embraces free expression, gender equality, and pluralism as cherished universal ideals.

title: Teen Suicide Prevention events in 30 US Cities
description: Saving Lives. This project provides 30 suicide prevention and mental health resource events in conjunction with campus and music festivals across the United States.  These upbeat events, staged in unique settings allow us to "reach people where they are". This nontraditional approach to suicide prevention de-stigmatizes talk about mental health by providing one-on-one peer support interactions, mental health resource kits, all in a environment that allows true, meaningful connection.

title: Kerala Flood Relief Project
description: In late July 2018, severe flooding affected state of Kerala due to unusually high rainfall during the monsoon season. It was the nastiest flooding in Kerala in nearly a century. Over 375 people died within a fortnight, while at least 956 people were evacuated, mainly from Chengannur, Pandanad, Aranmula, Aluva, Chalakudy, Kuttanad & Pandalam. All 14 districts of the state were placed on high alert. Project aims to help over 1,500 families will increase as we grow here & as we gather resources.

title: Better Health and Safety on Ugandan Construction
description: Accidents on construction sites result in many deaths and major injuries each year. Improvements in construction health and safety have been successfully implemented in many countries, with significant reductions in accidents, so why not Uganda?  World Action Fund plans to work with Industry, Government and Educators to promote improvements to the standards of health and safety on construction sites. This is the first NGO to take on this challenge. Method proposed is education, mobile App. task

title: Support Multiple Sclerosis People
description: After Hurricane Maria destroyed Puerto Rico, there was no water, electrical power and no communication. After that we started to help people with MS that have been affected by Hurricane Maria in Puerto Rico by sending them portable mini air conditioning that will help them keep cool in these hot temperature. We want to continue supply a portable mini air conditioning to each MS patient. The hot temperature is one of the enemy for the Multiple Sclerosis condition. Please help us.

title: Saving Viable 24-Week Preemies
description: For two decades Angels In Waiting have recruited hundreds of nurses-foster parents and saved countless childhoods. As well as creating a California state law to protect our growing medically fragile foster care population and do so through the hearts and hands of  our devoted nurses. The founder's son Sammy, a 23 week gestational age preemie-who is now 17 years of age, has inspired our charity to reach-out and protect our viable 24+ week gestational age preemies who are about to be aborted...

title: Feed and educate orphaned and needy kids in Kenya
description: This project will help feed and educate more than 1000 kids in the slums who live in the orphanages and the poverty stricken surrounding slums and also very needy widows and their kids, providing school supplies and building classroooms. It will benefit kids and widows  without discriminating them based on ethnicity, race nor religion.  All funds raised through this project will strictly benefit widows, orphaned and needy children and not any other cause

title: Donate to THE GRAND CHILDREN EDUCATION FUND UGANDA
description: The biggest number of orphans in Uganda are left under the care of their grand parents, This is mainly caused by HIV/Aids, With the financial difficulties these elderly grand parents are characterized with, its quite hard for them to take these little ones to school  THE GRAND CHILDREN EDUCATION FUND UGANDA is set to have this problem solved by taking the children left under the care of the most disadvantaged older persons to school.  "EDUCATION is a right to every child"

title: UPCYCLING HANDMADE PRODUCTS BY 100 KENYAN ARTISANS
description: This project aims at reducing the effects of water hyacinth weed that has invaded Lake Victoria (Kenya) making fishing and water navigation impossible thereby affecting the livelihoods of families which depend on the lake. We aim to utilize the water hyacinth weeds to make functional products which we shall sell and in the process create employment for 100 artisans at the shores of Lake Victoria.

title: A House for Cats and Kids
description: Given our experience on rescue, care, and re-homing, of unwanted, homeless and injured dogs and cats, we would like to work helping kids with special needs by bringing them together along with cats that have endured difficult conditions.  Our project intends to provide the facilities for a group of children with special needs to interact with 30 rescued cats. Our main objective is to build a shelter in the Bogota Savanna where cats and kids can interact and play.

title: End domestic violence via business opportunities
description: This project aims to empower 300 women in the rural areas of Afghanistan where financial problems are the main source of domestic violence. Majority of the poor families sells and marries their daughters to rich old men which have resulted into many suicide cases. Your donation will provide these women with significant and effective business training in tailoring, livestock farming, embroidery and handcraft skills and start-up loans to stand on their feet, have their own earnings and not beg.

title: Transforming The Lives of Children in Cartagena
description: We started this project nearly three years ago with the goal of transforming the lives of 50 children in one of the poorest neighborhoods of Cartagena. Since then, we have distributed over 10.000 meals and provided a host of educational, recreational, and health-related support activities. Now we are looking to build new facilities to expand our services to the 200 children that are most vulnerable to malnutrition, domestic violence, gangs and drugs.

title: Special Education With Therapy to 100 MR Children
description: Special education basically refers to "Educational programs and practices designed for students- who are with mental, physical or emotional disabilities.  In Ujjain  ,M.P Viklang Sahayta Samiti is running   Special School Manovikas    with a noble mission to cater those students who have special educational needs due to Intellectual or multiple disabilities . Along with  special education we also provide therapeutic facilities .

title: SAVE HIGH RISK TEENAGE PREGNANCIES IN KENYA
description: This project will provide clinical outreaches to high-risk pregnant teenage girls without clinical facilities to reduce maternal mortality in Rachuonyo North Sub-County in Western Kenya.

title: Go Green and Drink Clean
description: Through this projects Hand Pumps / Water wells be installed in remote areas of Tharparkar, Sindh Pakistan. 20 Hand Pumps will be installed out of 20 Hand Pumps 10 Hand Pumps will be deep and 10 will be house hold level hand pumps to help the poor communities who travel 2-3 Kilometres to fetch 10 litres of water bucket.

title: Educating one person, saves many from HIV
description: The purpose of this project is to educate 1500 adolescents and their teachers in rural areas near to Medellin about HIV/AIDs and how to prevent it. The proyect Includes: 1) Set up workshops to address the social and medical aspects of HIV 2) An Art Exhibitions with pieces collected from urban and rural artists 3) A video that includes the important aspects to prevent HIV. 4) A traveling educational exhibition that reinforces the concepts transmitted through the workshops.

title: "Help working children return to School"
description: Previously, in the mountainous area of the center of the state of Veracruz, Mexico, coffee was the main agricultural production of the region. The entire population depended on its cultivation and processing. However, since the 1990s, the prolonged aromatic crisis has dramatically changed the physiognomy and living conditions of the population, which are already deteriorating. Unemployment and the process of migration of men and young people to the United States and large cities of the country

title: GVI Emergency Relief Appeal for Kerala Floods
description: Kerala is facing the worst floods in 100 years with dams opened and all rivers in spate. Heavy rains continue and over one million people have now sheltered in around 3000 relief camps, 50,000 houses have been destroyed, and more than 410 people have lost their lives in what could be said as the worst monsoon in nearly a century!

title: School 135 poor Cambodian children to prosperity.
description: Two schools for vulnerable, disadvantaged children from poor families that have operated for 10 years in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap, Cambodia need donors.  Administered by a registered NGO of 25 years, Salvation Centre Cambodia (SCC),  the schools teach English, Maths, Agriculture, Music to 135 students for free. Without these schools, the children will have reduced opportunities to pursue further education, get well-paid jobs and help lift their families, communities and country out of poverty.

title: Educate 175 Underprivileged Children in India
description: This project will help provide quality primary education to 175 out of school children in the state of Uttar Pradesh in India, who have limited resources & facilities to receive good education. Access to quality education at primary level is crucial for these students as it builds a strong foundation and motivates them to stay in school for higher education. More than 80% children educated under this project are first members in their family to go to a school and more than 50% are young girls.

title: Give 300 Zimbabwean Children an Education
description: This project will give 300 rural Zimbabwean children a quality education and a brighter future. Breakfast, Masuwe and Sekebelo Primary Schools are severely under-resourced. Full classroms where teachers often instruct multiple grades in the same classroom. Basic education materials are severely lacking. Parents cannot afford to pay school fees and the few teachers often work unpaid for months.  Help us provide the support and basic necessities to give these children an education - and a future.

title: Life-saving surgery for 24 children in S.E Nigeria
description: This project will provide life-saving surgery to at least 24 babies and children from disadvantaged families in Ebonyi State, S.E. Nigeria. AMURT Assisted Health Centre's are receiving increasing numbers of patients with life threatening conditions as their reputation for high quality care grows. Many of the cases are babies and children whose families are impoverished and unable to pay for surgery to save the life of their loved ones.

title: Restore the hope of 1000 refugee women and girls
description: Restore my hope will provide Group and Individual Trauma counseling services to 1,000 conflict affected refugee women and children living in Adjumani Refugee settlement of Uganda. Adjumani settlement currently hosts over 240,000 refugees, 65% being women and children below the age of 18 years. 60% of the women and girls living at Adjumani have either been raped, tortured or lost loved one, leaving them extremely traumatized. This project will improve on their mental and physical health.

title: Access to clean water for 400 vulnerable malagasy
description: This project will enable provision of safe water in vulnerable households living surrounding protected areas in Madagascar. Two hand pumps boreholes will be installed with a budget of $5,994 to boost the livelihood of 400 people. One borehole costs $2,945, has a capacity to pump between 20-35 liters per minute and serve 200 people. This project will improve well-being, reduction in women and children's burden collecting water. Starting with just $14.98 you can boost the livelihood of 1 person

title: A dignity kit,a lifeline to girls' stay in school
description: The project seeks to provide dignity kits to 1600 adolescent girls in 3 public primary schools in Pap Onditi. The kit contain 3 sets of under wears, soap, a wash cloth and 2 packets of sanitary towels. The project will provide educative sessions to the girls on menstrual hygiene, protection, adolescences, sexual and reproductive health and gender based violence, linking them with local health service providers, thereby restoring the dignity of the girl and enabling her to focus on learning.

title: Helping Parents and Babies through Prenatal Tests
description: Around 1,200,000 women in Japan become pregnant each year. More than 95% of women have prenatal scans, which can potentially find fetal defects, causing a great deal of anxiety and uncertainty. In fact, there are more than 200,000 women is choosing abortion every year. We offer non-directive information and support to parents before, during and after prenatal screening; when they are making difficult decisions. It can also give babies the opportunity to have a fetal therapy.

title: Create 4,000 UK Young Leaders from Deprived Areas
description: This project will provide life changing opportunities for 4,000 young people experiencing high levels of disadvantage across the UK, including at risk youth and refugees. Our transformational programme is underpinned by service learning, and develops the leadership skills in young people, by providing them with the opportunity to learn from, and meet one of our 14 inspirational Nobel Peace Prize winners.

title: Literacy = Libertad.
description: We believe that literacy provides freedom for expression and creativity to teachers, students and the whole community.

title: Support Orphans to access education for four years
description: Centre for counties research and development agency plans to support need total orphans to access secondary education who hail from the most poorest sub-county of Awendo -Migori Kenya, by paying secondary school fees for four years. This project will support 15 total orphans to access secondary education for four years and make them better leaders of tomorrow.

title: Robotics for young women with disabilities
description: Help empower girls with disabilities through robotics and STEAM training.  Join the Fundacion Omar Dengo to help young women with mild cognitive disabilities or who are deaf or hard of hearing in Costa Rica, move forward and succeed with robotics and STEAM courses. Help us improve girls' lives despite the challenges they face, and give them the opportunity to use technology to improve their logical thinking skills, creativity and collaborative work.

title: Stop Violence Against Children Worldwide
description: ISPCAN unites over 1000 Child Abuse and Neglect professionals from more than 100 countries to create a diverse and the multi-disciplinary community from the fields of psychiatry, psychology, medicine, nursing, social work, education, legal, law enforcement, faith communities and government.  ISPCAN reaches over 6000 professionals each year dedicated to preventing child abuse, neglect and exploitation. ISPCAN's vision is that all children will live and grow in rights-respecting environments.

title: Replanting fruit trees in Brazil
description: The Fruit Tree Planting Foundation is planting thousands of fruit trees and provides horticultural training in the severely deforested municipality of Mococa, Brazil to create a sustainable source of healthy food for families while reforesting the region. Trees are planted at schools and community centers as well as distributed directly to families. Harvests provide quality, fresh nutrition to local families, and the trees fight climate change and provide critical habitat for local wildlife.

title: DACKANA EARLY CHILDHOOD CARE AND EDUCATION
description: DACKANA is providing care and early childhood education and support to young children of adolescents who have been victims of early marriages and unplanned pregnancies, living in one of the poorest areas of Kabwe in Zambia and who have been given a second chance to go back to school but have no one reliable to care for their children during the period they are at school and will provide free sanitary towels to these adolescent mothers.

title: Hong Kong Pride Parade 2022
description: The Hong Kong Pride Parade promotes equal rights for and anti-discrimination against the LGBT community. More than 12,000 people joint the parade to support LGBT+ equality in HK in 2018. Due to the pandemic and current situation of the Hong Kong society, we are unable to hold a rally in the past 2 year.   This year's Hong Kong Pride Parade will continue to gather us together in the form of a Rainbow Market that every corporate, organization, and participant can celebrate as one.

title: Sponsor a child today
description: Sponsor a child today, so that no one will be left behind. This project aims at sponsoring 12,000 vulnerable children to access health care and quality education by 2025. These children live mostly in underserved and rural communities in Ghana who often are subject to child abuse, and become targets for child trafficking, labour, prostitution, and streetism. To help RAHE GHANA's intervention, you can sponsor a child for $39 a month or $468 per year.

title: Food, Livelihood, Nutrition Support for Women
description: The project will provide food, livelihood and nutrition support for 700 poor women and their families so that they are able to live with dignity.

title: Save headwaters of Yerbal Highlands and forests
description: Please support the construction of an Agroecological Center oriented to the protection of the biodiversity of the fluvial systems of the second most important reserve of fresh water in South America. The high basin is at risk from mining and forestry. The architectural design of the Center will be a bioconstruction of the world-renowned architect Gernot Minke and will be located in the heart of the first protected area of Uruguay that currently preserves several species in danger of extinction.

title: Returning spider monkeys to Belize's forests
description: Charlie, Duma, Mattie, Mel and Penny - all rescued from the illegal pet trade. This project will return them to the wild. These five endangered spider monkeys, now a close knit family, will soon be released as part of Belize's first structured reintroduction, establishing a new population in the north east forest. This ground breaking approach will result in a replicable model for future spider monkey releases in Belize and the region, increasing long term viability of this species.

title: Help rural farmers in Africa gain access to land
description: Seventy-five percent of the world's poorest people live in rural areas where land is a critical asset, but more than half these families lack either access to land or a secure stake in the land they farm. Landesa partners with governments to provide policy and implementation support to strengthen the land rights of millions of men and women in rural African communities. Your donation will support our activities across Africa, including targeted projects in Liberia, Tanzania, and Zimbabwe.

title: Therapy Services for 80 Cambodian Families
description: Children in Families is a local Cambodian NGO and exists to place vulnerable children in loving families. The ABLE (Accepted. Belonging. Loved. Empowered.) project will ensure that 40 families caring for Children with Disabilities (CwDs) in Cambodia are equipped and supported to address their special needs through home and community-based therapy, medical support, equipment support, nutrition support, and family education.

title: Empowering Survivors of Sexual Abuse to Heal
description: Sacred Innocence International (SII) empowers survivors from all kinds of sexual abuse to overcome their past, stop the abuse from continuing, and tap into their full potential through their 14-session program HEAL. HEAL is a healing curriculum for adult men and women survivors that our organization offers through online, over the phone and peer-to-peer support groups. HEAL is also available in book form and will soon be available through an interactive online website.

title: REDUCE POVERTY FOR 1000 POOR  WIDOWS IN GICUMBI
description: This project targets to reduce poverty level for 1000 poor rural widows families in Gicumbi District in Rwanda, The poverty levels in the district are high compared to the national levels, with 49.3% of the population under poverty line and 33.9% of the population in extreme poverty, national levels being 44.9 and 24.1% respectively. The project intends to use two interventions likely (i) Promotion of small livestock for 1000 targeted widows (ii) adoption of  horticulture and fruits plants.

title: Provide Medical Care to Bangalore's Street Animals
description: Since 2013, Charlie's Animal Rescue Centre (CARE) have rescued and rehabilitated over 10,000 of Bangalore's orphaned, abandoned and abused animals. However, the number of distressed street animals in need continues to grow. With your support,  we hope to continue to protect street animals across the city. As a specialty hospital for street animals in need, your generous donations will help us ensure that these animals receive the best medical attention possible.

title: Leave no Girl behind: Education is our right
description: The project will support girl children from 5 primary schools in Masama ward due to lack of better toilets,  facilities and sanitary pads hence most girl children drop out from school during menstrual days. Through better washing and toilet facilities construction, training in basic sanitation for teachers and students and providing skills for making  local sanitary pads using local materials will be   cost less  for majority to afford and will consider  care for health, environment for girls.

title: Educate 300 marginalised children in Bihar, India
description: The Knowledge Hub for Education and Learning (KHEL), run by the Diksha Foundation provides 300 first generation learners; girls and boys, between the ages of 5-18, from socially and economically vulnerable communities in central India, with a creative learning resources that, in addition to supporting their literacy needs, is empathetic, violence free, nonhierarchical, and vibrant.

title: Auxiliary Therapy for children with special needs
description: Tamahar is a strong believer in the power of auxiliary therapies as an aid to the core therapies. Auxiliary therapies are proven to have a strong positive effect on the complete wellbeing of children with special needs and together, they hasten the child's recovery. The therapies provided at Tamahar are -   1. Physiotherapy  2. Occupational Therapy  3. Speech Therapy 4. Yoga   5. Music     This campaigns aims at raising funds for this program for 1 year.

title: Richmond Community Centre
description: Richmond is a small Karoo town in the northern cape.  This project started as a soup kitchen feeding children in the community as the unemployment rate is about 85%. Due to unemployment, poverty faces many children daily in Richmond.  With the support of individual donors and strong community leaders, we are able to feed over 200 daily. The Community Centre has become a safe space for many children to be themselves and to take part in the educational activities the organization had to offer.

title: IMPROVED DAIRY FOR 1,000 KENYAN YOUTH AND WOMEN
description: The Kenyan dairy sector is unique in the world. It is characterized by small scale farmers, mainly women in rural homes rearing 1-3 cows each.The sector's future is gloomy in that many youth do not see it as a profitable venture due to various challenges among them quality, quantity, markets and lack of basic equipment.To ensure sustainability and improve family food security, income and livelihoods, Future Focus Development will build capacities of 1,000 youth and women.

title: Ending Poverty by educating 122 Ethiopian Children
description: This project  in Arba Minch, Ethiopia will help fund 122 children, who live in extreme poverty, get an education, medical care and food.  These are children who have been identified by the local govenment as the poorest of the poor.  Without this assistance these children would be forced to beg or resort to other means in order to eat and assist their families.

title: Building the new normal of 300 adolescents in Peru
description: The Experiencia Visionaria is a collection of three complimentary programs that bring quality education to schools in rural areas of the Cusco Region, so that adolescent students who have had their education affected by the pandemic, commit to their personal development and take action to fulfill their visions of success for themselves and their communities.

title: Buy palm oil plantation and bring back the forest
description: An Indonesian oil palm plantation is up for sale and we have a golden opportunity to buy this land and restore the lush forest that once stood there. This will provide shelter for orangutans and other endangered animals, and create a vital asset for local communities. By donating, you will help return this land to the forest and wildlife to whom it once belonged.  Our plan is simple. Working with our local partners we wil we will buy and restore this 890 acre site to its former natural glory.

title: Creating a haven for kids through football and art
description: Santa Marta is located on the Caribbean coast in Colombia. The region is marked by 50 years of military conflict and 32% of the population live in poverty (less than 90 US$/ month). More than 80% of the 7,000 people living in the neighborhood "La Lucha" have been displaced by violence. Schooling and other opportunities to make productive use of free time are missing. This makes the population vulnerable to joining gangs and to teenage pregnancies.The rate of domestic violence is alarmingly high.

title: Updated: Restore Eyesight to 20,000 Villagers
description: RestoringVision will transform the lives of 20,000 people around the world who struggle with uncorrected vision impairment and are considered by the UN to be "ultra-poor." Through our network of nonprofit partners we will reach those who live in remote areas where glasses are not available. Near vision impairment is a growing critical health and socio-economic problem with one of the easiest and most cost-effective solutions - a simple pair of glasses.

title: Train & Kit 500 Gombe women to crochet for income
description: With rising unemployment and little opportunities for income generation, we are supporting women with training and start-up materials (the kit) to start crocheting for income. With the security challenges in Northeast Nigeria our beneficiaries can sell their products within and outside the zone through a physical shop and online marketing. There has been tremendous interest and a waiting list of women and girls waiting to join the program.

title: Save Earth through yoga & meditation in Costa Rica
description: 203 children from schools in high-risk communities in Costa Rica invite you to be part of the answer to save Mother Earth. Through yoga and meditation, they are learning and teaching to create conscious, healthy and sustainable lifestyles. To scale the project around the country, declared Champion of the Earth 2019 by UN, yoga and meditation were declared of public interest; the project was declared of educational interest; and, the Ministry of Education signed a Work Plan with Gaia Foundation.

title: Improve the life of 270 rescued dogs in Venezuela
description: Updated project for 2021. We have 270 rescued dogs under our watch in Venezuela. Due to the extreme situation of our country, several years have passed since the last time we were able to provide more to them than just food and basic care.  We are asking for your help to change their everyday life with simple things that every dog should have.

title: EMPOWER 60 FAMILIES WITH SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE
description: Puente a la Salud Comunitaria aims to empower 60 small-scale farmers in Oaxaca, Mexico, providing training, tools, and agro-ecological farm inputs to allow them to grow amaranth and other crops in a sustainable and natural process. Amaranth is considered a superfood because of its nutritious properties, resistance to climate change and potential market value. Thus, they will produce healthy food that prevents degrading their soils and water sources and also reduce certain health risks.

title: Fund Life Saving Maternal Care for Women in DRC
description: Hope for Our Sisters plans to establish a Maternal Health Fund at the Wellness Clinic in Goma, DR Congo. This fund will provide local women access to life saving, critical maternal care (cesarean deliveries) when the women and/or families cannot pay. These funds are effective in preventing devastating birthing injuries (fistula) and protecting women and children from death during childbirth. Women in the DR Congo should be able to choose health and hope rather than suffering and death.

title: School Buses for Yazidi Refugee Children
description: Four years after terrorist attacks on the Yazidi people, villages remain shattered and insecure. Returning soon is not an option for the 100 families GHNI is working with. Children of these families living in Northern Iraq haven't been able to go to school for 4 years. The government has opened a school for refugees, but many of the camps are too far away. GHNI is raising funds to purchase minibuses that a local organization will own and use to transport the Yazidi children to school.

title: Accelerate into the New School Year with GGRF
description: This September, help the GGRF Athletic Scholars in Ethiopia get back to school!  We're raising $30,000 to invest in 120 girls in the Mecca of running in Ethiopia - Bekoji. Your investment will help fund a full year program that integrates education, life skills, safe spaces, athletics, savings groups & entrepreneurship to holistically address the challenges facing girls. Join Jason & Trent on their journey to running the NYC Marathon & empower 120 women & girls to achieve their goals with GGRF.

title: Support Safe Haven for LGBTQ Iraqis
description: The LGBTQ community of Iraq faces persecution and discrimination, including threats to their safety or lives, because of their identity. Youth Speak plans to relocate LGBTQ community members from across Iraq into safer areas within the country, provide safe housing and ongoing case management services for them to ensure their physical and emotional wellbeing. Funds will be spent on rent for safe housing, medical and psychological support, and to help those relocated get on their feet.

title: Break Near-starvation Cycle for Congolese Farmers
description: Micro-farming project in remote Kafubu Valley, Democratic Republic of Congo, will increase corn production above current starvation level by teaching 250 subsistence farmers best practices . Top quality hybrid corn seed, fertilizer, insecticide, and guidance by professional agronomists is provided. Profits from sale of corn provide families better nutrition, money for school fees, healthcare, and repayment for seed and fertilizer, thus providing funds to serve more families the next year.

title: Empowering 3000 women in Kenya against injustice
description: To create income generating activities for 500 women in Kenya Kilifi County, Kanamai sub location and educate 3000 men and women against women injustice. The project addresses gender based violence that mostly comes as a result of poverty and cultural practices that adversely affect women in the area.

title: 600 Youth Volunteers Find New HIV Cases for Less
description: One Tent Health partners with local grocery and convenience stores in Washington, DC's highest-risk neighborhoods.  We provide free pop-up HIV screening through a canvas tent, screening kits, and passionate student volunteers who deliver HIV screening and PrEP navigation to low-income, under-served communities at one-third the national average cost.   We empower young people to get actively involved in their communities, both through the volunteer program and by hiring young innovators.

title: Empower Malawian villagers to make a difference
description: This project will connect student leaders from the US and Malawi to work towards better health and education among 2,000+ villagers across two villages in Blantyre. Since our goal is to build LASTING relationships, students partner with village leaders to tackle each village's needs on a case by case basis, finding unique and sustainable solutions to the problems they face.

title: Support Children with Rare Hip Disease
description: Nearly 40% of rare disease families borrow money to pay medical bills. Legg Calve Perthes, a rare childhood disease, is triggered by a  loss of blood supply to the hip, and produces a painful limp and chronic inflammation in the joint. Many children require surgery and equipment in order to heal. As adults, they are prone to degenerative osteoarthritis. Chronic pain, potentially lasting from childhood into adulthood.

title: A barefoot run to support flood victims of Kerala
description: Kerala has just seen its worst floods in nearly a century, with several animals stranded and left to fend for themselves. This is a special appeal on behalf of these animals that we are trying to help give a second chance.  Thousands of animals have been rescued and help will be needed for a long while when the spotlight fades and others leave. That is when it is most needed; when disease sets in and food runs out. This effort is a fund-raiser that will help re-home several pets from harm's way.

title: URGENT HELP to preserve fresh water spring
description: "Protecting water spring" is our initiative to save and recharge fresh water spring providing drinking water to 30 families in HP, North India. These springs were perennial source of fresh water for residing population and local wild life. In recent times they have turned seasonal where few have even dried out. Their importance towards natural biodiversity cannot be measured. Under this project we will protect identified springs located in forest for a community using holistic approach.

title: Educating Migrant Brick Kiln Workers Children
description: The project aims to provide an innovative educational model to enhance the literacy and mathematical ability of migrant brick kiln worker's children (about 600) in Chaksu area, near Jaipur (Rajasthan). In order to address the special educational needs of migrant children, as they have no consistent access to education, the Brick School model has been piloted over 17 sites. We are requesting funding to continue and expand our program so that it serves larger numbers of migrant children.

title: Healthcare Support to 450 Destitute Indian Elderly
description: Healthcare is a major concern for the destitute elderly in India. Agewell Foundation has identified over 5000 destitute elderly who urgently need healthcare support and proper food. Agewell Foundation will provide a range of healthcare equipment to destitute and bedridden elderly including: wheelchairs, walkers, adult diapers and food packets to destitute and elderly living in slums across India.

title: Donate to end Dependence for Refugees
description: Refugee Empowerment International is an independent non-profit organization. We support projects that provide opportunities for refugees to lead an independent normal life while staying near home and their loved ones. We ensure that the positive impact of all funded projects reaches beyond its primary beneficiaries creating a ripple effect that allows refugees to build sustainable communities in the long term. Projects that we fund address a broad range of sustainable development goals (SDGs).

title: Life for at-risk unborn babies in Pakistan
description: This project aims safe child-birth at our hospitals, of women living in urban slums of Lahore and at risk of maternal and infant mortality by unskilled birth attendants.

title: Rehabilitate 350 disabled children in south India
description: ADD India facilitates rehabilitation of 350 children with disabilities in rural areas of Karnataka and TamilNadu, India. Children with severe disabilities are given physiotherapy through regular camps and art based interventions through home visits. Parents are trained to continue the therapy at home. In addition, ADD India conducts camps for assessment, skill development and building self confidence of children, ensure they are enrolled in schools and receive entitlements from the Government.

title: SHEudyami-livelihood for 240 women entrepreneurs
description: This Project will provide a sustainable Livelihood to 240 marginalized Girls and women of 18-35 age group by Vocational skill training of Sewing in 18 months. Women's technical skills in the areas of commercial stitching and tailoring will build up and well train and serving the market by their technical skills. They have undergone through 95 days or 380 hours. The aim of this initiative is to equip these women with advance technical and entrepreneurial skills to contribute apparel industry.

title: Strengthen 100 Vulnerable Households in Calabar
description: This project will strengthen and empower 100 women who are primary caregivers in vulnerable households in Calabar, Cross River State with the required knowledge, skills, inputs and financial habits to facilitate their exit from extreme poverty as well as providing an operational structure for sustainability.

title: Provide care for 25 battered girls in Argentina
description: Hogar San Jose Home provides shelter, food, emotional support, education and love to more than 100 girls that go through our Home during the year. A judge has taken them away from their homes because they were sexually abused and battered by someone in their own families. The safety and support the girls receive in Hogar San Jose helps the girls break away from the abusive pattern in which they grew up.

title: Laundry Training Centre for 48 Disable Person 2019
description: The project's purpose is to promote economic and social growth by supporting young persons with disabilities to successfully integrate into commercial life.    This project is to mainstream the recruitment of young people with disabilities by highlighting the business case for hiring them by recognition of their abilities and skills.  Following completion of the training and once in employment, laundry graduates will receive ongoing support from Job Coach as required.

title: Tailoring skills  to 50 youth in Kampala, Uganda
description: The project shall equip the Somero Uganda's Community Youth Information and sports corner with tailoring and knitting machines and other equipment. This shall be aimed at providing vocational skills training in tailoring and knitting to 50 out of school youth in Nakawa division, Kampala Uganda. The youth shall receive a six months training which shall include a month of field practicum in a fashion and design shop. The training shall also include business management and entrepreneurship skills.

title: Clean and Safe Water for Better Health
description: Unfiltered water is at the origin of several Hydric diseases and has a negative impact on longevity in rural areas. This project will install water filtration equipment in 3 rural communities. This equipment by nanofiltration will allow the target populations to no longer worry about the source of the water. This system can destroy 99.999% of germs, bacteria, and other microbes instantly.

title: GIRLS: MENSTRUAL ,SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH
