description: This project will support Global Peace Foundation Philippines' emergency response efforts for hundreds of families affected by Super Typhoon Mangkhut in Sanchez Mira, Cagayan Province in the Philippines. Each family will receive emergency supplies (food and medicine), water purifier, and solar lantern to assist them as they recover and rebuild.

title: Helping People In Need In Iraq-Mosul-Ninavah plain
description: after liberation from isis villages surrounding Mosul have been liberated. The number of individuals residing and beginning to reconstruct their lives in newly liberated villages increases almost daily. Living in areas that are so severely damaged presents many challenges. so these families need all kind of help like start new projects to get support and start their life back  to sustained the life providing food and education services  and helping women and girls that survive from isis crimes

title: YouMeWe Language in the cloud-Philippines
description: We have rolled out www.nightzookeeper.com software as a language platform to connect children in Japan with children in other countries over the internet. We have started a lab in Boracay, Philippines given a tablet to a fellow NPO focused on early childhood development in Jakarta, Indonesia, set up a lab in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia as well as a refugee camp volunteer center in Samos, Greece.  Our goal is to connect the children using the software.

title: Emergency Response to Typhoon Mangkhut
description: Typhoon Mangkhut, locally known as Ompong, made landfall in the Philippines on September 15. As the strongest storm across the world in 2018, the typhoon reportedly produced waves reaching almost 30 feet high, caused excessive flooding, and resulted in more than 40 landslides. International Medical Corps is deploying an emergency advance team to the affected areas to rapidly identify the most critical needs and reach those most affected by this devastating typhoon.

title: Zero Hunger Project
description: Our project is geared towards ensuring that all people can have at least a daily meal in the communities where we operate in Africa. Our centers will provide and serve meals for less fortunate. Furthermore, the project will also collect and distribute cloths, household items and food staples for those who cannot afford to visit the center. The volunteer team will be divided into those who prepare the food at the centers and serve people in need through our Zero Hunger Project.

title: Oxfam's Relief Response to Typhoon Mangkhut
description: Oxfam is working with its local partners to respond to the devastation caused by Typhoon Mangkhut that made landfall on September 15th in the Philippines and brought with it high winds and torrential rains. The destructive force of Typhoon Mangkhut affected over three million people. Oxfam and its partners are working to restore access to safe drinking water and emergency shelter.

title: RAISE A YOUNG PIG FARMER IN SOUTHERN NIGERIA
description: This project focuses on a young struggling pig farmer in Southern Nigeria who despite all odds of family neglect decided to start a pig farm on borrowed Piece of Land. It aims at assisting him to secure adequate land for farm expansion, introduce him to experts who will educate him on new and improved stock management practices and ensure that he assist in raising interested Pig farmers with the assistance he has received.

title: Support GK USA Relief Efforts for Typhoon Mangkhut
description: Typhoon Mangkhut (local name, Typhoon Ompong) hit the Philippines on Saturday, September 15, packing rain and winds of up to 165 mph. Northern Luzon island was hardest hit, affecting 250,000 individuals.  Gawad Kalinga's Philippine operations team mobilized as early as Friday, preparing evacuation shelters and food for the displaced. $10,500 will feed 5,000 people for a week. Damaged roofs will be repaired at $250 per home, while farms and fishing boats can be repaired at $800 each.

title: Typhoon Mangkhut Relief
description: Typhoon Mangkhut, locally known as "Ompong", crossed over northern Luzon causing heavy devastation in its path.   Over 270,000 in 30 provinces are affected by the storm.  About 57% or 154,185 individuals are housed in various evacuation centers  and need assistance. Reports show massive flooding in 79 areas. World Vision is responding with emergency relief supplies and assistance in Cagayan province. Your gift will help provide immediate relief to children and families impacted by this storm.

title: Food  and Shelter for Typhoon Mangkhut Survivors
description: In September, 2018, typhoon Mangkhut delivered destruction in the Philippines, killing an estimated 60 persons and more than 105,000 homeless.  The main areas hit by the typhoon are the most productive farming lands in the Philippines, are now under water. This will drive up the prices of rice and corn which have more than doubled in 2018-19. We are conducting emergency relief services, providing food and water to thousands of families. We also provide shelter materials, hygiene and medicine.

title: Support the BRIDGE Registry
description: BRIDGE (Basic Registry of Identified Global Entities) aims to revolutionize social sector information sharing. The social sector is a complex and critical web of organizations that play different roles in solving society's greatest challenges. In order to fully understand each organization's activities, impact, funding, and more, we must be able to firmly differentiate one organization from another and easily piece together the dispersed information about them.

title: Mercy Corps Responds to Hurricane Florence
description: In the wake of Hurricane Florence, one of the strongest storms of the year, Mercy Corps has team members on the ground in North Carolina to assess the damage from the storm and determine the biggest needs of the hardest-hit communities.

title: Send 250 sexually abuse girls to school
description: The project is design to take 250 girls hawking off the street, who on daily basis are being exploit sexually in other to sell out, ki through enrolling them in schools, provision and supply of adequate books and learning materials and paying them little stipends to encourage them remain in school.

title: Empower Costa Rican girls in technology & robotics
description: Our Project "Ellas programan" is an initiative that is based on the need to offer opportunities for exploration in STEM areas to girls in Costa Rica.  According to studies in the country, out of every 10 graduates in these areas, only two are women. This alerts us and motivates us to open empowerment spaces for women in technology so that they have opportunities for professional and economic growth.  We provide workshops in robotics and programming to girls and young people 4 years old onwards.

title: Child-Centred Education for 400 Children in India
description: Gramin Shiksha Kendra (GSK) promotes child-centred education, fostering interactive education environments. Underprivileged children in rural Rajasthan, India are encouraged to ask questions and enjoy their education. Your donation will support 400 first-generation learners across 11 villages near Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, attending 3 Uday Schools run by the community.

title: JA-Arconic "Sustainable Green Leaders" Program
description: The Sustainable Green Leaders program is a semester long program, which is designed for students who are 10-12 years old. The program will foster responsible citizenship by teaching 280 primary school students about environmental protection and sustainable development, through classroom activities that will explore the balance between energy development and city construction. The community that program serves is Kunshan, Jiangsu Province and Arconic will actively support the community growth.

title: Assistive devices for Flood Hit Kerala
description: Beginning of July 2018, severe floods affected the south Indian state of Kerala, due to unusually high rainfall during the monsoon season, causing floods and landslides.  Over 483 people died and displacing thousands. Our job is to improve the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the poorest communities those who lost their mobility aids in the floods.  Our objective is to provide assistive aids and appliances.

title: Train young Colombian women for a career in STEM
description: In June 2023, unemployment for young women in Colombia between 18 and 25 reached 22.9% and YOU can help us reprogram this reality!    Makaia's Bootcamp offers women from vulnerable contexts hands-on technical and vocational training in code and programming to find employment in tech, and overcome the gender IT gap. Help us improve the economic prospects of 100 women by enhancing their chances of getting sustainable, high-paying jobs in the IT sector.

title: Repurposing Toys for Low Income Kids
description: Since 1998, Go Green Toy Foundation has directly tackled two very important issues in the Dominican Republic: environment and poverty. Our model is directed towards creating and repurposing toys for low income kids through the use of recycled materials. This has expanded to tutorials, trainings and seminars, so that these kids can be educated regarding environmental preservation. Funds collected will be used to educate kids, get storage space for donations and materials to produce the toys.

title: Switchback Cyclery
description: Switchback is a retail and service-focused, community-oriented local bike shop.   We are also a non-profit Employment Social Enterprise with the mandate of creating meaningful and fulfilling employment opportunities for vulnerable people in Toronto. Our employees all have significant barriers to employment, including: chronic poverty, long-term unemployment, a history of homelessness, mental and physical health problems, and addictions.

title: Affordable Housing for people with Disabilities
description: We are faced with more people with disabilities becoming homeless due to a lack of affordable housing. Unless & until housing is treated as a human right rather than a privilege disabled individuals will continue to be at risk due to lower income & rising rent prices.  Addressing the root issues of affordability in the greater community, the disparity between rental prices & disability payments, & the serious lack of sustainable income opportunities for those who need flexible accommodations.

title: Save lives & ease suffering of people in crisis
description: Doctors Without Borders delivers emergency care in more than 60 countries around the world.  We supply free medical care in ongoing crises situations throughout the world. With your support, we can react to emergencies as soon as they occur and give high quality care to those who need it most. Rehabilitate hospitals & clinics, assist victims of violence, war or armed conflict provide clean drinking water, battle epidemics, feed malnourished children, respond to natural disasters & much more

title: You Are  Hearts Of Gold!
description: Hearts of Gold has over 10 years of service under our belts. We began by providing direct services to vulnerable individuals and grew into an organization that strengthens the skills of nonprofit leaders through education and mentoring and fundraising. Hearts of Gold has the honor of partnering with nine community organizations, and also direct beneficiaries. working on education, selfcare, acquiring skills to find jobs and much more

title: BRING SMILES TO KERALA FLOOD AFFECTED CHILDREN
description: Children are back to school without Essential school kits. Their loving school kits, clothes, foot wear etc. washed away by massive floods. This project will provide school bags, note books, pen, pencil, eraser, sharpener, geometry box, foot wear, clothes, blankets Etc to 1000 children. Support their dreams by contributing these urgently required school kit and other materials.

title: Support 200  AIDS Orphaned Children in Uganda
description: This project will build  an orphanage Center in Kasanda County in Mubende District in Central  Uganda,  to provide Basic needs  and social support services  to 200  AIDS Orphaned Children affected by  absolute Poverty, HIV/AIDS as a result of  civil  Wars  and  on and off immigration.

title: Help Provide Food to Children with Special Needs
description: In India a child born with special needs are presumed to have a life of dependency. For the poor this situation is extreme. The children with special needs are considered to be a financial, mental and physical burden The project aims at providing nutritional meals to Children with special needs attending educational services at Save The Children India that offer holistic interventions of catering to Nutritional and health needs, academics and extracurricular and employability skills training.

title: Gift Sound To Hearing Impaired Child In India
description: Dhvani (means sound in english) -Early Intervention Centre is comprehensive project of Save The Children India aims to reach out to young hearing impaired children between 0 to 3 years of age. Created with an aim to provide quality service to hearing impaired babies from all strata's of society. It not only provides early intervention services to poor and needy children but also facilitates interventions of providing  good quality hearing aids and cochlear implant surgeries.

title: Peace and reconciliation through Rugby in Israel
description: Using rugby to build trust and respect with school children of different racial and religious backgrounds in Israel

title: Children's Heart Surgery Program
description: If you want to make a life-changing, life-saving difference for a baby, child or other Vietnamese, Vets With A Mission Children's Heart Surgery Program is an opportunity to do so. Vietnam vets return to the country, specifically to Thua Thien Hue Province the third most bombed and shelled during the war, to sponsoring heart procedures for economically disadvantaged families. Since 1989, fifty-four Vietnamese the majority babies, children or adolescents have been recipients of heart operations.

title: Provide Diagnostic Hearing Evaluations for Infants
description: We will purchase an Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) system to become a Diagnostic Center and provide specialized hearing testing free-of-charge to uninsured infants identified as having possible hearing loss. We will serve 30-50 infants annually from under-served areas of Washington, DC who are at risk of having untreated hearing loss. Currently there are only three clinics in the city that provide diagnostic testing for infants, which leads to long wait times and delayed intervention.

title: Stand To Educate an African Girl Child
description: Jackie is a 19 year old young woman whose father died when she was four years old.  Jackie's mother abandoned her later.  Unfortunately, Jackie was not able to attend school when she was growing up and therefore can not read or write.  Our academic assessment team placed Jackie in a Grade 2 education level.  Because of this lack of education as well as her history, she experiences a lot of stigma in the community.  St. Jerome Emilian Academy accepts between 10-20 older students every year.

title: A Christmas Wish; From Calgary to Cuenca
description: Imagine spending a Christmas with out basic essentials like bread or sugar. Simple things, like toothpaste & shampoo are considered a luxury, especially when putting food on the table is a challenge. This Christmas YOU can change this for an Ecuadorian family. Your gift of a Christmas "Canasta" full of staples such as lentils, rice, beans and toilet paper or the gift of Candy Bags for children, (or both!) will ensure there are many relieved sighs and grateful smiles this Holiday season

title: Feed The Children
description: In Bangladesh, undernutrition continues to be a serious public-health problem. Almost 41% of Bangladeshi underprivileged children are underweight. Since 2007, JAAGO Foundation has been responding to the urgent needs of underprivileged children in Bangladesh through nutrition and education. Let us stand together and give these children a basic human need. Your generous donation can change a child's life forever.

title: School Rehabilitation & Maintenance Program
description: A big part of our efforts in Nicaragua is to make sure that all local children from pre-school through to the end of high school have access to local education. To support this effort we have either built or restored 7 schools over the past 9 years but there is still work to be done. Each year we choose one community and one local school to focus our efforts on. Once completed we take on a maintenance and support role with the school ensure that it remains in excellent condition.

title: Feeding minds and tummies of 230 children
description: The Murakaza school is a beacon of hope for 230 children and their families living in a slum outside of Bujumbura, Burundi. As well as teaching them literacy and life skills, they are mentored to integrate the national school system to continue their education. An important development was when the school began to offer a daily nutritious meal - often the only meal that the children will receive a day. In addition, the school grows its own food, also helping to employ local people.

title: Giving Smiles Has Never Been Easier
description: Everyone needs a place they can call home. For some that is a house, for others it is a safe place that fosters a sense of community and belonging. Often times, nonprofits are a safe haven for children looking for comfort. We are honored to work with 4 excellent organizations that are serving 300+ youth in need. By supporting these institutions at their core - their staff, their volunteers, their programs - we ensure that more children receive the support and education that they deserve.

title: Community Arts and English Programs
description: Waves of Hope has been providing local English classes three times a week to children and adults since 2009 and since 2016, Waves of Hope has been sponsoring a three-part arts program that has been running classes twice a week for music, visual arts and dance.

title: Sprout of Love! Care Children in Community Network
description: Underserved children in Taiwan are lacking resources and suffering from low self-confidence. The Mustard Seed Mission devotes to provide an all-round development for them. With a Community Social Welfare Network, to support vulnerable children in Taiwan in 5 aspects: Safety Needs, Physiological Needs, Social Belonging, Self-Esteem, and Self-Actualization, providing equal chances for them to get educated and empowered; gain courage to overcome the future obstacles, walk stably and independently.

title: Gift of Education - Learning Can't Wait
description: We've established 79 primary and 7 secondary schools in remotest areas of Bangladesh where previously there was no government school. Our students have continuously outperformed the national average. Key to our success is to hire and train teachers from the community. Using pre-fabricated structures, our schools are easily dismantled and relocated in the event of a natural disaster to quickly resume classes. To bypass the isolation, we use ICT-aided classrooms powered by solar panels.

title: Empower 120 differently abled kids in Tamil Nadu
description: We have identified 120 differently abled children in the Tiruchirappalli region of Tamil Nadu whose lives could be transformed with simple medical interventions.  For these kids, access to physiotherapy, basic medical care, or an assistive device would change everything.  A donation to this project gives mobility and independence to a child who cannot walk, education and connection to a child isolated by deafness or learning differences, and a clear mind to a youth afflicted with mental illness.

title: Help 300 tribal women scale their enterprise
description: Women from the Kui tribe in Odisha are dependant on the forest for their livelihoods. They often travel long distances deep into the forest to pick siali leaves, which they then stitch together to make disposable tableware, plates and bowls. Industree is extending support to this community by providing training, introducing new technology to improve productivity and quality, developing new ranges of products, and establishing new market linkages to enhance livelihoods for these women.

title: Helping the Mangkhut victims in Abra, Philippines
description: The project aims to reach out to the victims, particularly the local farmers of the communities of Dolores, Abra devastated by typhoon Mangkhut, locally known as Ompong.   OISCA through the OISCA Abra Agro-Forestry and Industrial Training Center based in Mudiit, Dolores, Abra is helping in the immediate relief operations to reach out to the victims, and later on in assisting the local farmers in recovering their farmlands that were damaged by the typhoon.

title: Re-Sight Islam podcast
description: Re-Sight Islam aims to illuminate and introduce to a largely Western audience the Islamic faith and its traditions from the Islamic perspective. "I believe my fellow Americans deserve a second look at Islam from the voice of an American Muslim-free of pundits and politicians," host Qasim Rashid says.  Support of the Religion News Foundation goes to promoting religious literacy through projects like this, and supporting the work of religion journalists around the world.

title: Restoring Nairobi's iconic public libraries
description: This project provides inventory and cataloguing for approx. 400,000 materials housed across all branches of Nairobi's iconic McMillan Memorial Library, providing digital records of the library's collection dating back to 1931. This project also provides access to contemporary storytelling and diversifies existing collections by adding children's titles by African authors.

title: Improving Access and Quality of Education in Nepal
description: Freedom to Learn's work in Nepal has revolutionised how children from some of the most vulnerable and marginalised communities gain improved access to and quality of education and improve their subsequent life chances. We achieve this by determining the barriers that impede education in state schools in Nepal and then develop and provide workable relevant responses to address these issues, from bikes to school, to teacher training, to school meals, for just under 5000 children across 6 schools.

title: Equip Underground Syrian Women&Children Hospital
description: Avicenna will allow Syrian moms + kids to seek healthcare in safety and security. Despite the sad reality that hospitals are regular targets of military strikes in Syria, it is essential that these women have the opportunity to receive the care that they and their babies need without exposing themselves to unacceptable risks. Our facility was built to protect patients and providers, we are committed to finding solutions that deliver world-class healthcare to resilient Syrian moms + kids.

title: Indonesia Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Fund
description: On September 28, 2018, a 7.5 magnitude earthquake in Indonesia created a 15-foot tsunami, killing more than 2,000 people and displacing more than 130,000 from their homes. After having provided emergency relief in the immediate aftermath of the disaster, this fund is now supporting long-term recovery assistance to survivors. All donations to this fund will exclusively support disaster relief and recovery efforts in Indonesia.

title: Disaster Response: Indonesia Earthquake & Tsunamis
description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the Indonesian island of Sulawesi on September 28, triggering a tsunami that slammed into Palu-the capital of Central Sulawesi province. On December 22, an unexpected and powerful tsunami resulted in damage on both sides of the Sunda Strait, which runs between the islands of Java and Sumatra. International Medical Corps is working with local partners to reach those most affected by these two disasters striking the country just three months apart.

title: Educate A Girl
description: In Bangladesh, women are often denied opportunities for education which puts them at a risk of trafficking and exploitation. JAAGO Foundation creates possibilities for women who are deprived of basic human rights and ensures a sense of safety and security for them. In addition, women are helped to develop their skills, make sound decisions and achieve economic power. Therefore, you can join us in our fight to aid women with their fundamental rights and help them explore their capabilities.

title: Earthquake and tsunami in Indonesia
description: On Friday, September 28, a 7.5 magnitude earthquake hit Sulawesi, Indonesia, followed by a tsunami with waves of up to 6 meters. There are an estimated 1.5 million people affected, over 78,000 people displaced and 2,100 people dead. ActionAid is coordinating area-wide response with a number of community-based organizations for immediate deployment of medics, mountain climbers, trauma counselors, and other first responders to provide urgently needed care to survivors. Will you help?

title: Indonesia Response 2018
description: COHI is in touch with our allies in Indonesia, supporting the locally-led response efforts after the terrifying tsunami took at least 800 lives. As per usual, we are prioritizing the needs of women and children as they are especially at risk during times of displacement.

title: YouMeWe Ghana
description: In an effort to connect children to the internet, we are working with the infamous teacher Owura Kwadwo, originally from Kumasi, Ghana,  teaching ICT in a rural farming community, which lacks basic equipment and resources for the task. "Every teacher has a way of presenting his subject to his students. This is my way,"  Now with the ICT skills, they will be focused on Social Impact through education.

title: YouMeWe Language in the cloud-Europe
description: We are looking to raise funds to purchase computers for the "Still I Rise" School in Samos, Greece where our colleague Nicolo Govoni has started a school to teach the refugee children in the camps.  We visited in early 2018 and installed donated computers from Morgan Stanley and look forward to expanding the program to not only connect the children in Europe with the children in Japan but to teach Digital Citizen skills for the 21st century online.

title: YouMeWe Language in the cloud-Indonesia
description: Working with our colleagues ReachOut Foundation in Jakarta, we are looking to raise funds for not only WiFi but computers to be connecting the children they are working with on early childhood development to have access to the internet and our Digital Citizenship program connecting the children in Japan.

title: Anti Discrimination and Racisme project
description: Awareness project! Our starting point is that music can connect and we notice that our community increasingly leads to negative influences. To counter these negative influences, we want to create a place where young people can come together and meet in a very low-threshold way with a master social worker and music teachers. Young people receive training and education in the field of Social Work and Music production. The combination ensures positive thinking and we use music as a powerfull tool!

title: Business training + loans for women & youth
description: HCU recognizes that a child's welfare is dependent on their home life as much as the education, so we started the Uplift program to support the households and businesses of Gulu. For the past 2 years, Uplift has been providing loans and financial training to 800 women, empowering them to achieve their small business goals and financial stability at home. These loans are returned with a small interest, which moves HCU closer to self-sustainability, our ultimate goal.

title: Help Moms of Slain Youth Tell Their Stories
description: THE SISTERHOOD: AN UNSILENCE INTERACTIVE EXHIBIT amplifies voices of The Sisterhood, a collective of mothers, all women of color, each of whom has lost a child to gun violence.  WITH YOUR SUPPORT, Unsilence collected testimonies and, featuring photographs by artist Cecil McDonald, created a free and open access digital exhibit narrated by the mothers.  PLEASE SUPPORT OUR NEXT PHASE to design a free educator guide for classroom use and community learning, and to build the exhibit's audience.

title: Educate & Empower, Change a Life in Kenya
description: Thousands of families in Kenya struggle to meet basic needs and provide quality education for children. 29% of students who enroll in secondary schools drop out before completing secondary cycle. This means that opportunities for these semi-literate children are severely limited. This project is helping boost education of 60 children by providing needed resources and breaking the cycle of poverty and unemployment of 40 youth and women through 2 areas: skills training and small business start-up

title: Build the USAP Community School in Zimbabwe
description: Education Matters is building a 11th and 12th grade high school for 90 high-achieving, low-income Zimbabwean students to access quality education that values critical thinking, integrity, sustainability and compassion.  The USAP Community School will prepare its students to access and excel higher education at world's top universities on scholarships with the aim of returning to Zimbabwe to build a better society. Join us  in this exciting initiative to build a truly transformative school!

title: Building Hope for Communities - Darkhan, Mongolia
description: The city of Darkhan is Mongolia's second largest industrial center, where poverty, unemployment, alcoholism, health problems, education problems, shortage of jobs and criminal activities prevail.   WHAT WE DO: 1. Improve protection to children by providing necessities of life. 2. Provide high-quality life education to children. 3. Provide various vocational training so they may become more employable.

title: Screening 6,500 vulnerable men of prostate cancer
description: The project offers an opportunity for men to be involved in their health affairs and to take a lead. Prostate cancer is the window to addressing some of the social and medical challenges in that community. The project brings all men regardless of age to receive health education and screening rural and marginalised communities.  Screening men in their community brings men together and gives them responsibility. Men in health has the capacity to have an interface with men .

title: Offer a sewing machine to a Rajasthani woman
description: Since 2007, Sambhali Trust has helped women of the centres to acquire some skills in sewing and embroidery to one day sell their products and earn money. These younger women have a greater chance of having an equal relationship with their husbands if they have financial independence. The Trust is fighting for gender equality.

title: Building a girls' Residence for Jipe Moyo School
description: In Tanzania, girls often become victims of sexual abuses during their secondary school years. In 2017, in the Tanzanian Kagera region, more than 300 Secondary School female students dropped out of school because of unwanted pregnancy, usually from abuse and sexual harassment.  For this reason, FOH ask for your help to build a girls' residence for Jipe Moyo Secondary School, so that we can protect them from these abuses and help them to successfully finish their education.

title: Indonesia Earthquake and Tsunami Response
description: This project will distribute vital humanitarian relief and provide mental health support to communities affected by the devastating earthquake and tsunami in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. IsraAID's team - including disaster response specialists, water engineers, and mental health experts - will conduct an assessment of the immediate and long-term medical, psychological, and water, sanitation, and hygiene needs in the affected area.

title: Volunteer Patient Advocacy Fund
description: Human Health Project plans to launch a Peer-Led Patient Advocacy Program in 2019 in Belfast, Northern Ireland and Los Angeles, California with more cities being added from 2020. This campaign will help us fund the costs necessary to launch the program that will help low income and underserved patients take charge of their health with the aid of advocacy by trained volunteer patient advocates. Every donation is generously matched up to $25k by ChildLife Essentials.

title: Help Save 3 Endangered Grassland Species in Mexico
description: The American bison, the golden eagle, and the Mexican prairie dog call the Chihuahuan Desert their home. These three endangered species-whose roles in the ecosystem are as crucial as they are emblematic-inhabit the largest and most biodiverse desert in North America, 2/3 of which lies in Mexico.  This fundraising campaign aims to continue habitat recovery and preservation efforts, veterinary care, education, and monitoring activities to protect these very special species in northern Mexico.

title: URGENT: Earthquake and Tsunami Devastate Indonesia
description: More than 1,300 people have died following a 7.5-magnitude earthquake and subsequent tsunami in Indonesia. Hundreds are injured, and some 65,000 homes have been damaged but the full extent of the destruction remains to be seen. Survivors are in urgent need. Your emergency gift today can provide: clean drinking water, emergency family shelters, sleeping mats, blankets, solar lights, and emergency hygiene kits.

title: Emergency Relief for Palu Earthquake
description: ACT Foundation is well known and trusted non profit organization in Indonesia. We have been working since the earthquake and tsunami destroyed Palu-Donggala, Indonesia.   This project will rescue the victims, will deliver aid to affected victims, the ACT Foundation will implement the recovery program; to build Integrated Community Shelters (ICS) that has emergency school, emergency medical clinic, emergency toilets, etc.

title: Dairy goats program for Widows in Kitui, Kenya
description: Gender disparities imposed by cultural and traditional practices keep women in subordinate positions in all areas of life in the Africa rural society. Cultural practices contribute to undermining the women's position. It increases their vulnerability to HIV/AIDS, and impacts negatively on livelihood resources such as natural capital, economic capital, human capital, social capital and physical capital. Yet in many cases women are left to take care of the children and grandchildren.

title: Unlock potential with the Together We Can Fund
description: We all want a better world. But no one can change things alone. To accelerate change we must enable more changemakers to be part of our transformative events that build bridges and share learning to create better, faster change. We want to share our learning more widely, and include people who without bursary support could never attend. You can support champions of indigenous rights, volunteers combatting sex traffic, frontline conservationists. Your support can be truly life-changing.

title: Indonesian Earthquake and Tsunami Relief Response
description: On September 28th a magnitude 7.5 earthquake hit the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, including the city of Palu. The earthquake triggered a tsunami that engulfed the city, devastating infrastructure and causing substantial loss of life. To date almost 2.5 million people are potentially affected and more than 1,400 have lost their lives. It is anticipated that the number of people confirmed dead will rise. Oxfam and its partners are assessing the damage and responding to immediate needs.

title: Renovate a training centre in Italy for volunteers
description: In the city of Ferrara, IBO Italia is renovating and equipping a training centre where to promote international solidarity and train at least 2.000 young people per year to voluntary projects locally and abroad.  The new centre will be implemented in an ancient historical building granted to IBO Italia by the Municipality of Ferrara and it will have different spaces for meetings, non formal activities and accomodation.

title: Protecting Threatened Lemur Habitat in Madagascar
description: In Madagascar, 90% of littoral forests have been lost due to human activity, endangering endemic species, including lemurs. Project Ala has increased the viable habitat for these species through corridor reforestation; strengthening regional conservation knowledge and capacity to reduce human impact on these habitats. Building on Phase I, Phase II will expand habitat corridors between forest fragments; addressing unsustainable resource use -protecting the littoral forest and its biodiversity.

title: Rebuild Livelihoods - Philippines Typhoon Mangkhut
description: On September 15, Typhoon Mangkhut ravaged the Philippines.  The powerful typhoon destroyed homes and buildings, livestock and agriculture, displacing thousands.  Many families still reeling from the destruction are overwhelmed with loss of property and livelihoods.  Peace Winds is partnering with The Citizen's Disaster Response Center (CDRC) to provide relief and recovery to communities affected by the disaster.

title: Radio Access for Tsunami survivors in Indonesia
description: A catastrophic 7.5 earthquake and tsunami left hundreds dead and over 300,000 people homeless in Palu, Indonesia. In addition to food, shelter and medicine, survivors need information and people rely on radio to broadcast information they can trust. Our solar powered wind-up Polaris radio lights provide 24/7 access to information, news and updates to displaced families and the disabled.The LED light provides light at night. The cell charging feature tops up cell phones (if survivors have one).

title: Aid Survivors of Indonesia Tsunami
description: Your gift will provide emergency aid and supplies such as drinking water, shelter materials, and medical care to families affected by the 7.4 earthquake and tsunami in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. More than 61,867 people are left homeless and more than 1,200 have died. Countless more are injured and waiting for help. World Concern and our partners on the ground are reaching people in need and providing emergency assistance.

title: Emergency Aid for Sulawesi Quake & Tsunami
description: A major crisis has hit the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, on which we have anti-trafficking operations. The large city of Palu has been decimated by a massive earthquake and tsunami. Isolated by infrastructure damage and lacking in water, food and shelter, safety and security have become a major concern within the city.  As active members of the region, we desire to help with the massive and aid and rescue operations.

title: A2Z care to 50 destitute senior citizen in Odisha
description: The project aims to address 50  mostly abandoned, destitute, disabled senior citizens nutritional food, clothing, shelter,  health care, recreational support, emotional support, disability care and personality development aspects in Cuttack district of Odisha. The identified disabled persons are mostly within the age group of 65-80 years and at present they are neglected by their family members and   and residing outside. They are satisfying their hunger by begging   and left uncured for surviv

title: Sulawesi - Indonesia Emergency Relief
description: A tsunami hit Palu - Central Sulawesi after a 7.4 Earthquake happen in this area. It kill more than 1400 people per Oct 4th. There are more than 600,000 people live in Palu and Dongala. We need to send more funds to our local partner to purchase basic supplies, hygiene, food, fuel and first aid kits to be distributed to families affected by the disaster. And also help to rebuild and renovate school for the children as soon as possible.

title: Educate 50 Girls To Help Them Escape Poverty Cycle
description: Avasar Foundation Scholarship began as a Voluntary Funded Program to support education of underprivileged girls. Parents facing extreme financial hardship usually end up choosing to withdraw schooling for girls.   This Project identifies meritorious students at grade 11 and support them for 5/6 years to study to become employable.  52 Girls have been enrolled in this program since inception in 2013. 4 Graduated and have been offered a full time employment, changing their lives forever.

title: ICAP Strengthens U.S. Global Leadership
description: Internationally recognized by The Economist's Global Diversity List and the U.S. Congress, the International Career Advancement Program (ICAP) assists highly talented mid-career professionals from underrepresented groups in advancing to senior leadership positions in international affairs.

title: Emergency relief after tsunami in Indonesia
description: Several earthquakes and a destructive tsunami hit the Island of Sulawesi on Sept 28th, 2018. The infrastructure of the island is severely destroyed. Currently, there is no power and water supply. Over 1.400 people were killed, 200.000 people are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance and 65.000 houses were completely destroyed. The member organisations of Aktion Deutschland Hilft are in Sulawesi and give humanitarian aid to the people who are affected.

title: International YouthBank Conference
description: As a member of YB international network for 7 years, within this project implementation term TOG would like to organize an international conference. 60 participants who are YouthBank members, youth workers and YouthBanks coordinators will come together to talk about the YouthBank project that will be organized in Istanbul at the dates of 27/30.11.2018.

title: Less work and more education for children in Quito
description: UBECI's market programme has resumed following 2 years of restrictions put in place to contain the spread of Covid 19.  Families have been hit hard by the loss of income as they are have only recently been able to return to work in the markets. This project will fund a further year of the salary of an outreach worker who can now return to work in the UBECI playgroups in the markets of Southern Quito, providing support to 600 working children.

title: VOCATIONAL TRAINING FOR 58 TEEN-MOTHERS IN HOMABAY
description: This project will benefit Teenage Mothers orphaned due to HIV/AIDS & those coming from families affected by extreme poverty with Vocational Training and Skills Development to enable them become self-reliant in life, evade forms exploitation, enjoy peaceful integration in families and compete for employment opportunities. It will also make the Teenage Mothers become tools for grater change  among young girls & Youths in the target community. It is targeted at Teenage Mothers of Homabay, Kenya.

title: Providing shelter for homeless children in Nigeria
description: World Nations Development Programme Initiative [WNDPI] is a Non-Governmental and Non Profit Organization registered under the Corporate Affairs Commission of Nigeria, and established with the sole aim of helping the Less Privileged across Africa. WNDPI's major target is to reach to the Poor as well as the Low Income Earners in the Society by Building Houses, Schools, Medical Centers and notwithstanding Training and Empowering of Youths through various Vocational Skills to earn a Living.

title: Building Home for Less Privilege People in Nigeria
description: Ife-ooye Women's Association is building homes for less privileged people in Nigeria. This project will help us continue to build housing for vulnerable and disenfranchised people and also provide for their basic needs, such as providing food, clothing and healthcare.

title: Become a monthly Sponsor of our animals
description: Help us continue this important service of rescuing and protecting animals and teaching the public about the social, climatic, economic and health advantages of a plant-based diet.  Juliana's Animal Sanctuary is a 501c3 non-profit registered in the state of Maryland.

title: Asset Financing
description: The organization will continue finishing its renovation project that started January 2018 but it is yet to be completed. The organization is to complete on proper electrical wiring; plastering and repairing the floor, toilets, kitchen; tiling floors, toilets and kitchen, putting sinks and toilet flash; repainting; adding more rooms upstairs. The project will need a budget of USD$ 7,314 to complete. The project will first work on completion of repairing of walls, electrical piping, plastering,

title: Clean Water For 1000 Families in Rural Nigeria
description: In Bichi community, Sabo, Kano in Nigeria, water shortage leads to various social economic problem such as water related diseases, high work load and burden of going too far distance river by women, poor hygiene at primary schools and disturbance of carrying water from home to school and low income due to high water expenditure. This project will improve access to clean water in the community through sinking of Water borehole and help to reduce the above mentioned challenges.

title: Reduce Stigma against Adolescents with HIV/AIDS
description: In Kano state Nigeria, poverty, illiteracy, unprotected sex and stigma play a role in making PLWHA hide their identity and infect other people (Nwokedi 2007).  According to the 2016-2017 multiple indicator cluster survey on stigmatization, 19.3% male and 6.5% female adolescents 15-19years respectively express accepting attitude towards people living with HIV/AIDS. This project will survey teenage girls on their KAPs and provide information on transmission, prevention and treatment.

title: Micro Donations to feed children in need in India
description: A micro-donation the cost of your next coffee can help immensely. It is important to help children access schools for education, health and to stay safe.  Help us in the mission to Leave No Child Hungry and to work on the fundamental need of food for children to help build a better future by ensuring children stay in schools, learn, play, stay healthy and safe.  Micro-Donations you can make monthly help feed meals to children every day.

title: Support 25 teachers in India with impactful tools
description: Teach A Class connects passionate teachers in India to the solutions they need to be effective in the classroom. We currently support teachers with four solutions. These include personalised learning, classroom libraries, comprehension assessment apps, and science toolkits. We've connected 135 teachers to solutions and aim to empower 500 teachers by 2020.

title: Enhance Digital Literacy for Orphanage School
description: We will provide computer sets and other accessories for printing and enhance digital literacy at Our Lady Mother of Perpetual Help Primary/Secondary School & orphanage Home. The orphans would have opportunity to access digital literacy for free while other people from the community pay to attend the school and acquire computer skills. The school will be able to print test and exams question from their facility which will also be paid for, thereby ensuring sustainability.

title: LIFE SKILLS FOR  100 TEEN MOTHERS
description: A pregnant class 8 or Form 4- A very disturbing situation; interrupted education, unwanted baby and lack of survival skills! Should nothing be done to equip Teen Mothers to support themselves and their children; the society should ready itself to face a storm of street children and crime, an up-tide in prostitution and related health implications; a clear cycle of  suffering. We are rebuilding lives of teen mothers  through Training in life Skills, in Tailoring, ICT and other Craft courses.

title: Little Sofia struggling with leukemia
description: Beautiful girl with big gray eyes and sad smile - Sofia from Ukraine. She is only 5 years old and for several years Sofia has been struggling with leukemia, which can take her life. To treat the girl constantly need expensive medications. Mom alone brings up Sofia and works as a teacher in a rural school. She asks to respond to all not indifferent people and help her daughter to be healthy and smiling again!

title: Support 20 women making 100% bio pads in Cameroon
description: Through False Labels Global Inc.we will help 10 million rural women and girls in overcoming the social barriers linked with menstruation by providing them with low-cost sanitary pads (KujaEcoPads),an innovation that produces 100% biodegradable sanitary pads from locally sourced banana stem fibers.We plan to buy land and build a production center for the 20 who are currently working in a very small rented space.

title: REPAIR & EQUIP CLASSROOMS FOR 193 KIDS IN KAMSAMA
description: Children in their young age need equal opportunities for development. Good classrooms & modern Teaching & Learning materials are needed for this! This project is aimed at renovating 4 classrooms in poor conditions in Kamsama village in Kenya & equip each of them with Modern Teaching/ Learning materials. This will enable the the children have better psychological, metal and physical development as they study in school.

title: Education for All (Myanmar)
description: This project was launched in June 2019 and is along sought-after education initiative which provides a targeted year of education, aiming to significantly improve the Grade 10 matriculation rate and future life opportunities for up to 150 students from 30 remote villages across western Myanmar (Burma).

title: Provide safe drinking water,tens thousands-postwar
description: Rural Women & Youth Coordination's water recovery-Links plans to provide sufficient safe, healthy water supply near villages hard-hit by water crisis in a post war ravaged northern Uganda, that recently suffered  prolonged drought ever, due to climate change. Putting the poorest families, orphans, widows and other vulnerable children at a high risk of serious outbreak of water-borne diseases, due to sharing dirty water sources with animals. To get scarce safe or clean water one needs a bicycle.

title: COMMERCIALIZATION OF HONEY FOR 600 YOUTHS IN KENYA
description: OPUK WOMEN GROUP AIMS to buy 1200 bee hives for 600 youths. Bees perform a task that is vital to the survival of agriculture: pollination and employment provision. In fact, one third of our global food supply is pollinated by bees. Bees keep plants and crops alive. Without bees, humans wouldn't have very much to eat.

title: Peacemaking with Samburu Warriors in Kenya
description: The Samburu, closely related to the Masai, are pastoralists who frequently raid other groups for cattle. They are egged on by the young women. With the advent of guns in the region, this custom has become deadly. Ezra Kigondu, the organizer of the Samburu project, has gained the confidence of the Samburu warriors, called "morans", in the three sub-counties of Samburu District. The purpose of this project is to bring the various groups together to promote peaceful co-existence.

title: WORKSHOP PROJECT FOR DISABLED PEOPLE IN KINSHASA
description: Many disabled persons especially women in Kinshasa are relying on beggary to survive! So CALFE ( www.calfe.org) help them get trained in tailoring handcrafts to start their own business and get financially independent. Then CALFE provided them 10 sewing machines and other tailoring supplies to start Income Generating Activities. They'd now be working and help themselves but they are lacking a place for this. Then this project will also help more disabled persons to learn tailoring.

title: Help 16 girls to go on an annual educational tour
description: This project builds resilience among 16 marginalized adolescent girls (10-18) in South India, providing them with rich and vibrant experience of going on an educational tour for 4 days  to places of historical & educational importance.  We plan to travel by air to New Delhi in January, 2019 and return by train .   These annual out of state tours exposes the girls to different cultures, languages and foods where they learn to embrace diversity & tolerance which forms the foundation of resilience.

title: UPCYCLING HANDMADE PRODUCTS BY 100 KENYAN ARTISANS
description: This project aims at reducing the effects of water hyacinth weed that has invaded Lake Victoria (Kenya) making fishing and water navigation impossible thereby affecting the livelihoods of families which depend on the lake. We aim to utilize the water hyacinth weeds to make functional products which we shall sell and in the process create employment for 100 artisans at the shores of Lake Victoria.

title: Educational Support To 75 Labour Rescued Girls
description: There are a number of girls, caught up in the endless vicious cycle of poverty over generations in the rural villages. Their only source of income is to work as daily laborers. The primary goal of the project is to motivate & counsel girls/parents/locals people, enroll them in schools and support them with the education material, educational fees, uniforms to at least 75 girl laborers and giving them an opportunity to steer their lives towards a more promising future through better Education.

title: Shelter, Food and Care for Oldage poor Women India
description: The prime objective of the project to provide Food, Shelter, Clothes, Medical treatment and social security to Oldage destitute Women. The proposed project has been implementing since two years to providing for Food, Clothes, Bed sheets, simple Medicines to the Oldage destitute Women by the help and cooperation of the Philanthropists, humanitarians and other Donor Agencies in Local and international for this cause. In Kurnool District frequent drought and famine are common in this area.

title: Provide Clean Renewable Sustainable Energy Source
description: Organization for Scientific Research and Youth Technical Development plans to build 2 Bio gas digesters at Future and Hope/Bethania vulnerable children's village/Vulnerable children's Drop In centre. These Bio gas digesters will produce clean sustainable renewable energy source for cooking.  This project will improve access to clean sustainable renewable cooking energy to marginalized vulnerable children at the village. Improving renewable sustainable clean energy poverty is our mission

title: Lerncafe - Free Study Support and Afternoon Care
description: The "Lerncafes" (learning cafes), a free afternoon educational support project focused on education and social integration, are a highly successful and internationally recognized service that has been established by Caritas all over Austria during the past years. On various locations, children from refugee and migrant families, as well as from host communities have access to free study support in order to succeed in school as well as enhance their language and social skills.

title: Support 500 Teen Single Mothers in Tanzania
description: This project will establish a youth vocational and resource center in Bunju Dar es Salaam, that will enable 500 teenage single mothers per year to have access to vocational training on tailoring and embroidery  as well as establishing markets and trade related networking for their products. Through the project, 500  single teenage mothers  will have the opportunity to restore their lost hope and dreams in businesses enterprises of their aspirations in accordance to their capacity and interest.

title: Medical Support for Lesvos Vulnerable Refugees
description: Lesvos Solidarity is an NGO offering humanitarian aid to vulnerable refugees in Lesvos, Greece. We also provide medical and psychosocial services, aiming to support the public health system amid the COVID-19 pandemic. This project will cover a year of medical care expenses for  vulnerable refugees living in Pikpa refugee camp. This money will help them to receive primary health care, medication, medical screenings as well as covering the costs of escorting patients to clinics and hospital.

title: Library Access to Hospice Care Workers Worldwide
description: This project will enable us to provide access to a high quality library to palliative care workers globally. It is important to keep up-to-date with current information, new evidence-based innovations in care, recent trends in patient treatments and outcomes.  Unfortunately, most individuals in developing countries do not have access to this data. Access to books and journals is expensive, scarce and difficult. The IAHPC Library provides access to over its thousand members throughout the world.

title: Help Sulawesi school children return to school
description: After a devastating earthquake and resultant tsunami in Sulawesi, Indonesia, we've received reports of 62,659 people displaced, 66,926 houses damaged and 67,335 families affected.   They're horrifying statistics and we're working with our partners to bring particular focus to returning children to school and families to normalcy.

title: #MoreGirlsTogether
description: With the motto #MoreGirlsTogether, the Na'leb'ak organization starts 2018 with a fundraising dinner for the dream of building its headquarters in Chisec, Alta Verapaz. Based on a model of regenerative agriculture that seeks to promote the recovery of knowledge and local species; this center would be a place to connect girls and adolescents in a more harmonious way with ecology, economy, soil conservation and food production.

title: Animal Assisted Therapy for Children in Guatemala
description: Following the unexpected passing of our previous therapy dog, Mo'os, the Fundacion Waibi donated a new therapy dog to Adisa. After five years of observed success with Mo'os, we made the decision to continue with our Animal Assisted Therapy program. This project will allow us to pay the costs of assisted animal therapy sessions so that our new therapy dog, Argos, can provide weekly animal therapy to 20 children with disabilities in Santiago Atitlan.

title: RESCUE ENDANGERED ELEPHANTS IN SRI LANKA
description: In the country of Sri Lanka, with a population of approximately 21 million people, there are about 5,800 elephants. With a land mass of 65,000 Km on this small island, it is easy to surmise that contacts between elephants and people are quite common. The ecosystem of the wild Asian Elephant (Elephas Maximas) is being encroached upon by human habitation, threatening the welfare of these endangered animals, as well as their human neighbors.

title: Book Relief ( Kerala & Coorg)
description: Several regions across India is recovering from the recent floods, there are several schools who have lost hundreds and thousands of reading material, some schools have lost entire libraries. This campaign is a small endeavour to provide them with some joyful reading material as they build back their schools. We aim to raise money for books and distribute it directly to the schools affected by the floods. We have identified 5 schools and are in the process of adding more schools. #BookRelief

title: Support Food Groceries to Helpless Old aged Women
description: The low economic and financial status of the families and the disintegration of joint families have made the lives of elderly people neglected and miserable.After experiencing all the hardships of life their way of living has become even worse at this later stage.Their age does not support them to work to earn their food.This program aims to provide food groceries including rice, yellow split peas, black gram, green gram, broken wheat, pearl millet to the needy and helpless old aged women.

title: Help Cheetah Experience turn waste into compost!
description: This project will allow us to turn food waste into compost, this is not only better for the environment, but we will also be able to sell excess compost to make a profit. Any money raised from selling compost can be used to buy more trees  and materials to create shade for the animals.

title: Hurricane Michael Relief Fund
description: Hurricane Michael was the first category 5 hurricane to hit the United States since 1992 and caused widespread damage and power outages in communities across Florida's Panhandle. From providing emergency food, water, and fuel to residents in the immediate aftermath of the storm to now supporting ongoing, long-term recovery, all donations to this fund will exclusively support recovery efforts for this disaster.

title: Emergency Fuel - Hurricane Michael
description: Category 4 Hurricane Michael crashed into the Florida coast on October 10th with surging winds of up to 155 mph, making it the most powerful storm to hit the U.S. mainland in nearly 50 years.  Unlike other storms of this caliber, Michael intensified from a Category 2 in just 24 hours, giving an estimated 4.2 million people in its path little to no time to prepare or evacuate. While first responders are focused on rescues, temporary shelter & food, FRF is the ONLY organization offering free fuel.

title: Business Skills for Women and Youth in Nigeria
description: We are excited to embark on a new adventure! In order to strengthen our ongoing commitment to grow human capital and eradicate poverty, we have become Street Business School (SBS) certified. This has enabled us add entrepreneurial education to our existing services. SI4DEV is currently the only SBS global catalyst partner in Nigeria!

title: Reading and Literacy for 1500 Children in Nigeria
description: This project will improve literacy and promote reading culture among over 1500 children, young people and their families in Obanliku LGA, Cross River State, Nigeria. Lacking vital literacy skills like reading holds a person back at every stage of their life. As a child they won't be able to succeed at school, as a young adult they will be locked out of the job market, and as a parent they won't be able to support their own child's learning. This cycle makes social mobility virtually impossible!

title: Hurricane Michael Response - Disaster Health Kits
description: Hurricane Michael made landfall Wednesday, Oct 10 as a powerful Category 4 hurricane with 150+ mph winds. More than 6000 residents were forced to evacuate their homes and are now residing in shelters and other locations.  This project will provide thousands of MAP Disaster Health Kits (DHKs) to hurricane evacuees in the Florida Panhandle. DHKs include essential hygiene items and health supplies to help prevent the spread of illness. One kit helps a person living in a shelter for a week.

title: Mangrove Planting (Community / Students) of Barada
description: We aim to achieve the development of self-sustaining mangrove planting and exploitation activities carried out by our young students and their families. This will enable the restore of the ecosystem, allowing the development of other activities and projects connected to it, being part of a network of projects aiming for the development of the locality of Barada and helping to improve the living conditions of its populations. It will also help to reduce the impacts from sea erosion and silting.

title: Education & hope for 250 children in Parkview
description: This project will offer quality education and basic needs to 250 orphans & vulnerable children in Parkview Orphans Achievers Shelter (POAS) so that they can enjoy their life like the ordinary child.

title: Support Child Health Project in 12 Villages
description: This Project is aimed to address the basic health issues of children in the age group of 0-15 years. To promote and implement child-to-child health education and concept to ensure better health for the children in the targeted villages.Motivate, educate and encourage the children on their health care and provide basic medicines/nutrition in support of their health.To provide early intervention to ensure child survival as well as holistic development of every children by conducting medical camps.

title: Help training of 40 Indian women with disabilities
description: ADD India will train 40 women with disabilities in Keeranur, Pudukottai district Tamil Nadu and in Siddlaghatta, Chikkaballapur district, Karnataka  to set up their own group enterprise. This is subsequent to the skill training given to them  in  2017, an outcome of facilitating regular forums for the women to share their experiences. ADD India continues to facilitate the platform for sharing for women with disabilities, while these 40 women now need to learn the ways of running an enterprise.

title: Hurricane Michael Disaster Response
description: The most powerful storm to hit the continental US in decades leveled much of the Florida panhandle. We are in touch with our supply distribution partners to coordinate hygiene kits and medical supplies but what is needed now, today, is cash to get into the hands of the pregnant women, LGBTQI evacuees, families with kids with special needs, survivors of sexual assault and domestic violence, and immigrants who don't feel safe accessing mainstream services.

title: Emergency Response to Hurricane Michael
description: Hurricane Michael hit the Florida Panhandle as a Category 4 storm with winds reaching 155 miles per hour, making Michael the strongest hurricane to hit the Panhandle on record, and the strongest storm to hit the continental U.S. in nearly 50 years. At the request of the Florida Department of Health, International Medical Corps has deployed medical personnel to provide support at health facilities and shelters as they deal with this devastating storm.

title: Indonesia Earthquake & Tsunami Response
description: On September 28th, a 7.4 magnitude earthquake shook Palu City and the regency of Donggala in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia, home to an estimated 2.8 million people. A tsunami followed shortly after striking the west coast of Sulawesi, hitting Talise beach in Palu City and the beach in Donggala. As of October 5th, the government has confirmed that 1,581 people are dead, 2,549 severely injured, 113 missing with 71,000 internally displaced (IDPs) and around 1.5 million potentially affected.

title: Hurricane Michael Veteran Relief Team Mission
description: After spending another week in Bay County Florida, we want to turn our focus (if possible) to the relief aspect of the mission, as well as recovery. This mission is what will help people get needed supplies before the cold season arrives. We would like to do a massive month-long blanket, hygiene, clothing and food operation that will help thousands get the very basics of normal life in-hand before the rapidly approaching Winter (and holidays) arrive.

title: Help California Wildfire Victims
description: Matthew 25: Ministries has been involved in disaster relief since 1997. Matthew 25 is responding to the devastating wildfires raging throughout California. Matthew 25 has shipped a semi of relief supplies to partners in California. The semi contained personal care kits, paper products, water, dust masks, tarps, baby items, laundry detergent pods and more. Matthew 25 will be sending additional shipments in the coming weeks, and will deploy our Disaster Response Team to help those affected.

title: Think Before Pink
description: Table will provide a rich free booklets to every female in the all educational institutes and working places, villages and poorest sections of the societies in the project area through 10 ambulatory campaigns in a month. In campaign train volunteers encourage to improve personal hygiene during her period, pregnancy, free & post delivery  encourage for breast feeding, table also provide 125 free screening test for early detection, free 20 breast cancer treatment & 25 women free rehabilitation.

title: Participatory Videos People's Voice in Development
description: This project will bring the people voice to the forefront of development and bring the reality of people living Nepalese remote villages to the government agencies, non-profit organizations and policy makers. The projects aims to build better community engagement  and help concerned agencies to make better decisions while planning and implementing projects and policies. The videos will be made by the community members themselves and will be filmed at local, district and central levels.

title: Palu & Donggala Emergency Relief
description: On 28 September 2018, Palu was hit by what BBC described as a 'worst case' scenario, combining a large earthquake with a 7.4 magnitude, followed by a tsunami, major liquefaction and landslides that devastated the regions of Palu, Donggala and Sigi, resulting in total destruction of most buildings in the area. This project aims to establish two emergency posts providing assistance to victims in the form of nutritious foods, clean water, health equipment, medicine and basic shelter.

title: Hurricane Michael: Help Babies in Florida
description: Hurricane Michael has devastated Florida. This fund will provide diapers at no cost to struggling families, who are recovering and rebuilding. When we think about disaster recovery, we tend to think about hunger, homelessness, and clean water. Diapers are an overlooked, yet crucial, basic need. All babies deserve to be clean, dry, and healthy.

title: Happy Meals for Poor Children and their Families
description: This project will provide highly-nutritious meals for 3 months to 200 very poor and severely malnourished children living in Lubilan, Naawan municipality, a remote mountainous village here in Mindanao in order for them to improve their health and nutrition and provide them with good chance in life.

title: Help 20 disabled children in India fight Autism
description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder that affects communication and behavior. Although autism can be diagnosed at any age, it is said to be a "developmental disorder" because symptoms generally appear in the first two years of life. Autism spectrum disorder is a serious condition related to brain development that impairs the ability to communicate and interact with others.Autism, as the whole world knows, is one of the most dreaded disabilities and a lifelong disability.

title: Happy Meals for 500 Hungry Children
description: Five hundred hungry children in remote villages that we are serving here in Mindanao shall partake of sumptuous meal  in order to make them happy, enjoy good food, improve their nutrition and well-being. The meal will be served by our teams and volunteers and will comprise fried chicken, rice, roasted pig, candies, chocolates and native delicacies. We will also provide toys and slippers for the children. We will target 1,500 children to be served by this initiative.

title: Food for Hurricane Michael Survivors
description: Before Hurricane Michael struck, volunteers in Orlando were packing disaster relief boxes with canned meats, fruits, vegetables and shelf-stable milkenough to meet basic needs of a family of four for a week.   The first truck of disaster food boxes has reached the devastated area, and we will provide food at no cost to disaster relief providers throughout the recovery period, while serving our local community.    We need your help! $10 will provide $90 worth of groceries for hurricane survivors

title: 2018 Annual Silent Auction
description: This project is our Annual Silent Auction, which is our big fundraiser that helps us to continue our financial support in maintaining and sustaining The Ishahayi Beach School and Ife Oluwa Primary School.

title: Help feed 168 tseltal children in Chiapas
description: Increase the community economy with orchards, poultry farms, permanent cornfields, irrigation systems, earthworm composts, mushrooms greenhouses, subsidized corn, bakeries and piloncillo factories, by developing community capacities with: workshops, techincal assistance and monitoring of agroecological and etnoveterinary activities. Collective management of incomes. Women leaderships enforcement.

title: Food for 200 Hungry Children
description: This project will provide fried chicken, rice, roasted pig, candies, chocolates and native delicacies twice a week to 200 hungry and malnourished children living in 3 remote villages in Mindanao in order for them to improve their health and nutrition and give them better chances in life.

title: Save the cow and secure their future
description: In india Cows are treated as God by Hindu Community.In Rural areas,People,Partially illiterate,Use to shelter the cows mainly for milk production.They are Practising the anncient method for providing food and health hygyne to those innocent animals.They trated them as a productive tools not as a creature.So when the cows get herted use to realease them quickly from shelter or sell them to slaughter house.Our organisation with the view to serve the animal has taken up a project to provide shelter

title: Plant tree, save earth & lives secure the future
description: BARNAMALA EDUCATIONAL AND CULTURAL SOCIETY aims to plant 20,000 plants in two years. Preserving the tree is an obligation for everyone without exception, one tree will absorb approximately a ton of carbon dioxide during the course of its life cycle. Tree planting can restore global warming. Bring awareness to children. Protect the planet for our children and grandchildren.

title: Bringing potable water to Babli's village in Mewat
description: Babli is a resident of Mewat region of Haryana, Hathin Block, district Palwal. She treks several miles daily to fetch water. With scorching Sun, parched land and rapidly depleting source of water, she does not know how long she will get water. She and many like her have abandoned their cattle as there is no water or fodder for them. She is not very old but due to drinking contaminated water day in day out her hair is almost grey, her joints are swollen and her gait is slow and laborious.

title: Sustainable Livelihood and Enterprise Development
description: This project will empower disadvantaged 100 women and girls through imparting skill training, Readymade Garment Making trainings, Animal Husbandry,Kantha stitch Training, Crystal Work and Self-help to each other, which will help to generate an income for their families and give a better chance of survival

title: Help Young Kenyans Brighten Their Neighborhood
description: The Changing Faces Competition has been a great launchpad for our Public Space Transformation program. Our team of enthusiastic young changemakers will soon begin work on another local public space that is in dire need of improvement and transform it into something attractive and productive. We will use the same strategy as before: - Choose a space of reasonable size - Engage local authorities and residents for permission, advice, and to ensure on-going maintenance. - Set a deadline - TRANSFORM

title: Pavitra-Menstrual Holistic Education-Rural India
description: Poor menstrual health and hygiene is affecting girls and women in rural communities across India. There is limited access to safe sanitary care products or menstrual education. Social taboos, myths and misconceptions are still strong and not allowing for a conversation about periods. Project Pavitra is taking menstrual education to rural India and urban slums through inspired women volunteers. We are running Menstrual Education Program to bring rural Indian girls out of the shame around periods.

title: Build Prosperity in Tlamacazapa, Mexico
description: Atzin's mission: reverse the trap of poverty by supporting people to reach their full potential. We call it: The Cycle of Prosperity. It's a complex task but one with lasting effects. With your help, and working hand in hand with families, we invest time, talent and resources so that people gain greater ability to achieve their goals. We create opportunity and provide the needed tools so that people can give back to their community. And the best part? We've seen success for the past 20 years.

title: Be a Super Friend for our children in Venezuela!
description: Vulnerable children suffer the most in Venezuela. Food insecurity, hunger, malnutrition, a broken hospital care explain the highest mortality rates, at some point with 6-7 children dying every week, and school dropout at +50%. Be the hero for +10,000 newborns & children, +1,000 students & teachers, and +300 health care workers that rely on Friends for nutritional supplements, formulas, medicines, medical supplies, and even a daily meal as an incentive to attend and stay at school.

title: Help India rise against hunger of 1000 people
description: This project will feed 1000 people in the slums and streets of 3 regions in the state of Goa, every day. Lunch is provided for the slum dwellers, poor and disabled on the streets. Our efforts are to eradicate malnutrition and hunger of the children and people in our proximity. People in tent facilities are surviving without the basic necessities and are prone to the dangers of starvation, malnutrition and nutritional diseases. Our goal is to provide a nutritious meal, one time a day.

title: Provide wheelchairs to change lives in Kenya
description: This project aims to provide 929 disabled people in Kenya with the wheelchairs they need to be mobile, healthy, independent and active.  We will focus on six regions of Kenya where disabled people live in poverty and are frequently isolated, helping wheelchair services to become sustainable and continue to provide vital wheelchairs in the future.

title: Creating a safe haven for Abuse and GBV Survivors
description: Shamwari Yemwanasikana will establish a One Stop Empowerment Center (OSEC) in Seke district as a halfway home for vulnerable girls. Our intervention strategy will cater for the emergency health examination and prevention against STIs and HIV transmission by ensuring the administration of Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) as well as provide legal aid, psycho-social support, counselling, economic empowerment activities and safe shelter to girl child survivors of abuse and GBV.

title: Complete Rugby Equipment for 2 Mozambique teams
description: ADEDAR Rugby has been growing rugby in Mozambique for 3 years, educating, providing positive environments, and fighting for gender equality through sport. We are lacking complete sets of equipment (jerseys, shorts, boots, socks, ruck pads, tackling bags, etc). As we begin to complete teams with equipment, rugby will grow in numbers, in strength, and closer to our goal as an organization. The more players we get, the more people we reach, the more education and confidence we build.

title: Junior Pele Soccer Tournaments
description: "Junior Pele" 2018 soccer Tournament (Dec. 2018) is Cup Foundation Ghana's Juvenile soccer tournament which is earmarking to take place in December on a national sports stadium every year in Ghana and other African countries. This tournament is a strategic tool to attract highly talented Juvenile soccer players from under 10-17 around the world to compete for the name "Junior Pele" annually . For value addition, Junior Pele would gain scholarship to study in a competitive soccer academy in UK .

title: Trauma Informed Yoga for the Incarcerated
description: We have offered classes weekly to Correctional Programming since 2014, and have grown to offering 8 classes/week, in each correctional facility in Duval County. It costs our organization $55,000 a year to run the program.  Every dollar donated will ensure our programing can empower those inside to believe that they are stronger than they know, that they are able to forgive themselves and make amends, and that they can change their own outcomes.

title: Help Fund Service Dogs for Veterans
description: Warrior Canine Connection (WCC) supports recovering combat Veterans and their families through the healing power of dogs.
