WCC enlists Service Members and Veterans suffering from symptoms of Post Traumatic Stress (PTS) and Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI) in the critical mission of training service dogs for their fellow wounded Warriors with physical disabilities. These highly skilled, Warrior-trained service dogs are placed with Veterans at no cost.

title: English Education for Rural Children in China
description: Millions of rural children in China do not have access to quality education and are enrolled in schools where they lack English teachers. This project provides weekly online English lessons to more than 3,000 disadvantaged children. Lessons are delivered by trained volunteers based all over the world. We have more than fifteen years' experience of  training and supporting  volunteers to teach English in China.

title: Help Youth Volunteers Find New HIV Cases for Less
description: One Tent Health partners with local grocery and convenience stores in Washington, DC's highest-risk neighborhoods.  We provide free pop-up HIV screening through a canvas tent, screening kits, and passionate student volunteers who deliver HIV screening and PrEP navigation to low-income, under-served communities at one-third the national average cost.   We empower young people to get actively involved in their communities, both through the volunteer program and by hiring young innovators.

title: Provide Free Art Camp to Children in Need (Japan)
description: Support vulnerable children by donating to the 10th Anniversary Designing Artists Academy in summer 2019. By investing in this project you can help children learn about healthy ways to express themselves through various art mediums in safe, therapeutic environment. This is an 8-day arts camp held in August - developed specifically for 40 kids living in children's homes in Tokyo, ranging in age from 8-15. Workshops include dance, music, crafts, mixed media, photography, painting, yoga and more.

title: Help Communities Recover After Hurricane Michael
description: On October 10th, 2018, Hurricane Michael hit the coast of Florida as a category 4 storm. 155 mph winds have left more than one million residents without power throughout the Southeastern US. The damage is shocking. Entire homes were swept away and destroyed by the storm, leaving families homeless and desperate for assistance. In keeping with our mission, All Hands and Hearts will be operating a Rapid Response Program to help underserved, heavily damaged communities regain a sense of normalcy.

title: Construction of School Building for Blind Girls.
description: Through the proposed project, a new building for Smt. Ambubai Residential School for Blind Girls shall be constructed on the land located at Gulbarga, Karnataka, India.The building shall comprise two separate floors. The ground floor shall comprise the primary, secondary and high-school to provide education for more than 100 blind girls, whereas the first floor shall comprise their dormitories, library, kitchen, dining hall warden rooms etc.

title: Support Families with Special Needs in Palestine
description: This project will enable the Four Homes of Mercy - a residential center for 65 residents with severe special needs - to expand the initial family support program  by creating several additional specialized groups to meet the needs of family members severely traumatized by Covid's restrictions. For 8 months now, some have been caring for their loved one at home causing enormous  strain on the  family's mental health, and decreasing their ability to provide adequate care for their loved one.

title: Help 250 Women to start a crochet business
description: Life in Gombe for women with no employment is very hard. Desert encroachment has made agriculture unprofitable. Lack of ponds makes dry season farming impossible. With high unemployment among the men, women have to find means of  family upkeep. Our skills training is designed to give women and girls the opportunity to start a business. We train them; provide them with material as grants to start-up their crochet business; and l help them to market their products.

title: Animal Assisted Therapy for Disadvantaged Children
description: AMURT NW works in some of Liverpool's most deprived neighbourhoods where rates of child poverty are at their highest. This programme will give 480 children from disadvantaged families the opportunity to work with ponies and experience some of the benefits of Animal Assisted Therapy. Animal Assisted Therapy can improve mental health and tackle feelings of isolation. It teaches children empathy, patience, responsibility, self worth, social skills and confidence.

title: Dancing I am happy: fulfilling dreams of children
description: Children in Medellin, receive dance classes every week. They learn respect and good treatment with their classmates. They generate bonds of friendship and are happy to have the dance as part of their lives. They want to be good dancers, but more than that, they want to live in peace, surrounded by love and opportunities. In each class, they learn from their teachers and also occupy their free time healthy, away from drugs, crime, violence and abuse. This project is a great opportunity for them.

title: Corcovado National Park Rescue Project!
description: Nat Geographic described Corcovado National Park as "the most biologically intense area in the world ";  and El Pais in Spain described it as one of the "25 Most Spectacular National Parks in the World" Unfortunately,  its financial situation is dreadful, the park only receives 10% of the funding needed to fully operate. In the mean time, illegal hunters, loggers and miners are hurting the fragile biodiversity of the park.  While park rangers lack of fuel and food to do their patrols.

title: Habitat for Humanity - Hurricane Michael Response
description: Habitat for Humanity International is activating its response to Hurricane Michael. Habitat is working with its local organizations throughout the storm's path to gather early assessments of the impact in their service areas. Formal assessments will take place over the next several days after first responders are able to complete their work. Initial reports indicate significant wind damage, storm surge and flash flooding in communities in Florida, Alabama, Georgia, the Carolinas and Virginia.

title: Support Girls Gotta Run Athletic Scholars!
description: Help raise funds & awareness for girls who are empowering themselves & their communities through running and education in Ethiopia. GGRF's raising $10,000 to invest in 40 girls in the Mecca of running in Ethiopia - Bekoji. Your investment helps fund a program that integrates education, life skills, safe spaces, athletics, savings groups & entrepreneurship to holistically address the challenges facing  girls.

title: Education can not wait for 500 children in Bimbo
description: Complexe Scolaire Maison Prisca plans  to provide free education to 500 children who come from the poorest strata of society in Bimbo  also providing them with schooling and free meals. The project also builds a library in Bimbo, providing a rich supply of books and literacy services to 500 children  traumatized by the civil war in the Central African Republic. Complexe Scolaire Maison Prisca offers high-quality school education to poor children who cannot access it otherwise.

title: NOSTALGIA SENIOR THEATRE RENOVATION
description: International Humanitarian Union Catharsis, the one of the first NGO organizations founded in the Republic of Georgia in 1990 and the largest nationwide charitable complex center of emergency, social and senior care is seeking support for its Nostalgia Senior Theatre's 6-month renovation project with the total budget of 14,466 (fourteen thousand four hundred sixty six) US Dollars.

title: Zimbabwe Disability in Focus Project
description: This project will mobilize and build capacities of community volunteers to lead in linking girls and women with disabilities to essential services and dialogue platforms on which policy decisions are made.  That will begin with enumerating persons with disabilities and developing a database thereof, which defines their individual challenges, before rolling out customized empowering activities that enable beneficiaries to solve their own problems through policy advocacy and entrepreneurship.

title: #InspireDreams
description: This project will empower 450 foster care children in South Africa by providing them with vital entrepreneurial, financial literacy, employability and workplace readiness skills and help them to start and grow their own micro-enterprises. The participants will be capacitated to become the authors of their own destiny. We bring hope and by starting a real business give them a greater sense of control over their own lives.

title: Support for Continued Education of Girls
description: Girls education, especially backward regions like Mewat in Rajasthan, has always been a challenge. After grade 8, girls start dropping out due to distance to schools, safety concern of parents and conservative mindset. While Ibtada has prepared enough ground to motivate parents, distance to school/college and inability to bear expenses becomes a hurdle. provide transport facility to girls and pay their college fee to enable continued education

title: WheelchairFund for 100 Romanians with disabilities
description: Your donation gives back freedom of movement and self-confidence to 100 Romanians with mobility disabilities, by funding the renovation and donation of 100 quality wheelchairs. This project is part of Motivation`s pledge to provide 1,500 appropriate wheelchairs annually in Romania through the Wheelchair Fund initiative. In Romania, 1 in 5 persons who need a wheelchair does not have one. Every 5 years, 42-78,000 Romanians need a new wheelchair, but only 15,000 receiv one.

title: Adopt-An-Animal and Transform Lives in Africa
description: Your donation will directly go towards purchase of goats, sheep, chicken, camels and cows for East Pokot people. Households of elderly, persons with disability, orphans, malnourished & widows   will be targeted as beneficiaries. In 2017, HAO ran a fundraiser themed Adopt-A-Goat where people donated $50 to buy & give a goat to one household in East Pokot, Baringo County in Kenya as extreme poverty eradication effort. More than 30,000 livestock were lost in a 6-year drought prior to the campaign.

title: STEP-UP SANTA 2018 - NIEU BETHESDA, SOUTH AFRICA
description: This project will focus on the 281 Foundation Phase & Primary School learners from the Lettie De Klerk Primary School in Nieu Bethesda, Eastern Cape, South Africa - all who come from impoverished homes.  The Step-Up Santa Project will provide a sturdy backpack filled with treats which will not only provide the delight of getting a special gift but most importantly, provide each child with grade appropriate, quality stationery and a school bag for the following year.  EDUCATION IS OUR "KEY".

title: Safe Lives of IDW Living with HIV and AIDS
description: Safe Lives of Internally Displaced Women (IDW) Living with HIV and AIDS in Cameroon is an Innovative project aiming at providing 50 IDW living with HIV who lost their daily income and fled to West Region of Cameroon due to the conflict in English Speaking part of Cameroon with micro-support to enable them generate income through small businesses to pay for Cost of their CD4 Counts test. The project was designed after noticing frequent hospitalization and death rates among the women.

title: Give Anti-Malaria Medicine and Save a woman life
description: Abraham's Children Foundation (ACF), is working to provide free ant-malaria medicine to save life of women from been treated for malaria with ineffective boiled local leaves or herbs in under-served rural poor family in Nigeria. Malaria related dead among children and pregnant women among poor families is on the increase due to inability for these vulnerable persons to have access to quality anti-malaria medicine. Your kind donation will reduce malaria associated dead among women and end the use

title: Empower 500 women rescued from slavery in India
description: Rural women development trust aims to empower 500 rescued bonded laborer women ( Slavery System) in Salem district of Tamilnadu in India those who rescued from in brick kilns, stone quarries, coir and textile industries.  At work places they were treated as slaves. Lack of livelihood resources and caste discrimination forced them in slavery.They will be given skill training and support to start their own income generation activities in coir making, bamboo basket, sewing and other micro trades.

title: Train 600 Girls in Kyotera on Menstrual Hygiene
description: Dreams of the Tropical Youth Uganda (DROTY) will train 600 needy and vulnerable adolescent girls in rural Uganda (Kyotera) with the skills they need to make their own reusable sanitary pads. We will also educate school leaders on how to debunk myths that stigmatize menstruation, which will empower young girls to gain confidence and remove the shame of menstruation.

title: Set Up a New Learning Center for Hokkaido Children
description: The 6.8M earthquake in Hokkaido in early September severely damaged the town of Hobetsu's only Learning Center for children. Damage was beyond repair and so the building will be demolished by the government. This project will purchase a Trailer House that will be used to provide a place for over 47 children to continue their extra-curricular learning programs, and activities to relieve post-traumatic stress following the earthquake.

title: Sponsor an Angel's Education in South Africa
description: Sponsor a child's education at African Angels so they can give back to South Africa.    Poor rural children are behind the proverbial eight ball in South Africa today.  63% of youth are unemployed.  Children without resources are relegated to substandard education.  Poor education means a reduced chance or no chance of future employment, and so the cycle of poverty continues.    Since 2012 African Angels has provided quality primary school education for poor rural South African children.

title: Transform 22 Children's Lives in Johannesburg
description: Our sister organization is a primary school for 250 children from deprived backgrounds in Johannesburg, South Africa. The teachers recognized that many of the children were not achieving academically because of the home circumstances they were returning to every day - no food or electricity, and in many cases no parents. Thandanani ("place of love") was formed to help the worst-of-the-worst of these children and to provide a loving home environment where they could thrive as individuals.

title: Animal Cruelty Prevention Project
description: This project will rescue and treat 300 dogs and cats that are astray and no longer taken cared of by their owners in order for the animals to feel the warmth and love of human companionship. Our rescue effort will include provision of food, medicines and shelter for the animals. We will also conduct information campaigns among pet owners about their responsibility and impart knowledge on nutrition, health and general care of their pets.

title: Assist 100 Post Cancer Mission Patients in Nigeria
description: This project will support over 100 Post Breast/Cervical/Prostate Cancer and maternal health medical mission surgical patients in Anambra State, Nigeria, provide financial assistance with their hospital bills, complete their chemotherapy cycles and treatments.

title: Coral Reef Monitoring Programme in Malaysia
description: Reef Check Malaysia will survey and monitor the health of coral reefs at over 200 locations every year. Malaysia is part of the Coral Triangle, home to more than 75% of the world's coral species. The data is useful to address any decline of coral reefs by mitigating human pressures. Many island communities depend on coral reefs and other marine resources as their main source of livelihoods. We need to track the changing status of our ocean to prevent irreversible damage to the marine ecosystem.

title: Support a Community Health Worker
description: Supporting a community health worker not only supports each CHW and their families but also ensures that life-saving health information is disseminated at a community level in Maara Sub County. In the last 5 months, HopeCore CHWs have visited 3,306 households in addition to conducting school visits.  By supporting this project you are ensuring that these CHWs have the skills and equipment they need to improve their service offerings in the community.

title: Skills training centre for 14-25 yr olds - Nairobi
description: Raising Futures Kenya is building a new Seed of Hope training centre in the heart of a vulnerable slum community in Nairobi.   Our Seed of Hope programme provides vocational training and business & computer skills courses, alongside counselling, food and support for 14-25 year olds, many living in poverty. Enabling young people to secure employment or start a business becoming self-reliant.  Our Nairobi centre currently runs from shipping containers on a plot of land, we want to change this!

title: Greenhouse farming for 35 disabled young adults
description: A group of 35 young adults with disabilities from Tanga, a coastal town in eastern Tanzania, realize their dream of self-employment by setting up organic greenhouse farming. The land is provided by the local government, animal manure comes from the group's own poultry farming and the products are for sale at the nearby markets in villages and Tanga town.

title: Help Eco-Agric Uganda Support Our Communities
description: Eco-Agric Uganda is an NGO based just north of the capital, Kampala. We work with the communities we live in to better the lives of our community members through teaching sustainable farming practices, HIV/AIDS outreach, construction projects for individuals and schools, and  empowerment of women and youth though vocational training. We are always looking to help as many people as possible and with a donation from you we can achieve that dream. Thank you for helping!

title: School Expansion in Rural India
description: Global Hope Network plans to construct 2 additional classrooms at a school in the village of Dhoker Jhara, India. Education is critical for these students and their families to end their extreme poverty.  The school opened in 2015 with 30 students, and now has 150 students. It is crowded and cannot accept more students until more classrooms are built. In addition to other subjects, children who attend this school are studying both Hindi and English, which is a rare opportunity in rural India.

title: Empower Rural Argentinian Children with Rugby
description: Generate development opportunities and quality of life  for 2000 children in rural Argentina where poverty levels have reached 50% of the population. Teaching the values of World Rugby: passion, discipline, respect, solidarity and integrity.

title: Complex Retinal Surgeries in Diabetic Retinopathy
description: Diabetic retinopathy is a condition of the eye, where the retina with blood vessels is affected due to diabetes. If not treated appropriately, will lead to decreased vision and blindness.Most diabetic population reside in remote areas. Ignorance, lean accessibility, poor socioeconomic background, makes specialised investigation and treatment non affordable. We use a combination of technology,medical expertise and methodology, to reach patients with subsidized and affordable cost.

title: Save Hope of 6,800 Girls drop out of school Uganda
description: The project will save 6,800 vulnerable girls from dropping out of school by providing a Package of scholastic materials, Uniforms, school fees and training on sanitary pads making as Menstrual Hygiene and management approach for girl child school retention in Eastern and Northern Uganda. The project targets 24 schools to boost education of girls affected by Poverty, war trauma, and cultural practices including early marriage. 12 boreholes will be drilled in 12 schools and nearby communities.

title: Early intervention and Pre-School
description: The Early Intervention Unit at Raksha is a service that provides therapy and education to children with cerebral palsy, Intellectual Disability, Autism and Multiple disabilities aged between few months to 6 years, in order for them to have the best chance at meeting their developmental milestones and achieving their potential.

title: Keep Pakistan Learning
description: Covid-19 is worsening inequities in our education system. Where school closures abruptly stopped learning for millions of children in low-income communities with limited access to technology, Teach For Pakistan Fellows established innovative learning routines for students using WhatsApp, SMS, calls, and printed learning packs. Moving forward, we want to support the system in offsetting the learning losses, caring for emotional & mental well-being of students, and safe re-opening of schools.

title: Treatment & Therapy for Nodding Syndrome Children
description: HCU is staging a special needs intervention at Uganda's care center for youth with life-threatening degenerative neurological disease, Nodding Syndrome (NS). If funding requirements are not met, the center will be forced to turn away its 300+ beneficiaries: the last time the center closed for 6 months, 5 children died in this period. Donate to help affected children, staff, medical researchers, and the surrounding community in the struggle to understand, cope with, and treat Nodding Syndrome.

title: Offer holidays to 30 refugee children in Greece
description: This project will provide 3 days of outdoor activities in a farmhouse located in the region of Karpenisi to 30 refugee children living in refugee camps in Greece, offering them the chance to escape from their difficult everyday life by sharing moments of joy, adventure and revitalization.

title: Reaching Out to Those Affected by Mental Illness
description: This project will help feed about 1,000 mentally ill patients in the Freetown Municipality and it environs in order to build relationship/confidence between them and the service providers (social workers and mental health nurses) after long term neglect by their communities and family members. It will create awareness and reduce the level of stigma against the mentally ill persons within these communities.

title: Build a Horse Therapy Centre for Disabled Children
description: This project aims to create a safe relaxing environment for disabled children and their families by building a horse therapy centre for residential stays and an equestrian riding arena. The children will attend therapeutic riding sessions twice a day, bond with horses, and enjoy beautiful surroundings. Their parents will have time to get away from the daily routine and experience respite. Our organization will provide all that to the disabled children and their families for free.

title: Education Breaks Barriers
description: Our project provides equal educational opportunities to the most disadvantaged children and youth in Ukraine, enabling them to develop their potential through education. We also offer mentoring for orphans who are in need of emotional and academic support due to traumatic life experiences. We hope to interrupt socio-economic inequalities facing marginalized children and contribute to building a more just, democratic, and sustainable society.

title: Economic Empowerment for 70 Colorado Refugees
description: Teach By Tech is focused on restoring the autonomy of Colorado refugees by emphasizing self reliance and education. Our economic empowerment programs provide refugees with financial literacy training, digital literacy application and English language acquisition. Our unique approach uses mobile phones and digital tools in addition to classroom meetings to reach a larger audience and tailor each course to the specific needs of the community.

title: Develop the Future Leaders of Cambodia
description: Inspire Cambodian youth to develop leadership skills through mentoring, workshops and excursions.

title: Faces of STEM(TM)
description: Talent is equally distributed, but opportunity is not. STEM Advantage mentors, prepares, and inspires women and underserved communities to pursue careers in STEM through paid internships, mentors, scholarships, professional development, and community. We  "level the playing field" and provide economic and social mobility to underserved groups, while providing a vetted pipeline of diverse talent to businesses. Our vision is to build a diverse, equitable, and inclusive skilled workforce.

title: Train Cambodian Women in Sewing
description: Our sewing program provides women with a sustainable skill that enables them to earn income after just three months. It provides training in sewing skills to an advanced level; microfinance loans to buy sewing machines, and skills to establish sustainable businesses to support the women and their families.

title: Educate 160 Rural South African Youth
description: Sumbandila's Holiday School mission is to enrich the lives of 160 rural South African children by providing a student-centered learning environment, access to world-class educational resources and intense psychosocial support.

title: Food security for women farmers in rural India
description: Thousands of women farmers across India with less than 2 acres of land struggle to sustain their crop farming due to droughts, floods, pests and soil erosion. This leads to increased poverty and greater food insecurity for their families. Help us to provide climate-smart greenhouses for 500 women. These will safeguard their crops from such perils, use 90% less water, produce 7 times greater harvests per acre and provide these women with the means to increase their food security.

title: Supply Treated Bednets to 7200 Children-Uvinza
description: This project will supply treated bed nets to 7200 children under five years who, are under care of marginalized women heads of household in  rural and remote areas, 10 wards, Uvinza district,  preventing mosquitoes causing Malaria , also providing sanitation and hygiene education for community members, at large, respectively.

title: Provide Toilets To Greatly Improve The Health
description: To build pit latrines in rural communities to reduce greatly the mortality rate caused by people relieving themselves in the bushes. Most of the villagers in the rural communities of Kakamega County relieve themselves in the bushes.  The few latrines available serve over 20 households.  donate $10.00  for so 20 bricks and we need 500 bricK   $ 15.00 for wire mesh we need 5 rolls  $25.00    for so 2 bags of cement--we need 50 bags $30.00 for 7kg nails we need 15kg  $100.00 Donation from villag

title: Tharparkar Famine Appeal
description: Severe drought continues to make life miserable at Tharparkar. The numbers of malnourished children are increasing all the times. According to the latest report, 2 infants passed away on Friday, increasing the death toll to 49 in the past 38 days. 432 children have passed away on the last 11 months in District Tharparkar due to malnutrition and lack of health facilities. After the increasing deaths of children now mothers started suicide due to depressed situation.

title: Impuls'her Projects-Girls'Entrepreneurship Program
description: Impuls'her Projects is our new program dedicated to empower girls and teenagers in Bolivia and Cameroon. Two classes have been created in both countries with young Girls who are strongly motivated to learn, to create and to discover the micro-entreprenarial world. This program is for Girls who have been raised in homes for vulnerable children victims of abuse. Help us to Impuls'her Projects by making a donation to finance training and coaching and to support their lifetime projects.

title: Life-saving Infant Feeding Training Liberia/Rwanda
description: MAITS has developed a life-saving infant feeding programme for high-risk babies which reached 58,985 babies. Complications for premature babies are the main cause of death in under 5's, responsible for 1 million deaths in 2015. Most premature babies will have difficulty breastfeeding. MAITS trainers & master trainers work directly with mothers & babies to establish breastfeeding. We plan to expand this to Liberia through a skill-sharing project & introduce weaning support in Rwanda

title: Prevent and Treat Cervical Cancer in Guyana
description: This project supports RAM's Women's Health Program - providing free, timely, and consistent cervical cancer screenings, HPV vaccinations, and diagnostic and preventative services to the remote villages of Guyana. Volunteer providers partner with local healthcare professionals to bring essential care to Amerindian women. Before COVID-19 travel restrictions halted efforts, this program expanded to provide diabetes and blood pressure screenings, pediatric and medical clinics, and vaccinations.

title: Helping Rural Xhosa children become literate!
description: We provide quality Montessori early childhood education to 30 young, rural Xhosa children in a safe and stimulating early learning environment, in one of the poorest regions of South Africa.  The children receive 2 nutritious meals and a calcium/Vitamin C supplement daily.  Our children are building solid educational foundations in all learning areas and this is setting the tone for successful later learning.

title: Keep Girls in School with Period Kits & Toilets
description: When Nigerian girls get their periods, school can be a challenging - even unfriendly - place to learn. Too often, girls miss school during their period because they lack access to affordable period products or safe, private hygiene facilities. Help us transform a school near Abuja into a safe place for girls to thrive. We'll build toilets, washing stations, and a school library with a spotlight on health/hygiene. We'll also give every girl two long-lasting PeriodPanties from our partner Be Girl.

title: Aid poor teen mothers of rape get a future hope
description: Care and education prevents re-abuse, restore hope and dignity to  survivors of sexual rape and open doors for success and a bright future. This project in action in rural Rulindo District of Rwanda assists teen-mothers of sexual rape from poor families with basics needs, clinical care, safety, psycho-Social therapies, education, economic well being and ability to influence the decisions that affect their lives.

title: The Girl Impact Program in Cape Town, South Africa
description: The Girl Impact, a gender equality program in Cape Town, aims to empower women and girls by focusing on safety and violence prevention. So many destructive influences put a third of children at risk of physical violence, finding a solution difficult. We believe training women in Art Facilitation, which in return can be implemented with other community partners, is the solution to the violence that women and girls are facing. This project aims to benefit 14 trainees and over 300 children.

title: IMPROVE EDUCATION FOR YOUNG WOMEN IN POVERTY
description: Project Objectives: The goal of the projects is to improve English, entrepreneurship, STEAM education and to promote mutual understanding through cultural, educational, and professional development programs, for young women in social disadvantaged, victims of sexual, physical and psychological abuse

title: Build a Nursery School in St. Lucia, South Africa
description: Currently, a nursery school in St. Lucia educates 30 students between the age of 1-6, in one tiny wooden classroom. The classroom has too many to count structural problems and limited shelter from rain and cold due to the large gaps. Additionally, because of the poor conditions, the government does not financially support the school, teachers or staff. Help us build a nursery school with three classrooms to educate an additional 60 students and provide the conducive learning space they deserve.

title: Economic empowerment for people with disabilities
description: Kadiwaku Family Foundation wants to help 650 individuals with disabilities living in rural areas in Democratic Republic of the Congo to participate in entrepreneurship training and will provide them with accommodation and devices designed to assist a person to perform a particular task or run a business activity, such as wheelchair, hearing aids, white canes, tape recorders so that they live live independently and be economically and socially included into society.

title: Give slum living kids a future through football
description: This project will fund Flame Cambodia's football program for the entire year of 2019 for 65 slum living children. It will provide football uniforms, training equipment, transportation for the kids, a coach, clean filtered water and more. The purpose of Flame's football program is to help transform slum living kids into educated leaders by building character and life skills, helping them overcome or avoid social issues rampant among the poor, and keeps them motivated in their school learning.

title: SOLAR LANTERN LIGHTS FOR RURAL GREEN SKILL SCHOOL
description: CYSD's Rural Livelihoods Training Centre - a Green Skill School at Koraput, is a Field Lab for farmers on agro-forestry, organic farming; building women enterprise & youth skill. RLTC's 2 halls, 15 rooms, dining require constant energy for use of lights, fans & computers. Sadly, recurrent low voltage & load shedding hinders conduction of programs, participants' safe stay in hostel. Solar Lanterns can ensure reliable lights to halls & rooms at power supply breaks and harmless leaning environment.

title: Help partners in Haiti recover from earthquake
description: Lambi Fund plans to provide recovery assistance to 16 partner organizations in Haiti who are in need of food and shelter after a magnitude 5.9 earthquake hit northern Haiti. These partners participate in livelihood development projects that are now either damaged or destroyed because of the earthquake.

title: Rescue Orphaned & Injured Animals in the Amazon
description: Help care for 500 wild animals rescued from illegal trafficking in Bolivia. CIWY's three wildlife sanctuaries provide veterinary care, rehabilitation, and whenever possible, reintroduction to the wild. // Sumario: Ayudar a cuidar a 500 animales salvajes rescatados del trafico ilegal en Bolivia. Los tres santuarios de vida silvestre de CIWY brindan atencion veterinaria, rehabilitacion y, cuando sea posible, reintroduccion a la naturaleza.

title: Hands of Compassion Food Pantry
description: Hands of Compassion Food Pantry operates in Atlanta, GA  in order to lend a hand to low-income families that struggle to provide a balanced diet to their children or even put more food on their table.

title: Help children play in a safe place!
description: This project will benefit more than 1500 participants from our free time activities, providing them a place to keep them safe from the negative factors of their context such as violence and gang presence.  The dome will provide a safe place to play and a welcoming environment to meet with families and leaders.

title: Computer skills for 200 young people in Bangladesh
description: We are working with 200 underpriviliged young people in Bangladesh to help them develop practical computing skills which will enable them to earn a living in the future. Past students have gone on to find work as freelancers, earning money online. They have also worked with international organisations such as Sesame Street in Bangladesh. Your donation will ensure we can continue this work and help our next generation of students to achieve similar success.

title: Grandparents Plus: Raising Native Children at Home
description: Children entering foster care most often come with only the clothing on their backs and Native American youth are placed into care at a disproportionately higher rate than non-Native children. Grandparents are not prepared. This project will provide critical support to grandparents and kinship families who are finding themselves raising family members by supplying "starter kits" of clothing, diapers, and underwear, cribs and beds, bedding and a blanket, and a teddy bear to love forever.

title: People4Nature Green Climate Fund
description: We believe no human should bear the burden of climate change because of poverty or lack of access to climate-smart technologies.  And yet these are the factors that have compelled rural communities to continue to destroy their natural resources in search of livelihoods.   The People4Nature Green Climate Fund seeks to provide the community around Kaya Fungo Sacred Site, other sacred sites, and rural communities with climate-smart technologies to adapt and mitigate the impacts of climate change.

title: Zamong Jazba Complex
description: Zamong Jazba Complex is an orphanage which has started by a social welfare organization named Zamong Jazba Welfare Society in which there will be almost 40 orphans. This organization will properly provide shelter home and all required basic facilities for these 40 deserving orphans.

title: Empower & Rehabilitate 200 girls in Rural India!
description: Sevikashram (Gandhigram), runs rehabilitation program for more than 200 girl children in rural Tamil Nadu, India. Sevikashram's mission is to empower women and girl children with education and life-skills for them to live a respectable life in the society. Sevikashram has empowered over 3000 women and children over the years. Your donation will help us in Education, Rehabilitation and Empowering the lives of these girls and give them wings to pursue their dreams.

title: build a social complex for the disabled girls
description: construction and equipping of a social complex on an area of 4168 m2 for 925 girls and children with disabilities in Azilal, Morocco to facilitate their empowerment, inclusion and access to basic services.

title: MicroFinance Program
description: 15 women from conditions of abject poverty will be assessed to determine the most immediate help each member needs. Through a combination of skills training, money management training, subsidy in transportation, and purchase of equipment, these women will be given the tools to help grow their micro-businesses. Over the following months, on-going mentorship will be provided to assist them in pushing towards their goals.

title: Support 100 Rural Household access Electricity
description: This project will install 100 pieces of X850 with Satellite TV stand along solar home lighting system to 100 household within rural communities of District 1, Grand Bassa County, Liberia West Africa.

title: Reusable pads for 5000 girls in Baringo County
description: With your support, GEWEC will establish a social enterprise for producing reusable pads from local raw materials as sisal and banana fibre. These pads will be distributed to needy girls in Baringo County; hence boosting school attendance, retention and self-confidence. Needy women in rural areas will also have access to the reusable pad; hence, help boost menstruation hygiene among rural women who cannot afford expensive pads. The women involved in sewing the pads will also earn a living from it

title: Enable 240 people with disabilities in Sri Lanka
description: Those with disabilities in Sri Lanka continue to face poverty and hardship due to stigma, lack of community support and infrastructure.  Prithipura Communities provides a home, rehabilitation, education and work opportunities to 240 children and adults with disabilities with little or no family support, across 4 locations in Sri Lanka.  This project will contribute towards the salaries of 50 experienced carers and teachers.

title: Help Build a Free Primary School in Nairobi Slums
description: We are building a high standard modern Container primary school suitable for an informal settlement (slum) in Githogoro, Nairobi, Kenya - to provide high quality education for poor families living below $365 per year. Our aim is to give free access to education for children who  have no access to education so they can break out of the vicious cycle of extreme poverty. Since 2005 we have given access to education for over 1,000 children from the slum and we want enroll more children every year.

title: Philippines - Typhoon Mangkhut Relief Fund
description: The Philippine government announced that 5.7 million people were affected by Mangkhut. At the same time, NDRRMC estimated that Typhoon Mangkhut caused a loss of 626.8 million USD in Philippines during the harvest season. As a result, this fund will aim at recovery work on local victims and affected families, helping them with daily supplies and farming in order to get recovery step by step.

title: Give 100 Persons w/ Disabilities a Career for Life
description: This project aims to provide 100 Persons with Disabilities a career for life in retail sector through an industry leading training and mentoring program that addresses the recruitment challenges of leading corporate retailers in India. Hence creating a sustainable livelihood for Persons with Disabilities and also promote inclusive growth in the retail sector.

title: Give new sight to 100 blind students
description: YPSA has been giving new sight to visually impaired students with the help of technology aiming to ensure their equal access to information, knowledge, and education. YPSA involved in the production of books, content and reading material in accessible formats for the people who cannot read the print version of reading materials. We provides training to visually impaired to build their capacity on operating computer and Smartphone with screen-reading software without looking at monitor or display

title: Build a School for 360 children in Apolla Uganda
description: Biggi Family Project is working to free orphaned children from the cycle of poverty by providing a high-quality free education, both formal and informal, to children who have been orphaned due to civil unrest in order to counteract pervasive poverty, and systemic deprivation. Your donation will help build four new classroom blocks, provide a pupil uniform, meals and medicine for one school year for the needy children in the rural, and sub-urban parts of Pamora Apolla village in Northern Uganda.

title: Support survivors of gendered violence in Myanmar
description: Jeepyah's safehouse provides shelter to women and often children who have survived domestic and/or sexual violence. This project will provide them with access to justice, access to healthcare, and financial independence. These three services will empower survivors to thrive despite trauma. Justice - hiring lawyers to take cases to trial Health - care for injuries, pregnancies from sexual assault, deliveries Financial Independence - vocational training, purchasing equipment, start- up costs

title: Support 4000 youths to be future ready in Lagos
description: Future Readiness Tour plans to equip 4000 teenagers in 20 public secondary schools across Lagos state, Nigeria with 10 future skills stipulated by the World Economic Forum to give them the edge needed to build a future for themselves. Through access to professional mentoring, design thinking training and resources (coding, digital fabrication) to build solutions to the problems in their community, these young people are empowered to take on the future.

title: Wellbeing activities for residents of East Leeds
description: Our activities will bring people together from across East Leeds. Helping to reduce social isolation, improve mental well-being and help create lasting friendships between people in East Leeds, through conversation, fun and creative activities.  Activities will include social groups, visits to local places of interest, walks and other physical outdoor exercise and arts, crafts and bushcraft sessions. All our activities will take place in accessible community venues in East Leeds.

title: Build a Cardiac Center in Kigali Rwanda
description: Since 2007, Team Heart has been providing life-saving cardiac care for children and teens in Rwanda during annual surgical development trips. A US team provides surgery for 8 days at our partner Oshen-King Faisal Hospital. Able to perform only 2 cases/day due to lack of OR theaters, Blood bank support and ICU beds this is only the tip of iceberg to address a desperate need. Rheumatic Heart Disease, a disease of childhood and poverty affects the impoverished population primarily from rural areas.

title: Flood Relief for Families in Sipi, Colombia
description: On October 5, 2018 the San Agustin River flowed out of its banks and into the homes of families living in Sipi, Choco, Colombia. Over 250 families lost all of their belongings, with many also losing their homes. You can help bring much needed ongoing medical care, basic need packages, and most importantly HOPE to the families impacted by this tragedy.

title: 50 NEEDY FAMILIES TO RISE OUT OF POVERTY IN UGANDA
description: The project  will equip (50) youths, women and persons with disabilities with literacy skills, vocational, essential micro-entrepreneurial and life skills that will enable them rise out of poverty, provide for their families health and well-being as well as create opportunities for self - employment within their local communities. They will acquire skills which will transform them into productive entities of the nation and become units of change as well as wheels of development.

title: 150 Women to Restore Biodiversity in Mole Park
description: NORTHCODE-Ghana plans to restore biodiversity loss around the Mole National Park by supporting 150 women in 8 fringe Communities with bee keeping, tree planting and skills training to enable them adopt sustainable income generating activities thereby reducing their overdependence and overexploitation of a designated Community Resource Management Area called the  Jilinkon/Kunlog ''Community Resource Management Area'', fringing the Mole National Park Reserve for their livelihood and income.

title: VENEZUELA: EDUCATE, FEED AND HEAL 400 SLUM KIDS
description: We ensure that 400 children receive a formal academic education, one balanced daily meal and basic healthcare, in  a violent and poor area in Caracas, Venezuela. Since 1997, the private foundation Madre Maria Luisa Casar, through the school Jenaro Aguirre Elorriaga, looks after the welfare of the students and the community of the "barrio 24 de Marzo", Petare.

title: HeartCoin: Help us create the true market for good
description: At HeartCoin Foundation we are ready to launch our solidarity token and begin to move this true market for good. We only need your help to carry it out: 1) We need funds to carry out marketing and achieve participation and alliances among all our solidarity actors such as people, social organizations and companies. 2) Because our solidarity token is based on the blockchain technology, we need gas to be able to operate and record the peer to peer transactions in this decentralized database.

title: Constructing a school in rural Papua New Guinea
description: We need to fund the construction of Kobo Primary School to enable the children of Kobo and Wainsoduna Village to receive an education. The funding that was promised to the project has not come through, so we're trying to raise money to improve one of the least developed areas in the Morobe province and give the residents the quality of life that they deserve.

title: "The Journey of an Individual Philanthropist"
description: LIN believes that everybody can be a philanthropist and each person has their own giving journey. In this campaign, LIN wants to propose to everybody a few options to continue on their journey or create a new path of giving. These are only our recommendations for giving options & you can always drive your own journey and make positive changes to our society. Through this journey, LIN hopes to inspire more people in our community to give back and join forces to build a stronger community together

title: A warm and safe day centre for vulnerable families
description: For over 30 years, The Family Haven has been a lifeline to vulnerable families in Gloucestershire. We offer a haven of warmth and learning to children under five in our nursery, while our trained staff bring desperately needed support to their mums and dads.  Just 5 from you could buy a hot lunch for a family who have nothing - and start turning a life of chaos into a brighter future.  Each year we support an average of 60-70 families, that is around 120 children and 100 adults.

title: Chhori (Daughter)
description: This Project will raise awareness on proper menstrual hygiene and sanitized better practices by providing sanitary napkins to the schools and communities which are produced locally. The money  will be reinvested in establishing quality education and build up clean and sanitized WASH facility in the schools.

title: Help the Homeless this Christmas in Leicestershire
description: No one should wake up homeless and alone on the streets over Christmas.  Falcon Support Services want to provide 3 emergency beds to those that are homeless in Leicestershire over the festive period from 3rd Dec - 3rd Jan. We also want to open our doors to the most vulnerable and isolated to provide a community Christmas Lunch. We will provide a warm bed, hot meal, breakfast, support, shower facilities, use of a washing machine and a memorable Christmas.

title: Save 10 000 Women & Girls from Human Trafficking
description: According to 2018 global slavery index, 74 out of every 100 Nigerians are vulnerable to human trafficking, and majority of  them are women & girls living in rural communities.   We have created HumansNot4Trade project to:   (a). Train 200 women in 15 communities as  advocates & empower them to  tackle women trafficking.   (b). Sensitize 10000 women, girls, and youth on dangers of human trafficking and migration   (c). Support two female survivors of human trafficking with skills and resources.

title: Disability Rehabilitation of 200 children in Kenya
description: The Proposed Project will address physical and health conditions and challenges associated with disability among poor children under age 12 in Busia and Siaya counties of Kenya through medical rehabilitation by reaching them through community clinics. The community outreach will provide comprehensive intervention care including Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy and provision of assistive devices to correct the suffering of the target children and help them lead a normal and productive life.

title: Help us to Grow the Green Army
description: Seeding Futures is an accredited 15-week program that teaches permaculture design to unemployed youth, equipping them with the skills to grow their personal, household and neighbourhood resilience and connects them to work in the local green economy.

title: Japan Disaster: Relief & Recovery
description: Japan has been affected by a number of natural disasters in recent years. From heavy rains in Hiroshima in 2018 to typhoons and mudslides in the summer of 2022 to earthquakes, flooding, and mudslides in 2023, Peace Winds has been working on short-term emergency response as well as long-term community-building and disaster preparedness activities in the affected areas.

title: Women who cultivate and transform their community
description: Provide to women in vulnerable situation with food insecurity a community garden to generate their own food and provide nutrition education through workshops to generate a healthier diet, self-sufficiency and collaboration among their community.

title: Train and operate 300 displaced women in Yemen
description: Millions of displaced people in Yemen have been left without work due to the war, providing little humanitarian assistance. The project aims to support families of displaced people on handicrafts and household industries, providing them with an income source and shifting from relying on relief assistance to productive families. The project is concerned with women in particular, through the selection of displaced families who lost their dependents.

title: School Gardens & Skills Training For 400 Gambians
description: Grace Foundation Gambia provides free meals, school gardens and skills training in schools to mainly 400 poorest girl children and youths in the West Coast region who come in schools daily on hungry stomach and made to engage in street trading where they face child trafficking, girl marriage, teenage pregnancy etc in order to feed at home. Since inception Grace Foundation has succeeded in rescuing 397 children from the streets and providing them with basic education and free school meals.

title: Help Girls to Complete their Education up to 12th
description: Number of Girls up to age  18  do not complete there education up to 12 standard ,Most of them leave education in class  6-12. This is due  poverty  because there parent not have money no guidance available to them ,Most of them helping there family earning practices and take duty of caring there small brother and sister when there parents go to field for for crop or animal feeding, few left education because they don't have bicycle to reach because there school and collage are too far to reach.

title: Keep 50 girls in school in Kenya
description: This project will award 3 high school scholarships to bright but needy girls who cannot afford to continue with  their secondary education,as well as provide 47 school supplies packs that otherwise cannot be provided by primary student's families or schools.

title: Emergency Afterhours Safehouse and Foster Care
description: The Sunlight Safe House (SSH) was established in 1997 under the auspice of Childline Gauteng.  The SSH is an after-hours service for abused and abandoned children, as traditional organisations are closed at night and during weekends.  SSH provides short-term care, in the form of the after hours reception centre and  loving community homes, for children removed by the South African Police Service (SAPS) until a suitable placement is found by the relevant statutory services.

title: Educating Minors in Prison Cameroon.
description: This project seeks to provide educational qualification and personal skills to some displaced youth caused by the ongoing crisis in the English regions of Cameroon to ease thier reintegration into the society upon release. Some have lost thier homes, perants and education due to this effect, because of hunger and unable to Carter for themselves, they  have involved themselves  into criminal activities thats has let them today in prison. Some are orphans and street childrens they need your help.

title: Support needy families attain quality education
description: We are a family-based; child focused non-for-profit organization in Uganda. We exist because we realized that in Uganda most people are young and poor. We therefore exist to tackle the great challenge of poverty through provision of accessibility to quality education to children and youth within the age bracket of 3 to 17 years. We intend to provide full education scholarships to at least 5 beneficiaries and their families every year. It will be 5 families added to our funding every year.

title: Nutrition & health for 150 kids Petare, Venezuela
description: This project will provide a nutritional breakfast and lunch for 150 students and teachers in our 2 schools in Petare. With the support of a team of doctors and other health experts, we'll diagnose students, teachers, and families to provide appropriate health treatments. In the process, we'll deliver workshops to teach healthy habits and disease prevention to attack the serious nutritional and health crisis that affects Venezuela. OSCASI has served low-income families in Petare for 60 years.

title: Amazon Research and Conservation Station
description: Sustainable Bolivia is seeking support to build the very first research and conservation station in the Bolivian Amazon.  This station will allow us to monitor and identify current and new species of flora and fauna, extend our reforestation efforts, and work to increase the size and scope of the Aquicuana Reserve. Furthermore, this station will allow us to effectively engage with local communities and policy makers, providing long-term opportunities for sustainable development.

title: Women Empowerment for Collective Action (WECA)
description: 600 poor & marginalized women will be organised and supported different capacity building training like leadership development, communication, legal rights etc. to increase self-confidence and skill based training like mushroom cultivation, Bee keeping, goat farming and different entrepreneurial activities to improve livelihood. As a result the poor marginalized women will be empowered and access their rights and opportunities.

title: Education Support for 150 Deaf Children,Bangalore
description: The school is facing challenge to provide quality education on regular basis due to shortage of funds for meeting salaries of special teachers, other staff, safety measures, hearing aids, and school maintenance.  Government and other donors are supporting to cover 80% of the total costs needed for providing quality education to 150 deaf children.   Therefore, it still leaves a critical gap of 20% costs. This shortfall would put the education of 150 disabled children at stake.

title: Teacher Training to improve Student's Learning
description: This project will help create a pool of trainers with the help of a Master Trainer who will be mobilised to the 5 public primary schools we work with. Every teacher is based in Janakpur, a rural expanse of Nepal. We will provide training on the pedagogy of teaching and teaching with compassion to benefit the larger number of children in the community. The training will also include school visit, cross learning, and peer review of the teachers work.

title: Support 12 disabled children through life skills
description: This project targets 12 parents of children with special needs through craft/jewellery, baking, tailoring and soap/detergent making. Parents are  undergoing training and work placements. They will then be provided with start-up kits to run their own small businesses. The aim is to increase access to special needs education for children with disabilities through enhancing livelihood option for vulnerable parents.

title: COMPUTER FOR DEAF STUDENTS IN TANZANIA.
description: Tanzania Empowerment for Persons with disability and Gender Health Organization seeks $6,736. to fund an innovative computer education program for deaf pupils in Pomerini deaf unit. The program will serve 45 deaf pupils and 7 teachers annually. The organization's  mission is to bridge the technological gap between hearing pupils and the deaf pupils. Located in Iringa town and the targeted school is located in 58kms from Iringa town.

title: Tackling Malnutrition in Young Children in Mexico
description: In Mexico, 14 million children under ten are living in marginalized communities. In these communities, they suffer from issues ranging from food insecurity to malnutrition and obesity. For over 20 years, Fundacion Nutriendo has served the children of San Luis Potosi by assisting them in combating situations where food affordability and instability are a constant concern in their communities. Our program currently serves 4,200 children, providing them with meals, and monthly medical evaluations.

title: Equine Therapy for Autism Horse SenseAbility
description: The Family Autism Center at The Arc of South Norfolk provides supports and services to people diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders and their families.  We provide respite care, specialized recreational programming, training for family members and provide information and referral sources to families looking for assistance.  Autism impacts 1 in every 40 children- we have seen an increase of 100 additional people EACH year- we serve 903 people currently.

title: End-Of-Year  Empower Girlz with Goals to Become
description: Make a #GivingTuesday donation to Girlz With Goals to empower young girls in Jamaica. On the annual day to give as good as you get, make a difference in the fight to help girls create a brighter future for themselves and their communities. Your #GivingTuesday donation can help fight food insecurity, send a girl to school, help girls learn skills, and empower girls in their fight against street harassment.    Start your holiday season with a donation to Girlz With Goals. Matching funds available!

title: 500 Colombian Children Learn Equality through Arts
description: Life Project Foundation is a round-the-clock safe space for over 500 Colombian children living in the slums. We provide arts, music, and theatre workshops focused on teaching about gender equality. The acceptance of diversity is our goal. The activities are supplemented with a nutritious snack every day. We also offer school tutoring to breach the opportunity gap.

title: Train 80 Guatemalans in Civic Advocacy
description: With your support ALG can offer high quality training in two-day camps to supervisors of NGO's and community leaders who work in remote communities. The goal of these trainings is to teach leaders how to create spaces for collective healing that can empower, equip, and inspire participants to restore democracy in their nation through the methodologies of Restorative Justice and Social Technologies which work to facilitate collective dialogues oriented to promote action toward the common good.

title: Gentle Giant Summit for Stakeholders in Kerala
description: Globally there are 40,000 Asian elephants; 27,300 housed in India. It is imperative to protect this endangered species in its last stronghold. However, relevant government ministries tend to operate in silos, which is driving wildlife crime and senseless tragedies. These ministries need to convene together, and commit to transparency, resource and knowledge sharing to protect the majestic elephants. Gentle Giant Summit will foster cooperation between government ministries, and protect elephants

title: Home Gardens for 100 Families, Oaxaca, Mexico
description: The project will support 100 rural households to establish home and community gardens. It provides families with the ability to produce healthy vegetables that are scarce and expensive in local markets because of COVID-19. Due to social distancing restrictions, access to food has decreased. The families consider these backyard gardens a solution to produce native and nutritious plants at a low cost, in a sustainable way, and secure family nutrition and health in La Chinantla, Oaxaca.

title: Support to Transitional housing for homeless men
description: We are working hard to raise the necessary funds to buy a property located at 3800 N. 27th street in Lincoln Nebraska,68504  We will convert this building into both a transitional housing facility and a vocational training center for homeless men in Lincoln Nebraska.  We will also provide transportation and job training for these men in dire need for assistance to get back on their feet and live a productive and very productive life. All this is possible if we join forces.

title: Let's give 500 families in Puerto Rico a safe home
description: Puerto Rico Rises is distributing building material to 500 families affected by Hurricane Maria.  Now we are adding those recently impacted by the earthquakes and daily tremors.  Buildings weren't strong enough and now they are getting weaker by the day.  Thousands are still living in unsafe houses.  We have already impacted 325 families and plan to reach 500 by July, 2021.

title: END SEXUAL VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN IN NIGERIA
description: This project will fund the design and implementation of visitation tours of 770 schools in Nigeria to sensitize pupils and students to their right to freedom from sexual violence as well as teach them life-coping skills, and provide counselling and therapeutic services to victims of sexual violence. Publish a book to teach children about body ownership, how to recognize abusive situations and protect themselves.  This project intends to donate the book to at least 770 schools in Nigeria.

title: Free Medical Care for Poor Lepers in India
description: We are giving every month free chemotherapy treatment (MDT) to all detected  leprosy  cases. Every new found patient gets MDT treatment for curing the infection. This activity aims to prevent deformity through early detection and treatment.      Physiotherapy treatment is also given to our deformed patients as well as active and passive exercises, wax baths and oil massages. Ulcer patients are getting ulcer dressing treatment and we advise these patients how to keep the limbs (hands &feet)

title: HELP 100 POOR CHILDREN FOR HEART SURGERIES
description: Children's heart disease is a very common birth defect globally and 90% of the children born have limited access to the care to lead a normal and healthy life. Nearly 180,000 children are born with Congenital Heart Disease each year in India. Of these, nearly 60,000 to 90,000 suffer from critical CHD requiring early intervention.10% of present infant mortality in India is accounted for CHD. We bridge the gap between the patient and hospital by financially supporting the surgery of poor children.

title: Stepping towards a new School Building
description: Our students are receiving a wonderful education but are crowded in to small classrooms. A new building would be more space and better conditions. The rent we now pay can be used to improve the asset and provide additional resources and supplies. The building  will have a library open to the community and the village will have a place to meet for English classes, computer classes and other gatherings.  This is "Step One" of the building project - a good foundation.

title: Recovery Housing for Women in a Rural Area
description: This project will fund The Gratitude House for Women, the only State-Certified recovery residence for women in the rural area of Talbot County, on the eastern shore of Maryland.   There is a desperate need for prolonged recovery support for women leaving treatment for substance abuse and recovery residences are a proven, evidence-based modality to improve recovery outcomes.   .

title: Integrate & Educate 2000 Street Children in Kenya
description: We are a charity trust organization in Kenya that focuses in finding solutions to the street families problems especially children who are the majority.  This project will focus on Street-Child Family Reunion through Counseling and reintegrating 2000 children back to their families for good social Care. To us, no love is greater than the love of a family. After this we enroll them to schools to continue with their studies for the drop outs and freshly join those who had never had an education.

title: Help with Construction of Porta Classrooms
description: The goal is to have five classrooms for the Computer Section, Library, Special Needs Section, Vocational Training and Creative and Performing Arts. The objectives are:  1) To provide activities designed towards holistic growth and development 2) To impart suitable training and equip students with the requisite skill sets for future employment 3)To provide space for Special Needs Children to develop in a comfortable and secure environment

title: Support a Library to Eradicate Poverty
description: Siaya Community Library, the only public library in a county of 920,671 people supports educational development and reduction of illiteracy in Siaya.  Literacy is important for economic and social development. The library makes available a wide range of materials and services.  It needs support to properly equip it and make it useful and accessible to the community.

title: GIVE LIFE TO 100,000 WOMEN & YOUTH IN SOUTH SUDAN
description: Project overturns issues of poverty, ill-health & illiteracy population rapidly growing into endangered future for children, youth, and women in Southern Sudan. The project builds capacity, community healthcare, and group economic activities in farming, livestock, produce distribution, and pass-on activities through retention process, 'each-one-reach-one' awareness, evening literacy class, & applied reusable shared effort to reduce costs & utilities for multiple time & purpose. More fund helps.

title: Empower 800 children with birth defects in Chennai
description: This project will help 800 children with birth defects such as club foot/ancle drop/ knock  knees etc needing appliances such as Dennis Brown shoes/ancle foot orthosis/knee brace.  By identifying and providing such appliances, our team at the Government Hospitals  will help these children walk;  play and grow up as independent adults. We will periodically replace worn out or need adjustments appliances used by the children.

title: Educate a girl child to fight child marriage.
description: This project will raise awareness on child marriage, develop transformative leadership amongst girls, build confidence through both formal and nonformal education programs. Rescue and Educate a girl child project by kyobe foundation seeks to champion the importance of education as an alternative to early marriage by ensuring enrollment of girls after withdrawing them from forced marriages.

title: A Permanent Space for Kranti School!
description: Kranti empowers girls from Mumbai's red-light areas to become agents of social change...and happiness! We currently work with 25 girls, ages 13-23, who are survivors of trafficking or daughters of sex workers from Kamathipura, Asia's most infamous red-light area. Unfortunately, since we started seven years ago, we've already been kicked out of five rented homes, forcing the girls to change schools, therapists and friends every year. PLEASE help us to buy (or build) a permanent space for Kranti!

title: Provide Drinking Water to Drought-Affectees in Pak
description: Through this project, approximately 12,000 population of drought affected area of district Dadu-Sindh Pakistan will be provided with safe drinking water by installing "common deep handpumps" in order to facilitate the maximum number of people most in need until they recover from this disaster-like situation.

title: Safe Habitat for Grand mum and her grand children
description: This project is proposing to refurbish a house for a vulnerable family which is headed by an elderly woman and she lives with her seven grandchildren. Through this project, AHCM plans to empower the family of this grandma this Christmas to respond to their immediate need for shelter by refurbishing the house. The project is to be started and implemented in January 2019.

title: Effective Mobility in children service
description: This project is aimed at purchasing a service van. The proposed new van will be used to deliver children to School and back to the Orphanage, field visits, as well as pick volunteers from airport. It will also be used for errands and medical visits in the community. Savings in vehicle hire costs will be significant.  The service van will fulfill these transportation components: - first, increase transportation options for the young children and simplify young children 's access to transport

title: Christmas Blessing Project
description: This project will enable 50 Households in Iganga tocelebrate Christmas together with joy and happiness, Many family are in agony because they could not afford to buy a special meal like rice and chicken on Christmas and with this project, a Christmas package containing some food stuffs will be given towards Christmas. they will receive gift hampers including but not limited to, sugar, soap, salt, rice, maize flour, cooking oil and bread this will enable them have a wonderful time on Christmas

title: School for young Mexicans socially disadvantaged.
description: Project provides continuity into senior high school studies for 159 young Mexicans living in 13 poverty communities. Education takes place in Community Learning Centers, which are physical spaces equipped with Internet, access to online studies platform of a public university, personalized follow-up and human skills workshops. At the end of project, they will have advanced 10 subjects of their academic syllabus and have received training in human skills to strengthen their personal development.

title: ENABLE the 300 Indigenous Samal Bajau Students
description: The Enhance Necessary Access to Basic Literacy and Education (ENABLE) program  will be an instrument for a developmental intervention designed for the indigenous communities of Sama Bajaus in Maluso, Basilan. It will focus on implementing education program for 300 students especially in assisting them in their basic formal studies. This program will definitely uplift their dignity and be respected by others. Education is the key to the development of the Bajaus

title: Improving health of 500 Guatemalan school children
description: This project will provide dental and health screenings, supplies and health education for 500 indigenous Mayan school children in Guatemala. The team will screen for dental cavities and anemia, monitor growth over time and provide preventive care, such as fluoride varnish and daily vitamins. These measures enhanced with health education each week by a community health educator will empower children to become healthier, allowing them to attend school.

title: Help an Indian Orphanage this Christmas
description: It's that time of year here at The Good Shepherd Agricultural Mission. We are pulling out the decorations, dusting off our tree and preparing to wrap another boat load of presents! The Christmas celebrations are about to begin!  It's no small job! There are 68 children, 55 Staff and volunteers and around 60 expected visitors! There are gifts and clothes to buy treat bags and stockings to fill, picnics, special meals, fireworks and decorations. All for around 200 people!

title: Help 15 Girls in Bali Graduate From High School
description: Many girls living in poverty may stop going to school, so they can work to help their parents and provide foods for their families, which leaves them without literacy and numeracy skills they need to further their careers. YKIP plans to provide a 3-year scholarship for 15 girls from disadvantaged families in Bali to complete their 12-year education and graduate from senior high school. The scholarship cost will include school fees, uniform, school supplies, daily allowances, and a workshop.

title: Delhi's Homeless need urgent support this winter
description: There are more homeless people in India than the entire population of Mauritius. In fact, if you gathered all of India's homeless people and put them all in a new country, its population would be larger than that of 83 countries. Delhi is homelessness capital with three districts among India's worst six. With the onset of winters in Delhi, these homeless people face life threatening cold climate. IGSSS's Winter Of Hope project is supporting the Delhi's homeless poor to survive harsh winters.

title: Toilet Outhouses Need Rebuilding
description: 200 Thatched outhouses from palm-fronds, have disintegrated due to the harsh weather conditions and need to be rebuilt with sturdy bricks.  The 6 year old outhouses have virtually disappeared, making the toilets unusable and the community is now practicing open field defecation.

title: Reducing maternal & neonatal mortality in Nigeria
description: In Nigeria lack of access to safe maternity services contribute to a range of adverse outcomes, like disability and death. With limited resources we can't meet the need for obstetric and neonatal care. Less than half of mothers have access to proper healthcare and there's a huge lack of trained health workers and basic medical supplies. If a woman goes into labour she won't be able to get to a hospital- even if she does, there probably won't be a trained midwife to give her the care she needs.

title: NEW LIFE TO SMALL BUSINESSES UNDER WOMEN AND YOUTH
description: The business acumen inherent in us if well nurtured over time will result in food security, education for children and dignity for family heads especially women headed families. Small savings to the tune of   $0.02 can be ignored but overtime results in a lump sum saving that will enable more funds when needed and when practiced in a non bank environment. Constantly these give stable families freed from evil vices in most informal settlements among the rural /urban poor.

title: Help 500 Thai children get an education
description: For many families in Northern Thailand, education is a luxury they cannot afford. Education Matters, our scholarship program, supports low income families to send their children to school by covering educational costs including tuition, school lunch and uniforms. By supporting children to complete high school and even attend university, these children will grow up better equipped to provide for their families, thus ending the vicious cycle of poverty, abuse and neglect.

title: Empower South African children with reading skills
description: The Youth4Literacy (Y4L) objective is to place reading assistants in each Grade 2/3 classroom in 22 schools in the Western Cape. Each classroom receives a box of storybooks and readers and each child in the class receives two or three paired reading sessions a week and has at least two stories read to class each week. In addition, each child is encouraged to read at home through the promotion of our data-free Storytime with Shine Mobi-Site and the provision of a quarterly @Home pack.

title: CaywoodBrown Drug Rehabilitation and Empowerment
description: This Project will help in the rehabilitation of 25 youths who came forward after our Drug Abuse Awareness Seminar 2.0.  Where they were exposed to the knowledge of the effects of Drug Abuse. They want to stop but they understand the effect of withdrawal syndrome they could suffer and want to be under specialist care to guarantee ultimate success.  We would be partnering with a Professional Addiction Treatment Centre which provides in-patient treatment for people eighteen years and older.

title: Affordable Health & Dental Care in Rural Haiti
description: H.O.P.E.'s Alyans Sante Borgne hospital offers affordable health and dental care, and fosters economic growth in the process by hiring local, qualified residents. This project will provide health interventions and treatments (such as general emergency services, cancer screenings, and dental care) to the men, women and children in the rural commune of Borgne, Haiti.

title: Save both Veterans and Rescued Dogs today!
description: This project saves the lives of many by empowering veterans, adults and children with disabilities to restore their freedom to live life through the training and use of their service dog. Our service dogs are commonly pulled from rescues and rescue groups to give them, as well as their handler, a new purpose and lease on life.  We provide everything for our clients while in the program, covering all costs including equipment (such as dog bowls, vests, etc.), veterinary bills, food, etc.

title: Entrepreneurial training 20 families in Tennessee
description: Our Program is designed to educate underserves, underemployed persons with professional soft skills to elevate them to a living wage. During our 6-week program taught at community centers, we empower self-sustainability through entrepreneurial training.

title: Help Families Fleeing Crisis Rebuild Their Lives
