description: When an emergency strikes, the International Rescue Committee arrives on the scene within 72 hours to assess the need and deliver urgent aid to people fleeing war, violence, or disaster. As one of the first organizations to respond in major humanitarian emergencies, we work diligently to gain an understanding of what resources are needed, so we can save as many lives as possible. We then commit to staying as long as we are needed.

title: Change the World, Fund a Teacher
description: Teach With Africa will send additional teacher training teams to rural areas in South Africa and Zambia to help provide quality education in the most underserved areas.  Since 2007, Teach with Africa (www.teachwithafrica.org) has reached over 150,000 learners and teachers in South Africa, but there are many more children who can thrive with well-trained and inspiring educators.

title: 2000 Young Girls 15 to 24 diagnosed HIV+ Weekly!
description: We are so Unique. HIV education programs to schools has the capacity to reach 80000+ young people in 2019. A severe lack in education of STIGMA is affecting the lives in this vulnerable group, they are now the highest risk group. We face fear head on.  Our project brings those groups together with real people living with HIV and have overcome STIGMA.  Our speakers and the story telling program bring the subject of STIGMA to the forefront. Education is power for an HIV FREE GENERATION.

title: Innovative Solutions for Social Impact in Colombia
description: "Doing" projects for social good is not enough. We maximize our impact by teaching and supporting other organizations to understand and manage theirs - and shifted our focus to respond. Now, we are going big: to support hard-hitting organizations at a greater, and more meaningful scale. We will give them the knowledge, technical support and resources they need to measure, manage and maximize the good that they do for the resources that they invest to create exponential social change.

title: Equip School Health Unit in East Indonesia
description: An education center for children with disabilities located in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia is in need of safe and proper facilities to conduct learning activities and therapies for their students. This project will provide needed equipment for the school health unit and suitable training for the teachers and parents.

title: Support Landmine victims in Quang Binh, Vietnam
description: Quang Binh province has about 19,928 landmine victims. Most of them are living in rural and mountainous areas with poor economic conditions. In addition, landmine accidents more or less affect their ability to work. Therefore, it's difficult for them to obtain a stable job with income. Without a sustainable economic base, they are also limited in accessing health care service. The project hopes to empower landmine victims to increase their income, self-sustainability and social participation.

title: Transformative Art Education in Madurai schools
description: This project shall spearhead a multi-disciplinary-art education in Madurai schools targeting 750-1000 students. It introduces the internet as a new media for artists and creators. They explore its global reach, complexity, and evolving ethics. AJ Trust has designed a transformative curriculum in conjunction with artists and scholars across cultures. This program is for all  school teachers and students. They are given space to think, express, and act clearly, critically, and collaboratively.

title: Educate and Feed a child in distress
description: Roxnana Learning Centre provides quality education and nutrition to 250 vulnerable children from the poorest segments of the population in Kasarani Slums of Nairobi City County.

title: Change lives in Zanzibar through music
description: This project will allow 30 young people with musical talent to continue their education at Dhow Countries Music Academy (DCMA) - the only music school in Zanzibar - and give them an opportunity not only to develop their talents but also to change their lives.  DCMA was established in 2002 and throughout the years had more than 1600 students. It has gained an international reputation winning a number of regional and international awards for teaching traditional music.

title: Hope for education to10 teen mothers in Zambia
description: DACKANA plans to send back to school 10 adolescent girls who are victims of early and unplanned pregnancies, pay for their school fees and provide them books, uniforms and sanitary towels monthly.  DACKANA will also provide early childhood education and health care services to their young babies at our premises in Kabwe, Zambia, during the period the girls will be at school.  By so doing we are confident that the girls will concentrate in school and be able to complete their education

title: Help 100 women in Sierra Leone escape poverty
description: This project will transform the lives of 100 illiterate young women in Sierra Leone by helping them to escape a vicious cycle of poverty.  It will empower them to feed themselves and their families, send their children to school and pay for vital medicine.  Peace Child will train the illiterate young women to create and develop their own business.  It will give them the self-confidence, skills and experience they need to become financially independent for life.

title: Provide 2000 with Water and Sanitation=WASH4Health
description: Supporting education and improved health for 2,000 people across communities, health centers and schools, this project will provide training to community pump caretakers, WASH Committees and volunteers on preventive maintenance and rehabilitation of dysfunctional water wells. For areas without access to water supply and toilets, we will deliver on making them available. The project will expand access to safe drinking water, improved conditions of health and increased school attendance for kids.

title: Awareness on safe and unsafe touch to 1 lakh kids
description: 1) 1 Lakh children (from 3 to 16 years) of government schools of madhya pradesh will be trained on safe and unsafe touch.   2) two School teachers from each schools and 5 children from each school  will be trained as master trainer to sustain the project.   3) School support staff will be trained to take care of children by child friendly practices.   4) 1000 schools in Madhya pradesh will be demonstrated as child friendly schools.

title: End Child Abuses in Cambodia by Positive Parenting
description: Sadly, Cambodia has the highest rate of violence committed on children by parents in the world; with more than 50% of the children experiencing physical abuse and more than 30% experience emotional abuse. ICS-SP is recognized by the government for parenting expertise and this project is part of Cambodian Action Plan to Prevent and Respond to Violence on Children 2017-2021. The plan focuses on strengthening parent's knowledge in positive parenting, providing long-term benefits to 500 children.

title: Put Resilient Roofs on Damaged Puerto Rican Homes
description: This project will support AHAH's long-term recovery work in Puerto Rico. Public attention and funding has turned to other issues/disasters, but thousands of people still need help after Hurricane Maria. All Hands and Hearts is committed to staying and helping our fellow citizens through the second anniversary, focusing on putting hurricane resilient roofs over the heads of suffering families, making these homes safe and secure. $20,000 buys materials/tools to repair 10 flat cement roofs.

title: Help Mothers of the Disappeared Find Justice
description: Since the start of Mexicos drug war in 2006, more than 37,000 people have disappeared. Authorities are often involved in the disappearances or are unwilling to resolve them, which has led to hundreds of mothers forming collectives throughout the country to personally search for their loved ones and to seek justice for these wrongdoings. We provide capacity-building training to these mothers in order to empower them in exercising their rights to justice, to the truth, and to receive reparations.

title: Train the next generation of environmental leaders
description: This project will provide critical resources for Green Corps to give top-notch training in organizing and advocacy to 20-25 young, aspiring environmental organizers through our yearlong fellowship program. Skills such as recruitment, media work, coalition building, leadership development, lobbying and campaign strategy will empower organizers to run and win critical environmental campaigns both during their Green Corps year and beyond as they launch careers in environmental and social change.

title: Support Social Entrepreneurs Combat Energy Poverty
description: 3.2 million households are living without power in Malawi. Social entrepreneurs in the energy sector are working to change that. But first, they need to gain essential technical and business skills to launch successful social enterprises that would change their communities. Your support will go towards specialized entrepreneurship training designed to help individuals launch social enterprises that provide and promote the use of safe and renewable energy sources.

title: Help Oakland Children Cope with Grief and Loss
description: The majority of low-income and minority children and youth in Oakland CA live in areas with high rates of gang violence, poverty, and environmental pollution. These factors have overwhelming led to parental and caregiver deaths, leaving children and family members emotionally and financially devastated.  East Bay Agency for Children's (EBAC) Circle of Care Grief and Loss program provides peer grief counseling support for low-income children struggling to cope with the loss of a loved one.

title: #TheyCanSurvive#Yemen
description: WHO reports show that from Sep 2016 to March 2018 1,103,683 suspected cholera cases were reported & 2385 deaths. There are more than half a million suspected cases of cholera in Yemen according to a report by the World Bank on Aug 2018. Burra in Al-Hodeidah has 12 health centers which are under developed & under equipped to combat epidemics. According to  Burra association,  No. of reported acute watery diarrhea cases in 2018 has reached 1,750 & it's increasing. Support Burra overcome Cholera!

title: Help 450 Rwandan Prisoners to Become Peacebuilders
description: Our Transformational Mediation in Prisons program is designed both to provide mediation and to train inmates in non-violent conflict resolution and mediation skills. This will empower them to resolve conflicts within the prisons as well as outside the prisons upon their release.

title: Educate 3500 Aids orphans in Kenyan remote areas
description: Hequeendo Compassionate Friends will provide basic education needs to 3500 poor Aids orphans in form of school uniforms,sleeping blankets,school recommended text books,sanitary towels,access to bursary schemes and nutritious meal to Aids orphans from poor remote villages in Bungoma county-Kenya in the year 2019.

title: Educate & empower 98 girls in Uganda for a year.
description: This project will help provide education, nutrition, and healthcare to the girl child with an aim of improving enrollment and retention of girls missing out of school in a very rural area of Kyangwali  in Uganda.  The rural areas of Hoima district are characterized by severe poverty, harmful cultural and traditional attitudes, beliefs and practices such as early marriage, and poor management of sexual maturation, impact of HIV/AIDS at household level, teenage pregnancy, dis-empowerment of girls.

title: MamaRescue:Emergency Transport for Ugandan Mothers
description: Access to skilled care is a critical need for Ugandan women. Each year 7,000 women die in Uganda due to complications of pregnancy. Access to care is impeded by the inability to afford transport to health facilities, and the poor quality of roads. Mama Rescue is an emergency dispatch platform helping mothers by using a voucher system. Our Babies & Mother Alive Program partners with local taxi and motorcycle drivers to ensure that laboring mothers reach health facilities in time.

title: Lighting Up Young Lives
description: The Choma community in Malawi is far from the electricity grid. Recent exam results are disappointing and the community has decided that for two months prior to the Standard 8 exams, the children camp out at their schools to get extra tuition in the evenings. When it is dark any tuition ceases. The Rotary Project will provide solar charged battery lighting for classrooms, offices and a Girls' Hostel as well as portable, rechargeable lamps put in sunlight by day and used in rooms by night.

title: Legal Advice for Older and Disabled Prisoners
description: This project seeks to reform inadequate prison healthcare services, advocating for the protection of older and disabled prisoners in England and Wales. Currently, the prison system lacks sufficient staffing and resources necessary to secure prisoners' right to health. By providing free legal advice and support through telephone, mail, and face-to-face outreach clinics, PAS will ensure that the medical and healthcare needs of chronically ill, disabled and older prisoners are rightfully met.

title: Empowering Foster Girls and Teens in Puerto Rico
description: We seek to heal the traumatic wounds suffered by girls and teens ages 6 to 17 victims of abuse neglect and/or abandonment.  A multi-disciplinary team approach assures that our girls receive particular attention to their needs. When residents age-out of foster care we provide assistance with higher education and related materials, room/board, nutrition, transportation, personal/career planning counseling and jobs placement. Our girls and teens grow into independent and empowered women.

title: A gift for life: a sheep for a family in Eritrea
description: The project was born from the necessity of improving the life conditions of the poorest families living in rural villages. Our local partner has operated in Eritrea since 1886, offering sanitary assistance, women empowerment, education, child protection and assistance to youths, aged and sick people and convicts. In order to improve the supply of food and the economic conditions of the population, the nuns distribute goats and sheeps, thus creating little domestic livestocks.

title: Stop Violence Against 3000 Women in Rural Tanzania
description: The project will work to fight violence against 3000 women and  young girls aged 5 to 49 years in rural areas, Tanzania. This project will provide legal aid to victims of violence, creating awareness to community to recognize women violence as a violation of women's rights for society to stick together against violence, as well as empowering women by raising awareness on policies and laws that protect women and address violence against women so as to build women's confidence to report violence.

title: Help expand "Young Smart Farmers" organic gardens
description: Warm Heart provides a home to 45 disadvantaged hill tribe children, providing them with a safe, loving home, healthy meals, and the opportunity to go to school. Without our help these children would have no future. Our Young Smart Farmer project is teaching these kids how to grow organic gardens, which provides them with a valuable skill and helps feed all of the children at Warm Heart.

title: I put myself in your shoes
description: I put myself in your shoes is a campaign aimed at children and adolescents who are part of communities affected by violence. A project that will provide sneakers to participants in sport for peace programs, where baseball, soccer and boxing are used as tools for social transformation, for the construction of peace scenarios in territories historically affected by armed conflict, in order to strengthen personal and community skills through sport.

title: Talent Academy for 1000s of Young Ugandans
description: This project will build an Institution for performing and creative arts in Uganda, to provide professional training for talented young people coming from humble backgrounds. They will be educated, equipped with skills in performing and creative arts, Leadership and entrepreneurship skills to help them manage their celebrity status & resources, & provide them with practical experience by the Troupe, a social enterprise of the organisation, to create alternative pathways for youth employment.

title: HELP 100 CHILDREN IN INDIA FIGHT CEREBRAL PALSY
description: This project will spread awareness on cerebral palsy through lectures, workshops and training 100 underprivileged children with cerebral palsy in Bengaluru, India.

title: Gift A Widow this Christmas with Ten Chicken
description: Under this project, 100 widows will be rescued from the inhuman wife inheritance cultural practices, they will be trained and receive a 10- Chicken poultry kit that will enable them earn US $ 10 per week, they will be organized in Kuku-kumi savings group and enlisted in a Community based Health care Financing scheme.  The beneficiaries are expected to increasing their self-confidence, nutrition level and sustain an economic growth.

title: TRANSFORM LIVES OF 3000 DRUG USERS IN KIBERA SLUMS
description: The project will continue providing comprehensive HIV services to people who use and inject drugs. The focus will include community outreach to identify the victims and link them to the clinics for provision of comprehensive services such as HIV testing, TB and  STI screening and treatment, condom distribution and extensive psycho-social  counselling including risk reduction counselling. This approach will be in line with the national policies and Kenya AIDS Strategic Framework IV.

title: Secure Brighter Futures for 3,000 Filipinas
description: This project will provide contraceptive services to 3,000 women and girls in Palawan who need them most. Our services ensure that women and girls avoid unplanned pregnancies which can derail their schooling and ability to work, and mire them in poverty. Our clinic is holistic and also provides prenatal checkups and HIV screening.

title: Provision of Sanitation for a village in Nepal
description: Gimdi is a village 45 miles south of Kathmandu and has a population of 2500 people over a 25km area and only one toilet. Our aim is to provide 70 long drop toilets, providing safe clean sanitation to the villagers enhancing the safety of vulnerable adults, young girls and boys and as an end result providing fertiliser for sustainable crop growth. Health, Welfare and safety of vulnerable adults and children are a major concern and with this project we can make a difference.

title: Providing Opportunities to Women in Ghana
description: A gift to this project is an incredible first step for many women in Ghana, a country with pervasive gender inequality. Our project provides sustainable skills training programs to local women in cooking, sewing and computer skills. Providing a 12-week cycle they join a 6-week program followed by becoming a mentor to a new student for the final 6 weeks. At the end of the 12 weeks, our team build career paths and opportunities for the women. Including small start-up loans from $50.

title: End Witchcraft Branding and Stigmatization (EWBS)
description: The End Witchcraft Branding and Stigmatization (#EWBS) project is an advocacy campaign designed to combat the widespread branding and stigmatization of children as witches in the southern region of Nigeria. BRCI will over the duration (24 months) of the project advocate for improved laws, train police officers ans other first respondents and engage traditional leaders and religious leaders on the need to end child witchcraft branding and stigmatization.

title: Provide Clean Water to 500 Families in the Desert!
description: This project is of extreme importance to serving humanity. By providing Clean Water to approx. 500 families in extreme far areas of Thar Desert. *(an average family size is 2 to 3 Adults + 4 to 5 Children = 8 Persons). Deep water-well's will be dug, and provided with a "hand-pump" for smooth operation, to the 10 villages. A regular maintenance is necessary every year to maintain the serviceability of these wells.

title: Support the successful start of independent life
description: One of the most important moments in every person's life comes when they leave their homes and parents to start their independent life and make responsible decisions. Some young people await this moment with excitement and readiness while others feel anxious and even fearful. What is most crucial in this life period is the family support available to the young person, as a precondition for building independent living skills for a successful start into adulthood.

title: Building Houses for 50 Hurricane Michael Survivors
description: This program will build and repair houses for families who lost everything as a result of Hurricane Michael. The program will support the long term recovery for 50 households in economically disenfranchised communities of Florida's Panhandle. HHDR will utilize your donations, volunteer labor, and community partnerships to provide these otherwise forgotten survivors with critical home repairs.

title: Kids: Plant Trees, Plant Water, Protect Life!
description: October 2018. The IPCC Report tells us we're heading for a temperature rise of 1.5 Celsius by 2030. Maybe sooner. Climate change: floods, fires, hurricanes, droughts - Bad News! This is about us, people. If we don't do something fast, we'll all be on the endangered species list. Good News: we know that trees = water, and water = life. So we're harnessing the energy of kids and youth to spread the word, roll up their sleeves and plant 5,000 trees to capture carbon, protect water and plant life.

title: Help children in Bolivia to overcome violence!
description: According to the WHO 2017 Bolivia is in one of the first places in the rates of domestic violence in Latin America. Hence, Bolivian children and youth are extremely vulnerable and highly exposed to violence. The goal of "WAWAS" Phase 2 is to reduce the rates of violence in a larger scale in the City of Cochabamba-Bolivia, through an effective intervention involving all the actors of the target communities, aiming mainly to protect children and youth as ultimate victims.

title: Provide school sanitation and education in Nepal
description: Working with the Rotary Club of the Himalayan Gurkhas to provide sanitation in 7 schools (we helped rebuild one in 2016/17 after  earthquakes); and to educate teachers in 8 schools to help over 3000 children, also teachers. The new facilities will greatly improve the attendance at school and will achieve health outcomes. The Early Learning Program will provide teacher training and  improved learning environments that serve as models for the area. Improvement of teaching skills will help others.

title: Train 25 women to sell Tiger bags in Nepal
description: The Advocacy Project and the National Network of Families of the Disappeared in Nepal (NEFAD) are seeking $5,000 to invest in the 25 women shown in our video and photos. All lost family members during the conflict. The women are getting noticed for their Tiger bags, but have asked us to send a skilled American quilter to Nepal to help them make even better bags! They also want to open their own shop in 2019. If they succeed, it would set a shining example for families of the missing everywhere.

title: STEM Education through Basketball
description: Many young Cameroonians are not afforded the opportunity to participate in science, technology, mathematics and engineering (STEM) education. The Manengouba Foundation (MF) will use basketball as a means to attract, nurture, and inspire young boys and girls to pursue STEM education and careers. This project aims at providing relevant and real-world exposure to STEM concepts and technical skills that are so very vital to meet the pressing needs and challenges of our changing world.

title: Celebrate kids who create with technology
description: Coolest Projects USA is a showcase event for young people who make things with technology. At Coolest Projects, young makers bring projects to share with fellow creators and the public, and they explore each others' work. Outstanding entries can win awards in different categories. All Coolest Projects events are free to enter and free to attend, giving more people the opportunity to become inspired to create with technology. The next Coolest Projects USA will be in Santa Ana, CA on March 23.

title: Project Lifesaver
description: Project Lifesaver is a program for individuals with developmental disabilities who are at risk of wandering. This program is available in both Escambia and Santa Rosa counties in Northwest Florida and is offered to those with a developmental disability, based on prioritization of risk factors. Project Lifesaver is a program that features bracelets that emit a radio signal that search and rescue personnel can use to track and locate an individual who is missing.

title: Help Us Change The World One Child At A Time
description: This Elementary Education sponsorship project is located in Uganda and it is ongoing. We are in need of your support in sponsoring 17 vulnerable and orphaned primary age school children. Your donations provide; school fees, meals, uniforms, and supplies for each child.   The purpose of this project is to improve access to basic education through sponsorship. Your donations make a difference and have a ripple effect that benefits these children, their families and the community as a whole.

title: Digital Leap
description: Digital Leap will enable TajRupt to scale access to our civic education curriculum through regional expansion across Central Asia. In the pilot initiative (January - March 2019), approximately 50 students across Kazakhstan will be able to enroll in our 10-week after-school curriculum live through our partnerships with local entities.

title: Give Life Kidney transplant to Children with CKD
description: Soffy Foundation gives support to children with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) from the moment that they are diagnosed until their transplant is complete. This project provides integral health to the patient and their family; It covers of all your medications for free, provides nutritional, psychological, human development and support to the life aspirations of the involved.

title: Hidden Figures: Supporting Somali Women for Peace
description: Somali women are powerful and capable leaders in preventing and resolving conflicts but often encounter more obstacles than men.  Conflict Dynamics empowers women to reach their full peacebuilding potential by increasing their ability to shape dialogues and address issues important to them. Join us to evolve strong networks of women working for peace at the local and national levels, including helping them address gender-related aspects of conflict that contribute to larger disputes and wars.

title: Clothes for Special Needs Children at Ashajyothi
description: This project will help the orphan children with special needs to get comfortable clothes twice or thrice a day since these children needs more clothes because they are poor in self help skills, they will go to the toilets on their bed so every time there is a need to change the clothes. This will reduce the skin diseases and stay comfortable all the day.

title: Educate 500 families living with alcohol use & NCD
description: "At the age of 17 years, Mahesh has given up his schooling to work as a salesman." Alcohol violence in the family is forcing a lot of children to join work force. We target to sensitize 500 children about the issue of alcoholism and NCDs & encourage them to continue their education. Uma's troubles became worse when her husband started using alcohol and abuse became an everyday affair. We intend to counsel, heal 240 women survivors of violence to seek help and to live healthy & productive life.

title: Antenatal care for 1000 rural Tanzanian women
description: This project brings a mobile outreach for (pregnant) women and children under two years, to people living far away from health facilities in Lower Moshi, Tanzania. It provides education, ante- and postnatal care, consultation and materials to the doorstep, bringing down maternal and child mortality. We endeavour a healthy future for all mothers and children in rural Tanzania, in which they all have access to basic healthcare so that the circle of poverty can be broken.

title: Help train 50 women as Community Paralegals
description: This project will train 50 female Community Paralegals to provide information and practical assistance to others related to their legal and human right to own and inherit property and live free from all forms of harm and abuse.

title: Help Livhuwani graduate in South Africa
description: "I grew up in a township and was orphaned when I was 16 years old. Through gracious support from individuals I got to University, but the high fees make it a challenge to get through one semester to the next. I hope to apply my knowledge to help create a more gender equitable society and help fund others' education."    With your help, Livhuwani will graduate from South Africa's North-West University with a Political Science and History degree by 2020. Livhuwani is supported through Feenix.org.

title: Darfuris need 150 capacity schools in Djabal, Chad
description: DOHS, a Darfuri-run charity, wants money to build two buildings containing a total of six classrooms and one teachers' office, plus four latrines, with a total student capacity of 150.  DOHS knows all about life for Darfuris in Chad, as our own Vice-President lived in Farchana camp from 2004 to 2007.   We know from frequent contact with camp leaders that needs in Djabal are dire.  That's why DOHS also wants money for 1,400 notebooks, pens and pencils and two 550 gallon drinking water tanks!

title: Build a house where 10 boys will become men
description: 20% of the confirmed human trafficking cases reported in GA in 2017 were males. There is no comprehensive restorative housing program available for those that have been victimized by human trafficking.  This project will allow us to break ground on a group home that will house 10 boys, under the age of 18. Along with having a safe place to call home, each resident will participate in a holistic program, working to restore every aspect of their well-being.

title: Help Protect Asylum Seekers
description: Families escaping gang violence and persecution in Central America are undertaking a dangerous journey to seek safety in the US. Seeking asylum at the United States border is legal--even during a pandemic. People travel to the southern U.S. border to seek refuge, including from political turmoil and rampant violence in Central America. While Trump Administration policies have left behind a broken asylum system, President Joe Biden can take bold action to create a safe, orderly and fair system.

title: CRADLE - help 125 new & expectant Indian mothers
description: This project provides the required nourishment for 125 disadvantaged pregnant women and new mothers & their infants in a south Indian fishing community. Our 10-week programs (twice a year) provide these women a strong understanding of their own bodies, of child development, and the skills to raise happy, healthy babies. We cover topics on basic nutrition, health & hygiene, age-appropriate intellectual and motor stimulation for babies and provide access to our staff throughout early development.

title: 100 Women Rendering Aid to Youth in Mental Crisis
description: Over 50% of the U.S. population will meet criteria for a mental disorder at some point in their life, many with their first onset during childhood or adolescence. Sadly, many young people with mental problems don't seek professional help. Early detection and treatment of a mental illness can help youth to more quickly recover and ultimately lead more meaningful and productive lives. Our project will train 100 women how to render first aid to a young person who may be developing a mental problem.

title: Provide Spaces of Healing for 30  Women in Mexico
description: The RECLAIMING/RE-FRAMING project will provide 30 women in Mexico City with spaces, tools and guidance to deal with traumatic experiences through art. While women's voices are louder than ever today, a majority of women continue to struggle with the effects of trauma alone. In collaboration with a local Mexican organization, La Lleca, we will lead workshops to help women begin their healing process using visual storytelling. (Pictures: workshops in Bangalore & Madhya Pradesh, India, July 2018)

title: Empowering  600  teenage mothers in Sri Lanka
description: This project will empower 600 teenage mothers living in Monaragala district, Uva province Sri Lanka,  who married without legal entity in aged between 16- 18 and victimized socially and economically due to the abandonment of the partners. This critical issue has not been addressed yet by the responsible authorities, therefore, the project will assist them to regain their lives by providing opportunities to protect their rights, to organize themselves and to develop their skills and resources

title: Empower 100 Pastoralist Girls in Northern Kenya
description: This project aims at empowering 100 underprivileged marginalized pastoralist girls in Northern part of Kenya, by funding their tuition, meals and accommodations. Those students who are lucky to be supported through this project can concentrate on their studies without any interruptions' and worries.

title: Integrated project development in agro forestry
description: The proposal identified strategic areas of conservation and development of the Department of Loreto pressed by anthropic action of population centers contiguous to the natural areas protected by the State or within geopolitical areas of development. Then, sectors that exert pressure were prioritized and evaluated deforestation, loss of biomass and carbon stock. The result showed alarming process of forest loss and the consequent loss of biodiversity and loss of aerial biomass.

title: Send 110 Students to High School in Belize
description: Most Caye Caulker children were forced to quit school at the age of 12 until Ocean Academy opened as the island's first high school offering an education to all children who want to learn.

title: Protect 200 domestic / Abandoned children in Haiti
description: This project plans to create a protective family environment for 200 vulnerable children who are victims of trafficking and / or abuse, in a situation of family separation and domesticities in the Department of Grand'Anse in Haiti.  Allow children in orphans and / or domestic servants to return to their biological families and return to school.  Raise the awareness of communities to contribute to the fight against family separation and violence against children.

title: Support La Serenissima's new release The Godfather
description: La Serenissima aims to bring Italian baroque music to the widest possible audience. New recording The Godfather will present uplifting music from Italians Brescianello and Vivaldi, alongside Italianate works by JS Bach, Telemann and other closely-connected composers. The record will provide new insight into the transfer of musical ideas and will develop La Serenissima's reach by expanding its musical footprint. The project provides opportunities to 23 skilled musicians, including young artists.

title: Universal Birth Registration to End Child Marriage
description: We propose interventions to enhance the enforcement of child marriage laws in rural areas of Bangladesh by ensuring universal coverage of birth registration of girls within the target group (aged 14-17) as well as creating awareness of a mobile-phone based surveillance and reporting system - connecting enforcing agencies with potential victims - to restrict the practice of child marriage.

title: DONATE A CUP OF PORRIDGE MEAL THIS CHRISTMAS
description: Children from poor financial backgrounds in Uganda miss out on anything to eat at lunchtime every day, and many will have had no breakfast, and find it difficult to concentrate and gain an education. Malnutrition affects their health, development and ability to learn. This project will provide a cup of porridge and sugar for a lunchtime meal and work with some schools to establish gardens to sustain the lunch meals for needy children. This Christmas please donate a lunch meal for a needy child

title: California Wildfire Relief Fund 2018
description: The 2018 California wildfire season was the deadliest and most destructive on record. Wildfires spread rapidly through both northern and southern California, destroying homes and prompting evacuations. This fund supported immediate relief efforts for people impacted by the fires in the form of emergency supplies like food, water, and medicine, and is now funding long-term assistance to help residents recover and rebuild. All donations to this fund will exclusively support wildfire recovery.

title: Spay/Neuter 500 homeless dogs in Tabio, Colombia
description: The indifferent treatment towards the homeless dogs and cats in Tabio has  inspired us into action. Our solution is to create a pioneer project to raise awareness on the current situation and to become champion for homeless animals whose lives are worth saving. We would like to invite you to become an integral part of this important project!

title: Shark Sanctuary Transition, Isla Mujeres, Mexico
description: We will create a shark sanctuary for multiple species of sharks in Isla Mujeres, Mexico and will be working very closely with the local community to transition from destructive fishing practices to sustainable ecotourism. This is a win/win situation, and a viable model for success that can be replicated in other prime sites around the world.

title: Build Library for village school and community
description: Access to good library is critical for scholastic development. School's small library is not sufficient for growing needs of school.   Also we want to expand our school library to serve the local community, who have no library access at all. We are close to two government schools and 4 villages. We want to create a learning hub for the whole community.   We plan to build 1200 sq.ft library, fully furnished with sufficient reading material and subscriptions. Total cost: INR 20.4 lakhs(USD 29000)

title: Support Refugee-led Solutions in Malaysia
description: Same Skies supports refugee communities in so-called 'transit' countries, but where resettlement to third countries is becoming less and less likely. We drive leadership and innovation in refugee action to increase their agency in gaining access to information and human rights. Through training and mentoring, we strengthen communities to become self-sufficient. We focus on the resilience of refugees, building on their skills and talents, rather than seeing them as vulnerable.

title: Uttrayan Save Birds Campaign (kite festival)
description: Uttarayan- Kite flying festival is celebrated on the 14th and 15th of January every year in India.  Kite-flying participants use glass coated threads - "Manja" to fly kites that cause severe wing injuries to  thousands of birds. Many such injured birds succumb to painful deaths while others are maimed for rest of their lives. We organize a special annual campaign - " Uttarayan Save  the Birds Campaign", in an attempt to save and rehabilitate as many injured birds as possible.

title: Education in rural South Africa - Vehicle needed
description: Children in the valley have broad smiles, frantic waving and greetings when they see our vehicle. They know that YOUPSA is bringing unforgettable creative learning with fun to them. BUT these schools are difficult to access and our current vehicle cannot travel these rough paths and farm roads. YOUPSA needs to get a strong 2nd-hand SUV for bringing educational and art programs to rural disadvantaged children and schools. Without this we are stuck.

title: Ugandan children shouldn't die from drinking water
description: The most vulnerable in rural Uganda are babies, children and the elderly. They easily fall sick because they are forced to consume water from contaminated and unprotected sources, shared with the grazing animals.       For just $3,000 Mission 4 Water can provide a whole community with a new borehole right in their village, providing everyone with clean and safe water. This not only improves the health of the people, but education and wealth also improve with reduced sickness.

title: Helping Children Grow Up In Loving Families
description: Children in Families is a local Cambodian NGO. We place vulnerable children in loving families, where they belong. We are dedicated to providing high-quality family-based care for orphans and vulnerable children in Cambodia, ensuring that children can grow up in loving environments and receive the education, nutrition and medical support they need to thrive in the future. We support families and communities to be safe environments for children, and advocate for family-based care globally

title: Safeguarding Frogs and Birds in Masuria, Poland
description: This project will protect and enhance the park biodiversity in Rynski Dwor, Poland through planting wildflower meadows, ferns, perennials, creepers, new leafy trees, evergreen and leafy shrubs, and also performing some sanitary and maintenance works on existing historic trees. Reconstruction of interior layout of the 19th century park will limit a pedestrian access to a refuge for endangered species. Modernization of didactic paths will protect their habitats and decrease further degradation.

title: Peace-making residence for 50 refugee teenagers
description: "Rebels for Peace" is a residence in Zeitz for 50 teenagers of different walks of life (refugees, migrants, challenging life scenarios, dysfunctional families) from Germany, Russia, Syria and Afghanistan. We work together in creative labs and site-specific workshops to build bridges between individuals and create a healthy interaction within local community. We reduce the level of aggression in the society and help teenagers from refugee families to establish better relations with their peers

title: nutrition support for 200 malnourished children
description: We work to reduce the incidence of Malnutrition in remote villages block Madawara of district Lilitpur bundel khand of Uttar Pradesh. Many children in district never make it past their fifth birthday falling victim to malnutrition, diarrhea and childhood illness. A cycle of poverty, illness and death occurs  this region.We identified malnourished children from these villages.Their families can't afford treatment of these children. Last three years we helped 920 children to get proper nutrition.

title: Mitigating of Child marriage vice in Uganda
description: The project aims to contribute towards mitigating the vice of child or early marriages & its negative consequences through effective grassroots intervention activities. In Uganda whose demographics is largely composed of a relatively young population (75%), the rising tendencies towards child marriage poses grave concerns. The project therefore proposes to engage in curbing the vice by systematically carrying out a number of activities at the grassroots community level & monitor effectiveness.

title: Educate Internally Displaced Anglophone Children
description: Two years into the Anglophone Crisis, hundreds have been recorded dead, over a thousand homes burned , dozens of schools attacked and over 250,000 people have fled their homes. Denis Miki Foundation is working with several local communities affected by the crisis to ensure that children are educated by finding educational opportunities and promoting online classrooms for Internally Displaced Children or those still living in conflict areas so as to ensure their proper education.

title: Help five young teachers change 1000 lives
description: Oasis South Africa  is a youth-led organisation. We plan to grow our More Than A Teacher programme, which inspires unemployed young people to train as educators in South Africa.    This project will recruit and train another five young people, enabling them to gain a teaching qualification whilst supporting the learning of 1000 pupils in schools across inner city Johannesburg.

title: Give A Gift, Spread the Love
description: This Project will bring great excitement, bright eyes, and happy faces on Christmas morning. We plan to buy them gifts and food to enable them celebrate Christmas in style for the first time, this children have never received any Christmas gift in life.

title: We Can Get There!
description: The Pimpri street- based drug user community Sahara works with is a dangerous and unsafe environment for children. The children desperately want to finish their education or wish to be placed in a 'safe' educational cum residential facility. Sahara has identified the most vulnerable of these who need immediate support. Many of the dropouts are induced into sex work, pick-pocketing or peddling drugs. Sahara has a Youth Support Group, 2 community Monitors, conducts regular life skills sessions.

title: Empowering 200 Youth to Rise Above Poverty
description: In this project we plan to train 200 poor and downtrodden youth of our community on organic farming - aloe vera and mushroom production, so that they can earn a decent livelihood. Our village, Masat is located in the South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, India. In 2006 the Ministry of Panchayati Raj named this place as one of the country's 250 most backward districts (out of a total of 640). As per data available, 45.41% of the people in this district live below poverty line (BPL).

title: Moving Mountains for Mental Health
description: Mental health Awareness - we are running a national campaign dubbed #MovingMountains for #MentalHealth to help raise awareness to normalize discussion on mental health in Kenya, and promote mental wellness. We are doing so by hiking major mountains in Kenya to prove two things; that it is possible to move the biggest mountain - mental health stigma in Africa, and that people with psychiatric conditions can overcome even the toughest mental and physical challenges, just like everyone else.

title: Helping Children Overcome Domestic Abuse
description: For most children, home is a place filled with love, security and the comfort of family. Sadly, for one in five children under the age of 18 in the UK, the routine and stability of their home is replaced by the fear and vulnerability of domestic abuse. Your Sanctuary supports children who have been affected by Domestic Abuse through creative and relational 1:1 support and programmes like our Domestic Abuse Recovery Programme. We offer them a safe space in which to recover from their trauma.

title: Buwunga Community Water Project
description: People of all ages in Buwunga, Uganda -- a small, remote, fishing village on the shores of Lake Victoria -- unanimously agree that clean, potable water is their most pressing need.   This project will install a water pump and purification point that will provide access to clean water to the entire community.

title: Sponsor A Child
description: The project provides educational opportunity to the orphan and vulnerable children from socially and economically disadvantaged communities including trafficked victims children, children of Devadasi, children affected by HIV/AIDS and children from excluded and Dalit communities aged between 3 to 18 years. The sponsorship programme helps support supplementary nutrition, school uniforms, textbooks and notebooks and skill training /vocational training for children from the age of 16 years.

title: Help 25 5th graders get a classroom by January2020
description: This project will provide classrooms to over 200 children at Imara School in Mwala, Kenya. ONE class is urgently needed. Imara school currently runs to 5th grade and we would like to add 3more classrooms to accommodate these children as they learn and grow.

title: Join our team - Support Todos Santos Youth Sports
description: Join our team. Help support Todos Santos youth sports programs.  Why sports?  Sports empower our children and create healthy communities.  Young athletes do better in school. Sports teach teamwork and problem solving. Sports teach lifelong positive lifestyle habits. Team security gives self-esteem and personal satisfaction. Sports promote character and build social skills. Sports are fun!  Improve the lives of children, build community and change the world. The future is calling, won't you help?

title: Addressing Overpopulation and Homeless Pit Bulls
description: Spreading awareness about the importance and critical need for broad accessibility of spaying and neutering.  Funding spay/neuter and puppy vaccinations for Pit Bull type dogs for low-income families and caretakers to help reduce the overpopulation of pit bull type dogs.

title: Empower 15 women as leaders, Improve health of 600
description: In Baitoa, Dominican Republic, many families suffer unnecessarily from illnesses because they lack access to knowledge & resources that would prevent health problems. Project Hearts (PH) provides health training to local women who then educate families in their communities. The training not only improves the health of their neighbors but also empowers the women as leaders, strengthening the whole community. Since 2013, PH has empowered 49 women, who have improved the health of 1,960 individuals.

title: Watersports for Disabled & Disadvantaged Children
description: All-Aboard Watersports are a small Bristol based charity supporting disabled and disadvantaged children and young people.  They remove physical, cognitive, emotional and financial barriers to enable access to the water for all, providing sessions and support all year round. This allows individuals to realise their potential and escape debilitating conditions.  All-Aboard creates an equal playing field, allowing able bodied and disabled children to support each other and learn.

title: Educate 35 war orphans - change their future
description: In one of the poorest countries in the world (average income of less than $60/month), education is reserved only for those who can afford it. We are educating 35 war orphans in eastern Congo, not only for basic schooling, but for life skills to be able to work and care for their own families one day.  We are building a permanent home for the children and are providing after-school tuition to help the children with learning challenges and girls who are forced to stay home during monthly cycles.

title: Active life for disability children in Bulgaria
description: This project will give the chance to more than 250 disabled children to gain access to adapted sports, including swimming, adapted skiing and surfing, mountain hiking and we will give them the opportunity to participate in specialized sports camps. Sport is unique

title: Save lives in Uganda with bicycle ambulance
description: With 336 deaths per 100,000 live births, Uganda's maternal mortality rate is among the highest. Daily 16 women in Uganda die of maternal and newborn death. This is huge problem, but has a simple solution: affordable and efficient emergency transport to clinics to give birth under professional care. With a causal link between maternal mortality and distance to a clinic our BICYCLE AMBULANCES will literally save lives. We will deliver 10 AMBULANCES and give 40,000 people access to health care!

title: Gift Handwritten Letters to 10000 Refugee Children
description: Letters of Love will deliver handwritten letters connecting people around the world to more than 10,000 Syrian, Iraqi, Yazidi, Afghan, Palestinian, South Sudanese & Rohingya refugee children. Aside these tokens of hope & solidarity which make the children feel special, this project will also provide youth-led psychosocial support in the form of creative toy kits, educational resources, art workshops et al in refugee camps & community centers in Turkey, Sudan, India, Bangladesh & Greece.

title: Engaging children in climate action:
description: Children not only will have to assume the consequences of a warming planet but also will hold solutions to adapt to a changing environment.  We will educate 1 thousand children using disruptive methods about personal actions to reduce emissions, we will connect them with experts and change makers to inspire their future careers and we will co-create solutions in their schools to reduce emissions in areas such as renewable energy, waste management, mobility, urban agriculture, among others.

title: Educational Inclusion of Children with Autism
description: The program INEVI (Educational Inclusion with a Comprehensive Intervention) was created to provide an opportunity to children and adolescents within the Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) to receive educational and therapeutic intervention. To give them tools to have a successful educational outcome in regular schools.

title: Give education opportunity to rural Ugandan youth
description: YANA Community High School project specifically addresses the need to provide affordable secondary and vocational education to youth in rural eastern Uganda. With a school like YANA, girls can access a nearby affordable school instead of staying home to do chores, and thus prevent teenage pregnancy and early marriages. At YANA's vocational training center, youth gain employable skills that will help them to obtain employment, increase their family incomes, and break the cycle of poverty.

title: Growing Smart Urban Forests (GSUF)
description: We all love trees but maybe not for the reasons we should. Urban forests are critical for keeping cities liveable and providing essential cooling. GSUF enables residents to connect and become local activists for the trees in their area through a digital media platform. Residents can adopt and 'talk' to trees through a mobile app or website, with the trees telling them (in real time!) what they need today. GSUF brings trees to life, empowering locals to care for and create smart urban forests.

title: Choirs to Improve English Literacy of SA Children
description: The  LEGACY Projects have demonstrated that initiating a choir in schools of impoverished areas can effect significant improvements in English literacy and cross-disciplinary learning. This project focuses on leadership development of principals & empowers music teachers  to become skilled conductors of  well-disciplined choirs. The Siyacula ("We Sing") Music Festivals celebrate progress annually in joint concerts with project partners. Participation in ABRSM Choral exams is strongly encouraged.

title: Feed to Educate 2,500 School Children in India
description: With the involvement of local community, this project will build and operate a semi-automated kitchen in rural Nellore District to feed  hot and nutritious meals to school going children to address classroom hunger.Our organization's core focus for this project is to address the malnourishment in young school going children and retain children in school to get an education. This project will address three of United Nations SDG's i.e. Zero Hunger, Good health and Well-Being and Education.

title: Tech changing child cancer detection (Mex State)
description: AMANC (first NGO in Mexico to help children with cancer, since 1982) commited with the development of an intelligent digital platform that facilitates the detection of child cancer and speed up the start of the treatment. State of Mexico joins in this national effort to raise the rate of early detection and survival of pediatric patients in our country.

title: Give Children a Safer and Happier Childhood
description: The Ludoteca Minga is a place located in Concon, a city in the Valparaiso region, Chile. Here the community can participate in free environmental workshops such as agriculture, community edible gardens, and more. Our program creates spaces that promote joint and collaborative learning, where children, youth an even older adults participate. We seek to promote community learning, providing them with the tools, skills and values they need to develop a society concerned about the environment.

title: Give at-risk children Artistic workshops in Cali
description: This project is aimed at building the extension of the Theatre called Casa Naranja, the only theatre in the neighborhood Aguablanca in Cali, where the highest levels of poverty and indigence are concentrated. It is a place where the arts and the community work give kids and young people the chance to improve their quality of live, the chance to dream, in an attempt to build healthy social human beings under the theme of life to find peace, tolerance and respect, our base values.

title: Rescue mistreated Mexican kids and create families
description: La Alegria de los Ninos is a shelter home for children from 0 to 6 years old rescued from violence or abandonment, that lived in dysfunctional environments and that require a safe place where they can be healed physically and emotionally. Our current project is oriented to strengthen our medical program and provide integral medical attention to the children in our Institution, in order to recover, maintain or control their health. THE RIGHT TO A GOOD HEALTH IS A FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT.

title: Life Changing Care for Disabled Filipino Children
description: This project will provide help to physically disabled children from impoverished Filipino families by developing a treatment plan, locating and providing services needed to change the life and future of a child. With our partners and service providers we can get treatment free or at a reduced cost.  We provide funds for doctor exams, x-rays, health insurance, physical therapy, prosthetics, orthotics, and travel expenses for a child and one parent.

title: Restoring Childhoods For 75 HIV Infected/Affected
description: Committed Communities Development Trust (CCDT) implements a comprehensive Residential Care Program that restores a wholesome childhood to children who are infected or affected by HIV/AIDS. These are children who are either orphaned or from single parent families that are not in a position to take care of them. We help restore a childhood to these children through medical and nutritional care, education, counseling, employability skills training, sports, recreation.

title: Welcome Weekend for 500+ U.S. Resettled Refugees
description: Welcome Weekend is free for newly-arrived to the U.S. refugees. At our 1st in October we provided 150 attendees with the experience of feeling welcome and "At Home" thanks to 30 volunteers, delicious food, beautiful outdoors, fun games, and insightful workshops. One attendee said it was the first time in 3 years that she was a part of America. Over Memorial Day wknd 2019, we will host another 150, in Boulder Creek, California. 2 more retreats after that are being planned which will host 350 more

title: Safe Home for Survivors of Domestic Violence
description: Our Safe Home is an initiative of Operation PeaceMaker of My Choices Foundation to provide a safe shelter home for survivors of domestic violence. The Safe Home provides vulnerable women and their children with counselling services, legal aid and vocational training. It can accommodate up to 12 survivors of domestic violence along with their children.

title: Restore a house to mobilize ignored labor pools
description: This project will positively influence 1200 ignored labor pools of young adults: chronically unemployed, lost one of their parents, recovering addicts, to address staff shortage to serve Madagascar hospitality and tourism industry. The renovation of this historic landmark will also signify the preservation of the architectural ensemble of the Old Town Fianarantsoa. For each collected donation, a painted mural will be dedicated to you or your organization

title: Let Kids Be Kids! Sports Day for Rohingya Children
description: Peace Winds Japan will organize the "Kids Be Kids!" event which will be held on January 25 for the Rohingya refugee children attending the Child Learning Center in Camp 14, Hakimpara Refugee Camp in Bangladesh. 200 boys and girls (ages 8-12) will participate in sports activities to promote exercise, teamwork, and mental health. The harsh conditions of the camps often rob these kids of a bright childhood. This event is an opportunity to restore some of what has been taken!

title: Free Engineering Education for kids of Armenia
description: The Union of Information Technology Enterprises (UITE) of Armenia will establish Armath engineering laboratories in Armenia, which will give the opportunity of free technological education to kids from 10 years old.  Engineering laboratories are located in the schools of Armenia. Now we have more than 230 labs in all regions of Armenia, 5350 kids involved in this project.

title: Help >1000 children with autism* in Vietnam
description: Our son, George, received a diagnosis of moderate autism eight months ago, when he turned two.  Since his condition has markedly improved with 1) Early diagnosis and 2) Early intensive intervention in Vietnam. Based on the many challenges we encountered and our NGO's mission, we will implement methods to reach and help children worldwide, with our initial focus on Vietnam.

title: Food security: Giving poor elderly people food.
description: The feeding scheme will benefit 90 sick and elderly people living in Mbekweni, Western Cape Province of South Africa. The food support will include free breakfast and lunch every day to 90 elderly people who do not have access to adequate food. This area has a significant number of sick and poor pensioners. These residents do not get adequate food and other social support necessary to live a decent life. In some cases they are neglected by their relatives and left to live on their own devices.

title: Marimba training, 150 kids, Alexandra Township
description: Our project will provide marimba (African Xylophone) training to a 150 disadvantaged children in the township of Alexandra one of Johannesburg's oldest and poorest townships with limited services and opportunities for children.   We will supply a full set of Marimbas, teaching equipment and training to implement the program.  Marimbas offer opportunities to keep children off the streets and holistic educational benefits. We have the expertise and experience to deliver on our mission

title: Save 1 million lives
description: DTI helps people waiting for an organ transplant to receive the gift of life! Your donation empowers doctors and nurses from Africa, Asia and South America to implement and operate organ donation programs in their respective countries to rescue millions of lives, help people avoid lifelong dialysis and dramatically reduce healthcare costs. Giving your loved ones a second chance in life is our passion. We'll save one million lives by training thousands of medical teams on how to do it!

title: Science for Every Child.  MUZEIKO in Plovdiv
description: A true story from a social media: "Several kids escape from school class in order to visit Muzeiko's travelling exhibit "The Inventions" in the House of Humor in Gabrovo - a small town in Bulgaria".   Yes, this happens when the travelling exhibit of Muzeiko - the children's museum in Sofia, goes to other towns in Bulgaria. When we give the opportunity for kids to learn by playing and experimenting.  When we inspire them to be inventors!  Now, we need support for its next stop - Plovdiv 2019!

title: Help WWF bring the lynx back to Bulgaria
description: Have you ever seen a lynx? The majestic big cat once ruled the forests in Bulgaria along with bears and wolves. Sadly, nowadays the lynx has turned into a myth, a forest ghost, and can only be seen in pictures, documentaries and the zoo. For the home this forest king once had - the ancient Bulgarian forests - is on the brink of being irreversibly destroyed. Commercial logging, construction, waste... All this leads to fewer trees, less food, no security, no chance to find a mate and rear kittens.

title: Wigs for a smile
description: Hair loss is an extremely traumatic experience for anyone, especially for a child. Put a smile on the face of a child coping with temporary or permanent hair loss by providing them with natural-looking, human hair wigs, free of charge.

title: Agroforestry with refugees and hosts in NW Uganda
description: It started with a crisis. Refugees from S Sudan needed to fell trees to build homes, farm and cook. But we knew they could also grow trees. We recruited foresters and refugee youth, set up a nursery, and sought to understand needs. Four years and over 500,000 trees later, we are happy to report that homes we work with have more poles, more fruit and more fuel to hand, and suffer less from weather extremes. Priorities now include natural regeneration of trees and scaling up.

title: Early Childhood Development Centre in South Africa
description: This project will address the issue of access to quality education faced by many South Africans, by providing early childhood development services to between 70 and 100, 2-6 year-old children in the Diepsloot area of South Africa. During the period from conception to formal schooling, a child's development is subject to the influence of nutrition, protection, language and emotion in his or her immediate environment. If the influence of these factors is positive, the child will thrive.

title: Red Dead: Reusable Sanitary Pads For Malawi Girls
description: This project will tackle the problem of menstrual health hygiene and in part of youth unemployment. Most school girls in Malawi come from poor families. They can't afford pads and end up missing classes. Our one-year program will recruit 10 volunteers.These female volunteers will be trained to train 2400 girls in Blantyre to make reusable sanitary pads usable for 3 years and train 600 girls to make art, jewelry or sandals for sale.7,200 pads made by the trainees will be given to 7,200 poor girls

title: Volunteer Corps Tutoring, Osun State of Nigeria.
description: VolunteerCorps is organising free intensive tutoring for 10,000 indigent senior secondary school students in public schools in Osun state of Nigeria. This increases their chances of success at the Senior Secondary Certificate Examinations and other similar qualifying examinations.  We provide free study materials   Provide free meals to students and tutors (on Saturdays when we have extended tutorial sessions).     We organise refresher courses for Volunteer tutors (public school teachers)

title: QUALITY EDUCATION FOR 3000 CHILDREN IN NIGERIA
description: This project will provide affordable and quality education for 3000 children in Nigeria, thereby  increase the number of children in school. Nigeria has the largest number of children in the world who are not being educated; Nigeria's population growth has put pressure on the country's resources, public services and infrastructure. Nigeria has 10.5 million out-of-school children - the world's highest number. Bridge the gap between the poor and the rich, between rural and urban areas.

title: Launch DC's First Youth Peer Support Center!
description: In 2019, FAN launched DC's first Youth Peer Operated Center, serving up to 110 children, youth, young adults, and parents/caregivers across all the Center's activities.  The new center, staffed by certified youth peer specialists, will house our after school program, drop-in hours for youth ages 16-25, recreational activities, support groups, mental health workshops, and targeted case management, support, and referral for youth and their families.

title: Create Sustainable support to Street Children
description: As planned, this project will provide educational materials (uniforms, shoes, books, meals, notebooks, pen, pencil, stationary, etc.) to more than 600 underprivileged poor Boys and Girls of Waterloo community, Western Rural so that they may able to develop their educational standard. The project will help these marginalized children to get better opportunities to be educated and to contribute in the development of society. Also it will further prevent them from going back to the street.

title: Enabling People to Own and Manage their Well-being
description: MySalus allows people of every geographic, cultural, social, and economic level to better their own health and well-being by coordinating all their health records and improvement plans in one secure location.  This community provides health resources, ways to develop self-help improvement plans, and to form peer to peer support groups.  It is ongoing so members may see their progress in achieving their goals of better health, reducing medical costs, and owning their overall well-being.

title: Educate and empower 700 Indigenous Colombians
description: This project will build a community center in La Guajira in northern Colombia, home of the indigenous Wayuu people. The center will feature a classroom for elementary and soft-skill training, a 75 square-meter workshop for producing traditional artisanal crafts, and a community kitchen for safe cooking and eating. Children will benefit from better education. Adults will benefit from training in innovation and business. All 700 residents will benefit from improved cooking facilities.

title: Clean Water for 1200 villagers in Burkina Faso
description: This project will ensure clean, potable water to the village of Dodougou, in Burkina Faso. We will drill a borehole and install a hand pump; all the villagers, around 1200 people, of which 800 children, will have access to the water. Women and children won't have to walk long distances to find clean water, the health of the whole village will be highly improved, as they won't use dirty water anymore. The soil will give more produce for an improved nutritional intake.

title: Help Us Keep Rescuing Refugees in Peril at Sea
description: Fleeing to seek refuge in Europe, thousands of people have died making the short sea crossing from Turkey to Lesvos. Setting off in flimsy rubber boats and wearing fake life jackets, many find themselves heading for rocks or sand banks that can readily capsize or sink a dinghy. Others abandoned by smugglers who drop them at beaches inaccessible via land. Our Search and Rescue crew and emergency response team are on call 24/7, working to prevent any more lives being needlessly lost to The Aegean.

title: Bottled Gas For Better Life: Microfinance for LPG
description: Bottled Gas For Better Life provides microfinance loans to help low-income African families in Cameroon, Kenya and Ghana purchase equipment (filled 12.5kg or 13kg cooking gas (LPG) cylinder, double burner stove and accessories) needed to switch to clean cooking, replacing harmful, environmentally polluting solid fuels. This reduces the deadly effects of Household Air Pollution from smoke from cooking fuels like firewood, charcoal and kerosene.

title: Keeping Girls at school in Rwanda - GirlsEducation
description: The Rwandan government enacted a policy that provides all Rwandan children with Twelve years of fee-free education. Yet, girls are still dropping out of school at far higher rates than their male counterparts. YOMADO hopes to eliminate this gap through its threefold approach, which pairs girls with mentors, organizes savings and loans groups, and implements community community score cards to keep girls at School

title: Give Marginalized Youth a Voice
description: Write Our World offers a digital library of bilingual ebooks by kids for kids focused on youth empowerment and cultural preservation. These books are written and orally recorded in two languages and include original illustrations and photos. With a current inventory of 180 books in 27 languages, our growing collection of authentic educational materials is a resource for teachers and students around the world to learn with and from each other.

title: Refurbish orphanages for 240 children in Uganda
description: We aim to extend and refurbish 7 houses in a children's village, each of which are home for up to 35 orphaned children. This totals around 240 children all of whom desparately need extra sleeping space, bunk beds, bedding and mosquito nets plus room to eat, play and study.

title: Make a Dream true for a street kid in Uganda
description: The project addresses social, emotional and economic needs of 50 streets children education issues by developing a Community Volunteer mentorship model (training, financial literacy, food security). It provides beneficiaries with the resources and knowledge to initiate their own projects based on dream drawing/family plan to meet the basic costs of attending school. It promotes team building, collective action, builds confidence and social skills for vulnerable children in Kabale District Uganda

title: Brilliant is Beautiful Fund - Dubai Gala
description: Brilliant is Beautiful is a global fund for women and girls' secondary education. We are in the next phase of the female revolution. Brilliant is Beautiful embodies the notion that when a woman sets her mind to something, she is unstoppable. She can accomplish anything. Her determination shines bright. It is brilliant. And what she creates - what she does - is what makes her beautiful. The impact she has is her beauty.

title: Remove Women's Barriers to Justice in South Asia
description: Most cases of gender-based violence and discrimination never see the light of day. Survivors are simply too afraid to share and the justice process is complex and inaccessible. SAHR's role is to give them access by working with survivors and grassroots defenders in South Asia and the Middle East to make justice a reality. We will provide user-friendly legal resources to 50 survivors and defenders to help them seek reparations and accountability.

title: Thorpe Bay Rotary's Appeal to Help the Homeless
description: We are working with local charities and organisations to make life easier for those living on the streets of South East Essex this winter. South East Essex has one of the highest rates of rough sleepers and homelessness in the country. Many of these men, women and young people have mental health and addiction issues that require various agencies to work together to address.  It can be difficult for individuals to ensure their donations make the most impact.

title: Transform Dozens of Communities Around the World
description: This project is to develop curricula and to offer support for individuals and communities who have been historically marginalized, allowing them to take charge of their lives, their communities, and to inspire others to do the same, reaching tens of thousands of individuals with a single curriculum.   Support us in developing the future curricula that allow us to continue to transform the world. All we need is a little bit of support from you, and the world will never be the same.

title: Empower 1500 women and children in Peru
description: We are working with 3 different communities in northern Peru where women and kids work hard for their health, education, housing, and even for their food. This is both challenging yet rewarding work because leaders and community members always work with us each step of the way. We provide a community library, community restaurants, early education for toddlers, and an enterprise program for women focused on empowerment so that they don't remain in violent relationships. Our goal is empowerment.

title: Give Child Refugees A Chance
description: The Syrian war, now in its seventh year, has taken an extraordinary toll on civilians, forcing over 5.6 million citizens to flee their own country and internally displacing even more. More than half of these refugees are children. Research shows children impacted by war and crisis suffer long-term emotional, psychological, and physical health issues. We are dedicated to bringing trauma-informed programs to these children to help minimize these effects. Join us in giving child refugees a chance.

title: BUILD FIVE BASKETBALL COURTS FOR YOUTH IN NIGERIA
description: HarryCares will help various cities in Nigeria to resurface five basketball street courts and install Basketball upright that are more durable for outdoor use.  By doing so, we are providing a safe space and place where various youth can horn their basketball skills while channelling their energy towards sports. This project will include a one day tournament for each court which becomes officially open in order to keep participating youth active and empowered while playing the game they love.

title: Restore Health and Skill to 5000 Nigerians
description: In January 2019 Beacon of Hope Outreach Health and Empowerment mission Project to underserved communities in Nigeria will save lives, alleviate sufferings , improve health, and quality of life of over 5,000 under privileged and medically disadvantaged children and families: The project will restore health, hope  and self-sustainability by providing quality health care and skills acquisition through FREE medical services, community health education and humanitarian program.

title: Vocation Training for 200 refugee women in Kampala
description: This project will help refugees in Kampala that are facing major problems of survival due to lack of work or professional, socio-economic insertion and so on. Refugees in general, face many difficulties in finding employment, they live in very difficult conditions, including food insecurity, school drop-out, lack of resources for medical care, lack of resources for pay rent, etc. Those who are not in the camps certainly experience these difficulties too and lack the assistance to live well.

title: Help Farmers for Rice Processing Machine
description: This project is designed to contribute to a sustained improvement of living conditions, stability and health in the rural population of four communities in Gbinleh Dixian Chiefdom Kambia district ( Sierra Leone) and enhance them to produce enough food to a level at which basic food becomes affordable, available and accessible The proposed major activities include: supporting agricultural activities, animal restocking and children education. The project will be implemented in four communities.

title: Give quality Education and skills to 200 children
description: The gift of a girl foundation Kumi district, Uganda plans to build a training center to give opportunity to 80 drop out girls to obtain skills that at the end improves their lives.

title: SUSTAINABLE SCHOOLING PROGRAMME FOR NEEDY CHILDREN
description: This project will, targeting at least 400 children from 10 rural schools will make them become more connected and collaborative internally and be more connected with the local community, in Mukono and Wakiso districts.Through SSP we develop sustaining projects like school farms, arts and craft, community digital libraries while providing scholastics likes books and chairs for the schools to use, skill students and accumulate finances for their stay in school.

title: Empower 100,000 children in Benin with Education
description: Graines de Paix is implementing innovative education solutions for strengthening sustainable peace in Northern Benin. If you care about building up peaceful communities where violence is widely spreading even among young children, for sure you can help us!
