description: People have expressed a strong need for a center to ensure that their daughters and children with disabilities have access to basic services, education, learning and schooling .  because among 44 rural communities of which consists the province of Azilal only two territorial municipalities which each has a similar center:  Demnate and  Afourer.People prefer to see their daughters and children thrive while enjoying their well-being and full rights to life,games,schooling...

title: COVID Response Program for Santiago
description: Did you know that many people in Santiago Atitlan suffer from chronic malnutrition?   Since mid-March this community has been under strict stay-at-home orders which has shut down their economy, demolishing incomes and exacerbating food insecurity issues. Mayanza has pivoted its mission to better support the local artisans, fisherman, farmers, and their families.  With the support of local partners,  individually prepared meals and bags of groceries are distributed to families in need.

title: Feed a family in Indonesia| COVID-19 responses
description: Help to provide food for 165 families in urgent need! In lockdown, Indonesian daily-wage workers' families are in hunger! We serve those living hand-to-mouth, those suffer the most from the sudden loss in income due to COVID-19 pandemic. They have no savings, no assets and now no income! Hunger is a more immediate threat to them than the virus. With $20, you provide 1 life-saving food packages to a starving family in urgent need!

title: Support 100 orphan girls sexually abused in DRC
description: We are seeking financial support to build a dormitory of 100 girls sexually abused and victims of wars for them to be safe and get free education...The civil war in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused and continue to cause great insecurity. People are fleeing Eastern Congo. Many are girls and young laddies who have lost their parents, homes and chance of normal life. But these girls have become victims of sexual abused , death , crimes ...as a result of a life on the streets.

title: Support Refugees from Syria
description: Your support will provide medical aid, food, and winter relief for children and families from Syria who have taken refuge in Lebanon. You are also supporting special schools for refugee children who are unable to attend local schools.

title: 500 Colombian Children Learn Equality through Arts
description: Life Project Foundation is a round-the-clock safe space for over 500 Colombian children living in the slums. We provide arts, music, and theatre workshops focused on teaching about gender equality. The acceptance of diversity is our goal. The activities are supplemented with a nutritious snack every day. We also offer school tutoring to breach the opportunity gap.

title: Mapping sexual violence in Kenya
description: We are mapping sexual violence in Kenya with our partner, Polycom Development Project who is a grassroots organisation working on sexual and reproductive health in Kibera, one of the largest slums in Nairobi. We are raising funds to help them train 5 youth leaders to map sexual violence and use the data collected to analyse trends and patterns which can further be used to engage institutional stakeholders in finding local solutions.

title: A Carnival free from Sexual Violence
description: Ahead of the Carnival in Trinidad and Tobago, we want to advocate for a carnival free from sexual violence.

title: Training 10 Youth Campus Ambassadors on Safety
description: We plan to train 10 Youth Campus Ambassadors to work on projects to further safety of women and girls to prevent sexual violence.

title: World Vision responding to Sunda Strait Tsunami
description: The tsunami caused by the Mount Krakatau activity in Sunda Strait, hit Sunda Strait shores on  December 22, 2018. The waves and the high wind caused massive damage to infrastructure. World Vision is on the ground, responding to the immediate and urgent needs of the affected population, especially children. In the relief phase of the response, World Vision will be focusing on the sectors of Health and Child Protection, Water Sanitation & Hygiene, and cash-based programming.

title: Constructing a school in rural Papua New Guinea
description: Morobe Development Foundation, a non-profit organisation located in PNG, is looking to fund the construction of Kobo Primary School. The purpose of this project is to enable the children of Kobo and Wainsoduna Village to receive an education. The funding that was promised to the project has not come through, so we're trying to raise money to improve one of the least developed areas in the Morobe province and improve the quality of life for residents.

title: End Witchcraft Branding and Stigmatization (EWBS)
description: The End Witchcraft Branding and Stigmatization (#EWBS) project is an advocacy campaign designed to combat the widespread branding and stigmatization of children as witches in the southern region of Nigeria. BRCI will over the duration (24 months) of the project advocate for improved laws, train police officers ans other first respondents and engage traditional leaders and religious leaders on the need to end child witchcraft branding and stigmatization.

title: Khudmukhtar - A Microfinance Initiative
description: Khudmukhtar - a-micro-finance-initiative working in Pakistan with envisions to eradicating chronic poverty/hunger through agriculture-based revolving livestock model based on "Form to Table" approach. Khudmukhtar invests in rural people, empowering them to reduce extreme poverty, increase food security, nutrition and strengthen resilience.  We empower rural families to turn hunger and poverty into hope, dignity and prosperity - but our approach is based on revolving livestock model.

title: Create with Code: Teacher training & Student clubs
description: You can empower 20 enthusiastic teachers in Ghana's government schools to teach Scratch and HTML! They in turn guide over 200 junior high school students in computational thinking, creative expression, and basic programming through our after school clubs. The project provides 3 training sessions, ongoing support, and other resources for 10 after school clubs through the year, a fun and educational coding challenge, and connectivity to share their projects with the world.

title: Improve living conditions for 3 destitute widows
description: We are requesting funds to rebuild the homes of 3 poverty stricken widows who have no other means of assistance. The structures are all but destroyed, and will not survive the rainy season of March. MDIH staff will find materials and provide labor. Without help, these widows and their children will be without any type of shelter. Your support is crucial and potentially life saving to these families.

title: Send a Child in Pakistan to School for a Year
description: Maa Ki Dua primary schools provide children in disadvantaged tribal areas with access to quality education in an interactive and joyful environment. Children are enabled to join mainstream schools, having become confident, independent learners.

title: Educating Impoverished Children in Kenya
description: The project will provide educational support to students in East Pokot to further their education and eradicate illiteracy. HAO has provided 55 scholarships, supported 13 schools with eLearning tools, trained 96 teachers on STEM and mentored 70 students. East Pokot has 4% literacy and 60% of children never attend school in their lifetime. Donations will directly fund scholarships, scholastic materials, mentorship and Sanitary products. Beneficiaries: girls, underprivileged, orphans and disabled

title: Emergency Ambulance for Whisper's Hospital
description: A life saving ambulance that will be used for transportation of dying children who need urgently oxygen and blood transfusion. This ambulance will also be in used to transport and give first aid to mothers in labour pain, mothers with complications after giving birth, and other major urgent maternity surgical procedures. This ambulance will be able to have a small laboratory and blood cross-matching equipment for urgent blood transfusion. The ambulance will be operated by doctors and nursers.

title: Educate 33 children with disabilities in Sri Lanka
description: Education is a human right that is often denied to disabled children. We train our teachers & parents to go against the accepted norm of low expectations for such children. Our pioneering program helps create productive stimulating lives by providing age-appropriate education, sensory-integration therapy, training, counseling, & support services to child and family. To help our families battle prejudice & poverty we provide our services for free. You help is needed for us to continue our work.

title: Ending Veteran homelessness in Michigan
description: This project will help provide affordable section 8 housing and food to homeless veterans and less privileged in Michigan. Michigan ranks #11 (608,271) in total Veterans Population (Sources: Population, VA Office of Data Governance and Analytics, US Census Bureau County, FY 2016) and with this project, HIRED Project aim to reduce this social issue of hunger and displacements of our Service Heroes. Provide them a place to call a HOME.

title: Help Orphans In India (GSAM General Fund)
description: This project is set up to support the day to day care of the children of the Good Shepherd Agricultural Mission in India.  In the heart of every child is a hunger for home. Not just for food and a place to sleep, but for safety and community. Most importantly: for love. The mission is more than a home for unwanted Indian orphans. It is a family. It is a nearly self-sustaining organization; a working farm, a vibrant school and all this while receiving no government assistance of any kind.

title: Feed a Child
description: Malnutrition is a critical risk in rural India and good nutrition and access to adequate food remains a challenge to child survival.  Poverty is a growing reality in Rural Karnataka that we face on a daily basis.  It largely affects children  from all demographic groups throughout the villages.  Feed the child program help fight against classroom hunger.

title: Creating livelihoods for youth in Timor-Leste
description: In post-conflict Timor-Leste, rural communities (70% of the population) are trapped in poverty. 74% is bellow 35 but most youth remain poorly educated with limited access to training and employment. Through a unique internship and on-the-job training we will leverage our successes in rural development and economic growth to empower 30 youth of the impoverished island of Atauro to pursue new livelihoods, generating income and becoming leaders of change for hundreds of others in their communities.

title: Sanitation facilities for 5 Public schools Uganda
description: The initiative aims to construct 5 drain-able girl friendly VIP latrines of 5 stances each with wash room, provide reliable hand washing facility for girls of menstruating age in the five public primary schools in Uganda. To reduce the high pupil to latrines ratio, and provide a separate girls' pit-latrine to avoid risk of harassment and school drop-out, this will ensure school attendance of girls during menstruation and increase the number of girls with qualifications.

title: Back to school with + Solidarity
description: It is estimated that more than one million students throughout Costa Rica will begin the school in february. However, for more than 328,848 families living in poverty, this means a real economic challenge.  The "Back to School with + Solidarity" campaign seeks to support this students by collecting school supplies, to be delivered to the students of the 17 public schools where we work.

title: Protect Coral Reefs in Malaysia
description: Reef Check Malaysia works to conserve Malaysia's ocean and marine ecosystems. Malaysia is part of the Coral Triangle, home to more than 75% of the world's coral species. Our Projects are based in 3 locations in Malaysia - Tioman Island, Mersing group of islands, and Mantanani Island. Our teams are based on these islands, where they work with the local communities to empower them to look after the marine resources.

title: Educate 200 Children Near Ranthambore, India
description: Gramin Shiksha Kendra Uday Community School, Jaganpura provides quality, activity-based education for 200 children from 5 villages on the fringe of Ranthambore National Park.  Our proximity to the park is key: the children are connected with wildlife through their backyard, schoolyard, and beyond.  GSK believes that schools are an extension of the community and the Uday Community School, Jaganpura is run by the community.

title: Friendly spaces for children affected by war
description: As the conflict in Yemen continues, children are suffering more and more they are leaving their schools, their rights have been lost, and they are suffering from serious psychological consequences of the war. Therefore, this should be remedied, so we have launched a project for children who are affected by the war. To allow children to overcome this ordeal, the project will focus on the physical and mental activities of children to enhance their abilities and build confidence in  themselves.

title: German Red Cross / Deutsches Rotes Kreuz
description: The German Red Cross is a member of the global community of the international Red Cross and Red Crescent movement, providing help without discrimination to the victims of conflicts and disasters and others in need. The German Red Cross is active in numerous missions concerning emergency response, rehabilitation after disaster, and development projects.

title: Help Our Orphanage with Operational Cost
description: Our Orphanage called Dormaa Children's home in Ghana has been commissioned. Currently, we have four Kids in our care. We take care of their feeding, shelter, healthcare, education and recreational needs. We do not have big-time donors for the orphanage. We rely on the goodwill of small donors to take care of the orphans in the home. We do not charge the children or parents for the services we provide for them. We have monthly budget of $800/month. We are the last hope of these children.

title: Gift early Learning to an orphan
description: Children who attend pre school before school age do better in school. However, due to lack of funds most Ugandan orphans are unable to attend school early enough. This project will complete an early learning centre to provide basic literacy and numeracy to children who were orphaned by Hiv/AIDS.

title: Alleviate Suffering of End-Stage Diseases Patients
description: This project will provide support to 30 very poor end-stage diseases  patients in order for them to not suffer miserably and have peace of mind as they struggle with their treatment. We will focus on cardiovascular, cancer, liver and kidney diseases which strike all, with the very poor, without access to resources, suffering miserably.

title: Building the Foundation for a Permanent School
description: Funding is needed to begin phase one of a multi-year project to purchase land and build a permanent school for students in Gbawe, Ghana and continue an Adult Education Program. This is in support of our mission to build communities through education to increase literacy and decrease poverty.

title: Build Safe School For Children In East Indonesia
description: This project will build a safe, sustainable school in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia providing a conducive learning environment and encouraging the local community to send their children to school. School that's currently in unsafe condition will be rebuilt to consist of safe foundation, walls, roof, and clean toilet, and equipped with indoor furniture, toys and outdoor playground. Teachers, parents and community members will also receive proper training so they can sustain the school.

title: Arsal Camps: Winter Crisis Relief Fund in Lebanon
description: This project will help 700 refugees' families (3500 people approx) that are currently in Arsal, northeast of Beirut, in Baalbek-Hermel Governorate, Lebanon.  (60% Female; 40% Male). The most pressing need today is 'winterization' items -  Shelter (plastic sheets), Fuel for Heating, Food parcels and winter clothes for children.

title: Help Build a Chimney Swift Tower
description: Chimney swifts are declining in number because of the loss of habitat.  They began nesting in chimneys as forests were cleared and houses were built.  However, they can not make nests in metal-lined chimneys.  With fewer available chimneys (those with metal liners or chimney caps prevent nesting) and hollow trees, their numbers are diminishing. We also hope to create an area for swifts to roost when they return from wintering in Peru from November through March.

title: Help children in Varna access free art courses
description: Dedal is an art school in Bulgaria that provides free classes in the art and sciences for children from orphanages, single-parent families, foster families and children with minor disabilities. In addition to free access, the centre provides the diverse social environment necessary for promoting social integration. Dedal has helped over 900 children overcome social isolation by developing their skills and talents while working actively with art professionals on a completely voluntary basis.

title: Catalyzing Next Generation Women's Leadership
description: Creating intergenerational coalitions has the potential to infuse new energy, skills and tactics into established movements. CHIME FOR CHANGE is partnering with Global Fund for Women to connect young activists with experienced advocates and grassroots organizations. Global Fund for Women will support 3 sister women's funds-Semillas in Mexico, HER Fund in Hong Kong, and ELAS in Brazil-to invest in, highlight, and build locally-led community investment for young women's leadership.

title: Health Post Funding in Nepal
description: Funding for running a health program in a health post in Bichhya, within the Bajura district. This funding will cover the cost of staff, transportation, training and activities related to health and hygiene. 2000 patients will be provided with primary treatment at PHASE-supported clinics, 25 child births will be supported by skilled birth workers, and 100 pregnant women will be visited at least once (ANC 1st) in PHASE supported clinics.

title: School Building for Neglected Children
description: This project ensures an extension of a school building which provides free education to poor neglected children. The present condition of school is so congested that in one classroom managing two classes and the whole floor is packed with 387 children from LKG to 7th standard. Next academic year, with new children awaiting to join is a major challenge. We propose to construct two more floors 6200 s.ft ($18.75 per s.ft) thus having 14 additional classrooms altogether, accommodating  900 students.

title: Global Teacher Training Initiative
description: Teaching is the most vital occupation, yet it is the most undervalued and often the most underappreciated of them all. Due to this fact, the quality of education and teaching capabilities are not where they need to be, especially in the more underdeveloped countries, as they're often isn't enough funding to maximise the training/ pay the teachers enough. Our goal is to maximise teacher training across all project locations so that we can enhance education and build economies.

title: FREE OF COST DISTRIBUTION OF BLANKET
description: This project will build a support Barisal  Division in Bangladeshi rural poor people and persons with disabilities. Planning, measuring and counting to implement adequate service delivery in action on free distribution of blanket as well as winter cloths. Employing more staff in the office. Also by assisting Government in health service as well.

title: FREE HOSTEL SERVICES FOR  CHILDREN WITH AUTISM
description: This project will established a shelter home for the Children with autism in Bangladesh. Planning, measuring and counting to implement adequate service delivery in action on free hostel services as well as food services. Employing more staff in the office. Also by assisting Government in social service as well in Raihanpur under district of Barguna at Barishal Divisions  of Bangladesh.

title: Sports for All
description: HERA's goal is to develop and support young women, girls and youth in Libya by using sport as an active learning tool around issues of social cohesion, health and reconciliation. Through their programs 'Sports for All' and 'That's Our Goal', HERA is delivering workshops in Libyan schools, IDP refugee camps and with the girl guides programs, breaking down cultural barriers and uniting youth through sport.

title: Educate Future Environmental Stewards
description: This project educates and empowers the future leaders of tomorrow to be more environmentally conscientious. The students are taught a wide range of practices to safeguard marine and freshwater habitats and also about the consequences of not doing so. The mission of Marine Education Initiative is to empower individuals to become responsible anglers through hands-on programs centered on fishing in a more sustainable manner to foster widespread community engagement and change.

title: AMBULANCE SERVICES TO DISEASE PEOPLE IN BANGLADESH
description: This Project will build a platform for the poor persons in rural area of Banlgadesh.Rural poor helpless disease persons  will be benefited from this project.Implement adequate service delivery in action on  health-rehabilitation and shelter. Employing more staff in the project area. Also by assisting Government in counting, providing inadequate ambulance support. implementing area is Patharghata sub-districts under Barugna district of Bangladesh.

title: FREE OF COST DISTRIBUTION OF ASSISTIVE DEVICE
description: This project will build a powerful strength for the  persons with disabilities in the rural area of Barguna district of Bangladesh. Providing the support and  to implementing adequate service delivery in action on free distribution of assistive device.  Employing more staff in the office. Also by assisting Government in social service as well. So many poor persons with disable people  will be benefited from this project.

title: Cervical Cancer Screening for women in Kosovo
description: This project will build a sustainable healthcare service that will offer free Pap-Smear Testing to thousands of women in Kosovo who cannot otherwise afford the expensive testing and diagnosis.

title: Help Fight Poverty in the Dominican Republic
description: The Go Green Toy Foundation works with low income children in the Dominican Republic, aged 4-12, providing them with skills to make and re-purpose toys. This has expanded to tutorials, trainings and seminars. The children learn and apply ethics, integrity, honesty and leadership that the later use in life AND they also learn to Green It Forward! You should see the joy in their eyes because they know we care...

title: Gonzaga College High School Fighting For A Change
description: As members of the International Business Internship Program, Izzy, Joe, Jaren, Annie, & John work weekly to address issues that our business partner Mr. Umar, who owns an automotive repair business, encounters in his everyday practices. We are working towards finding business solutions which will bring about benefits for both our business partner and his entire community.

title: Trousseau Pediatric Hematology Unit renovation
description: A key renovation & humanization of pediatric hemato-oncologic Unit in hopital Trousseau, Paris. This unit has to be completely rebuilt and rethought.  Laurette Fugain has been a key partner of this unit since years, and wants to contribute to the huge support needed to make a news, clear, cosy place for these severe ill children.

title: Funding 4 leukaemia research projects
description: Leuka would fund 4 innovative research projects to improve current treatment of leukaemia.  Our funding will nurture the next generation of top scientists to improve the lives of people affected by leukaemia and blood cancers.

title: Gender-Based Violence Among Young People in Italy
description: One in three women will experience violence in their lifetime. Young women and girls experience the highest rates of Gender-Based Violence (GBV). In 2014, Vital Voices launched The Justice Institute on GBV to facilitate the creation of holistic responses to GBV. Supported by CHIME FOR CHANGE, Vital Voices will leverage the successful methodology of the Justice Institute to convene allied advocates and facilitate survivor-centered approaches to address GBV among youth in Italy.

title: Training on safe and unsafe touch to 5000 kids
description: 1) 5000  children (from 3 to 16 years) of government schools of Indore city will be trained on safe and unsafe touch. 2) two School teachers from 20  schools and 5 children from 20 school will be trained as master trainer to sustain the project. 3) School support staff will be trained to take care of children by child friendly practices. 4) 20 schools comprising 5000 children in Indore city of   Madhya pradesh will be benefited.

title: Empowering Youth Through Higher Education
description: Hill Tribe Children in remote mountain villages of Northern Thailand have little chance to escape a life of poverty. Educational opportunities are minimal. Too often they turn to the sex trade for survival.  We offer an alternative choice. We begin by helping them learn the Thai language so they can attend public school, providing required uniforms, transportation, after-school tutoring, health care, and a safe home. Then we support them as far as they can reach for higher education.

title: Help Young Women Break the Glass Ceiling in Nepal!
description: Women LEAD plans to deliver professional development workshops and professional mentoring for young, aspiring women leaders in Nepal. We aim to equip these young women with the skills and knowledge they need to become leaders across all sectors of Nepalese society. Women LEAD will also provide young women with seed funding to implement their own community advocacy projects which challenge traditional attitudes and norms that are preventing young women from achieving their potential.

title: New Home for Abandoned Girls with ID
description: For as little as $35 (the cost of 1 sq.ft.) you can help Sri Arunodayam construct a new home for abandoned girls with intellectual disability (ID). Sri Arunodayam was founded in 2002 as a registered public charitable trust and recognized as a Reception Unit by the State Government of Tamil Nadu in 2008. Sri Arunodayam rescues, cares for and rehabilitates children with ID who have been abandoned by their families.

title: Trafficked Women Defense Fund
description: Young women living in remote villages often yearn for a better future by travelling to the cities, often enticed by friends and contacts who are already there. They are often victims of human traffickers and when this happen, their future is ruined, never to be bright again. This initiative will provide fund to assist trafficked women escape from their predicament by giving them shelter, legal help, food, transportation and communication support.

title: Help Fund Learning Resources for our School Laos
description: Laos is a country with education inequality, particularly affecting the poorer communities and young girls. Due to education in Laos only being compulsory for 5 years, the education they do receive is often poor quality and under-resourced. This project aims to tackle the education inequality in these areas by providing quality educational resources, teacher training and improved facilities to encourage children to continue their studies into higher education.

title: Reducing Poverty and Inequality in Urban Cambodia
description: Regeneration is the aim of this project. In Phnom Penh there is around 300 informal settlements where people have made their home and have a lack of water and sanitation. Although Cambodia is one of the fastest growing economies the country remains one of the most least developed. A problem we can't tackle alone, partnered with University of New South Wales we are able to access their resources to help build up resilience from the bottom, using their support for research to build a better slum

title: Investing in Young People to be Powerful Champions
description: Young people are changing the world today, creating the reality of tomorrow. Supported by CHIME FOR CHANGE, the Women Deliver Young Leaders Program connects outstanding young advocates with the platforms, the people, and the resources that can amplify their influence on a larger scale. With an emphasis on sexual and reproductive health and rights, Women Deliver elevates the work of young people taking a stand for gender equality.

title: Youth Led Solutions to Systemic Problems
description: Change Architects transforms youth into change makers through community development and social entrepreneurship using design thinking.  250+ innovative teachers volunteer their time to facilitate activities for their students. 5,000+ youth identify problems in their communities, brainstorm ideas and implement sustainable solutions. In doing so, they develop 21st Century skills such as: empathy, collaboration, communication, leadership and confidence in their own capacity to generate change.

title: Support Young Women Activists in the Middle East
description: Equality Now is partnering with CHIME FOR CHANGE to mobilize activists to drive progress in the Middle East and North Africa. We'll support these activists - especially young women activists - to advance legal change that promotes gender equality, particularly laws around child marriage, male guardianship, sexual violence and sexual harassment, and nationality and inheritance laws.

title: Support 30 Disaster Relief Projects in Philippines
description: Hello everyone! I'm Grace and I will be GlobalGiving's Field Traveler in The Philippines for 2019! Over a three-month period, I will be visiting 30 of our local nonprofit partners. I will be supporting their work in helping communities to rebuild livelihoods after the devastation of multiple super typhoons in the past decade. While in the field, I will be conducting site visits, meeting with community leaders face-to-face, and organizing training workshops to help them work and grow effectively.

title: Support 30 nonprofits in Rwanda & Uganda!
description: My name is Leena and I'll be helping 30 nonprofits in Uganda & Rwanda grow their impact within their communities. I'll be using my risk management experience for social good, and I'm hoping to get your support. While I'll be offered a modest stipend; I'm expected to cover the majority of the cost of this volunteer experience. Any support you contribute will go towards helping me manage daily expenses. No contribution is too small: from sharing my project with your network, to making a donation.

title: In person support for 60 South American NGOs
description: Hola! I am Viktorija, a volunteer Field Traveler for GlobalGiving. During March-September 2019 I am visiting nonprofit partners in South America (Chile, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru). During 6 months in the field my role is to strengthen connections with existing nonprofit partners through project site visits. Apart from that, I am also leading workshops about efficient fundraising, facilitating peer discussions on vital topics and providing a platform to learn from and share success stories.

title: Help Support 30 Kenyan Social Changemakers
description: Hujambo (Hello)! In early 2019, I will be travelling Kenya to connect with thirty of GlobalGiving's nonprofit partners driving community-led change across sectors. As a field traveler, I will be working to better enable our partners in becoming more sustainable, connected, and responsive, in order to optimize their community impact. My work will involve conducting one-on-one consultations at project sites, leading workshops, and providing support in building partner crowdfundraising capacity.

title: Medic Outpost Africa
description: Medic Outpost's mission is to provide training and equipment to remote first responders in rural Kenya.  Medic Outpost will be training community healthcare workers in the Maasai Lands of Southern Kenya.  Our goal is to develop basic healthcare capacity in rural villages by providing training, education, and resources to Medic Outpost trained Community Health Volunteers.  Volunteers will receive extensive training in preventative health, maternal and child health, and first aid.

title: EMPOWERING YOUTH RESEARCH DEVELOPMENT IN AFRICA
description: WIN-ARC in a 5-year project (2019-2023) shall strengthen capacities of Youth Research clubs within Ugandan Academic Institutions for innovation and creativity to real life Research Solutions. Phases: Training & Guidance  Research competitions, Unique Idea Problem solving research Projects, implementation & Production.  Outcomes: We shall create jobs, increase national tax base, Expand on National exports, Social and economic Development  & change research methods based on World problems in real.

title: Provide Health Support to Communities in Cambodia
description: Access to clean water and sanitation is a struggle for a large portion of our population, however, with 77% of people in Cambodia living in rural areas, their struggles are increasingly more intense and difficult. Students have limited access to resources that keep basic hygiene, with teeth brushing and handwashing being particular problems for them. We aim to provide our students with basic hygiene kits alongside regular workshops to teach the importance of basic hygiene practises.

title: Providing Scholarships to Children in Cambodia
description: In Kampong Cham, school days provided by the government typically last half the day. To recieve a full education students need to pay and attend an internatioanl school. We want to make sure that all of our students receive a full day of education by sponsoring students to attend afternoon drop in centres/ international schools or public schools operating in the afternoon. For students not able to attend even half a day of school, we would like to sponsor them so they have access to an education

title: Support 56 Non-profits in West Africa
description: My name is Dalila. I am GlobalGiving's Field Traveler in West Africa for a period of 6 months. I will be conducting 56 visits to GlobalGiving's partners to evaluate their work and running 8 workshops to train our current non-profit partners in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Ghana. I'll also be acquiring new strategic partners and much more.

title: Life with Inclusion
description: Our project gives children with special needs a chance to be supported by tutors, ABA specialists and paraprofessionals in state comprehensive school and preschool environment due to the total absence of such practice in current legislation. Children experiencing challenges in learning desperately need inclusive education.

title: A2Z Care to 50 destitute senior citizen in Odisha
description: The project aims to address 50  mostly abandoned, destitute, disabled senior citizens nutritional food, clothing, shelter,  health care, recreational support, emotional support, disability care and personality development aspects in Cuttack district of Odisha. The identified disabled persons are mostly within the age group of 65-80 years and at present they are neglected by their family members and   and residing outside. They are satisfying their hunger by begging   and left uncured for surviv

title: An egg a day for kids in middle west China
description: The One Egg Program initiated by Shanghai United Foundation (SUF) is to improve children's health in poverty areas in China by giving an egg per day to every child. SUF runs the program in cooperation with local grassroots NGOs and village schools. An egg only costs 10 cents but it means a lot to hungry kids. This fund will support more than 22,000 children and their teachers of 158 kindergarten and primary schools in poor districts of West China for Spring semester of 2019.

title: Meals for "Shared Pot" at Paraiso (Lima)
description: This 2022, we continue supporting people who need food. The pandemic might be over soon, but the impact will stay with us for longer.  According to Action Against Hunger, 73.4% of the population in Lima live under food insecurity, 1 in 8 people suffer from malnutrition and 40% of the the population between 3 to 35 months suffer from anaemia. Due to this crisis, we are focusing on those who need more now: our community partners in Lima. Please, help us.

title: Adopt a Dream, Sponsor a Child
description: With this project, we will be able to continue our work with children, adolescents, and their families in Tierra Bomba Island. We currently work with the community, directly impacting 1,006 people and indirectly 2,672 people. We welcome over 500 children from the island and seek to involve the entire family nucleus to contribute to the eradication of poverty, through the implementation of our comprehensive model, which promotes six areas of human development.

title: Safe water & Sanitation for Kouk Srok Village
description: Transform the lives of 1,711 villagers in Kouk Srok through the provision of safe water and sanitation. Access to safe water and sanitation will alleviate the many hardships the community currently face: frequent waterborne illnesses, consequential absences from school and employment, and expensive medical costs by providing them with Biosand filters (BSFs), latrines and hygiene education.

title: Supporting Women & Girls of Color to Innovate
description: Women and girls of color are at the forefront of the gender equality movement to ensure safety, health and economic opportunity for all women and girls in the United States. Supported by CHIME FOR CHANGE, the Ms. Foundation for Women plans to provide targeted innovation grants for grassroots movement building by women and girls in some of the least resourced communities in the United States, including the South.

title: Empowering 600 teenage mothers in Sri Lanka
description: This project will empower 600 teenage mothers living in Monaragala district, Uva province Sri Lanka,  who married without legal entity in aged between 16- 18 and victimized socially and economically due to the abandonment of the partners. This critical issue has not been addressed yet by the responsible authorities, therefore, the project will assist them to regain their lives by providing opportunities to protect their rights, to organize themselves and to develop their skills and resources

title: Rescue-Spay/Neuter 200 dogs abandoned in Mexico
description: Our Dog Rescue Center plans to provide medical care, including vaccinations and neuter/spay operations, for 200 dogs in Santa Rosalia, Mexico. Stray dogs roam the streets and the number will continue rising unless we shift the trend by providing veterinary care, promoting adoption, and increasing animal treatment education. We will improve the health and safety of the community by improving the health and well-being of the stray dogs.

title: Advent International for PIH
description: This year Advent International is supporting Partners In Health to bring lifesaving health care to women in need.  Poverty makes womanhood, motherhood, and early childhood dangerous, even fatal, when basic care is too far and expensive to access.  We must expand access to women's health care in Haiti, Malawi, even the Navajo Nation, right here at home. That means family planning, safe births, and the regular check-ups every family deserves.

title: CREATING JOB OPPORTUNITY TO MITGATE MIGRATION
description: Migration in Ethiopia, especially in SNNPR, Hadiya Zone Lemo Woreda Shurimo Town and others economic, poverty and lack of job opportunity has become an issue, as the absorptive capacity of the communities is already limited due to the high population density, the division of plots of land into smaller parcels despite poor productivity, and the exploitation of land by poor management. In addition, the push factors for youth's migration in the projected area are lack of job opportunities,

title: Sport-social base in BG - hosting 90 youths/year
description: Our goal is to buy, renovate and develop a sports-social base 100 km from Sofia (80 % highway) and located in a wonderful ecologically clean mountainous region. With the development of the base, our goal is to create an innovative space that combines many positive features - eco cleanliness, opportunities for non-formal education, sports, tourism, active rest, social contacts and work. We have also targeted our nearby partners that offer additional mountain and sports experiences.

title: Sustainable Economic Empowerment for 200slum women
description: Daughters Of Kenya has found out that 1 in every 3 girls in Mukuru kwa Njenga slums of Nairobi are young mothers solely shouldering the heavy burden of raising their children without any economic means to do so. The project seeks to use the self help group concept to improve their livelihoods through training on life skills and micro enterprises; soap making, cake baking, mat making and bead work for 150 out of school girls and women.

title: train 250 widows in benin city,$576 each
description: skill training and financial empowerment of 250 widows and  vulnerable persons in Benin city of Nigeria.we intend to help women undergo skill acquisition in various art and craft,textiles and designs,beauty and fashion,catering and confectionery etc. afterwards we will empower with small funds to either startup or accelerate their business.

title: Nurse me: milk powder for malnourished kids, Benin
description: This project wants to cope with the widespread issue of child malnutrition in the regions of Zou and Atacora (Benin), through the supply of milk powder to undernourished newborns in the Hospital of Tanguieta and in three local accommodation centres.

title: FREE OF COST STREET CHILDREN EDUCATION BANGLADESH
description: Under this project, 200 street & poor slum children will be given education as well as Nutrition food, Gift, New Dress, Lunch/Dinner, Toys & Happiness. The Program will be quite unique. For poor street & slum children all this is a dream. But will it be possible. A meal & gifts for 700 poor children life will become a golden memory in Barguna & Barisal Bangladesh.

title: Train 155 Youth to Teach 2325 Sri Lankan Children
description: Tea Leaf Trust will train 155 amazing, hardworking students to teach critical English lessons to 2,325 children a year. These lovely children are from the remote Sri Lankan tea estates and unable to access or afford classes. English offers them the chance escape a future of near slavery. The students will develop key professional skills that are crucial to their futures. The project also empowers them to become leaders of change in communities facing abject poverty and complex social issues.

title: Save 1000 girls from Child Marriage in Nakaseke,Ug
description: The project will establish a platform to provide free vocational marketable skills to 1000 vulnerable girls in rural Uganda Africa. We will provide training materials like sewing machines, baking ovens, hairdressing and Jewelry making materials to vulnerable girls at-risk, married, and/or formerly married.  ACCESS will build classrooms and hire experts to impart entrepreneurial skills. Once empowered, girls will get startup capital for business and empower other members.

title: 50 YOUTHS TO GET PRACTICAL SKILLS  MAKINDYE-UGANDA
description: The project  will equip (50) youths, women and persons with disabilities with literacy skills, vocational, essential micro-entrepreneurial and life skills that will enable them rise out of poverty, provide for their families health and well-being as well as create opportunities for self - employment within their local communities. They will acquire skills which will transform them into productive entities of the nation and become units of change as well as wheels of development.

title: Eradicate Drug Trafficking in Soweto Schools
description: Nyaope- a cocktail drug comprised mainly of heroin, marijuana and various other substances is ravaging our community, our schools, and, in its wake, destroying the lives of many a child before they even reach maturity. Children from impoverished communities as young as 12 are targeted by drug dealers to not only sell this drug in schools, but with the deliberate intention of getting these children severely addicted - thus creating the type of destructive environment conducive to their own profit

title: REHABILITATION OF THIRD GENDER IN BANGLADESH
description: This project will build a strength in Bangladesh providing rich training.The Persons with Third gender in Bangladesh will be awareness in the society. Planning, measuring and counting to implement adequate service delivery in action on rehabilitation of third gender peoples.Employing more staff in the office. Also by assisting Government in social service as well.Post: Raihanpur under district of Barguna at Barishal Divisions  of Bangladesh are the project area.

title: Keep our Children's Hospital Open
description: Our children's hospital in Jinja, Uganda has treated over 70000 children since we opened in 2016. We don't know any other charity that saves more lives for a given donation, and the hospital has such a good reputation that patients can travel for hours to see us.   We're looking for more kind friends like you to help keep it running by making a regular monthly donation.

title: Access to Menstrual Products in East Africa
description: Menstrual stigma, lack of access to menstrual products, and low education on reproductive health are putting girls' and women's health at risk. It also limits their life opportunities and, therefore, opportunities for their families and communities. This is worse in low socio-economic and rural communities in Tanzania and Kenya. Over 70% of women said they couldn't afford menstrual products for their last period. Femme International is working to support these communities.

title: Restore the livelihood of 250 youths in Luwero
description: Youth Empowerment Trust Uganda (YETU) will conduct financial literacy classes, coaching & mentorship and give micro-loans to 100 youths whose livelihood has been adversely affected by Covid 19 pandemic in Luwero District, Central Uganda. This will help the youths to start income-generating activities and restore their livelihoods

title: Support 125 children at Refugio Rafael in Bolivia
description: Refugio Rafael, located outside Cochabamba, Bolivia, provides core programs for vulnerable children and families. The transitional housing opportunity for single mothers and their children, currently serves 4 families who previously were homeless or unable to provide the basics for their families. The after school program serves 100 children who need critical educational support to succeed in school. Economic development, health care and social services complement the central programs.

title: Fund PostSecondary Education for Girls in Tanzania
description: Girls Education International is partnering with Project Wezesha, a local NGO, to ensure that young women in Tanzania have access to the education, support, and skills necessary to achieve their dreams and become whatever they desire. In this program, we support young women in their pursuit of education by providing scholarships to those seeking university and vocational training and covering the fees associated with their high school education.

title: PeaceJam Timor-Leste
description: This project will empower hundreds of young Timorese with the knowledge and skills to become leaders committed to positive change in themselves, their communities, and the world.

title: Invest in creating powerful voices!
description: Objective and critical voices are under attack from increasingly polarizing politics, uncivil discourse in mainstream media and a digital culture easy to manipulate. This project allows donors to contribute to RNTC's Scholarship Fund to be used to train young, critically minded media professionals (journalists, bloggers, vloggers) worldwide, so they can act as guardians of public interest. With 50 years of experience, RNTC trains professionals worldwide in the use of media for social change.

title: Plant Trees to Restore PreyLang Wildlife Sanctuary
description: This project will enable Cambodians, especially youth, to plant thousands of endangered rosewood trees in the Prey Lang Wildlife Sanctuary, a heavily deforested "protected" zone.  Cambodians from diverse backgrounds will come together for a 4-day Tree Planting Camp to learn about the forest and climate change, support the local communities who protect the forest, and develop connections and ideas about how to engage in the critical environmental issues of today.

title: HELP EDUCATING 209 SPECIAL CHILDREN IN RURAL INDIA
description: Our Program Key Objectives Are: To educate & provide preventive, intervention and rehabilitative services to Children with Intellectual & Developmental Disabilities and/or Hearing Impairment To conduct training and capacity building in the field of rehabilitation to make a pool of better equipped professionals, parents, care-givers  To ensure, advocate and promote equal rights of the special needs children To motivate and sensitize all stake holders for the special children's training

title: Protecting the Big 5 in South Africa
description: Africa is known for its incredible biodiversity & the picturesque backdrop that house its iconic species. However, with forever increasing human populations & anthropogenic pressures on wildlife populations, numbers continent-wide are dwindling. Africa's species need our protection & local wildlife research organisations are taking big leaps forward in working towards this common goal. Understanding the ecology of species, such as the big 5, to ensure their longevity, is crucial.

title: Learn to Earn! Trades training in Gulu, Uganda
description: 20 years of civil war left many in Gulu, Uganda with few skills to earn a living. The Family Harvest Foundation, a charity started and operated by people from Gulu, is approved by the Uganda Ministry of Education to provide much needed vocational training. The trades training will allow those trained to sit examination by the Directorate of Industrial Training and be certified. The project funds will subsidize student fees, pay a small teacher's stipend and purchase training equipment.

title: Enabling Access to Safe Drinking Water& Sanitation
description: Supporting education and improved health for 2,000 people across communities, health centers and schools, this project will provide training to community pump caretakers, WASH Committees and volunteers on preventive maintenance and rehabilitation of dysfunctional water wells. For areas without access to water supply and toilets, we will deliver on making them available. The project will expand access to safe drinking water, improved conditions of health and increased school attendance for kids.

title: Training for 70 teachers
description: 70 teachers and 70 youths in the poorest rural areas of Burma/Myanmar will receive Teacher & English training who otherwise would not have access to such training. The training will enable 70 students improve their English proficiency, critical thinking and problem solving skills, and leadership qualities which are important for them to prepare themselves for the future and to succeed while 70 teachers will deliver improved quality teaching services to 2000+ students every year.

title: Empower communities to end child marriage - Mexico
description: Mexico is one of the countries with the highest rate of child marriage in the world. Almost 300,000 of today's girls and boys have been forced into marriage, most of them sold, and to an older spouse.   Facilitating community processes, we have already ended the sale of girls for marriage in 3 communities. We want to continue impacting many more communities in Mexico where child marriage persists.

title: Preserve Big Cats in South Africa
description: With forever increasing human populations & anthropogenic pressures on wildlife populations, numbers continent-wide are dwindling. Current population trends for big cats across Africa are decreasing. Cheetah, leopard & lion populations are all suffering from habitat loss, human-habitat conflicts & individuals taken from the wild to place in captivity. Preservation of these species is only possible through education and research on the ground, at the heart of the problem.

title: Life-changing Orthopaedic Surgery for 100 Children
description: Children with disabilities are severely stigmatized in rural and urban India, especially those children who are born into families which are poor or below the poverty line. When a child develops a disability, it is often seen as a tragic event by the family and community.  Rehabilitation Centres For Children was founded in 1973 to provide comprehensive multidisciplinary treatment for these children. This project will provide free surgery and rehabilitation for 100 children in Kolkata, India.

title: Train and Employ 1500 impoverished women in India
description: SHAPE N.G.O. is implementing its 'Township level Women Welfare Project' in 200 villages. This 15-month project will help 1500 women of Tiruvannamalai, a drought-prone district of India. These preidentified beneficiaries include impoverished, Dalits, disabled, HIV-AIDS victims, widows and downtrodden. They will gain free vocational (sewing/computer) training along with Personal/English Language/Interpersonal Development, Legal/Rights/Health/Environmental education and Psychological Counseling.

title: Onondaga Jr/Sr High School Fighting For A Change
description: Dylan is a sophomore and the Team Lead of the International Business Internship Program (IBIP) team at Onondaga Jr/Sr High School along with his sister Natalie and classmate Nicole. IBIP is run by Leadership Initiatives, which works to transform the lives of hard working business owners in developing nations. Along with his sister and classmate, the Onondaga Team is partnered with Shehu Gagare, the owner of a fish farm in Nigeria.

title: COVID-19-Support for Elderly : Kolkata Initiatives
description: The lockdown in wake of COVID- 19 has been particularly catastrophic for the poor and those falling in the daily wage bracket. Within this group too, the most severely affected are the women, especially young girls and senior citizens primarily above the age of 50 who have no money to survive. With essentials commodities like ration, medicines and daily hygiene products already difficult to access, the lockdown has further reduced their ability and opportunity to procure these items.

title: Educate a Girl Child & Gift her a Better Life
description: Girls give up their education due to limited resources, household chores, having to babysit siblings, or an early marriage. For every 100 girls in rural India, only a single one reaches class 12. A key focus for Children's Hope India is creating an equal playing field, so that girls have the same opportunities to go to school as boys, through its Educate a Child program in Bhopal, India. For only 50 cents a day (or $200 a year) a donor can help educate a girl child, empower her for the future.

title: Provide Doula Care To Teen Survivors
description: Your contribution to this project will provide pregnant and parenting teen survivors of sexual violence with trauma-informed care as they journey towards being new parents. You will help them heal, cope with triggers, and cultivate healthy attachments with their new little ones. This program is an extension of the holistic healing services provided to child survivors of sexual trauma by The Firecracker Foundation.

title: Empowering Women and Girls with UNICEF
description: Girls face violations of their rights around the world. As a global community, we can do better and do more to empower women and girls. UNICEF's Gender Programming focuses on addressing barriers to women's and girls' rights through innovative paths that focus on sustainable outcomes. An example is Techno Girl, a program that focuses on minimizing gender disparities in education and encourages girls and young South African women to consider careers in science, technology, engineering and math.

title: Restore & Rebuild J-FLAG's Office, Rainbow House
description: On Sunday, December 30, 2018, our office -- affectionately monikered 'Rainbow House' -- was destroyed by a massive fire causing damage 90% of the building and its contents which value between $50,000 and $60,000. This has put a severe damper on our spirits and is a significant impediment on our operations. Rainbow House was a safe space where activities were hosted for LGBT Jamaicans to build community, discuss issues affecting the community and educate persons about laws and policies.

title: Tosepan Kalnemachtiloyan: "La escuela de todos"
description: Tosepan Kalnemachtiloyan is a bilingual indigenous school in the Sierra de Puebla, initiated by the Tosepan Titataniske indigenous cooperative, as a response to the hard life of indigenous children in local schools. The purpose is to better serve bilingual indigenous children and improve their ability to adapt to the school context. To glimpse the possibility of which they pass through the basic school years, diminishing the repetition and the scholastic abandonment.

title: Refugee Women's Fitness
description: Provides a safe and consistent place for women to gather and practice aerobic dance and strengthening exercise in two Syrian Refugee camps.  This program improves the physical, mental, and emotional health of participants, creates community, and trains leaders from within the community.    Women have seen dramatic weight loss, better self-image, increased confidence and energy, less sickness, healthier marriages and families new friendships, and empowerment to serve their communities creatively.

title: Disasters Risk Reduction in Tharparkar Sindh
description: Ravi Foundationproposes a project with an overall objective to prepare communities for disaster risk reduction and adopt effective mitigation strategies for safety of livestock and pet animals selected 40 rural communities for 5 union councils of district Tharparkar. These are areas which are affected by drought& famine for the past many years. The primary focus is to Formation of Village Disaster Committees for the safety of Livestock and Pet Animals.

title: Food For Life & Value Education for Youth.
description: Food for Life Global is a non-profit vegetarian food relief organization operated by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Its efforts span the globe, with projects occupying over 60 countries.Volunteers provide up to 2,000,000 free meals daily. Food For Life engages in various sorts of hunger relief, including outreach to the homeless, provision for disadvantaged children throughout India, and provision for victims of natural disasters around the world.

title: Sewing Center a Women's Empowerment Initiative
description: Indian Women and Child Welfare Trust utilises creativity and enterprise to break the cycle of poverty for Indian women. We are creating an environment of self determinism and economic independence for marginalised women by harnessing their local craft traditions.

title: Cry for help from partly blind child in kgf
description: This is the sad story of Ramu (name changed) a disabled child from a very poor family  in Kolar Gold Fields.  He lost his vision after a medical complication when he was an infant of two months. With great difficulty his parents managed to get his eyes operated but it was not successful as he is able to see only blurred images. Another operation is scheduled but his parents are unable to pay.  The doctors are confident of success with the second operation.

title: Help Orphans Attend School in DR Congo and Burundi
description: Orphan education, especially in the poor regions of Africa, Uvira city-DR Congo and Kabezi city in Burundi, has always been a challenge in these areas, many children have lost their parents during the war fighting between rebels groups and government troops.   Widows are unable to pay school fees for their children, so they can continue education.  To help with this issue, Jaribu Africa Inc. is working hard to buy land to build an Orphans School and Widows Center.

title: Keeping Girls at School in Rwanda
description: The Rwandan government enacted a policy that provides all Rwandan children with Twelve years of fee-free education. Yet, girls are still dropping out of school at far higher rates than their male counterparts. YOMADO hopes to eliminate this gap through its threefold approach, which pairs girls with mentors, organizes savings and loans groups, and implements community community score cards to keep girls at School

title: A child in the sky
description: Sharing HAPPINESS with sick, hospitalized, palliative or distressed children ... that's what our reason is every day! We offer them all kinds of activities (sports cars, planes, helicopters, motorcycles, bicycles, agricultural tractors etc) which will make them forget the time of a day the hospital world . A lot of people can be mobilized for an extraordinary time just for them

title: Climate AND Disaster Relief - A New Way in PR
description: Climate Change has brought about an unprecedented number of natural disasters of never before seen power and intensity.  This trend is predicted to only increase in the foreseeable future.  This Project will reduce suffering, dislocation and potential medical emergencies in the immediate aftermath of a natural disaster.  It will also promote long term rebuilding efforts and overall disaster resiliency while treading lightly on the environment.

title: El Poder de las M- Empowering women in Puerto Rico
description: This program seeks to empower women both personally and professionally. Through various workshops, seminars and classes we seek to reinforce and focus on their strengths and talents in the various areas of life.  Through nominations, we will choose 10 women entrepreneurs on their way to open their own business.  They must present a business plan and a media plan with which they will seek the votes of the community to win the competition that will grant them $ 10,000 to start their own business.

title: Help 228 Mexican teenagers to stay in school
description: A large number of young people in Monterrey drop out school because they don't have the economic means to buy school material, they have transportation difficulty or live in families that think that they should work instead of going to school. For this reason, Caritas de Monterrey provides, courses in human development and values, psychological and economic help to young people that live in a condition of economic poverty, so they can stay in school and finish their studies.

title: A day just for them
description: Sharing HAPPINESS with sick, hospitalized, palliative or distressed children ... that's what our reason is every day! We offer them all kinds of activities (sports cars, planes, helicopters, motorcycles, bicycles, agricultural tractors etc) which will make them forget the time of a day the hospital world This little film made in 2018 to show that hundreds of people can mobilize for an extraordinary day, a day just for them

title: Samburu Girls Foundation Education Fund
description: This project will support to have a fund in Northern Kenya dedicated to the support of  education and mentorship to 400 girls rescued by Samburu Girls Foundation.   The education fund will support the girls to undergo trauma counselling, training in leadership and mentorship and become agents of change in their communities.

title: Save Lives of Snakebite Victims in Rural India
description: Snakebite kills 45,000 people annually in India - mostly simple village folk. Anjali Health Center (Pithora, Chhattisgarh) & Divya Chhaya Hospital (Subir, Gujarat) are very small primary level hospitals supporting over 6000 economically vulnerable tribal families. These hospitals treat more than 200 snakebite patients every year. TIES is providing them with adequate supplies of Anti Snake Venom (ASV), medical supplies for wound management, and snakebite management training for staff.

title: Fight Sexual violence against Women and Children
description: The situation of Women and Children in Somalia, more than twenty years of conflict, mostly in southern Somalia, destroyed much of the infrastructure, economy and legitimate institutions. After Siad Barre's government collapsed, in January 1991, the country fragmented. In 2012, a new federal government was established in Mogadishu and an African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM) force joined the Somali forces to fight the militant Al Shabaab group.

title: Help Cancer Patient-Give life
description: Tulasi Suffering with Bone cancer.She was admitted in mgcancer Hospital in Visakhapatnam.she has two little children, her husband worked as Dailywage agricultural labour.they are very poor to taking treatment in this hospital.Tulasi don't know how cancer effect her body,she don't have knowledge,lack of awareness of Cancer. This project will help, financial support to poor patients fighting with cancer.

title: Project Kenya
description: This project will help to build a structure that will have school, housing, drinking water and infirmary in Embu Kenya for poor children.

title: Send 3000 Children in Somalia to School for a year
description: FENPS runs 40 schools which host over 21,000 children (48% girls) across Somali regions. This project complements  FENPS activities, and improves access to life-saving quality education for 3000 school children from internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Somalia. The project focuses on rehabilitation and expansion of 15 schools, establishing of 48 gender responsive latrines together with provision of hygiene promotion supplies, learning and teaching materials and daily nutritious school meals.

title: Girls' Education Trust Fund
description: The Girls' Education Trust Fund will provide 30 girls with the financial resources to cover education expenditures such as tuition, textbooks, lesson fees among others. It will also help cover registration costs for external exams such as the West African Examination Council (WAEC), and Joint Admissions and Matriculations Board (JAMB).

title: Clean Water & Nutrition for 1,000 Interfaith Girls
description: Poverty, hunger, communal violence and  limited public health  plague Muslim Mindanao, Philippines. Sulu Province remains near the bottom of the UN's Human Development Index. A school-aged population of some 350,000 impoverished children -- more than half girls and 12 percent Christian -- lack clean water.  Worldwide, female students are most affected in similar schools. We will assist schools with a total of 1,000 girls, to create clean water systems, improved hygiene and daily nutrition.

title: Helping Syrian change agents get their education
description: A Project aligned with the Costa Rican foreign policy and its historical tradition as a land of asylum and refugee. A proposal based in the fundamental liberties, Human Rights, peace and democracy. A humanitarian, neutral, non for profit, apolitical and non-religious initiative working for the right to education of the Young Syrian people who have seen their studies interrupted due to the war conflict. We provide relocation, lodging and education for our students. We help them rebuild Syria

title: Challenge supports work on discard for development
description: Many people love cars while many want to make the world a better place BUT only some like Alan Braithwaite a UK based car enthusiast are able to bring these together to create Trans India Challenge.   In October 2019, Alan & his wife Pat will drive 5,600 Kms in their beloved Morgan 3 Wheeler across India to raise funds for Goonj- an internationally acclaimed India based Nonprofit for their environmentally sustainable work.

title: Provide Clean Water to 2,000 households in Kenya
description: Our goal is to raise funds to build a 250 meter- deep borehole and provide water distribution lines to support 2,000 households (approximately 10,000 people) with clean and safe water.

title: Supporting 700 IDPs in Bui Division, Cameroon
description: This project will provide basic food and hygiene management items as well as psycho-social support to 700 women, men and children displaced from their homes and villages to other  villages in Bui Division as a result of the ongoing war in the anglophone regions of Cameroon.

title: GIVE A NEEDY CHILD A LUNCH MEAL-A CUP OF PORRIDGE
description: Children from poor financial backgrounds in Uganda miss out on anything to eat at lunchtime every day, and many will have had no breakfast, and find it difficult to concentrate and gain an education. Malnutrition affects their health, development and ability to learn. This project will provide a cup of porridge and sugar for a lunchtime meal and work with some schools to establish gardens to sustain the lunch meals for needy children. This Christmas please donate a lunch meal for a needy child

title: Help LHR Continue its Vital Programming in Greece
description: Since 2016, we have provided dignified psychosocial support to people living in a prolonged state of emergency in Ritsona Refugee camp.  Offering safe spaces to gather, play, learn, and generally regain a semblance of normalcy, we endeavor to be a beacon of light and hope to children and youth who have experienced trauma and extreme hardship. Activities range from English classes to football tournaments to music workshops, based on requests from the community.

title: Eldorado Park Technology Hub
description: The project focuses on providing underprivileged youth with access to basic computer skills and access to technology. Our target is to train 3,536 youth over the course of 221 days with basic and intermediate computer literacy skills. When learners exit the programme they should be comfortable using a computer and the basic functions of Microsoft Office. Learners should be able to do basic research on the internet.

title: Dignity Kits for 1000 Female Students in Iraq
description: Supporting vulnerable female students in intermediate and high schools in IDP (Internally displaced persons) camps and rural areas. The project seeks to support 1000 female students with dignity kits and raising their awareness on hygiene and health care.  Dignity kits contain hygiene and sanitary items, as well as other items explicitly tailored towards the local needs of girls of reproductive age in particular communities. Preserving dignity is essential to maintaining self-esteem of the girls

title: Sheltering the flood affected in Kerala, India
description: 2018 Kerala floods killed 500 people, destroyed 16,000 houses and pushed a million people to the camps. Having provided relief and 300temporary shelters Project Vision will provide 25 permanent house. Government is unable to provide houses to everyone immediately. Ours houses are given to special cases like the disabled, widows and the elderly. We build 500 sq ft houses with RCC roof having two bed rooms, kitchen and hall, costing five lakhs each. 4 already handed over & rest under construction.

title: Washington-Lee High School Fighting For A Change
description: Since September 2018, Lindsey, Juliana, and Atti of Washington-Lee High School have been working with Leadership Initiatives' Orphan Care Program. Along with their translator, Tamar, they are developing solutions to improve the quality of life of the orphans who rely on the program.

title: Helping Girls and Young Women in Bujumbura Slum
description: Girls and young women bear the brunt from the conflicts in Burundi with many of them migrating to the Kamenge slum where the Ntaseka Clinic is located. They need much support. 267 women are HIV+ and there are now 128 self-help groups for 3013 women. The community needs HIV+ testing and family planning. Counseling is given to HIV+ children and to pregnant HIV+ women. House girls will also be taught to read and write and then be encouraged to  organize themselves into self-help groups.

title: REVOLVING LOAN TO EMPOWER RURAL WOMEN IN LIBERIA
description: Train and empower rural women, particularly female heads of household who are parents of our scholarship students to strengthen their income generating ability and financial situation. Over time, this will help families "graduate " from needing scholarship assistant, and open room for new students in the program. This support will provide a revolving loan between (200UD-400USD for a period of 6-12 months to 15 female heads of household to start with

title: Olive trees in Palestine in memory of Jeremy Hardy
description: The British comedian Jeremy Hardy's life was lived by the Jewish principle of tikkun olam - repairing the world. High on his repair list were the occupied and refugee Palestinians who he supported in benefit after benefit, including doing gigs for Jewish anti-occupation groups.  In the spirit of tikkun olam, our Jewish charity, the British Shalom-Salaam Trust, plans to celebrate life, renewal and hope for a just peace by planting trees in Jeremy's memory.

title: Help Rwanda's next generation of peacebuilders
description: Our goal is to consolidate peace and inclusion in Rwandan society by enhancing citizens' participation and ownership of reconciliation processes, policies and programmes.  We work with Rwandan genocide survivors, former prisoners and local partners, and address issues with deep historical roots, dealing with the impact of the genocide including trauma, social cohesion and economics.  Thanks to your support, we can continue to build Rwanda's next generation of peacebuilders.

title: Owner Of My Time (And Life!)
description: This project will provide per-hour work with dignity to 10,000 women in Peru: single mothers with children, young domestic workers and migrants from Venezuela. We will develop the First Peruvian Cleanning Internet Platform that will connect these women with per-hour work opportunities as cleanning ladies. They will receive trainning and monthly incomes over Minimum Wage, allowing them to provide for their families, look after their personal responsibilities and go for their dreams.

title: FREE OF COST THERAPEUTIC SERVICES
description: This project will build a health support centre in Bangladesh where providing therapeutic services.Persons with disabilities in Bangladesh will be benefited.By  measuring and counting to implement adequate service delivery in action on free distribution of therapeutic services.Employing more staff in the office. Also by assisting Government in social service as well.

title: Support an agribusiness run by 20 Tamil women
description: This is the second phase of this project.  The first phase gave women farmers training in sustainable organic practice.  Now we are helping 20 of these women to move their produce up the value chain by training them to create and market canned products. These products will not only net more than the sale of raw produce, but their longer shelf life allows for a more flexible response to changing conditions such as COVID restrictions, and will open up new markets.

title: Giving vulnerable  children in Nepal an education
description: Children living in poverty have no chance of a future without the opportunity that education provides.  Our program is a proven approach to developing and empowering kids in Nepal. We're currently supporting nearly sixty kids from Primary school through to Uni.   During the Covid-19 Pandemic we're also providing home schooling for 20+ Children in the IGWR Houses, and supporting a number of children and their families with essential supplies as many families now have no income.

title: Gift a non-schooling Girl with Sanitary Napkins!
description: Majority of out-of-school teenage girls trade sex-4-money to buy napkins. 834 girls will access pads in 2019.  These funds will cover production costs of $0.36 per packet: the girls will cost share @ $0.20 per packet to meet administrative costs. However, girls who wont afford $0.20 will access the napkins for free as they receive life skills training . The project will provide a source of income for at least one teenager (btwn 16-18years) to manage the project, developing to more opportunities.

title: Transform the lives of illiterate women in Liberia
description: Your donation will help to transform the lives of 810 marginalised young women who are illiterate and have little or no education.  You will help them to escape a vicious cycle of poverty. You will empower them to feed themselves and their families, send their children to school and pay for vital medicine. Your donation will do this by funding life-changing training for the young women.  They will learn how to create, develop and adapt their own business.

title: 10 Computers for School Dropouts in Manila
description: Young Focus wants to tackle computer illiteracy among school dropouts. Young Focus already has a special 'Catch-UP' center for school dropouts at the edge of a large squatter area in Tondo, Manila. We want to set up a computer room with 10 computers to give 200 children and teens an opportunity to develop their talents through educational computer programs.

title: Centro de reproduccion para futuros Perros Guia
description: With the construction of a canine maternity center for responsible reproduction, the number of dogs in the graduate guide given to blind people in Mexico and Latin America can be increased to 70%.

title: Peacebuilding through Agricultural Partnerships
description: The project fosters opportunities for Palestinians and Israelis to work together to improve cross-border agribusiness and value-chain development in the olive, date, and vegetable sectors through trainings and agriculture extension services for community farmers, farm innovators, and youth agronomists. The goal of the project is to improve conditions for economic collaboration between farmers and industry actors.

title: Kydesa Homeless Youth Initiative
description: The Initiative established four main goals to address LGBT youth homelessness: i. Create independent living housing and support for 45 LGBT homeless youth in Nakuru annually  ii. Collect data on the scope and dimension of LGBT youth homelessness in Nakuru area iii. Advocate for policies that protect LGBT youth in shelters and group homes ministry of youth affairs iv. Educate the community, policy makers and funders on the importance of addressing LGBT youth homelessness v. Provision and referral

title: Provide one classroom bench for 2 kids in Cameroon
description: This projects sets out to ameliorate access to education to pupils (04-15 years old) by providing 200 two seater benches to 400 kids  in four rural public schools in Garoua Boulai , East region, Cameroon.

title: Empower Women and Adolescent Girls of Rural India
