We will use the Care Group approach, which utilizes home-based follow-up to each mom to increase knowledge, provide greater peer and community support, and develop stronger commitments to health activities.

title: Bring Project Promise Home!
description: This project will renovate a 2-story building for daily, on-site programming. Having a space to engage our at-risk youth and provide them with mentoring, life coaching, career exploration, empowerment initiatives, cultural programs and family support services.

title: Help Nicaraguans Achieve a Professional Education
description: Help Fundacion A Jean Brugger build a center to serve our students and graduates. We have been providing university scholarships in San Juan del Sur, Nicaragua for 18 years. Over 70 young people have graduated, and 40 students currently have scholarships. Our new building will have offices for the staff and a library where students can work on their homework and do research online. A space for student meetings is envisioned, where our scholars can meet to plan their community service projects.

title: STEAM & social empowerment for Girls in Colombia
description: Geek Girls LatAm is a women-led technology community that promotes and offers opportunities where girls, youth and women in Latin America can use, appropriate and actively link with the creation of technology. GGL inspires, empowers and connects with the STEAM areas to positively transform the environment of women and contribute to the construction of a more prosperous, diverse and equitable society. Help us to bring social empowerment to 300 girls in Colombia. #SponsorAGeekGirl

title: 6,000 Kids Build a Compassion-Smart Future
description: Every day 44,000 people become refugees due to climate change, war, etc. Half are children. Incredibly, many people don't care! Creating a compassionate point-of-view toward others and stimulating kind actions by children is a clear solution. Our new kids' book inspires kindness toward newcomers, including the new kid in school, as well as immigrants, and refugees. With your help 3,000 parents, grandparents, and librarians will influence attitudes of their kids -- our future decision-makers.

title: Upcycling for young carers and visually impaired
description: We will work with young carers, and visually impaired young people and teenagers in pupil referral units within Barking and Dagenham to bring back to life old unwanted furniture which we will sell on ebay and at the local Dagenham market. The furniture will be unique and of high quality. Participants will work together to make the old new!

title: Building Resilience in Appalachia
description: This project will fund Community Food Initiatives, a non-profit in Appalachian Ohio, as we work for food justice and community resilience through building a thriving local food system.  Donations to this campaign will fund school and garden programming, food access mapping, and our Donation Station, all of which promote valuation of regionally grown or produced food.

title: Prevent Violence and Migration in Honduran Youth
description: This project will contribute to FUNADEHs work with violence prevention projects in high risk communities throughout Honduras by supporting our skill-building trainings. We give young people the opportunity to have access to formal education and other trainings so they can develop professional skills in order to get jobs or even start their own entrepeneurships. With this activities we aim to reduce gang violence inside the communities and avoid Honduran migration.

title: Help Edwin Cadena finish College and avoid poverty
description: Edwin Cadena had to attend 11 different schools because his family had no money; yet his grades earned him a government scholarship to study Computer Sciences at a leading university in Colombia.  But his weak high school math slowed him down; he has 3 semesters to go and he ran out of funds. If he does not graduate on time, he has to return the $17,500 scholarship. Please help Edwin secure the US$5,270 he needs to graduate on time, get out of poverty and become a contributing member of society.

title: Gender based violence in the Anglophone silent war
description: What began as a peaceful protest in Cameroon, in 2016, became a brutal and deadly situation for Southern Cameroonians resulting in the displacement of girls and women. Nigeria is hosting over 45,000 refugees from Southern Cameroon of which 80% are vulnerable women and children exposed to sexual violence. The turbulence of war and the desensitization of soldiers have endangered women and young girls, ages 10 years to 55 years, to sexual violence. This project intends to support 200 victims.

title: Project  Venue for Resource Centre
description: We are currently looking for a venue to relocate the program as the current one is no longer available in Tobago.  Please, join our 1 million brick campaign where every dollar goes to helping us build a venue to keep the program going to provide support to a wider group of children.    We help students with educational support, including reading programs to assist as reading is a challenge for some of the children in the program, training to help develop their social and emotional skills.

title: Empower 25 digital entrepreneurs in Vratsa
description: Vratsa Software's goal is to build an IT community which through quality education gives the people of Vratsa and the region the opportunity to have challenging and well-paid jobs in their hometowns. We've educated more than 400 people so far. As a next step we want to create a modern space to unite this digital community. It will enable the trained professionals to work together, to exchange experience, ideas and resources, as well as to attract digital nomads from Bulgaria and the world.

title: Lifeskills and values for Guatemalan youth
description: Guatemala is a developing country, which has great potential but faces great challenges in education, safety, job opportunities and irregular migration. For many young people, education is an investment that is beyond their reach. This project seeks to transform the lives of 30 low-income young people of Guatemala by instilling values, life skills and allowing them to play a constructive role in society, through Scouting. The aid will be used to pay young people's expenses in Scout activities.

title: Build a dorm for 50 street girls and mothers
description: Challenges faced by Street Youth continue to increase with the barriers brought in by the COVID-19 pandemic. Through the support of our donors via GlobalGiving, we have been able to construct a boy's dorm that has the capacity to host 60 and assist the street boys. However, the pandemic has worsened the situation for girls. Kenya reported a 40% increase in monthly teen pregnancies that includes a significant number of street girls. Our next step is to build the dorm with daycare for the girls.

title: Musical instruments for 150 children in Argentina
description: This project is aimed at the vulnerable youth populations of Buenos Aires. Many children around Buenos Aires do not have all the tools for the full development of their rights and capacities, due to the socio-economic situation and even, in many cases, not having networks family containment or to guide them in this important stage of his life.  Our challenge is to develop an innovative and inclusive orchestral and music learning program that fights against poverty, exclusion and inequality.

title: Fund a Trip Campaign
description: The Food Bank Singapore is a registered charity that aims to end food insecurity in all forms. We collect various types of food from ambient to fresh produce and even cooked food and redistribute them to member beneficiaries daily. With our service area around the whole country of Singapore, each day, we are making an average of 10 collection or delivery trips.  Fund a Trip Campaign is to encourage potential donors to not only donate food items but also to keep our vehicles on the road!

title: Southern Africa A.T Information & Advocacy Project
description: A mobile app and website database called AT-Info-Map is being implemented by SAFOD to collect and disseminate information on the availability of Assistive Technology (AT) within 10 countries in Southern Africa, to help Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) find suppliers and services of AT. Upon the expiry on Feb 28, 2019 of the 3-year funding from Google.org, we seek to sustain provision of  AT information and awareness with long-term goal of increasing access to AT and independent living for PWDs.

title: Support 500 Teen Single Mothers in Tanzania
description: This project will establish a youth vocational and resource center in Bunju Dar es Salaam, that will enable 500 teenage single mothers per year to have access to vocational training on tailoring and embroidery  as well as establishing markets and trade related networking for their products. Through the project, 500  single teenage mothers  will have the opportunity to restore their lost hope and dreams in businesses enterprises of their aspirations in accordance to their capacity and interest.

title: South Sudan's women initiative to end GBV
description: The project seeks to use a local women/girls inclusive approach to tackle the issue of women and girl rights violation(GBV) in Magwi county of South Sudan through building the capacity of native iconic women as volunteers to spearhead rights protection advocacy. The project intends to rely on capacity building of women nominated volunteers to mobilize and organize their colleagues and pave way in advancing a women led agenda using community based women situational room discussion and symposium.

title: Support 120 pediatric cancers in Danang, Vietnam
description: This project aims to provide psychological and financial support for children treated cancers in Danang Oncology Hospital. We will give gift cards for poor families in need. we will provide hats, scarves and blankets with Global Giving logo and equip playing rooms and provide craft materials, puzzles and games to children receiving therapy in the hospital. Finally, we will offer events on Children Day, Mid Autumn Festival, Christmas and Happy New Year for these disadvantage children.

title: Re-train Public School Teachers in Nigeria.
description: Bunmi Adedayo Foundation (BAF) is fixing the problem of quality education in Nigeria by retraining primary school teachers in the areas of lesson preparation, delivery, subject knowledge, teaching aids creation and school leadership. Through this intervention, each teacher accesses 6 workshops, 6 classroom-mentoring and 4 online-trainings in the same academic session. 300 teachers have benefited and BAF wants to train 750 more. 70,000 children annually access quality education because of this.

title: Education Through Sports for 400 girls in Tanzania
description: Stop inequality in education, we want Tanzanian girls to school. They are oppressed and hardly graduate from secondary schools. Through sports, health and life-skills education, 13 to 19 years old girls learn health and life-skills, increasing their self-awareness & confidence, academic performance, reduce teenage pregnancies and raise awareness of their rights. Influential community members and traditional initiation leaders are mobilized to improve girl friendliness in communities.

title: Share a table food with 25 Moldovan children.
description: Through this project we address the issue of poverty and lack of education in rural Moldova and we offer a concrete, immediate impact solution for the children suffering from hunger and who are most at risk of pre-school abandonment.

title: PROPOSAL TO COMBAT COVID - 19 IN Tamil Nadu India.
description: Five things you need to know: 1. Create Awareness among all and strictly follow the Governments instruction to combat the Corona Virus.  The fake health advice you should ignore. 2. Stay at Home, take good food, good rest & be with family in good & safe environment until further instructions from the Governments. 3. You can protect yourself by washing your hands frequently, avoiding touching your face, and avoiding close contact (1 meter or 3 feet) with people who are unwell, and as well as .

title: TeenTech: Help Teens in Poverty Carve Better Lives
description: One in three teenagers in Armenia lives in poverty. Chances of breaking the cycle of poverty in a stagnant economy are fragile. To help them secure a brighter future, TeenTech initiative teaches them a full 7-month course of web programming and design, business and soft skills, and helps them secure jobs and internships with IT companies. For only 23 dollars per week teens get skills of high demand and access the dynamic and inspiring environment of tech entrepreneurs and endless opportunities.

title: Learning by earning for DEEP impact
description: The goal of DEEP impact is to set up an African Beads & Print Crafts & 'Jua-Kali' Vocational Enterprise Training Unit (VETU) in 9 slums of Nairobi. VETU will train 480 unemployed youth in two years to reduce victimization from HIV, Drugs abuse, Child headed households grief, teen age pregnancy, school dropouts and such kinds of poverty ridden circumstances vanished their primary goal of life. The trainee will earn average $60 while learning by selling their finished product to VETU's associates.

title: SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES
description: This project involves tree planting and farm land conservation. Aiming at strengthening existing community based natural resource management committees in Blantyre District. The project will contribute to Disaster Risk reduction through environment management. The project has four key components; community mobilisation for increased participation, Tree planting, firewood saving stoves, and monitoring, coordination and supervision.

title: Help Misty Against Blood Cancer in India
description: MISTY,a baby girl of age 3.5 years who is diagnosed with blood cancer and is suffering from this deadly disease.Her elder sister Deepika thought of fighting for her when misty is diagnosed with the disease.The baby girl is suffering from high fever,stomach  ache and chest pain. Deepika found hope that her sister can live a happy and healthy life when she will be treated with advance medication which costs about $6318 (4,55,500 INR). She needs help to gift her sister a new life.  PLEASE HELP!

title: Parents and Community Sensitization Programme
description: This project will enhance, coordinate and facilitate parents and community to provide support to school management to increase enrollment and improve learning outcome.

title: IMAGINE THESE ARE YOUR CHILDREN, BE THEIR HOPE
description: According to the latest IPC analysis, from December 2018 to January 2019, a total of 15.9 million people, i.e. 53% of the population analysed are severely food insecure, despite ongoing humanitarian food assistance (HFA). This includes 17% of the population. 7.5 million people in need of nutritional assistance, including  2.9 million acutely malnourished \400,000 children under 5 suffering from life-threatening severe acute malnutrition. Sanid today fighting to help large number of children.

title: After-school Youth Empowerment In Oaxaca
description: Paz & Play is an after-school program for local public school children that arose from a community-identified need for affordable and educational after-school care. Our program provides English language immersion, environmental education, and pro-social skill support. Paz Oaxaca is opening a second Paz & Play location in a semi-rural community that has identified similar needs. We anticipate serving 12 children and are fundraising to support this new location for one academic year.

title: Save a Childs Sight and Change a Life In Rombo
description: The Rotary Club of Lisburn want to save the sight of hundreds of  the Masai people in the Rombo District of Kenya, by building a specialised Eye Clinic to offer Cataract Operations, Eye Tests and education programmes to over 80,000 people in the region.

title: Personal development to 750 disadvantages malagasy
description: Ank'Izy plans to bring personal development to 750 pupils in Madagascar. This will be done through ludic activities and also by giving support to these disadvantages children  school supplies, kit sanitary  and food.

title: Basic Medical Services for 1 Million in Ethiopia
description: Due to a limited supply of essential services, adults and especially children suffer from hunger, malnutrition and ill health.  We are working to raise funds for basic diagnostic equipment to benefit Dembi Dollo General Hospital in the Oromia region of Ethiopia - specifically, an x-ray and ultrasound machine.  This hospital serves a population of nearly 1 million in an area that has been affected by major crises including drought, displacement and armed conflict.

title: Food Rescue for Hunger, New Food Bank in Mexico
description: Alimento Para Todos (APT) is an institution with more than 24 years and has a new mission, install a food bank in Tultitlan, Estado de Mexico that allows to recover, store and dignify food and other goods to continue supporting a vulnerable population with the aim of ensuring access to food through the weekly delivery of food packages and food orientation.

title: Educate 75 adolescent girls in Liberia
description: Liberia, one of the world's least developed countries, has limited technology and few people skilled in modern information technology. Basket of Hope, Liberia will be offering computer training to students for competitive edge both in school and university study and most importantly while seeking employment. Most students skilled in computing are hired immediately upon completing the Basket of Hope Liberia course while others choose to go to college.

title: Sustainable Jobs for Trafficking Victims in India
description: This project seeks to provide sustainable employment and holistic care for women survivors of trafficking and prostitution in India. We currently have 6 women ready for employment and hope to expand our reach to 20 women by then end of 2019. These women will make fair trade products that will be sold in various parts of the world.

title: improve SRHR of 300 women in Norther state
description: The project will provide medical equipment to the delivery room in 2 villages in Northern state to reduce maternal mortality and infants rates

title: Empower 10 Refugee Families in the United States
description: This project empowers 10 low-income families that have been approved asylum in the US-Mexico Border to build their new lives with dignity and guide in their new home.  To alleviate some of the constraints these families face while waiting for their approval, such as poverty, this project will provide shelter, transportation, food assistance, and a backpack with toiletries and "Know Your Rights"bilingual guide to 10 new families receiving Asylum acceptance in the U.S.-Mexico Border.

title: A Wheelchair spot on planes
description: All Wheels Up (AWU) is funding and conducting the research needed for a wheelchair spot on planes.  AWU is crash testing wheelchair securement systems for in-cabin use and wheelchairs as airplane seats to prove the feasibility of a wheelchair spot on planes.   our humanitarian project is creating tool kits for emergency coordinators for mass evacuations of people who use wheelchairs during emergency situations.

title: Vision and quality of life for older people.
description: This project is aimed at poor patients in rural areas of the state of Morelos in Mexico, who suffer from visual diseases such as cataract, glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy, who are treated at the ACREC ophthalmological clinic, and do not have enough money to have surgery and recover their sight. With surgery, people recover their vision and improve their quality of life.

title: Reviving Pakistan's Dying Dawoodi Language
description: This project will mobilize the small community of 400 people in Pakistan's Hunza valley to revive their ancient language. They have stopped using their own language in private and public domains because of stigma attached to it. Once spoken in many villages, this Old Indic language is dying. The project will collect words and develop learning materials to teach the language to younger generations. The community elders will support organizing teaching and learning activities.

title: Lets lift 100s of families  out of poverty
description: This year, we are looking forward to your support in lifting 100s families in Pakistan out of poverty. With an average donation-based interest-free loan size of $250, you can permanently lift a poverty-stricken family with our entrepreneurship microloans. Through our 17 years of operation, Akhuwat has brought 3.3 million people irrespective of their religion, caste, and gender into socioeconomic inclusion. Learn more about how your little donation can change many lives.

title: Empower visually impaired for employment in Rwanda
description: Provide appropriate assistive devices (low techs) to 40 visually impaired youth and train them on the use of the devices including computers in Kigali City, Rwanda because most of them are unable to access them after finishing school. The devices will help them to access information for their development and use them in their daily life.

title: Educational and sport tutoring in Huejotengo.
description: A project that seeks to generate life skills for children from 6 to 12 years old; contribute in improving the performance and academic, personal and sports growth of children, because we believe that they are the actors that can change the current reality of the community.

title: Create Access to Glasses with #ReadingGlassesDay!
description: We're Celebrating Reading Glasses Day on June 7!    Reading Glasses Day (RGD) is a commemorative date dedicated to raising awareness about the lack of access to reading glasses in developing countries, and the impact that glasses have on people's lives.   Our goal is to raise $20,000 to create access to glasses for 25,000 people living in impoverished communities in Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania. Thanks to our Board, every dollar donated up to $10,000 will be matched!

title: Twentieth Youth Congress on the Environment
description: Since 1990, The Ecological Center "Los Cuartos" has promoted environmental education in favor of sustainable development.  Every year we celebrate World Environment Day with the participation of 60 girls and boys of the fifth and sixth grades, selecting those who stood out for their participation in our educational camps, giving them the opportunity to participate for 3 days in the "Twentieth Youth Congress on the Environment." Through this program, participants become environmental ambassadors.

title: Restore schools for children in Peruvian Amazon
description: This project is aimed to improve and restore the infrastructure of two schools in poor conditions located in the riverside communities of Santa Rosa and Nuevo Israel, in the Peruvian rainforest. This task will be performed through the improvement and restoration of the school's infrastructure and the delivery of school supplies and furniture. With these actions, 114 students and 6 teachers will be benefited.

title: Restore Dignity to Girls in West Nile, Uganda
description: Ever wondered what difference a five dollar donation can make in a world where there seems to be endless problems? In one small village in Uganda, it makes all the difference! Alwi sub-county is located in Pakwach district in West Nile. Because this village has water problems, girls find it difficult to take care of their menstrual hygiene. They can not afford pads, so they lose over 24 school days every year staying home during their periods to avoid humiliation. We want to change this.

title: Sport Dans La Ville
description: Sport Dans La Ville is the leading professional integration organization through sports in France. The aim of the Sport Dans La Ville program is to provide a springboard for Young people by offering support, education, guidance and help to enter the world of work.

title: Bulldog Barn - no bulldog left behind
description: Buckeye Bulldog Rescue is seeking to expand our program by opening a facility to house some of our more medically and behaviorally needy dogs while still maintaining a foster-based model.    We want to build a facility that will mimic that of a home life for dogs in our care, but have "rooms" where each dog could be separated during their stay.  There will also be private boarding in the back to help fund the building for future, continued use.

title: HELP EMPOWER 100 DISADVANTAGED GIRLS IN KENYA
description: We are out to empower young disadvantaged girls between ages 12 to 20.  Specifically the girl called a house girl who perhaps never went to school or dropped out or orphaned.  This girl has no formal qualification other than primary and the only job available for her is  from anyone offering house work.  They are often abused and exploited by their employers.  We will empower them with life and technical skills.  Will turn them into future employers through entrepreneurship ventures & mind shift

title: Help 5 NYC Kids Attend Camp!
description: With summer around the corner, we want to help give five children living in poverty the opportunity to attend our beautiful Wagon Road Camp in Chappaqua, New York. These five lucky children will be able to combat summer learning loss through our fun educational projects, and get plenty of exercise in our swimming pool, ropes course, and other exciting activities.

title: Educate and Treat the Invisible Children of Haiti
description: Haitian children with disabilities have little hope of accessing the specialized healthcare and education they need. But ever since Sebastien's mother started bringing him to Pazapa, he's found his stride with a little help from Juliet (pictured), who can often be found at his side during her recess in Pazapa's School for the Deaf. With your support, Pazapa can reach 25 more children like Sebastien and Juliet, who have nowhere else to go for disability-inclusive education and healthcare.

title: Poverty Reduction In Africa Through Empowerment
description: The aim of this project is to fight poverty among rural African children through provision of soft loan assistance to their families to start small scale business while educating the rural kids on importance of financial literacy. 25 homes of rural children have been selected to get soft loan of 1000 each home to support this vision

title: Help Deaf Children learn to read and write
description: DID YOU KNOW that deaf children make up an illiterate and excluded population? In Argentina, Spanish is their second language, but there are no materials for them to learn how to to read and write. To prevent school desertion and to match their opportunities to access culture, we will elaborate a textbook for deaf children to become literate. Literacy is a gateway to the world.

title: Fund eBooks for Global Theological Education
description: The Open Access Digital Theological Library (OADTL) is the world's largest provider of free access to high quality digital books for students and researchers in religious studies. Each 43 cents you donate results in one book being added to our freely accessible global collection. The OADTL never charges its readers for access to books or journal articles. Please help students around the world to have access to high quality religious studies books in multiple languages. Thanks!

title: Educate Children At Yucubka Village in Hiiran
description: Education plays vital role on lifting up crisis and conflict affected populations. Bulay Development Organization (BUDO) supports vulnerable children at Yucubka village in Hiiran region of Somalia. The project will affect 250 school age children (120 girls and 130 boys) through rehabilitation and re-establishment of 8 classrooms, distribution of learning and teaching materials, and also construction of 6 gender responsive toilets with hygiene supplies and hands wash kits.

title: Open doors for people with autism
description: In 2018 Canisha launched a training program for autism assistance dogs and since then demand for this type of assistance dogs has skyrocketed. Autism assistance dogs reduce stress and panick attacks in indivuals with autism, they bring structure and confidence into their lives, the confidence to go out into the world and they are a reliable buddy who does not need speech to connect. These dogs do not only open doors literally but also, and most importantly, figuratively.

title: Incubation for 35 start up entrepreneurs in Malawi
description: 90% of small and medium enterprises in Africa face challenges due to lack of business development support leading to stagnant growth or failure.  Mzuzu E-hub developed the Bizcubation program to support 35 start up enterprises with three months capacity building workshops, access to office space, and three months implementation support through mentorship, investment support and expert coaching.

title: Bring Anti-Nukes Abolitionists from Africa to UN
description: Africa is the most unprepared for a nuclear war. Africa is dependent on aide-mostly from states that would be involved in a nuclear war. Nuclear winter would destroy crops and raise the price of food.  The rate of cancers would dramatically increase. Africa would never recover.  To address this scourge, medical students from Ethiopia, Kenya, Zambia, and Nigeria are coming to NYC for an anti-nuke conference and youth forum in April. Once they return, they will develop advocacy plans.

title: STEM  through Art, Dance and Theater- Summer camp
description: This is the summer camp project.   AJ Trust runs three camps in a year.   Summer camp is a major event.  Each year the Trust works with a theme, to simulate thinking and decision making capacity.   All camps involve formal lectures,  activities to enhance cognitive, kinesthetic and social skills.   During this summer the theme is about Kaadu - meaning the forest.   The participants are from a tribal village surrounded by small hillocks and forests.   The theme is in their honour.

title: Empowering Environmental Education in 14 schools
description: This project aims to ensure in perpetuity the conservation of the Volcanoes National Park  rich biodiversity resources include threatened mountain gorillas through strengthening of environmental outreach education programs in schools. The project will be implemented in 2 to 3 pilot Schools of each of Musanze, Burera, Nyabihu and Rubavu Districts. The project will assist in creation of environmental awareness through school outreach programs.

title: Menstrual health program for 1,000 girls in Uganda
description: Girl Power Gulu addresses menstrual health barriers for young girls in northern Uganda by giving them feminine hygiene products and educational courses on reproductive health. This program provides women with knowledge of menstruation and safe sex, empowering them to stay in school and advancing the well-being of families and communities.

title: Support for 40 orphans and school maintenance
description: Happy Totos Foundation is seeking support to help acheive quality education and health for our orphans and students. The school was established in 2014 to offer primary level education for our children and community.  We are in need of completing our well to provide clean water and purchase of scholastic supplies like computers, reading and other teaching materials . We also have ongoing needs for the orphans in our care who require food, clothing, bedding and medical care.

title: Winona Senior High School Fighting For A Change
description: Jade, Katherine, Anissa, Lance, Zaid, and Grace are students from Winona Senior High School who are part of the International Business Internship Program, or IBIP for short. IBIP is a program that combines high school students with community leaders located world wide. We are all new members to the program and enjoy being partnered with an Orphan Care Program in Nigeria to help better their facilities and the lives of the kids there by fundraising here in Winona.

title: Toilets for 80 rural children - Eastern Cape
description: This project will build a brick structure to house  3 Solar toilets, 3 urinals and 3 hand basins at Ncinci One's Montessori in the rural Eastern Cape, South Africa.  The toilets are for the 80 young, rural Xhosa children who use our education facility on a daily basis.  We have 30 young children attending Ncinci Ones Montessori in the morning and we have 50 children in Grades 1 - 3 attending the Siyafunda After School program.   A safe toilet should be a right for a child, not a luxury!

title: Improving the lives of Carriage Horses in Jakarta
description: Since its founding in 2008 JAAN started to help the carriage horses working in Jakarta's heat and busy traffic. The carriage horses' are pushed over their limits with little or no medical care provided. Often the owners and handlers don't have much knowledge about horse care and the carriage horses are literally worked to their very early death, when normally with better care,  horses can reach a very old age.  Horses are not provided the correct food or rest areas.

title: Support very vulnerable MIGRANT WOMEN in Bulgaria
description: This project will support migrant women who have numerous vulnerabilities that need to be addressed such as health issues, being single parents, the risk of trafficking and exploitation, limited access to the labour market due to residency status, childcare responsibility, etc.  CLA Voice in Bulgaria will provide legal aid and it will play a significant role of a mediator between the different stakeholders that should be engaged in supporting vulnerable women or victims of violence in Bulgaria.

title: Financial Education for underprivileged children
description: "Save and start", is a program of social, financial and entrepreneurship education for girls, boys and young people of limited resources between 6 to 18 years of age. EDUCA, through this program, promotes creativity, leadership and entrepreneurship in them through the development of skills that allow them to improve their quality of life and their community.

title: Repairs to Hogares Teresa Toda post H. Maria in PR
description: Hurricane Maria literally shredded our town of Loiza, Puerto Rico and our project facilities sustained serious damages.  Currently we are still in need of sealing roof where residents dorm, replace main entrance doors, paint interior of all facilities and build a cement hanger to protect our passenger vans used to transport our residents to and from schools, doctor's appointments and other vital services. In addition, a new fire alarm system must be installed for residential units.

title: Sanitation and Hygiene for 250 Mexican children
description: This project will repair and refurbish 2 bathrooms (one for girls and another for boys with 5 stalls each). This implies purchasing a water tank, 6 toilets, 3 dry urinals, 6 hand basins, and 10 stalls, in addition to tiles on walls and installation costs. The bathroom will be used by an average of 250 students each year who use our education facility on a daily basis. Hygiene should not be a privilege but is rather a basic part of education!

title: Provide School Lunch for Tacloban Kids Yearly
description: We prepare packed lunches for 30 poor kids in Tacloban City during the school year. These lunches consist of fortified rice, meat, vegetable, and fruit. we call this project #ProjectBaon. "Baon" is a Filipino word for meals prepared by parents for their kids to bring to school. The meals not only provide nutrition but also allow the children to keep their minds focused on their studies rather than their tummies. Full kids stay in school and do better in school according to studies.

title: #ProjectBaon: Sitio Dumpsite, Antipolo
description: "Baon" is a Filipino word for packed meals prepared by parents for their kids to bring to school. Sadly, 10 out of 30 kids in the Philippines don't get the food they need every day. Since learning depends on good nutrition, these kids may never reach the same potential for learning as well-nourished kids. #ProjectBaon will ensure the provision of healthy meals to malnourished kids living in Sitio Dumpsite.

title: Comic Book for Cervical Cancer Prevention in LMICs
description: Although cervical cancer is preventable, it remains a leading cause of death worldwide, with 90% of deaths occurring in low & middle income countries (LMICs). This unequal burden is due, in part, to lack of education about cervical cancer, its causes and means of preventing it, including the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine. GO's comic book dispels myths & misconceptions associated with all cancers and teaches readers of all ages the importance of getting vaccinated to prevent cervical cancer.

title: Train up 10 refugee aid projects for better impact
description: Campfire Innovation is helping the helpers. We bring visibility to the work of passionate and innovative people helping refugees in Greece. We mapped 100+ teams across Greece serving 5000+ refugees. For them, we created the Impact Platform: an easy online tool to track their impact. We provide it for free along with free training and ongoing support.  You can help us train 10 inspiring groups on how to tell the story of their impact and meaningful work through data and connect to supporters.

title: #ProjectBaon: Trento, Agusan Del Sur
description: "Baon" is a Filipino word for packed meals prepared by parents for their kids to bring to school. Sadly, 10 out of 30 kids in the Philippines don't get the food they need every day. Since learning depends on good nutrition, these kids may never reach the same potential for learning as well-nourished kids. #ProjectBaon will ensure the provision of healthy baon to malnourished kids living in Trento.

title: Provide school supplies to 2000 Liberian students
description: This project will help 2,000 students in Liberia start the school year with the supplies every child needs. Recipients will display academic excellence (with average grades of 90% and above) and are drawn from grades one to six. Students will be provided with a school bag, school supplies for the year, and a $20 USD stipend to purchase school uniforms.

title: Horse Sanctuary
description: The goal of the Horse Sanctuary is two fold: Firstly, in the short-term, we want to create an environment where the horses can live happy, fulfilling lives through the construction of a stable, riding grounds, and a pasture. Secondly, our long-term goal is to create a foundation to promote better care for horses and natural horsemanship so that other horses in Moldova will not find themselves being sent off to the slaughterhouse, like what had almost happened to our four horses.

title: Sponsor Runners to Help Orphans in Japan
description: Traveling from Tokyo to Fukushima on a Shinkansen at the speed of 270-300 km/h takes 85 minutes. It is also incredibly convenient and relaxing. Now, imagine running that 300 km (Not an easy feat). And compare that to going to university without computers (Again, not an easy feat). In 21st Century Japan, it's normal for kids to have computers. However, thousands of kids in Japan in institutionalized homes struggle to prepare for life outside these homes once reaching the age of 18.

title: Drug Assistance for Internally Displaced People
description: The serious political crisis in Cameroon has resulted in internally displaced English speaking Cameroonians who are now in very remote, rural areas/forests where there are many mosquitoes, resulting in many malaria cases and other illnesses, but no health care facility. RECEADIT needs financial assistance to: 1) employ ten RECEADIT female nurse; 2) purchase more needed drugs; 3) help transport these drugs & nurses; and 4) pay their salaries to travel 70 miles in bushes to provide health care.

title: Hurricane Michael 10 Houses to Build in 2019
description: This program will build and repair houses for families who lost everything as a result of Hurricane Michael. The program will support the long term recovery for 10 households in economically disenfranchised communities of Florida's Panhandle. HHDR will utilize your donations, volunteer labor, and community partnerships to provide these otherwise forgotten survivors with the resources need to rebuild their homes.

title: #ProjectBaon: Plainview Elementary School
description: "Baon" is a Filipino word for packed meals prepared by parents for their kids to bring to school. Sadly, 10 out of 30 kids in the Philippines don't get the food they need every day. Since learning depends on good nutrition, these kids may never reach the same potential for learning as well-nourished kids. #ProjectBaon will ensure the provision of healthy baon to malnourished kids at Plainview Elementary School, Mandaluyong City.

title: Stop the Smoke -  Reduce Global Warming
description: For 4 years, this project has taught small-holder farmers to make biochar, cutting greenhouse gas and PM2.5 emissions. It has trained 3,000 in Thailand and 7,000 in Africa who have made thousands of tonnes of biochar that they sell or use to restore soil, mitigate climate change and increase yields. Stop the Smoke! works in N. Thailand (that has among the worst air quality in the world) and Africa, but the project model can raise public health and food security, and slow climate change globally.

title: Skill 260 rural Indian women to be self-reliant
description: The Jagruti program of Light of Life Trust is focused on providing a sustainable livelihood to 260 women from Murbad Village in Thane district of Maharashtra. The program is equipping underprivileged women and girls to develop creative skills like Sewing, Beauty Training which can be used to generate money from sale of the products created and services rendered. Once earning, they can supplement the house hold income and become providers for the family.

title: Unused schools into Community Development Centers
description: Over 300 schools were closed in Puerto Rico leaving 27,000 students without a classroom and over 2,000 teachers without a job. It is our intention to acquire 6 of those unused schools and turn them into Community Development Centers with the firm purpose of helping communities to develop, the leader to grow and the individual to empower themselves. Developing educational projects, promoting self-management, social welfare and a robust, diverse and fair economic development.

title: City Year Inc.
description: City Year unites young people (ages 17-24) of all backgrounds for a year of full-time service to help students succeed in school and stay on-track to high school graduation. As tutors, mentors and role models, City Year's diverse leaders - corps members - are deployed in teams to work in low-income urban communities, transforming schools and neighborhoods and making a difference in the lives of underserved children.

title: Aussie Wildlife Recovery & Emergency Preparedness
description: This project will assist in the ongoing recovery of habitat and support for wildlife after emergency weather events. Bushfires and flooding destroy habitat and food sources. In the 2020 bushfires alone an estimated 3 billion native animals were lost. Additionally this project will assist WIRES in developing systems and capacity to respond to future large scale events such as the 2022 flood disaster.

title: HELP SAVE THE LITTLE HEARTS OF MEXICO
description: We fundraise so that every Mexican child, gets the best surgical heart treatment and attention. We do this by supporting a group of outstanding  doctors in an innovative  hybrid model combining  efforts of the  public and  private sector.  This allows us to increase  the number  of children we can help  while improving  the quality of each  surgery. Kardias provides the highest  quality of  treatment for Mexican children with congenital heart defects.

title: College Building Construction Fund
description: To raise funds for construction of a new college building for underprivileged children at Malikpur.

title: Lebanese Educators Helping Vulnerable Students
description: Teach For Lebanon (TFL) is a Lebanese NGO working to ensure that all children in Lebanon, regardless of socioeconomic background, have equal access to excellent education. Our core project is the TFL Fellowship. Under this project, we recruit and train qualified, motivated university graduates and young professionals, our fellows, and place them in underprivileged school communities to serve as teachers for two years.

title: Clean Water for Dominican & Kenyan Communities
description: Partnering with our local heroes who lead Project Hearts in the Dominican Republic and the Watha Project in Kenya, GRACE Cares will bring greater Water Access, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) to under-served communities. This initiative will drastically improve the health and quality of life for the people of the Baitoa region in the Dominican Republic and the members of the Watha tribe in the Galana region of Kenya.

title: Promote art classes for 150children at social risk
description: Mensajeros de la Paz creates opportunities for children from at-risk areas in Argentina, where poverty surrounds every aspect of their lives. Through art classes, family groups can express themselves, connect, and solve problem situations. The classes will include: dance lessons and music workshops (teaching to play instruments).

title: Prevent Youth Suicides In Japan
description: This project aims to train 60 crisis lifeline support workers over the next 12 months and provide more support during the 2020 Olympics. Youth suicides in Japan increased by almost 6% last year, with the leading cause being school issues, such as bullying. Your donation will help change lives by allowing more youth in crisis access support when they need it, helping vulnerable kids to reach their full potential. Saving lives takes a community working together, will you help be a part of ours?

title: Love of the Game
description: Save the Player, Save the Game.  We, the "Love of the Game" team, are working to protect the sports we love by protecting our players. We are searching for positive solutions to prevent, diagnose and treat head injuries, concussion and related problems through Science, Technology and Innovation.  We do this to:  Reduce risks to players   Maintain sports as we know them  Reduce fear of taking part  Speed return to play after injury  Lengthen sporting careers

title: #Start_a_chance for 60 special needs children
description: This project will deliver a new purpose-built Lonwabo Special Care Day Centre for 60 children in Mfuleni, near Cape Town.  The centre will form part of an integrated campus development to promote inclusivity and create opportunity for these children to flourish and develop optimally. There is an urgent need to complete the new centre because the existing facility is threatened by closure.

title: Hydrotherapy Pool for Youth with Special Needs
description: Hydrotherapy promotes physical well-being and joy for children with special needs! Help us build the first warm water, fully accessible pool in northern Moldova to provide free hydrotherapy to disabled youth and swimming lessons to poor students.

title: New School Kitchen and Meals for 100 Eswatini Kids
description: Eswatini is a lower middle-income country & 63% of Swazis live below the poverty line. Education is the ladder of poverty alleviation and we hope to see Eswatini children have a good learning and developing in schools. A healthy school environment will help children succeed in schools. However, most of school kitchens are old in Eswatini which need to be renovated or re-built. TFCF kitchen will deliver healthy school meals to Eswatini children and benefit for children growth and development.

title: Support access to justice in South Africa
description: Lawyers for Human Rights has been providing free legal services to individuals & communities in South Africa for 40 years. Celebrate our 40 year anniversary with us by donating to ensure we can continue to facilitate access to justice through legal advice and representation, and the development of young black lawyers from the communities we serve.  Support LHR to bridge the gap between rights and reality, to Make Rights Real.

title: Gender Equality for at-risk Kids in Costa Rica
description: This project will encourage and guide 200 kids, in the urban vulnerable community of Carpio in San Jose, Costa Rica, to deconstruct stereotyped gender roles and rebuild their perceptions of male and female to promote gender equality and a coexistence free of gender-based violence among them, their families and their community.

title: #MathFor3Million
description: Our goal is to reach out to 3 million children from marginalised backgrounds studying in public schools of Karnataka, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh in India over the next three years. And we need your support! This campaign will help us provide quality math learning to about 14000 elementary grade children studying in 1400 public schools while enabling the teachers and empowering the local communities around it. Be our partner in making math experience joyful to our children.

title: Bikes and Books For 100 Vulnerable Girls
description: We are giving books and bikes to vulnerable girls who live in rural and poor villages in Kilwa Tanzania to help them get better education. Many young girls walk hours one way to school, and these long distances often keep them from attending regularly. Safety is another reason to give young girls bikes, as they are very often the targets of human trafficking, rape, sex trade and sweatshops. Bicycles and books are the first simple answer to improving both their safety and access to education.

title: Temporary Shelter for Hurricane Florence survivors
description: Lutheran Services Carolinas (LSC) will provide temporary housing assistance to  vulnerable Hurricane Florence survivors, including those who are elderly, disabled, and low-income, who have been displaced from their homes because of the widespread flooding caused by the storm.

title: food baskets distribution for refugees in Athens
description: To feed about 2500 families every day for 30 days (starting from may/1/2019). We aim to reach some of the most vulnerable families, particularly families that are deprived of decent housing and as such are forced to live in informal squats and refugee camps.

title: Building Organizational Resilience
description: After hurricanes Irma and Maria hit Puerto Rico in 2017, Jovenes de Puerto Rico en Riesgo, Inc. (Puerto Rico Youth at Risk, Inc.) has worked non-stop to reestablish the prevention programs that distinguish our organization. Our committed staff, volunteers and supporters enabled this recovery. Our focus now is to continue building our capacity to recover from financial and organizational devastation caused by the hurricane's impact and to respond effectively to future catastrophic events.

title: Cyclone Idai in Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi
description: Cyclone Idai just hit Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi, causing widespread destruction, flooding, and displacement. Local ActionAid offices and community partners are coordinating immediate relief, including supplies like food, fuel, hygiene kits, and school books.

title: Cyclone and Flood Recovery in Malawi
description: Catastrophic rains and floods caused by Cyclone Idai killed at least 50 and displaced hundreds of thousands of people in Malawi.  Partners In Health is working to rebuild homes, deploy mobile clinics, and ensure families are safe, housed, and fed in the rural Neno district--where we have worked in partnership with the government providing high-quality health care since 2007.

title: CYCLONE IDAI- MOZAMBIQUE
description: The Cyclone Idai began as a tropical depression in the Mozambique channel on 4 March, dropping heavy rain over Mozambique and Malawi before heading back eastward in the direction of Beira, by which time it had become a cyclone.  This in known as the worst weather-related disaster to hit the southern hemisphere, and the UN says more than 2 million people have been affected whereas 1 000 people may be at risk of death. The Storm-surge floods of up to six metres have caused widespread devastation.

title: Allow 20 Thai students to learn English for a year
description: Our charity provides English education to over 800 students at two government schools in Phuket. In order for these children to receive a free English education, we must raise funds to pay for their fully qualified, fluent English speaking teachers.  The amount we are currently fundraising for will provide 20 underprivileged Thai students with an entire year of English education by covering a portion of the teacher's salary and the cost of class equipment and materials.

title: Improve Basic Education for 500 Zambian Children
description: The Community school of Katulumba, in the underprivileged Fishing Camp compound of Siavonga, Zambia, has 3 classrooms and 8 latrines for 500 students; Guardavanti plans to build 4 more classrooms and 18 more latrines, allowing proper education and improving sanitary conditions of attending students. Moreover, the school will be able to accept all the kids of the compound currently excluded from schooling due to lack of space. The funds requested cover the first half of the project's structures.

title: Cyclone Idai damage in Zimbabwe
description: The Damage from Cyclone IDAI in Zimbabwe Summary The violent Cyclone Idai has been and is now dissipating but it has left a trail of destruction and devastation. People all over the Province of Manicaland Zimbabwe have suffered heavy losses, in terms of property, livestock, homesteads including human life and are now struggling to recover and rebuild. This project aims to assist the reconstruction and rehabilitation of a village that has been devastated by the cyclone.

title: Cyclone Eloise Emergency Response
description: In the early morning of January 23rd, Cyclone Eloise made landfall in Mozambique early with winds of up to 140km/h and intense rain. The IsraAID Mozambique team is continuing to assess the situation, whilst planning to install water filters, distribute PPE, and provide other essential non-food items.

title: Cyclone Idai Relief Fund
description: Intense Tropical Cyclone Idai was one of the most powerful storms to ever hit southern Africa, killing more than 1,000 people and leading hundreds of thousands more to flee their homes. This fund will provide immediate relief to people impacted by the storm in addition to longer-term recovery assistance. All donations to this fund will exclusively support disaster relief and recovery efforts in Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Malawi.

title: Rebuild New Bern
description: In September 2018 Hurricane Florence struck New Bern, North Carolina, with that deadly confluence of hurricane storm surge and rainwater flooding. The result was literally thousands of homes flooded and made unlivable. Most of these homeowners were without flood insurance. And many are low-income and lack the wherewithal to rebuild themselves. Fuller Center Disaster ReBuilders is committed to restoring the homes of those with no other alternative. We do this with volunteer labor and donations.

title: Help 500 families in Zim affected by Cyclone Idai
description: Manicaland and Masvingo provinces of Zimbabwe hit by Tropical Cyclone Idai have faced massive destruction of infrastructure, property and loss of lives with an estimated 12 500 to 15 000 people affected and over 300 losing their lives. HOCIC project's main focus is Education Assistance to households and schools affected by the Cyclone. The project is mobilising school furniture, textbooks, writing books, pens, pencils, bags, uniforms, sanitary wear and other essentials for the affected children

title: Emergency Fuel for Mozambique
description: Cyclone Idai made landfall in Mozambique on March 15th, bringing strong winds, torrential rains, widespread flooding, and massive destruction. Several hundred people are confirmed dead while hundreds more remain missing. Scenes from the ground show extreme devastation and whole towns submerged under water. With the power grid down, millions of people are suffering. FRF will provide free fuel to those in need, as well as to hospitals, water treatment plants, first responder vehicles & equipment.

title: Empower 350 Girls In Coding and Robotics In Ghana
description: The project will train young girls from slum communities of Ghana to develop problem-solving skills through coding and robotics to empower them to facilitate technology creation to generate opportunities for societal transformation and poverty alleviation.

title: Disaster Relief for Zimbabwe after Cyclone Idai
description: Zimbabwe has been hit by an intense Tropical Cyclone. Idai, Regarded as one of the worst tropical cyclones on record to affect Africa and the Southern Hemisphere as a whole. The storm has caused catastrophic damage over Zimbabwe and its people, with the death toll rising, they are in dire need of support.

title: Radio-lights needed for Idai & Kenneth survivors
description: Communication is aid. Cyclone Idai, the worst storm to ever hit the Southern Hemisphere, left a trail of destruction across Mozambique, Zimbabwe & Malawi, killing an 1,000 & displacing tens of thousands. 6 weeks later Kenneth, another category 4 cyclone lashed northern Mozambique. This is unprecedented. Survivors depend on radio to deliver updates on where to get aid, to find missing loved ones, the latest health bulletins, weather info, etc. World Vision is our local distribution partner.

title: Help Concern Respond to Cyclone Idai
description: Cyclone Idai has caused severe flooding in Malawi, Mozambique, and Zimbabwe. Concern Worldwide is already on the ground in Malawi, where the floods have affected more than 900,000 people, leaving over 125,000 people homeless. The Malawian government declared a State of National Disaster on March 8, and the displaced are scattered across 173 makeshift camps. Concern is initially responding by providing essential items to the displaced, with plans to carry out shelter and hygiene activities.

title: Turning houses into homes
description: We endeavor to provide, those individuals and families who have been adversely affected by life's circumstances, with furniture that they need to build or rebuild their lives. We hope to provide the clients with the basic living furnishings and fittings needed to make their house into a home. This is currently being accomplished with donated furniture however we hope to be able to purchase new modestly priced appointments.

title: Furniture Replenishment after Hurricane Florence
description: Carteret Warriors for Recovery helps victims of Hurricane Florence in Eastern North Carolina recover by providing furnishings, such as mattress sets, dining tables, living room furniture and dressers, and linens and housewares.  Many of our families have used all their resources either repairing their homes or finding a new place to live.  Many of our clients were also out of work for weeks or months due to hurricane damage and are low on finances due to this set back.

title: Help People in Myanmar Protect Vulnerable Forests
description: Farmers with secure land rights are better able to take care of their land and respond to the impacts of climate change. In Myanmar, Landesa is working with local communities to promote Community Forest Certificates, which legalize a way of life local people have been practicing for generations: farming among the trees. Besides giving families rights to farm and live in the forests, CFC's also gives community members responsibilities for caring for this important natural area.

title: Rebuilding 478 lives in Eastern North Carolina
description: This project will help two-fold: 1) restore 100 low income families, in eastern North Carolina, whose lives were devastated by Hurricane Florence by supporting relocation expenses including basic needs items, 2) aid in replenishing two elementary school libraries with books and media equipment, in Eastern North Carolina, that were submerged by the hurricane's flood waters.

title: Advancing Girls' Education in Afghanistan 2.0
description: The draconian suppression of women's rights and freedoms since the Taliban seized power in August 2021, has led to a dramatic decline in the wellbeing and life chances of Afghanistan's women and girls. The government is systematically erasing women and girls from public life. Because of that, 80% of school-aged Afghan girls and young women are out of school (UNESCO 2023) and restricting women from working can result in an economic loss of up to five percent of the country GDP. (UNDP2022)

title: Rebuild 6 Hurricane Florence Damaged Homes
description: Wilmington Area Rebuilding Ministry (WARM) plans to help six low-income homeowners rebuild and recover from Hurricane Florence damage. Utilizing volunteer labor and matching funds, we will repair and replace roofs, windows, doors, siding, and any other repairs needed to make the home stronger and sager than before.

title: Cyclone Idai and Kenneth Children's Relief Fund
description: The children of Mozambique are facing unimaginable circumstances. After two historic cyclones, Cyclone Idai and Cyclone Kenneth, have devastated the already vulnerable country, families are without shelter and in desperate need of food and clean water. Save the Children will scale up our existing response to support emergency relief efforts across Mozambique, as well as Malawi and Zimbabwe.

title: Creating a more resilient environment on St. Croix
description: From the mesmerizing corals and sea turtles in the underwater world, to the land dwelling St. Croix Ground Lizard and Eggers Agave that are both endangered and endemic to St. Croix, to the hundreds of resident and migratory birds that take to our skies, SEA is committed to preserving the island's natural environment for the health of all of its inhabitants. Through education, conservation and advocacy, our goal is to create a more resilient environment.

title: In Memory of Sachiko "Jackie" Wall
description: When My Mom passed away, I wanted to do something to honor her memory. My Mom never had much money. But she was always rich in love & gave anything she had away freely, never expecting anything in return. I thought that helping the kids supported by YouMeWe their future would be the perfect way!

title: Alleviate the plight of Cyclone Idai Survivors
description: This project seeks to support over 13 000 women and girls in Chimanimani area of Zimbabwe that was hard hit by the Tropical Cyclone Idai which left them homeless and vulnerable by providing them with hygiene and sanitary wear.

title: Change the lives of homeless people in Mexico City
description: Mi Valedor is Mexico's first street paper generating a legitimate income for homeless and at-risk populations, following in the footsteps of the UK's 'The Big Issue'. The magazine works as a social tool to facilitate access to opportunities. At the Creative Center, we offer a variety of workshops for the vendors, which focus on recovering the self esteem and social skills that are often a symptom of social exclusion. Through these workshops, the vendors contribute to the editorial content.

title: Educating The Marginalized Child
description: We at The Cecil & Iris Chaudhry Foundation (CICF) strongly believe in the power of education. It is our conviction that education is one of the best defenses against exploitation and oppression. It is this belief that compelled us to establish The Youhanabad Education Center. The Center is providing quality education and coaching to underprivileged children whose families are barely able to survive on a daily basis.

title: Promoting Paediatric Pain Management
description: There are few things more distressing to witness than a child suffering from unrelieved pain. Medicines that reduce and relieve pain in children are available but few doctors are skilled in prescribing them. As a result, millions of children diagnosed with serious illnesses suffer needlessly. Their pain is under-assessed and inadequately treated. This project aims to raise awareness of the need for assessing a child's pain and upskill medical professionals to provide appropriate treatment.

title: Technology for Learning
description: Electricity, the internet, projectors and smartphones have created new and exciting opportunities to improve students' learning, but rural schools in Kenya and Uganda struggle to use these tools due to a lack of facilities, resources and training. This project will help EPAfrica's partner schools level the playing field through investment in e-learning, projectors, the internet, computers and solar power, and by supporting teachers with capacity building and training.

title: Provide a Year of Medicine to 50 Virgin Islanders
description: This project helps those with chronic illnesses in the US Virgin Islands which are still in recovery from the unprecedented 2017 hurricanes. Medical infrastructure remains compromised, so it is critical to keep islanders at the lowest level of care for their chronic health issues. Compliance with prescribed medications is an essential part of community health. No person should have to choose between basic needs like food and shelter and the medication they need to stay healthy and productive.

title: Movement for conserving bees in the Western Ghats
description: Bees pollinate 16% of the total 250000 flowering plants species known so far. One-third of the human diet is said to be derived from products of bee pollination. About 90% of the world's plant food production is mainly based on 82 products derived majorly from only 63 plant species. The importance of bees can be realized from the fact that for 39 of these plant species bees are major pollinators.  This campaign aims to conserve both - The species and the economics associated with it!

title: Revitalizing Children's Activities
description: This project will support interim and ongoing activities for our children, as well as transportation to and from activities on our small islands, and start-up of a new interim local facility and a Bookmobile.  These are needed because all public facilities in Coral Bay available before the storms for activities were completely destroyed in Hurricane Irma, as were the basketball court, and parks and open space vegetation. Physical restoration is beginning and will take years.

title: Provide meals in Mozambique following Cyclone Idai
description: In response to the devastation caused by Cyclone Idai, World Central Kitchen has activated #ChefsForMozambique to provide thousands of meals a day to support and empower the local community on its long road to recovery.

title: Mission: University
description: At the Good Shepherd Agricultural Mission, a large children's home in north India, our goal is to enroll all of our ambitious 12th class graduates in top colleges. The Mission: University program is into its fourth year and will soon have 25 participating students working hard in a variety of challenging disciplines. We invite all supporters who know and love these kids already, or those just looking to make a real world impact, to help us give them this life-changing opportunity.

title: PLAY International
description: PLAY International is a pioneer among organizations using sport as a tool for education and social change. The NGO developed initiatives in over 20 countries, creating ways for children to learn, be included or overcome a trauma through sports play.

title: 100 Children Develop Artistic & Sports Skills
description: In memory of Hector Rivas who dedicated his life to work with children and last year dies because of violence. Project seeks that 100 Salvadoran children of low income & who are in social risk develop their creative, artistic, cultural, sports and human skills allowing them to be resilient in the face of the scourge of violence that affects children and young. Training is complementary to their formal education and seeks to motivate them to remain within the educational system or to be rejoining

title: Build a School Cafeteria & Kitchen in Nicaragua
description: Providing nutritious lunch is an important feature of Escuela Adelante. For some students, this may be the most nutrition they get all day. We currently make do with the small kitchen that was already on-site when we moved, but it's far from adequate for our expanding student body.  The learning kitchen and garden will help Escuela Adelante impart food education and environmental education through project-based learning. The students take part in growing, harvesting, and preparing food.

title: Support A No Kill Shelter
description: The Humane Society of Dallas is the sole no-kill animal shelter in Dallas County.  We do not euthanize for space or for easily treatable illnesses as is the practice of other Dallas shelters.  We are a strictly non-profit organization so our funds come only from donations and other charitable contributions.  However, donations are down this season and the Humane Society of Dallas cannot do what we are most passionate about: animals, without your help!

title: Finance Microloans to Empower Women in Uganda
description: This program will fund a self-sustaining microloan program that provides microloans and business skills training to women recovering from a brutal, 20-year insurgency in northern Uganda. Our clients receive small loans, typically between $50 and $150, which they invest in livestock, agricultural projects, and other small business ventures. Nearly 95% of loans are fully repaid at the end of each 3-month loan cycle. Our mission is to empower women to walk their way out of poverty with dignity.

title: Provide Sanitary Pads to Women and Girls in Uganda
description: Our Healthy Periods Initiative (HPI) aims to address the many obstacles faced by young girls in northern Uganda with regards to menstrual health. We manufacture sanitary pads which are distributed to school girls, refugees, and throughout the community. Our program hopes to mitigate the challenges of proper hygiene, access to information, and negative stigma while providing employment opportunities to young single mothers through our small social enterprise.

title: Integrated Water Resources Management IWRM
description: IWRM project will be able to supply 50 smallholder families with drinking water: 1. 1 water user committee will establishe at the project site which ensure that the rainwater collection systems are managed sustainably.  2. Trainings of 50 families in maintenance.The expected effect is that the population commits themselves in repairing the cisterns and improving the health situation. For this purpose 50 water filters will be provided.  3. one cistern will be rehabilitated.

title: NYC Green Maps + Climate Action
description: Green Map NYC published its first map highlighting climate change in 2006. Today, with climate urgency transforming our priorities, Green Map System seeks your support for a variety of replicable local climate justice action projects, on the map, in the media and on the streets. Soon, we will "activateNYC" to provide training to local nonprofit staff members, interns and others to use the Green Map Platform to highlight themes in accordance with their own missions. Follow at GreenMap.org/nyc.

title: Help us spay&neuter +500 dogs in Venezuela
description: Our organization is aiming to extend our spay & neutering campaigns to deprived communities in Venezuela. Many independent protectionists have rescued animals that they feed and protect that need to be spayed in order to improve their living conditions. And we need to cover all the costs of these surgeries because they don't have the means to cover it. Help us continue extending our help

title: Support for family Homes in Nginda, Kenya
description: The project wants to guarantee daily meals, medical care and schooling for orphans or abandoned children in the Nginda village, Kenya, supporting the families of this community to properly take care of needy children. The other objective is the awareness of the population and social integration of the many children left to themselves.

title: Help bring St. John residents home.
description: Hundreds of homes on St. John, USVI were partially or completely destroyed by Hurricanes Irma and Maria. HUD estimates up to 74% of low/middle income residential structures on the island were damaged. Our Resilient Housing Initiative seeks to rebuild homes belonging to seniors, families, and persons with a disability or illness who have received little to no recovery funds. We employ St. John businesses and residents to get the job done. Help us bring St. John's residents home by donating today.

title: Build a School in the Cloud for Pisamal, Colombia
description: Everyone has the right to learn, therefore we have designed a learning center called the SOLE Lab. Help us build one in the village of Pisamal whose public internet kiosk got shut down affecting a community of 450 people. This coffee growing community in Colombia has been using SOLE for 5 years to learn and also to find ways to support their own community projects, all with limited internet access and precarious infrastructure. Now they want to take a step further and build a SOLE Lab.

title: Help Women Learn to Read and Write in Uganda
description: Northern Uganda is a post-conflict zone, still recovering from the effects of neighboring Sudan's brutal civil war. During this turbulent time, women and girls missed the opportunity to go to school. Many are formerly abducted child soldiers and/or victims of horrific sexual violence. Ten years after the war, they are now recovering and rebuilding their lives. Learning to read and write enables women to run businesses and support families, and empowers them to secure a brighter future!

title: Frederiksted Spring Clean Up
description: During Earth Week (April 22-28, 2019) Clean Sweep Frederiksted is hosting a town-wide Spring Clean-Up. We are encouraging the community to join forces to collect and safely dispose of litter from our streets, parks, and beaches and declare that litter degrades the beauty of our environment and is not acceptable.

title: HEAL VICCC Recovery Project
description: Heritage Education Arts Legacy (HEAL) Virgin Islands Caribbean Cultural Center (VICCC) Recovery Project integrates discussions, interactive workshops, culturally-sensitive trauma counseling, COVID19 masks, replacement of collections and new media resources that strengthen and provide opportunities for restoring comprehensive multi-cultural resources and programs that teach COVID19 protective behaviors complementary to actions for sustainable disaster recovery and preparedness.

title: Help 100 Sickle Cell Anaemia Children in Uganda
description: Sickle cell anemia is a hereditary incurable defect confined to red blood cells. The basic defect is in the structure of hemoglobin molecule of the red blood cells which acquire sickle like shape in oxygen deficient environment. Due to this effect there is destruction of the cells which could even lead to the death of patients. This disease is now prominent in Teso Sub-Region in Uganda. SCOEN is working for betterment of these patients using HYDROXYUREA TREATMENT recommended to children

title: Build a Children's Home in Kassanda
description: This project will build a residential home for up to 15 orphaned, vulnerable or abandoned children in need of immediate care, support and protection living in the village of Kassanda, Uganda. This home will also have a guest room to house volunteers that come in support of assisting these children or KCA and will provide needed resources to continue and develop or expand new programs.

title: School Bus for 250 Poor Tribal Girls in India
description: They love Agragamee School as it makes learning so much fun! In their own villages, just one or two teachers to 5 classes, over crowded classrooms, parents too poor to even afford sufficient notebooks make school learning so difficult. Their parents are even more eager to send their children.  This project will provide a bus for the girls to come, as many children come from villages as far as 20kms away.

title: Children's Book and Film Festival
description: Started in 2015, the Frederiksted Children's Book and Film Festival is an outdoor fun family event that pairs an award-winning children's book with its corresponding movie.   Held during the summer, starting the last Friday and July and continuing every Friday for four weeks, attending families receive a free copy of the featured book, dinner and enjoy kid-friendly activities.

title: Construct Center for Autistic & Dyslexic children
description: HHH Center for Child Development and Learning Disabilities works to give highly subsidized intervention technique and life skill training to children from 2 to 18 years of age. We intend to create another Intervention center for children with developmental/learning difficulties like Autism, Dyslexia in Rajkot, where children and parents of lower socio-economic background can get facilities at a highly subsidized cost.  A one stop centre to create awareness for such children with learning issues.

title: Support 15 Youth to Make Art & Stop AIDS in Malawi
description: The Make Art / Stop AIDS project will train 15 college students on participatory arts techniques and sexual and reproductive health and rights in order to create art that will combat the high rate of HIV in southern Malawi. These college students will go on to train and mentor 150 secondary school students through the same process, as a part of the efforts to create an AIDS-free generation. Through interactive performances, these young people will reach thousands of their peers.

title: Water 'bout the li'l ones?
description: We look after 575 underprivileged kids from the lower Himalayas - education inclusive of nutrition, healthcare and more, books, uniforms and exposure. But summers are here and they just don't drink much water! So.. how about a Steel flask? It's durable, NON-PLASTIC and good for summer and winter both!   The theme for World Water Day 2019 is 'Leaving no one behind'.  Please help us encourage the habit, and keep them fresh through the day, all year round? Gift a kid a non-plastic bottle :)

title: Simple eye surgery to restore sight to Ethiopians
description: Orbis plans to conduct simple eye surgeries in remote regions of Ethiopia in the hope to cure thousands of people suffering from the painful, blinding and life destroying eye disease - trachoma.

title: Fostering Sustainable Women's Cooperatives
description: This project equips women in Uganda with the skills and training they need to lift themselves and their families out of poverty. By learning skills that enable them to generate income through agricultural cooperative work, women are better able to overcome poverty-related challenges - health, education, water and sanitation, and much more. And, we are seeing these skills-based trainings transform not only families, but also entire communities!

title: Georgetown Visitation Fighting For A Change
