We have just opened two English classes (beginners and advanced); we are reopening our Basic Computer Skills Workshop (very practical, we feel); a wonderful technician - a member of the community - will teach everything to do with cell phone repair. And we are definitely going to restart our Hebrew Language course, so essential for finding a job in Israel.

title: CONSERVATION FARMING FOR FOOD SECURITY
description: The conventional farming system of tilling soil using animal traction and applying fertilizer is not well adapted to the cycle of reoccurring droughts, declining soil fertility and lack oxen and inputs in the Moyo district of west Nile region of Uganda. The result of these problems is a chronic shortfall in food production at the household level as families are forced to become more dependent on food relief. Project will increase 100 household food security through consevation farming

title: Water for Zokotu Community
description: Project Summary: The people of Zokotu community in Kuje Area Council, Nigeria have lived without clean water all their lives. The only available source of drinking water available to the small village of over 2000 persons looks visibly muddy and unclean for animal consumption, yet the people drink it without any form of purification.  Many children have died due to complications arising from the consumption of the dirty water, while others suffering skin reactions and other water borne diseases.

title: Cancer Care for Children in The Philippines
description: We work on the island of Mindanao in the Philippines, at the Southern Philippines Medical Centre (SPMC) and five other Shared Care Centres. We support these centres to increase childhood cancer diagnosis and survival rates by helping to train local healthcare professionals. To remove barriers to accessing - and continuing - treatment, this project also helps to support families most in need by funding medical and travel costs.  We expect to see around 350 children being treated this year.

title: Help End Maternal Mortality in Sierra Leone
description: An estimated 8 women die each day from giving birth in Sierra Leone.  Most of these deaths are preventable with proper care.  Quality care while pregnant, during labor and after delivery can help these women enjoy the precious gift of motherhood without the fear of losing their lives or even their baby's lives.  The Healey International Relief Foundation is helping to end maternal mortality by providing life-saving medical supplies to the 10 clinics and hospitals in our Charity Health Network.

title: DRAWING FOR VISIONARIES for 50 young people Mexico
description: This program will ignite a one year experience of teaching  to draw for  50 young people, in Northeast Mexico. Learning to draw, is a powerful tool for developing self esteem, creativity and attention. Young people in this region are considered vulnerable population because they are target of crime organizations recruiting, so it is import to give them options, tools and valuable knowledge to face their complex environment. The first group of alumni, will be a group of future teachers intraining

title: Improve the livelihood of the Children
description: HELLO, YAWEH SAVE LIFE FOUNDATION GHANA IS A NON GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATION REGISTERED UNDER THE COMPANIES CODE OF GHANA.WE SUPPORT VULNERABLE AND DISABLED CHILDREN IN THE POOR VILLAGES OF THE KWAHU EAST DISTRICT OF GHANA.WE HUMBLY WISH TO APPLEAD FOR YOUR DONATIONS TO PROCURED SOME FOOD STUFFS AND CLOTHINGS FOR 500 CHILDREN IN THE POOR VILLAGE CALLED ANKOMAN IN THE DISTRICT TO IMPROVED THEIR LIVING STANDARD IN THE VILLAGE .WE HOPE THIS REQUEST WILL MEET YOUR KINDEST CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL .

title: Support people with Down Syndrome in Mexico
description: This project supports 1,500 people with Down syndrome and their low income families each year. We offer educational, medical and psychological programs to children, teens and adults.

title: Iloca builds the 27F Tsunami Memorial
description: Huella Local Foundation (FHL) is committed to recover Iloca's public school building, which was devastated by the Earthquake and Tsunami of February 27th, 2010. The project will be a memorial and community centre for the people of Iloca, Duao and La Pesca, small fishing coves of Licanten Commune, one of most underdeveloped territory of southern Chile. FHL will provide professional assistance to co-design and build, alongside beneficiary community and municipal staff, the project.

title: DONATE 100 BEDS TO OKOMFO ANOKYE TEACHING HOSPITAL
description: The donate 100 beds to the KATH hospital in KUMASI, is a project that seeks to solve in part, the inadequate bed situation in the afforementioned hospital,GHANA.  Donors should care about this project because their donations will save lives that would have died as result of being turned away from the hospital because of inadequate beds. The story of a 70year old man who died in Accra as result of no bed at the LEKMA hospital last year, 2018, is what is motivating ALANDA to do this project.

title: PUNARJANI
description: In Kerala, India, the district of Idukki, a place, suffered a massive devastation in August 2018 with flood and land sliding. People dispossessed of all they had, have no place to go back to and no place to build anew. Hilly and inaccessible, Idukki is also an easy target for frequent natural disasters.Project Punarjani is an initiative for building a community for 7 of such families who lost their dwelling.

title: TRALALA    Everybody Should Play Music
description: Music is shown to be beneficial to students to reach success in society, in school, in developing intelligence and success in life. However, access to musical education is limited in all educational establishments in Guatemala, derived from government regulations, and in some educational centers there are no teachers of artistic education, which limits the teaching of integral education for youth.  Help us together for 100 guatemalan youths get musical education throug technologie.

title: Taiwan Children Nutrition Subsidy Program
description: The Foundation currently serves almost 400 rural schools in Taiwan, caring for more than 5,000 children of poverty-stricken families. In addition to monthly financial subsidies, the Nutrition Subsidy Program is initiated over a period of long summer time to ensure that children's meals and leisure activities are catered for during summer vacation Nutrient boxes and school camps are organized so that 3,000 children who have urgent needs for supplies can enjoy themselves throughout the summer time

title: Educate and Empower 75 under-served youth in India
description: Education, Employability and Empowerment (E3 for Youth) is a programme to engage with 75 adolescents and youth from M East Ward (most underserved ward in Mumbai, India) to enable them to complete higher education, develop aspirations and gain employability skills with a focus on sustaining livelihoods. They will also become community leaders through Life Skills and Citizenship training.

title: Sports for Women and Girls in Rural India
description: The project aims at empowering 30 women and 70 girls from the most backward and vulnerable communities of rural Tamil Nadu (India) through the medium of sports. The medium of sports will help create a safe platform and encourage increase in female participation in sports, which has always been a male dominated space. The project will also facilitate overall physical and emotional development of participants by giving them the opportunity to build their skills and achieve self- independence.

title: Vocational Training for 150 poor Girls in Sudan
description: enhancing livelihood of 150  drop- out poor girls in Khartoum state through training them in new vocational training fields such as electricity,  mechanics, carpentry, cooling and refrigerator maintenance  which helped them find a source of income to overcome the poverty as well as continue their education

title: Educate 40 children from the slums of India
description: We provide children from urban poor communities a chance of a better life and a future through scholarships to English-Medium schools, as well as after-school clubs and homework help. This is simply a must to have a chance to break inter-generational poverty traps in India.  Today 40 of our children from the slums of Bangalore are missing funding for their next year of education. By donating you will be giving them a chance to get a fair start in life.

title: Special Need Service for 45 Elderly People in UG
description: Elderly people face several hardships in life which include chronic diseases like arthritis and disease, dental problems like tooth decay and infection, poor housing, malnutrition, stress among others. In addition to this, most of the elderly people come from poor families making it extremely hard to meet the basic necessities of life. This also puts their lives in danger. Therefore, this project will promote the well-being of elderly people.

title: Reducing the breast cancer mortality and morbidity
description: This project aims to increase the awareness about the screening and early detection of breast cancer by imparting knowledge and skills to conduct clinical breast examination to healthy women between ages 30 to 69 years with intact breasts in the selected blocks of Tirunelveli district. Women will be identified through household surveys, and the purpose of the visit will be explained to them. After obtaining written informed consent from all participants, the trained female health workers

title: RESTORE FUTURE OF PRISONERS' CHILDREN IN UGANDA
description: Children with incarcerated parents in Uganda lack a support system. This project will empower the child, caregiver and the incarcerated parent for sustainable positive impact, interrupting the criminal behavior cycle.    47 at risk (at promise) children will be kept in school, their caregivers trained in commercial farming for sustainable livelihood, and their incarcerated parents taught parenting and craft making. Also, parent-child visitation trips will be conducted to build family cohesion.

title: DONATE SOLAR LIGHT TO 5000CHILDREN IN RURAL UGANDA
description: Pearl Entrepreneurs Academy (PEA) is a charitable Community Based Organization based in Mayuge Uganda founded by the young people to give back to the community.At night, for lighting, they have no choice but to use kerosene lanterns and open flame candles. The smoke from these lights sources is hazardous to their health. The flames are also a fire hazard. PEA is helping to address these issues by providing safe, renewable, solar-powered lights to kids and students read, study and do school work

title: Integral Attention For At-Risk Mexican Children
description: This project will help reduce the risk of children ending up on the streets. Trough our model, we provide them with a safe home, food, medical and psychological attention, a better education, and especially, better opportunities once they become independent. We provide integral attention to these children by covering all of their necessities and fomenting the importance of studying as much as they can, as well as having a career.

title: Shea Butter Processing Facilities for 200 Women
description: This project will build a Shea Butter processing facility for 200 Women in the poorest part of Northern Ghana to ensure good health and safety environment and improve quantity and quality to attract better market prices to earn better income to support the family and their livelihood.

title: Cultural education for 25 Oaxacan schools
description: This project will bring children from 25 rural schools in Oaxaca to learn about pre-Columbian art in Mexico and take cultural workshops in the museum. Thus awakening their interest in culture and the arts, forging future Oaxacan artists.

title: Save the Stories: A QTBIPOC Storytelling Project
description: After 1 full year of being on the ground responding to COVID-19, our team has shifted from only training interns in digital media advocacy to supporting LGBTQIA+ led initiatives. We are proud to advocate for Indigenous, Black, people of the global majority to tell their stories, from a firsthand perspective. We are working with grassroots organizers, Trans and Queer farmers, and creatives to addresses the crises that disproportionately impact Indigenous communities, both rural and urban.

title: Help the Poor Go for Cancer Screeing (DECIDES)
description: DECIDES PROJECT-Demystifying Cancer Infection- Do early Screening DECIDES project provides free testing and cancer screening to the poor women. Cancer infections have cleared many family lifelong savings and investments, pushing them to extreme poverty.  the project enhances the recognizing and possible warning signs of cancer and taking prompt action leading to early diagnosis and treatment. this saves families from pain, high costs and leverage household incomes.

title: Help 300 Survivors of Violence Start Again!
description: 3 seconds!   That's how often we blink our eyes. Sadly, its also the Exact amount of time that lapses before someone becomes a Victim of Violence! That's 1200 times per hour. A whopping 28,800 times a day!   Its shocking to think of what happens in the Blink Of An Eye!  Let's Join together to Fight for Survival!     Your Contribution will make an impact to help Survivors Break Their Chains, Get Support and Find a Safe Haven.   Help Bring Hope. Breed Trust.   The futures calling, won't you help?

title: Healthy smile for 1500 Rural Children and Orphans
description: This project will provide 1000 free dental treatments and dental kits(toothbrush, toothpaste, dental floss) to children between age 2 and 17 in five rural communities where basic dental treatments like scaling and polishing, dental fillings and extraction would be carried out and fully sponsored referrals will be done when necessary. The Healthy Smile project is targeting the most impoverished children in rural areas of Ekiti State. These include orphans, vulnerable, children, street children.

title: Renovate 9 Classrooms for 211 kids in Nigeria
description: MfDI is seeking funds to complete the following for the benefit of the 211 pupils and 13 teachers of St Luke Primary School, Iro Ekiti which was initially constructed in the 1960s: 1. Repair 3 blocks of classrooms comprising 9 classes and 3 toilets. 2. Fixing of 9 classroom boards 3. Repair 3 toilets areas (one in each block) 4. Construction of classroom furniture such as chairs and desks  Your donation will not only help us to complete these work for 211 students, but for many more yet to come.

title: HELP TO EDUCATE UNDERPRIVILEGED CHILDREN IN INDIA
description: Our project will help poor and needy children to get proper education in the remote area of central India {Bundelkhand area} by providing them proper educational material and holistic development

title: EDUCATE  40 ORPHANS  IN KENYA
description: During the 30 years of the global HIV epidemic, an estimated 17 million children have lost one or both parents due to AIDS;  In addition, 3.4 million children under age 15 are living with HIV. The number of children affected by or vulnerable to HIV remains alarmingly high.Kenya now has a growing number of orphans and vulnerable children.They often suffer from emotional distress, malnutrition, labor exploitation, homelessness,  lack of health care, and poor or no access to education. we plan

title: NAWRC GG Project
description: We are building an Animal Welfare Trust (AWT) with the motive to make our welfare activities sustainable for long time. Nepal Animal Welfare and Research Center (NAWRC) is serving needy animals (including stray dogs population management, anti-rabies vaccination, rescues and treatments, supporting abandoned baby calves, serving victim wild animals, post-disaster supports etc) in remote villages of Kavrepalanchok District of Nepal. We are a registered non-profit, non-governmental organization.

title: Stimulation Therapy for 250 People w/ID in Chile
description: This project will create the first Stimulation Center in Chile for 250 people with intellectual disabilities providing over 5000 educational, cognitive, sports and physical therapy sessions annually.  It will consist of certified professionals such as special educational professors, kinesiologists, physical educational professors, occupational therapists, phonoaudiologists, psychologists that will diagnose, evaluate, and treat each person according to his/her situation.

title: Second home for 130 pupils - Witajcie w domu!
description: The project ensures support for 130 pupils of Polish descent from the east (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Georgia, Moldova, Armenia, Belarus, Russia, Ukraine) in the Dormitory. Children come from poor families, who can not afford to fully pay the costs of them living and studying in a Polish high school.  Pupils live in the School's Dormitory for 10 months a year. The Foundation collects funds to provide them with food, care (both pedagogical and psychological) as well as cleaning/hygenic products.

title: empower-1000-unemployed-youth-in-lesotho-africa
description: Lesotho nowadays is all over news channels because of its poverty, Unstable government, highest unemployment rate and it's a second country in the world with highest HIV prevalence.  This project empower  youth with sustainable economic development and  job creation skills. It will also facilitates ethical leadership skills to ensure democracy and good governance. It will be implemented in 5 districts and 73 community councils of Lesotho and it will impact 500 youth who will impact others.

title: Maid Strong: Stop Trafficking of Adolescent Girls
description: This project will tackle incidents of underaged vulnerable girls being trafficked as house helps or engaging in transactional sex for financial independence.  The centre will engage in adult education    for these girls, give them intensive marketable and life skills training to help them develop critical thinking, self-awareness, healthcare, and heightened aspiration to improve themselves and become successful adults.

title: Relief Support for  Displaced  Cameroon Children
description: YAPCEC (Youth Advocates for Peace and Community Empowerment Cameroon) , with mission to provide children and youths with relevant skills and knowledge that will empower them access opportunities to improve their lives and community, plans to provide basic human right relief support to the internally displaced crisis affected children, youths and women  who hail from the south west region of Cameroon,to stay alive and regain education.

title: Construction of School Building for Blind Girls.
description: Through the proposed project, a new building for Smt. Ambubai Residential School for Blind Girls shall be constructed on the land located at Gulbarga, Karnataka, India.The building shall comprise two separate floors. The ground floor shall comprise the primary, secondary and high-school to provide education for more than 100 blind girls, whereas the first floor shall comprise their dormitories, library, kitchen, dining hall warden rooms etc.

title: GIFTING SMILES TO VULNERABLE CHILDREN IN KILIFI
description: Our passion is gifting smiles to the vulnerable children in Kilifi County. Our work involves restoring hope and a future to bright needy students through access to funding for education. We do this through calls on social media, call for support from well-wishers, scholarship funds and the community at large. Additionally, we do collect books , sanitary pads , geometrical sets and other school requirements in a bid to retain and support needy students in school.

title: Bring home 4 lions from Ukraine to Africa
description: After the successful rescue and relocation of 4 lions in 2018 we are going to do it again. Four lions living in cruel or unsuitable conditions have been found in various facilities throughout Ukraine. They will be undertake the 70 hour trip to South Africa where they can lie in the African sun and walk on grass. They can for the first time in their lives be lions.

title: Gift clean & safe water to 25 villages in India
description: "Water is life & its gift is the best"  Under this project UWAD will provide clean & safe water to 25 drought hit villages. Women & girls  walk long distances and spend many hours in a  day to collect water and due to water crisis majority of people  are using unsafe water that leads to many diseases. This program will focus on providing potable water, water filters, water treatments, health education for safe water storage and management,  awareness and prevention from diseases.

title: ICT Empowerment For Burundi's Children Education
description: Computers For Schools Burundi's goal is to close the digital gap in the education of Burundi's children. Two schools in Burundi, one primary and the other secondary will be equipped with ICT labs of 43 computers connected to the Internet. Students will learn ICT, coding, research, and digital entrepreneurship. The Project will also train 40 instructors to teach the ICT curriculum to 1,560 students this will help prepare Burundian youth to compete in the global economy's job markets.

title: Send a Child to School in Romania for a Year
description: This project will buy children everithing they need to go to school. Every penny is worth it because it can be the reason why we have successful leaders in the coming future. It will also protect a child against discrimination, violence, and exploitation.

title: A Family Of Learning, After School Program by GMM
description: The core objective of this project is to help out-of-school youth from different schools in Cameroon, by developing their skills & creating an emotionally safe place, to help them catch up with the topics they would have learned formally in school.  The program curriculum is designed on 'Make learning fun' motto, to help youth understand & implement, theoretical & practical knowledge - in real life. The project also aims to develop interpersonal skills along with technical skills.

title: 5000 seedlings for ethnic women to restore forests
description: Ethnic minority women in the Northwest of Vietnam are currently facing increasing deforestation which has negative effects on their lives and livelihoods. We believe that a bottom-up movement coming from the villagers is needed to effectively tackle this problem. We want to enable these ethnic minority women to replant the lost forests around their villages which will have a sustainable positive impact on their lives and living environment.

title: TO EDUCATE THE CHILDREN OF SEX WORKERS IN PUNJAB
description: There are lots of girls and women who are forcibly introduced in the prostitution in punjab .Our organization CAPTAIN GURDEEP SINGH SOCIETY saves 800 girls from this racket and gave them vocational trainings so they will be able to do some work and live independly but still there is a big problem they are unable to educate thier children with their earning . So being an organization we adopted all the childrens for education. Education is the important tool for them to accept new face of life

title: Help a Girl to complete primary Education
description: Community Development Foundation will establish adult literacy & training center in sub urban population of Jacobabad CDF will announce admissions in local new papers or cable TV network for collecting profiles of 30 out of school adult female learners aged 10-15 who have never went to school or left school due to any reason.  CDF will educate adult learners through non formal education package in class rooms and audio visual lab. There are 3 basic subjects of NFE Package A i.e Sindhi, English,

title: Support 6 housemothers in care of children in need
description: 17 children in need are currently in the care of our amazing housemothers at Diani Children's Village (DCV). These housemothers support the children, ensuring they have a clean, secure, and comfortable place to live. DCV supports the housemothers wherever they  can, including covering their own children's schools fees, providing them with access to good healthcare, etc. This project will support six housemothers in their personal family lives for the next year.

title: Develop reading skills of 500 children in Ayawaso
description: United Way Ghana's literacy project seeks to promote childhood literacy and inculcate reading habits in primary school children in underserved schools located in slum communities.

title: MAKING  MEN  OUT OF 2000 BOYS IN THARAKA -KENYA
description: In the effort to prevent and reduce gender based violence within Tharaka Nithi county,PCOSES aims at making responsible men by reaching out to adolescent boys and youth through support in education, mentorship, and support with start up kits ( income generation activities) to help them move from vulnerability to resilience. This will reduce the current alarm trends of violence against girls All stakeholders will be involved at all levels of the project to ensure transparency and sustainability

title: Education Support for 280 Disabled Children
description: This project is aimed to provide special need education materials, school feeding, life skill training and personal hygiene training to children with different types of disabilities. Moreover, the charity will provide awareness enhancement training to community members about persons with disabilities. The project also provides sign language and braille training to special need teachers functioning in the project area.

title: Keep Child-Family Together By Positive Parenting
description: All children should grow up in a safe, non-violent, and positive family environment, allowing them to fully enjoy their rights and grow to their full potential. To achieve this vision, the proposed project will provide locally coordinated training sessions to parents, giving them the confidence and Positive Parenting skills to be excellent role models for their children and their communities.

title: Seeds & Agriculture Training for Farmers in Uganda
description: Farmers in western Uganda are often unable to afford enough seed for each growing season and families go hungry.  Seeds4Seeds equips farmers with seeds and the necessary agronomic practices to grow maize, beans, and rice to increase food production, reduce poverty through the sale of surplus produce, save their own seed for the next season to avoid buying counterfeit seeds on market and to be able to pay school fees for their children.

title: Help Provide Labor for Family Farms in Colorado
description: A lack of available labor makes it difficult for Colorado farmers to sell more of what they grow. The Mobile Farm Workforce (MFW) offers veterans, members of the refugee community, and experienced farm-hands a living wage, while providing efficient, on-demand labor to Colorado farmers and ranchers so that they can bring more of their products to market.

title: New American Africans "Sweet Sixteen" Campaign
description: We're looking for 16 people to give $1,000 each. If you can't give $1,000, we're looking for people to be our NAA Sweet 16 ambassadors-donate a gift of $16 or more to NAA, share the "Sweet Sixteen" post on your social media pages. Be part of the future of NAA and continue to support Newcomers in New Hampshire.

title: Saving 4000 Little Hearts from India
description: Congenital Heart Disease (CHD) is the largest cause of Child Mortality in India. In India, 300,000 children are born every year with CHD. Because of problem of Availability, Affordability, Accessibility; 25% among these die within 1st year of birth.  Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Pediatric Cardiac Hospitals in India provide Totally Free of Cost Treatment to all and have performed over 20,700 surgeries in 10 years. This project aims to support 500 such poor and needy children in India with CHD.

title: Restore 600 rural women's livelihoods in Zimbabwe
description: This project will create and enhance climate-smart interventions as a means of livelihood, through entrepreneurship trainings, provision of inputs and infrastructural support. The project will procure 1500 indigenous chicken breeds, supply 2 solar-powered hatcheries and construct 2 brooding fowl runs for 600 resource-limited rural women in Bulilima District of Zimbabwe.

title: Light Up Dreams Dimmed by Wars and Disasters
description: Peace Warabe Japan aims to support young people from around the world who experienced natural or man-made disaster to join a one-week summer camp in Japan. At the camp, they will meet other students of diverse backgrounds and will learn about world issues and leadership by participating in interactive, fun group activities. Through exposure to new perspectives and ideas, they will discover positive ways to view and digest their own past experiences and use them to realize their full potential.

title: The Survival of Orphans and Vulnerable Children
description: This project will provide shelter and care for 50 Orphans and Vulnerable Children especially those below one year of age and whose survival is threatened by all causes. Nigeria's under Five Mortality Rate increased from 87 in 1997 to 120.77 Per 1,000 Births in 2018 making Nigeria rank the 9th leading country globally (WHO) . TenderLife will provide key food/nutrition, shelter and care needs (immunizations, Baby milk, Organically/locally sourced nutritional foods, diapers, clothes and baby cots)

title: Personal development to 2000 disadvantaged malagas
description: This project will bring personal development to 2000 disadvantaged pupils from public primary school in 6 different region in Madagascar. This personal development is done by benevolent willing to bring changes to their community through ludic activities

title: Help 50 children in need live healthier lives!
description: SAFALIN (Salud - Familias- Infancia) is an initiative created to reduce rates of childhood obesity among families at risk of social exclusion, as it is proved that children from low-income families are more predisposed to suffer obesity. Despite being preventable, nearly 1 in 5 children and adolescents are overweight/obese.  In particular, this project will provide 50 children with healthy habits workshops which will help them have better health opportunities in their future.

title: Rebuilding St. Croix, USVI
description: The St. Croix Long Term Recovery Group (LTRG) was formed after the impact of two back-to-back Cat 5 hurricanes: Irma and Maria. It is also mobilizing post-Dorian. The LTRG is a collective of individuals, businesses, non-profit and faith-based institutions whose goal it is to unite recovery resources with community needs.  The LTRG ensures that the most vulnerable among Virgin Islanders can safely return to their homes as quickly as possible and be wholly recovered from ongoing impacts of storms.

title: Educate 20000 Namibian teenagers on HIV using Arts
description: Namibia is one of the countries most affected by the HIV pandemic. We have put massive efforts to curb the impact. However, teenagers remain vulnerable. With an estimated age of sexual debut at 15 and the absence of condoms in schools, many teenagers put themselves at risk. This project works directly with teenagers using a medium they relate to. Through the power of dance, drama, youth-friendly publications, OYO creates safe spaces for teenagers to learn, share and adopt saver behaviours.

title: 50K Cans of Drinking Water to Post Disaster Areas
description: This project will supply the disaster stricken community of Eastern Oklahoma with 50,000 cans of clean drinking water through a partnership with the Community Food Bank of Eastern Oklahoma . The communities we serve are already overlooked and when disaster strikes, the struggles of obtaining critical necessities like clean drinking water are compounded by the stress and chaos.

title: Save island from becoming a petroleum terminal
description: This project will help save Bona Island, a pristine marine life sanctuary in Panama from being devastated and converted into a petroleum terminal. CIAM will draft the legislative initiative to promote its "Wildlife Refuge" status. Our project will protect the numerous marine bird species, coral reef communities, sea turtles and humpback whales; but will also work to help the local communities in the area that rely on artisanal fisheries to protect their sources of livelihood.

title: water-and-sanitation-for-1500-ghanaians
description: 1. This project will build 3 no. 4-seater latrines for 1500 school children. 3 no. Rain Water Harvesting Tank to 3 deprived basic schools in Northern Ghana, which will serve 1500 children. It will ensure the formation and training of 3 School Health Clubs and the Provision of 18 Hand Washing with soap facilities in the selected schools. The project will also Sensitize 800 school girls on menstrual cycle management in the selected schools

title: HELP EDUCATE 60 DEPRIVED CHILDREN IN NAGALAND
description: Agape plans to add 3 classrooms to Bethsaida Christian School that had been introduced at Wokha Town  in Nagaland for Urban Poor of the society. The  objective of this school is to provide opportunity to Urban Poor's children to obtain school education absolutely free of any cost. Pupils are selected from the underprivileged sections like Economically weaker section (EWS) students , Orphans, Children of HIV/AIDS afflicted parents & Drug Abusers and are provided free Mid-day meals as well.

title: Support 45 children with hearing loss in Mexico
description: Support 45 children with hearing loss, from disadvantaged backgrounds in rural, indigenous and peri-urban communities of Oaxaca State to improve their communication and inclusion at school and in society, allowing them to achieve their potential and lead dignified, fulfilling lives.

title: WAY FORWARD AFTER THE RESCUE
description: Rescued Girls are admitted to our Homes and stay with us till they are released as per the Courts.   Once released they are either united with their families, or repatriated to their countries.  Some of them choose to stay back and complete their studies or trainings and pursue jobs.  Over the years we have had nearly 25 such girls who choose to not go back home.  They have been provided temporary Care & Protection in our Group Home.  The Proposed Project is to provide Care, Protection to them

title: Support 150 Mauritian Youth Agripreneurs
description: This project will introduce modern organic farming techniques to 150 youths from underserved communities. The benefits are manifold:  Participants learn sustainable farming from a real-world social enterprise that benefits both people and planet; The program elevates the perception of farming among the younger generation - farmers don't have to be poor and uneducated;  The program sows the seeds for teens who may consider a career in agriculture and become tomorrow's agripreneurs.

title: Help a Child return Home
description: Ensure 60  previously trafficked girls  receive the care they deserve. Your investment will provide  counseling, case management, emergency shelter and strengthen families so the girls can be reunited into family care.  Please help give these girls the opportunity for a future they deserve.  Happy holidays and thank you for caring.

title: Healthcare and Water, sanitation and Hygienic
description: The Khowai & Dhalai areas are most family are poor.  Most of the parents are marginal farmer and day labour. Socio-economically it is most backward District of the state.The corona virus outbreak is affecting all of us. But only some of us have access to essential services, Water, hygiene facilities and the safety of our homes. The economic conditions is poor for lack of required infrastructure and inaccessibility of many tribal areas the Districts is still very backward.

title: Preventing Suicide by Gatekeeper Training, India
description: IASP is implementing Gatekeeper Training Programme in rural communities in Andhra Pradesh, where suicide rates are some of the highest in India. Gatekeeper Training is a sustainable initiative that extends knowledge, skills and practical application throughout communities and raises awareness of suicide risks and prevention. Early identification of suicide risk is crucial for suicide prevention; many people at high risk of suicide often do not seek help though recognizable risk factors exist.

title: Skilling Blind Youth of India in Massage Therapy
description: This GSP-Swadhar's project will transform the lives of 30 needy unemployed blind youth in India ( Maharashtra region) by providing them specialized training fin Acupressure-Massage Therapy. This training course is for six months and the project will ensure that these youth will claim remunerative employment as a therapist and come out of poverty and deprivation. With increasing lifestyle diseases there is good demand for the therapists. The course is innovative & highly effective for blind youth

title: Improving maternal/new born health in Cross River
description: The occurrence of high maternal and new born mortality ratio is evidenced in Cross River State, Nigeria. This project will continue to conduct sensitization campaigns involving the stakeholders to increase demand for timely utilization of quality Maternal and Neonatal Health/Family Planning services (MNH/FP), improve the capacity of existing community structures for increased uptake of MNH and FP services, and facilitate access to timely and quality MNH/FP Services ( Emergency Transport System)

title: Free Mental Health provision for 42 individuals
description: This project directly supports marginalized and vulnerable individuals from Sarajevo, who are falling through the cracks of the post-war system in Bosnia and Herzegovina and whose human rights have been violated. Victims of domestic violence, war traumatized individuals, and children from families with low income, suffering from mental health issues and disorders, are provided with counselling, psychotherapy or psychological and psycho-social support who cannot pay for therapy.

title: Supporting Isolated Older People in Dorset. U.K.
description: This project supports older people in Dorset, by providing a wide range of activities and opportunities for those vulnerable and isolated people. Our vision is 'a world where no-one is unfairly disadvantaged or excluded because of age or infirmity and where every person can enjoy life'. We will provide support to individuals within communities, to enhance the advancement of health, alleviate isolation and loneliness and to 'slow down the slide into dependency'

title: HELP US BUILD A SCHOOL FOR 150+ CHILDREN IN ZAMBIA
description: Most rural areas in Zambia have poor or no infrastructure to support the education of children. Public schools are very few, overcrowded and far to reach for children in many parts of these areas. Community schools make an alternative place of learning for children who cannot walk the miles to attend class at far away learning facilities. Building Futures works with communities to build community schools and support their education systems to increase access to quality education in rural areas.

title: Help 5 communities restore forests in Mozambique
description: Cyclone Idai devastated vital forest areas around the Chimanimani National Park in central Mozambique. MICAIA will work with 5 communities on re-planting forest areas in critical zones. We will integrate 'useful' trees (native species of food and medicinal plants, bee-friendly plants) along with fast-growing species. We will establish community nurseries for expansion and we will provide information on sustainable farming and forest conservation to local schools.

title: Solar for Internally Displaced Persons Camps
description: Solar for Internally Displaced Persons Camp (Solar for IDP Camp) is an initiative of GIFSEP;  It is aimed at powering all IDP Camps in Nigeria with Solar. The insurgency and communal crises have displaced about 2 Million people who are taking shelter in Internally Displaced Persons Camp in different parts of the country and nearly all the camps are without electricity. Our goal is to provide clean energy access using solar kits to at least 5000 shelters providing power to at least 50,000 people

title: Give the Gift of Hearing to a Child Without Ears
description: Give the gift of hearing to a child without ears. Every day in Russia babies are born without ears. These children are destined to live in a world of silence. Parents feel scared, helpless until they learn about American surgeons who create inner ear canals and outer ears where none exist. And then children can hear. It's a miracle! But for the parents, the cost of ear surgery plus travel to the U.S. is staggering. Help bring a child to America and give them the gift of hearing.

title: Pathways to autonomy: tzotzil women's empowerment
description: Twenty young indigenous women 50% single mothers, face discrimination, gender violence, and economic marginalization. Integrating gender perspectives in to this project will support a development program to strength their leadership by economic empowerment, entrepreneurial skills integrating gender perspectives, to advanced their inequity life conditions.

title: Fund a Music Program for a Primary School in Kenya
description: Music builds a sense of belonging, discipline, confidence, creativity, movement skills, cooperativeness and extends the world of possibilities for gifted students. But despite this almost universal interest, our primary schools were not allowed to mentor these wonderful talents. Things have changed and we finally have new curriculum which has allowed us to mentor these wonderful talents and empower the needy to bring a lasting and positive change in the lives.

title: Back 2 School 2019 at CILA!
description: As the '18/'19 cycle ends and we get ready to kick off '19/'20, CILA is buzzing with energy! With a crop of excited new students ready to take join the CILA family, we need your support! This summer make a donation to help us start the year with smiles and positivity! Our students need supplies, and we need your help! Get in on the fun this summer by supporting children and families in Mexico.

title: Build Center to Care for Sexually Abused Children
description: COIN has worked since 2016 to identify and provide services to children who are victims of commercial sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and violence. Given the need and the exceptional results achieved, the government of  Veron/ Punta Cana has donated 2,000 m of land for the construction of a Center to provide psychological, medical and legal services to these children and teenagers and work with the community and families to improve their lives and ensure they can thrive in a safe environment

title: Transportation for the homeless and volunteers
description: Friends Can Make It Happen. Works with the homeless and less fortunate families in Pennsylvania. Our greatest challenge is transportation of volunteers who help provide services needed for the homeless such as food, clothing, sanitary kits. We also help transporting them for court appearances, doctors appointments, job interviews and family re-unification. We are badly in need of a min-van to make our work more easier. That's why we took this opportunity to come on Global Giving to seek for help

title: Shelter-less widow required urgent support
description: At the age of 30 years, Bibi Hurran lost her husband in 1966. The brave lady   brought up the orphan daughters and well look after the house and property of her husband. Over 83 years, the hardest days are the last four years, when she  lost her house partially in the flooding of 2010 and completely in the flooding of 2015. The hardest days of her life, during  her 53 years widow-ship, she is  moving from many relatives for shelter dragged from pillar to post. She is looking for shelter

title: Happy Period for 600 Nepali girls in 7 schools
description: Helpcode is committed on bringing health education and sustainable menstrual solutions to 600 girls in rural Nepal. Without basic hygiene education and sanitation, rural girls often miss many days of school ultimately dropping out. Partnering with Helpcode Nepal, we provide safe, nice, easy to use and long-lasting washable menstrual kits along with our important health education. Our Kits are produced locally in our sewing workshop in Chitwan providing employment to vulnerable women.

title: Bring 70 Malawian Youth to School!
description: Tingathe is a Malawian NGO which provides free-of-charge vocational training to the most vulnerable youth in Malawi; those living in peri-urban areas. As such, our students have difficulties attending class due to the transport costs incurred in daily travel.  This project will enable Tingathe to purchase a bus which will transport our students to and from classes on a daily basis. This will enable our youth to thrive in their education by ensuring that they successfully complete their education

title: Repairing the Hope-Mobile!
description: The "Hope-Mobile" as we like to call her, is vital to HCU's work. Having a sturdy vehicle that can travel long distances to remote villages ensures we can provide over 3,000 otherwise unreachable people with education and access to services like reproductive health workshops and sanitary pads, micro-finance loans and business training sessions, and sensitisation to issues like gender-based violence and children's rights to education.

title: Save 136 refugee children along EU-Serbia borders
description: Help APC camper - mobile office with a team of lawyers, psychologists and social workers to help young refugees & migrants across Serbia, the last migration buffer zone on the EU's borders. More than 6,000 refugees/migrants, out of which over 1000 are in the open, with no shelter, food, hygiene, health care, no legal/psycho protection nor proper information. We will come to them by using our camper - mobile office. With our help, 136 children will be safe, informed and empowered.

title: 150Voice recorders-Visual Impaired pupils,Tanzania
description: We request donation of 150 Voice Recorders for Visually impaired pupils at Luhira primary school, Ruvuma region, Tanzania. The school has a shortage of special teachers for this category of children. The visually impaired study with normal ones,fail to catch up like others thus denied equal opportunity in education.Voice recorders will provide a solution to this problem, will enable replaying of the teachings after classes and type the notes using the few braillers machines available at school.

title: Provide one classroom bench for 2 kids in Cameroon
description: This projects sets out to ameliorate access to education to pupils (04-15 years old) by providing 200 two seater benches to 400 kids(internally displaced and refugees)  in four rural public schools in Garoua Boulai , East region, Cameroon.

title: Rescue 20 children from the streets in Ashaiman
description: We look for the most vulnerable children on the streets of Ashaiman, Tema and Accra, who are willing to seize the chance for a better life. We provide them with temporary shelter away from the streets; where they can build trust and make friends. We prepare the children for school life as well as we support them during their course of education. We give our best to build individual opportunities of reintegration into family and society.

title: Technology Afterschool Clubs for Girls in Nigeria
description: The W.TEC Academy is an after-school programme designed to inspire girls in public secondary schools to pursue computer science careers. The girls go through a year-long computing curriculum, which includes Computer Architecture & Networking, Alice Programming and Digital Arts. With clubs in Lagos and Kwara states of Nigeria, we expanded to Obalaju High School, Joga and Yewa College, Ilaro, both in Ogun State. In 2022, we will broaden the curriculum and expand to more public schools.

title: Rural schools Students setting up Library.
description: Project Background : The Government of Tamilnadu - run a high school at Kilpalur village in Tiruvannamalai district has earned laurels for facilitating to all the students in the institution to establish a library on their own in their houses. Putting together the books donated by friends, teachers and issued as prizes in competitions, 310 students studying in Government High School located at Kilpalur have established a small library in their houses. As many as 310 students of our school.

title: Educate 300 Potential Child Warriors in Kenya .
description: This project will enroll and educate 300 out of school children at risk of being initiated into  negative cultural practices; cattle rustling, Female Genital Mutilation and early forced marriages in Akoret. It will build permanent classrooms and dormitories, provide up to standard desks, books, uniforms, nutritious meals, clean drinking water, facilitate tree planting, school gardens and community sensitization forums on long term impacts of education to end  rustling  practice.

title: Help A Child Get Back to School
description: The Ngao Foundation knew very little about COVID-19 but now we know that it is going to be with us for a long time. It has come with unintended consequences as so many children still remain at home roaming streets even after school reopening.  As children stay longer out of school, we are witnessing a greater risk that the poorest among them have never returned to school. We are experiencing increased cases of violence, child labor, and child marriage, and their mental wellbeing.

title: Children Center in Soweto, Kayole slum in Nairobi
description: Tunaweza Pamoja Children's Centre serves neglected, orphaned, vulnerable, deprived and destitute children from the Kayole-Soweto slum area in Nairobi. We help the children by paying their school fees, giving them shelter, food, clothing and medical attention. We provide a loving and safe, family environment that gives children the right to a happy, educated, skilled and healthy life. Help fund support for the 100 children we are serving!

title: Training Center for Malagasy Tourism Workforce
description: Help Halt Poverty build a training center for ignored labor pools: chronically unemployed, lost parents, LGBT, recovering addicts, to address staff shortage serving Malagasy tourism industry. The site will include a library, a training venue (food preparation, rooms, etc.) for hands-on demonstrations. The renovation of this historical landmark will also signify the preservation of the architectural ensemble of the Old Town Fianarantsoa. Now we need to raise $5,000 funds for Anay center project

title: Integrate & Educate 2000 Street Children
description: We are a charity trust organization in Kenya that focuses in finding solutions to the street families problems especially children who are the majority.  This project will focus on Street-Child Family Reunion through Counseling and reintegrating 2000 children back to their families for good social Care. To us, no love is greater than the love of a family. After this we enroll them to schools to continue with their studies for the drop outs and freshly join those who had never had an education.

title: Empowered Parents, Inclusive Communities for Deaf
description: The Project will train and provide start up loans to 180 mothers of deaf children who are unemployed in rural Uganda. The small businesses include: goat rearing, vegetable growing, chicken rearing, mushroom growing, tailoring and small scale shop. The training will include: Business skills, Planning, Market Research, and value added production. By learning a marketable skill the mothers will generate income and lift themselves out of poverty to sustain their deaf children in education

title: Build Peace Through Agroecology in Bogota
description: Sembrando Confianza recovers spaces in neighborhoods of vulnerable communities, through organic urban agriculture in order to strengthen the social  fabric and promote healthy and sustainable consumption. We provide installations and training to children and adults to promote intergenerational meeting spaces to build more resilient, conscious and peaceful citizens.

title: Dignity for victims of  bandits attacks
description: The project will pay secondary and college  fee for 30 girls who will be drawn for the maasai  community(Ilchamus) of baringo county who are orphans and victims of bandits and cattle rustlers attacks

title: Fund a teacher and support more than 250 students
description: Remember when life was about the morning bell, who was your favorite teacher and who sat next to you? A good teacher can be the one who inspires you, who supports academic success, and the one who you are still thankful for today. One fundamental piece that is missing in the Guatemalan school system is the quality education of teachers. Most teachers are poorly educated and underpaid and the curricula and teaching methods are outdated.

title: World Cleanup Day in Albania
description: World Cleanup Day will take action on problematic waste hotspots (such as rivers), aiming to build specific civic engagement to help with a clean environment. We will identify all problematic hotspots across the country. National cleanup advocates will organize cleanup actions at hotspots. Through actions, we will bring attention to citizens, institutions, NGOs and media. Raising national awareness about pollution, this action will address the urgent issue while also providing positive progress.

title: Blessed Generation High School
description: The school aim at providing high/secondary education and social support  to many students who could have missed the chance of getting education completely. Most of them come from vulnerable background. Others are orphaned or destitute.  All the current students have been under the wings of Blessed Generation Child care since they were small. For over 30 years Blessed Generation has helped many children in education up to university.

title: Empowering 50 rural young people in Oaxaca, Mexico
description: Accompany us and together we will contribute to the initiatives and learning of young people of rural and indigenous communities of the Mixteca Alta region in the Mexican state of Oaxaca. With the capacity building of the School for the Common Good they want be stronger so as to practice their rights for a dignified life in peace and harmony with their environment and to integrate and benefit their community.

title: Give livelihood skills to 30 kayayo girls in Ghana
description: This project will return and give integrated vocational and life skills training to 30 vulnerable girls from Northern Ghana working as head porters and sleeping in the streets of Accra and Kumasi. It will also provide start-up package for the girls upon completion of the skills training.

title: Integral Development of Street Children of Oaxaca
description: Canica de Oaxaca A.C. is a non profit organization established in 1992 in Oaxaca, Mexico.  Our goal is to promote development of children who work on the streets through an integral program that provides, food, education, psychological care, recreational, cultural, artistic and sports activities for 75 families who live in poverty or extreme poverty.

title: Removing the Shame in Menstrual Cycle , Zimbabwe
description: This project will build a community center in Masvingo, Zimbabwe, to provide a space to teach young girls and women how to sew reusable sanitary pads and supply basic business training. Rural areas do not sell menstruation pads, and if they are provided, they are often too expensive for most households. Tese Foundation aims to spur business opportunities for women through the selling of pads, as well as increase educational opportunities and health in the area.

title: Growing agribusiness entrepreneurs in East Africa
description: Unemployment is soaring in sub-Saharan Africa.  Yet there are huge opportunities for new agribusinesses as food imports into Africa are already high and are expected to increase further.  The Agripreneurship Alliance is training young people in East Africa in Entrepreneurship in Agribusiness to help them create their own businesses to generate income and employment.  In particular, we encourage and support young women to become entrepreneurs.

title: Empowers 100 Zapotec women to be government
description: Espiral por la Vida, trains 100 indigenous women from 5 poor municipalities in Oaxaca to access the governments of their communities and be agents of change and gender inclusion in their communities.

title: Heart Surgery for 100 Children in South Africa
description: What would you do if your child was one of the 1 in 100 children born with a heart defect? Parents are willing to move heaven and earth to save their child's life, but often, their options and finances are limited. Sadly, routine surgical procedures freely available in the developed world are out of reach in almost every African country. With your generosity, we can change this by providing 100 vulnerable South African children with heart surgery at no cost to their families.

title: Save a child heart in Mexico
description: In Mexico there's no enough hospitals to take care of children with congenital heart disease, so sometimes families need to travel long distances to see a heart pediatrician.  We're in Guadalajara, Jalisco, and take care of the children from around, so they don't have to go to Mexico City, because families cannot afford to pay for medical attention and transportation. We need help to be able to save the life of more children.

title: End youth unemployment.Support trade education.
description: Youth unemployment in Nigeria continues to rise due to lack of skilled or inability to afford the cost of training. This project will empower youth in public secondary schools with the needed hands-on skills in Electrical, plumbing and refrigeration trade to secure for gainful employment with industries or to pursue self-employment. The beneficiaries will be able to take care of their families and contribute to their communities. Over 150 girls and boys will benefit from this project yearly.

title: Statewide Flooding Recovery
description: May 2019 record rainfall has created flooding in all 77 counties in the state.  Thousands of families have been displaced and homes damaged.  Tornadoes, hail, and high winds have also added to the numbers.  Your opportunity to help families in crisis, recover homes damaged, and be the hope disaster survivors need is now.  Your funds will directly impact a families home by providing for needs like roofing, flooring, drywall...  Please help families who have no means of recovery on their own.

title: Art-Prenuership for environmental sustainability
description: This project plans to train 5000 children across West Africa and we utilize fun and creative ways to introduce to  children good conservation and recycling habits, also to educate them on innovative and creative activities towards lifetime environmental sustainability.

title: Schools for Homeless children
description: HDPSL is about to initiates environmental School boarding homes for children of mudslide and Ebola. It is certainty that this kids were neglected since they have lost both parents at hand, and we making it as a dream comes true to educate this children and to achieve their goals in the near future. We are determine to improve toilets, water facilities, greenery,educational new technologies, training teachers, etc; At this very moment they are living on temporary building which are not ideal,etc

title: Welcome Home Program
description: WHP)Support Women who have transitioned into permanent housing to help them settle into their new home with confidence while providing ongoing support to ensure they maintain a successful life. DfD provides women with a Welcome Home Kit containing  new personal care products and new household supplies.  For women with children, new toys and books are included. DfD (WHP) includes five free year-long skill-building classes and self -enhancing workshops for women to participate in.

title: Literacy for 100 Vulnerable Children in Liberia
description: Teaching children to read is critical to breaking the cycle of poverty and investing in a future where every life matters. RESTORE HOPE: LIBERIA helps meet the needs of disadvantaged children in the country's remote Kolahun District. RESTORE HOPE will train 6 tutors in phonics-based literacy instruction. The tutors will provide focused after-school literacy instruction to 100 children - improving their fundamental skills, boosting their confidence, and offering them a life-changing opportunity.

title: VOCATIONAL TRAINING FOR YOUTH WITH DISABILITY
description: GCRC provides services for children and youth with disability since 2009 (GCRC, 2015) including those who come at the daily bases and for those who stay over the centre.   The aim of these services is to ensure that their talents and abilities are identified, trained to be able to use the skills back to their community.. This includes vocational and community skills such as carpentry, cooking, tailoring, chicken rearing, dairy farming, gardening, leatherwork, safety, shopping etc

title: Transform lives of 30 Filipino Leprosy Patients
description: Leprosy is a chronic, infectious disease of the nerves and skin.  It is curable yet the stigma and discrimination may last a lifetime, leading to poverty.  This project will help support the school needs, health care, and counselling of 30 Filipino children and young adults who have leprosy or whose parents have been disabled by leprosy. Formal education and skills training will enable them to gain income, escape poverty, overcome stigma and discrimination,  be productive and live with dignity.

title: "No Child Wet Behind" Diaper Bank
description: The diaper project will assist low income families in Madison County, IL  with infants to toddler age to receive the basic needs, clean diapers & wipes. On average, infants need 10 - 12 diapers a day, toddlers about 8. Disposable diapers can costs around $70 - $80 per month per baby. No state or federal child safety-net program allocates dollars specifically for the purchase of diapers. Our "No Child Wet Behind" diaper project will help fill the gap for the  families in Madison County, Illinois.

title: Water & Sanitation Needs for Ethnic Students
description: This project aims to build 5 water and sanitation facilities for 5 kindergarten schools in Nam Giang Mountainous District, Quang Nam Province, Vietnam. This will provide safe running water systems for 742 ethnic minority children who are currently living and enrolling in these schools. In addition, we will create friendly and accessible sanitation facilities that will promote daily personal hygiene in order to improve their health and reduce their school absence.

title: Support women survivors of violence in Myanmar
description: Jeepyah's safehouse provides shelter to women and often children who have survived domestic and/or sexual violence. This project will provide them with access to justice, access to healthcare, and financial independence. These three services will empower survivors to thrive despite trauma. Justice - hiring lawyers to take cases to trial Health - care for injuries, pregnancies from sexual assault, deliveries Financial Independence - vocational training, purchasing equipment, start- up costs

title: Girl Child Education
description: RASTA, a not-for-profit organization, which has been engaged in educating the poor, especially girls, since 1994, has so far educated about 23000 children.  It has won several awards for its achievements.  Rasta needs financial support to continue its good work.

title: Educate and empower 2700 students in rural India
description: This project will provide digital education, teach students managing school in a democratic way, grow their own vegetables for nutritious mid day meal.

title: 1000 Surgeries for the Poor of Kalangala:
description: The goal of our project is to offer 1000 free surgical procedures to the less privileged people in the Kalangala District of Uganda in Eastern Africa. Kalangala district consists of 65 islands with human settlement located in Lake Victoria. Many people on the islands are very poor and cannot afford medical or surgical care. For this reason, we send health aid workers to camps to save lives and rescue people from the chronic pain and disability.These procedures will include general, plastic, opht

title: Palliative Care and pain Management in Kenya
description: Access to quality palliative care is an important aspect of health care.  To achieve this, Kenya Hospices and Palliative Care Association is organizing an Annual Fundraising Dinner on 15th November 2019 at Laico Regency Hotel, Nairobi. Funds raised  will be used to improve palliative care services and offer pain management to patients in marginalized areas within the country. Bringing palliative care close to the patients in need will ease their need to travel far for access to pain relief.

title: NUTRITION AND SANITATION PROJECT IN KAGERA REGION
description: Malnutrition and poor sanitation have become the most serious public health problems and possibly leading cause of deaths whether directly or indirectly.  The most vulnerable groups in this regard are children between ages of six and five years, younger infants, older children, adolescents, pregnant women, breastfeeding women and other adults are affected.  Unsafe water, along with low sanitation and hygiene represent the leading cause of death in developing countries.

title: Opportunities and jobs to villagers in Colombia
description: The Afrodescendent community from La Boquilla has lived in extreme poverty over generations due to structural racism, slavery and inequality. They really want a better life, but struggle with how to do so in a city with so much unemployment. English is our bestbet, because in Cartagena international tourism is growing and there is a lack of local people who speak English. Through our program they will receive 200hrs of English lessons over 1yr, which will help them to communicate and find a job.

title: Food & Accommodation for young VI Entrepreneurs
description: IAB has been working for 34 + years in empowering people with visual challenges through education, training, employment, and support services. One of the new initiatives is providing training & entrepreneur kit for the young visually challenged entrepreneurs. These training provided to the young visually challenged entrepreneurs helps them to grow better and lead a dignified life.

title: Training and Sales Kit for young VI Entrepreneurs
description: IAB has been working for 34 + years in empowering people with visual challenges through education, training, employment, and support services. One of the new initiatives is providing training & entrepreneur kit for the young visually challenged entrepreneurs. These training provided to the young visually challenged entrepreneurs helps them to grow better and lead a dignified life.

title: Passing the support - From Fukushikma to Nepal -
description: This project aims to build a multi-purpose community center (health post, classroom, emergency evacuation center) for the villagers who have lost their homes by the earthquake in 2015. The building will be using a temporary housing unit from Fukushima made from Logs built after their disaster in 2011 and waiting to become a waste. The aim is to provide safe community space and education for a new building type and material the village can grow/build on empowering their economic in the long term.

title: Help cancer patients in Russia
description: We provide psychological support to cancer patients and their relatives over 18 years old in Russia across several cities (Moscow, Voronezh, Yarsolavl, Tyumen and Saratov to name a few) to help reduce mortality rate and to improve cancer patients' quality of life. This is done through organizing various programs and events, such as art therapy,  individual one-on-one psychological therapy, beauty days and so on. We also provide informational support mainly by collaborating with oncology clinics.

title: Build a school for 150 children in Burkina Faso
description: Hello! This project aims to finish building a primary school for 150 children in the remote village of Bogoya in Burkina Faso. There is no school in the area; children  have to walk for 40 km to reach the closer village, others don't go to school at all. Education is one of the key for lifting people out of poverty, it provides stability and hope! Thank to contributors we have been able to buy the land and start to dig a water well. We found water so now it's time to put the bricks up!!

title: MAMA WORKSHOP KANO STATE NIGERIA
description: This project will provide a sustainable and credible living (food, shelter and other personal needs for healthy life) for women of the marginalized community especially the young (under 25 of age) divorcee. At the end of each training sections, we will be providing start-up kits to participants for immediate operation.  The Initiative has come on board to train 100 carefully selected youths brought forward by the community head of communities identified in Kano State, Nigeria.

title: Provide Clean Water to 4000 People in the Desert!
description: This project is of extreme importance to serving humanity. By providing Clean Water to approx. 500 families in extreme far areas of Thar Desert. *(an average family size is 2 to 3 Adults + 4 to 5 Children = 8 Persons). Deep water-well's will be dug, and provided with a "hand-pump" for smooth operation, to the 10 villages (Approx. 4000 persons). A regular maintenance is necessary every year to maintain the serviceability of these wells.

title: Train Local Brigades to Fight Forest Fires in MX
description: Forest fires have increased in the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve due to climate change conditions and to human pressure  that leads to destroying ecosystems that are refuges to precious and endangered biodiversity. Currently across Mexico communities are unable to control forest fires because of insufficient resources. We seek to prevent fires by creating local rapid response brigades and by educating communities on fire prevention and the importance of forest conservation.

title: The 2019 African Primatological Society Conference
description: 60% of the World's 504 species of primates are threatened with extinction. Africa is home to a third of the World's primate species yet 'home-grown' conservation and activism remains very limited. The African Primatological Society (APS) Conference will ensure that native Africans working in the primate field across the continent - who are at the forefront of conserving Africa's biodiversity - are able to actively engage in the international arena in order to protect our remaining primates.

title: Educate 150 poor orphan girls in Kigali City
description: The project will consist of providing educational materials such as school fees, uniforms, books, notebooks, sweaters, pens, pencils etc, to 150 poor orphan schoolgirls in 2 rural areas surrounding Kigali City so that they may be able to stay to school and not go to be babysitters or stay in the streets of the city begging for money. This project will help those poor children girls to get better opportunities to be educated which will help them to get jobs in their future life.

title: VOLUNTEERCORPS TUTORING, OSUN STATE OF NIGERIA
description: VolunteerCorps is organising free intensive tutoring for 10,000 indigent senior secondary school students in public schools in Osun state of Nigeria. This increases their chances of success at the Senior Secondary Certificate Examinations and other similar qualifying examinations.  We provide free study materials   Provide free meals to students and tutors (on Saturdays when we have extended tutorial sessions).     We organise refresher courses for Volunteer tutors (public school teachers)

title: Leaders without title.
description: 18twenty8 empowers young women, between the ages of 18 and 28, by developing strategies for their educational and personal development. We encourage our beneficiaries to view higher education as an attractive and necessary tool for their long-term empowerment. Our leadership development programme for undergraduate young women address the challenges that they contend with at university and enable them to graduate as resilient leaders.

title: Environment Reporting Network
description: We are building a permanent home for environmental journalism in America and making it a permanent part of civic life. In May, we showed what the network can do. We published a project called "Middle America's Low-Hanging Carbon," a collaboration of 14 local newsrooms in the Midwest. We are expanding the network across five regions. Our model is built around collaboration, rather than competition, to better serve the public interest at a crucial time.

title: Certify Nurses with HEAL Haiti
description: We will train and certify nurses to improve healthcare delivery and provide economic mobility to at-risk populations in Haiti. A facility is pivotal to the success of our Project PREP and other programs. Small amounts given over time will help us secure a facility and conduct healthcare education and intervention programs. Do your part to improve health and education in Haiti. Be a part of something awesome.

title: Prepare Southeast Asian Women to Lead
description: Women from Myanmar, Southern Thailand and the Philippines are determined to prevent violence against women and make a contribution to peace in their communities. With the goal of protecting their communities without the use of weapons, 25 women will be brought together to learn leadership skills through training and sharing experiences with each other. You can help these women protect themselves and their loved ones as they participate and advocate in local peace processes.

title: Coach 30 African queer womxn founders & fund 5
description: As a community of 1000+ African queer womxn entrepreneurs and professionals, our mission is to empower and advance each other through access. We've set a BOLD goal to raise a minimum of $15,000 to coach 30 African queer womxn entrepreneurs and provide funding for 5 queer womxn owned businesses through the 2021 QWB+A Startups Pitch Challenge program. The first virtual business development program for African queer womxn founders. To date, we have coached 56 and funded 12 businesses!

title: Mobilizing 1000 students for Community Engagement
description: A lot of the problems facing communities in Ghana result mostly from behavioral and attitudinal problems. These include indiscriminate disposal of waste and refuse, including food particles, poor sanitary and hygiene practices. The Research and Grant Institute of Ghana (REGIG) has successfully mobilized 50 students to undertake community engagement activities in four communities to change these behaviors. REGIG is scaling-up this initiative by mobilizing 1,000 students for community engagement.

title: Send Social Leaders to Leadership Training
description: This project will raise the funds to provide full scholarships to three social leaders with limited means, Gaby, Marie, and Sachin. They will join the Perennial Fellowship, a two-week transformative leadership program in Seattle, Washington, USA.  Perennial consciously designs and facilitates experiences for social leaders to help them thrive as lifelong leaders. We understand that if leaders are to sustain their work, they must know how to live a balanced, aligned and grounded life.

title: Rwamwanja Refugee Settlement Food Forest
description: We are building a 10,000 tree native food forest at the Rwamwanja Refugee Settlement in Uganda. The settlement houses over 70,000 refugees, most with little food access or employment opportunities. Our food forest will employ refugees, provide healthy food sources, and decrease soil degradation. With a 100 acre piece of land already donated, we are raising funds for income for the refugee forest workers, tools, and seedlings.

title: T.L.P. Drug Free Youth Program
description: The Littles Project plans to provide an alternative to a negative lifestyle and negative decision-making. We offer positive community resources, assistance and provide a positive outlet for our youth.

title: Help Build Safe House for The GBV Victims in Kenya
description: Gender Based Violence (GBV) is one of the most persistent violations of human rights across the globe. According to the WHO, about one third of women worldwide have experienced violence.  In Kenya, a recent study found that 32% of young women aged 18-24 years  reported experiencing sexual violence before the age of 18. Gender-based violence reduces the bargaining power to negotiate safer sex, stay on treatment or remain in school. We plan to rescue these girls and give them holistic safe space.

title: Giving Girls Confidence: Girls on the Run - DC
description: Numerous studies have documented that girls' confidence typically peaks in grades 3-4 and then drops precipitously starting around age 10 or 11 and throughout adolescence. By donating today, YOU can help girls feel greater confidence in who they are and what they can accomplish by helping them access the character development program.   Your donation will empower 16 girls and help them find the positive in themselves and others.

title: HRFP's Safe House for 50 Minority Victims Per Year
description: The project plans to build a double story Safe House in Faisalabad, Pakistan to provide Shelter, Livelihood , Medical facilitates and Legal Aid for 50 Minority victims of religious persecutions belonging to religious minorities. Construction will be done on already available land which will later serve as sustained protection center with other possible Assistance.

title: EMPOWERING RURAL KIDS WITH GLOBAL CLASSROOMS
description: The 'Global Classroom' project is connecting rural schools in Maharashtra  to global subject matter experts online, to give rural children global knowledge, skills and exposure for quality education and confidence building. We aim to connect 1000 rural schools this year offering girls empowerment and academic excellence programs to bridge the gap. We plan to create innovative platform to engage experts in the service of rural India for IT infrastructure as well quality education improvement.

title: Build a Humanist school in Mbarara District-Uganda
description: This project will build an extension class room at Reason Foundation School to enable us enhance and extend affordable but yet quality secular education for children-at-risk and orphans, from poor families and those with special needs in Mbarara District south western Uganda. The the classroom structure will provide study space/shelter to 50 extra children to attend class in a conducive environment. currently we have limited space and yet we would love to accommodate more children.

title: e-NABLE Hands for Response & Sustainable Recovery
description: e-NABLE galvanized around the site www.enablingthefuture.org. We design, create and give away open source arms and hands to anyone, anywhere. After sending devices for 2 years to camps, we need help implementing a sustainable solution for the chapters and refugees.
