description: Embodying refugees' traumatic stories through visual expression opens our eyes to prejudices and stereotypes, sparking empathy through reflection. This art collection presents the inhuman plight of refugees while showcasing the human narrative embodied within this dark landscape. Refugee children leave everything behind, yet they hold onto their dreams. By providing educational programs to children, Education Unbound improves their future job prospects and keeps their dreams alive.

title: Food For Work (Support Flood Victim In East Nepal)
description: Food For Work is a program that feeds people and works through them to rehabilitate suffering communities. Through this program, people are given work, such as building and repairing bridges or other community resources. In return, they are paid so that they can buy food for themselves and their families. In addition, the work that they have done helps strengthen and develop their communities, many of which have fallen victim to natural disasters.

title: Help Lithuanian Kids in their Battle with Cancer..
description: This project will provide care to children with cancer in the two major hospitals in Lithuania. Medical, psychological, financial, and palliative support will be provided to the children and their families. Our new and very important project "Family home" needs a support. More information about this project added to documents . (youtube video  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9e0PQsCISY )

title: Construction of 50 rainwater tanks in Veracruz, Me
description: This project consists on the construction of sustainable rainwater harvesting systems with a storage capacity of 19 thousand liters in the region of the High Mountains in the state of Veracruz, Mexico, which will allow the supply of water for families, improving access to water, sanitation and hygiene in girls and boys living in vulnerable communities with a very high degree of marginalization.

title: Emergency flood response for Bangladesh
description: Bangladesh is prone to natural flooding. Monsoon floods wreck havoc fast. In recent years the frequency of extreme flood have increased causing severe damage to life and livelihood. The flood this year has been dreadful. 22 districts are flooded. 4 million women, children and men are living marooned in water without shelter for ten days. 12 people died. Forecasts warn new districts will be flooded as the water is moving down streams. The project will support 500 flood affected families.

title: GIVE DROPOUTS A CHANCE TO GO BACK TO SCHOOL
description: Young Focus has a strong passion for disadvantaged children who have dropped out of school, wanting to give every child - from the Smokey Mountain squatter area in Manila - the chance to discover and develop their talents, as well as recapture their love for learning. Young Focus 'Catch-UP' provides opportunities for school dropouts to go back to school through different programs, depending on age and academic level. The goal is that after a year they are ready to go to a regular school.

title: STEM, Art Education for Homeless Young People
description: This is a curriculum adapted from the previous programs for regular school children. The children will be from under served and high risk neighborhoods. The children and the young people under 18 years will receive the following art and academic classes: Painting, music, dance, mathematics, geography, science and technology. The basic computer skills as well as English language, multimedia, internet surfing, basic navigation.

title: Mangrove Information, Education & Research Centre
description: This is an URGENT APPEAL to support communities living near Sundarbans coastal areas, whose livelihoods are being impacted because of the COVID-19. They have little or no access to basic food supplies and other fundamental necessity. Your support will provide emergency foods and rehabilitation assistance to the affected families. These communities are key stakeholders in helping protect our natural environment and work closely with us to conserve ecosystem across Bangladesh.

title: Washable  menstruation kits for 1600 girls
description: Many young girls lack the adequate solutions to manage menstruation. 80% of adolescent girls use unhygienic practices such as; old rags, ashes and husk sand and many lack safe spaces for managing periods,  a crisis that contributes to school dropouts, infections, Child marriage as well as trafficking.  Hence through this project,  we want to provide sustainable washable  menstruation kits,  toilets and WASH education to all the little girls to keep them in school.

title: Reunite a HIV affected child with the family
description: Our request for support is to reunite children affected with HIV - who are currently living at our children's home. The financial support will benefit the children through basic needs, education and the medical check up so that they are not a burden to their families who are below poverty line and have very limited access to basic resources. This will also help improve their psychological and physical health .

title: Richmond Computer Centre - Erudio Project
description: The Erudio Project as part of GHISA diverse programs delivers technology and e-literacy programs to children and young adults in under-served communities with the goal of developing basic computing skills. Fundamental to this vision is that the availability of and proficiency with technology is key not only to provide people with the insight and exposure they need but also with the skills and capabilities they need in order to develop a deeper understanding of the world in which they live in.

title: #GivingTuesday - Health and Education in Uganda
description: For nearly 10 years, The African SOUP has been improving the wellbeing of its students and the community through transformative learner-centered education, income-generating activities, and early interventions addressing malnutrition and preventable disease including HIV/AIDS.   To expand and improve our supportive services, we must repair three classroom floors and renovate our students' boarding facility to increase safety and ensure students feel at home in our care.

title: Disaster Relief during heavy floods in Pakistan
description: Thousands of people affected and are still vulnerable by severe flooding in Southern and northern part of Pakistan. Recent heavy rain in Karachi and Sindh Province killed 15  people due to urban flooding and have destroyed properties and valuables of worth billion of Rupees. Donations will provide relief to survivors in the form of supplies like food, shelter,  water, and medicine in addition to longer-term recovery assistance to help residents recover and rebuild.

title: Empower Venezuelan migrants with "Yo Migro" app
description: Our project seeks to empower migrants, preventing them from being victims of abuse and violations through the delivery of reliable information in one place at their fingertips. We want to empower 20,000 migrants who need information.

title: support for Assam Flood
description: Assam is reeling under devastating floods. More than 30 lakh affected in 25 districts. Hundreds of villages are underwater and thousands of families are forced to take shelter on roads, highways and schools. As many as 83,000 people evacuated from flooded areas have been accommodated in 183 relief camps across the state. Road connectivity to Upper Assam has been cut off. Ferry services were called off earlier due to water strong currents. Agricultural activities in the state have also been hit,

title: Legal Advice for Women Prisoners
description: This project will provide free legal advice and support/intervention to women prisoners in England & Wales. In doing so we will advocate for the protection of their human rights, which are compromised by the general imbalance of power in prisons between staff and prisoners. Our interventions and legal advice (given by telephone, mail, and face-to-face outreach clinics in prisons) will ensure that the human rights of women prisoners are defended and upheld.

title: U.S. Border Crisis Children's Relief Fund
description: Children's rights continue to be violated at the border. Vulnerable and terrified, young boys and girls are being held in custody longer than the legal limit, being separated from their families, and more. Save the Children is on the ground at the U.S.-Mexico Border, assisting families who have been released from U.S. detention facilities. A donation to our U.S. Border Crisis Children's Relief Fund will support our programmatic and advocacy work at the border.

title: Let's vaccinate 1,000 Venezuelan dogs (rabbies)
description: On September, 28th we will be commemorating World Rabies Day and we need your help to continue fighting this disease in Venezuela. We want to vaccinate 1,000 dogs before the end of the year, with a special focus in Zulia State where rabies is an endemic disease.

title: Bachuma Hospital Well - Ethiopia
description: The Bachuma hospital's construction was completed roughly three years ago, however, it has yet to open due to an inadequate water supply. Due to this shortage, the hospital is unable to provide comprehensive care to the surrounding communities. VHP is committed to raising funds to construct a well and assisting in the installation.

title: Brighter Future For Australian Indigenous Youths
description: Several projects are trying to tackle the social gap among the Indigenous people in Australia. Our project is focused on the youths of Indigenous communities in Australia. These youths face many issues that lead to them dropping out education and/or ending up in the criminal justice system. Working with them our objective is to enhance their skills through ways they can relate and helping them to become ambassadors for change within their community and Australia.

title: Fighting Corruption via Reform In Moldova
description: This project will translate the Moldovan Small Enterprise Alliance's 4 years of experience dealing with corruption and bureaucracy facing Small Businesses into concrete, actionable reforms that we can champion to fight corruption.   Our members are advocating for a better future here. They are raising their voices to demand a community without corruption and the stagnation of endless bureaucracy - but we need your help. We need to hire experts to help convert our experience into real change.

title: Aid People with Disabilities in Mumbai
description: In response to an RTI in 2016, the government stated that the total population of Persons with Disability (PWD) in M East Ward, was 1,500 out of a population of 8.5 lakh (0.17%). The team at Apnalaya were concerned as the number does not align with its field experience, where Apnalaya works with over 1000 PWD in Shivaji Nagar alone - a small part of M East Ward. Apnalaya has comissioned a survey to arrive at a reliable number of PWDs to start advocacy for basic services for PWD in M East Ward.

title: Rebuild lives of 500 children affected by floods
description: This project aims at rebuilding lives of 500 children affected by the devastating Assam and Bihar floods that have displaced close to 1.11 crore people so far. CRY and partners are working to save lives and reach the most vulnerable children to provide urgent relief to hundreds of flood-affected families. There's an immediate need for items like food packets, temporary shelters with drinking water, sanitary napkins and learning material for at least the next 3 months. We need to act NOW!

title: Build a church for 628 worshipers in Kenya
description: This project will assist St.Francis of Assisi catholic church to be constructed at Kavovi villages in Machakos Catholic diocese. The proposed area has an estimated 628 direct catholic faithful's. Population is poor and unable to construct a church. This situation has forced the community to request the nearby primary school to be allowed to worship or walk for 6 kilometers to nearest catholic church.Most affected are the women with kids on their backs,children,aged and pregnant women

title: Support for Students Devastated by Homelessness
description: Every week, School on Wheels' volunteer tutors give hope, educational assistance and support to children living in homeless situations in Southern California.  We need you to support our mission so that we can provide 2300 students with one-on-one online tutoring in 2023.

title: Assam Floods Ravage Millions of Lives
description: Assam Floods Ravage Millions of Lives  Summary: Assam, a small state located in northeast India is reeling under devastating floods. More than 3 million have been affected in around 25 districts. Hundreds of villages have been inundated with several families taking shelter at the public facilities, schools and community halls. Normalcy needs to be restored at the earliest, with several million still struggling for basic necessities including food, water, medicine and shelter

title: School girl dropout empowerment with life skills
description: We work to provide the disadvantaged girl child Education and life skills to improve their lives and community. We also provide life skills to women  (Mothers) of the children in our support to better their families.

title: Improving Academic Performance of Girls in School
description: This project will build 10 girl-friendly latrines in schools if not available, train girl students to create re-usable pads using local resources, and provide financial support to 10 poor girl students in remote areas of Nepal. This project will help to improve the academic performance of school going girls in remote areas of Nepal.

title: Send Girls Back to School in Ethiopia
description: This project will keep 15 children and 4 university students in school this year. Enhance Worldwide will provide 15 children with uniforms, shoes, backpacks, books, personal hygiene and nutritious food to learn, grow and succeed. The project will provide 4 young women enrolled in university studies with tuition, books, and food while also supporting their tuition and providing transportation.

title: Transforming lives of 60 Children in Cartagena
description: This project will allow 60 children from the poorest sections of the Boston neighborhood of Cartagena to have free breakfast before going to school. These children did not have breakfast, because their family is immersed in extreme poverty and they do not have enough resources to supply this vital food and so they cannot study properly. Through this project we want to provide 60 children with food security until December, where they can have a safe breakfast, from Monday to Friday.

title: Safe Haven for 100 special strays in Colombia
description: Vivatma plans to buy its own piece of land to create a Safe Haven for the most vulnerable, non-human members of the community of Tabio in Colombia. Our target group is blind elderly homeless, often demented dogs, exposed to so many dangers. Our existing project, the House for Kids and Cats, will also become reality there.

title: Supporting New Arrivals from Venezuela to Colombia
description: As rampant inflation and political unrest intensifies in Venezuela, over one million refugees have left their homes and crossed the Simon Bolivar bridge into neighboring Colombia in the last year. Reports from Colombia estimate that more than 5,000 individuals cross the border each day, settling in adjacent camps lacking basic infrastructure. Urgent humanitarian aid is desperately needed to support Latin America's worst-ever refugee crisis with protection needs of vulnerable populations unmet.

title: Feed 50 Vulnerable Children in Uganda for a year
description: Regular, nutritious food is a basic right of any child, and vital for their development. Unfortunately, many children arrive for care at the Children's Home in a state of malnourishment.  The Victory Child Care Project - Ty Cariad Children's Home is a childcare institution approved by the Ugandan Government, with a remit to Rescue, Rehabilitate and Reintegrate the children. It currently looks after 50 children at the home, and their needs include love, security, food & nutrition, and education.

title: Rescue 20x more food in Rhode Island
description: In 2018, MEANS recovered nearly 22,000 pounds of food in Rhode Island. However, leftover food makes up nearly a quarter of Rhode Island's landfill mass. MEANS needs to do more, and with your help, we can! In Philadelphia, MEANS was able to recover 20 times more food by providing free transportation to users that don't have the resources to transport donations themselves. Given our success, MEANS plans to implement a similar volunteer transportation program in Rhode Island to expand our impacts.

title: Support visual health for 1000 Guatemalans
description: Providing solutions to common eye conditions is one of the simplest interventions to dramatically increase quality of life among the poor. In late 2022, GuateBUENA re-opened our Visual Health services for the first time since before the pandemic, offering more than 300 free eye exams and high-quality glasses at minimal cost. We are seeking your help to expand this work so that we can reach more communities with visual health campaigns, and to diagnose and treat more common eye problems.

title: C.A.R.E. Charity, Assistance, Relief, Equity
description: Charity Foundation Caritas Moldova provides medical care, home visits, and day treatment to over 100 vulnerable elderly in Chisinau Municipality and Glodeni district of the Republic of Moldova. Our beneficiaries are typically poor, and without family support, and many of them are bedridden.  Funds raised will help to accomplish their most basic needs: meals, showers, laundry services, paramedical items that will support their health/life.

title: House 50 Hurricane Survivors in the FL Panhandle
description: This project funds immediate needs services, temporary housing and transition to permanent housing for 50 of the most vulnerable people impacted by Hurricane Michael in the Florida Panhandle. Solution: housing Provides a platform for recovery Housing Provides Safety Housing Provides connection with community Housing Saves the community in emergency services

title: Buy Palestinian - Trade Shows that Create Jobs
description: Sending fresh herbs from Gaza to NYC has the potential to lift the ongoing blockade. For the past 12 years, Israel's blockade of Gaza has frozen exports at 17% of 2005 levels, closing factories and wiping-out jobs. Recently, West Bank Palestinian products were successfully shipped to U.S. buyers. Rebuilding Alliance wants to organize 'Buy Palestinian Trade Shows' timed when the herbs arrive to sign more buyers and create more jobs.  We need your help.

title: Children's Heart- LIFE-SAVING CARDIAC SURGERY
description: The Children's Heart Program aims at reducing the mortality rate in developing countries of children affected by congenital or rheumatic heart diseases, with particular attention to the less privileged population. Three pillars: LIFE-SAVING CARDIAC SURGERY - CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING - PREVENTION 8 Countries of intervention (currently) Goal 2019: to save 200 children

title: Build Container Schools For African Children
description: There are countless creches (kindergartens) in disadvantaged areas in Port Elizabeth that arent government funded & poverty stricken. Parents of children do not pay school fees. The classrooms are made of tin shacks, commonly overcrowded, cold in winter and hot in summer, with little ventilation nor space to move. We are dedicated to changing this. We buy/remodel shipping containers to create better learning environments. We also revamp the entire creche turning it into a fully fledged school.

title: UPS Batteries (uninterrupted power supply) in Pak
description: The average summer temperatures in Attock, Punjab, Pakistan ranges from 99 F to 109 F. While the 3 co-ed Morning Schools take a summer break from June 1st to August 14th, the 3 Evening Schools for Girls continue through the hot weather daily. Power cuts, commonly known as 'load-shedding,' last for many hours daily.   Barakat Pakistan obtained 4 UPS with 16 batteries (4 batteries/UPS) from a Turkish organization, TIKA, in 2015. All 16 batteries have run out completely and need replacing urgently.

title: Skills Development Center for the unemployed youth
description: The Mankosi community in South Africa deals with poverty and unemployment. In cooperation with skilled Xhosa individuals, the Skills Development Center will offer individuals the right program that provides them of insights in the possibilities of job opportunities and a sustainable income. The Skills Development Center is about regaining confidence in their own capacities and future possibilities. This way we can break the poverty circle!

title: Equip Cambodians with Tech to Protect Their Forest
description: This project will equip and train 50 Prey Lang Community Network (PLCN) members with smartphones to document forest crimes in the Prey Lang forest. Prey Lang is one of the last remaining large lowland forests in Cambodia. It is quickly shrinking due to widespread illegal logging.  The PLCN will patrol the forest and document the location and details of the crime with the smartphones. They will use this data to advocate for forest protection on social media and at national and global events.

title: Make+200 senior rescue Venezuelan dogs feel athome
description: We have +200 rescued dogs under our watch in Venezuela. They have all been rescued from extreme situations of abuse, malnourishment, sickness and hunger. Due to the crisis in our country, adoptions have stopped, abandonment has increased and most of our rescues are now senior dogs over the age of 8, very unlikely to be adopted. We are asking for your help to continue providing them with the everyday things that these seniors deserve to have so they can feel at home.

title: Create 2 Resiliency Centers in Cano Martin Pena
description: Hurricane Maria took down Puerto Rico's entire power system. There was no water, power or communications. Cano Martin Pena's community organizations performed disaster recovery without adequate resources. After Maria, Puerto Rico's government shut down 400+ schools island-wide, leaving empty buildings subject to blight. We will rescue 2 schools and create solidary-community kitchens/resiliency centers to be available during emergencies, empowering people to perform grassroots disaster recovery.

title: A safe space to grow.
description: Club de Ninos y Ninas in San Luis Potosi, works with vulnerable kids that need a safe space to grow and develop all their potential. We provide tuition in homework, to avoid school desertion, we also have fun activities like arts (dance, paintings, music) and sports (basquet, volley ball, gymnastics, tae kwondo and soccer) for our members that come from the sorrounding communities and are often children of working mothers that woul be left alone at home or in the streets without the Club.

title: YOUth can change the future for Kosovo
description: This project empowers youth from different ethnic groups in Kosovo with ways to use sport as a tool for social good to repair the divisions that continue to separate their society. PLAY International supports inspiring young people to lead the way to a more hopeful future of tolerance, acceptance and inclusion.

title: Reduce religious conflict in Sri Lanka
description: This project supports local peacebuilding in Eastern Sri Lanka, led by interfaith councils of community-based religious leaders. Their work builds social cohesion across ethnic and religious divides, and helps community members resist extremist trends.

title: Quality HIV services for youth in rural clinics
description: South Africa has the largest HIV epidemic in the world, with approx. 400 000 children aged 0-19 years living with HIV. Our goal is to keep this vulnerable population in care, however it is this group where deaths due to AIDS is not decreasing due to a number of factors. CHIVA provides a holistic approach to these challenges that improves and sustains services for our youth so they can live a long and healthy life. We invite you to join us on this journey to provide a future for our young people!

title: Ending Veteran Homelessness In Michigan
description: This project will help provide affordable section 8 housing and food to homeless veterans and less privileged in Michigan. Michigan ranks #11 (608,271) in total Veterans Population (Sources: Population, VA Office of Data Governance and Analytics, US Census Bureau County, FY 2016) and with this project, HIRED Project aim to reduce this social issue of hunger and displacements of our Service Heroes. Provide them a place to call a HOME.

title: Support Dog Welfare in Kenya
description: Homeless, Stray or abandoned dogs are a common site in all Kenyan urban centers. They are often sick, malnourished and full of lice. Children as well as adults often abuse them. Some of the dogs become feral and rabid and are a danger to the community. We are seeking to vaccinate and treat at least 10000 dogs and help other 500 that are critically ill, abused or abandoned by providing them shelter, food and veterinary care.

title: PROVIDE SAFE, CLEAN WATER FOR KIBERA SLUMS, KENYA
description: Access to safe, clean water will be located at The Centre of Love community center. The water storage and supply facility will benefit 500 households in Kibera, the largest slum in Kenya. Although Kibera has water, the supply is unreliable and the taps are often dry. Without access to clean water, disease spreads rapidly. We're committed to teaching the importance of hand washing, hygiene and sanitation throughout our community.

title: Sustain 160 Children Living with HIV in Luwero
description: This project will provide children Living with HIV of ages 0-17years with education, scholastic materials, lunch and income generating projects at household level where the child lives, address stigma and discrimination, counselling and strengthen linkage to treatment and sustain their general wellbeing.

title: Teaching 200 Impoverished Children in Madagascar
description: The Community English Center of Fort-Dauphin, Madagascar, seeks to expand their innovative education program providing language and life skills to 200 out-of-school youth in one of the poorest regions of the world - where >80% of youth don't attend secondary school and 84% live in poverty.  Equipment will expand the range and versatility of classes the Center provides. New teachers will allow more children to attend the Center, building life-skills and job prospects beyond arduous manual labour.

title: Water - Donate This Gift to 170 Kids in Uganda
description: The biggest issue in Africa is the inability to find fresh, clean water for drinking and daily living. Most people in Africa rely on surface water and don't have the technology or the money to dig wells to harvest groundwater. The mission of Smile for Africa foundation is to make the small donations add up to a big change. With our current project we will help Greenfield Kids Foundation in Kabale, Uganda and will support 170 students to have clean water.

title: Help 570 children with their educational licenses
description: Ninos de Guatemala (NDG) provides 550 low-income Guatemalan children with access to the quality education they deserve. NDG operates 3 own schools, and helps children get "skills for success"  in education and life. The skills NDG works on are: Emotional intelligence, language skills in Spanish and English, Technology and Digital Citizenship. In 2022 NDG will have a hybrid education program and will need funds to cover the 4 main educational licenses necessary for all the students in 2022.

title: Transitional housing for 10 families in emergency
description: TECHO is a youth led non-profit organization present in Latin America & the Caribbean. Through the collaborative work of families living in extreme poverty with youth volunteers. Your Donation will contribute to the work that TECHO has done with the communities by giving solutions for the housing deficit in which millions of colombian families currently are living and will provide finnacial resources to  the community development projects

title: English Skills for 10,000 Indonesian Youths
description: Solve Education! is a non-profit organization that is committed to helping children and youth around the globe receive quality, effective education. Whether these children and youth don't go to school, or the traditional education they do receive is ineffective, we are here to help. Our team is made up of experienced educationists, technologists, and business executives. What do we have in common? Our driving passion is to close the global education gap, one child at a time.

title: Empower Makoko Fishing Community
description: Makoko is a huge slum in the heart of Lagos, Nigeria. It is also a fishing community, this project would empower the fishing community in the area with better equipment to increase their fishing yield and boost their income. Equipping these fishermen with better equipment would boost fishing and thus stimulate the local economy. Helping the Makoko Fishing community would alleviate poverty, provide food, and increase decent work and economic growth

title: Medical care for 400 children in Equatorial Guinea
description: Our project consists of direct intervention of pediatric surgeons and other specialties, from the two best hospitals in Spain that travel to Equatorial Guinea to care for children and their families, who in other circumstances could not access adequate medical care. They are two teams of volunteer doctors who perform medical consultations and surgical interventions. We want to obtain financing to pay for some of the medical material they will use.

title: Kick out Child abuse in Shinyalu/ikolomani kkc
description: Western Young Leaders Society is a civil nonprofit organization anchored in grassroots initiatives inspiring the community in addressing social injustices brought by human rights violations and all form of abuse hindering the well being of the society. We do this by engaging the community leaders like Chiefs, opinion leaders and religious leaders. We use the leaders to conduct mobilization and use their platforms to provide awareness and sensitization. We seek to address the a societal taboos.

title: "Pattal Dawat" :) Sponsor food plates for children
description: We look after 560 underprivileged kids from the lower Himalayas - education inclusive of nutrition, healthcare and more, books, uniforms and exposure. But our kitchen needs a makeover now and we're hoping you will help us with it! Used extensively over the years, our plates are now dented or cracked and call for urgent replacement. To inculcate proper eating etiquette, we also want to start encouraging children to eat their meals with spoons and not by hand.

title: Support Self-Help Groups for Women in Ethiopia
description: This project will work to support and establish 50 Self-Help Groups to empower 1,000 vulnerable women in Ethiopia. The foundation of the Self-Help Groups is the belief that women have the power to address needs in their community when equipped with knowledge and expertise. Within the groups, the women gain self-esteem and confidence to change their situations through saving and training. They gain skills in business development, prepare a business plan and become skilled in financial management.

title: Creating 2,000 Jobs for Jobless Nigeria youths
description: We are training 2,000 Nigerian youths with vocational skill and equip them with necessary tools as a mean of creating Self-reliance Jobs for teaming unemployed Nigerian youths  and women which will definitely save many life against premature death arising from criminal engagement altitude of Jobless youths in search of daily survival. .This project  is targeted at providing Vocational job acquisition for 60,000 youths  over a period of 4 years to better their future.

title: Recycle Storages for 17 Villages of Java Island
description: Indonesia has been being the second biggest plastic waster in the World, after China. Those plastic mostly end up in the ocean. It formed gigantic plastic soup, which travels arround the world. It kills marine lifes. Seafoods deliver poisons into our plates. Our children are on danger. We need to stop this catasthrope. Greenwave NGO strives to facilitate people in Pacitan regency to sort their waste from home. By donating to this project you save the planet earth from the household levels

title: Sponsor 18 Kindergartners at Yaowawit in Thailand
description: This project provides healthy meals, clothing, health care, hygiene items, and study materials to 18 kindergarten students on a semester basis. Yaowawit selected these children because they come from underprivileged families-some have no parents, and others suffer from various kinds of abandonment. Yaowawit provides these disadvantaged children with free quality education, life-skill training, dormitories, and above all a safe home where they can grow up as happy children.

title: Feed 1000's of children in Africa - Project Hunger
description: This project aims to address the issue of severe, acute malnutrition which is a crisis among the children of our country. Many children do not attend school as they are too hungry to concentrate, or get sent to school with empty bellies and no lunch or snacks. Through this project, we can provide food to more schools in impoverished areas, reaching more children who would otherwise go hungry.

title: Fly High! Empower Disadvantaged Children in Taiwan
description: 60 children live in MSM children's homes in New Taipei City and Hualien. They are mainly from dysfunctional families with issues like poverty, abuse, and abandonment, etc. They often suffer from trauma and low self-esteem. This project provides a safe environment to them and striving to equip them for future life; helping them to discover their own potentials and find out their own advantages via self-reliant training, character-building course, and mental health counseling.

title: corona virus relief fund for India
description: You can help communities all over India stop the COVID-19 pandemic.  The Covid-19 has been spreading fearlessly in India. We are donating equipment to the hospitals in order to save as many lives as possible in this pandemic situation. We are also delivering grocery bags with food and products to the over 700 citizens and single moms, donating sanitizing kits in order to support them soon

title: HOPE BEYOND CANCER
description: This project aim at improving  life of cancer survivors through psycho-social support, home visit and home based palliative care. your support and contribution to this project will improve  patient survivorship.

title: Assisting 5600 hurricane Irma survivors in Florida
description: The Resilience through Education and Design Clinics focus on educating property owners and renters, design professionals and contractors on the process of holistic, survivor-centric recovery.  Through expert-organized forums and community engagement, REDC aims to bridge the knowledge and action gap for residents and businesses of northeast Florida affected by hurricane Irma.  The program's goal is to empower families and neighborhoods that have fallen through the cracks of the recovery efforts.

title: Children with Disabilities in Todos Santos, Mexico
description: You can help improve the quality of life for up to 50 children with various syndromes and disabilities by providing treatment and therapies. This care is not covered by government-funded medical insurance, and families cannot afford this care without your support. You will provide cognitive, speech, equine, and vocational therapies, as well as therapies for autism. Children in our program also receive medical evaluations and treatments in addition to psychological and social work support.

title: "What is Google?"
description: Imagine not knowing what Google is, or how to use the Internet. We give people the skills they need to join the digital age so they, LIKE YOU, can use it to look for work, promote a business, learn a skill, or access information. Millions in South Africa cannot and do not know where to start. Many have a smartphone but only use it for WhatsApp or Facebook. Does this matter? Yes. "Digital skills provide the poor a catalyst to break out of the cycle of poverty and empower themselves." G20, 2018

title: Build for Unity
description: Austin Habitat's integrated community collaboration build. The Build for Unity house bands together members from all communities, both interfaith and intercultural, to create a home for a local family. This project showcases the best of what Austin is: a city that celebrates diversity, inclusion, and home.

title: educate 100 orphans for one year in uganda
description: This project will sponsor 100 orphans in school through feeding, tuition fees, scholastic materials and other school requirements for one year in Uganda at New Junior school Mityana

title: We can all be Stewards of Children
description: Stewards of Children is a 2.5 hour group prevention-education program, developed by Darkness to Light, Inc, and presented locally by Lampion Center. The training provides adults with important facts about the prevalence of child sexual abuse, how to prevent it, and how to get help for those already affected. It highlights steps necessary to protect children. The SOC program is evidence informed and proven to help adults reduce, prevent, and respond to occurrences of child sexual abuse.

title: Nutritious food for TB patients in South Sudan
description: Charity and Empowerment Foundation (CEF) support undernourished patients of tuberculosis (TB) in South Sudan by providing them with nutritious food to prevent them contract diseases resulting from under nutrition. Through provision of nutritious food, we are helping 100 TB patients overcome the effects of the disease and recover from the sickness

title: USD 10 educates a child for a year in South Sudan
description: Charity and Empowerment Foundation (CEF) supports children in rural villages of South Sudan to access primary education through the supply of exercise books, mathematical sets, pens, pencils, schoolbags, chalkboards, and chalks. Through the supply of exercise books, mathematical sets, pens, pencils, schoolbags, chalkboards, and chalks, we are helping 10,000 children from 50 primary schools in Jonglei and Northern Bahr El Ghazal to achieve their dream of bright future.

title: Taking WASH to rural Tiar-aliet in South Sudan
description: Charity and Empowerment Foundation (CEF) support children in rural villages of South Sudan to access primary education through the construction of fit latrines and hand-washing facilities, and hygiene promotion campaign. Through construction of fit latrines and hand-washing facilities, and hygiene promotion campaign, we are helping 9,344 children from 34 primary schools in Northern Bahr El Ghazal to achieve their dream of bright future.

title: Education & Empowerment for Girls in Guatemala
description: The MAIA Impact School provides a holistic education with an equal focus on academics, culture/identity, and personal development for 150 girls (grades 7-9). Creating a generation of empowered female leaders who can lead choice-filled lives and ignite transformational change. The combination of local leadership and deep engagement with families creates an ecosystem of support that meets the unique needs of marginalized indigenous girls in rural Guatemala to create long-term, sustainable impact.

title: Renew CATS (Community Animals To Service)
description: There are two phases under our project. First, we will implement a program that will increase our capacity to provide mass sterilizations and freedom flights for hundreds of cats every year and secure a long-term location for rescued cats and kittens until they are ready for adoption. The second phase will focus on creating wider social impact by creating jobs and improving mental health support for Puerto Ricans.

title: Support 1000 young mothers with beehives in Uganda
description: Budongo Women Bee Enterprises (BUWOBE) supplies young mothers in sugarcane-dominated mid-western Uganda with five beehives each to produce honey, increasing their income by up to 60%. Sugarcane fields occupy most arable land, affecting 20,000+ immigrants, including young mothers, who can spend over 10 hours a day working to feed their families. The BUWOBE Cooperative trains the young mothers on less time intensive, eco-friendly honey & byproduct producing skills, and provides access to markets.

title: First Pediatric Hospice in South America
description: We will build the first pediatric hospice where cancer and non-cancer children can live with their families in their final stage of life. With the technical advice of the EKR Chile Foundation, we will create a building of approximately 800 m2, where we will receive 9 children with their families so that a space for children entering palliative care.  We need to equip each building space according to the medical conditions indicated by the doctors.

title: Empower 50 refugee children in Armenia
description: As a consequence of the armed conflict in Syria, millions of people have been forced to leave their homeland and seek refuge in different countries. This project will help 50 Armenian refugee children from Syria overcome this crisis and the ensuing challenges it has caused by providing them with psychosocial support.

title: Safe water springs for 3118 people in Ruteete
description: The project will construct 6 protected water springs in 3 villages of Kyamusa Kyairweisenya and Kimuhon which will serve over 3118 people who are in dire need of safe  (hygienically clean), and reliable water as per our field visits. The provision of protected springs will significantly reduce water borne diseases and will improve the health of women and girls. Children's performance in schools will increase as they will easily fetch water and women will have time for more profitable activities.

title: Inspire & Empower Girls to Pursue STEM
description: Career Girls inspires and educates girls to pursue careers in Science, Technology, Engineering, Math (STEM) and beyond. Career Girls built and continues to expand the largest girl-focused online career knowledgebase, featuring 11,000+ videos of diverse women who are accomplished in their professions. This project will amplify our work and bring STEM career resources and inspiration to even more girls.

title: Provide literacy to vulnerable adults in Colombia
description: With this project, Bien Humano Foundation provides quality education to Colombian adults in vulnerable conditions, who do not know how to read or write, or have not finished primary school and who cannot otherwise access or afford it, allowing them to access the basic right of education that for some reason was denied to them. The training processes are aimed at acquiring basic reading, writing and arithmetic operations skills applicable to the context, improving the daily life of each student.

title: "Dirt Girls" Can Close the Gender Gap in STEM
description: Dirt Girls is an empowerment program dedicated to exploring scientific habits of mind through garden-based learning. Grounded in research-aligned approaches to identity development and environmental education, Dirt Girls has the potential to inspire dozens of girls to pursue STEM careers. Outdoor sessions engage youth in authentic projects that teach how to care for plants, ourselves, and each other. Cross-age interaction and mentoring promotes relationships that grow long-term resilience.

title: Provide education to over 150 children in Belize
description: Global Aid Consultants addresses the social problem of improving educational opportunities to communities in need. Our actions are proactive contributions to decreasing human trafficking, poverty, and violence. Global Aid Consultants solution is to show that access to early education (K-12 grade) promotes autonomy for self-determination and creates lifelong success.

title: Help 40 pregnant adolescents build bright futures
description: This project will provide the first health and empowerment workshops for pregnant adolescents at El Centro De Salud El Vallado in Colombia. The girls range from ages 12-17 and will be guided through a series of workshops sought to inform and inspire their path to motherhood and beyond. Held in partnership with the local medical center, informative health talks, mindfulness practices, and vocational education will be provided in order for our participants to feel empowered to take on the future.

title: After-School Program for children in Nepal
description: SuMa After-School provide academic, emotional, and medical/nutritional support for close to 200 children living in extreme poverty in Nepal. Our program provides a safe place away from traffickers; healthy meals and regular medical checkups; and a creative, hands-on STEM curriculum that teaches students how to think critically and creatively. Our mission is to provide pathways out of poverty for Nepal's most vulnerable.

title: Pray & Help for Heavy rain flood affected Nilgris
description: Monsoon has wreaked havoc in Kerala. Red alert has been issued in four districts - Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad - following heavy spells of rain, gusty winds and landslides across the state. The second spell of the south-west monsoon intensified, resulting in such deluge. Water levels in most of the rivers and dams across the state have risen flooding nearby areas. VETNGO fundraise to support Wayanadu and Pandalur affecetd areas. 9951 displaced people in camps.

title: Build school in rural Uganda for children in need
description: The Create Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization with the mission of empowering the youth of Uganda and creating lasting positive change by constructing and operating an eco-friendly, sustainable Secondary School which will provide children in need a 100% free education, as well as serve members of the local community through job opportunities, educational programs and community outreach initiatives.

title: Holistic School Sponsorship for 20+ Swati Students
description: This project provides 20+ orphaned and vulnerable Swati high school students with all the tools they need to succeed in school, and enter the next phase of life as confident, motivated and responsible young adults. Along with providing all necessary materials and tuition costs to attend school, we also teach sustainable skills, host motivational workshops and provide guidance, mentor-ship and psycho-social support to our sponsored students within Lobamba Lomdzala, Eswatini (FKA Swaziland).

title: Covid-19 & Preventing Homelessness for Veterans
description: A roof over your head is a fundamental human right; Yet homelessness is part of a bigger picture negatively impacting on society. Working at grass roots level we support a very vulnerable section of the population; those who often have nowhere to go and who without our support would become street sleepers.     Covid-19 saw much of essential support going 'virtual' and it has stayed that way. We deliver face to face support, in real time, to real people who want to live in their communities.

title: Educate and support 65 orphans in Kenya
description: Many people in the world easily take for granted the positive things that life has offered like a family, an education and a place to call home. But there are millions of children in Kenya who are abandoned, orphaned and vulnerable. To survive they need help. Ntimi Home of Hope aims to alleviate poverty and facilitate lasting change in the lives of orphans and the most vulnerable children and families living in Kenya through education, health and livelihood programs.

title: Empower and Educate Vulnerable Ugandan Girls
description: Imagine a girl, the daughter of an abusive, alcoholic mother, feeling left with no option to feed herself other than prostitution. Girls like this roam the rat-infested, flooded alleys of Kampala's Namuwongo slum every day, scavenging for food and searching for shelter. Uganda Hands for Hope aims to alleviate their poverty and facilitate lasting change in the lives of the most vulnerable children and families living in Namuwongo through education, health and livelihood programs.

title: Sailing to Cohesion (S2C)
description: We are looking for funds to run the Sailing 2 Cohesion (S2C) project. It will be a social cohesion project using restorative justice values and sailing as vehicles for bringing disabled and able young people together to reduce prejudice and negative stereotyping, while reducing their isolation, improving their health and increasing their skills and confidence.

title: Building Classrooms for Zvamaida Primary School
description: UPDATE - THE 6 CLASSROOMS HAVE NOW BEEN BUILT. WE NEED MORE FUNDS THOUGH TO COMPLETE THE PROJECT- The school furniture of desks etc is currently being supplied. The school library - currently built to foundation level, needs completing, which is our next priority. To follow this will then be solar panel and electricity, more toilets, and wash basins. The children now all have classrooms to be taught in and desks coming soon.  Children and community delighted and grateful!

title: LWFCI SPORT CLUB - Football for young people
description: LWFCI-UK Sports Club is an inclusive sports club for boys, girls and women of all abilities . The aim is to develop people's confidence, aspirations, improved relationship and social development as well as improving physical and mental well-being.  We are seeking for funding to expand football projects engaging more young people in sports and offering opportunities to our young people to learn play football and also providing exercise fitness and yoga for women and girls to keep fit for life.

title: Spay and Neuter Cats and Dogs in Rural Eswatini
description: SAWS plans to sterilize 150, and provide basic veterinary care to at least a further 240 cats and dogs from low income households in rural Eswatini.  Due to high incidence of poverty, these households are not able to cater to the needs of their animals, which results in high mortality rate caused by diseases, uncontrolled breeding and emaciation.  This project will improve the quality of life of cats and dogs in selected communities in need by providing them with the much needed veterinary care.

title: Kerala Floods 2019 - Relief & Rehabilitation
description: Monsoon fury has once again descended on Kerala. Torrential rains are wreaking havoc on the people who are still recovering from last year's flood, which was the worst in a century. Massive landslides have already claimed more than 30 lives in a single day, with many more missing. Over 70,000 people are in relief camps. This project aims to provide urgent relief and rehabilitation support to the people of Kerala, to overcome the current calamity.

title: Empower Young Women to be Leaders, India
description: WEP enrolls young marginalized women (ages 15 to 24) in our Leadership Academies, at grassroots NGO partners across India.  Academy students learn to make informed choices for themselves and positive change in their families and communities. Within a spirited community of peers, they gain knowledge, skills, and an understanding of their opportunities. Alumnae receive scholarships to training and higher education before entering formal sector careers or alternative livelihoods.

title: Covid-19 for Mexico: education cant stop
description: This project plans to give 300 mexican vulnerable children a free community musical education during the COVID-19 contingency in the middle area of San Luis Potosi, Mexico. We will give them virtual classes with professional personal in places where violence, drug traffic, alcoholism, and other social problems are.

title: Give Light to S. Sudan Refugee Children in Uganda
description: Give Light to South Sudan Refugee Children in Uganda is an initiative to provide 100 solar lamps and Solar power to Children and villages in Bidibidi refugee settlement zone 1 that have no access to Electricity or light source at night to allow them read or revise their books at night.

title: Camp for Disadvantaged Youth in Lesotho
description: Mosepele Foundation Development Forum plans to build camp to provide weekly intensive leadership training, personal development and business enrichment skills and activities to the disadvantaged youth in Lesotho. These individuals will be hosted at the camp in a weekly period undergoing indoor and outdoor enrichment activities that will help them to be more effective in life. The project will impact 4700 disadvantaged youth in a year.

title: SUPPORT A CHILD WITH DISABILITY ACCESS THERAPY
description: The project intends to improve the progress of children with disability, prevent regression and loss of achieved motor functions. Occupational therapy exercises will help the child develop and coordinate accurate movements of speech apparatus which will help produce of speech sounds. Physiotherapy will ensure functional independence which will lead to inclusion of children with disability in various projects as one of the pillar for vision 2030

title: Help Syrian Children with Cancer in Learning!
description: Children with cancer have a hard time managing at school while having to face periodical treatment courses, which happen during school-time. Therefore they are not able to keep up with their lessons. Our project will work with 6 teachers on offering additional lessons and activities to 50 children with cancer from poor families. This will help build self-confidence and improve their mental state after being behind their friends at school for so long because of their treatment courses.

title: Transforming the lives of rheumatic patients
description: Fundacion Maritere will open a clinic based on an integral attention model for low income rheumatic patients in the state of Puebla, Mexico. This clinic provides physiotherapy, psychological, medical and nutritional intervention, as well as training for self-employment all in a single space. The mission of the project is to avoid disability and improve the lives of more than 100 patients and their families, through movement recovery, emotional and physical improvement, and employment.

title: Send 100 Girls to school in Nepal
description: ADWAN has been working for 20 years to send Dalit and poor girls to primary school through high school.  Help us reach our biggest challenge yet - supporting an education for 100 girls to attend high school, which is not free.  We at ADWAN know that education is the most lasting and effective way girls and their families can escape the cycle of poverty and discrimination.  Education is a double investment - in the girls as well as in the future of their families, society and country.

title: Hurricane Dorian Disaster Relief Bahamas - Jezreel
description: This project will meet the initial recovery needs of the most destitute of families who have been devastated by Hurricane Dorian. The needs are overwhelming and we are doing all we can.   Items included in each shipment can be: nonperishable ready to eat foods, baby and children's supplies,  personal hygiene products, new bedding, disinfectants, cleaning supplies, garbage bags,  building supplies and so much more. ... Jezreel has sent 12 shipments of aid to date with 5 more in preparation.

title: Help Build 8 Classrooms Destroyed By Flood Waters.
description: Last year, all the eleven classrooms were swept by floodwaters displacing 400 pupils. Currently, most of these pupils are learning under trees. We do our best to get the kids back to their school. So far, well-wishers have helped rebuild 3 of the 11 classrooms. The remaining 300 children are in urgent need of support to rebuild the remaining 8 classes.

title: Provide Adaptive Art for a Child with Disabilities
description: Ephraim's House plans to offer a free four-week adaptive art enrichment program for 10 children with significant learning needs who reside in low-income neighborhoods south of Chicago.

title: Support 13 villages to save the Bornean Rainforest
description: The Bornean Rainforest is home to immense biodiversity and hundreds of Indigenous communities but is one of the world's most endangered ecosystems. Much like the Amazon, socio-economic inequalities are root causes of practices like forest burnings wildlife poaching, and oil palm plantation expansion. Planet Indonesia's SMART Patrol program works with local community members to form patrol teams to deter illegal activities while working with poachers and loggers to build alternative livelihoods.

title: Flood Damage at M'Lop Tapang
description: In August, 2019, M'Lop Tapang's Education Center as well as our Arts Center and Transitional Home were severely damaged due to flooding. In addition to structural damage caused by the water, the floods also resulted in damaged furniture, equipment, computers, and many other supplies. The costs of recovery will be in the tens of thousands of dollars.

title: Heart Surgery for 100 Children in South Africa
description: 3,500 South African children will have a treatable form of congenital heart disease this year and they will die if they do not receive corrective surgery. Prof. Kinsley has done countless surgeries and saved thousands of lives.  Although he donates his time and expertise, he cannot do it alone. Donations are needed for correct cardiac diagnosis and rehabilitation of these children. We now have the technology to save young lives. We must bring it to those in need. Donate to save a life!

title: Help Ugandan Children Thrive at School
description: This project will serve 6,416 Ugandan children at 20 rural primary schools by building strong, collaborative education communities that are empowered with the tools they need to improve education quality for their children.  We believe that local communities hold the keys to drive lasting, transformative change at their school. Our work supports them to achieve this ambition.

title: Educate 150 poor orphan girls in Kigali City
description: The project will consist of providing educational materials such as school fees, uniforms, books, notebooks, sweaters, pens, pencils etc, to 150 poor orphan schoolgirls in 2 rural areas surrounding Kigali City so that they may be able to stay to school and not go to be babysitters or stay in the streets of the city begging for money. This project will help those poor children girls to get better opportunities to be educated which will help them to get jobs in their future life.

title: Train Communities in Trauma Informed Care
description: Mental Health has become the second global pandemic, impacting nearly every human on the planet. Our project equips leaders around the world with culturally responsive mental health knowledge and skills via an online self paced certification course designed for everyday lay persons. Topics include how to cope with stress, anxiety, and trauma and promote self and community resilience, so survivors can heal themselves, support others, and break generational cycles of trauma and harm.

title: Trauma Informed Care Trainings in Nepal
description: This project provides trauma healing for thousands of survivors of trauma and violence in Nepal. Each year, our local team trains hundreds of teachers, parents, and community leaders to become Healing Advocates, so they can disrupt cycles of trauma and violence in their families and communities. They also host a mental health podcast to break silence and stigma about mental health.

title: LIBRARIES AND TOILETS FOR RURAL SCHOOL KIDS
description: This organisation was formed after being moved by the story of a grandmother who walked several miles in search of a pencil so that her grandchild could attend school Pencils and Smiles is an initiative that aims to alleviate the effects of poverty, empower neglected communities, improve standards of living and seeks to bridge the gap between education and poverty. We started by distributing pencils to every child, we are now looking into building libraries and building toilets for rural schools

title: Bring water to health clinic, 500 villagers in CAR
description: This project will provide running water for Senitizo's maternal and child health center in the Central African Republic, as well as provide access to safe drinking water for the population in the immediate vicinity of the health center (roughly 500 inhabitants). It has three main components; digging a well, building a water tower, and installing indoor plumbing in the health center.

title: Giving Health. Giving Life. Giving Tuesday.
description: At the Foundation for African Medicine and Education (FAME), we believe that everyone should have access to compassionate, high-quality health care. With 27,000 patient visits annually, FAME seeks to raise funds this Giving Tuesday to boost our sustainability and life-saving work across departments: Outpatient Clinic, Inpatient Clinic, Laboratory, Radiology, Labor & Delivery, and Maternal & Child Health Services. Please join us on Giving Tuesday to support healthcare in rural Tanzania.

title: Floods wreak havoc in India
description: Rains intensified in many parts of the flood-hit states including Kerala, Maharashtra and Karnataka where over 12 lakh people have been affected. The death toll is rising and people are losing their lives due to monsoon fury.  Kerala - The landslides at Kavalappara and Puthumala in Malappuram and Wayanad districts have worsen the situation and more than 50 people are missing.  Karnataka - The death toll rises to 48, while 12 are still missing and subsequent landslides are reported in the state.

title: Help Flood Victims in Culvert community, Freetown
description: The flooding took place on Friday, 2nd August, 2019 in several communities in Freetown, including Culvert, one of the most affected communities. So many houses were destroyed in that community. The tragedy has left more than 13,000 homeless and majority of the survivors are children and women who need urgent recovery from this disaster.

title: Informal to Formal Entrepreneur and Business
description: Informality has too much effects on the economic accountability and growth. Economic freedom is hindered in such circumstances, entrepreneurs won't see business as a means of economic freedom couple with the too many constraints of being informal. In Cameroon majority of the  Small and medium size enterprises (SMEs) are informal - a recent study showed that. This project provides a sure way for converting informal entrepreneurs to formal businesses for their long term sustainability of SMEs.

title: BUILD SCHOOL FOR CHILDREN FROM LOW INCOME FAMILIES
description: This project will help to expand our registered daycare center from daycare program to primary school program, and will help 94 children from marginalized families of Muriet ward, in Arusha Tanzania to able to join primary school after completing the daycare program. When the project will complete, it will help children to acquire quality education which would be difficult for them to acquire from profit based schools.

title: Self Defense: Empowering Women of Kurdistan
description: World Council of Credit Unions recently visited refugee camps in Kurdistan. Many women left behind in the war on ISIS were powerless. Many have been beaten, abused and suffered unspeakable violence. One such camp recently started offering self defense training for women and girls and through this activity, have regained a sense of self-confidence and dignity. World Council would like to support these classes into the future and is seeking to raise $25,000 for support in 2019-2020.

title: CLIMATE CRISIS: AMAZON&AFRICA WILDFIRE RELIEF FUND
description: Wildfires are burning "Earth's lungs". While the world has been shocked by the Amazon fires, across the Atlantic Ocean, similar blazes are burning across central Africa. In NASA images, forest fires in central Africa appear to burn alarmingly like a red chain from Gabon to Angola. International leaders at the G7 summit have agreed to provide logistical and financial support to help fight fires in the Amazon rainforest.

title: Educate 40 Widows and vulnerable children in Jos
description: This project will educate 40 widows, their wards and underpriviledged youths in Jos,  Nigeria. Providing free education to the girl child and other youths who hail from the poorest sections of society will help them attain their fullest potentials and be self reliant.

title: Provide shelter for 50 at risk girls in Cameroon
description: Survivors' Network plans to provide a temporary shelter to 50 displaced women who are at risk of being trafficked in the South West region of Cameroon. Women will be provided with accommodation and essential services, such as medical assistance, psychological support, and food. They will also receive skills training and help setting up a business.   As the armed conflict continues in the South West region of Cameroon, many people are fleeing rural areas in the hope of finding safety.

title: Give to starving families in Yemen
description: It is the biggest humanitarian crisis in the world: the conflict in Yemen that has been going on since March 2015 has plunged the country into immense hardship. More than 24 million people depend on humanitarian aid - around 80 percent of the population. Together with our partner organisations, we are on the ground to prevent  hunger and  the spread of diseases.

title: 6,000 BREAKFASTS A WEEK FOR CHILDREN IN TANZANIA
description: Following a successful pilot project, we'll roll out this project to more primary schools on the island of Ukerewe in Lake Victoria (Tanzania).    Schools there have adjacent land which is uncultivated. We set up an environment club, train pupils & selected staff to grow sogum crops for own consumption. Surplus is sold to buy seed, school kit eg chalk, pens & paper.  Porridge is cooked and served by pupils to typically 500 kids 3 days a week encouraging  attendance and improving concentration.

title: Veteran and Family Members Appreciation Day
description: This is a day of fun and family enjoyment to help breakup the stressors of life in and out of the military.  Veterans suffering from some form of disability have a harder time connecting with family.  Injury's from a deployment last forever and so do the memories made with a parent. This music and comedy festival will help veterans reconnect with their children and spouse. Rides, Face Painting, Balloon Animals, comedy and music, this is how you through a party for a Veteran and their kids.

title: Combatting child marriage in rural Malawi
description: This project will deliver a series of ten locally led workshops tackling the issue of child marriage and sexual violence against women and girls. Each workshop will be for a maximum of 20 girls aged between 10 to12 years old. The intended result of these workshops is to provide support and education, raise awareness of child marriage and encourage community dialogue on these issues. The workshops provide a space for girls to talk about these issues, where it takes away the shame and stigma.

title: Educational Camp
description: This educational camp allows children to have a closing of the year in which they thank for everything shared. 70 children are the beneficiaries of this unique opportunity in which they live during a weekend in nature and doing recreational activities. These children live in a critical context with high social vulnerability, so an experience of this style allows them to leave this world of violence and daily restlessness. In the camp they go to the beach, they play, we make a stove with dances,

title: Bring Computers to Orphan Students in Tanzania
description: Orphans Africa's project is to bring computers, accessories, printers and a power grid to the students at Mwaji Secondary School in rural Western Tanzania.     These students started their education in a bamboo and thatch hut and would be thrilled to have computers in their new school.  They know learning with modern technology would be a tremendous advantage to furthering their education.  Be a computer hero and help the students raise themselves out of poverty!

title: Livelihood & Life Skills for Impoverished Youth
description: Kenya has one of the world's largest youth populations - over 75% of its 45 million residents are under 30. Of these, 14% are unemployed and about 25% are underemployed.  With only 1 in 10 attending university, most lack formal sector job skills. This project will provide in-demand trades, entrepreneurship and computer training, health education, and life skills support to youth from the informal settlements in Nyeri. Our goal is to help youth lift themselves from poverty through employme.

title: Books for Kids Ghana Africa
description: Project Description: Footprint will assist children in rural areas of Ghana, Africa achieve their full potential with support they need for education. We will deliver 6,000 books to 1,500 elementary students.  The books are READY TO SEND.  Once the books arrive the work starts and a lending library will be set up.  But first we need the shipping charges and then kids can read to their hearts content!  Help please.

title: Sustainable Farming to Relieve Hunger in Malawi
description: Most of those who live in East Africa see wide, treeless vistas of straggly corn, degraded, dusty, red soil. Rains are increasingly unpredictable and storms more terrible. Temperatures are rising, crop pests multiplying and old diseases spreading again. Every year, fires rage across the countryside, the smoke reddening the sun and killing thousands of the young and elderly.  Sustainable farming with Biochar offers a simple, easily accessible solution to many of the problems and feed thousands.

title: Sponsor meals for indigenous Taiwanese children
description: Bright Side provides year round nutritious plant-based meals to indigenous children in two regions of Taiwan who lack access to  cooked meals on weekends when food programs do not provide services.  For 7 years we have been combating malnutrition and food insecurity in our day camps on weekends by creating food with children to empower them with basic kitchen skills and to prevent hunger pangs. Funds also supports quarterly delivery of rice and other staple foods to 25 indigenous families.

title: Help Survivors of Trauma and Violence in Mosul
description: Thousands of women, men and children who survived the three-year ISIS occupation live without access to medical treatment. Many survivors suffer from Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression or chronic pain. Additionally, there is urgent need for surgical interventions and sustained medical treatment. In 2018, Jiyan Foundation established a treatment center in Mosul where doctors and psychologists treat survivors and provide transportation to our center, free of charge.

title: Afforestation project for liberated areas in IRAQ
description: Plants, including trees, especially within cities, are one of the urban development signs and increasing awareness in these communities, which is the immune resistance to climate Circumstances and consider as lung for cities which witness population and urban growth to compensate the rate of the oxygen decrease in these cities, after the occupation of the terrorist groups to Mosul city, the surrounding towns about it and the continuation of military operations for several years

title: Livelihood supports for poor IDPs in Borno State.
description: This project will build the capacities of 120 IDPs  from 3 LGAs badly affected by the Boko Haram insurgency in Borno State who will produce and disseminate 50000 efficient biomass briquettes to 1000 displaced households for their cooking needs. In addition, it will provide food, clothes, quality mobile healthcare services and improved living conditions for victims of Boko Haram insurgencies in 3 IDP camps. The project will also support the education of 50 separated children in the area.

title: Ndihmojme vullnetaret kunder COVID-19
description: Numerous volunteers have joined the fight against COVID19, serving the country in these hard times of pandemic entirely on a voluntary basis. But the conditions in which they are operating are unfortunately not at all satisfactory and safe; lack of essential hygienic materials, food meals, sleeping spaces for volunteers from other cities engaged in Prishtina, etc., make their mission more difficult. Let's help the volunteers by donating to this fund!

title: LAND PURCHASE TO BUILD A NEW SCHOOL (MOA)
description: Mentor Orphans Africa is non-governmental, not for profit organization that was established to help support orphaned and vulnerable children access basic needs i.e. better health services, education, and shelter among others. MOA fosters a dignified and protected life for children who have fallen victim to the scourge of poverty, solitude and are at the risk of HIV/AIDS. We aim at restoring hope and lobby opportunities for OVC in Uganda.

title: k-s-f-y
description: Kick start for the youth. We are helping the youth at an early age to the age of 35 with skills development and training in all aspects of their interest of their choices 60 people on arts,60 on free basic computer course. Arts and culture catergorically,Free computer basic course, business entrepreneurship training .This will impact on drop unemployment rate ,crime ,xenophobia will drop. The number of teenage pregnancy drop in South African Nkomazi schools in our communities of the rural areas.

title: JCO REVAMP
description: Help Jayla's Community Outreach (JCO) revamp the lives of disadvantaged women and children throughout Maricopa County, Arizona. JCO assists low income, homeless or veteran women and foster care children by providing case management and support services. JCO provides women & children with hygiene products, gently used clothes, clothing vouchers, school supplies, emergency food boxes, foster care bags, bus passes, and referrals. JCO offers life skill training and employment search assistance.

title: Agavi:  Offline Digital Learning for Ukraine
description: Digital education systems are built by privileged people for privileged people.  Everyone else is relegated to systems that were already antiquated in 2000.  This project will develop the Agavi learning system, a smartphone-based learning system that allows teachers to build immersive task-based activities for students that use the smartphone as a partner in learning (rather than a portal to videos and quizzes).  We will deploy this system in war-torn Ukraine to help students keep learning.

title: Educate & Support Underprivileged Children
description: Las Marias Education is a newly-set community project in one of the poorest regions of Argentina - Chaco, the Impenetrable. By early 2020, we plan to provide free education, health care and a balanced daily meal to 300 children in this region. Our vision is to give these children a chance to change their future and of their communities. We strive to empower children and their families to enable them to break out of a life of poverty.

title: CONSTRUCTION OF MODERN EARLY LEARNING COMPLEX
description: We are seeking your support to help CBSECEK build a Modern Early Childhood Education and Teachers Training Complex in order to help fill the gap post by Political, Social and Economic aspect within many communities in Kenya. This Complex will be a center of excellent and a learning point for the Republic of Kenya in an effort to implement SDG goal Number 4. It is designed to help CBSECEK realize the need of proper foundation in early learning. ECDE is a human right that a child must get in life.

title: Health care for the children and pregnancy women
description: Burundi is a developing country, and one of the 5 poorest countries in the world, the health system of Burundi is not more developed, there is a high rate of malnutrition, children-maternal deaths in the world.  a lack of care facilities with competent staff, the long journey that communities have to reach a health care structure is a great risk of death along the way by complications in these rural areas.

title: 2500 Waterproof Backpacks 4 students Sierra Leone
description: Backpacks for students in school is an important part of student life. Plenty of children living in impoverished communities around Sierra Leone and Nigeria are left using a plastic bag, paper bag or torn bag or simply wrap their books with a rope because parents cannot afford to buy their children one. Be Rose Foundation, will use all donations to provide 2500 students with a waterproof backpack to secure their books & school supplies during the raining season in Sierra Leone and Nigeria.

title: GIVE THESE CHILDREN LIVE WITH CLEAN DRINKING WATER
description: (DNPG) have recognize the need of help to build a small water project to maintain and protect natural source of water with a collection chamber and solar pump with substructure for the tank and water pipe as well as all necessary material around the project that everything is completely installed and the clean water for all from the line trickles. A good source of water over a drilled Borehole, situated in Jarra Barra Kunda on the arabic school.

title: Udzungwa Botanic Garden
description: We are creating a tropical botanic garden to support forest conservation. The garden will serve three purposes: (1) A seed source for rare and threatened plants, mostly trees, for use in restoring deforested areas; (2) A regional training centre for forest restoration; (3) A peaceful location for charitable ecotourism, where tourists can learn about plants and watch local wildlife [birds, monkeys, butterflies] between the excitement of the other safari adventures that the region has to offer.

title: Autistic Rehabilitation Project
description: The overall goal of the project is to contribute to the welfare of children who have autism in the Theni District.  We will work to improve their functional abilities; working with their physical & mental health needs.  We will promote awareness in local communities to address the needs of the children and their families.   The main objective of the project is to create awareness about autism, and provide assessment and focused intervention and rehabilitation.

title: Give child labourers an education in Bangladesh
description: This project will give 300 child labourers a foundation in education and support to progress into school or vocational training. The children attend regular learning periods in literacy, numeracy and life skills with specialist community teachers at education centres local to their workplace. They also get medical care, food and time to experience the joy of learning and being a child. In parallel we work with their families to help them out of poverty so they can provide for their children.

title: Safe homes and education for Child Headed families
description: Through A Family for Every Child, CPS has been working with children in Chimanimani district who were orphaned and/or separated from their families as a result of Cyclone Idai in March 2019. The loss of life led to child headed households in need of a home, nutrition and education support.
