Our research shows: our model of improved cookstoves reduce the need for fuel up to 75%. Our goal: Every household in our villages (and beyond) uses improved cookstoves, ideally with locally made bio-charcoal.

title: Save the Sea Turtles
description: This project will help us distribute wildlife crime-busting technology to sea turtle conservationists throughout Central America. The InvestEGGator is a decoy sea turtle egg embedded with a GPS tracker. We need your help to distribute these eggs so that the conservationists can use them to track the illegal trade of sea turtle eggs. Sea turtles are threatened with extinction, especially the leatherback and hawksbill turtles that nest in Central America.

title: Help BASECO Community Build Climate Resilience
description: BASECO is a densely populated slum community built on a garbage landfill, with 60,000 countryside migrants seeking a better life in the city living in poverty and hunger. They live in shanties that are constantly threatened by rising sea levels, flooding and storm surges that become worse each year. Climate change has made life more difficult but the people strive to adapt for their survival. Let us help build climate change resilience and food security in BASECO.

title: Happyair Inspiring Kids: Severe Asthma
description: Lovexair Foundation, with the help of our Young Ambassadors: Arran Strong affected by Alpha-1, a rare disease & Elena Marti, a Spanish champion with asthma, are  committed and active young athletes who pursue their lifetime goals and dreams, inspite of their serious health issues.  #InspiringKids for severe asthma

title: Soap, Scrub, Rinse:Clean Hands for Healthier Kids!
description: This project will support hygiene awareness session for children living in urban deprived communities in the Philippines. The campaign aims to emphasize the importance of hand washing with clean water and soap as the most effective and affordable way to prevent the spread of germs that caused sickness among children.  To enhance their learning and encourage good practices at home, the children will be provided with complete hygiene kits.

title: Inclusion and Creative Project
description: When youth feel isolated, it  brings social anxiety. This creates tendencies for youth who feel like they do not have support to have an increase of  conflicts with their peers. With your support, we will be able to offer in the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles County : 1. Leadership engagement training 3. Self care activities and mental wellness coaching 4. Community Service Projects 5. Reflection and personal action plans.

title: IYD Sports Development Programme for Schools
description: The primary objective of the IYD Sports Development Programme for Schools is to expose learners to different sporting codes, develop and nurture their talents; and to help them improve their physical and mental health. In addition, the aim is to also provide a platform for practical learning for the Sports Science university students by affording them the opportunity to train the youth in the Inanda township.

title: ADAPTATION, MITIGATION OF CLIMATE CHANGE IN DRC
description: Human negative activities on the environment continue to accelerate the evolution of climate change. The most vulnerable environments and the associated species continue to disappear gradually and the harmful consequences on the human and animal populations cause casualties. The development of diseases and immigration and climatic emigrations, as well as famines are associated with these consequences. If we do not intervene we will find ourselves in an irremediable situation.

title: End Violence against Palestinian Women in Israel
description: Sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) is a major issue facing Palestinian women, connected to the multiple discriminations they face as a minority and as women. Kayan addresses this in creative, empowering, and publicly engaging ways. We hold lectures, artistic events, consultations for survivors, awareness-raising workshops, and an annual intensive 16 Days Campaign against SGBV. Our campaigns reach thousands of people every year, generating conversation about SGBV and making change possible.

title: Fill the School Meal Gap for 4000 children in RSA
description: The Covid-19 pandemic has lead to a hard lock down in South Africa with all schools closed since March 18th 2020. Most children in South Africa rely on 2 nutritious meals at school to survive and thrive. This project will fill the school meal gap with providing meals to these pupils' households through community based nutrition programmes.

title: In Albania, Changing Lives Through Education
description: For up to 200 young people in southern Albania every year, access to Nehemiah Gateway's schools and programs expands opportunities, opens doors, and provides a strong and stable foundation to a dignified and self-sufficient existence. Donations to this project support high quality educational programs for Albanian and Albanian Roma students in need, as well as children with special needs, pre-kindergarten through university, at Amaro Tan, Nehemia School, and Nehemiah Gateway University.

title: Help Rescued Horses Rescue People
description: We are passionate about giving second chances and healing traumas for horses and humans alike. We rescue horses who are slaughter-bound, thrown away after serving mankind, rehabilitate them and those that choose to trust again partner with our coaches to help humans heal traumas.  We focus on survivors of domestic abuse, human trafficking, at risk youth and Veterans. Through the horse-human connection we are able to unpack and identify traumas and help humans heal and step into a fulfilled life.

title: Empower 10,000 Colombian Children with Education
description: In Colombia, thousands of children in vulnerable conditions are prone to drop out of school. The story of Eneidys is common in regions affected by violence and conflict. With this project, we offer access to special education for children like her who have been away from school for several years. They are accompanied by inspiring educators, who follow comprehensive capacity development programs and receive pedagogical materials in their schools to help students reach their full potential.

title: Grow Food for 100 Homes in Uganda (Wakiso area)
description: The community farming program started in May 2019 with the aim to empower households, increase food security, and improve nutrition.  This project targets 100 households and 600 individuals including girls and boys, along their parents. Our specific goal is to improve nutrition and ensure these orphans and vulnerable children attend primary school at Mwererwe Church of Uganda. The lunch program keeps children coming to school and off the streets since they would not be fed a meal at home.

title: Protect Guatemalan Forests with Clean Cookstoves
description: Imagine! You can empower our community-based clean cookstove project in Guatemala's Lake Atitlan basin. With your help, we can provide 250 families with an energy-efficient, clean cookstove that will lower the rates of burns and respiratory diseases, improve family finances, and heavily reduce deforestation. You will be empowering a project notable for its focus on environmental education, its sensitivity to the local culture, and its long-term sustainability.

title: No Waste, All Taste: Fish to Feed Horn of Africa
description: Fish can help solve many challenges in the Horn of Africa. It can feed hungry and malnourished people, and generate income and livelihood opportunities if used properly. Today, much of the fish is wasted, due to a lack of knowledge and skills. FairFishing aims to change this by initiating a portable 'No Waste, All Taste' kitchen - which will not only serve a delicious, free soup to those in need, but also teach them how to utilize fish waste to cook a cheap and healthy meal themselves.

title: Help autistic orphans in Romania get an education
description: The Delia Foundation will provide education for autistic orphans/foster care children in Barlad, Romania, including specialized teacher training. A label of autism prevents a child from attending school. By providing teacher and community education, we can change the way these children are labeled and introduce them into the mainstream school system. Our goal is to give 60 children with skills needed to become productive adults, through our Delia's Learning Center which serves disabled children.

title: Helping to tackle loneliness in older people
description: This project Plans to help tackle Loneliness in older people. To provide older people the opportunity to get out of the house and receive both mental and social stimulation by creating Adult day care services in the community here in Lagos Nigeria which will help the older people stay in their community and function well to the best of their ability

title: The 100% Project
description: The Nepal Trust is working in the district of Baglung in West Nepal with local organisations Daughlagiri Intergrated Rural Development Centre (DIRDC) and the Nepal Development Foundation to tackle and eradicate the illegal and dangerous practice of Chhaupadi. During their monthly period woman and girls are exiled from their homes and schools to unhygienic cow sheds or similar. They are considered unclean and a danger to the fragile purity of the home and traditional culture.

title: Support Families Displaced by Somalia Floods
description: Somalia is struggling to cope with the worst flooding in decades. While the country experiences a range of climate extremes - including regular droughts and flooding - this year's floods are an exception to this pattern, displacing more than 270,000 in a matter of weeks.

title: Give Bilingual Education to Children in Nicaragua
description: You can give children in San Juan del Sur an excellent bilingual education! Escuela Adelante currently provides over $2,000 a month in tuition relief, to enroll hundreds of low-income students who otherwise could not afford high-quality education. Escuela Adelante is a non-profit organization with no government funding for its children's programs - donors like you make its important work possible! As families enroll for the school year beginning in January, YOU can cover a child's tuition!

title: Emotional intelligence classes for 30 kids under 8
description: The depression and suicide rates among children has increased 200% in the past years. One of the main reasons is the lack of emotional intelligence due to over exposure to digital electronics and absent parents. To lower the statistics, we offer a space where kids can learn to identify and channel their emotions with yoga, painting, crafts, singing and meditation. Through weekly classes for three hours, the kids are exposed to a different way of learning about emotions in a safe environment.

title: Give Liberian Children Healthcare, Education, HOPE
description: 84% of Liberians live in extreme poverty and over 50% of the population is under the age of 18.  RESTORE HOPE: LIBERIA supports disadvantaged children in the remote Kolahun District with healthcare, education, and economic opportunity. Providing healthcare and teaching children to read are two of the most fundamental interventions to overcome poverty.  Disadvantaged children-orphaned, disabled, chronically ill-are more likely to escape poverty if they are healthy, educated, and skilled.

title: End Poverty for 5 Students with Big Dreams!
description: Through the Barrio Planta Project (BPP) non-profit schools, students from some of the poorest neighborhoods in Mexico and Nicaragua gain access to job-targeted education, like computer science, to become industry leaders in their local communities and leave poverty behind.

title: Human Trafficking
description: Human Trafficking is a crime against humanity; it is the second most profitable transnational crime after drug trafficking.  Medical Mission Sisters around the globe are fighting against this modern form of slavery by educating, advocating, lobbying, networking, and offering a safe place for rest and recovery for some of the most vulnerable people in the world.

title: Come to school boys and girls with Cerebral Palsy!
description: We are an Educational Center where we provide education and service to children and adolescents with Cerebral Palsy. Through the Conducted Education model, students enable their movement, strengthen their cognitive abilities and develop a strong sense of inclusion in the world of differences. We work on the will and socio-emotional skills of girls and boys. School and group work provide a joyful environment for everyone. We want more children to come to school. Support now with your donation!

title: Humanitarian Relief for Yemen
description: Yemen has been deemed the world's worst humanitarian crisis by the United Nations. Currently, 80% of the population - over 24 million people - are in need of aid. Over 20 million people are food insecure, with 14 million people in acute need (at risk of famine). Over 70% of the population does not have access to clean water. The Yemen Relief and Reconstruction Foundation has three strategic aims: increasing awareness of the humanitarian crisis underway in Yemen, facilitating humanitarian aid pro

title: Engaging community through Festival de la Tierra
description: It is a festival that encourages citizen's participation towards sustainable development, through arts and culture. Since 2008, it has connected more than 1,500 people and organizations who do take care of community and environment, having a direct impact on social cohesion and in recovering public spaces. The next "Festival de la Tierra" will have its 12 annual edition from April 22nd to 26th, 2020, as a part of the Earth's Day celebration in Monterrey city, Mexico.

title: Train 500  Refugees on Disease prevention-Uganda
description: High burden of Infectious diseases and influx of 1.2 million refugees have put strain on the health systems in Uganda.The malaria prevalence in West Nile is 79% by rapid diagnostic tests confirming the high burden that makes children miss school days when sick and can be fatal as it causes anemia or brain damage if not treated early. IHDI's project will train 500 community volunteers on prevention of malaria, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS and diarrhoea to reduce on morbidity and mortality by 10% in 2020.

title: Provide Clean Water to 500 Families in the Desert!
description: This project is of extreme importance to serving humanity. By providing Clean Water to approx. 500 families in extreme far areas of Thar Desert. *(an average family size is 2 to 3 Adults + 4 to 5 Children = 8 Persons). Deep water-well's will be dug, and provided with a "hand-pump" for smooth operation, to the 10 villages. A regular maintenance is necessary every year to maintain the serviceability of these wells.

title: Break the youth poverty cycle in Vietnam
description: For 20 years, KOTO has enabled 1,000 Vietnamese youth and their families to escape poverty through our holistic hospitality training program.  This project will enable KOTO to provide an additional 15 places to disadvantaged youth from ethnic minority backgrounds, particularly women, to complete our 24-month internationally-certified hospitality program. Full board, commercial cookery or hospitality, English language, computer and our crucial life skills program are included.

title: Change Architects
description: Change Architects transforms youth into change makers through community development and social entrepreneurship using design thinking. 500+ innovative teachers volunteer their time to facilitate activities for their students. 5,000+ youth identify problems in their communities, brainstorm ideas and implement sustainable solutions. In doing so, they develop 21st Century skills such as: empathy, collaboration, communication, leadership and confidence in their own capacity to generate change.

title: TUTORING 10,000 STUDENTS IN OSUN STATE
description: VolunteerCorps is organising free intensive tutoring for 10,000 indigent senior secondary school students in public schools in Osun state of Nigeria. This increases their chances of success at the 2019/2020 Senior Secondary Certificate Examinations and other similar examinations.  We provide free study materials   Provide free meals to students and tutors (on Saturdays when we have extended tutorial sessions).     We organise refresher courses for Volunteer tutors (public school teachers)

title: Help us to Save A Dad
description: Nearly 12,000 men die from prostate cancer every year in the UK.  And over 47,000 men are diagnosed with it.  Tackle Prostate Cancer acts as the patient voice for just under 100 prostate cancer support groups across the country and this project will allow us to support those groups with grants to carry out PSA tests in the community to help with early diagnosis. We want to #SaveaDad.

title: Give 18 children in South Africa a safe home.
description: This project will provide a secure environment for vulnerable and at risk orphaned and foster children to grow and thrive in. The foster village they live in is currently unsecured and the children are not safe from intrusions by strangers and stray dogs. Help us to help them by giving us the means to secure their village with a wall and security gates so that they can live and play in safety.

title: Support Mental Health Care & Psychosocial Support
description: Our transformative mental health initiatives in Tanzania offer vital services to address the mental health needs of over 5,000 people. Through interpersonal counseling, empowering group talk therapy, relevant psychoeducation, and referrals, we offer comprehensive support. The project aims to bridge the mental health treatment gap, reduce stigma, and foster resilience in the community. It will empower people and create a stronger, more compassionate society that prioritizes mental well-being.

title: Reducing malnutrition among children 0- 5years
description: Project is targeted at nursing mothers with children under 5 years. The aim is to reduce malnutrition among children under 5 years and the objective is to train and equip mothers with skills and zero interest llan empowerment facility, to facilitate the processing of nutrition related products for young children. Planning meeting will be held with stakeholders to develop and agree on the criteria for selecting mothers.

title: Maternal child healthcare awareness
description: a) Make healthcare readily accessible and affordable to expectant mothers, children, the elderly and the local community in general. b) Pool local resources (financial, human and physical) for the establishment and running of a community based health facility.   c) Creation of HIV/AIDS awareness and, where resources permit, establish a functional Voluntary, Counselling and Testing Centre within the Dispensary. d) Establish a centre for HIV/AIDS home-based care and management.

title: Help Students Get Better Access to Internet
description: Computers and access to internet are rare commodities in Liberia for most students.  Liberia Career Pathways is bridging the gap by providing computers and access to the internet at our Center for Career Discovery.    Through access to the internet students are gaining better information to career choices vital to Liberia's economic growth.  Your help will change the trajectories of these students lives and eventually strengthen communities and the nation.

title: Toilets Reduce Absentees for 200 Kenyan Students
description: Primary school age children in Western Kenya is on the rise and new schools are being built.  However, there are little to no funds to build toilets and hand-wash stations.  Consequently, children pass germs, get sick and miss school.  Chronic absenteeism reduces a child's academic performance and lessens their ability to achievement in later life.  Our project will build two six-stall toilets and multiple hand-wash stations to increase health, reduce absenteeism and increase academics.

title: Help an abused woman and her children
description: This project will save a mother and her children's lives providing safe shelter into a modern center, quality social services, as psychotherapy, medical and legal assistance, a course of qualification for the victims who don't have a profession or a qualification, financial aid after relocation, consisting in the payment of the rent, utilities and a monthly food allowance, for a period, everything that is necessary for the abused woman and her children to start from scrap.

title: Venezuela: mending our social fabric via 150 kids
description: The deep humanitarian crisis has deteriorated our social fabric, affecting the most vulnerable: our children. OSCASI with 65 year experience improving lives in Petare is in a position to mend this situation. With this project we will feed, heal, educate and offer care to 150 kids that attend or two alternative schools in Petare, the largest slum in Caracas. We'll pay special attention to monitoring and providing nutrition to our children.  We'll also work with the community close to our schools.

title: BITS ETC --We are still here!
description: From clients with autism, to volunteers who struggle with ADHD, and board members who are themselves physically disabled, we "walk the walk" at BITS ETC, encouraging those who come here with what is called a disability, to pursue a quality of life that we all deserve.    The pursuit of happiness for many, starts on the back of a horse.  BITS ETC provides the well trained equine partners in the process.  Your donation will support the care of our horses and the programs that serve our clients.

title: Thrive
description: Thrive provides assistance to families with urgent needs that can't be helped elsewhere. Thrive can help a working mom that needs a new car battery to get back and forth to work; a senior citizen that must choose between their prescription and heat bill; a recently laid-off father of two with rent to pay. Thrive helps keep families afloat during challenging times.

title: Low Income Moms Need Breastfeeding Support
description: This project aims to address the inequities in breastfeeding duration in  underserved communities and the effects of low breastfeeding rates on the health of babies from low income families.  This project will provide monthly grants to families in need to rent highly efficient hospital-grade breast pumps to help low income and often uninsured mothers with issues such low breast milk supply, providing breast milk after going back to work , feeding multiples, and breastfeeding with split custody.

title: Protect and rehabilitate livelihoods of Vulnerable
description: The strategic objective of this food security and livelihoods intervention is to protect livestock from diseases and pest through provisions of veterinary services such as vaccinations and treatment to ensure the increase in access and availability of healthy food amongst highly vulnerable male and female remote rural-based pastoralist

title: 450 Haitian students benefit from new library
description: This project will establish a library in a rural school in Haiti in the community of Jean Bellune. The school has 450 students from kindergarten to the junior year of high school. Many of the adults in Jean Bellune do not know how to read and write. Literacy support for young people is essential not only for themselves, but also for the whole community. Jean Bellune has no electricity. The library will serve as a study space for the students, in addition to foster a love of reading.

title: Rise Up for 424 Teachers in Southern Haiti
description: Hope for Haiti supports salary subsidies and professional learning communities for 424 educators in 24 southern Haiti communities. 186 educators will meet in three workshops to study assessment, lesson planning, and self-reflection together in their native Haitian Kreyol. This project will strengthen local community institutions and empower student achievement for over 7,000 schoolchildren, catalyzing generational change and creating opportunities across the region.

title: Screen 500 babies for congenital diseases in Ghana
description: Most babies in Ghana are not screened for inherited congenital anomalies. These conditions go unnoticed and  lead to catastrophic health outcomes such as  intellectual disabilities, severe illness, or premature deaths. This project seeks to  screen 500 babies for more than 50 inherited congenital disorders in Ghana. When detected early, these babies can benefit from early intervention to reduce developmental disabilities, infant morbidity and mortality.

title: Maternal and Infant Care in Borgne, Haiti
description: This project will provide health interventions and treatments for pregnant females and infants in the rural community of Borgne, Haiti.  Maternal and infant medical care, made possible by your donations, will help improve life expediencies in Borgne, which are about half of that of the United States.  Your donation will help improve their infant mortality rate (currently at levels to match the poorest of nations in the world).

title: Provide Life-changing Skills to Cambodian Parents
description: We provide daycare and family support to twelve at-risk families living near Phnom Penh's notorious Dangkor landfill. While the children are provided with a safe and stimulating environment, the parents follow a family action plan designed to empower them to break out of the poverty cycle. Continuing this line, we would like to offer the parents one year of vocational training, so that they can walk along with more experienced workers, learn important skills, and be surrounded by role models.

title: Women Enlightenment & Empowerment (WEE) Program
description: Alhaj Shamsul Hoque Foundation (ASHF) wants to provide free education for 500 women who have been deprived from the lights of knowledge in the rural area of Bangladesh. Later on they will ready for self-empowerment.

title: Stop cholera from killing thousands in Yemen
description: The project aims at reducing the incidence of cholera epidemic by providing preventive means (drinking water purification filters, water containers, personal hygiene bag, chlorine tablets), building the capacity of community volunteers, educating people about hygiene and methods of prevention of epidemics in rural areas of Sana'a city - Yemen.

title: Nutrition for 1120 vulnerable Afghan Children
description: Based on our rapid assessment in the Ghazni, Wardak and Kabul provinces during August 2019. Almost 1120 IDPs children living with families/relative in main cities. The vulnerable children have 2 major problems with the children on the move or IDPs. Malnutrition and lack of food for children and lack of hygiene and education opportunities. DELO will provide targeted children with energy biscuits and milk on daily basis for 6 months and establish 3-5 child friendly spaces and 15 community classes.

title: Educate the Whole Girl & Her Community in Zambia
description: In pursuit of Fallen Peace Corps Volunteer Elizabeth Bowers' (Beth's) dream, our small, all-volunteer organization enabled a paradigm shift in attitude toward  women's education in remote NW Zambia.  By building a Memorial Library, the first pre-school, and Phase I of a secondary school (two 3-classroom blocks, two teachers' houses, and a girls' lavatory), we empower hundreds of girls to further their education and attain their dreams.  Now Phase II:  a 3-classroom block and a teacher's house.

title: Higher education in Europe: a students' tale!
description: Our world is rapidly digitizing. Higher education, especially in STEM fields, can not leap behind. It must adapt to the needs of future students and graduates. A key aspect of doing so is to give students the opportunity to state their opinions and share their experiences. Your donation contributes to making a  high-impact programme around Digital Literacy in European higher education, run by Board of European Students of Technology (BEST). So join us today in creating a better tomorrow!

title: Provide solar lanterns to poor school children
description: This project will provide safe, environmentally friendly solar lanterns to students and families in remote villages in developing countries that are not connected to the power grid or lack reliable electricity. Now children can do their homework at night and adults can engage in productive activities. These lanterns light their paths to a brighter future.  Our organization is all-volunteer. We rely on volunteers and partners to help us make the most of every dollar that you donate.

title: Support Christmas Party in the Slum
description: Christmas is a season of sharing and showing love to the haves and have not. Over the years statics and research has it that kiddies in slum,  hinterland and hood don't feel the joy that comes with the season. Your assistance would help us provide Food stuffs, Cloths, shoes, beverages  The best way to teach love is to show love, via this event we will practically teach and exhibit love,affection and empathy which will automatically become the template which the children will grow with.

title: Help 250 Poor Nica Women re-build their businesses
description: A disastrous socio-political crisis in 2018 has resulted in a 40% shortage in micro-loan funding for the poorest segment in Nicaragua. Many micro-entrepreneurs and their children are now at significant financial risk. Micro-loans will help enterprising women to re-start and build their businesses and make more money. More money will help them obtain better health care and nutrition, make small home improvements and continue to grow their businesses.

title: Provide Books to 30,000 Children in Afghanistan
description: This project targets the most vulnerable, marginalized and underprivileged children in Afghanistan who are deprived of reading materials with proper contents in their mother tongue. The project will publish 30,000 copies of 15 story books in Farsi-Dari, Pashto and Uzbeki languages and make them available for children in all 34 provinces of Afghanistan through the network of 277 ABLE libraries. Additionally, it will establish 5 new libraries in the remote districts in Afghanistan.

title: Help pay teachers during political unrest in Haiti
description: English in Mind Institute (EIM) provides high quality, affordable English classes to adults in Port-au-Prince, along with job placement assistance. English education opens doors to employment, promotions, university scholarships and more - in a country where most of the population doesn't have formal employment, and lives on dollars per day. EIM is Haitian-led and serves as a platform of advancement for over 200 students (more than 40% women).

title: Clean Water for the Watha
description: Crocodile attacks are the norm for the Watha people of Kenya. Although there is a constant threat of crocodile attacks along with the possibility of contracting cholera and typhoid, the only option for the Watha is to collect water from nearby rivers. This project will allow local hero Guyo of the Watha Project, a GRACE Cares partner, to build a well that will serve 1,027 of the Watha, drastically improving their health, safety, and quality of life.

title: Big Reads in Mexico with 1,200 kids for 2020
description: Children want to read!  But they don't always have access to books and non-textbook reading is not always included in the curriculum in the public education system in central Mexico.  Can you imagine your childhood without the magic of books?  Libros para Todos would like to plan 2 big reads for 2020: one in May and the other in November.  Each would include at least 600 children between the ages of 9-15 years of age. Each child receives his or her own book and then the author meets with them.

title: Mental Health for Exploited Girls & Boys in SF Bay
description: This project focuses on the SF Bay Area's most vulnerable youth - victims of sex trafficking - providing them with mental health treatment and group support, healthcare, and workforce training. Our youth-inspired Dream Youth Clinics are vibrant and trusted locations that provide compassionate health care for youth who are homeless and/or sexually trafficked. But in order to truly change their trajectory, we need your help to fill two important gaps: mental health care and economic opportunity.

title: Horses for Veterans and First Responders with PTSD
description: Casey's healing hooves equine assisted therapy and rescue is a 501c3 Non profit. We are a family owned farm who provide equine assisted learning and activities to people in need, with the horses we  rescue  and rehabilitate. We are currently fund raising for our Vetarens and first responders with PTSD program. equine therapy seems to be the perfect answer for certain Veterans coping with post-traumatic stress and other disorders, both mental and physical.

title: Empower 30 Special need children through skill
description: This is pioneer project of Zunnorain Welfare Society , in which initially 30 persons with special needs will be trained and skilled through vocational training of Fashion designing, sewing, handicraft, jewelry making, professional cooking etc helping them escape vicious circle of poverty by ensuring a sustainable livelihood  for these financially challenged, persons with special needs. ZWS aims to provide this sheltered training space a sustainable one, to empower more persons with special needs

title: Support hundreds of pregnant teen girls in Uganda
description: This project will Support 100 pregnant teen girls in Kampala, Uganda at Wakisa Ministries which is a temporary shelter for pregnant teens with unplanned crisis preganancies. At Wakisa, the pregnant teens receive medical care, counselling, clothing and toiletries for the girl and the baby and also learn life skills and vocational training. At Wakisa the girls will also receive free meals.

title: Train Regenerative Farming for 200 Refugee Women
description: The project will empower 200 women refugees with practical permaculture and nutrition knowledge and skills allowing them to attain sustainable food and income for their households.   Each of the trained women will set up permaculture vegetable gardens to produce sufficient and nutritious food for their household and be able to sell the surplus to earn an income.

title: Safe water , sanitation for 4500people in Kambia
description: Studies proved that 14% of 341,690 people have access to safe drinking water ,16% to latrines in the district. There is the incidence of cholera, diarrhea every dry season when unsafe water sources get dry and polluted. Lives are lost, poor people spend a lot for treatment. Women and girls are abused in fetching.Pupils dont do well in school for distant fetching.The project will construct 70 water points and 200 latrines to reduce risk of new outbreaks of health epidemics for 4500 people.

title: Environmental education children's handbook
description: This handbook will reach over 3000 users and beyond. This book will aid us in spreading awareness for the leopard, the project and will be used as a teaching tool in our environmental education programs.

title: UNLEASH YOUNG TALENT AND BREAK DOWN INEQUALITIES
description: We co-design creative, safe spaces with young people and embed them in Barnet's most isolated communities, giving them access to creative skills training and wrap-around support. In our main hub, we run a weekly nail bar, a music studio and a design studio where young people can get education/employment support and work towards qualifications (Arts Awards). Embedded in the spaces are specialist mentors who provide support around mental health, abuse, violence and other risks.

title: Empower disadvantaged Armenians with legal advice
description: Last year CAIA helped 400+ vulnerable people of all ages born in 26 different countries through advice and practical support about their rights as refugees/migrants, as isolated older/disabled people, women/children subsisting on low incomes, poor accommodation or threatened with homelessness. CAIA enables them to address the inequalities they experience such as cultural exclusion, language and digital barriers to progress from surviving, coping, to adapting and thriving in society.

title: Empower 265 refugees to make Brazil home
description: Compassiva has 4 projects; the biggest is HOME (LAR), which seeks to respond to refugees' most basic and urgent needs as they rebuild their lives in Brazil. 4 pillars work together to ensure that refugees are able to restore their autonomy: Portuguese course; legal assistance from general documentation to degree revalidation in partnership with UNHCR; support for finding work; and general support, ensuring the most basic needs such as food, housing and medical care are met.

title: Empower & Trasforme Women and girls in East Africa
description: LAFA Is accommunity Based Organization ( CBO) Established with the aim to bring Women and girls from many groups in the Rural  together, to reduce Poverty by  providing knowledge & skills with free courses; Tailoring, ICT, healthcare & beautician for School leavers and women. This project will help to build technical School to change the lives of thousands women & girls to avoid teen pregnancy and HIV/AIDS infection rates. They will be economically indipendent to access their Sanitary pads

title: Coding a brighter future for 15 youth in Yemen
description: Millions of youth in Yemen have been cut off from traditional ways of making a living due to political and economic strife.   In July 2019, we opened applications for the first-ever coding bootcamp for youth in Sana'a, Yemen. We received an overwhelming response of 1000+ applications. Sadly, we only had the capacity to accept 15 students. We're now raising funds to launch our next program. Our goal is to bridge the growing digital divide and empower youth to become leaders through technology.

title: Rehabilitation and Education for blind children
description: Sponsorship of the pre-basic annual educational plan of Santa Lucia College: The course consists of 7 friendly and intelligent children with visual disabilities in vulnerable context. The opportunity to study at Colegio Santa Lucia allows them to rehabilitate, train and produce knowledge in an innovative way and with the support of a professional team wWe extend their studies.

title: Restore Livelihoods of 100 Rural Farmers in Ogoni
description: This project supports 100 Ogoni farmers suffering effects of oil polluted lands and rivers through training in alternative livelihoods agriculture on livestock, food crop, and aquaculture production (i.e. poultry, piggery, fishery, snail farming, and mushroom growing) for food support and socio-economic adaptation; and the Centre rehabilitates affected household-farmers in difficulties by transforming their helpless state-of-need to self-supporting status of six-month livelihoods strengthening.

title: Transforming Lives through Education Rural Oaxaca
description: In a traditional indigenous, Zapotec village, where schools and teachers do not typically have the energy to dedicate one on one time with the children, understanding the needs of each child and how to best support them, Ananda Learning Center offers alternative, holistic, nature based, "private" school education at public school costs. We also offer trainings to public school teachers and directors so that Montessori and other alternative methodologies do not need to be so inaccessible.

title: Quality education to 20 children from Paraguay
description: Ensena por Paraguay plans to provide quality education to 950 children from rural communities in Paraguay. These students will receive instruction and support from excellent professionals who, from the classroom, will lead projects based on academic and socio-emotional skills. This project makes it possible for 20 children to have access to the programs that Ensena por Paraguay promotes.

title: Pathways for All
description: Everyone learns differently. We understand. For 23 years, LPLC has been working with students, families and schools to understand and overcome obstacles to learning. The goal of the Pathways to All project is to expand our one-on-one services for students with learning and attention challenges by removing financial barriers to education. Regardless of income, this project seeks to create pathways to learning for EVERYONE.

title: Transforming Haiti One Village at a Time
description: CEI's work in Haiti is thriving despite current civil unrest because it's 100% Haitian-led and managed, community-wide, and holistic. People closest to the problems have the most say. A reputable Haitian nonprofit manages it all: goats, ag, women's & youth groups, financial education, entrepreneurship & leadership training.  CEI's democratic framework generates trust & transparency and builds civil infrastructure while meeting basic needs. To date, we've helped 400 families in 8 villages.

title: Active listening for 500 women during COVID 19
description: Vital Voices Costa Rica created virtual training and a platform that mobilizes professional psychologists, coaches and mentors to volunteer on an Active Listening Brigade. The brigade's mission is to bring emotional relief and support to rural communities. The main service the brigade offers is one on one virtual sessions in a non-judgmental environment. So far 126 people (mainly women) have received free active listening sessions, our goal is to serve 500 more during the holidays!

title: Empower U.S. Women Through Music: Jobs & Education
description: Herizon Music Foundation, a 501c3 nonprofit envisions a music industry where any woman can make a living based on merit, no matter her age, appearance, familial status, or orientation. Our mission is to uplift the next generation of women in music through education, experience, and role-modeling programs.

title: Help rural Haitian communities thrive!
description: The Colorado Haiti Project exists to support & investment in rural Haitian communities, empowering local leaders for self-sufficient, thriving communities. We believe that our locally-driven, long-term partnership is a special one. By focusing on one community, we help local Haitian leaders make a lasting impact in their community, one family at a time, through programs in education, agriculture & conservation, girls' empowerment and health. Please join us in supporting these amazing leaders!

title: Training & mentorship for 300 Nicaraguan women.
description: Since the onset of the 2018 crisis in Nicaragua, thousands of women have lost their formal jobs. Left with few options, a large majority of them have had to start small business efforts to continue providing for their families.  At Voces Vitales, we know a small entrepreneur stands a much better chance at succeeding when she is able to access training, mentorship and a supportive network.  We want to guarantee that in the midst of this crisis, women and girls can access opportunities to thrive.

title: Title :Pad up the vulnerable girl for free.
description: Helping  the helpless . Many girl's of menstrual age cannot afford sanitary pads and this sometimes make them vulnerable , and fall into hands of predators  who promise to buy them.Some girls actually use rags as pads ,a girl of 13 years needed to by sanitary pad  and turned to a man ready to get her some if she allowed him to have sex with her.She ended up with pregnancy. Free reusable pad is the answer.

title: Life opportunities to Colombians through education
description: In Colombia, around 25% of the population that finishes High school completes a degree at the University, this information is based on statistics of the Colombian Education Ministery. One of the main reasons that people do not access or do not finish University is economic problems. These difficulties have led us think about how we can contribute people and we have been implementing partial scholarships to people over the years.

title: Community Training Center
description: We are in the process of constructing and equipping an ADDITIONAL community center for the youth and mothers of the 35,000 person village of Chivoc that have overcome chronic malnutrition and could otherwise be victims of human trafficking. This project will initially serve 600 mothers and children in a center that includes a kitchen, bakery, confectionery, hair salon, carpentry, tool shop, medical center, and technology center for the training and the benefit of this disenfranchised community.

title: Help Cocoa for Peace. Colombia
description: 230 men, women and complete cocoa growers families located in the North of Tolima Colombia, subsist from the production of cocoa. Cocoa for peace emerges as a subsistence mechanism for farm families who also find a way of social and economic transformation of a territory historically marked by violence. The farmers was victimized by various scourges such as drug trafficking, violence, sexual and labor exploitation against women and children by guerrillas and armed groups outside the law.

title: Improving lives of 3,000 disabled children in DR
description: This project contribute to improve the life conditions of the  disabled children of La Altagracia Province in the Dominican Republic, especially those living in poverty in the Punta Cana region, through the operation of a specialized health center in the community of Veron that will benefit to more than 3,000 children

title: End Sexual Abuse for 4000 Children in South Africa
description: Unimaginable. Unspeakable. These words come to mind when we talk about child sexual abuse.  Keep a Child Alive with its partner Bobbi Bear is addressing this abuse by implementing a comprehensive approach to reduce child sexual violence in Kwazulu Natal, South Africa. The Bobbi Bear Center works tirelessly to rescue and uphold the rights of sexually abused children, to help them survive and thrive. The Center reaches 4,000 children every month supporting them in the aftermath of sexual violence.

title: East Bali Education Project - The Hearts Company
description: Our projects in East Bali include building 2 necessary elementary school buildings as well as the village's first computer room filled with 30 desktop computers. This will affect thousands of children for generations exposing them to the knowledge and education they need for chances at brighter futures.  Our goal at The Hearts Company is to provide sustainable educational resources for underprivileged children so that our impact will be long lasting even after we are gone.

title: Diplomas, Not Diapers!
description: At 16, Nicole is pregnant with her first child. She's dropped out of school. After she gives birth, she has a one in six chance of getting pregnant again before she turns 19. Without a degree, her options are severely limited. Nicole is just one of 200,000 Filipino teenagers who get pregnant every year.  This project will provide education and services to 3,000 young girls in Palawan, Philippines, to give them a better chance to avoid Nicole's fate and stay in school.

title: Support 50 disabled children in Yemen.
description: In this project, 50 children with physically and mentally disabilities will be targeted in Hajjah Governorate /Yemen by providing them with transportation fees to go and return from the  physical therapy center as well as providing food for them and their families and providing wages to receive physical therapy that enable them to continue their lives normally and practice their life activities such as education and play like other kids and to live better.

title: Support Early Learning for 2,000 Children, Uganda
description: This project will support early childhood development (ECD) for 2,000 children delivered through IREAD's 10 Uganda ECD Centres. Donations will help to train teachers, provide school uniforms, and maintain the Centres.

title: Empower 100 students with vital IT skills in Ghana
description: With an ever changing world and economy which requires one to have knowledge in digital and soft skills, Grow Ghana seeks to empower, engage and orient students for a digital future. Having built a newly furnished IT lab with your help, we want to reach out to more students in rural Ghana. We plan to use the newly built IT lab for coding workshops and also engage in mobile training by taking our Raspberry Pi project to schools and giving students the opportunity to experience the art of coding.

title: Save 200 Rural kambari girls from Child Marriage
description: This project will create awareness on the negative effects of child marriage and the importance of the girl child education. It will empower 200 girls through skill acquisition training and literacy support and their by save them from child marriage and its negative effects like child maternal mortality, poverty, illiteracy, STDs, rape, IVF etc.

title: Empowering communities to coexist with elephants
description: Elephants for Africa gives rural villages in Botswana access to information, training and education to enable them to decrease the cost of living alongside elephants and increase opportunities to benefit from wildlife. By engaging and assisting villages bordering protected areas we enable people to live alongside wildlife to ensure a safe and secure future for both elephants and humans. The requested money will fund fuel and vehicle maintenance to access three communities for a year.

title: Environment, Economics, Empowerment in DRC? YAS!
description: What is it like to be a woman or girl living in rural DRC? Caught in the crossfire between crushing poverty, subsistence farming, and harmful traditions that confine women to defined roles and spaces? Not easy. This project, 3E, is 3-pronged: targeting vulnerable women (pygmies, widows, sexual violence survivors, women with disabilities/illness) to learn crop cultivation, establish an economic cooperative so they can buy - not rent - the land they work, and to heal the environment. Win-win-win.

title: Empower 240 children and adults with disabilities
description: This project supports the youngest at Prithipura Communities - babies and young children with disabilities who live at the Infants Home.  The first few years of life are crucial to a child's development, especially those with disabilities, and through specialist care, therapy, pre-school education and a lot of love we provide maximum opportunities for growth and independence.

title: Renewable Energy for Improving Rural Healthcare
description: Our environment is in crisis, it is a problem for all of us. In Nepal every year around 8,500 women and children die from the effects of polluting cooking stoves. We will be working with off-grid communities in Surkhet District of Nepal to improve the healthcare provided through introducing renewable energy. Getting communities off the grid will allow them to be sustainable and independent, whislt making sure it is affordable for all. We aim to improve the health of over 4,728 community members

title: Build Resilient Communities With Solar in Nepal
description: This Nepal project is using solar energy to help improve remote rural communities' resilience, with a focus on improving health, flood-safety and the livelihoods of 2,750 vulnerable people in two isolated communities in Surkhet District. Renewable energy is a way for communities to go off the grid whilst becoming more independent and affordable at the same time. This isn't easy as not all communities have the funding and knowledge to implement renewable energy which is where we step in...

title: Send your LOVE to 100 TB affected Families
description: Tuberculosis patients often feel stigmatized and alone due to their condition and prolonged period of treatment. Providing a simple gift of generosity from a "Secret Santa" will impact their overall well-being just simply showing them that someone out there cares.

title: Empower mental/emotional wellbeing in Puerto Rico
description: Our program  provides individual, and family counseling, psychotherapy, personal development workshops for the community, and local schools.  Using the strategies of Artistic Creative Therapies like Music Therapy, and Dance Movement Therapy the workshops helps improve the wellbeing of families, one person at a time, and transform their lives, empowering them to lead fulfilling lives.

title: Creating school farms to fuel education in Haiti
description: The project will create a school farm (gardens, chickens) to help feed students in a K-6 school in rural Labiche, Haiti.  Providing food to the 105 students, all from desperate living conditions, is essential to their learning.  The farm will reduce food costs, offer hands on learning, and provide economic benefits both in the construction and maintenance of the facility.  Fencing, coops, soil enhancement, fruit trees, seeds as well as labor are accounted for in the funding request.  Thank you.

title: "Safe to Skate" - Skateistan Winter Campaign
description: Donate today to give our students a place where they feel free from fear!   Skateistan's winter campaign has started and we need support to continue providing a safe space for children to skate in. A haven, where they are protected from discrimination and judgment, free to express themselves and develop their talents, in order to become the leaders of tomorrow.

title: Improve Living Conditions for 3 Destitute Widows
description: We are requesting funds to rebuild the homes of 3 poverty stricken widows who have no other means of assistance. The structures are all but destroyed, and will not survive the rainy season of March. MDIH staff will find materials and provide labor. Without help, these widows and their children will be without any type of shelter. Your support is crucial and potentially life saving to these families.

title: Build A Civic Center for Children in Trenton, NJ
description: Next year, we would like to open a community civic center for our youth. This new building would give them regular access to fitness classes and new programs we plan to introduce. It would include a gym for our fitness programs. This building would service 50-60 children from all over our city. These programs would include basketball, boxing and more.

title: Tranzmission Emergency Housing Fund
description: Asheville has no shelter that will appropriately house a transgender person. No safe place to sleep, falling temperatures, and no accommodating shelters in the area means that many face the cold winter months on the street with little to no support. Tranzmission's Emergency Shelter Fund is set up to help eliminate the dangers of living on the street. We offer financial assistance to those who find themselves without a place to stay and offer a stipend for those who can offer safe harbor.

title: Transforming children's lives through music
description: El Sistema Greece is a community music project that provides free music education to children and young people in Greece. All children - no matter their origin, nationality, or religion - are not only inspired to strive for a better future but thanks to music, they are given a platform for dialogue and togetherness across diverse communities.  We believe that a music instrument for a child works as a vehicle towards self discovery and development into the magic world of music.

title: Community Transformers
description: This project will work with Youth and Women groups In Zanzibar, empowering them with knowledge and resources to fight against climate change challenges and introduce income generating activities that are friendly to environment, build resiliency livelihood and  preserve the environment.

title: The Teapot Challenge
description: Help the people who pick the tea that keeps you going through the bad times, warms you up when it is cold and is at the centre of any family celebration.  We are encouraging supporters to collect change every time they have a hot drink. Donations will help us bring high quality education to 320 young people and 2,100 children from some of the most isolated and hope-hungry communities in Sri Lanka.

title: School dining room for 286 children in Oaxaca
description: This project will build a scholar dining room in the indigenous school "Vicente Guerrero" located in Santa Maria Xadani, Oaxaca,  this is a state with a social and economic lag. This school is integrated for 286 students and 12 teachers, who wants to improve their school for the children's development and feeding, they require support for the scholar dining room building  it helps can have two meals per day

title: Ultimate Peace Graduates Making Change
description: Ultimate Peace (UP) is a groundbreaking leadership program, annually uniting 400 Arab and Jewish youth in the Middle East. Playing the self-officiated sport of Ultimate Frisbee, teens compete, resolve disputes, build trust, and bond. As young adults, program graduates like Zeinat, a 22-year-old M.D./Ph.D. Technion student, apply UP values daily. Seeing her Arab and Jewish classmates segregated, Zeinat ignited a unifying movement. As she said: "I know better from growing up in UP". More below!

title: Tell her she's not alone, support a woman w/cancer
description: We want that 50 women with cancer in Baja California feel accompanied in their disease to live the process with quality of life, for which we will provide psycho-emotional and nutritional assistance, second opinion consultations, advice on oncoimaging, turbans, lymphedema sleeves and personalized council, oncological bras and breast prostheses, so that they can not only cope better with the disease but also reduce the risk of sequels.

title: Art Workshops against violence in Oaxaca
description: Pequespacio feminista was born in 2017 as a proyect of 4 women who wanted to stop violence against women starting from childhood. We started visiting neighbourhoods in suburbs of Oaxaca, with artistic workshops for children and their families, opening conversations on gender violence prevention and sexual diversity in childhood. We want to promote in the children and their families an awarenes of their rights and help raise a message of non-discrimination, social inclusion and self acceptance.

title: Give 21 HIV+ orphans in South Africa a future
description: This project will secure diapers and baby formula, hot meals, school uniforms and shoes, and trauma counseling for sexual abuse for HIV orphans living in the Winnie Mabaso Foundation orphanage South Africa.  Positively Alive plans to renovate and equip 10 schools for 1,000 children and hire 50 teaching assistants for 1 year.

title: 12 Days of Christmas: Wheelchair Edition 2019
description: The 12 Days of Christmas fundraising campaign seeks to highlight and fully-fund 12 wheelchairs for 12 beneficiaries over the Christmas period. Give the best Christmas gift of all, the Gift of Movement.

title: Empower 200 African deafborn kids to hear and talk
description: Carel du Toit Centre will support 200 children with hearing impairments from poor families in South Africa in 2020. Our unique methodology makes it possible for children to hear and speak and acquire language and knowledge  Support includes audiological management of hearing devices, professional therapies, schooling, transport, aftercare and meals.  Children progress from Grade 3 at the Carel du Toit Centre to mainstream curriculum schooling to become the best versions of themselves as adults.

title: Assisting the Blind from Less Privilege Families
description: This project will assist 50 blind persons from poor homes and remote villages to go to school and another 50 of them  to engage in vocational training.

title: Assure bright future for students at risk
description: School Miracles is a project which creates leaders among students from underprivileged communities who grow up to become positive role models for others demonstrating that hard work and education can take you wherever you want, regardless of where you start from. We achieve this through a holistic program targeted at students 10-18 years and their parents which aims to equip students with the needed knowledge, skills, and mindset in order for them to change their lives for the better.

title: Help the NSPCA raise disaster funds for 2020
description: Fires, Floods, Droughts are not uncommon in South Africa, they are all enormously destructive and impact heavily on the lives of people and animals. Disaster has a tendency to come at the worst of times and the NSPCA knows that the only form of planning for disasters is to have the resources ready. We ensure that there are specialist inspectors dispatched when animals are in dire need and we need your help.

title: Sponsor 100 children in Kayole, Soweto in Nairobi
description: Tunaweza Pamoja Children's Centre helps neglected, needy, orphaned, vulnerable, deprived and destitute children mostly from the Kayole-Soweto slum area and also from the Children's Department. We help the children by paying their school fees, giving them shelter, food, clothing and medical attention. We provide a loving and safe, family environment that enables children the right to a happy, educated, skilled and healthy life. Currently we are helping 100 children aged between 3 to 15 years.

title: Help Ukrainian inventors get to IC Worldwide 2020
description: Ukrainian students have the opportunity to join the international inventive community and present their inventions at the Invention Convention Worldwide 2020. Help raise funds to transfer participants from Ukraine to the United States.

title: Creating a Generation of Wildlife Warriors
description: WildlifeDirect plans to take 3000 children from public primary schools across the country to national parks and reserves. Through day trips and camping expeditions, children will be engaged with research and activity books to educate them about nature and wildlife and be inspired to treasure and act to conserve it.

title: Stop deaths related to firewood-cooking in Kenya
description: Bio-briquettes are bottom-up fabricated sources of cooking energy that can make a BIG difference in the lives of women and children in Kenya. 64.6% of Kenya's households depend entirely on firewood for cooking - supplies that are rapidly shrinking. Poor households' budgets strain under this constrained supply making them revert to agro-waste use that releases large amounts of particulate matter, which causes respiratory ailments, diabetes mellitus, etc. Support our brio-briqueting to change this

title: Help redevelop Maunga school, Livingstone, Zambia
description: Maunga Primary School is located in the rural Maunga community comprising of 8 villages and a population of a bit over 3000. Family income levels in this area are low, and so many children are growing up surrounded by extreme poverty.  Our aim is to increase the capacity of the school to offer higher learning possibilities for their pupils.  The school is severely resource-limited with classes that are over-crowded and lacking educational materials.

title: Seeing Hands Rwanda
description: This project will help employ ten to fifteen visually impaired persons living in Rwanda through training them in massage therapy and providing them the skills needed to pursue careers in the field.    Visually impaired people have the highest rate of unemployment of any demographic in Rwanda and can't even meet their most basic needs and provide for their families. Seeing Hands Rwanda aims to end the stigma against visually impaired persons and those with other disabilities in Rwanda.

title: Family to Family Campaign
description: We're raising $5,000 to help 100 local families in need of safe shelter, educational opportunities, counseling, and other life-changing services. When you give to the Family to Family campaign, your family is extending a loving lifeline of care to another local family in need.

title: More and better water through ecotechnics
description: Increase availability of clean water for the benefit of peasant families through the construction of cisterns, Increase availability of drinking water for peasant families through the installation of filters, Reduce the pollution caused by the disposal of gray water into the environment with the installation of artificial wetlands at the family level, Increase availability of clean water for community use through the construction of cisterns, Promote good practices for the efficient use of water

title: Building a future, path to higher education
description: In Chile there are only a few vocational guidance programs, which is why we are looking to improve our website, to build a vocational guidance portal and improve our training services for teachers, parents and students. In this way, we are going to support 7 municipal schools in Temuco, directly benefiting more than 500 young people. We will deliver vocational education and more information on access to Higher Education to students who come from the most vulnerable region of Chile.

title: Aid for Families in Syria
description: With the war in Syria in the midst of its eleventh year, the devastation continues. Today, 13.4 million Syrians are in need of humanitarian assistance, many of whom have been forced to flee their homes. This project supports the health of affected families with essential access to clean water, food and basic hygiene items.

title: Championing Girls' Rights On and Off the Field
description: Too Young to Wed's mission is to empower girls and end child marriage globally. TYTW partners with Falling Waters Schools and Samburu Girls Foundation in Kenya to run ongoing sports programming which encompasses scholarships, rescue and reintegration, psychosocial support, and emergency assistance, keeping girls in school and preventing them from returning to child marriages. Playing football / soccer is more than a game for these girls; it is a pathway to safety, healing and leadership.

title: Compassion for Community Refugee Education Project
description: Compassion for Community has started a school to take care of the refugees and host community children educational needs. Our school classrooms are in bad state... This has forced us to propose the construction of Compassion for Community  community  school to take care of the refugees and host community education needs.

title: Clean Water for Families in Yemen
description: After 6 years of ongoing conflict, Yemen continues its standing as one of the world's worst humanitarian crisis, those displaced are some of the country's most vulnerable people. In 2021, 66% of the country's population will require some form of humanitarian assistance, and a staggering 14 million people are in acute need of assistance. This project will support the health of families through the provision of clean drinking water and basic hygiene items.

title: Tech: key to re-empower 30 surviving communities
description: In 2023 we are re-empowering 30 indigenous/rural communities, survivors of the armed conflict, with SOLE Methodology: transforming public spaces into Self-Organized Learning Environments, where a few computers and Big Questions are the path to learn, dialogue and take action collectively around themes like mental health, economic growth and real life challenges... weaving lives with hope and building peace, together. Since 2014, SOLE Colombia has reached over 420,000 people.

title: Send 175 Students to High School in Belize
description: Most Caye Caulker children were forced to quit school at the age of 12 until Ocean Academy opened as the island's first high school offering an education to all children who want to learn.

title: Youth Activism on the Nuclear Weapons Ban Treaty
description: Inspired by the Climate Change Movement led by youth, this project will educate, empower, and motivate youth to become activists by bringing them to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons' Forum in Paris. Afterwards, the youth will organize outreach and educational events on their university campuses, engage with diplomats, and spark a movement. Ultimately, this project aims to inspire a movement led by the next generation of global leaders.

title: Educate and Empower 300 rural girls Sierra Leone
description: Youth Help works with girls to excel extreme poverty, gender-based violence, and stop early child marriage, gain socio-economic empowerment and better health. Girls sponsored will access education, mentoring and power to drive change in their communities. To achieve the above, provision will be in the form of scholarships/fees, clothing and food at home, access to information and communication on girl-child education, ending child marriages, gender-based violence and learning for over 300 girls.

title: Building peace communities in Dominican Republic
description: This project promotes an education process of actions as best practices for building a culture of peace in Dominican Republic providing communication and education resources in order to contribute to social change in a positive way and facilitate the establishment of lasting peace and support preventing violence. The initiative will impact more than 4,000 youth and adults from different social strata, with gender equality and territorial representation.

title: help old people find a family and meaning of life
description: As part of the project, we will improve living conditions and social conditions for adaptation in a nursing home located in rural areas of Kazakhstan, as well as build a large center for the stay of the elderly and their physical activity. The implementation of the project will make it possible to provide comprehensive professional support to more than 3,000 lonely elderly and disabled people every year. The main goal is to create our home comfort, not only existence, but also the return of inte

title: Girl Power
description: Many young girls forced in marriage homes are suffering and lack of business skills. Our mission is rescue, educate and inspire them to start their own business/start-ups, and support them in the challenging early years especially when being a female entrepreneur. They will be connected to local and big cooperatives, to local Start-ups ecosystem. When these married girls succeed as entrepreneurs, fully participate in the economy, prosper in the workforce, and have their dignity.

title: Gift 1000 Story Books to Promote Literacy in Kenya
description: Quality education transforms students' opportunities, and gives them a pathway out of poverty! For many children in marginalized communities, access to story books is simply a luxury. We want to change this by providing a much needed supply of story books to students to promote literacy, and connect them to a world of stories. This project will enable us to start mini library boxes in schools so that children can have access to engaging materials to enhance their learning experience.

title: A ride to a brighter future
description: In Cambodia, many students have to travel a long distance between home and school. According to research conducted by USAID, long-distance travelling accounted for 10% of the total dropouts. A bicycle allows a student to get to school, and also take one or two siblings alongside. At the beginning of 2019, we initiated a project "A ride to a brighter future", we provided 100 bikes to the students in a rural part of Siem Reap. We want to extend our goal for the year 2020 to provide 300bikes.

title: HELP TO ENHANCE PREVENTING POVERTY WITH TREES
description: The charity Organization Compagnie Agricole et Environnement (CAE) wants to continue training other 240 local students to plant and protect 240 000 life-giving trees. These trees will provide food, water and income for their families by bearing fruits to improve nutrition, protecting their cattle's water supply from evaporation and boosting their crop harvests by enriching the soil.

title: Empower 70 Kibera Youth to Become Self-Sufficient
description: This project will create jobs, start businesses, and develop opportunities for 70 young men and women ages 18 to 25 living in the Kibera slum - ultimately reducing unemployment among this vulnerable age group and starting them on a path toward self-sufficiency and a better future for themselves and the entire community.  We work with each individual program participant to discover their skills and interests and develop a route out of poverty that best utilizes their own inherent strengths.

title: Help Keep the Wheels on our Food Bus Turning!
description: As part of our mission of Enriching Communities, we have turned a double decker into a mobile greengrocers and community space. This unique bus brings low cost, fresh produce to areas where residents experience food insecurity, and have limited access to healthy, affordable food. Operating in South London, the Food Bus offers a more affordable way to shop on the bottom deck, and a Cafe, with seating and Wi-Fi, on the top. With solar panels, it's a sustainable way to shop and socialise

title: Eliminating Violence Against Women and Children
description: Domestic Violence is common in Cambodia. Women often suffer physical, sexual, emotional and economic abuse. Violence is regularly used towards children as a means of discipline and control.  Violence is never ok and through support, education, campaigning and ending the silence around domestic violence it can be eradicated.   Support us to help Cambodian women and men understand equality, rights, safe communication and how to manage anger through workshops, counselling, campaigns and support.

title: Give a new life to 200 rural Ugandan women
description: By improving farming methods in rural Uganda, our project will support 200 poor women to increase their incomes. Women provide most of the farming labor in Uganda but lack access to modern farming technology or larger plots of land. Thus, they only farm for family consumption and make little or no income.  We help farmers to pool their land and provide modern technology, high-quality inputs, and agricultural training for women so that they can farm for profit and work their way out of poverty.

title: Thrive Bangladesh:Feed a school in the Dhaka slums
description: Piet Van, a Thrive partner school, provides free education to 120 underprivileged children living in the Dhaka slums. Our aim is to ensure these children receive the brain-fuel needed to learn and achieve their fullest potential. In Bangladesh, nearly 75% of children's diets do not meet the dietary variety standard (FAO 2010). By providing healthy meals, Thrive fills essential nutritional gaps in the daily diet of over 2,500 underprivileged children attending 13 schools across Bangladesh.

title: Give the gift of education to transform lives
description: Your gift will help us empower women and girls worldwide with education through scholarships, training programmes and mentoring.   We work with 27 women-led local partners to create solutions to the issues affecting women and girls' access to education, breaking the cycle of poverty. Last year, we supported 20,097 women and girls in 18 countries through our work.   Help us increase our impact next year!

title: A new centre for new opportunities
description: This project is a new hope to expand education and create new opportunities for the community. Our hopes for the new centre include:increased space for activities (e.g. 13 x 15m for each of two floors; a playground up to 40 x 10 m), parking 20 x 10m, design as a partnership with the community e.g. women from our SaPune social enterprise will sew curtains; young people to be involved in designing and creating murals with educational and inspirational messages. Indeed a chance to grow as a whole!

title: Help Syrian Chilren with Cancer in Learning!
description: Children with cancer have a hard time managing at school while having to face periodical treatment courses, which happen during school-time. Therefore they are not able to keep up with their lessons. Our project will work with 6 teachers on offering additional lessons and activities to 50 children with cancer from poor families. This will help build self-confidence and improve their mental state after being behind their friends at school for so long because of their treatment courses.

title: Equip, Mentor and Empower Kenyan Youth in 2020
description: In the year immediately after high school where young people await their examination results and subsequent eligibility for continuing education, most Kenyan youths are idle therefore there is an increased likelihood for them being lured into high-risk activities & unhealthy relationships. This project will promote their sustainable development by equipping them with skills training & mentorship to increase employment & income-earning potential for long-lasting economic self-sufficiency.

title: Help Us Limit Holiday Hunger
description: Every day in the UK, half a million children go to school hungry. This is worse in the school holidays, where the two million children who qualify for free school meals cannot access them. At Be Enriched, we believe children deserve more. Our Kids Clubs seek to alleviate "holiday hunger" in South London, by providing nutritious food when there is no access to free school meals. Our Kids' Clubs also provide a chance for adults to meet and socialise, and fun educational activities for all to enjoy

title: All Children Deserve to Dream
description: Every child deserves to dream, but in Ecuador dreaming is a privilege.Some children do not know when their next hot meal is going to be.Others study by candlelight, and many more lack the medicine they need to make it through the day.We are honored to work with 5 organizations that are serving 350+ vulnerable youth, covering their basic needs and giving them the chance to dream.Now, we want to show Ecuadorian children that dreams do come true, and we need your help to fulfill each one of them.

title: Humanitarian Crisis Affecting 13 Million Syrians
description: The conflict in Syria has resulted in the biggest humanitarian emergency of our time, and one of the largest refugee crises in history.   Over 11.6 million people have been forced to flee their homes. More than 13 million Syrians are in need of humanitarian assistance, with medical care remaining a top priority.

title: BACK TO SCHOOL
description: This project is aimed at providing free Education for more than 100 out of school  children living in marginalized communities in Niger Delta region of Nigeria, and also providing medical support and free meal for children.

title: Empowering Our Girls: Girls on the Run - DC
description: Last year, Girls on the Run - DC offered financial assistance to 76% of girls who participated in the character development program and continue to see that need grow. By donating today, YOU can help girls feel greater confidence in who they are and what they can accomplish. Your donation will support program scholarships for 20 girls and help them find the positive in themselves and others. You're giving girls social, emotional and physical well-being at a critical time in their lives.

title: Action Hope Food Security project
