description: This project will provide child care support to   35 Orphans and vulnerable children (disabled, Hiv/AIDs victims, abandoned, streetchildren, and orphans) the fundraiser will provide tuition sponsorship to these children, provide meals for the children(breakfast and lunch,( this means that the children will be able to acquire education. Many of these children in our child care are disadvantaged and do not have access to nutritional foods.

title: Developing a  Permaculture Resource Centre in Seke
description: zimconserve intends to set up a  Permaculture centre for Subsistence farmers . Zimconserve shall erect the fencing right round its  plot and install a borehole. Projects, such as mushroom farming, aquaculture, permaculture gardens and ecological buildings are to be established. The objectives of this project are to empower the locals through these income-generating projects, for food, nutrition, revenue, and as well as to bring awareness to environmental conservation issues within the community.

title: Help Transport 7000 women for Cancer treatment
description: This project seeks to support, transport and accommodate over 7,000 woman receiving cancer treatment at the only cancer treatment hospital in Uganda- women who are mostly from the rural regions with little to no access to financial support to afford accommodate and transport themselves while receiving treatment.

title: Help 175 Malawian Children become Seizure Free
description: This project will provide Epilepsy Medications to 175 Children with Disabilities attending our Epilepsy Clinics.  Children of Blessing Trust runs 2 Epilepsy Clinics at our main site in Lilongwe each month and at least one clinic each month in our 10 Outreach Communities.  The children are assessed by a health professional and provided with medication for 1 month.  Children who are new or not stable on medications are seen at the main site.  Children who are stable are seen at the Outreach Clinic

title: The Amazon Burning - Kids and Bugs to the Rescue!
description: Support the Alliance for a Sustainable Amazon's work in Peru! We conduct research and environmental education focused on insects, the tiny yet incredible creatures that run the rainforest. We study how bugs maintain the delicate ecological balance of the Amazon and aid in its restoration, and share this information with our local kids-It is they who depend most directly on the health of the rainforest and it is they who ultimately will decide its fate.

title: Help investigate philanthropy
description: Giving by wealthy individuals, endowed foundations, donor funds and everyday people shapes the world around us for good or ill. It needs rigorous coverage by media you can trust. This project will create a series of dedicated investigations to keep challenging the field to serve with maximum impact and accountability.

title: Literacy can change the lives of 150 families
description: Brazil is 260 years behind. A recent report by the World Bank, states that Brazilians will need 260 years to reach current OECD's reading results if the current trend persists in the country. How could Brazil grow and deliver a better standard of living to its citizens if education as a whole is so far behind? Your support will help to change this cruel reality for 150 students by helping them to become passionate about reading. Let's help them to write a better ending for their life stories.

title: Empowerment of HIV+ women through entrepreneurship
description: Women are frequently the worst affected when it comes to unemployment and poverty and are often the sole income earners for the family. In particular those affected by HIV/AIDs are stigmatized by their communities and struggle to earn enough to support themselves and their families. In an economy where 80% of the jobs are in the informal sector, the project aims to empower vulnerable women in need of socio-economic independence through entrepreneurship.

title: Give Education to the most vulnerable Somali Girls
description: Somalia has been ravaged by famine and war, leaving a large majority of the population in poverty. Education opportunities for many Somali Girls are somewhat limited. Somalia has one of the world's lowest enrollment rates for primary schools. Only 30 percent of children in Somalia are in school and only 40 percent of those children are girls. This project will give lifesaving and education opportunity for 250, of the most vulnerable girls in Mogadishu's IDP camps.

title: Mint400 Military Challenge for Marine Raiders
description: The Marine Raider Foundation is honored to be a charity partner at the 2020 Mint 400 Military Challenge to raise awareness & financial support for military veterans & to highlight the military's ongoing involvement in off-road culture. The Marine Raider team will race for the Marine Raider Foundation to support its mission that includes providing adaptive equipment to wounded, ill & injured Marine Raiders, as well as funding for programs that promote personal, professional & family resiliency.

title: School bus for children on vulnerability condition
description: Haceres Foundation is currently hiring a bus that picks up the children on vulnerability conditions who attend on a daily basis. In order to provide a safer and more flexible transportation service we ask for your kindly support, in order to be able to provide our children more activities for them to be able to see the world in a different way and learn that there is much more than just the four walls they live in. If we can buy the bus we will be taken our children to many places such as museum

title: Sustentabilidad para la Vida en la Sierra Huasteca
description: El proyecto es vital para la salud comunitaria y proteccion de ecosistemas, construira tecnologias sustentables en 6 comunidades nahuas y tenek y es parte de una trayectoria de empoderar pueblos originarios y mujeres en la Huasteca de San Luis Potosi  ---  This project is vital for community health and ecosystem conservation, installing sustainable technologies in 6 Nahuatl and Tenek villages as part of a long history empowering indigenous peoples and women in San Luis Potosi's Huasteca

title: Careers Fair for 2000 yr10-12 students in Lagos
description: The aim of the Careers Fair is to help our students focus on the world of work, begin to develop their  ideas about employment and make important choices about their future.  The Careers Fair will bring industry experts in contact with students from public and private schools, giving the youngsters more information on the different post-secondary options they have and industry experts an insight into the talent pool which will be available to them in the nearest future.

title: Addressing both Food Sovereignty & Climate Change
description: Earth And Man plans to establish a self-sufficient 2,5 acre vegetable market garden, addressing hunger and local food sovereignty in South Africa. We will provide meaningful, dignified employment and development, for youth in particular. The farm will serve as a best-practice demonstration farm, showcasing the productivity and viability of regenerative agriculture while simultaneously tackling climate change and environmental degradation. This model can and will be replicated across the country.

title: Solar for Internally Displaced Persons Camps
description: Our project addresses the problem of lack of clean energy for lightening in Internally Displaced Persons Camps and communities in North East Nigeria. The insurgency in North East Nigeria caused  by the terrorist group Boko Haram have displaced over 2 million people who are taking shelter in different internally displaced persons camp in different parts of the country. Nearly all the camps are without electricity. Our project is to provide electricity at the camps using Solar Energy

title: End period poverty 57000 girls rural schools.
description: Our NGO- Grace World Africa Foundation is organising a pads drive to raise 57000 pads in 57 days.As a small organization with great hopes, we want to restore women's dignity affected due to poverty. This campaign aims to keep a girl child in school through collaborative cross sector partnerships, bring to a halt school drop outs of girls who are unable to attend school  and help disadvantaged women due to them not having means to provide themselves with sanitary pads.

title: Tutoring K-3 student in Reading/Leadership Trainin
description: Program to assist low-income children K-3 students in their reading skills, helping to prepared them for the goal of the Alabama Grade-Level Reading Campaign by 2022.  This is a required for all of Alabama's 3rd-graders to read at, or above, grade-level proficiency.  Our tutors & space is limited to 10 student per session. Our goals is to have 3 training session per week with ten students per session.  A Program "12 week budget boot camp" teaching intense  training to take control of our finance

title: Art & Education to Save a Bird from Extinction
description: Apolinar's Wren is an endemic bird in Colombia with a decreasing population trend, in the brinks of extinction. We want to help reverting it, by providing a new approach to environmental education in rural schools at Lake Tota (main location of its habitat), as a model with a potential to be spread out. Aiming to increase affection, participation and awareness, designed to be fun and creative, combining transmedia storytelling, in which children will also be introduced to various art forms.

title: Educate 20 Vulnerable Tanzanian Children This Year
description: Ikirwa School Project is looking to sponsor 20 vulnerable children from village of Midawe to attend our English-medium school for a another year. The kids you support have experienced hardships early on. Some have lost one or both parents, some were born to single moms. Most are girls. All are hoping for a better chance to have a good life. Along with an excellent education, these children will receive 2 to 3 nutritious meals a day, a uniform and have a safe space to live, study and play.

title: Improving education for 80 kids in La Guajira
description: Orropsco school is located in La Guajira, Colombia. This school belongs to the Wayuu community, one of the largest indigenous community in Colombia. The school has 80 students and it runs without any source of electricity, hence they struggle everyday with academic and other different activities. Light4Education will install a 1.1 kWp solar PV system for the Orropsco school in La Guajira, Colombia.

title: Young Indigenous Women Empowered with Basketball
description: In Chiapas, women's conditions are limited in their access to education, health, recreation and public spaces. Women from an early age must engage in housework and be prepared for the fulfillment of the role of being mothers. We find sports as a tool that improves development and physical well-being and strengthens leadership, teamwork and companionship.  To achieve our goal of empowering more than 50 indigenous young women, we need to form in basketball.

title: Border Rapid Response Efforts
description: Our program's primary purpose is helping refugees, asylees & asylum seekers with basic needs, transportation, and transitional services. When they are released from detention at the San Ysidro border, we are there waiting. We provide them with quick and safe transportation from the border to a hotel or host family. We provide them with clothing, suitcases, hygiene items, baby formula, diapers, and essential items. Then we ensure their safe travel to their family.

title: New Classrooms for Costa Rican Children
description: Village Classroom provides classrooms to children in underprivileged villages of Costa Rica. We believe the classroom is a very important learning place for improving the living circumstances for the children and changing their future. Your donation goes towards the critical classroom infrastructure for improving the learning environment, a new roof, a blackboard, bathrooms, clean drinking water, and handwashing stations for 3 schools in small Costa Rican villages.

title: Give Vulnerable Populations Access to Therapy Dogs
description: Oknooshoon provides canine-assisted interventions (CAIs) in Armenia with a certified CAI Team (Therapy Dog and Handler). This will mutually benefit dogs and people in Armenia, by giving vulnerable populations access to therapy dogs and improving the troubled human-canine relationship through education. After a 12 week pilot at four facilities for institutionalized youth and individuals with disabilities, the project will be assessed for impact and expanded to more target populations.

title: 2020-21 Enrichment/Workshops for 120 Scholars
description: At CasaSito, we believe that the school grades that our scholars earn are important, but personal and professional success depends on much more, especially critical thinking, talent development, and emotional support, all lacking in Guatemalan schools. That is why we have developed our enrichment clubs (art, theater, debate, math, English, music, writing, volunteering) and workshops for the scholars and their families. Money is needed for transportation, materials, teacher stipends, etc.

title: Help CIWY Survive Crisis / Ayuda CIWY en Crisis
description: Over 500 rescued animals rely on CIWY for daily care. During the pandemic we  lost almost all our normal income from the volunteer program. CIWY needs $22,000/month to continue operating until volunteer numbers go back up.     ~~    Sumario: Mas de 500 animales rescatados dependen de CIWY para su cuidado diario. Durante la pandemia perdimos casi todos nuestro ingreso normal del programa de voluntariado. CIWY necesita $22,000/mes para continuar operando hasta que el numero de voluntarios aumenta.

title: Empower 250 Refugee Families to Thrive
description: Imagine being forced to flee your home because of war or persecution, leaving behind all your belongings and even family members. After spending years in a refugee camp, you are resettled in the US with limited English and little understanding of the culture. This project will provide newly arrived refugees with the comprehensive support and empowerment to not only integrate into their new homes, but to rebuild their lives and become successful, thriving members of New Hampshire society.

title: Cheer dance program has started!
description: This project is new chance to our members with intellectual disabilities (we call them "Athlete")who like dancing. We are planning to work on cheer dance. We think that cheer dance can be a valuable experience for them, since they can feel bonds of friendship and wonderfulness of supporting with their colleagues. We started the program last month, but now it will be necessary to make uniforms and to secure regular venues.

title: Tackling the Global Antibiotic Resistance Crisis
description: Phages for Global Health is teaching scientists in Africa and Asia how to develop cheap, natural antibiotic alternatives (phages) that can kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Antibiotic-resistant infections are expected to kill 5 times more people each year than HIV did during the peak of that crisis. Sadly, almost 90% of those deaths will occur in the developing world. Phages have been used for >100 years in certain regions, but they have not been broadly utilized in developing countries.

title: Water for jaguars and farmers in Gaira, Colombia
description: Fundacion Bachaqueros is contributing to the survival of Jaguars and the preservation of their endangered habitat sites in the Gaira Valley of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta. With scientific and ancestral knowledge we are protecting and restoring a threatened dry forest jaguar habitat and water source in the Carrizal Jaguar Reserve. We help the local farmer and indigenous populations find a balanced relationship with this endangered feline, and conserving the resources for future generations

title: New Heights Educational Group
description: New Heights Educational Group, Inc., promotes literacy for children and adults by offering a range of educational support services. Such services include the following: assisting families in the selection of schools; organization of educational activities; and acquisition of materials.  We promote a healthy learning environment and various enrichment programs for families of preschool and school-age children, including children with special needs.

title: Sending Letters to Orphans Worldwide
description: Paper Bridges is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that strives to provide orphans with this much needed love through a letter writing system. We  provide hope for children in orphanages by sending them letters, and small gifts to remind them that there are people who care about them. Our letters are written by people of all age groups and walks of life, each full of love and encouragement. We can forge powerful bonds that span across oceans and connect people from different worlds.

title: Empowering 450 young people in Mexico
description: Join SerVers MX to provide socio-emotional skills to 450 students from vulnerable high schools in Mexico through 45 recreational workshops. With your support, they will be able to acquire skills that allow them to self-manage a better quality of life and make decisions for greater well-being. Together we are that ray of hope for those young people from 15 to 20 years immersed in a series of disadvantages that deprive them of receiving an integral and quality education.

title: Global STEM Awareness in Youth for next Generation
description: Globally, current generation is facing  STEM talent crisis, primarily due to an under-resourced STEM education system in certain under-privileged areas . This is contributing to the decline in the interest among the younger generation and potentially could generate a huge gap in the future demand for the STEM skilled workforce. Our mission is to motivate and trigger interest in Youth around the world by introducing them to interesting way of learning technology in their field of interest.

title: Quality education for the youth in Cuetzalan
description: In partnership with TEC, we offer high school studies online combined with face-to-face workshops. We encourage young people to learn, to value their culture and to develop their talents and those of their communities. We offer food and lodging to students. We offer trades and crafts workshops: farming, bamboo, textile, and graphic arts. We encourage youth to become proactive; to keep on perfecting their talents; and to participate actively in the well-being of their communities.

title: Stop the bleeding: Sumatran tiger snare sweeping
description: This initiative mobilizes civil societies and local tribes to secure at least 20 Sumatran tigers from snares, the most direct and lethal human activity, through intensive snare sweeping in a human-dominated habitat in West Sumatra, Indonesia.

title: RESURFACE STREET COURTS IN NIGERIA
description: HarryCares will help various cities in Nigeria to resurface five basketball street courts and install Basketball upright that are more durable for outdoor use.  By doing so, we are providing a safe space and place where various youth can horn their basketball skills while channelling their energy towards sports. This project will include a one day tournament for each court which becomes officially open in order to keep participating youth active and empowered while playing the game they love.

title: Food Rescue Project - Cooked Food for the hungry
description: To salvage excess cooked foods from F&B establishments and provide meals to beneficiaries in need.

title: 5000$ for Kijana Cafe-Young people Story of Change
description: Kijana Cafe, a mobile 4-hour semi-recreational activity, where people come to bear witness and listen to youth state-of-the-art ideas/solutions. The event intends to fuse knowledge brokers and youth together in a the simplified setting, to expound ideas to fruition. But also, Kijana cafe features simple games, delicious bites, colourful and creative poetry performances all under our one roof, to vibrate the session. The project is championing intergenerational solutions.

title: Training of 10 Midwives in Helping babies breath
description: There is a need for well-trained personnel (midwives,  and health personnel) in obstetrics. The activities after the birth and the necessary skills have to be learned so concretely that this is the approach to the project. For example, it is easy to learn to reanimate a new-born with respiratory depression. A problem is the fact that women often suffer from fecal or urinary incontinence due to weakening of the pelvic floor as a result of inadequate care of birth injuries and poorly perform

title: WILDLIFE CONSERVATION  SURROUNDING NYIKA RESERVE
description: Expenses on Wildlife activities in communities surrounding Nyika reserve include conducting civic education meetings where dramas, shows, dances and sporting activities will be performed in order to attract the attention of people. Organising trips for key personnel in the communities to visit and appreciate the reserve, aiming at influencing their subjects to help protect Wildlife. Major concern is on animal species that risk being wiped out like Zebra and Antelope due to heavy poaching.

title: Give clean water to 20,000 people in South Sudan
description: This project target returnees, internally displaced persons and the vulnerable host community members in Yei, South Sudan. The project will provide clean water through repair of 40 boreholes. NID will train 10 technicians who will do the repair. 20 hygiene promoters and 40 water management committees comprising of 5 members each will be trained so that they  disseminate messages specifically safe water handling to avoid contamination. This project will target surrounding villages of Yei town.

title: Train 50Trainers who will inturn train 1000 others
description: Ageing population increase  at a time of war, challenges for health, changing climate, emerging infectious diseases, Furthermore, the ongoing war in NW, bad governance, violence, and conflict have driven aged persons from their homes.This project will empower the older persons to know their rights and join the civil societies that are working with and for older persons to advocate to the government to release the draft validated national policy on aging.

title: Peer Education for women with Spinal Cord Injury
description: This project will improve the quality of lives of 60 women with spinal cord injury in Eastern Tanzania who were discharged from the hospital without proper information about the affect caused by spinal cord injury

title: Protect Wildlife by Educating Poor Communities
description: Wild animals are a treasure and pride of every nation.They should exist naturally in the wild and be free from hunger, thirst, pain, injury, discomfort, fear, distress, and able to express their normal behavior. However, they are the source of food and income for poor communities living in wildlife areas who kill them in very inhumane and painful manner. We are protecting these animals by educating children and unemployed youths who will in turn get employed and cease from relying on them.

title: Support 200 Flood Victims in South Sudan
description: Since July 2019, South Sudan has experienced unusually heavy rainfall and flooding, has reached unprecedented levels, displaced 1,000,000 million people. Devastated peoples' livelihoods - farms washed away, health centers, homesteads completely submerged. In October 2019, South Sudan Government declared a State of Emergency in flood affected areas. 3 million people in flooded areas were already affected & displaced by the South Sudan war crisis, people are now facing double tragedy to cope with.

title: hard winter is coming
description: This Project will build a warm home in the coldest time in Romania. We care for more than 250 animals, traumatized and wounded mostly by humans. You help us to fight against the cold winter and give them a chance to calm down and find homes for the future.

title: Support the Bulgarian Natural Science Teams
description: This Natural Sciences Olympic Teams Association project aims to financially support all stages of preparing the Bulgarian natural science teams for the international Olympiads. Organizing and conducting National workshops on Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Informatics, Mathematical Linguistics, Astronomy, Astrophysics, as well as supporting the Young Physicists Academy, are critical for the good performance of Bulgarian youths at the Olympic Forums.

title: Prevention of Child abuse/rape in Kakamega County
description: Western Young Leaders Society is a civil nonprofit organization anchored in grassroots initiatives inspiring the community in addressing social injustices brought by human rights violations and all form of abuse hindering the well being of the society. We do this by engaging the community leaders like Chiefs, opinion leaders and religious leaders. We use the leaders to conduct mobilization and use their platforms to provide awareness and sensitization. We seek to address the a societal taboos.

title: Help us create Bulgaria's Green Educational Centre
description: The Bulgarian educational system is obsolete and essentially fails to prepare students for the future. The Green Educational Centre ELA will be a place where, connecting with nature, students will develop their creativity, confidence and analytical thinking. We already purchased an old school building with 4000 sqm of land and are transforming it into a inspiring learning and activity park accessible to all kids, embracing their differences. Download the attached file for Bulgarian translation.

title: EMPOWERING 800 SCHOOL GIRLS HYGIENE IN LILONGWE
description: Reusable sanitary pads are sustainable and easily renewable resource allowing the girls to wash and reuse them rather than having to buy disposable pads every month. In addition, they are comparatively inexpensive and environmentally friendly. We aim to target 600 girls  in schools and it will roll out in the rural communities within the city of Lilongwe in 3 school namely Minga Community Day Secondary School, Chiwamba Community Day Secondary School and Mseche Secondary School

title: Unlock the leadership potential of 150 young women
description: Resonate builds leadership and confidence for women and girls  in East Africa through storytelling workshops. For a young woman, self-confidence can be the difference between learning a craft and becoming an entrepreneur, or between having an idea about how to fix a problem and rallying others to implement community-based solutions.  By investing in women leaders, you invest in their ability to leverage their knowledge and skills to create a better future for themselves and their communities.

title: Help set up a STEM learning centre
description: The World Economic Forum believes nearly two-thirds of children entering school today will work in jobs that don't yet exist. This means there should be a fundamental shift in the kind of skills that we prioritise among our youth. And yet Young people in Livingstone have limited access to technology & material necessary for a great stem education. We believe inculcating STEM skills and giving the youth this centre will help them to grow.  The centre will cater to over 300 young boys and girls.

title: Textile Skills for 40 Marginalized Women in Brazil
description: The Eldorado Textile Project provides training in textile skills to 40 women from the marginalized area of Eldorado, Sao Paulo, giving them a safe space to work, community support, therapeutic creative activity and an opportunity to earn a small income that increases their independence and self-esteem.

title: GIVE CLEAN WATER AND SANITATION FOR 435 STUDENTS
description: Did you have ever to walk 5 kilometers with a water jerrican in hand in search for water? Or stay for two days without bathing your body or washing clothes?. Scarcity of water and sanitation is the experience of  435 students(boys and girls) of Maueli mixed secondary school  are facing today.They use contaminated with industrial waste from Nairobi industries and  polluted sewerage wastes from slums areas of kibera and kajaba slums of Nairobi city.the school has 4 pit latrines to be shared.

title: Educate Internally displaced children in Cameroon
description: This projet will strenghten two (2) primary schools in Koutaba rural council by building two (2) classrooms and providing free education,a rich supply books and critical literacy support services as well as free meals to two hundred (200) internally displaced children (boys and girls) traumatized by security crisis in North West and South West regions and also by Boko Haram in the Far North of Cameroon.

title: Protect the brains of unborn children
description: This project aims to increase the supply and intake of iodine in the diet, especially for women who become pregnant. Iodine is critical in the development of the neurological system, and a deficiency of iodine can lead to lifelong irreversible impairment. This means that children are born without their full cognitive potential and are not able to perform as well in school or get secure jobs. The IGN addresses this by working with partners in all countries to develop salt iodization programs.

title: STEAM education classes in South Africa for 100
description: This project will provide opportunities for pre-k to 10th grade students to tinker, design, build and explore in order to solve local problems. They are exposed to basic coding, robotics and creatively solving science, technology, engineering and math concepts instead of just learning the theory. In South Africa 66,8% of children live in poverty. This project will give 100 children tools to break out of the cycle of poverty. Education helps people to move out of survival mode into thriving mode!

title: Saving Lives through Embryonic Stem Cells
description: We are seeking funding to pay for cord blood stem-cell storage for qualifying families who have a history of cancer, are in receipt of welfare or on a low income, and would therefore be unable to afford the cost of private bio-banking. The goal is to offer vulnerable families the opportunity to store their baby's cord blood for 25 years, which will be available should the child or another member of the family require them. These cells are taken from the umbilical cord at the time of birth.

title: Buy 100 desks for Nangondo Primary School Malawi
description: This project will procure 100 classroom desks to provide a supportive learning environment for 300 learners annually in standard 5, 6 and 7 at Nangondo Primary School in Machinga, Malawi. Currently, only standard 8 learners sit on desks while standard 1-7 learners sit on the floor contributing to high absenteeism rate. The school is located in a remote area with total enrollment of 940 pupils. Despite being government owned, the Ministry of Education has no financial resources to support this.

title: Solarized Water Pump & TV for 4 Centers in Pangil
description: ASHI aims to deepen the technical know-how of farmers by providing them continuous education thru Financial Literacy and Advanced Farming Concept Training. This is provided at the center level which are mostly located in off-grid areas. While, the solar-powered systems utilize open water sources like lakes, rivers, streams and even creeks. ASHI aims to provide a long-term assistance to the farmers by providing adequate farming facilities.

title: ZAKKI Empowering The Elderly in Indonesia
description: ZAKKI (www.ZakatKasih.org) is an organization that focuses on helps the elderly and people with disability get better livelihoods in order to build an inclusive community in Indonesia. ZAKKI focus to help the elderly and people with disability who working in the informal sector to get better livelihood through micro-business management assistance and giving them exposure to the greater market.

title: Rebuilding Children's Dreams
description: 6 months ago we suffered a serious fire that left one of the houses of the "Home Rights Protection" completely destroyed. In order to have an optimal attention of our 50 children and adolescents, we need to rebuild it and create the bedrooms and classrooms. Our children have been victims of different types of abuse, such as sexual abuse, child labor, etc. Fortunately none of them suffered injuries or problems in their health, but to continue with their education and well-being we need some help.

title: Help 26 Korean Gay Soldiers Fight for Freedom
description: The goal is to support victims of Korea's military law which criminalizes gay soldiers. First, this will provide legal assistance for 8 of the 26 victims who are or will be brought to trial. Second, it'll assist 3 or more active-duty soldiers suffering from disadvantageous dispositions, stigmatized as sex offenders. Also, it'll aid 11 constitutional appeals repealing the sodomy law. As such, this project will organize a civil movement to end discrimination.

title: Hands-on LIS Training for 1,000 Lab Users in Ghana
description: Laboratory Staff in rural and urban areas of Ghana use laborious paper-based laboratory information system (LIS) because they do not have hands-on training on how to use available electronic LIS. Working with Georgia Tech, USA and some Labs in Ghana, we have successfully tested and can offer a solution - free(open source) LIS. Our project will provide 1,000 lab users with the opportunity to develop vital technology skills to use electronic LIS.

title: Healthy Screenings for Uninsured Families
description: There is a huge unmet need for health care by a population that has no access to care due to a number of barriers (i.e. transportation, food, health insurance or ability to pay). Villa Therese Catholic Clinic (VTCC) is the only venue that provides free medical, dental, and vision to a population which has no alternative. VTCC holds 2 off-site medical, dental, and vision screening clinics monthly in coordination with churches, other health organizations, and social services organizations.

title: Workshops on Lifeskills for Foster Youth in Poland
description: This is a long-term program enabling the care leavers to meet on regular basis during the school year (twice a month, every workshops last about 5 hours) and learn important life-skills in group, and at the same time get emotional support. Program helps care leavers to preaper to independent life. Part of these meetings is dedicated to housing, law, health and vocational topics -training, writing CV, job appointment,  labor standards and rules ect.

title: Renew Puerto Rico: Clean Energy Transparency Hub
description: After the most devastating power blackout in US history killed more than 4,000 people in Puerto Rico, the island passed a law calling for the most rapid transition ever to renewable energy.  RenewPR provides crucial, rapid education and coordination campaigns to get more clean energy and battery storage deployed, while cutting out the 30% of electricity that's wasted.  The Transparency Hub makes important energy policy issues easy to understand, and teaches leaders how they can get involved.

title: Hope for Ethiopian children with deformities
description: In Ethiopia, access to safe and effective reconstructive surgery for children disfigured by bodily and facial deformities has been almost nonexistent. Not having safe access to life-changing reconstructive surgery can mean a lifetime of pain and suffering.  The Haddis Agape Foundation plans to solve the problem of limited access to reconstructive surgeries for children with deformities by organizing and funding surgical missions. But we don't want to stop there. In order to make our project sust

title: Help feed orphan & vulnerable kids in Eswatini!
description: We serve over 650 meals per week to orphaned & vulnerable children in Eswatini, provided needed nutrition to kids in communities impacted by HIV/AIDS.

title: Empower Vulnerable Children in Peru and Cambodia
description: Globalteer is a UK registered charity running a Child Protection Programme for children vulnerable to abduction, trafficking and sexual abuse in Cusco, Peru and Siem Reap, Cambodia. The Programme provides local teachers with knowledge and resources to teach children how to keep themselves safe outside of their classrooms. Empowering and educating children regarding self-safety will reduce the violence and risks that children in Cusco and Siem Reap are exposed to, benefiting the wider community.

title: Centro de reproduccion para futuros Perros Guia
description: With the construction of a canine maternity center for responsible reproduction, the number of binomials formed (blind person - guide dogs) in Mexico and Latin America can be increased to 70%.

title: Help Save Abandoned Animals like Duke
description: When he arrived, Duke was abandoned and on the verge of starvation. Dogs like Duke not only require medical care, food, rehabilitation, shelter, and love, but are usually heartworm positive and suffering from other serious injuries and medical issues. We serve a rural community that has been hard hit by unemployment, poverty, and drug addiction.There are more animals like him in great need in our community than we have room or money to help. With your support, we can save the lives of many more.

title: Connectivity is a Lifeline for Venezuelan Migrants
description: More than 31 million men, women, and children have left Venezuela. They walk a treacherous path over barren land to the border of Colombia and beyond. As aid agencies establish relief sites along the path of migration NetHope has partnered with them to provide vital connectivity hubs.  Connectivity is a lifeline for Venezuelan migrants. Without access to good information, people already in crisis face the risk of exploitation and abuse.

title: Develop 70 mentors for Fatherless youth in Oregon
description: This project will fund the recruitment and training of 70 men in Oregon, providing a mentor for at-risk boys and young men that are experiencing fatherlessness so that the next generation is better equipped to support women, children, and families.

title: Help Adults with Disabilities in Mexico Create Art
description: El Arca en Queretaro, welcomes 25 adults with intellectual disabilities, focusing on identifying each one's personal gifts.  The staff stimulates creativity in activities such as painting, carpentry, dance, handicrafts, and baking.  Respect and empathy foment emerging abilities and meaningful relationships. Mexican folk art has lead the beneficiaries toward greater self-confidence, alternate ways of expressing themselves, increased productivity, social recognition and inclusion.

title: Help Survivors of Abuse Rebuild Their Lives
description: DeeCilla Comfort Center will house young women, ages 16-28, who have suffered various forms of abuse, such as domestic violence, sexual assault, and human/sex trafficking. These traumatizing issues can strip people from reaching their full potential. But we understand that just because these issues have happened to them, all is not lost; there is still HOPE and, they are not what happened to them. We want to restore their HOPE for the future with a new beginning with your help.

title: Serve 3,000 children with lifesaving vitamins
description: For undernourished children, vitamins are life-giving nutrients. The Global Renourish Organization (GRO) plans to supply three thousand children with lifesaving vitamins in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea.  Although small in size, vitamins are necessary for life, health and growth.

title: CDEA's Fashion & Design Incubator &Accelerator
description: The fashion and design Incubator and accelerator will provide skills development in collaboration with a vocational training institution to 40 fashion and design practitioners in urban and rural Tanzania. The products and services developed will be linked to both domestic and international markets using and e-commerce platform. The project will later train fashion and design practitioners in Uganda and Kenya.

title: Caring for Your Mental Health During this Crisis!
description: Give an Hour is producing materials to help the public with their emotional health.  Give an Hour has supported our nation through devastating natural disasters and man-made tragedies and now  - the COVID-19. Give an Hour has the capacity to help those experiencing trauma, loss, grief, and anxiety through its national network of volunteer mental health providers throughout the country who are eager to do their part. There is a critical need to provide help and hope to those who are suffering.

title: Good Living for 130 indigenous children in Chiapas
description: The School Feeding Circle seeks to ensure a healthy, safe, diverse and culturally appropriate nutrition, for 130 tzeltal and tsotsil children from Los Altos de Chiapas, seeking the effective exercise of the human and universal right to food. Based on the concept and practice of the food sovereignty, community is organized to carry out a scheme of production, gathering and preparation of food that is served in schools: the Good Eating Festivals, ensuring an adequate nutrition for children.

title: Tales of Migratory Birds with Broken Wings
description: Tales of Migratory Birds with Broken Wings is a visual storytelling project working to create social change. We work with refugees in Bosnia using anthropological approaches and photo documentation, to document human rights abuses and gather cultural information and understandings to solve refugee and displacement related issues. By amplifying refugee voices we aim to encouraging tolerance and integration through improved understanding amongst displaced and host communities.

title: Promise for Androy, Madagascar: Change for Women.
description: In Madagascar girls as young as 9 years old get sold off to marry much older men. With 80% of the population relying on farming as a source of income women become commodity. Nofy i Androy equips girls with tools to fight early child marriage, early pregnancies and gender inequality. This project will promise girls college degrees and brighter futures. We redefine the meaning of a "woman" by providing quality education, leadership training, sex education, and women's workshops.

title: Girls Hope - A Dream of Education
description: Girls' Hope, has conducted workshops in the Moduli District in Tanzania to educate the community about gender inequality, the importance of education for girls, and the medical and psychological effects of FGM.  The construction of a new school in the area gives the group the opportunity to conduct a pilot program where girls are given extra support from a young age to encourage them to stay in school through regular visits from guest speakers from Girls Hope and additional educational resources

title: Educate Unprivileged Kids through Free of Cost
description: Bangladesh Samajik Agragati Sangstha ( BSAS ) plans to build 5 schools  to provide free education for unprivileged children who comes from poorest section of society in Magura of Bangladesh,also provide them vocational training besides their primary education.  This project builds 2 Library along with vocational training tools to support service to 2000unprivileged children

title: Free Heart Screening
description: 4 out of every 5 persons that suffer a Cardiac Arrest end in death. This can be greatly reduced by earlier detection of those at risk and also training lay rescuers to identify early arrest victims and initiate response prior to arrival of advanced help or health care providers.

title: Bring Joy to a Survivor For the Holidays!
description: 3 seconds! That's how often we blink our eyes. Sadly, its also the Exact amount of time that lapses before someone becomes a Victim of Violence! That's 1200 times per hour, 28,800 times a day & 10,512,000 a year! Its shocking to think of what happens in the Blink Of An Eye! Let's Join together to Fight for Survival! Your Contribution will make an impact to help Survivors Break Their Chains, Get Support and Find a Safe Haven. Help Bring Hope. Breed Trust. The futures calling, won't you help?

title: Poor Patient Fund
description: "Poor Patient fund" aims to contribute in alleviating the suffering among the Palestinian families in  Gaza Strip in facing the siege impact, through afford the medicines to patients, the expenses needed to the people travel abroad for treatment, and surgeries costs. Hoping that we has contributed in alleviate the pain for those patients, reduction of aggravation of their health and economic matters.

title: ReBuild Panama City
description: On October 10, 2018, Hurricane Michael struck the Florida panhandle, the first Category 5 hurricane to strike the contiguous United States since Andrew in 1992. The extreme winds damaged caused catastrophic damage to literally thousands of homes. Many of these homeowners are low-income and lack the wherewithal to rebuild themselves. Fuller Center Disaster ReBuilders is committed to restoring the homes of those with no other alternative. We do this with volunteer labor and your donations.

title: Life Changing Care for Disabled Filipino Children
description: This project will provide life changing care to physically disabled children from impoverished Filipino families. We help develop a treatment plan, locate services needed, and with our partners and service providers we are able to secure treatment free or at a reduced cost. Our primary purpose is to cover travel expenses for one child and a parent. We also provide funds for health insurance, doctor visits, diagnostic services, orthotics, etc.  as needed.

title: LET HER BE - A touring production for 30 schools
description: 'Let Her Be' is the story of the struggle of a girl who chooses determinedly to pursue her dreams despite her father's obvious disapproval of her constant attempt to learn things that 'only a boy should do'.  With the accompaniment of beautiful choreographic movements and sweet medley of African drums, this theatrical piece highlights the necessity to identify the woman as free from old social limitations and customs. It extols the self-fulfilment and self-development for women.

title: Recognition of Service - Thankful
description: Briana and coworkers want to thank Military Service, Veterans, with card of support, care packages and other humanitarian efforts throughout the year, through the voice of youth ages 5-25.   This all began when a group of high school students teamed up with the support of  team members from various companies, led by Bri, to take on the challenge to provide cards recognition to those who risk their lives for us every day. Now, youth are leading campaigns to support those in need year round.

title: Planting trees to save the planet!
description: 12,000 years ago humans started to farm. Since then, nearly half the world's forests have disappeared, and today we are facing, simultaneously, a global pandemic. and a devastating climate crisis. One of the quickest, most efficient, most cost effective ways to tackle climate change is by planting trees. (IPCC, August 2019) Reforesting 900 million hectares will capture 25% of the carbon in the atmosphere, help stabilize the climate, provide clean air and protect our water resources. Let's do it!

title: Empower Children to Spread Health in Rural China
description: China has made incredible strides in access to health facilities. However, many preventable and treatable illnesses still become lifelong disabilities or chronic diseases due to a lack of proper sanitation and hygiene. CWEF works with rural communities and schools to address this issue through a program called HEAL ("Health Education, Advocacy & Literacy"), which tackles both the need for proper health-related facilities and the knowledge and behavior change needed for healthy living.

title: Monthly Dignity Packs for 120 Swati Kids in 2022
description: For years, Moya has done our best to identify children & adolescents within our communities who are living without the most basic hygiene necessities. We try to create and maintain a sense of dignity for the most vulnerable youth by providing Dignity Packs.  Receiving hygiene items give young beneficiaries, 70% of whom are girls,  confidence to fulfill their potential, stay in school and continue working towards a bright future. This campaign will bring more structure to this project in 2020.

title: Support Early Childhood Development Caregivers
description: Your donation will provide the necessary funds to Education Africa's Train the Trainer project, where ECD caregivers in impoverished communities are taught how to create a productive space for learning and developing for their children.

title: Help build Kindergarten in Central Java, Indonesia
description: ars86care foundation is an Indonesian based foundation which focuses on the environment, children and education spesifically early childhood education. We have long been an advocate for children's right to a proper access to early childhood education. This year our project will help children from Sri Mulia Karangtalun Kindergarten gain a proper school building which has been in poor physicall condition since it's establishment in 1985.

title: Provide Physical Therapy to CoastalBelt,Bangladesh
description: WHO report,around 10% of the population of Bangladesh have different types of physical disabilities. However, lack of adequate medical facilities and often poor diagnosis of diseases by rural doctors put the lives of the children with physical or mental disabilities at risks.The treatment and rehabilitation programs for the people with disabilities can be extended and expanded through creating awareness.So we are thinking for opening aTherapy center in Bakergonj on an urgent basis to serve peope

title: Project Stand Up - Youth Leadership Program
description: The Youth Leadership Program (YLP) will enable refugee youth living in Malaysia to become leaders in their community, through transformative peer to peer training. Using a human-centered design approach, YLP builds the soft skills of young refugees, boosting their capacities to identify and solve the challenges their communities face. YLP has been designed and will be implemented by the Project Stand Up team, who are refugee youth themselves and aim to inspire youth to become change agents.

title: Build 100 toilets for poor Villagers in Bangladesh
description: Survey result in southern areas of Bangladesh 28% and above poor families are not using hygienic sanitary latrine.Due to using unhygienic latrine people are sufferings different diseases Cholera, Dysentery, child diseases & growing unhealthy society.Need to provide hygienic sanitary latrine to under served people.They are not capable to take services with cost.As a result if the people take these facilities from us then  reduce rate of child diseases &  unhealthy society in this  areas.

title: Best Winter Ever
description: Change the hostile Afghan winter to the most beautiful experience of joy, warmth & education for 1100 kids. The underprivileged girls and boys will be enjoying the program in 9 locations (Incl. IDP camps) in 6 provinces: Kabul, Bamyan, Mazar, Herat, Khost and Samangan. The deprived kids, safe and secure from the bitterness of the winter will be learning different School Subjects, English, Computer, Environmental Protection, Artistic, Social and Life Skills while having enormous fun with circus.

title: Give 150 Unpaid Carers a Party!
description: Unpaid carers make huge sacrifices, often putting their own life and wellbeing on hold to focus on the person they care for. Your gift could treat an unpaid carer to a well-deserved celebration evening - with a delicious meal, live entertainment and fun with fellow carers. The Celebration Party will take place in late January 2020. Your donation would help host the evening which as many as 150 carers may attend. Show an unpaid carer you care and treat them to a rightly earned party!

title: After School support to 45-50 needy kids in Nepal
description: We are seeking to start our second program to help children living in poverty; kids that have only the rote learning of school and little stimulation or adult support within their home or institution. The School+Plus program is a proven approach to developing and empowering kids; it provides two hours of daily tutoring, art and music classes, regular health check-ups, and daily nutritious meals, in a caring and loving environment. And we're planning Adult Literacy Classes to help families.

title: Building kindergarten for 100 kids in Uganda
description: "Building kindergarten for 100 kids in Uganda" is a sub-project of our bigger project - "Building a school and orphanage" which is partial funded. "Smile for Africa foundation" has the courage to realize the dream of buying land and build a school, orphanage and kindergarten in rural Uganda. Our purpose is to give home for around 100 orphans and care and education for more than 300 children.

title: Empower Peruvian Women Living in Poverty
description: The Women's Empowerment Project, run by Globalteer in Peru, empowers and educates deprived women living in rural villages near Cusco, for free. We provide the resources, market knowledge, financial backing and emotional support so that these women can become successful business owners, build their confidence and achieve economic independence. Please help us in supporting these women to provide for their families and offer their community an alternative future to poverty.

title: Empower Agents of Change
description: At UWC Costa Rica we make the impossible possible: we bring together 200+ students from 70+ different countries from across the socio-economic spectrum.  Our cross-subsidized tuition model and strong philanthropy program make it so 80% of our students to receive the financial aid they need.  And we don't stop there!  Our distinctive educational model, grounded on experiential learning, empowers our students to become empathic agents of change committed to shaping a better future.

title: Train 10 Women + Keep Weaving Alive in Kenya
description: Imani Collective is a socioeconomic empowerment program focused on creating dignified jobs and taking a holistic approach to empowerment. We care about the whole person and want to ensure that they get adequate training to be able to excel in this life.  This project will allow us to expand our program by adding capacity and training for 10 new weavers, which will simultaneously create a brighter future for these artisans, and preserve the art of weaving in Kenya.

title: Hot Meals for Vulnerable Seniors
description: The "Hot Meals for Vulnerable Seniors" project rescues surplus meals in the afternoon from corporate cafeterias and hotels.  The meals are then transferred to distribution hubs where they are refrigerated overnight, and then the next day are reheated in stainless trays and transported in thermal containers to senior citizen's day care centers and meals on wheels programs for the housebound where they are served for lunch.

title: #GivingTuesday Year-End Campaign
description: As 2019 comes to a close, join RAM in our end of the year campaign, which launches on #GivingTuesday, December 3, and runs through the end of the year as part of the global holiday giving season. This year, Remote Area Medical will be counting on your support. Our goal is to raise $90,000 with a theme of #healthyholidays in order to continue to provide quality care to those in need. Thank you so much for your support.

title: Hearing Equipment Supply Cabinet
description: Chattering Children is raising funds to stock a hearing device supply cabinet, complete with cables, ear hooks, batteries and accessories from each manufacturer. This will enable us to quickly provide children what they need when their devices break. In our effort to serve children with hearing loss and help them succeed, we need to have the necessary supplies and parts on hand so that they always have access to sound.

title: Happy Meals for 300 Hungry Children
description: We will provide sumptuous meals comprising fried chicken, rice, roasted pork, chocolates, milk and ice cream to 300 hungry children this Holiday season. These food are favorite Filipino delicacies of which most children from poor families only dream about. At least, only for this Christmas and New Year, these food will bring smiles to their faces and hearts.

title: Give Life-Changing Education to 500 Maasai Girls
description: Even prior to the COVID, only 1 in 16 Maasai girls living in Kenya's Loita Hills graduated from primary school. Without access to electricity or internet, students there had no access to remote lessons provided by the government during COVID-school closures. This project scaled offline education to hundreds of those students in 2020. The unique access it offered to interactive digital STEM, arts & literacy content was so successful we have added it to our core programming.

title: Chicken Farms for War Widows
description: Tens of thousands of war widows and wives of the missing have been forced to become the primary income earners.  Even after 10 years since the end of the war several families in the war affected areas are still in need of assistance to generate a steady income stream.  The "Chicken Farm project" will be a self-help project as a means of income-generation and self-sustenance. The initial phase of this project is to help 25 families to get established with this income generating stream.

title: Provide Holiday Cheers this Christmas
description: Thousands of poor farming families are affected by severe natural disasters and we aim to provide them goodies this Holiday Season comprising loved and sought-after food delicacies, books, toys and clothes for the children and some cash assistance that they will be able to use for their own needs.

title: Tools Empowering Women in Zimbabwe
description: Women in Zimbabwe struggle to feed their children in a country ravaged by inflation and unemployment. This project will help 200 women in Zimbabwe survive; with the tools and training to generate income.

title: Prevention of Genocide against Pygmies in the DRC
description: This project assists the Programme d'Integration et Development (PIDP), a Bambuti NGO which documents human rights abuses against Bambuti Pygmies, especially women and children, in the Ituri Forest of the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. PIDP desperately needs a heavy-duty vehicle to reach isolated Bambuti communities - to document human rights abuses, and to provide emergency services like health care and food parcels. This forms part of the PIDP Campaign for the Prevention of Genocide

title: The Gorilla Guardians of Bwindi, Uganda
description: This project protects endangered Mountain Gorillas in Uganda by supporting community members to become Gorilla Guardians - teams of community volunteers who are trained to monitor gorilla health and safely herd them back into the forest when they have strayed out of the protected areas.

title: Warm Clothes for Pakistani Kids in Extreme Winter
description: In Pakistan, the lack of financial resources and extreme poverty makes 30% of the children in Pakistan extremely vulnerable during winters. At average, there are 3 children in each family of Pakistan and majority gets seriously ill due to extreme cold in winters and without having excess to warm clothing. A Small Clothing Package can make their winters warm and special. AWARD will provide warm clothing to 150 children from the extreme poor families in the giving season of December in Faisalabad.

title: Empower 220 women in Kenya with $20 for 2 chicken
description: The project will support 220 women to have 2 chicken that will allow them to support at least 3 children's livelihoods in Sotik town, Bomet County, Kenya. Through your donation of $20, a mother will acquire 2 mature improved indigenous chicken to initiate an enterprise that will earn her income and improve her family's livelihood. By the end of this project, 220 women and 1100 indirect beneficiaries in Sotik, will have improved livelihoods contributing to improved economy, in line with SDG 8.

title: Skills training for 200 learners in rural Zimbabwe
description: This project will enable 200 learners across all 10 provinces of Zimbabwe to participate in the National Business Case Competition. Over a space of 6 months, learners will be challenged to develop integrated solutions to Zimbabwe's most pressing business and economic issues. In doing this learners will gain practical problem solving skills and competencies necessary to create sustainable business solutions for themselves and the communities around them.

title: The best start of a newborns life
description: This project will support the mothers from the slums that might not be able to fund the needs of their new born child. Supporting these mothers makes sure that their child has the best start of life as possible.

title: Settecento: our new album for a global audience
description: La Serenissima's vision is to enrich life through sharing our passion for Italian baroque music. Recording is a vital part of our mission enabling us to make our highest quality work freely available (via radioplay and streaming). New album Settecento places neglected composers Brescianello, Mancini and Vandini in the context of more famous musicians Scarlatti, Tartini and Vivaldi. Tabea Debus (recorder) will play a central role in the album, bringing her artistry to a wider audience.

title: Vocational skills for 70 teens at risk of violence
description: This project will teach a vocational skill to 70 teens who are at risk of violence. The kids are referred by schools and social services because they have a difficult or very poor background, and are at risk of leaving school with no qualifications and becoming either a victim or perpetrator of violence. This project teaches them welding, electrics, barbering, tailoring, decoration or cooking, as well as offering schooling support, discussion groups and family psychotherapy sessions.

title: Help LHR Face Challenges Beyond the Shore
description: For the past five years, Lighthouse Relief (LHR) has offered a dignified humanitarian response on the north shore of Lesvos and Ritsona Refugee Camp on the Greek mainland. In 2020, refugees and asylum seekers in Greece faced unprecedented challenges, with increased tensions on Lesvos and the threat of COVID-19. In August of 2020, we relaunched our in-person psychosocial support activities in Ritsona. As we continue to provide a dignified response, help us to forge a path ahead.

title: Affordable Education for International Students
description: By the end of March 2020, we aim to secure funds for partial scholarships for financially disadvantaged prospective students from post-communist countries. Financial support in the amount of 20% of the cost of tuition for the first year of education will be provided to 10 scholars in August 2020, for Academic year 2020/2021. Even if we don't manage to raise the whole amount, we will proportionately distribute whatever we have collected by the deadline.

title: Community Based Water Quality Monitoring Program
description: The Futaleufu River and one of its main tributaries, the Espolon River, are under increasing environmental threat from development. The Futaleufu Riverkeeper is working to establish the region's first water quality monitoring program to serve as the first line of defense against polluters. We will pair with Global Water Watch to develop a community-based monitoring system, in which local volunteers are given EPA-certified training to collect and analyze samples.

title: Farm equipment for rural Ugandan tribe
description: The Karamojong tribe we are working with in rural Uganda are the poorest of the poor.  They struggle with lack of water, poor health, hunger, and lack of education.   They are learning to become farmers.  They have good tillable land on which to grow their crops.  It is a huge backbreaking task when the only tools they have are simple hoes. They have a tractor and plow, they need other equipment.   The people will be able to raise more food for themselves and have excess to sell.

title: Rehab Gaza children traumatized by war
description: This project addresses the extreme need for mental health services and psychosocial rehab. Gaza children are suffering from different forms of violence and abuse as a result of political, economic, and social deterioration in the strip. PAMA Youth are US youth who stepped up to help their counterparts in Gaza. They are collaborating with Al-Ahli Arabi hospital in Gaza. Please join them and help our people in Gaza.

title: End Period Poverty and Give Girls, Women Hope
description: Girls and women living in poverty struggle to afford essential period products to manage their menstrual hygiene. As a result, many low-income girls miss valuable days of school or work every month. Education rises out of poverty, and when girls are unable to fully participate in educational opportunities, their potential of breaking the cycle of poverty is diminished. Mothers struggling to work will struggle to care for their families.

title: Community wants to provide water to seven families
description: The Puerto Rico Community Foundation (Fundacion Comunitaria de Puerto Rico) joins Giving Tuesday 2019 to support the Algarrobo Community Aqueduct Inc., in Aibonito, to raise $7,316.86 to facilitate access to drinking water for seven (7) families. This women lead community aqueduct provides access to water to more than 70 families (250 individuals) in the isolated rural community of Algarrobo, Aibonito-Puerto Rico.

title: Help 45 Special Needs Children in Uganda
description: Jake's Diapers serves previously abandoned babies in devastatingly difficult situations, where sometimes a choice has to be made between food, diapers, and medical care. Jake's donates cloth diapers at no cost to orphanages and rescue centers so these organizations can afford basic living expenses and focus on a solution for problems such as malnutrition and starvation. Cloth diapers provide a long-term solution from birth through potty-training, truly changing the lives of these children.

title: DRINKING WATER SUPPLY PROJECT AT  RUGERO SCHOOL
description: Helping the Rugero I Basic School and the inhabitants of Rugero I, in Kirundo commune and province in Burundi, to have clean water is to cover the lives of students, teachers and the surrounding community who are in danger and raise development obstacles, particularly in rural areas. The municipality of Kirundo has a very low access rate to drinking water. It is estimated that about 10% of Burundian population in rural areas have access to drinking water.

title: Start the Celebration by Giving an Education
description: Give back by providing the necessary items a low-income child needs to receive a great education in 2023.   By giving to Centro Infantil de Los Angeles, you are helping over 80 children receive the education and nutrition they need to be successful in kindergarten and beyond.   Isn't that a great present? We can't think of anything better!

title: Empowering Kenyan Girls
description: This project is based in Bungoma County, Kenya where there are many families and children in the sprawling and often poor small villages. We have initiated many local projects, which have brought a new optimism into their community.  Now we are focusing on the girls and women and fully engaging them in becoming advocates for their own needs. They are speaking out and taking on their own projects, not just feminine hygiene, but community building.

title: Support 100 children access assistive devices
description: Katalemwa seeks to support 100 children with disabilities access assistive devices to aid their healing process during post surgery and therapy, support their mobility and enhance participation. We annually support over 15,000 children with disabilities in Uganda both in the community and at the center to access medical rehabilitation services. 50% of the children, require assistive devices in form of wheel chairs, prosthesis, orthesis, walkers, Cp chairs, standing frames, orthopedic shoes.

title: Rescue Endangered Wildlife in Guatemala
description: ARCAS is a Guatemalan NGO dedicated to wildlife rescue and rehabilitation.  It receives 250 - 500 confiscated animals per year, including white-fronted and red-lored parrots, yellow-naped amazons, scarlet macaws, coatimundis, spider and howler monkeys, iguanas, crocodiles, margays, jaguars, raccoons and kinkajous.  This project will support the feeding and medical costs of animals undergoing rehabilitation in ARCAS's three main project sites: the Pacific coast, the altiplano and Peten.

title: 600 computers for 600 Japanese Orphanages
description: Across Japan, 30,000 children live in orphanages and children's homes.   As digital literacy and internet access become mandatory for modern life, the gap between children in the homes and their peers widens.   To bridge this gap, YouMeWe is campaigning to put a computer in each home, so that each child has the best chances possible to connect with their education, seek employment, and access learning opportunities.  Our first targets are the 28 homes along the old Tokaido Road.

title: Indigenous women save the sacred Mayan bee
description: The melipona bee is a species without sting, in danger of extinction, that is native of the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico. The relationship between the melipona bee and the Mayan people dates back to millenary times. The Mayans consider them a gift from the gods. Groups of indigenous women, guardians of this bee, are dedicated to their daily care, protection and reproduction. This activity allows these Mayan women with lack of economic resources to have an income for the welfare of their families.

title: Empower Internally Displaced Youths
description: This project aims to provide business opportunities to 40 Internally displaced youths (IDPs)  in conflict-affected communities by assisting internally displaced young men and women from Kumba and Buea to create businesses by March 2020.  Thousands of youths have been left jobless, lost their property and businesses to fire and are now likely to join armed groups, have unwanted pregnancies and suffer extreme poverty.

title: Help SPCA get justice in court for murdered Benji
description: The Cape of Good Hope SPCA in Cape Town have been seeking justice in our courts for the past 18 months. SPCA Inspector Siviwe Noko needs your support to continue fighting this case on behalf of Benji- an innocent dog brutally stabbed to death in Kayelitsha, Cape Town , South Africa 2018.   We will not give up until justice is served and we can give a voice to the voiceless victims of animal abuse - like dear Benji. Help us continue to fight against Animal Cruelty on #GivingTuesday

title: Albania Earthquake Relief Efforts
description: Albania was affected by a major, 6.4 magnitude earthquake the morning of 11/26. Over 20 people died, more than 600 injured, and thousands left homeless. Our organization has quickly responded to provide ground support. With expertise on mother and infant care, we are preparing boxes of food and clothing for families with children, helping maternity hospitals with medical supplies, and providing psychological care for traumatized mothers. We need your help to maximize our efforts!

title: Resolve Human-Chimpanzee Conflicts w/ Water Wells
description: Wild chimpanzees in Uganda need our help to survive. Habitat destruction forces them into competition with villagers for space and resources, including access to surface water at forest streams. We will provide an immediate solution: building hand-dug wells in villages away from the forest. Wells give people access to clean safe water, and reduce daily, sometimes dangerous encounters with chimps. It's a win-win! A generous external (non-Global Giving) donor will match contributions up to $4,200!

title: Help 600 Students Living in Guyana Learn to Read
description: Blossoms of Guyana plans to renovate the reading room and donate 500 books to provide literacy education for 600 primary school children who come from the poorest areas in Guyana.  Blossoms will also provide school supplies for students and teaching supplies for teachers.   This project creates a library at the local school, provides a supply of books, school and teaching supplies which will help improve the educational outcomes of students.

title: Help us build a school for 100 students in Nepal
description: Education is an undeniable right, and we here at Diyalo Foundation believe that not even a natural calamity should be able to take that away from us. So we're asking you to join us on this road to recovery, to renew the future of 100 young children. We want, we need, your unwavering support and faith to build a School, and to bring the light of education to those who do not have the ability to grasp it.

title: Aid for Albanian Earthquake Survivors
description: A deadly 6.4 magnitude earthquake hit Albania in November 2019. 51 people were killed and 2,000 were injured. Government relief efforts are focusing on population centers like Durres and Tirana; moving forward, Nehemiah Gateway will help earthquake survivors living in poverty in rural villages. Many lost their homes, but cannot leave because livestock is their greatest asset. We are helping them with humanitarian aid and home reconstruction, because winter is a terrible time to be homeless.

title: Help 1000 mothers access child birth services
description: This project will prevent maternal and child mortality by providing at least four(4) sessions of antenatal care services, which involves health education,physical examination, vitamin and mineral supplements, important laboratory investigations,malaria IPT etc for 1000 rural economically disadvantaged women in Iseyin LGA, Oyo state Nigeria. We will also distribute birthing consumables to all the enrolled pregnant women within our target community.

title: Great Education for Impoverished Preschoolers
description: Every year, thousands of children are left to sit at home or in backyard creches with little to no education. During this critical stage, they sit stagnant. Their teachers lack the training and tools to prepare them.   Botshabelo is passionate about transforming their stories. Partner with us to empower 150 women to uplift the standard of education in 50 Gauteng preschools in 2020 through training, educational resources, and mentoring support.   Together, we give 2500 children a brighter future!

title: Promote Clean Water & WaSH to Girls in Nepal
description: Our ambitious project seeks to bring water access, sanitation and menstrual hygiene management to three high hilltop schools and surrounding communities in Nepal's Gulmi District.  With an anticipated timeframe of April 2020 to October 2025, this project will bring water access to more than 1,031 school children and reach over 4,640 indirect beneficiaries with improved WaSH practices.

title: Forest restoration for biodiversity in Malawi
description: WeForest aims to restore the ecosystems in and around Mount Mulanje, a highly degraded forest reserve in southern Malawi, characterized by a high biodiversity with species that don't exist anywhere else in the world. Sadly, native forests have been disappearing rapidly affecting the local wildlife population as well.  WeForest is restoring two types of native forest - Afromontane forest and Miombo woodland - while also providing alternative sources of income and training to local communities.

title: Blorange days - 5 open sports festivals 2020
description: Footura Blorange day - #blorange * We will do 5 Open Sports festivals for youths, active people, everybody - 3 Sports: Table Tennis, Soccer and Tennis.  *(from blue-orange - both Association Footura colors) All events will have a mass character - participation and sports, Fairplay and friendship, motivation and sports-active lifestyle culture are important! We also retain the Charity model and anyone can donate during sporting events for personal or social causes that we will support together.

title: Big Move for Cheetah Experience!!
description: Our dream has always been to secure bigger land for our animals and we are excited to say that we have found the purrfect place!! 272 Ha of African bush where we can build bigger enclosures for the animals, with lots of trees and scrub land! The first hurdle is as ever money! This is where you come in!  While we have successfully raised money for the enclosures, now we need to raise money for the meatroom, electric fencing as well as much more! The dream is big but so are our, and your hearts!

title: Oral Health Story Book For 10000 Rural Kids
description: Support us to donate 10000 more copies of "the girl who found her smile" to rural children across Africa. Donating $50 means 5 rural children can get this book for free.

title: Empowering Women for a Better Tomorrow
description: Women Literacy & Empowerment Program is zealously working to provide functional literacy to underprivileged illiterate adult women of deprived communities. The women are unable to perform basic day-to-day activities such as reading newspapers, reading bus numbers, and helping children with the studies. Education is imparted via the Computer Based Functional Literacy Program and are taught basic Hindi and Arithmetic. Currently, we are organizing 414 Women Literacy Centers in North Delhi.

title: Support the USAP Community School in Zimbabwe!
description: This project supports the USAP Community School which launched with 45 Lower Sixth (11th grade) students in Zimbabwe in January 2020.  This unique residential A Level school educates high-achieving, low-income Zimbabwean students to excel at the world's top universities and return home to build society. Seeking the brightest students from underserved communities in Zimbabwe, the Quaker school teaches Cambridge Science A levels, critical thinking,research methods,computer literacy and Humanities.

title: Christmas with TECHO
description: As an organization, TECHO works for community developments in slums.  To aim that we have developed an education assistance program for kids at risk in those communities.  Most of the time, public education doesn't fill all their necessity of knowledge so we look to earn a better quality education for those kids.   With your support, we gonna be able to keep working in improving primary education skills in kids in social risk. At this moment we have the program active in 10 communities in Mexico

title: Support to Families of the Earthquake in Albania
description: Partnere per Femijet is supporting some of the most poor and desolate families affected by the earthquake that hit Albania that has left them sleeping in plastic and flimsy tents or in temporary shelters and without the basics for life.  The project will support the families with food, clothes, bedding, nappies, medication, support to find accommodation and psychosocial support and activities for the children.

title: Together, let's grow up, let's open possibilities
description: Les Ideateurs is a 16-year-old non-profit organization.  We are totally convinced that human potentials doesn't have an age nor a label.
