While there supposed to go through one timeline but at different time in someone's life, we work to connect the education world and the entrepreneurship world so each can share energies and experiences.  We know that the new generation, the youth can create great things for the future of all of us.

title: Giving Tuesday w/Girls Empowerment Sierra Leone!
description: It's Giving Tuesday & we at Girls Empowerment Sierra Leone (GESL) could use your help! Through our year-round core programs emphasizing personal & leadership growth, community service, health & sexual reproductive rights, innovation & creativity, GESL has successfully impacted the lives of over 300 girls in the past 7 year!  This Giving Tuesday, please consider donating towards sustaining our programming that helps girls in Sierra Leone find a voice and become tomorrow's leaders!

title: Power Safety for Detained Immigrant Families
description: During this holiday season, we are partnering to provide urgently needed relief to Indigenous families from the U.S.-Mexico border.  Many detained families require safe respite and together we can provide solar powered renewable energy for warm showers and food, and legal, language and cultural support.  Please join us as we work with an overburdened Indigenous center that is a beacon to families in crisis who have been swept up in a system that separates children from parents.

title: Support Proven Solutions: Youth Climate Award 2022
description: Over the last decade, WAFA has honoured community-based "silent heroes" throughout the world for their innovative grassroots solutions. Expanding its mission, WAFA has launched the Youth Climate Award in April 2021 to support young "climate warriors" who are working for community-based sustainable development. These under 25 sustainability enthusiasts are the committed future good citizens, who need to be supported, exposed and nurtured.

title: Give school to abandoned Children in Pakistan
description: Street Children are mostly involved in begging, rag-picking, drug peddling and only a handful of them are working as cobblers, paper boys, waiters and flower sellers. They beg, steal and sometimes even work as prostitutes. Their lifestyle makes them vulnerable to anti-social behaviour. The terrorists may be picking their fodder from among them. FRDP Planing abandoned Orphans getting food, education, uniforms, clothes. Children are access to sports & games, computer skills training.

title: Cultivating youth social change leaders
description: CONCAUSA aims to bring together 51 social change leaders from across the Americas to develop their capacity as leaders and strengthen the sustainable development projects that they are carrying out to make a positive change in their communities.

title: NUTRITION SECURITY FOR CHILDREN
description: Gift Angels Foundation project will provide child care support to 200 Orphans and vulnerable children (disabled, Hiv/AIDs victims, abandoned, streetchildren, and orphans) the fundraiser will provide tuition sponsorship to these children, provide meals for the children(this means that the children will be able to acquire education. Many of these children in our child care programs are disadvantaged and do not have access to nutritional foods and supplements .

title: Building and supporting sustainable peace in Kenya
description: This Project aims at empwering communities of men, women and youths with peace building, conflict resolution and social justice advocacy skills with the  goal of positioning them as agents of Peace and Change at the community level so that they are able  to mediate and intervene with Alternative Dispute Resolution skills to conflicts that keep on emerging in their localities without relying on external expatriates every time a conflict arises.

title: Restore the incredible Zambian Miombo forests
description: The incredible African Miombo forests - home to iconic wildlife, a significant global carbon stock, and supporting the lives of millions of people - are under threat. Through community-based forest management, WeForest is establishing thousands of hectares of forest regeneration and conservation. WeForest is working with farmers and local communities to protect and restore these forests.

title: Infertility Project
description: INCIID (pronounced inside) is a nonprofit charity helping individuals and couples explore their family-building options. It provides current information and immediate support regarding the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infertility and pregnancy loss. INCIID was first on the WWW in 1995 and has helped 10's of thousands of people become parents. In April 2004, INCIID launched the first and only National IVF Scholarship program. We need an updated site to continue our work & Scholarships

title: Projects on the Go - Girls Reading to Succeed
description: This project will take its mobile makerspace activity clubs to underprivileged girl's schools. Serving 1000 girls from 10 low income government schools. It will provide them with hands on learning opportunity in Arts, Crafts. Electronics, ICT and Photography. It will allow them to tinker, experiment, create and analyze critically and help these 1000 girls to career direction and start small business from homes.

title: Protecting 1469 Yemeni children from malnutrition
description: Yemeni people face the  risk of malnutrition, especially pregnant and lactating women and girls and children under 5 years old. This project will reduce levels of malnutrition by 2020 through  community-oriented strategy .Supporting proper nutrition, health care, teaching women and raising community awareness are vital pillars in the project that will reduce excess morbidity and mortality caused by malnutrition amongst 285 of children under 5 years of age and 639 of pregnant and lactating women.

title: Train 30 Social Entrepreneurs to Create BIG Impact
description: Flame Tree Initiative will train, mentor, and empower social entrepreneurs in Malawi to build successful businesses that create change in their communities.

title: Preventing Future Generation from Abuse.
description: One of the major drivers of domestic abuse is lack of financial independence.Domestic abuse also leads to economic set backs resulting from controls, disability,depression. Through this project we hope to teach victims and survivors of domestic abuse certain skills that will enhance their confidence and financial independence. We shall be teaching  100 women ceramics, basic computer lessons, Arts and Crafts,,sewing, crafty cakes, and basic entprenuership skills over a period of one year.

title: Give 300 Kids in Angola Access to Education
description: Every child has the right to education. RISE builds primary schools in rural Angola to educate children, empower communities and contribute to the rebuilding of the country. We target vulnerable and marginalized children who have been impacted by years of war and its aftermath, those living in poverty that face multiple barriers to education, and deserve the basics that all children deserve.

title: Help Bring Clean Water to the Navajo Nation
description: Through women for water, Global Water Challenge is partnering with DigDeep to provide clean, running water to women and their families on the Navajo Nation while raising awareness around the transformative impacts that clean water access provides for women all over the world, including in the US. With support from its partners, the Navajo Water Project is deploying locally-led solutions through the development of sustainable water systems, including those utilizing solar-powered infrastructure.

title: Keep Girls in Rugby
description: Shamas Rugby Foundation engages 568 young girls between the ages of 10 and 18 from 8 informal settlements in Nairobi and Kiambu County to learn and practice life skills through the sport of rugby. The aim of this project is to keep our girls in rugby by identifying what hinders them from being consistent in the game and providing these necessities to keep them engaged on the pitch.

title: Bringing Justice
description: Our Multi-front Strategy to Stop Human Trafficking begins with focused influence through training and coaching with governments to bring into place policies that work to end trafficking.  We bring civic groups, police, justice, and educational leaders into relationship and training toward identifying at-risk or those in trafficked situations quickly. Advocating for change, bringing justice and training those in power will lead to an end in slavery globally.

title: Support 50 Vulnerable Children in Calabar
description: This project will support 50 vulnerable children in Cross River State, Nigeria with access to education, health and psycho-social services by paying their tuition fees, medical bills, providing school materials and psycho-social support.

title: Help us build a school for 100 students in Nepal
description: Education is an undeniable right, and we here at Diyalo Foundation believe that not even a natural calamity should be able to take that away from us. So we're asking you to join us on this road to recovery, to renew the future of 100 young children. We want, we need, your unwavering support and faith to build a School, and to bring the light of education to those who do not have the ability to grasp it.

title: Care for a Child's Heart
description: This Project is an extension of Help Mend a Broken Heart in Kenya, a 20-year Initiative of providing life-saving surgeries for over 1000 children with heart ailments in Kenya and neighboring countries. Cardiologists and surgeons from the United States and Europe voluntarily travel to Kenya 3 times per year to donate their time and professional skills to perform these operations. Children & Charity International collaborates with Care for A Child's Heart (CFACH) to support this worthy cause.

title: International Cultural House Kilkenny Ireland
description: By having an International Cultural House combining all Nationalities and groups regardless of background or status gives a unique opportunity to support and develop cultural activities through their regular contact. By offering the support and advice on many different subjects of Interest we can develop and socially inclusive society through integration. With our support and European connections, we offer a brighter future. We will help develop individual identity through Culture & Education

title: Polio Home Renovation - Ho Chi Minh City
description: Project funded through other source.

title: The Mexican Sea Turtle Revolution
description: This project will provide support and professional advice to five Community Sea Turtle Camps that focus their efforts in the rescue and preservation of the sea turtle in the Oaxaca coastline. We work with the local communities and people who were once eggs poachers and now have become the best guardians of the beaches. We also work with 6 elementary schools leading environmental education workshops to generate conservation actions to protect the sea turtles that arrive in their communities.

title: Quality education for Peruvian Amazonian Children
description: We believe in the power of education and trust in the potential of all Peruvians. We want a country where every student has the opportunity to realize their purpose and achieve their dreams. To do so, we work daily inspired by our vision which is to achieve that by 2032, at least 8 out of 10 children in Peru receive a quality education. Our goal is to raise $10,000 to continue providing education of excellence to amazonian students who are returning to classes after 2 years of hybrid education.

title: Language Enrichment in a Nurturing Environment
description: This project will provide reading and writing support for 30 middle schoolers who are not prepared to enter high school and are at high risk for drop out. By sixth and seventh grade, these students still cannot read or write well enough to do classwork or homework.  The project will provide after school programming with fun and enriching activities that teach both reading and writing skills as well as a love of learning.

title: Job Training for Poor Mothers - sick children
description: Help poor mothers with sick children currently undergoing hospitalization or treatment far from home. Help the mothers  to be near the children, generate income and to find jobs.

title: Training 1,500 Women Entrepreneurs in Pakistan
description: Pakistan is ranked second to last worldwide in terms of women engaged in the workforce. Gaining support of male family members, Moqah Foundation provides young women with training to learn entrepreneurial skills to start or grow businesses so that they may send their children to school, and lift their families out of poverty.

title: Gifts that keep giving
description: Give the gift of empowerment this Christmas with one of 12 special gifts from Women's Resource Center, Cambodia. With your help, WRC can break down participation barriers such as transportation, and provide more support and resources to women in need. With an estimated 125,000 tonnes of plastic packaging thrown out at Christmas time, an e-gift card from WRC is the perfect zero-waste gift for your loved ones. So what are you waiting for? E-gift cards will be sent within 24 hours of purchase.

title: Syrian Women's Workshop for Self-Reliance
description: In our Support to Life community centre in Sanliurfa, a Turkish city bordering Syria, we find the opportunity to meet women who had to flee from their homes due to the Syrian conflict. Now they have to care not only of themselves, their children, and their family. This project seeks to improve the lives of the refugee women by providing a resourceful workshop, and their very own Brand, so that they can produce together, in solidarity, and gain economic independence.

title: Help Afghan Girls Like Mehrin
description: 11-year-old Mehrin sells chewing gum on the streets to help her father support the family. One year after registering at ASCHIANA, Mehrin can read and do math. She hopes to someday become a doctor and treat the poor in her community.

title: Build a Learning Centre with us in Southern India
description: Enabling Futures 2020!  We at Thamarai stand for the values of full potential and well being of all. After 13 years of providing educational services in temporary or rented spaces, we are building a learning centre and sports ground on land offered by Auroville to us for village well-being activities.   Thamarai is the Tamil word for lotus flower and supports a daily playgroup for 36 children, two after-schools for 100 children and natural health care educations and services for all.

title: Refugee Families affected by economic crisis
description: Through this project Naba'a organization is planning to support the most impoverished refugee families living in the camps whom are affected by the recent deterioration of the socio-economic and political situation in Lebanon,  knowing that those families are already suffering from hazardous and difficult situations. Knowing that, due these difficult situations the poverty rate in these camps reached 73% and 65% suffering from unemployment.

title: Child education to 150 needy children in Uganda
description: The project aims at providing primary education to 150 orphaned and underprivileged children in our community. 4/5 children cannot afford quality primary education in Uganda. At completion of the primary level, a child is equipped with basic knowledge and skills. Orphans and vulnerable children in disadvantaged communities are our target group. Supporting these children with scholastic materials and school fees will enable a child to stay in school and complete primary education.

title: Our Sansar Winter Warmer 2019/20
description: Winters are getting colder & colder in Nepal and we have a growing number of street children to support now across the Our Sansar home and the CHildren's Helpline. We have a list of items that we are hoping you can support us with this winter to keep the children, warm, safe, healthy & happy.

title: Inspire 80 students to transform their communities
description: Inspirate is a mexican high school students bootcamp held in Saltillo, Coahuila. During three days, 80 students develop, building upon their self awareness, their social leadership skills so that they can positively impact their communities.

title: Help women to tell their stories
description: femLENS' workshops for the most vulnerable and resourceless women will teach visual, technological and storytelling skills. femLENS encourages women from diverse economic and cultural backgrounds to tell their stories through documentary photography, empowering them and making them more confident, as well as helping them become role models in their communities. With the workshops we hope to raise global awareness on social issues through first-hand accounts.

title: Rural food processing - reversing migration
description: We propose a type of food drive to give temporary work opportunities to recently-returned migrant workers who'd otherwise hang out till spring.  We're fundraising for raw ingredients and some equipment, while staffing and space (at Eco-village Moldova) will be provided.

title: Anita, Alex and Annabel Nicholson Memorial Fund
description: Anita, Alex and Annabel Nicholson lost their lives in the Sri Lanka bombings on Easter Sunday 2019. The Anita, Alex and Annabel Nicholson Memorial Fund has had enormous support in their memory and is being used to create a legacy to the optimistic and positives lives they led.  Our partner projects across Asia are creating a safe,fun environment where children can be themselves, with high quality education,health,well being and inclusion at the core. All of this is done with the ethos of rugby.

title: Kenya - empowering women and orphans
description: Through a process based on relationship and coaching, women are being trained in income-generating skills, like sewing/tailoring, baking, and hairdressing, allowing long term independence and freedom from extreme poverty.  Children, orphaned by the AIDS epidemic in Kenya, are being cared for by the villagers who are training the children to become sustainable long term.  This project provides resources for growing food, education, clean water, and basic life skills that prevent disease.

title: Project Optics
description: The purpose of optical shop  is to offer accessible optical services mainly to the low- and middle-income population of 10 municipalities of the department of Chontales, Nicaragua. By establishing an optical service and shop, enough profit will be generated to create a source of permanent revenue to help social programs such as the Ruach Foundation  in Juigalpa: a local foundation that responds to the needs of social protection and support for adults with intellectual disabilities and inclusion

title: Transmitter for women's community radio in Nepal.
description: Help support women's radio in Nepal and create jobs for women in media. There are very few women's media outlets in Nepal and this is perhaps the only 100% women owned and operated community radio station. We need to change the narrative about women by changing the narrators to women!

title: Support Women Peacebuilders in Asia
description: Women in Asia through Peace Circles are breaking taboos around menstruation, highlighting wrongs of child marriage, building bridges across religious and tribal divides, mobilizing men to promote women's participation in policy making and advocating for transformational and healing narratives in their society. The Peace circles led by our dedicated Creators of Peace Facilitators have made a significant contribution to these changes. These women need support to enable them to continue and expand.

title: 180 Scholarships for Vocational Training in Haiti
description: This project will provide scholarship funds to 180 men and women to be certified through Extollo's vocational training programs in Welding, Masonry, Concrete, or Electric. Graduates can use their training to find jobs in the construction industry and on average earn 2x more than they did before being trained.

title: Seed capital for Oaxacan artisans
description: From the Oaxaca Community Foundation, we want to contribute to strengthening and boosting the productivity of small groups of artisans from the State of Oaxaca, through small investments of seed capital and support in their development. The intention of this project is to generate a fund that allows small donations to be given to artisan groups that are close to the Foundation and who, due to their size or lack of experience, cannot access broader resources or calls from specialized institutions

title: Teach Sewing to 38 Rwandan Women and Children
description: This project will provide a six-month training in sewing and handicrafts for 23 Rwandan women, as well as provide literacy workshops for 15 Rwandan children in a low income neighborhood of Rwanda's capital Kigali. A locally-founded and administered NGO, Isano Women and Youth Empowerment has already trained over 50 women and currently has a waiting list for their vocational and literacy trainings. The next session beings on January 13th and they urgently need funds for their operating budget.

title: Support 15 local food entrepreneurs & teams
description: We are looking to fundraise to set up a modern Agri-Hub space that will support 15 local startup teams in Mauritius, that will in turn support the local food supply on the island. These local agripreneurs will be assessed based on three main criterias: (i) novelty of their idea, (ii) their ability to provide a positive benefit to the local food system, and (iii) their overall impact on people and planet.

title: Water Project
description: The Water Project's mission is to provide clean water service to the 30,000 Darfur genocide survivors. About 85% of survivors are women, children and elderly in the refugee camp in Chad. Desert winds and rain displace sand from afar filling refugee water wells during the summer. Refugees depend on ponds for drinking water during the rainy season, but suffer water shortage due to contamination. While refugees volunteer to clean up the buried wells, they need tools and resources to maintain them.

title: 6000 Safe Stoves for Darfur Refugee Mothers
description: 7,000 Safe Stoves for Darfur Refugee Mothers provides 7,000 Darfuri refugee families with a safe and efficient way to prepare meals using the Mud Stove, created and implemented by Darfur Women Network. Safe Stoves positively impacts survivors of genocide in Darfur refugee camps. Providing these stoves for refugees reduces health and safety risks as well as encourages ecological preservation.

title: Millions face hunger in Southern Africa
description: More than nine million people in Southern Africa are facing severe food shortages after the worst drought the region has seen in 35 years. Shockingly this number is expected to increase to a staggering 45 million over the next six months. ActionAid is responding through local partners to provide life-saving food, water tablets, and safe spaces for women and girls.

title: Save Burmese Refugee Children  with Heart Disease.
description: For 50 years the Myanmar generals have oppressed minorities, stealing land, burning villages, driving families to the borders.  Refugees live in camps in eastern Thailand. China Cal has partnered with the Mae Tao Clinic, Burma Children's Fund and with refugee schools to find and treat children with heart disease.  In 2020, China Cal will screen the hearts of 10000 Burmese refugee children and proved support for surgeries for those found with heart disease. We need your help.

title: Emergency Relief for families in Kashmir
description: "Please Help my Kashmir in this difficult situation."We are responding to this plea with an EMERGENCY RELIEF program to address immediate and desperate needs as winter takes hold in Kashmir. The situation in Kashmir is very unstable and many families no longer can earn an income to feed themselves. The Relief program seeks to help at least 50 families to support them with one month's food and grocery supply.

title: Disaster Relief and Recovery
description: As the number and severity of disasters continues to increase, Red Cross must urgently scale up its capacity to respond.  This means significant investment in our people and our emergency systems.  Our goal is to create stronger, more resilient communities with increased capacity to anticipate, respond to and recover from crises. Together, we have a duty to be ready for each and every disaster-as well as the possibility of facing multiple events both at home and beyond our borders.

title: Holistic education for 50 children in rural Peru
description: The key to development in Peru is education. Providing a quality education from an early age will be contributing to the good development.  The Yachay Kuska School 's mission is to be a center of high quality education that respects, maintains and rescue the traditions of the area, which is intercultural and inclusive.

title: Cancer Awareness & Screening for 200 Anambra Women
description: This project will conduct a massive awareness and education campaign on breast and cervical cancer, its warning signs with a focus on the importance of early diagnosis in treatment of cancer  in the 3 selected communities. It will create a bridge between the masses and the health specialists through an advocacy visit to the hospitals for affordable screening and referrals services. The primary beneficiaries will be 200 women (18 - 60years) in Uru, Obosi and Amaenyi communities in Anambra State.

title: Drug Awareness & Business Skills for 90 Kano Youth
description: This project will encourage youths on business enterprise and how to improve their business using skills that are innovative and feasible in their environment. These business skills will effectively build individual esteem to be independently sufficient. Being unemployed can lead to depression, low self-esteem, drug use and other mental health issues. We will emphasize the importance of good socio-economic orientation and create awareness among the youth on why they should avoid drug abuse.

title: Help a Poor Child in Nigeria Stay in School
description: This project will take place in Farawa Community, Kano State, which has a very high rate of out of school children. A lot of these children are out of school due to being orphaned, extreme poverty, traditional beliefs and poor state of infrastructure of the schools within the community. This project seeks to empower 105 out of school children a with uniforms, sandals, and school fees so they can get back to schooling. The school will also be equipped with effective learning aids such chalk, etc.

title: Food Security and AgriBusiness Skills for 20 Women
description: The program will train 20 women in Ugwogo Nike community who are engaged in agriculture on how to convert poultry droppings to cooking energy and biofertilizer to reduce greenhouse gas and promote food security. Reports show that the marginalization of women rights and their lack of decision making power results in high rate of poverty as women are deprived of realizing their full potential. With relevant skills, they can improve agricultural production and lift their families out of poverty.

title: Support Healthy Adolescents Development Ibadan
description: The project will address depression and other mental health issues (substance abuse, anxiety and suicide) among Secondary School Students 13 - 19 years; promote healthy development of adolescents, protect their physical & mental health and prevent emotional and behavioural problems through training them and equipping them with problem solving skills and interpersonal skills; building self-esteem and confidence; developing coping skills to manage emotions and engaging in community services.

title: SURVIVORS  IN TEARS - SADNESS - WITHOUT SHELTERS
description: CELEBRATING CHRISTMAS DAY IN TEARS - SADNESS - WITHOUT SHESLTER On December  22, 2019 -- At least 15 persons died including children,   over 30 others were injured  and hundreds of homes destroyed  at a neighborhood in Burundi's commercial capital Bujumbura,  flooding caused by Saturday night's heavy rains. The location that has been more destroyed and affected by the torrential floods is called  "Winterekwa". Today in this location and  surrounding areas there are tears and sadness of survivors

title: Let All Kids  Play (Leaving No One Behind)
description: This project aims to change the lives of hundreds of children especially those with disabilities by building two pilot playgrounds (one in a needy school that is located in a big community and one in a camp for persons with disability) thus giving them the chance to play with their peers and be included in their communities.  iPlaygrouds Business Startup which is managed by persons with disability,  will be responsible for building the playgrounds. This makes this project a win-win-win for all.

title: Developing the Next Generation of Conservationists
description: With nearly half of Uganda's population under age 15, young people have a significant role to play in preserving Uganda's natural resources, both now and in the future. The Kasiisi Project informs and inspires a new generation of Ugandan conservationists by fostering a connection between education and conservation, and embedding programs in 16 forest-edge primary schools that promote academic excellence, good health and care for the environment.

title: Typhoon Ursula Relief and Recovery Initiative
description: We will provide food packs, hygiene kits, house and latrine repair kits and vegetable seeds for 2,000 very poor families in remote communities affected by Typhoon Ursula (Phanfone) in order to lower morbidity and mortality and improve the level of living of vulnerable affected families.

title: Provision of Safe Water and Sanitation in Uganda
description: Water Out Of Safe Holder (WOOSH) Ltd is a non-profit organisation formed and legally registered with the government of Uganda aimed to stop water borne diseases escalation by increasing access to safe drinking water through improved filtration systems and improved sanitation.

title: Providing books, desks & food to 300 slums kids.
description: Raise education centre is an education institution that enrols children residing from poor and disadvantaged children in Mombasa slums. As a result of change of the national academic curriculum, the school intends to purchase new text books ,desks, and other learning materials to  300 children. In addition, provide  lunch under its feeding program which provides nutritious meals to facilitate cognitive  academic alertness and concentration.

title: Give hope to the Families of the Valparaiso fire
description: The project consists of three relevant activities focused on helping families affected by the fire that occurred on December 24th, 2019 in Valparaiso. The activities in the short term are: Ludic workshops for local children and sustainable construction workshops for young people and adults. In the long term, we will build a LUDOTECA for emotional support and socio-emotional development of children in vulnerable environments.

title: SUPPORT LIVELIHOOD SKILLS TRAINING FOR WOMEN
description: New Era Educational and Charitable Foundation fosters youth leadership development that promotes pluralism and rejects corruption. We support youth with skills to become peer-leaders and agents of peace capable of helping themselves, of shaping a positive and sustainable society that rejects violence, and who insist on communicating excellence and unbridled compassion for all.

title: Amplifying Voices for Racial Equity in MD-DC-VA
description: In 2017 Montgomery County's Police reported an 26% increase in bias incidents compared to the prior year. Of the incidents reported, roughly half were motivated by bias toward religion and half were motivated by bias toward a race or ethnicity. Story Tapestries took this report as a call to action and collaborated with other local organizations, including the Strathmore and Impact Silver Spring, to call upon our wide networks of concerned individuals to begin meeting and form a Task Force.

title: Emergency Response in the Philippines
description: The people of the Philippines have faced the devastation from Typhoon Phanfone and the eruption of the Taal Volcano. International Medical Corps is in the Philippines to assess and address the most urgent relief and recovery needs for the women, men, and children affected.

title: Give LULAC the Support to Empower Hispanics
description: LULAC Institute will fight discrimination based on race, ethnicity, or national origin by providing support to civic participation, civil rights, economic development, education, health, housing, immigration, leadership, public service, technology, women, youth, young adults, and the 50+ demographic.

title: HOME OF HOPE PROJECT IN UGANDA
description: An increase in child abandonment and a lack of assistance in the Mubende District of Uganda has increasingly become a serious problem. 'Home of Hope Project' intends to create a program that supports Uganda's most vulnerable children.

title: Classrooms and farming help Tanzanian school kids
description: 5 years ago, we - a group of Rotarians from the United Kingdom - started a project on the island of Ukerewe in Lake Victoria (Tanzania) to help schools grow crops to feed their pupils. 7 schools (7,000 pupils) participated. Now we have raised enough funds to extend it to 1 new school. Thank you for those who responded to the appeal. We want to do more to help these kids - we want to make their classrooms safe by repairing some damaged ones and reduce classroom overcrowding by building new ones.

title: Emergency Appeal: Again Flooding Across Jakarta
description: Again, flooding across Jakarta in 2021. The ACT Foundation would deliver the emergency response aid such as public kitchen (cooked meal), supply clean water, clothes, blankets, medical services, shelters, etc in Jakarta, Bogor, Depok, Tangerang, Bekasi those affected by flood have been distributed on the emergency phase and much much more....

title: Improvements to rural school in Nepal
description: Panchakanaya school is 43Km North-West of Kathmandu. Schools in Nepal only receive a minimum of Government funding and the remainder has to be found by the local communities, which is a difficult ask in some rural farming communities. IGWR-Nepal will be working with Dharmik foundation who have adopted Panchakanya as their second project after successful completion of a second floor of classrooms they built for another rural school in the Kavre district which has proven to be a great success.

title: Sustainable Empowerment Breaking Gender Roles
description: Her Farm Films is a women's empowerment program that is breaking all gender roles and providing real, sustainable incomes for independence.   Real empowerment means an income that enables a woman to support herself and not live a life of dependency on a male member of the family. Unless and until a woman can achieve the level of income she has not been empowered, she's been further enslaved. Small incomes go to the male members of the household and the woman simply has more work to do.

title: Help combat hunger and poverty in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone is one of the poorest and hungriest nations on earth. It is therefore prudent to support farmers to grow food which would help them eradicate hunger, poverty and joblessness. Many have left farming because of lack of seeds, finance, tools, farm inputs, machines etc. This project would therefore provide them with the above listed materials to revert to farming. This will increase food availability in the villages and the country as a whole.

title: Bishop John E McCarthy Memorial Catholic Build
description: The 2020 Bishop John E McCarthy Memorial Catholic Build brings together Catholics all around Austin to build a home for a hard-working family. Funding will be used to cover the construction materials of the home.

title: Unlock 10000 students' potential through education
description: The project focuses on training and empowerment of students in order to acquire practical skills and mentorship especially in underfunded schools of Uganda, to encourage students to further their education and pursue an innovative and entrepreneurial mindset. It also sponsors the school fees for orphaned children allowing them to attend school and have better livelihoods. Such empowerment is key to both breaking the cycles of poverty and developing our young leaders of tomorrow.

title: Red Dots
description: With the high rate of school dropout and missing out of school activities due to inaccessible period products, the Red Dots provides comfortable and clean reusable pads and pant liners for menstruators to keep them in school.   The period kit also has an illustrative menstrual education and a customizable period calendar to aid period tracking. Pads last between three to five years.

title: Help Rebuild Damaged Schools in The Philippines
description: In 2016, Typhoon Haima (known locally as Lawin) made landfall in Cagayan as a Category 5-equivalent storm. Just two years later, Typhoon Mangkhut (known locally as Ompong) also made landfall in the Philippines as a Category 5-equivalent storm, becoming the third-strongest typhoon worldwide in 2018. This project will support AHAH's long-term recovery program, while our teams are working to support communities in the aftermath of both devastating storms and rebuild their heavily damaged schools.

title: Australia Wildfires Relief Fund
description: In 2019 and early 2020, high winds and drought conditions caused extensive wildfires to spread rapidly through Australia, prompting mass evacuations, destroying homes and killing hundreds of millions of animals. All donations to this fund will exclusively support wildfire recovery across Australia.

title: Help Build Resilient Schools in Mozambique
description: On March 15, 2019, Cyclone Idai made landfall near Beira, Sofala Province, Mozambique. With sustained winds of up to 185 km/hour and torrential rains, Idai has been classified as one of the Southern Hemisphere's most devastating storms on record. This project will support AHAH's recovery program in Mozambique, where our teams are working to support communities in the aftermath of this devastating storm and rebuild their heavily damaged schools.

title: SEND HEALTH AND HOPE TO THE NEEDY FAMILIES
description: Building Competence through Confidence!  We believe in education for All!  That is why, with your help, Candles of Hope will provide school fees, lunches, and learning materials to more than 2000 underprivileged girl students of the rural regions of Kabale and Kasese district, so that they may be able to develop their educational standard. This project will provide marginalized children an opportunity to be educated so they can contribute to the development of society.

title: SUPPORT TO 40 FARMERS TO FIGHT HUNGER IN SINKUNIA.
description: Sierra Leone is ranked 179 out of 188 in the Human Development Index and the third hungriest country in the world says Global Hunger Index. There are more than 6.4 million people living in Sierra Leone, 52.9 percent of who live below the national poverty line. Roughly 60 percent of the population lives in rural areas, the majority of whom rely on subsistence agriculture for their livelihoods. Malnutrition has been the greatest cause of child mortality in Sierra Leone, accounting for nearly half

title: Empower 50 IDPs with Disabilities in Cameroon
description: REWAC plans to provide free mobility aids to  fifty (50) internally displaced persons with disabilities, victims of armed conflict, who hail from the most remote and poverty stricken areas of the North West Region in Cameroon, to lend them  support to enjoy freedom and independence  as they undertake financially independent ventures for poverty alleviation in their homesteads.

title: Provide 150 kids School Supplies in Benin City, NG
description: The children of Benin City, Nigeria need school supplies yearly, and the mission is to provide at least 150 students with the supplies for the year.  Many of the Benin City children live in poverty homes, and they cannot afford education resources.  The foundation has requested that the parents of the Benin City students submit a list to include supplies and books for the school term.  The Foundation will then award the first 150 children supplies from the project funding to support the mission.

title: LRBT Eye Hospital (New) -Rahim Yar Khan
description: Punjab, has a population of around 110 million people, the vast bulk of who live in abject poverty. Eye care facilities especially in smaller towns and rural areas are either not available or are far beyond the reach of the poor and even the lower middle class. LRBT with its free eye car services is their only hope.  There are an estimated 12. 1 million blind & visually impaired  people in Punjab of which an estimated 1.2 million are blind . An additional 120,000 go blind every year.

title: "Documentation Matters" Support Abandoned Voices!
description: Project has been paused due to COVID-19!     "Abandoned Voices," a 3-years project, is bibliographical research on Iranian women's singers who face fanatic obstacles and discriminations that prohibit them from performing publicly. The initiative is dedicated to documenting women's struggles for equality, restoring a narrative of artistic resistance, and the role of female voices in Iran's culture in the past century.

title: Shea Butter Processing Facilities for 200 Women
description: This project will build a Shea Butter processing facility for 200 Women in the poorest part of Northern Ghana to ensure good health and safety environment and improve quantity and quality to attract better market prices to earn better income to support the family and their livelihood.

title: Guatemala distance learning + capacity building
description: Schools and organizations serving vulnerable communities in Guatemala are under-prepared to face the COVID19 crisis. They've closed or are struggling. Yet community needs are more acute than ever. The El Centro team will deliver innovative new programs and support organizations and communities to build resilience, capacity and adaptability. Collaborating with our broad and deep network, we aspire to create and implement responsive opportunities locally and at scale.

title: EARLY HEPETITIS B INTERVATION PROJECT
description: Hepatitis B originally came from Congo .DRC and affected North East part of Uganda in 2003.hepatitis B a viral diseases  affects liver cells that causes liver malfunctions.Hepatitis B is a cantigeuons disease which causes to sex,blood transfusion,blood contact,sharing sharp object like safety pins,through sweats,through labor.The process of Hepatitis B immunization programme is a bit expensive to local people and to low income earners

title: Junub Refugee Youth economic empowerment project
description: This project will  assist 100 refugee Youth, women and Adolescent girls to  overcome  both  unemployment , abuse  physical  and psychological   obstacles   that   displacement   presents.   It   promotes   psycho social well being  and  cognitive  development;  helps  Women and youth refugees  to  regain  a  sense  of  security, independence, dignity, and self-worth and  provides YOUTH refugees  with  skills  and  knowledge  to  become  employed in various candle sectors and be self sustaining

title: Australia Bushfire Relief: Nappies for Children
description: Bushfires (wildfires) are devastating the continent of Australia, forcing thousands of families to flee their homes. In this devastatingly difficult time, these families need help- and diapers (nappies) are an overlooked yet so desperately needed item. All babies deserve to be clean, dry, and healthy. This fund exists to serve families displaced by bushfire, both in short and long term recovery, by providing complete supplies of cloth nappies to last from birth to potty learning.

title: Educate 110 Marginalized Batwa Children in Uganda
description: This Project will provide Education sponsorship in terms of scholastic materials such as books,pens and uniforms to 110 Batwa children living in extreme poverty in Rural Uganda. When you sponsor a child's Education under Cherie Wilshire Foundation, you provide them with a continuous Education up to university. Education helps to transform the lives of the little neglected Batwa children in western Uganda who have been evicted from their ancestral homes.

title: Build a preschool for 100 Batwa Children.
description: The Batwa Pygmies once entertained for the Royal Family of Rwanda. Now, they often live as social outcasts in  famine, poverty and neglect.  Pygmy Survival Alliance partners with the Batwa Village of Cyaruzinge, Rwanda to empower these fabulous entertainers to adapt to the modern world and once again achieve greatness. This project will build a new preschool with traditional music, song, and dance, to enable this ancient culture to survive, and thrive in a rapidly modernizing world.

title: Help care for 100 children with cancer in Mexico
description: 70% of children with cancer are treated in hospitals in our state of Sonora. Most of these children come from all areas of the  northwest  with their parents, or caregivers. The hospital in our area is the only one availlable with  specialized medical resources and treatment , including chemotherapy.  With this project we intend to give 2 meals a day,in our Soup Kitchen, which we call " SULAM" meaning  Stairway To Heaven, and  including help to  pay for bus fair,or housing expenses,ect

title: Donate to build a Day care centre: Uganda
description: Children with severe disabilities are perceived to be a burden, as they require continual care which prevents caretakers from seeking employment and engaging in  meaningful activities. Katalemwa seeks to build a day care centre to support annually  50  children with severe disabilities like cerebral palsy, neurological and multiple conditions. This day care will retain these children as their Parents/caretakers go to work, at school or engage in other activities.

title: Combating loneliness in Teenagers with Cancer
description: 87% of young people diagnosed with cancer have lost contact with their peers, 83% experience loneliness which is reported as a potential risk factor for poor mental health, often linked to early death - on a par with smoking or obesity, demonstrating the importance of strong social connections.  91% of the young people leaving our last Activity Stay reported having a strong support network, nobody left the Stay feeling lonely and there was dramatic decrease of 83% towards feelings of isolation.

title: Building A School For Next Generation Leaders
description: The Bell has been rung! It is time for the Swarachna School to reach more children in need, especially girls.  Milaan's Swarachna School, a fun, creative and safe space in the heart of rural Uttar Pradesh has been providing education for 12 years to children from socially and economically challenged communities. For the last 4 years, we have had 100% results in both 10th and 12th, a feat we are extremely proud of given the context of education in UP.

title: Mobile Team for Children with Cancer
description: Treatment of children with cancer is difficult and uncertain. Children and their entire families need substantial support once they leave the hospital. Mobile Team will provide much-needed support for children across BiH. A psychologist, social worker, pedagogue, and other professionals will provide care, support, and assistance for the more effective reintegration of these young cancer survivors into their local communities. Help them overcome obstacles, reach out and lend a helping hand!

title: Puerto Rico Earthquake Emergency Fund
description: SOS NOW! A strong 6.4 magnitude earthquake hit the southwest part of Puerto Rico followed by 1,200 more on a lower scale. Every day there are few. PR Rises is providing first aid supplies. Also, workshops to communities offering the necessary tools for better execution and decisions made when facing a disaster. Currently, there are more than 20,000 refugees.  People are sleeping on the streets including elders and infants.  Natural disasters do not wait, do not warn we need to be ready.

title: Avoid ship strike for whales in French Polynesia
description: The MMO (Marine Mammal Observer) aims to detect humpback whales over long distances to minimize the risk of collision. When the distance between the animal and the ship is less than 200 m an avoidance maneuver is triggered (change of course and reduction of speed).  In 2018, this program accounetd for 556 hours of real time observation during 13 644kms. This allowed us to prevent 96 potential collisions.

title: Disaster Legal Aid for Communities in Puerto Rico
description: This is a disaster legal aid initiative with a legal empowerment perspective. We provide legal education and support to families and communities recently affected by Fiona. This program trains pro bono housing and just recovery advocates who accompany communities and also leads advocacy words to ensure equitable recovery. Since 2017, Ayuda Legal Puerto Rico has led disaster legal aid and advocacy efforts regarding recovery in Puerto Rico.

title: Urgent aid for El Geneina area West Darfur, Sudan
description: Your donations to buy --in El Geneina, Darfur-- blankets, food, clothes, shoes, sleeping mats and tarpaulins, and also provide cash assistance for people displaced by recent attacks on  the city  of El Geneina and Kereneik town.  Our board in the US and our team in Darfur are from the area, so we are better able to communicate directly with people there.  From June 2020 through June 2022, we have already distributed such aid to 1,327 displaced families and another 1,234 displaced individuals.

title: Empowering Cambodian children with language
description: ODC has been offering free English lessons to underprivileged children in Cambodia since 2015. Covid-19 has not halted our students' education as our teachers quickly moved to delivering packages and online learning, when many NGOs have closed. Our reputation for delivering excellent education has resulted in many more children enrolled in 2021. Two new classrooms and more teachers will be needed  in 2022 to accommodate nearly 200 children enrolled in our full and part time programs.

title: Educate a Vulnerable Child in Uganda
description: Education is a human right and a form of empowerment. The more education someone has, typically a higher income and better health outcomes follow. Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVC) in Uganda often do not complete their education because they cannot afford the school fees or they have to drop out to begin working. Many even become caregivers themselves to other OVC. OCE intends to change that, helping to send vulnerable children to primary and secondary schools in Lyantonde District, Uganda.

title: Environment in Education: Planting 100,000 Trees
description: The recent environmental crises around the world have stopped us all in our tracks; while there is a lot being done to provide immediate relief, we are asking ourselves what can we do at an individual, organizational and community level to make a difference. What action can we take to ensure such catastrophes do not repeat themselves? Inspired by young Climate Champions around the globe, we asked ourselves: how can we equip the future generation of students in Kisumu to join the movement.

title: Operation Address The Homeless
description: This project will raise funds needed to operate the current programs of OATH, and towards the renovation of our building into a transitional housing for homeless who qualify. We currently provide showers, clothing, food, laundry, haircuts and job opportunities to our area homeless population. We can get them "off the street and back on their feet!".

title: End child servitude in 9 Haiti rural communities
description: Limye Lavi foundation works with five rural communities in the south east department of Haiti to end the restavek System (Child servitude ). Five child protection organizations were created to fight the system. About one hundred restavek children return in their community. The foundation supports vulnerable families in improving their economic situation. It plan to reinforce child protection system in these communities and start collaboration to eradicate the system in three new communities.

title: Rebuild Schools Damaged by Earthquakes in Mexico
description: This project supports our long-term disaster relief efforts in Mexico, following the 2017 earthquakes. Our work will assist heavily impacted and under-resourced rural communities and hundreds of families that have still not received aid. AHAH is rebuilding the schools at the center of these communities, which in turn strengthens them and prepares them (through Disaster Risk Reduction training) for unknown disasters of the future.

title: Support WWF's Response to Australia's Wildfires
description: Please support WWF's response to Australia's devastating bushfires.  As of January 6, these massive fires have burned more than 20.7 million acres-an area bigger than the Brazilian Amazon and Californian fires combined.  Dozens of people-including several volunteer firefighters-have died. Estimates suggest that more than 1 billion animals may have been killed from the fires.    Your donation will support WWF's immediate response, animal care/rehab, and longer-term restoration and reforestation.

title: Kangaroo Island Wildlife Recovery
description: Australia's Kangaroo Island, its wildlife and their habitats were devastated in the 2019-2020 Black Summer bushfires. We need your help to provide affected wildlife with essential habitat. We are currently working on a new project to support bushfire affected wildlife in South Australia. Thank you for your donation to this appeal.  To our Australian donors, please note that your donation is not tax deductible when donating here. Our website shows alternatives.

title: Education and for Children in Rural South Africa
description: Our adapted offerings for Early Learning, After-school, and more in-community programmes support children & households in many ways. We will continue to provide children and guardians with equal access to learning that empowers them to become agents of change and develop into engaged and confident young adults, as well as build food sustainability in our community. Supporting this project helps provide over 850 children and 320 households with learning and food sustainability opportunities.

title: Sports for children with intellectual disabilities
description: The mission of Special Olympics is to provide year-round sports training and athletic competition in a variety of Olympic-type sports for children and adults with intellectual disabilities, giving them continuing opportunities to develop physical fitness, demonstrate courage, experience joy and participate in a sharing of gifts, skills and friendship with their families, other Special Olympics athletes and the community in Chile.

title: Puerto Rico Earthquake Response
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck Puerto Rico at in the early morning hours of January 7, 2020. The earthquake marks the strongest in a string of escalating seismic activity that started on December 28, 2019. More than 200,000 people may require humanitarian assistance. International Medical Corps' Puerto Rico team is on-the-ground working to reach those most affected by the earthquake to provide emergency response care.

title: Arropando de esperanza a Puerto Rico
description: On January 7, 2020 PR was hit by an earthquake, which affected the southwest area of our island. We still feel tremors of smaller magnitude at the island level. Some of the residents in these areas lost their homes and others suffered significant damage to their structures, so they are mostly sleeping in tents, cars or outdoors. They are lacking blankets to cover themselves, with these funds we would be providing with 100 blankets for the people impacted by the earthquake in PR.

title: Reduce parrot poaching in 10 Indonesian villages
description: Cockatoos rapidly decline in the wild mainly due to local poaching for the pet trade. We produced a documentary focusing on the local parrot trade and showing success stories of alternative livelihoods to poaching birds. In this project, we would like to share the film with 10 selected local villages in Eastern Indonesia, which are the most involved in harvesting wild parrots, and start discussions with the communities about the most fitting sustainable solutions for the future.

title: ECONOMICAL EMPOWERMENT WOMEN LIVING WITH HIV/AIDS.
description: This project is necessary to reduce vulnerability among women living with HIV and AIDS in Kaalo village empowering them through income generating activities to enable them to earn income to take care of themselves and their families.Women living with and affected by HIV/AIDS in Kaalo village are among the most vulnerable groups due to poverty,high illiteracy levels and absence of appropriate inheritance policies.The districts lies in the central region of Uganda with an HIV .

title: Indonesia floods response
description: Jakarta, Indonesia, is facing the worst floods in decades. At least 66 people have been killed and 36,000 displaced. ActionAid is coordinating community-led disaster relief for thousands of families.

title: Restore sight to 200 villagers in rural Nigeria.
description: Ben & Victoria Ononeze Foundation (BAVOF) plans to provide 200 cataract operations to 200 villagers in south Eastern Nigeria. BAVOF also provides annual free eye tests, glasses and medicines for most common conditions (e.g. diabetes, high blood pressure and malaria) to the villagers.

title: The IDEAS Hive
description: The IDEAS Hive is an interdisciplinary, inter-generational community Think + Do Tank designed to educate the public about sustainability and develop their ideas into local action projects.  The IDEAS Hive meets in communities to grow stakeholders and educate them around the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Through seminars, field trips, action projects, and film screenings, The IDEAS Hive is designed to transform communities to advance positive change.

title: KIWL 2021 Events
description: KIWL is an amateur international group of Japan-based men & women who 'get fit & give back' through sporting events. Since 2012, KIWL has raised Y98.3 million for disadvantaged children in Japan, particularly those in institutional care due to abuse or neglect. KIWL has chosen to continue its support for YouMeWe NPO in 2022, who transform the hopes and dreams of the children by giving them IT and life skills and thus, better prospects of becoming a more successful adult with a meaningful career

title: KIWL 2020 Bike Ride
description: KIWL is an amateur international group of Japan-based men & women who 'get fit & give back' through sport & social events. Since 2012, KIWL has raised Y66.5 million for disadvantaged children in Japan, in particular those who are in institutional care due to abuse or neglect. Through YouMeWe NPO, KIWL aims to support the Digital Citizens project, transforming the hopes of the children and giving them prospects of a more successful outcome in adult life. www.kiwl.net

title: Helping families terribly impacted by earthquakes
description: Arenas community in Guanica has been affected by natural disasters. The community has come together to propose the creation of a resilient center, which would host a food bank, a communal kitchen, a medical dispensary and a supply center to respond during emergencies; a library, an elderly center,  and a gym with the main purpose to care for the mind, spirit and soul. Also, a community garden, a sewing workshop and printing press, to provide a hopeful sustainable and self-managed future.

title: Educational support for Orphans Children in Ethiop
description: Orphan and vulnerable children who have either lost one or both parents live in extreme poverty with their guardians with little access to basic needs. Shalom Yebego Aderagot Derejet Capacity building, Care and Support of poorest women, orphan and vulnerable children project covers children's school fees, tutorial lessons, after school meals, school uniforms and materials. Children receive after school meals and tutorial lessons at our drop in center with a library and other services.

title: Taal Volcano Eruption Relief Fund
description: We will provide immediate assistance to very poor evacuees affected by the volcanic eruption of Mt. Taal. Our relief assistance will include food packs, basic medicines, hygiene kits, tents, blankets and heavy-duty face masks. Aside from the delivery of relief, we will train locals in the identification, assessment and provision of the relief items and in so doing, localize and sustain our efforts.

title: Youth-led Taal Volcano Disaster Response
description: We will focus our disaster response by providing 3,500 youth with direct support comprising food, water, heavy-duty face masks, hygiene kits and communication access via mobile phones. We will mobilize local youth organizations present in the disaster sites so that together with them we will be able to ensure their well-being.

title: Clean Water & Sanitation for Schools in Kenya
description: Fathers And Kids Camping (FAKC) are partnering with Project Maji to bring sustainable access to clean water & sanitation, to three neighbouring schools in the water-stressed region of Machakos County, Kenya. FAKC is a non profit group established in Dubai in 2010, specialising in bringing fathers and their children closer together through life-lasting challenges, and create tangible impact for communities in need.

title: Taal Volcano Eruption Food Security Initiative
description: We will provide immediate food packs to 4,000 local residents who evacuated and opted to stay with relatives and friends as they are the most vulnerable and under-served compared to those in government-supported evacuation centers.  Aside from the food packs, we will provide them with vegetable gardening inputs so that they are able to start small-scale container gardening and generate food on their own and spend fruitful time while waiting for normalcy.

title: Help Bring Water to the Thai Child Foundation
description: BBS is launching an emergency campaign to assist the Thai Child Development Foundation (TCDF) farm operations and school from closing.  All the funds raised will go towards critically needed water tanks and drip irrigation systems that will water their fruit and vegetable gardens. Their farm is a key revenue  source with the funds rasied from the sale of the produce going directly into operating the special needs school, currently serving 52 children,  in the forest community of Paksong.

title: THE SEND A SEED WOMEN'S PROJECT IN KABALE -UGANDA
description: The Send a Seed Women's project in Kabale Uganda is a women's Project based in Kabale,Uganda aimed at sustaining the indigenous good seeds and utilizing seeds  not only as food sources but also as an income generating project for the families of the women involved.Also natural farmyard manure,compost manure and other forms of organic manure are used and not artificial manure to increase soil fertility.

title: Emergency Appeal: South Africa Power Shortage
description: The South African Government is corrupt and failing their people, since 2007 the country has been experiencing loadshedding when they are cut off from power as the country can't meet demand. The issue is businesses are loosing money, children can't learn and all the global issues are getting harder to fight without power. We need to help our projects move to renewable energy and not reply on a corrupt and useless government. We can also help our footprint by using renewable energy

title: Science Workshops for 1,500 Children in Turkey
description: This project will build an aeronautics and space room in the innovative learning center to provide free education for children whose families came to Izmir through internal and international migration, and who have poor access to education and also have adaptation problems to the city.

title: Bring the Ocean Alive for Children in South Africa
description: This project aim is to introduce and develop young marine conservations from under-resourced townships. Often young people living close to the ocean but under their national poverty line have never even seen the ocean. Our project aims to engage 80,000 young people a year in ocean conservation and work to create youth ambassadors to help save our ocean by engaging their wider communityty. The youth voice is strong, let's help educate it to save our beautiful blue ocean.

title: Skating into Africa
description: Zimbabwe is lacking community spaces for children and youth to meet and discuss issues which they are facing on a day-to-day basis. By contributing to a skateboard ramp in the cyclone affected area, children will not only be able to learn how to skateboard and have a safe space, but also be able to participate in educational workshops focusing on topics such as gendered violence, HIV/AIDS and environmental issues.

title: Fund a Youth Scholarship for a Future Leader
description: The United Nations and their work reach most corners of the globe, and even though their work is incredible, many people, especially the youth are unaware of how to become involved or begin actioning change within their own communities. This project is based in Australia and is geared towards recruiting aspiring and passionate individuals to become UN youth ambassadors and offer international experiences to boost their career opportunities and provide them with valuable skills.

title: Support Australian wildlife rescue to release
description: Your help to support Australian wildlife rescue to release, will ensure our 365 days a year, 24  hours a day Wildlife Rescue Team can continue to provide rescue advice and assistance for native wildlife and the community. We are called to help hundreds of thousands of orphaned, displaced and injured native animals annually. We received over 200,000 calls in the last year. WIRES provide full-time mobile Wildlife Emergency Responders operating across New South Wales, SE Queensland and Tasmania.

title: Taal Volcano Eruption Women Support Fund
description: We will provide food, clothing, water and hygiene support for 2,000 very vulnerable women and children affected by the eruption of Taal volcano. Tens of thousands have evacuated as Taal volcano erupted spewing hazardous fumes and ash and we will be particularly assisting women and girls who has meager resources before the eruption and made more destitute as the disaster strikes.

title: Free learning resources for 100 children in Peru
description: Valuable assets to children's learning are unavailable in Cusco, where there are no public libraries and therefore no free learning resources.  'La Pagina en la Puerta' library provides the local community's children with these otherwise unaccessible resources, in order to expose them to the joys of reading and help them improve their literacy skills. The longtime goal is to better the children's future prospects by improving their literary abilities, their confidence in reading and self-esteem.

title: Helping Street Kids in Bali
description: "Who could they become?" This question keeps us up at night. I have to wonder, who could these children become if they weren't enslaved to a life of begging on off the streets of Indonesia? There are 4 million children living on  the streets of Indonesia and they are open to pedophiles, physical and sexual abuse.  Your donation will provide a loving home to protect them from abuse, a good school education and a supportive community to 80 street kids.   Donate today and change a child's tomorrow.

title: BUILD A CENTRE FOR VULNERABLE CHILDREN IN MWANZA
description: The amount of money that will be raised will directly go to the project of building a centre for vulnerable children to live permanently. This centre will comprise of classes for these children to get education, a library, kitchen, toilets, bathrooms and hostels for both girls and boys and other important things as stated in the budget.

title: Emergency Rescue: Saving Endangered Turtles
description: Our project rescues, rehabilitates and releases stranded and distressed sea turtles as part of our conservation mission. With the support of organisations and volunteers along the Western Cape's coast, hundreds of sea turtles have been saved, reared to full strength and released back into the wild. Loggerhead and leatherback turtles nest on the coast and are common patients of our clinic, we regularly rehabilitate stranded green, olive ridley and hawksbill sea turtles that wash up on our shores.

title: Post Covid-19: 'Teach a rural child' intervention
description: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, this project aims to promote in-house education of 400 pupils and students of Kahida community area at Gwagwalada Area Council of Abuja, by offering critical literacy support services through  capacity building for hired home-service teachers using the local community volunteers for sustainable, effective teaching and learning; provision of education materials and sensitization on POST COVID-19 health safety precautions as well as conduct child education advocacy.

title: The House of Restoration
description: A house of safety, established in 2007 for abused and vulnerable women with their own children as well as teenage girls where they find shelter and safety, so that they can grow and learn life skills whilst keeping their children with them. Their basic needs are met such as healthy nutritious food, toiletries, clothing and shelter. We provide trauma debriefing, counseling and life coaching to help them find peace and acceptance with the past and help them move forward and plan for their future.

title: Emergency Response: Tackling a Plastic ocean
description: The United Nations calls our oceans "the lungs of the earth", which is why it is so essential for us to develop sustainably so that we do not suffer in the future, unfortunately, at current rates plastic is expected to outweigh all the fish in the sea by 2050 and if we don't act now the damage could be irreversible. This project aims to create awareness among local communities around the globe as well as funding clean-up and research initiatives to help keep our oceans and it's species healthy

title: Mental health refuge: Free therapy for refugees
description: This project will help both children and adult refugees and asylum seekers living in camps in Bosnia. Most are escaping conflict and human rights abuses whilst others are fleeing economic poverty. We, at Wings of Hope, having supported conflict-traumatised individuals in our country, empathise with refugees and asylum seekers who need vital mental health care to help with the trauma of their difficult experience, but cannot pay for therapy.

title: KickNKnowledge Fall Fashion Show
description: A fall fashion show highlighting our students designs. We will host a fashion show highlighting a group of KickNKnowledge Kicks Academy Students Street Wear Sneaker centric designs.   We will have a group of students model the clothing and host, run and operate their own fashion show learning about the many opportunities with in the sneaker and fashion industries.   They will be in. Charge of hair, makeup, styling, model timing, event invites, setup, breakdown, and overall run of show.

title: Donate to help build two fire trucks
description: The RFBAQ leads and represents the interests of the over 1400 brigades and over 33000 volunteer brigade members in Queensland. Burketown RFB and Birdsville RFB have been identified as Rural Fire Brigades to receive these "Rural Fire Heavy Attack" fire trucks, at a cost of $454,333 +gst each. The trucks carry 3000L of water and are capable of fighting bushfires, grass fires, and building fires. Can also be used for road crash rescue, incident control and support, and for local aerodrome response.

title: Improving learning outcomes for slum children
description: Providing free education through remedial classes to 550 slum children/year in the age group of 6 to 18 in order to give them  a solid foundation and ensuring that learning gaps never widen as they move towards primary and secondary level of education. Also ensuring all round development of these vulnerable children by providing them 2 free meals and regular health check up, counselling support and vocational training support where needed

title: Ending Gender-Based Violence in India
description: My Choices Foundation, through project Operation PeaceMaker has devised multiple intervention and prevention strategies to ender gender-based violence in Indian communities by empowering local women called "PeaceMakers". They are paralegal workers who educate women and children on their rights and prevent abuse by running awareness workshops.   We have 5 counselling centres in Telangana which provide free support to victims of domestic violence through qualified counsellors and lawyers.

title: Educate and Empower 18,000 Girls in Zimbabwe
description: Our trio of programs work together to make change: Kidz Kan and She Kan are outreach programs to educate and empower children, adolescents, teachers and community members about sexual abuse, the law, the role of duty bearers, and the rights of women and girls. The He Kan program is a means to proactively prevent sexual abuse done to women and girls by educating boys on what constitutes sexual abuse, the effects that has on a person, responsibility, and holding other boys accountable.

title: Puerto Rico Women's Health Disaster Response
description: Natural disasters like Hurricane Maria and the recent earthquake in Puerto Rico place women and children in the eye of a different kind of storm increasing their vulnerability to dangers ranging from complications during pregnancy and delivery to the need of oxygen for newborns. COHI is on the ground in Puerto Rico working directly with our partners CentroMAM and local midwives, nurses, and physicians to provide medicines, care, and supplies.

title: Australian Bushfire Relief: Food and Groceries
description: Foodbank is playing a crucial role in the unfolding and unprecedented bushfire emergency in Australia. As a trusted organisation forming part of the official emergency response network, Foodbank is providing essential food, water and grocery supplies to stricken areas. We support the work of first responders and emergency services, and provide ongoing assistance to affected communities during the months and years that it takes to recover.

title: Help 500 Girls in Rural Uganda to speak about SRHR
description: This project will support the expansion of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) programing for 500 girls and young women (aged 10-24) in rural Buyende district in Eastern Uganda. It intends to contribute towards girls and young women's increased uptake and access to quality, integrated and gender responsive sexual and reproductive health services through greater knowledge and capacity development.

title: Train 700 girls to sew sanitary pads&face masks
description: This project is training girls, boys, women and men to sew sanitary pads, it has already trained 533 people (208 Women, 199 Girls, 54 Men and 72 Boys) to make hygienic reusable sanitary pads using terrycloth, poplin cloth, fine polythene and Velcro. The programme also works to dismantle menstruation stigma by holding menstrual sensitization training in communities, as well as discussions with school authorities, parents and church leaders about the need for safe places for girls to change pads

title: Emergency Fund: Women's Health in Disaster Zones
description: Este Fondo de Emergencia ayudara a Taller Salud a cubrir los costos de servicios de justicia reproductiva para las mujeres afectadas luego del terremoto. Mientras las mujeres esperen por vivienda digna y ayuda, trabajaremos para asegurar su salud sexual y reproductiva.  \  This Emergency Fund will help Taller Salud cover reproductive justice services for women in the midst of earthquake recovery. While our women await housing and aid, we must work to ensure their sexual and reproductive health.

title: TO EDUCATE 250 CHILDREN IN PARKVIEW
description: This project will offer quality education and basic needs to 250 orphans & vulnerable children in Parkview Orphans Achievers Shelter (POAS) so that they can enjoy their life like the ordinary child.

title: EMPOWER 100 VULNERABLE CHILDREN IN KIAMBIU
description: The main goal is to support the Glory center school located in Kiambiu slums in Nairobi in order to provide free education to around 100 children who hail from the poorest in the informal dwellings. It will also support them with other basic needs which will create a conducive learning environment.

title: TO HELP 22 SPECIAL CHILDREN IN SIAKA
description: The main goal is to support around 20 blind special children by funding the Siaka School located in western region of Kenya.  Through your help we will be able to provide them with special stationery like braille books, beds and other basic needs therefore those lovely children will have a conducive environment to study which will promote good results. They will not feel stigmatized when they grow up and will find a proper place in the society. Disability is not inability!

title: EMPOWER 35 VUNERABLE HIV WOMEN IN KENYA
description: Our aim is to empower 35 vulnerable HIV women living in Kiambiu slum, Nairobi. These women do odd jobs in order to sustain themselves that pay pennies. In order to improve their living standards and that of their families. We came up with a Petroleum Jelly project. Where the women make it from scratch and sell at an affordable price. However, there is need to scale up in order to have a greater impact to the women. With your help you can surely achieve this objective.

title: Expand mobile sterilization clinic operations
description: Lanta Animal Welfare is the only veterinary source for the surrounding islands and mainland areas. Due to funding levels, the mobile sterilizations and vaccination clinics visit 7 areas annually.  Many rural communities outside of these locations do not know how to get help, resulting in severe overpopulation and suffering of the cats and dogs.  Expanding the mobile clinic operations will dramatically improve cat and dog welfare and reduce the risk of human rabies.

title: Rebuild preschool for 100 children in South Africa
description: Do you see our broken walls?  Without your help our school will close. Berakah Education Foundation needs to repair a building being used in its dilapidated condition as an early childhood learning space for 100 preschool children in an at-risk community in Pretoria, South Africa.  Without repair, our school is hindered from receiving an occupancy certificate needed for registration as a partial care facility/Early Childhood Development Centre with the Department of Social Development.

title: Support for 96 indigent children for 2 years
