Lack of water supply is also preventing these people from adhering to good hygiene and sanitation practices such as using a toilet and handwashing. The project aims to benefit 482 individuals from 102 households and 75 students from a community school in Juke, a rural community located in the hills of central Nepal, through access to potable water supply.

title: Control & Prevention of the Covid-19 at School
description: As the children in Haiti are resuming school amid the Covid-19, the most pressing action for the organisation "LIGHT" is secure them against a potential spread of the virus through our existing medical platform. This project aims at building the capacity of teachers and students on preventive measures to adopt against the virus and Implementing in schools a warning system for suspicious cases through our app. phone called, Virtual Medical Assistance Center (VMAC).

title: Remote learning in rural Kenya for 1,000 children
description: When COVID19 stops schools reopening what happens to the children?   In Kericho County, Kenya the children are working in the fields, collecting water and firewood, vulnerable, tired, hungry and open to exploitation.  They are losing out on their childhood, losing out on learning.  This project will change that by supporting community based learning groups to bring children together in small groups where they can learn, thrive and be safe for part of everyday.

title: Health Insurance for 200 Widows & Orphans in Abuja
description: Only 10% of Nigerians have access to health insurance,  widows and orphans have to make out-of-pocket payments which is more expensive; as a result they have limits access to health care. For only $50 Health Insurance premium A widow and her orphans can access to basic health care, surgical care and eye care. WEWE project requires $50,000 to provide 200 widows and their orphans in Abuja, Nigeria. Donate today to give 200 widows and their orphans improved access to healthcare and save lives.

title: Support 500 people with rare diseases in Romania
description: This project will support 500 patients with rare diseases in Romania, providing them with the support to face their daily challenges through face to face and online medical consultation, therapies, counseling and psychological support for patients and families at NoRo Center and NoRo Center online services: www.centrulnoro.ro. We will bridge the gaps between medical and social services establishing and training a support network of community nurses to orient patients  to the services they need.

title: COVID 19: Food and Water for families in need
description: Due COVID-19, Chile is the fifth country with the most infections per 100,000 inhabitants and 2.3 million people have lost their jobs. Your donation will allow the poorest people in Chile to have access to protection elements against the virus to prevent them from being infected and for childrens from these families without income to have food to continue developing in a healthy way even despite the effects of the virus. Make it possible today!

title: Support Women Building Lives Free from Violence
description: Gender violence is a painful reality for women and girls in Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay. The lack of basic services and limited access to rapid and vital assistance put them at constant risk. Grassroots organizations, generally based in remote locations, work as first responders in their communities, saving lives. They provide legal and psychosocial support, deliver training courses, disseminate information, sustain women's shelter and hotlines, and advocate for their rights.

title: Sowing Maasai Women and Girls Future
description: This project will create a resource hub, skill center and safe space for at least 1240 vulnerable women and girls in the Maasai community in Isara. They lack a safe space for psycho social support, skills for sustainable livelihoods, and resources to support adolescent reproductive health and  teen mothers waiting to return to school. The Kenyan government has closed schools and as a result adolescent girls have had a high pregnancy rate due to lack of activities and spaces to engage them.

title: Connect poor preschoolers to books in Tucuman
description: Join us to connect 4-year-old preeschooler Maxi and his friends to books for the very first time. Maxi lives in Tucuman, one of the poorest regions in Argentina. Together, we can help Maxi and his community beat the odds, by creating home libraries for 60 preschoolers like him and giving parents tools as their child's first and most important teacher.

title: Empower WAYUU women through handcrafted bags
description: Do you know the Mochila bag? It is a beautiful handcrafted bag made by Wayuu Indigenous women who live in the middle of desert. without electricity, lack of water, and poor access to basic education and healthcare. They have very few options to feed their children. We want to create a self-supporting system using Mochila bags to generate income, to educate girls and women and to help them solve the problems they face as a community.

title: Stand Up for Women's Land Rights in Tanzania
description: Stand For Her Land is advocating with and for women in Tanzania for secure and equal rights to land. With secure land rights, women not only have safe shelter but a chance at a more sustainable livelihood. Despite laws and policies that strengthen women's land rights, women around the globe, and many in Tanzania, face obstacles in exercising those rights. Stand For Her Land is working to close this gap between the laws and practice, empowering millions of women in the process.

title: Providing Masks to High-Need Communities in Brazil
description: Through women for water, GWC is partnering with Ford Fund and Rede Asta to produce 27,000 fabric masks for high-need communities in Brazil. The project will also empower women artisans through mask production. The artisans will receive a stipend for their work and participate in Rede Asta's Artisan Business School program and learn skills to develop their own businesses.  For every dollar donated, Ford Fund will match 100% up to $24,000 and GlobalGiving will match 50% for over 2.5 the impact!!

title: Shaping careers of 500 young people  in Kampala.
description: This project will inspire and guide young people 15-23 years on how to make informed career choices. To help them find their passion and enhance workplace productivity in the future, the young people will have virtual sessions focused on increasing self-awareness and information on careers opportunities available. .  This will not only benefit the young people, but will also influence and bring about local transformation to their communities.

title: HOME BASED CARE TO ELDERLY IN KENYA ON COVID 19
description: This project will build a day care center in Western parts of Kenya, providing rich comprehensive care to the elderly with compromised immune systems that are susceptible to the effects of Covid 19 and Life limited diseases. The pandemic has brought great confusion that elderly are neglected while services and crucial services are geared towards the productive members of the society. This project will improve health of 700 elders and reunite them with their families with sustainable programs.

title: EMPOWER 200 RURAL WOMEN AND YOUTH WITH BEEKEEPING
description: The project will empower 200 unemployed youth and women, providing employment and reducing ecological damage in Abia, Imo, Sokoto and FCT.The primary aim of the project is to improve the economic condition of the rural youth through beekeeping as a natural based- resource for climate action and rural resilience. During the training period, beneficiaries will learn the basic tools of beekeeping such as Bee Hive Components, Honey Production, Packaging/Honey processing, Marketing, Money Management.

title: Food Safety-net for Okinawa
description: Okinawa Prefecture has the highest child poverty rate in the nation (+30%). At the same time there is virtually no place for those households in need to access food assistance in an emergency.   Prefectural government is concerned about this situation, but even their proposed plan will reach less than 3% of those children in need. And the "assistance" that will be provided is the equivalent of two meals a month. Their hands are tied at the moment.  However, we can make a difference.

title: Medical Kit for 700 Children living in Cemetery
description: 700s of children between 1 and 14 are living in the Pasay City Cemetery. Children are exposed to disease with a lot of dirt and rotting water from the cemetery. They got a small wound and skin disease of unknown cause. Without getting the right treatment, they just leave it until the wound and disease get better. Under this project, 700 poor children will be given medical kits (Vitamin, Wound ointment, Bandage, etc), health check-up, hospital treatment and antibacterial mask (Facing Covid-19).

title: Buy a House for Children Without Parental Care
description: This project will accelerate the closure of the "Bjelave" orphanage and will enable children without parental care to move from the orphanage in House and finally live in conditions that every child deserves - a family environment. The capacity of the House is a maximum of twelve children. Children who have the experience of staying in orphanages with a capacity of 100-120 children, after replacement, quickly see and feel the advantages of this form of care.

title: Help 100 Children in Soweto, Kayole in Nairobi
description: Tunaweza Pamoja Children's Centre helps neglected, needy, orphaned, vulnerable, deprived and destitute children mostly from the Kayole-Soweto slum area. We help the children by paying their school fees, giving them shelter, food, clothing and medical attention. We provide a loving and safe, family environment that enables children the right to a happy, educated, skilled and healthy life. Currently we are helping 100 children aged between 6 to 15 years.

title: Adivasi Women Train Youth on Forest Foods in India
description: The project supports Adivasi youth training on wild foods from women experts at the Forest Food Field School in Adukkam, India. The scholars will learn to identify, document and harvest nutritious food from the wild, prepare meals from forest resources, and grow and maintain their own food gardens for food resilience.  For as little as $15, help preserve this traditional knowledge from Adivasi elders so that the youth are able to carry on the old tradition of healthy diets from the forest.

title: Train 100 hill tribe children to read
description: Along the Thai/Myanmar border,roughly 1,000,000  hill tribe people live in poverty for generations.   Most hill tribe children have never had anyone read to them. When they enter school they fall behind the other students in learning to read, and eventually drop out of school.   EACM provides neurofeedack training so they can learn to read which gives them more options in life.  Neurofeedback is a proven technology to train young children's brains to learn to read.

title: Relief/Recovery for flood affected in Pakistan
description: Millions of people have been affected and are highly vulnerable by severe flooding in Southern and northern part of Pakistan. Recent heavy rains in Sindh,KPK and Punjab have killed thousands of  people due to urban flooding and have swept away livestock, properties and valuables of worth billion of Rupees. Donations will provide immediate relief to survivors in form of supplies(food, shelter, water, and medicine) in addition to long-term recovery assistance to help residents recover and rebuild.

title: Help 250 Ethiopian women to be solar entrepreneurs
description: Ethiopia is a sun-rich, fuel scarce. However, poor rural women in  Ethiopia spend a lot of their time collecting and selling firewood to make a living. Fetching firewood is a risky and time-consuming job for women. This project will provide solar electrified bakeries for 250 rural women in Ethiopia thereby create self-reliant and self-sufficient income, employment. Besides reducing women's' health risks and deforestation, the project helps to eliminate energy poverty for rural poor women.

title: KOTO's Little by Little
description: COVID-19 hit the restaurant industry in Vietnam hard. With lockdown and no international tourists, we sadly had to close the doors to KOTO Training Restaurant at 59 Van Mieu. However, we're going to come back stronger than ever. We're fundraising to purchase much-needed items for our new restaurant. The KOTO restaurant is the training grounds for our trainees. It's here that they make mistakes, learn to work with one another, develop new cooking techniques and practice their customer service.

title: Impact 650 Displaced Families with WASH in Benue
description: ACORN Initiative intends to address the urgent need of Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) facilities for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Benue State, Nigeria. The IDPs travel over 10 KM to fetch water from the nearest river, which causes them water-related diseases and child mortality. Open Defecation (OD) is common practice due to dilapidated toilets, putting females at risk of rape. The project aims to provide relief by building a borehole for water supply and toilet facilities.

title: Help 500 Kenyan Nonprofits Move Volunteers Online
description: Onsite volunteering has dropped by 90% due to COVID19 globally.  At VoluCulture, we have seen the effect of this pandemic on Kenyan grassroots nonprofit organizations. Many have lost access to onsite volunteers and lack the technology or training to adapt and reach virtual volunteers quickly. Through our online platform, grassroots nonprofits recruit and manage volunteers. We also offer support through volunteer management training to teach on partnerships, managing, and stewarding volunteers.

title: Help Needy in Remote Villages in India Fight COVID
description: The impact of COVID-19 in India has been highly disruptive, destroying both lives and livelihoods.  As we adapt to these unprecedented circumstances, Educate Girls is continuing to serve the most marginalized and vulnerable communities who have been disproportionately affected with the loss of livelihoods, lack of food, poor access to health facilities, sub-optimal education and other basic needs. We were able to impact 500k people and 250k children last year through this. Need is much more now!

title: Mushroom Theatre Studio Appeal
description: For many years Westcliff Rotary has supported the students of The Mushroom Theatre Company who are supporters of their sister organisation EPPA (Charity No 1116649). The aim of the group is to promote the benefits of the performing arts, coupled with the aim of creating a fully inclusive Theatre Company for the community. They integrate disabled and able bodied children in all classes and performances. This approach is beneficial for everyone and helps to break down  barriers that might exist .

title: Help US Send 220 Children To School in Haiti
description: The goal of Home Roots Foundation is to remove money as a barrier to receiving an education in Haiti with your help. Recent political unrest followed by the COVID-19 pandemic has made a bad situation dreadful. School directors have lamented that students are staying home because of inability to pay. With your help, we can pay tuition, fees, and uniforms for students. We can also provide books, pens, backpacks, tutoring and hope.

title: Arianna's Center Community Relief
description: This South Florida based project will administer stipends for transgender women of color and immigrant experience, many of whom are living with HIV and who are disproportionately affected by unemployment, homelessness and discrimination. It will also provide assistance to guide clients through the name change process.These stipends are designed to help with every day needs such as paying for groceries, phone bills and utilities, gas and transportation and range in amount from $25 to $200.

title: Skills training for 50 rural women in Nigeria
description: Barrister Sam Otoboeze Foundation, (BSOF) provides economic opportunity and skills training for rural youths, women and girls at Ochima Community in Enugu State. Our skills training in the production of quality bags, shoes, fashion designing(clothes) and beads making is an income generating program and offers stable employment to these women, girls, youths and the physically challenged. Through our skills acquisition training centre, several women and youths and the physically challenged persons

title: EDUCATION AND FOOD FOR EVERY GIRL CHILD IN NIGERIA
description: To promote access to school education, food provisions and money and household advice and guidance for orphans and other deprived girl children and their families in remote and disaffected communities in Nigeria. This will include supporting them by subsidising school fees, equipment and materials, as well as delivering essential foodstuffs and sanitary products to communities, as well as training by volunteer teams. We will need to fund transportation of resources and storage.

title: Decolonizing Education with White Mountain Apaches
description: A deep ecology education curriculum teaching mindfulness as a means to develop agency in the creation of identity, purpose, and wellness.  Lesson plans are developed around participatory engagements to install bio-intensive gardens, including reflection activities around ecology, place, culture, and resilience.  The program is a partnership with the tribally controlled Theodore Roosevelt Indian School.  Shalitha Peaches, a tribal member with a passion for horticulture, is the program lead.

title: Give +10k dogs&cats in Venezuela a second chance
description: In 2021, we have big plans to transform the lives of more than 10,000 abandoned, low-income and rescued dogs and cats in Venezuela. This includes: - Rescue and heal at least 50 critical cases of abandoned dogs & cats - Spay & neuter at least 7,000 dogs & cats - Provide integral attention to +200 senior rescue dogs (including food and vet care) - Provide veterinary attention to +350 animals  - Vaccinate +2,000 dogs & cats against rabbies in Zulia State - Assist +350 community animals

title: Boost microbusinesses in Puerto Rico
description: Semillas Incubator changes the lives of people helping them develop entrepreneurial skills to start microbusinesses based on solidarity, and social responsibility. Because of current challenges, and to facilitate participation we are also leading a Virtual Business Training Cycle with 19 workshops on business topics and over 80 hours of one-on-one business consulting to 25 participants. We will continue to do both virtual, and face-to-face workshops alternately.

title: Fast Track Education for Ugandan Girls in Sciences
description: We are building a Medical School in Gulu, Uganda to promote Medical knowledge of 400 young girls in our communities. The northern region of Uganda has been traumatized by war and urgently we need healthcare workers to improves lives in the community. Young mothers are dying of birth as we don't have enough midwiferies, nurses, Doctors or clinical officers in the region. By supporting building the medical school, we will overcome the healthcare workers shortages and improves lives.

title: Grow Recycling in North Metro Atlanta
description: Keep North Fulton Beautiful operates the Sandy Springs Recycling Center as a community drop off for household recycling.  This project will create media to educate the citizens of the North Metro Atlanta area on best practices for community recycling and will ensure citizens' engagement is met with ample support and clean updated facilities via the Sandy Springs Recycling Center.

title: Second chances for stray dogs in Tela-Honduras
description: Perros sin nombre  is working on getting our own shelter,  We are looking to dignify the life of stray dogs in the Port of Tela-Honduras, small town with more that 10000 stray dogs. Our organization look for solutions  through the implementation of comprehensive programs of population control, with campaigns of spay/neuter, medical help to those most in need, vaccination, and adoption responsible.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, high school students Ella, Kara, Hannah, Hana, and Brynn have been working with LI to help create & sustain businesses in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to build a business development center. At this center, vulnerable men and women will receive training in life, vocational, & business skills to empower & equip them to escape extreme poverty.

title: Support Literacy in Rehoboth Beach
description: This project will provide continued support to the Rehoboth Beach Public Library.  Located a few blocks away from the beach in downtown Rehoboth, the library provides residents and out-of-town visitors with access to a plethora of reading materials, technological services, and programs for adults and children.  The donations we receive help us to expand our collections, hire performers for our special events, and keep the building operating.

title: Skills and employment opportunities for the youth
description: In the North-west region of Cameroon, the school's drop -out rate is high which means that many young men and women do not complete their education and do not have the necessary skills to generate substantial income for their families. CAMAAY has created 7 proposals that aim to create vocational training in Hairdressing, Cooking, Metalwork, Tailoring, Mechanics, Agriculture, and Woodworking. The Cameronian youth can attend one of these workshops and get skills to become economically independent.

title: Shaping Stronger Futures for 200 kids in Cambodia
description: Angkor Buddhist Organization is a school providing free education and community-led development for eight local villages in Siem Reap Province.  ABO provides critical support and education to shape a stronger future and reduce poverty, working toward sustainability in communities.  This project will shape the future for village children in Cambodia by providing free English language lessons and basic computer skills courses to increase pathway options for better-earning potentials.

title: Transport 1,500 blood donors to save 4,500 lives
description: 34% of maternal deaths in Kenya are a result of blood shortage. These deaths are preventable! Kenya's blood banks are beginning to run dry. The country relied for years almost entirely on U.S. aid but the funding was discontinued.  We formed RedSplash to avail safe and free blood to all patients on time. We collected over 3,000 units of blood from 2019. But we lose 1 for every 2 donors recruited because they don't have the fare to commute. Paying $2-3 moving to the hospital is costly for donors.

title: Help improve mental health of 2 million Nigerians
description: We are attempting to save over 40 million Nigerians from depression, mental health & suicide.  Nigeria ranks as Africa's most depressed country. With our care outreach we will be delivering professional counselling that will sustain a good mental health care system for Nigerians who are depressed and need to feel better. Help 2 million Nigerians annually speak to a psychologist anywhere and anytime. Help reduce the rate of suicide amidst this pandemic. Help provide job opportunities.

title: Restoring edible landscapes in Ghana
description: AGRI-WEB seeks to plant fruit trees and annual vegetable crops in 1,500 Ghanaian households. We are passionate about restoring the edible landscapes of Ghana where most fruits and vegetables are home grown and organic. The fruit trees we are planting include Mango, Coconut, Avocado, Citrus and Soursop whiles vegetables such as carrots, tomatoes, chili pepper and aubergines will be included. Building interest in agriculture is essential for economic development and environmental protection.

title: Support for the victims of Hurricane Laura, Haiti
description: Hurricane Laura killed at least 31 people with many missing and injured in Haiti. The toll of material damage, concentrated in the South-East and West departments, states that more than 6,200 houses were flooded, more than 2,300 damaged and 243 others destroyed.   800 families urgently need your support. You can help with life-saving relief efforts. Your secure donation will help survivors by providing emergency supplies like food, water, shelter, and house repair materials.

title: Empowering Winterveldt, South African Youth
description: Bokamoso Life Centre (BLC) empowers disadvantaged youth through individual and family counseling, life and job skills training, HIV/AIDS and reproductive health education, computer training, artistic and recreational expression, scholarships for tertiary education, vocational training and a Cultural Exchange Program to the United States.  More than 1,300 students have completed the program, 270 youth have participated in the Exchange Program, and over 400 scholarships have been awarded.

title: HELP THE FLOOD AFFECTEES OF SINDH, PAKISTAN
description: Floods are one of the most common hazards in Pakistan. FLOOD 2022 hits Pakistan putting people of Pakistan in crisis thrice in a year. SINDH province is badly affected as houses are damaged, livestock and crops flashed away, and people are on roads. This project intends to help 200 poorest of the poor families of CALAMITY affected villages of District Khairpur and District Sanghar. People are in dire need of livestock support and winterization kits

title: Support Utila Ongoing Fundraiser
description: Support Utila started in response to COVID-19, and continues post pandemic in providing various support to the island of Utila.  Ongoing campaigns include environmental, medical, education and animal welfare.  There is much to do improve Utila for the future. Your help is needed.  Please help us expedite improving the resources needed to keep the people, pets and environment of Utila safe, strong and healthy.

title: COVID-19 Emergency: Prevent Return to Child Labour
description: Emergency funding is needed to prevent children returning to child labour. ACE (1997) withdraws children from hazardous labour in the cotton fields of Telangana, India, so that they can receive a quality education, enjoy their childhood and secure their independence. Due to the global pandemic, schools and vocational training centres are closed. We are offering the most vulnerable families with financial support and children with home educational materials and food, to safeguard their future.

title: Help 80 Mothers Access Breast Cancer Treatment.
description: In Kenya, 5985 women are diagnosed with breast cancer in a year, with 2,553 dying, which makes breast cancer the 3rd leading type of cancer in the country.  High cost of cancer treatment in the country makes it almost impossible for middle to low income earners to seek treatment,as they do not have the luxury of a medical cover. Through this project, we aim to help 80 breast cancer patients access professional breast cancer treatment and after care and save a family the pain of losing a mother.

title: Boost 10 Transitional Entrepreneurship Projects
description: The Covid 19 crisis emphasizes the need to re-think the way many companies conduct their business. This project will finance 10 scholarships to support students who choose to participate in a transitional enterpreneurship project (societal, environmental, digital, technological, organizational) in addition to continuing their studies in Grenoble INP Engineering and Management Institute. These scholarships will allow beneficiaries to focus on their project rather than doing odd jobs to survive.

title: Empowering 250 South African kids fighting Cancer
description: Our program empowers cancer children in South Africa and Africa who are in the fight for their lives. They go through lengthy and sometimes painful treatments, alone and hungry. We empower them through Martial arts moments, breathing and meditation techniques which enable them to take control over their pain, fear and frustration. As they focus on their breathing during their painful procedures, they have the ability to keep their mind & body calm which makes the scary procedures less traumatic

title: NDES Vocational Training & Sports Center
description: NDES is building a facility to promote the development of underserved children from the neglected rural communities of Cameroon. The facility will provide a safe haven for up to 300 children and youths a year, offering workshops in vocational skills, counseling, and sport. With some basic training in a marketable trade, increased self-confidence, and a network of support behind them, these children will be able to build economically secure futures for themselves and their families.

title: Sustainability Ambassador Program
description: Cultural professionals want to be sustainable but don't know how. Ki Culture's Sustainability Ambassador Program combines tools, resources, and support - empowering and enabling everyone, everywhere to work towards a sustainable future. The backbone of the Program are our freely available Ki Books, which are the step-by-step guides specifically designed for cultural professionals on HOW to be sustainable.

title: Saving Children on India's Dangerous Roads
description: Almost 50 children die everyday in road crashes in India. Most of these fatalities happen while a child is around school or on the way there. No child should have to risk their life to get an education, and no family should have to suffer the devastating loss of these young lives. SaveLIFE Foundation (SLF) is working on the ground in India to prevent road fatalities, particularly among the most vulnerable including children. Make a gift today to protect children and make India's roads safer!

title: Sindh Flood Relief
description: Heavy, record-high monsoon rainfall has caused flooding, landslides, and widespread damage and destruction throughout the Sindh province of Pakistan, including its provincial capital, Karachi.

title: COVID-19 Emergency Response in Dzaleka Camp
description: This project will directly benefit 400 refugee women, girls and gender non-conforming groups (Trans people) at high risk of COVID-19 in Dzaleka Camp including elderly persons, single mothers, women and girls living with disabilities and women with chronic conditions. They will be educated about COVID-19 and the best way to protect themselves and their family from disease. They will also be provided emergency food provisions and hygiene kits to help them get through the Coronavirus pandemic.

title: Help Street Children of Mwanza go back Home Safely
description: This project will bring back the joy and dignity of the children that they will unite with their safe family after trauma healing process for the child and his/ her parents/ caregiver.

title: Without you, AVAZ cannot be heard enough.
description: The general objective of the project is to develop civil society activities and the voluntariness in the region, through providing applied trainings and micro funds to the local youth between 14-27 ages, on project design-writing, project management, reporting, and social entrepreneurship.

title: SAVE LIVES OF 600 MALNOURISHED CHILDREN IN UGANDA
description: Imagine battling child malnutrition without any hope of a helping hand to prevent early death! Unfortunately, this is the story of over 2 million children in Uganda. The situation is even dire with COVID-19.  As Child and Family Foundation Uganda, working with community health workers and peer mothers, we seek your donation to identify 600 malnourished children this year and provide them with healthcare and nutrition support to restore healthy growth and prevent death. Donate now.

title: Safe home for the victim's domestic violence in BH
description: "Zenski centar" Foundation based in Trebinje has been trying for a longer period to establish a shelter for women and children victims/survivors of domestic violence for the very patriarchal Eastern Herzegovina region in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The establishment of a Safe House would contribute to empowering victims to leave such families and regain the sense of personal safety. Our director and founder was a victim of domestic violence that helps other women and children victims to survive.

title: Supporting Single Mothers affected from COVID-19
description: In light of Egyptian Food Bank's efforts to fight hunger & as a second stage for supporting day labor;EFB has decided to provide feeding boxes to the underprivileged COVID-19 cases,especially Single Moms who lost their jobs &income,by giving them Healthy Nutritious food boxes enough for their families,till they are back to their jobs.The main objective of this initiative is providing main &sufficient nutrition for mothers that have been negatively impacted due to the COVID-19  continuous spread.

title: Improve the wellbeing of 10,000 Orphans in Kenya
description: Over 10,000 Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVC) in Lurambi Sub-County, Kakamega, Kenya lack basic needs, cannot access adequate support services, experience high levels of abuse, teen pregnancies, and an increasing rate of HIV/AIDs.  Our objective is to build the capacity of local communities, families, caregivers and Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) to provide a range of critical services for the OVC including community and home-based care and access to health and social services.

title: Send 24 minority girls to film school
description: Placing a camera in the hands of a minority girl and empowering her to tell her own stories can be life changing. Black Girl Film School will provide a rich online multimedia learning program to teach underserved minority girls how to master the technology and technical tools of film production as early as middle school. We need 24 video camera kits so that our learners can complete the BGFS training program using the proper technology and equipment.

title: A longterm home for 200 rescued huskies a year
description: What if Husky Rescue Ireland didn't exist? What would happen to the 200 huskies and akitas that we rescue, work with and find homes for each year? It doesn't bear thinking about, and that's why we're seriously thinking about the future. Right now, we have a great location. But we rent it. Can we still be here in 2, 5 or 10 years time? Who knows. We have to begin planning ahead while we have time, rather than when it might be too late. Help us begin the long road to finding HRI's forever home!

title: #CloseTheGap with computers for students in Mexico
description: Virtual learning lets us see the educative, socioeconomical and technological gap students in Mexico live. Most students don't have the tools to continue their education.    Together with Georgetown Alumni, Stanford Alumni and Texas exes, we can give 350 computers so all the students of CBTiS 99 - a technical high school in Monterrey - continue with their education. Our goal is to raise 100 computers in GlobalGiving until September 21st.

title: Help Preserve Traditional Dance and Music in Mali
description: Mali is at a tipping point of becoming a region with its cultural heritage in crisis.  Always known as a culture with a strong history of traditional arts,  an increasing fragile security situation combined with the rapid pace of globalization means that many of the traditions are disappearing.  This project will construct a music and dance center to provide a place for local and international artists to study dance and music traditions and provide programming for local children and schools.

title: Create a turning point for 50 Ugandan students

title: A school for children with no chance for education
description: Adele gathers sticks in front of her hut. She puts them in several rows. She imagines that this is a classroom. She dreams to become a teacher, but she don't go to school. title: PROVIDING HEALTHCARE TO CHILDREN IN RURAL KENYA
description: The Children's Health Program (CHEP) brings medical care to children whose parents cannot afford healthcare at established health centres in Central Kenya. Children aged 4 to 14 years old have yearly checkups, are de-wormed 3 times a year, given vitamins and supplements, administered tests as required and treated. Importantly the program helps to ensure critical illnesses are caught and proper treatment given early to prevent serious complications in children or even death.

title: Covid Relief for Special Needs Families
description: Our Mobile inClusion Relief Center will travel through Los Angeles County.  Due to COVID-19, thousands of families are under served and at high risk for infection, sickness, neglect, abuse and malnutrition.  Our Mobile Center will provide a safe space where we provide relief to families in areas such as education, food, supplies, support groups, sensory activities, behavioral services and life and social skills while maintaining physical distance.

title: Support Talented Youth from South of Poland
description: "This grant gave me wings and made me believe in my talent" said Justyna, one of our scholars. Thanks to the scholarship she made her own, professional and  artistic  film, shown at festivals. Zywiec Development Foundation help young people from small communities  to believe in their talents and develop into profession.We plan to support 15 talented young people from small communities in the South of Poland. By giving them scholarships we open them chances for success based on their talents.

title: Basic medical equipment for children in Senegal
description: The health of 12,000 extremely poor people in Senegal depends on Sor's Maternal and Childcare Health Center  However, it lacks basic equipment and the roof is about to collapse.   This project will provide basic health equipment and repair the roof to protect pregnant women and children.

title: HELP BUILD ABLUTION BLOCK FOR 170 TEENS IN ZAMBIA
description: This project will raise matching funds to build an Eco-friendly ablution block at Katombora Reformatory School in rural Zambia for 170 teens who are in conflict with the law. The ablution block will be independent in its water and power supply and will include 3 toilet cubicles, 3 urinals, 4 sinks, 4 shower cubicles, store room, service duct, 4400 liter water tank, borehole, solar powered water pump, and septic tank. This project will help restore dignity and self-worth to these forgotten teens.

title: Preventing infection in mothers & babies in Uganda
description: Essential hand sanitiser, scrubs and specialist training enable health workers to combat infectious diseases, including COVID-19. Infections cause 20% of maternal mortality in our partner hospitals in Kampala where around 30,000 births take place every year. This project helps mothers and babies stay healthy and prevents deaths. We need your support to maintain our established hand sanitiser production and dispensing at the hospitals, local procurement of scrubs and infection training for staff.

title: COVID-19 relief help for the undeserved in Uganda
description: In contemporary times, the world has never been affected by a catastrophic pandemic disease like the one it is facing now. Covid-19 has affected almost every country in the world and it's still spreading. Your donation will help cope up with the disease challenges in the helpless communities of Uganda in the following ways; It will help to send doctors, nurses, and other front line responders to refugees' camps and remote areas. It will help buy masks, ventilators, and other lifesaving medicals

title: Digital education for Syrian refugee children
description: In 10 years, 90% of jobs will require digital skills. Syrian refugee children have limited to no possibility to acquire these skills. TSF provides them with a welcoming environment to learn digital skills in an engaging way. No matter what their background is, children can start learning from day one and building the blocks of a brighter future. With COVID-19 significantly hampering educational opportunities, this solution allows Syrian refugee children to continue their learning even remotely.

title: Playground for Rural First Nation Community
description: The First Nation in Lytton is isolated from mainland British Columbia by the Fraser River. It was home to an operational residential school until the late 1970s, and at one point was known for being the suicide capital of Canada. Over 40 years later, the effects of this traumatic history are still prevalent. We aim to change that narrative by building a community center, sustainable playground, and multi-sport field to give children the gift of play, and the community a space to come together.

title: Help St Martins School Open its doors in 2021
description: Covid-19 is having a severe impact on the pupils of St Martin's school in Kibagare slum, and area already enduring widespread suffering. The school is a sanctuary for over 1000 children from Kibagare providing not just a place of education but a safe space for them from the hardships of their daily lives. St Martin's is a space where the children can be children and at the same time receive regular meals, kindness and care.  Now Covid-19 is threatening the existence of our school.

title: Give clean water filters to 105 vulnerables!
description: The village of Kabisine in Rwanda suffers from many water-borne illnesses due to their access to water being a river below their mountain homes. The furthest walks 2 hours to fetch the water they need for the day which is dirty and contaminated.  The water genie will filter out 99.9% of parasites, bacteria, metals and sand, whereby, the 105 villagers will have clean water in their homes for the first time. The water genie filters 30,000 liters. The clean water will drastically change lives.

title: SOCIAL AND LABOR REINSERTION OF 120 WOMEN VICTIMS
description: This project helps to strengthen and restore dignity to a group of 120 women leaders who are victims of the armed conflict, who as displaced have precarious living conditions, the incomes will be supported with the creation of a sustainable community business through transformation of discarded tires into handicrafts and furniture for domestic use. Municipality of Calima - Darien Colombia

title: Fund training for women formerly incarcerated
description: Less than 50% of women who have been imprisoned find work within the first year of being released. For those who find employment, their income is usually no more than minimum wage. This project provides women employment training and provides them the opportunity to demonstrate their skills through an internship that results in job placement so that women who have been incarcerated have a better chance at self-reliance and stability for themselves and their children.

title: Support Syrian disabled children meet their rights
description: Nine continues years of War in Syria, resulted in leaving hundreds of thousands of vulnerable families facing extremely severe conditions with unknown future. Thousands of disabled children are now living in very poor situation suffering from lack of access to basic rights: shelter, protection, education, health & treatment needs, etc. This fund will support the caring of disabled children & their families through securing suitable shelter, protection, education, health, and livelihood services

title: Install 20 water cisterns in rural Puerto Rico
description: Water is life! Access to clean water in rural Puerto Rico is unstable due to constant power outages, exacerbated since Hurricane Maria in 2017. In this new context of COVID-19, combined with non-stop earthquakes and a hyperactive hurricane season, water becomes essential to the very survival of those that are at a higher risk when low hygiene conditions are present. We look to provide the means for some of the most vulnerable families to have access to water during service shutdowns.

title: Buy a Brick - Build a new HOME
description: COVID-19 hit the restaurant industry in Vietnam hard. With lockdown and no international tourists, we sadly had to close KOTO Training Restaurant at 59 Van Mieu. Since the future of the tourism industry hangs in the balance, it's not a viable strategy for KOTO to "sit and wait it out".   We hope you consider supporting KOTO by being one of the first to "Buy a Brick - Build a new HOME" for our new restaurant, all funds will go towards building KOTO Villa which will be a new home for the trainees.

title: Family units for 100 OVCs in Got Osimbo
description: We have acquired a 5-acre parcel of land near Lake Victoria, situated along Kisumu - Busia highway at Got Osimbo. We are planning to put up hostels for Orphans and Vulnerable Children(OVCs), classrooms, medical clinic, community multipurpose hall, guest wings, Already we have drawings/plans and bills of quantities.  Also carrying out farming activities on parts of the land for the supply of basic food commodities needed for the OVCs, the school and for sale in outside markets.

title: ZAKKI Empowering The Elderly in Indonesia
description: ZAKKI is an organization that focuses on helps the elderly and people with disability get better livelihoods in order to build an inclusive community in Indonesia. ZAKKI focus to help the elderly and people with disability who working in the informal sector to get better livelihood through micro-business management assistance and giving them exposure to the greater market.

title: Mental Health Resources 4 Underserved Communities
description: This project will allow Yoga 4 Change to provide mental health resources to more veterans, youth, individuals experiencing incarceration and those living with mental health conditions.  Yoga 4 Change programming provides tools for individuals, to use in their daily lives, to reduce stress and anxiety and increase mood, sleep and positive, healthy coping skills.

title: TRAIN 80 TEEN MOTHERS IN VOCATIONS  IN GHANA
description: CEWEFIA is seeking support for 80 Vulnerable teenage Mothers who are school drop-outs due to teenage pregnancy and are single handedly taking care of their children and have not acquired any employable skills to enter into other businesses apart from the fish processing business which for the past ten years is in serious crisis due the dwindling Fish Stocks.

title: Black soldier fly larvae production
description: The project will consider the feasibility of rearing Hermetia illucens (black soldier fly or BSF) using their larvae to primarily supplement fish and livestock feed . Considerations will also be given for the utilisation of the larvae castings as organic fertiliser.

title: Sustainable Sponge Farming
description: Sri Lanka is a biodiversity hotspot, because of that reason so many different sponge species can be observed around the Sri Lankan coastal waters. Due to overharvest and disease, wild sponge stocks worldwide are in decline. Farming sponges is a solution to overcome the market demand. Sponges have been commercially cultivated in many countries worldwide. But Sponge farming is a very new field to Sri Lanka. The project will be established in Northern region of Sri Lanka supporting the communities.

title: Empower 100 Orphan Girls
description: The project is gear toward building the capacities of 100 adult orphan girls in Liberian orphanages through Vocational and Technical Skill; enhancing their ability to serve sustainability, and enlighting their mind to Small Business Management and Life Coaching before they transition orphanages. It is going to ensure that the livelihood of girls is built as they transition to independent living after the orphanage.

title: Organic food & education for families in Rio slum
description: This first phase of the project will provide organic food for 3 months to 100 low-income families from Vidigal, a favela slum in Rio de Janeiro, while they participate in workshops focused on organic agriculture, nutritional education, and health. This initiative will help boost the local economy with green jobs, disrupt current pesticide filled food supply chains, and improve the quality of life of the residents.

title: New lives for 100 orphans in Nigeria
description: Thousands of orphans in Nigeria between the ages of 15 & 19 live on less than $1 a day. With your support, we will train 100 orphans in highly demanded fashion skills and donate required tools. They will learn skills (like fashion designing, bag making, bead making, shoe making and Tie & Dye) and how to successfully build a small business.

title: 100 Refugee Women Launch Micro-Businesses in Camps
description: This project will lift 100 women refugees and their children from extreme poverty to economic independence by promoting  entrepreneurship.  Mercy Beyond Borders (MBB) provides basic business training and $200 loans for South Sudanese women in refugee camps; the women then launch their own enterprises. We already have a strong success record in 6 camps. Be the one who lifts the next refugee woman!

title: Support 60 families on their Journey to Recovery!
description: The home should be a place of safety. For thousands of Puerto Ricans, this is not the case. Recurring earthquakes and slow government response has forced families across the island to live in unsafe homes.   Your donation will support 60 families' journeys to a safer home through our Ruta a Una Casa Segura program (RUCS), including ATC-20 home inspections, structural engineering reports, and case management to navigate the complex recovery process that takes a toll on the families' wellbeing

title: Help 50 Survivors of Human Trafficking Heal Trauma
description: We are passionate about giving second chances and healing traumas for horses and humans alike. We rescue horses who are throw away and slaughter-bound. We rehabilitate them and those that choose to trust again partner with our coaches to help humans heal traumas.  We focus on survivors of domestic abuse, human trafficking, at risk youth and Veterans. Through the horse-human connection we are able to unpack and identify traumas and help humans heal and step into a fulfilled life.

title: Advocate for cancer patients not getting treatment
description: In Mexico, cancer patients are not receiving their treatments, making them susceptible to being in danger of death. Due to covid19, government agencies converted hospitals to treat those infected, leaving aside patients with other conditions. It is essential to support cancer patients to reduce the risk of contagion of Covid19, have comprehensive support services and receive their cancer treatments despite the hospital reconversion. Cancer was not quarantined! This is a matter of life or death!

title: LGBTI HUMAN RIGHTS
description: The work of these 2 civil associations and a community group provide direct care to the most vulnerable LGBTI population: people living on the streets, sex workers, people with HIV, recovery of LGBT bodies abandoned in the morgue, drug users, migrants, accompaniments in human rights violations: forced disappearance, homicides, trafficking and attempted homicides

title: Prevent Human Trafficking at Major Sporting Events
description: No human being should ever be sold. When Katariina was a young teen, she got involved with a group of friends who betrayed her trust. The so-called 'friends' exploited her and forced her to have sex with men while they made a profit. Our prevention campaign, during Super Bowl LV in Tampa, Florida, will educate the tens of thousands of attendees, the ride-share drivers, and hotel & motel staff to spot the signs of exploitation & human trafficking, learn how to make a report, and help end it.

title: Help Masurian kids to learn competences of future
description: We conduct free classes for youth (11-16 years) from 10 rural schools in Masury region. Through volunteering, they learn in practice of cooperation, creative thinking, entrepreneurship, leadership, responsibility, empathy and digital skills - we awaken curiosity and development opportunities. We use active forms of work (games, gamification, etc.). During 1 school year we work with 150 kids. In the next 5 years we plan to run lessons for 1000 kids from 50 rural schools.

title: 45 Cookstoves for Vuelta Grande
description: From a firsthand look at the manufacturing an Aller Clean Cook Stove to the installation of 45 Aller stoves in the village of Vuelta Grande. We'll take you through our teams' meeting with the village leadership to the signing of the contracts by each family. We'll highlight the installation in homes and the training that takes place after the installation is complete. All of this from the comfort of your own home. We'll post videos and have the team highlight the process throughout.

title: Adequate nutrition for young children and mothers.
description: This project will help women to produce a protein-rich food supplement to offer to young children and mothers at the Mother and Child Health Clinics in Lesotho, in Southern Africa, so that children with adequate nutrition will survive past their fifth year, grow to their proper height and children and mothers will develop their immune systems to fight off disease.  Other youth and women will grow and sell organic vegetables in the community at a reasonable cost and improve their own livelihoods.

title: Educational intervention for youth at-risk for HD
description: The New Horizons kids program supports basic needs for 350 kids at risk for Huntington's disease. We have also established a series of "Escuelitas/Talleres" (Workshop Schools) to ensure that kids receive basic education, learn a trade, and have access to psychological support. Kids & adolescents come from two towns in Venezuela with the highest incidence of HD in the world. Our teachers and psychologists ensure they get a chance in life. Participating students get a meal as well.

title: Ecological Cribs & Food for 3000 kids in Colombia
description: we seeks to  save the lives of  children in Colombia and help in the migratory emergency of displaced Venezuelan families, a journey through the creation and delivery of ecological cribs. our foundation plans to develop and deliver 3,000 cribs to children living in the streets or low-income families, along with basic grooming kits and clothes for the little ones. Educational workshops will be developed to educate women and children to to dignify their lives.

title: Rescue 3,000 people's lives due to floods in Yemen
description: The torrential rains in the governorate of Rayma have caused an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe, leaving behind a devastation. Most of the drinking water sources were washed away / buried. People suffer heavy losses. Now struggling to survive, the project aims to save 3,000 lives from disease and death through the immediate provision of drinking water and the rehabilitation of clean water sources.

title: Build Sustainability Skills of Ten African Leaders
description: COVID-19 has wreaked havoc across Africa both in terms of health and the economy.  Many economic development plans are being created by governments and private entities to re-build the same type of systems that provided the opportunity for a pandemic to flourish.  Through training, information and networking on impact assessment techniques, this project will build the expertise in ten local leaders to respond to community needs and foster sustainable development.

title: Continued Learning During Covid-19 (and beyond!)
description: Help our teachers as they engage our 400+ students in this new school year - whether it be in-person classes or distance learning. Children growing up in Vietnamese orphanages face isolation. The past 6+ months of the covid19 pandemic has heightened this isolationism as many orphanages have locked their gates, limiting contact with Kidspire staff. These teachers aren't just providing a S.T.E.A.M. focused learning program. They offer much needed: Encouragement. Motivation. Confidence. Hope.

title: Little by Little- Tahanan
description: Tahanan ng Pagmamahal Children's Home, Inc wants to sustain the basic needs of the 45 children including food and medical to boost their immune system and to prevent them from COVID 19 Pandemic and other illnesses.

title: COVID-19 Palliative for 1200 households in Nigeria
description: This project will cushion the impact of economic hardship, hunger, and poverty on 1,200 households in selected rural agrarian communities in Osun State, Nigeria that are impacted by COVID-19. The benefiting households from the selected communities of Inisa, Eko-Ende, Aagba, Iree, Ada, and Igbajo will receive raw staple food materials of 10 kg each of Rice, Beans, and Gari each to alleviate their economic situation.

title: Provide Health Supplies to 50 Children in Uganda
description: Poverty continues to deprive children from the most basic necessities to live a better life. According to UNICEF , 1 child in 11 dies before the age of 5 in Uganda.  Especially, children born in rural, impoverished areas face significant risk. Inaccessibility of health supplies and services remains a pressing issue due to variety of factors such as families low income to a shortage of health workers. Many of health challenges might be prevented through health education and awareness programs.

title: School renovation for 1,700 children in Nigeria
description: The Amuro/Mgbom Community Primary and Secondary School is located between two villages in the state of Ebony. Around 1,700 children from different villages attend the school. The situation in the classrooms is awful: several classes in one room, extremely hot, very limited equipment, broken walls and roofs. The school complex consists of 10 buildings, which will be refurbished over time. In addition we modernize the school kitchen, establish water supply and toilets and equip the classrooms.

title: Hands On! Equip Deaf youth to work in Zimbabwe
description: Sanganai means "Come together" the inspiration for Sanganai Project aimed at bringing deaf youth together to build a stronger deaf community through vocational and skills training. Youth are mentored and taught practical skills. Partnerships are fostered with local companies to give deaf youth experience in industry; and local communities are exposed to sign language and deaf culture, building acceptance and inclusion. Your support will give deaf youth opportunity to become capable entrepreneurs

title: Help Save Lives with Team Survive
description: Team Survive, a PCI Media initiative, tells stories that educate people about COVID-19 to keep themselves and their communities safe. These stories address COVID-19 health practices, ways that essential workers can stay safe, and how to cope with the emotional fallout of the pandemic. We understand the power of using the right platform to reach the right audience.

title: Empower Communities to Adapt to Climate Change
description: PCI Media works with local communities and partners to raise promote sustainable behaviors. Our radio dramas, films, and social media and political advocacy campaigns have reached over 2 million in West Africa and 4.2 million farmers in Central America. Policy makers, like the Mano River Union in West Africa, have come together to prioritize natural resource management because of our work.

title: DADS ARE NOT DEAD BEATS -THEY'RE DEAD BROKE!
description: We cannot move One Million Moms OFF Welfare by 2030 without addressing the needs of fathers!  Fathers are a part of the solution, not the problem.  To this end, we are creating an animated adult comedy to address issues that have plagued African American low-income communities as both friend and foe (i.e. child support and welfare dependency).  By increasing awareness, this project will help empower men in their roles as parents and partners.

title: Provide Cassava milling machine for 120 Farmers
description: This Project will reduce poverty in Bukpe Community, Nigeria, by providing  Cassava milling machine in Bukpe community, Kwali Area council, Abuja. The machine will be used to process harvested cassava. The machine will increase the production and sales of Garri which will increase the income of 120 farmers in the community, promote a culture of entrepreneurship using the street business school curriculum.

title: Support Humanity Fund for Peace and Justice
description: Humanity Fund supports the struggle of victims and survivors of human rights violations in Indonesia to access justice. The fund supports the community in conflict areas by providing access to legal and economic, social, cultural rights. This activity will also involve young generation to be able to interact with the survivors to preserve the memory of past human rights violations that have not been resolved and to increase public awareness on the current human rights violations.

title: Health access to Low-Income Children
description: During the Covid-19 pandemic, many children with disabilities and polydiagnosis have stopped receiving medical care. In Colombia, state resources have been prioritized to face the current health crisis, leaving in second place the needs of medical and specialized care of the population with disabilities or high-cost illnesses. Our Foundation supports this population through specialized consultations, medications, and therapies that helps to improve the physical and mental health of children

title: Give hope for underserved youths in Singapore
description: Gift A Hope: Small Steps, Big Impact (by Trybe Limited) is a call for us as a community to empower youths facing adversities. By guiding them and celebrating their small accomplishments, we are encouraging young people to push through their struggles and aim for a better future. Your donation to this project will help us continue our services that improve personal, social, educational, and employment outcomes for underserved youths in Singapore.

title: Educate Her Empower Her
description: Since 2018, iPartner India has steadfastly provided unwavering support for educating young girls residing in Rajasthan, within a community that fosters the perpetuation of traditional sex work practices. As a result of this commendable education campaign, 227 girls have been afforded the opportunity to pursue education and strive towards constructing a prosperous existence that transcends the confines of their accustomed environment. The most vulnerable are enrolled into boarding institutions.

title: Fund for Sindh Rain Flood 2020 Affected Families
description: The aim of this disaster relief fund to minimize sufferings for heavy rain flood 2020 affected 5737 families in Sindh province of Pakistan by providing them emergency assistance like cooked/dry food items, clean drinking water, hygiene/sanitary items, medicines, mosquito nets, non-food items and temporary shelter. This immediate humanitarian assistance can minimize their hardships, diseases and death as well as support in early recovery of severely affected families.

title: Enhance disaster relief action of 50 NGOs in China
description: China has the highest number of disasters happening in the past 10 years. To effectively save lives and help affected population, Chinese NGOs need to improve their relevant knowledge and skills. The project will develop and localize humanitarian training modules and provide online trainings to key staff from 50 front-line NGOs active in disaster relief, which will help these NGOs to deliver better emergency responses and ultimately benefit the people affected by disasters in China.

title: ReBuild Hurricanes Laura & Delta
description: On August 27, 2020, Hurricane Laura slammed into the southwest Louisiana as the 10th strongest hurricane to ever make landfall in the United States. The extreme winds damaged caused catastrophic damage to literally thousands of homes. Many of these homeowners are low-income and lack the wherewithal to rebuild themselves. To compound the misery Delta struck the same area on October 9th. We rebuild with volunteer labor and your donations.

title: JAC's COVID Conversion For Its ReEntry Clinics!
description: COVID was able to provide many people with different prospective of items that were important to their productivity and economic development.  We have been able to   assisted dozens of clients safely with their credit reports, credit discrepancies and credit counseling.   Vaccinations and PPE have allowed us to provide this service with privacy and confidentiality.   Your support will help us secure adequate PPE, space to socially distance, and other adjustments necessary.

title: Improve Housing Conditions for Cancer Patients
description: To improve our housing conditions include bigger bathrooms, more space in the dinning room to guarantee physical distancing of at least 1 meter, portable sinks in different spots for frequent hand-washing or disinfection, provide medical masks to everyone at the house, disposable gowns and gloves for the nurses to wear.   All this key measure expenses to protect against Covid 19 weren't part of our 2020 budget, and since we paused our fundraising events this year, we are cash flow constrained.

title: Fund Workshops to End Trafficking in Canada
description: Aura Freedom's counter-trafficking work is focused on an upstream, intersectional feminist approach by addressing root causes, upholding human rights and advancing equity. This approach is the framework of our ground-breaking online Human Trafficking Info Hub, and is reflected across our workshops and consultations for GBV sector workers, frontline staff, school boards, government, educators, youth, the private sector and more.

title: The Acts of Kindness Fund & Learning Program
description: Creativity and innovation are at the core of creating sustainable and long-term impact.  Since 2020 this fund has featured the innovative approaches of BBS supported projects and today we highlight our goal for 200 youth to participate in the Photo Start programs. Their innovative photography curriculum integrates visual storytelling with digital literacy using applied learning to equip students with much needed skills so no one is left behind in today's digital world.

title: Help construct 1x2 classrooms for 115 Vulnerable
description: Rural Children's Hope plans to construct two classrooms to provide free Early childhood Education for 115  vulnerable children  from poor families in Nyakuwalo village, Sinda District, Eastern Province in rural Zambia  .

title: Help Khmer Social Workers Care for Foster Children
description: MRO owns three second-hand cars to provide transport and reintegration services to orphans and vulnerable children in Cambodia, including those cared for in our Emergency Foster Care program and those rescued from abusive situations.  The cars (a 2001 Toyota Land Cruiser, a 2001 Toyota Highlander and a 1999 Kia Visto) carry out on average 178 missions per year to help about 850 vulnerable children. These cars are becoming unsafe to drive, and new ones are needed to continue our life-saving work.

title: Help families affected by COVID-19 in the DR
description: The Project is an initiative of the Joyas de Cristo Boys and Girls Foundation and sponsored by the Funcomas Foundation that seeks to save the lives of thousands of hundreds of families that are being affected by the current crisis caused by COVID-19. This project gives you the opportunity to help guarantee food, health and education for affected people and their direct dependents. As well as dependents of people who have been unemployed due to the pandemic.

title: Tuijkinge na Corona! - Our defence against Corona!
description: We want to help vulnerable population of the Iringa district (central area of Tanzania)to protect themselves agaist the Coronavirus.Our actions are aimed at the people with disabilities and poor families, who need help throught the emergency. Our activities will involve the translation of informative tects about the prevention of the virus, the distribution of sanitary kits and informative meetings with the population. We will also install 5 water wells that will fuction thriught a pedal-system.

title: Free Cataract Surgeries of 3000 Poor Patients
description: The goal of this project is to perform 3000 Free Surgeries of poor people suffering from preventable blindness or vision problems due to Cataract, especially those living in under-developed areas of Pakistan. We strive to address preventable blindness in poor people by performing Free Cataract Surgeries at Free Eye Camps in rural and suburban areas of country and at our Hospitals. This strategy resolves this issue completely and has an impact on the lives of the beneficiaries almost immediately.

title: Help Support LGBTIQ+ Refugees in Southern Africa
description: Ntsako Wa Wena will support LGBTQ+ refugees from across Africa in South Africa through provision of destitution services, asylum support, legal service provision, facilitating for the refugees to obtain support to further their education or entrepreneurship development and access to health related services that include psycho-social support  and refugee activity co-ordination.  This project aims at livelihood improvements of the LGBTQ+ community and creating a 'Home' away from 'Home.'

title: Computers for Children`s Crisis Shelter in Ukraine
description: Six computers will be provided for classroom of  Children's Center for Rehabilitation and Social Adaptation. Children aged 7 - 18 years from poor and crisis families are living at a Center`s social dormitory in Odesa, Ukraine, fully supported by the Way Home Foundation.  Your donation will help the them to get access to school distance education during the COVID-19 epidemic. In addition, they will learn computer literacy and coding basics. More than 50 children a year will benefit.

title: To Prevent spread and mitigate impact of COVID-19
description: Bamenda is a densely populated and conflict-prone area and a host to more than 25000 IDPs, and pre-existing vulnerabilities that are likely to be exacerbated by the pandemic. IDPs and vulnerable families may not be able to feed and provide basic needs for their children and families in the coming weeks. Within this context SUDAHSER is implementing a project with objective to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and mitigate the socio-economic impact for vulnerable and conflict affected communities

title: Bearfoot Ranch Fundraiser
description: This project will establish an emergency vet reserve for our 35 plus rescue horses.  We plan to use these reserves for vet visits, emergency medicines and treatment providing our animals with the best care. Additionally, we will fund the ongoing cost of the special needs riding program including farrier visits, hay, food and supplements to keep our horses healthy.

title: School Supplies for those Affected by CA Wildfires
description: As wildfires continue to ravage California, beloved farming communities are getting hit the hardest - destroying homes, barns, crops and livestock. Despite these struggles, one of the top needs that farming families have identified is assistance with getting their children prepared for school and at-home learning. In light of these requests, Can'd Aid is working to rapidly assemble and ship a large donation of art and school supplies to the Salinas, CA region.

title: Arts education for 100 Trinidad & Tobago youth
description: This year long art as cultural diplomacy program offers 100 youth ages 14-18 an opportunity to develop their creative abilities, build entrepreneurial skills and explore their own solutions for some of the world's most pressing issues. The  program builds practical skills in Theater, Visual Art, Dance and Music while addressing themes of Gender Equality;  Good Health and Well-being; Decent Work & Economic Growth; and Climate Action. Our goal is to groom youth to be future catalysts for change.

title: Family Autism Center Support During Covid & Beyond
description: During these challenging times, The Family Autism Center remains committed to supporting individuals and their families either remotely or in socially distant settings, providing advocacy, supports and services; navigating DDS, Mass Health, ABA), recreational and social activities for children and adults, support groups for parents and grandparents, workshops and trainings such as IEP training and financial planning, ABA/Behavioral Interventions, Basic Rights and informational resources.

title: Empower Malawian students to promote mental health
description: Young Malawians develop skills and knowledge to design and manage new responses to the mental health challenges that are increasingly affecting their peers. Zamumtima Sizawekha (meaning 'if you have a burden, you do not have to carry it on your own') breaks the barriers and stigma around mental health among youth, using participatory research and performances.

title: Providing food baskets to students in Mozambique
description: This project will provide monthly food baskets to vulnerable schoolchildren and their families across six rural villages in Mozambique. Schools are closed due to COVID-19 and students are no longer able to depend on daily school lunches. To prevent these children from going hungry at home, the Mozambique School Lunch Initiative is providing monthly food baskets to over 1,000 children and their families, stocked with key staples and fresh produce purchased from local farmers.

title: Saving Russia's leading independent LGBT media
description: This project will save 'Parni PLUS', Russia's leading media outlet produced by LGBTQ people for LGBTQ readers, from dying. It will enable our growth into a strong independent media resource covering all the issues that matter to our audience. It will help us strengthen our contribution into the fight for LGBTQ and human rights in Russia. It will facilitate our projects and initiatives targeted at HIV prevention and providing access to PrEP among LGBTQ people and high risk groups.

title: Support the completion of Mkanthama school block
description: Mkanthama is one of the poorest rural communities in Lilongwe where access to education for children is very hard to find. The next school close to where our school project is situated is about 3 Kilometres away which is very difficult for children to walk to. In 2017 we started this school project so that children in this area can also have the opportunity to go to school and learn. Due to the closure of schools because of Covid-19 we started constructing a school block which has 3 classrooms.

title: Atlas Corps: Global Impact
description: Make a donation to Atlas Corps and we will follow-up with the link to join us and celebrate #GlobalImpact on December 16th, 12pm ET.  Amplify your donation on this day and support the #GlobalImpact of Atlas Corps.  Support our community of 850 social change leaders from 99 countries! you empower our global community that innovates in addressing the world's most pressing issues by training global social change leaders!

title: Little by Little Campaign for Family Support
description: The Family Autism Center at The Arc of South Norfolk provides supports and services to people diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders and their families.  We provide respite care, specialized recreational programming, training for family members and provide information and referral sources to families looking for assistance.  Autism impacts 1 in every 68 children- we have seen an increase of 100 additional people requesting our services in the last 12 months alone- we serve 652 people currently

title: My sanitary pads My Education
description: This project will assist young vulnerable girls in Primary and secondary education in Uganda to access sanitary ware. These girls come from very high need families that can not afford sanitary pad (1 U$ day). As a result many end by being irregular at school and eventually drop out of school. The project will support 1000 girls from 10 schools as for the start.  For sustainability, the project will carryout a feasibility study to establish a cheaper production facility of  the sanitary pads

title: Help our Eco Village get off-grid and sustainable
description: This project will focus on getting the Nourish Eco Village to become more sustainable by minimising our environmental footprint. Honoring the Sustainable Development goals -we will develop a grey water system for all our waste water including showers and toilets and convert all our electricity to solar.  We run a preschool, library, and feeding program and committing to going off-grid will help us afford more impactful upliftment projects and become sustainable; environmentally & economically.

title: Walking in Jaffa's Shoes
description: Discriminatory policies in housing and education, police brutality, and eviction orders, make it nearly impossible for young Palestinians in Jaffa to build a future in their city, and resist the removal of their community. The mainstream story often told of Jaffa enables these trends of forced removal to continue. We seek to train Jaffa's young people, and those seeking to stand in solidarity with them, to lead alternative tours of the city and speak up.

title: Fund Musical Resilience for At-Promise Youth!
description: This project gives students in economically distressed and culturally or racially marginalized communities the chance to learn to play guitar in a restorative, responsive community of peers, taught and guided by a specially trained GITC guitar instructor. Each student who completes a semester of  guitar learning is rewarded with a beautiful guitar to call their own!  At this time, we are running successful guitar programs in San Diego and L.A. continuation, alternative, and urban high schools.

title: Help flood devastation recovery in Odisha, India
description: In August, continuous heavy rains for many days caused major rivers to overflow, resulting in terrible flooding in communities in Bihar and Odisha. So far, 17 deaths have been reported, 20 districts are affected and thousands of homes are damaged. Some people have been evacuated to flood relief centres but with numbers affected entering the millions, many are left coping in their flooded communities.   In the area our partners work, 57,500 people are affected by extreme flooding.

title: Help 20 refugee children study for their future
description: Refugee children have a lot of difficulties to have a good education: no schools, family moving from one site to another.  We help refugee children to attend a boarding secondary agricultural school called the LAP (www.asaplap.org). This school gives stability for the students and an adapted education for her/his future.

title: Strengthen Families in Thailand
description: This project will support the training and administrative expenses required to accomplish six key objectives. We work in cooperation with government agencies and private organizations to 1. support and encourage strong and healthy families. 2. prevent social problems in Thai society. 3. develop good leaders. 4. support and create education opportunities. 5. establish counseling centers to address family problems, addictions, and abuse. 6. provide expertise and collaboration with 49 partners.

title: Support Mobile Clinics in Syria
description: Support SEMA's mobile clinics to deliver health care to thousands of IDPs in Northwestern Syria
