title: Empowering Women to Light Villages in Nepal
description: Women Light the World is helping women in Nepal to become leaders in sustainable energy and in their communities.  Our unique model trains women -- selected by their own villages -- to become solar engineers, installing and maintaining solar panels back home.  Our vision is to expand educational opportunities for women; promote economic self-sufficiency; provide safe, clean energy; and build a sustainable futures for generations to come -- one woman... one home... one village at a time.

title: TRANSCRIBE SCHOOLBOOKS IN LARGE PRINT AND BRAILLE
description: Our project consists of transcribing textbooks in large print and in Braille for blind and visually impaired students in Cameroon. These manuals will then be distributed free of charge to the needy through our network of associations for the visually impaired. These textbooks cover essential subjects such as mathematics, science, physics and chemistry. Due to the limited resources of our association, we are currently dealing with primary school books.

title: Urgent Provide flood emergency relief foiinnAT Pak
description: As u know that a huge flood of river swat hit swat in the previous month, which destroyed hundreds of homes , land sliding and cause houndreds of death of poor people's, the remaining people's are migrated to safe places but have no shelter ,clothes medicine and food .soo we need help to support these people  to provide food,shelters food medical relief and other daily needs on emergency basis. We have 30 workers already working in the flood affectd area but we have shortage of fund to help

title: Combating Food Insecurity in the Bolivian Andes
description: The food security project addresses the climate change effect in Micani, rural Bolivia, by relying on two methods: First, the implementation of micro-irrigation systems and greenhouses to contribute to healthy and stable nutrition supply, and secondly, through workshops in which the population learns to apply sustainable agricultural practices independently. This will help to provide village schools, farmers and their families in Micani with permanent access to healthy food.

title: Typhoon Vamco and Goni Permaculture Support
description: Green Releaf is raising resources to support 300 farmers from Tiwi, Albay after being impacted by Supertyphoon Goni and Vamco in November 2020, using its permaculture solutions after prototyping them for the last 3 years.   In partnership with the Sustainable Agriculture program of the Diocese of Legazpi, we are helping to raising funds for:  a) open pollinated and organic seeds b) repair of farm tools and equipment c) permaculture training and materials (print outs and videos) for sharing.

title: Little By Little: Witness To Witness
description: The struggles facing frontline responders are inflated by a host of unprecedented consequences, including depression, anxiety, and suicide. MCN takes these facts into account, providing direct peer support to those requesting it while also developing educational curricula to educate the wider public about the toll facing this at-risk group. These efforts acknowledge the rampant moral wounding occurring, interjecting accountability into the status quo via awareness, education, and outreach.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Gianna, Naika, Samantha, Liah, Kyrene, and Amelia from Advanced Technologies Academy have been working with LI to help create & publicize human rights campaigns for various rights issues in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to connect with local nonprofits in Bauchi to research, document, and advocate for various human rights issues within the area.

title: Decatur Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Margo, Hayden, Reina, Lucca, Nina, Yana, and Quinn from Decatur High School have been working with LI to help create & sustain businesses in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to build a business development center. At this center, vulnerable men and women will receive training in life, vocational, & business skills to empower & equip them to escape extreme poverty.

title: 150 h/holds with Water access for COVID Prevention
description: This water pan project will increase the availability of clean water to at-least 1600 direct beneficiaries in Kitui County . The project aims at ensuring that community member have reliable,safe and clean water even in the toughest climatic moments.The project goal is promote youth and women empowerment through hygiene interventions and vegetable production increasing availability and affordability.

title: Project Legacy Kid's Club & Scholarship Program
description: Project Legacy is our children's education and scholarship program reaching at-risk children and youth.  Marginalized children are in need of scholarships due to lack of household income to pay monthly and enrollment school fees, supplies, uniforms, etc..  Due to COVID, an online study room has been set up to accommodate children without access to wifi and assistance with homework.  The after-school program includes a healthy snack, games, quality story-time and necessary life skills training.

title: The Kakichihiwewin Project
description: The Kakichihiwewin Project aims to create strong bonds in Indigenous communities by continuing the healing process of those affected by forced assimilation efforts, ie: residential and boarding schools, forced adoption and foster care. The legacy of traumas we face often make us feel like we're walking alone... but we aren't. The Kakichihiwewin Project is asking for your help to build our communities back up by creating accessible healing circles and community care kits.

title: Wildfire Emergency Relief 2020
description: Fast-moving fires are forcing thousands of our neighbors to leave their homes in search of safety. Oregon Food Bank is providing emergency support - including water, food and other critical supplies - and getting it to meeting points and food assistance sites. Though wildfires have impacted some locations, the vast majority of pantries and meal sites remain open. Your donation helps local families, farmers and ranchers throughout the region. Together, we can emerge stronger from this crisis.

title: Tidal Wave of Poverty in the Himalayas
description: A tidal wave of poverty is sweeping across South Asia as a result of COVID-19. The Himalayan country NEPAL is particularly hard hit, as literally millions of migrant workers across South Asia have lost income and livelihood due to continued lockdowns. Himalayan Life has set out to meet this need through providing relief to families and communities in Nepal.

title: empowerment of widows & poor women in pandemic
description: The project will  economically empower about 330  disadvantaged widows & poor women in rural communities of  Enugu state Nigeria  in West  Africa who have lost their source of livelihood due to the pandemic. The project will be  supporting them with $150 each to feed their children and to  start petty trading and farming to sustain them further to go through the pandemic  and stand on their own in life . This $150 will be life saving for these  category of  women and their children.

title: World Central Kitchen: Oregon Wildfire Response
description: Southern Oregon is being scorched by wildfires. WCK is on the ground to provide meals to families and first responders affected. We have provided more than 10,500 meals in a number of days and will continue as long as we are needed and have the resources to do so.

title: Support & empower 1900+ persons with Down syndrome
description: The Down syndrome community is marginalized and lacks opportunities for independent living. The Karachi Down Syndrome Program (KDSP) is a one-stop solution advocating for the value, acceptance and inclusion of individuals with Down syndrome and providing quality, subsidized or free of cost services to them and their families including Early Childhood Intervention therapies (Physical, Occupational and Speech), Education, Skills Development, Healthcare, Family Support and Awareness.

title: Gift a Diwali kit to Visually challenged Families
description: Diwali, a festival of lights - is also a great festival for those who do not see lights.  Just like you, these differently-abled kids & Families have a dream of celebrating Diwali with much joy and vigor.  The COVID -19 pandemic & lockdowns have coupled with their weak financial condition making their situation more worst & vulnerable.  This project helps socio-economic visually Challenged kids & Families celebrate this Diwali with 2 sets of New dresses, Groceries, and snacks.

title: Grand Mother for Change Project Uganda
description: The Project will work  both rural & urban communities to improve the lives of women & children, especially of girls, using an innovative Change through Culture approach.  This approach builds on community knowledge, experience, empowers communities to promote positive change for the benefit of all. Grandmothers have great influence on their families; experience & wisdom is respected; are culturally responsible for socializing adolescent girls & make lasting changes.

title: Support street-connected girls & women in Tanzania
description: Life for girls and young women on the streets is particularly hard and the support they need is challenging to provide. Our aim is to help teenage girls and young women on the streets of Tanzania, South Africa, Burundi and India to rebuild their lives and realise their rights.

title: Stony Coral Tissue Loss Disease Intervention
description: Stony Coral Tissue Loss Disease is a highly lethal coral disease affecting 22 species of reef building corals and was first diagnosed in the TCI in 2019.  There is a treatment (amoxicillin in a special ointment base) that is effective approximately 90% of the time in stopping disease progression, but it must be applied on a coral head by coral head basis so it is time consuming and expensive. This project will allow us to continue are treatment efforts and will help to save the reefs of the TCI.

title: Community based safe space for 100 girls in Kenya
description: Empowered girls and young women are the seeds that propel a every society to greatness. Creating a safe space within a community where the AGYW can call on for support, life skills development and linkage to a referral system for essential services can help actualize  their  DREAMS. Having ready mentors, skilled counsellors and  few materials mobilised, such girls can be capacity built to enhance life skills to surmount the challenges like early sex and teen pregnancies.

title: Migrant Leaders Development Programme
description: Our aim is to provide bespoke support to equip talented young 1st and 2nd generation migrants with the knowledge, skills and confidence to enter and take on leadership roles in major public and private sector organisations. Concurrently they will feel productive and valued members of British society, thereby boosting social mobility, tackling discrimination and strengthening communities. The programme is free and participants gain mentoring, workshops, work experiences and connections.

title: Give the Gift of Literacy to 100 Lives in Illinois
description: The Bestow Foundation gives the gift of Literacy to children, students and adults - helping them achieve reading success. Teaching mothers, daughters, fathers and sons literacy, digital and life skills is our literary mission. Through the Literacy ROCKS Initiative, this project will impact hundreds of lives, offsetting academic failure by providing books, computers, and critical literacy support services to undereducated and low-income households throughout Illinois. Give the gift of Literacy!

title: Virgin Islands Children's Museum Art Exploration
description: The Virgin Islands Children's Museum has ongoing Art Exploration projects that require funds for the purchase of art supplies. Art initiatives such as those administered during Toddler Tuesday, our Music Explorations Exhibit, Dance Room, Community Events, and our At Home Discovery Kit Program aim to keep kids engaged and creating in all art mediums. Donations help keep the reoccurring cost of running these programs and events going and growing!

title: Help Us Raise Wetland Conservation by Prizing Kids
description: The Mucura Award for Wetland Conservation stimulates knowledge and recognizes commitment of rural children & youth to the conservation of wetlands in provinces, each year. A first pilot focuses on the province of Sugamuxi (Boyaca, COL) which consists of 13 towns, but we are willing to gradually spread this over into more regions. It rewards positive actions on local rural wetlands made at an early age, aiming to raise awareness on securing its multiple services, especially on climate challenges.

title: Healthy Meals for 130 Children - South Africa
description: This project aims to provide a nutritious meal daily for 130 children from the rural impoverished communities along the Greater Kruger national park. These children aged from 6 months to 13 years come daily to the Nourish eco village for a warm meal. For many children this forms one of their main meals in the day. This feeding scheme project  has the goal of feeding 130 children a warm meal daily;  ensuring health, and development in children through nutrition. We need $44 per child monthly.

title: Big reads for 1,200 children in Mexico in 2021
description: Children want to read! But they don't always have access to books and non-textbook reading is not always included in the curriculum in the public education system in central Mexico. Can you imagine your childhood without the magic of books? Libros para Todos has many activities to promote reading including Big Read campaigns, summer courses, workshops for teachers and special events.  Our staff is busy year round to keep children reading and we need your help!

title: Computers for Refugee Children
description: Koung Jor Shan Refugee Camp was founded on the Thai-Myanmar border in 2002, when the people fled from fighting between the Burmese military troops and the Shan State Army. There are 303 people living in the camp, 117 are children. The computer classes are very popular and vital to the children's education, teacher's preparation for classes and to connect the community to the outside world. This project aims to replace their broken computers and connect more computers to the internet!

title: Provide STEM @ Home kits for underserved girls
description: This project will help Afro-Tech Girls provide STEM @ Home Kits for 200 underprivileged girls in Lagos.  The STEM @ Home Kit is a simple yet engaging way to encourage STEM enthusiasm and make learning more accessible to every girl regardless of background especially with the recent adaptation to remote learning.   The kit contains two experiments (how to make your own lip balm and build a robotic prosthetic arm), materials required, a brief on the STEM principles learned and a step-by-step guide

title: Gift a Water Well & Empower Street Families -Kenya
description: This project will build a water well at our Rescue Centre for street women, babies and children.  Having a water well will enable them to be self sustainable by selling the water to the rural community.

title: Ladue Horton Watkins Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Marissa from Ladue Horton Watkins High School have been working with LI to help create & publicize human rights campaigns for various rights issues in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to connect with local nonprofits in Bauchi to research, document, and advocate for various human rights issues within the area.

title: Child Rescue Fund
description: The project provides support to chronically ill children who suffer even more than others and have to  live in "critical" condition so they are able to live as normal or closest to normal.  The three critical incidents are:  1. Children with disability and chronically ill that require urgent and continuous treatments  2. Children who live with ill parents or with dependent elderly  3. Orphans who are needy and vulnerable. The supports are: 1. Medication 2. Home building 3. Food& Others.

title: Helping Single Thai Mothers Keep Their Babies
description: Home of the Swallow serves disadvantaged women in Thailand who experience unplanned pregnancies and are facing cultural, financial, or familial pressure to abort or reject their babies. Using a holistic approach, Home of the Swallow provides opportunities for education, counseling, life and job skill training, parenting classes, and emotional support within a safe and encouraging environment. We hope to empower the women to become independent, loving mothers to their children.

title: Support with Housing of Students Affected by War
description: The Second Artsakh War started a new wave of displaced people from Artsakh. Many school-aged children were left without homes and access to education. From the first days of the war, we hosted an Artsakh family and began fundraising for the project. Thanks to the donations of several organizations and individuals, it became possible to renovate 3 private rooms, a shared kitchen, and a washing room. At the moment two more dormitories need to be renovated in order to host 8 more people for a year.

title: Sponsor Runners to Help Orphans in Japan 2020
description: Join us virtually this Boxing Day to raise awareness and funds for children living in orphanages in Japan. COVID 19 has raised the awareness of our health and fitness at the same time has limited our ability to connect face to face. This year FocusCore Group has organized a virtual marathon day where we can all be connected, get fit and give back.  Join us December 26,2020.

title: KIWL 2020 Go-Go Run
description: The 2020 Knights in White Lycra Go-Go Run is working in tandem with YouMeWe NPO to provide funding for Tokyo area children's homes. Throughout November, run or jog a minimum distance of 55km (55 means "go go" in Japanese). Measure your distance using a GPS watch or a GPS activity tracker app on your smartphone and upload to KIWL's club for the event.

title: Support Children in Albania post COVID-19
description: From the needs assessment for the COVID-19 situation conducted by Save the Children Albania, the data show that 70% of respondents stated that they do not have the financial means to provide protective equipment and hygiene to protect themselves from COVID-19. The project will provide support with hygienic packages for families and especially for children.

title: Ayni Relief Fund for Indigenous Peoples of Peru
description: Peru has been decimated by Covid-19. This project will help the indigenous community of Chincero recover in several ways. Over 80% of their economy  has come from traditional textile weaving, but markets have disappeared due to the pandemic. Tourism-dependent families are starving, elders and children are at risk. The Ayni project revives traditional agricultural methods to provide food, help bring technology to children for education and protect the elders and traditional teaching and wisdom.

title: Musical School: Estrellas de Birongo
description: Become a change-maker and help Birongo's children to rescue their cultural education! This project seeks to build a Musical School which will be co-designed with members of the Birongo community in order to promote, cultivate and preserve musical and cultural heritage to present and future generations. Birongo is an Afro-Caribbean community located in the north of Venezuela, with great challenges such as violence, teenage pregnancy, drugs, and self-demotivation. Let's change that reality!

title: Natural horsemanship for Moldova's village horses
description: This project will train at least 10 local natural horsemanship practitioners as multipliers to improve the life of 100 horses from Moldovan villages and their owners over the course of the next 2 years. We plan to create a natural horsemanship program that will be kind to the horses and will be effective for the horse owners, in order to save the village horses from being used, beaten and sent to the slaughterhouses into extinction in the next decade or so.

title: 500 pink bikes to bring Cambodian girls to school
description: With the "Pink bicycle project" Helpcode plan to buy 500 Bicycles to support Cambodian girls from the poorest communities in the South of Cambodia get to school and begin peddling their way out of poverty to an education and a better life!

title: Evacuating Orphans & Families, Bringing Aid
description: Kidsave's evacuated 30,000+ orphans and others from Ukrainian war zones and has brought 1,000 tons of humanitarian aid to Ukrainians caught in the war. Current needs are immense, with daily trips in, but we are also preparing for a time of healing. We are the building a retreat in western Ukraine to bring war trauma training and therapy to Ukrainian kids and families, lodging, skills-building for young adults, a summer camp and other services plus space and time for connection and healing.

title: Planting 1.8 Million Trees in Kosovo
description: Planting a 1.8 Trees is a major forest restoration campaign with a goal of mobilising everyone to plant a million trees throughout Kosovo.  Trees provide so many benefits to our everyday lives. They filter clean air, provide fresh drinking water, help curb climate change, and create homes for thousands of species of plants and animals. Planting a Million Trees can help save the Kosovo environment  from deforestation.  It's a big number, but we know we can do it with help of donations

title: Stop forest fires to save jungles in Konkan,India.
description: The Konkan region in the western ghats of India is losing its biodiversity due to Forest fires. the lack of awareness and management is making the situation worst. This project will aware people and train them to prevent forest fires. we are planning leaflet distribution, awareness board, community meetings, and workshops for 164 villages to create awareness.

title: Creating Change in Zanzibar
description: Like everywhere, 2020/2021 has been very challenging in Zanzibar. However, it's because of the generosity of our donors that we have been able to quickly adjust our plans and continue supporting our communities and local teams through expanding our activities and setting up COVID-19 relief projects. This fund will allow our education, health and conservation programs in Zanzibar to restart when health recommendations, government regulations, and community situations allow us to do us.

title: Creating Change in Moshi, Tanzania
description: Like everywhere, 2020/2021 has been very challenging in Moshi, Tanzania. However, it's because of the generosity of our donors that we have been able to quickly adjust our plans and continue supporting our communities and local teams through expanding our activities and setting up COVID-19 relief projects. This fund will allow our gender equality, health and empowerment programs in Moshi to restart when health recommendations, government regulations, and community situations allow us to do us.

title: Creating Change in St.Lucia, South Africa
description: Like everywhere, 2020/2021 has been very challenging in St.Lucia, South Africa. It's because of the generosity of our donors that we have been able to quickly adjust our plans and continue supporting our communities and local teams through expanding our activities and setting up COVID-19 relief projects. This fund will allow our education, healthcare and empowerment programs in St.Lucia to restart when health recommendations, government regulations, and community situations allow us to do us.

title: Creating Change in Cape Town
description: Like everywhere, 2020/2021 has been very challenging in Cape Town. It's because of the generosity of our donors that we have been able to quickly adjust our plans and continue supporting our communities and local teams through expanding our activities and setting up COVID-19 relief projects. This fund will allow our education, gender equality and empowerment programs in Cape Town to restart when health recommendations, government regulations, and community situations allow us to do us.

title: BRAC Global COVID-19 Response
description: The COVID-19 pandemic poses unprecedented challenges globally. In addition to widespread loss of life, the virus is overwhelming health systems, eroding livelihoods, and devastating economies. These impacts disproportionately affect people living in poverty. BRAC has leveraged our network of 50,000 frontline staff and volunteers by sharing public health information, providing emergency supplies like food and water, assembling handwashing stations in public spaces, and distributing cash support.

title: Godmother and Godfather for a Day
description: Through this project, we seek to ensure that children and adolescents in vulnerable situations remain in the Ecuadorian educational system with the equipment and supplies necessary for successfull learning. The Foundation provides material support and individual assistance to ensure an adequate education throughout the school year. We are asking for your financial support to provide technology, schooluniforms and internet access.    Help us to guarantee this RIGHT, together we can do it!

title: Trauma Care Centre for Stray Animals and Birds
description: Through this project, we provide treatment and rehabilitation to all diseased and distressed animals & birds. We have two separate, fully equipped, multi-specialty treatment units for them under the same roof, and every month we treat over 3000-4000 animals & birds with the help of our facility. Apart from the treatment, we conduct various awareness programs for local communities and students to improve animal welfare and conservation in our society.

title: Save 500 Suffering Animals in India
description: Known as the SHELTER WITH HEART. Our Cows run free and are happy cared for by a devoted Staff of 25 plus 3 full time persons. They're not just in captivity. They have a life. OUR BELIEF IS THAT DEEP HEALING ONLY TAKES PLACE IF A CREATURE FEELS SAFE, CARED FOR,AND LOVED. We use traditional and alternative medicine AND LOVE to lift suffering from over 500 homeless cows,and tens of thousands of others. 1ST-TIME PEOPLE SOMETIMES GET TEARY. THEY DIDN'T KNOW A PLACE SUCH AS OURS EXISTED.

title: Support us reach 250 girls at risk of FGM in Kuria
description: Msichana Empowerment Kuria will reach 250 girls at risk of being subjected to Female Genital Mutilation(FGM) in Kuria East & West, south western rural,Kenya in October,November &December. FGM is a harmful cut of the girls genitalia which has immediate & lifelong health complications.We need support deliver basic essentials to girls rescued from FGM in our safe shelter this number increases daily & transport to reach the most vulnerable girls.

title: Fair Haven Rape Crisis Center General Support
description: Fair Haven RCC is the only Stand-Alone Rape Crisis Center in Indiana & provides survivors of sexual violence with a 24/hour crisis response line.  Our Direct Service Advocates respond to all 10 emergency rooms within our community.  Advocates are: professionally trained, the continuum of care and can help navigate the complex waters of the medical & judicial system FREE of charge! You are not alone!  This was not your fault!  We believe you!

title: Fair Haven Anti-Trafficking Program
description: Human trafficking ranks as the fastest growing & second largest criminal enterprise in the world and generates approximately $150.2 billion worldwide. Fair Haven Rape Crisis Center has recently received a Federal Grant to help build advocacy and direct support services to survivors of Human Trafficking in Northwest Indiana, but we need your help!

title: Second home for 144 pupils- Witajcie w domu
description: The project ensures support for 144 pupils of Polish descent from the east (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Georgia, Moldova, Armenia, Belarus, Russia, Ukraine) in the Dormitory. Children come from poor families, who can not afford to fully pay the costs of them living and studying in a Polish high school.  Pupils live in the School's Dormitory for 10 months a year. The Foundation collects funds to provide them with food, care (both pedagogical and psychological) as well as cleaning/hygenic products.

title: A home of peace and beauty for Bethlehem
description: After Covid 19 lockdowns, Bethlehem is even poorer than before. Most of the people of Bethlehem lived on tourism but the town is still empty. Many are unoccupied and live under poverty line. Help us build and start our activities in the Dar Al Majus Community home: a multifunctional center for vocational training, educational and health support and cultural activities for both the people of Bethlehem and tourists.

title: National Pet Food Bank Program
description: Humane Canada will establish an effective, efficient and sustainable model for a cross-Canada pet food bank program providing short term aid to companion animal guardians experiencing financial hardship. This program will help vulnerable companion animals to stay with their families during the deepening financial crisis.

title: Comprehensive Child Eye Health Network in Ningxia
description: This project will establish a multi-phase, comprehensive child eye health network in Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region and a training center in Shanghai. Within Shanghai municipality, the project will scale up SEDPTC's successful myopia prevention efforts, and in Ningxia will build on SEDPTC's models of myopia treatment/prevention and care of children's eye disease.

title: Help Migrant Teachers Teach Out-of-School Children
description: There are over 700 migrant teachers currently serving in more than 70 Migrant Learning Centers (MLCs) in Thailand. The migrant teachers work with inadequate resources, have fewer training opportunities, and are underpaid for the valuable work they do to ensure that migrant children are not left uneducated. In response to the urgent needs of these at-risk migrant teachers, BEAM is raising funds for the remuneration, capacity building, safety, and security of 20 migrant teachers for one year.

title: Keep 100 students affected by Covid-19 in school.
description: This project will support 100 school going children who have been forced to drop out of school because their parents or guardians have lost their  sources of income due to Covid-19 . The project will provide school fees, school uniform, books and free meals to help them stay in school.

title: Improving living conditions for Russian elderlies
description: "Enjoyable Aging" is a charitable organization that helps the disabled and the elderly living both in nursing homes and alone. We aim to solve the problems of individuals as well as more universal issues in nursing homes located in different regions of Russia. We help more than 300 nursing homes as well as support people with disabilities at their private homes.

title: Support LULAC's work to provide a fair shot
description: Launching during Hispanic Heritage Month, 'A Fair Shot' will kick off in 2020 with a mobile response unit that will aid immigrant communities in Los Angeles, Houston and Chicago. The mobile response unit, an Airstream trailer staffed and supported by WAAH and LULAC volunteers, will provide essentials, including personal care items and household supplies, supporting the citizenship journey.

title: J.M. Wright Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Abnerline, Luckerlyne, Leilah, Mayechele, Emmanuelle, Breana, and Habigaelle from J.M. Wright Technical High School have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Decatur Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Natalie, Karah, Molly, and Ivie from Decatur High School have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Regenerating 100-Hectare Forest in Mt. Fuji
description: This project aims to regenerate the 100 hectares shirabe forest at the foot of Mt. Fuji in Yamanashi Prefecture, which was damaged by insects. Since 2007, in collaboration with the government, forest experts, companies/organizations, and forest workers OISCA initiated the planting of 40,000 pest-resistant broad-leaf seedlings of different species. This action is crucial to the conservation and protection of Mt. Fuji as a World Heritage site.

title: Help Bangladeshi Flood Victims During the Pandemic
description: Bangladesh is facing its worst floods in a decade, and coupled with the COVID-19 pandemic and Cyclone Amphan - the strongest in 30 years, they are devastating the remote, northern river islands of the country. Friendship NGO's comprehensive disaster preparedness and management interventions are fighting to preserve the lives, livelihoods and lifestyles of those affected, stemming from years of experience in the field doing the same. However, support is needed, given the enormity of the task.

title: Reconciliation of Refugees Returning from Exile.
description: The 2020 post election period in Burundi opened an opportunity for those who fled the country in 2015 crisis to return to Burundi. Two convoys from Mahama Refugee's Camp in Rwanda returned back to Burundi on September 7, 2020. Those coming from Tanzania never ceased to return back during the election period. Those living in RD Congo claimed to come back to.  Through workshops and dialogues, this project will bring reconciliation between returnees and those who stayed in their home communities.

title: Self Help Recovery Groups
description: IBC wants to enable weekly self help groups in Africa in order to reach people who are at risk of drinking and support people to deal with their addiction. In most African locations there is no residential treatment available but IBC model reaches vulnerable people and enables them to take significant steps towards recovery and healthy life. We use 12-step model that is based on Finnish Blue Ribbon's Compass framework. We would warmly welcome your support for this very cost effective work!

title: Community COVID Housing Program- 5,000 Home
description: The Community COVID Housing Program (CCHP) is a transformative plan that will rebuild the lives of 5,000 people over the next 2 years. The CCHP will focus on multiple strategies including  Housing, Diversion and Mental Health Case Management. This program will permanently house people who are currently experiencing literal homelessness (e.g., living in shelters, encampments or on the streets) as well as those who may fall into homelessness as a result of the economic effects of the coronavirus.

title: Partnering to Deliver Palliative Care in Nepal
description: A cancer disease diagnosis in Nepal is really no different than anywhere else; but the ability control cancer differs in Nepal due to less developed and accessible health care services.  Two Worlds Cancer Collaboration is building capacity for palliative, end-of-life and curative interventions. We collaborate with health professionals to support patients dying of cancer by sharing knowledge through teaching, advocacy for pain management, hospice care and care at home in rural villages.

title: ICT skills for youth with disabilities in Nigeria
description: Imagine a world without information and communication technology (ICT).Persons with disabilities (PWDs) are often excluded in the use of ICT devices. This program will equip persons with visual, hearing, physical disabilities, and albinism with skills and opportunities in ICT. The goal is to equip 100 PWDs with relevant and practical technology skills required to compete in the 21st century and connect them with decent job opportunities and entrepreneurship.

title: Sustain Palliative & Hospice Care in Lebanon
description: The devastating blast in the port of Beirut on August 4 and its economic repercussion on the national level has driven us to rearrange our priorities, bringing our sustainability at the forefront of all our concerns. This project will help SANAD to sustain its provision of comprehensive free of charge home-based hospice care to advanced chronically and terminally ill patients and their families in Lebanon, while preserving their dignity and enhancing the quality of their remaining life.

title: Help us to Save A Dad
description: Nearly 12,000 men die from prostate cancer every year in the UK.  And over 47,000 men are diagnosed with it.  Tackle Prostate Cancer acts as the patient voice for just under 100 prostate cancer support groups across the country and this project will allow us to support those groups with grants to carry out PSA tests in the community to help with early diagnosis. We want to #SaveaDad.

title: Build classrooms for 200 students in rural Togo
description: This project will build three basic classrooms in improved "apatam" style in the village of Dafolenyame in southern Togo. The classrooms will also be equipped with locally manufactured school benches to enable 200 primary school students to learn in a safe and adequate environment. Finally, face masks and hand washing systems will be provided in the classrooms to protect the students from COVID-19 infections.

title: Quality education for 5,000 poor children
description: The TEACH Cote d'Ivoire Program aims to train 180 transformational teacher teachers in five years to impact the lives of 20,000 children from poor and disadvantaged backgrounds in Cote d'Ivoire, giving them the opportunity to have access to quality education. Focusing on leadership, Teach Cote d'Ivoire project aims to help end the inequalities and inequities in the Ivorian educational system so that all children, irrespective of their socio-economic background, can access to quality education

title: Virtual Camps - Empowering Girls Around the World
description: This project will fund a series of virtual camps for girls led by diverse women leaders in artificial intelligence (AI), entrepreneurship, environmental science, and financial literacy. These inspirational camps feature industry-leading role models and are offered free of charge to girls of all backgrounds. Career Girls believes girls and young women have the right to dream. Your donation gives girls education and resources to make their dreams come true.

title: 160 Sessions of Free Mental Health Support
description: This project will provide free mental health support for marginalized and vulnerable individuals from throughout Europe whose human rights have been violated. Victims of domestic violence, war traumatized individuals, and children from families with low income, suffering from mental health issues and disorders, are provided with counseling, psychotherapy or psychological and psycho-social support free of charge.

title: Give Life skill  to women on livelihoods in semuto
description: SAI operates in different parts of Uganda (semuto) through fellowship and skills training to young women/ single mothers and the youth from underprivileged villages . We encourage and support women and their families who have been affected by domestic violence and neglect. We teach women to generate income through skills and provision of training materials. Our objective  is to build a vocational centre for women for purposes of mentoring  ,skills training and empower them in their livelihoods .

title: ADDUCTION D'EAU POTABLE ET SALUBRE DANS LE KWANGO
description: This project aims to develop sources of drinking water for the target populations of 5 villages in the Province of Kwango in order to - prevent water-borne diseases, - reduce infant mortality linked to the consumption of improper water and - contribute the reduction of women's jobs. CHALLENGE: reduce the water-borne mortality rate by 50% after 2 years of intervention SOLUTION: ensure sustainable access to safe and potable water IMPACT: sustainable development

title: Social.Eyes - Social Space
description: This project will create a Social Space to provide educational opportunities such as the English Language, Arts and Crafts, and use non-formal education to improve the skills of children. The space is open to all children, especially the ones who come from vulnerable families. The project will supply stationary, cover rent and utilities for the implementation of the project.

title: School completion & securing agric-land in Uganda
description: Since we have reached our goal to finish classrooms, now great people as we are on the way to become a standalone organization, join us to contribute towards the securing of the an agricultural land for the school.

title: Storm Alex: help reconstruct northern Italy
description: Following last week's floods that have struck the region, the Foundation is committed to help reconstruct the areas that have been severely damaged by the waters. Specchio dei tempi has already done some first site inspections to understand the type of intervention that is needed. We have identifies a series of areas such as the Formation Center and kindergarten of Ceva, the bridge of Tanaro, the park of Ormea, the central roman road of Limone and help the businesses of Garessio.

title: Synapse Research Project #48571
description: Children with lifelong neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism and cerebral palsy will soon benefit from ground-breaking studies carried out closer to home after East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust launched an innovative new research centre.   The Synapse Centre for Neurodevelopment brings together paediatricians, speech and language specialists, clinical psychologists, physiotherapists and researchers to translate biomedical research into practical therapies.

title: Winter Relief Appeal in Lebanon
description: As in every year, URDA has launched its winter relief campaign as the winter season approaches. The "Winter Wish" campaign for 2020/2021, will be targeting the underserved in Lebanon of all nationalities in various Lebanese regions, to make their wishes come true and provide them with warmth by providing necessities, the most important of which are: food parcels, blankets, mattresses, heating fuel, winter clothes, and tent tarpaulins which refugees depend on to protect their tents from water.

title: To maintain the clinics in good function
description: The project is to maintain the operations and function of the clinics for those who don't have access to healthcare and live in an extreme poverty. We aim to maintain our clinics active to prevent diseases and promote health and safety, to improve health of local population and abroad. Through partnership, our centers tend to influence changes of people behavior, provide the necessary services, and save their lives.  Our goal is to provide medical services to the underprivileged.

title: Support Internally Displaced Persons in Cameroon
description: Four years into the Anglophone Crisis coupled with the COVID-19 pandemic, hundreds have been recorded dead, over a thousand homes burned and over 900,000 people have fled their homes. This has led to a fragmented health care system, primary school education, suboptimal water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) Food insecurity and high rate of malnutrition. CAMAAY is working with several local communities affected by the crisis to ensure that Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) are supported.

title: Foreign Medications for Children with Cancer
description: Children with cancer need foreign medicines; otherwise, the treatment of certain children will be incomplete and compromised.  Owing to selfless and compassionate philanthropists the Tabletochki Charity Foundation supplies medicines (chemotherapy, target therapy, immunotherapy, and supportive therapy), which are unavailable in Ukraine and are to be purchased and brought from abroad. With these medicines, children are endowed with a priceless gift - a chance to conquer the disease.

title: Build 5 homes for 26 vulnerable children in Rwanda
description: Shelter Them Batarure provides homes to vulnerable and underprivileged children in Rwanda, by making sure that they are integrated in an environment where their basic growth and development needs are met. We also give their families the tools and resources they need for these children to have a bright, independent and sustainable future. Your donation goes towards building homes next to an Early Childhood Development Center where kids under age 6 receive a fair start to a quality education.

title: Fires out of control in Argentina
description: There is a new fire outbreak along the Parana river, in Argentina, mainly in the Province of Santa Fe. The fire has already consumed more than 200 thousand hectares and approximately three new sources of fire are registered in the area daily. Our national fire brigade is intensely working on fire containment with minimal resources to intervene in this critical situation.

title: Building Brighter Futures For Children in Niger
description: Closing the education gap closes the opportunity gap - opening up paths to brighter futures in Niger. This project funds construction at the Agadez Learning Center for Rural and Nomadic students in Niger, including:  - a girls dormitory (sleeping and living space for 25 girls and constructed to allow for second story expansion) - 4 girls bathrooms & showers - reinforcement for the boys dorm to allow for 2nd story expansion - storehouse for dry food goods. Give today to help make a difference.

title: Help us end education inequity in Latinamerica!
description: Millions of children and young people in Latin America need, today more than ever,  an education that allows them to reach their full potential.  Join Ensena por Mexico and the 10 countries of the Teach For All Network in Latin America.

title: Reducing Maternal Mortality in The Gambia
description: This project aims to reduce 1000 Gambian women from dying during child labor annually. Many women experience severe complications or even faced death as they give birth from lack of prenatal care, severe bleeding, infections because they don't access to proper health care. We plan to provide training for community skilled birth attendants as midwives and nurses, medical supplies and nutritions program for pregnant women at health facilities in rural and urban areas.

title: Safe Drinking Water for Children in Cambodia
description: This project will provide clean, safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene education to up to 1,800 children and community members in rural Siem Reap Province, Cambodia, helping to alleviate waterborne disease, illness, and death caused by drinking contaminated water. The beneficiary school will receive an AquaTower, delivering clean, safe drinking water and handwashing facilities to students, and an AquaSan, providing capability to sanitize the school to WHO standards.

title: Kids in the Middle - HS STEM Mentor-Coach Program
description: Through our "Kids in the Middle" High School STEM pilot program focused on building up Gen Alpha, through mentoring and coaching, we connect with partners and supporters to assist young people from under-resourced families and communities, who have an interest in pursuing careers in Science, Technology, Engineering and Math. The goal is to remove barriers to a successful future and have these kids live more balanced, fulfilling, and purpose-driven lives.

title: Support children with cancer around the world
description: Over 400,000 children worldwide develop cancer each year. If the disease is detected early enough, many of these children can be cured -  80% of children with cancer in the high income world survive. However, in low and middle income countries, survival rates can be as low as 10%, with many children dying without effective pain relief.  A reason for this inequality is that many children remain undiagnosed, or are diagnosed too late to be cured, due to a shortage of trained doctors and nurses in-

title: Sponsor A Girl's Education in Rural Morocco
description: Education For All Morocco ensures girls in the High Atlas region of Morocco can access secondary school by building and running safe, superbly staffed, well-equipped boarding houses. We have 6 boarding houses accommodating over 200 girls. It costs $3 a day to give a girl 3 nutritious meals, a cosy bed, access to books and computers and a 'family-feeling' community of dedicated staff and friends for ongoing support and encouragement. This project will sponsor 50 girls in our new house!

title: Child Development Centre for 180 Children Uganda
description: Miroi Child Restoration Centre aims to education, provide care & support to 180 orphans, sickle cell, HIV/AID infected and affected children education, health, shelter. The Centre will have 5 Care Takers, 6 Teachers. Abandoned Orphans getting food, education, uniforms, clothes. Children are to access to sports & games, computer skills training at the CDCwill host both pre-primary and primary section. By donating online to SCOEN build the future of the needy children

title: Provide healthcare to 20,000 people in India
description: People living in India's informal housing settlements (commonly known as slums) do not have access to primary or preventive healthcare. Women have no prenatal care, children go without pediatric care, and most families are unable to seek treatment for preventable diseases like tuberculosis. We currently operate 3 clinics in Jaipur, India, with plans to open another. This project will fund our 3 clinics for a year, providing care to more than 20,000 people.

title: Wise Climate Change Action Using Impact Assessment
description: Greater involvement of impact assessment (IA) specialists is vital to making smart global COVID-19 recovery and climate change choices. They have the expertise to provide oversight for the worldwide infrastructure transition to achieve a net zero carbon target in 30 years. Through this project, IA specialists will provide expertise to banks, insurance firms, attorney organizations, journalists, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Arctic Council.

title: Family Literacy Initiative (FLI) in Liberia
description: FLI is a cooperative effort between the FOL, the WE-CARE Foundation, and HIPPY-International, with the goal of teaching parents of preschool children in under privileged communities how to engage in nurturing and learning activities that prepare their children for school. The goal is to prepare 3, 4 and 5-year old children for long-term academic success and help parents become more effective at working with their children. WE-CARE Foundation delivers the program in four Liberian communities.

title: Supporting  Children & Migrants in Sierra Leone
description: Ibrahim Bangora has been helping impoverished,  vulnerable children in Makeni, Sierra Leone for the past 10 years.  He has managed to provide them with food, schooling, and clothing.  He has also been instrumental in repatriating local women who have been trafficked abroad.  AAI recently rented a house to serve as an office and emergency shelter and started a sponsorship program to provide schooling for some of the children. More help is greatly needed for these deserving women and children!

title: Early Breast Cancer Detection For Salvadoran Women
description: Being El Salvador is the smallest country of Central America; Its population is very dense. A total of  6,220,397 people,  3,268,766 of these are women; mainly single mothers  -The percentage of breast cancer patients has increased amongst younger women in recent years. It is the second cause of death in women nationwide. -Salvadoran women are especially vulnerable regarding breast cancer. Women do not have access to breast examination in the public health sector.

title: Safeguarding Indigenous Seeds in Southwest Morocco
description: This project will gather, grow, reproduce, store & distribute indigenous Amazigh Anti-Atlas variety of barely, millet and wheat seeds increasingly under threat of disappearing. These graints have grown over mellenia and are entirely adapted to the dry mountain ecosystem. Providing some 40 local farmers who practise livelihood farming with these varieties will decrease their expenses, their dependency on external sources and provide them and families with bread, major food staple in the region.

title: Adjumani Palliative Care Fund
description: This project seeks to improve the quality of life of 56 refugee and host community patients with terminal illnesses especially cancer, and sickle cell patients currently in active care in Adjumani. The project will provide the targeted patients with mobility aids (wheel chairs, tricycle, crutches), cater for specialized investigation fees (CT scan) and transport to Mulago Cancer Institute for ongoing management.

title: PLANT 100 FRUIT TREES IN EACH SCHOOL
description: The project will serve many undernourished children from poor homes who leave during school and lunch hours to the bush to search for fruits to eat, thereby missing classes and exposing them to hazards.We are Planting 100  trees in each of the 24 public primary and secondary schools in FCT to make fruits available and protect school communities from heatwave, wind and soil erosion. It will provide basic skills to students to mitigate climate change and land degradation while increasing awareness

title: Help Rebuild Lives of 500 Flood Affectees in Sindh
description: Recent rains have completely destroyed livelihoods of many individuals in Sujawal, which is one of the poorest districts of Sindh. Medical facilities are rare, hunger is on the rise, and even clean drinking water seems like a distant dream now. Persons with disabilities remain the worst hit by this calamity.  Help NOWPDP build our relief center in Sujawal to provide 1) food, 2) clean drinking water, 3) primary healthcare, and 4) skills for 500 persons with disabilities.

title: Sponsor a child living in poverty in India.
description: Sponsorship enables the poorest children to take part in all aspects of the OSCAR football, education & life skills programmes. Participation creates the foundation for change, for the individual, their family, community & future generations. OSCAR children live very challenging lives, which makes them vulnerable to negative external influences. Child sponsorship plays a vital part in ensuring no OSCAR children slip through the net. This project is at the heart of OSCAR's work & you can help.

title: Saving hundreds of street children in Tanzania
description: Kivuko is a Swahili word for "ferry" or "passage". Our Kivuko project is a journey; we help children travel from a dangerous street life to a destination of safety and security, where they can fulfil their incredible potential. Our projects range from the simple and urgent, such as immediate medical care and counselling for street children, to family reintegration, business training for teenagers and parenting programmes for families.

title: Hurricane Delta Relief Fund
description: This disaster relief fund will support people impacted by Hurricane Delta in the form of emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. The fund will transition to provide longer-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support communities and first responders impacted by Hurricane Delta.

title: Hurricane Delta help sustain 100's of families
description: Hurricane Laura was only the beginning of a series of emergencies in this region. Late last evening (OCT 09) Hurricane Delta came into Louisiana and destroyed weeks worth of progress in rebuilding.  All around, agencies that provide relief are stretched thin this year. We need you, our friends, community organizations and individuals with kind hearts to team up with us on this endeavor. We can help Louisiana rebuild together over the next year, just as we did in Florida after Hurricane Michael.

title: Educate 20 Teenage Girls in Cameroon for 1 Year
description: NDEF seek to provide accommodation, school fees and study materials for 20 girls who have forced to drop out of schools due to the loss of their parents and/or have been displaced and are currently living in dire conditions due to the ongoing anglophone crisis in Cameroon. Educating a girl is educating a nation. We believe with the help of our donors, sky will be the limit for these girls whose life are going to turn around for the best and change the way they are being perceived in the society.

title: Girls' Day Shelter Maria de Nazareth, Nicaragua
description: The Girls' Day Shelter offers girls from extremely poor problem families a place to come during the day, before and after school. Girls can spend time at the shelter, receive meals, take showers, get help with their schoolwork and participate in creative activities. In critical situations, they may stay overnight. The girls' backgrounds may include alcohol, drugs, prostitution and sexual abuse. It was founded by two activist Nicaraguan women in 1999 and supported by Nicaragua Projekt since 2006.

title: 200 Women and children confront Covid-19
description: To empower vulnerable and disadvantaged women and children in remote villages to learn to protect and care for themselves as they face the COVID-19 pandemic, thereby increasing local self-reliance and sustainable food production.  It is 6 months  project actual starting date will depend on fundraising through GlobalGiving 6 months period. Total expected Number of Participants 200  Vulnerable women and Children. Requested budget $5,000.

title: Keep a girl in school all year for $12
description: This project will ensure consistent monthly supply of sanitary pads to 1000 refugee girls in their final year of primary schooling. Each girl will receive one pack of pads monthly over 12 months period which will help these girls complete and sit for their final primary leaving exams. In 2018, more than 200 refugee girls at Adjumani could not sit for their primary leaving examinations due to lack of sanitary pads and poor performance among girls was attributed to absenteeism during menstruation.

title: Provide 26,965 people in Uganda with healthcare
description: Katulikire Health Center (KHC) serves internally displaced persons from the Lord's Resistance Army rebellion (LRA) in Northern Uganda and refugees from East Africa. Almost 30,000 people have remained in the area. KHC provides their primary care including curative and preventive services, but sicker patients are referred to further away centers, which are often cost-prohibitive. We will upgrade to a HC 4 to provide in/outpatient services to ensure we can treat the poorest, sickest patients.

title: Get our children to school; Help us buy a bus
description: Warm Heart exists to provide loving homes to at-risk children from remote villages who need a safe haven and access to school.  A few years ago, we lost government school bus funding and had to quickly convert a small truck to use for transporting the kids. Our school bus recently died. We need a larger, safer bus to carry our children to school and provide access for community elders and disabled of all ages to doctors' appointments and events.

title: ADOPT A FAMILY FOOD DRIVE
description: The Covid19 pandemic led to many people in the local slums we work in loosing their jobs. Most are casual workers paid daily, and employers were afraid of the risk of infection as they live in congested areas. This consequently led to the sick and elderly being abandoned. We thus decided to fundraise for food packages to assist them. This contain enough food to feed a family of about 5-8 person for a bout 2-3 weeks. We have a fortnightly distribution system, with a focus on the sick and elderly.

title: Mikono: Made by the Hands of Refugees in Nairobi
description: Mikono - The Refugee Craft Shop is an innovative model that promotes the economic inclusion of refugees in global value chains.  Firstly, JRS identifies refugees with artisanal skills. Secondly, it helps refugees create strong artisan groups. Thirdly, and most importantly it connects these groups with fair trade buyers around the world. Mikono is the Global Compact on Refugees brought to life.

title: YOU CAN! Empower Taiwan Youth for Social Impact
description: According to our statistics, the up to 90% of youths we serve encounter more difficulties in finance than normal families. Thus, the Mustard Seed Mission not only provides living expenses subsidies to these youths in need, but also provides a four-year training program to help young people understand themselves, improve their inner abilities, and then have the self-confidence to face the future more positively. The expected number of beneficiaries is 150.

title: Connecting Brazilian Slum Residents to Resources
description: At Favela Inc. we use technology to deliver responsibly and at scale, emergency resources and development opportunities to low-income communities, focused on high risk, socio-economically  vulnerable, low-income community residents in Brazil. We leverage the power of data to ensure resources are going directly into the hands of those who really need them, thus optimizing impact and giving more visibility to these underserved populations.

title: Help Survivors of Child Sex Trafficking Thrive
description: We believe every child deserves dignity and the right to be free. With therapeutic support and education, children who have been sold and sexually abused will thrive. Since 2013, we have been the only government licenced comprehensive rehabilitation program for survivors of child sex trafficking in Costa Rica. Our 24-36 month comprehensive residential program for survivors between the ages of 8 and 18, empowers them to heal and acquire skills to thrive.

title: The "18 by 18 Challenge"
description: 18 by 18 Challenge is sponsored by Nehemiah's Restoration and is designed to support our efforts to break the cycle of poverty in Western Kenya due to HIV/AIDS.  This challenge offers an opportunity to nominate a friend on social media to post a video doing something 18 times using #Beyond18Years, and then give at least $18 to the cause at Beyond18Years.org. Our goal is to help raise up orphaned children impacted by HIV/AIDS who require support in order to grow up to be self-sustaining adults.

title: Educate Over 45 Disadvantaged Children in Greece
description: Our project aims to support over 45 disadvantaged children and youths in Crete, Greece in receiving an education. Refugee children confront huge obstacles and challenges to receive the education and support they need to have a better future and find employment. COVID-19 is making it even harder. We provide in person and online practical assistance and lessons preparing children for a brighter future, work and better integration. We need your donation to insure urgent and impactful support!

title: Livelihood and education for  vulnerable children
description: This project aims at sustainably improving livelihood and education by for 120 OVCs aged 0 - 18 years especially girls and their households within a family setting with adult care givers. It will help OVCs especially girls and their households to carry out Income Generating Activities (IGAs) to deal with poverty, trauma, unemployment plus food insecurity and nutrition. The project will work with 40 out of school OVCs girls to help them start their own jobs like sewing services after training.

title: Help transform colombian children & their families
description: The project seeks to change the standard of living of 232 children and their 185 families who are part of the community of the Centro Social Unidad, located in a non-privileged neighborhood of Bogota. This will be done through continuous accompaniment, courses and workshops that provide psychosocial tools that lead to improving intra-family ties and, in turn, to decrease the dropout rate, which will be reflected in a better quality of life, making them protagonists of their own history.

title: Synapse: say no to illiteracy
description: This project will improve the performance in Portuguese and Math of the students that reach the 3rd grade in one of the poorest regions of Brazil (Vale do Jequitinhonha, Minas Gerais). It will work with approximately 16 schools, 500 students from 1st to 3rd grade, and 35 literacy teachers. It also will set up a local center to later disseminate this work in neighboring cities.

title: Renaissance Center Mathematics Academy
description: The Renaissance Center for Culture and Education is doing everything it can to make things easy for linguistically and culturally challenged immigrant families and their children to get up and running with distance learning. Through our purchase of computers and laptops from COMCAST Internet Essential low income program, we are working to bridge the digital divide of Washington DC area immigrant community access to the internet for school, work, and daily life.

title: Support education of girls in Minembwe, DR Congo
description: Recent armed conflicts in the Democratic Republic of Congo have caused massive displacements of the population, who often cannot provide education for their children in these circumstances. This project is dedicated to promoting the access to education for girls in the region of Minembwe in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This will be done through providing school materials, uniforms, and teaching materials.

title: help to construct hospital, care center and homes
description: During a single illness espisod sickness of older patients are often treated in multiple distinct sites including the emergancy room, ICU unit a general medical Floor and a skilled nursing facility.Such changes in pysician, in nursing care rewriting orders,and physical dislocation change and this can affect Outcomes  of the Treatment.Partial solution include a Team Approach to care,electronic medical records.GSF shall serve more than 100000 serve each year by offering Health and Food from 65 yrs

title: Food Pantry for Veterans Homeless
description: This project will build a Food Pantry in Bronx NY and at Militar Hospital in Santo Domingo - Dominican Republic, providing free healthy food to 1000 veterans per week, veterans homeless or at risk to become one - individuals or with families - affected with PTSD due to traumas by the war during their services and cannot have a normal life or a job due to this trauma.

title: Abortion Access for All
description: Every person has the right to determine their own sexuality, reproductive health, and future. That's why Ipas, as part of the broader reproductive justice movement, works to ensure that governments recognize abortion as an essential health service-and that all people have access. During the COVID-19 pandemic, your support helps us train abortion providers, ensure women have the information they need to access abortion, and educate young people on sexual and reproductive health and rights.

title: Music Lessons for Vulnerable Communities!
description: Musicians for the World provides free, virtual music education within the most vulnerable areas of the world. We partner with music programs in underserved communities, offering uplifting musical opportunities and providing the tools and support needed to grow. MFW is already offering masterclasses, private lessons, and music theory to over 300 students in Kenya, Belize, Haiti, Trinidad and Tobago, Suriname, Mexico, Peru, Uganda, Honduras, Guatemala, Philippines, Argentina, Uruguay, and Mexico.

title: A School to build Conscious Global Citizen
description: The School is aimed to address 3 challenges through education ( Academics, Life Skills & Culture) and work with the community to bring positive change through progressive learning in local rural communities.  The Primary school system will be based on human curriculum  designed to support the children from low income families receive an international standard learning experience from Pre-K to grade 5; and will create volunteer teaching opportunities for young people from all over the world.

title: Adequate nutrition for young children and mothers.
description: This project will help women to produce a protein-rich food supplement to offer to young children and mothers at the Mother and Child Health Clinics in Lesotho, in Southern Africa, so that children with adequate nutrition will survive past their fifth year, grow to their proper height and children and mothers will develop their immune systems to fight off disease.  Other youth and women will grow and sell organic vegetables in the community at a reasonable cost and improve their own livelihoods.

title: Change a Child's Life and Help Save Nature
description: SAVING OUR PLANET THROUGH EDUCATION  Children from disadvantaged communities never get to experience or learn about wildlife. Sometimes they live only a few kilometers from a game reserve! It is time to change that and get children in touch with the natural world and helping to preserve our home, Planet Earth. We are sending 300 children on a 3-day wildlife camp, to learn to love and protect nature. Help us get them there. There is no better feeling than helping a child.

title: Provide Rehabilitative Care in Haiti During COVID
description: STAND: The Haiti Project is initiating a COVID safe, year-round rehabilitation clinic in Port-de- Paix. The clinic serves adults and children in one of the lowest income communities in Haiti, providing physical therapy, prosthetics, wound care, primary medical care and health education. During COVID, the clinicians provide care to northwestern Haiti by conducting socially responsible home visits, providing community education, as well as ensuring people have access to safe rehabilitative care.

title: Support INVENTIVA, STEAM education to latina girls
description: On INVENTIVA we broadcast live educational videos on YouTube about knowledge in the STEAM areas in a creative and fun way. Its objective is to arrive in territories in Latin America where academics and schools in areas like science and technology are limited. It is a project created by Geek Girls LatAm, ValPat, and Academia de Inventores. Help us to connect more geek girls to learn about STEAM.

title: Healthy Kitchen for 6500 poor household in Banglad
description: In rural Bangladesh, over 90% of women use wood &traditional stoves for cooking, inhale smoke and subsequently damage their health& environment. Inefficient wood based cooking increase deforestation. 25500 families use 76500kg wood daily and 60% can be saved by the use of fuel-efficient stoves.The Project aims healthy Cooking to support25500 HH by providing efficient 5-star stove & setup a pellet mill using waste biomass. Families will be benefited in health and environment with job opportunity.

title: Support 450 People Living with Disabilities
description: This program is for the empowerment of the disabled in which all types of 450 Deprived people with disabilities will be provided better health, education, livelihood & also linked to social security and along with this they will also be provided the help of assistive devices and materials.

title: Solace Women's Aid
description: Solace Women's Aid exists to end the harm done through Violence against Women and Girls. Our aim is to work to prevent violence and abuse as well as providing services to meet the needs of survivors particularly women and girls. Our work is holistic and empowering, working alongside survivors to achieve independent lives free from abuse.

title: No More Trash Bags for 30,000 Kids in Foster Care
description: This project will provide new Comfort Cases and duffel bags, instead of trash bags, to more than 30,000 children entering foster care in 2023! When children are removed from their homes by police or social services, they are often given a trash bag to carry their belongings.   "I remember carrying a trash bag and feeling worthless, like nobody cared about me." - Comfort Cases founder, Rob Scheer.  Help us provide dignity and a Comfort XL duffel bag for children entering the foster care system.

title: VENEZUELA: EDUCATE-HEAL-FEED 400 KIDS MID COVID-19
description: We provide health care, education and balanced meals to 400 children in a poor slum in Caracas during the COVID-19 pandemic. The success of the Foundation started 23 years ago and is based on the life stories of more than 550 alumnus who have achieved differentiating goals through formal education. The true significance is that they emerge from marginalization and enter the productive society by accessing formal jobs.

title: EMPOWERING AT RISK  ENTREPRENEURS IN TANZANIA
description: Tanzania has estimated 13 million people living below the poverty line. The government efforts to expand access to social services like education have been undermined by their declining quality as the population grows. Tertiary education graduates have incapability of seeking opportunities due to prevalence of skills mismatch. We have developed the Kuwezesha Project to reduce the skills mismatch by providing opportunities for tertiary learners to innovate and run small entrepreneurial ventures.

title: Give a boy without arms basic human needs
description: Talandira aboy born without arms now an Orphan after his mother died due to COVID19 left him without nothing to eat, wear, need health attentions, his eyes ussually itches a problem from birth he need much food every morning you can imagine once given food and he talks.

title: Protect Endangered Species
description: Donations to this project support WWF's global efforts to protect endangered species, restore critical ecosystems, and identify nature-based solutions to help mitigate further habitat loss and the impacts of climate change.

title: Educate and Nourish 100 Dominican Children
description: The Abba's House Children's Center educational and feeding project will provide  educational materials, teaching, and meals for 100-150 children living in Cienfuegos, Dominican Republic who are traumatized by homelessness, abandonment, and/or extreme poverty. Items needed include children and teacher furniture, bulletin boards, computers, printers, books, white boards, art supplies, maps, rulers, calculators, and funds to provide two meals per day, five days per week, per child.

title: Send 210 Cambodian Youth Back to School
description: Public school is free--but not the notebooks, backpacks, or uniforms. When Cambodian youth go back to school in January after a 10-month break due to Covid-19, some students won't be going. They don't have the basic supplies they need to attend. With your support, we can send 210 youth back to public school with a full backpack! Mission Dove Cambodia has identified the most at-risk students in our 4 target communities to receive this support.

title: Education and National Registration Program
description: Education delivery in Zimbabwe's rural communities has all but disintegrated and experts warn that any gains made after independence are rapidly being reversed in the continuing economic meltdown. As basic commodities become more unaffordable by the day, rural parents, who mostly depend on farming, are also feeling the pinch: they can hardly afford the school fees for their children.

title: Access to Education for Talented African Students
description: The Ashinaga Africa Initiative (AAI) is an international leadership program that cultivates the next generation of leaders to contribute to the development of sub-Saharan Africa.  AAI Scholars come from disadvantaged backgrounds and are committed to returning to the Continent to initiate change, innovation, and development. The AAI provides financial support for international uni degrees, along with leadership training and guidance that Scholars need to become changemakers in their communities.

title: COVID19 Emergency Food Relief Distribution Namibia
description: This project aims to help over 500 families of the most vulnerable affected by the COVID19 pandemic in Namibias capital city Windhoek.  We will provide people who live in informal settlements with food packages (including corn flour, pasta, rice, canned beans, sugar, veggies). Wadadee Cares e.V. is a well established NGO and has previously conducted food relief package initiatives in and around Windhoek (Pictures attached).

title: Van for Shelter for Abused Women and Children
description: The van will be used to transport survivors of domestic violence to a safe space. It will also facilitate the safe movement of survivors from the shelter to the hospital, courts, police station, and to get supplies.

title: Enroll and keep girls in school in Ghana by 20%
description: Teenage pregnancy and school drop out rate has been on the ascendancy with Western Region scoring 78%,89% and 46% for primary,Junior High, and Senior High schools respectively. For  effective advocacy on the rights of the child and ending child marriage we would work to secure evidential information to help policy makers and duty bearers act in  favor of the marginalized and vulnerable  to increase educational and career opportunities to reduce poverty and better the lives of the citizenry.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Aishani, Ananya, and Sudiksha have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign and community workshop to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Rescue abandoned babies in Kenya
description: Diani Children's Village was formed in 1994 to help abandoned and abused children. With changes in the Socioeconomic environment, the focus has shifted to becoming a Rescue Center. The number of abandoned infants has increased, babies who often have not received the best neonatal care and are vulnerable from the moment they are born. That first year is crucial and our team of carers are dedicated to give the babies the best chance of survival and a solid start to a good life.

title: Making a difference through clean water
description: Water Survival Box is the initiative of the Rotary Club of Chelwood Bridge, England. Its purpose is to provide a rapid response to victims of natural or man-made disasters. The  Aquafilter is an essential item which protects against water-borne disease.  The box also contains a range of essential items including cooking pots, bowls/plates, mugs, and utensils; health and hygiene items; basic shelter & simple tools. The project is entirely volunteer led which keeps costs to a bare minimum.
