title: Help bring Christmas to isolated & excluded people
description: Normally at this time of year we would be holding 3 community Christmas lunches across the borough where everyone gets together, to dance, eat and greet each other. But this year everyone has to be apart.   It will be lonely this Christmas for elderly, vulnerable and disabled people who can't get out and especially for families who have no income.  We want to ensure everyone eats and sees someone else on Christmas day, so we're bringing the cheer right to their doors.

title: Longterm Accompaniment: Indigenous Entrepreneurs
description: Indigenous Guatemalan women face layers of oppression as women in a patriarchal society, a discriminated-against Indigenous minority in a colonized country, and as Indigenous people, they are three times more likely to be living in extreme poverty. Join us in implementing long-term accompaniment through micro-investing & providing jobs and job training, peer-to-peer counseling and health services, and the tools & guidance needed to gain the resilience and self-determination they need to thrive.

title: AID FOR REOPENING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ORPHANAGE
description: The project targets to enable the orphans to resume school amidst the covid-19 after the government announced school reopening  Guidelines and SOPs which are essential for every institution and  require immediate funding therefore our aim is to offer full free education to the orphans under our care which includes the finalist that will seat for their exams march early next year. we need to expand our classroom blocks , toilets and dormitories for social distancing, teachers quarters, sick bay.

title: Crack a Smile - Relief for Kids
description: The critical winter season in Pakistan starts from mid-December to mid-January every year. Populations below the poverty line; hit by cold and Covid-19 pandemic this winter will end up in critical situation.  Children of daily wagers will be prone to food scarcity and winter chills. To cater reality of approaching winter and food insecurity,  PMS will provide food ration packs and winter clothing for greater social well-being by sharing hope and solidarity with impoverished  children.

title: Support for children severely damaged by floods
description: Typhoons and floods in the central provinces of Vietnam in October 2020 have threatened the lives of more than 1.5 million children. This project will support 300 extremely difficult children in these provinces to stabilize their lives after the terrible flood through providing a package of essential items including books and school supplies, clothes, blankets, personal hygiene kits, and life jacket.

title: Give reliable fresh water to 2,500 Kenyan children
description: 2,500 children at eight schools in Embu County, Kenya, will benefit from water wells supplying reliable, fresh, clean water for drinking, washing, cleaning, and watering of crops. This will make a huge difference to their lives for less than ten pounds per child. It will end reliance on unreliable rainwater, enabling schools to grow crops to feed needy children. No longer hungry, and freed from time-wasting water collection, children will spend more time learning and thus make better progress.

title: Build Power: Community Paralegals in Puerto Rico
description: The Legal Empowerment Curriculum for Community Paralegals in Puerto Rico  will provide 15 community stakeholders  with tools to monitor, exercise and defend their right to housing, resist displacements, and promote legal efforts towards equitable development and climate justice. This program paves the way to socialize legal education and strategies, promote community paralegals in order to nurture grassroots power and continue the work towards just recovery in Puerto Rico

title: United Against Hunger in the Rio Grande Valley
description: COVID-19 is more than a viral pandemic in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas. It has created an economic crisis affecting a disproportionate percentage of our population. The Rio Grande Valley is one of the poorest places in the United States. The safety net isn't large enough or sturdy enough to support all of those who are suffering from food insecurity stemming from near record unemployment levels. We are distributing food--lots of food. And we're working together to do it better.

title: Sustain Tigrayan/Ethiopian refugees in the Sudan
description: The civil war in Ethiopia led to more than 61,000 Tigrayans to flee to the Sudan as refugees. Many are internally displaced. The people left their villages and towns in Tigray due to the war that started on Nov 4 2020.  Many refugees report they left their homes unplanned due to bombardment and attack on the life of their loved ones. Many families are separated and are stressed due to the traumatic experiences. There are children with no parents. The project plans to improve their resilience.

title: Help Indigenous Papua Women Access Safe Childbirth
description: Indigenous Papuan women have the worst maternal health outcomes in Indonesia. They live in rural areas, have epidemic levels of HIV and syphilis and often experience trauma and discrimination when they seek medical care. The Bumi Sehat clinic offers Indigenous-staffed and run maternal health services for women in the Sentani district of Papua. We promote a culturally sensitive approach to healthcare delivery and maternal health services for Indigenous women.

title: Wet Land Mangrove promotion and Conservation
description: Since ROSI Foundation's previous experience of Mangroves plantation, 1000000 mangroves are to be planted in Coastal of Bay Bengal in Tiruvarur, Thanjavure, Pudukkottai and Nagapattinam districts as 2nd phase in next 3 years. 200000 coastal community as fishermen, students and environmental groups will be motivated in plantation, caring and conservation of mangroves. These areas are stretched continuously by 110 KM with strong coastal community such fishermen, farmers, saltpan workers, etc.

title: RCRA Outreach Programs to Support Women & Children
description: This project will raise funds to support the maternal and child health work of RCRA. RCRA is the product of the people of the Rwenzori region's work to overcome the challenges of their mountainous environment and provide care for each other.

title: PROVIDE FOOD ITEM FOR 300 NIGERIA VULNERABLE WOMEN
description: This project will help in providing  food items for 300 vulnerable women who lives in the local community in FCT Abuja. This women and their families are helpless and have no food to eat in their homes. This will help to alleviate hunger and hardship Caused by COVID-19 PANDEMIC which has left fear of the unknown in the minds of these Vulnerable women and families. This project will bring them Hope, Joy and  Happiness knowing that Our Organization cares for them and brings food relief items.

title: Upgrading Compassion Orphanage in Zambia
description: Association for Zambians in Belgium, Pamodzi plans to upgrade a community based orphanage called Compassion Orphanage in Northern Zambia which provides care,  educational, welfare and emotional support for 40 orphans who hail from communities affected by High rates of HIV/AIDS related deaths.

title: Food & nutrition for the 3000 IDPs in Cameroon
description: The ongoing crisis in the two English speaking regions of Cameroon has generated more 500,000 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). Exacerbating the situation of poor families who barely feed on less $5/day. Some are trapped in forest and bushes with little or no supplies for survival. The conflict is understood to be one of the most neglected in recent times by the United Nations and allies. Children are dying everyday from malnutrition-related complications-we urgently seek nutrition support.

title: Chitral Women's Sports Club
description: Due to strict patriarchal gender roles, girls in Chitral, Pakistan rarely have access to sports clubs and programs. This project will offer a safe, fun, educational space for girls from the area to engage with sport and play activities. Chitral Women's Sports Club will leverage the power of sport and organize football camps and tournaments for girls; advocating for equality, actively challenging gender stereotypes and encouraging girls participation in sport.

title: PEACE PROMOTION AND YOUTH EMPOWERMENT IN S. SUDAN
description: The overall objective of the NRI proposed project is to mitigate conflict among the Youths in South Sudan most especially in Juba so as to enhance peace building initiatives by providing a platform for peace & life skills. In this case skills will help to empower the youth and consequently enable them live very happy lives. Also NRI will ensure the beneficiaries receive timely sport for peace & life materials to carry out their activities. priority will be given to youth and  children.

title: Rehabilitate Bereba Library to honor David Pace
description: David Pace visited Bereba village regularly over for more than ten years starting in 2007, doing photography and teaching students in the Santa Clara University Reading West Africa program. He was a regular supporter of the Bereba Library, a small one-room library established in 2001. The library is in need of rehabilitation and book collection in need of renewal. Help us honor the legacy of David, who passed away in October 2020, by contributing to the Bereba Library rehabilitation fund.

title: Empower 140 Women in Tribal India
description: This project promotes self-sustainability in women through a unique program called the Mahila Gruha Udyog, a women-focused institute where SRLC provides infrastructure, tools & networks to allow women to build & sell handmade products. All revenue is pumped back into the program, ensuring self-sustainability. The aim is to uplift the status of women across rural villages. Currently, 160 women are part of the program & with your support, our goal is to expand the program to 140 additional women.

title: Science Education for 220 Girls in Tribal India
description: Investing in gender equality and girl education can unlock human potential on a transformational scale. Yet, gender based discrimination is rampant in rural Indian society, where girls are struggling with poverty, low education and poor health. This project is focused on providing high quality Science education (Bachelors and Masters degree) to ambitious young girls at SRLC's own science college, and provide them with a path for financial freedom.

title: Stand with poor aged people in kenya.
description: The project is one of its own kind in Western Kenya , Nyanza and Homabay county. The project addresses the issue of seclussion of the elderly and abandonment after being abandoned by villagers or distant relatives after loosing their next of kins .Most of the elderly are being affected or infected by HIV/AIDS as they take care of orphans as they awaits death. We therefore work to increase the number of elderly living a life like human beings with dignity and respect in the society.

title: Planting the seeds of a better future in Guatemala
description: "Planting the seeds of a better future" is a campaign that aims to help Mayan families in the Huista region of Guatemala establish a sustainable, reliable source of quality food that goes far beyond their immediate needs. Donations will be used to provide the seeds, materials, knowhow and support to help these families establish their own subsistence gardens, providing food, health and hope both today and in the future

title: Temporary Home for Girls at Social Risk in Arg
description: La Balsa is a long-term residence for homeless cisgender and transgender girls and adolescents who arrive at the Home because of the violation of their rights. Our main goal is to help these girls in the adoption process and/or recovery of family ties. Currently, La Balsa is the only Center that attends to these young women by providing food, care, and a roof to sleep overnight in Buenos Aires. We focus on accompanying them in their journey toward empowerment from a gender perspective.

title: Build an inclusive future for kids with disability
description: KCDC plans to construct a purpose-built Therapy and Rehabilitation Centre to help achieve our vision of a world where children with disabilities and their families can live without stigma and discrimination. Together, we will be able to help address the specialised needs of children with disabilities in western Uganda, by extending the care that we provide and creating equal opportunities for an additional 3,000 children across the region over the next 3 years.

title: OIUSA Rural Community Medical-Surgical Mission
description: OIUSA/Canada's Annual Medical Mission aims to provide comprehensive healthcare access to underserved Ikwerre communities in Nigeria. We provide physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other medical personnel, at no cost to the individuals seeking care to relieve burdens of poor health. Services include preventative healthcare, malaria testing and treatment, HIV screening, counseling, dental care, women's health care, pediatric care, surgical evaluation, ocular (eye) care, and much more.

title: Empowering 140 disabled children in Toba Tek Singh
description: The project will support the disadvantaged disabled children who are neglected by the society. This project will help them become a recognizable and equal part of the society. We will provide 50 children with wheel chairs, 40 children with crutches, 25 children with walking frames and 25 children with hearing aids. This will help these children to participate in social activities and will provide them easy access to recreation and education institutions.

title: Save 50 Flood Survivors to rebuild their houses.
description: The project supports the housing restoration and re-building shelters among the families whose houses were fully submerged and or sunk by the water flooding. The availability of shelter will improve the mental health and general well-being of families supported. The children from such families will be able to attend school in peace as there will be great convenience due to enhanced social family fabrics. The project enhances participation of its beneficiaries at all stages including planning.

title: Help for refugees in Burkina Faso
description: A camp for refugees and displaced persons is founded on the suburbs of Ouagdougou, the capital of Burkina Faso.  There are 450 of people with children. They came from the north of the country escaping from terrorist attacks. To live, they need everything: food, hygiene measures, clothes, education of their children. We have to help them. The fundraised money will be passed to missionaries, who will buy for them the necessary products and  pay for education of the children.

title: Let NEW MASCULINTIES  shine!
description: Amidst confinement and economic tensions, domestic violence is on the rise; we believe punishment or imprisonment is not the answer to the problem.  Using psychosocial methods this project intends to challenge social mores that naturalize violent behavior in boys and men.  During a 12 month period, with the assistance of professionals, we will raise awareness, train staff, volunteers, and community members by means of workshops, information, and training in gender equality and New Masculinities.

title: Providing Long-term Mentorship for Vulnerable Kids
description: Friends of the Children Austin's mission is to break the cycle of generational poverty. We do this by pairing professional, salaried, full-time, bilingual mentors (called "Friends") with children who are facing the greatest challenges and at-risk of continuing harmful cycles. We commit to these children from kindergarten through high school graduation, providing long-term, wrap-around support for 12+ years - no matter what.

title: Disaster Relief and Recovery
description: As the number and severity of disasters continues to increase, Red Cross must urgently scale up its capacity to respond. This means significant investment in our people and our emergency systems. Our goal is to create stronger, more resilient communities with increased capacity to anticipate, respond to and recover from crises. Together, we have a duty to be ready for each and every disaster-as well as the possibility of facing multiple events both at home and beyond our borders.

title: Accompany 200 women that live violence in Oaxaca
description: Violence towards women, adolescents and girls have increased significantly in this time of COVID-19 confinement: only between January and April 2020, 13 women were murdered violently in Tehuantepec isthmus, and an increase in domestic violence was reported. Indigenous women in many time don't know the complaint mechanism or lost much time for inefficiency of some authorities. These situations lead the women, in many times to desist from the process, then, this violation of rights goes unpunished

title: Deliver Maternal Health Care in Lombok
description: Lombok, next to Bali, has had serious setbacks in recent years. First a devastating earthquake in 2018, then COVID-19 and the loss of tourism has left the local economy devastated and thousands without homes. People can't afford food, basic goods or healthcare. Many are still living in tents, even 3 years later. Bumi Sehat Lombok operates both a permanent clinic and a mobile health service in the North. The area was already underserved before the quake and healthcare needs are critical.

title: Supporting 777 EvergreenWorld Champions
description: The Project aims to improve lives of all creatures by educating people of Homa Bay County on the benefits of protecting their environment from any form of pollution or destruction. To achieve this, 777 EvergreenWorld Idea Champions will be trained on ways to keep the ecosystem pure for every creature to enjoy its existence. The Project will assist schools in establishing EvergreenWorld Action Clubs that will be maintaining tree nurseries to avail seedlings for making homes and forests evergreen.

title: Clean and Safe Water for the elderly in Namungalwe
description: This project aims at improving water, sanitation and hygiene in the rural areas of Iganga District in (namungalwe sub county) targeting the elderly who can't access clean and safe water for domestic use.

title: Restore Food Source for Indigenous Community-Peru
description: Help us repair our INMED Aquaponics system, which hundreds of children and their families rely on for fresh produce and fish in the food insecure indigenous Amazonian community of Yarinacocha, Peru. A recent fire swept through the school campus where our system is located, burning the crops, killing the fish and damaging the piping and greenhouse structure. Hungry children are depending on us!

title: Beat Covid & up wellbeing of +500 elders in Brazil
description: We are providing care, protection, and wellbeing support. We are infusing hope to older adults living in long-term care institutions in the outskirts of Sao Paulo city (Brazil), and to their families. We are giving protective equipment, educational, health and key emotional support to more than 500 older adults, the most vulnerable public to complications and death caused by Covid 19, representing the leading risk factor for a catastrophic situation. For us to continue, your donation is vital!

title: Ultimate Peace Grads Making Real World Impact
description: Ultimate Peace (UP) is a groundbreaking leadership development program, annually uniting 400 Arab and Jewish youth in the Middle East. Playing the self-officiated sport of Ultimate Frisbee, teens compete, learn to resolve differences, build trust, and become friends across cultural divides. While COVID-19 has curtailed in-person activities, Leader in Training Program graduates are charging forward in their young adult lives, enacting the values of Ultimate Peace in the most profound ways.

title: Help Increase Food Access and Security in Rural NC
description: Carteret Local Food Network (CLFN) addresses food security, equality, and access in Carteret County, NC through its Mobile Market program. CLFN provides low-wealth communities access to healthy, fresh, local food at reasonable prices while creating new markets for small- to mid-sized farmers. The organization supports local economic growth and sustainable agriculture. CLFN is dedicated to promoting a more resilient and equitable food system in the region.

title: COVID-19 Food & Home Relief for Families in Oyugis
description: Living conditions in Kenya were already tough, then COVID-19 hit and things got even worse!   Families in desperate need are asking for your help...they are out of food, and many are about to lose their homes and become homeless.   Wages have been stopped or severely cut. Many families already living on less than $1 a day lost even that minuscule amount.   Your help is needed today to feed families, keep them in their homes and help them survive through this tough period.

title: Empower disadvantaged girls in Indian slums
description: This project will help empower young girls in the low-income communities of Mumbai. It will provide them with support for their education, access to quality football coaching,  education in health and hygiene, sanitary materials, supplementary nutrition and national and international exposure visits.

title: Support 100 Children attend ECD Centre in S.Africa
description: A Gift to this project is life changing. Our school is the heart of a local township in South Africa and acknowledges that the child's first six years are critical for the development of the brain, language, and their physical, social and emotional growth. Our project ensures children will have a sense of belonging and they will take pride in being apart of our program and demonstrate care, compassion and mutual respect towards themselves and each other. Our teachers are changing lives

title: Employment for 40 poor women in door mat weaving
description: VDC aims to promote training and employment for 40 dalit and poor women in door mat production by using waste cotton from textile companies. The beneficiaries will be given 10 days training in entire activities such as assembling, detachment, attend minor repairs, shaping the waste cotton, weaving, designing, price fixing, purchase and sale points and market linkages. This helps women to earn average Rupees 160 per day.  Recycling cotton waste into door mats will help to prevent pollution.

title: Surgeries for Sri Lankan Children -  Restore Hope
description: Long waiting lists, lack of surgery equipment, tools, and medicines makes it difficult to obtain medical care and surgery for children, mainly from poor families in Sri Lanka at the time they need it. Restore Hope is a very special project to help provide surgery and medicine to children under 14 years having orthopedic deformities and disorders. You can help thousands of children benefit from life changing medical interventions.  Restore Hope works with the Lady Ridgeway Hospital Colombo.

title: Promote stay in school & decrease drop out rates
description: This project will help to buy school materials for 500 children from extremely poor families and save them from dropping out of school due to COVID-19 in Nyanza District, Southern province of Rwanda.

title: Christmas dinner party for the homeless
description: This project will provide Christmas dinner party to over 60 homeless in Stoke-on Trent Staffordshire United Kingdom on Christmas day. Give them a feel of love from the community the belong.

title: NOSTALGIA SENIOR THEATRE RENOVATION (Revised)
description: International Humanitarian Union Catharsis, the one of the first NGO organizations founded in the Republic of Georgia in 1990 and the largest nationwide charitable complex center of emergency, social and senior care is seeking support for its Nostalgia Senior Theatre's 6-month renovation project with the total budget of 13 262 (thirteen thousand two hundred sixty two) US Dollars.

title: Coastal Turkey and Greece Earthquake Relief Fund
description: This disaster relief fund will support people in Turkey and Greece impacted by the 7.0M earthquake in the form of emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. The fund will remain open to provide long-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support communities and first responders impacted by this disaster.

title: FOR 15 3000  FAMILIES TO GET OUT POVERTY
description: This campaign uplifts rural poor communities especially women and youth living in extreme poverty by breeding rabbits. Kigezi Healthcare Foundation(KIHEFO) has been supporting families by giving five females and one male rabbit.Rabbits multiply fast and only eat vegetation. One female rabbit produces an average of 60 in a year and up to 20 female rabbits can be retained for breeding. This gives the family up to 1,600 if they eat 400 they can sell 1,200 at $3 and earn $3,600 per year or $10 daily

title: LEGAL AID FOR ASYLUM SEEKERS IN GREECE
description: A.Ss.I.S.T. currently provides vital legal aid and information to asylum seekers, most of whom reside in Vial Reception Identification Centre (RIC) on Chios, renowned for overcrowding, substandard living conditions and inadequate medical, legal and other basic services. Since the start of the COVID-19 Pandemic, A.Ss.I.S.T. has been delivering services digitally and is now serving clients in the larger Athens metropolitan area, using a cloud-based, virtual country level office.

title: Sponsoring 70 orphans in Yemen
description: 1. This project will provide the  food and education expense for 70 orphans in Yemen who are under 13 years old and lost their parents in the current civil war.   2. 60$ is the estimated budget to sponsor one orphan per month and $720 per year; the food basket is composed of a 50 kg flour, 10 kg rice, 10 kg sugar and 4L food oil.

title: We Love Reading
description: We Love Reading (WLR) is an award-winning program seeking to create a generation of change makers by fostering a love for reading among children aged 2-10 throughout Jordan and the world. We train volunteers-who we call Reading Ambassadors-to run libraries and read aloud to children in their community, leveraging in-depth research we conduct with elite international institutions to inform our methodology. WLR operates in 60 countries and aims to reach all children around the world end of 2022.

title: Rescue 100 children from  Malnutrition.
description: The Project will provide 3 grafted fruit tree seedlings, 2 laying chickens, 5kg of iron rich bean seeds and build 1 household vegetable garden to each of 100 disadvantaged families to prevent malnutrition among children with disabilities or born from parents with disabilities from Nyanza District in Kigoma sector.  The project plans to train 100 representatives, 1from each family on making organic manure  and modern farming methods. They will also be trained on nutritional good practices.

title: We are in Need Pleas Help Us
description: We are from Nepal, Nepal is Asia 's poorest country,  We are in need We need your support so we can save the lives in Nepal, Due to the nationwide lock down for a month long, families' dependent on waged labors deprived from the opportunity of work, daily income. Finally, many people in very worst condition, they unable to  daily meal and proper health care, This project will help the reach the food and health and safety to one thousand families.     Please consider our request for donation.

title: Emergency Response for Izmir Earthquake Survivors
description: The program will deliver humanitarian aid for the survivals of Izmir - Turkey earthquake. This project will deliver necessity aid during the emergency response phase for instance food package, blankets, hygiene kits, much much more for survivals who affected by the earthquake with the magnitudes of 7.

title: Let's take care of the elderly in DR from COVID-19
description: El Proyecto es una iniciativa de la Fundacion Xiomara Urena B. en equipo con la por la Fundacion Funcomas que busca salvar vidas cientos de adultos mayores que estan siendo afectadas por la crisis actual causada por el COVID-19. Este proyecto te da la oportunidad de apoyar a garantizar alimentacion, salud y educacion para los envejecientes afectados y sus dependientes directos. Ademas, con este apoyo damos un respiro economico a sus familias con ancianos, que son que no cuentan con el respaldo.

title: Super Typhoon Goni/Rolly Relief Fund
description: Super Typhoon Goni (known locally as Rolly) made landfall with sustained winds of 135 miles an hour. This relief fund will support emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. After initial needs are met, the fund will transition to provide long-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support Super Typhoon Goni relief and recovery efforts in the Philippines.

title: Rotary Club of Ballymena fights to end Polio
description: Rotary international is a founding member of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative. Since 1985 Rotarians across the world have been working tirelessly to rid the world of polio by ensuring universal access to the vaccine. Recently Africa has been certified as wild polio free but the job is not yet complete! The Rotary Club of Ballymena, which has raised almost 15000, hopes to play its part in a final determined push to raise funds to ensure total eradication of polio across the world.

title: Community Micro-Irrigation Solar Project for Women
description: The goal of this project is to empower the women's productive capacity in a small-scale irrigation system powered with solar energy for vegetable farming activities for more food and also free the women and girls from the manual irrigation burden which is hampered women socio-economic development and girl's education. The immediate results are the removal of the burden of manual crop watering by girls and their mothers. On average, women and girls spent between 8 to 12 hours a day.

title: Super Typhoon Goni/Rolly Food and Sanitation Fund
description: This project will provide food and sanitation relief and recovery support to 3,000 poor families affected by the Super Typhoon Goni/Rolly by the provision of hygiene kits and farming inputs in order to ensure that the problem of sanitation is responded to and the damaged agriculture is rehabilitated soonest.

title: Super Typhoon Goni/Rolly Food and Sanitation Fund
description: We will provide food packs, vegetable seeds, root crops and hygiene kits to 7,500 families affected by Super Typhoon Goni in 12 villages in Albuera, Leyte and in Daraga, Albay. Although the villages in Leyte are not directly hit, they too are severely affected by strong winds and rain with vast agricultural lands damaged and harvest compromised. In Albay, we will focus on villages where we have local volunteers and partners with our previous response when Mayon Volcano erupted.

title: Together, we shall come back stronger
description: In recent days, flooding and landslides in Central Vietnam have left trail of destruction with complicated developments. Central Vietnam has been directly and indirectly affected by the historical Storm Linfa, Nangka and Saundel (Storm No. 6, 7 and 8 in 2020).   Aid for social protection program Foundation Vietnam (AFV) has worked in co-operation with Vietnamese government and local partners to launch the "Together, we shall come back stronger. Take action for Central Vietnam" programme.

title: Super Typhoon Goni/Rolly Children Fund
description: We will provide food packs, medicines, hygiene kits and starter livelihood packages to 2500 children affected by Super Typhoon Goni in 10 villages in Albay province.  We will work with local youth-based associations in the identification and delivery of these support and then strengthen them for long-term recovery and partnership efforts.

title: Alumni Monthly Fund
description: This project will sustain Achvat Amim as a platform committed to building vibrant Jewish and international participation in broader movements for racial, economic, and gender justice. It will resource diverse cohorts of activists with the relationships,  analytic frameworks, and practical tools they need to function as sustained actors within larger democratic movements and in solidarity with Palestinian civil resistors leading popular struggle in the region.

title: Canine Commandos, Inc.
description: Students (400+) of thirty elementary schools learn compassion and empathy, teaching basic commands to shelter dogs and raising adoption rates for the homeless animals.

title: The Museums come to you
description: Going to the museum while staying at home ? It will soon be possible with the ARTZ association's home visits !  To break the isolation of nearly 2000 isolated elderly people with Alzheimer's in Ile-de-France, ARTZ will develop an online application containing a hundred works of art with commentary and accompanied by images, sounds and videos.

title: COVID-19 HARDSHIP RELIEF FOR VULNERABLE FAMILIES
description: COVID-19 Pandemic is threatening everyone's way of life but for those vulnerable people living in poverty, the potential impact is massive. Help and funding are needed urgently for 500 vulnerable families who have been hit severely by the effect of coronavirus pandemic. Your donation will be used to address the emergency need of these vulnerable families in Nigeria and enhance their chances of surviving the onslaught of this pandemic.

title: Nutritious lunch for 1,367 Ugandan school children
description: Entebbe Primary School in Wakiso district Uganda serves 1,200 children. During a community visit, we found that many children were struggling to learn because their families could not afford to feed them regular meals each day. Not knowing where their next meal would come from, these children struggled to focus on their lessons with an empty stomach. We will provide nutritious lunches to 1,000 school children every day for one year to ensure they can thrive in school and beyond.

title: BUILDING A BETTER FUTURE FOR 100  WIDOWS IN OGUGU
description: Help Enhance Lives Peace Initiative Int'l is unveiling a Project that will provide a Sustainable Livelihood to 100 young widows in Ogugu Olamaboro Local Government Area of Kogi State in Vocational skill training (Tailoring).  This will help to curb the problem of unemployment and also to ameliorate the sufferings of the young widows in Ogugu communities and have a Sustainable Livelihoods, to which will be Helpful in eradicating social evils and other criminalities in the communities.

title: ARTivism: Inspiring Activism Through The Arts
description: ICAAD's ARTivism initiative launched in 2020 to inspire greater public awareness and social action through the arts. Our inaugural Artivist is lawyer Harbani Ahuja, whose virtual public arts project Dicta explores the gap between law and justice through blackout poetry of US Supreme Court decisions. We brought on 5 new Artivists from around the world in 2022 - your support will allow us to create public art projects for each artist to share their work with the world and advance social justice.

title: Keep Maasai Girls Learning in Kenya
description: This project helps reestablish our core programs to keep girls in school since schools re-opened from COVID-19-closures in 2021 and scale them to neighboring regions in southern Kenya. Specifically, the project will increase Maasai girls' access to education by activating local leadership to support and champion girls' education, enrolling children in primary school and working with schools and communities to add on secondary day schools, providing low-cost secondary education to thousands.

title: Adjivou Tech Village Project
description: The Tech Village project consists of renovating the primary school of Adjivou in Togo and lighting it with solar panels and of building a computer classroom equipped with 40 computers for 400 children to learn digital literacies without which no learning is possible today.

title: Izmir Earthquake Emergency Response
description: IHH Humanitarian Relief Foundation has been Conducting searh and rescue activities with 250 teams in Izmir since the first hours of the earthquake and trying to help earthquake victims in every possible way such as hot meal, water, hygiene kit, food packet, cloths, baby diaper and biscuit, blanket distribution and psychological helps. Your donations will relieve the wounds of earthquake wictims.

title: Support Lifesaving Emergency Care in Tanzania
description: FAME advances high-quality health care for under-resourced communities in rural Northern Tanzania. Serving a catchment area of 2.9 million people, FAME operates a modern hospital, lab, outpatient clinic, maternity center and reproductive & child health clinic. This year FAME has partnered with local government to take the lead in Covid-19 treatment, prevention and management in our region. Please join us on Giving Tuesday to help boost our pandemic and overall emergency response capabilities.

title: Sponsor 500 Syrian Patients
description: This campaign aims to alleviate the suffering of the vulnerable patients in northwest Syria through sponsoring the costs of medical consultations and surgical operations.

title: Help 90 Deprived & Marginalized Families in Nepal
description: The project will improve livelihoods of 90 marginalized & indigenous families through self-sustainable eco-tourism and commercial farming business model by women only in Gardi village of Chitwan, Nepal. These families are deprived, poor and non-mainstreamed in developmental activities by government. By raising goats and farming duck/pig/fish/poultry in a holistic approach, the women group will earn money as well as it will earn money by promoting eco-tourism within the Chitwan National Park.

title: A NEW YEAR HOPE FOR VULNERABLE CHILDREN IN NIGERIA
description: This project is Inspired by the sad reality of a growing number of the less privileged, neglected, indigents, orphans and vulnerable children in Nigeria. Tabitha Home gives these children (whose vulnerabilities ranges from Neglect, Lack of Basic Needs, Sexual and Physical Abuse) access to all deserving rights and needs of children like Shelter, Nutrition, Psychosocial Support, Education, Medical, Protection, Rehabilitation, Child development, Social Integration and Sustainable Entrepreneurship.

title: New Well and Clean Water for 127 Nicaraguans
description: More than one-third of the children in rural Nicaragua get their water from contaminated streams and rivers. In partnership with rural Nicaragua residents in San Antonio, Camoapa, El Porvenir will drill a well capable of providing 127 men, women, and children clean, safe water. Access to this high-quality drinking water, free of deadly waterborne illness, will allow parents and their children to not only survive but to thrive.

title: Hurricane Eta Relief Fund
description: Hurricane Eta first made landfall in northeastern Nicaragua with sustained winds of 140 miles an hour and widespread flooding rains across much of Central America, the Caribbean, and Florida. This relief fund will support emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. After initial needs are met, the fund will transition to provide long-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support Hurricane Eta relief and recovery efforts in the impacted regions.

title: ESTEBAN
description: Esteban  was born at 26 weeks of gestation, is currently 10 years old, and lost one of his eyes due to retinopathy. Esteban and his family are part of FUNDEP's recycling program. Our friend Esteban currently requires specialized medication because he suffers from convulsions. He is a child of 10 years old, but his behavior is that of a 6 year old, for which he requires therapies that are not covered by his doctor and must be covered in a particular way. Esteban needs your support in order

title: Start Alternative Cultural Center in Serbia
description: This project will start an Alternative Cultural Center in small town in western Serbia, providing a multi functional space for many types of cultural activities such as: art exhibitions, amateur theater, movie nights, poet nights, rock band and rock choir rehearsals and concerts and many forms of artistic workshops for all free of charge. Also the space will be provided for other NGOs who are working on improvement of life in our town and share the same values free of charge as well.

title: Help Protect Critically Endangered Sea Turtles
description: In the past the Seychelles larger granitic islands had a healthy sea turtle population. Recent research, however, indicates an alarming decline in the nesting populations due to a complex combination of threats, including illegal poaching, loss of habitat and human disturbance. As part of its longterm sea turtle monitoring program, MCSS is undertaking conservation, research and education activities with the goal of addressing the threats facing turtles and their habitats on Mahe in Seychelles.

title: Sponsor-A-Meal for a Deaf beneficiary at NID
description: The National Institute for the Deaf (NID) is home to 92 elderly and multiple-disabled Deaf beneficiaries. We provide a home where they are loved and cared for with compassion and understanding for their special needs.  Beneficiaries received 3 meals daily that are prepared on campus by Deaf employees & students. Food security is one of our top priorities. Your donation will ensure nutritious and sustainable meal provision that meets their dietary needs for an active, healthy, and quality living.

title: Environmental Education: Eco-kids for Future
description: This project aims at connecting 200 kids and 20 youths to nature. It focuses on enhancing environmental awareness among children and develops environmental ethics and makes them environmentally conscious citizens. These kids/youths will also be involved in the planting of 2000 (Prunus Africana) and bio-monitoring aimed to conserve their long-degraded community forest and water catchment serving 10,000 persons.  Eco clubs will be created and the holding of outdoor and mega competitions.

title: Relieve the COVID 19 impact on Patients in Nepal
description: 2020 has been a challenging year. So many people have been sick, lost loved ones, jobs, and livelihoods. But how much more impact has this year had on those who were already on the brink of poverty and disease throughout the world? Please help us relieve the impact of COVID 19 on our patients in Nepal. We know how effective Acupuncture and Herbal medicines are on patients with all viruses, from COVID 19 to flu, to chronic disease and malnutrition. Help us make a difference this holiday season.

title: Year End Fundraiser for Utila, Honduras
description: As a difficult year comes to an end, we look back and reflect on what we have been able to accomplish in providing help to Utila, thanks to the ongoing support of our donors.  We're looking to end the year on a positive note, and this month we've already distributed school supplies, baseball equipment, additional medical supplies (both for people and animals!), PPE and disinfecting supplies - and we have more distributions of food and more still going out this coming week.

title: Help St. John Prepare
description: The core mission of Love City Strong is to ensure that the community of St. John, USVI is prepared for emergencies and natural disasters. Through community outreach and empowerment, stockpiling supplies, and first responder training for our team we seek to strengthen the response capacity of the island.

title: 12 Days of Christmas: Wheelchair Edition 2020
description: The 12 Days of Christmas fundraising campaign seeks to highlight and fully-fund 12 wheelchairs for 12 beneficiaries over the Christmas period. Give the best Christmas gift of all, the Gift of Movement.

title: Distribution of family planning to 300 rural women
description: The project diseminates information and enables access on family planning and family planning devices to the rural poor women. This eases the burden of food, poverty and lack of education occasioned by unplanned families.

title: For you, Beirut
description: In Response to Beirut Blast crisis and as an Emergency Response Action plan, AICA started implementation of a project, funded by Catholic Relief Services, for providing general practitioner consultations, medicine and psychosocial support free of charge to cover 1000 beneficiaries per month. During implementation it was noticed that the need is much bigger and that primary health care services and mental health services should be provided to around 3000 beneficiaries per month.

title: Combat Corona to the Last Mile In Kenya
description: In Kenya, most people live from hand to mouth, with 40% of the people living  below the poverty line and 50% just above it. For our community, staying home makes it difficult to get necessities like soap, food, and salt. This project   is acting in response to the COVID outbreak or its consequences, through raising awareness about prevention, supporting vulnerable populations during the economic stop-down. MCDC plans to support 200 households to access ,food ,shelter,education and healthcare .

title: Emergency Response to Turkey Earthquake
description: On October 30, a 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck off Turkey's Aegaeon coast. Over 100 people have died, over 1,000 were injured, and at least 17 buildings have been damaged-making it the deadliest earthquake to hit Turkey in nearly a decade. Dozens of people remain unaccounted for and over 2,000 have been displaced from their homes. International Medical Corps is working with local partners to provide immediate relief and recovery support as part of the Government of Turkey's response efforts.

title: Help Setup Village Classrooms Amid School Shutdown
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has adversely affected the primary education of children since the Government shutdown and due to the implementation of safety measures, primary schools have not reopened. As an alternative, FFLV has come up with an idea of home schools for small kids till 5th grade for whom online classes would have been too difficult if not impossible. Not only can we provide these students with the essential learning but can also reconnect with them and know they are safe and well.

title: Enhancement of accessing fundamental rights
description: This project covers the needs of Migrant workers and enhances access to fundamental rights. FED methodology is one of "working alongside", encouraging and empowering individuals and communities - FED uses a rights based approach.  Addressing the needs of migrant workers affected by the coronavirus pandemic to ensure the accessibility of health care, justice and social recovery by both governments.  Raising awareness of the coronavirus protection and prevention knowledge among migrant population.

title: Bring the future for 2000 Syrian students
description: Education for all children is critical, but for millions affected by humanitarian war in Syria, is very urgent. 0.5 million children are deprived of education in Northwest Syria. The educational sector suffers a lack of basic resources to carry out the educational process. Our project aims to secure access to safe, equitable and quality education within tented classrooms in Jarablus district- Zoghra camp by provision learning and teaching materials, rehabilitation, and recreational activities

title: Sijonge Kuwe job creation&poverty alleviation
description: Sijonge Kuwe Youth Development Project is a community- based project in Khayelitsha,one of the fastest growing townships in South Africa.Our key focus area is economic empowerment in the form of art/cultural skills training, business skills training,computer skills training as well as mentorship for the unemployed youth,women and people with disabilities.The aim of this project is to create jobs opportunities for our people and fight unemployment in our country which is 30%.

title: Typhoon Rolly (GONI) Emergency Response for Luzon
description: CDRC, TABI, and STPRC started the Damage, Needs, Capacity Assessment (DNCA) immediately after the typhoon struck. Based on the assessment, many cities and towns still do not have electricity and are still submerged in floodwaters including some areas in Batangas City, Quezon Province, and Bicol Region, disrupting access to water as well as communications. Aside from the immediate relief needs, people are in dire need of support to restore their livelihoods.

title: Gift an Education to 5 girls in Kenya
description: For these 5 talented girls in Kenya, education is their only means out of poverty, yet their families cannot afford to take them past the 8th grade in school. Uneducated Kenyan girls are vulnerable to child marriage, early motherhood, poor health, and a life of continued poverty. Help these smart, aspiring girls stay in school by supporting Resurge Children East Africa today. Give them the support and resources they need to achieve their full potential.

title: Social college, a community experience
description: The social school project, a community experience, is a bet that allows helping the most vulnerable, offering them a space for their  virtual classes Accompaniment to tasks,  Food  Recreational/artistic activities Children are served from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Most of the families work or are looking for work. The Covid crisis has unleashed a series of problems in the population and it is essential to support to resolve the situation.  180 children are cared for.

title: Scientific Research - Childhood Cancer Institute
description: Child and youth cancer is the leading cause of death from disease in the age group of 1 to 19 years in Brazil, according to INCA - National Cancer Institute. For Brazil, in the 2020-2022 period, there will be 4,310 new cases in males and 4,150 in females, totaling 8,460 cases. The project aims to generate knowledge, through research, that can be used to increase the chances of curing children and adolescents who face childhood cancer.

title: Help Provide for thousands of starving children
description: Help us feed thousands of starving children this Christmas. We strive to help make a difference in the lives of veterans and their families, children that are in need in the poorest communities in South Florida, the Caribbean, and Latin American Countries. Our project Happy faces helps us provide food, clothes, shoes, toys, and first necessity items to young and their mothers. With our conferences, we reach out to communities and provide helpful tools for personal motivational growth.  Feed

title: Open First Addiction Center in Benin
description: This project will finance the construction of three treatment pavilions (gazebos/shaded shelters) for the opening of the first addiction center in French speaking West Africa.   Located in Dassa, Benin, 256 people will receive residential treatment for addiction and mental health problems.  The  pavilions (3 total at $5,000 USD each) will provide a sheltered outdoor common space where residents will gather for discussion groups, art, and other therapeutic and relaxation activities.

title: USVI Hurricane Recovery & Building Forward
description: The Community Foundation of the Virgin has served as a catalyst for initiatives promoting recovery from Hurricanes Irma and Maria, as well as building forward in ways that enhance the well-being of residents of the US Virgin Islands.   This project has a variety of goals centered around addressing continued needs in the long-term recovery process, including priority areas of environmental resilience and hazard mitigation; housing; and workforce development.

title: UNITED WE HELP HONDURAN FAMILIES STORMS ETA /IOTA
description: Hurricane ETA has deepened the challenges in the areas of economy, health and education that the most vulnerable communities in Honduras faced due to the almost 10 months of confinement as a preventive measure against COVID - 19. While we work supporting families affected by Storm ETA, Hurricane Iota arrived in our country leaving more rain and destruction, floods and landslides could be aggravated by the effects of both hurricanes in less than 15 days, affecting the same areas.

title: Winter Relief Aid for Children at Risk
description: Despite being affected by winter every year, this year the lives of the families in the Sindhupalchowk district have become difficult because of the massive landslide erupted from a fragile landmass, weakened by the 2015 earthquake and its powerful aftershocks.  Therefore, this project will distribute 1 warm blanket and 1 jacket to 200 children affected by the landslide in the Sindhupalchok district. These children are currently living in tents as their homes have been destroyed by landslides.

title: Help indigenous women conserve the environment
description: Our goal is to restore the forests that preserve rivers and springs in the mountains of the indigenous territory of Boruca, Costa Rica, together with 25 benefited indigenous women and their families and more than 100 annual volunteers who visit the community. Through the planting of native trees, regenerative agriculture and cultural tourism. The project requires continuous funds for the trees and their maintenance, training, salaries, among others, so that the community continues to restore.

title: No more Girls and Women illiterate in Albania
description: This project will provide free books and literacy support services through Mobility Teaching Sessions for at least 300 illiterate girls and women in Albania, coming from marginalized groups such as  victims of trafficking, early marriages, domestic violence, Roma minority etc.

title: Giving Potable Water, Saving Lives.
description: This project is aimed to install 1 small scale - solar water supply systems, to benefit 379 low-income households (children and women) of Nwachicoluwane-rural ares, where  water puddle is the only place where they can fetch water. And also the  primary school with 873 pupils enrolled will have access to water and 10.000 handmade facemask. This will lead to decrease of school dropout and school performance increase, for girls who suffer doubly (fetch water for their families and early marriages.

title: Urgent Covid Relief for Girls to Continue Learning
description: Edu-GIRLS' agenda to lift girls out of poverty using its 10 Mantra approach had been jolted by COVID threatening financial ruin, leaving girls on the street and arresting learning. A $100,000  COVID Action Agenda I has distributed 1M meals, set up 600 digital learning devices and motivated  teachers to worker smarter. With COVID wave 2, the fight intensifies. Vaccination drives and basic treatment facilities need to be set up to save girls, families and staff and prepare for school reopening.

title: Emergency Response to Typhoon Goni - Philippines
description: On November 1, Super Typhoon Goni struck the Philippines with winds up to 195 mph-the strongest since Typhoon Haiyan in 2013-leaving 151 cities and towns without electricity and displacing hundreds of thousands of people. Current reports place the death toll at 20 people; with many affected communities still out of reach, damage could take days to assess. In response, International Medical Corps is launching efforts to address relief and recovery needs.

title: Social enterprise owned by indigenous mayan women
description: Two years ago, Adriana, our beloved founder, friend and mentor, began dreaming of a project that could contribute to the autonomy of indigenous craftswomen:  a social enterprise based in Chiapas, Mexico built in unity, diversity, respect and harmony. Unfortunately, Adriana passed away recently, but despite her physical absence, her legacy remains alive in us and her honest vision continues to guide us. Today, you can be part of this dream.

title: Teach Rural African Children to Conserve Wildlife
description: Meet Felicia - a young girl living in a remote, rural community in South Africa - Her prospects to succeed and prosper are limited. Just imagine if access to the internet allowed her to develop skills needed for a better life. Imagine, with a quality education, if she could inspire conservation efforts to protect her natural heritage. Are you ready to make this happen? We are. Join us to deliver education through solar internet to Felicia and pals in 3 schools in Greater Kruger National Park.

title: Restoration of the degraded hot spots
description: Agency for Rural and Urban Development is implementing a program aimed at restoring ecosystems' health and improving livelihoods of riparian communities. The organization members are strategically located within the upper, middle and lower stream of the  Mubuku -Nyamwamba catchment with the focus of tackling the ecological challenges within the area without compromising the livelihood of the riparian communities.

title: Food and gifts to 300 street Poor Children (Benin)
description: This project will provide food and gifts for the street hungry after the harmful drought devastated plants in rural areas. It will also bring these desperated street hungry children back to love, joy and hope in Benin.

title: Turner syndrome awareness in Ecuador
description: This project plans to tour the largest provinces of Ecuador to provide information and sensitize at least 200 people.

title: educate 40 orphans for one year in uganda
description: This project will provide  quality education to 40 children living in rural Uganda. Your donation will go towards required school fees, learning materials and feeding to orphans who would not be able to attend otherwise. Helping a child reach their full potential with a solid foundation of learning allows them to become confident community leaders with the ability to solve their own  problems.

title: Cambrian Wildwood
description: Habitat and species restoration in the Cambrian Mountains of Wales. We are restoring native forest, heathland and blanket bog on 350 acres. The aim is to increase to 7,000 acres, reserving a significant area for wildlife and for recreation. Education and wellbeing programmes form a major part of the project. Local schools come for days out on site, learning about wildlife. We host youth camps where teenagers spend a week camping on the land and learn practical and life skills.

title: A Bridge for Community Resilience
description: Las Piedras is a stream that runs through 15 km of urban neighborhoods in Buenos Aires and is prone to flooding. During periods of heavy rainfall, which is exacerbated by climate change, the communities of El Molino and Eucaliptus are often isolated from the rest of the region. Recently, four people, including two children, died trying to cross the stream. This project involves the construction of a new vehicular bridge to ensure that these communities are accessible during such periods.

title: Send 120 Children to School In Ghana For a Year
description: Beginning in January 2021, our "Send a Child to School" initiative will support the education of 120 children from some of the most disadvantaged communities in Ghana, namely, Osunu Dompe, Ahomahomasu, Besebuom & Tafi Mador. Over the next year, we will work closely with these children and their families, helping them to  purchase school uniforms, stationary, books and other vital educational resources. In addition, we will be providing mentorship to each of the 120 children & their families.

title: Support the journey towards justice with education
description: Iran Academia plans to deliver the very first open online course (MOOC) in Persian on transitional justice processes. The course targets students from countries with histories of mass atrocities, such as Iran, who are denied access to education on issues related to accountability and truth-seeking. It provides students with the opportunity to learn about judicial and non-judicial mechanisms needed for restoring the dignity of victims and finding durable solutions in fragile societies.

title: Educating the Stateless Community of Machar Colony
description: To provide quality education to the stateless community of Machar Colony where the largest age group is of 5- 15 years old children. As the community is stateless i.e. without identity, the opportunities to learn and grow are near to nothing  Imkaan established Khel - a learning & recreational centre. With an informal education component, Khel focuses on a holistic approach to learning through a multi-age teaching structure where children are divided according to the learning level then age.

title: Education support for 370 orphans
description: 1.Roma ovc care is an organization that provides care,support and ensure nutritional environment to orphans and vulnerables,we also explore the children to different activities and give them love and encouragement both physical and spiritual,so as they grow,they know God and helping these children realise their full potential by affording them a chance to be educated.This is through paying school fees,provision of school requisites and promoting economic strengthening activities to caregivers/g

title: Promoting Child & Family Wellbeing in Tanzania
description: This project seeks to provide for the physical, social, and mental well-being of the children and families in Amani's community. Amani provides medical care for all children at our center, including on-site first aid as well as emergency and chronic condition care coverage at the area's top medical facilities. We also have an on-site social worker, who provides counseling for children and their families. We provide art therapy, nature education, and sports programs to support emotional healing.

title: Educate a Jamaican child experiencing poverty
description: Christel House provides children from some of the most challenged neighborhoods in Jamaica with life-changing, quality education, health care, nutritious meals, character/life skills development and continued guidance after graduation. Our goal is to help children overcome the barriers of poverty and empower them to identify and realize their goals, dreams and human potential.

title: Ensuring Food Security for Children in Maasailand
description: Amani Children's Home provides full-time residential care to vulnerable children and youth in Tanzania. However, our arid region is prone to droughts and famines that make staples like corn, beans, and rice inaccessibly expensive. This project addresses the duel challenges of the current and future food insecurity. We 1. provide balanced, nutritious diets for our students; 2 stockpile food for difficult seasons and 3. invest in sustainable agriculture and energy to ensure financial stability.

title: Give Solar Lamps to School Children in Myanmar
description: This project aims to provides solar powered lamps to school children who live in off-grid communities in Myanmar, such as the Hlegu Center and Saytanar Mercy Village. Jezuba is a non-profit organization that works with the next generation on solutions to hard-to-solve problems such as poverty and the environment.    Check out: https://www.jezuba.org/

title: Black, Indigenous, POC Sci-Fi Screenwriting Lab
description: Sci-Fi and Fantasy genres in mainstream Hollywood often leave Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC) out of the equation. Justice for My Sister is raising funds to bring back our BIPOC Sci-Fi Screenwriting Lab in 2021. Our first edition gave a safe space to working adults committed to imagining ourselves into the future, powerfully. Their TV pilot scripts called on ancestral wisdom to course-correct climate change and incorporated critical race theory to paint a pathway to liberation.

title: More than 1 million Yemeni children DO  NEED us
description: The Coronavirus Crises (COVID-19) outbreak and its consequences for children, youth and related families are going to have a very negative impact in the future. Thus, We are extending our commitment to be the builders of tomorrow's generation with high morals and empowering skills while they are setting at home "The little star" we designed our project using the PYD concept, framework and toolkits in order to assist and guide children and youth of our community to stay healthy and positive.

title: Break Poverty, Build Hope: Support Migrant School
description: We are One-Forty, a non-profit organization committed to empowering Southeast Asian migrant workers through education. Our mission goes beyond helping them adjust to life away from home; we aspire to extend our impact to their homelands, equipping them with the tools to achieve financial independence. Our goal is to break the cycle of poverty that has entrapped them and unlock doors to brighter futures not only for themselves but for their families and the generations that follow.

title: Healthy Mothers, Smiling Babies
description: No woman deserves to lose her life while trying to bring forth a life. This project will contribute to reducing maternal and infant mortality in 6 Regions in Ghana, ensuring that we have Healthy Mothers, Smiling Babies.  The Project will:  1. Increase the use of essential maternal and child health services, including those related to sexual and reproductive health, by women and girls   2. Improve the provision of a gender sensitive and rights-based Maternal and Child Health care

title: Provide 500 GBV victims with Counselling & Support
description: Gender Based Violence (GBV) is rife in Alexandra and urgent interventions are needed on all levels. Every day our team working in Alex are made aware of cases of women and children being abused and treated in unacceptable ways. The scourge of GBV has become far worse since the start of lockdown, almost a year ago, as women are "locked down" with their abusers, with limited means to escape and nowhere else to live. We need help to provide counselling and support to the victims of GBV.

title: COVID19 and Hunger Alleviation Program
description: Sri Lanka continues with various attempts towards peace. Issues ethnic, gender based violence and prosperity have not been successful solving. Such as natural disasters poverty. now the prevalence of the COVID19 epidemic, which is currently wreaking havoc on the world's population, has been reported in Sri Lanka and over virus infections has risen to 13,900 as on 09.11.2020 and further health promotion bureau stated that there are active cases 5449 individuals are under observation and receiving

title: Congo Girls' Project
description: To address the exploding rates of early pregnancies, forced marriages, and sexual violence against girls in Tanganyika province due to the Covid-19 pandemic, we will educate 25 adolescent girl coordinators on laws against sexual violence and on women's rights, develop school education activities targeted to reduce and prevent sexual violence, and through girl-led radio and social media broadcasts, communicate critical information to the entire community, in particular to women and girls.

title: THE SEND A SEED WOMEN'S PROJECT IN UGANDA
description: The Send a Seed Women's project in Kabale Uganda is aimed at sustaining the indigenous good seeds and utilizing seeds  not only as food sources but also as an income generating project for the families  involved.Also natural manure and other forms of organic manure are use,and not artificial manure, to increase soil fertility.In times of COVID-19 pandemic,nutritious food is essential.

title: Be a Bridge Builder for At-risk Kids in Virginia
description: Despite being the one of the most affluent regions of the nation, many of Northern Virginia's children never get the opportunity to achieve their dreams, because they are economically disadvantaged, are neglected or are unable to adapt to traditional learning environments. INMED USA's 2-generation approach gives vulnerable children a healthy start in life, helps at-risk youth develop vital life skills and provides disadvantaged parents with the resources they need to build stable families.

title: Help Build A Women and Girls Education Center
description: Queen Sheba Village organization is setting up an Education Social Center in the city of Mbour, that will enable girls and women to have access to education in an easily accessible location. At this center, they will have the opportunity to learn(be educated), share in participation, and meet other like-minded individuals. The center will focus on 3 main objectives. * Micro Credit Entrepreneurship Opportunity * Health & Hygiene * Spreading Awareness of Female Genital Cutting.

title: Empower women and girls through digital access
description: Your gift will empower women and girls to learn, lead and thrive in our digital world. Around the world, a lack of opportunities and resources prevent many women and girls from gaining the digital skills that connects them with greater opportunities, leaving them marginalised and disadvantaged. With your support, we will work with our local partners to ensure the women and girls in our programmes can not only access technology and data, but also receive training to become digitally literate.

title: Basildon People's Mental Health Matters
description: COVID 19 has caused more mental problems in society.  In Basildon we have experienced local Charities and CIC's developed by local people for local people, but the funding of it is severely strained.  BASILDON NEEDS YOUR MONEY TO HELP THESE LOCAL ORGANISATIONS MEET THE DEMAND!  We are appealing on behalf of two of these local mental health groups  Motivated Minds and The Listening Post. Please give generously to this appeal to help the mental health of people in the Basildon Borough area

title: Help us make our Safe house a home
description: We are soon to open a new women's refuge in North West Surrey.   We want to make our families feel as comfortable as possible as they adjust to their new home.  Small things will make a big difference to make the house feel as homely as possible.

title: Spay and Neuters on Dogs/Cats in Bucharest
description: Animal Spay and Neuter International has a team of vets that travel around the world spaying and neutering peoples pets. This is funded by donations and the operations are carried out free of charge. This in turn reduces the amount of stray dogs on the streets.   Currently focusing on Romania ASNI will carry out the sterilisations at the Center of Hope Animal Hospital near Bucharest in Romania, which was built and is run by Romania Animal Rescue ASNI's sister charity.

title: Poverty reduction for 150 Ugandan families
description: Nurture Africa campaigns to support poverty striken families in Uganda access healthcare, education, nutrition & sustainable income generation. This project will seek to provide:  - 50 families with treated mosquito nets (essential in preventing malaria) - 25 children with access to Primary Healthcare - 25 families with nutritional support - 25 people with access to HIV care & treatment - 30 most at risk mothers with Maternity care - 10 families with income generation support

title: SEA Annual Summer Education Program
description: SEA's annual summer program brings students together for environmental fun and learning through games, art and interactive demonstrations.  As one of our most important programs, the SEA Summer Program inspires students to be environmental leaders through hands-on activities in conservation, restoration and preservation led by local experts.  Through this program, SEA and our community partners are cultivating the next generation of environmentally responsible citizens.

title: Help Get Hearing For Little Angel
description: Zainab Fatima is a five year old girl that hails from the city of Rawalakot in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Like every other girl her age, she has her dolls, is always ready to play, loves to roam around and also aspires to go to school. But, there's one obstacle in her life that differentiates her experience from that of other children - she cannot hear.

title: Changing lives of 500 IDP girls in Cameroon
description: This project is an initiative that seeks to respond to the plight of war-torn girls in the North  and South west regions of Cameroon. This project will better develop a mechanism of assistance, socio-legal and economic support adapted to each identified situation. It will equally intend to develop advocacy to take into account the specificity of the needs of these girls from the affected regions

title: COVID-19 Relief: Guatemalan & Kenyan Communities
description: GRACE Cares will provide much needed relief to communities affected by COVID-19 in conjunction with our local heroes who are leading Community Finance Guatemala (CFG) and the Watha Project in Kenya. This initiative will dramatically improve the quality of life and healthcare for the Kakchiquel Maya in Guatemala and the Watha in Kenya in their struggle against the current pandemic.

title: HELP 100 ORPHANS AND VULNERABLE  CHILDREN TO STUDY
description: MAEC organization facilitates the orphan and vulnerable children to get education so that to have a good future.We are currently seeking the support to buy scholastic materials, books, uniforms, chairs and desks for the centre. Please join us through your donation in the journey to helping our children reach a brighter future

title: Kindergarten for 100 Syrian children in Lebanon
description: This project provides funding for 100 Syrian kindergarteners in the south of Lebanon, giving the children an important education while also addressing their psycho-social needs during a time of insecurity. They learn numbers, do art work and play team games that encourage teamwork, self-discipline, trust and sharing. On top of this, the teachers for the school are from the refugee community, providing them an opportunity to use their professional skills.

title: THE NYABIKONI WOMEN CROP GROWERS,KABALE -UGANDA
description: The purpose of the project is to eliminate hunger,poverty,diseases ,illiteracy,from the community where it is being implemented. It also serves as demonstration for neighboring communities on promotion of plant food against animal food and using natural fertilizers to get good quality food safe for human consumption as well as protect the environment.

title: Education for 1000 slum children in Goa
description: This project is a uniquely designed program that prepares slum children, for formal education by taking the school to them. This project will provide 1000 children who are living on the edge, marginalized, and deprived of basic education, health facilities, and with no financial security with education and comprehensive support services.

title: Help Save Primates and their Habitat
description: Located in one of the top twenty-five biodiversity hotspots, the project promotes the conservation, preservation and protection of six primate species including the nationally threatened Angolan colobus monkey and their disappearing coastal forest habitat. Programs focus on habitat conservation and community links, animal rescue/rehabilitation, and education. It is the only primate rehabilitation centre in East Africa and the only primate conservation organization operating in Kenya.

title: Victims of Disasters Receive Extended After Care
description: The outpouring of generosity often benefits victims of natural disaster in the immediate aftermath of the horrendous trauma. Often victims are left alone to discover their post-disaster normalcy. In their vulnerability, victims are often preyed upon by human traffickers. GRACE provides awareness, counseling services and financial assistance through the next weeks, months and year. Provisions are customized to their needs and may include funds for groceries, clothing, furniture, and housing.

title: Help 1000 young entrepreneurs in Eswatini
description: Eswatini has the 3rd highest youth unemployment on the planet (1 in 2 youth are without work). The economic crisis resulting from COVID has worsened the situation and riots erupted there in July 2021. Entrepreneurship & quick employment is the only hope for this desperate situation. We help youth start enterprises & get business tr. Your donation will support entrepreneurship awareness & training, micro-loans & business mentoring for 1000 youth in Eswatini.

title: Let 100 girls form the future of Myanmar
description: The Atutu Learning Center provides a high school education to girls from under-invested regions in Kachin State, Myanmar. Atutu has asked the Tekkatho Foundation to support the girls with learning during Covid-19 closures and beyond. With your donations to this project, we can provide quick and reliable access to world class educational resources to the girls of Atutu through our low-cost, offline digital library: MyLibrary. Funds beyond $1250 will go toward a further new eLibrary in Chin State.

title: Collegefund for students with Tourette syndrome
description: Disability rights include access to a college education. Students with Tourette syndrome are challenged with equity in opportunity due to the symptoms that impact their basic living, learning, and gainful activity. This project seeks to enhance the educational opportunity for high school graduates by improving enrollment and thus access, to a college education for individuals with the disability Tourette syndrome.

title: Deliver Pandemic Maternal Health Care in Bali
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has devastated the Bali tourism economy. The Indonesian government requires pregnant women to pay for a COVID-19 test before giving birth. Families may borrow money or take away from other essentials, like food or medicines, to cover birth costs. Bumi Sehat Bali provides maternal health services  by-donation or free, so Indonesian families in Bali don't go into debt or poverty for healthcare.

title: MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS
description: Carlos is a 25 year old Young man, suffering from Multiple SCLEROSIS, and we are looking for Help to buy him a wheelchair  Please Help us

title: Protect Earth's last wildernesses, $5 per acre
description: Wilderness landscapes have incredible wildlife, Indigenous cultures, and vast carbon stores. We aim to protect 5 MILLION acres by 2030 and protect it FOREVER, working closely with Indigenous peoples. In Western Australia, 1 acre (4000m2) of pristine land costs US$5 per acre - the average cost of a cup of coffee. In 2022, with the help of donors and impact investors, we bought over 500,000 ACRES of incredible habitat and important sacred sites dating back 40,000 years.

title: Special COVID-19 Relief
description: During the global pandemic, most countries in Southern Africa went into a hard lock down in March 2020. This left many people loosing employment and facing the threat of food insecurity. Loss of income also meant the inability to have hand sanitisers and face masks. HOPE Africa has been working in partnership with communities to raise funds for food distribution, food vouchers, clothing distribution and the distribution of santisers and masks.

title: SCREEN 3,000 CHILDREN FOR BP & OBESITY IN LAGOS
description: Cardiovascular disease, the leading cause of death, begins during childhood and tracks through adolescents with complications such as stroke and kidney failure. Hypertension, a significant cause of CVD is highly underdiagnosed in children and adolescents in developing countries due to poor skills in the measurement of BP in children.
