The project will screen 3000 schoolchildren, and train primary healthcare providers on BP interpretation in 2 LGAs in Lagos over 12 months.  Project cost is $49100

title: SUPPORT CROATIAN CHILDREN CARING FOR EACH OTHER
description: We have designed 5 new workshops to address fears, in particular the fear of Covid 19, which will include children aged 7 to 14 and people with disabilities. We will include at least 25 school children from Zagreb and 25 people with intellectual disabilities of the Regoc Association from Slavonski Brod. Workshops "Skillful Hands " and learning how to make handicrafts from wood and fabric will alleviate the stress and fear of Covid 19, but also the fear for their loved ones.

title: GivingTuesday Match for Integral Heart School
description: GivingTuesday is the single biggest fundraising day of the Integral Heart year. We are working to close out our year-end plans and start the new year in a strong position. This year is exceptional with $1 million dollars being made available by GlobalGiving in a Proportional Match - meaning, the more we raise the more get!  Your support will go directly to support the communities of our children and families who are most at risk with the expansion of our home-study and food delivery programs.

title: Provide Water For 3 School Districts In Argentina
description: In Argentina, over 7 million people lack access to safe drinking water and over 50% of surveyed schools do not have piped water infrastructure. This project will go towards building 3 separate rainwater harvesting systems for schools in the province of Chaco, Argentina. In addition to the installation, we will provide sessions to promote awareness around the health and importance of clean water.

title: Let us build a school for 300 Pakistani Girls.
description: Rehman Colony is situated in the suburb of City Jauharabad district Khushab Punjab. Here a poor community having different religions and sects living peacefully. Unfortunately not a single public school exists there for 300  girls of the community, though they have transferred land of 20000 Sq. Ft. to the government for this purpose, but current policy doesn't support them. However Government agrees to establish a public school if building is provided. Let us support them in this Nobel Cause!

title: Help Support Construction of New Classrooms
description: With about 600 children, there is no school in this community depriving these children their right to education and exposing them to child labour activities. The construction of a three unit classroom block with an office and a store room by CRI would provide education for these children and remove/reduce their risk of entering into child labour activities.

title: Care and education of 70 abused girls in Mexico
description: Remar Mexico Seeks to guarantee protection, food safety, hygiene and education to 70 Mexican girls rescued from situations of mistreatment and sexual abuse, so that they can develop their life plan and skills for work.

title: Socioemotional Art Classes for Elementary Students
description: You Can Academy (YCA) is a weekly after-school program that provides assistance with homework, technology, reading, and enriched spiritual activities to the academically at-risk kids in our community. YCA has an art component as part of STEAM( Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math) Curriculum. The art program allows students to learn and development socioemotionally at an age appropriate level. This program is taught by a local community artist.  #GivingTuesday

title: Hygiene Kit Backpacks with Toys for Kids
description: For Giving Tuesday, Good360 and Disaster Services Corp. SVDP-USA are partnering on a new initiative to help disaster survivors across the nation. To meet the basic needs of disaster survivors and to deliver toys and hope to children during the holiday season, we are assembling and distributing 5,000 backpacks filled with hygiene , personal care and emotional care products (toys and games).  Each kit costs $15 for the products and distribution.  Our goal is 5,000 kits, so we need to raise $75,000

title: A Solar WASH project benefits 750 people in Nepal
description: W.A.S.H. - Water, Sanitation and Health - a great goal for our project, but you can't WASH without water!  The Rotary Club of Danetre, Daventry, along with other Rotary Clubs of District 1070, aims to install a solar-powered water pumping system to supply clean water to a school and community in Kavre Pokhari high up in the hills of central Nepal. Why do we want to do this? Because people living at altitude have to carry water uphill for up to a mile each day to meet normal daily requirements.

title: A Christmas Gift for Abatex in the Philippines
description: Some may ask, "Why help others so far away during a pandemic?" Airline Ambassadors International (AAI) has partnered with Jesus Our Great Shepherd Church in the Philippines. Our goal is to provide clean drinking water and nutritious meals for the children from the impoverished Abatex Dumpsite community. Every time AAI volunteers board a flight to Manila, we know why. When we hold a child in our arms, we understand why. Please help all of us at AAI make this special Christmas wish come true!

title: Help kids to overcome educational lag in Mexico!
description: Education in the rural community of San Miguel Viejo lags significantly for many reasons. Indigenous communities are disproportionately poorer than non-indigenous communities; most families lack critical resources, and many children complete education through 6th grade before leaving to earn necessary income. This project aims to overcome the educational lag and keep children interested in learning through integrated learning programs that include tutoring, arts, literacy, sports, and mentoring.

title: Typhoon Vamco/Ulysses Food Support Project
description: We will provide food packs comprising warm meals to 2,000 individuals affected by Typhoon Vamco and then later on, when the situation near-normalize to start with the distribution of vegetable seeds so that families in hard-hit villages can start vegetable gardening and improve their access to nutritious food. We will also provide mats, blankets and mosquito nets.

title: English Education & Community Leadership in Haiti
description: English in Mind Institute (EIM) provides high quality, affordable English classes to adults in Port-au-Prince, along with job placement assistance.

title: Empowering Youth in S. Africa - Marias Restaurant
description: This project will empower youth in S. Africa by creating a restaurant for Maria. Maria Gaba runs an orphanage and  youth she cares for will learn business skills and a way to support themselves in the future. She has a desire to grow food and works with Jhoanny  spearhead a training program where youth will learn the ins and outs of opening a restaurant.  Funds raised will provide the cost of opening the business, purchase needed equipment and hire staff.  Profits will help support Marias House.

title: Dream Home for Janani's Children
description: We make an appeal to help our children to get a new house which provides all required facilities stipulated by the Government of Puducherry. Now we have been living in rented buildings. We face the hardship of increased rent every year. Huge payment of rent takes away all our resources nevertheless the maintenance of the building. By shifting the place often, we need to make arrangements for the school, transportation, and change address in records. Hence we make an appeal to you!

title: The Philippines Super Typhoon Relief Fund
description: November 1, Super Typhoon Goni (known locally as Rolly) with a sustained wind speed of 225km/hr made landfalls. More than 24 million people in 8 regions, 32 provinces, 44 cities and 357 municipalities are affected by the Typhoon. This relief fund will urgently deliver a 3-Week Food Relief Package (including rice, cans and sugar) to 650 most affected families, with a focus on single parents, women without families, elderly, people with disability.

title: Digital Revolution Awards to help build a Hall
description: St Martins School, at the heart of Kibagare, is a safe haven for more than 1000 students from the Kibagare slum. The population here lives on less than $2.00 a day and most are poor. The school not only provides education, but also provide regular meals, space to play, access to computers, and a child-friendly environment. Our focus has been on education and technology but we are keen on empowering the families of the children that we support with the knowledge and skills to be self-reliant.

title: Life Support Skills for Prosperity
description: The project will teach 20 adolescents brick moulding and bricklaying skills, 12 girls and 8 boys, who are school dropouts between the ages of 13 to 25. The project will result in the construction of 20 sanitation facilities in homesteads of Jongela Village, Nkayi, Zimbabwe. Jongela Village has a total of 110 households and only 18 have sanitary toilets and the remaining 92 had no toilets and get water from unprotected sources. The sampled households have boys and girls aged between 13 to 17.

title: Butte County Sheriff's Search and Rescue New Boat
description: Our team is currently using a 30-year-old boat that is not capable of performing the rescues we need it to. We are hoping to raise funds to help replace this boat with a new boat that will increase our rescue capabilities immensely.

title: Give safe water to 82 Ugandan orphans
description: Can you imagine walking several miles to fetch unsafe water to drink? Safe water is life. This project will help St Mugagga Boy's Home drill a new water well and install a solar-powered pumping system to provide clean water and sanitation for 82 orphans and vulnerable children in our care.   Help each child have clean, safe water to drink, experience good health, and feel more hope for a better life.

title: Connectivity for Children with Hearing Loss
description: With school being conducted virtually in most jurisdictions due to the pandemic, children with hearing loss are more vulnerable than ever to falling behind in their speech, language, academic and social skills. They are at an added disadvantage when it comes to using computer technologies. We would like to be able to provide assisted listening equipment and training to children who are receiving services through teletherapy, attending school virtually or participating in a hybrid program.

title: MEDACROSS - AIDS patients are not alone in Myanmar
description: There are more than 240 thousand people living with AIDS in Myanmar. For those people, finding a job and have medical healthcare is a daily struggle, because AIDS is a strong stigma in Myanmar. Coronavirus has worsened their situation since they are heavily immunosuppressed.  MedAcross help AIDS patients in South Myanmar with free medical visits and medicines, giving health counselling and providing safe food and water to avoid additional illnesses. Help us don't let down who has no one else.

title: Improving the lives of children with special needs
description: This project will contribute to improving the living conditions for children with special needs in the Aida and Al Azza refugees camps in Bethlehem, Palestine and will benefit more than 150 children through rehabilitation work such as physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, osteopathy, a mental health program, autism class and a focus on children with learning difficulties.

title: Hurricanes Eta & Iota Emergency Response: Honduras
description: In Honduras, Hurricane Eta left a trail of destruction. Thousands of acres of crops were washed away, causing even more shortages in communities already experiencing severe food insecurity as a result of the pandemic. And now, Hurricane Iota is following Eta's path and making matters devastatingly worse. Your support and solidarity are urgently needed to help equip our partners with emergency supplies so they can reach and assist families and small farmers whose homes and crops were destroyed.

title: Typhoon Vamco/Ulysses Small Business Assistance
description: We will support 200 small business damaged by the devastation caused by Typhoon Vamco in our project areas affected before by the eruption of Taal Volcano. Most often small business such as food vending, small grocery store, raising of animals such as pigs and chickens and vegetable gardening are destroyed by floodwaters and this needs to be revived soonest since this is often the only lifeline for poor families.

title: Help La Serenissima make Brescianello Op 1 happen!
description: Brescianello is a very special discovery for La Serenissima. We know little about his life, but his music is of outstanding quality, reflecting pan-European influences. We will record Volume 2 of his Opus 1 in February 2022 - creating work for our team after more than a year of restricted activity. We look to followers to support the post-production work needed to release this second album of the project & in doing so, help us to maintain connection with our audience.

title: Amplify HIV+, black, LGBTQ voices!
description: Positively Positive is the only artist in the entire world who is living with HIV at birth who writes about the experiences of blacks, aromantics, asexuals, queer, and transgender peoples. {Asexuals} do not experience sexual attraction. {Aromantics} do not experience romantic attraction. {Asexuals} and {Aromantics} are a demographic {part of the LGBTQ community} missing from the overall conversation so Positively Positive bridges that gap to provide music, workshops, opportunities.

title: Build Latin America's next generation of leaders!
description: Improve Latin America's future by investing in its next generation. Sponsor students to enroll in LALA's next Virtual Leadership Bootcamp.  High school students committed social impact will tackle our intensive one-week curriculum of leadership training, expand their networks of peers and mentors, and enter LALA's lifelong community of alumni support.  Scholarships will be awarded to students with the greatest need, eliminating financial barriers for our promising leaders.

title: Make education a force to unite!
description: At UWC Costa Rica, we create a more peaceful world by bringing together an intentionally diverse community where we celebrate differences with more than 70+ nationalities represented and 80% of our students receiving scholarship support.  We provide a transformative educational experience grounded on experiential learning to empower our students to become empathic agents of change committed to shaping a better future.

title: Emergency Response in Cagayan
description: This project will support Global Peace Foundation Philippines' emergency response efforts for hundreds of families affected in Sanchez Mira, Cagayan Province in the Philippines as the whole province is currently submerged in floodwater. Each family will receive emergency supplies (food and medicine), water purifier, and solar lantern to assist them as they recover and rebuild.

title: Empower 40 Children with Disabilities in Kenya
description: Early Milestones plans to support 40 children aged 0-8 years Diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy from Kiandutu Slums in Thika, Kenya by providing 1 year therapy services that are 100% catered for to promote their Independence. These children are desperately poor and cannot afford the much needed healthcare services that will help them thrive. As a result, they are at risk of disability. Their Mothers will also be trained and educated for free on the best way to take care of their children at home.

title: Support Children Education in Rural Liberia
description: More than half (51.1%) of the Liberian population reside in urban areas (MSU, 2020), and education expenditure is about 3.8% of the GDP.  According to UNICEF, Liberia has the world's largest out-of-school children, with 56% of primary-school-age children currently missing out on education,15-20 % of 6-14 years out of class 54% of children completing primary school. We will help address the need by providing school fees, learning materials, exercise books.

title: Save 500 slum families from COVID19 in Uganda
description: CESA-Uganda intends to save Kamwokya slum families from getting infected with COVID19 by providing Hands free wash taps-a new technology of washing hands without touching. 500 out of 2,000 families are targeted in this project at estimated cost of $50,400. The project will also select and train 10 people as community based health trainers (COBAHTs) & practically train them in COVID19 prevention, soap,mask & Hands free tippy taps making to support other people for sustainability

title: Help build a safe home for street girls in Malawi
description: Our Therapeutic Centre for Street Girls in Malawi will effectively rescue and house up to 60 girls between the ages of 0-18. Through the implementation of specific trauma informed models of care, we will provide them with a secure, loving environment that empowers them to become self-reliant, productive and healthy members of their communities, setting them on the path to become leaders for social change. Please help us reach our goal, and support these girls to not only survive, but thrive!

title: Dealing with Water shortage in Sierra Leone
description: Sierra Leone is one of the poorest country in West Africa. This country fought a war between 1996 - 2006.  Most of the government establishment were destroyed, this including the water facilities.  As a result of this, many cities are faced with acute water shortage.  Most women and children have to go in search of water in the Eastern part of Freetown.  This takes them for five to six hours a day.  This project is for the provision of a borehole in Orogu new site , Allen town, Freetown.

title: Covid 19---A Love Story
description: How a small therapeutic riding center in NH plans to give the pandemic a KICK!  Fighting back against depression and isolation in the time of Covid 19.

title: A COMPUTER FOR EVERY STUDENT
description: According to UNESCO,  24,901,925 students in Turkey have been affected by school closures due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Education is being provided through online distance learning platforms and access to a computer at home is a prerequisite to use these platforms. However, only 40% of disadvantaged students have a computer at home in Turkey. Therefore, CYDD  started a campaign to provide computers to disadvantaged students who are already getting scholarship from CYDD.

title: Re-Open a Community Library Hit by Hurricane Eta
description: This project will provide necessary funding to re-open Riecken Community Library La Libertad that provides access to information, training programs and literacy skills to several hundred community members. The extensive damage caused by Hurricane Eta and subsequent flooding, closely followed by Hurricane Iota, requires repairing building infrastructure, and computers, replacing destroyed books and damaged furniture. The funding will be supplemented by required community investment.

title: Hurricane Eta and Iota Relief for Honduras
description: In Honduras, COVID-19 has hit very hard, with many people losing their jobs, food and medications becoming scarce, and prices skyrocketing. Hospitals are overrun and the COVID death toll continues to rise. Hurricane Eta has further devastated the country. It took Honduras over 20 years to recover from Hurricane Mitch, and now Hurricane Eta has caused similar devastation-this time during a pandemic. Mayor Potencial will help mitigate the effects by providing care packages and shelter.

title: Life saving supplies for displaced children
description: UNICEF provides displaced children in Syria, Lebanon and Jordan with winter clothing, medical kits, nutrition, and teaching materials to give hope in times COVID-19 poses an extra burden on the lives of these children. Join us and choose for a better 2021.

title: Get 15,000 Kenyan children safely back to school
description: Education has been on hold for thousands of Kenyan children since schools closed their doors in March 2020 as a result of the COVID-19 crisis.  As schools in Nairobi's informal settlements prepare to reopen in January 2021 without any government support, they need your help to create a safe space for children to return to learning.  Dignitas believes that all schools should be vibrant places for children to thrive and succeed so that no child is left behind!

title: End cruelty to bears in the bear bile industry
description: Bears held in captivity for their bile across Asia endure a lifetime of intense physical and mental suffering. They are confined to tiny cages, unable to express their natural behaviours and forced to undergo torturously painful extractions - sometimes daily. We are raising public awareness, microchipping and monitoring captive bears and improving the legal protection of bears. Together, we can bring a permanent end to this cruel and unnecessary industry.

title: Botswana's future environmental stewards
description: This project will provide stimulating and fun environmental education for 4 schools (140 students) in rural Botswana; teaching children ecological concepts, environmental awareness and problem-solving through games and hands-on activities. These activities will build the environmental stewards of tomorrow, enabling them to tackle the issues rural communities face, and will increasingly face due to climatic changes and competition for resources, as well as prepare them for future employment.

title: Braille Education for Blind Children in Ethiopia
description: Ethiopia is believed to have the world's highest rates of blindness and low vision. Based on the assessment of the presenting visual acuity, the national prevalence of blindness is 1.6% and that of low vision 3.7%. There is accessibility issue and limited special education schools for the visually impaired. Hence, this project is designed to undertake Braille education program  for  20  children with visual impairment a year in order to integrate them in the formal education system.

title: Help Kenya's Only Community-Run Elephant Sanctuary
description: Reteti Elephant Sanctuary aims to reunite, rescue, rehabilitate and re-release orphaned and abandoned elephant calves from across the north Kenya landscape, whilst creating much needed benefits for more than 100 local people. As a community-run project, Reteti requires ongoing funds for milk, medical care, rescues  and staff salaries, as we give injured, traumatised or abandoned elephants a second chance at life.

title: Empowering Female Refugees in the Netherlands
description: She Matters' Lotus Flower Programme provides 9 weeks of career readiness training, mentorship and job placement opportunities for female newcomers in the Netherlands. Our program provides opportunities to empower women who have overcome tremendous odds to gain transferable skills and earn a living wage. It transforms lives and has an immediate positive impact on our participants, communities and economy.

title: Support 65 Children with Special Needs in Beirut
description: Join our journey in lifting the spirits of Lebanese children with special needs this Christmas season. This project aims to bring a smile to the faces of children with special needs, whose homes and education were affected by the Beirut explosion, by providing them with an individual gift box, each including a tablet, educative tool and school supplies, enabling them to continue their online studies. In challenging year in Lebanon, these children need our love, care and attention more than ever.

title: Women in coffee: Empower Today Reimagine Tomorrow.
description: The International Women's Coffee Alliance (IWCA) Uganda Chapter is reimagining the future - one where families and communities thrive because women are empowered. This challenging work requires dedicated staff with a track record for executing with excellence. The project will collect resources to sustain the three Chapter Secretariat staff.

title: Teaching children in Chiapas how to grow forests
description: Can you imagine a world with no trees? The principal cause of deforestation in Chiapas is the lost of traditions among indigenous communities. Their way of living which is centered in the use of wood for heat, cooking, building and also the agriculture methods burning the ground are causing an accelerated destruction of the forests. Teaching the children how to create and protect the forests is centered in recovering the tradition of caring for nature and producing wood to cover their needs.

title: Cape CARES: Returning to Honduras
description: With your help, Cape CARES will get back to providing free medical and dental care to the southwest region of Honduras, THIS YEAR! We cannot do it without you!

title: Empowering L.A. Youth to be Great Leaders
description: YRTTF's enrichment program is designed to empower and prepare youth to a successful work path in career development and life skills. Our workshops and mentorship provide youth with opportunities to gain work and volunteer experience, while learning the skills to be great leaders for their community.  By introducing these skills early on, youth have a greater chance of success by building confidence, learning responsibility, and preventing poverty and homelessness in Los Angeles.

title: Educating the Next Generation of Global Leaders
description: This project will make high-quality educational events and programs on international affairs, including talks, conferences, and competitions, more accessible to the 150,000-plus students in Orange County. While the world becomes more interconnected than ever, education on world issues is still lacking in our communities. With this project, younger audience will be exposed to the insights shared by leaders more closely, and learn and share knowledge of world issues among their peers nationwide.

title: Hurricane Iota Relief Fund
description: Hurricane Iota, a category 5 hurricane, made landfall in Nicaragua with sustained winds of 155 miles an hour and unleashed mudslides, tore apart buildings and left thousands homeless across Central America. This relief fund will support emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. As possible, the fund will transition to provide long-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support Hurricane Iota relief and recovery efforts in the impacted countries.

title: Providing 570 students with digital education (Gt)
description: This project will allow us to buy tablets for our secondary and high school students. The tablets will be used as an educational device, they will complement face-to-face education and will allow the students to access education from home when needed, making it more dynamic, considering the "new normal" that the COVID-19 pandemic has brought.

title: Help 1,000 babies reach their 5th birthday - Kenya
description: This project will support women to give birth safely and have access to essential services ensuring their baby will survive and thrive to celebrate their 5th birthday.  COVID-19 has reversed progress made in supporting mothers and babies in poor and marginalised communities in Kericho County, Kenya.  Inaccessible health services, fear of COVID-19, lack of soap and water has increased unsupervised home births which risk the lives of mothers and babies.  Help us reverse this trend.

title: Support Displaced Families This Winter
description: This has been an especially challenging year, with COVID-19 impacting all of us. For refugee and displaced families, the future is particularly uncertain. Families living in crowded refugee camps find social distancing impossible. In countries already ravaged by years of war, their weakened health systems lack doctors, ventilators, medicine, and testing capabilities.  Your gift will help us provide communities with vital assistance, including clean water, lifesaving food, and face masks.

title: Reusable Sanitary Pads for 5,000 Girls in Nigeria
description: The She Needs A Pad Project will provide Menstrual Hygiene Management (MHM) education and empowerment to 500 girls and women in rural underserved communities in Nigeria. It will provide menstrual materials and supplies and teach the production of reusable pads. Small peer discussion groups would be organized to ensure adequate and accurate information is discussed on menstruation and related matters.

title: Intellectual Disability needs attention in Sindh
description: NDF has established "NDF REHAB CENTER" in Nawabshah, which is run by grants, individual philanthropy, Zakat, to cater needs of rehabilitation services like Physiotherapy, Psychotherapy, Speech Therapy, Occupational Therapy, non formal Education & sports for 100+ children with boarding & Day Care. This is only facility in rural area of Sindh. It needs your attention to donate please. NDF scaled up services in Larkana with new unit to reach remote areas of Sindh. NDF 02 centers need your kind help

title: Cancer school program detects cancer early in SA
description: Our cancer school programme educates students about the importance of detecting cancer early and how to support cancer patients in their communities. Education is the best weapon against cancer, which lacks due to the diverse society in South Africa, where cultural taboos, stigmas and a lack of knowledge about the subject is plentiful. One student's educational goodie bag is likely to reach 7 others due to the household situation in South Africa. We educate about cancer for US$ 1.10 per student.

title: Flood Victims Emergency Response Fund
description: This project will provide emergency food and non-food items to 100 vulnerable households representing over 500 individuals (women, children, elderly and persons with disabilities) that have been displaced by recent floods, have lost all properties/crops and are now sheltered in schools, churches, and make shift structures in the refugee settlements. The overall goal is to avert the looming danger of malaria, pneumonia, hunger and malnutrition.

title: Enhancing the Nutrition of 1000 Children in Abuja
description: This project tends to provide and enhance the nutritional requirements of malnourished children in Abuja Communities. It will help reduce the mother child mortality rate and promote healthy living among vulnerable children in rural areas including expectant mothers. It will help reduce complications associated with mineral and essential micronutrients deficiency at child birth, build a strong immune system and healthy living in COVID-19.

title: Help Support 673 Disadvantaged Benin Schoolgirls
description: On page 25 of the "Plan Sectoriel de l'Education" it is written: "Despite its progress, Benin is still ranked 166th out of 177 countries worldwide". At this Covid-19 time in Kpodaha, this poverty is influencing many girls. They are often out of school, marginalized and plagued by backward traditions, starvation and diseases too. The few girls who survive forced marriage and child trafficking are the most affected. This project will empower 673 countryside girls to be educated and emancipated.

title: Support Legal Services for Zambian Children
description: This projects aims to provide access to legal assistance for children who come into conflict with the law as well as social services to children who are detained in and released from correctional facilities. Legal representation will be provided to ensure that all child cases undergo fair trial devoid of prejudiced judgement. Children and families will be provided with various types of social support during the child's detention and after the child's release including food and therapy.

title: The Aviation Education 4 Kids Workshop
description: Youth Inspiration Nation's mission is to provide motivation, inspiration and education through aviation. Our program serves over 100 kids annually. We teach our young aviators the fundamentals of flight, the science behind keeping an aircraft in the air, test their skills with building activities, and actually teach them how to fly in static and full motion flight simulators. Aviation education improves focus, builds self-confidence, and exposes kids to a multitude of STEM related professions.

title: Empower 1500 Orphan & Vulnerable Children in Kenya
description: This project will provide   food, Sanitary towels, inner wears, Hygiene items, hand washing Systems,face mask, build empowerment center, training, clean water, guidance and counselling  to 1500 Orphan and Vulnerable children  subjected  sexual abuse,child labour and psychological stress in Kenya. The emergence of COVID-19 has compelled impoverished girls to indulge in sex in exchange for food, sanitary towels resulting to child pregnancies and  child marriages, STIs and HIV/AIDs infections.

title: Help Root Foundation build a children center.
description: After 8 years renting the facility that serves as a safe space for over 300 hundred children every year, Root Foundation is raising the money to purchase the building to serve as the children center. If Root Foundation achieves this milestone, the organization will be able to own a building that is more children and youth friendly, more education friendly and be able to spend more money on personal development and scholarships for more vulnerable children.

title: Skills for 65 Disadvantaged Teens in Ghana
description: The project will provide skills training and mentoring opportunities for 65 girls from disadvantaged backgrounds, some of whom are inmates of a Girls Correctional Center in Accra, Ghana. The skills training will be in garment making, hair dressing, catering and small business management.    Young offenders and youth from disadvantaged backgrounds often need greater support to complete their education, learn skills, build a family and participate fully in society as responsible citizens.

title: Shield the elderly from loneliness and isolation
description: Covid-19 has hit the Halstead Day Centre hard.  The work of this much valued centre, which supports its members to enjoy Independent Living, is being frustrated by current restrictions of the pandemic. The number attending is now limited to 6, whilst the day to day running costs that ordinarily provide facilities for 20 members, remain much the same. Our aim is for the Centre to maintain the excellent service that it provides to the elderly people of Halstead and the surrounding villages.

title: Wakashio Recovery Action Plan
description: The MV Wakashio ran aground less than 2 km away from Ile aux Aigrettes (IAA), an island nature reserve par excellence managed by the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation (BirdLife Partner & IUCN member). 800 tons of oil spilled out in the lagoon, heavily impacting on the marine and land ecosystems. IAA is home to sub-populations of rare endemic plants and animals. MWF plant and animal biologists, apart from having to carry out the normal routine work now have to investigate the impact of the oil spill.

title: Inspire Girls around the world to aim high!
description: We believe in the power of role models. Our organisation seeks to raise the aspirations of young girls around the world by connecting them with amazing women. By introducing girls aged 10-15 to a variety of careers and options, we can combat the gender stereotypes which still play a major role in their future education and career choices. We work with thousands of volunteers across the world to help empower young girls to follow their dreams.

title: Teach 3,000 Indonesian Children to Read
description: Reading is the beginning of a child's education, but more than half of Indonesian children leave primary school unable to read and understand a simple text.*  This project will equip teachers working in poor communities with high-quality teaching materials and inspiring practical training, enabling them to spark a love of reading in children from poor communities in Indonesia.  *See https://www.sayasukamembaca.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Indonesia-Learning-Poverty-Brief-2021.pdf

title: Give seeds to Women Farmers of Burkina Faso
description: The money you donate here is added to a FarmWallet and used to subsidize seeds to smallholder women farmers of Binde in the South-Central region of Burkina Faso. This also provides training on the production of solid and liquid compost to improve food security through regenerative agriculture, with an emphasis on community-based, participatory methods. Through this program, women are organized into agricultural cooperatives to give them more bargaining power.

title: SUPPORT 500 WOMEN TO ACCESS HEALTH CARE IN NIGERIA
description: Greater Hands Foundation intends to support 500 most vulnerable pregnant women and girls in Ikom Local government area (LGA) of Cross River State, Nigeria with basic health care social support services that encourages facility services uptake and improved mechanism to cope with  covid-19 and post pandemic health challenges, also providing 300 young women and girls of reproductive age with sanitary pads, addressing gender gaps and engender improved health and well-being of the marginalised women.

title: Vinnies COVID-19 Appeal (NSW, Australia)
description: As a result of COVID-19, many Australian families are experiencing job loss or hardship in these uncertain times. Children are particularly impacted by the distress of their parents.  St Vincent de Paul Society NSW is working with families to reduce the risk of homelessness. An emergency food hamper may not seem like something that can change a life - but it is. That is why a donation is so important.   On Giving Tuesday help provide essential support to vulnerable families by making a donation.

title: Support CT Refugee Women and their Families
description: Our mission is to help build brighter futures for refugee women and children in the Connecticut area. We envision a community that respects and celebrates diversity and provides equity of opportunity to all members. We provide refugee and immigrant families with ESL classes, health literacy classes, and prepare our clients to take the CT DMV driver's license examination. All of our services aim to empower refugee women to embrace their independence and autonomy within their communities.

title: The Friends of Arhaus Children's Home
description: The Friends of Arhaus Children's Home is the first home in Everest region to provide safe, quality, & free educational opportunities for children, especially those who are orphaned, abandoned and vulnerable, i.e., at high risk of trafficking, forced child labor, & abuse, a safe place to live; educational opportunities; & life skills training such as farming, employment in tourism, leadership &  business sectors, and finding & creating new opportunities in their own social background & culture.

title: Rainforest and Turtle Conservation In Costa Rica
description: With a primary focus on marine & wildlife conservation, in Costa Rica, our projects support the conservation of rainforest and sea turtles. Situated in a landscape of bursting biodiversity, we work with local organizations and communities to conduct research and activities which contribute towards the management of the National Park and the ongoing conservation of this amazing biodiversity hotspot and the endangered species which depend upon it.

title: Help our Holistic Programs Shine in 2021
description: Walk alongside us as we fight to break the generational cycle of poverty in Kenya through holistic artisan empowerment. Our goal is to raise $100,000 by year-end to cover all expenses for our 2021 holistic programs, which are at the heart of our mission.  Imani Collective is socioeconomic empowerment program centered around creating employment opportunities, as well as the necessary resources and community support to raise up artisans holistically.

title: Help 100 Children in Kayole in Nairobi
description: Tunaweza Pamoja Children's Centre helps neglected, needy, orphaned, vulnerable, deprived and destitute children mostly from the Kayole-Soweto slum area and also from the Children's Department. We help the children by paying their school fees, giving them shelter, food, clothing and medical attention. We provide a loving and safe, family environment that enables children the right to a happy, educated, skilled and healthy life. Currently we are helping 100 children aged between 3 to 15 years.

title: At great risk of being left behind
description: Since March, due to Covid, the needs of young people with special needs have been neglected by the Department of Education, as they are unable to study or receive therapies and services that are necessary to continue their education.  It is widely recognized that remote education is not adequate for this exceptional population. The project seeks to defend the rights of this under-served population by ensuring they receive some form of face-to-face education and other essential services.

title: "We Got Us!" Tiny Homes for Teens
description: Utilizing a Mutual Aid Framework, we will offer community living for up to 4 weeks to Detroit teens experiencing recurrent trauma. The four tiny homes will be stationed at our "Sincerely, Detroit" Youth-led Community House. Youth will help build these homes where other youth can employ as a safe haven to call home as they heal, and find resources and support. Additionally, the house will provide culturally-rooted trauma-informed care, wraparound services, and utilize restorative practices.

title: ReNew Hope for Autism in Covid Times
description: Family dynamics has a big impact on a family's wellbeing. When a member(s) has autism, designing, implementing and managing a structured, predictable environment, and routine improves day to day living for all. We provide our families and caregivers tailor-made personal advice, guidance and intervention strategies to address their family dynamics. We have re-invented our services to help and accompany our families meet their needs, while ensuring our community stays safe, healthy and productive.

title: Save the Seahorses of Mozambique
description: This project will help protect seahorses of Vilankulo, Mozambique that are particularly vulnerable to poaching since Covid-19 decimated tourism. We will help the village fisheries committee by guiding them and equipping them with them with bouys, kayaks, snorkel gear and training to demarcate and patrol protected seahorse habitats to keep the poachers out and let biodiversity thrive.

title: Enhancing  Maternal and Child Health in Liberia
description: The project seeks to improve the health status of Mother and Child and improved access and quality Reproductive and Child Health services with focused attention to the most vulnerable sections of the society. The project will conduct primary Health check-ups, Antenatal & Post natal care; provide vitamins A and deworming, multivitamins and micronutrient. The project will provide an opportunity to identify and reduce existing health risks in mothers and children and prevent future health problems.

title: Against the Odds - Education for 230 Adults
description: As of January 1, 2021, Creamos will implement an Adult Education Program, enrolling 230 adults in government-accredited elementary, middle and high school. This program ensures that everyone has the opportunity to study, no matter their age, gender, economic status or background.

title: changing communities through sport  for 500 kids
description: We use sports to build relations with children in disadvantaged communities of Mount Hampden. We provide recreation, identify neglected but talented children, know them through fun activities during sports time, and help some return to school. Our aim is not to target bright kids but afford equal life opportunities including digital literacy.  The need to provide a school has risen due to the imminent removal of children from land earmarked for govt projects. Their lives cant stall

title: Agroecology for farmers & nature health in Ecuador
description: This project will duplicate the actual number of Mushuk Tukuy Agroecological farmers network and their direct beneficiaries. The network member produces for self-consumption and sells their surplus products such as vegetables, cereals, medicinal plants, chickens, eggs, honey, and community tourism services.The network currently direct benefits 100 individuals from three local communities that belong to Pintag and San Jose de Minas Villages located in the Pichincha Province, Ecuador.

title: Disability Advocate Training in Zambia
description: Special Hope Network (SHN) currently has 6 Community Care Centers (CCC) that work with children with intellectual disabilities and their caregivers in specific compounds (high density neighborhoods) around Lusaka, Zambia. In 2021, our Community Outreach Team began partnering with schools, churches, clinics and other local community members in those compounds that have a CCC, to host Disability Advocacy Trainings.

title: Education of Mayan Midwives in Guatemala
description: Maya Midwifery International supports training of indigenous midwives in Xela, Guatemala. Through formal nursing education, young midwives - who have historically been excluded from the formal Guatemalan health care system- are able to integrate the traditional wisdom of indigenous midwifery with contemporary medical practice, allowing them to provide up-to-date care in the Asociacion de las Comadronas del Area Mam (ACAM) birthing center located just outside of Xela.

title: Give 470 Colombian children a fair chance
description: This project will help the Portal Foundation protect and educate 470 children born to prison inmates or from low-income, vulnerable Colombian families. The Foundation, created in 1968 and located in the Picota prison in Bogota, is on the brink of collapse as revenue has dried up because of the Covid pandemic. The Foundation gives these children, ages 6 months to 12 years, opportunities to develop physically, intellectually, emotionally, and spiritually to become successful adults.

title: 10,000 Ruby Cups for 10,000 Girls in Kenya
description: Poverty and lack of access to menstrual products in rural Kenya often force young school girls to resort to unhygienic solutions and miss school while they are on their period. Our project aims to equip 10,000 girls with a comprehensive menstrual health education and a long term solution: a Ruby Cup. These cups last for up to 10 years and ensure that no girls need to stay home while she is menstruating. Girls face enough barriers to their education, their period should not be one of them.

title: Educate to Empower Girls Living in Poverty!
description: An educational mentoring program to empower at-risk girls in Egypt. It provides underprivileged adolescent girls with access to education, leadership, life skills development opportunities: a character development program, nutritional healthy lifestyle techniques, anti-bullying, and sexual harassment awareness. The training is delivered in a nurturing and safe environment. By equipping 20 instrumental facilitators & 100 mothers, Heya Masr helps girls stay in school and avoid child marriage.

title: HELP RURAL CHILDREN OF ZIMBABWE
description: This organisation was formed after being moved by the story of a grandmother who walked several miles in search of a pencil so that her grandchild could attend school Pencils and Smiles is an initiative that aims to alleviate the effects of poverty, empower neglected communities, improve standards of living and seeks to bridge the gap between education and poverty. We started by distributing pencils to every child, we are now looking into building libraries and building toilets for rural schools

title: Women Empowerment Through Skill Training
description: BASAMH aims to empower poor women through skill training on sewing and tailoring so that it provides them the opportunity for self-employment. A small support and proper guidance can help these women start a small business and help them survive on a monthly basis. The project is focused on destitute women in Bangladesh including Rohingya refugees.

title: GIVE THE GIFT OF KNOWLEDGE
description: Iraqi orphans and children from poor families attend public schools in Iraq, where class sizes average of 75 students. Many of these children have physical or cognitive disabilities, but no one knows that. Imagine being deaf from birth, but not one person in your life realizes that you cannot hear. Imagine being autistic and being beaten daily because no one realizes that you are autistic. These are challenges Iraqi orphans and poor children face in their lives.

title: Giving Well University Tour - Invest in the Future
description: "Giving Well University Tour - Invest in the Future" which will take place from 17 March to 17 April, aims to raise awareness of Vietnamese students about the local nonprofit community and giving well in Vietnam. The tour targets to help 400 students from LIN's four partner universities to access the knowledge about the local nonprofits, social impact, as well as provide tools and skills for the students to get involved and play an active role in creating positive changes in the community.

title: Help End the Illegal Wildlife Trade in Vietnam
description: The illegal wildlife trade is destroying our Earth, pushing endangered species to extinction, and threatening public health on a globally deadly scale. Vietnam is a major player in the widespread trafficking of wildlife, with high demand for wildlife, and as a wildlife trafficking hub. Education for Nature - Vietnam (ENV), the first of its kind in Vietnam, is a local NGO fighting to end Vietnam's illegal wildlife trade by educating the public and taking strategic actions against wildlife crime.

title: Stationery Kits for 250 Children with Disabilities
description: Mother Charitable Foundation (MCF) is a registered nongovernment initiative working for the children with disabilities, who are often at a disadvantage with state approaches in Sri Lanka. Hence MCF plans to provide 250 kits of stationery to 250 children with disabilities selected from remote areas in Sri Lanka where the state attention & approaches to assist them are little to zero. The selected children will be from underprivileged families with low income, ensuring their rights for education.

title: Educate 150 disabled girls amidst covid in mpigi
description: Girls with disabilities in our community suffer from sexual violence and education related challenges. This project will support 150 disabled girls in Mpigi district Uganda return back to school amidst COVID 19. It will provide scholastic materials including school bags, books, pens, sanitary towels and school uniforms. Hold Behavioral change, life skills, sexual reproductive health rights sessions with girls, parents $ care takers and hold community radio talk shows.

title: 1 Sleeping Bag for 1 Life
description: Due to the pandemic and the collapse of the economy, Nepal is facing a humanitarian disaster of an unprecedented scale! 40% of Nepal's population, approximately 12 million people, is poor.  Most of these people live in villages in higher altitudes between 500m and 1500m. For many children, the combination of malnourishment and a lack of  adequate protection from the freezing cold will have fatal consequences. The project aims to provide Sleeping bags to this target group.

title: Empower 50 child brides with income generation CMR
description: This project will set up and equip 4 vocational skills training centers for empowerment of women, girls and OVCs, to learn specific trades. It will provide small start up capital to 50 child brides to own small businesses for income generating activities, provide full academic support for continued education to 20 girls at risk. It will build a shelter to provide safe space to victims of abuse for healing and reinsertion. It will also provide daily basic bodily upkeep and health needs to victims

title: Help Save Lily the Pangolin
description: As with many pangolins rescued from the illegal wildlife trade, Lily had been held captive for a number of weeks with no food or water and so she was found in a critical condition. She was severely dehydrated and under weight.  Did you know 288 Pangolins are snatched from the wild every day! Every life counts and it is imperative that she is helped back to prime health and fitness as quickly as possible. We need your help to return her to where she belongs, the wild!

title: Help Children Learn Online During Covid-19
description: MyBodhiTree.org is building Modern Learning Centers (MLCs) across Thailand within already established schools. We provide the equipment, online tools (and a fresh coat of paint for the room) so that teachers can continue teaching online even while quarantine measures are being implimented. With your help we can do this all for FREE.

title: Save a new life by supporting pregnant woman
description: The aim of the project is to help pregnant women living in a difficult emotional or financial situation to see that they are capable of raising a child. Also to support women in need who have already given birth so they can focus on their emotional well-being. We want to provide women and babies with necessary hygiene and other items so that their basic needs are met. Also to offer psychological counselling to both pregnant women and those who have just given birth, all of which at no cost.

title: Build classes/kitchen for 180 orphans in Namibia
description: After SchoolProgramme for Orphans and Vulnerable Children (ASPOVC) plans to build three Classrooms and a kitchen to provide free education and free nutritious meal to 180 orphans and vulnerable children infected and affected by HIV/AIDS or vulnerable in Eenhana town.

title: Give Clean Water & Energy to 350 Somali Families
description: There is an urgent need for safe water, phone charging and lighting in Puntland, Somalia. The OffGridBox will serve over 2,400 Somalis, who will get access to clean energy and clean water at an extremely low price with no impact on the environment. The box will employ 2 local women, and its maintenance costs will be shared with local landowners.  This is an all-in-one easy-to-install system that uses solar energy to purify water and distribute energy for local dates production.

title: Relief for Refugees in Greece's Largest Camp
description: Lighthouse Relief provides a rich array of fun activities to support the mental health and psychosocial well-being of children, teens, and women in Ritsona refugee camp.  Sports, arts and crafts, language classes, music lessons, a library, and more offer residents a welcome respite from the monotony of life in a dreary, isolated camp and opportunities to release trauma-induced stress.   This support helps build resilience in the face of increasingly harsh conditions for refugees in Greece.

title: Trauma Counseling for Child Survivors of War
description: This project will provide Trauma Counseling Programs and Psycho-Social Support to 2500 children and youth that have survived civil war in Uganda and South Sudan.   Music, Dance, Art and Play Therapy Programs will be provided by our trained staff to help children and youth express and share and alleviate trauma during civil war in northern Uganda and South Sudan.  Trauma Counseling Training will also be provided for Teachers and Community Leaders to ensure that this program continues for others.

title: Engage 1000 women on resilient farming in Cameroon
description: CDVTA plans to engage 1000 rural women farmers on climate-adapted resilient food systems in Cameroon. Project will train 720 women through innovative crop farming necessary for improved food security, increased income and natural ecosystem preservation. Project will use vegetative methods to empower farmers on tree production, while protecting dry farmlands and fighting climate change. Project will be participatory with farmers able to adapt and develop their own local farming best practices

title: Moringa for Health and Water Purification
description: Moringa for Health and Water Purification project will provide 500 Community Members from Tharaka Nithi County with 50 Moringa tree each to plant on their farms. Planting these high yield trees will go a long way to address malnutrition and contaminated water in Tharaka Nithi County.

title: WErto: Gardening that connects people
description: This project will help 50 low-income families start a WErto, an organized community that shares resources and knowledge to jointly grow organic produce. WErto uses an innovative model that, unlike a conventional community garden, requires no common space to cultivate.

title: Enhancing 500 child-headed households in Ha Sekake
description: You only know you need it when it's gone!  It is very unfortunate that they didn't choose to lose their parents at this early age! The elderly in the child headed household experience a lifelong struggle having to bear their own burden while also striving to support their siblings. SMARTD seeks to make a difference; enhancing their livelihoods by supporting nutrition and micro income generation, by providing 500 households in and around Ha Sekake with vegetable seeds for production.

title: 60 special children need your love during COVID-19
description: COVID-19 is a time when the 'HAVES' should help the 'HAVE NOTS'. This project is specifically aimed at sustaining 60 underprivileged families with seriously disabled special children, by providing much needed food and sanitary aids,   Corona virus pandemic has affected people globally, confining them to their homes and denying them the means of earning and sustaining their families.  Special children are the most affected as their cries fall on deaf ears. Our aim is to help such community.

title: Empower 30 Malawian Families with Solar Irrigation
description: Eagles will build a solar irrigation system for 30 farming families in Malawi. The families will be able to eat throughout the year and sell extra food to pay for school fees and medical bills. The farming families will provide food for 12 surrounding villages. We will train the families to maintain  the system and ensure ownership through a participatory process that shifts mindsets from dependency to determination, using local resources, including the sun, to solve their own problems.

title: Child right and orphanage care
description: HRID is a national organization in south Sudan working to uplift children that have been seperated with their families as a result of war, Mahad orphanage center is located in Juba with around 500 children mostly at age renging from 3 years to 15 years old   We are calling upon any will individuals or organizations to join hand with us and raise this young generation   Luck of food, cleaning materials, clean water and shelter and sleeping mattresses are some of the biggest challenges We have

title: LGBTIQ+ Refugees in Southern Africa
description: Ntsako Wa Wena will support LGBTQ+ refugees from across Africa in South Africa through provision of destitution services, asylum support, legal service provision, facilitating for the refugees to obtain support to further their education or entrepreneurship development and access to health related services that include psycho-social support  and refugee activity co-ordination.  This project aims at livelihood improvements of the LGBTQ+ community and creating a 'Home' away from 'Home.'

title: EMPOWER 650 UGANDAN GIRLS TO CREATE MENSTRUAL PADS
description: This project will equip 650 girls with skills in making re-usable menstrual pads and provide counseling services to enable girls cope with menstrual-related emotional challenges like fear, shame, distraction, confusion, mood swings and the physical discomfort. We will provide health education so as to dispel the myths associated with menstruation and empower the girls to appropriately manage their lives during such periods.

title: Funding for Echocardiography Heard Defects
description: We are working with children diagnosed with congenital heart defects (CHD) born in underprivileged families. We have been reaching out to such children and families through our various programs.  After 7 years, we are proud to say that we have impacted more than 15000 children through free screening for congenital heart diseases- PraDAAN program Saved 54 lives by providing financial assistance for treatment to the families- CHF HRIDAAN program

title: Construct Autism Computer Learning Centre in Ghana
description: The project seeks to established Autism Computer Learning Centre , a software  educational programme  which will be designed for  500 children with autism Spectrum Disorder  condition ,parents and guardians and professionals that would offer a comprehensive curriculum , individual assessment tools ,staff and parent training modules ,data tracking and progress reporting and professional support alternatives programmes.

title: Proper Sanitation for Village in Coastal Ecuador
description: Imagine having to defecate in a plastic bag!  This is the only option for many  residents in San Raymundo II, a coastal Ecuadorian village rising from the dust of a drained swamp and struggling to become a community.  This project will bring bathroom facilities to about 100 families in total, creating a much cleaner, healthier environment for all. Only $275 per bathroom will give residents a proper toilet which provides them with improved hygiene and restored dignity.  No more pooping in bags!

title: Support San Andres, the Caribbean region and Choco
description: Thank you for coming here and looking for ways to help families in poverty.  If you are here it is because you know the crisis that San Andres, Providencia, the Caribbean region are going through due to Hurricane Iota and the serious floods that Choco is experiencing and you want to help rebuild and support the affected families

title: Soap-making programme to help 900 Ugandan children
description: A proven measure to curb the spread of Covid-19 is to wash your hands with soap and water - but what do you do if you don't have soap?   Just a Drop has previously provided Buwambo Primary School in Uganda with safe water and hygiene education, but now they need a sustainable supply of soap. Help Just a Drop implement a soap-making programme and help 900 children stay healthy by washing their hands! The programme will also help the school prosper,  generating income by selling the excess soap.

title: Support children without family care
description: This project aims to assist 7,000 vulnerable children and youth without family care or at risk of losing it, also assisting families who depend on our support, affected by COVID 19 pandemic. We would cover the basic needs in terms of food, hygiene, psychosocial and educational support at 5 provinces in Argentina: Lujan, Rosario, Mar del Plata, Cordoba and Obera.

title: "Because every child needs a Super Heroe"
description: Super Heroes will rebuild 2 classrooms of Jose Acevedo Alvarez School in Aguadilla Puerto Rico to provide Montessori education, specialized therapy and parental assistance to 20 children (age1-6) with impairments whos family lack the economic resources to cost these essential need.   The funds will go towards the Childs's educational cost and furnishing the classrooms.

title: Christmas boxes for children living in Refuges
description: Due to COVID-19 cases of Domestic abuse have risen dramatically. Many more children than ever before are now living in Refuges, as their homes are no longer safe. Parents are often not able to afford even basic necessities, as many families fled with just what they were wearing. Life is stressful enough for victims of violence but even more so at this time of year if you are worrying about the possibility of not having a Christmas/Seasonal Holiday gift for your child/ren on Christmas Day.

title: T:>Care
description: In solidarity and alliance, T:>Works establishes and administers T:>Care - a Creative Action Resilience Enabling initiative to support projects created and developed by women to make positive change in our communities. This year's projects include some of the causes and organisations that are featured in the Women of N.O.W. digital exhibition.

title: Build a Refugee Social Innovation Lab in Cyprus
description: Project Phoenix is launching "Constellation", a unique social innovation lab and entrepreneurship space co-created with the refugee community in Nicosia, Cyprus. The space will serve as a workspace and community space for refugee-led projects to develop and sell their products. In addition to providing a entrepreneurial hub and safe space, Constellation will organize mentoring and coaching sessions, workshops and events. In the future we plan to add a community kitchen, a cafe and more.

title: Give a Saving Hand to A Sick Child
description: Currently Kodike County health statistics shows 90% of people live in poverty, thus finding it hard for parents to access proper medical care for their children. Common health problems can turn into a lifetime of serious health conditions. This project will build a healthy community of Kodike in Eastern Uganda, with young healthy people through the initiative to provide preventive information to the community and easy access to proper medical care as well as medicines.to sick children.

title: One Million Moms OFF Welfare (1MMOW)Strategic Plan
description: 11.9 million children live in poverty in the United States. Fifty-eight (58%) percent of all poor children live with single-mothers. By helping poor mothers nationwide access adequate training and support to earn higher incomes, we can alleviate mothers off of welfare and millions of children out of poverty.   Help support our strategic plan, 1MMOW toolkit, and web interface designed to educate and provide resources to help one million moms and their families escape welfare dependency.

title: MUTIMA CENTRE HEALS TRAUMA AT SOUTH KIVU -RD CONGO
description: Coopera Congo provides psychosocial treatment to heal the collective trauma of South Kivu people and build their resilience in the face of conflict, epidemics, and natural disasters. The MUTIMA Psychosocial Reference Center is under construction. The center includes specialized services for the psychological and psychiatric treatment of adults and children.  With this project, we will build 4 therapy rooms, hire 4 psychologists, and train them to care for 400 people per month.

title: Outdoor Learning Space for Children in Rural Nepal
description: This project will support our two schools & a hostel facility in two remote villages in Kalikot district in Western Nepal to buy new land & to manage the existing lands to be used as outdoor playing, learning & farming spaces for 248 students at the schools & for 30 orphans & children in need of support at the hostel facility. Consequently, the children will continue their education, enjoy outdoor learning, & feel safer & comfortable at school during these difficult times of COVID-19.

title: Fund High School Diploma for Mexican Deportees
description: This project will provide 10 Mexicans deported from the US with the opportunity to obtain a high school diploma, which will enable them to secure employment at higher wages in Mexico.

title: Central America Hurricane Relief Fund
description: Hurricane Iota and Eta made landfall in Nicaragua with sustained winds of 120-155 miles an hour and unleashed mudslides, tore apart buildings and left thousands homeless across Central America. This relief fund will support emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. As possible, the fund will transition to provide long-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support Hurricane relief and recovery efforts in Guatemala.

title: Help us fight child and womens malnutrition
description: The project consists of workshops for pregnant women and mothers with children up to 6 years old, to promote healthy eating habits and family relationships. Fruits, vegetables, simple recipes and seeds will be provided so that they can create their own garden and practice self sufficiency. We aspire to work with 300 families in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and train community center workers throughout the country to adopt and improve healthy habits with the children they assist.

title: Clean Water for 1,500 Children in Uganda
description: 20 million Ugandans lack access to clean water, leading to easily preventable diseases. Among those most at risk are children, whose developing immune systems can't handle the physical stress imposed by COVID-19, malnutrition, and waterborne diseases (the #2 killer of children). We will install our Purifaaya filter, which eliminates 99.9% of bacteria from water, and our handiClean handwashing station, in three schools in the District of Mityana, impacting 1,500 children and their families.

title: Empower environmental defenders in Mexico
description: People in many communities throughout Mexico have been deprived of their land and have suffered the destruction of their environment due to unsustainable megaprojects and political interests. We ask for your contribution in order to help us provide 10 communities in Mexico with  legal aid and fortify their capabilities so they can possess the legal tools to protect their land, their natural heritage and their human rights.

title: Redefining Community Development in Puerto Rico
description: This project is designed to deepen our work and address the need for profound social change in the Eastern region of Puerto Rico.  The goals are broad: fair recovery processes; prevention programs for our children; and economic development for communities. To do this, we are strengthening our role in the region and reimagining what community development can be.

title: Provide Fresh Meals to 30,000+ People in Florida
description: As COVID-19 continues to impact food security for many individuals, we must create more sustainable and viable options for producing healthy food in our communities. Marine Education Initiative seeks to launch an aquaponics food security effort to sustainably grow fresh vegetables and fish to help provide those in need with highly nutritious meals.

title: College Scholarship Program ,Ghana West Africa.
description: All students deserve a well-rounded education to prepare them for successful careers.  Two final-year high school students will be selected from each of the sixteen regions in Ghana, totaling 32 students, to be awarded a full-ride scholarship. The program is scheduled to start September 2021-2022 academic year. Together we will make an positive impact, as well as to give these needy but brilliant students from the rural areas of Ghana an opportunity  be productive members in their communities.

title: Chamwino Secondary School Fundraiser
description: We're raising money to provide additional books and e-readers for the students at Chamwino Secondary School in Tanzania through Worldreader.   Worldreader brings a free library of digital books to parents and caregivers via their mobile phones. This library enables children to continue learning from the safety of their homes while schools are disrupted.

title: Save 200 mothers from preventable deaths in Ghana
description: African Health Now plans to provide prenatal and postpartum health education, support access and engagement in maternal health and reproductive services, and COVID-19 resources to 200 expecting mothers through their Pregnancy School Program initiative. Upon completion of the program, expecting mothers will receive African Health Now's signature Maternity Go-Box" equipped with personal hygiene products, diapers, and other supplies to support new mothers and baby's during their first few weeks.

title: Sustainable Employment Skills by Programmable Arts
description: People with physical disabilities are facing  challenges to get trained in the latest STEM technologies. Robbinsville Innovation 4-H Club is anchored to provide formal and informal education systematically and enduringly in STEM Programmable Arts area. This program will help in setting up a State-of-the Art Technology Innovation drop in lab for FREE access to all in need. We also help in improving capacity to promote knowledge and competencies for sustainable development.

title: Educate 100 children with disabilities in Uganda
description: The project aims at providing access to education for 100 children with disabilities in slums of Makindye Division in Kampala with limited or no access to education in Uganda during and after the pandemic. AWDI plans to support 100 children with disabilities who always miss out on the opportunity to access to education services. They will be supplied with scholastic materials, reading and revision packages for their respective grades and attached to nearby teachers to teach and assess them.

title: Hope Hub: Resource Center Serves Community Needs
description: Things don't always go as planned. Those are the times our support networks matter most. Where would you be without those people who have your back? For many, Jake's is that group.  What started as a goal of helping 15 babies at an orphanage in Peru grew to a nonprofit able to support diverse hygiene and basic modern needs.

title: Keep a Girl child safe and Educated in Malawi
description: A Girl Child is at risk of being raped, dropping out of school because of lack of academic resources, leading to early marriages. Malawi has registered an extremely increase (63%) in teen pregnancies and marriages especially during this period of COVID-19 pandemic. Our project aims at providing access to academic resources to the less privileged girl child learners around Ndirande community as a means to keep a girl child active and occupied. We will conduct awareness campaigns on sexual abuse.

title: Rebuilding Homes, Rebuilding Lives
description: Super Typhoon Rolly forced them to evacuate to save their lives but they returned to their homes reduced to ashes.  On November 1, 2020, around 400 coastal families, including 50 fisherfolk families, were left homeless after a fire broke out in the adjacent barangays of Alima and Sineguelasan in Bacoor, Cavite. Relief efforts by non-government and people's organizations came soon enough but now they need our help to rebuild their homes and help them rebuild their lives this Christmas.

title: Equality Champions
description: Our children and youth have lost 5,120 hours of class due to the hurricanes, earthquakes and pandemic Puerto Rico has endured in the past three years. Living in vulnerable communities, BGCPR participants are experiencing more inequalities than ever. To bridge the gap, we are providing virtual academic and socioemotional support, meals and free internet access. A small donation now will bring the certainty of better futures and will help them succeed over time.

title: TO PROVIDE  TWO HANDRED/200 CHILDREN IN FOOD SECUR
description: This project created to solve the challenges of two hundred/200 children those who are in great challenges in food security,health care,clothing and educational materials in  Kellem Wollega Zone. In this target area there are  the gorilla fighter form 2018-today.So, in  the case of this fight the  people in this area still they are facing  many challenges in all  their life system.Therefore,the Generation Pillar Organization create  this project  at list to support these two/200 children .

title: DE traumatizing Chimanimani Cyclone IDAI Victims.
description: NATCAZ will introduce the Healing Power of Creative Arts where respite; comfort, positivity and hope can be found enabling, communities in Chimanimani affected by Cyclone Idai to relate their stories through Safe Women, Youth and Children's Hubs (SWYACH) through performing and visual arts recordings, involving the affected communities. 169 perished 328 went missing and 11,255 were displaced. Described by the UN as 'one of the worst weather-related disasters in Africa'.

title: Family Resilience through Support
description: Building Family Resilience through Intensive Support for families of babies and young children with special needs and/or disabilities

title: Educate and Empower 300 rural girls Sierra Leone
description: Youth Help works with girls to excel extreme poverty, gender-based violence, and stop early child marriage, gain socio-economic empowerment and better health. Girls sponsored will access education, mentoring and power to drive change in their communities. To achieve the above, provision will be in the form of scholarships/fees, clothing and food at home, access to information and communication on girl-child education, ending child marriages, gender-based violence and learning for over 300 girls.

title: COVID-19: help women victims of violence
description: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 crisis, the number of calls from women victims of violence has increase by 70%. In only 2 months, we provided as much assistance as we did for the whole year least year. We provided urgent accommodation, psychological and financial support to over 70 women. We need to keep our effort to bring solutions to endangered women especially in these times of increased domestic violence. Help us to continue supporting abused women.

title: Help 150 children heal with horses in Cape Town
description: Tom Ro Haven is a registered NPO which rescues abused and neglected horses.  Our herd of 17 horses & ponies are then used in equine assisted programmes, focusing on children and young adults deemed to be at risk, or who have suffered from physical or emotional trauma.   Our aim is to build on the existing number of children that we currently work with to help them overcome their trauma, as well as educating them about how to respect and care for horses and animals within their local communities.

title: Safe childbirth in Africa this Christmas
description: You can help Maternity Africa (www.maternityafrica.org) make childbirth safe for new mums and their babies in rural Tanzania this Christmas.    Your gift will help reduce the chance of birthing injuries, or even death for mother and/or baby.    Thank you!

title: Braille embosser for visually impaired children SL
description: Due to the neglect and marginalization of the community people, the local and central government administration as well, the visually impaired children and youths in the various primary schools for the blind and visually impaired mainstream secondary schools, colleges and universities  are not having the necessary study materials in Braille. This is as a result of the absence of a computerized Braille press for blind and visually impaired children to braille their textbooks in accessible format

title: Holiday dinner for 300 children with cancer
description: We believe that children must remain children despite their illnesses. Celebrating milestones, like having a joyous holiday dinner should always go on in some form, despite obstacles. These events brighten the days of children who are suffering and raise the spirits of their families. Your gift will help us provide holiday dinners and celebrations for families in need, while their child is in cancer treatment. 300 children with cancer will celebrate the season with peace, tranquility and dignity

title: Support 50 women ex-prisoners start life in Kenya
description: 346 Women prisoners inEldoret have been released in the wake of COVID 19.
