Re-entry services for women  leaving prison are pretty much limited to not even a bus ticket home during release after spending months or years in prison, wherever that might be. While the biggest fear for a  women ex-prisoners  might be arrest, the biggest fear for women in general in prison is what will happen to them when they are released. These women have returned to their communities especially in the slum  desperate

title: TRAINING + SANITARY PADS FOR GIRLS WITH DISABILITY
description: Training for  200 girls with AUTISM and other neuro-developmental disorders on safe, hygiene and  dignified monthly period.    Training for 150 parents/caregiver on how they can assist their adolescence girls with disability to have safe, hygiene and  dignified monthly period.   To create 50 training manual and simple pictorial explanation to be used  by trainer of trainer(ToT) all over  the country.  Provide 200 kit (disposable or reusable) sanitary pad depending on cognitive ability .

title: Montessori Training for East Pokot Teachers
description: This initiative supports members from the Pokot community to train as Montessori teachers and gain a nationally recognised teaching qualification. Skilled and motivated teachers from the local community are key to increasing access to quality education and contribute to breaking the cycle of poverty in the East Pokot region.

title: Support Enforcement of Covid-19 Protocol in Market
description: The project  will educate and enforce social distancing guidelines and use of personal protection equipment in markets and parks in Karu LGA  of Nasarawa  State. Markets and Motor Parks are  overcrowded and no physical distancing, no face masks wearing, no hand washing points in the entry and exit point.  We will  enforce adherance to covid-19 prevention protocol  in this places,  distribute face mask, soaps, hand gloves, sanitizers and setting-up handwashing facilities in 50 markets and parks

title: Help 100 talented kids affected by Cameroon crises
description: The project will empower 100 talented or gifted children who have been badly affected and lost by the Anglophone conflict in cameroon through a contest, with 50 children coming from each of the two Anglophone regions.  The program will reduce the rate at which Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAFAAG) are being recruited into the rebel groups and will foster soc-economic empowerment. 400 kids will be registered/trained and 100 selected for empowerment from the two regions.

title: Help Lucas & Friends Fly to USA
description: Lucas and four of his friends, all survivors of abuse, are now rehabilitated and have the chance of a lifetime!  They can fly to the US and start the next chapter of their life. They can escape the shelter right before winter.  There's nothing for them in Azerbaijan. Please help us get them to New York where they can find their perfect family.

title: Enhancing Livelihood for 100 poor women in Bia B.
description: FOWAC invests in women and girls'. Organizes functional groups; promotes modern farming; gender Equity; mental well-being; diversifies economic activities; climate change advocacy to ease their plight and to improve quality of life. Enhancing livelihood project (ELP) will be executed in Northern Uganda to boost food security, income, climate smart farming for 100 female grassroots small Holder Survival farmers; to rebuild their livelihood after the two decade of civil war in the region.

title: Save 5000 lives from Sudden Cardiac death in Lagos
description: Out-of-Hospital sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) has claimed hundreds of lives in Lagos. With a bystander intervention through Basic Life Support (BLS), Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation & correct use of Automated External Defibrillator (AED), SCA victim's survival chance is INCREASED BY 31.4%. CeSAHA is set to increase the availability, accessibility & functionality of AEDs; number of trained first aiders in strategic locations; sensitize the importance of timely response & create National AED Registry

title: Recover after C19; Support 25 kids at risk in BiH
description: Children without parental care and children from families at risk in Bosnia and Herzegovina with this project will have healthy role model in their life -Older brother and Older sister- young volunteers which help them improve their self-esteem and develop basic social skills like using public transportation, eating in a restaurant, how to behave in museum or how to be safe. Volunteers play important role in C19 crisis as a support for kids in online school and leisure activities in isolation.

title: A child, a book
description: Facing the standard of living of the moroccan desert' families, buying books isn't a custom. They have other priorities to cope with before. No one of the desert children have book, however, books present a lot of benefits for them : new activity, vocabulary and reading improvements, aknwoledgement of a langage, help at school. To make them taking advantages of these, we are giving book. It's their own book, in their langage. We hope to give a book at 2000 desert children through their schools.

title: Help us to build a permaculture centre in Zimbabwe
description: Zimconserve is a local non-profit making organization in Zimbabwe whose mandate is the promotion of permaculture as a viable and sustainable mode of agriculture to the so-called conventional farming. This model is specifically targeted at the most vulnerable farmers as it demands less in terms of input costs. And towards this end,the organization is focused on setting up a permaculture centre within Seke rural ,in order so as to fully propagate and advance these ideals  on a broader scale.

title: Provide food kits for 300 families in Argentina
description: The main goal of this project is assisting 1,500 people (300 families) who are in social vulnerability in Argentina. Your help will provide them nutritious food, prepared under the supervision of a nutritionist, who performs a personalized follow-up.

title: Lunch Donations to Nurses and Healthcare Workers
description: During COVID-19 pandemic, Go Only Electric is supporting the essential workers of our community with free lunches and donations of necessary medical supplies.  With your help, we can continue this important non-profit work and continue to assist frontline staff and essential workers. But we cannot do it alone. Your support plays a key role.  Underserved communities need your support today.

title: Rotary Walkathon for Northern Irish Charities
description: Members of the Rotary Club of Armagh will be walking at least 10,000 steps over the weekend of 5th and 6th December with President Ian hoping to do 50,000 in that period with the aim of raising much needed funds for 4 local Charities whose work has been substantially affected by COVID 19. Each club member has been asked to do this physical task as they spend more time at home. Through sponsorship and other donations our Rotarians are determined to reduce the gaps in funding.

title: Sustaining Small Businesses-COVID-19 and beyond
description: This project will build the capacity of 50 women and 75 youth owned businesses which have been adversely affected by the COVID-19 pandemic in five communities in Ejisu Municipal, in the Ashanti Region of Ghana. Freeworld International plans to train the target groups on business sustainability strategies, assist them them with grants for business expansion and train them in four agricultural trades (Beekeeping, Piggery, Rabbit Production and Local Poultry) as supplementary livelihoods.

title: Campaign to build eco toilets in rural Nigeria
description: Nigeria is amongst the nations in the world with the highest number of people practicing open defecation, estimated at over 46 million people. Another 56 million people are estimated to be added during the next ten years. The goal is to build twenty eco toilets at targetted public spaces such as; schools, health centres, market centres and motor parks in rural communities within Nigeria. The community-led educational sanitation and hygienic programs.

title: Restoring Edible landscapes in Ghana
description: AGRI-WEB seeks to plant fruit trees and annual vegetable crops in 1,500 Ghanaian households. We are passionate about restoring the edible landscapes of Ghana where most fruits and vegetables are home grown and organic. The fruit trees we are planting include Mango, Coconut, Avocado, Citrus and Soursop whiles vegetables such as carrots, tomatoes, chili pepper and aubergines will be included. Building interest in agriculture is essential for economic development and environmental protection.

title: Together we can Make Music and Change Lives
description: Music can benefit everyone physically, emotionally and socially. Music is the key to moving forward and thriving.  This project will give 50 young children from South London music or singing lessons and access to our music groups and choirs for a whole year free of charge, when they would otherwise not have been able to afford to follow their musical dreams.

title: Support Spanish Primate Sanctuary
description: The Mona Foundation provides sanctuary for rescued chimpanzees, and other primates, where they can live out their lives in the most natural environment possible. The primates in our care have all been rescued from abusive or unsuitable situations. Many are from the pet trade or entertainment industries where they have lived through extremely traumatic events like seeing their family killed or suffering physical abuse. MONA rehabilitates these primates, as they cannot be returned to the wild.

title: Access to Climate Informaton for farmers in Uganda
description: The changing weather and climatic patterns continue to pose hazards and disasters to food security in northern Uganda. There is need for a proactive and holistic approach to combat the challenges presented by these changes. This project will develop climate change information management and early warning systems for Northern Uganda. The project will play a vital role in informing policy and provide the information bank for farmers to improve agriculture in northern Uganda.

title: Help 160 Afghan Widows Become Self-Supportive
description: HEMEFund plans to start 7 vocational training centers to provide free sewing training to 320 Afghan widowed mothers and orphaned girls who are the poorest and the least protected populations in Afghanistan and help them start home tailoring businesses to become self-supportive by providing them free tailoring business startup kits.

title: Help Raise 50K for Haitian Farmers to fight Hunger
description: For 25 years, La Gonave's Institute of Learning has pioneered and implemented sustainable solutions in education and agriculture. It has trained over 72 schools and reached  7000 children. They use AQUAPONICS which raises fish and plants together, REDUCING water usage by 90% and DECREASING dependence on a single crop. TERRACING slows down water flow creating richer, more fertile soil and creates new crop land for  ORGANIC VEGETABLE GARDENING reduces dependence on fertilizers and harsh chemicals.

title: Educational digital skills for children at risk
description: This project aims to guarantee access to formal education through the implementation of digital skills in children and adolescents at risk  in the context of the post-COVID pandemic. The project will provide formal education, pedagogical support, homework support, internet access, workshops to improve digital skills and access to online educational content

title: Food for children in refugee settlement Uganda
description: Bidi Bidi in Northern Uganda is the largest refugee camp in Africa. Only about 25% of the refugees in the settlements are supplied with sufficient food. But the situation in the host communities is also precarious. Together with other partners we are helping to improve the food situation. This food relief project supports 500 refugee families in need living in Bidi Bidi refugee camp. SCOEN will implement emergent relief to provide rice, beans, posh to the most vulnerable refugee families.

title: Create a refuge for the Axolotl in Xochimilco
description: Did you know there is a whole ecosystem with unique species and history within Mexico City?  Xochimilco is that place, we're working with the people living there to recover this important wetland which in turn, is the habitat of the mexican Axolotl. In this project, we will keep running a Conservation Center, a space where locals and visitors will learn, work and train on species conservation. In this place, we will also produce native trees, that will help to recover the habitat of this importa

title: Saving Abaco's Dolphins after Hurricane Dorian
description: This project is using a science driven conservation approach to save a declining population of bottlenose dolphins that was directly impacted by the catastrophic winds and storm surge generated by hurricane Dorian.

title: Home Safe Storage for Homeless/Unhoused Families
description: Housing is the foundation of personal and societal well-being and stability. Unfortunately, an eviction tsunami is coming, driven by COVID-19 & causing widespread unemployment especially in sectors employing many women. You can help unhoused women & children find affordable housing faster!  They can seek right-sized less expensive housing when their belongings are safely stored.  They will enjoy some peace of mind knowing they can start over with something rather than starting over with nothing.

title: Hurricane Iota Cartagena CO Flooding Recovery
description: Hurricane Iota left 70% of Cartagena under water.  The poverty rate there before the pandemic was 26%. After the months of lockdown, it increased to +40% as over 100,000 people lost their source of income.   Covid was the first blow, now Iota dealt a second blow. This project is administered through Conviventia who will provide emergency relief to the worst affected families and give them a chance to rebuild their lives.

title: Empower 60 youths through job training
description: The project plans to increase the employability of 60 recent school drop-outs (aged 16- 22) and unemployed youths (22-30) - both male and female, within the first one year period through vocational training.

title: Stopping Deaths Caused by Antibiotic Resistance
description: Antibiotic-resistant infections are predicted to kill 10 million people each year by 2050 -- even more than the 1.4 million deaths caused by coronavirus during the first 11 months of the pandemic. Thus, we urgently need antibiotic alternatives, particularly in Africa and Asia where 90% of the antibiotic-resistant deaths will occur. Phages for Global Health helps scientists in Africa and Asia develop cheap, natural antibiotic alternatives (phages) that can kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

title: Bring Soccer Balls To 100 Rwandan Boys and Girls
description: In 2013, the Bwiza Sun Team won second place at a Rwandan soccer competition - a great victory for the poorest kids around . COVID-19 interrupted team sports and now the boys and girls need equipment to be able to bring a team back together. Children and young people need joy and play in their lives. Happiness and social competition will grow their self-esteem and positive outlook on life, and will help the community address social problems  like substance abuse, depression, and violence.

title: Support and Educate Orphan children in Ethiopia
description: Imagine a child left homeless when his mother is sent to prison for defending herself against an abusive husband. Children like this roam the rat-infested, flooded alleys of Sebeta town slum all day, scavenging for food and searching for shelter. Without help, they would not survive. Shalom yebego Aderagot Derejet aims to alleviate poverty and facilitate lasting change in the lives of the most vulnerable children and families living in sebeta town through education, health and livelihood program

title: XPRESSION - Anti Addiction Event for 15000 Youths
description: Xpression is a Mega Youth Programme by ISKCON Kanpur to Empower to the Youths for Achieving High Character, Determination and Goal. Xpression is a clarion call to the Youths to rise to their full potential as the world class leaders by Equipping them with Values to overcome Self Destructive Habits and Facilitating their  We're Bringing 15,000+ youths together for a positive transformation. If you have the inner passion to change the face of the World for the better best, JOIN US & SUPPORT US

title: Mass sterilization day 2020 at CFTBF
description: Change for the Better foundation is aiming to sterilize 40 animals in our surrounding community in December to help control over population.   1 unsterilized female dog and her offspring can produce 67 000 puppies within 6 years!   1 unsterilized female cat and her offspring can produce 370 000 kittens in 7 years!  Sterilization reduces abandoned animals, control disease spreading, less overflowing welfares ect.   Our life saving aim statistic: 20 cats: 2 590 000  20 dogs: 1 340 000

title: SEWING SKILL FOR 150 SINGLE MOTHERS GIRLS IN GHANA
description: 150 single mothers will be trained with on the job-trained skills on dressmaking of which will help them establish their own sewing business, and be able to put a three daily square meal on their table. In addition, these single mothers will be able to take care of the basic needs (medical care, clothing, and feeding, academic materials) of their children. The young teenage girl who will also go through the training will become useful to herself and the society, rather than living bad lives.

title: Financial Literacy
description: Financial Literacy programme: Basic expenses cannot afford to pay. Example, water and gas bills, foods, education, daily expenses. No monthly saving. Higher cost in rental and education. We have done a house visit every 3 months. And also reviewing our existing beneficiaries with a test on their budgeting and expenses. And the results is poor and low average for saving.

title: Philippines Typhoon Food Relief
description: In less than 2 weeks after Super Typhoon Goni (Rolly) made landfall in the Philippines, another  Category 2 Typhoon -Typhoon Vamco (Ulysses) struck the island of Luzon last Nov 11, 2020. Barely recovering from the first typhoon and with the threat of COVID-19 still remaining, families in poor communities are at risk of facing hunger daily. Flooding has left many without homes and access to food. This project will provide Food Relief to assist thousands of families during this time of crisis.

title: Widowhood in Nepal
description: Women in traditional Hindu culture marry in to their husbands' families and live in their husbands' multigenerational homes. This set up provides security as long as a woman stays within it. But if a husband is dying young, the wife will be blamed for the untimely demise of her husband and she will remain stigmatized for the rest of her life. If she was "unfortunate" and gave birth to daughters only and a male inheritor is absent her husband's family might refuse to care for them.

title: Provision of Food and Medical to 45 children
description: The project will provide nutritious food and medical assistance to 45 abandoned children for better growth and development.    To help the children to recover from malnourishment and boost their immune system for better living specially this time of COVID 19 pandemic.

title: Food ...a basic source of Warmth
description: EFB launched this campaign  to emphasise that food is an essential source of both warmth and safety during winter. The campaign will be promoting two feeding programs: Monthly Feeding and School Feeding in addition to the Hot Meals initiative (distributing 5 million hot meals in all govern orates around Egypt)

title: Keep a student in school
description: Education is the greatest equaliser. It gives children, even from the humblest of backgrounds, a fighting chance in life - a ticket that we all aspire. This ticket, however, is not available to all children. Nearly one million primary school -aged children in Kenya are still out-of-school - the ninth highest number of any country in the world, mostly due to poverty (Oxfam, 2017).  Affecto plans to educate 400 students every year. Currently 86 students are beneficiaries of the program.

title: Christmas Fundrasier for Children in Cameroon
description: This Christmas, CAMAAY is creating a fundraiser to ensure that these children will have access to basic needs; for example clothes, toys, and food. This fundraiser will provide an event over the duration of three days where these children in need can have access to non-violence education, child's rights education, games, singing, and dancing.

title: Let's support Choco-Colombia in this emergency
description: The torrential rains and flash flooding caused by Hurricane Iota have hit Choco, a jungle province in Colombia with a history of extreme poverty and situations extremely hard.    As Quarry Lane School's Spanish Club, we strive to raise money and awareness for humanitarian crises all over the world. We believe that by partnering with TECHO, an organization that brings people together to lift Latin American communities out of poverty, we'll be able to really make a difference in Choco.

title: Covid-19 Hygiene Supplies for Rural Health Centers
description: We will provide much-needed hygiene supplies comprising face masks, alcohol, soap and compact hand washing stations to 125 rural health centers in Misamis Oriental province. The Covid-19 pandemic has decimated supplies in health centers located in rural areas and the need to re-supply them is urgent with government agencies favoring the provision of supplies to large health facilities located in the city.

title: 10 Years of TYCL | Youth-Led Community Action
description: Trust for Youth and Child Leadership (TYCL), India, turns 10 in March 2021! We are celebrating 10 years of Local Action for Global Change.  In the last ten years, TYCL has reached half a million young people and their communities to prevent youth suicide and promote their rights to achieve safe, inclusive, and participatory spaces for young people.  Donate to support youth-led community action to promote positive mental health, gender justful families, and pro-environmental behavior among youth.

title: Empower Guatemalan students through digital tools
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has sent home more than 4 million children and youths in Guatemala. The already fragile education system within the country seems more threatened than ever.  This program that will benefit more than 100 families seeks to improve the mental health of students, teachers, and parents, reduce the digital gap and facilitate learning and educational enrichment now and in case of future educational disruptions.

title: Build Greenhouse! Train, Feed Poor Kids and Youth
description: Help us to restore a greenhouse on social farm in the Odessa region, Ukraine. Thanks to your donation, 110 vulnerable children and women in the Rehabilitation Centers and Pre-schools of our Foundation will be provided with vegs and greenery for the whole year.  Maladapted young people with mental difficulties and orphans from countryside will be able to acquire the skills of modern farming during their training in order to have a job, income and to be successful in society in the future.

title: Grow the Green Army
description: Seeding Futures is a 11-week Accredited Skills Program that grows real resilience skills in un- and under-employed youth and prepares them for work opportunities in the local green economy.

title: Gift Hope: Sponsor a Child in Zambia
description: Due to the effects of the pandemic, 20% of children in our program have lost their sponsorship and the waiting list for the new school year in January is growing. Our partner, Almoayed Ventures, is currently matching all new full sponsorships! This means when you sponsor one child, two children will receive an education! Make a one time donation or donate monthly & we'll send you details of the children you have sponsored. For about a dollar a day you'll be providing two pathways out of poverty.

title: Improving Welfare For Captive Bears & All Animals
description: Bears in captivity were traditionally kept in sparse concrete pits, while visitors peered down at them. While many facilities have since changed how they care for them, sadly a number have not, resulting in hundreds of bears around the world still suffering. We work tirelessly to change this, providing bespoke training, advice and support to captive wildlife facilities worldwide to improve the way they care for bears and other animals on a daily basis, ensuring they live a life worth living.

title: Christmas Ribbon Appeal 2020
description: THE ROTARY CLUB OF BALLYCASTLE , NORTHERN IRELAND annually raise funds for local charities by selling yellow ribbons which are then put on the Christmas Tree to remember loved ones not with us and , in doing so,  raising much needed funds for  local charities whose essential work has been adversely impacted by Covid 19.

title: Fund Skateboards & Wellness for Indigenous Youths
description: Seeding Sovereignty's Medicine Wheels is a community-based mutual aid, mental health and creative arts initiative by and for Indigenous youths who face extreme social and resource isolation, high rates of substance abuse, and epidemic rates of depression and suicide.  Our participatory youth program pays  Indigenous youth leaders, distributes free skateboard gear and food at monthly events, and empowers, heals, and teaches new skills to build confidence, community and dreams of a better future.

title: Help Rehabilitate Sloths and Costa Rican Wildlife
description: Alturas Wildlife Sanctuary rescues injured and orphaned sloths, monkeys, anteaters, and other Costa Rican wildlife. We provide the care they need to recover and be released back to where they came from. Quality care is given in our clinic and sometimes many months are invested when raising baby sloths or anteaters to adulthood. Wildlife taken from the illegal wildlife trade are also brought to try and reintroduce to nature or provide permanent sanctuary when they are not able to be released.

title: Digital skills teachers trainings
description: This project aims to train 2,500 teachers online in digital skills to improve student learnings in  the Caribbean.

title: ACTIVITIES FOR ELDERLY IN THE ECUADORIAN AMAZON
description: Elderly people need to feel useful, have inter-generational contact, be active physically and stimulated with new ideas in nature.  Yachana is built with the needs of older people in mind.  Visitors will get a feeling of satisfaction out of working with gardening and other activities of the foundation.  The innovator of the program is Douglas McMeekin, who is 80 years old, has lived at Yachana for 31 years and can relate to the needs and limitations of his generation.

title: Workshops on Lifeskills for Foster Youth in Poland
description: This is a long-term program enabling the care leavers to meet on regular basis during the school year (twice a month, every workshops last about 5 hours) and learn important life-skills in group, and at the same time get emotional support. Program helps care leavers to preaper to independent life. Part of these meetings is dedicated to housing, law, health and vocational topics -training, writing CV, job appointment,  labor standards and rules ect.

title: Creating Affordable Housing Options in Chico, CA
description: This project will let us continue our work with creating affordable housing options in Chico, via master-leasing homes and acquiring homes, to ensure that every person in the Chico community has access to housing they can afford. CHAT seeks to help develop housing opportunities and supportive services needed to keep people in housing, while nurturing human relationships that will help people help themselves.

title: National Anti-Racism Initiative
description: As Canada's largest charitable organization serving kids and teens, our Clubs open their doors to all young people, of all backgrounds, in 77 diverse communities across the country.  We want to help our Clubs create even more safe spaces and empower even more youth  that identify as BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, People of Colour).

title: BUILD A HOUSE FOR A WIDOW
description: Help BUTERABA construct back her house. BUTERABA is a widow with only two children, her house was demolished by strong winds and heavy rainfalls leaving her with no where to stay.

title: RAM's #HealthyHolidays Year-End Giving
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has created massive unbudgeted and unforeseen costs. Despite these added challenges, RAM continues provide free dental, medical, and vision care at our clinics. Please join RAM during this global holiday giving season, which launches on #GivingTuesday, December 1, and runs through the end of the year. We thank you for your support as we provide free, quality healthcare to those in need. Donate now and give the gift of #healthyholidays.

title: FEED 100 ABANDONED ELDERLY IN UGANDA
description: Old age is said to be the golden years of a person's life. After a lifetime of responsibilities and duties, old age is supposed to be the time to take it easy and enjoy the fruits of your labour. For many elders in Uganda, this isn't the case. Many are abandoned due to domestic violence, poverty or death of family members  due to chroic illnesses like HIV/AIDS.

title: Community Based Education During a Pandemic
description: The COVID pandemic has interrupted the progress made in this rural community over the last ten years.  Our young students could hope for new career opportunities in engineering, technology, banking, or teaching. They could plan for more education. All this is threatened by the pandemic.  We are providing community based school every day so that children don't lose their hard won learning. More than 100 children attend. We need more supplies, books, paper, tablets, chairs and tables.

title: Help GESL support our girls!
description: In this Covid-19 period, GESL has maintained our programming & support of girls. Through our SHE series (Staying Safe, Healthy, & Empowered), we've been able to maintain our girls' learning & skill development through videos/podcasts/posters. Our IGNITE E-learning Series has held virtual classes for girls throughout the West African region. Through donations, we've provided emergency support to girls & families. Our passion is keeping our girls safe,& we hope you'll help us continue our mission!

title: Support MCN's #HeroesOnTheFrontline
description: For 36 years, our organization has focused on establishing health justice for migrant and mobile populations by providing support services to the frontline clinicians who work with them. In 2020, the global pandemic has presented unparalleled challenges to the frontline clinicians confronting COVID-19 within these populations and beyond. Their efforts have made our work possible, and that is why we have decided to focus our GivingTuesday campaign on celebrating all of our #HeroesOnTheFrontline.

title: Don't Let COVID Keep Kids Off The Diamond
description: COVID continues to adversely impact each of us. Often forgotten is the lack of safe recreational activities for our children. In response to the pandemic, the CDC has instituted stricter safety regulations that require children to use his/her own equipment to return to safe play; thus, children can no longer share equipment. This change has tripled the demand for equipment requests from our organization. Help us ensure kids can get outside and play baseball and softball during the pandemic.

title: Support Kenyan Youth with Sustainable Livelihoods
description: This project will ensure that youth from underprivileged backgrounds in Kenya are trained with skills in basic ICT, Entrepreneurship, Life skills & get a mentor while learning to create packaging products from recycled materials earning an income that can ensure the most basic needs, saving for college or capital to start a micro business.

title: Community Edible Forest to Empower Rural Women
description: This project will create, in a rural community in Colombia, 5 plots of edible forest, an ecosystem of useful plants, carefully designed and maintained that will provide food in abundance to more than 125 people in the long term, while maintaining the benefits of a natural system.

title: Sponsor Online Learning at an Afghan Girls' School
description: The School of Leadership, Afghanistan (SOLA) is Afghanistan's first and only boarding school for girls, enrolling nearly 100 girls in grades pre-6 through 11. This project will enhance our capacity to maintain continuity of learning during our ongoing study abroad program and amid the global COVID-19 outbreak, allowing us to safely offer our students a remote and online educational environment.

title: Providing school lunches to kids in Mozambique
description: This project will provide daily school lunches to 1,700 students across six rural primary schools in Mozambique. The closure of schools in early 2020 due to COVID-19 has increased child hunger and put more kids at risk of dropping out of school. As Mozambique reopens schools for the 2021 academic year, this school lunch program will be even more critical to get students back in school and ensure they have the nutrition they need to grow and learn.

title: Native Lands Advocacy Project
description: The Native Lands Advocacy Project (NLAP) is initiative of Village Earth a 501(c)(3)nonprofit organization with over 20 years promoting tribal sovereignty and self-determination with Native peoples and tribes in the United States.

title: Feeding Hungry Stomachs and Minds
description: Students in Tanzania missed 3.5 months of school due to COVID-19, causing us to realize our programs are in need of an upgrade to respond to the special challenges these children are now facing. Therefore, this Giving Season, The Toa Nafasi Project is seeking support for our special needs students affected by the pandemic through two significant interventions: 1) Learning and Testing, and 2) Health and Hunger.

title: Warm Clothes for Nomad Students in Tibet
description: Winter has arrived on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and 122 students are in desperate need of warm clothing. The government provided radiators in the schools are not working and coal stoves are not allowed in the classrooms for fear of coal poisoning. We need to provide warm clothing and wood burning stoves and wood for the student to stay warm this winter.

title: Empower 1,200 Mayan girls and youth from Chiapas
description: Achieving gender equality and women's empowerment is the world's greatest human rights challenge, according to UN. The COVID-19 pandemic eroded the limited achievements in this regard, especially for indigenous women and girls who continue facing complex and intersecting forms of violence linked to patriarchal structures, racial and ethnic discrimination, and various human rights violations. We contribute to prevent violences that impedes gender equality and reproduces toxic masculinities.

title: Curbing Infant Mortality Rate in Machar Colony
description: With the aim to decrease the infant mortality rate Imkaan established a 24/7 maternity home in January 2018. The only maternity home catering to a population of 800,000 people, the women of the community can finally opt to give birth in a medically conducive environment, get a consultation on high-risk pregnancies, track the progress of their baby, and be guided regarding nutrition throughout their pregnancy and initiating a process of learning and awareness regarding their own health issues

title: Support the treatment of kids with type 1 diabetes
description: Did you know that diabetes mellitus 1 is not preventable, it is not curable and the treatment is very expensive? This project will support 80 low-income children living with this condition with medical supplies (glucometer, blood glucose test strips and lancets). Our goal is to prevent serious and chronic complications that affect the quality of life of these children.

title: Secret Santa for the Displaced of  Karabagh
description: On September 27, 2020 a full-scale war was broken in Nagorno Karabakh region. 90,000 ethnic Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh have spontaneously arrived into Armenia. 57.2% don't have source of income, 79.6% of families do not have money to buy food, 57.2% don't have source of income, 63.7% of families do not have enough food, 58.7% household members are very depressed and scared. The project can provide 200 food packages for 200 selected families and 400 Christmas gifts for 400 children.

title: Equip A Computer Room For Girls in Rural Morocco
description: EFA builds and runs boarding houses for girls in the remote High Atlas area of Morocco so they can access school. We would love to support the investment of computers in our newest boarding house. Digital skills are essential for the girls' future opportunities in education and employment, yet they do not have access to them in their homes due to poverty. Accessing them at EFA means they can research, form online study groups and build digital confidence so they can succeed in their education.

title: Connie's Home - A Group Foster Home for Children
description: Connie's Home is a group foster home in northern Thailand providing care for children awaiting international adoption. Some 50 children have been adopted out over the life of the home.  Food and diapers are among the highest expenses in operating a healthy home. We provide some of our food from an on-site Aquaponics project to help offset the cost of nutritious food.  Salaries for our Thai staff, some who are former drug mules from the Juvenile Detention Center, are our greatest monthly expense.

title: Give the Gift of Joy this Christmas
description: This project will give essential supplies to help support a girl in rural Tanzania to complete her education in safety and comfort. Since 2012 Lyra has built 11 hostels, housing over 1,000 girls per year.   Our Christmas appeal aims to give small gifts directly to the girls in Lyra hostels, helping to make their learning and living environment more comfortable, and to extend the learning equipment they have available. We need your help to give them the much-needed gift of Joy this Christmas.

title: Help 100 teen moms return to school in Dzaleka
description: Imagine if a teen mom would not face enormous obstacles to complete school after baby delivery? This project will support 13- 19 years old, 100  teenage mothers in Dzaleka  Camp to complete tertiary education, providing learning materials, a baby upkeep Centre, skills training and advocacy campaign to reduce the rate of school dropout due to early pregnancy  and forced marriage. With effective support, refugee teen moms will rise against their past to achieve their dreams.

title: Save a life of 4000 Syrian IDPs this winter
description: With the advent of winter, the suffering of 1.5M internally displaced people (IDPs) in Northwest Syria increased, while cramped living conditions, limited hygiene facilities and medical care constitute a new burden and risks of crisis-affected people during winter. The project will rescue 4000 persons live in Kelly camps-Idleb governorate with essential winter items including Blankets, mattress, winter clothes kit, stove work with coal, heating coal. This support is considered as a life-saving.

title: Support feedback in the fight for racial justice
description: Feedback Labs believes that nonprofits, foundations and governments should listen to the communities they serve and act on feedback. We are highlighting the amazing ways that BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, People of Color) activists and leaders are listening to communities in a blog series called "Listening for Justice." These funds will allow us to compensate these activists for their time and thoughts as they contribute to this conversation.

title: Empower a caregiver...Reduce Gender Based Violence
description: The project will empower 50 caregivers who are survivors of violence and their businesses was affected by the Covid 19 pandemic and Economic recession in  Nigeria. OCDI plans to mentor and support the beneficiaries in running a successful business till their businesses becomes stable again and they in turn become financially  independent.

title: Sponsor Empowerment for a Teen Girl in Morocco
description: Project Soar envisions a world where all girls know their Value, Voice, Body, Rights and Path: The 5 Soar Pillars of Empowerment. This project will support the empowerment of Girl Squads, or groups of 20 marginalized teen girls, across Morocco through the Project Soar in a Box award-winning program. Our 25 workshops spark a transformative process whereby squads of girls further develop their self-confidence; speak up; embrace their adolescent body; fight for their rights; and set future goals.

title: LGBTI HUMAN RIGHTS
description: The work of these 2 civil associations and a community group provide direct care to the most vulnerable LGBTI population: people living on the streets, sex workers, people with HIV, recovery of LGBT bodies abandoned in the morgue, drug users, migrants, accompaniments in human rights violations: forced disappearance, homicides, trafficking and attempted homicides

title: Creating digital inclusion through game
description: The pandemic has shown that even though technology is a powerful educational tool, it also widens the inequality gaps in the territories where connectivity or access to technology is limited. For nine months, Tiempo de Juego has put all of its efforts into bringing a high-quality educational offer for thousands of children from vulnerable communities around Colombia. We want to keep providing educational opportunities for children through radio, digital platforms, and social media diffusion

title: Help Make Santa's Visit to IBSF Kids a Reality!
description: Our annual Christmas party is coming up on December 11, 2020.   This year has been particularly difficult for many of our students due to effects of Covid-19  & we wanted to help bring some holiday cheer to them.  Having this Christmas party will allow our students to celebrate with each other, enjoy some refreshments & take home gift items.   Your donation & support will be instrumental to making this a reality. Thank you for your continued support of IBSF.  We wish you all lots of blessings.

title: Holistic Health for Youth and Women in Harlem
description: At the end of 2019, IBREA opened Harlem Brain, a holistic training center at the heart of Harlem, New York City. After 4 years working with Harlem youth in a public school in West Harlem, IBREA decided to open this space to help the wider community manage the many health concerns they face as well as issues related to mental wellbeing, focus and motivation.

title: Covid-19: Supporting street children in Mumbai
description: This project will provide support and information to 600 street children and their families during the Covid-19 pandemic in Mumbai. Forced to survive in the streets, the pandemic and the lockdown have put them in a very vulnerable position. Making use of a mobile unit, called the "Smiling Bus", we will provide them with support, resources and information to help them dealing with this terrible situation.

title: Support Choco with TECHO Colombia
description: The torrential rains and flash flooding caused by Hurricane Iota have hit Choco, a province in Colombia with a history of acute poverty, extremely hard. Quarry Lane School's Spanish Club is partnering with TECHO to provide food kits to those that were affected, especially low-income families and women. We're working with reputable NGOs on the ground in Choco to make sure the kits get to people that need them most, and we know that with your help, we'll be able to really make a difference.

title: ts Isaias Recovery to 500 families in Pennsylvania
description: We will be assisting families in need of long term recovery support throughout eastern Pennsylvania stemming from tropical storm Isaias.  The services provided will be through our disaster case management and damage assessment teams, affording the families the social service support they need to move their recovery from stalled to completed.

title: A Covid Xmas: Gift 150 Cancer & DV Survivors
description: Trapped in the Discomfort of Home! COVID-19 has destroyed countless lives & thrust millions into needless suffering. The Masses have lost their zeal for life & hope for tomorrow! This Xmas let's make a difference to remind us Daily that Together, We're Stronger Than any Obstacle! Working Together we provide Masks, Food, Supplies, Gifts & Support to Survivors and Thrivers! Proving that Social Distancing is Not Social Isolation! We Are in this Together & We Will Win!

title: CloseTheGap: Rural Communities Connected 0 Poverty
description: Having to climb a tree for making a call or have enough internet signal to send a message, walk more than two hours to a hill or ride kilometers in a motorcycle to reach the nearest village and get three lines of phone signal that allows internet connection is what most rural youths and children must do during COVID-19 to access education, information, and opportunities. We aim to provide rural youths with a connectivity KIT with energy and internet access and essential IT equipment.#CloseTheGap

title: SUPPORT HEALTH NEEDS OF 1000 ADOLESCENTS IN UGANDA
description: Child and Family Foundation Uganda (CFU) will work and train local stakeholders and peer adolescent leaders to meet comprehensive health needs of 1,000 adolescents in rural Uganda. CFU will provide in peer groups, trainings and services for preventive and curative adolescent health services, income generation activities, saving and credit access through linkages with CFU community medical services, nearby public facilities, saving and credit groups.

title: Hope for first-generation college students
description: College is hard on a normal day, but imagine being a first-generation college student. Then, add in virtual learning and the complications of a pandemic. We're offering tangible support and hope for first-generation college students. Help us help students find success in college.

title: Educate 81 orphans in IDP camps in Nigeria
description: This project will enroll 81 (34 males and 47 females) identified displaced and economically disadvantaged out-of-school children into secondary school in Benue, FCT and Katsina States of Nigeria, and also pay their school fees for two years.

title: Hold Onto Hope
description: The Barrio Planta Project will provide educational opportunities such as Computer Science and English as a Second Language, as well as technology access to hundreds of children in overlooked communities of Latin America in 2021.

title: Help grandmothers stop child marriage
description: Grandmother leadership training will be conducted with 60 Grandmother Leaders to empower them to promote girls' education and protect them from child marriage. The training increases grandmothers' knowledge of adolescence and their confidence to educate girls and their families about the dangers of this traditional practice and to take collective act to stop it. Training natural grandmother leaders is an effective and sustainable way to stop child marriage and promote girls' well-being.

title: Support Social Work in South Hebron Hills
description: Living in the South Hebron Hills is defined by insecurity. A dedicated social worker who can travel to the 30+ rural villages is vital because she can assess and address what help is needed. Whether encountering women suffering from domestic violence or home demolitions, or children bullied at school, a trusted social worker with roots in the community can understand how the ongoing trauma of the occupation is intertwined with other problems and can respond quickly.

title: Bright up education for indigenous children
description: Unleash the power of light and technology to change a child's future! Accelerate Omar Dengo Foundation plans to install at least one photovoltaic system to provide electricity, computer equipment, and learning proposals on educational informatics to 30 children, their teachers, and family members. Be part of this awesome opportunity and help us boost education in the indigenous community of Altos Guaymi, Golfito, Costa Rica.

title: Support to 50 widows to fight hunger in Sierra Leo
description: Sierra Leone is ranked 179 out of 188 in the Human Development Index and the third hungriest country in the world says Global Hunger Index. There are more than 6.4 million people living in Sierra Leone, 52.9 percent of who live below the national poverty line. Roughly 60 percent of the population lives in rural areas, the majority of whom rely on subsistence agriculture for their livelihoods. Malnutrition has been the greatest cause of child mortality in Sierra Leone, accounting for nearly half

title: MAMA Kits for Expectant Mothers, Baringo, Kenya
description: This project will provide 100 covid-19 maternity kits equipped with surgical gloves, medicott sanitary towel, cotton wool, surgical blade, umbilical cord knot, disinfectant, gauze, baby wrapper, baby blanket, bibs, toiletry bag and face mask. The delivery kits will restore dignity of expectant mothers seeking services of unskilled traditional birth attendants. Proper equipment reduces chances of complicated birthing and infections.

title: Bright Christmas 2020 for children of Covid year.
description: A & V Rhythmic  club bringing together young girls from diverse backgrounds and to make them feel included in the sport and community through Christmas party and Christmas gifts. Covid 19 has ripped though families and grounded UK economy. Lockdown has affected children's mental health, boredom, stress and loneliness is a reality for many kids in lockdown. Many children said that their club is very important for their wellbeing over the lockdown and have look forward to Xmas performance.

title: Distributing Antibiotics within COVID Guidelines
description: After eight months of Covid-19 restrictions, Orbis has recommenced sight-saving activities in Ethiopia. Trachoma is a bacterial infection of the eye which can cause irreversible blindness. Unfortunately trachoma affects many people in impoverished regions of Ethiopia. However, there is an antibiotic, costing just 12 cent, that treats and prevents the disease. Orbis aims to distribute the antibiotic to 150,000 people in the Dita and Oyida regions of Southern Ethiopia before the end of this year.

title: Help abused and trafficking women at Hagar
description: Hagar serves trafficked and abused women in Cambodia, Vietnam, and Afghanistan by providing holistic recovery services, such as residential care, trauma counseling, legal support, literacy education, and employment.

title: A Better Future: quality education & companionship
description: This project will allow 51 boys and girls who work on the street to continue with their basic education and develop technological skills in a safe space. They do not have access to technology to access online education and are at risk of dropping out of school. To support them, we will provide academic monitoring and access to technology in three groups in our day centre. It is here the construction of a decent future begins - let's give access to education and technology.

title: From Poop to Fuel
description: We are thrilled to announce that we are embarking on a new and exciting project designed to take action on fecal pollution which is threatening the very existence of Lake Atitlan, the availability of pure drinking water for all of us living around the lake and the future of Lake Atitlan as a tourist destination.

title: JA China Career GO! Online Program
description: The Career GO! Online program is designed for university students to prepare for themselves in terms of career planning, job searching and interview skill.

title: Give 3D Printed Free Hands, Learning Tools & PPE
description: 1 in 1500 are born with an upper limb difference, but do without prosthetics that are expensive & quickly outgrown. Our volunteers (including need knowers, students, professionals) collaborate in project based learning to design and gift free arms & hands; share training and tech; develop workforce skills  to create opportunity & uplift business and community resources; make PPE & open source medical supplies for disaster response. Help us work outside with mobile labs and virtual workshops.

title: Stand up for the right to read in Manabi, Ecuador!
description: A few years ago, Clara Luna started a program that deals with two local social issues: In the community, 50% - 60% of pregnancies are from teenage mothers, because a high percentage of minors begin sexual relationships early and do not receive timely sex education. Lack of access for girls, boys and young people to an education process based on development education that informs, forms, raises awareness, and encourages and commits individuals to address short- and long-term development problems.

title: Support Women in Japan Experiencing Domestic Abuse
description: Domestic violence has skyrocketed since the onset of COVID-19, as more women have needed to stay home. It is crucial that individuals know they can reach out to TELL and that there will be someone to listen, help them access shelters and develop safety plans if necessary. Studies have shown that suicide can be prevented when a person has someone who will listen to them. By supporting this project, you will help to fund the training of 60 crisis lifeline support workers over the next year.

title: FOOD DISTRIBUTION FOR COVID-19 RELIEF
description: We are distributing essential food supplies to families in need in Nusa Penida, (part of Bali Island) who are still affected by the Covid-19 Pandemic. Due to this pandemic, Bali was closed for International tourism for over 2 years and many people are still struggling to provide food for their families.  Right now tourism is slowly coming back, but especially the rural areas in the mountains of Nusa Penida don't benefit yet enough from this effect!  Meaning: the need for help is still essential!

title: FREE Mental Health Support To Arab Women In War
description: The more access our women have to mental health support, the safer they feel. Post-crisis humanitarian primary aid should not be only food, shelter, and medicines. FREE Drama Therapy sessions are offered to help our women lead healthier lives and cope with the trauma of war. This project aims to support 1 Million Arab Women for Peace to overcome war-affected trauma.

title: Support Media that Makes Change
description: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, PCI Media has launched Team Survive to tackle crisis and emergency communication, based on our Ebola work in West Africa in 2015. We partner with communities to produce content that communicates vital information, empowering people to make informed decisions in emergency situations. Our COVID-19 response educates about contact tracing and vaccination, impacts on women and girls, food security, and more. Your support helps us create more media for change.

title: Goats for Tamil Nadu Cyclone Nivar recovery
description: The Nivar cyclone has caused torrential flooding, driving 175,000 people from their homes. In the immediate aftermath, we worked with our partners in the area to distribute emergency food relief and roof tarpaulins. Now we are providing goats to widows struggling to recover after losing almost everything.

title: Legal Commons: Community Legal Support Hub
description: In Nigeria, accessing justice is an expensive endeavor, bail is 'free' yet thousands remained locked up for months sometimes years because of lack of access to legal representation.  Building on success our Abuja based ImpactCove, this project will support the setup of a 'LawyersHub'in Nigeria; a co-working community of lawyers with litigation support, pro bono clearing, event centre, related services bringing justice closer to low-income Nigerians, small businesses and nonprofits

title: Support for Youth Mental Health during COVID
description: The mental health of young people needs more support than ever before with the ongoing environment brought on by COVID-19. This project aims to train 60 crisis lifeline support workers over the next 12 months, to provide more support during the 2021 Olympics, and to ensure that awareness of these resources are reaching the youth that need help, in a medium that works for them. Be a part of saving lives and making the future possible for struggling youth in Japan.

title: Rebuilding sustainable homes after bushfires
description: We're sharing our expertise in sustainable building and renewable energy to help those who lost their homes during the devastating Australian bushfires last summer. With your support, we're helping fire-affected people to plan and rebuild their homes so they are resilient to our climate for years to come.

title: Assist 400 Sierra Leonean teenage to live better
description: This Action is aimed at mobilizing $ 48,709   from online donors to Increase household incomes for 400 teenagers in the Manor River Basin of Sierra Leone. The 400 teenage girls benefiting from the project, cannot adequately meet their immediate basic needs  (food, shelter, and clothing);  cannot meet the medical expenses of family members, when they fall sick.  The Manor River Basin is on the boarder with Liberia,  is  hard-to-reach and an isolated rural enclave, about 300 miles from Freetown.

title: Help The Ethiopian Wolf, The World's Rarest Canid
description: With their distinctive red coat, long legs and bushy tail, the Ethiopian wolf is the world's rarest canid, the family of wolves, coyotes, foxes and domestic dogs. Ethiopian wolves are only found in the highlands of Ethiopia and are   Africa's most threatened carnivore. With fewer than 500 Ethiopian wolves left in the world, every single one counts! Born Free supports the vital work of the Ethiopian Wolf Conservation Programme (EWCP), the only conservation initiative focusing on protecting them.

title: Project Combating Acute Global Malnutrition
description: In Chad, malnutrition remains a major public health problem, despite the efforts made by the Government and its Technical and Financial Partners. The results of the 2019 nutrition survey reveal that the prevalence rate of acute malnutrition in children aged 6 - 59 months   is 12.9%.

title: Secure food safety for 100 families amidst drought
description: Besides COVID-19 shutting down alternative income from tourism, Andean llama farmers are now facing the worse drought since 2002. This year they have survived with their crop reserves from last year. But the lack of rain and freezings have ruined this year's production. With your donation you will provide non perishable products so families can get through these challenging months. Andean llama farmers work to protect fragile mountain ecosystems and water resources, help us help them!

title: Empower Girls with College Education in Pakistan
description: Khadija Girls College is a state-of-the-art college facility located in a backward area of Karachi, giving access to qualiy education to the Girls from low-income families. The college has qualified faculty with science and computer labs, library, sports and other facilities. We are currently supporting the education of 290 girls studying in the fields of Science (Pre-Medical, Pre-Engineering, Computer), Humanities and Commerce and empowering young women who didn't have the chance otherwise.

title: Empowering 200 women and 100 Kids in Masisi/DRC
description: The project provides training on sustainable agricultural method and encouraging women to create Co-operative for trading Maize and Soy bean in the territory of MASISI in Democratic Republic of Congo. This project will support 200 women victims of war and sexual violence to have employment training. We also provide free education for 100 child soldiers to regain their childhood and confidence to build a better future.

title: Help us build our Somo Mombasa Hub!
description: We have made our first investments in Mombasa and graduated our 2nd cohort of trainees! We are getting ready to launch our Mombasa hub later this year. Please consider contributing to our campaign to help us grow our physical presence in Mombasa.

title: Support the Projects of Over 65 Honduran Leaders!
description: The Solidarity Project is a 501(c)3 organization working with a network of Honduran Community Leaders in seven partner communities to execute development projects of the communities' choice through our Community Micro-grant program, Mesa Comunitaria.   With the impact of Covid-19 and Hurricane Eta & Iota, many projects will support rebuilding and expansion of damaged water systems, reconstruction of a collapsed bridge and funds will support our Covid-19 response work in health and food security.

title: Book Bikes - Girls Reading to Succeed
description: This Project will run a bicycle library in 6 low income communities of Lahore, Pakistan and will provide a rich supply of books to 300 children on average. This is an action to bring smiles to children stuck at home in times of covid; battling mental stress, uncertainty, school closure and loss in income of their parents. This critical literacy support service will not just bring activity based learning but will also act as psycho-social therapy for these traumatized children.

title: Your giving can bring a smile: Mobile Clinic
description: In developing countries like Nepal, oral diseases are the most common problems due to a lack of education and awareness. The most common dental problem of the Nepalese is dental decay and periodontal diseases. The underserved community is not getting oral health care at all. This project would be helping about 5000 people living in remote villages by providing awareness, prevention, and treatment of Oral Diseases. The primary beneficiaries will be school children and underprivileged. Thank you!

title: #BelieveHer
description: The Wise 4 Afrika Defense Fund provides advocacy and legal support for victims/survivors to access criminal and civil justice. We invite you to #StartByBelieving women when they say they have been sexually abused and to  #FundTheFight so we may support victims and survivors in their journey to access justice through criminal and civil justice systems.

title: Medicines for All, All for Medicines
description: UAEM Europe is part of the global Universities Allied for Essential Medicines (UAEM) movement of university students organizing on their campuses and beyond to ensure that publicly funded medicines and medical innovations are affordable and accessible to the public. UAEM Europe works to empower student-volunteers at over 40 university chapters across 10 countries to address the issue of access to life-saving medicines through advocating for fair and equitable licensing principles.

title: Help a Special Needs School Adapt to COVID Context
description: COVID-19 has had a devastating effect on public education in Ecuador, especially for children & teens with special learning needs. Classes have been online since 03/2020, but students will gradually begin returning to the classroom in 02/2021. The Ayni Ecuador Foundation is partnering with the only special needs school in Otavalo to bring vital infrastructure, hygiene supplies and training necessary to successfully and safely integrate these special students into this blended learning structure.

title: Formal education for the children of Cameroon
description: The socio-political crisis in Cameroon is hurting the most vulnerable; the children. Their quality of life is affected by the current situation, leaving many of them without one of their basic rights: education. They are the future and they need hope. There is no better answer than to provide them with access to a decent formal education.

title: Support 200 NYC Makers and Help Fat Cat Fab Lab
description: Fat Cat Fab Lab is an award winning, 100% volunteer-run NYC makerspace & only makerspace founded by a jazz club in 2013. Our mission-to share the magic of making to inspire everyone to grow- drives us to teach & share tools for 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC routing, welding, sewing, electronics & more. In 2020 we helped found NYCMakesPPE & gave thousands of face shields to health care workers. To stay open, 200 artists, students, engineers, hobbyists, & startups need sponsored memberships.

title: AS WE UNITE AGAINST COVID 19
description: We are building and installing handwashing stations as well as training others  as well as educating the people on COVID 19 and the importance of handwashing throughout Uganda. We have also created a tutorial program to help the children  continue their studies while the schools are closed. And our newest project is helping the elderly by providing food/medical care/basic service around their farms and home.

title: Temperature Control for an Educational Environment
description: For a study environment in the Caribbean, temperature is important; "When the heat increases, school performance decreases." A study of academics from Harvard, UCLA and Georgia state universities came to that conclusion, who analyzed the test results of 10 million high school students over 13 years in the United States.   Temperature has a direct impact on the body. Therefore, we must take care of it so that the temperature becomes an ally and for this our community participants count on you.

title: Build a Native Tree Nursery for the Daintree
description: The Queensland Trust for Nature (QTFN) and Rainforest Rescue were given the opportunity to rescue Lot 83 Cape tribulation Rd from development. QTFN committed to covering the costs and has granted Rainforest Rescue long-term access to create a large-capacity rainforest nursery for restoration. Our plan is to build the Daintree's most productive nursery that will ultimately produce 150,000 trees per year, increasing our current output from 12,000, fighting climate change and protecting species.

title: Help to fund a girls lifesaving cancer surgery
description: One of our students was diagnosed with rectal cancer some time back. After taking some medicine to see if it would heal it, she had another hospital exam yesterday (30th of November) where the diagnosis was, that the tumor has grown by 3cm and she needs surgery - the faster the better!!  Help us to save our precious girls life by donating everything you can! We count on you in these desperate times so that we give her a chance to fight this deadly disease!!

title: More Power for the Community Center
description: With the national emergency of COVID-19, the community center has expanded with an industrial kitchen, 3 freezers and two refrigerators to feed the entire community. The community does not have the necessary infrastructure, thats why the community center had to be resilient and 100% off grid in solar energy, it has two cisterns and its rainwater collection system. With this new worl wide emergency we have increase our energy consumption and are in the need to expand our energy storage.

title: SUPPORTING HONDURAS EMPLOYEES  - ETA & IOTA
description: Fifteen coworkers in Honduras lost their homes, and all their belongings, after hurricanes Eta and Iota. Their powerful winds and torrential rains caused flooding and landslides. They are putting one foot in front of the other to resume our lives, but they need your help. Their families are currently staying in shelters or with friends. This is a campaign for people worldwide to support their colleagues in Honduras.

title: Bahamas Emergency Fire and Ambulance Services
description: Eleuthera Emergency Partners is a volunteer-run organisation that provides communities with fire and medical assistance. With no hospital and no government-run emergency programme, this network provides essential community services. With increased demand due to COVID-19, even more lives are saved by this vital link in medical evacuations. Donations help cover the costs of new vehicles, basic operating costs, token stipends for the cadre of dedicated volunteers, training and life-saving equipment

title: Aviva Lilia Bernardo Kullberg Women in ScienceFund
description: Aviva Lilia Bernardo Kullberg had a huge heart and loved everybody with her bright smile and radiant energy. Our precious Aviva passed away unexpectedly after severe heart complications.  Though she had bouts of bradycardia (slow heart rate), doctors were puzzled and weren't able to figure out what afflicted her. Piles of data and lots of tests couldn't reveal anything abnormal. In Aviva's memory, this scholarship fund will help further the advancement of science of heart disease and its causes.

title: Black Girls CODE the World
description: Founded in 2011, Black Girls CODE (BGC) was built on the pillars of empowerment and education and is dedicated to leveling the playing field for girls of color in STEM. Through the organization's tech education-focused programming and initiatives-designed for young women between the ages of 7 to 17-BGC aims to inspire youth to become innovators in STEM fields, leaders in their communities, and builders of their own futures.

title: Mangrove Rehabilitation Project
description: Mangrove Rehabilitation Project aims to plant new 200,000 mangroves per year and it aims to contribute to the resrotation of ecosystem, climate change as well as conserving marine wildlife. The project will achieve to rehabilitate 102 Acres of mangroves. The Project will support provision of biodiversity and environmental education to more than 250,000 youth per year. New mangrove forest will conribute to the reduction of green house gases and help contribution to climate change.

title: Gift an Education to 900 Women and Girls
description: We will provide alternative education services to 300 rural women and girls who are no longer in school in order to improve their abilities to provide income and nutrition for themselves and their families. Alternative education will focus on home economics, on and off-farm livelihoods, micro-entrepreneurship and social skills. These are provided via modular learning and on-site educational activities in our training and demonstration center.

title: Gift of Blankets, Mosquito Nets and Solar Lamps
description: We will provide blankets, mosquito nets and solar lamps to 750 very poor farming families in order to enable them to live comfortably. We often overlook these basic items but with very poor families possessing blankets, mosquito nets and solar lamps is often a luxury and not given priority. With blankets, they will not sleep cold at night, with mosquito nets, they prevent mosquito-borne diseases and with solar lamps, they can do productive work early evenings.

title: Gift Food to 600 Poor Families
description: We will provide food comprising rice, noodles, meat, fish, milk, eggs, vegetables among others to 600 very poor families affected by disasters, climate change and the Coronavirus pandemic with the food supply to last until 2 months in order for the families to experience the contentment and happiness of having adequate supply of food in their homes.

title: Educate and Improve the Lives of 500 Poor Farmers
description: We will provide education on small-scale integrated farming technologies to 500 poor farmers in order to emancipate them from the perennial lack of resources and capacities. The venue of our education program will be our training facilities and integrated demonstration farm. Aside from farming technologies, we will also teach them basic skills so they are able to venture into farm businesses.

title: Saving 500 Elephants from Electrocution
description: In India's West Bengal state, 1-2 elephants die each year from accidental or deliberate electrocutions. But by November 2020 up to 10 elephants had been electrocuted. While some cases were caused by sagging wires, deliberate electrocutions have been surging during COVID lockdown, with farmers protecting their crops using illegal electrical fences. This pilot, based in Jalpaiguri district, aims to thwart elephant electrocution by using friendly fences and community outreach to create awareness.

title: Give Education to 400 Disadvantaged Youth
description: We will provide education, small livelihoods, emergency, health and sanitation support to 400 disadvantaged youth in order to provide them with head-start in life enabling them to face a bright future. This assumes very great significance with local communities suffering from low economic activities due to the Coronavirus pandemic.

title: Gift Poor Children  with Basic Essentials
description: We will provide food and basic essentials like food, toys, educational supplies, clothes, footwear, blankets and mosquito nets to 900 children whose parents are too poor to provide these to them due to extreme poverty. We target our gift-giving to be whole year round and targeting remote villages who are often left-out.

title: Reduce Children's Malnutrition by Supplying Food
description: We will provide nutritious food to 900 malnourished children by providing them with food as well as teaching their parents to grow and raise food in their homes in a cheap and sustainable manner and in so doing improve the lives of children of poor families who otherwise would grow as stunted individuals.

title: Tree Growing to Save the Planet
description: We will engage upland farming communities to plant and take care of trees as a means to combat climate change and to save the planet. Tree growing has taken secondary focus among farmers as the need for food and income remains paramount during times of scarcity but the need to inform, educate and provide tree growing inputs to the vast majority is urgent amidst the problems caused by changing climate.

title: Sponsor a child's education for USD 10 per month
description: We offer an educational platform that integrates children through e-learning as well as a physical component that is complemented by constant aid through the phone, with online access to 500 books, use of applications to develop their mathematical (MABA) and communication skills, daily e-learning interactions with their tablet to promote digital literacy, guided reading with teachers, modules designed and printed for the development of metalinguistic skills in children who cannot read.

title: Everyday Gifts: Food, Seeds and Mosquito Nets
description: We will provide food, vegetable seeds and mosquito nets to 1,200 very poor villagers who lacked this basic amenities for their daily needs. The supply of food is urgent during this time when the Coronavirus pandemic is spreading even in remote areas. This is coupled with changing climate and the virulence of natural disasters. Vegetable seeds will be utilized to improve food security and mosquito nets will be to ward off mosquito-borne diseases.

title: Rapid Disaster Relief
description: Since 2015 Filters for Families has engaged in relief projects in Nepal, Puerto Rico, Peru, and Malawi. As disasters increase in our Project areas there is a need for rapid deployment of urgent items. We need to stock filter units, washable sanitation pads and baby diapers, formula, whistles, solar lights, hygiene & first aid items, and other materials.  The two week window following a disaster is critical, especially for vulnerable populations without reserves.

title: SUPPORT TO RIOSUCIO-CHOCO
description: Thank you for coming here and looking for ways to help families in poverty. If you are here it is because you know the crisis that Choco  is going through serious floods and fire. Is experiencing and you want to help rebuild and support the affected families

title: Gift of mobility to 50 persons with disabilities
description: Imagine the joy of a kid with disability who will now be able to attend a school like his brother. For a person who is not able to move out of his home, it is extremely difficult to access educational and economic opportunities. We are in urgent need of 50 wheelchairs for our colleagues with disabilities who want to use it for their access to education and vocational training.

title: Better lives for 1,000 families in Ramdhuni, Nepal
description: ETC will support 1,000 marginalized women and their families in Ramdhuni Municipality, Sunsari District, Nepal. Building on decades of success in Nepal, we'll work in partnership with village residents, teachers, and local leaders to address the most pressing problems: food insecurity, lack of income generating opportunities, lack of resources in schools, and COVID prevention. All activities will be undertaken with due precautions for the safety of our staff and program participants alike.

title: Seedlings and Organic Fertilizer for Food Supply
description: We will provide vegetable seedlings and organic fertilizer to 700 ultra-poor farming families in order for them to improve their farm production, increase their income and access to food and lead them to a more happy, sustainable and healthy conditions compared to this time wherein poverty, malnutrition and general malaise is their situation.

title: Tree Growing for Food and Biodiversity Improvement
description: We will promote the growing of trees in 15 upland villages in order to improve food and nutrition access to upland dwellers as well as improve biodiversity, improve the condition of the soil and so that local communities will be able to enjoy the multiple benefits of improved biodiversity.

title: Women-led Agro-reforestation Project
description: We will engage women farmers and their families to implement agro-reforestation activities in their farm lots. Agro-reforestation will be the growing of trees and crops side by side in order to achieve multiple aims of increased income and food and enrichment of nature in order for nature to provide in turn multiple benefits.

title: Youth-led Permaculture Initiative for 800 Youth
description: We will train and provide farming inputs to 800 youth in order for them to undertake small-scale sustainable integrated farming ventures so that they are able to increase their menu of income sources, regenerate their farm and become progressive farmer-models in their respective communities.

title: The EMPOWER Project for Education through WASH
description: With Ebola aftermaths and recently the COVID-19 crisis, Sierra Leone continues to be saddled by huge challenges of addressing past and current recovery shocks. The odds have not been in the favor of majority of children, more so girls hoping to complete their education. Access to conducive learning spaces; basic toilets and water  constitutes a daily nightmare in addition to poor hygiene conditions. With this project, we hope to rewrite these access gaps in favour of particularly the girl child.

title: Relief from Burevi cyclone in coastal villages
description: This project will support 150000 people severely affected in recent cyclone with emergency care of food, medicines care & support. Will provide shelter care replacing  and provide dry ration  materials and dress materials for needed familes

title: Help Bring Christmas to Street Families amid COVID
