title: Send an orphan to school in Cameroon in 2021
description: This project will provide quality education, accomodation and nutrition facilities to an abandonned orphan in Cameroon for a year

title: Emergency aid after floods in CAMELEON center
description: After typhoon Phanfone and the earthquake that hit the Philippines a year ago for Christmas, heavy monsoon rains and flooding took place on January 1 and 8, 2021. The flood heavily affected the island of Negros. 70,000 people were affected, including CAMELEON's children, families and staff. We kindly appeal to your generosity for reparing damages, in particular in our center where 26 young girls aged 5 to 17 are sheltered with 8 staff, to strengthen and rebuild the perimeter fence.

title: COVID19 Awareness & Safety Kit for Kenyan Children
description: Kenya continues to see a rise in COVID-19 infections and fatalities daily. With children going back to school, it has become urgent to find ways to reduce the spread of the virus, especially for those in marginalized areas. This project will create an Awareness and Safety campaign to teach on preventing the virus and teach Kenyan children, aged 5-12 years. Each child will receive an Awareness and Safety kit which will include an educational book, a box of crayons, a face mask, and a bar of soap.

title: Pakistan Emergency Medical Fund
description: This is an emergency medical fund - no questions asked - when Pakistani hospitals refuse to treat a dying or injured patient who has no money, as famously took place a few days ago in Karachi.  This is a citizens' project and response to one young girl dying when a local hospital allegedly refused to treat her without a PKR 500,000 advance, as reported in local newspapers.

title: Rehabilitate Terrat's water system for 3000 people
description: The Maasai plains of Northern Tanzania are - for most of the year - a very dry place. Without water, life is impossible. This project aims to rehabilitate the community water system of Terrat - one of the main villages in Simanjiro District - to ensure that the community has a sustainable and secure source of clean water year-round.  This will provide the water essential for human consumption, cooking and washing, as well as for the livestock on which most Maasai livelihoods are based.

title: Trees for Us
description: Have at least 1 tree planted (species selection depends on local needs and conditions) per year for each person in the 4 pilot districts, making use of wilderness areas, public places, temples, schools, cemeteries, road sides etc. Proposed locations are: Vien Pa Pao District in Chiang Rai Province, Ban Phai District in Khon Khan Province, Sai York District in Kanchanaburi Province and Klong Toom District in Krabi Province.

title: Developing libraries in 20 Underprivileged Schools
description: This project aims to develop libraries in 20 underprivileged schools based in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. These libraries will be donated bookshelves, books, and will be monitored for educating underprivileged and socioeconomically deprived children about good reading habits and critical educational skills. The duration of the project is 6 months, and will benefit 30,000 families who are dependent on these schools for their education and academic requirements.

title: Big Mobility Appeal
description: 1000s of disabled children and young people in the UK urgently need specialist mobility equipment that relieves pain, improves health, enables freedom and independence and increases confidence. We raise funds to provide the perfect item of equipment to improve physical and mental wellbeing and foster inclusion. Also, and uniquely, we also cover all costs for maintenance and repairs for the equipment we provide.

title: Dollar for Peace Campaign
description: GPFA increases access of women and youth to quality education through its scholarship program. Our 360-degree program provides healthcare, assistance with job placement after college, housing in some cases, and other financial assistance beyond tuition to students who come from impoverished backgrounds. Over the last nine years, we have supported over 600 students who study in Africa, Europe, and Africa. Your donation will provide 200 scholars with quality education and leadership training.

title: Psychological Empowerment For Women In Business
description: The first-ever psychological support program for Lebanese women entrepreneurs through the use of Drama Therapy. Intisar Foundation is launching this program in partnership with a local NGO to ensure that women entrepreneurs receive the psychological support needed to improve resilience and tackle work-related burnouts.

title: Build A Farm! Feeding children and training youth
description: This project will develop the farm at Sky Is The Limit in Fort Portal, Uganda, to provide daily, nutritious meals to 400 schoolchildren, aged 3-14 years, including 45 residential children living with HIV/Aids or who have lost parents to the disease, and are in need of a safe, caring home.  The farm will also offer practical training in agriculture to local young people and graduates of Sky Is The Limit School so that they can gain vital skills for employment, and provide for their families.

title: Help 450 Vulnerable Children - Cabo Verde
description: THE ACHADA GRANDE TRAS FOOTBALL SCHOOL, also known by the acronym EFAT, is a non-profit organization that aims at the social promotion of children and teenagers from Achada Grande Tras, and surroundings, one of the problematic neighborhoods of Praia City. EFAT try to bit those problems through sports, cultural, recreational and academic activities, thus changing society and the world, starting with the most vulnerable and fragile, childrens.

title: Rebuilding Children's home and dreams in Colombia
description: In PAN we transform lives throught affection. As a non profit organization, we work everyday for Colombian children and families. Unfortunately, in July 2019, one of our foster homes in Medellin was destroyed in a fire caused by an electrical fault . Be part of the transfromation helping us to rebuild it and support our children so they can have a renewed space. Here they will learn about robotics, arts, and yoga, and they will have a library and a computer lab.

title: SEED TO WEALTH
description: This project will enhance the capacity of rural women and smallholder farmers in Nigeria to end hunger, poverty and curb land degradation. We are teaching them how to regenerate their land resources,helping them plant and grow fruit (economic) trees, crops and vegetables for a sustainable livelihood.Seed to Wealth trains and empowers 25 beneficiaries in each selected community/corporative on sustainable land management,seedlings, beekeeping and alternative skills for enhanced economy and nature

title: Support Young Women Changing the Status Quo
description: BBS supports Fora: Network for Change and their work to place young women at the centre of decision-making processes. Their signature Global Summit returns in 2022 and will bring together 30 delegates to build their advocacy skills, grow their confidence as advocates, and build networks in order to advance gender equality and women's leadership in their home countries.  Through the Summit, Delegates will be prepared to advocate in local, national and international decision-making spaces.

title: Empower A Women, Empower The World
description: Until There's A Cure Foundation has been raising funds and awareness for HIV/AIDS since 1993. We have been a proud partner with Reaboka Foundation, who's vision is to facilitate economic empowerment of South African women in rural areas. This project will allow our foundation to keep supporting and purchasing items from these talented ladies. This will not only create positive work opportunities, but also support these women who are heavily impacted by HIV/AIDS.

title: CREATE A SAFE PLAY SPACE FOR CHILDREN IN ARGENTINA
description: POTENCIALIDADES creates early intervention spaces to give 700 kids the chance to flourish their potential in safe and nurturing spaces of play and development. We provide support for children in socially vulnerable situations in the Buenos Aires suburbs.   Help children who live in poverty in Argentina recover their childhood! Let's create a playground to convert the space into a well- equipped play area, by providing emotional support and stimulation. Let's bring back the fun, laughter and joy!

title: Help Maya Midwives Save Lives in Rural Guatemala
description: Maya women in Guatemala are 10 times more likely to die from pregnancy or childbirth than women in the US, in part because of  the barriers and discrimination they face in the public health system. Our Mobile Health Program provides trusted midwives with training and smartphone technology, along with 24/7 access to medical staff, so they can detect problems early and get mothers  more advanced care when necessary, saving mothers' and babies' lives.

title: Pregnancy Prevention for 200+ Teenagers in Zambia
description: In Kafue, Zambia, the challenges adolescent girls and young women face to access reproductive and menstrual health services have been exacerbated by COVID-19.  Teenage pregnancies and STIs are on the rise. AEP will enhance its sexual, reproductive, and menstrual health services for its 200+ young women to include: weekly health text messages; monthly access to pregnancy and STI testing; access to monthly consultation and distribution of  contraceptives; and access to reusable menstrual products.

title: Give 35 families food security in Uganda
description: This proven 'Grains for Growth' project will improve food security for subsistence families in rural Uganda. Our experienced team provide women with essential agronomy training and grain storage equipment. They learn to properly dry their meagre harvest & store it in airtight containers, reducing grain loss from around 30% to almost zero. The whole family's nutrition improves; the women's own income increases through crop sales; and they can afford vital medicine & education for their families.

title: Donate Wheel Chairs for Disabled Persons in Sindh
description: The mobility devices like Wheel Chairs, Tri-Cycles, Tri-Motor bikes, Walkers, Elbow Sticks, Crutches are necessary helping aids to ensure mobility of persons with physical disabilities. if mobility ensured then empowerment is ensured. The Wheel Chair is the most needed mobility device for persons with disabilities. There is no NGO or Government body to provide free wheel chairs in Sindh Province of Pakistan. The rural area of Sindh has acute need of wheel chairs, we want to provide.

title: Build Bright future for 25 marginalized Girls
description: This Project will provide a sustainable Livelihood to 25 marginalized Girls aged between  15- 35 by Vocational skill training of fashion designing and Sewing, Handicraft and Hand Bag making.  The project targets out-of-school girls, street girls, orphans and adolescent mothers.  A reliable source of income has the power to transform their lives and the lives of their families.

title: Women's Empowerment for over 1,000 Girls & Women
description: This collaborative project supports a host of initiatives across Latin America, Africa and Asia that support women's empowerment that will collectively improve the lives of over 1,000 girls and women. The goal of this project is, across multiple stakeholders and communities, to improve equality for women, by improving access to quality education for girls; access to education and skills development for women; women's health and reproductive health; and income generation opportunities.

title: Help Support Female Ranger Teams in Africa
description: The female ranger movement is gathering momentum in Africa. Nyaradzo, Felicia and Talent are women who live in different countries but have a common goal as female rangers to protect the wildlife. For many, they have suffered from abuse, illness and extreme poverty but becoming a ranger has empowered them. They are now breadwinners and positive role models in their communities and to women around the world. How Many Elephants supports these brave women that are protecting the natural world.

title: Guarantee education for 430 Children in Jordan
description: This project seeks to guarantee the education of more than 430 boys and girls in Amman (Jordan), mainly Iraqi children who are refugees. We accompany girls and boys in a comprehensive way, working in 3 schools integrating digital and innovative tools and providing family accompaniment and support.

title: Support the education of 200 children in Honduras
description: The population in Arena Blanca (Honduras) is about 850 people, of which 406 are men and 445 women with almost 10% of illiteracy. The project "Comunidad Socioeducativa Guarataro" has as a main goal the improvement of the quality of life of more than 200 children and their families through a comprehensive perspective with education as the main pillar. The project also contemplates to implementate healthcare, food and ecology modules.

title: Covid Aid- provide food for vulnerable adolescents
description: This project will help 35 young young people who had to leave the institutional shelter when they recently turned 18 years old. They don't have strong family ties or any government support. Due to the strong coronavirus sanitary, social and economic crisis in Brazil, they lost their jobs and need help to cope with this very difficult time. Your donation will provide food and internet access (to help them search for jobs and free professional training courses) for 12 months.

title: Funding Jose Nel's Triplets University Education
description: Jose Nel a neurosurgeon, passed away on January 30th at the age of 53. He is survived by his wife Maria Constanza and their triplets, Santiago, Juan Jose and Maria Jose. Jose Nel always lived to serve others, putting the needs and well-being of his patients before that of his own. The love he felt for his patients was only surpassed by the love he felt for his family. His children were his pride and happiness. Let's honor his memory and his legacy by securing his children's education.

title: Promoting Innovation in 50 schools of Rural Nepal
description: Nepalese students are unable to excel in innovation and creativity due to inadequate STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) equipment and innovation orientation. ICA Nepal plans to conduct innovative awareness training workshops and provide STEM equipment in 50 rural schools of Nepal. This project will help to promote innovation and creativity among 2000 students through orientation, training and equipment support.

title: Support sexual violence survivor-activists
description: Sexual violence survivors are increasingly becoming their own advocates, working tirelessly to demand their rights in relation to justice. They are not however always given the chance to adopt an activist role. Thus, capacity-building of survivors is key and can lead to their enhanced empowerment and involvement as agents of change. To contribute to this, we will organise a training-of-trainers on better understanding all forms of sexual violence and using this knowledge in advocacy efforts.

title: Nourish Colombian children with vegetable gardens
description: In Colombia, 54.2% of families are nutritionally at risk. This means that more than half of Colombian families do not receive a minimum of three meals a day, nor the necessary nutrients to guarantee a healthy diet.   Together, we can create community, domestic and sustainable vegetable gardens that allow families to organize their own "Food Encounters" and thus have better access to fresh, nutritious and varied food.

title: Caritas Lerncafe - Free learning support
description: The "Lerncafes" (learning cafes), a free afternoon educational support project focused on education and social integration, are a highly successful and internationally recognized service that has been established by Caritas in Austria during the past years. At in total 56 "Lerncafe" locations, children from refugee and migrant families, as well as from host communities get access to free study support to succeed in school, enhance their language and social skills as well as afternoon care.

title: Her Voice My Voice Fund
description: The project will support 500 women and girls in Cameroon, facing financial hardship, food insecurity, stress and uncertainty which creates conditions for an increase in consequences such as abuse, sexual and gender-based violence in homes and communities and in transactional sex - which can lead to an increase in sexually transmitted infections including HIV, unintended pregnancies among adolescent girls, serious health problems and devastating emotional issues due to stigma and discrimination.

title: End Cervical Cancer Worldwide
description: Cervical cancer claims the lives of over 340k women each year, while over 600k are diagnosed. This statistic is rising in low-income countries where it is the leading cause of cancer deaths among women 35-45.  Cervical cancer is preventable and curable, but women face significant barriers to accessing vaccination, screening, and treatment. Help end this tragedy by prioritizing healthcare equity for women & girls; because no woman should die of a preventable disease.

title: 1 Million Trees Argentina
description: We seek to strengthen the "tree week" and the "1 million trees" initiative: the main donation, adoption and planting of native trees campaign in Argentina, which was born in 2012. To this end, the main objective of the project is to strengthen our native plant nursery and achieve the production, donation and planting of 30,000 native trees in the country by 2022, raising awareness among citizens, regenerating native forests and increasing urban trees.

title: Unlock Gender & Economic Equity with AI
description: AI Education: An Economic Imperative. Our free annual event, the AWS Global AI Challenge, launched in 2019, has the potential to reach millions of marginalized females, college/university students and entrepreneurs across the globe. Our goal is to provide beginner-level builders with virtual AI education, access to scholarships, apprenticeships, internships. job opportunities, startup accelerators, funding and more.

title: Support for the Maniema Liberte Community Radio FM
description: The Province of Maniema (eastern DRC) has more than three million inhabitants. Landlocked, access to information is via FM radio. It is confronted with armed groups and the governance of local resources. For peace and social harmony, populations, often manipulated by politicians' radios, need community radio for impartial information in which it can express itself. We need a solar kit to keep broadcasting.

title: Fight for girls equality through football
description: ISF uses football as a tool to educate, motivate, and empower children. Help us to sponsor a girl's football team to promote education, social inclusion, gender equality, and life and soft skill development through sport for disadvantaged young women and girls in Cambodia.

title: Provide safe access to 25 cleft surgeries
description: We provide safe access to surgery to infants and children from the most remote and disadvantaged areas of Ethiopia. For families in rural communities the cost and distance of reaching the capital prevents infants from accessing essential treatment and surgery for a cleft lip or palate, which left untreated impacts child development, social integration and the ability for them to reach their full potential.

title: Midwife and Traditional Birth Attendant Education
description: GHC will provide lifesaving infant and maternal training to local midwives and traditional birth attendants (TBA's) in Myanmar.  Our training will empower young women to advance in their critical roles as local health workers. These women will in turn help other women (and infants) by assisting in dignified and safe births by training them on basic and emergency obstetric care via simulation training.

title: Invest in waste collectors & reduce ocean plastic
description: Since 1950, 8,300Mt of virgin plastics has been produced across the globe, generating 6,300Mt of plastic waste, of which 9% has been recycled, 12% incinerated, and 79% accumulated in landfills. Each day, 8MM pieces of plastic end up in our oceans. The plastic crisis disproportionately affects poor communities, who are also our frontline heroes collecting plastic waste for recycling as informal waste collectors. Our job is to support their efforts by investing in them and their families.

title: Pads and Books
description: This project is focused on supporting rural Ugandan girls with re-usable menstrual pads and empowering story books to inspire girls to stay in school and to overcome a low self-esteem caused by poor menstrual management.

title: Empower Women and Girls with Digital Competence
description: Women's Protection Center in Odessa, Ukraine provides the temporary safe shelter, legal, psychological and medical assistance for the violence victims. Our clients are vulnerable girls and women who are very low-income or have no job and no professional education and special skills. Digital competence is essential for learning, work and active participation in society for them.  We will give access (PCs) and training for the girls and women on computer, social media and cybersecurity literacy.

title: Let it flow! Menstrual hygiene for colombian girls
description: 5 out of 10 girls and women in Colombia do not have access to products and information on menstrual hygiene. As a way to strengthen our sexual and reproductive health programs for girls and women from our communities, we want to focus on this issue. With your support, we want to bring more information on menstrual hygiene to our participants, and deliver useful kits containing basic hygiene tools and alternative menstrual products with low environmental impact.

title: Between seams, embroidering my Rights.
description: Este proyecto impulsa y brinda  talleres para aprender un oficio de costura y bordado, mientras se llevan a la par temas de conocer y reconocer sus derechos en comunidades Indigenas y Afromexicanas en el municipio de Santiago Pinotepa Nacional en la costa de Oaxaca, Mexico. / This project promotes and provides workshops to learn a craft of sewing and embroidery, while taking issues of knowing and recognizing their rights in Indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities in the municipality of Santiago

title: Educate 150 Orphans and vulnerable girls in Uganda
description: While it is true everyone has struggled with the unprecedented impact of the Covid pandemic, it has had a more devastating impact on the girl child.   As the government of Uganda plans to reopen schools after 1 year, many of the girls may not be able to resume school because they lack uniform, books, fees.  FOWAC plans to dedicate International Women's Week to create hope in 150 Orphans and Vulnerable Girls in Kitgum to return to school decently, by providing them with basic scholastic needs.

title: Back to school supplies
description: Children across Southern Africa will be returning to school. There is a need for school shoes, uniforms and stationery. Many children walk long distances to school and a comfortable pair of shoes is a necessity. HOPE Africa raises funds annually to support many vulnerable children across Southern Africa.

title: Help 250 kids in Uruguay
description: According to a recent research, the poverty rate in Uruguay increased 38% in only the first three months of the pandemic. Our Center for Attention to Children and Families (CAIF) has the aim of attending the needs of more than 250 boys and girls (from 18 months to 3 years) and their families at social risk in Montevideo. We focus on comprehensive care for families, with our interdisciplinary team that seeks to meet the multiple and increasing needs of children and their families

title: Help to Empower Women in Opportunity Home
description: The problem of homeless people is a reality that is not alien and that is constantly growing in Spain, particularly for women. This Opportunity Home in Madrid and with a space for 8 people, aims to offer temporary accommodation and comprehensive support to women at risk of socio-residential exclusion. We seek to promote their empowerment with a rights perspective, through a comprehensive approach, contemplating their physical, mental and emotional health to give ththem a new chance at life.

title: Support Yemeni Children's Education in Rural Areas
description: This project will provide children with 350 school kits at Al-Fath school in Al-Qanawis district - Al-Hodeida city - Yemen. The kits will contain the most needed stationary for students. Due to the current conflict in Yemen, teachers has not received their salaries since 2015. Therefore, the project is also designed to provide 7 teachers with monthly salary of 50$ for 8 months. Moreover, personal protection equipment will be distributed to take the necessary measures against COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Promoting inclusion for visually impaired women
description: Fucho para Ciegos Puebla plans to develop 20 activities based on games and sports with at least 30 women with and without visual disability in Puebla, Mexico, promoting adapted sports with a gender perspective.  We plan the consolidation of the first soccer team for blind and visually impaired women "Topas FC", made up of at least 12 women with and without visual disability that will strengthen their interpersonal relationships and improve their social skills such as self-esteem and autonomy.

title: GOLBO GIRLS SCHOOL OF EXCELLENCE
description: This project will contribute to constructing a school of excellence for girls in Golbo village in Moyale constituency, Marsabit County, Kenya. The school will be the only school of excellence in Kenya's entire northern region & will educate 450 girls drawn from three neighbouring counties of Marsabit, Mandera & Wajir. In addition to providing quality education for bright pastoralist girls, the school will foster peace & cohesion amongst the pastoralist communities in northern Kenya.

title: Community Nursery School for 60 children
description: The Sarmiento neighborhood in Buenos Aires faces many socio-environmental problems and families are in a highly-vulnerable situation. The Jardin de la Montana is the only educational space for preschool aged children there. It serves 40 children from 1 to 3 years old and also offers school support and multiple recreational activities. Having this space is essential so that mothers can access educational and work opportunities. The project consists of increasing the garden's capacity by 50%.

title: Support the 15q Clinical Research Network Clinics
description: Specialized Care: 20 US sites and 4 International sites. Each 15q clinic is completely comprehensive yet has its own unique capabilities that leverage the expertise and specialized care available from each partnering organization. Individuals have access to professionals all specializing in syndromes affecting the 15th chromosome:  Clinical geneticist  Neurologist Psychiatrist Psychologist Speech Language Pathologist Physical/Occupational Therapist Genetic counselor Social worker Nutritionist

title: Speaking Through Dreams
description: Speaking Through Dreams is a haunting, bold and genre-bending film. Tyson Conteh, the film's Director, embarks on a spiritual journey to investigate, the unnerving circumstances surrounding the death of his girlfriend Fatmata, who bled to death after a forced female circumcision ritual. Shortly after her death, she began to appear in his dreams - angry, crying and restless and pleading with him to bring the true cause of her death to light.

title: Clean Water for Better Health in Rural Thailand
description: This project will provide water well, pump, transmission line and storage tanks to remote villages in northern Thailand.  The lack of a clean water supply increases health risks, hinders agricultural development, and requires much time and energy to obtain the water necessary for daily living.  Our goal this year is to install / improve / renovate water systems in 50 villages to improve the quality of life for thousands of families.

title: Support 20 disabled young women for tailoring
description: Young women with Disabilities in our community face sexual reproductive health challenges of which some are exacerbated by the effects of COVID 19. The project will support 20 Young disabled women with modern commercial tailoring. Products will be sold off to the community members because there is available market. The project will provide sewing machines  and materials for making tailoring

title: Regenerate Maya Mountain North's Forests!
description: The 36,000-acre Maya Mountain North Forest Reserve (MMNFR) plays vital roles in providing wildlife habitat across southern Belize, and for local livelihoods, through the country's first community cacao agroforestry concession located within a protected area. Decades of illegal logging and agricultural land clearing have greatly degraded MMNFR's broadleaf. Ya'axche, with the help of Kimbolton School, seeks to reforest 12 acres of degraded land and monitor landscape wildlife via camera traps.

title: Empower 200 Girls in NYC with Education and Sport
description: OUR MISSION: Figure Skating in Harlem helps girls transform their lives and grow in confidence, leadership and academic achievement. We are the only organization in the world for girls of color that combines the power of education with access to the artistic discipline of figure skating to build champions in life.   OUR VISION: To empower every young girl with the skills and foundation to achieve her dreams.

title: Protecting girls in Cambodia during COVID-19
description: We do whatever it takes to protect adolescent girls from trafficking and exploitation, but the recent outbreak of COVID-19 in Cambodia is jeopardising that freedom. The majority of our girls are in the most restrictive red zone, where food is scarce and markets are closed, so are distributing essential food relief to girls and their families so they can continue building a future post COVID.

title: Help Educate 1,100 Students in Kuru Kururu Guyana
description: Blossoms of Guyana plans to donate 1,500 books to provide literacy education for 1,100 primary school students who come from the poorest areas in Guyana.  Blossoms will also provide three laptop computers to help support teachers in their work along with teaching supplies and learning aids to help support the education of students.  Blossoms donations will also include school supplies for students and teaching supplies for teachers along with a  printer for the school.

title: Give the Gift of Education!
description: We are rallying our donors and sponsors to Give the Gift of Education in 2022! The last few years have brought unprecedented changes worldwide and Nicaragua is no exception. Next year we are asking for donations to our scholarship drive to help support Nicaraguan families and provide a high-quality bilingual education for all students. We are providing scholarships for girls in our new Jump for Joy program. We ask donors to consider becoming a recurring donor to make a lasting impact!

title: Send 25 children to school in Egypt for a year
description: Imagine to this day, children unable to go to school as the nearest public school is 3 miles away of rugged territory, marshes, or unsafe highways. In Egypt, many underserved impoverished rural & Bedouin areas suffer from lack of close by schools. Young children have to walk hours back & forth for long dangerous hectic trips dreaming of a close by school. Girls usually kept home safeguarded from many risks such as rape; and many children suffer from child labor.

title: Together for Lebanon
description: The situation in Lebanon is described as one of the worst global financial crises  stated by the World bank! More than 55% of the Lebanese and 90 % of the Syrian and Palestinian refugees live below the poverty line due to economic, social, political crises and the outbreak of Covid-19, which affected the prices of food that have increased by more than 100 %, due to the collapse of the value of the local currency against the dollar. Lebanon is facing an uncertain future threatening everyone !

title: Clean water for 442 households in Kenya
description: Clean water is essential for good health.  Right now 55% of households across Kericho county, Kenya have to use dirty water from rivers and ponds.  Access to clean water and good sanitation is a basic human right.  This project will support 2 key areas - protection schemes for 4 natural spring water sources serving 442 households with a population of 2,260 and protecting childrens' health in over 300 schools through provision of rain water harvesting, toilets and handwashing stations.

title: SAVECats: A MD No-Kill Community Cat Program
description: SAVECats provides free spay/neuter surgery, rabies vaccination, and ear tipping to community/feral/homeless cats in Anne Arundel County, MD.  The goal of this project is to increase our geographic scope and level of veterinary assistance to low-income parts in Maryland and adjoining states. This way, we ensure full and proper vet care for the cats that come to us, help decreasing cat over-population and increasing cat quality of life. With your help, we can save all cats.

title: Feed 400 Neglected Disabled Children in Ghana
description: In most part of Ghana, thousands of disabled children are neglected with the misconception that disabled children are possessed by "evil spirits". Some are left on the streets or by the rivers to die and their single or widowed mom's treated as outcasts. These disabled children are maltreated and physically abused to the point of death.  This project seeks to recue and save the lives of these children and their families by providing food, clothing and shelter. No disabled child deserves to die!

title: Aid Gas Attack Survivors in Halabja Kurdistan Iraq
description: On March 16 1988 civilians from the city of Halabja were bombarded with mustard gas and the deadly nerve agent sarin by Iraqi fighter jets of Saddam Hussein's horrific regime. One of the most infamous events of the Anfal Genocide, the effects this chemical attack have had lasting repercussions for survivors and their families. Nearly 35 years later thousands of survivors suffer from cancer, miscarriages (miscarriages in Halabja still outnumber live births), birth abnormalities and PTSD.

title: Female empowerment project in Namibia
description: NamPads focuses on the production & distribution of reusable sanitary pads. The project is initiated to support young women in Namibia with a product that would not only be hygienic but also very affordable. Furthermore, it focuses on bringing financial independence to the women& to dismantle menstruation stigma by holding menstrual sensitisation training in communities & bringing awareness of the challenges many women face during their period without access to appropriate and hygienic products.

title: FUNDING FOR FARMERS AFFECTED BY HERDSMEN ATTACKS
description: At the moment, there are numerous cases of farmers-herders conflicts across Nigerian states, particularly within the South Western part of the country. These conflicts have primarily affected farmers and their surrounding communities of farming and endangered farming operations, food production, distribution and security of lives and property, thereby making farmers less productive by reducing standard of living among farmers.

title: European Food Banks Federation (FEBA)
description: Your contribution will support FEBA's mission which consists in contributing to the reduction of hunger and malnutrition in Europe, through the fight against food waste and the call for solidarity, by supporting and developing Food Banks in countries where they are most needed.  FEBA represents 30 members across Europe; in 2021, the 341 Food Banks belonging to our membership redistributed 907,280 tonnes of food to 45,810 charities providing food assistance to 11.8 million most deprived people.

title: Water For the Girls
description: This project will provide clean drinkable water to an impoverished community by enabling us to build an underground concrete water tank,  collect rain water in this tank, purify the water and use it to run our Maid Strong and Health Care projects and pipe the water for community's usage. Access to water will improve hygiene, especially in this COVID time. Not having to buy water will ease financial burden on poor parents who traffic their adolescent  girls as housemaids in the face of hardship.

title: Solar Lanterns for Emergency Relief - Puerto Rico
description: Great news! We finalized an agreement with the Salvation Army Emergency Disaster Services in Caguas, Puerto Rico to provide 1200 lanterns this year. These will be distributed to victims of the latest earthquake. Any lanterns not needed for that purpose will be stored for the hurricane season. This is a very efficient arrangement. SEI will pay for the lanterns and shipping to the port. SA agreed to pick up the lanterns, and pay port fees and customs.   With your help, we can have a huge impact!

title: Become a Burro Buddy!
description: You are invited to become a Burro Buddy. By becoming a Burro Buddy, you are helping us cover the ongoing cost of providing life-long care for our burros.

title: Restoring the worlds rainforests
description: This project will establish 1 million trees by June 2023 in rainforests across subtropical and tropical Australia and Indonesia. While engaging with local and Indigenous people this project will increase the size, health, and functionality of these rainforests for their longterm survival.   These rainforests are biodiversity hotspots and have experienced devastating deforestation yet they all hold immense opportunity for restoration and local community involvement to save these ecosystems.

title: Empower disabled women in agriculture project.
description: Most of the members in this organization are unemployed, so they sustain their lives by depending on their relatives as well as relying on Good Samaritans, which leads them to lose hope, experience life hardship and with no future. Also our memberships are poor particularly women/girls with disabilities are in bad situation since of our natural. In case we have not received this grant in fact we will be in poorer situatio, our aims and objects will not be implemented and reached as planned.

title: A second chance for teenage mothers in Tanzania
description: Until November 2021, teenage mothers were banned from continuing their education in public schools, and even now there are few public schools that meet their needs. We are setting up a new inclusive and stigma free learning center in Tabora, Tanzania to help these girls regain their education goals and eventually access higher education, vocational and other technical training. Such Alternative Education Pathways (AEPs) are a proven model of enabling teenage mothers to continue an education.

title: Coping with Loneliness, Anxiety & lack of Purpose
description: Our goal is to support seniors who live in homes and are over 60 years old.   Most of them struggle with health situations and are alone and do not receive visits.  The project that we are asking you to support are the activities that we provide on  regular basis.  We aim to increase the capatity to share with others their own age and learn from each other. We have aleady seen very positive results.  That is why we want to give others this opportunity and you can help.

title: Emergency Food Distribution in Madagascar
description: The extreme food shortages and economic impacts of COVID-19, combined with the severe climate-induced drought in southern Madagascar, have rendered over 1.14 million people acutely food insecure. Women and children face heightened vulnerability to hunger, contributing to life-threatening surges in the incidence of malnutrition. Since February 2021, SEED's Emergency Food Distribution Programme has been working to improve the immediate health and long-term resilience of food insecure communities.

title: Land Purchase to Build  Two New Classrooms
description: ADR is a nonprofit operating in Pallisa, Uganda to support the rights of Orphaned and Vulnerable Children and school dropout youth with access to a quality education. ADR promotes and advocates for these groups to ensure that local and international resources mobilized are prudently managed in an open, accountable and transparent manner. This project will support the construction of a school for OVC's, a vocational institute for dropout youth, as well as a health center for the community.

title: Help Venezuelan teachers continue to teach values!
description: Alive to the World, a proven values-based character formation program, has been effective teaching integrity and reducing pregnancy and violence in Venezuelan schools. Currently, with the pandemic our lessons must be remote, and our teachers and students in Sabaneta, a poor and violent neighborhood in Aragua, need improved connectivity. With your help and monthly support, we will now equip them with digital devices and mobile data plans to continue receiving training in values and life skills.

title: CHILDREN Who Depend - Streets - For their Survival
description: SHARE NGO fosters a dignified and protected life for children who have fallen victim to homelessness. How do you feel when you meet an orphan or a needy child begging for help from strangers on the streets? Kindness and compassion fills your heart I can imagine. Have you contributed in any way to help these underprivileged meet their everyday needs and fulfill their God-given gifts and talents? Other than giving sweet, there are a number of activities you can support a needy child in the streets

title: Reusable Menstrual Kits Keep Girls in School
description: The project will deliver 7500 menstrual kits to girls in Eastern  and Northern Uganda. One kit contains 3 regular size pads + 1 maxi pad + 1 storage bag + 1 booklet with information on menstruation. They can be reused for upto 4 years that is 100 washes. We relieve girls of the economic burdens caused by having to take care of their menstrual hygiene care by  offering a more sustainable method. We would like also to help dispel myths and taboos about menstruation.

title: Community actions for road safety in Uganda (CARS)
description: Uganda registers over 12,000 road accidents annually with over 3,800 deaths; where school children are often victims. The poor mechanical and physical conditions of vehicles courtesy of the limited capacity of local mechanics to maintain and enhance safety systems; is very under-looked among reported causes of accidents yet such vehicles dominate the roads in Uganda. This project will train over 50,000 local mechanics, school children and motorists on road safety from a technical standpoint.

title: Art for community development
description: In underserved communities, adolescents and young people do not have qualified opportunities for work and income. The result is that many of them end up continuing their parents' cycle of poverty. This one-year project will benefit 110 adolescents from Santa Luzia do Itanhy. It will provide an art & design residence with Ronaldo Fraga (well-known Brazilian stylist) and Miro Dantas (Brazilian artist) to introduce new illustration techniques using digital technologies.

title: Build 30 little libraries for 30 villages in Ghana
description: This Project will build 30 little book sharing libraries in Northern Ghana.  The project will provide supply  of books and Literacy support to 20000 children in Northern Ghana.

title: The Joy of Giving
description: The education project of Calcutta Rescue - an overview  650 underprivileged slum children are nurtured in the 2 education centers through a holistic approach Not just education but health, proper nutrition, extra-curricular activities are all managed. Life skill education is given a special emphasis All children are provided with uniform, school bag, winter and puja garments, books, copies and stationeries and 2 free meals A safe environment is provided to the children where they grow up

title: Supporting Children with Disabilities, Bangladesh
description: MAITS will work in partnership with the Centre of Rehabilitation for Paralysed (CRP)  in Bangladesh to train 15 Master Trainers (MTs) who will upskill therapists in resource-poor regions to support children with developmental disabilities.   These include children with cerebral palsy, Down's syndrome and autism.  All MTS will train Community Health Workers across Bangladesh benefitting 160-180 vulnerable families over 12 months, supporting families to better meet the needs of their children.

title: Gulf International Bank UK Ltd- Mogbencha Village
description: This project aims to form a partnership with Mogbencha community and will address several critical areas.  The project activities will address water, sanitation, gender inequality, and health. It will also train young people, hold educational workshops and help the residents to form committees and structures to ensure community ownership and that changes are sustainable, long-lasting and create meaningful impact.

title: Keep 300 schools in rural Kenya safe from COVID-19
description: Children do not have access to basic handwashing facilities in school like clean, running water and soap.  How can they be protected from COVID-19 transmission when schools don't have these basics?  This project supports 300 schools across Kericho county to create a clean, safe environment for children with rain water harvesting, handwashing stations, improved toilets, hygiene education and teacher training.  Over 104,000 boys and girls will stay healthy and stay in school.

title: Keeping Girls in School through End FGM/C in Amoli
description: This project will reduce the FGM/C prevalence rate at Amoli community of Enugu State, Nigeria from the current baseline of 62% to 25% and it will also reduce the child marriage prevalence rate in the community from the current baseline of 48% to 20%. The project is aimed at increasing the girl child school enrollment and retention in the community from the current baseline of 30% to 65% and also improve the economic life of various women and girls from the current baseline of 30% to 65%.

title: Empowering 43 female artisans in DR
description: The artisan workshop is a social initiative to promote entrepreneurship and fight against poverty that seeks to provide knowledge and skills to women from vulnerable communities in the Punta Cana region, through technical training for the design and production of marketable crafts and whose manual elaboration comes from the use of mostly recycled materials

title: Help us to get our supplies for Scotty's
description: This project is to help us get our shipping container from Canada to Kenya.  We are having a container sent o us to fill Scotty's Rescue Centre with all of the necessary supplies to help complete it.

title: Smokeless stoves saving lives in 1,250 households
description: Every day, families across Kericho county, Kenya are risking their health just by getting up and cooking breakfast because their means of cooking is indoors over an open fire.  The smoke they inhale leads to serious illness including childhood pneumonia, bronchitis, heart disease.  Women & children are especially vulnerable.  3 hours is all the time it takes to turn this around with the installation of a smokeless cooking stove that extracts the smoke and burns more safely and efficiently.

title: Send 350 young adults to agricultural workshops
description: ROOT BIZ is a program that will build youth interest in agriculture and entrepreneurship in Cameroon, Africa by providing monthly - quarterly workshops that will provide agricultural skills, tips, and insight into sustainable agriculture.  Participants will spend a day with NASLA and experience a 3-hour classroom training with professional instructors then participants will tour local farms within the community for field demonstration.  ROOT BIZ is geared toward young professionals 18-35 years.

title: The Media Lab: Giving Youth a Voice
description: The Media Lab is a dynamic learning space that fosters an innovative environment for youths to learn creative tools to advocate for social issues and nurture democracy through civic engagement, public discourse & media literacy so they become responsible, socially conscious and active citizens. The Lab helps youth develop their innovation and interpersonal skills whilst also developing practical skills in photography, filmmaking etc. which allows for a holistic understanding of pertinent issues.

title: Talleres - Workshops for young people in Honduras
description: The training center offers disadvantaged young people in the rural region of Honduras the opportunity to gain practical work experience. By learning a trade, they literally take their future into their own hands.

title: Translating Sustainability into 16 Languages
description: Sustainability is only achievable if we all work together. We believe that culture can inspire transformative change through engagement, education, and leading by example. We want to translate our Ki Books, step-by-step guides on how cultural professionals can practice environmental and social sustainability, into 16 of the most commonly spoken languages in the world to ensure that everyone, everywhere has access to effective resources and solutions.

title: FOR $10 HELP A VULNERABLE CHILD BACK TO SCHOOL
description: This project helps to send vulnerable children to go back to school after COVID-19 pandemic. In Uganda, all schools were closed in March 2020 as part of total lockdown due to COVID-19 pandemic. This affected 17 million learners countrywide. Partial easing of the lockdown started by sending candidate classes back to school in October 2020 and the statistics from the ministry of Education indicates that 40% of the learners could not go back to school because parents/ guardians could not afford

title: Hope Village of Allentown
description: Hope Village of Allentown will be a community where homeless people can feel safe and secure their belongings, go to work, and live life. A place that offers addiction and mental health services to individuals who need them. Most importantly Hope Village will be a way out of the cycle of homelessness and back into being an stable and integrated member of society again. Helping the homeless community regain their empowerment, and achieve their goals, helping to their quality of life.

title: Embracing math in the mexican youth, mainly girls
description: Mexican Youth ranked 53rd out of 65 OECD countries participating in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2018 study.  Boys outperformed girls in mathematics by 12 points, a larger gap than the average gender gap in math in OECD countries: 5 points. Mexican girls significantly outperformed boys in reading; the gender gap was 11 points.  We must enable them to have better academic results and foster their mental health. We can detect and correct learning difficulties.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, high school students Nikhita, Sanjana, Sruthi, and Malini have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Renovations for Holistic Center for 86 Artisans
description: This project will renovate a building in Mombasa, Kenya providing a larger space to house all of our holistic programs including our fast-growing childcare program, our computer literacy, ESL, and financial literacy programs as well as our food program all of which are offered to our artisans free of charge.  In order to empower women, we must provide them all of the tools they need to thrive. This is the heartbeat of our holistic programs and we need your help!

title: A Better Life For India's Stray Animals
description: SAFI is a 501(c)3 charitable organization founded by Ujwala Chintala in Florida, USA to fight for India's animals. India's nearly 80 million stray animals face not only a brutal climate and limited resources but must contend with a culture that views them as pests or threats. We are shelter and foster focussed, working to build a strong, compassionate animal welfare network in Hyderabad, India, providing shelter infrastructure, vet care, supplies, guidance, resources, education, and manpower.

title: Educate to Save Syrian Lives
description: Through this campaign, we aim to help youth medical staff to promote their capabilities, provide high quality health services, and to contribute to re-building the damaged healthcare system in Syria. We seek to provide certified, accredited, and high-quality medical training programs, in collaboration with Gaziantep University, for 150 healthcare providers in North Syria

title: FEED 500 SLUM CHILDREN OF MATHARE IN KENYA
description: Victory Foundation Programme's plan for the 500 Orphans-Vulnerable slum children of MATHARE, MIHANGO, MUKURU KWA NJENGA & KIBERA Kenya for 2021 - 2023, is to provide food to increase retention at the rescue centers, safer homes to free them from hunger, improve their health and nutritional needs, to improve concentration levels thus improving academic performance. VFP will provide virtual learning and free feeding to the children and street families, empowering them for sustainable livelihood.

title: Feed 5000 impoverished children in South Africa.
description: We identify impoverished households in rural communities that have no source of income and have children, providing them with food parcels and empowering them with tools and skills to establish food gardens for a sustainable source of food. We also promote the importance of nutrition and leading a healthy lifestyle.

title: Protecting Nests! Parrot Conservation in Guatemala
description: ARCAS fights to protect endangered parrots in Guatemala.  As a founding member of the COLORES consortium, it is saving the last 500 yellow-naped amazons (Amazona auropalliata)  on the Pacific coast of the country.  In the northern, Peten region, it is working to save the last 350 scarlet macaws (Ara macao) left in the wild by releasing captive-bred birds into the wild.  We work with local communities, landowners and officials to protect nests and stop poachers and traffickers.

title: Help us Build an Auditorium
description: Now that we have our offices constructed, thanks to our generous friends and donors, we would like to build an auditorium in our patio space. We will use this for student workshops and meetings, and workshops and programs for the community. There is no meeting space available in San Juan del Sur at this time, so not only will this allow the Fundacion to provide a new form of service to the community through programs for adults, it will be available to rent which will provide a revenue stream.

title: Support hygiene of homeless women
description: KOSHISH provides short-term emergency residential psychosocial support to marginalized women who are locked, caged, chained, homeless, or abandoned in street even during COVID-19 pandemic . On average, at a time 30 women reside in quarantine center &therapeutic safe house of KOSHISH. The staff maintains their hygiene & cleanliness, gives fresh set of clothes every day, and changes bed-sheets from time-to-time. With availability of a washing machine, it would be effective to maintain cleanliness.

title: Support Peace's family to get a nutritious meal
description: Meet Peace (not real name) she is 15 years old, she takes care of her other 2 siblings and their mum, their dad abandoned family and married another woman in another district in central Uganda after infecting their mum with HIV, 2 of the children are infected too, our project is supporting them to access basic care, the mum is I'll and cannot do any work, Peace has to bake bricks to earn some money for food, her bricks are not yet ready yet we don't want them to starve without food.

title: Help Strengthen Organizations in Argentina!
description: The pandemic has shed light on the fact that Civil Society is a key actor needed for the transformation of our society. However, the crisis that has arisen since has left several CSOs vulnerable and with scarce resources. This fund intends to help CSOs to afford costs of the Network's membership, which will strengthen their capacities, facilitate new resources and connect them with relevant actors related to sustainable development.

title: Educational Sponsorships in the Philippines
description: Shepherd of the Hills Children's Foundation, (SOTH) is a Christian child care and child development organization focusing on children and youth who are in need, abandoned, neglected, orphaned, dependent, & underprivileged. They also teach music, arts & vocational skills like baking.  We have visited since 1999 and many of us have fallen in love with the children. Here is an opportunity to provide educational sponsorships for children at SOTH as well as children from the local community.

title: Educate 50 Deaf Children, Create a Future - Mexico
description: EEESMA School for the Deaf provides free education and vocational/computer tech training to those who are Deaf, at all levels and for most age groups. A bi-lingual model of Mexican Sign Language and written Spanish ensure that the students can thrive in an inclusive environment where they learn and progress within a community of their peers sharing their own Deaf Culture. People who are Deaf take great pride in their Deaf identity & EEESMA works to help build the added confidence they need.

title: Treat 80 Children With Epilepsy in Cameroon
description: This project will treat up to 80 children of internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Cameroon who are also suffering from epilepsy.  WE TOUCH LIVES will pay for the treatment of these children by specialists in Buea and Nkongsamba regional hospitals, support their development/rehabilitation, and support their families.

title: Youth Empowerment Project Summer 2021
description: Green Mountain Conservancy will bring a cohort of at-risk youth to the Deer Run Nature Preserve to reclaim a wetland from invasive plants so they can 1. learn critical work skills, 2. be introduced to an iconic wilderness setting,  3. recognize that they can protect the environment and promote resilience against climate change; and 4. understand that, with their peers, they will be the stewards of this preserve into the future.

title: Support Roma Pupils Playing Music Instruments - MK
description: Musically talented Roma children and youth have lack of access to musical instruments and music education due to living in poverty and social exclusion. The Roma Rock School (RRS) is working with Roma pupils from the biggest Roma settlement in Europe, Shuto Orizari -  N. Macedonia using an unique curriculum combining Rock with Roma traditional music. Make your donation to support this socially innovative program of securing free music education and future music career of Roma children and youth.

title: Adult prisons - No Place For A Child
description: Currently children as young as 14 are being  imprisoned in adult prisons for minor misdemeanors and drug related activities. In many prisons children have limited access to  medical care, education and individual development. Overcrowding can lead to violence and poor sanitation/hygiene. This Life Without  Bars (TLWB) program will increase the knowledge of judges, police and prosecutors about diversionary measures as alternatives to  imprisonment, whilst supporting the child and their family.

title: support 8 child heads families in Rakai with needs
description: The project aims at  helping 8 child headed families in Rakai  with unmet needs.They will be helped with  phys social support,including counselling,and guidance , be given material support like food, ,pay school fees to enable have education ,provide be dings and to help them access good health and medical services, 64 children are going to be helped with the above  support.  the project will take 12 months in all the the sub counties  ..Local leaders will be involved in selecting  beneficiaries

title: Rhino Scholarships: Education is Conservation
description: Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya aims to provide 40 children living in neighbouring communities the opportunity to dream big by offering them a four year holistic secondary education experience. By ensuring that 100% of the funds go to our beneficiaries, we will not only be empowering them with education, we will be contributing to bringing up a generation of young people that can positively impact their communities and become conservation and wildlife ambassadors.

title: Help Sponsor Children to Access Education in India
description: With 35% of the country still illiterate, the state of education in India is not where it should be for a number of reasons. We work with a number of local partner organisations- schools, a relief settlement and vocational schools, our aim is to empower individuals, especially students to create a new future for themselves by increasing access to quality education through scholarships for all ages. Working towards SDG4 - we hope to increase the number of children in school and improve education

title: Help us to Buy an Animal Ambulance for animals
description: We often see injured, wounded and sick animals on the road by the traffic accidents. The main purpose of Mobile Veterinary Services is to provide year round access to meet the emergency and critical care demands of the street animals in the necessary quantity and quality. Timely and prompt delivery of the veterinary service to the site, and to the right animal patient, giving the right veterinary medical care at the right time are some of the critical areas in emergency response services

title: Global Disaster Relief Fund
description: CURRENTLY SUPPORTING FAMILIES THAT LOST THEIR HOMES IN A TOWNSHIP FIRE ON 22ND NOVEMBER 2022 IN SOUTH AFRICA.   Natural disasters are unpredictable and devastate millions of people, habitats and species every year and can range from cyclones and tornadoes to flooding and wildfires. They can affect all parts of the world and people from all walks of life, however, not every person and community is in the position or have the resources to rebuild their lives after the disaster. Th

title: Fund Rehabilitation for Disabled Children in India
description: With this project, we aim to provide the teachers at a School in India with Physiotherapy equipment, PT assistant/aide training, as well as Emergency First Aid training. Children with physical disabilities can experience one or more of the following, each of which can be addressed with PT: muscle atrophy/tightening, loss in joint range of motion, muscle spasticity, pain in muscles and joints, joint inflammation and contractures (muscle rigidity).

title: Young Antiracist Leadership Project (YALP)
description: In Mexico, racism is another variable to the huge inequalities that racialized people (Indigenous, AfroMexican, and brown-skinned) still experience, although racism has been historically swept under the rug due to our colonial past. This has prevented a unified antiracist movement, so our project aims to provide young leaders the necessary tools to help them develop their own creative solutions to promote racial justice in their communities and to create a network of future antiracist activists.

title: Let's Build a Kitchen to Feed the Children!
description: Thanks to the generous donors we have enough money to build Community Kitchen. The Cyaruzinge Village is so pleased as they look forward to their children having a daily nutritious meal of hot porridge. The long-term goal is to build up the Kitchen into a Cafe where commuters,  neighbors, and community members pay to eat. With this Feed the Children can become a self-sustaining endeavor. This takes time, and so for now, we need financial help towards reaching our goal.

title: No Shame to Bleed (NSTB)
description: Visible Impact has been advocating for safer and healthier menstruation by enhancing knowledge, skills and participation for both boys and girls. It also aims to advocate with the government for formulating and implementing policies to eliminate all forms of discrimination that occurs with girls and women during menstruation. Under the project of NSTB, various School based workshops on MHM, Youth activism, Research on Menstrual Health has been conducted in many districts across Nepal.

title: ORGANIC WELLNESS CENTER
description: Estudio Damgo 9, a group of Architecture students of Foundation University aims to address the current challenges in livelihood and the economy brought about  by COVID 19, wherein a majority of the community have lost their means of livelihood due to unemployment.  The project will build a processing facility for producing and packing alternative medicine at the same time provide employment and livelihood for people in the locality.

title: 1000 young Kenyans engaged in wellbeing activities
description: Today in Kenya young people face unprecedented challenges - no jobs even with a college education, parental and school pressure, bullying, loneliness, and other economic pressures - such as predatory loan sharks. We are losing our youth to drugs, violence, and more often now death by suicide.  Young people are lonely and disconnected. Green String supports cultural, emotional, wellbeing, & peer support circles for young people 10-24 years old that is transforming their lives through connections.

title: SUPPORT CHARITY IN THE HOLY LAND
description: The Holy Land, the land that God chose to become a man, where Jesus lived and spread a new teaching of love and where St. Paul preached unlimited charity, today is suffering because of unending conflicts. Inspired by St. Paul's teaching today, after 2.000 years, we carry on several charity works in support of our brothers and sisters in the Holy Land. Through our emergency centers we distribute food, primary goods and medicines for those in need and bring hope in places where none is left.

title: Food for abandoned children in Colombia
description: All children must be guaranteed sufficient, accessible and healthy food; It is for this reason that from the Acarpin foundation we work daily to offer this fundamental right, however, in the face of the contingency of COVID-19 we have seen a significant reduction in support. Today we are very concerned about the economic situation of the foundation and that is why we have decided to access this initiative to guarantee the nutrition of the 62 children and adolescents who live in our foundation an

title: Protect,Feed $Educate A needy Child in rural Kenya
description: In this project we are looking to raise $16k to buy 2 acres of land in rural Kenya, so that the CBO Township Foundation Education Centre can become self sufficient in the provision of 2 x nutritious meals per day to 475 children from impoverished, mainly orphaned, backgrounds. Currently they're only receiving one meal a day of essentially just porridge which is nutritionally deficient over the long term .Let's get together to GIVE during this TX's-giving, we all deserve a nice and a healthy meal

title: Digital Skills & Online Safety 4 Nigerian Children
description: How safe are children online?  Children are fast becoming active cyber citizens in the online community and we need to ensure they are safe and responsible navigating the digital world. TechQuest STEM Academy through our "Digital access and safety Project", will provide digital skills training and practical online training programs for 500 children from mainly public schools in Nigeria.

title: Send Ngabe-Bugle Indigenous Youth to High School
description: Approximately 82% of Indigenous youth in Ngabe-Bugle communities in Panama are not able to complete high school. Located in very remote areas of the country with a 92% poverty rate, families cannot afford the costs of transportation, room and board, uniforms, technology, and other supplies required for their teenagers to attend middle school and high school. By donating to Native Future, you will directly support 29 Indigenous youth in overcoming these obstacles to pursuing their education.

title: School for 15 Students w/ Disabilities in Zambia
description: Special Hope Network (SHN) opened the Resource Center (RC) to reach students w/ intellectual disabilities who have no access to schooling that challenges their unique abilities. Because of an unstable economy and the COVID19 pandemic, families are unable to pay the RC tuition rate. Partial student scholarships will allow the Resource Center to reach students and families of students who serve as key stakeholders in creating an inclusive Zambia where education exists for all children!

title: ACCESS TO EDUCATION FOR CHILDREN IN COLOMBIA
description: We supply tablets and connectivity (either 4G or WiFI) and equipment (computers or tablets)  to children that doesn't have access to virtual education due to their household income and the  isolation conditions. We will enable their education and reduce school drop-outs by up to 40%.

title: Change Lives in Sierra Leone!
description: Sierra Cares Foundation (SCF) focuses on helping orphan children with no other source of support, aiding vulnerable women to gain education and employment and funding child education. We believe that prevention, not reaction, is the key to changing communities and supporting them for long term sustainability.  SCF assists women and children who are vulnerable to poverty, human trafficking and need food.  We are a newly-registered official US non-profit and appreciate your support!

title: Help Start Small Businesses in Rural Thailand
description: This project will establish a capital investment fund to provide no-interest loans to small business ventures such as self-sustaining pig farms, buffalo / cattle ranches, or organic agricultural farms.  Each business venture will be supervised by a team of advisors with specialized training to help insure long-term business success.  Prospective business owners will be required and assisted in submitting a detailed business plan that will aim to repay the loan within 4 years.

title: Help & relieve patients, caregivers, carers
description: We are implementing a comprehensive national program of workshops led by recognized specialists to assist patients, caregivers & healthcare staff : art therapy, socio-aesthetics, coaching, physical activity, virtual reality =>Many positive effects for patients (experience hospitalization better; prevent/limit side effects & medications), parents/siblings (physically & emotionally), and facilitates post-healing life. Dedicated/shared sessions for healthcare staff are included since the pandemic.

title: Empower Girls in Cambodia With Education
description: Girls face additional challenges in accessing education in Cambodia. In the Steung Meanchey community, the site of a former massive garbage dump, persisting poverty makes it particularly difficult for girls to receive the quality education they deserve. This project not only provides education to girls but addresses the multitude of obstacles standing between them and education, ensuring they and their families are supported and they have the chance to succeed in school and beyond.

title: Help 195 Fijians Access Food & Education Safely!
description: This project will build a shoreline shelter, stairs with railings, and a dock for the 195 people of Wainidova, a tiny village located on the bank of the formidable Navua River (Fiji's longest), allowing them to access food, education, and healthcare in a safe way. COVID-19 hit Fiji's tourism hard- the largest export, and it has exacerbated the poverty in the village. The villagers have the choice to decide between using money to update the decaying river transport OR to feed their families.

title: One toilet for one poor family in Pakistan
description: Recently, a UNICEF warning announced that an alarming 41 million people in Pakistan lack access to adequate toilets; forcing them especially women and children to defecate in public and making these groups most vulnerable to diseases and safety.   Construction of the soak-pit toilets for the most deserving families who are unable to construct it by their own will be the priority of AWARD in 3 suffering districts Faisalabad, Muzaffargarh and Toba Tek Singh.

title: Improve the Opportunity Center in Hrazdan
description: The most powerful weapon in the 21st century is  knowledge. For this purpose with a group of women from our community we decided to launch a community opportunity center as a unique powerhouse of initiatives,  where the youth and women, in particular, will not only improve their skills and capacity with the help of center-provided resources, but will also be supported to fulfil their ideas ranging from crafts to social enterprises. This center will bridge  the community with the outside World.

title: Support female survivors of Boko Haram in Nigeria
description: Women and girls escaping violence at the hands of Boko Haram and other armed groups often face stigma, sexual gender based violence and rejection when returning to their families. Your donation will ensure our team can provide psychosocial and economic support, family counselling and dialogue sessions, gender-based violence assistance and safety measures, education services, and other essential support for these vulnerable survivors and change attitudes in their communities.

title: Food support for 250 women with disabilities
description: It is undouble that COVID-19 has hit hard on not just the health sector, but every facet of society. In Sierra Leone, Socio-economic state of women with disabilities who are mainly single mothers is appalling. In these difficult times when lockdowns and stay home measures are instituted, women with disabilities suffered with starvation, with barely little or nothing to eat with their children. Donating to a fund that will provide food for these hungry single disable mothers will save lives.

title: Construction of Health Center in Rural Uganda
description: This project will build a health center in Rwamwanja rural community to solve  the five major causes of death in the reproductive age/pregnant women (identified causes of death are; postpartum hemorrhage, preeclampsia and eclampsia, sepsis, abortions and malaria during pregnancy). These causes are preventable and manageable

title: Educate 500 girls coding & robotics in Ethiopia
description: Provide coding and robotics skills  to 500 girls and gave them the ability to change their lives entirely. Your donation will go toward educating 500 girsl in Ethiopia. Learning coding and robotics skills  stimulates creativity and builds confidence, especially for girls; and it unlocks the best careers in their lives, with the potential to lift up an entire generation out of poverty. Coding is empowering and gives girls an equal shot. It increases their odds of having well-paid STEM jobs.

title: Help A Family In Living Life With Dignity!
description: This year, we are looking forward to your support in lifting 100s families in Pakistan out of poverty. With an average donation-based interest-free loan size of $250, you can permanently lift a poverty-stricken family with our entrepreneurship microloans. Through our 17 years of operation, Akhuwat has brought 3.3 million people irrespective of their religion, caste, and gender into socioeconomic inclusion. Learn more about how your little donation can change many lives.

title: Vital community education for a 'lost generation'
description: There is a 'lost generation' in Kenya. Thousands of young people who did not return to school after COVID-19 closures. Education breaks the poverty cycle. We are supporting teenage girls who are now mothers to form peer support groups, we are providing training and resources for income generating projects, delivering Life Skills courses, training community ambassadors to deliver sexual & reproductive health workshops to boys and girls. This project needs your help to keep their futures brighter.

title: Endemic Seeds Bank to empower women and girls
description: Endemic and extinction plants are devastating the cultural and ecologic environment in the Lacandona jungle. This seeds bank will serve as a nursery base within the Lacandona Forest, promoting the protection of plants in danger of extinction. The collaboration between the recollection of seeds by  women and girls will generate a synergy of local trade throughout a collaborative scheme for knowledge and economic empowerment for girls and women.

title: Education for Dominican & Zambian Communities
description: GRACE Cares, in partnership with our local heroes, will provide educational opportunities to Project Hearts in Baitoa, Dominican Republic and the Munali Youth Empowerment Program (MYEP) in Lusaka Province, Zambia. In the Dominican Republic, Project Hearts will train women in basic health and medical knowledge in their Community Health Leadership (CHL) program; and in Zambia, MYEP will provide books and learning materials to children 0-9-years-old in their Mobile Book program.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, high school students Meeraa, Nainika, Ankitha, Nithya, and Vibha have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Help to empower 1000 Nigerian women in SMEs
description: Our Empower Women program is designed to empower young Nigerian women (18-35 yrs) to live more meaningful lives by equipping them with handy, marketable, and practicable skills, such as creative bag- and shoe-making with Ankara, advanced pastry-making techniques, and cake designing, etc., along with the financial and technical support in setting up their own businesses, and marketing their products to an expanding clientele base.

title: Ending poverty & inequality in Vietnam
description: Passerelles numeriques Vietnam (PNV) offers a free 3-year IT training program at our center, for the most vulnerable and marginalized youths aged 18-23 in Vietnam. Our mission is to truly develop our students' employability which will allow them and their families to escape poverty in a sustainable way. PNV's additional objective is to reduce inequality between genders by setting the enrollment ratio of at least 50% female students.

title: Girls Protection from Forced Marriage and Abuse
