The poverty we are attacking with our intentionality goes beyond the material. We want to recover the essence of our youths through the offering of vocational training and innovative so as to actualize their potentials.

title: myME Box & Portable Digital Classroom (PDC)
description: We have a practical, low-cost, easy to install and use solution to the education crisis in Burma (Myanmar), a country where schools have been closed for over a year due to a severe humanitarian crisis. The Portable Digital Classroom (PDC) with myME Box is designed for out-of-school children and youth (OOSCYs.). It is available online or offline. In 2022-2023, Burma Humanitarian Mission will support 10 PDCs for OOSCYs living in rural and remote regions in Burma.

title: Disaster relief & humanitarian aid, S/East Nigeria
description: Insecurity has resulted in population displacement, disrupted livelihoods, food insecurity, and protection concerns in southeastern part of Nigeria. Insecurity continues to restrict access to basic services, and both displaced people and vulnerable host communities are in need of emergency food assistance, safe drinking water, relief commodities, as well as health, nutrition, protection, shelter, and water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions.

title: Help 10 local family in Syria to have a home.
description: This training program will help to train 10 local Engineers to help building 10 home for local destroyed propertties in Syria.  Reviving Home is driven by its Trustees. These can be individual Social Mobilizers and Construction Experts, or other parties in the form of NGOs or companies - all of which have been certified by Reviving Home. Your donation will go directly towards the training of these Trustees via the One Project Away Challenge. Every Trustee will be able to help one family Home.

title: Rehabilitation for addicted street connected youth
description: Facilitating of street connected youth from Kitale to attend at residential rehabilitation at a treatment centre in the neighbouring town of Eldoret. For alcohol addiction the period of rehabilitation is 3 months and for drug addiction the period is 6 months. Following the period of rehabilitation the youth will be supported in terms of appropriate accommodation and in provision of skills and opportunities for earning a livelihood.

title: Tibetan Girls in Sports, Spirit and Success
description: This project makes possible the continuation of a sports program for Tibetan girls in Tibet that has already resulted in two college scholarships.  The program builds skills and self-esteem, and puts Tibetan girls in play for athletic scholarships in China, where Tibetans boys are sought out for their greater physical capacity, including oxygen uptake and other high-altitude adaptations.  Trainings embrace physical self-care and the pursuit of excellence through practice and teamwork.

title: Inclusive education for children with disabilities
description: This project aims to help around 300 children with disabilities to access inclusive education because all of these children have severe disabilities and their education was impossible due to lack of appropriate support and families' poverty. This project will address their problems by building an inclusive school with an accessible environment and materials with professional teachers and healthcare. Children will be supported to access habilitation and rehabilitation to meet primary needs.

title: Kabati YMCA Public Library in Naivasha, Kenya
description: From Books to Brilliance is partnering with the Kabati YMCA in Naivasha, Kenya to create the area's first public library. The library will occupy two rooms at the YMCA and community leaders will select a rich supply of books and materials and purchase them locally. Initially established for children, the library will grow to serve residents of all ages. This educational center will act as a catalyst for economic growth, helping to improve the lives of many Kenyans now living in abject poverty.

title: FREE MEDICINES FOR ORPHANAGES IN NIGERIA
description: According to USAID's last referenced Global health report, there are c.17.5 million orphans and vulnerable children in Nigeria. Due to several environmental factors, these children face enormous challenges to their health and development. Although there are several orphanages, the resources of most of these organisations have been overextended. Project drug-aid box aims to relieve some of the pressure these organisations face by continuously providing medicines and other First-Aid materials.

title: Support Healthcare for Women and Children in Syria
description: We need your support to maintain a healthy lifestyle for the war-affected women in Syria along with their newborn babies, so we can lessen the consequences of war and minimize the gap created after many reproductive health centers and hospitals became out of service. On the other hand, we would like to cross the bridge to the future with less diseases and with healthy generations that will enjoy good health to contribute to the reconstruction of the country.

title: Mental Health Awareness to 500 youth in Rwanda
description: After the Covid-19 pandemic hit in 2020 a lot of young people were desperate and worried about their future. The pandemic brought a lot of effects in the community including job loss, business shutting down which affected people's mental health as they became hopeless. This project aims to reach out to 500 young people including men and women in the age range of 15 - 24 years old  to talk about mental health and how to overcome the challenges brought by the pandemic

title: Lighthouse of Knowledge 2022
description: In the 6th generation of the project in 2022, with your help, we will train 60 high school students to develop and implement 15 projects in 15 underdeveloped municipalities in Serbia. High school students will, with the professional help of mentors and experts, work on designing and preparing projects on one of the five topics: environmental protection, public health, tourism, culture and social activism. All projects are designed and implemented to help local communities and their development.

title: Menstrual health  to 500 damsels in Nigeria
description: According to UNESCO, 1 out of 10 girls in Africa miss school during their menstrual period and eventually drop out. In Nigeria, sanitary pads costs an average of $1.30 per pack, while most families live below the poverty threshold of $1.20 per day. The high cost of sanitary pads in Nigeria have made them inaccessible for poor girls. In some situations, girls face sexual abuse in their quest for money to buy sanitary pads. SOHF aims to curb this ugly trend and reinforce the confidence in them.

title: Sports for children deprived of a family
description: Due to the current global situation with the pandemic (COVID19) along with the poor conditions in which many Venezuelans live in, the increase in the vulnerability of children and adolescents with disabilities, results in less access to an educational environment, games, and recreation. To combat these negative effects, Hogar Bambi Venezuela promotes the Sports and Recreation Project for Children and Adolescents Deprived of a Family.

title: Support parentless babies with their development
description: Due to the economic and social situation in Venezuela, more families are getting into extreme poverty, with lower income and few employment opportunities. As a result, there is an increase of abandoned children without any type of protection or shelter. This is why Hogar Bambi takes care of babies from 0 to 2 years old who arrive in unfavorable health conditions. These children are included in an early stimulation program in order to regulate their performance and sensorial responses.

title: Rewilding Australia
description: Undertaking Australia's most ambitious rewilding program - Newhaven Wildlife Restoration Project. Prior to European settlement, central Australia teemed with wildlife. Today it is a vast marsupial ghost town at the epicenter of global mammal extinctions. Introduced feral predators (cats and foxes), have robbed Australia of its natural capital and are the most significant driver of mammal extinctions. Cats kill around three million mammals, two million reptiles and one million birds every night.

title: EDUCATING HEROES
description: CHILDREN WITH CANCER NEED TO BE EDUCATED, MANY OF THEM HAS ABANDONED SCHOOL BECAUSE HOSPITALIZATION AND MOST ARE AWAY FROM HOME AND THEIR SCHOOLS.

title: Give succor & Refuge to 150 homeless poor in Niger
description: The recent flooding in Nigeria has affected the lives of many people, and the situation is still evolving.  Many of these families are living in shelters, which are overcrowded and unsanitary. They need food and water, medical supplies, clothing, and other necessities. They also need someone who cares enough about them. There are thousands of others who are in need of help. We know this is not an easy thing for us as individuals-but it is something we can do with our community support.

title: Sponsor a Student
description: Due to the Global Pandemic, we have not been able to host our annual silent auction so this year we are going digital! We are asking for our donors to help sponsor a student at the school. The Shining Light School, in the remote beach town of Ishahayi, has 182 students enrolled for this school year. We hope that this fundraiser can help us continue to raise funds for the school.

title: Build for Education in Humla
description: *Please note that the project is temporarily paused while some re-structuring gets finalised; thanks for your support and patience.*  Many government schools in Humla are not fit for purpose. This project will restore 16 schools to provide good  teaching facilities for over 2600 pupils and 112 teaching staff. A prime focus will be to ensure that girls receive similar  choices to boys and raise their educational standards and life chances.

title: Multipurpose hall construction in  S/East, Nigeria
description: The purpose of this multipurpose hall construction in Southeast Nigeria serves as a home for social enterprise of the organization, for empowerment purposes, youth Education Center and Information Technology Center connecting the village to the outside world. It will leverage educational and financial resources to increase and improve the life options for underserved rural communities in developing nations.

title: Underprivileged Children Education in Bangladesh
description: We have been supporting two primary schools since 1998 in remote Ramu hilly area of Cox's Bazar district to educate underprivileged children with the support of generous people like you. The schools educates the children from pre-schooling to Grade V.  Then the children are mainstreamed to local secondary schools. We have own school campus with sufficient building facilities. There are 350 children in 2 schools. Your donation will provide the teachers' salary, school furniture, children uniform,

title: Zakat can Empower Poor Parents in Bangladesh
description: We are committed to supporting the poor parents who are in economic hardship and engage their children in child labor. We are supporting 35 families of remote Ramu hilly area of Cox's Bazar district. We provide them an asset like sewing machine, rickshaw van, cows, goats, and poultry for their income generation activities. From your zakat, we will the support. The support will go to the extreme poor families of the school going children and trying to get rid of them from extreme poverty.

title: AUTISM AWARENESS 5KM RUN
description: The Autism Awareness 5KM Run will build a therapy center for children living with autism and provide free occupational and speech therapy services to over 300 children from rural areas in Kenya. Your donation to this project ensures maximum autism awareness is created in Kenya's rural areas and access to crucial therapy and education services is guaranteed for free.

title: CLEAN PLATE NUTRITION AND THERAPY PROJECT
description: Many children with disabilities in Kenya are limited in access to therapy services and nutritious foods that can help them improve their physical, emotional and mental health. The clean plate nutrition and therapy project serves children with Autism, cerebral palsy, and Down syndrome, in Mathare slums by giving them occupational and speech therapy services for free every week. The children also get nutritious food parcels each month. You too can be part of their recovery journey by donating now.

title: Ansys YouMeWe Charity Donation
description: A year like no others. Ansys is giving back to the community.   Across the Asia Pacific, the group will be doing a virtual 5K marathon from the middle of December until January 2022.  Funds raised will be disbursed across NPOs in Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the Philippines, and India that are focused on children and technology as they prepare for not our future but theirs.  When donating, please indicate in the comments box which country of NPO you wish to donate to.

title: I-CAR: an equipped minivan for Carmela
description: Carmela suffers from a serious genetic disease and the car the family uses to transport her is now obsolete, small and without adequate equipment. Having learned of the problem, we at IBO Italia felt called into question. We believe it is appropriate, as a community, to get involved in supporting her family in addressing this need. We have decided to donate to Carmela a new lifting system that can allow her to move more comfortably and safely with her loved ones.

title: Provide life changing education to children in DRC
description: Kimbilio has opened an amazing primary school, the only one in the area, offering the chance for former street children & local children living in poverty, to attend school! We will be giving the children the very best opportunities in life. Your support will enable more children to attend, as well as offering quality education. We are the only school in the area to provide computers and IT training, putting Kimbilio students ahead of the game when it comes to further education & finding a job.

title: Train streetconnected youth in organic agriculture
description: This project will enroll up to 12 street connected and homeless youth in a months residential training in organic agriculture in Kitale. Following the training we will look to see how the young people can apply their newly learn skills preferably back in their home community or otherwise on hired land.

title: Support Families with Children of Gaza, Give Hope
description: The Gaza Strip has an area of 365 km2,and is inhabited by more than 2 million people, with a population density of 5,453 people /km2,the highest in the world. Israeli attacks in Gaza have killed hundreds, injured thousands, and displaced tens of thousands. The Hope Foundation of Palestine Team in Gaza is ready to provide emergency aid to poor and needy families with children either directly or by creating projects that employ parents.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Donna and Maheera have been working with LI to help create & sustain businesses in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to train local entrepreneurs. Through this, vulnerable men and women will develop capacities in vocational & business skills to empower & equip them to escape extreme poverty.

title: Help Blind People in Syria to Work and Produce
description: Through this campaign, SEMA aims to provide material and logistical support for this center to continue supporting the blind and scale up its activities that train and care for them and help them secure an appropriate income. Your donation means that you light the way for the blind to work, produce, and invest the rest of their delicate senses to create products with a unique human sense made with insight from their hearts and souls.

title: Build Homes for 5 Women and their Children
description: This project will build and furnish 5 homes for disadvantaged widows and their children in Kassanda District of Uganda. We aim to strengthen families by providing brick homes for secure, healthier living with support of small community. Single mothers caught in the cycle of poverty, are often illiterate, malnourished and unable to meet their children's basic security needs.

title: Hearts Of Tomorrow I Fundacion Cognos
description: An initiative of the Cognos Foundation and FUNCOMAS designed to strengthen human values and life skills in low-income children who will soon become the generational replacement of our society.

title: Provide education, safe space for women & girls
description: Access to information and knowledge is the most effective method of self-empowerment. This is why at Gulu Women's Resource Center we provides free informal education to women and girls,  Safe space for all, Psychosocial support and GBV referral services  in Northern Uganda. Our workshops on topics such as women's health, women's rights, domestic violence, positive parenting and financial literacy help women gain the skills and confidence they need to change their lives for the better.

title: Helping families in Kenya survive the pandemic
description: Right now this pandemic is about day to day survival for the communities we work in Kenya - COVID-19 is far from over.  Everything is more difficult now.  Families are struggling without income or economic support, where health facilities are overwhelmed and progress on issues like gender based violence have gone into reverse.  Lives are in danger.  Our programmes provide the solutions to make sure these families are not left behind as the rest of the world emerges from this pandemic.

title: Akuafo Go Solar
description: Akuafo Go Solar is a Solar-Powered Drip Irrigation Model for Ghanaian Farmers in the Eastern Region of Ghana. The project is starting with the set up of a working model of the system and intends to reach 500 farmers in the region to improve and advance growing stability, as well as the full range of support needed to market products grown and preserved in the region. The project builds on research developed by a collaboration between The University of Ghana and Technical University of Denmark.

title: Empower with literacy
description: Imagine not being able to read, write or communicate. Literacy opens the doors to learning and a world of endless opportunities.  That's why we're transforming lives through this innovative, best-practice program for early years education.   We break the cycle of illiteracy and disadvantage by empowering community members to teach vulnerable children the literacy skills required for success at school and beyond. Because we believe literacy is freedom.

title: Send a Child in Nigeria to School for a Year
description: The mind is a terrible thing to waste."Thousands of children in Africa drop out of school each year simply because their parents cannot afford to cover tuition and school-related costs.  Their minds and potentials are wasted. The hopeful news is that together we can help create a new start for these children.We can mobilize a life-changing surge of love and support, by providing scholarships. These scholarships will ensure that children stay in school for a year covering tuition and related cost

title: Clean Water for Children in the Philippines
description: Planet Water Foundation has been working to address water poverty for over 10 years. Our approach creates change at both environmental and behavioral levels by providing clean safe drinking water through our community-based water filtration systems; promoting water-health & hygiene education; and prioritizing ongoing system monitoring & sustainability.  Our projects are focused on rural elementary schools as it is here where we can have the most impact.

title: Afghanistan Refugee Reception in Italy
description: We must act: Mission Bambini in partnershio with Fondazione ARCA wants to help to offer an answer to the needs of the thousands of Afghan refugees who, following the leaving from the country of the US and allied military forces, with the subsequent take of power of the Taliban had to leave Afghanistan. We have decided to act by supporting a project partner already active on this front offering, in addition to an economic contribution, its own specific experience in the educational field.

title: Help AmeriCorps Change the Landscape of Nashville
description: Our AmeriCorps members are often the first crisis response our neighbors see. In the past two years, our AmeriCorps have been on the front lines of flood relief, tornado response, and hunger through our food bank.   Here at Martha O'Bryan Center, we host more than 10 AmeriCorps each year to help us with our mission of defeating poverty in our community. While our programs run year-round, our AmeriCorps' approach to service learning and volunteering is vital in our work.

title: Advocacy 4 Mental Health Awareness, S/East Nigeria
description: Mental health disorders have a negative impact on the individual, society and global economy. The prevalence of mental disorders is increasing in young people, and if unaddressed, research has shown that they may develop into severe and chronic illnesses. Since 2012, SOHF has provided a holistic approach to help our youth overcome the scars of mental health and excel in life. We provide a nurturing environment with psychological and educational support. We're proud of our 100% development.

title: InHisName United Community Food Distribution
description: Funding would ensure that InHisName United can continue addressing food security concerns in our community. Many parents and the elderly depend on our food distribution program. The purchase of a transport vehicle and the onboarding of staff for our organization would greatly improve our processes regarding food distribution. Funding would allow for the onboarding of additional staff as well as extending our operations to reach more organizations that are willing to donate to this worthy cause.

title: Greenworks:  Student Engineering Projects Fund
description: This program funds student engineering projects around the world as part of our Greenworks Global Classroom.  Students who participate in the program work with our Global South partner classrooms to engineer tools and equipment (such as drones and microsatellites) to help their sister classrooms carry out their environmental stewardship work.  The engineering program works with disadvantaged students in the US Virgin Islands, US, Ukraine, Brazil, South Korea, and Indonesia.

title: Emergency Appeal For Primate Rescue Center
description: The last 18 months have been nothing like we could have anticipated with nationwide lockdowns, curfews, international travel restrictions, a struggling economy, and uncertainty about the future as the Covid pandemic persists. And in this incredibly challenging time the need for Colobus Conservation's services to rescue and care for threatened primates continues. And indeed the threats facing Kenya's primates are sadly increasing while our resources are critically stretched.

title: Changing scars into hope
description: 60% of the burnt victims around the globe are less than 6 years old. One of the main causes such as hot liquids is the case of  Ruth, Jack, Lucas and Griss whilst in the case of Jefrey, Italo and Niko is fire. The consequences these burn lesiones leave take up to 3 years to recover. 5 of these 7 children must travel a 30-hour trip from the outskirts of Lima and rural areas to receive their therapy sessions in ANIQUEM.

title: Support 200 mothers access maternal care in Ghana
description: #OperationHope: African Health Now plans to provide prenatal and postpartum health education, support access, and engagement in maternal health and reproductive services to 200 expecting mothers through their Pregnancy School Program initiative.   Furthermore, AHN will support Madina Polyclinic with medical equipment, supplies for new mothers and babies' during their first few weeks, and funds to cover essential medical expenses (Blood tests, vaccinations, ambulance transportation, etc.)

title: Releasing Rehabilitated Condors in Patagonia
description: PUMALIN and LIQUINE are two condors named after the places where they were found in 2020, unable to fly or survive on their own. They were taken to a Rehabilitation Center (CRARChile) for their recovery, and TODAY THEY ARE READY TO LIVE FREELY. Both will be translocated to PATAGONIA NATIONAL PARK to be released in January 2022. The project seeks to return these birds to the place where they come from, and contribute to the education and appreciation of the community about this species.

title: HIV Nutritional and Medical support.
description: This project helps us assist in the support of Cuban patients who are dealing with HIV in their lives. It is focused on an array of people, including men, women, and families. This project does not aim to provide the HIV drugs needed to treat these patients.  However, our goal is to provide the medications needed to deal with all of the side effects of the disease, as well as support in nutritional needs of the patients.

title: Support social enterprise project S/East, Nigeria
description: This project will help the organization's project sustainability plan. The food processing involves the processing of clean and harvested crops into marketable food products. The foundation engages into this as a way; to carry out her mission objectives, for Community, financial and organizational sustainability, to build a wide supply chain network and to help those that have vocational skills to acquaint themselves with entrepreneurial skill so as to be resourceful and be useful to themselves.

title: Food Distribution for Vulnerable Afghan People
description: Two months have passed since Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan, was taken over by the Taliban on August 15th. In August, people were fighting with anxiety, thinking about the possible problems that might face them in the future. Now their anxieties have become more realistic and are confronting them; lack of access to food. This project provides food packages to those who are in the most vulnerable place in Nangarhar province in Afghanistan.

title: Typhoon Maring (Kompasu) Early Recovery Response
description: This project will provide initial capital for the least-served and most affected families of STS Maring ("Kompasu") in La Union, Philippines. The target beneficiaries are from fisherfolk and farming communities. Hard hit areas are located in coastal barangay which primarily rely on farming and fishing with a total of 254 households that were selected through consultation with local People's Organization and LGUs.

title: Candles of Hope
description: Reviving Home's Candles of Hope program aims to provide education resources to students in war and crisis-torn countries. Phase 1 involves a small classroom of 10 students in one grade level in their home country. Due to years out of school, students will be assessed and periodically reassessed to determine their education level. Project enables COH by RH to develop an effective, scalable system for deploying education resources, with benefits that will endure beyond the demonstration project.

title: Provide Urgent Medical Attention To Syrians
description: This campaign aims to support URGENT medical needs of those most in need in northern Syria through supporting our hospitals, medical centers and mobile clinics located there

title: Support childhood safety and education in Vietnam
description: PeaceTrees Vietnam addresses the harmful legacies of the Vietnam War by clearing the land of explosives, building schools and libraries for local communities, and providing opportunities for sustainable agricultural development. Our programs include community and education centers, gardens, libraries, and kindergartens, which provide early education and food security for more than 3,500 children each year. This work would not be possible without your support.

title: Protect Zambian Forests with Clean Cookstoves
description: Kukula Solar plans to distribute 10,000 modern clean cookstoves to 10,000 families in rural communities of the Eastern Province of Zambia to reduce deforestation and avoid 100,000 tons of CO2 in the next 5 years while improving  health, quality of life,livelihood of people and protecting the forests.

title: fight 4 Gender Justice & women's Rights n Nigeria
description: Girls and women across Nigeria have fallen victim against sexual assault, rape and human trafficking. In Southeast, an estimated one in three women  experienced physical or sexual abuse in her lifetime. Samonyemaechi is committed to addressing gender-based violence through investment, research and learning, and collaboration with stakeholders . SOHF will launch an intensive program of education in 20 rural communities and schools to understand and prevent sexual violence.

title: Empower mothers to build their careers
description: Ukrainian children with disabilities face higher risks from war. The Russian declaration of war means the pressure on single mothers will increase. We purchase work equipment or pay educational course fees for moms of disabled children to ensure that they have the basic skills and supplies to work or run a business. Despite the duration of war, people will need the services these women train in, such as hairdressing. Their income eases their reliance on welfare and charity.

title: Digital Revolution Awards to Build a Boys School
description: Thank you! This year's Digital Revolution Awards have already raised nearly EUR 5000 towards St Martins school in Kenya. With your help, we'd like to double it. That's why we've created a new fundraising drive to raise a further EUR 5000 during the event itself, which would take us to an incredible total of EUR 10,000. Tweet using #DigitalRevAwards will see the organisers donate EUR 5 each time the hashtag is used, but you can also contribute through this page, too.

title: Shelters for 343 E Bali Earthquake Victim Families
description: A 4.8 Richter scale earthquake struck East Bali at 4.18am on Saturday 16 October when most people were sleeping. The epicentre was right under our steeply sloping mountain village of Ban on the northern slopes of Mounts Agung and Abang in East Bali, causing extreme damage: 363 houses totally destroyed, 762 suffered light to medium damage; and 123 Hindu temples were damaged, some severely. All 363 homeless families urgently need temporary houses, especially now the rainy season has started.

title: She's Making an Impact-Build a Classroom With Us!
description: Girls' education is not just about getting girls into school-it's about equipping girls with the life skills, knowledge, and confidence necessary to make informed decisions about their lives and future. By constructing and resourcing one of the 12 needed classrooms at Village Impact's new all-girls school, you'll help 600 vulnerable girls in Kenya to complete high school and gain the skills and confidence they need to realize their full potential.

title: Servicios Legales de PR (SLPR) GivingTuesday 2021
description: This #GivingTuesday, Puerto Rico Legal Services (SLPR) will launch a fund dedicated to ensuring thousands of people and communities access to the legal system and justice through education, training and legal representation. We need your support to continue offering free legal services to the nearly 50% of Puerto Ricans who qualify because they live in poverty.

title: Bless A Pastors child This Christmas 2021
description: Pastors Pastor pastors!!! All we think of when we hear of pastors is take prayer requests, ask them visit a sick sister or brother, ask to interpret a dream we don't understand or a scripture to mention but a few. I wonder even how many times these pastors ever get someone asking them how their family is, if they had food or their children are going to school. All we always think of is us first. Many Pastors families struggle with finding time for their families and others with expectations by c

title: Christmas gift or meal for your sponsored child
description: As we come to the holiday seasons, we would like to have the children celebrate Christmas as this is a holiday that every Ugandan child look up to because they expect some good food and a gift but this may not be so for many of the children in Uganda and we ask you to help them celebrate it

title: End illiteracy in Afghanistan by the end of 2025
description: An estimated 4.2 million children are out of school in Afghanistan - one of the most challenging places to be a child. For many Afghan children, completing primary school remains a distant dream. Global Education Campaign will provide a one-room school startup kit (2 Whiteboards, 40 mini chalkboards) and volunteer teacher training to help kick off 2,500 volunteer-run, one-room schools, educating 100,000 out-of-school children.

title: Empower Cambodian children with quality education
description: ODC has been offering English lessons to underprivileged children in Cambodia since 2015. By providing quality education, we help combat inequality and empower individuals. Being proficient in English opens opportunities for higher education and employment. Despite Covid-19, our 2022 enrolment increased to 190, with 30 on the waiting list. With increasing needs, our goal is to expand the number of classes and employ more local teachers, and if funds allow, to build a new library.

title: Supporting Afghan evacuees & asylum seekers
description: To support Afghan evacuees and people seeking asylum with their essential needs in the UK.  There are more than 700 Afghan evacuees and a similar number of people seeking asylum (from other countries) living temporarily in hotels in Kensington and Chelsea. While the Home Office is providing food and shelter, many things needed to create dignified living conditions are absent or in short supply. This project is to raise funds to provide personal clothing to 320 Afghan women.

title: DG Keith's EHAAT Charity Challenge
description: District Governor Keith Brownlie has chosen the Essex & Herts Air Ambulance as his Charity of the year. The Air Ambulance does a fantastic job in saving lives and Keith's aim is to help them save more. He is asking everyone in Essex and East Hertfordshire to donate whatever they can to support this lifesaving charity.

title: AVP WORKSHOP FOR STUDENTS IN RWANDA
description: The Alternatives to Violence Program (AVP) is a hands-on training program that prepares participants to deal with potentially violent conflict in new, positive, and creative ways. Schools in Rwanda are faced with various forms of violent conflict that students experience. Because of this problem, the Alternative to Violence program is the best solution to those violent students. 300 students from 10 secondary schools will be equipped with relevant skills to mitigate violence.

title: Give Free Antenatal Care to Poor Pregnant Women
description: This project will help poor pregnant women in Anambra State to register and go for Antenatal Care (ANC) free, in oder to protect their health and that of the unborn child. During antenatal care, women learn about healthy behaviors and can also access micronutrient supplementation, treatment for hypertension to prevent eclampsia, immunization against tetanus, as well as HIV testing services and medications to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HIV.

title: Higher Education reduces HIV stigma in Thailand
description: Our project offers infected and affected Thai children a secure and lovely environment, providing each child with a sense of self-worth and value within Thai society. We also offer our children the opportunity to continue their education through college or university. The foundation aims to provide the best opportunity to find their dream job and return to care for their family as a result of a better education.

title: Strengthen 1000s of Indian Families w/ Healthcare
description: People in India's informal housing settlements (aka slums) live one hardship away from slipping into an inextricable cycle of extreme poverty. Those hardships are often health related; an accident or a chronic but addressable consequence of poor nutrition. We support the independence and self-sufficiency of more than 20,000 people in Jaipur, India through 3 health clinics using education, treatment, and aid to help people avoid or recover from health and food security setbacks.

title: Support 42 indigenous women access better incomes
description: By boosting productive entrepreneurships of decorative items, bakery, water purification filters and wood saving stoves, indigenous tseltal women of Ch'ol, Selva Alta and T'uliha regions will be able to provide their families a better healthcare, home and income conditions, that enhance their possibilities to continue to build a dignified way of life.

title: Dedicated wildlife rescue vehicle
description: Rescuing snared animals requires input from dedicated people from various disciplines. These operations can be at any time of day or night and in inaccessible terrain. To get to these animals and to undertake snare sweeps we are in need of a rugged 4x4 vehicle with some added accessories. The rescue vehicle will be equipped with the necessary rescue equipment, veterinary medical supplies, recovery equipment and emergency equipment. This is vitally important to conduct wildlife rescues.

title: Wheelchair for Handicapped persons Living at Slums
description: This project will help the handicapped persons who are living in slums in Trivandrum district, Kerala state. These persons are physically challenged and face poverty and other financial issues. So we are planning to provide wheelchairs and tricycles for these people to do their daily wants and needs. And they can earn income through doing jobs like lottery ticket selling or other small-scale jobs. It will help them to improve their standard of living and stand independently.

title: The dream to walk again: new prosthetics for Ricky
description: "My dream? New prosthetics, so I'll have a normal life back." Cancer is taking Ricky's right lower limb. Ricky, 20 years old from Sanremo (Italy), has been visiting hospitals for 4 years. Now, despite 50 chemotherapies, a steam cell transplant and infinite post-surgery scars, the leg will be amputated to save his life before his 21st birth-day. So, Ricky needs bionic prosthetics with the necessary "accessories": foot and ankle joint. But the cost is 150,000: we need to stand by him.

title: Giving Tuesday 2021
description: This Giving Tuesday you will have the opportunity to strengthen our vision for peace and equity starting from our base in Loiza. With your donation we will be able to continue developing community health-workers, providing free psychological and psychosocial services for survivors of domestic violence, promoting community leaders and violence interrupters, creating community building activities and developing neutral violence-free zones in the communities and advancing human rights policies.

title: Education for Young Women in Kenya
description: Historically, the education of women and young girls has not always been a top priority for developing countries. Many families are impoverished, but girls are often the students who drop out of school because of extraneous reasons such as domestic responsibilities, menstruation and early. School closures in Kenya have had consequences for marginalized learners. Due to the pandemic, COVID-19 has deeply affected female education in Kenya. PCI plans to provide support for 100 girls in rural areas.

title: Working Together to End Orphanhood
description: Our vision is for every child to grow up in a safe and loving family and reach their full God-given purpose. World Without Orphans Europe calls and equips national leaders to collaborate in solving their countries' orphan and vulnerable child crisis through prevention and intervention efforts.

title: Providing a Safe and Loving Home for Every Child
description: Every child needs a nurturing family to fulfil their God-given potential. We want to make this a reality for thousands of children in Europe who are orphaned or unable to live with their family of birth. We identify and equip in-country leaders in their context. They work in their own communities to inspire families to provide homes, and partner with others to influence practice in the best interest of the child. We aim to improve the lives of 60,000 children in the next three years.

title: Support to Venezuela Migrant Families in Colombia
description: In PAN we transform lives through affection. We currently accompany Venezuelan migrant families who are in a vulnerable condition. We do this by contributing to the strengthening of families, we bring them closer to offers of institutional services and we guide them in the generation of income to meet their basic needs and their health, education, legal status and food security requirements. Be part so that more families who left their country of origin have all the opportunities in Medellin.

title: Help Youth in Cambodia Keep Their Learning Center!
description: Every year, PEPY's Learning Center Program in Siem Reap, Cambodia enables over 60 rural youth to get the confidence, resources, and technical skills they need to find skilled employment and pursue higher education. We need the support of our community to help keep this project afloat in 2022, as some of the foundations we partner with have unexpectedly lost their funding. Your donation, big or small, will help the recovery of the Cambodian economy and help youth achieve their goals.

title: PUTUP HEALTHFACILITY IN ZAMBULKURA FOR 10000PEOPLE
description: The project is to build second phase of 40 bed health facility in Zambulkura, recruit health professionals to provide quality care to 10000 people in 9 villages. Pregnant women, sick children, snakebites and emergencies will get quick access to care and reduce complications due to delays.The current 5% supervised hospital deliveries will increase to 95% within a year of operation to enhance safe child delivery.The facility will serve as immunization center and training of mothers on nutrition.

title: Vinnies NSW Christmas Appeal 2021
description: The Vinnies Christmas Appeal brings hope to those less fortunate in these uncertain times. Vinnies will provide material and emotional support to families experiencing immense hardship and struggling to feed their families, pay their bills and put toys under the tree at Christmas time. As the global pandemic continues to push people into poverty, your donation will make a difference in the life of those less fortunate.

title: Wildlife Corridors to Save Kangaroos
description: Australia's smallest tree kangaroo needs your help. We are building habitat in tropical Australia where over 90% of lush rainforest has been cleared here for agriculture.  This habitat is critical for the threatened Lumholtz Tree-kangaroo that lives only in this region.   We will plant 2,000 trees to create a wildlife corridor between two national parks that enable the endangered Lumholtz Tree-kangaroo to travel between these areas to find new habitat, food and mating opportuntities.

title: Help change the lives of pregnant women in Zambia
description: Help us build a new Mothers' Shelter for expectant mothers at the Kanyanga Rural Health Post.  Currently women walk up to 45km to arrive at a hot, dusty shelter, made of mud and poles with no facilities. Heavily pregnant women sleep on the hard ground and have only a grass enclosure for their toilet. These women walk a kilometre to fetch water from a muddy dam which is shared by cattle and other animals, and they carry the water in buckets on their head to use for bathing, drinking and cooking.

title: Community Reading Days
description: This initiative seeks to engage children (4-12 year olds) and their parents in fun-filled reading activities and parenting talks. The intention is to make the children fall in love with books, LEARN to READ so they can READ to LEARN and deeply get parents involved in their education.

title: Help us find local families for abandoned children
description: Diani Children's Village was formed in 1994 in Diani Beach Kenya. It's our aim to rescue abandoned children and babies and give them the needed care and attention that every child deserves. Over the last years the number of children who are committed to the Home and whose families or relatives are untraceable has grown tremendously. Therefore, our ultimate goal is to have every child in a stable, loving Kenyan family environment in which they can have the best possible shot at a normal life.

title: Mobile Digital Literacy lab for refugees in CO
description: This project will build a mobile computer lab that will provide computer and digital literacy training to adult refugees and immigrants in Colorado. Teach by Tech will travel to community spaces throughout CO to provide customized workshops helping participants emerge with new technical skills. Courses will teach basic to intermediate digital skills using Microsoft Office Suite and Google accounts.

title: Changing the World One Bedside at a Time
description: Palliative Care addresses health related suffering and is an essential primary health care service. IAHPC provides educational resources to  our members  to help them support their patients who are suffering. They also need to educate their policymakers and the public about palliative care. Advocacy is strongest when it includes the voices of those who deliver and those who receive palliative care. Few such resources exist to support palliative care advocacy or clinical care.

title: Keep 30 girls in school through theatre projects.
description: Girl child Art Foundation plans to provide 30 young girls exposed to domestic violence, sexual violence (rape), drugs abuse, early pregnancies, and emotional trauma the opportunity for free but formal education and a safe space to thrive through theatre arts. This project will ensure that underserved girls who drop out of school in the urban slums of Nigeria receive quality education through activities like stage performance classes, dance, singing, and psychosocial support.

title: BUILD A PLAY CENTER FOR CHILDREN IN ARGENTINA
description: POTENCIALIDADES creates early intervention spaces to give 700 kids the chance to flourish their potential in safe and nurturing spaces of play and development. We provide support for children in socially vulnerable situations in the Buenos Aires suburbs. For security reasons, we must leave the place where we are now and build a play center elsewhere. Help children who live in poverty in Argentina recover their childhood by building a new play center! Let's bring back the fun, laughter and joy!

title: Help 2400 families in Kerala - Flood Relief 2021
description: As peninsular India is staring down the barrel of climate catastrophe as a result of climate change and faulty land-use practices, flood is becoming an annual occurrence in Kerala.  Around 2400 families are taking refuge in Adimali and Cheruthoni flood relief camps. This project aims to provide flood relief to them in the form of ration kits, clothes, utensils, and educational support to 600 school-going children of the camps.

title: Sponsor an elephant @ The Elephant Valley Project
description: HELP US, HELP THEM. We are committed to providing a better life for the amazing retired and rescued elephants under our care, but we could not do this without you. Join our mission and sponsor your favorite elephant today! You can choose to sponsor monthly or make a one off donation! When you sign on as a sponsor you will receive a full color sponsorship certificate by email, periodic updates on your elephants, and your name  added to the donor list on our website and at the basecamp.

title: Send 50 Children Hawkers to School in Nigeria
description: This project will support the education of 50 children hawkers in Anambra State for 1 year. It is said that children of today are the leaders of tomorrow and as such, we must bring them up properly with the right skills, attitude and mindset to prepare them for future challenges, as they deserve quality life anchored on sound education and quality healthcare. Most of these children hawkers are from poor families, living with a guardian or orphans.

title: A Glass of Milk for Uruguayan Children
description: This project will provide 7,500 litres of milk per month to 3,552 vulnerable children of 13 social organizations in Uruguay.

title: PIFBS Hurricane Ida Relief Fund
description: This project will help us provide baseball and softball equipment to those affected by Hurricane Ida. Extensive damage has been reported along the East Coast, and recovery efforts are now underway. Our goal is to ensure this disaster does not keep kids off the diamond in 2022.

title: This #GivingTuesday we are Better Together!
description: The foundation of who we are lies in our holistic prgrams. We believe that radical transformation can happen through the empowerment of the whole person.   We are commiitted to improving our artisans economic, spirtual, emotional and social well-being.   Our desire is for generational cycle of poverity to be broken among our communities through the access of education, our artisans are improving their standard of living and cultivating a brighter future for their famlies.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, high school students, Anirudh, Vinay, Chetan, and Aayushi, have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Life Skills for 50 teens in Mexico
description: Promote the economic empowerment of women through the development of soft skills and trades in order to have better economic and employment opportunities to achieve autonomy and economic independence that allows them to develop skills to prevent them from living or tolerating situations of violence, exploitation and abuse.

title: Support Afghan Refugees in the United States
description: Following the withdrawal of US troops and the collapse of the Afghan government, tens of thousands of Afghans refugees have been evacuated to the US and to third countries around the world; many of those currently in third countries ultimately hope to reach the US. Those already in the US will need support in starting a new life and adjusting to their new society. This project will help refugees integrate in to their new communities and help with basic necessities.

title: Give A Stray A Chance for Christmas
description: They are unloved, neglected, starving, sick, injured and sometimes dying - they are the estimated 4000 stray and unwanted animals that will be admitted to our facility in their thousands this festive season. This is not only shameful - it's a crisis! A crisis in compassion for the human race and a financial crisis for the SPCA, these animals will all need to be transported to our facility, they'll need food, shelter, veterinary attention and lots of love to give them a Chance for Christmas.

title: Teach 30 underserved young women textile design
description: GCAF plans to provide thirty underserved young women and girls with a beneficial and safe environment to learn textile design. The project is for girls exposed to discrimination and sexual violence (rape), drugs abuse, hawking and opportunity for free training and a safe space to thrive through textile design. The training includes creating designs, batik, tie and dye training, and fabric pattern designs. The foundation offers textile training along with psychosocial support.

title: Free Physiotherapy to 100 people with disabilities
description: People with physical disabilities require physiotherapy services to achieve daily activities and independent functional mobility. AIFO India started a free physiotherapy service for people with disabilities who can't afford physiotherapy services. People affected by leprosy, people with disabilities, burns victims, stroke, and daily wage labour will benefit from this project.

title: Elevate Education for Rural South African Children
description: Providing educational opportunities to over 1000 infants, children & adults in rural South Africa to build essential life-skills, numeracy, literacy and agricultural skills. Our mission is to empower people to create their own successful lives as contributing members of society. Our holistic approach includes skills development and feeding schemes that encourage self-sufficiency. Our staff is employed from within the community and in 2022 we aim to expand our offerings to help even more people.

title: DISASTER RELIEF AND RECOVERY
description: DDEF is a cooperative body that is made up of representatives from faith-based, non-profit, non government, business and other organizations working within DDEF to assist individuals and families as they recover from COVID-19. The goal of the DDEF is to unite recovery resources with community needs in order to ensure that even the most vulnerable in the community recover from the disaster.

title: Help give 10 000 girls washable sanitary pads
description: Many girls in South Africa do not go to school because they cannot afford menstrual products each month. African Angels, a social enterprise in partnership with Days for Girls, creates employment for women in Chintsa East, South Africa, making washable sanitary pads - our Kit.  Our beautifully made washable pads last up to three years, reducing plastic pollution, creating employment, and helping keep girls in school. Help us provide our Kit to over 10 000 South African girls by the end of 2022.

title: Louisiana Tornado Relief Fund
description: This disaster relief fund will support people impacted by the tornados in Lake Charles and the surrounding area of Louisiana in the form of emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. The fund will transition to provide longer-term assistance as needed. All donations to this fund will exclusively support communities and first responders impacted by these storms.

title: Support Human Rights Activists in Syria
description: The Syria Justice and Accountability Centre relies on a network of documenters and activists across Syria and refugee communities who work with survivors and their families to record the details of their experiences. This documentation work is extremely challenging and highly technical, and documenters need customized, Arabic language trainings to gain the skills necessary to collect detailed documentation that can be used as criminal evidence and help survivors achieve their vision of justice.

title: Make Cloth Diapering Accessible for US Families
description: We support partners in the United States who work with families struggling to afford diaper need. Our reusable cloth diaper kits help save on funds for other basic needs while also maintaining health and sanitary conditions for the people they serve. In the United States, 1 in 7 children live in poverty. Oftentimes, these families are sacrificing one basic need to afford the other. This can include choosing between food and diapers. We aim to end that choice.

title: Providing-potable-water-to-thousands-in-india
description: The lack of uncontaminated water for drinking, cooking and bathing is a serious problem in Odisha, one of India's most impoverished states. SevaChild International has installed clean water systems in two of Odisha's leper colonies, and has earmarked nine rural villages in Odisha that are without uncontaminated water. Villagers in some instances need to walk as far as five miles to find clean water that they take back to their homes via heavy pots -- a difficult task.

title: Zululand Pangolin Recovery and Research Node
description: Pangolins are the most trafficked mammal in the world with more than a million poached in the last decade. The Zululand Conservation Trust works hand-in-hand with the African Pangolin Working Group (APWG), and the Johannesburg Wildlife Veterinary Hospital to manage the rehabilitation of confiscated animals. The costs associated with rewilding pangolins includes monitoring, satellite & VHF tags, equipment and veterinary costs. Funds are needed to develop our Pangolin Recovery and Research Node .

title: Empower Rural Tribal People Through Education
description: This project will equip the Lahu tribes of northern Thailand to read and write the Lahu language.  In the process of learning their own language, they will see the many connections between the written Lahu and the rich Lahu cultural heritage they have inherited.  The skills of reading and writing Lahu will allow many to advance in their field of work, being able to communicate through the written word.  These skills will also help them to learn other languages providing additional opportunities.

title: Help support the refugee community on Samos!
description: This project will support the refugee community on the Greek island of Samos. A new camp has recently opened which despite improvements in infrastructure and facilities, lacks a feeling of warmth and opportunity for residents to connect beyond the camp walls. That is why, we have been working together with the camp residents (our community volunteers), to create a greater feeling of community.

title: Improving Nursing & Midwifery Care in Liberia
description: The FOL-Liberian Health Team will offer innovative and unique continuing professional development workshops in January 2022.  20 nursing and midwifery faculty will attend Monday to Wednesday; 21 hospital supervisors will attend Wednesday to Friday; the overlap day with both groups, will allow academic and practical sides of health care delivery to talk. The goal is to enhance competencies and evidence-based theoretical and clinical performances of faculty, nurses, and midwives.

title: The Lester Howse Fund
description: Many Indigenous elders who were victims of the forced assimilation efforts put forth by the church and state via residential and boarding school systems are in need of housing and stability in their later years. The Lester Howse fund has been established to help elders who face financial hinderances with home repairs and safe housing accessibility.

title: Plan, Build & Sell-Help Build & Outfit Classrooms
description: Girls' education is not just about getting girls into school-it's about equipping girls with the life skills, knowledge, and confidence necessary to make informed decisions about their lives and future. By constructing and resourcing one of the 12 needed classrooms at Village Impact's new all-girls school, you'll help 600 vulnerable girls in Kenya to complete high school and gain the skills and confidence they need to realize their full potential.

title: SUPPLYING CLEAN WATER TO THE ORPHANAGE -  SCHOOL
description: Having access to adequate sanitation is the only way that would help reduce illness and deaths of young children and people caused by drinking unclean water, from different sources, located nearby or far away of the Orphanage and Iwacu Kazoza School. A  Well has been drilled and Water has been found; it is pure and plenty of water. The remaining work to be done is to install water solar pump, pipes, build water tanks then to supply water  to the school, orphanage and surrounding community.

title: SOARing Through Difficult Times
description: COVID has taken its toll on everyone, whether physically, emotionally or financially. BITS is no exception. We are working harder than ever to help the increased number of people in our community combat depression, anxiety and loss. Costs of doing so has grown, as expense of caring for our horses has grown nearly 200% due to COVID. We need your help to support BITS in any way you can. By making a recurring donation to BITS, YOU will help us lift our community from the harmful impacts of COVID.

title: Ballymena changing lives through Rotary Foundation
description: Rotary Foundation aims to advance world understanding, goodwill and peace by improving health, providing quality education improving the environment and alleviating poverty. The Rotary Club of Ballymena aims to raise funds to support the various Foundation initiatives, including polio eradication, being undertaken across the world.

title: Language Justice Trainings in Sonoma County
description: This project will fund language justice workshops for community based organizations and local government who are providing day-to-day services and activate during disasters in Sonoma County. Language justice centers on equitable communication: practices that support each person's capacity to communicate authentically in their language(s), and hence to participate fully in the contexts where they work, live, think, and interact. These workshops offer an introduction to the concepts and practices.

title: Risk mitigation in urban settlements in Cartagena
description: In Cartagena de Indias, the most vulnerable populations such as Afro-descendants, indigenous people, and migrants are  concentrated in the areas with the highest natural risks, having the highest levels of poverty in the city. Through participatory workshops, we seek to increase the resilience capacity of these communities, so that they are not so affected by catastrophic events and that they can recover better, through community risk maps, reinforcement of homes and greater awareness of risk.

title: Health Screening Ship to Remote Islands in Palau
description: Peace Winds has outfitted and staffed a former cargo ship to provide basic medical services to the Republic of Palau-an island nation comprised of more than 340 islands in the Western Pacific. The Kenshin, Japanese for "checkup," is currently providing basic hospital services, health check-ups, and capacity building for the prevention of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Palau's remote islands.

title: Support Reproductive Healthcare in Tanzania
description: FAME is an in-patient hospital and clinic committed to advancing quality medical care in rural Tanzania. From the beginning, we set out to provide communities in the northern highlands of Tanzania with a unique healthcare experience - one marked by patient-centered care and high-quality service. In that spirit, FAME endeavors to meet the medical needs of ordinary Tanzanian people, and currently has a catchment area of 2.9 million Tanzanians living in the most rural parts of the country.

title: Indigenous-led Renewable Energy Initiative
description: 1 in 3 Native Americans lives in poverty.  For many, discriminatory energy pricing is a primary reason. Indigenized Energy Initiative is a first-of-its-kind, indigenous-led effort to empower Native American tribes to regain sovereignty by taking control of their own energy systems and deploying regenerative solar and other renewable technologies as a culturally-appropriate way to diminish energy poverty, mitigate climate change, and restore vitality, vibrancy and hope to American Indian tribes.

title: Christmas Appeal
description: As 2023 is approaching, we at Building Futures in Malawi are raising funds to meet our 2023 plans and mission. 2023 looks like it will be a very exciting year for us and in addition to our current projects we are working with the commissioner for refugees in the hope of delivering an education programme at Dzaleka Refugee Camp which is close to our base in Lilongwe. We will continue to implement all our projects in the 8 schools that we work with the hope of expanding to some other schools

title: Stop child sexual abuse through global education
description: Stop the Silence is moving forward with our national model (awareness-raising, education, training, policy reform) of comprehensive child sexual abuse (CSA) prevention and mitigation in the U.S. and other countries around the world in partnership with governments, local non-profit groups, corporations and foundations.

title: Include Us - Zimbabwe Deaf people and Families.
description: Nzeve is an organisation of deaf and hearing people promoting the rights of children and youth with disabilities to participate fully in society. Nzeve works with families, communities, deaf leaders & role models ensuring children with disabilities receive early intervention and support; deaf children in schools receive the resources they need for their education; deaf youth have the opportunity for tertiary education and employment; and deaf communities have a voice to advocate for their rights

title: Feed 1000 Guatemalan Children for 10 Months
description: This project will provide free daily nutritional supplements to 1000 Guatemalan preschool students living in rural communities for the next 10 months as a part of the Let's Be Ready educational program.

title: Bachelor degrees and jobs for at-risk Uruguayans
description: ANIMA is an educational organization with the goal to bring together the job market and the world of education by providing at-risk Uruguayan youth with tuition-free education in the areas of IT and business administration. With a special focus on the professional and human development of our students, ANIMA is committed to help reduce the high rate of youth unemployment in Uruguay as well increasing the chances of youth obtaining their high school diploma.

title: Support children with disability to get education
description: This project will create a disability-friendly environment for children 4-19 years of age (who either dropped out of school or never enrolled in schools due to their physical disability) at Raymond Empowerment Foundation community schools. Our immediate objective is to adjust our school facilities to: have wheelchair accessible doorways, ramps at entries and exits of buildings, widen corridors of buildings for easy access, and construct accessible washrooms for physically disabled children.

title: Madagascar Famine Relief Fund
description: Madagascar is prone to devastating disasters, including the impact of tropical cyclones, recurring drought, and development challenges. The island country faced the world's first climate-caused famines in 2021.

title: Improving The Welfare Of Captive Primates
description: Primates are often illegally smuggled to be sold as pets and many end up living in isolation. Globally many trafficked wild animals are confiscated by government authorities, which puts pressure on captive facilities to take in animals and many are not equipped to meet their welfare needs, causing further suffering. Wild Welfare provides support to captive facilities sharing skills and species-specific knowledge to help ensure that individual primates are not only able to survive but thrive.

title: Rural Myanmar Women Prosper with Pig Farming
description: Pig Farming in our rural partner villages has proven effective in increasing household income. New pig farmers receive financial, technical, and material support from Muditar, our sister organization in Myanmar. Farmers pay back the cost of their pig after the first year. As the farmers gain experience, they share knowledge with new farmers through group discussions and committees. Providing livelihood opportunities to women empowers them to become more confident leaders in their communities.

title: Empower 350 Liberian Women
description: This project addresses the Liberian mental health crisis where more than 40% of Liberians suffer from post-traumatic stress and/or a major depressive disorder. We will expand our existing 12-week evidence-based interpersonal group therapy program for women in several ways. We will increase the number of weekly group sessions, create Train the Trainer therapy coaching, provide compensation to therapy Leads, and offer transportation to and from group therapy sessions.

title: Build Cooperatives with Indigenous Women in Mexico
description: This sustainable community-led development project serves to empower rural and Indigenous women entrepreneurs through the Sierra Madre Network, a cooperative incubator based in rural Hidalgo, Mexico. Through biweekly skills training, community impact projects, and dynamic networking opportunities, four women-led cooperatives learn how to propel their businesses forward, hone personal and professional development skills, and combat social, economic, and gender inequality as local changemakers.

title: Empower 2100 young women through quality work
description: Your gift will transform the lives of 2100 women by providing them with the resources to gain fairly-paid, safe employment once they finish their education. Around the world, less privileged and marginalised women face exploitative work environments, and are at greater risk of sex trafficking and abuse. With your support, we can work with our partners to ensure women receive mentoring, vocational training, and scholarships, so they can pursue empowering work and gain financial independence.

title: End Poverty, Empower Rural Women in Congo
description: Under this project, 1000  poor rural women will be connected with banks (Saving Groups) to start  businesses and create sustainable jobs for themselves and their peers. Here training would be provided in the area of capacity building, life skills, tech and agribusiness (food production and processing, beekeeping, goat farming, organic manure, dairy, etc) for increasing their self-confidence level, livelihood growth and empowerment

title: Play, sport and debat for a better living together
description: The objective is to train and support actors in priority neighbourhoods to make sport an effective tool for education. The diversity of the proposed training programmes will make it possible to meet the needs of the partner communities or associations, which will also be able to choose the themes of Living Together that best correspond to the challenges of their territories from among a wide range of content (including discrimination, violence, disability, etc.).

title: Build Health International Giving Tuesday
description: We believe that achieving global health equity requires approaching each day with the tenacity to make a sustainable impact. On any given day, the scope of our work can shift to address natural disasters, infectious diseases, or political instability. With each challenge that arises, we remain committed to delivering healthcare solutions that serve low-resource communities. In the spirit of approaching each day with impact, we hope you will join us by making a gift to BHI this Giving Tuesday.

title: Help us journey with more youth facing adversities
description: In celebration of Trybe's 26th Anniversary, we thank you all for being part of our journey. We journey with our youth, their families, volunteers, donors, working partners and staff.  During this pandemic, nobody is spared. Many of our youth come from complex family backgrounds with little or no support. Every day is a struggle, yet many work hard, showing resilience above their adversities in life.  Please support us, help us journey with more youth facing adversities.

title: Support Beekeeping-Save our People & Biodiversity
description: Around the JUCHOFAIM School Farm in Maluku County - Kinshasa Province, in the Democratic Republic of Congo AgroMwinda supports 12 associations  of beekeepers. We have also established our own city of bees composed of 250 bee hives. In a context of COVID-19 and strong pressure on natural resources, beekeeping represents an opportunity to diversify agricultural income, while encouraging integrated and sustainable management of land, forest resources and biodiversity.

title: Supporting ECD Centres in Rural Public Schools
description: 30% of the children who join grade 1 drop out in grade 1 before they learn to even write their name. Most if not all of them have never had a chance to go attend pre-school or any ECD centre.  This project aims to support the set up and operation of Early Childhood Development (ECD) centres in rural public schools in Uganda. This will provide access to quality education and a learning environment for millions of pre-school children across the country, setting them on a success trajectory.

title: Complete safewater project for 168 rural learners
description: This project will complete a safe water project for  children at Mt Matedzi Secondary in  Manicaland District. The school  has an enrollment of 168 learners who battle for clean water in long queues at a community borehole . The project will set up pipes and taps in the school premises so that learners can safely access drinking water and water for the toilets . Children are currently missing out lessons as they spend time seeking water , this also affects their performance .

title: Join us to break the cycle of poverty
description: We need to strengthen IPTI Brazil to keep developing social technologies to break the cycle of poverty. We will use the knowledge acquired by IPTI during its existence to fast forward its impact in the next five years.  In the last 18 years: +34,000 beneficiaries, 40 municipalities, 8 Brazilian states, 5 local businesses (creative and digital).  For the next 5 years (our goal): +120,000 beneficiaries, +100 municipalities, 4 new "Santa Luzia do Itanhy".

title: Empower Haitians With Disabilities Now!
description: Empower Haitians With Disabilities Now! provides scholarships for academic and technical training and associated supplies to five physically impaired adults, resulting in increased self-esteem, economic autonomy, and respectful inclusion in Haitian society.

title: Help a young mom in Cameroon receive an education
description: CAMAAY plans to send teenage mothers in Cameroon back to school, granting them education to attain success and opportunities for themselves and their families.

title: Promoting Inclusive Education of Blind Girls
description: In Nepal, education policy-makers are not aware of what inclusive education really means. The government is therefore failing to ensure an inclusive high quality education system for Dalit ("untouchable") girls with blindness who are between 5-16 years of age. As a result, in remote rural Nepal, illiteracy remains high among Dalit women with blindness.  Dalit girls with disabilities face multiple forms of discrimination and violence because of their caste, gender and disability status.

title: Provide Care for the Elderly in Nigeria
description: Care For Healthy Life Initiative plans to support 100 elderly people in Anambra State. Aging is associated with functional decline plus health and social support needs. Older people worldwide consume the most health spending of any age group and there is also an increasing number older people worldwide, especially in developing countries like Nigeria.

title: Safe Periods for girls in Nigerian urban slums
description: This project will provide sanitary kits for underserved girls in the urban slums of Nigeria. Providing Sanitary kits for underprivileged girls in slums will help girls stay in school, reduce transactional sex for pads, and reduce teen pregnancy.  The project will also equip the girls with menstrual health management knowledge to help them care for themselves, understand their bodies, and protect them.

title: Prevent Child Trafficking Through Mentorship
description: In Northern Thailand, The Freedom Story works with children at risk to prevent human trafficking and child sexual exploitation through our 3 primary programs; Education, Human Rights & Sustainable Livelihoods. Our Education Program provides holistic support to keep at-risk children in school. One way that we do that is by pairing our students with staff mentors to ensure they have stable, adult relationships that they can rely on in times of need.

title: Rehabilitation for burn survivors in Taiwan
description: Sunshine Social Welfare Foundation will help 350 people suffering from burns in Taiwan regain their physical functions, self-confidence and ability to live independently by providing comprehensive and specialized burn rehabilitation services. This includes physical and occupational therapy, pressure therapy, in addition to psychosocial support. Services are offered at the Sunshine Rehabilitation Center in Taipei, as well as through home outreach visits.

title: Give burn survivors access to rehabilitation
description: This project will provide training to enhance burn rehabilitation skills of professionals like therapists and social workers from low-middle income countries, either through trainings held in their own country, or through internships held at Sunshine Foundation in Taiwan. By building the skills and knowledge of burn professionals, we ensure that burn survivors can receive better care locally, and regain their physical functions, self-confidence and ability to live independently.

title: New therapy concepts for childhood leukemia
description: Every fifth child does not respond to the currently available therapies and suffers a relapse. These relapses are very difficult to treat and a cure is unfortunately often not possible. Prof. Bourquin and his team therefore aim to find new points of attack for the treatment of highly resistant leukaemias in children. Donate now to this cancer research project and make a significant contribution to improving the chances of cure for children with high-risk leukaemias.

title: Grow business and leadership skills for 100 girls.
description: The Foundation plans to educate 100 young women in Nigeria on business and leadership skills for a profitable livelihood. The project bridges the gender inequality gap in society and rehabilitates victims of sexual violence (rape), and drugs abuse. The business and leadership training has a curriculum that includes strategizing, effective communication, training/coaching, delegating, ethical values, innovation, and mentoring alongside mental fitness to enable them to thrive in a safe space.

title: 'Oasis Projects' for kids across Venezuela
description: The Oasis Project will transform a barren area in Petare - the biggest slum in Venezuela - into a fun, safe place where 1000 kids will be able to play, rest, and have a source of clean water; a place designed by 76 of the children themselves. In 2021, we raised enough funds to make this Oasis a reality - and as we build it this year, we're refocusing our fundraising efforts to raise money to replicate it in other areas of the country, so even more children can have their very own Oasis.

title: Give a Gift 2022
description: This holiday season Help Colombia wants to put smiles on the faces of 1000 LESS-FORTUNATE CHILDREN from two of Medellin's most vulnerable neighbourhoods - Barrio Moravia & El Botadero.   Most of these kids don't receive Christmas presents since their parents can barely afford to put food on their tables. However, with your generous donations, we can change that! We'll make sure that all of these kids feel a little more special, loved, and remembered this Christmas.

title: HELP FIGHT CLIMATE ACTION IN S/EAST NIGERIA
