description: This project will engage rural communities in planting trees and minimize the use of fossil fuels, and focus on developing alternative sources of energy that are clean and sustainable. We will focus on both carbon emissions reduction and carbon removal with our biochar program. We will reach out to small  farmers in rural areas and show them a better way to handle their crop waste. It will increase awareness towards reducing global warming, to give our earth a chance to heal and rebalance.

title: Help Fund Cape CARES Fall Clinic's in Honduras
description: Cape CARES was founded on the principle of continuity; providing medical and dental care year after year, serving the needs of long-term health care in rural Honduran communities. It all started with the realization by our founders that there was a huge gap in follow up care from the medical and dental mission trips to the global south.  Since 1988, Cape CARES has treated families and communities for three generations, making us one of the oldest NGO's in Honduras!

title: Help 750 families in TamilNadu - Flood Relief 2021
description: After three years, rain fury and floods have returned to haunt Tamil Nadu. The tropical cyclone activity in the northern Indian Ocean (the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea) is yet another glaring example of Climate Change that the world is witnessing. Around 600 families have taken refuge in the relief camps of Chennai.This project aims to provide flood relief to them in the form of ration kits, clothes, and utensils.

title: Raise Khanyisa Orphaned Elephant Snaring Survivor
description: Orphaned albino elephant, Khanyisa's journey of survival is nothing short of inspirational! Her story has touched the world. She was found in January 2020, as a four-month old calf - alone, without her herd in sight, with a poacher's snare around her cheeks and ears. Her injuries were severe. Wildlife vets estimated that she spent four days stuck in the snare. Now two years old, Khanyisa (meaning Sunshine in Shona) is fully rehabilitated and has been integrating into a rescued elephant herd.

title: Biochar: Bringing toxic land back  to life
description: The overall  goal of this project to work together in collaboration with the  local  people to use Biochar to convert land that has been degraded by small-scale gold mining into arable land; to change soil structure by removing toxins and heavy metals from the soil, and plant trees to maintain vegetation and forest, restore destroyed coffee and cocoa farms with tree inter plant and boost local economy for 1000 people in Ghana.

title: Bringing Sustainability to Nigerian Conservators
description: Ki Culture promotes sustainable practices within the cultural sector on a global scale. The Ki Futures program, which provides an international network of coaching and interactive training, empowers cultural institutions and professionals to take action for sustainability. Unfortunately, sustainability is currently not affordable for all. Our aim is to enable 13 conservators from Nigeria to attend Ki Futures: computers, internet access and transportation is all they need.

title: 100 Hope Bus Scholarships for Iraqi girls and boys
description: The Iraqi Children Foundation's "Hope Bus" project is an initiative to fight child labor, early marriage, lack of education, malnutrition, and physical and emotional wounds after years of war and poverty.  These colorful, child-friendly buses provide academic tutoring, healthy lunches, psycho-social services, and childhood fun to some of Iraq's poorest orphans and street kids.  A scholarship for one boy or girl at the Hope Bus is $100 per month.

title: 2021 Campaign: Educate at-risk youth in Kenya
description: We operate a residential school in rural Kenya where we support more than 220 orphans and at-risk youth from preschool through 8th grade, providing them with a nurturing home, food, medical care, and one of the best academic programs available in the region. We consistently rank among the top schools in our district of over 140 schools and have ranked 1st multiple times in the last 5 years. We work hard to maximize the impact of our resources and operate on a lean budget of $1 per child per day.

title: Tackling illegal trade in North American songbirds
description: For hundreds of years, songbirds have been caged to meet demand for melodious songs and beautiful plumage. Many songbirds are threatened by illegal and unsustainable trade. Some species found in the wilds of North America end up in cages in other parts of the world, including the European Union (EU). Some of this trade is facilitated by poor enforcement and use of legal loopholes. To tackle this little-known issue, research to support enforcement and inform consumers is needed.

title: Internet for Impoverished Myanmar Students
description: Thousands of students in Myanmar have been forced out of school due to the February 2021 military coup, COVID-19, and intensifying violence in the country. While the population in general faces a humanitarian crisis, millions of youth do not have access to education. This project will enable around 400 Myanmar youth access to quality online learning programs for their future academic and career success, at the National University of the Union of Myanmar (NUUM).

title: Drops of Hope: Winter Relief in Lebanon
description: The project is targeting the most vulnerable families that are not living in deplorable conditions of all nationalities to provide them with their needs according to the latest needs assessment and as per the needs of each targeted population.  The beneficiaries from Aarsal and Beqaa from the distribution of food parcels, heaters and fuel, plastic sheets, blankets and mattresses.

title: Make Christmas special for DRC street children
description: We like Christmas to be special for all the children we support at Kimbilio. Each year we have a special party.  We make sure all the children get a present. For children who have been living on the streets an event like this is a big deal & being offered a present rather than begging on the streets means a lot.  This year we opened a Primary School for over 150 former street children & children whose families can't afford to send them to school. We'd like them to have a party & present too.

title: Stop Children signing up to a Gang in South Africa
description: In South Africa we are working in one of the most dangerous gang lead townships. Many parents are unemployed, leaving an increase in gang recruitment across all ages. Since COVID School has dropped to part time leaving the children on the streets for longer. IGNITE is a community lead project that provides a support network for children in the community. Currently 127 children attend and get a free meal, often the only food they get, support with homework and play games/sport with our team

title: A textile collective for Eldorado-Diadema, Brazil
description: The Eldorado Textile Collective facilitates training in textiles and sustainable fashion for approximately 40 women and young people from the disadvantaged community of Eldorado, Sao Paulo, giving them a safe space to work, support from the ACER community centre, an opportunity to earn an income and to widen their personal and professional horizons, find meaningful employment and contribute to the local economy.

title: "Hygiene and menstrual health in adolescents"
description: Strengthen attitudes, habits and knowledge for a healthy life of 500 girls, boys and young people from rural schools in the towns of Los Altos de Chiapas. Implement educational workshops in 4th. 5th. and 6th grades of rural primary and secondary schools in 6 localities with the theme "Menstrual health and hygiene in girls and adolescents. Train and strengthen knowledge for parents, teachers and educational committees.

title: Empowering 50 women entrepreneurs to beat poverty
description: Currently, a large number of young women and girls in semi-urban and rural areas support their family incomes by managing a combination of small and micro-enterprises. However, they don't have the required skills to sustain them. The 50 women in Rajasthan, who will receive support belong to extremely resource poor backgrounds, have always been left behind due to their gender, and have the determination to become independent and self-sufficient. Your support will help them build these skills.

title: Build SA's 1st Free-Tailed Bat Flight Cage
description: This project will build the only free-tailed bat rehabilitation flight cage in South Africa! Providing the safe space needed to get them back on the wing and enabling the bats to build up their flight muscles, so that they can be successfully released back into the wild. 100's of free-tailed bats end up in rehabilitation centres after either having been orphaned or injured. Without a flight cage for release preparations, they must either spend the rest of their lives in cages or put down.

title: Empower 300 girls to end gender based violence
description: iPartner India aims to empower 300 vulnerable girls and women in the urban slums of Kolkata, West Bengal, India. These girls and women face gender-based violence and abuse at home and extensive limitations on their ability to move freely and to make decisions affecting their work, education and marriage. We aim to build the leadership and negotiation skills of the young girls and women in the community through gender and sports training to end gender-based violence, discrimination, and stigma.

title: Ojala! Spanish learning app for refugees
description: Ojala! is the first app to learn Spanish for people on the move. Offering courses in languages such as Wolof, which are not offered by existing apps and to people limited literacy, it can be an essential tool for migrants and refugees on the Canary Islands to access social and legal services and the labor market, as well as for integration into the local society. Beyond disseminating and improving the app, the team will train local teachers on the Canaries to teach Spanish as a foreign language.

title: Close the Imagination Gap for Girls Worldwide
description: Your donation will help us close the Imagination Gap and reach our goal of welcoming more girls to our 6 Virtual Camps planned for 2023, as well as expanding our in-person Career Girls Clubs to new schools in the SF Bay Area and Washington D.C. Metro Area.

title: Progress for 100 Dominican kids with special needs
description: This project prepares children, adolescents and young people with special needs to face the challenges of living in a society that is still developing to be totally inclusive. With the orientation and support of our foundation and their parents they will be able to go to school, learn skills for employment, be included in their family, community and the Dominican society as a individual with the same needs as any other person plus some extra. The outcome depends on the level of their disability.

title: Provide An Empowering Workplace for Women in Ghana
description: Global Mamas puts an emphasis on creating a space for women to succeed and achieve financial independence by following fair trade practices and supporting a safe and empowering work environment for women producers.

title: Programming to help Argentinian low income youth
description: The crisis is increasingly harming the formal and professional labor market in Argentina. However, the software industry grew more than 300% over the last decade, creating a fast-growing demand for technological profiles. IntegrarTEC is a scholarship program specially designed for those who want to be programmers. It is mentor-based and benefits from the knowledge accumulated during 16 years of experience supporting vulnerable students and preparing them to join the labor force.

title: Help leaping our students' influence in 2022!
description: We look back at a year full of impact: from several powerful initiatives to updates in governance, reinvented branding, a new virtual infrastructure for all oikees & the opening of several new chapters for 2022! Together with our student community for sustainability in economics and business education, we have started a year full of exciting initiatives & mind-opening projects that will shape the future of our organization. Will you be part of our impact?

title: Harnessing the Power of the Sun
description: Warm Heart needs to go solar to cut our negative impact on the environment. We grow our own food, the programs we promote help reduce greenhouse gas and PM2.5 emissions, improve public health & reduce rural poverty. But we still depend on traditional power, power that is generated with coal and increasingly with Mekong River killing hydro! The minute we go solar and get off the grid, our weight on the environment is lifted, and our children will have a stable power source for online learning.

title: Empower 250 kids through sport & education
description: VUSA provides a structured after-school programme for vulnerable children in Langa, an under-resourced community of Cape Town where substance abuse and crime is rife.  VUSA offers children access to sport and academic support, recreational outings and a daily meal. Apart from the obvious health benefits, sport is an incredible teaching tool, teaching valuable lessons about team-work, discipline and respect. Most importantly, VUSA creates a safe space for children.

title: Therapeutic Community for 600 victims, Hyderabad
description: Over 2-3 million women and girls are trafficked for the purposes of commercial sexual exploitation in India. Removing them from places of exploitation, providing them a safe space to heal and recover, protecting them from toxic and harmful influences and facilitating access to educational and vocational skills is a multi-layered intervention which requires concerted efforts. This project aims to support 600 victims of sex trafficking in their journey to regain dignity and build a life.

title: A Safe Space for Cambodia's Vulnerable Children
description: The Poipet Reception Centre provides emergency and immediate care to unaccompanied Cambodian migrant children returned from Thailand. These children are victims of unsafe migration or trafficking. Our Reception Centre offers children a safe space to live and receive education, meals, and medical care while our staff attempt to locate their families and determine if reintegration is feasible and safe. In cases where it is not, we refer children to our other programs that provide long-term care.

title: Sharing the love of learning around the world.
description: Lilipad is on a mission to improve children's lives by promoting the love of learning and reading. We open children's libraries in underserved communities and we strive to transform them into safe havens where the children can learn, grow and have fun. Since 2017, we have installed 7 Lilipad libraries in Uganda, Morocco and Germany, and our objective for 2022 is to continue growing our reach and impact. Our vision is for every child in our communities and beyond to reach their full potential.

title: Create Positive, Lasting Change for Horses.
description: Create positive, lasting change to ensure every horse is safe, healthy and valued by caring for neglected, abused and at-risk equines, providing leadership, support and education to owners, the community and law enforcement.  Donations provide our rescue horses lifesaving care and allows our team to assist with urgent requests to save horses suffering from neglect and abuse. Each horse in our care receives specialized veterinary treatment, rehabilitation and training to prepare them for a loving

title: "Speak Volume With Your Action" Campaign
description: In Nigeria, evidence has shown that laws alone have not been successful in preventing sexual violence and increasing access to justice. Hence, the need for a survivor-centred and community approach would touch hearts and stimulate reflections that lead to tangible actions and improve the SGBV response. We want to continue to create awareness by showcasing survivor stories through an art exhibition, particularly to amplify and give voice to women and girls who have lost theirs due to abuse.

title: Light up a school and change the lives of 159 kids
description: We aim to electrify 18 classrooms at Escuela de la Calle. Children from low-income families are educated at this school. This equipment will aid 2,000 houses in the area while also assisting the school's operations. The installation will serve more than 17 new generations of children throughout its 20-year life span. Currently, the school serves 159 boys and girls who receive primary education.  Children must be hopeful and receive opportunities for progress to break the cycle of poverty.

title: Increase HIV/AIDS knowledge and care in 8 villages
description: December 1st is World AIDs Day. To raise awareness on AIDs, Blossom will organize an awareness raising event across 8 villages, 2000 people, in Virudhurangar district over 2 days. 10 HIV+ EduClowns use drama and humor to educate people on AIDs and the resources available to them in an entertaining and engaging way. Your generous support will allow us to reach thousands with critical, life-saving information on World AIDs Day and tackle the obstacle of unequal access to information and care.

title: Change the Lives of 240 Vulnerable Youth in Kenya
description: This project will support and champion the empowerment of underserved youth in the poor neighborhoods of Nairobi and Kamagut a rural village in Kenya, by building their capacities and competencies that will be achieved by conducting training in basic ICT, Craft Skills, Entrepreneurship, Life Skills, and Mentorship. The Good Kenyan model applies a mix of learning methods including classroom-style training, individualized mentorship & coaching applied over a 3 month period.

title: Post secondary Education for Girls in Burkina Faso
description: This project provides scholarships to nursing, midwifery and primary school teacher training for 300 village girls who have completed secondary school at the top of their class in northern Burkina Faso. Because their parents are subsistence farmers, these scholarships are the only source of funds these girls will have to enable them to further their studies in primary school teaching, nursing or midwifery.

title: Needed: School Lunches
description: The project pays for a noon meal for village girls who attend the Lycee Moderne de l'Amitie (a middle/secondary school).  Their parents, who are subsistence farmers, cannot afford their schooling. Girls walk 6 km to and from school each day and have no other source of food during the day. These girls score outstandingly well on national exams compared to their peers throughout Burkina.

title: Providing angioplasty to 100 Afghan patients
description: The French Medical Institute for Mothers and Children (FMIC) provides high-quality angiography and angioplasty for patients with coronary heart diseases. Averagely, we have more than 100 patients with coronary heart diseases in a month. These patients usually come from deprived and remote areas of Afghanistan to visit FMIC, a hospital located in Kabul, and avail themselves of the services. FMIC will cover part or the full cost of the poor patients through the patient welfare program.

title: Clean a river in Migingo & stop plastic pollution
description: This project will clean up a polluted, refuse and plastic-filled stretch of the Mathare river in central Nairobi, Kenya, transforming what is currently a dumping ground for garbage into an urban garden where the community can meet, children can play safely, and where the community can grow vegetables to help their food security and livelihoods. This will also remove this garbage from the river system, allowing plastic and other items to be recycled instead of washing down into the Indian Ocean.

title: Community Empowerment for Guatemalans & Kenyans
description: GRACE Cares partner's Community Finance Guatemala (CFG) and the Watha Project in Kenya want to implement community empowerment projects in their under-served communities. CFG's goal is to build resilience in the Kakchiquel Maya community by donating 5 chicks to each family, providing seeds and home gardening skills, and resilience-based goal setting education. The Watha Project, working with village elders, will construct a new well to provide clean and safe water to hundreds of Watha.

title: Fundraising to Invite Youth Trainees to Japan
description: Human Resources Development is the central and integral component of our work. Our 22 training centers located in 11 countries including Japan have facilities for agriculture, livestock, and food processing. Our 4 training centers in Japan located in Aichi, Kagawa, Osaka, and Fukuoka have empowered more than 5,000 youths, mostly from developing countries since 1967. Most of our graduates are engaged in community development projects worldwide to improve the quality of life of the people.

title: Help stateless children receive an education
description: The Seed of Hope Dorm, in Northern Thailand, boards 33+ children who wouldn't otherwise have access to education. We are seeking to build an education center that will nurture these students' educational pursuits.  The center will have a library to give them a love for reading, arts and crafts room where they will learn traditional crafts by their village elders so their heritage will not be forgotten.  It will also feature classrooms for students to study and be tutored.

title: Help Asylum Seekers & Refugees Transcend Barriers
description: In Greece, over 100,000 refugees and asylum seekers urgently need psychosocial support and emergency services. Gaps in service provision are growing, whilst camps are becoming increasingly isolated due to the building of walls. Lighthouse Relief provides psychosocial support and emergency services to refugees that bolster wellbeing and resilience. This approach provides tools with which people can build their futures, beyond the barriers of their current situation.

title: Support laboratory Analyses in Burkina Faso
description: Burkina Faso is one of the poorest countries in Africa, ranks 182 out of 189 countries in the human development index. Additionally, it ranks below average compared to countries in Sub-Saharan Africa. Action10 is now aiming to raise funds to provide lab equipment to the laboratories in Burkina Faso that currently experience a lack of resources. This will enable the laboratory to bring the research, on water quality among other things, forward and improve the standard of living.

title: Minibus for Special Needs Orphans in Macedonia
description: This Giving Tuesday, join us in providing a minibus for The JOY Home Day Center for special needs orphans. This week, we began accepting children, giving them a place where they they can experience hope and healing through individualized care and therapy. However, we can only reliably transport 3 children at a time, and bringing children in wheelchairs adds more complications. All money donated will go directly to purchasing a used transit van, and every gift is appreciated.

title: Educate and Empower in Uganda with Nurture Africa
description: This project will provide Vocational Education to 20 most vulnerable youth in 2022 at the Nurture Africa Vocational Training Centre.

title: Let's continue creating opportunities - Autism
description: We are a private, non-for-profit program, and for many children with autism, the only educational alternative in Venezuela. We serve more than 450 families annually, a 45% increase in ten years. We provide specialized, comprehensive education, assessment services, family advice and need-based financial support. 2021 is our 15th birthday, 5475 days of hopes and achievements. Your trust and unwavering support motivate us, the resilience and gratitude of our families inspires us.

title: Prevent Trafficking Through Literacy
description: While Creative Life Foundation's education program continues to be necessary for breaking cycles of poverty and exploitation, we realize our students don't live in a vacuum. If their mothers remain at risk, so do they. To undergird our ongoing scholarship and mentorship program, we seek to eliminate maternal risk by providing a program focused on Thai literacy.

title: Help launch our Newest Class of Fellows in Ghana
description: "When we invest in women and girls we are investing in the people who invest in everyone else."- Graca Machel. Having nearly completed our first round of Fellowships, we are launching a new campaign to provide 2-year fellowships to 10 more up-and-coming female educational leaders in Ghana! By providing leadership training, mentorship, and micro-grants to these rising stars, we empower them to provide inclusive, equitable, quality education for all.

title: Brighten the Holidays for Spaulding Rehab Patients
description: With your help, we'll make the holidays warmer and brighter for the youngest patients in our care at Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital. You can sponsor special holiday gifts and activities for our pediatric inpatients, or help us meet the unique needs that come up for each patient and their family this time of year - especially around transportation, food, and other resources.

title: LET'S BUILD THE FUTURE TOGETHER
description: Children are like a blank canvas. It is our duty to fill their early years with color, ideas, and dreams, expanding their learning opportunities. They are the future and they need all of our support to be able to believe in a better world. Your help would allow us to continue welcoming thousands of children in our centers, in spaces of learning and development for life, where tolerance, legitimate respect for the other and the love in living together are formed without any discrimination.

title: Cepac Brazil Solar Panel
description: In compliance with SDG 7, 10, 11 and 17 (Sustainable Development Goals) and in the midst of this economic and social context, the institution aims to contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gases by replacing its energy matrix with a renewable and clean system with the installation of a photovoltaic solar energy panel at its headquarters unit, where it serves around 500 families in socially vulnerable situations per year with its projects and programs.

title: More Healthy Meals to Children
description: The project aims to guarantee food and nutritional security to more than 500 children that live in social vulnerability in Brazil. All donations will be used to distribute food baskets for poor families, milk and supplement for children in need, and guarantee nutritional and medical orientation for more than 300 families. This project will reach more than 1,500 people.

title: Protect Endangered Wildlife Against Exploitation
description: Endangered animals are being exploited by humans to make illegal products, traditional medicines, and to be kept as pets, in order to elevate their social status, pursue health myths, or for entertainment. By offering a toll-free hotline for the public to report crimes, facilitating animal rescues, assisting law enforcement in catching criminals, and encouraging the prosecution of wildlife traffickers, Education for Nature - Vietnam (ENV) strives to protect endangered wildlife from exploitation.

title: Leadership Initiatives Students Creating Change
description: As members of Leadership Initiatives' [LI] International Internship Program, Krishna and Liz have been working with LI to research and learn about public health crises in Bauchi State, Nigeria. To transform lives, the team & LI are working to create a public health campaign and community workshop to raise awareness and educate the people of Bauchi on these various public health issues.

title: Social Gardening: Green Together!
description: Biodiversity and climate have never been more relevant, especially in the city: when someone has little to no resources (financially, socially and/or intellectually),''concrete'' gardens are the rule rather than the exception. 200 volunteers team up to make such gardens low maintenance, low budget but highly sustainable and green! In 3 years time we strive to help 1300 vulnerable citizens in The Hague. With this project we seek to do justice to the sustainable development goals no. 1, 11 & 15.

title: Healthy Learners: Home Grown School Meals in Kenya
description: This project ensures that ~ 1,000 children at 3 schools in rural Kenya eat a nutritious home grown meal each day. The project will: a) fund staple foods purchased from women farmers b) utilize school land to grow nutrient dense fruits and vegetables, c) maintain small livestock programs, and d) train school youth to grow their own food for future self-sufficiency. 100% DIRECT GIVING: 100% OF YOUR DONATIONS SUPPORT SCHOOL FEEDING AND FARMING PROGRAMS IN KENYA.

title: Save Guatemalan Wildlife and Biodiversity!!!
description: Guatemala is home to some of the world's most endangered wild animals and habitats.  ARCAS rescues, rehabilitates and releases wild animals confiscated from traffickers.  Some of these animals exist nowhere else in the world.  It also protects forests, beaches and wetlands that these animals need to survive.  This project will support the food and medical costs of animals undergoing rehabilitation and will help manage protected areas for wildlife in Peten, the Pacific coast and the highlands.

title: Support Kanan Kab to plant 25,000 trees in Yucatan
description: This Giving Tuesday is all about offsetting our carbon footprint!  One of the nine biggest deforestation fronts is located inside the Selva Maya, the highest carbon reserve in Mesoamerica. Yucatan State is part of the Selva Maya and unfortunately, it has lost 17% of green cover since 2001 until 2020.  Trees are urgently needed to remedy this problem! Therefore, Kanan Kab has the challenge of producing and planting 25,000 native trees every year. May you help us?

title: Prevent Child Abuse: From Our Families to Yours
description: From our families to yours, we can prevent child abuse by supporting parents. Over the past year, 70,000 mothers and caregivers like Jasmin, have received the support and resources they need to thrive. This project will fund a new initiative for parent graduates of Healthy Families America (HFA). This initiative will help train HFA graduates to serve as mentors to new parents and to advocate for family friendly policies in their communities.

title: Deer Run Nature Preserve Bridge Project
description: GMC is committed to building trails that are accessible by raising the needed funds and working with a contractor and volunteers to construct a bridge this summer, making the many attributes of this beautiful Preserve open to more and more people, including meandering through forests that are home to many avian visitors including the black-throated blue warbler and the Northern Parula, a visit to Indigo Bunting Junction and cathedral like deer yards, and several 100-mile vistas.

title: Saving W.Bengal Elephants from Deadly Train Tracks
description: Unsustainable development including railway tracks and roads that cut through core habitats are a major cause of elephant deaths. Every year 2-3 elephants die in train collisions. Speed restrictions are enforced inside protected areas but not outside where most accidents occur.  We are piloting an early warning system to alert train drivers of elephant presence, with enough time for the speeding train to stop. The sirens will also warn elephants about the trains, preventing them from crossing.

title: Combating Antibiotic Resistance in Africa and Asia
description: Antibiotic-resistant infections are predicted to kill 10 million people each year by 2050 -- five times more than the roughly 2 million deaths caused by COVID-19 in 2020. Thus, we urgently need antibiotic alternatives, particularly in Africa and Asia where 90% of the antibiotic-resistant deaths will occur. Phages for Global Health empowers scientists in Africa and Asia to develop inexpensive, natural antibiotic alternatives (phages) that can kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

title: Help 500+ Youth in Liberia Reach Their Potential
description: Youth are 65% of Liberia's population; empowering youth will change the nation's future. We deliver proven, successful models to help students prepare for college and in-demand careers. Our students outperform their peers in every academic category, earning high marks in standardized public exams. Plus, we provide community health screenings, health education, and disease prevention efforts. Help Liberian youth reach their full potential through college and career readiness and health education.

title: Food Security & Income for People in Poverty
description: Esther is giving thanks this Giving Tuesday for the gift of the INMED Aquaponics Social Enterprise, which has transformed her drought-ravaged farm into an award-winning agro-enterprise that is supporting her family and creating jobs and food security for her impoverished community on the edge of the Kalahari Desert in South Africa.  We're scaling the INMED ASE to Jamaica, Peru, Brazil and the USA to transition historically marginalized populations from poverty to self-reliance.

title: TRAIN 3K WIDOWS IN SNAIL FARMING, S/EAST, NIGERIA
description: This project will help widows' sustainable livelihood. Window's empowerment is a must when the question of national economic stability arises. It is required to drive away poverty and establish widow's position at home and in the society. Unfortunately, many widows are the worst sufferer in this prospect, most of them go about begging to support their family. They are not given priority in family decision making for their poor income. Self-income generating activities can tackle this problem.

title: Gift a future to youth in Uganda
description: An opportunity to change young lives for the better through professional qualification and training. Your donation goes towards help socially vulnerable young people to attend the Comboni College, a vocational training school located in Lira in the North of Uganda. Founded and run by missionaries, it provides very practical skills and education to rural people This has a lifetime impact on the student and their family who receives scholarship funds

title: Food/Winter Packs for families in Afghanistan
description: This project will provide urgently needed food and winter items to 1,500 internally displaced or disaster victim families in the regions of Kunduz, Kabul, and Herat inside Afghanistan.

title: Provide Safe & Loving Home to 130 Children
description: Based in Sangkhlaburi, North-West of Thailand, since 1990, Baan Unrak has sheltered hundreds of children and single mothers fleeing the civil war in Myanmar. We now provide a home, food, medical care, education to over 130 stateless children. Focusing on educational skills is the only way to secure their future. We provide a supportive environment and try to raise their self-esteem, thus launching students towards their vocational goals that will give them hope for a brighter future.

title: Live Performances in Tunisia and Egypt
description: The Freedom Theatre, a theatre that defined the meaning of cultural resistance, needs your help in order to embark on its tour of Carthage Theatre Festival and Cairo International Festival for Experimental Theatre with a brand entirely new productions; Keffiyeh / Made in China and the contemporary dance show; +970.  The Freedom Theatre has been described as one of the world's most revolutionary artistic platforms. We believe it is now time to connect Arab and Palestinian artists and facilitate t

title: Support Education for People on the Move
description: Action for Education works hand in hand with the communities it serves to provide innovative solutions that fit their educational needs. The Nest, in Athens, provides a positive and safe space for children to play and learn, while their parents can attend English or arts classes.  In the coming year, AFE is set to further expand its efforts to promote refugee education and we need your help to do so!

title: #GivingTuesday End-of-Year Support Jookender
description: Support Jookender in our efforts to build a strong, vibrant, and giving back community of 1st generation refugees/immigrants from the Russian-Jewish Origin.   If we raise $5000 and have at least 50 donors, we'll get a dollar-to-dollar match from a private foundation. All November 30 donations will be partially matched by the Global Giving Platform. if we raise $10,000, we'll be featured in several giving guides/publications, and have a few more opportunities for matches.

title: Warm Clothes for Nomad Students in Tibet 2021
description: Last year, thanks to donor support, we provided warm clothing, wood burning stoves, and fuel to schools and 122 students on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau. The program was such a success we once again will provide warm clothing and fuel for 126 students to keep them in schools and cozy in the cold Tibetan winter!

title: End Hunger in Madagascar with Girls' Education
description: In Madagascar girls as young as 9 years old get sold off to marry much older men. With 80% of the population relying on farming as a source of income women become commodity. Nofy i Androy equips girls with tools to fight early child marriage, early pregnancies, and cyclical famines. This project will promise girls with college degrees and aid vulnerable communities in fighting cyclical famines caused by climate change. We believe education is the only way to get out of poverty.

title: HOUSE FOR HOPE
description: RUWAI works to support many marginalized and low-income rural families impacted by climate change and poverty, helping them develop livelihoods resilience to build and bounce back better. During the peak of Covid, six-year-old Ugo Uzor lost her house to a cooking fire.  She was severely burned along with her mother. RUWAI provided for their medical expenses and began reconstruction of the Uzor's home.  With your help, we will complete the construction of their house, and equip it.

title: Pacific NW & British Columbia Flood Relief Fund
description: An atmospheric river has dumped torrential rain on the Pacific Northwest and British Columbia, resulting in widespread flooding, spawning mudslides, and causing more than 2,000 households to evacuate.

title: Feed the Hungry,Warm the Cold-Support Afghanistan
description: Afghanistan faces a humanitarian crisis that is caused by change of regime after 46 years of war. It remains one of the world's most acute and complex humanitarian emergencies. The  withdrawal of international forces, and cut offs from the supports by donors has exacerbated the situation, driven by escalating conflict and natural disasters. The level of vulnerability has increased. Families cannot afford even the basic needs due to increase in prices, unemployment, and closure of jobs.

title: TRIPLE the Impact: Become a Fundraising Champion!
description: For more than 35 years, Migrant Clinicians Network (MCN) has advanced the pursuit of health justice for migrant and mobile populations. With the effects of the global pandemic stretching into a second year, our work has never been so necessary. This is why we at MCN have an ambitious goal--to bring in $15,000 through Giving Tuesday. Courtesy of an ambitious awareness campaign, we have nearly half that amount promised in matching funds. Will you join us by becoming a fundraising champion today?

title: Indigenous Women's Health Center in Mexico
description: Indigenous women from Oaxaca are seeking to guarantee their right to proper health care during this pandemic. You can make it possible for 90 women to become health promoters through a training program that allows them to develop their own herbal medicines and medicinal gardens to build a community health center. This will utilize ancestral knowledge and techniques practiced by grandmothers and natural healers to attend to physical, mental, and emotional family health

title: Wildlife Rescue and Rehabilitation
description: This project will provide treatment and rehabilitation to wildlife rescued for release in Chiapas. Our expert partner in conservation medicine is Tivu AC. Our facilities are basic, we need land, material and specialized equipment to develop a rescue and rehabilitation center. We will rescue  400 wild animals annually. We also carry out education, research and community participation to raise awareness and contribute to a harmonious relationship between society and nature.

title: Support Mobile Healthcare for Displaced Syrian
description: When we raised the slogan "We hold good for all," we took it upon ourselves to deliver medical services to the most marginalized and vulnerable groups of the society, particularly to the displaced community in the camps.  Today we launch our campaign to support mobile health centers in northern Syria, and to continue providing flexible and accessible health services to the most vulnerable patients around the world.

title: Help LIFT End Thai Child Online Sex Trafficking
description: LIFT International formed to end human trafficking by partnering with law enforcement agencies to help victims through prevention and prosecution. We offer comprehensive trafficking case management services that include investigation, legal support, social work, and forensics. We analyze data, investigate Child Sexual Abuse Materials (CSAM), and provide evidence to law enforcement. Recently, our focus has shifted to combating child online sexual exploitation, which increased during the pandemic.

title: Christmas Fundraiser 2021
description: It's that time of year here at the Good Shepherd Agricultural Mission. We are pulling out the decorations, dusting off our tree and preparing to wrap another boat load of presents! After a difficult and different year last year, we're hoping things are a little more normal for this one!

title: A recognised education for children Cote d'Ivoire
description: Imagine attendIng school throughout childhood yet never having that education recognised. 1.6 M school-age children in Cote d'Ivoire still don't receive a recognised education (2016). 25% only get non-formal education offered by poorly-trained religious structures. Graines de Paix works with the authorities to ensure that these children receive a broader-based, considerate, violence-free, education to reduce inequalities, increase national cohesion and provide a positive future for all children.

title: Vet Books for Africa
description: African veterinary faculties are battling to adequately educate their veterinary students due to the lack of resources. South African veterinary students aim to empower other students by delivering much need resources to African universities, communities and sanctuaries during a 7 week expedition, creating a ripple effect in the struggle that is conservation.

title: Acquiring New Skills to Access Better Job
description: This project aims to make tourism better, not only for guests but also for local people. Attracting domestic tourists and becoming less reliant on long-distance visitors are quite a juvenile target for a destination such as Madagascar. There are no half measures, operating legally, and ensuring the safety and quality to tourists are essential. To respond to the situation, we need to train and upgrade the skills of culinary, hospitality and tourism professionals

title: Present A Home
description: We aim to give underprivileged residents (teenage mothers and refugees) of The Hague a home, giving them the opportunity to participate in society again. We offer our volunteers the chance to contribute to the quality of life of fellow citizens. As a side effect, we offer the children of the target group a clean and safe environment and create understanding between different groups in society. At the end of every project there is a tangible result: a home.

title: Midwives Save Lives: Train 40 New African Midwives
description: Every day, over 800 women in sub-Saharan Africa die from pregnancy and childbirth-related causes, of which 80% are preventable. With $10,000, we can train 40 community midwives who can provide potentially life-saving care for up to 20,000 women in a year. This campaign will also supply midwives with kits and bicycles to help them reach remote areas and give critically needed care with the necessary supplies. Help us give mom & baby the strongest start of life!

title: Connecting 100 Afghan Women to Digital Economy
description: Now more than any other time it is needed to CONNECT Afghan women entrepreneurs with the buyers worldwide. CONNECTING Afghan women to sell online specially outside Afghanistan is teaching them how to fish. Yes, Afghans and the world are concerned about the current economic crisis and everyone is talking about giving Afghans fish which is only short-term. WE ARE THINKING LONG-TERM! How about you? Will you support our long-term plan to create an online sales platform for Afghan women?

title: School Meals for 350 childrens in Honduras
description: Will achieve direct participation in the fight against hunger in our beneficiaries at school stage in situations of vulnerability, poverty and extreme poverty, generating in turn inclusive and nutritional activities that promote the return to school and good health of childrens, as an incentive to reduce school dropout rates in the beneficiary communities.

title: HERD - Community Development Project
description: Community involvement is a critical aspect of any conservation success story. HERD Trust has started working with Mpisi School on a project focusing on both mental and physical well-being. Through a Nutrition Project we can assist in the physical well-being of developing school children through supplementary nutrition and a community vegetable garden. Through the Scouts Program we will introduce extra curricular activities at the school that will assist in mental and personal development.

title: Climate change resilient families in Honduras
description: This project will strengthen the climate resilience capacities of 50 small farming families in Intibuca, Honduras, working primarily with indigenous youth and women. By converting agricultural waste into organic compost, these small agroecological farms can more efficiently grow crops for subsistence and to generate extra income. We will implement environmentally friendly alternative technologies such as solar greenhouses to dry crops and a facility to produce organic fertilizers and pesticides.

title: Can you help rescued baby giraffe Shuri?
description: Shuri is a baby giraffe who was brought to the Hoedspruit Endangered Species Centre for care. When just 3 days old, she was found weak and dehydrated but clinging to life. Shuri is now almost 3 months old and still needs to be bottle fed for at least 6 months. As she grows up, she will be given nutritious solid food in the form of lucerne and 'boskos', organic pellets that are the closest feed to the natural diet of herbivores. She further requires medication and regular veterinary checkups.

title: Christmas boxes for children living in Refuges
description: Due to COVID-19 cases of Domestic abuse have risen dramatically. Many more children than ever before are now living in Refuges, as their homes are no longer safe. Parents are often not able to afford even basic necessities, as many families fled with just what they were wearing. Life is stressful enough for victims of violence but even more so at this time of year if you are worrying about the possibility of not having a Christmas/Seasonal Holiday gift for your child/ren on Christmas Day.

title: Help girls become leaders in their communities!
description: Modeled on our very successful Grandmother Leadership training, a Leadership training program for adolescent girls will be developed.  The training for 40 adolescent girls will increase their self-esteem, communication, problem solving and leadership skills so they can take collective action in their communities to promote girls' education, and decrease child marriage, teen pregnancy and female genital mutilation (FGM).

title: Train a teacher for South Africa's Zama Montessori
description: Zama Montessori School located in Johannesburg, SA has been serving impoverished children and their families for more than 30 years, helping many to break the cycle of poverty.  The school embarked on training a young adult to become a Montessori teacher at the Indaba Institute to serve the elementary-age children.  COVID19 wrecked their financial plan to pay for that training as families lost their jobs and donors stopped giving.  This project will cover the gap created by the pandemic.

title: IOM GAF: Assisting Trafficking Victims & Migrants
description: IOM's emergency Global Assistance Fund (GAF) offers personalized, immediate protection and direct assistance to migrants facing violence, exploitation and abuse, such as victims of forced labor and sexual abuse; unaccompanied children, and victims of trafficking. GAF provides those facing extreme vulnerabilities with broad services including safe accommodation, food & non-food items, psychological support, healthcare, family reunification, safe and dignified return and sustainable reintegration.

title: Sharing
description: More than five million children in Afghanistan are on the brink of starvation, with the nation enduring the worst drought since records began against a backdrop of political and economic turmoil. We provide lunch, food packages, and food supplements for some of the most underprivileged families while mobilizing the youth to create joyful activities and bring hope into their communities.

title: Rural Education in Cambodia: Believe in Me
description: After learning that some children were unable to attend public schools due to living in extreme poverty and lacking safe access to schooling, LWB decided to bring education directly to the kids through its Believe in Me schools. These LWB schools serve over 375 impoverished children in the rural villages of western Cambodia. This project will provide the support necessary for 150 additional waiting children to enter school and experience the gift of hope that only an education can provide.

title: Mercy Alumni Monthly Sustainers Fellowship
description: This fund will bring together the alumni of Mercy In Action College of Midwifery in a powerful way to join in monthly support of our outreach arm in the Philippines,  midwife-led freestanding birth centers providing maternity care in low-resource, high-mortality areas at no cost to the families. Graduates of our midwife training programs are uniquely qualified to understand and support solutions to the problems facing pregnant women, newborns, and postpartum mothers in poor parts of our world.

title: STEM After-School Academy
description: The Alberta's Lillie After-School STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Math) Academy opening in the South Suburbs of Chicago will be offering young people the opportunity to advance in Mechanical Engineering (Robotics), Aviation and Agricultural Sciences after-school programming. Be a part of the breakthrough by becoming a financial partner and help make hundreds of young people's STEM dreams come true.

title: Planting trees for people and birds
description: The Highlands of Chiapas are a region rich in unique wildlife, but also one of high poverty and marginalization. Land use change, illegal logging and urbanization are causing the loss of forest and consequently the loss of water for human populations. We will grow and replant native trees to recover lost forests and wildlife habitat. By directly involving local communities, from the very young to respected elders, building understanding and commitment at the personal level to the native forests.

title: Help youth facing adversities in Singapore
description: Lunar New Year is a season for celebration, generous giving and reunion in the Chinese calendar. However, this is not the case for many of our youth because of the adversities they face in life.

title: Support Rural Community Health Leaders in Honduras
description: Help the Solidarity Project invest in over 15 community health volunteers in seven rural communities in Honduras. Since the global pandemic, we have created this network of health volunteers to respond to health emergencies and the needs in their communities.   Your support provides training to strengthen health volunteers' ability to respond to first aid emergencies and essential access to medicines through a sustainable community pharmacy program.  Help us continue this work in 2022!

title: Hold Onto Hope
description: The Barrio Planta Project (BPP) provides relevant educational opportunities to hundreds of children in overlooked communities in Nicaragua with high-quality programs in ESL, Computers, the Arts, and more. BPP covers the cost of students enrollment and tuition through donations. In February, our school year begins, and we are hosting a fundraiser now to secure the enrollment of our students for the upcoming school year.

title: Healthy Mothers Program
description: This program supports a health education program that works with a group of indigenous Maya mothers from the community of Tzanchaj, Guatemala.  This program focuses on topics such as nutrition, hygiene, sexual health and reproduction, and  women's empowerment  to improve the health of their families and community.

title: SUPPORT CHILDREN EDUCATION IN TURKEY WITH TABLETS
description: This Project focus on children at the villages and schools in the soci-economically disadvantaged areas of the cities at Turkey, where there is substantial inequality in terms of access to quality education.TEGV will provide tablets for free to the 100 children at schools,so they will also facilitate the participation of children in the EBA system created by the Republic of Turkey Ministry of National Education for distance education. They will have opportunity to attend TEGV digital education.

title: Fund Childline and help a child every 25 seconds
description: Childline is a free confidential service just for young people. It can be contacted online and on the phone, 24 hours a day, every day of the year.   It's a place where young people can get the help they need in the way they want it. They talk to us about things like abuse, self-harm and suicide; problems they feel they can't speak to anyone else about.   On average, a child contacts Childline every 25 seconds.

title: Feeding Native Peruvian Children
description: Native Peruvian Children live on very little, and often go without a healthy lunch. Their parents must leave the village for the day to go and labor in the fields. Our missionary partners are working with the women of the villages, that don't leave, to prepare hot and healthy meals for the children who wouldn't have them otherwise. $0.50 feeds a child a hot and healthy lunch. They also need large pots and cookware to be able to cook for many children. You can make a lasting difference!

title: Help Youth Stay in School and Grow Academically
description: This project will provide guidance and support to at-risk youth to ensure school retention and academic progress. Due to the effects of the pandemic, Puerto Rico's students are less motivated than ever and need an encouraging environment. Caney (Centro de Apoyo Academico y Espacio Seguro) are academic centers offered in schools to foster a safe space for students and other at-risk youth in San Juan, Naguabo, Juncos, and Canovanas.

title: Learning Disaster - Teaching Repairs
description: Oklahoma ranks 3rd in the U.S. for disasters.  Home repair for disaster survivors who can not recover on their own is a constant need.  COVID-19 has reduced volunteers to historic lows leaving many impoverished families waiting over 81,506,637 seconds of their lives for help.  Families across the state have been isolated to small sections of their home due to damages, mold, and access.  Recovering Oklahomans After Disaster, Inc. (ROAD) is working to make that long wait end!

title: Invite a child in need one healthy meal
description: The food scarcity is a severe issue that impacts the optimal growth and development of young children that Albergue supports. With your help, we can make it possible for a child to eat three meals a day and the essential nutritional follow-up necessary for their integral development.

title: You can Light a Candle too-University Scholarships
description: With the 'We will guide them and they will guide the future' motto, CYDD supports university students who are able to enter universities despite their limited resources. University students from both genders are supported with monthly scholarships. The aim is to bring positive developments to education, to provide equality in education and to support the students to have a comprehensive education by the time they start their careers.

title: Education for children with disabilities, Kenya
description: Most children with disabilities in Kenya don't attend school because of myths surrounding disability, inadequate facilities and lack of trained staff. This project will enable up to 100 girls and boys with learning disabilities to receive an education, learn life skills and reach their full potential. Your support will also ensure that up to 20 older children can graduate, successfully transition from school to adult life and contribute fully to activities in their families and communities.

title: In-home help for differently-abled in Palestine
description: Families with a differently-abled person in Palestine,  face community stigma and a lack of  lack of knowledge and resources to deal with their loved one's condition.   Families  often hide their loved one away and thus deprive him/her of essential assistance and themselves of support.    The Homes' outreach program provides in-home diagnoses, equipment, support  and education on how best to care for their loved one--thereby improving the lives of all family members.

title: Toys for Challenged Children During The Holidays
description: The Team Up For 1 Foundation (TU41) holds an annual toy drive called, "Team Up For Toys".  The gifts we purchase with financial donations support 500 challenged children who attend five Baltimore inner-city schools. For many of these children, the toys we donate may be the only gift they receive during the holiday season, making this program crucial to maintain and grow. Our goal is to deliver at least 500 toys each year, with the hopes of expanding our reach year after year.

title: Cyclone and Floods Relief in Andhra Pradesh, India
description: This project will gives an emergency relief to  cyclone,floods affected families in several districts  of Andhra Pradesh in India with dry ration food grains, sanitary kits, clothing, cooking utensils and support to house repairs.  And also work for the rehabilitation activities with government and other like minded organizations to become normal lives of the affected families. We work to bring back to the normality of the lives of the flood affected families with our disaster preparedness team.

title: Help Social AgroBusiness of Rural Youth in Ukraine
description: Your donation will help the Way Home Foundation to equip a Shop on Wheels in a minibus to strengthen social farm enterprise Liebenthal in the Odessa region, Ukraine. The mobile shop will sell farm products in the city: greenery, vegs, honey, flowers, which are raised by disadvantaged young people from the Liebenthal agricultural community. They have received training in the skills of agricultural business and they want to earn their own living and start their own business.

title: Help Casper & Friends Fly to Canada
description: Casper and NINE of his shelter friends have a chance of a lifetime.  On March 22, 2022, all ten are boarding a plane destined for Canada, where they can find loving families to adopt them. Casper has waited over TWO years for this chance. Some of his friends have waited three years.  Each one is a SURVIVOR. They've been through the unimaginable. That's in the past now, and nothing but a life of color awaits them in Montreal. In a few short weeks, everything can change for them with this flight.

title: Computer lab for English students in Haiti
description: English in Mind Institute (EIM) provides high quality, affordable English classes to adults in Port-au-Prince, along with job placement assistance.

title: Training 20 Turkish and Refugee Journalists
description: The aims of the project are trifold:  1. To bring together migrant and host community journalists to collaborate and learn with, not about, one another;   2. To enhance professional capacities of the journalists through 12 targeted skills trainings;  3. To raise awareness of the issues of xenophobia and hate speech vis-a-vis refugees in Turkey, fostering empathy with the displaced on an international scale.

title: Sustainable Communities Ending Child Slavery
description: Limye Lavi has worked for 30 years to end child slavery in Haiti, strengthening rural communities and their ability to nurture and protect their children. Our project has four elements:  1. Educating parents about the realities of child slavery.  2. Supporting schooling for children recently removed from child servitude.  3. Providing sustainable ways for communities to generate income.  4. Mobilizing partner communities to identify common challenges and collaborate toward shared solutions.

title: Food baskets to 50.000 needy families in Colombia!
description: The Holiday season is the time to give, share and be hopeful. The Food Bank of Bogota has taken a great challenge: to deliver 50,000 food baskets to those in need, those who had suffered the anguish of hunger and who struggle every day to obtain food to continue living. More than ever, we need to celebrate life. Help us to bring joy and wellness to thousands that leave in extreme poverty. Our goal is that in Colombia food becomes a right, not a privilege! We are not recipients of public funds.

title: Ten Scholarships for Grassroots Feedback Leaders
description: Often, decisions are made for the community rather than with them. Feedback Labs believes that people are the best experts in their lives and should drive the policies and programs that impact them. At Feedback+Jacksonville, those who are committed to making feedback the norm will have the opportunity to learn and improve their feedback practices. This project seeks to sponsor attendance for grassroots leaders in an effort to remove financial barriers and create a more accessible experience.

title: ILGA World Conference 2022
description: Since the 1970s, ILGA World Conferences have brought together LGBTIQ leaders and activists from all over the world. They have been fundamental events for our movement ever since, and are moments to shape the life of our organisation.    ILGA World is queer democracy in action, and it all starts at ILGA World Conferences.   The 30th ILGA World Conference, hosted by the It Gets Better Project, will be held in LA Long Beach, California, United States from to 2 to 6 May 2022.

title: Flood relief for the people of Puducherry
description: Puducherry has experienced 36.2 mm of rainfall in the month of November 2021 causing huge damage on houses and people living in low lying area were evacuated and accommodated in disaster relief shelters. Still efforts are made to clear water. The Meteorological Department forecast heavy rainfall in upcoming days.

title: Christmas Dinner for Children orphans and homeless
description: This project will provide Christmas dinner party to over 60 homeless in Stoke-on Trent Staffordshire United Kingdom and 40 orphans in Nigeria  on Christmas day. Give them a feel of love from the community they belong.

title: Help life-saving  to displaced People in Ethiopia
description: The conflict in Ethiopia has developed into a humanitarian disaster and the humanitarian situation is rapidly deteriorating in large parts of the country. A year into a conflict between government forces and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), Ethiopia has seen thousands of lives lost and more than a million people displaced. Now, a larger humanitarian crisis looms, with nearly half a million facing starvation in Amhara.  To avert this humanitarian catastrophe Life-saving action needed

title: Building a pit latrine for God's Love School
description: Construction of pit latrines will improve hygiene conditions, reduce the risk of water borne diseases and promote better enrollment and attendance rates. Therefore God's Love Home  is working to mitigate the risks facing vulnerable children by strengthening community support networks. Pit latrine construction project aims to connect the children and their caregivers with services and support to meet their needs.

title: Healing Children's Hearts in Costa Rica and Beyond
description: This project will fund pediatric surgical missions to Latin America. Since 2014 Surgeons of Hope has been committed to higher standards of pediatric heart care in Latin America. We have partnered with Hospital Nacional de Ninos(HNN) in San Jose to strengthen their pediatric cardiovascular program. Since the start of our partnership with HNN,1500 children have received life-saving heart surgery. We recently started a partnership with the Hospital Pediatrico "Ninos de Acosta Nu"  in Paraguay.

title: Christmas Blankets for Native Peruvian Children
description: Native Peruvians often still live in huts with only an open fire for heat.  Providing them blankets for Christmas will bless them with protection from the weather and improve their health and well being. They do not have insulated houses and often have to sleep during wet and cold nights.

title: Gift of Hope for Our Youth
description: Give our youth a Gift of Hope and encourage them to stay resilient during this difficult period. Many marginalized youth do not have many things, families, and friends like what we have, each day they do their best and show resilience above their adversities. Your support will help young people make responsible decisions for themselves, creating a positive impact on our community.

title: Families fighting against the health & food crisis
description: The damage that the current food industry is causing to public health and the environment demands us to continue generating alternatives that are increasingly fair, transparent, comprehensive, community oriented, and in harmony with nature in both rural and urban areas. That is why we will promote food production in urban and peri-urban environments where the population depends on employment and consumption, and barely has the skills and means to produce and exchange food.

title: Hampers of hope this holiday season
description: Give hope this year and reach out to vulnerable communities that need support the most. As communities try to put together their lives after COVID-19 pandemic, there is so much that we can provide to help them get back on their feet. The holiday season is a time for giving hope and charity that allows the most vulnerable to experience the joy and delight of Christmas followed by new hope for the new year. We appeal to your goodwill in providing joy and hope.

title: Ultimate Peace 2022 - Reset, Renewed, Recharged
description: Ultimate Peace (UP) has provided groundbreaking sports and leadership programs to thousands of diverse Middle East youth since 2010. Sadly, COVID-19 in 2020 and the Middle East upheaval of 2021 stopped all UP programming. The precious interwoven cross-cultural connections and friendships, bound by years of hard earned trust, were pulled at the seams. Yet they were not torn. After a year of listening to and planning with our youth and staff, we will proudly launch reinvigorated programs in 2022.

title: Supports Colombian families in need of a house
description: In a world of "gets", giving is beautiful! When you give money to TECHO you are helping the work we do in communities across the country. And that is beautiful! This is the opportunity for us to provide emergency housing to families in poverty and support community development projects. So join us and let's build a better Colombia together.

title: Political unrest relief fund for Moya Communities
description: As it is in many countries experiencing political instability, women and children in the country have become the most disadvantaged and in some cases, the targets for abuse. Your generous donations would go into: - Transport costs for our Psychosocial support team to tend to GBV, Restorative Justice and sexual assault cases which are currently on the rise - Financial support for medical assistance for survivors - Food support for child and or elderly led households

title: Transform Lives, Help Us Build A Soccer Field!
description: Our participants don't have access to fields where they can safely play sport. Too often they play on rocky fields that have more dust than grass and this makes it difficult for them to develop their skills.  We need your support to help us build a second soccer field where our participants can safely play sports, learn from their coaches and have fun with their peers. The second field will help us reach more children, broadening our reach. Thank you for helping us transform lives through sport!

title: Recovery & Resilience
description: Madagascar is currently experiencing extreme food shortages and rising prices caused by the economic impact of COVID-19, pest outbreaks, and the worst drought recorded since 1981. The Deep South is particularly vulnerable to food insecurity, with 1.5 million people in the region, approximately half of the population, unable to find enough food to eat. The number of people living at imminent risk of famine is expected to double over the lean season, the period between planting and harvesting.

title: Better Lives for Vulnerable People in East Africa
description: We're raising funds to fulfil Advantage Africa's strategic goal of better lives for the most vulnerable children and adults in East Africa. Your support will help vulnerable people to overcome poverty in ways that last. It will enable our partner organisations to provide essential services and support vulnerable people to advocate for change that releases them from poverty. You will also be helping Advantage Africa to become a more sustainable organisation that's changing lives - for good.

title: 12 Days of Christmas: Wheelchair Edition 2021
description: The 12 Days of Christmas fundraising campaign seeks to highlight and fully fund 12 wheelchairs for 12 beneficiaries over the Christmas period. Give the best Christmas gift of all, the Gift of Movement.

title: Help Women lead their communities out of poverty
description: This project will recruit 100 women and provide them with a series of training in gender and empowerment, sales and marketing, cash management, and business skills. These new entrepreneurs will be given a $300 line of credit to purchase energy-saving products that they can sell within their community. This project will take place in the remote and impoverished villages of  Eastern Province of Zambia.

title: Support families fighting torture in Mexico
description: In Frayba we want to continue walking alongside torture survivors and their families who are fighting to build justice and truth. Most of them are women who are committed to a more just world for everyone, to punish those who practice it, in the midst of a context where the Mexican government makes it invisible and denies that it is used as a method of investigation by the authorities themselves.

title: Support Kids 4 Afghan schools
description: Kids 4 Afghan Kids (K4AK) was founded in 1998 in Michigan by teacher Khris Nedam, and her sixth grade students, to help kids in rural Afghanistan.   Since then, the US students have helped raise the money to build four schools (including two girls schools) a deep water well and a medical clinic. Construction of a small hospital is underway. Kids 4 Afghan Kids is 100% volunteer, so your 100 % of your donations are used to educate children.

title: Help rehabilitate 9 elephant babies in India
description: This wildlife rescue and rehabilitation project in Assam, India rehabilitates orphaned elephant calves back into the wild. At times, elephant babies are orphaned and abandoned by their herd following the tragic death of their mothers, either due to electrocution, poaching or conflict. To ensure their survival, our trained team of veterinarians and animal keepers bring them to our rehabilitation center, where they are nurtured for 3-4 years until they are ready to return home, into the wild.

title: Help Afghan refugees in Russia
description: After the collapse of Afghan government and Taliban taking power, hundreds of people from Afghanistan got stuck in Russia. Returning to Afghanistan poses the threat of torture, imprisonment or death to them. They are all so-called 'refugees sur place': endangered by events in their homeland while already being abroad.  Due to Russian migration policy most of them don't have legal status and can't work. We will support the most vulnerable people providing basic necessities and legal help.

title: Ihtiyac Haritasi / Needs Map
description: Needs Map is an online platform that brings people in need together with the supporters. It acts for Inequality, Economic and social poverty, Neglection of local economy due to centralized humanitarian assistance, Lack of coordination and use of unsustainable methods in humanitarian response. It facilitates cooperation and solidarity in different areas such as education, health, culture and arts through verified geospatial data technology and community-based verification functionality.

title: 1000 Microloan for Rural Women in Zambia
description: This projects funds a self-sustaining microfinance initiative issuing collateral-free, interest-bearing loans, for as little as $50, to poor women in rural Zambia to assist them in starting businesses, building assets, and gaining business skills so that they can generate income on a long-term basis, permanently improving their household living standards, and achieving financial independence for themselves and their families.

title: RESCUE JUNCTION NEEDS A NEW HOME
description: Well so far what a journey it has been. Over 3000 children have come through the doors of Rescue Junction, some lost, some trafficked, victims of abuse, all in need of protection care and love. But now due to the huge increase in the numbers of children and the age of the current premises we need to build a wonderful purpose built bright new centre fit for the wonderful children we serve.

title: Saving Belize's Birds 2023
description: Belize Bird Rescue is the only multi-species avian rescue facility in Belize, rehabilitating for release orphaned, injured and illegally trafficked parrots and other wild birds of the Central American rainforest.

title: Indonesia Disaster Relief: Food Aid and Recovery
description: Indonesia is located on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a long chain of active volcanoes, and 90% of the world's earthquakes source. The natural disaster risk index in Indonesia for tsunamis, floods, landslides, drought, and forest fires is also relatively high compared to other countries. ACT is on the front line responding to the emergency, providing basic needs on the ground such as shelter, food, and medical assistance. Following with post disaster program: recovery & economics empowerment.

title: Fighting the MMIP Epidemic
description: The number of Missing and Indigenous People (MMIP) is still unknown. Despite the efforts of Indigenous communities and awareness groups, this epidemic sadly remains unaddressed. Systems in place for other communities fail ours. Often family members search on foot, sharing photos of their last seen relative on social media, communities respond in crisis, victims of violence and loved ones of murdered relatives are tragically left to try to heal alone. This is for them.

title: Internet Service & Allowances for Myanmar Teachers
description: The Feb 2021 military coup & COVID-19 in Myanmar have caused a humanitarian crisis. The population is facing food shortages, lack of access to education, losses of jobs, and a health crisis. Inflation has jumped to 40% within 8 months and the economy has shrunk considerably. Schools and universities are still closed due to the political crisis and COVID-19 outbreak. The National University of the University of Myanmar (NUUM) provides educational opportunities for Myanmar students & teachers.

title: One Child One School Bag Project Cameroon
description: The ongoing sociopolitical conflict in the English Speaking regions of Cameroon has had devastating effects on the economy of the population. Ahuge number of the affectedpopulation are children and young adults who have missed several years of school. Factors preventing these children from fully participating in schoolare; poverty, lack of didactic materials,inability to pay fees, loss of household bread winnersto the crisis. This project will provide school supplies, scholarships &library.

title: Save Elephants And Giraffes - Africa's Giants
description: Elephants and giraffes are under threat. Majestic elephants poached for ivory. Gentle giraffes killed for meat and skins Africa's giant herbivores need our help. Across Africa, elephants are slaughtered in their thousands every year. Close-knit elephant families decimated, leaving traumatised family and orphaned young. Giraffes also suffer at the hands of people who value their skin and body parts over a beautiful living animal. Extinction means forever. If we don't act now, it'll be too late.

title: Gift of mobility to 60 persons with disabilities
description: Imagine the joy of a kid with a disability who will now be able to attend a school like his friends. For a person who is not able to move out of his home, it is extremely difficult to access educational and economic opportunities. We are in urgent need of 50 wheelchairs for our colleagues with disabilities who want to use them for their access to education and vocational training.

title: Defending Human Rights of Migrants and Refugees
description: This project seeks to provide financial resources to the Casa San Romero Shelter, located in Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua. In the aim that migrant and refugee people and families receive quality care with a focus on human rights, providing them food, accommodation, medical, psychological, and legal assistance. This will allow them to rebuild their life project.

title: Purpose built school for Quality education,
description: This project will establish a purpose-built school building in a population of over 10,000 for the children of the less privileged people who have worked in brick kilns for a generation. Their children are currently reading in a rented, home-structured building for the last six years that lacks proper classrooms, washrooms, computer lab, library, and other modern-day facilities. This situation restricts the students from utilizing their capabilities creatively to get contemporary education.

title: Good360 Hope & Hygiene Backpack Campaign 2021
description: Good360 and Disaster Services Corp. SVDP-USA are repeating last year's successful initiative to help disaster survivors across the nation. The need is great for basic goods and personal hygiene products.
