Once this social fabric is achieved, they will strengthen their knowledge in farming, food preparations, and we will provide assistance to achieve an impact on consumption of varied and nutritious food.

title: Save the Sacred Forest and Build Tribal Economy
description: The Alik Sacred Forest, is the last home of the Higa-onon indigenous people, the sacred place to exercise their beliefs and cultural traditions, and the house of endangered species.   50 ha of the Sacred Forest are threatened to be bought by a mining company. We can buy it back and preserve it for perpetuity by giving it the status of common land. Support us in preserving biodiversity and ancestral knowledge. This is the first phase of a larger vision for building a tribal economy.

title: Relief for Acute Trauma in Besieged Ukrainians
description: One of the greatest humanitarian crises since the World Wars is happening NOW.  Hundreds of thousands are under continual attack and without basic medical services or relief.  IMCRA has mobilized to recruit dozens of Ukrainian and Russian-speaking medical specialists to: 1) Advise lay people on how to care for acute traumatic injuries in family and friends, 2) Provide online remedial medical education in specialties needed by besieged populations and not available under present circumstances.

title: The worst forest fire in Korea ever, Please HELP
description: The Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasure Headquarters announced that 15,420ha of forest damage  is estimated by 6 p.m. on the 6th due to forest fires on the east coast. This is the size of about 53 Yeouido areas (290, inner area of Yunjung-ro embankment). In terms of the area (0.71414) of the soccer field, it is 21,597 times more. Forest damage such as 12,695ha in Uljin, 656ha in Samcheok, 1,825ha in Gangneung, 169ha in the East Sea, and This forest fire is the biggest damage in 22 years.

title: Empower 200 Farmers in Kebbi Achieve More Income
description: The Agropreneur Intervention is focused on  building the business and technical skills of 200 Kebbi Farmers  providing access to inputs and  Access to Business advisory services  This is to help them achieve better yields and consequently increase their income.

title: Ukraine: Help Orphans Affected by War
description: Russia has invaded Ukraine. This war will affect millions. As the war destroys Ukraine, the most vulnerable people will suffer. About 100,000 children live in about 650 residential institutions nationwide. Many of these are children who have physical and learning disabilities. Many have no primary carers. Many are unlikely to have a chance to flee and seek refuge elsewhere as the war approaches. These children living in specialized institutions should not be the forgotten victims of this war.

title: Empower Women, Educate Youth
description: In the heart of every family are mothers willing to fight the hard fight to provide for their children, taking this as an opportunity to create change, strategic economic intervention will be provided and distributed by YCAB Foundation to pieces of training that are not limited to Financial Literacy, Online Marketing Strategies, and many others to strengthen the entrepreneurship skill of womenpreneurs.

title: Support vulnerable communities during Ramadan
description: Vulnerability is extremely high in Lebanon, distinctly in the city of Tripoli, due to the challenging economic and financial crisis, Lebanon is facing along with the spread of coronavirus. In order to support the vulnerable community in Tripoli, especially those who have no source of income; are women-headed; or who have a member with a disability, SHiFT will equip its already established kitchen and use it to prepare and distribute warm and nutritious meals during the blessed month of Ramadan.

title: MEET FRANCISCA: A girl with a desire to progress
description: Francisca's (18) life changed in 2008, when her father abandoned her family. "After that, my childhood is over. When would I go to high school if I had to take care of my siblings and clean the house?" she says. She spent almost three years without going to school, her days were divided into cleaning, cooking and taking her brothers to school. Thanks to Hogar de Cristo, she is now back to school. We need your support to continue helping young women like Francisca

title: Schooling two Ukrainian kids with special needs
description: At Celia and Pepe School we want to welcome two new kids. They are coming from Ukraine together with their mothers and running away from the horror. They have no place and no school to go to. Thus, we have committed to provide schooling for them until July 2022 and to look for jobs for their mothers.

title: Peace Education | Art | Communication - PEAC
description: At this time, it's easy to pull away in fear & not want to feel anything. Here at PEAC, we ask you to feel all that is happening fully, so we have the information and tools needed to move forward! We are working locally & internationally, pushing for policies that highlight anti-racism and decolonization. We sit on several policy committees at the United Nations and the State & City level.   Please help us ensure intersectionality and anti-racism stay at the forefront!

title: Relief for Victims in Ukraine
description: Gift of the Givers relief intervention in Ukraine is focused on providing emergency relief items to orphans, elderly, families and individuals. We have mobilized volunteers within Ukraine thus broadening our reach within "hot spots". Our immediate approach is a resourceful one given that many areas are no entry zones, and this includes the identifying of specific needs, locating shops & suppliers, providing funding, & immediate delivery of aid from within.

title: Emergency Fund for Ukraine
description: For those who stay behind in Ukraine fighting not only the outside war, but the war with diseases and injuries. Patients. Their families. Injured people. Medical staff.   Give Life works with local contacts to gather necessities from hospitals across Ukraine and send to the boarder medication, equipments and medical supplies.

title: Ukraine emergency: an hope for future
description: 24 February 2022: the day when the Russian occupation of Ukraine began, when the world's security was threatened by a potential third world war and started the worst refugee crisis in Europe since the end of the Second World War. As of today, there are approximately 2 million Ukrainian refugees, 1.85 million internally displaced persons, and some 12.65 million people directly affected by the conflict, who are currently facing cold, hunger and constant flight from bomb and weapons.

title: HELP UKRAINE - Humanitarian relief in Chernivtsi
description: More than 2 million refugees left Ukraine. Many of them come from the most war-torn areas of the country, through the Chernivtsi region and then to the Romanian border.   IBO Italia has been working in cooperation with local partners (schools, universities, associations) in the Chernivtsi region for more than 10 years. With this project IBO Italia aims to support Internally Displaced People and Refugees, providing them with essential goods and psychological support.

title: Empower 100 Nigerian Youth thru Entrepreneurship
description: Complex societal challenges are preventing many  children attaining education. Many of them suffer from low income, low financial literacy, and high debt levels. Financial hardship and complex societal challenges directly influence a person's cognitive ability. Sam Onyemaechi Humanitarian foundation supports vulnerable and underserved children by providing partial and complete tuition fees, learning materials to overcome some challenges on a need and merit basis.

title: Humanitarian Medical and food Aid for Ukraine
description: Respected Humanitarian  Tens of thousands of helpless, vulnerable people are fleeing their homes with barely any supplies or belongings to reach the safety of temporary shelters and relief camps. There is an immediate need for emergency medical supplies, basic food and essential supplies to fulfill the needs of these overcrowded centers. This need will continue to grow in the coming weeks and months till peace is fully restored in the country.

title: SAYes Mentoring - Support our Mentors and Mentees
description: With global lockdowns, we had to think of new ways of continuing to support our mentees. We opened up our mentoring programme worldwide and the response was fantastic.  However, remote mentoring has its challenges, not least the cost of training, phones and data. The money raised will help towards these costs.  SAYes Mentoring was founded in 2008 to improve personal, social, educational and employment outcomes for under-served children and young people in South Africa, through mentoring.

title: Help Kids in Ukraine in Time of War
description: The terrible war is ongoing in Ukraine. Russian invaders bomb cities, hospitals, houses, killing civilians without remorse. Ukrainian kids with cancer and other serious diagnoses are more vulnerable than most in such a situation. They need medicines, medical supplies, food to survive in Ukraine and transportation when evacuation is possible.

title: Emergency Fund: Together for Ukrainian animals
description: The situation in Ukraine is desperate. After millions of people abandoned their home, heading to West countries, many animals remained in war zone. Pets who lost owners; animals abandoned or injured saved in shelters from across Ukraine need food, supplies, medical care. ROLDA is just 8km from the border with Ukraine (Reni - Giurgiulesti) Your donations enable us to send vital assistance to shelters and rescuers from all over Ukraine and help some dogs be transported to ROLDA in Romania.

title: Supporting a More Resilient Arts + Culture Sector
description: Houston Arts Alliance is a local arts and culture organization whose principal work is to implement the City of Houston's vision, values, and goals for its arts grantmaking and civic art investments. HAA also executes privately funded projects to meet the needs of the arts community, such as disaster preparation, equity in the arts and arts education, research on the state of the arts in Houston, and temporary public art projects.  HAA helps artists and nonprofits be bold, productive and strong.

title: Support Beirut Art Center's 2022 Program
description: Beirut Art Center has been conceiving its programming around structural and material conditions in the visual fields in Lebanon and beyond. In addition to being a platform for creative and intellectual output, BAC is examining the socio-political struggles with which the workings of the center intersect. Our goal is to build interdisciplinary projects that use art as a conductor for community-building, political action and radical imagination.

title: Regenerating Rainforests in Madagascar
description: Health In Harmony partners with Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities living in and around the Manombo Forest in Southern Madagascar to implement community-designed solutions to halt deforestation. Manombo is shrinking rapidly under the pressures of slash-and-burn agriculture, logging, and hunting, which are rooted in food insecurity and a lack of healthcare and other livelihoods in the region. Communities requested support for healthcare, education, and training in regenerative livelihoods.

title: Ukraine Crisis Urgent Humanitarian Aid
description: Brutal conflict in Ukraine has sent more than 3 million people on a desperate race to escape. Homes and infrastructure have been destroyed. Families have been separated. Lives have been lost. Our partners are working in Przemysl (Southern Poland) to meet the immediate needs of these refugees - providing support such as food, bedding and temporary accommodation in reception centers at the border.

title: Emergency Relief for the Crisis in Ukraine
description: As the Japanese NGO working in conflict/disaster-affected areas for world peace since 2001, we can't ignore the victims of the crisis in Ukraine due to Russia's invasion. This project provides humanitarian relief and long-term support to  affected people by the crisis in Ukraine. We need your help and stand for world peace.

title: Support civil society in fight for global justice
description: The Coalition for the International Criminal Court (CICC) is the world's largest civil society partnership advancing the cause of international justice. With member organizations in 150 countries, the Coalition is leading the global fight for a fair, effective, and independent Court and promoting broad accountability and redress for the victims of serious international crimes. To ensure broad participation, adequate translation and interpretation services are needed.

title: Donate a Vehicle for NDF Rehab Center Nawabshah
description: NDF Rehabilitation Center Nawabshah is providing free life therapies to 100+ children with Intellectual Disabilities. In our Center the retention of children for therapies is big component to contribute in the rehabilitation process, the rehabilitation process is prolonged to bring the impact, the parents can not bear the patience to bring the child at facility regularly, it results to avoid bringing their children regularly. The Vehicle will provide free pick & drop to the children.

title: Train Caregivers to Prevent Child Sexual Abuse
description: This project will equip parents and caregivers in Kenya with the skills to identify, prevent and respond to child sexual abuse. In a society where conversations on sexuality are taboo, this project will help parents teach their children about body autonomy, good versus bad touch, and how to recognize and prevent child sexual abuse. With 16% girls and 6% boys being sexually abused before the age of 18 in Kenya, this project will help keep the next generation safe.

title: Let's get ready to rebuild Ukraine
description: This madness will stop, eventually, and after that, we'll clean up, put the pieces back together and move on.  Over the last 15 years, we've managed multiple construction crews here in Moldova, building the Eco-village complex, Katalyst Kitchens, and repairing houses and apartments for many friends and family.  We have a lot of experience, and contacts.  But what if you intersect that with our professional backgrounds in non-formal education?  Let us introduce the Katalyst Vocational School.

title: ebdaa center
description: This project will provide Syrian refugees in Lebanon between the ages of 7 to 17 with Ebdaa Centre, which will give the necessary training and support to enhance their talents. The Talent Sponsorship Project aims to give Syrian refugees a haven where they are free to express themselves through art, sports, acting, inventions, and music.

title: Comprehensive Sexuality Education to Young People
description: APLAFA provides comprehensive sexuality education to young people in Panama, through its Juventud con Opciones program. During the last five years, 15,452 youngs and adolescents have received sex education. Your donation provides transportation, food, work materials and even options for contraceptive methods to each of the young participants; and collaborates in the prevention of child sexual abuse, teenage pregnancy, gender violence and poverty, in our communities.

title: Emergency Response to Ukrainian Families
description: This project will provide urgently needed food, shelter, Hygiene items, and PSS to Ukrainian families in Ukraine and Moldova

title: The Her Pad Project in Misungwi, Tanzania
description: This project strives to provide access to sanitary pads for 1,000 rural school girls , and helps these girls manage their periods comfortably and safely while at school.   This in turn increase their school attendance, self-esteem and self-worth resulting to improved academic performances. The girls are given a reusable pad and given the tools and knowledge to make their own pads.

title: Month of Togetherness: Ramadan Aid
description: This project aims to help the most vulnerable communities in Lebanon receive their basic needs. This year, URDA is launching an initiative that aims to remind the needy, poor and fragile that hope is still alive and that compassion still has a positive impact in the world. This project is a reminder to every person in need that they are not alone in their struggles.

title: Die Arche - Help for refugees from Ukraine
description: In addition to our offers for our Arche children, we are currently also committed to the refugee families from Ukraine. The images and the effects of the war, which is forcing hundreds of thousands of people to leave their homes, are of great concern to us at the Arche. Our Arche locations distribute clothing, food, water, and hot meals to the refugee families. In addition, we organize schooling and programs for refugee children and consult the arriving families on further steps.

title: Emergency Response for Ukrainians
description: Following the initiation of the military offence of Russia against Ukraine on 24 February 2022, as of March 11th, 34.392 individuals with Ukrainian citizenship have entered Turkey. Most of the refugees are composed of women, children, elderly and individuals with vulnerablities. With this project, ASAM is aiming at meeting the urgent needs of the individuals to prevent further suffering and decreasing the risks that they may encounter. To do that, ASAM will provide emergency assistance.

title: Edgar Cahn's Legacy - Plant Seeds of Change!
description: Edgar Cahn passed away on the morning of January 23, 2022 at age 86, leaving behind an immense legacy of making revolutionary change by planting seeds wherever his heart, mind, and soul were invested.  He embodied the highest ideals of mobilizing communities to come together to express their strengths and to restore mutual care.   In the spirit of Edgar Cahn, we wish to carry on his legacy by helping you plant your own seeds of change.

title: Botswana's future environmental stewards 2022-2023
description: This project provides stimulating and fun environmental education for 140 students in 4 schools in rural Botswana; teaching children ecological concepts, environmental awareness and problem-solving through games and hands-on activities. These activities will build the environmental stewards of tomorrow, enabling them to tackle the issues rural communities face, and will increasingly face due to climatic changes and competition for resources, as well as prepare them for future employment.

title: Activities for childhood cancer survivors
description: We organise several activities for childhood cancer survivors. Childhood cancers survivors often face physical and mental late effects. The activities empowers them in their lives after the childhood cancer. Our activities are a form of peer support that offers them a possibility to exchange experiences, learn from each other and also have fun together. This empowers them to regain control over their lives. The activities are: - camps  - sport activities  - social meet-ups - pub quizzes

title: Safe Space to Talk: Psychological help for Ukraine
description: The project focuses on psychological help for 100 000 Ukrainians. In the situation of military aggression by the Russian Federation and under the pressure of the humanitarian catastrophe taking place in Ukraine, therapists, psychodynamic counselors, crisis and clinic psychologists, and University professors joined efforts to help fellow citizens in this difficult time of war.

title: Resiliency Gardens for Ukrainian Refugees and IDPs
description: This project will fund seed access and education programs to establish home and community resiliency gardens in Poland and Ukraine. By working with local schools and communities, we will support vegetable production and community building for Ukrainians and the communities that support them.

title: Empower 20 Young Africans as Agents of Change
description: The African narrative has been that of a dependent continent and its arising problems have put the future of the African youth in despair. The Africa Matters Ambassadors Program (AMAP) tries to break the programmed curse affecting the future of Africa. AMAP is a one-year virtual African leadership development program which provides successful applicants with skills development, cross-continental networks, mentorship from industry leaders and the implementation of community engagement projects.

title: Japan Earthquake Relief Fund
description: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake in Japan has caused widespread damage across Miyagi and Fukushima Prefectures, only days after the 11th anniversary of the earthquake and tsunami that devastated Japan in 2011. Your donation to the fund will help affected communities in Japan recover.

title: Provide Shelter for 120 Vulnerable Indian Children
description: Children are vanishing from India's chaotic and busy railway stations every day. They are kidnapped, snatched, trafficked and sold into slavery. Forced into child labour or sex work most of these children are never seen again. Railway Children run Open Shelters located close to railway stations, safe places for lost or otherwise vulnerable children to give us the time and space to work with children and decide the best long-term solution for them - preferably back with family members.

title: Support 5 female deaf for hairdressing & salon
description: MPWDA intends to implement a project titled "Support 5 female deaf youth for hairdressing and start a salon". In Mpigi district we have a number of female youths with deaf disability who are unemployed because of their low levels of education and limited access to both formal and informal jobs. MPWDA would like to start a saloon for deaf girls to get employed, earn a living and lead dignified lives

title: Ukraine Crisis Response
description: International aid organization World Vision is swiftly ramping up its response to the Ukraine refugee crisis, as the number of refugees today hit a staggering 3 million. The response will target the most vulnerable children and women with Non-Food Items (NFI's), cash assistance, child-protection, anti-trafficking, mental health and psycho-social support (MHPSS), and education.

title: Global Hunger Crisis
description: Conflict, climate, and COVID-19 are driving hunger and a sharp rise in the lack of food in many fragile and humanitarian contexts. In FY20, World Vision delivered humanitarian aid to 27.9 million people, of which 15 million received food assistance. World Vision is able to reach suffering families and children in the hardest-hit countries as the World Food Program's largest partner. Because of donor partnerships, every dollar that you invest with World Vision becomes eight dollars.

title: Ukraine: Help Children's Hospitals to Save Lives
description: War crimes are being committed in Ukraine as hospitals are attacked, and citizens are displaced. Half of Ukraine's power grid is crippled, causing prolonged nationwide power and water outages. As a result, healthcare professionals are struggling in tough conditions. This, combined with massive state underfinancing, means that hospitals are desperate for help. We provide essential medical tools, supplies, and life-saving equipment to ensure effective medical care for children.

title: Social Impact Bond for reuniting families
description: You Me We have taken the initiative to explore what a SIB could look like in the out-of-home care space in Japan and have approached Social Outcomes to develop a SIB proposal that could be shared with the Japanese government. The proposal will focus on a program which re-educates parents in order to prevent children from entering the out of home care system, or to successfully reunite those who have already been removed back with their parents.

title: Support Girls' Education in Afghanistan
description: Following the Taliban takeover of Afghanistan in August 2021, girls have faced unprecedented barriers to accessing education. Overall, girls' education in Afghanistan is uncertain, unprotected, and highly at-risk on a daily basis, with the context varying dramatically in the marginalized communities. Working through our grassroots networks, Bamyan continues to promote and support girls' access to quality education, in order to develop the next generation of critical thinkers and change-makers.

title: Supporting 25 displaced families on Crete, Greece
description: What would make us and our families leave our home, work, and travel to an unknown country at high cost and risk? War, violence, discrimination, poverty are pushing millions to move into the unknown. The recent war in Ukraine has shown us how quickly things can deteriorate for millions of people. We are helping refugees and asylum seekers around us irrespective of their religion, gender and nationality with immediate solutions to food insecurity, accommodation and other essential needs.

title: UKRAINE: Help beyond Borders!
description: Ukraine is facing a violent conflict against the Russian Federation since February 2022. The centre "The House of Mercy", that previously hosted 100 children with disability, has been evacuated due to the war. Now it is hosting hundreds of displaced people that need immediate assistance. Thanks to this project Aleimar and Fondazione Don Gnocchi want to provide emergency medication, first aid kits and humanitarian aid that will be fundamental to save their lives.

title: House of Hope for Ukrainian Refugees
description: One Humanity Institute (OHI) is creating a Welcome Center that will provide transitional housing and permanent residence for families rendered homeless by Putin's war. Located in the historic center of Osweicim Poland, OHI will renovate two buildings to provide much needed housing and personal services. OHI has been on the border touching many lives with our teddy bears, translators and supplies. Now it is time to provide housing. THE REFUGEES NEED OUR HELP AND WE NEED YOURS TO MAKE THIS HAPPEN!

title: Texas Wildfire Relief Fund
description: Wildfires across central Texas have displaced thousands and destroyed beloved homes and businesses. The Eastland Complex Fire is now the largest fire in state history and has destroyed dozens of homes. All donations to this fund will support wildfire relief and recovery efforts in Texas. Your donation will go to vetted nonprofits providing food, water, and shelter to people and animals in need.

title: Digital Transformation for schools in Burundi
description: The project goal is to facilitate    the digital transformation for Burundi's education system, It will equip fifteen schools with ICT Labs with 300 computers connected to Internet for students to learn ICT ,digital entrepreneurship    and research. The project will also train 300 teachers, who will instruct the ICT curriculum for 18,000 students from those schools. It will prepare Burundian youth for the ability to compete in the global economy with needed skills for Innovations and job market

title: Ukraine Journalism Relief Fund
description: In the midst of war in Ukraine, the need to support true journalism and disseminate information to the local and global public is of vital importance. We are raising funds to directly support the only local TV channel currently running in Kyiv and to support local media network families while their loved ones remain in Kyiv broadcasting true stories first-hand.

title: Hakuna Matata - capacity building
description: Hakuna Matata program is a five-year-long program for marginalized children of the age group 12-17 belonging to low-income families and ethnic minorities from the slum areas of Kathmandu. Due to the lack of education and overall personality and capacity development activities, Hakuna Matata program will help the children develop social and communication skills, higher-order thinking, positive identity, and better future beliefs and emotional skills during their monthly workshops over 5 years.

title: Free Mental Health Support for Ukraine
description: Ukrainians are mentally and emotionally traumatized by the Russian aggression in their country. Bosnian citizens are particularly able to understand the struggles of Ukrainians because of their experience with war in the 1990s, and the team at Wings of Hope is well-equipped to provide services to victims, both adults and children, from Ukraine who need vital mental health care to help with the trauma of their difficult experiences but are unable to pay.

title: Your Zakat transforms 12,000 students' learning
description: Teach For Pakistan Fellows - outstanding university graduates - teach full-time in public schools, accelerating learning for students who are on average 4 years behind grade-level. As our students strive to close the achievement gap, they face a shortage of everyday learning resources, e.g., stationery, reference books/materials and copying funds. Your Zakat, sadqa, and donations equip 12,000 students across rural Islamabad with the tools to build the tomorrow of their dreams.

title: Gift an education, make*life and change vulnerable
description: Raise education centre has a population of more than 300 pupils which provide high quality school education in both c.b.c and 844 curriculum to slum urban area in Kenya who cannot access or afford it. The education centre adopt a nurturing ,holistic to education helping children learn joyfully.350 of the children get fully scholarship by the centre through donors .while the rest pay a subsidized fee . your donation goes towards critical infrastructure  and purchasing of land. the school feeding

title: ORTHOPEDIC AIDS AND PHYSICAL THERAPY
description: The objective of this project is to provide the orthopedic and physical therapy aids that the patient requires, to facilitate their mobilization, and give them the necessary care according to the indicated medical prescription once they have undergone surgery. Some patients have had to be amputated in some of their lower or upper limbs due to cancer and therefore require special assistance.

title: 50 edu-libraries to children in poverty in Africa
description: In South Africa, thousands of parents rely on Early Learning Centres in the impoverished communities where they live. Most of these little schools have little to no education resources or toys. This project aims to provide 50 edu-libraries to Early Learning Centres in the poverty-stricken communities that we serve. Edu-libraries are a compact educational libraries for children to use as a key part of their development.

title: Build a new Neonatal Care Unit, Haiti
description: HHA's existing Neonatal Unit opened in 2012, able to treat up to 8 unwell babies. It quickly became stretched beyond capacity, regularly caring for 14 babies at a time who are forced to share cots and oxygen. We have now finalised plans to build a new Neonatal Care Unit, with the capacity to accommodate 16 babies, a breastfeeding/family care room, postnatal ward, chapel, training room, staff offices and accommodation.  This unit will save the lives of thousands of babies in the years to come.

title: support to cancer affected people
description: 10 lakh new cases of cancer occur and 7 lakh die of various forms of cancer every year in India. In Tamilnadu, burden of cancer is predicted to increase by 32 per cent in 2016, translating to 55,000 new cancer cases per year as per a study by cancer institute. 80% of the cancer patients go to a doctor at an advanced stage and this hampers the treatment. VETNGO plans to do awareness&screening camps and referral linkages so as to facilitate early detection, timely treatment in kallakuric district.

title: Beautification & Greening of schools in Kenya
description: The Mabati Technical Training Institute is planning to harvest and store rainwater during the upcoming rainy season in September to store over 1,500,000 litres of water. The dam measuring 1059 cubic metres if repaired with High-density polyethylene (HDPE), can last between 10 to 30 years & supply enough water to irrigate our kitchen garden to produce  vegetables to support our school feeding program and to  educate our youth  on the importance of environmental conservation  and tree planting.

title: Uganda women's economic empowerment loan fund
description: Little by Little, small donations put together, can enable economic empowerment of disadvantaged women in Uganda, who against all odds are struggling to put food on the table for their families. They are hawkers, vendors, traders, artisanal entrepreneurs, smallholder farmers, who need access to inexpensive finance & financial literacy to enhance profitability of their enterprises & improve livelihoods. Together we can establish a community loan fund to give 200 women loans & financial literacy.

title: Welding apprenticeships to empower youth in Uganda
description: Little by Little, small donations put together can help disadvantaged youth in Uganda to acquire artisanal livelihood skills, so that they may be able to earn incomes & be able to feed hundreds of desperate households. 78% of Ugandans are aged 30 years & below, of whom 48% are a dependent population, aged 14 years & below. Thus, youth aged 15-30 years, 30% of Uganda's population, are mostly bearing the  burden to provide for its 40 million people; & yet, youth in Uganda are largely unemployed.

title: Support a New Generation of Changemakers in Ghana
description: A central part of GEC is our Changemaker Program where students learn about famous figures past & present, historically significant events, and Pan-Africanism. Students also participate in community events throughout Ghana and engage with individuals making a local community impact. This helps students reflect on an ever-changing society and their important role within it. We believe this work equips our students to be the next generation of change-making leaders of the Diaspora and the world.

title: Help kids with challenges Team Up for Esports!
description: Due to COVID, the mission of Team Up for 1 had to be put on hold. We are now returning to in-person activities, however, many of our kids with challenges have high health risks and still may not be able to participate in in-person team sports. As such, we are expanding our programs to now include esports. Esports is competitive organized video gaming that is popular on most college campuses. This project will allow 25 kids to pilot our new program with several colleges in the Mid-Atlantic area.

title: Accelerating Positive Youth Development in Kisumu
description: With the underlying challenges facing young people in Kisumu, including poverty, dysfunctional families, peer influence, lacking a basic foundation for personal development, and more, it is becoming increasingly important to support young people in their developmental process to enable them to meaningfully contribute to their families, community and the country. This project is meant to support the staff and the young people within the youth-serving institution.

title: Cape CARES Fundraiser for Soccer Balls
description: As observed during our brigades, soccer (or futbol) is a well-loved pastime and the national sport of Honduras. However, because over 66% of Honduras live in poverty, having access to soccer balls isn't a reality. Soccer is a way for community members to connect, form important relationships, and simply have fun in a stressful life burdened by intense poverty. For kids, soccer is a way to further cognitive development and socialization through the development of important social and language.

title: Provide Kenyan families with the means to survive
description: Inequalities created by climate change, conflict and COVID-19 threaten the lives of the families we work with.  Now more than ever they need the programmes we have developed over 20 years that support every family member.  Girls protected from teenage pregnancy so they finish school and have better options in life; boys with knowledge and direction needed to grow into responsible men; mothers kept safe in pregnancy and childbirth; men and women with lifeskills for growth and empowerment.

title: Championing A Kenyan Women's Microbusiness Program
description: This project addresses generational poverty in rural women through an innovative entrepreneurship training and mentorship program.  Entrepreneurship drives economic growth, creates self-sufficiency and solves some large-scale development problems women face. Our project serves the unique needs of women at the base of the economic pyramid. It supports them to start sustainable businesses ventures rooted in the local economy, such that they can have a reliable income stream long into the future.

title: Help Support Palliative Care Patients in Ukraine
description: The war in Ukraine is a major problem for adults and children receiving or needing palliative care in Ukraine. An estimated 500,000 adults and children in Ukraine are dying or have palliative care needs in Ukraine annually. These seriously ill people, the sickest in our health care system, are stuck in Ukraine or are being moved to palliative care programs in Poland, Romania, and Moldova. Our colleagues in these countries are being overwhelmed and need your help!

title: Fund Community Rehabilitation Workers in Uganda
description: Working in BidiBidi and Palorinya refugee settlements in Uganda, our Community Based Rehabilitation workers (CBRs) ensure the most vulnerable refugees can access disability and nutrition support. Our CBRs are a dedicated team, many of whom are refugees themselves, with unrivalled knowledge of the needs of persons with disabilities in the settlements. They provide education and refer individuals to our projects, including wheelchair distributions and nutrition and agriculture programmes.

title: Outdoor Cats Enclosures
description: Home Dinev Foundation is registered to help sick and injured stray dogs and cats. From the moment of registration until today, 100 cats and 200 dogs are under the care of our small team. All animals arrive in very serious health condition and after recovery preparing for adoption.  Until we find a suitable adoptive parent, they remain in our care.

title: Protect the Bravest: Help Ukrainian Children
description: Today bravery has gained a new meaning. While Ukraine is fighting for freedom, Ukrainian children have one more battle against cancer. During these challenging times, they remain brave, strong, and courageous. But sometimes, even the bravest ones need help. Today you can support Ukrainian children battling cancer with your donation. It is so essential for them. And subscribing to a monthly donation will have an even more significant impact. It is a guarantee of continuous treatment for children.

title: Help keep the Ukrainian refugee center safe.
description: The project will be used to protect the refugee center as long as Ukrainian refugees who are tired of the war, feel safe. At least 100 to 3,000 people will be beneficiary. The center, which was built by cleaning and repairing the space that had been abandoned for 9 years, had collapsed the ceiling and water and electricity are in trouble one after another. Even the interest of other donors has disappeared, and the manpower that helped clean up has over, and staffs are exhausted. Give your help!

title: Project Access Safety Net Rural Elderly & Disabled
description: In a rural district of 54,000 people and only 4 doctors, the public health nurses have no time for home visits. The elderly and disabled of all ages live in dire conditions, without food at the end of the month, bedsores, no way to get to a doctor.  Warm Heart's Project Access ensures rural constituents have home care and access to medical care.  We bring wheelchairs and safety ramps.  As the population ages, there are more elders at risk.  Our staff coordinator and volunteers fill the gap.

title: EEqual: The Power of Youth Leadership
description: EEqual is a for-youth-by-youth non-profit working to overcome student homelessness by raising awareness and increasing access to higher education.   There are 25 EEqual Chapters. Chapters are youth-led groups, spread across the country, organizing with their peers, addressing the problem of youth homelessness.  We hope to grow and expand our Chapters program through the Power of Youth campaign. Our goal is to double the number of EEqual Chapters by the end of 2022.

title: Education for Dominican & Zambian Communities
description: GRACE Cares, in partnership with our local heroes, will provide educational opportunities to Project Hearts in Baitoa, Dominican Republic, and the Munali Youth Empowerment Program (MYEP) in Lusaka Province, Zambia. In the Dominican Republic, Project Hearts will train women in basic health and medical knowledge in their Community Health Leadership (CHL) program; and in Zambia, MYEP will provide books and learning materials to children as part of their Mobile Book program.

title: Emergency Aid To Forgotten Refugees in The Balkans
description: Thousands of refugees seeking safety in the EU are stuck in the Balkans, largely forgotten by the media but still desperately in need of urgent help. The ForRefugees network provides emergency basics to refugees of all ages, all genders, from any country, but as the number of refugees grows so does the pressure on our resources. Donations to our campaign will help us give refugees the things they need right now: food, clothing, healthcare, hygiene items, legal advice - and humanity.

title: Make the Invisible Visible: Rural Water Census
description: More than 2.3 million Argentines live in rural isolated communities that are impacted by an extreme climate, socio-economic vulnerability and lack of access to water and sanitation.  The lack of data on these local populations is a limitation for designing public policies to address the issue of water access. This project aims to gather this key information and involves developing a mobile app to facilitate those tasks.

title: Help Women Impacted by Conflict Access Education
description: Around the world, 82.4 million individuals, mostly women and children, have been forced to be displaced. Under these fragile and conflict affected situations, only 13% of females are enrolled in higher education. This project will work towards raising funds to help women under these circumstances continue their higher education.

title: Donate Your Zakat for Education
description: Zakat is one of the pillars of Islam that must be met by the Muslims who meet certain criteria. Zakat is a blessing, symbolising purity, kindness, and a contribution to the development of entitled recipients. At JAAGO, we are aiming to raise donations/Zakat (Muslim obligatory charity) for underprivileged students to support their education and provide them books, stationery, healthy food, uniforms, school bags etc. Currently, JAAGO is educating 4200 students across 11 schools in Bangladesh.

title: Handwashing Stations for South Sudanese Schools
description: This project includes establishing handwashing stations at twelve (12) junior schools and eight (8) high schools in Central Equatoria, South Sudan. Diarrhea and pneumonia are globally two of the leading causes of death for children. Handwashing with soap is among the most effective and inexpensive ways to prevent these diseases. This simple behavior can save lives, cutting diarrhea by almost one-half and acute respiratory infections by nearly one-quarter. (ref. globalhandwashing.org)

title: Detroit Rain Catchment & Produce Washing
description: We partner with urban farms to provide water solutions to aid in agricultural growth, community development, and resource management. We're building a water catchment system for irrigation and produce washing for Nurturing Our Seeds, a nonprofit farm in Detroit. The wash station will be a shared space for a local Black farmer collective to wash and pack their produce to more effectively provide food to their communities. This project will support this amazing local partner in more ways than one!

title: Support women, girls and trans in Hong Kong
description: In Hong Kong, women, girls, and trans face incredible challenges to their safety, success, and rights. With your support grassroots women organisations and associations are transforming the lives of their communities. Your support will fuel these communities to shift power and privilege into equity and equality for all.

title: Ending Period Poverty for rural girls in Tanzania
description: Girls in rural Tanzania face a toxic trio of barriers around their menstruation: significant cultural taboos & stigma; insufficient relevant menstruation education; & lack of access to safe & reusable sanitary pads. This leads to girls missing out on their education each month. Lyra's will provide youth friendly menstruation education to rural students & their teachers as well as supply locally made reusable sanitary pads for rural girls, so they can fully engage in their education each month.

title: New Rescue Vehicle to Save Street Animals
description: We need a new Rescue Vehicle to collect and transport sick and injured animals to our animal hospital in rural Rajasthan, India. TOLFA has been saving the lives of street animals since 2005. We have a busy hospital able to care for 600 patients at a time. We have increased the number of street treatments which now keeps one of our existing vehicles occupied. We need a new Rescue Vehicle to attend to emergency rescue calls and take sick animals back to our hospital for treatment and care.

title: Reforestation for the future of the Amazon
description: You hear a lot about Amazon DEforestation, but not much about REforestation! At our field stations we are working to grow native high quality timber, medicinal and fruit trees for reforestation of degraded areas, and to promote community-level reforestation activities. These trees sequester carbon, protect and create wildlife habitat, support biodiversity, and serve as living bank accounts for rural communities. A small investment now can result in a lifetime of benefits for the Amazon.

title: Covering basic needs of families in Guatemala
description: In 2020-21, the COVID-19 pandemic has worsened a long list of existing problems in Guatemala, one of the countries with the most inequalities in all of Latin America. Families have been particularly affected by the pandemic, as parents have been forced to figure out ways to meet their most basic needs despite job insecurities, increasing debts, persisting concerns about health and safety, and prevalent closures of schools for over two years.

title: Invest in entrepreneurs to change the world
description: We are raising funds to invest in our next group of change-makers. One entrepreneur you can invest in is Macharia. Through Earth Hub, he is building affordable and resilient housing for the average Kenyans in the urban settlements using interlocking bricks. By not using costly cement, they reduce the costs of homes by up to 40%.  Another example is Sofia. Through Eco Jiko, she manufactures hybrid steel cookstoves that use biomass briquettes, providing a clean & affordable cooking option.

title: Empower 500 women farmers in Mozambique
description: This project will enable 500 women smallholder farmers in the Beira corridor of rural Mozambique to gain access to quality inputs, basic technology and trainings such as financial literacy, business skills,couples training and market linkages to strengthen their business to grow and sell vegetables to support their families. A woman is empowered when she is an equal economic decision maker in her family and a leader in her community.

title: Providing Critical Medicines for Ukraine Crisis
description: Direct Relief is working with Ukraine's Ministry of Health and other groups in the region to provide requested medical aid-from oxygen concentrators to critical care medicines-while preparing to offer longer-term assistance to people displaced or affected by the war.  Mass displacement leads to a host of health problems. Direct Relief is already working with medical manufacturers to source medical aid needed in the coming weeks and months.

title: Support for 200 homeless youths in Bangkok
description: Every month more than 200 children and youths living on the streets of Bangkok depend on Childline Thailand Foundation (CTF) for basic needs support. CTF provides services through our harm reduction shelter 'the Hub' and offers daily meals, showers, a safe space to rest and access to health services, counselling, education and life skills. Situated in the heart of Bangkok, the Hub has been helping children in street situations for 10 years.

title: Let Rural Girls Dream Big
description: In India, women have traditionally been discriminated against and excluded from decision-making in public and private spheres, especially in rural areas. Girls often drop out of school to get married or take care of the family, which prevents many of them from finishing high school or going to college. Only 21% of local students who pursue STEM degrees are women. This program helps them graduate and find employment in a technical field.

title: Educating Colombian children for a better future
description: In CRAN Foundation in Bogota, we have under our protection 65 children between the ages of 0 and 12 years. Our goal is to ensure that each of our children have an education that allows them to build a better future.

title: Safeguard habitat for wildlife in Central America!
description: Invest in Central America and our planet! Your gift will help build wildlife corridors that foster a connection between people and nature. Support wildlife conservation, community work, citizen science, our Junior Ranger program, reforestation efforts, and innovative technology. Gifts will be applied to projects in Nicaragua and El Salvador that need the most attention at the time of your donation. If you love wildlife and people, or just want to help generally, this project is for YOU.

title: Educating Caregivers working in orphanages
description: Transicion a la Vida is an organization fully dedicated to supporting youth placed in orphanages. Working for 10 years with different institutions across Panama, experience has shown that working only with youth resolves one part of the problem. By educating their caregivers with whom they spend the majority of the time, we ease the transition from living in an institution and give them the best chance to become independent members of society.

title: Help Feed Sick and Injured Wildlife
description: This project will provide the food needed to feed orphaned and injured animals being nursed back to health at ReWild Rehabilitation Centre in South Africa! ReWild hand rears orphaned wildlife and prepares them for release as well as treats injured, sick and poisoned wildlife so they can be returned to the wild as fit and healthy animals.

title: Sponsored walk to help tackle food poverty in UK
description: President Peter Bradley, of the Rotary Club of Edgware and Stanmore, will be doing a virtual sponsored walk at the end of April 2022 from one end of the UK to the other, Lands End to John'O'Groats, to raise money for My Yard and awareness of food poverty in the United Kingdom. His progress can be followed via the app Conqueror in real time on Google Earth. The charity "My Yard" not only provides food to those in need it takes into account dietary requirements and teaches people to cook healthily

title: One bedroom apartment for vulnerable single lady
description: This project will build a one bedroom apartment with kitchenette and swage sink in a vulnerable single lady in eastern Nigeria, providing a a place for her to live and a healthy and  safe environment.  Her human dignity will also be maintained.

title: Listening to people affected by crisis in Ukraine
description: Loop is a feedback and accountability service for people affected by the crisis in Ukraine to feedback in Ukrainian and Polish and is accessible via WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger, as well as online.  Anyone affected by the crisis, including Ukrainian refugees across Europe and displaced people still in Ukraine, can tell their stories and ask for the right help, safely and freely.

title: Protect Nigerian Children from Malaria Infection
description: This project will provide long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) to 250 households in Anambra State, in order to protect the people, especially children under 5 years of age from malaria infection, as the nets are very effective in preventing malaria. Malaria is a life-threatening disease which is preventable and curable and caused by plasmodium parasites, transmitted to people through the bites of infected female anopheles mosquitoes.

title: Raise $8K for Ndirima Litembo Montessori School
description: Ndirima Litembo Montessori School will provide a rural farming community far outside Songea, Tanzania with their own primary or early childhood school once it has acquired Montessori classroom materials and a trained Montessori teacher.

title: Well Repair-Help Life Re-Blossom for a Community
description: Water for South Sudan (WFSS) is committed to creating sustainable water systems for rural communities in great need. The WFSS well rehab team returns to the organization's older wells to bring them up to a new, stronger design standard, and responds to local requests to rehabilitate wells drilled by other organizations.   WFSS delivers sustainable quality-of-life services to and with the people of South Sudan by efficiently providing access to clean water, sanitation, and hygiene education.

title: Airlink's Airlift Ukraine - Flights to Deliver Aid
description: Already, Airlink donors have helped deliver 300+ responders and 354+ tons of aid.  Tons more ready to go if you help today.  Curious how critically needed donated aid will reach refugees, and people in Ukraine?   AIRLINK coordinates and provides free flights, removing the high costs and logistical challenges of transporting emergency humanitarian aid that can prevent or delay it reaching people in need.      Your donation provides sustainable funding to secure/fund airlift and logistics.

title: Empowering 30 Latin People in Mexico
description: Promote the development of 30 latin people in vulnerable situations who live in Mexico, so that they can develop a business plan project that allows them the correct management of their productive activity; through an online business and life skills training, with emphasis on entrepreneurial, productive and training initiatives, so that they can self-employ and/or exercise an honest, useful, productive, and well paid quality job.

title: Support four Uyghur small businesses in Turkey
description: The Uyghur diaspora is struggling on daily basis with very little help. Unemployment and poverty are on the rise among Uyghur communities. Microenterprise Program addresses this issue by assisting Uyghur small businesses and promoting economic growth, beginning with Turkey, which hosts over 50,000 Uyghur migrants and refugees.

title: Stand with Afghanistan - Emergency Relief Ramadan
description: Afghanistan is experiencing the largest humanitarian crisis in the world. 95% of the population is endangered by food insecurity or malnutrition to an unprecedented degree (UN OCHA). Our solidarity is needed now! In Mazer-e Sharif, we are organising a humanitarian relief for families in Afghanistan during Ramadan, the Islamic month of fasting. Our goal this year is to raise 35.745 to support the nutrition of 300 families for 2-3 months. Can we reach this goal together?

title: Connecting refugees fleeing the war in Ukraine
description: 4M refugees have already fled Ukraine to seek refuge in the neighbouring countries. Families are separated, since it's often women and children who can leave the country. Being forced to leave part of their family behind and having little information on what awaits them beyond the border puts them in a distressing situation. TSF provides them relief through free internet connectivity which helps them remain in contact with their relatives and look for essential information for their future.

title: Mental Health Initiative
description: AarogyaSeva's Mental Health Initiative is a holistic approach that promotes awareness about mental health issues, provides medical support and reduces stigma and discrimination of people with mental illnesses. Through this initiative and similar such partnerships in the future we aim to promote mental wellness and destigmatize mental illnesses.   Covid 19 has left us taking several steps behind in this effort and significantly affected numerous frontline workers.

title: East Africa Food Crisis
description: The Horn of Africa is facing one of the worst droughts on record with some 14 million people in Ethiopia, Kenya, and Somaliland facing severe hunger and water shortages. ActionAid is working with local partners to provide food relief.

title: Support our COVID19 Vaccination Mobile Clinic
description: Since the launch of the COVID19 Vaccination Campaign by the Government of Zimbabwe in 2021, only 48% of the rural population have been vaccinated. This low vaccination drive in rural areas has been caused by lack of health facilities in remote locations to facilitate vaccination, and lack of vaccine education causing people to be worried about the unknown effects of the vaccine. The country continues to see onward infection due to lack of access to vaccine information and the vaccine itself.

title: SUPPORT FOR ACCESS TO HOUSING FOR 50 VULNERABLE
description: The Batwa as well as the other vulnerable people of certain Burundian communities live in the most deplorable conditions in isolated sites and pitiful makeshift dwellings. This problem of non-access to decent housing makes them discriminate against other communities of the Burundian population. This situation has been aggravated by COVID-19. This Project aims at the construction of 50 new houses and a durable and comfortable toilet per family which will make 375 beneficiaries.

title: Help Uyghur mothers with Childcare in Turkey
description: This project will assist Uyghur mothers whose employment is jeopardized because they cannot afford to pay for childcare.

title: Emergency Cholera Response Assistance in Cameroon
description: This project is an emergency response to the recent cholera outbreak in the South-West Region of Cameroon that is threatening lives of many people. In the Limbe, Kumba, Buea and Tiko health districts, we are working with community health volunteers to carry out community sensitization on cholera reaching a minimum of 600.000 inhabitants. We also increase the consumption of safe drinking water through the distribution of aqua-tabs to 26.664 households.

title: Help 3 750 rural children have a meal at school
description: This project is to provide food for lunch at 15 primary schools in rural area of Burkina Faso. Food is a very important factor in the child development and a very strong motivator to attend school. For many of the 3.750 children of those 15 schools, food is scares at home. The lunch program of rice, beans, oil and salt is essential for those kids.

title: Reproductive Sexual Health for Venezuela
description: The project is aimed at responding to the urgent needs of Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) of the most affected populations in Venezuela. The project will consider the following activities: Prevention of maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality in the States: Apure, Amazonas and Guarico. Ensure the availability of life-saving post-abortion care in selected health facilities. Prevention of unwanted pregnancies in Apure Guarico and Amazonas.

title: Help Ukrainian Refugees Access Mental Health!
description: This project will help set up pop-up clinics throughout the UK and the EU to provide mental health services to Ukrainians fleeing war in their home-country. We will train 30 practitioners from all over the United Kingdom and Europe and are already setting up clinics along bordering countries with Ukraine to provide trauma-informed care to migrants and refugees coming in.

title: Empowering women and girls in Mexican communities
description: The rights of women and girls in Mexico need to be guaranteed. For more than 30 years, Fondo Semillas has been the only feminist fund in Mexico. Our mission is to contribute to gender equality and fair social change by providing economic resources, institutional strengthening, and training for groups of low-income women leaders in their communities. Fondo Semillas knows that the leadership of women is essential to achieve a more just and equitable society.

title: Study Aid for 16 Palestinian University students
description: This project aims to assist 16 Palestinian Scholarship students who are pursuing university studies in Malaysia and are in need of financial assistance to cover living and other expenses. With this financial support, we hope to relieve them of their financial stress so that they can focus on their studies and successfully acquire their degree.

title: Fund Our New English School Building in Laos
description: WE NEED YOUR HELP TODAY! A gift to this project takes us one step closer to our goal to build a sustainable english educational centre in a very neglected rural farming community in Laos. English is such an important asset for Lao students because the major industries require international cooperation. In this farming community, higher/vocational education isn't readily available and your gift will provide a place for the community to learn.

title: Reduce the Literacy Gap through Dance - USA
description: This project will advance literacy learning through dance for underserved children across the USA by providing diverse books, dancewear, and mentorship for all children in our programming.

title: Education for growing food and environment care
description: This project consists in the construction of a community greenhouse and an environmental education workshop cicle in the Valparaiso Region, Chile. The objective of these spaces is to meet the educational and recreational needs of communities within the framework of caring for the environment, contact with nature and food sustainability. The main beneficiaries of this initiative are children and older adults, positioning them as main agents of the changes that our planet needs today.

title: Food security in Cundinamarca
description: Our project is based in 5 semiurban and rural towns, located in the metropolitan region of Bogota, where 426 families participate. We promote the consumption of fruits and vegetables through nutritional education and agroecological practices in communitarian orchards and edible forests. We provide income generation training to improve livelihoods and empower them in their economic development, in subjects as marketing, personal finance, administration and communications.

title: Holistic development of slum residents
description: This project aims to resolve the dearth of early childhood care and guidance for all slum children along with the unavailability of alternative avenues for the academically unsuccessful students in addition to the scarcity of free clinical consultations, pathological diagnosis, medicines, nutritional supplements, hygiene kits, and health education sessions for the underprivileged people including the scantiness of public toilets, hand washing units and other sanitation facilities in the slums.

title: Scholarship for Nang Mwe
description: At We women Myanmar we believe in equal opportunities for everyone, irrespective of gender or ethnicity, culture, education and religious believes. We assist ambitious women who are working towards an equal society, with the ultimate goal of an established, self empowered and influential community of women leaders. This specific scholarship is part of our leadership project, we want to support Nang Mwe  in her endeavour to achieve equality for her community in Shan State.

title: Kitengela Academy Primary Sch supports 50 orphans
description: This project aims to keep a private school and orphanage from closure, following the impact of covid on income from fee-paying pupils. This project aims to support the school with its immediate shortfall in income and to help to build a sustainable cost and revenue model to provide long term security for the children it serves.  Closure of the school would leave 30 orphans without a home, care, food or education and a further 20 orphans would be without education.

title: Big Ride 2022: Cycling for Children in Palestine
description: The ongoing occupation of Palestine has traumatized children & caused psychological damage. Physical activity improves mental and physical health and provides children living under occupation a taste of childhood. The Big Ride for Palestine is teaming up with MECA to raise funds to give Palestinian children opportunities to cycle and play. Ride with us for Freedom, Justice & Equality for the Palestinians! Sign up for the Big Ride at www.thebigride4palestine.com and support our fundraiser

title: Sekoly: Sarisambo
description: Project Sekoly is SEED's ongoing school construction project aiming to improve health and education outcomes for children in rural communities of southeast Madagascar. This project with the Sarisambo Primary and Lower Secondary Schools will repair and construct a new school building, 6 classrooms, a teachers' house, 10 latrines, 2 clean water sources, and 2 menstrual hygiene management facilities allowing the 726 annual students to learn in a safe and comfortable environment.

title: This Ramadan, Educate 3000 Students in Afghanistan
description: Teach for Afghanistan Organization is working relentlessly to provide better learning opportunities to students in Parwan and Nangarhar provinces. With your donations, our 60 fellows can create mathematics and science-based teaching models and laboratory equipment with proper resources and educate 2000 girls and 1000 boys.

title: Help 40 Marginalized Youth Access Higher Education
description: With your help, BEAM Education Foundations will financially support 40 marginalized Myanmar youth to take the international high school equivalency examination (GED) and attend college. BEAM provides academic knowledge and fosters youth participation at the community level within the Thai-Myanmar border area and inside Myanmar. Students need support with the GED exams fees to certify their education level. The GED exam is made up of 4 subjects and a previous "Ready Test" for each subject.

title: Help for the wounded in Ukraine during the war
description: Innocent Ukrainians are dying and suffering every day from Russia's barbaric actions - they are ruthlessly shelling our homes, kindergartens, hospitals and even maternity wards. Russian forces have no pity for children, pregnant women or the elderly. But despite the fear of death, Ukrainians continue to help each other. Doctors and medical staff are forced to live in their workplace. In addition to the wounded, there are also non-transportable patients in medical institutions.

title: FEBA #AllTogether4Ukraine
description: As FEBA we are supporting our members in Ukraine and in the neighboring countries who are helping the people of Ukraine.  We are actively monitoring the situation to map, identify and provide support to the immediate as well as medium and long-term needs of our members, especially in Ukraine, Moldova, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia.

title: Habitat for Humanity: Ukrainian Refugee Response
description: Right now, Habitat is addressing the immediate and mid-term shelter needs of Ukrainian civilians seeking refuge in Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia, with special attention to vulnerable individuals, such as single mothers, the elderly, people with disabilities or chronic illnesses, and nationals of third-party countries residing in Ukraine when the conflict began. As the situation within Ukraine continues to unfold, we remain flexible in our approach in neighboring countries.

title: Changing the lives of 250 indigenous Girl Students
description: Indigenous girls are facing many challenges particularly in rural India Most of the rural families don't encourage their girls to attend schools and colleges due to poverty and discrimination; parents also feel girls are burden to them. Parents are forced to decide to get their daughters married. They live in rural areas where there are no colleges for their higher education. Some are discontinuing their studies. Initiated  to bring change in the lives of girls through educational support.

title: Save heroes who protect world from evil in Ukraine
description: Project will help injured warriors, civilians and children to heal 4 times faster with wound VAC therapy. Millions of Ukrainians have been thrust into the midst of military and humanitarian disaster, with the number of injured and murdered rising by the day. While Russian crimes in Ukraine have horrified and scared the world, Ukrainians' bravery in fighting for their freedom, democracy and the fundamental values of a sovereign country has garnered the support of millions of people worldwide.

title: Artistic and feminist camp for the rights of indig
description: The artistic and feminist camp for the rights of indigenous and Afro-Mexican girls is a proposal that promotes the autonomy and empowerment of girls and young women through comprehensive sexual education and the development of socio-emotional skills, from an intercultural and anti-racist perspective, for the prevention of sexual violence.

title: Harbir needs clean water!
description: The community of Harbir have asked HOPE to help them gain access to clean water.  They know that when clean water is locally available, health will improve, children will be able to attend school regularly, more food will be grown and adults will have more time to pursue economic-related activities which will benefit their families and community.  Clean water will bring hope for their future.

title: Haiti sale adelante // Haiti gets ahead
description: Queremos lograr la meta de dar atencion medica junto y talleres de prevencion de enfermedades a 1000 familias afectadas por el terremoto de Haiti en comunidades excluidas del sur del pais. // We want to achieve the goal of providing medical care and disease prevention workshops to 1000 families affected by the earthquake in Haiti in excluded communities in the south of the country.

title: SUPPORTING A SCHOOL OF MUSIC IN HONDURAS
description: This project aims to raise funds for the purchase of musical instruments for the Municipal Music School of Villa de San Antonio in Honduras. It currently serves 55 children and young people between the ages of 6 and 18, offering free piano, violin, percussion and flute classes. This school aims to teach music, values and the strengthening of self-esteem, to contribute to the education of children and young people from the municipality and nearby communities.

title: Shuttle Service as a Sustainability Program
description: Having a second minibus will help take our kids to school and also generate some funds for our daily programs. The minibus will also be used as a shuttle bus to help us bring in revenue from our growing tourism business. We will be creating travel arrangements with hotels, tourism companies, other businesses and schools that need transport services. Profits from this business will be used to keep our youth centre sustainable and help it grow.

title: Tropical Storm Megi Relief and Recovery
description: We will provide food, hygiene kits and livelihood support for 1,200 families in Leyte affected by Tropical Storm Megi (local name: Agaton). The Tropical storm is the first for this year to hit the country resulting to massive flooding and loss of livelihoods among thousands of families. We will provide food packs, hygiene kits such as soap and livelihood support to families affected by the tropical storm.

title: Help vulnerable children in Akkar during Ramadan
description: The deterioration of the socio-economic status in Lebanon, the skyrocketing prices and the COVID-19 have affected many families. This Ramadan, followed by Eid El Fter, the expenses further increase. People in Akkar who were already struggling to meet their needs, do not have enough money to prepare for the holy month and buy the essential food.  Help us to ensure that deprived individuals in Akkar will not be left hungry in Ramadan and will partake in the joy of Eid.

title: Sewing For Hope
description: The aim of the project is to introduce a group of up to 45 women to professional sewing. We currently have10 sewing machines and one trainer. Women were trained over the course of 6-9 months, after which they have acquired a specific and employable skills.  With this fundraiser Partners For Conservation aims to purchase 35 additional sewing machines and materials to enable women to work together towards their social economic inclusion and welfare. Please watch the video for more information.

title: Send Street Child Team Nepal to the World Cup!
description: Help us send Street Child Team Nepal to the Street Child United World Cup and transform their education and future.  The event unites street-connected young people from across the world to take part in a football tournament, a festival of arts, and advocate for street children's rights and protection. The event will highlight the challenges street-connected children face on a daily basis, including their limited access to education, risk of exploitation, and constant threats of violence.

title: Tropical Storm Agaton/Megi Relief Fund
description: Tropical Storm Megi, locally named Agaton, left a devastating toll on the eastern and southern coasts of the Philippines. Since making landfall, more than 75 people have been killed and hundreds of thousands have been displaced. This relief fund will support emergency aid like food, water, medicine, and shelter. After initial needs are met, the fund will transition to provide long-term assistance as needed.

title: Regenerate the Amazon!
description: Our goals are simple: planting native trees on deforested lands in the Peruvian Amazon and protecting pristine acres of rainforest - while generating long-term sustainability by empowering local communities through diversified agroforestry systems.   We work with native species in forest-imitating agroforestry polyculture planting systems - never monocultures. And we work with native communities to maximize socio-economic impacts. The right trees in the right places with the right people.

title: Spay and Neuter 10,000 Dogs & Cats In The Bahamas
description: Operating our new mobile spay and neuter clinic, we aim to reduce the number of stray and suffering dogs and cats in the Bahamas through sterilization. Our goal is to perform 5,000 surgeries annually for the next two years. We will be concentrating on the main island of New Providence, with some smaller clinics on the family islands. We will also provide educational community outreach that focuses on responsible pet ownership for sustainable results.

title: Provision of safe and clean  water to 4000 people
description: The recurring conflicts in South Sudan have displaced thousands of people from their homes and disrupted their livelihood, making them vulnerable to access to safe and clean drinking water.      1) Provided safe and clean drinking water to 4000 Internal displaced persons and returnees.   2) 20 community members acquired skills in boreholes minor pump mechanics, water usage committees, and hygiene promoters   3)Drilling of four boreholes to provide clean water to 4000 people in rural communities.

title: Rock for Ukraine - music therapy for children
description: If you ever wanted to make a real difference in your lifetime here is your chance - LET'S HELP THE UKRAINIAN CHILDREN here in Poland and let their voices send a message around the world that can't be ignored...

title: HOPE Africa disaster relief
description: Disasters such as fires and floods destroy entire informal settlements leaving South Africans who live below the poverty line with no shelter, food or belongings. Mobilizing resources to assist these communities is always delayed or never arrives due to bureaucracy. This initiative will assist at least 60% of disaster stricken families within a week. People will receive food, clothing, school uniforms, building materials and blankets to rebuild immediately after a disaster.

title: South Africa Flood Relief Fund
description: At least 440 people have died in flash flooding and landslides in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa after hours of torrential rain. GlobalGiving is working closely with our partners on the ground in South Africa to get emergency support to impacted communities in this time of need.

title: Tropical Storm Agaton (Megi) Support Project
description: We will provide immediate food and home essential support to 300 families affected by Tropical Storm Megi in 3 bady-hit villages in Baybay City, Leyte as well as in 1 village in Albuera Municipality where we are based. The massive landslide has caused widespread destruction and the need for support to affected families in urgent and important.

title: Floods in Colombia Emergency Fund
description: The Ayapel region (NorthEastern Colombia) continues to face climate-caused flooding. Families have been displaced. Crops have been lost. Thousands of families need help right now.

title: Right tree, Right place, Right product
description: Collecting 1 million seeds of Zambia's indigenous trees best suited to maximising carbon storage and reducing effects of climate change.  Not all trees produce seeds each year so we will develop a seed bank to store and maintain seeds when they become available, until the most opportune time to plant.   Smallholder farming communities will get skills in establishing tree nurseries and tree planting schemes so they can take ownership of forest regeneration that also improves their livelihoods.

title: Integrated support for refugees from Ukraine
description: Romania is preparing the transition from emergency solutions offered to refugees fleeing the war in Ukraine, to longer-term solutions to be offered especially to the most vulnerable willing to settle in the country. Groupe SOS and Ateliere Fara Frontiere, along with public and private partners, are launching a pilot program to provide a 360 solution to 50 vulnerable households (100 beneficiaries), for 6 months, from medium-term accommodation to full social support (legal, social, psychological).

title: Early Education & School Development in Ghana
description: While most children in Ghana do attend school, the standard of education can be fairly low, and schools are often under-resourced and/or overcrowded. GVI Charitable Programs is partnered with nearly a dozen local schools in the community of Kokrobite to provide additional staff training resources, recruitment and onboarding of new teachers, necessary materials for learners (books, writing utensils, computers, stable internet access), and first-aid training to school staff.

title: Support a Nigerian Nonprofit to Buy a Motorcycle
description: This project will support us to buy a motorcycle in order to improve on our community engagements and better achieve our goals.
