Your donation to the Haiti Crisis Relief Fund will provide emergency assistance to people in need and support long-term response efforts led by local organizations who continue to deliver vital services.

title: Engaging youth in awareness for children's rights
description: CAMELEON's 65 Youth Advocates, and 40 girl survivors of sexual abuse who practice circus, act together to raise awareness about children's rights and sexual education in their local communities in the Philippines. They combine social circus with workshops addressed to children and parents from disadvantaged background in rural areas. They inform them about children's rights, Internet dangers, the fight against sexual violence, as well as sexual education and teenage pregnancy awareness.

title: Increasing Inclusion in Somalia
description: In Somalia, a toxic mix of conflict, severe drought and floods has left the country with almost 4 million displaced people. Loop has provided a  safe, free, independent and anonymous  platform for people to report on aid diversion and human rights violations. The time has come to extend our reach to marginalised groups and excluded communities, who, tragically, remain unheard. Join us in this vital mission, for their voices deserve to be acknowledged and amplified.

title: Prevent homelessness of the elderly in Puerto Rico
description: There are thousands of older adults in Puerto Rico at imminent risk of experiencing homelessness. Most of them face social determinants of health that expose them daily to losing their homes, such as economic stability, education access, and quality, health care access and quality, neighborhood and built environment, and social and community context, among others. Our Community Development Program impacts more than 1,000 older adults in Puerto Rico to prevent them from becoming homeless.

title: COMMUNITY-BASED SOLUTIONS FOR WATER, AIR AND FOOD
description: The uniqueness of WAFA is to present silent heroes and share stories of how they have addressed their challenges and solved them with local, sustainable resources for communities that can be shared across the world.  We want to acknowledge and reward pioneering projects in WATER, AIR and FOOD with at least two years of proven results. We want to give recognition and assists communities -through exposure for the finalists and winners of the awards to attract public attention, funding, partnership

title: Feed 300 Families This Christmas
description: Help us in feeding 300 families this Christmas. We would like to help families get through the Christmas season by providing them with food parcels.

title: Heaters for winter in Kharkiv Ukraine
description: This project will provide simple heaters and cookers to many families in Kharkiv, Ukraine who, because of war, have been left with no electricity or means to cook their food or to keep warm.  The Heaters/Wood stoves are manufactured by a Ukrainian company, Grafix, and carried out at cost. Website: www.grafix.in.ua   Wood can be purchased through a Ukrainian government website at:  https://drovae.gov.ua

title: Connect Rural Youth to Digital Learning - Honduras
description: Fabretto is launching a technology integration program in rural secondary (7th-12th grade) schools in Honduras, directly impacting at least 2,000 underserved rural youth and their 140 teachers, who otherwise would have no access to technology. Fabretto and local partner Bayan will distribute kits of hardware and digital resources to make learning accessible offline, using the open-source Kolibri platform, and train teachers to integrate tech in the classroom.

title: Leukemia & HIV diagnosis for 200 kids in Venezuela
description: Fundacion Jacinto Convit seeks to impact 200 vulnerable children in public hospitals in Venezuela during 6 months, by providing them with a free of cost, early, precise and personalized molecular diagnosis in leukemia & HIV. This project will significantly improve the quality-of-life of diagnosed patients, their prognosis and response to treatment, as well as their survival rate due to early detection, stratification of disease risk and the possibility of determining the most adequate treatment.

title: Young people are leaders of change in Iraq
description: Establishing a center in Iraq to rehabilitate and educate young people in an interactive and applied manner, and education methods focus on building mental, emotional, spiritual and economic capacities and rejecting violence and extremism. The curriculum aims to teach youth entrepreneurship skills - financial skills - life skills, personal characteristics, and renounce violence and extremism. Young people can overcome the trauma of war and violence and help them discover opportunities for growth

title: Help 100 Female Entrepreneurs from Rio de Janeiro
description: The work that www.asplande.org.br has been developing since 1992 has already impacted the lives of about 10,000 women entrepreneurs. We support female entrepreneurship through courses, individual and collective mentoring and networking among entrepreneurs. The main objective of this project is to continue to help these women in the ASPLANDE's program "Mulheres em Rede Compartilhando Saberes" (Women in Network Sharing Knowledge), we hope to support the enterprise of about 100 women in 2023.

title: Help young women in Togo end computer illiteracy
description: The full-Blown and Independant Women  project provides a co-practising space for young computer illiterates women in the southern region of Togo. Through a well designed program, we train young women in computer skills such as coding, office automation and female leadership. More than thousands of young girls have been sensitised on the importance of ICT and good leadership to empower them being active players of a sustainable development.

title: Building an alternative Network to Stop VAW
description: This project will build a support network of alternative actors to support women with low educational levels who are living in violent circumstances. This support network will be trained to provide proper emotional support to women who are victims of violence and will be trained to mitigate the factors that contribute to victims not reporting their experiences or asking for help.

title: Support food security & Livelihood of 1000 Ugandan
description: The project  address food insecurity and livelihood in karamoja Uganda (Abim and Kotido). Through donor support will distribute agriculture inputs to 1000 beneficiaries 500 kotido and 500 Abim districts which are in a crisis of food shortage due to food insecurity, flooding, drought and farming practice in this community are very poor resulting into problem of food insecurity, poverty and environmental degradation. PERDL to provide technical guidance, training & agriculture inputs as a solution.

title: HeadStart Festive Food Drive
description: The HeadStart Trust would like to support 72 families of Jongensklip Primary this festive season by distributing food hampers to these underprivileged children, low-income families and vulnerable communities. These food hampers will assist the recipients and their families with adequate food supply for the festive season. With support from current and prospective donors, we can spread a message of hope this festive season through the joy of giving.

title: School supplies for children in Nepal
description: The main duty for all kids is to study. Children of Nepal face a number of challenges on the way to getting educated because of different socio-economic reasons. Walking long distances to reach the school holding books in hands - it's their everyday reality. FOH will help kids from rural Ramechhap area of Nepal with uniforms, sneakers, school bags and main school supplies.  These children are enlightened leaders of tomorrow, let's help them together.

title: RESCUING 5 GIRLS FROM HUMAN TRAFFICKING
description: You can help 5 girls survive the slavery of sexual exploitation and thereby achieve freedom and a life of dignity.

title: Help Survivors Flashflood West Bali Indonesia 2022
description: The rain pouring down Bali, especially in the Jembrana Regency since the weekend of October 15, 2022, has caused a number of villages along the river in District Jembrana to experience mudflows carrying fallen wood and trees. A flash flood on Sunday, October 16, 2022, impacted four sub-districts and more than 3,000 families living in seven evacuation sites. Help is needed to provide these survivors with warm clothes, clean water, and blankets as the rainfall continues pouring into the District.

title: Support Women's WONDER Hubs in Tanzania
description: The WONDER Hub initiative is part of the Women's EARTH Project which provides One Health training to rural women in Tanzania. One Health is an approach that recognizes the link between human, animal, and ecosystem health and is critical to restoring balance between humans and nature. The WONDER Hub network will enable women across Tanzania's Southern Highlands to collaborate on regenerative solutions to strengthen species-wide health, climate resilience, and biodiversity protection.

title: Beehives for life in the Bornean rainforest.
description: The Bornean Rainforest is home to immense biodiversity and hundreds of Indigenous communities but is one of the world's most endangered ecosystems. A lack of economic opportunity can drive practices like forest burning and wildlife poaching. Planet Indonesia's team works with communities to provide the tools, skills, and knowledge for them to set up new enterprises, such as itama honey bee keeping that provides a biodiversity-based livelihood and gives back to the forest.

title: Resilient Communities Through Mindful Practices
description: The program provides disadvantaged communities with sustainable wellness education and practices. Its use of the science of mindfulness such as Yoga and Meditation, sports, arts and crafts, creative recycling, and journaling helps in developing resilience, improving self-care, inculcating positive coping strategies, and promoting positive social transformation. The goal is to train abused women beneficiaries to be mindfulness teachers to cultivate a culture that is independent and engaged.

title: Building secure Livelihoods
description: Together, we've impacted the lives of over 200 vulnerable children by tackling the root causes of poverty by further helping small-scale farmers build their farms into commercial businesses that can generate enough income to enable them to send their children to school, have better health and nutrition, protect children from violence especially stopping child marriage.

title: Give a Rabbit, improve Incomes of Ugandan farmers
description: The micro project will provide rabbits of good breed self-help groups also called Village Savings and Loans Association (VSLA) of 20 members. The rabbits will not only improve the families' nutrition but will also diversify the farmer's incomes through rabbit sales. Rabbit manure will be collected and used to improve their soils as a substitute for synthetic fertilizers. Replication model; the first round of baby rabbits will be given to other self-help groups, thus ensuring continuity.

title: 10000 trees for coastal protection in Bangladesh
description: This project will initiate 10 km roadside tree plantation program for coastal protection in Bangladesh. These donations will help empower women and girls in disaster risk reduction and environmental protection. Project will reach to 2 million disaster vulnerable coastal people of Bangladesh in South Asia.

title: House 80 Rural Liberian Students Annually
description: Limited access to secondary schools in rural Liberia compels over 20,000 rural students to pursue secondary education in urban communities each year. But the lack of support to accommodate these students forces them to drop from school and return to their rural communities where they continue to live in poverty. Your donation will go towards the construction of an initial housing unit to provide charitable urban accommodation for rural students as they seek to overcome this challenge.

title: christmas meals for 700 needy children in ghana
description: Christmas is a time where Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus christ through celebrations, feasting and showing love to one another but unfortunately many needy children in slums and deprived communities in Ghana go hungry. We at dels foundation and you our donors believe this should not be the case and therefore,this is an opportunity to feed 700 of such children

title: Help 175 Malawian Children become Seizure Free
description: This project will provide Epilepsy Medications to 175 Children with Disabilities attending our Epilepsy Clinics.  Children of Blessing Trust runs 2 Epilepsy Clinics at our main site in Lilongwe each month and at least one clinic each month in our 10 Outreach Communities.  The children are assessed by a health professional and provided with medication for 1 month.  Children who are new or not stable on medications are seen at the main site.  Children who are stable are seen at the Outreach Clinic

title: Nigeria Flood Relief Fund
description: Communities across Nigeria are experiencing the worst floods in at least 10 years. More than 600 people have been killed and 2.8 million people have been displaced from their homes. The floods are striking during a difficult period in Nigeria with soaring inflation and a growing risk of catastrophic levels of hunger. Your donation to the Nigeria Flood Relief Fund will provide immediate and long-term relief in affected communities.

title: Art Festival for Community Development in Lima!
description: NEXOS COMUNITARIOS is supporting The Art Festival For Community Development, a project led by our partners from PUCKLLAY. This Festival is a unique opportunity to reduce the distance between the city and the peri-urban areas of the it (mainly inhabited by migrants from the Andes and Amazon) through the use of different expressions of Art.

title: Boys and Men Alliance Project
description: This project will be an essential step in helping to end child marriage in the rural district of Sinazongwe in Zambia, 1 of the top 15 hotspots for child marriage in the world.  We intend to run workshops that will reach 500 boys and men who are relatives of girls participating on our Own your Destiny Girls' Football League.  Workshops will include training on how become a community advocate for girls' education, as well as teaching about important Government policies that support girls' rights.

title: Baemedi program: Sponsor and match with a Child
description: General individuals, who we fondly call Baemedi's, from all over the world choose to sponsor a child's monthly fees, ensuring the future of Ratanang and our impact in the lives of young families.

title: Computer Training Centers for Afghan Girls
description: AAFF operates 2 computer training centers within public schools for Afghan girls in Northern Afghanistan. Many Afghan girls do not have access to technology and lack basic knowledge of computer skills. AAFF's courses taught by qualified female Afghan teachers equip the next generation of girls valuable computer skills that will enhance their education and equip them for a brighter future. The courses have the capacity to provide computer literacy training to hundreds of Afghan girls a year.

title: Support Access to Rights for Refugees in Bulgaria
description: The Foundation for Access to Rights - FAR is a Bulgarian NGO, which provides legal aid to migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and stateless people in situations of system-based obstacles in the access to their fundamental rights such as asylum, safety, liberty, healthcare, family unity, labor, prohibition of inhuman and degrading treatment, etc. We work towards solutions that can ultimately enhance wider social justice.

title: Warm To Be
description: Under the slogan "Warm To Be", the Union of Relief and Development Associations in Lebanon launches the 2022/2023 winter campaign, with the aim of providing basic necessities to confront the winter cold and its dangers. Beneficiaries from the most vulnerable groups in Lebanon will benefit from necessities such as food, shelter, heating and other relief items.

title: Lighting Up Tharparkar
description: Global-Giving and NHSD has constructed 30 houses in Mithrio Charan and Mithrio Suttar in District Tharparkar. And these same houses now have light because of solar panels installed in the same 30 houses. Now they have a lightbulb and a pedestal fan.  They are given these blessings, but we hope to expand this for tubewells and other residents of Tharparkar. We want to light up Tharparkar, and your donations will assist in making this possible.

title: End Child Marriages for 2000 Young Girls in Malawi
description: This project will bring back to school 2000 girls from two districts in Malawi who were forced into child marriages due to harmful traditional and religious practices and peer pressure. Social Development and Advocacy Centre (SODAC) will work with the Government of Malawi to protect young girls from child marriage and other harmful practices by increasing knowledge and understanding among traditional/religious/community leaders on the harm associated with child marriages and teenage pregnancies.

title: Educate one Empower Thousands:changemaker LinKham
description: Educate one Empower thousands, supports women into leadership positions, this campaign specifically generates funding to access higher education. This month the spotlight is on Lin Kham, a young Myanmar role model who aims to achieve education equality for migrant youth. Lin Kham is a dedicated change maker in the world of education for Myanmar migrants in Thailand. She needs financial support to finish her Ma in Social Science, so that she can improve educational access for migrants.

title: Future is NOW! Direct Support.
description: This Project is raising money to provide flexible funding support to BGC Canada in order to support and provide opportunities for the over 200,000 Canadian youth we serve annually.   For 120+ years, BGC Canada has been creating opportunities for millions of Canadian kids and teens. As Canada's largest child and youth-serving charitable and community services organization, our Clubs open their doors to young people of all ages and their families at 736 locations nationwide.

title: It Takes a Village
description: According to the UN, children's malnutrition rate in Venezuela has reached a staggering 26%. Since 2019, Healing Venezuela has been providing two cooked meals and a snack to 100 children at risk of malnutrition in Guaraunos, a remote village in Venezuela. Thanks to our support and the involvement of the entire community, malnutrition rate in the village is 4%. Children's health has improved, encouraging school attendance, and parents and children can look forward to a better future.

title: Stolen Girls... Stolen Futures
description: Journey to Destiny Ministries is on a mission to alleviate the abuse of young girls and women all over the world. We currently have a Center in the Dominican Republic that rescues girls 7-15 from human trafficking and one in Kenya E. Africa offering a vocational training program to girls that have been rescued from forced child marriages.

title: Safe water for 1,000 families in the Philippines
description: This project will distribute tabletop water filters to 1,000 families in installed upland water projects in the Philippines. The tabletop water filter will purify the water of bacteria, parasites, and turbidity, ensuring these families of clean and safe drinking water. It will help to prevent diseases like diarrhea, cholera, parasites, and other waterborne diseases.

title: Affordable Healthcare for Women in Rural India
description: The Indian healthcare system ranks 112/191 countries. Rural areas are especially disadvantaged, with limited state-run infrastructure in place. Mann Deshi is aiming to provide quality healthcare services to last mile women at subsidized rates, through our health center and other services. This funding will go towards covering costs of transportation for patients, maintenance of/investment in new/existing facilities & medical equipment, HR costs & operating costs (inc diagnostic supplies).

title: Support Kasanka National Park's Wildlife Rangers
description: Wildlife rangers work under extremely challenging conditions from being exposed to bad weather, difficult terrain and armed poachers. In Kasanka National Park (KNP), the Resource Protection Unit has been instrumental in combatting poaching activities, guarding the protected areas and preventing illegal land encroachment. Our scouts are always on the frontline of conservation, 24/7. Kasanka Trust Ltd (KTL) directly funds each scout's salary, trainings, rations and equipment.

title: Blooming in La Montana of Guerrero, Mexico
description: With this project we will benefit 250 indigenous children, adolescents and adults, from the Nuu Savi (Mixtec) ethnic group of La Montana of Guerrero, one of the poorest regions in southern Mexico, so they can have access to quality education, healthy food, better nutrition, better income through the sale of crafts, and improve the environment in their communities. Thus, manage to preserve their Mixtec legacy and have the opportunity to achieve their dreams.

title: Recycling Education: Emotional Outlet making toys
description: This project gives children an outlet to their emotions while teaching them about the environment: we have workshops that include talking about the environment and using recyclable materials to make cool toys.

title: Memorial Sensory Garden for Salama Primary School
description: On October 25th, 2022 11 girls (ages 7-10 yrs) were killed in a dormitory fire at Uganda's Salama Primary School for the Blind. The first priority for funds will be purchasing fire extinguishers to prevent this tragedy from ever happening again. Next, a memorial garden including name plaques, fragrant/soft plants, seating, and musical features will be created to foster community healing. Once this project is fully funded we will install a large rain tank for safety, hygiene, and hydration needs.

title: Keep 31 Students in University in Zimbabwe
description: We have 31 incredible Makomborero students enrolled at local Zimbabwe universities! Their university fees have increased from $100usd to $700usd per semester and we are struggling to pay the fees. Help us to clear our bill for this semester and fundraise towards next semester starting in January 2023!    These students are the future leaders of Zimbabwe, and have already overcome incredible obstacles to achieve what they have so far.  Our goal is for them to finish their education well!

title: Change the Future for A Child with Scoliosis
description: In October 2022 a young beneficiary of our organization was diagnosed with Marfan Syndrome, requiring extended therapeutic intervention to give him the best outlook for his future.  We need your help in covering the cost of therapies, devices and equipment required over the coming years.   While we can't be sure of the exact costs our initial target of $3500 is to cover a year of his medical insurance costs. Join us as we walk this journey in helping Alex face this challenge life has presented.

title: Rebuild 100s of Lives and Communities in Ukraine
description: Ukraine and its people have been torn apart by war. Life-saving emergency relief remains important but there is now a need to start to rebuild lives and communities. Well over 800 schools have been damaged (over 100 totally destroyed) as well as many hospitals. Young lives will have severe psychologically trauma. This project will support small scale programmes run by local organisations to rebuild and re-equip communities and rebuild lives.

title: Climate Disaster Fund
description: Founded by Chef Jose Andres, World Central Kitchen (WCK) is first to the frontlines providing fresh meals in response to crises. Climate crisis-fueled extreme weather leads to most of the disasters to which we respond. WCK launched our Climate Disaster Fund so we have the resources to activate immediately and support affected communities with food, water, and other needs. WCK responds to climate disasters including hurricanes, monsoon rains, cyclones, and wildfires.

title: Sustainable and key support for Kibagare Community
description: St Martins School and the Kibagare Community, Nilinde Nijijenge aims to support a sustainable community and in doing so enable this Community to maintain the support that they give.  Working and focussing on those most in need and those who can be enabled.  By creating self-sufficiency across households, we are improving the community in itself.  Kenya is enduring its worst drought in 40 years.  Food and water shortages, coupled with skyrocketing prices are hard-hitting in slum communities

title: Celebrating Six Year's of Supporting Bed-Stuy
description: On October 2016 Playground Coffee Shop opened its doors and in 2018 Playground Youth was created. Through the past six years we have made a commitment to serving our Bed-Stuy community.  As we look forward to the year ahead we are asking for monetary support to cover overhead costs and the upkeep of our change making initiatives. With your help we will be able to expand our impact by guaranteeing more healthy meals, literature, and a safe space to exchange knowledge.

title: YouthAlert! (YA!) "Youth Peace" Program PA
description: Violence, bullying, and abuse, are the "Head of The Snake". They are the number one root cause of many of society's woes including mental health, social health, physical health, substance abuse, unhealthy eating, risky behaviors, and extreme poverty. Fortunately, we know how to stop it; school-based universal, cross-cutting, comprehensive violence prevention education for youth. We must reach all 1.8 billion youth between the ages of 10 and 24 biennially.

title: Educate the Girls-Educate the Nation-Balochistan
description: Education is one of the fundamental rights of citizens secured by any state. The  state guarantees this right through the  Article 25A of constitution which states;  "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of five to sixteen years in such manner as may be determined by law." But, the education for Girls and Boys is very less. Through this project we will provide resources for girls ages 4-20 to get their education in the Province of Balochistan.

title: Breaking the silence: Reproductive Health of Bride
description: Child marriage actually increases exposure to sexual coercion, physical violence and marital rape. Therefore, the ideal is to work with couples and in-laws in the communities to inform them about the health, social and economic benefits of late motherhood and improved birth spacing. Brides represent the largest percentage of sexually active youth and have the lowest rates of contraception and condom use. Brides know less about HIV/AIDS, are less able to negotiate condom use than their unmarried.

title: Combating Antibiotic Resistance in Africa and Asia
description: COVID-19 caused 3.55 million deaths globally in 2021, but antibiotic resistant infections were associated with 4.95 million deaths in 2019 - and that number is expected to rise to 10 million by 2050. Thus we urgently need antibiotic alternatives, particularly in Africa and Asia where 90% of the antibiotic-resistant deaths will occur. Phages for Global Health empowers scientists in Africa and Asia to develop inexpensive, natural antibacterials (phages) that can kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

title: Children's Medical Escort Program
description: Airline Ambassadors International (AAI) provides volunteer escorts for children coming to the United States for medical care that their families cannot afford or is not available in their home countries.  Over the years our flight attendant volunteers have escorted thousands of children.  This program is a unique and rewarding way for airline personnel to volunteer to act as a guardian for a sick and/or frightened child.   Most medical escorts are 1 - 3 days.

title: Build a Middle School in Burkina Faso
description: The Konkourona Alliance Foundation (KAFO), Inc and Mami Siara Na Association of Konkourona (MSN) will build a middle school in Konkourona, Burkina Faso. The number of students progressing to middle school in Konkourona has increased by approximately 15 fold as a result of the partnership between KAFO and MSN and there is currently no middle school in the village.

title: Ukraine Winter - Powering Hospitals & Shelters
description: Our local partners & communities in Ukraine are already facing dire challenges and life threatening situation.   SmartAID is urgently appealing to raise US$250,000 to help make sure that these shelters, hospitals and communities can access electricity and heating to survive the harsh winter and escalation of the war.

title: Medicines for Nigeria's Flood Victims
description: Nigeria is experiencing its worst flooding in over a decade which has displaced millions and killed hundreds with over 200,000 houses either partially and fully damaged. The aftermath of the flood which is often ignored is just as dangerous, as flood waters serve as breeding grounds for mosquitoes and contaminate boreholes and wells. Drug-Aid Africa is working to provide essential medicines to the different Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp set up in the different states affected.

title: Clean Water & New Skills for Uba Dama
description: The community of Uba Dama has asked HOPE to help them gain access to clean water. They know that local, safe water means: health will improve, children will be able to attend school regularly and adults will have more time to pursue economic-related activities which will benefit their future.

title: Protect & Empower Syria's At-Risk Teen Girls
description: Having faced war + trauma, internally displaced Syrian teen girls are at high risk of gender-based violence + child marriage. Project Soar empowers these girls to understand their Value, Voice, Body, Rights + Path using our 25-workshop award-winning teen girl curriculum. With your help, Project Soar will help displaced Syrian girls to speak up, advocate for their rights + set future goals. "A girl without self-confidence is nothing...Project Soar made me a flower blooming..." - Syrian Girls

title: Support Equal Access to Education in Nicaragua
description: We are rallying our donors and sponsors to Give the Gift of Education in 2023! The last few years have brought unprecedented changes worldwide and Nicaragua is no exception. We are asking for donations to our scholarship drive to help support Nicaraguan families and provide a high-quality bilingual education for all students. We are providing scholarships for low-income students who qualify. We ask donors to consider becoming a recurring donor to make a lasting impact!

title: Construction of a health center in Kpangalam
description: At the request of KPANGALAM - CHATEAU's dwellers, the NGO CAV proposes to set up a health center in this corner estimated at more than 6000 persons. The goal of this project is to bring health care closer in this corner. That is part of the second Result  of the NGO's strategic plan, relating to the reduction of the rate of morbidity and maternal and infant mortality by the end of 2025.

title: Give Clean Water to 500 children in Uganda!
description: We were contacted by the Kafunjo Community Project through the connection of a Poured Out volunteer! They are an amazing community group who hosts a school and orphanage for children in Uganda. They are currently undertaking building a secondary school, free clinic, and expanding their agricultural projects to better serve their community. They are in need of a clean water system to supply all the children at the school and orphanage with drinking water.

title: Nigeria Flood Response
description: Flood-prone communities in Nigeria are facing a natural disaster. Perennial flooding has become a challenge for millions of Nigerians who now face an increased risk of displacement, loss of livelihood, or worse. Through ActionAid's signature community-led approach, our team is responding immediately in the most impacted areas.

title: Educate Dominican Republic Families to End Poverty
description: Despite the Dominican Republic's growing economy, more than 30% of the population still lives in poverty. Baitoa is one of many rural areas where families have lived in poverty for several generations. Research shows the most effective means to end poverty is via education, clean water, quality health care, economic security, and empowerment of women & youth. Since 2011 Project Hearts (PH) has served Baitoa with these proven solutions and helped residents achieve a dignified quality of life.

title: FOUNDERS' GIFT
description: Investments in education have an incredible multiplier effect, providing returns for generations. Founders' Gift aims at raising financial resources for a fully owned TSIBA campus, ultimately enabling an organisational purpose to profoundly change the future trajectory of young people from systemic and inter-generational poverty.  TSIBA has created better humans, better communities and a better planet since 2004. It is from our dream campus that we intend to continue this work for decades ahead.

title: Build a self-reliant community in rural Malawi!
description: This project fosters sustainable growth through building long lasting community partnerships. Our mission is to promote community-driven development by utilizing the collective nature of human interaction. Our programs create long-term solutions designed to enhance the lives of rural Malawians. Help us feed 430+ students today and build infrastructure tomorrow. Our integrated approach allows us to support projects across many development sectors. Your gift reaches every corner of our community.

title: Glad's House Football Extravaganza 2023
description: Following the success of Glad's House Kenya "Football Extravaganza" back in 2007, it is our aspiration to run another event in Aug 23 to help reignite, not only the GHK football programme in Mombasa but all our sports programmes, which have suffered greatly following the challenges and restrictions of the past few years. We aim to use this event as a catalyst to create a sustainable sports programme for the local community and more importantly the "Street Children and Young People of Mombasa".

title: Resilient Communities Through Mindful Practices
description: The program provides disadvantaged communities with sustainable wellness education and practices. Its use of the science of mindfulness such as Yoga and Meditation, sports, arts and crafts, creative recycling, and journaling helps in developing resilience, improving self-care, inculcating positive coping strategies, and promoting positive social transformation. The goal is to train abused women beneficiaries to be mindfulness teachers to cultivate a culture that is independent and engaged.

title: Urgent Appeal: Children With Cleft Lip and Palate
description: Children who live in remote areas of Ethiopia already experience food insecurities due to environmental, social and economic factors, these difficulties are heightened for those with cleft lip and palate. Project Harar plans to provide access to life changing surgeries and help end stigma surrounding cleft lip and palate.

title: Bridging the education gap in Venezuela
description: This project will work with local, community-led organisations in Venezuela to reduce the education gap that has resulted from many years of complex humanitarian crisis, and has been further compounded by the pandemic.  By providing incentives to stay in school, resources and training to improve the quality of education that kids receive, and opportunities beyond school, we will improve attendance, achievement, and aspirations. Because these children are the future. And they deserve a future.

title: Influencing Land Rights for women Karatu District
description: Majority of women in Karatu District are illiterate, unaware of existing entitlements and their involvement in land administration is limited. Our practical experience reveals that women's access to land and property is central to women's  economic empowerment as land can serve as a base for food production and income generation. TAJPI will therefore facilitate Land formalization and acquisition of Title Deeds to 100 women. In a long run, it will promote human rights to women community

title: GivingTuesday Match Day  -  NOV 29 2022
description: GivingTuesday is the single LARGEST funding day of the Integral Heart donation calendar. This one day sets us off on a stable footing for a bright and successful 2023 school year.   In partnership with GlobalGiving, we are offered access to a $1.2 MILLION Match fund. The math is simple: THE MORE WE RAISE THE BIGGER OUR SHARE OF THE MATCH POT.  We are 100% Crowdfunded.  All donations raised via GlobalGiving go directly to the Integral Heart School.

title: Be a Hero for the Elderly
description: The Bringas-Haghenbeck Foundation (FBH) is a non-profit, private assistance Institution and authorized grantee in Mexico City. It has more than 87 years of uninterrupted work, assisting the less favored sectors of the community with educational services, housing and care for the elderly, and assistance to the community through open centers; thus, responding to the mission and intention of the founders of the Institutions that have merged into what FBH is today.

title: Get your Gift Matched On GivingTuesday
description: Since 1988, Cape CARES has treated families and communities for three generations, making us one of the oldest NGO's in Honduras! Returning to each community multiple times a year has allowed for Cape CARES to build a team-centered primary care practice that provides medical and dental treatment, follow up care, preventive care, health education, and community needs assessments. None of this would be possible without you, and the generous support of donors like you! Get your gift matched today!

title: TELL: Mental Health Support in Japan
description: TELL is a community mental health NPO serving the international community in Japan.  TELL operates an anonymous and confidential  Lifeline (phone and chat), a mental health clinic, and an outreach program that engages with communities to raise awareness about mental health issues through workshops, trainings, and community support in Japan. TELL has been serving Japan's international community since 1973, and relies on donations to fund these programs.

title: Tropical Storm Nalgae (Paeng) Response
description: Save the Children Philippines is distributing 1,000 hygiene kits, 1,000 household kits, 1,000 jerry cans, and 1,000 learning materials to help children and their families in Western Visayas and Maguindanao survive and recover from the impacts of Severe Tropical Storm Nalgae (local name Paeng).   Save the Children Philippines continues to find ways to ensure that no Filipino children and families will be left behind.

title: Tech Skills&Jobs for 1000 Underserved Youth-Kenya
description: This initiative will provide access to quality digital skills training for 1,000 young people from underprivileged backgrounds from 4 regions in Kenya.The program will also focus on empowering persons with disabilities, girls, and young women, who are often marginalized and face discrimination. It will also help these young people develop the skills they need to succeed in the digital economy, improve their socio-economic status, and make a difference in their communities.

title: Refugee Handcraft Economic Empowerment in DRCongo
description: Over the years since 1996 when the war started in DRCongo, the international community abandoned refugees for reasons which we do not know yet up to now. Rwandan refugees who left Rwanda during the Genocide in 1994 and others in DRC do not enjoy International Protection, forgotten by DRC Government and highly facing hostilities from local hosting communities.  Women and young girls have paid a heavy price over the years, and many are living in dire situation. The only hope is from us now.

title: Support  the identification of refugees in DRC
description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has a long history of hosting refugees but a big number of people came from the period of 1958-1959, the period of 1964-1965, the period of 1975-1976, the period of 1990-1993, the period of 1994-up to now and then 2015. These refugees are mainly from Rwanda and Burundi and live with the host communities but they all not identified and this exposes them to vulnerability and lack of opportunities, to access land and other economic opportunities in order to survive.

title: Educating children in vulnerable conditions rural
description: This project arises as an alternative to guarantee access to education for 500 boys and girls children of single mothers, who due to their condition of poverty and vulnerability do not have the capacity to buy school supplies, shoes and uniforms, thus limiting the children's right to education, being this a universal basic right.  In addition, comprehensive training processes will be promoted, as well as the promotion and strengthening of economic initiatives led by single mothers.

title: Carbon Farming to Mitigate Climate Change
description: This project will pilot a farmer-based climate mitigation solution via carbon farming and the promotion of community-based carbon farms. Small-scale farmers are one of the best drivers in climate mitigation by the practice of regenerative agriculture and promoting the practice via social media and physical farm visits. We will also partner with business so that they will be able to help this initiative.

title: Resilience through agroforestry in Kalimantan
description: The island of Borneo is home to some of the last tropical forests on the planet. Nested in the Indonesian part of Borneo, Central Kalimantan faces many environmental and social challenges such as slash-and-burn methods, deforestation, poor acid sandy soils and an extensive use of chemicals for farming.  Working in Bukit Batu, the project aims to develop and impart agroforestry methods to smallholder farmers to rebuild soil fertility and increase their livelihoods.

title: Keep Early Learning Alive in Rural South Africa
description: Thanda's Early Learning Initiative provides high-quality learning opportunities for 260 children aged between 2 and 5 years old in the rural area of Mtwalume on the south coast of South Africa. Our proprietary curriculum and specially trained teachers and facilitators teach the children more than just numeracy and literacy but also essential life-skills like empathy, critical thinking and self-confidence. Our mission is to empower people to create their own successful lives.

title: Back-a-Budding Entrepreneur
description: The "Back-a-Budding" Campaign supports the provision of entrepreneurship training, seed funding, and micro-grants for young entrepreneurs in JA programs across Africa.  By offering our students a diverse array of programs, opportunities, and resources, we are developing a generation of well-rounded and inspired leaders equipped with the skillsets and mindset to build thriving communities. Help us raise $100,000 to fund 100 entrepreneurs to foster job creation and innovation.

title: Digitally upskill youths in Congo Brazzaville
description: This project will equip a multipurpose room, with computers and books, to serve as a computer lab and library, giving free access to young people in Congo Brazzaville, with the aim to digitally upskill and provide critical literacy support to most especially school dropouts.

title: Rescue baby Kenya
description: Diani Children's Village was initiated in 1994 with intent to Shelter abandoned, abused, and vulnerable children. With poverty being the leading problem, many people can't take care for their infants and end up abandoning them. DCV steps in and takes custody of these children. A medical checkup is undertaken and the best care is administered. Background checkup to trace any living relatives is done and reintegration is encouraged. For those without family a adoption process will start.

title: Help CRUZ ROJA CHAPALA Provide CPR Training
description: Help CRUZ ROJA CHAPALA Provide Emergency CPR, First Aid, Safety, Comfort and Hope to Those in Need. The first responders, Cruz Roja Chapala need more training mannequins and supplies to teach a higher-level CPR and First Aid Classes. The board of Directors of Escuela De Artes Industriales (Have Hammer Will Travel A.C) has seen the need for training mannequins and class supplies, HHWT is asking the friends of our school to partner with Cruz Roja Chapala this Giving Tuesday and get matching funds.

title: Global Hunger Crisis Appeal
description: Right now, 345 million people around the world are facing acute food insecurity.        Among the hardest hit are 22 million people in the Horn of Africa - Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. The worst drought in over 40 years, combined with grain shortages from the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, has resulted in a growing humanitarian crisis unfolding before our eyes.      The land is bone dry. Livestock are dying. Crops are failing.

title: Water and Warmth IOM Giving Tuesday 2022
description: USA for IOM is proud to announce our #GivingTuesday campaign for 2022, "Water and Warmth."   We are seeking to support the delivery of important resources at an especially vulnerable time of crisis for the people of Somalia and Ukraine. Any funding raised through this year's Giving Tuesday campaign will support the Water and Warmth project. In short, the Project will effectively continue to provide life-saving support to millions of migrants in the midst of historic climate crises and conflict.

title: New therapy unit for the elderly
description: The Bringas-Haghenbeck Foundation (FBH) is a non-profit, private assistance Institution and authorized grantee in Mexico City. . Since 1989, elderly people have been attended in a personalized way, through a team of professionals, who manage to reduce the physical, mental, cognitive and emotional deterioration of the residents, thus promoting a better quality of life and reducing the risk of hospitalization.

title: Pain relief medication for children with cancer
description: Through the Palliative Care Program pain relief medication, a special diet and equipment loan are guaranteed not only to the child, but also to the family, in order to give the patient, the possibility to stay comfortable in the household. In this delicate stage, psychological accompaniment it is also provided to the whole family. The Palliative Care Model is being replicated in 4 Latin American countries.

title: Rescue Vulnerable Colobus Monkeys
description: This project will help Colobus Conservation purchase a new vehicle to expand its rescue operations. Through the purchase of a new car, the population of the Angolan Colobus Monkeys will be rescued protected and preserved, resulting in the sustainment of the species. Additionally, the expansion of our operations will provide resilience against climate change for the local communities, due to the increase in the indigenous trees we will be able to supply support in restoring the forest landscapes.

title: Texas and Oklahoma Tornado Relief Fund
description: At least 150 homes have been destroyed and two people killed after more than 12 tornadoes passed through Northeast Texas and Southeastern Oklahoma on November 4th, 2022. With search and rescue missions and damage assessments still underway, your donation to the Texas and Oklahoma Tornado Relief Fund will help people in impacted communities.

title: Support Community Development in the Bahamas
description: Lend a Hand Bahamas was founded to bring more activities, opportunities, and resources to socio-economically disadvantaged areas of the Bahamas. Currently, we are planning and implementing new programs and projects in certain areas of the Bahamas with the long-term goals of connecting with others to offer a collaborative approach towards solving problems around health, education, food security, and the environment.

title: Medical Imaging Suite Improves Diagnostic Ability
description: Modern diagnostic tools are a necessity in today's healthcare. Advances in imaging technologies have transformed medicine and improved health around the world. Without these tools, accurate diagnoses and treatments of diseases and injuries are severely impaired. A new Medical Imaging Suite at the rural Mwandi hospital in western Zambia will provide safe spaces for a variety of current imaging tools allowing physicians to make more reliable diagnoses and provide better care for their patients.

title: CHILD RIGHTS AND CHILD PROTECTION IN 20 PR SCHOOLS
description: SHIPO keeps track of the different needs in the schools and has identified 20 schools which are the most needed ones in terms of School facilities such as Water supply, Latrines, and Dinning all with Kitchens. Therefore, if the schools shall have those facilities, health and performance increase shall improve too. Beneficiaries of the projects are Pupils of 9812 Girls and 6894 Boys as well 160 teachers and 480 orphans. Considering the climate change, Water recharge shall be considered.

title: FHCI University Matching Campaign
description: We are launching a campaign for our University Program! All donations raised will be DOUBLED thanks to Ragan Communications who will be matching our funds!  This means YOUR donation will have DOUBLE the impact!  Donations will cover tuition fees and enable FHCI's students with top grades to further their education and be what they dream to be. In order to successfully achieve this and enable all 11 of FHCI's students to go to university, we need to raise $10,000.

title: FOR $10 HELP REFUGEES HOST COMMUNITIES IN UGANDA
description: Uganda hosts an estimated1.5 million Refugees in the West Nile region. Most of these refugees are from South Sudan and Democratic republic of Congo (DRC). These refugees live with host communities who have welcomed them and they live together. The refugees and host communities togeter share commom public goods that include schools, Health sstems,markets, water,roads and land. Most of these refugees are likely to remain in the country for quite a long time.

title: Help build a maternity hospital in Nairobi's slum
description: This project aims at building a low- cost special maternity wing to help the vulnerable and underprivileged  mothers surviving on less than one dollar a day in the slums of Nairobi to deliver safely in a well equipped facility with qualified healthcare service providers.This will reduce maternal deaths by 90%  and newborns will have a promising and a safe start in life.

title: Send a Child in Aleppo to School for a Year
description: This project focuses on providing literacy and quality education for 100 disadvantaged girls and boys affected by war and ever-growing poverty in Aleppo, Syria. At-risk young people attending public schools, and vocational or university courses, are funded and mentored to ensure school retention, literacy and future livelihood. Today, 86% of Syrian live below the poverty line. Even if public education is free, it is out of reach for many. Through your support, we can give Aleppo children hope.

title: Provide food, water, and critical care in Haiti.
description: Sonje-Ayiti's work continues amidst chaos, violence, Cholera, lockdowns, roadblocks, lack of food, water, medicine and power.  Case managers support 100 community members in a program to alleviate extreme poverty. Food is safely distributed or stipends given to the families of many of the 296 students now unable to have a daily meal to buy seeds for fast-growing crops. Treatment and monitoring are provided to 52 severely malnourished children, and mental health community support for depression.

title: Support Learning centres for slum Children- India
description: BASS India operate  3 After-School Transformational Learning centres for the slum children in Guntur. These slums are situated far from city and where no educational facilities are available. Most of the children's families are living in poverty and are not able to send their children too far to private educational institutions. This project  provides quality primary education to enhance children's ability, confidence, learning levels and skills  and also makes a part of local formal schools.

title: Christmas for 200 families in a Lagos slum
description: Our community impact Christmas project makes Christmas possible for families with low or no income, who are experiencing poverty and cannot afford to put decent  meals on the table or provide Christmas gifts for their children. Every family deserves to experience the love, hope and joy of the season and children should feel loved, special and valued in the joyful spirit of the holiday season. Our goal is to  support 200 underprivileged families in our community to not go hungry this Christmas.

title: Help Form 3000 New Political Leaderships in Brazil
description: RenovaBR will prepare common people into becoming outstanding politicians by selecting and qualifying Brazilians from the most diverse origins, beliefs and political views to make good politics. We understand that we can strengthen the Brazilian democracy by preparing people who are willing to make their communities better through politics.

title: Help the elephants of Cambodia & EVP post pandemic
description: Help us to continue to help the elephants of Cambodia! Currently we are caring for 12 retired & rescued elephants at our sanctuary, while also operating a Mobile Vet Team. Previously reliant on tourism income, ELIE is still feeling the funding shortage due to the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic. Funds raised will support the long-term care for elephants, critical vet programs and support the indigenous Bunong communities we work with, while the tourism industry recovers.

title: Keep 100 Families Warm in NW Syria
description: This campaign aims to provide urgent winter aid for the displaced needy families in Northern Syria. The aid will include emergency winter kits of winter wool clothes, boots, blankets, heaters, and coal. The initial goal of $30,000 will help 100 needy families in NW Syria.

title: Esperanza en la Oscuridad - Hope in the Shadows
description: In "Hope in the Shadows," painter and activist Rita Andrade explores the deep-rooted social issues that young people face in Honduras, and the hopes that keep the country's youth moving forwards. All funds raised through the sale of the paintings will be donated to the NGO educate., which works to provide educational opportunities to underprivileged children and youth in Honduras. (Note: to buy a painting, please also email us at educate.ngo@gmail.com with the name of the painting to reserve it)

title: SOLELab: The future's Library in Boca de Camarones
description: Imagine living without connectivity and Internet access. We believe that technology should serve all of us equally. That is why we are working on:  1. A SOLELab for an indigenous Wayuu community in Colombia: A public space where they can use the Internet to get access to education, digital literacy and create new opportunities, such as economic growth for their community.   2. An open source "solutions guide" for Internet connectivity, so that people can learn alternatives to be connected.

title: RAIN WATER HARVESTING & WATER RECHARGE SYSTEM
description: There is sufficient evidence supporting the fact that climate change and   variability are pervasive realities that are strongly impacting both human and natural systems, including conservation of edible orchids in Southern Highland of Tanzania. Rainwater harvesting (RWH) is one possible appropriate technological option to improve water supply and water recharge for restoration of the water to its nature.

title: ISER Caribe Water & Climate Change Lab
description: The goal of our fundraising is to jumpstart the Water & Climate Change Lab. Water, along with energy, food, healthcare, and communications, are the foundations of sustainable and resilient communities.   The WORP will integrate topics of environmental justice, climate change, and sustainability & resilience (S&R). The Water Lab will be in our new headquarters so that we, as well as other organizations, communities can use them to perform water quality tests.

title: Specialized push-button telephone for blind users
description: The need for a blind person to be in touch with their family, friends and acquaintances seems to be unquestioned. This need became especially urgent for the blind from Ukraine, during the military aggression by Russia. But how can a blind person dial a number? How to find it in the notebook? How to blindly type an SMS or, moreover, read it? For example, about the air raid alert and the need to go to the shelter. Or ask for help during the shelling.

title: Provide income to 250youth by recycling inTanzania
description: NESODO will benefit 60 youth and women in 10 groups of 6 people. These teams will receive training and support to collect, process, and commercialize plastic waste along Lake Victoria. Repurposing and commercializing plastic waste and recycling or reusing plastic in art crafts can provide economical options to women and youth groups and help solve environmental pollution. The groups will receive training in agroforest so that its harvest help them get income in the future.

title: "A Hand Up not a Hand Out" to our local farmers.
description: One of BonZeb's goals is to give support to give assistance to local farmers and right now that aid to supply a second oxen team and plow so that more farmers can get their crops planted. The plow allows them to dig deeper harrows and that means better yields in the long run. The second part of this campaign is to obtain a mule train to move our feedstock down the mountain to our kiln site. This is where the grass is converted into charcoal for cooking. These purchases will also create new jobs.

title: Christmas fund supporting individuals at TN
description: This fundraiser will enable 48 craftsmen and women from the co-operative Tigoung Nonma to buy food and other necessities in time to celebrate Christmas. The association Tigoung Nonma and it's members are experiencing difficulty operating because of the poor security situation in country (ISIL) and the cost of living. There are no tourists in country. Large craft fairs have been cancelled all due to insecurity so the members cannot earn a living.

title: Support a unique education model in rural India
description: Started in 1996 in rural Visakhapatnam, BCT Residential High school caters to both boys & girls of 12-16 yrs. Offering value-based skill-oriented rurally-biased education, it follows the state syllabus for academics. Students also learn vocational skills & train on diverse subjects ranging from computers & robotics, to traditional charkha spinning & folk arts. Even specially-abled children learn academics & vocational skills, making it possible for them to become breadwinners for their families.

title: Climate Change: Mangrove Restoration & Planting
description: Mangroves play a vital role in our critical fight against climate change and time is running out so it really is our final chance to step up and save our planet. Mangroves can be up to 10 times more efficient that terrestrial ecosystems at absorbing carbon long term, making the critical to our fight against climate change. However in Africa they continue to cut them down to make way for tourists, Thailand, Mexico and Indonesia they cut them down to make shrimp pens and in Florida they have few.

title: Give refugee and migrant women a chance to thrive
description: Everyone deserves a chance at a happy life. Unfortunately, thousands of women across the world are forced to leave behind the lives they know in search of safety from violence, war, poverty, and other factors. Once they arrive in a new place, their journey is far from over. You can give migrant and refugee women in our programmes the resources they need to earn a good income, learn the local language, and make connections so they can thrive. We support women from Ukraine, Afghanistan, and more.

title: Help Repair Vital Food Source in Jamaica
description: The INMED Aquaponics Social Enterprise (ASE) farm is a vital source of adaptive agriculture training and food production in Jamaica. Thousands of people in food-insecure communities have benefited from INMED Aquaponics for more than a decade. A recent break-in at the INMED ASE farm resulted in significant theft and damage to the aquaponics system, rendering it temporarily inoperable. We urgently need US$ 5,000 (or about J$ 750,000) to get it running again and properly secured.

title: Improving Nursing & Midwifery Care in Liberia 2023
description: By providing professional development workshops for nursing/midwifery faculty and practicing nurse/midwife hospital clinicians, we hope to continue improving health care outcomes in Liberia. Faculty share updated skills and knowledge with their student populations for a multiplier effect that will reach several hundred soon-to-be health care professionals. Supervisory nurses and midwives will share their newly acquired knowledge with their front-line staff producing another multiplier effect.

title: Adult and Family Literacy in Liberia 2023
description: FLI is a cooperative effort between the FOL, the WE-CARE Foundation, Comic Relief USA, and HIPPY-International, with the goal of teaching parents of preschool children in five impoverished communities how to engage in nurturing and learning activities that prepare their children for school. The goal is to prepare 3, 4 and 5-year old children for long-term academic success while helping parents become more effective at working with their children as they develop their own literacy skills.

title: Provide Meals for 530 students
description: Ninos de Guatemala has taken into consideration nutrition as something very important to ensure student performance. In our case, due to the conditions of the communities in which we work, there are several factors that affect the nutrition and development of students.   By donating to our program we can increase the quality, quantity, and frequency of meals that NDG provides to our 530 students from three Schools.   #KidsShouldFocusonLearningNotOnEmptyStomachs

title: Help Mountainside School Fight Illiteracy
description: The Saul Louis Community School (academic/vocational) will provide 315-350 students and 10 teachers with standard school supplies, proper facilities equipment, and a safe, physical environment, which will fuel quality learning, teaching and success. It will also equip the community's vocational students, currently studying music, and teachers with the instruments needed to produce highly skilled and trained professionals, who can earn a living providing services in their mountainside community.

title: Save Africa's most endangered gorillas
description: The relatively intact highland rainforests in Cameroon are home to populations of critically endangered Cross River gorillas, which are threatened with extinction due to habitat loss and poaching at a time of overlapping global crises. Working with local communities, our project turns poachers into Community Rangers, empowering them to protect great apes and their habitat, while generating income for their families, addressing poverty, food security and youth employment needs.

title: Community Empowerment for Guatemalans & Kenyans
description: GRACE Cares partners the GuateBuena Association (formerly Community Finance Guatemala) and the Watha Project in Kenya are seeking to implement community empowerment projects in their under-served communities. GuateBuena's Reproductive Well-Being program will help 350 women with their menstrual health and family planning while the Watha Project, working with village elders and volunteers, will build its sixth well to provide clean and safe water to hundreds of Watha.

title: Help the animals in Ukraine survive the winter!
description: Happy Paw is a charitable foundation that has been supporting and taking care of animals in shelters throughout Ukraine for over 10 years.   And now, when the critical infrastructure of Ukraine is constantly under attacks because of the war, we must urgently buy firewood, heaters and stoves to give the shelters the opportunity to warm up and cook food for the animals. Otherwise, the animals will simply get extremely cold in winter!

title: Protect a Colombian Child From Sexual Exploitation
description: The project supports children affected by, and at risk of, conflict-related sexual violence and commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) in the cities of Quibdo, Cartagena and Bogota by strengthening the capacities of children and young people to overcome the trauma they suffer as a result of their experiences and to help them understand how to protect themselves from future violence. This project is implemented by two of our partner organizations: CDE and ACJ.

title: Support youth's mental health-social reintegration
description: This project provides a novel community-based narrative approach to psychosocial care, trauma, and reintegration that would help children and young people(CYP) who 1 at risk of joining gangs and 2 were victims of forced recruitment, to gain access to the resources and skills they need to deal with a variety of traumatic situations and stigmas. The project will enhance positive bonds within the community and change situations of vulnerability and criminality through narratives of resilience.

title: Help us Prevent Forced Recruitment Through Footbal
description: The project aims for three hundred Afro-Colombian children divided into twenty two football teams in Choco, Colombia to develop socio-emotional skills and improve their capacities to participate in peace-building processes, towards the prevention of forced recruitment. Sport helps young people connect with their peers and community, gives them a sense of belonging, and helps children develop skills in critical thinking, empathy and managing emotions.

title: Romanian dogs need a safe space to live in!
description: On our DsN farm in Giurgiu, Romania we are currently taking care of 251 dogs and 40 cats. There are dogs that are restricted in many European countries, so we keep them on our farm and take care of them. Those souls need a safe space to live a peaceful life. Unfortunately, their current kennels are in very bad condition, they need new kennels - especially before cold Romanian winter begins! That's why we will build 11 new kennels for them which takes times, energy and costs a lot of money.

title: Hurricane Nicole Relief Fund
description: On November 9, 2022, Hurricane Nicole made landfall near Freeport, Bahamas as a Tropical Storm and then in Florida on November 10 as a Category 1 hurricane. It has caused significant damage and at least four people were killed in Florida. Homes have been seriously damaged and thousands have been left without power. A number of these communities only recently came out of Hurricane Ian, a devastating storm that hit Florida barely two months ago.

title: Educate and Empower - Children/Teens with Autism
description: To provide access to outstanding diagnostic and specialized education for children and adolescents with autism. When a child develops the skills to become more independent and autonomous, his family dynamics get better; The professionals that serve them -and their families- benefit from the opportunity to work and thrive. As a result, the well-being of all parties involved improves.

title: Help Empower 500 Rural Youth and Women
description: This project will empower 500 underprivileged youth and women from Devashtich District of Tajikistan through establishment of a resource centre in School 10 of Ghazantarak Village, which agreed to provide premises for free. The resource centre will empower rural youth and women to get necessary skills and knowledge to find jobs, start their own businesses and create jobs for others. To do this, the center will organize courses and training workshops  on the topics of concern.

title: Give Food Security this Holiday Season!
description: Everyone deserves access to nourishing food that allows them to lead healthy lives, and that's why we need your support this holiday season. The unfortunate reality is that many people in our local communities are coping with food insecurity. Your support helps us to connect individuals and families with immediate food resources, increase access to short-term support, and drive positive lasting change on a legislative level.

title: Wildlife Rescue Centre in Cerro Alux
description: This Giving Tuesday, ARCAS is initiating a campaign to establish a rescue center and offices in the Cerro Alux Reserve, on the outskirts of Guatemala City.  We are currently housed in San Lucas in a rented house that is much too small for our needs, especially for the needs of the animals we receive.  After over 3 years of searching for a suitable site, negotiating, and jumping through bureaucratic hoops (Building permits, EIA) we are now launching our campaign to relocate and rebuild!

title: VENEZUELA: 25 YEARS EDUCATING-FEEDING-HEALING KIDS
description: 25 years later FMMLC continues educating, healing and feeding 400 children each year at the U.E. Jenaro Aguirre.  Students receive 2 daily meals and participate in extracurricular activities: music, art, English, sports. We offer scholarship for our students to continue high school and in some cases college education. Our medical facility provides pediatric, general medicine, gynecology and odontology to our students, their families, and the community.

title: Support Rural Leaders to Drive Change in Honduras!
description: The Solidarity Project is a 501(c)3 organization working with a network of Honduran Community Leaders in seven rural partner communities to execute development projects, cultivate Honduran leaders, and support rural health initiatives.      This project will provide seven micro-grants, leadership programming, stipends for four community interns, community health worker volunteers, and our community pharmacy program with the goal of supporting community driven change in Honduras.

title: Help 2 Mobility Disabled Women in Ethiopia
description: BDO plans to support 2 critically mobility disabled women and girls by providing a wheel chair to ease mobility; provide saleable commodities to generate revolving income to empower economically; and supply hygiene keeping supplies. Acquiring a wheelchair tended to improve social relationships, self-care, play, and mobility.  Access to a wheelchair also has impacts both on social and health needs of the user.

title: Food &Water for 500 Distraught Elephants- Phase II
description: As forest resources rapidly dwindle in Odisha due to development pressures, distressed and famished elephants are entering villages/ cropland to find food and water, by crossing major highways. This is intensifying human-elephant-conflict and a staggering number of elephant deaths caused by vehicle collisions. Restoring degraded habitats with favored elephant plant species and creating waterholes in their habitats can prevent them from crossing treacherous roads for food and water, saving them.

title: One Million Individuals Fighting Against Cancer
description: In Nigeria today, we have six centers with functional radiotherapy machines and they are in Abuja, Lagos, and Enugu. "Based on the International Atomic Energy Management Agency recommendation, any community that has 1,000,000 people is supposed to have a radiotherapy machine. With that said, we require finances in order to provide a brachytherapy unit and a Comprehensive Cancer Treatment Center in a centralized and accessible location in Nigeria.

title: DIRECT AID to Ukrainian Villagers and Soldiers
description: Krzysztof A from Osweicim Poland has been driving supplies into Ukraine since Putin's War began.  He goes directly into the small villages dotting the countryside and brings much needed food for People and Pets.  Dr. Oksana is working on the frontline to help save the lives of wounded soldiers.  Both need funds for the medical supplies, food and blankets.  Krzysztof also needs funds for fuel and vehicle  maintenance.  You can support both of these HEROS - you can help SAVE LIVES NOW!

title: SAVE THE DISABLE CHILDREN IN BANGLADESH
description: SonakhaliManobkollanSebaSangha is an association for working the development of poor special children with disabilities in Bangladesh, we are planning, Measuring, Counting and educating to implement adequate service delivery in action of special Education, health and rehabilitation. Through this project our- organization intends to achieve remarkable improvement of destitute, disadvantaged and most vulnerable children groups in the community. A total 250 disable children would be benefited from

title: Life skills + Soccer for 350 boys in Brazil
description: This project will provide essential life skills to 350 8 to 14 year old boys through futsal classes and workshops providing them with a positive pathway away from drugs and involvement in criminality. We shall occupy public hard courts in the community providing structured classes for children who only get 5 hours of schooling per day - either in the morning, in the afternoon or at night.

title: Champ Needs You To Make His Stay Less Stressful
description: Champ was thrown out at our gate. Can you imagine going from thinking you were part of a family to being dumped out like garbage? Your first few days at an animal shelter can be scary and making this adjustment can be eased by having a clean, safe and comfortable place to lay your head. Champ and others like him need new kennels, repairs to existing kennel doors, new kuranda beds, and new water pails. Champ needs you because life can be scary, but your help gives them hope that someone cares.

title: Ashraya - Social Upliftment Center
description: The objective of "Ashraya" is child protection, to provide systematic education to economically deprived children and empowering women by skill development facilitating their livelihood.

title: Feminist Football Club "La Nuestra"
description: Feminist Football Club "La Nuestra" aims to guarantee an owned space for women and people from the LGBTIQ collective in sports and culture.  La Nuestra maintains its practice dedicated to football played by women and diversities in Villa 31, Buenos Aires, Argentina. The practice links training days with group spaces where sport becomes an area of containment, reflection and expression for those who participate.

title: Giving Tuesday 2022
description: This Giving Tuesday you will have the opportunity to strengthen our vision for peace and equity starting from our base in Loiza. With your donation we will be able to continue developing community health-workers, providing free psychological and psychosocial services for survivors of domestic violence, promoting community leaders and violence interrupters, creating community building activities and developing neutral violence-free zones in the communities and advancing human rights policies.

title: Help Ukrainian children facing two wars
description: No one should left alone in the battle against severe disease. While Ukraine is fighting for freedom, hundreds of Ukrainian children have one more opponent to fight - cancer.   And victory has become one of their sincerest wishes.

title: Help 200 youth in sustainable agriculture Tanzania
description: Help Networking for Society Development Organization to implement the project of solving among of the main challenges facing youth in Tanzania which is unemployment caused by population increase hence accumulation of skilled and unskilled youth. Project aims at increasing opportunities for youth access to implement self employment based on profit making through cultivation of high value crops by using irrigation technology and equipping 200 youth on moneymaker pumps to increase employment

title: Mobile Clinic for Burmese migrants in Thailand
description: Myanmar is undergoing an economic crisis that has led 40% of the population to live below the poverty line. Many Burmese seek a better future in Thailand, where they are easily employed in agriculture, fishing and construction often without health assistance.  MedAcross has activated a mobile clinic that visits migrant villages every month offering medical checkups and training Community Health Volunteers to inform people about their health rights.

title: Bring The Spirit of Christmas to Abaco
description: Your gift will help to increase food security for families in Abaco that are still recovering from the devastation of Hurricane Dorian and the effects of the COVID 19 Global Pandemic. You will be providing supplies for over 200 Backyard Farmers, and providing breakfast to 235 school children.

title: Help 300 Kenyan Youth Break the Cycle of Poverty
description: This Project will increase access to Basic Computer skills, Basics of Entrepreneurship, and Life skills and connect to one-on-one mentorship for three hundred underserved youth in Kenya's biggest informal settlement and the rural village of Kamagut in 4 cohorts of three months each.  It will enhance the social enterprise approach of using recycled paper and waste fabrics to make packaging products subsequently contributing to the livelihoods of these youth and eventually program sustainability.

title: Save Life- Michaela Heart Surgery
description: Michaela is one year old now. She was born with an abnormal opening in the wall (spectrum) between the heart two upper Chambers. The doctors recommended Michaela to go for heart surgery scheduled in January 2022. The total cost of surgery is huge. We kindly request for your support.

title: Therapeutic Riding for 90 NH Youth
description: This project responds to the current mental health crisis by providing 250 hours of combined therapeutic riding and mental health counseling at our center to 90 youth or young adults in Central NH, giving them the critical help they need to respond to their individual challenges.

title: Provide Living Wages & Training for Women in Ghana
description: As a fair trade organization, we are committed to upholding traditional skills while simultaneously creating space for African women to succeed as entrepreneurs and achieve financial independence.

title: Empower teachers to help children in Mexico thrive
description: We are raising $10,000 to help pay for 6 daycare and preschool teachers educating and caring for children from low-income working families in Mexico so that they can increase their potential to thrive.

title: e-Commerce Development for Latin American Artisans
description: Although the pandemic made it much worse, most Latin American artisans and especially indigenous artisans have difficult to earn a living wage by selling their crafts. There are two important reasons for this. They often make goods that they like, not the market. Also, their only customers are those that walk by their small storefronts or souvenir shops.
